1.name: Fettis
pages: * The injury to John Filan saw Roy Hodgson forced to look for a new  goalkeeper for Blackburnin order to cover any possible absences on the part off Tim Flowers. In Alan Fettis he found the ideal substitute. Despite his youth the Northern Irish keeper has good international experience with his country and Roy Hodgson knows that if he needs to call upon him, Fettis won't let him down.

* Alan Fettis is a brave keeper with good reflexes and excellent agility. Slowly but surely is becoming safer when he comes off his line for high balls, probably the weakest part of his game. On the other hand he is a keeper who can be trusted when he is required to used his feet, and it is no surprise to discover that he has also given a very good account  of himself on the exceptional occasions that he has played as an outfield player. He has even allowed himself the luxury of scoring a couple of goals.
x

* 18 full international appearances for Northern Ireland. 
* 2 "B" international appearances. 
* A youth and schoolboy international.

* Born in Belfast he came through the youth ranks at Irish club Ards, signing for Hull City on 14th August 1991 for 50,000 pounds. In his first season in England he played in 43 league games.
* During the 94-95 campaign he was involved in one of the seasons most curious stories. Unable to play in goal due to a thumb injury Fettis made his debut as an outfield player. He even managed to find the back of  the net against league leaders Oxford United, and went on to round off the season with another goal this time against Blackpool.
* He began the 95-96 season with Hull, but on 20th November 1995 he was loaned out to West Bromwich Albion where he played, this time as a goalkeeper, on 7 occasions.
* On 13th January 1996 he was transfered to Nottingham Forest for 250,000 pounds. He was signed by the club to cover the absence of second choice keeper Tommy Wright.
* He made his Premier League debut on 19th April 1997, in a game against the Leeds United at the City Ground. However, he had already made his first team debut for the club in a Cup tie against Chesterfield, coming on when first choice keeper Mark Crossley was sent off.
* He has been a Blackburn Rovers player since 10th September 1997. Fettis arrived at Ewood Park to cover for the injured John Filan.

* With Mark Crossley being an automatic choice in goal for Forest Alan Fettis was forced to spend most of the season on the substitutes bench. Alan made his debut in a cup game against Chesterfield, when he had to come on, as a result of Crossley's sending off. His league debut came four games from the end of the league season. Although he was in goal for Forest in each of those remaining games he was unable to do anything to prevent the club from being relegated to the First Division.

2.name: Filan
pages: * John Filan was signed by Blackburn Rovers to cover the gap left by Shay Given following his departure to Newcastle. The Australian keeper didn't have too much luck at Coventry, where, year after year, Ogrizovic kept his place as an automatic choice in goal for the Sky Blues.  Unfortunately, the injury he suffered at the beginning of the 97-98 season (a broken arm), will now keep him out of action until next season.

* John Filan is a reflex goalkeeper, with great agility and speed, and blessed with tremendous natural athleticism. He is decisive when he comes  off his line, and brave when he has to go down at the feet of opposing  forwards. Technically correct, he is, however, sometimes unsure when going up for high balls into the area, an aspect of his game in which his lack of top level experience is still evident.
x
* Australian under-21 international.

* John Filan began his career with Austrialian club Budapest St. George, based in Sydney.
* On 12th March 1993 he was transfered to Cambridge United for 40,000 pounds. He made his debut on 3rd Abril in a game against Newcastle. 
* A regular member of the side during the 94-95 campaign, the following season he was loaned out to Nottingham Forest although he didn't make  a first team appearance for the club. 
* He arrived at Coventry on 2nd March 1995 i exchange for 300,000 pounds. With Ogrizovic injured, the Australian got the opportunity to make his Premier League debut on the 9th May at White Hart Lane. That day the Sky Blues defeated Tottenham Hotspur 1-3.
* He began the 95-96 season as first choice in goal at Coventry,  under Ron Atkinson, although Ogrizovic's recovery saw him back on the bench Before the end of the season.
* During the 96-97 season he saw just 5 minutes of league action, after coming on for Ogrizovic in the game against Arsenal at Highbury. Ogrizovic broke his nose following an incident with the England international Striker Ian Wright.
* In June 1997 he was transfered to Blackburn Rovers for 700,000 pounds. Unfortunately, with the 97-98 season barely underway he suffered a broken arm following a collision with Sheffield Wednesday striker Wayne Collins.

* For yet another season John Filan had to make do with being Steve Ogrizovic's stand-in at Coventry. His only Premier League appearance came in October when he came on for his colleague five minutes before the end of the game at Highbury against Arsenal. Throughout the season he never really forced his way into Gordon Strachan's plans. On the other hand, he had the good fortune to be called up to the Australian national side coached by Terry Venables.

3.name: Flowers
pages: * Tim Flowers has earned himself a reputation has one of the best goalkeeper in England. An automatic choice at Ewood Park, he made a decisive contribution to Blackburn Rovers title triumph in the 94-95 season. However with regards to the national side he has had to live in the shadow of David Seaman who for the moment has blocked his path to the full England side. During the 97-98 season Tim Flowers will be hoping that on the one hand he can help get Blackburn back in the title race and, on the other, that he is chosen to play in goal for England in the 1998 World Cup Finals in France...with the permission, of course, of David Seaman.

* Tim Flowers is a good technical goalkeeper who prefers to hold onto the ball rather than parry it, and who always looks to be secure when faced with even the most powerful of shots from opposition forwards. The Blackburn keeper is also an expert in one on one situations where he makes the most of his agility and experience. Temperamental, authoritative and with tremendous powers of concentration, his will to win spreads itself on to his teammates. Often a spectacular keeper, is critics point out the few, although blinding mistakes he occasionally makes. Nevertheless, for the quality and consistency he has shown throughout is career, Tim Flowers is one of the best goalkeepers in England.

* League Championship winners medal 95. 
* Charity Shield medal 94.

* 8 full international appearances for England. He made his debut on 13th June 1993 in a friendly game against Brazil played in Washington D.C. (1-1). 
* A member of the England squad for the 1996 European Championships in England, David Seaman's good form prevented him from getting a taste of the action, failing to make appearance in the tournament for Terry Venables' England side.
* 3 under-21 international appearances. 
* 3 youth international appearances.

* The son of Ron Flowers, ex-Wolverhampton Wanderers and England midfielder, Tim began his career at his father's old club, joining them as a schoolboy in March 1981. An apprentice from 1983 from 1983, he took the step up to the first team squad on 28th August 1984. Flowers had already made his debut three days earlier at home against Sheffield United (2-2). That season Flowers played in 38 games, but was unable to prevent the club from being relegated to the Third Division. The following season Wolves were relegated again, this time to the Fourth Division, and Flowers found himself sharing the first team goalkeeping spot with Scott Burret, limiting him to just 25 appearances.
* His ability didn't go unnoticed by Southampton, who he joined on 13th June 1986 in exchange for 14 million pesetas. However in his first season at The Dell he was unable to make a first team appearance, his path to the side being blocked by the legendary Peter Shilton, one of the best English goalkeepers of all time.
* On the 23th March 1987 he was loaned out to Swindon Town. He played justtwo games for the club and the end of the season returned immediately to Southampton, although in November of the same year he returned to Swindon Town. 
* In the 88-89 he finally settled down in the side at Southampton, making himself an automatic choice in goal for the Saints for four consecutives season. In 1993 several clubs were interested in signing him, among them Liverpool. Nevertheless, on 4th November 1993 he was trasnfered to Blackburn Rovers for 2,400,000 pounds, a record fee at the time for a foalkeeper in British football. With his signing, Jack Walker laid another of the fondation stones in his dream of making Rovers one of the best clubs in the country. 
* Tim Flowers arrived at Ewood Park to take over in goal at Blackburn Rovers from Bobby Mimms. He made his debut on 6th November 1993 at Rangers Stadium in a 1-0 defeat against QPR.
*  Blackburn Rovers ended the 94-95 season as Premier League Champions, with Flowers as one of the side's star men. At the end of the season he was chosen as the goalkeeper in the Premier League's Ideal Side. Upto the end of that campaign he had been booked on four occasions during the course of his career and sent off once. In that same period his average of goals against per game was 1.603, and he had managed to keep a total of 78 clean sheets. 
* During the 95-96 season Blackburn played in the Champions League, only to put together a series of disapointing performances. Despite the side's poor campaign Flowers kept his place as England's second choice goalkeeper  behind David Seaman. Terry Venables called him up to the England squad for the 1996 European Championships, although he didn't manage to make an appearance in the tournament.

* Once again Tim Flowers kept his place as number one choice in goal for Blackburn Rovers despite the fact that the competition he faced from Shay Given was more intense than ever. His excellent performances proved to be vital in keeping the Ewood Park club in the Premier League. Although at the beginning of the season he lost his place in the England squad, slowly but surely, he won the confidence of Glenn Hoddle, who included him in the list of place called up for Le Tournoir tournament in France during the summer of 1997. During that tournament he played in the game against Italy which England won 2-0.

5.name: Croft
pages: * Since he arrive at Blackburn in March 1996 Gary Croft hasn't had too many opportunities. His appearances in the Premier League at the beginning of last season, coincided with a poor run for the side, which prevented him from showing his worth. With Roy Hodgson on the bench, sooner or later he will no doubt get another chance and, perhaps, this time luck will be on his side.

* His natural position his left back, although his versatility allows him to give a good account of himself in more advanced positions. A very tight marker, forceful when he goes in to tackle opposing forwards, he needs more experience of competition at the highest level.
x
* 4 under- 21 international appearances for England.

* A product of the Grismby Town youth system, he turned professional in July 1992.
* On 29th March 1996 he was transfered to Blackburn Rovers for 1,700,000 pounds. He made his Premier League debut on 28th September 1996 in an away game at Coventry. A few days earlier he had already made his first team debut in a League Cup game against Brentford.

* He made his first team debut for Blackburn in September, in a League  Cup game against Brentford. His good performances in that particular match allowed him to keep his place in six of the next seven games. However, he then returned to the reserve side, where he remained until the end of the season.

6.name: Henchoz
pages: * Roy Hodgson's presence in charge at Blackburn Rovers was what  persuaded Stephane Henchoz to sign for the English club. The Swiss international hadn't forgotten that it was Hodgson who gave him the chance to make his debut for the national side. After two years in the German Bundesliga, Henchoz is ready to be a success in the English Premier League.

* He generally plays as a central defender, although he can also play just in front of the defence doing a ballwinning job. Tall and strong, he takes full advantage of his physical presence to dominate with some authority in the air. Although he seldom moves forward to support the attack, he is capable of passing the ball about more thoughtfully than the majority of central defenders.
x

* 19 full international appearances for Switzerland. He made his debut on 23rd January 1993 in a friendly game against Japan played in Hong-Kong (1-1).  
* He played in the 1996 European Championships in England.

* He began his professional career in the 92-93 season in the ranks of Neuchatel. At the Swiss club he teamed up with manager Roy Hodgson, who, a few years later, as Swiss national manager, gave him his debut for the full national side.
* In the summer of 1995 he was transfered to German club Hamburg for three seasons.
* On 21st June 1997 a deal was agreed which took him to Blackburn Rovers in exchange for 3,000,000 pounds. Henchoz also had an offer from Manchester United, but chose the Ewood Park club as a result of the opportunity of being able to team up once again with Roy Hodgson.
* The 96-97 campaign was his  second season with Hamburg, who finished their Bundesliga season in 13th position, a poor showing for such a historical club.

7.name: Valery
pages: * Patrick Valery arrived at Ewood Park to give more security and forcefullness to the Blackburn Rovers' defence. In England, the    Frenchman is setting out on a new stage of his career, in which he will be trying to prove to be as successful as some of his fellow countrymen have been. Valery is not a star and doesn't  to be one. With him in the side Blackburn won't become a more spectacular side but may well become a more effective one.

* He generally plays at left back, although, on occasions, he will take up a position in the centre of the defence. Forceful and disciplined, he doesn't hesitate in fighting for every ball or in going in hard if he feels he needs to. His attacking contribution is virtually non-existent, and he is seldom seen to leave his defensive position. Precisely for that reason it is almost impossible to find him being caught out of position. He should, though, try to improve the timing of his tackles on opponents, in order to try to reduce the number of yellow cards he is shown.
* French League Championship winners medal 1988.
x

* He began his career with modest French sided Brignoles, his home
town club. * In 1984 he joined Monaco, although he didn't make his first team debut until 18th July 1987 in a 3-1 victory against Marseille. 
* In 9 seasons with Monaco he failed to score a single goal. However, he did win a French League Championhip winners medal in 1988 as well as a French Cup runners up medal in 1989.
* In October 1995 he was transfered to Toulouse, then in the Second Division; but, in the summer of 1996, he moved on to Bastia, where he played during the 96-97 season.
* Having completed his contract with Bastia, on 24th June 1997 he signed  for Blackburn Rovers for one season.

* Last season Patrick Valery played in 30 French league matches for Bastia, showing some tremendous form and helping the club to end the season in 7th position. Nevertheless, Valery did have quite a few problems  with referees and was actually booked 17 times and sent off once.

8.name: Tore Pedersen
pages: * Tore Pedersen is one of the globetrotters of European football. The Norwegian international has played for several clubs and is now setting out on his second spell in English football after a brief spell with Oldham Athletic during 93-94 season. Tore probably doesn't have particularly happy memories of that year, as he was kept out of the World Cup Finals in the United States by a series knee injury. He will now be hoping that history doesn't repeated itself and that Blackburn Rovers can prove to be his own personal springboard to the World Cup Finals in France in 1998.

* His natural position is at the heart of the defence, although he can also operate in either full back position. A forceful tackler, he is also quick and decisive and shows extraordinary confidence in himself  in everything he does. He is also an excellent team player. His vast experience has given him tremendous defensive know how, although, on the other hand his contribution to the attack is a very limited one.
x
* 41 international appearances for Norway.

* He began his career with Norwegian club Brann. After leaving the  club he set out on a continuous pilgrimage from one club to another, which even took him to a side based in the Japanese city of Hiroshima.
* In December 1993 he joined Oldham Athletic on loan from Brann. He made his league debut on 7th December, in a victory at home against Swindon Town (2-1).
* Unfortunately, in March 1994 he suffered a cruciate knee ligament  injury which prevented him from playing for Norway in that year's World Cup Finals in the United States.
* After brief spells with Gothenburg and Lillestrom,  he was transfered  to German club Saint Pauli in 1995.
* In 1997 he was a member of the St. Pauli side that was relegated to the German Second Division.
* On 10th September 1997 he was transfered to Blackburn Rovers for 500,000 pounds, signing a three year contract. On his arrival at Ewood Park he stated that his intention was to have as good a season as possible with Blackburn in order to force his way into the Norwegian squad for the 1998 World Cup Finals in France.
* Last season wasn't a good one for Tore Pedersen, who was unable to do anything to prevent his side, Saint Pauli, from being relegated to the  German Second Division.

9.name: Kenna
pages: * Since he arrived at Ewood Park in 1995 Jeff Kenna has been a regular member of the Blackburn Rovers' side. The Irish international has always responded to the demands of the club's coaches and has more than shown the versatility that allows him to play in a number of different positions. Initially it would seem that he is likely to form a part of Roy Hodgson's plans, although, bearing in mind the increasingly stiff competition in the squad, he will have to earn his place on a day to day basis.

* Although throughout his professional career he has alternated between  both full back position, the truth is that Jeff Kenna is at his best on the right hand side. When he plays on the left his lack of technique with his left foot noticeably affects his performance, as he constantly feels the need to get the ball onto his stronger right foot. Nevertheless, the Irishman makes up for this weakness with his commitment and non-stop effort. Effective in defence, he is decisive when he has to cover across the back as the last man, and shows good pace when he moves forward to support the attack, putting reasonable crosses over into the area. He rarely has a shot an goal, for which reason, logically, he seldom findes the back of the net.
x

* 17 full international appearances for Eire. He made his debut in April 1995, in a game against Portugal.
* 1 "B" international appearance. 
* 8 under-21 international appearances.
* Youth and schoolboy international.

* Born in Dublin, Jeff Kenna's professional career began in England. After coming through the ranks at Southampton, he turned professional on 25th April 1989. However, he didn't get to make his debut until 4th May 1991 in a game against Derby County.
* He began the 91-92 season as stand-in for Jason Dodd, although from January onwards he forced his way into the starting line up, keeping his place for a long spell in the side.
* After several seasons at The Dell, he was surprisingly transfered to Blackburn Rovers on 15th March 1995 for 1,500,000 pounds. He made his debut three days later at Ewood Park against Chelsea. Kenna played left back in a 2-1 victory for Rovers with goals from Shearer and Sherwood. On 20th April of that same year he scored his first goal in a Blue and White Blackburn shirt against Coventry City.

* Last season he played in 37 league games, all of those as a member of the starting line up. He began playing at left back, covering for the injured Graeme Le Saux, although following Le Saux's return to the side, and Coleman's injury, he moved back to his natural right back  position. It was from then on that Jeff Kenna hit his best form, which also allowed him to force his way back into the Republic of Ireland side.

10.name: Duff
pages: * Damien Duff is one of the promising young players at Blackburn Rovers.  The fans at Ewood Park consider him a player who can unbalance other teams.  He is able to change the course of a game with one turn.  The Irish-man with a good left foot has shown that he has more than enough quality to play in a category as demanding as the Premier League.

* A midfielder with an attacking nature, he can also play as a forward.  His skilful turn is his most outstanding characteristic.  Very left-footed, he will usually play on the left, although at times he has drifted over to the other wing to take advantage of his shot with left after cutting infield.  Young, daring and with talent, he is more than just a promising player.
x
* Youth and schoolboy international for the Republic of Ireland.

* Trained in Lourdes Celtic, a modest Irish club, he signed for Blackburn Rovers on the 5th of March 1996.
* His debut in the Premier League took place on the 11th of March 1997, in a game against Leicester City played at Ewood Park (2-4).
* He made his debut for the first team in the last game of last season against Leicester at home.

11.name: Andersson
pages: * Anders Andersson arrived in England hoping to be a success in a competition as prestigious as the Premier League. At Ewood Park he will have the oportunity of playing alongside Martin Dahlin, his teammate in the Swedish national side. Initially it would seem that he is likely to have a real fight on his hands to try to force his way into Roy Hodgson's side, although he will have to make sure  that he is ready to take full advantage when his opportunity comes.

* He generally plays as a central midfielder player, a position where  he shows his ability to dictate the way the team plays. He possesses good individual technique which allows him to play accurate passes. He is decisive when he moves forward to join the attack, and, when given the slightest opportunity, will show off his powerful shooting ability. On the other hand he needs to work on his defensive contribution.
* A full international for Sweden.

* He began his playing career in 1991 the year in which he made his debut for Malmoe in the Swedish First Division. In his first season for the club he saw just a few minutes of action, coming on in place of a teammate. 
* On 9th July 1997 he was transfered to Blackburn Rovers for 500,000 pounds.
* Tore Andersson had a magnificent 96-97 season, although his contribution wasn't enough to help Malmoe snatch the league title from the all-powerful Gothenburg.

12.name: Flitcroft
pages: * Last season allowed Garry Flitcroft to forget his unfortunate debut in a Blackburn shirt in March 1996, when  he was sent off after just three minutes play. During the 96-97 season Garry was able to demonstrate that that had been no more than an accident and that he has the ability he needs to go on to become a success in the Premier League. Now, with Roy Hodgson in charge, he will be trying to confirm that those observers who considered him to be one of the best young prospects in England  weren't mistaken.

* A hard working midfielder, who knows where the goal is, Garry Flitcroft is one of the brightest young players in England. Good with either foot, he is a thoughtful passer of the ball while his tremendous reserves of stamina allow him to cover plenty of ground and win a lot of possession for the side. A very competitive player, he works hard to polish up  his defects and improve the stronger aspects of his game. Still in the learning process, his performances are getting better each year, all of which suggests that great things can be expected of him in the not too distant future.
x

* 11 under-21 international appearances for England. With 3 goals. 
* 1 youth international appearance.

* Two years younger than his brother David, who plays for Chester City, Garry Flitcroft was playing in the junior sides at Manchester City when he turned professional on 2nd July 1991. However, he made his league debut playing for Bury where he went on loan on 5th March 1992. Two days later he formed part of the side that lined up against Chester.
* An England under-21 international, during the 92-93 season he began to settle down in the side at Maine Road. He began the 95-96 season with Manchester City, but, on 26th March 1996, Blackburn Rovers splashed out 3,200,000 pounds to take him to Ewood Park.
* His debut for Rovers couldn't have been more unfortunate, being sent off after just 3 minutes of the Blackburn-Everton game, for elbowing Everton's Tony Grant and then arguing about it with Duncan Ferguson Blackburn Rovers went on to lose 0-3.

* He began the season as a regular member of the side, until an injury forced him out of the side. However, following the departure of Ray Harford he won back his place under the guidance of Tony Parkes. Garry then went on to become one of Blackburn's most important players, and was a genuine exmaple of commitment and effort for his teammates. His goal against Arsenal at Highbury, with just five games of the season to go assured Blackburn of remaining in the Premier League, and, in the process robbed the Gunners of any remaining hopes they might have had of lifting the league title.

13.name: Bohinen
pages: * Lars Bohinen will be trying to make the 97-98 season a totally different one to the previous campaign, when he found himself relegated to the role of substitute a Blackburn Rovers and out of the Norwegian national side. The departure of Ray Harford was a real blow forthe player, since the ex-Rovers' manager was one of his chief admirers. Nevertheless, the arrival of Roy Hodgson opens the door for Bohinen to try to get back to the form he showed a couple of years ago.

* An outstanding playmarker, Lars Bohinen is a central midfielder with great technique, ball control in both feet, excellent vision and tremendously accurate passing ability. He also has the ability to beat a man and is a dangerous player in and around the penalty area. He is not afraid to take on the responsibility of dictating the pace  of the game, making himself the chief orchestrator of the side's attacking play. A classy footballer, he is very accurate from free  kicks. His mere presence in the side guarantees that the ball will be past around accurately and that the team, tactically speaking, will be well organised, something which is well appreciated by coaches and managers.
* On occasions he plays as a left sided midfielder, a position where he is less involved in dictating the way the team plays, although playing down the left he can prove to be more of a threat in terms of goalscoring.
x

* 47 full international appearances for Norway, with 10 goals.
* A member of Norway's squad for 1994 World Cup Finals in the United States, he played from the start in two of Norway's three games, against Mexico (1-0) and Italy (0-1). Against the Republic of Ireland (0-0), he came on in the 68th minute in place of Leonhardsen.

* An under-15 international for Norway, Lars Bohinen always wanted to be a footballer. However, on more than one occasion he has stated  that he was never particularly attracted to British football and that the English league often even sent him to sleep. The young Bohinen admired Michel Platini and dreamt of playing in Spain, Italy or Germany.
* Lars Bohinen's playing career began in his native Norway in 1988, in the ranks of Valerengen. Transfered to Viking in 1990, his spell at this club was brief to say the least. In the 90-91 season he went on to play 22 games for Young Boys, a club based in Berne, Switzerland.
* The game that change his life was the one that saw Norway clash with England in the qualifying stages for the 1994 World Cup Finals in the United States. Bohinen began the game on the bench, although he later came  on and scored one of Norway's two goals (2-0). His performance didn't go unnoticed by Frank Clark, then manager of Nottingham Forest, who contacted the Swiss club where he was playing at the time.
* After a series of complicated negotiations, on 5th November 1993,  Bohinen arrived at the City Ground in exchange for 450,000 pounds. The  following day the Norwegian made his debut in English fooball in a game against Birmingham City. Forest won the game, away from home, 0-3.
* Although still a Forest player during the first months of the 95-96 season he was transfered to Blackburn Rovers on 14th October 1995 for 700,000 pounds. That same day he made his debut at Ewood Park in a 2-1 victory against Southampton. Bohinen scored the first goal of the game, and, following the final whistle, was highly praised by Rovers' manager Ray Harford as well as his Southampton counterpart, Dave Merrington. Both manager picked him out as the man of the match.
* A home loving man, he has stated that after each game he shuts off from football completely.  He only watches big matches on television, preferring to spend the rest of his time in the company of his family.

* Last season was one to forget. Injuries and loss of form prevented Bohinen from making himself a regular member of the side during the course of the season. His appearances for Blackburn sporadic and he also lost his place in the Norway's squad. Perhaps the highlight of his season came at Old Trafford, where he scored an outstanding goal.

14.name: McKinlay
pages: * The departure of Ray Harford opened the doors to the first team for Billy McKinlay. The Scottish international was able to demonstrate from the moment he broke into the side that he was a player who had all the qualities needed to play in the Premier League. During the 97-98 season he will be trying to settle down at Blackburn Rovers and, along the way, try to do enough to get into the Scottish squad for the World Cup Finals in France.

* A midfield player, he stands out for his attack minded approach to the game. He continually gets forward in support of the attack, backed up by his good technical ability and his eye for a goal. He is a good passer of the ball, keeping it moving all the time, whilst he also helps out with defensive responsibilities, never hesitating to go in hard on opponents when he feels he has to.
* Scottish Cup Winners medal 94.

* 21 full international appearances for Scotland, with 4 goals to his name. He made his debut on 17th November 1993, in a game between Malta-Scotland (0-2), which formed part of the qualifying stages for the 1994 World Cup Finals in the United States. McKinlay played the whole game, and scored Scotland's first goal.
* He was a member of Scotland's squad for the 1996 European Championships in England. He played just 35 minutes of the game against Holland (0-0), after coming on in the second half for Gallagher.
* Under-21 international for Scotland.

* After learning his trade with Scottish club Hamilton Thistle, Billy McKinlay became a free agent in 1996. Dundee United took advantage of the situation to make him a member of their first team squad on 6th June of that same year. He spent 8 seasons with the club and was an automatic choice in the last 7 of those campaigns. In 1994 he won a Scottish Cup Winners medal. 
* On 14th October 1995 he was transfered to Blackburn Rovers for 1,750,000 pounds. One week later, on 21st October he made his debut in the side's visit to West Ham United (1-1), coming on for Tim Sherwood in the 64th minute. On 8th November he made his first starting appearance at St. James' Park against Newcastle and had to wait until 13th April 1996 to scored his first goal in the Premier League, against Nottingham Forest at the City Ground (1-5). 
* At the end of the his first season in England he played in the European Championships, although he was only able to make one appearance, and that came as a substitute.

* The beggining of last season was a tough time for Billy McKinlay, hardly coming into the reckoning for manager Ray Harford. Following the departure of Harford and his substitutions by Tony Parkes, the Scottish international began to form a more regular part of the Blackburn Rovers line up. He played in a total of 25 league games, 23 of those being as a member of the starting line up, while he scored one goal, against Manchester United at Ewood Park.

15.name: Sherwood
pages: * The image of Tim Sherwood lifting the Premiership trophy in 1995 represented the realisation of all the ambitions of the Blackburn Rovers' captain, and one of the best footballers in the side. Although luck hasn't always been by his side, it is still not easy to find a good reason as to why he hasn't been called up more often to the England squad. The truth is that Sherwood has more than demonstrated the class he possesses. An automatic first team choice under Kenny Dalglish as well as Ray Harford, everything suggests that he will go on been so with Roy Hodgson now in charge at Ewood Park.

* A very classy midfield player Tim Sherwood stands out as the orchestrator of the side's attacking play, although, on occasions, he lines up  on the right hand side of the midfield. Backed up by excellent basic technique, good vision and ball control, he sprays the ball around accurately over both short and long distance. A leader out on the park, he doesn't shy away from defensive responsibilities and makes a good contribution to the job of winning possession. He has a very powerful shot from distance and finds the back of the net with some regularity. For all of these reasons, he is considered one of the most complete players in the Premier League.

* League Championship winners medal 95.
* Charity Shield medal 94.

*  One "B" international appearance.
* 4 under-21 international appearances.

* Now captain of Blackburn Rovers, Tim Sherwood's playing career began in the ranks of Watford, where he turned professional on 7th February 1987. His league debut took place on 12th September of that same year in a game against Sheffield Wednesday.
* After three seasons with the Hornets, in which he experienced the  disappointment of relegation to the Second Division in 1988, he was transfered to Norwich City on 18th July 1989. A regular member of the side in the old First Division, on 12th February 1992 he signed for Kenny Dalglish's Blackburn Rovers side in exchange for 500,000 pounds. The Ewood Park club were then in the old Second Division, although they were on the point of winning promotion to the Premier League, in time for the inaugural season. Tim made his Rovers' debut ten days after his arrival at the club, against Middlesbrough away. 
* At the end of the 94-95 season Blackburn Rovers became Premier League champions with Tim Sherwood, as captain of the side, proudly lifting the trophy. That season he also formed part of the Premier League's "Ideal Team" voted for by his fellow professionals.
* In 1995 there was speculation surrounding his possible departure to a London club, but, finally he decided to stay at Ewood Park.

* Tim Sherwood was together with Jeff Kenna, the player who made most appearances in a Blackburn shirt during the course of last season. He missed just one league game and gave everything he had to make sure that the club stayed in the Premier League. The presence in the side of Billy McKinley allowed him to adopt a more attacking role. Nevertheless, bad luck prevented him for scoring more than 3 goals in the league, 1 in the F.A. Cup and 1  in the League Cup. However he did, unfortunately, rather more yellow cards than he would have liked.

16.name: Hendry
pages: * Colin Hendry has become one of the key man in the side for both Blackburn Rovers and Scotland. Easily recognisable with his blonde hair, the security and apparent ease with which he goes about his  work in defence is well appreciated by the supporters and valued by the club's coaching staff. One of the best central defenders in the Premier League, he is hoping to once again taste the glory that came the club's way in 1995, when Blackburn lifted the league title, due, amongst other things, to the phenomenal job that the Scottish international defender did. This season he will also have high hopes for the World Cup Finals in France, for which Scotland have deservedly qualified.

* Although at th beginning of his career Colin Hendry played as a centre forward, throughout his career he has demonstrated that his natural position is at the centre of the defence, where he has  consistently played to the highest of levels. A forceful player and a safe marker, he is also almost unbeatable in the air, helped out by his stature and positional sense. Very experienced, he reads the intentions of opposing forwards and cuts out counterattacks with great efficiency. Though occasionally a hard player, he always goes  in fairly. Perhaps his only weak point is his lack of speed, although he tries to make up for this disadvantage with his anticipation and know how. In attack, he makes the most of his power in the air to move forward into the opposition's penalty area for set pieces, occasionally finding the back of the net.

* League Championship winner medal 95. 
* Charity Shield medal 94.

* 19 full international appearances for Scotland with scoring once. He made his debut on 19th May 1993 in a 3-0 victory over Estonia in a qualifying game for the 1994 World Cup Finals in United States played in Tallinn. He scored his first international goal on 17th November that same year against Malta in Valletta.
* A member of Scotland's squad in the 1996 European Championships in England, he was a member of the starting line up in the three games that Scotland played, against Holland, England and Switzerland.
* 1 "B" international appearance. 
* 1 under-21 international appearance.

* After coming through the ranks at Islavale, his first professional club was Dundee United, who he joined in 1983. On 7th January 1984 he made his league debut, in a game against Hearts. He spent three and a half seasons with the Scottish club before signing for Blackburn Rovers on 11th March 1987 in exchange for 30,000 pounds.
* Curiously, in his first season at Ewood Park he played as a centre forward. he made his league debut on 14th March 1987, against Stoke City, at home while he managed to score in the two following games against Derby County and West Bromwich Albion. That same season he scored the winning goal against Charlton in the Zenith Data Systems Cup Final.
* Reconverted back to the centre of the defence in the 87-88, a contractual dispute saw manager Don Mackay decided to leave him out of the side, a situation which brought about his transfer to Manchester City on 16th November 1989 for 700,000 pounds. His two first seasons at Maine Road were sensational, although, in his third season at the club he lost his place in the side to Keith Curle.
* Two years after his original departure, Hendry returned to Blackburn Rovers. On 8th November 1991 the Ewood Park club paid out the same amount Of money (700,000 pounds), that they had received from Manchester City in 1989. The Scottish international defender's contribution proved to be decisive in Blackburn winning promotion to the Premier League. Blackburn were now under guidance of Hendry's fellow Scot Kenny Dalglish.
* During the 94-95 season Colin Hendry enjoyed the best moment of his career as a professional footballer, when Blackburn won the League title. One of the side's most outstanding performers, Hendry was chosen for the Premier League's "Ideal Team" for 1995 voted for by his fellow professionals.
* Up to the end of the 94-95 campaign he had been booked 20 times, although he had never been sent off.
* A member of Scotland's starting line up in the 1996 European Championships in England he put in some godd performances, although he was a victim of one of the best goals of the tournament when Paul Gascoigne lifted the ball over his head before smashing it into the back of the net with a  superb volley. This, however, wasn't enough to tarnish a great season in which he was voted as Blackburn's Player of the Year for 1996.

* For the sixth cosecutive season Colin Hendry was one of the pillars upon which Blackburn Rovers built their game. The Scottish international was a member of the starting line up in all 35 of the league games in which he played and only missed games as a result of an injury he picked up in October. At the end of the season he decided to put back an operation he required until the summer so as not to leave the side without one of their main sources of inspiration in the final decisive run in to the end of the season with the threat of relegation looming over Ewood Park.

17.name: Ripley
pages: * Stuart Ripley has now gone three seasons without scoring a goal in the Premier League. The Blackburn Rovers player still going through a seemingly  never endind bad run, which has been made worse by losing his place in thse side. It remains to be seen how things work out following the arrival of Roy Hodgson. Perhaps under his guidance he will be able to get back to something like is best form. Without doubt the Ewood Park supporters would be happy to see him do exactly that.

* A player with a good ability to beat a man, with good pace and an incisive passer of the ball Stuart Ripley plays down the right hand side of the midfield, although he can also take up other position in the centre of the park. He generally picks up the ball tight under touchline from where he sets off on runs towards the opposition penalty area, sending in good quality, dangerous crosses. However, he is a far from prolific goalscorer, not possessing a powerful shot whilst neither is he a particularly good header of the ball. On the other hand, he makes a good defensive contribution and always helps out with ballwinning responsibilities.

* League Championships winners medal 95. 
* Charity Shield medal 94.

* 1 full international appearance for England. He made his debut on 17th November 1993 in a game against San Marino played in Bologna. England Won 7-1, but still failed to qualify for the 1994 World Cup Finals in the United States.
* 8 under-21 international appearances, scoring once. 
* 2 youth international appearances.

* Born in Middlesbrough, he learnt his trade in the youth set up with  home town club. He made his first team debut at just 17 years of age in a game against Oldham Athletic on 5th February 1985. On 20th November of that same year, on his eighteenth birthday, he signed his first professional contract with Middlesbrough.
* Shortly afterwards on 18th February 1986, he was loaned out to Bolton Wanderers, who were then in the old Third Division. Back at Middlesbrough, he formed part of the side that won promotion to the First Division in 1988, as well as the one that went straight back down a year later.
* Transfered to Blackburn Rovers on 20th July 1992 for 1,300,000 pounds he made himself a regular member of the side from the moment he arrived at the club. He made his debut on 15th August of that same year at Selhurst Park against Crystal Palace. A member of the league title winning side of 1995, he is currently going through an alarming goal drought, having failed to score a single goal for two consecutive season. (94-95 and 95-96).

* Last saeason wasn't a good one for Stuart Ripley, who, although he began the season as a regular member of the side, soon lost his place to the challenge of the Greek playe Donis. His cause wasn't helped by   the injury he picked up in the first third of the campaign. His end of season statistics didn't make particularly positive reading: 13 games played, but only five starting appearances.

18.name: Per Pedersen
pages: * In his first season in England Per Pedersen had a few problems adapting to the style of play in the Premier League. The Ewood Park's supporters had high hopes of the player, who was, in fact, the first signing that Blackburn made following the departure of Alan Shearer. The Danish international will be out to try to improve his form during the 97-98 season, where he could find himself playing alongside Chris Sutton in the Blackburn forward line.

* Per Pedersen is a striker with international experience. He is strong, quick player who is a good header of the ball. His game is based more on physical power than on skill. A very quick mover, he is at his most dangerous when he is given space in which to work. He generally operates pushed out wide towards one of the flank, although his goalscoring instincts also allow him to play as a centre forward.
x
* 7 full international appearances for Denmark, with 6 goals.

* He began his playing career in 1987 in the ranks of Odense, a club in the Danish First Division.
* In 1991 he was transfered to Lyngby, where he remained until the beginning of the 95-96 season, when he returned to Odense.
* On 22nd February 1997 he was transfered to Blackburn Rovers for 2,500,000 pounds.
* He made his Premier League debut that same day in a game against Liverpool at Anfield. He scored his first goal for Blackburn on 5th March 1997, against Chelsea at Stamford Bridge (1-1).

* He arrived at Blackburn Rovers in February and immediately won himself a regular place in Tony Parkes' side. However, he never managed to find the form that was expected of him and he soon began to find himself on the substitutes' bench. Without doubt he had a few problems adapting to the Premier League. He scored just one goal against Chelsea at Stamford Bridge.

19.name: Dahlin
pages: * Roy Hordson was the man who discovered Martin Dahlin. Under the guidance of the British coach, Martin made himself leading scorer and also won a Swedish League Championship medal with Malmoe. All of that coming at  the beginning of a tremendous career which has had, as one of it's highlights the 1994 World Cup Finals in the United States. After a brief spell in   Italian football Martin is now setting out on a new adventure in England. A Blackburn Rovers he will be lining up with his compatriot man Anders %% Andersson,  while, once again, Roy Hodgson will be watching from the touchline.

* Martin Dahlin is a quick strong striker who is constantly moving along the whole of the forward line. He has a good ability to beat men while he is in full flight and is particularly dangerous when he is given space while he is also an expert in one on one situations. An outstanding finisher whit either foot, his ability to get up above defenders makes him a specialist in the air. As well as all these qualities, he has the advantage of tremendous experience at the highest level, Which gives him the know how to enable him to get the better of opposing defenders.

* Swedish League Championship winners medal 88.
* Swedish Cup winners medal 89.
* German Cup winners medal 95.
* Voted Swedish Footballer of the Year 1993.
* Top Scorer in the Swedish League 88.

* 47 full international appearances for Sweden scoring 26 goals.
* He made his debut in April 1991 against Brazil.
* He played in the 1994 World Cup Finals. He scored 4 goals; against Cameroon, Russia (2) and Saudi Arabia.
* An Olympic international, he played in the Seul Games 1988.

* He began his career with Malmoe, one of the most important clubs in the Swedish First Division. Roy Hodgson was the coach who recommended that he should be signed, despite the reluctance of the club's directors.
* In 1990 he was on the point of signing for Genoa based club Sampdoria. 
* An international since June 1991, he scored 4 goals in his first 4 games for the Swedish national side.
* In 1992 he was transfered to Borussia Moenchengladbach.
* He was one of Sweden's heroes in the 1994 World Cup Finals in the United States, where he scored 4 goals.
* In the 96-97 season, he was transfered to Roma. However, Martin never really adapted to the Italian League and, shortly after, returned to Borussia Moenchengladbach, although this time he was on loan ar the German club. 
* On 9th July 1997 he was transfered to Blackburn Rovers in exchange for 2,500,000 pounds. Initially, his girlfriend, who is a designer, was opposed to the move because she wanted to leave in London, although, finally she agreed to set up home in Blackburn. At Ewood Park, Dahlin met up once again with Roy Hodgson, the coach who had discovered him years earlier.

* Martin Dahlin arrived at Roma from Borussia Moenchengladbach with the season already under way. However, the Swedish striker proved to be a disappointment during his time in Italy. After just five games in the Calcio he was  soon returning to Borussia Moenchengladbach, who had a mediocre campaign in the Bundesliga.

20.name: Sutton
pages: * Blackburn Rovers need Chris Sutton to be at his best. Following the departure of Alan Shearer to Newcastle, Sutton took on the side's goalscoring responsibilities. He did a good job in that role last season, although injuries and illness prevented him from finding his best form. The English striker will be hoping that, during the 97-98 season, luck is on his side and that he can make a contribution to rebuilding a championship winning side for Blackburn.

* A strong harworking striker, Chris Sutton uses his power and speed to get the better of opposing defenders. He is a player who likes to get inside the area to make the most of his powerful shooting. Technically good, although he doesn't stand out for his ability to beat a man, he is excellent at holding the ball up, waiting for support to come through from his teammates to whom he lays the ball off thoughtfully. Chris never holds anything back, giving everything he has got for the good of the team, as a result it is no surprise to sign him unselfishly helpin gout in midfield. On occasions he has also played as a central defender, where he makes the most of his ability in the air which is as effective in his own penalty area as it is in the opposition's.
* League Championship winners medal 95.

* 2 "B" international appearances for England, scoring 1 goal.
13 under-21 international appearances, scoring once.

* The son of Mike Sutton, ex-Norwich, Chester and Carlisle United player, during the 1960's, Chris followed in his father's footsteps by beginning his career at Norwich. On 4th May 1991, he made his debut in the old First Division against Queens Park Rangers, after coming off the bench to Replaced Ian Crook. At the end of that season he turned professional on  2nd  July 1991. Although, in the early stages of his career, he played as a central defender as a replacement for Ian Butterworth, he soon got his chance to play up front.
* Third top scorer in the league during the 93-94 season with 25 goals to his credit, his move to Blackburn Rovers made him, for a spell, the most    expensive player in the history of English football. On 13th July 1994 Chris arrived at Ewood Park in exchange for 5 million pounds.
* He made his debut for Rovers on 20th August 1994 against Southampton atThe Dell (1-1). Three days later, on his home debut at Ewood Park, he scored the opening goal in a 3-0 victory against Leicester, and, four days later scored his first hat trick in the Blue and White shirt of Blackburn Rovers, at home against Coventry (4-0).
* He formed an attacking partnership with Alan Shearer, and, between the pair of them, they managed to score 49 goals during the 94-95 season,  helping Blackburn to win the league championship. As a reward for his work   that season he was included in the Premier league's "Ideal Team".
* In December 1995 he suffered a serious ligament injury which kept him out of action for several months.

* He was unable to begin the season with the rest of his teammates, due to an injury he picked up during the summer of 1996. By the time he was fit again, Ray Harford had already left the club, and Tony Parkes had taken charge of team matters. Sutton soon got back to form until, in February, a virus once again kept him out of the side. Despite so many setbacks Chris ended the season as the side's top scorer with 11 league goals to his credit.

21.name: Gallacher
pages: * Kevin Gallacher is a player who just wants to look to the future. In  1994 he broke his leg in three different places. After a long, painful process of recovery, which took several months, he was unlucky enough  to suffer the exact same injury on the day of his comeback. Once again  he was back in hospital. When finally everything seemed to indicate that he would at last be able to force his way back into Blackburn Rovers' plans a new injury put him out of action yet again. However, so much bad luck hasn't managed to affect the moral of thsi talented Scottish midfielder. Last season he proved to be the best player in the side and the one of the pillars of the Scottish national team. Now he will be looking to win some honours with the Ewood Park outfit and do a good job for Scotland in the World Cup Finals in France.

* A slightly built, but very talented midfielder, Kevin Gallacher stands out for his ability to pop up by surprise in the opposing penalty area. A player with great mobility, he seems to be able to find spaces all over the attacking third of the field, and, once he gets possession,  is a very unpredictable opponents. Gallacher is not a prolific goalscorer, although he is a specialist at creating opportunities for his teammates.
Quick and dynamic, he has a good ability to go past defenders and is an accurate passer of the ball. In short, he is a fine footballer who has, unfortunately, been robbed of some of his speed, and his confidence in himself, by injuries.
* U.E.F.A. Cup runners up medal 87.

* 31 full international appearances for Scotland scoring 5 times. He made his debut on 17th May 1988 against Colombia in Glasgow (0-0).
* A member of the Scotland squad for the 1992 European Championships in Sweden, he played in 3 games, including the defeats against Holland and Germany plus the victory over the C.I.S.
* He was also a member of the squad for the  1996 European Championships in England, and played from the start in Scotland's first game against  Holland (0-0), although he wasn't included in the remaining games by manager Craig Brown.
* 2 "B" international appearances.
* 7 under-21 international appearances, scoring 2 goals .

* Grandson of the legendary Patsy Gallacher, who played for Celtic between 1911 and 1925, Kevin Gallacher arrived at Dundee United, one of the most  prestigious clubs in Scotland, in 1983, from Duntocher Boys Club. He made his league debut on 14th December 1985 in one of the Scottish Championships classic fixtures against Glasgow Rangers.
* A full international since 1988,he was transfered to Coventry City on 29th January 1990 for 900,000 pounds, and immediately made himself a regular member of the side.
* On 22nd March 1993, Blackburn Rovers paid out 1,500,000 pounds to sign him. The deal also saw Roy Wegerle move in the opposite direction to Coventry City. On 3rd April Gallacher made his debut at Ewood Park, against Liverpool, and scored one of the goals in Blackburn's  4-1 victory. Alan Shearer's absence due to injury allowed him to settle down in the forward line alongside Mike Newell and win the admiration of the club's supporters.
* A 1994 a triple fracture of his leg, kept him out of action for a numberof months and prevented him from making a contribution to the clubs championship triumph in 1995. In fact, during the 94-95 season he only managed to get back into the action right at the end of the season, although he did scored the winning goal against Crystal Palace (2-1). However in that same game he suffered a relapse of his injury and  had to be put into plaster once again.
* He had a disastrous start to the 95-96 season picking up an injury in the first game of the season. Once fit again, months later, he was called up to the Scotland squad for the 1996 European Championships in England.

* Kevin Gallacher was, without any doubt, Blackburn Rovers' best player during the course of last season. The Scottish international scored 10 goals in 34 league games, many of those strikes giving the Ewood Park club valuable points which eventually kept them in the Premier League. He was also a key member of the Scotland side, and was especially outstanding against Austria in a qualifying game for the World Cup Finals in France, when he scored both of Scotland's goals.

22.name: Wilcox
pages: * Jason Wilcox is one of the players who has come through the Ewood Park youth system and who currently shines in Blackburn's first team. Still fresh in the memory are his excellent performances alongside Alan Shearer, who he supplied with plenty of goalscoring opportunities If Jason maintain his progress, sooner or later, he will no doubt return to Glenn Hoddle's England squad, and, who knows, may even form part of the England party that travels to the 1998 World Cup Finals in France.

* A hardrunning midfield player, Jason Wilcox is capable of covering the whole of the left flank, makign a contribution in both attack and defence.  A creative player, he is comfortable with the ball at his feet, and distributes it thoughtfully. He puts good passes through to his teammates and makes the most of his speed to reach the byline and help out the strikers with good quality crosses. He is good in the air and has an eye for a goalscoring opportunity, while in defence he gets back quickly to cover and keep opposing forwards under constant pressure. Wilcox is, above all, a very complete footballer.

* League Championship winners medal 95. 
* Charity Shield medal 94.

* 1 full international appearance for England. He made his debut on 18th May 1996 in a friendly game against Hungary at Wembley (3-0). 
* 1 "B" international appearance.

* A product of the Ewood Park youth sytem, Jason Wilcox turned professional on 13th June 1989.  He didn't make his first team debut, however, until the 16th April 1990 against Swindon Town.
* A regular member of the Blackburn Rovers' side since the 91-92 season, the departure of Scott Sellars in the summer of 1992 allowed him to take up his position on the left hand side of the field. With Ripley on the right and Wilcox on the left, Shearer, Newell and Gallacher have all been guaranteed plenty of services.
* In autumn 1993 he caught Legionnaire's disease, which kept him out of  action until October.
* He was a member of the side that won the League title in 1995, although in February he suffered a serious cruciate knee ligament injury, which forced him to undergo surgery an kept him out for a number of months. 
* Jason Wilcox was on the verge of being included in Terry Venables' squad for the 1996 European Championships in England. The England manager gave him the chance to make his debut for the national side in May, just weeks  before the tournament began. However, although Wilcox gave a good account of himself, Venables finally decided not to call him up into the squad.

* He missed the start of last season due to a knee operation, although,  as soon as he had recovered he once again took up his place in the Blackburn Rovers' side. He was a member of the starting line up in 26 Of the 28 league games he played in. He scored 2 goals, the first of those against Liverpool at Ewood Park and the second against Nottingham Forest at the City Ground.

24.name: Gerrard
pages:
* An under-21 international and valued at 1,500,000 pounds, Paul Gerrard looks destined to became Everton's number one goalkeeper over the coming years. With patience and hard work it would surprise nobody if, given the ability he possesses, he went on to also become a future England goalkeeper. 
* Now in his second year at Everton, he managed to make four consecutive starting  appearances during the previous season, in which he made a tremendous impression. Southall will have to be on his guard with Gerrard threatening to make the most of the slightest opportunity that comes his way to dislodge him from the side.

* A brave, dominant keeper, despite his youth he shows tremendous personality and character out on the park. Authoritative, he positions his defenders well, and spreads a sense of security to the rest of the side. Quick to come off his line, his desire to win at all times occasionally sees him being too hasty in his decision making. A strong player, he stands out for his long goalkicks, with which he is capable of creating danger in the opposition penalty area. He needs time to work on his defects, but, nevertheless, shows all the qualities a good keeper requires.
x
* 17 Under-21 international appearances for England. He managed to keep a clean sheet in in 12 of those 17 games..

* After coming through the youth ranks at Oldham Athletic, he signed as a professional on 21st November 1991. 
*In 1993 he suffered a serious knee injury which temporarily put him out of action. In 1996 he broke his jawbone, an injury which put him out of the final games of the season.
* In the summer of 1996 he was transfered to Everton for one and a half million pounds.
* He made his Premier League debut for Everton on 11th November 1996 against Coventry City at Goodison Park (1-1).

* In his first season at Everton, Gerrard didn't get too many chances to get a taste of the action, bearing in mind that Neville Southall remains an automatic first team choice. He made five appearances, four of those coming as a member of the starting line up. However he came out of his four starting appearances positively, with the side winning twice, drawing once and losing the other. Of those four games, the first one against Newcastle was his worst performance, conceding four goals, nevertheless in the other three, he managed to keep clean sheets.

25.name: Tiler
pages:
* Signed for Everton in November 1997. 
* Carl Tiler is a footballer who has not been accompanied by good luck in the last few years.  After signing for Nottingham Forest in a costly move, he was unable to settle into the team due to injuries, something which also happened at Aston Villa. With a little bit of luck, Tiler will be able to take advantage of this chance and will try and contribute as much as possible so that Everton can avoid relegation to the First Division.

* A central defender with a lot of presence, he uses his stature to dominate the aerial game in both areas, being hard to beat in his own area and dangerous in the opponent's box. In fact he has scored a reasonable number of goals with his head during his career. Left-footed, he is calm and safe with the ball at his feet, although he doesn't hesitate to punt the ball away if he runs into difficulty when trying to play the ball out. He tries to counteract his lack of speed with the resources of an experienced defender when faced with fast skilful forwards, the type of player that cause him the most problems. The two serious injuries that he suffered in the last few years have cut short his progress.
x
* 13 times under-21 international for England.

* Tiler was trained in the lower ranks of Barnsley, making his debut in the first team on the 7th of May 1988 in a game against West Bromwich Albion. On the 2nd of August of this same year he signs as a professional.
* His move to Nottingham Forest occurs on 30th May 1991 for £1,400,000. The departure of Des Walker in August 1992 opens the doors to the first team. However, an ankle injury suffered at the end of the 92-93 season forces him almost definitively onto the Forest subs' bench.
* Tiler is loaned to Swindon Town on 18th November 1994, and makes his debut two days later against Bristol City.
* He starts the 95-96 season at Nottingham Forest, but on 28th October 1995 he is transferred to Aston Villa for £750,000. He makes his debut the same at Villa Park, his team beating Everton 1-0, but, unfortunately, Tiler is seriously injured and remains in dry dock until the end of the season. 
* Tiler is transferred to Sheffield United on 26th March 1997 for £650,000. His debut with the Blades is on the 31st of this month against Huddersfield Town and he scores his first goal for the team against Stoke City on the 25th of April.

* It wasn't Carl Tiler's season. Still convalescing after the injury that he suffered on his debut for Aston Villa, he was not available for selection until October, when he had a few games, and he even managed to score a goal against his former team, Nottingham Forest. He is not a regular in Brian Little's line-ups and so moves to Sheffield United, the team that needed his services due to the injury to Michel Vonk. With the Blades he settles into the team and plays 6 games for them, scoring another goal.

26.name: Bilic
pages:
* Bilic arrived at Everton at the peak of his career, after having demonstrated during his time at West Ham that he is currently one of the best central defenders in the Premier League. An automatic choice for his country, Croatia, he will no doubt be one of the first names to be included in the squad, if Croatia finally make it to the World Cup Finals in France.
* Slaven Bilic is a very respected man both on and off the pitch. Cultured and educated, his charisma is clearly evident wherever he goes. He was, in fact, made captain of German side Karlsruhe, shortly after his arrival in the country.

* As a central defender, he stands out for his power in the air, an area of the game in which he is almost unbeatable. Despite his technical limitations, his extraordinary physical power, positional sense and decisiveness, make him a fundamental member of the side. His tremendous personality and will to win transmits itself to the rest of his teammates, in whom he is able to inspire confidence, and motivate. For all of these reasons, he very often appears to be the manager's right hand man out on the park.

* 1 Croatian League Championship winners medal. 
* 1 Croatian Cup winners medal.

* 30 full international appearances for Croatia. He made his debut on 5th July 1992 in a friendly game between Australia and Croatia (1-0), played in Melbourne.
* He was a member of his country's squad for the 1996 European Championships in England. He started all 4 of Croatia's games, against Turkey (1-0), Denmark (3-0), Portugal (0-3) and Germany (1-2).

* Slaven Bilic has a degree in law and speaks four languages.
* He gained an international reputation while he was playing for Hajduk Split, where he won the only two major honours of his career, a Croatian League Campionship winners medal, an a Croatian Cup winners medal.
* In 1993 he signed for Karlsruhe. His charisma saw him become the only foreign player in German football to be named captain of his team in his first year.
* He put together some tremendous performances for Karlsruhe, making a decisive contribution to help the German club manage to win a place in the U.E.F.A. Cup after finishing in the top four in the Intertoto Cup. His quality and ability saw him  chosen for the Bundeslige's ideal team.
* On 4th February 1996, he was transfered to West Ham United for 1,300,000 pounds. He made his league debut on 12th February in a 1-0 victory against Tottenham Hotspur at White Hart Lane.
* In June 1996 he played in the European Championships in England as an automatic choice in Miroslav Blazevic's Croatian side. Germany knocked Croatia out of the tournament in the quarter finals.
* On 14th May 1997 he signed for Everton, who paid West Ham 4,500,000 pounds to take him to Goodison Park.

* He was the focal point of the West Ham defence, missing just three games all season. He was chosen as West Ham's Player of the Year at the end of the season by the Hammer's fans. He found the back of net twice, against Liverpool and Sunderland,  and was called up by the Croatian national manager on a number of oocasions to play in the qualifying games for the 1998 World Cup Finals in France.

27.name: Thomas
pages: * Known as "the tank", Tony Thomas has spent the whole of his career at Tranmere Rovers, a club he helped to get promoted from the Third Division  to the First. Now Thomas has the chance, for the first time, to do a job for a Premier League club; proving that it's never too late to get a taste of competition at the highest level.

* Thomas is a defender who can play down either flank. He likes to move forward in support of the attack and reach the byline, from where he puts over some dangerous crosses. In defence he is a consistent performer who is difficult to beat, although on occasions  he goes in harder than he should.
* Associated Members Cup Winners medal 90.

* He is one of the players whose brilliant peformances took Tranmere Rovers from the Third Division through to the First.
* He signed for Everton on 6th August 1997 after having spent nine seasons as a Tranmere player.
* The 97-98 season is his first as a Premier League player.

* Despite being on a week to week contract, Thomas had a fine season. He was in and out  of the side at the beginning of the campaign, but once the season passed the halfway stage he began to put together some tremendous performances, both at right back as well as on the left hand side.

28.name: Phelan
pages: * Unable to make himself a regular in Ruud Gullit's Chelsea side, Phelan decided to move on to Everton last January. He moved initally as the replacement for Andy Hinchcliffe, but, once he had made his debut, nobody proved to be capable of dislodging him from the side. This season, with Hinchcliffe now over his injury problems Phelan will have a tremendous battle on his hands as he tries to win the confidence of manager Howard Kendall.

* A very mobile left back, Terry Phelan is a quick defender, who is very difficult to take on for pace. Although he frequently moves forward to support the attack, he is at his best when he is doing a containing job, where he is a very safe, secure player when he goes in to win the ball from opposing forwards, on occasions with particularly hard tackles. Technically limited he doesn't stand out for his attacking contribution. However, he shows commitment and hard work throughout the whole game, something which is well appreciated by his teammates. Very much a left footed player, if there is one characteristic of his game that stands out then that would be his pace.

* F.A. Cup winners medal 87-88.
* Charity Shield medal 88.

* 37 full international appearances for the Republic of Ireland, he made his debut on 11th September 1991. He was a member of the Irish squad for the 1994 World Cup Finals in the United States, where he played in two games as a member of the starting line up, against Mexico (a 1-2 defeat ) and Italy  (a 1-0 victory).
* 1 "B" international appearance.
* 1 under-23 international appearance.
* 1 under-21international appearance.
* 1 youth international appearance.

* He began his playing career in the youth ranks at Leeds United, where he turned professional on 3rd August 1984. However, he didn't get to make his debut until 7th September 1985 in a game against Shrewsbury. 
* In 1986 he completed his contract with Leeds and moved on to sign for Swansea City on 30th July of that same year. After a season in which he played in practically every game, he was transfered to Wimbledon on 29th July 1987 for 100,000 pounds. He was one of Bobby Gould's first signings at the club. 
* In his first season with the Londoners, he helped Wimbledon win the F.A. Cup, against all the odds.
* Born in Manchester, in 1992 he was offered the opportunity to play for one of the city's two big clubs. So, on 25th August 1992 he was transfered to Manchester City for 2,500,000 pounds. His excellent performances made him a regular in the Republic of Ireland side, and also won him a place in the Republic's squad for the World Cup Finals in the United States in 1994. 
* He began the 95-96 season with Manchester City, but on 15th November 1995 he was transfered to Chelsea for 900,000 pounds. He made his debut on 9th December in a 1-0 victory against Newcastle at Stamford Bridge. 
* On 1st January 1997 Everton paid 850,000 pounds to sign him from Chelsea. He made  his debut that same day against Blackburn at Goodison Park (0-2).

* Signed from Chelsea, where he was hardly given a game under Ruud Gullit, Phelan arrived at Everton in January 1997. Initially he came as a replacement for Hinchcliffe, but, after just a few games, he demonstrated that he wasn't at Goodison Park just as a substitute. A series of good performances, in which he lived up to his reputation as being a fast attacking left back, won him the respect and the admiration of the Everton fans. He also made two appearances for the Republic of Ireland.

29.name: Short
pages:
* The early days of Craig Short's Everton career were not exactly brilliant. He noticed, far too obviously, the step up in division and the pressure of playing in the Premier League. The Goodison Park supporters began to get impatient, fully aware of the amount of money that the club had paid out to sign the player. When all the signs were that he would never really settled down and become a success at Everton, Joe Royle's insistence in naming him in the side finally paid off and helped him to raise his game. 
* Today the Toffees' supporters know that in Craig Short they have a fine defender in their ranks, and it would surprise nobody if he went on to become the natural succesor to veteran Dave Watson.

* A central defender with a tremendous physical presence, he is also a danger to the opposition when he moves forward to join the attack. He frequently moves forward into the opposition  penalty area for dead ball situations where his poweful heading ability allows him to occasionally find the back of the net. Defensively, he is dominant in the air, and, in recent years, he has shown  noticeable progress in his ball control, showing more idea when it comes to setting up counter attacks. As time has gone by he has also developed a more aggressive attitude, making him a more difficult defender for opposition forwards to get the better of. He has good positional sense which makes him a very effective player when he is required to cover acroos the back line. Craig Short is, essentially, a good defender and a threat that his side can make use of at set pieces.
x
* An England youth international.

* Voted in 1995 as the "First Division's Best Central Defender," Craig Short took his first steps in the world of football with modest Pickering Town, from where he moved on to Scarborough on 15th October 1987. 
* On 27th July 1989 he was transfered to Notts County for 100,000 pounds. 
* His move to Derby County on 18th September 1992 became the most expensive in the First Division, with the transfer fee being set at 2,500,000 pounds. .
* He has been an Everton player since 18th July 1995 after the Goodison Park club paid out 2,700,000 pouds. He made his debut for the Toffees on 17th September of that same year at the City Ground against Nottingham Forest, losing 3-2. On 26th December of that same year he scored his first goal in an Everton shirt, against Middlesbrough at Goodison Park,(4-0).

* He began the season well, playing in 11 of the first 13 games, although his appearances in the side later became more sporadic, due to injury problems. When he reappeared in March he took up his place once again of the heart of the defence, until an injury in the derby match against Liverpool kept him out of the last three games of the season. In total Short made 23 appearances, scoring twice.
