30.name: Watson
pages: * Now very much one of the Premier League's veterans, Dave Watson sets out on his twelfth season with Everton, hoping that he can help to give the side the same defensive stability that he managed to when he formed defensive partnerships with Kevin Ratcliffe during 1980's, and with Martin Keown and later David Unsworth during the1990's. The Everton captain is not the type to give in without a fight.

* A central defender, very much of the old school; excellent in the air, both in defence and in attack, he is technically weak when he has the ball at his feet. A hard player, very often his experience is all he needs to get himself out of tight situations. Solid and consistent Watson is an example in professionalism for every other player in the Premier League. Now in the twilight of his career, he makes up for the decline in the physical aspects of his game with his experience and know how.

* League Championship winners medal 86-87. 
* F.A. Cup winners medal 94-95.
* League Cup winners medal 84-85, with Norwich City. 
* Second Division winner medal, 85-86. 
* Charity Shield  medal87.

* 12 full international appearances for England. He made his debut on 10th June 1984 in the Maracana stadium in  Rio de Janeiro, in a game in which England beat Brazil 2-0.
* 7 under-21 international appearances.

* He is the brother of ex-Liverpool player Alex Watson.
* After coming through the club's junior ranks he signed professional for Liverpool on  25th May 1979.
* Without getting to play in even one minute of league action with the Reds, he was transfered to Norwich City on 29th November 1980, in exchange for 100,000 pounds.
* He made his debut for Norwich on 26th December 1980, in a game against Ipswich.
* On 22nd August 1986 he returned to his home city to sign for Everton. His transfer valuation had risen to 900,000 pounds.
* In 1992 he suffered a serious injury that kept him out of the side for a number of games although he went on to make a tremendous recovery and was even recalled to the England  side.

* He was one of the most important players in the Everton defence, just as he was in each of the previous ten seasons he had played at the Goodison Park club. He suffered a knee injury in the first game of the season that kept him out for approximately two months. Once he was fit again he got back to the form and consistency that he had always given the side. He played in a total of 29 league games, and scored once against Derby County, a goal which clinched a victory for Everton.

31.name: Ward
pages:
* Signed for Everton in November 1997.
* Mitch Ward is a man who comes from the youth squad at Sheffield United and in whom Dave Basset, his former manager, didn't have a lot of confidence as he put him on the transfer list and thought that he was a player who wasn't going to make a big contribution to the team.
* However, after the departure of Bassett and the arrival of Howard Kendall Mitch Ward's aspirations at Sheffield United did an about turn. Since the arrival of the latest manager of the Blades this footballer has improved greatly and so it is not surprising that he signed a contract binding him to the club for two and half more seasons. Now Howard Kendall wants him at Goodison Park.

* Ward is a wide defender or wide midfield player who can operate on either flank although he is more usually seen on the right. He is very attacking and joins in the attack frequently helping out the midfielders or strikers according the position he is playing in. He is quick in his actions, and also has a great determination. He has good technical resources, skilful and dribbles well, allowing him to get past rival defenders. He puts over excellent crosses, a lot better from the right than the other side and  likes to get to the baseline and give a lethal pass. He is always aware of the position of the forwards. He has a great physical resistance as has been well demonstrated, and an acceptable playing vision. Finally, it has to be said that he is a good penalty taker, very secure in this aspect.
x
x

* Ward was trained in the lower ranks of Sheffield United, signing as a professional in July 1989. He makes his league debut on 8th September 1990 against Manchester City and scores his first league goal on 14th december 1991 against Aston Villa.
* He is loaned to Crewe Alexandra in November 1990. He plays his first game on 3rd November 1990 against Mansfield Town and his first goal in the league competition is his team's winner against Cambridge United on 30th November 1990.

* Ward was a man used by Howard Kendall in almost all of the possible positions on the pitch, wearing a seven different numbers. However, despite such positional instability, his performance was one of the most consistent during the course of the season in which the Blades were on the verge of promotion to the Premier League. In total he played 34 games and scored 4 goals.

32.name: Thomsen
pages: * A player of enormous physical power, and not lacking in quality either, Claus  Thomsen gives Everton the adaptability of a player who has the ability to play in a number of different positions. Nevertheless, he is not going to have an easy time of things as he battles to try to make himself a regular member of the side, although he will no doubt get into the action in plenty of games.

* If one thing stands out about Claus Thomsen it is his versatility which allows him to play as a midfielder, as a central defender or even as a centre forward. He is a very dangerous player when he makes late runs into the box from deep positions at set pieces. He is a player of enormous physical power who is involved in everything his side does, both in attack and defence..
x

* A Danish international at Under-21 level, he made his full international debut on 5th April 1995 against Macedonia. He has played in 14 games for Denmark, playing in the 1996 European Championships in England in which he played in 3 of the 3 games that the Danes played before they were knocked out.

* Ipswich Town signed him from Danish club Aarhus in June 1994 for 250,000 pounds. His league debut came on 24th September 1994 against Manchester United, while he scored his first goal on 19th November 1994 against Blackburn Rovers.
* Everton signed him in January 1997 from Ipswich Town for 900,000 pounds. He made his debut on 23rd February 1997 against Arsenal at Higbhury (3-1).

* He arrived at Everton in the month of January from Ipswich Town, and made his debut against Arsenal. He began by playing at the heart of the defence in his first few games, but eventually ended up playing in the centre of the midfield. He also had the  misfortune of scoring in his own net in the derby match against Liverpool.

33.name: Oster
pages:
* John Oster is one of the best young prospects in British football. Already an under-21 international with Wales, if one day he goes on to play for the full side, with Ryan Giggs, they could well form one of the best pairs of left footed attacking players in Europe. Quick and skillful, Oster took just  one season in the first team at Grimsby Town to make the move up to the Premier League.
* His quality is in no doubt, and being the sort of player who doesn't come along every day of the week, if he is fully fit, then it seems more than likely that Howard Kendall will be regularly putting him in the side.

* Oster has just about everything he needs to go on to become one of the most  important players in the Premier League over the next few years. Left footed and very quick, Oster has an impressive ability to beat a man, one of the qualities in his game which most catches the eye. He normally plays behind the main strikers but also possesses the quality to play out wide tight on the left hand touchline, either in midfield or as a winger. Despite his age, he has a good knowledge of the game, and, on more than one occasion, has already embarassed a couple of  Premier League defenders.

* 4 under-21 international appearances for Wales.
* Welsh youth international.

* He came through the youth ranks at Grimsby Town, taking the step up to the  club's first team squad in July 1996.
* In the space of just a year he has gone from being a complete unknown, to becoming  one of the brightest prospects in British football.
* The quality of his performances attracted the attention of a number of talent scouts from Premier League clubs, though finally it was Everton who managed to tempt him to sign on the dotted line. The Blues paid Grimsby 1,500,000 pounds to finally get their man.
* The 1997-98 season is Oster's first as a Premier League player.

* At just 17 years of age he delighted the supporters who had the opportunity to see his quick fire style of football. His superb season brought managers and coaches such as Kenny Dalglish and Terry McDermott to Grimsby Town to watch him in action. He was also called up to the Welsh under-21 squad.

34.name: Williamson
pages: * A product of West Ham United's youth system, Williamson is a very talented footballer whose progress was brought to a halt last year due to injuries. His move to Everton could help him to get back the confidence to allow him to reach the form he showed during the 95-96 season with West Ham, when his passing ability and capacity to surprise defenders by coming from deep, brought him the admiration of both the press as well as supporters.

* Danny Williamson is a very complete midfield organizer who can also play as a link up man between the forwards and the midfield. He has plenty of tricks up his sleeve, good vision and an eye for a goal. He distributes the ball thoughtfully and is always available for his teammates. He is always willing to help defensively, putting in a tremendous amount of effort, never shirking a physical challenge. He fights for every ball, and shows great enthusiasm all over the pitch, all of which makes him a player to keep an eye on. His talent and youth make him one of the brightest prospects in English football.
x
x

* Born in the West Ham district of the East End of London, during his career in schoolboy football Danny Williamson was the star of the Newham and Essex  district schoolboys' team. After coming through the ranks at Upton Park, he turned professional on 3rd July 1992. 
* He went out on loan to Doncaster Rovers on 8th October 1993, and made his league debut the following day in a game against Lincoln City. 
* Once back at West Ham he made his first appearance for the Hammers on 30th April 1994 in a 0-2 victory against Arsenal at Highbury.
* On his debut at Upton Park on 7th May 1994, he managed to find the back of the net against  Southampton, scoring his first goal in a West ham shirt, (3-3). His goal made him the first West Ham player to score on his Upton Park debut since Tony Cottee in 1983.                    * During the 95-96 season he played in 29 games and put together some outstanding performances. At the end of the season Julian Dicks  declared that his vote for "Hammer of the Year" had gone to Danny Williamson.
* On 14th August, having completed his contract with West Ham he signed for Everton.

* An ankle injury gave him problems throughout the season, and, as a result, Danny  Williamson was unable to reproduce the form he had shown during the 95-96 season, and, as a result, confirm himself as a top Premier League prospect. He started well, playing in West Ham's first six games of the season until injury struck him down, keeping him out of the side for three months. Once he had recovered, he came back to play in 7 games until another injury put him out of action again. The season ended for him in March against Chelsea when his injury jinx struck yet again.

35.name: Farrelly
pages: * Without a place in the side at Aston Villa, this season Farrely has decided to have a change of scenery and try his luck at Everton. He is not going to have an easy task forcing his way into the side at Goodison park either, but is certainly a player who will be out to prove Aston Villa wrong, and will be trying to give Howard Kendall a few headaches when he sits down to choose his side.

* A midfield playmarker, his technique allows him to play in several different midfield positions. A very correct passer of the ball with good vision, he makes an equal contribution both in attack and in defence, showing a maturity beyond his years. If he maintains his progress he could go on to become an important player for Everton, given the versatility that allows him to efficiently cover several positions.
x

* 3 full international appearances for the Republic of Ireland. He made his debut on 29th May 1996 in a game against Portugal in Dublin (0-1). 
* 8 under- 21 international appearances.

* He came through the Aston Villa youth system and went on to sign professional for the club on 21st January.
* He went out on loan to Rotherham United on 21st March 1995, making his debut the following day in a game against Bristol Rovers.
* He had to wait until the 95-96 campaign before making his league debut for Aston Villa, when he played against Leeds United on 3rd February 1996, at Villa Park, (3-0). He came on as a second half substitute in place of Andy Townsend.
* In July 1997 Everton signed him from Aston Villa for  700,000 pounds.

* He didn't see too many opportunities come his way at Aston Villa, where he played in  just three games. Villa manager Brian Little had other players ahead of Farrely on his list for the midfield places, meaning the Irishman was able to make only a very limited contribution.

36.name: Grant
pages: * A young player who has come through the Goodison Park youth system, he is a young man with a brilliant future ahead of him, and who, slowly but surely, has begun to get the opportunities he needs to show just what he can do. He made 18 first team appearances, and, this time out, could well set out on the road to stardom.

* A skillful midfielder he possesses good vision and a fine touch on the ball, while his main asset is his passing ability. A good midfield organizer, he is a player who, given his youth, has plenty of time to develop and progress.

* After the coming through the ranks at Everton, he turned professional on 8th July 1993.
* He made his league debut on 1st February 1995 against Newcastle. He went on to  make his first starting appearance in a game against Queens Park Rangers, a game which ended in a 3-2 victory for Everton.
* A boyhood friend of Liverpool's Robbie Fowler, Grant has seen how his own career has come to a little bit of a standstill while his Liverpool counterpart has shot to supertardom..

* Last season was undoubtedly his best since turning professional with Everton. He played in a total of 18 games, playing in 10 of those as a member of the starting line up. Unfortunately an ankle injury he picked up just after Christmas put him out of action for the rest of the season.

37.name: Parkinson
pages: * Joe Parkinson's main asset is his fighting spirit, a quality which allowed him to  take the step up into the Premier League, and also took him to an F.A. Cup final,  coming away with a winners medal. An insatiable hard worker, he is out to get more honours under his belt as soon as he can.

* A right footed midfielder, he basically does a containing job in the middle of the park. He generally plays just in front of the defence, a position which allows him to win plenty of possession for his side. A good passer of the ball, despite his youth he keeps his composure well in tight situations. Technically good, he poses a threat when he moves forward, although he is not a tremendously gifted attacking player.
* F.A. Cup winners medal  94-95.

* He made his league debut for Wigan  Athletic on 30th September 1988 in a game against Blackpool. A product of the club's youth system he turned professional on 1st April 1989. 
* On 1st July 1993 he was transfered to Bournemouth for 35,000 pounds. 
* On 24th March 1994, he moved to Everton, who paid 250,000 pounds to take him  to Merseyside.
* Up to the end of the 94-95 season he had been booked 18 times.

* He was one of the regulars in Joe Royle's side until injuries prevented him from getting the continuity he would have wanted. After missing five games just after Christmas, he eventually went on to make a total of 28 appearances, failing to find the back of the net.

38.name: Beagrie
pages:
* He was loaned to Everton in March 1998. 
* Peter Beagrie has spent the last two seasons in Manchester City, an experience which could only be classed as a nightmare, only playing in half-a-dozen games with no continuity due to repeated injury problems for the English winger. His sale to Bradford City has surprised all and sundry, though it could be that Beagrie is looking for a chance to show the coaches at Maine Road that they were wrong about letting him go. In form, he could and should be a regular for Chris Kamara.

* A very fast winger, he moves with the ball stuck to either of his feet as he can use either well. One of his favourite moves consists of advancing down the left, selling constant dummies to the defenders, whether it be to his right while coming out to the left or vice versa, to then make a centre or shoot powerfully with either of his feet.

* Top scorer at Sheffield United 86-87 together with Steve Foley. 
* Top scorer at Stoke City 88-89.

* English B and under-21 international, he made his debut on 8th September 1987 against East Germany, forming part of an English team which included Tony Dorigo, Paul Gascoigne, Tony Cottee and Nigel Clough.

* A player from the lower ranks of Middlesborough, Beagrie turned professional in September 1983.  He made his league debut on 2nd October 1984 against Oldham Athletic and scored his first league goal against Shrewsbury Town on 11th May 1985. 
* Transferred to Sheffield United in August 1986 for £35,000, he made his league debut on 23rd August 1986 against Shrewsbury Town, substituting for Peter Withe, the player who scored Aston Villa's winner in the final of the European Cup in 1981 against Bayern Munich.  He scored his first goal on 2nd September 1986 against Millwall. 
* Stoke City sign him in June 1988 for £210,000. He made his debut on 27th August 1988 against Ipswich Town and scores his first goal on 1st October 1988 against Bournemouth, a goal which turns out to be the winner. 
* Beagrie was transferred to Everton in November 1989 for £750,000, playing his first game for the team on 5th November 1989 and scores his first goal in the league competition on 13th January 1991 against Manchester City.
* He is loaned to Sunderland in September 1991, and makes his debut on 28th September 1991 against Middlesborough. He scores his first goal against Brighton & Hove Albion on 5th October 1991. 
* Finally, he is signed by Manchester City in March 1994 for £1.1 million. He plays his first game on 26th March 1994 against Oldham Athletic and scores his first goal for them against Aston Villa on 2nd April 1994. 
* Beagrie is transferred to Bradford City in the summer of 1997 for £50,000 pounds. 
* Beagrie celebrates his goals with a double somersault.

* The bad 95-96 season turned into a horrible one for Peter Beagrie as he only played one game in the whole of the league due to various injury problems and decisions of the coach who only let him play this one game, coming on as a substitute and even playing against Middlesborough in the Cup. Despite this lack of playing time, the Peter Beagrie of old could be seen on the pitch.

39.name: Madar
pages: x

* Madar plays at centre forward and is noted, above all, for his physical strength, in which the whole of his game is based.  Opportunistic and with an acceptable ability to score goals, he has a good header.  With the ball at his feet he is not so skilful nor effective.
x

* He has had two full international caps. 
* He was at the England European Championship, but didn't play a single game. 
* He played his first game for the first side on the 11th of October 1995, in a game between Romania and France (1-3).

* Deportivo didn't pay a single penny for him as he didn't have any contractual ties in June 1996.
* He has a contract until the 30th of June 1999. 
* His cancellation clause was £4 million. 
* He made his debut in the French First Division on the 25th of March 1987 in a game between Toulouse and Sochaux (2-1). 
* He played his first official game for Deportivo on the 31st of August 1996, in a game against Real Madrid in the Riazor Stadium (1-1). 
* During the last pre-season he had a run-in with the manager, Carlos Alberto Silva, and the club kept him out of the line-ups for the first eight games of the season.  He was reintegrated into the team when Silva got his marching orders. 
* He was transferred to Everton in December 1997.

* In the last League he played 17 games (1,124 minutes), and scored three goals.  He received one yellow card and one red one.  He was one of the big disappointments at Deportivo and at no time did he live up to the expectations placed in him.  In his defence, it has to be said that an injury kept him out for 26 weeks, which made his adaptation to Spanish football a lot harder.

40.name: Cadamarteri
pages: * Another product of the Everton youth system, Cadamarteri is one of the  Toffees' brightest young hopes for the future. His ability has saw the English F.A., move to become the first to offer him the opportunity to play for their under-21 side, bearing in mind that Danny is able to choose from six countries, all of whom he is eligible for at international level. Howard Kendall knows that he has a rough diamand in his squad, who just needs polishing up to allow him to shine in games, and, it seems quite probable that he will be getting plenty of opportunities to do just that, as a member of the starting line up.

* A right winger who likes to play tight on the touchline, he has tremendous ability in one on one situations, above all when he is in full flight on the run. Constantly moving about in order to lose his markers, he is a very direct player when he has the ball at his feet. Without being a natural goalscorer, he has a powerful shot when he has a go at goal.

* At the beginning of the 96-97 season he signed his first professional contract which tied him to Everton for the next five years.
* He made his debut as a Premier League player against Chlesea at Goodison Park, (1-2) on 11th May 1997.
* Due to his family roots, Cadamarteri can choose from any one of six countries to play for at international level, (Nigeria, Italy,England, Ireland, Scotland or Jamaica). Everthing seems to indicate that England is the country that Cadamertari is going to choose to get his international career underway.

* He made his debut for Everton against Chelsea, coming on at half time.  That was Cadamarteri's only first team appearance all season for Everton. He played the majority of his games for the reserves.

41.name: Barmby
pages:
* Despite his youth, Nick Barmby has already given more than a few glimpses of his  talent. Together with players of the class of Fowler and Caskey, he formed one of the best national youth sides in Europe and maintained a tremendous rate of progress year after year. A player with very clear ideas about what he is doing, and where he is going, he was looking for a first team spot at Tottenham, and, when it didn't come his way, he decided to move on to make a name for himself under Bryan Robson at Middlesbrough. However, last season, an irresistible offer from Everton saw him make the move to Merseyside.
* He became an international under Terry Venables, although he also scored the first goal of Glenn Hoddle's reign as England manager against Moldova. Of Barmby, Pele himself said that he would go on to become one of the best players  In the world. It's also been mentioned that the great Brazilian knows a thing or two about the game himself....

* Although he himself prefers to play up front, Barmby is often lined up as a midfielder, a position which allows him to demonstrate his tremendous vision. He is a very skillful footballer, with the ability to beat men with appearent ease. He makes tremendous runs from deep and has a real eye for a goal. An intelligent, hard working player, he always does the simple thing when setting up attacks, and unselfishly sets up plenty of goalscoring chances for his teamamtes. His constant hard work also sees him helping out with defensive duties, all of which makes him a very valuable player and one of the most promising English players of recent years.
* European Under-20 Championship winners medal, beating Turkey in the final, (1-0).

* 10 full international appearances for England, wth 4 goals to his name. He made his debut on 29th March 1995 in a friendly game against Uruguay at Wembley.
* On 23rd May 1996 he scored three times against China in a friendly match in Beijing.
* He was a member of the England squad for the 1996 European Championships in England. He came on for Sheringham, in the final minutes of each of the three games he played in against Switzerland, Holland and Spain.
* 1 "B" international appearance.
* 4 under-21international appearances.
* 8 youth international appearances.

* He joined the youth ranks at Tottenham Hotspur in March 1990. He quickly went form being a trainee to a fully fledged professional, signing his first contract on 9th April 1991. He made his debut on 27th September 1992 in a game against Sheffield Wednesday.       * An England international at all levels and a regular member of the Tottenham side, during the 94-95 season he played alongside Jurgen  Klinsmann  and Teddy Sheringham, scoring 9 times and laying on plenty more for his teammates.
* His problems with Spurs' chairman Alan Sugar, and the opportunity of living nearer his home town of Hull, saw him eventually moving to Middlesbrough on 8th August 1995. Boro chairman Steve Gibson paid out 5,250,000 pounds to sign Barmby,  a club record until it was broken one year later by Ravanelli's move to the North East club.
* Although he wore a Boro shirt for the first time in a friendly game against Hibernians,  his official debut for the club came on 20th August 1995 at Highbury, against Arsenal. Middlesbrough drew 1-1, with Barmby getting the side's goal, following a one on one with David Seaman.
* The legendary Pele has declared that Barmby will become one of the stars of the future.
* On 23rd May 1996 Nick scored three times for England in China. A few days later England manager  Terry Venables decided to call him  up to the squad for the 1996 European Championships in place of the veteran Peter Beardsley.  
* He began the 96-97 season at Middlesbrough but on 30th October 1996, he was transfered to Everton  for 5,750,000 pounds.
* He made his Everton debut on 4th November 1996 at Goodison Park against Coventry City (1-1).
* He scored his first Premier League goal for Everton against Derby County (0-1), at the old Baseball Ground, on 16th December 1996, clinching a 0-1 cvictory for the Blues with a goal just four minutes before the end of the game.
* The goal he scored to clinch victory for England against Moldova, in a qualifying game  for the 1998 World Cup Finals in France, was the first of Glen Hoddle's reign as England manager.

* He arrived at Everton in November, from Middlesbrough, where, up to that moment, he had played in 10 games, scoring once. He broke Everton's transfer record with his move to the club, who had never paid out so much money for one player. With the Goodison Park outfit he played in 25 games, and found the back of the net four times. He played one game for England, against Moldova in Chisinau (0-3) and managed to score his country's opening goal.

42.name: Branch
pages:
* Paul Branch is one of the brightest prospects at Everton, especially so bearing  in mind the fantastic season he had last time out. Despite being just 18 years of age, Paul scored a number of important goals that allowed Everton to pick up some vital points.
*His age and lack of experience, could become the main obstacles that prevent him  from forcing his way into the side on  a regular basis. Nevertheless, it seems quite likely that Kendall will be using him as an extra option when the going gets tough in certain matches and Branch's presence out on the park is required to get the side back into the game.

* Branch is a quick, direct striker, capable of finding gaps in the rival defence with apparent ease. Technically good, he shields the ball well, and shows a good ability to beat a man. Despite his youth, he is a very natural player and shows a surprising amount of awareness. Given his lack of experience at the highest level of competition, he has plenty of time to progress and develop his game. If his development doesn't come to a sudden halt, he could well go on to become a very important striker in the future for Everton.
x

* 2 under-21 international appearances for England. 
* An England youth and schoolboy international.

* After coming through the youth ranks at Everton, he signed professional on 24th October 1995. He made his league debut in a defeat against Manchester United at Old Trafford on 21st February 1996, after coming on as a substitute, in place of Tony Grant 
* His first appearance as a member of the starting line up came on 27th April of that same year at Hillsborough against Sheffield Wednesday. Everton were well and truly beaten by five goals to two.
* He scored his first goal in an Everton shirt in the Premier League on 7th December 1996 against Chelsea at Stamford Bridge, (2-2).

* In his second season in Everton's first team squad, he managed to establish himself as a genuine member of the side, making 25 appearances, scoring three times. He didn't play from the start in all of those games, although he gave plenty of glimpses of the class that marks him out as a player with an excellent future. He struck his first Premier League goal, against Chelsea, and added another two, against Leicester City and West Ham United.

43.name: Ferguson
pages:
* The player who, in the summer of 1993, was the subject of the most expensive transfer in British football, arrived at Everton with something of a tarnished reputation, following an unpleasent incident which saw him banned from Scottish football for the rest of the season. Loaned out by Rangers, the Everton coaching staff discovered that behind his impetuous, even rebellious character, there lay a potentially top class footballer. Although not yet a genuine star, his youth and his goals could well represent the future of the club.
* This season could be the one in which he finally arrives on the scene in the Premier  League. Ferguson remains very much a fiery character but seems to have learnt how to control his temperament, and, without doubt, his performances have benefitted. His form has finally lived up to expectations, and he will no doubt be one of the key men in Howard Kendall's line up, and, if he decides to make himself available for Scotland once again, will no doubt be in the squad for the 1998 World Cup Finals in France.

* Duncan Ferguson is, above all, a goalscorer. Blessed with the classical instincts of a striker, his style of play reminds the supporters of those battling, defence breaking centre forwards, so characteristic of Bristish football. He possesses great physical strength which, together with his height makes him a very dangerous player in the air, seemingly able to get his head to any ball which is played into the area. With these characteristics, it is no surprise that he scores a lot of his goals from dead ball situations. With the ball at his feet he shows a good ability to shield it while he waits for support to come through from his teammates. If he manages to improve his touch on the ball, and control his fearsome temperament, his contribution to the side could be even greater than it already is.
* F.A. Cup winners medal  94-95.

* 7 full international appearances for Scotland.
* 7 under-21 international appearances, scoring once.

* He signed for Dundee United from modest Carse Thistle on 1st February 1990. On 10th November of that same year he made his league debut against Glasgow Rangers.
* An automatic first team choice at Dundee United, he was transfered to Glasgow Rangers on 20th July 1993 for 4,000,000 pounds a fee which made him at the time, the most expensive signing in the history of British football. 
* Whilst playing for Rangers, in a game against Raith Rovers, Ferguson attacked an opponent, an incident which saw him suspended for the rest of the season and also even spending a short spell in prison, after the opposing player reported the incident to the police.
* His ban in Scottish football hastened his move on loan to Everton in October 1994, eventually joining the Toffees on a permanent basis for  4,400,000 pounds.
* He was a substitute in the F.A. Cup final in May 1995, although he did get into the action when he came on in place of a teammate.
* Up to the end of the 94-95 season he had been sent off 3 times and booked on 23 occasions.

* Last season he was undoubtedly Everton's best player. Ferguson made the most of his physical attributes, and also demonstrated that he can also play with the ball at his feet. Ferguson was always involved in all the big games, and was especially noticeable at Old Trafford where scored a spectacular goal. In the 33 games he played in, he scored 10 goals, and it is very probable that without his contribution Everton would today be a First Division club. Ferguson was also called up to the Scotland squad, which eventually managed to qualify for the 1998 World Cup Finals in France.

44.name: Van der Gouw
pages: * Rai Van Der Gouw's presence in the squad at Manchester United reflects Alex Ferguson's desire for a quality goalkeeper to cover any  possible absences of Peter Schmeichel, either through injury or suspension. An experienced goalkeeper, Van Der Gouw was born in the same year as the "Great Dane". In the few opportunities he had last season Van Der Gouw showed the quality he possesses. It seems initially that his situation at the club will not change much this season, but if injury or suspension occurs the supporters can rest assured that the United goal will be in Van Der Gouw's safe hands.

* Raimond Van der Gouw is an experienced, solid and effective keeper. Safe in the air, Van der Gouw is not a spectacular keeper, his know-how and experience assures he is always well positioned making him a very difficult man to beat. If there is one quality which stands out in his play it is his consistency which he has maintained throughout his career..
* Charity Shield medal 1997.
x

* He has spent the majority of his career with Vitesse in the Dutch First Division. Between the 1991-92 season and the 94-95 campaign Van der Gouw appeared in every club league game, and took part in European competitions.
* On 12th July 1996 he was transfered to Manchester United as cover goalkeeper following the departure of Schmeichel's previous understudy Tony Coton.
* He made his Premier League debut on 21st September 1996, in the game against Aston Villa at Villa Park (0-0).

* With the first choice goalkeeping spot firmly in the hands of Peter Schmeichel, Rai Van der Gouw's opportunities were more than limited. In fact he played in just 2 Premier League games. He did defend however United's goal in several League Cup games and also in the Champions League semi-final against Borussia Dortmund. Despite the Reds' defeat in the semi-final first leg Rai had a fine game demonstrating that behind Peter Schmeichel United have a very safe deputy.

45.name: Schmeichel
pages: * Peter Schmeichel currently enjoys deserved world wide reputation. His performances, both for Manchester United and Denmark have won him international acclaim and have made him an automatic first choice both at Old Trafford and the Danish national side; to the point where his many great saves are given rightly deserved credit, his few errors are quietly dismissed. He has quality, ambition and personality, and despite having won everything is still hungry for more. Tremendously experienced although relatively young for a goalkeeper, Schmeichel is likely to remain with the "Red Devils" for a few seasons more. Bad news no doubt for all the strikers in the Premier League.

* Considered one of the best keepers in the world Schmeichel possesses great agility and sharp reflexes. His imposing stature allows total domination in the air as well as in one on one situations where he is a genuine specialist proving tremendously difficult to beat. Constantly shouting orders to his defenders he often comes off his line proving to be as competent with his feet as he is with his hands. When he has an inspired day Schmeichel becomes a real wall, proving unbeatable to any striker. 
* If he has one weakness it is his occasional inconsistency, alternating between moments of brilliance and calamitous error, not something in-keeping with a man of his stature.

* European Championship winners medal 1992.
* English league Championship winners medals 93, 94, 96 and 97.
* F.A. Cup winners medals  94 and  96.
* League Cup winners medals 92.
* Charity Shield medal 93, 94, 96 and 97.
* Danish League Championship winners medals  87, 88 y 89.
* Danish Cup Winners medal  89.
* European Super cup winners medal 91. 
* Chosen as "Goalkeeper of the Year" 1992. 
* Chosen as Danish footballer of the year in 1990 and 1993.

* With 95 full international appearances for Denmark Schmeichel made his debut against Greece on the 20th of May 1987 (0-5).
* A member of his country's squad for the 1988 European Championships in Germany Schmeichel played and lost in two games, one against the host nation and one against Italy (0-2 on both occasions). 
*A member of Denmark's victorious European Championship side in Sweden in 1992 Schmeichel was a member of the starting line up in the five games he played for his country, Denmark going on to win the tournament defeating Germany 2-0 in the final. 
* Schmeichel was also included in the Denmark squad for the 1996 European Championships in England. He played in Denmark's three matches in the first phase of the tournament against Scotland, England and Switzerland.

* Considered by many as the heir to the legendary Gordon Banks, Peter Schmeichel has for a  number of years been ranked amongst the world's top goalkeepers, an unlikely fact considering he took his first steps in the football world as a striker. 
* He is the son of a musician who plays the piano, the flute, the guitar and the drums. 
* He began his career in the ranks of Gladsaxe-Hero from where he moved to Hvidovre and later to Brondby where he won honours and international recognition. 
* On 12th August 1991 Schmeichel was transfered to Manchester United for £550,000. From the moment of his debut on the 17th of August against Notts County Schmeichel made the first team goalkeeping spot his own personal  property. 
* Schmeichel's performance was decisive in helping Denmark win the 1992 European Championship in Sweden. Still fresh in the memory is the incredible save he made against Jurgen Klinsmann in the final with the Germans already celebrating the goal. 
* In the 94-95 season Schmeichel suffered a back injury preventing him playing a number of vital games for his side. 
* In September 1995 Manchester United were prematurely eliminated from the UEFA Cup by Rotor Volvograd. Schmeichel however took up his place in history after scoring with a header in the last minute of the game at Old Trafford. No other English goalkeeper has achieved anything similar since the days of Alex Stepney

* Once again, Peter Schmeichel proved to be irreplaceable in goal at Manchester United throughout the whole of the season starting in 36 of the club's 38 league games though his form suffered a few ups and downs during the course of the season. Particularly painful for him were the away games at Newcastle and Southampton. In the space of six days Schmeichel conceded 11 goals in two games, 3 at  St. James' Park and 6 at The Dell. Despite this setback and the back problems he suffered during the course of the season the Danish keeper managed to get back to his best. He made one of the most spectacular and memorable saves in a Champions League game against Rapid Vienna which was compared by some with Gordon Banks' legendary save from Pele in the 1970 World Cup finals in Mexico. 
* Schmiechel rounded the season off by winning his fourth League Championship in five years.

49.name: Berg
pages: * Alex Ferguson was interested in signing Henning Berg for a long time before the paperwork was finally signed, suitably inpressed by the form Berg had shown during a trial spell the Norwegian defender had completed at Old Trafford a few years earlier. At that time Berg was a promising  youngster - today he is an experienced mature footballer, his talents more than demonstrated both at Blackburn Rovers and with the Norwegian national side. By signing Berg, Ferguson has brought to United a superb defender who has every chance of becoming a regular member of the side.

* Judging him purely on his defensive qualities Henning Berg can be judged one of the best full backs in the Premier League. Playing at right back Berg shows himself as a tough solid defender frequently executing his superb hallmark sliding tackles. Fast, with plenty of attributes to his game Berg anticipates situations well, is very difficult to beat for speed, and is always quick to get back into position when he has to. Although his passing is good, Berg however rarely gets involved in the attack, an aspect of his game he should try to improve, as he undoubtedly possesses the ability to do so.
*  Given his wide range of defensive strengthsBerg has often been used as a central defender, where he has always given a more than decent acount of himself.

* League Championship winners medal 95.
* Charity Shield medal 94.
* Chosen as "Norwegian Player of the Year" in 1995.

* 45 full international appearances for Norway, with 4 goals to his credit Berg made his debut on 13th May against the Faroe Isles.
* As a member of his country's squad during the 1994 World Cup in the United States Berg played as a member of the starting line up in the first three games for Norway against Mexico (1-0), Italy (0-1) and the Republic of Ireland (0-0). 
* 15 Under-21 international appearances, scoring five times.
* 2 Under-20 international appearances.

* Signed from Lillestrom, one of the most important clubs in Norway, Henning Berg arrived at Blackburn Rovers on 26th January 1993 in exchange for £400,000. Berg made his debut on 2nd February 1993 against Crystal Palace. During his first season in England however Berg barely played in the first team. The good form of David May and an injury suffered by Berg himself kept him waiting until the 1993-94 season when he finally established himself in the side. 
* Berg was a first choice for Norway during the 1994 World Cup Finals in the United States. During the 1994-95 season Berg proved one of Blackburn's most outstanding players, making a decisive contribution to the club's league title triumph. As a reward he was voted "Norwegian Player of the Year" in 1995. 
* On 11th August 1997 Berg was transfered to Manchester United for £5,000,000. The club's manager Alex Ferguson had been trying to sign him for nine years, dating back to when Berg was at Old Trafford on trial in 1988 at just 18 years of age. The impossibility of obtaining a work permit however caused the move for the young Berg to fall through.

* Henning Berg was one of Blackburn Rovers' most consistent players throughout the whole of last season. He began the campaign at right back but a tactical switch saw him moved to the centre of the defence where he proved to be efficient and forceful in the 36 league games in which he played. Berg made a decisive contribution to help Blackburn eventually retain their position in the Premier League scoring a crucial goal in the vital game against Sheffield Wednesday.

50.name: Johnsen
pages: * Ronny Johnsen, together with Ole Solskjaer is one of the flag bearers of Norwegian football currently operating in England. Unlike some of the players who arrive in the British Isles from other countries the Scandanavians seem to adapt very quickly to the Premier League - undoubtedly an advantage. Last season, thanks to some highly convincing performances, Johnsen won the trust of manager Alex Ferguson. Nevertheless, a shadow hangs over his future in the side: the manager's apparent obsession with signing a new central defender.

* A strong and powerful central defender, Ronny Johnsen has a wide range of defensive strength and abilities picked up over the course of his professional career. Though he is excellent in the air at both ends of the pitch he rarely finds the back of the net. Johnsen is comfortable when presented with an opponent playing a physical game but has more problems when faced with quick, skillful players. Conscious of his limitations the Norwegian keeps things simple when playing the ball from defence. Johnsen is a good defender but one who needs to improve his ability on the ball in order to increase his contribution to the team's attacking play. He can also play just in front of the defence where he does a good job gaining possession for the side more often than not.

* English League Championship winners medal 97. 
* Charity Shield medal 1997.

* 20 international appearances for Norway, scoring once.
* He made his debut on 8th August 1991 in a game against Sweden.

*  Johnsen began his playing career with Eik, in the Norwegian Second Division. In 1992 he took the step up to the First Division when he signed for SFK Lyn where he played for two years.. 
* in 1994 Johnsen was transfered to Lillestrom, where he was on the verge of winning the title. After just one season he moved on to Besitkas, one of the most important clubs in Turkey. 
* His arrival in England came on 26th July 1996 with  Manchester United paying £1,200,000 for his signature. Signing with the Old Trafford club coincided with the departure of the veteran central defender Steve Bruce to Birmingham City. 
* Johnsen made his Premier League debut on 17th August 1996 in a 0-3 victory against Wimbledon at Selhurst Park coming on as first half substitute for injured Nicky Butt.

* In his first season in England Ronny Johnsen played in 31 league games, 26 of those appearances coming right from the start, but despite his efforts he couldn't open his goalscoring account. Johnsen never found adapting to the Premier League a problem, at all times looking a solid and forceful player - qualities which allowed him to win the the trust of Alex Ferguson. As it turned out only injuries kept him out of the side. Without doubt Johnsen can rightly consider himself one of the star contributions in United's title triumph.

51.name: Phil Neville
pages: * The younger of the Neville brothers, Phil is one of the most promising young players in England. Slowly but surely he has won the confidence and backing of Alex Ferguson, his presence in the Manchester United side no longer considered a novelty. All factors seem to indicate that the 1997-98 season should turn out to be another step forward in his development, one he will take with his eyes very much fixed on the 1998 World Cup Finals in France. Phil has just one problem: his brother Gary is the main obstacle blocking his path into the first team.

* Although he has often played as a central defender Phil Neville is more at home when he plays as a left back. He's quick, passes the ball well, has good vision and possesses the ability to bring the ball out from defence backed by his defensive colleagues. Out on the pitch Phil shows signs of a maturity way beyond his years. Blessed with excellent basic defensive qualities he never allows opposing forwards a second. He is also good with his head and shows a fine sense of anticipation allowing him to read strikers' intentions. With all these qualities - and taking into account his youth - there is no doubt that Phil Neville is a player with a great future ahead of him.

* League Champions winners medal 96.
* 96. 
* Charity Shield medal 97. 
* F.A. Youth Cup winners medal 95.

* 6 full international appearances for England. He made his debut on 23rd May 1996 in a friendly against China in Beijing. England won 0-3.
* Called up by Terry Venables for the 1996 European Championships in England Phil was unable to make an appearance during the competition.
* 7 Under-21 international appearances.
* 3 youth international appearances.

* Two years younger than his brother Gary, Phil Neville also came through the Old Trafford youth system. 
* He was captain of the United side that won the F.A. Youth Cup in 1995.
* He didn't get the opportunity to make his league debut with the first team until 7th May 1995 in a game against Sheffield Wednesday at Old Trafford (1-0). 
* The 1995-96 season saw him finally settle down in United's starting line up and also make his debut with the full England side. He was even called up into the England squad for the European Championships in England at just 19 years of age. 
* During the 96-97 season Phil suffered a number of different injuries as well as a serious illness which even threatened to put an end to his career.
* In September 1996 Phil renewed his contract with Manchester United for another five years.

* Phil Neville didn't have too much luck during the course of last season struck down as he was in September with a serious illness which threatened to put an end to his playing career. Previously Phil had had to undergo surgery on an ankle after having been a member of the starting line up in the first three league games of the season. He also suffered an injury warming up  minutes before the Champions League game against Juventus at Old Trafford. As a result of all these setbacks Phil was limited to just 18 league appearances, 15 of those however as a member of the starting line up. Despite his problems his name still appeared regularly among the list of players called up into Glenn Hoddle's England squad.

52.name: Gary Neville
pages: * The battle for the full back places at Manchester United is very much a family affair. Gary Neville has his brother Phil both as a team mate and a rival for a place in the starting line up, both at United and the England side. With the 97-98 season now underway Gary faces a double challenge; to establish himself in the line up at club level in a season in which United will once again attempt to win the Champions League, and also make sure he stays in the England side hopefully going on to do something big in the World Cup finals in France.

* Gary Neville generally lines up as a right back although if necessary though his talents can stretch him out to left back or even as a central defender. An excellent tight marker Gary is quick, good in the air, and gets forward well working hard up and down the flank for the whole of the 90 minutes, always available as support for his teammates. Possessing good technique and ability on the ball his skill allows him to take the ball and push it forward from the back simply and effectively. Although he lacks a powerful srike Gary is good passer which he demonstrates through quality accurate crosses. Nevertheless, the maturity and security that he shows out on the pitch make him an excellent full back.

* League Championship winners medals 95-96 and 96-97.
* F.A. Cup winners medal 96. 
* Charity Shield medal 97.
* F.A. Youth Cup winners medal  92.

* 22 full international appearances for England. He made his debut on 3rd June 1995 in a game against Japan (2-1) at Wembley forming part of the Umbro Cup tournament. 
* As a member of England's squad for the 1996 European Championships in England, he was a member of the starting line up in the first four England games played against Switzerland, Scotland, Holland and Spain. Being shown two yellow cards, he was unable to play in the semi-final against Germany.
* 10 youth international appearances.

* A product of the Manchester United youth system like younger brother Phil, Gary Neville took the step up to the first team on 29th February 1993. A few months earlier in January of 1993 he made his first team debut in the U.E.F.A. Cup game against Torpedo Mosow. 
* Gary made his league debut on 7th May 1994 in a game against Coventry although  it wasn't until the 94-95 season that he was selected with more regularity by Alex Ferguson, his discoverer and chief admirer.
* Gary really confirmed himself as a first teamer in a Cup tie against Crystal Palace with a performance proving decisive in getting United through to the next round. He had the honour of playing in the 1995 F.A. Cup final after having played in just 18 league games. United's defeat at the hands of Everton however spoilt the big day. 
* Gary Neville proved to be one of the revelations of the 95-96 campaign helping United to the league and F.A. Cup double. Gary also made himself a member of the starting line up for the national side for the European Championship in England under the guidance of Terry Venables.
*  It had been 30 years since two brothers teamed up together in the England national squad but that run was ended when Gary formed part of the squad together with brother Phil. The last pair to enjoy that experience were the Charlton brothers Bobby and Jackie. 
* In September 1996 Gary renewed his contract with Manchester United for another five seasons. . 
* Gary scored his first goal in the league on 5th May 1997 in a game against Middlesbrough at Old Trafford.

* Last time around Gary Neville was a starter in 30 of the 31 league games in which he  appeared. At the start of the season he nonetheless saw himself out of the side, replaced by brother Phil. He won his first team place back from the third game of the season against Blackburn Rovers managing to retain it until the end of the season. In May against Middlesbrough, Gary scored his first goal as a professional. It was a goal which virtually assured Old Trafford the title - a fine way for Gary Neville to celebrate the renewal of his contract which ties him up for another five years with Manchester United.

53.name: Irwin
pages: * Denis Irwin is one of the figureheads of the greatest Manchester United sides of recent years and has been a key man in all the club's triumphs during the 1990's."Red Devils" manager Alex Ferguson has a special affection for the Irishman who impressed him while playing for Oldham Athletic. Irwin is a player who is appreciated and respected both by his teammates and the Old Trafford fans who have enjoyed watching him now for a number of years. A hard worker with tremendous discipline the quiet man of the side has won the respect of everybod both out on the pitch and back in the dressing room. With a fantastic honours list against his name and having past his thirtieth birthday, a triumph in the European Cup Cup would do nicely to round off a superb career.

* Denis Irwin is a full back who can do equally as good a job on either flank. Despite the fact he's right footed he has now played hundreds of games at left back. Blessed with good stamina he is also a lot quicker than he might first appear. He does his job at the back with composure and takes part confidently in the side's attacks. Possessing an exellent touch on the ball, he is an accurate passer and stands out above others at free kicks due to the power of his right foot. Although he can take corners and penalties expertly perhaps his greatest asset is his calmness and the confidence he has in his own ability, something which is evident in his play, especially when finding himself under pressure.

* European Cup Winners Cup winners medal 91.
* European Super Cup winners medal 91.
* League Championship winners medal 93, 94, 96 and 97.
* F.A. Cup winners medals  94 and 96.
* League Cup winners medal 92.
* Charity Shield medals, 90, 93, 96 and 97.

* 45 full international appearances for the Republic Ireland with 1 goal to his credit Denis Irwin made his debut on 12th September 1990 in a game against Morroco in Dublin (1-0). A member of Ireland's squad for the 1994 World Cup Finals in the United States he was a member of the starting line up in the first two Irish games - against Italy (1-0) and against Mexico (1-2).
* One "B" international appearance.
* One under 23 international appearance.
* Three under-21 international appearances.
* A schoolboy and youth international.

* Denis left his native Ireland in March of 1982 to become an apprentice with Leeds United. He signed his first professional contract on 3rd November 1983 and went on to make his debut at Elland Road on 21st January 1984 against Fulham. 
* Although he soon won himself a place in the first team during the 85-86 season he lost it to Neil Aspin becoming a free agent at the end of the season. He later moved to Oldham Athletic who he signed for on 22nd May 1996. At Oldham Denis was to replace the veteran Willie Donachie as the club's number one right back. In his first season there Oldham won promotion to the First Division and a place in the League Cup final eventually losing to Nottingham Forest. The club also qualified for the F.A. Cup semi finals where they  lost after two dramatic games against Manchester United. Alex Ferguson had been highly impressed with the Irishman's performance. 
* On 20th June 1990 Denis Irwin was transfered to Manchester United for £625,000 making  his debut on 25th August of that same year in a game against Coventry City. 
* Alex Ferguson quickly game Denis a place in the side and in his first season with the "Red Devils" he lined up to play in the League Cup final against Sheffield Wednesday. United lost 1-0. Just a few months later he got a taste of glory in the European Cup Winners Cup final against Barcelona. Ferguson's side ran out winners by two goals to one, both goals coming from Mark Hughes. 
* That same year - 1991- Irwin made his debut for the Republic of Ireland.
* The first time he returned to play at Boundary Park in a Manchester United shirt Denis scored twice against his ex-club Oldham Athletic who were eventually beaten 3-6. 
* During the 94-95 season he scored two spectacular goals in the F.A. Cup against Wrexham and Crystal Palace.

* During the course of last season Denis Irwin made 31 league appearances, all of those except 2 coming as a member of the starting line up. His start to the season couldn't have been more spectacular, finding the back of the net in the first game against Wimbledon. He wasn't however, to score again all season. Nevertheless, he remained a regular in Alex Ferguson's side with only injuries preventing him from taking his place. One of his absences coincided with Manchester United's defeat against Juventus in the Champions' League.

54.name: Pallister
pages: * For several seasons Gary Pallister has formed a partnership with Steve Bruce at the heart of the defence. Their understanding at the back reached the point of near perfection, with one another knowing each other's strengths and weaknesses complementing each another perfectly, winning titles and getting more than just the occasional taste of glory. Following the departure of Bruce the Manchester United fans asked who would partner Pallister in the United defence. The Norwegian Johnsen last season proved himself to be a serious candidate for the position, both players giving the side a fine defensive platform upon which to build. The 1997-98 season may see this new partnership really establish itself especially if Gary Pallister can steer clear of injury.

* Gary Pallister is a central defender who stands out for his physical strength, his forceful  marking, ability to read the game and his dominance in the air. Technically limited he sometimes has problems bringing the ball out at the backwhen he is put under pressure by opponents. His sheer size and build can cause him to struggle when he comes up against quick, skillful strikers. He can prove extremely dangerous when moving forward to support the attack at corners and free kicks and to get in headers on goal. He cleverly manages to pace himself throughout the match able to keep his efforst going hard for the full 90 minutes.

* European Cup Winners Cup winners medal 91.
* Euroepan Super Cup winners medal 91.
* League Championship winners medals 93, 94, 96 and 97.
* F.A. Cup winners medals  90,94 and 96.
* League Cup winners medal 92.
* Charity Shield medal  90, 93, 94 and 97.
* Professional Footballers Association "Player of the Year", 1992.

* 22 full international appearances for England. He made his debut on 27th April 1988 against Hungary (0-0) in Budapest.
* 10 "B" international appearances.

* Gary Pallister began his career with modest Billingham of the Northern Premier League where he put together some outstanding peformances. Having attracted the attention of  Middlesbrough he eventually joined the club on the 7th of November 1984. He had to wait  until 17th August 1985 to make his debut against Wimbledon who won the game 3-0. 
* On 18th October 1985 he was loaned out to Darlington where he played in onlyt seven league games. That season Middlesbrough were relegated, although during the 1986-87 season they managed to win promotion, due, among other things, to the fine performances of  Gary Pallister. His contribution once again proved to be fundamental during the 87-88 season when the club managed to win promotion to the First Division.
* On 29th August 1989 he signed for Manchester United for £2,300,000. His transfer fee was, for a long time, a record for a defender in the English game. 
* An international since 1988 Pallister has enjoyed by far the best and most succesful period of his career as a Manchester United player. He has been chosen as the club's player of the year on several occasions, and in 1992 was honoured by his fellow professionals as  P.F.A Player of the year.
* Up to the end of the 94-95 season he had been booked 13 times in his career and had scored five own goals. 
* For a number of years he formed a solid central defensive partnership with Steve Bruce. In the 95-96 season he suffered a back injury preventing him from playing regularly and kept him out of the 1996 European Championships in England. At the end of the season, Steve Bruce, his defensive colleague for so many seasons, left United to join Birmingham City.

* For the second succesive season injuries prevented Pallister from enjoying the continuity that he would no doubt have liked. He began the season as a first team regular but  a knee injury followed by a recurrence of his back problems put him out of the side halfway through October. More injury problems came along during September. In  December however he managed to get back into the action and, more importantly, was back in good form ready for the decisive second half of the season. He scored twice against Liverpool at Anfield and once against Southampton at Old Trafford before adding another league title triumph to his own personal roll of honour.

55.name: Nevland
pages: * Following in the footsteps of his countryman Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, Erik Nevland arrived at  Manchester United ihoping to start off a brilliant career with one of English football's big clubs. The Norwegian striker will have to fight for a place in the side with Andy Cole, Paul Scholes and Solskjaer himself. Initially it would seem that he is not likely to be given too many opportunitues, but with youth on his side he will get the chance to learn plenty from some of the biggest names in the Premier League - something which could prove to be a great help in what looks to be a bright future ahead of him.

* Erik Nevland is a classical centre forward with a genuine goalscoring instinct. A player of great mobility, he enjoys pulling out wide to open up gaps to allow midfielders to come through. He makes the most of his speed as well as his change of pace to get in front of rival defenders. He is good in the air and strikes a ball well with either foot. Still very young, he still makes the mistakes expected of a player of his limited experience.
x

* Two under-21 international appearances for Norway.
* Three under-20 international appearances.

* Whilst still a player with Viking Stavanger he arrived in Manchester in 1997 for a trial with United. Erik impressed  Alex Ferguson by scoring several hat tricks in various practice matches. Before being able to join the English club nevertheless he had to return to Norway to complete his national service. 
* He has been a Manchester United player since 30th May 1997.
* "I've got a lot to learn, and believe it will take me a couple of years to get into the first team," stated Erik on finalizing his transfer..
* He was unable to make himself a first team regular in the side at Norwegian club Viking Stavanger. He did an excellent job nevertheless whenever his presence was required out on the park.

56.name: Sheringham
pages: * Teddy Sheringham arrived at Old Trafford with a huge responsibility on his shoulders: the task of replacing Eric Cantona, Manchester United's charismatic flagbearer of the last few successful seasons. It seems unlikely that Teddy will manage to achieve the same level of adoration that Cantona inspired, but that won't worry him too much. In fact quite the opposite is likely to be the case with Sheringham being one of those players who is more than capable of going through a game unnoticed until he produces just one touch of brilliance which is often enough to decide the outcome of a match. With United he will be out to put some honours into his trophy cabinet and on the way win himself a place in the squad for the 1998 World Cup finals in France in which England will no doubt be out to reach for the very top.

* 'Teddy' Sheringham is a natural born striker whose main asset is his ability to surprise defenders. He stands out not just for his skill or for his speed but for his positional play which allows him to get away from defenders giving him the time and the space to get in efforts on goal. An intelligent player and an excellent header of the ball, he is a real source of danger for the opposition at dead ball situations. Despite not being a spectacular player, he is extremely effective. Physically strong he battles away constantly with rival defenders. He is a very dangerous player when he appears at the far post, losing defenders with a quick dip of the shoulders, slipping away into space where he can have a go at goal without being closed down quickly by opponents. Right footed and technically sound, he is not a genuine star but would be a vital member of any side.
* Second Division championship winners medal 87-88.

* 28 full international appearances for England, with 8 goals to his credit he made his debut on 29th May 1993 in a qualifying game for the 1994 World Cup Finals in the United States against Poland  in Chorzow (1-1). He scored his first goal for the national side on 8th June 1995 in a friendly against Sweden at Elland Road,  Leeds (3-3). He was a member of the England squad for the 1996 European Championships in England. He was also a member of the starting line up in all five of the side's games. 
* One under 21 international appearance. 
* Eleven appearances as a youth international, scoring five times.

* Teddy Sheringham's career statistics include 9 hat tricks, a figure which places him amongst the top strikers in England. His first hat trick came on 13th December 1986 against Huddersfield Town while his most recent came against Newcastle United on 3rd December 1994. 
* As an apprentice at Millwall he signed professional on 19th January 1984 although he had already made his league debut four days earler against Brentford. 
* On 1st February 1985 he was sent out on loan to Aldershot although he barely made an   appearance for the club. 
* Back at Millwall he teamed up with Irishman Tony Cascarino to form a fine partnership in attack. 
* On 23rd July 1991 he was transfered to Nottingham Forest for £2,000,000 and on his debut at  the City Ground scored a superb goal. 
* On 28th August 1992 he was transfered to Tottenham Hotspur for £2.100,000. Two years later he found himself playing up front alongside the German Jurgen Klinsmann. On 27th June 1997 he moved to Old Trafford for £3,500,000 as a replacement for Frenchman Eric Cantona, who, just a few weeks earlier, had announced his retirement from professional football.

* Teddy Sheringham was Tottenham Hotspur's top scorer with 7 goals in 29 league games. The team however had a disappointing season in which Sheringham was one of the few men to stand out. He set up plenty of goalscoring chances for his teammates but sorely missed the presence in the side of an out and out goalscorer such as the injured Chris Armstrong. In every game Sheringham played he showed himself to be an intelligent footballer, a quality which has certainly won the faith of Glenn Hoddle the new England manager having Sheringham's name down as one of the first in his squad. Teddy responded to the confidence he was shown with good performances and goals, managing to score in three consecutive international games.

57.name: Solskjaer
pages: * When Ole Solskjaer arrived at Manchester United, everybody, including  Alex Ferguson, considered him to be one for the future, a player who would need plenty of time before becoming a success in the Premier League. On his first appearance at Old Trafford however he made such an impact that even Ferguson decided he was the man he was looking for. The Scandanavian striker proved himself to be an extraordinary footballer, beneath his boyish appearance. If he can stay clear of injury Solskjaer could well go on to really prove his ability in the 1998 World Cup Finals in France.

* He can play either as a striker, tucked in behind the two main strikers, or even out wide preferably on the right. He is a very quick player and when he has space in front of him to run into is extremely dangerous. He can cross the ball in well with his right foot and when he gets into his stride he is well capable of outstripping most defenders. He is also adept at finding space to get in shots on goal, never needing to be asked twice when he gets an opportunity. Given his age however, he is still very fragile physically, often having problems when he comes up against strong, physical defenders. Nevertheless, he is undoubtedly a class player with a great future ahead of  him.

* League Championship winners medal 1997. 
* Charity Shield medal 97.

* 11 full international appearances for Norway with 5 goals to his credit. He made his debut on 26th November 1995 in a game against Jamaica.
* 19 Under-21 international appearances, scoring 13 times.

* He began his professional career with Clausenengen of Kristinasund in the Norwegian Second Division in which he scored plenty of goals and attracted attention as a genuine prospect. 
* He signed for First Division club Molde and immediately established himself as one of Norway's best players, forcing his way into the Norwegian side. In June 1996 he scored an extraordinary volley against Azerbaijan, after first controlling the ball on his chest. 
* His ex-coach Aage Hareide, who once played for Manchester City, announced some time ago that Solskjaer would go on to become a big name .
* In the summer of 1996 he was transfered to Manchester United for £1,500,000. At Old Trafford he teamed up with his compatriot Ronny Johnsen, a central defender who had recently arrived at the club from Turkish club Besitkas.
* He made his Premier League debut on 25th August 1996 in a game against Blackburn Rovers at Old Trafford (2-2). Solskjaer came on as a substitute in place of  David May in the 61st minute. Seven minutes later he scored his first goal in a United shirt, pulling the Red Devils back from 2-1 down, to 2-2 concluding the match.

* Ole Solskjaer proved to be one of the more pleasant surprises of last season. His breakthrough into the Premier League couldn't have been more spectacular scoring against Blackburn just seven minutes after coming on as a substitute for David May at Old Trafford. Slowly but surely he made himself a first team regular and went on to end the season as the club's top scorer with 18 league goals. He also had an outstanding run in the Champion's League making 10 appearances. It was a fantastic season for him, rounded off by winning his first league title.

58.name: Jordi Cruyff
pages: * Jordi Cruyff's first season at Old Trafford proved to be a particularly tough one for him. Facing up to a serious knee injury, problems in adpating to the English game, as well as the inevitable comparisons with his famous father, the great Johan Cruyff the media were constantly hinting at his imminent return to a Spanish club. However, as Jordi himself has pointed out, he always enjoyed the support of two of the most charismatic characters in the history of Manchester United: Alex Ferguson and Eric Cantona. Although the Frenchman is no longer at the club, Cruyff will no doubt be out to repay all the faith that has been shown in him.

* In a lot of games, Jordi has played as his side's furthest man forward, although maybe he is best thought of as a player who will play behind the two main strikers, rather than as an out and out striker himself. Playing in behind the strikers he can make best use of his qualities, such as his pace coming from slightly deeper, his change of direction and the good shot he possesses in either foot. He often plays out wide from where he will either try and make progress down to the by-line, or cut inside to set up an attack from a more central position. He is also reasonably good in the air and possesses good vision. He is a skillful, elegant player, who is very clever in the final third of the field and one who has undeniable class. Despite not being physically powerful, some say being rather fragile, he has shown that he is capable of imposing his class and ability on defenders much stronger than himself.

* League Championship winners medal 97. 
* Charity Shield medal 97.

* 8 international apearances for Holland. He made his debut on 24th April 1996 against Germany in the De Kuip stadium Rotterdam. The Germans won 0-1 thanks to a Jurgen Klinsmann penalty. 
* He was a member of the Dutch squad for the 1996 European Championships in England. Cruyff played from the start in all four of Holland's games and managed once to find the target against Switzerland in the final phase. Holland eventually lost in the quarter finals against France.

* Jordi is the son of Johan Cruyff, one of the greatest players of all time, whose football delighted the whole world during the 1970's. with his father's credentials Jordi has often found himself in the spotlight for the wrong reasons, subjected to unfair criticism which in reality, was very often directed not at him but at his father, the ex-Barcelona manager.
* He started his career as a footballer in the famous youth system at Ajax of Amsterdam. He moved on to the youth ranks at Barcelona in 1988 when his father took charge of the Spanish giants. In April 1993 he formed part of the Catalan club's second string, Barcelona "B", in the Spanish Second Division.
* Due to his fragile physique he was forced to follow a strict diet and training routine in order to build him up to compete with more powerful defenders. 
* He ended the 93-94 season as the side's top scorer with the 12 goals together with team-mate Oscar, who scored seven from the penalty spot. Once the season was over, Johan Cruyff decided that his son should go on the clubs pre-season tour of Holland with the first team. Jordi, in the absence of Brazilian Romario, was Barcelona's top scorer in the summer's pre-season tournaments and kept his place as a member of the first team squad. 
* He made his Spanish First Division debut on 4th September 1994 against Sporting Gijon in the El Molinon stadium. Coming on in the 65th minute in place of Beguiristain he was unable to prevent Barcelona form going down 2-1.
* Jordi possesses dual Spanish-Dutch nationality which gave him the option of choosing which of the two countries he wished to play for. In April 1996 he decided to play for Holland despite the intentions of Javier Clemente - the Spanish national manager - of calling him up to the Spanish national squad. On 24th April 1996 he made his debut for the Dutch and, shortly afterwards was called up by manager Guus Hiddink to play in the 1996 European Championships in England. 
* His departure from Barcelona was preceeded by the sacking of his father as manager of the club just before the end of the 95-96 season. In the first game at the Nou Camp after Johan Cruyff's departure Jordi found the back of the net, later leaving the field to a tremendous ovation from the supporters which the player duly acknowledged in his fathers name. 
* Although his contract with Barcelona didn't expire until June 1997 the club declared that Jordi could leave in the summer of 1996. The player reiterated his desire to stay with the Catalans, but new manager Bobby Robson declared that Cruyff junior didn't form part of his plans. As it turned out, he was soon on his way to Manchester United for a fee of £1,400,000.
* He made his Premier League debut on 17th August 1996 in an away victory at Wimbledon (0-3). Four days later he scored his first goal in a United shirt against Everton at Old Trafford. 
* In his first season in England he wore his surname, Cruyf, on the back of his shirt. This time round however he has decided to change this for Jordi, his christian name.

* Jordi Cruyff's first steps in the Premier League were very promising, scoring twice in his first three games. A serious knee injury however kept him out of action for four months. When he finally worked his way back into the squad, his logical lack of adaptation to the English game was evident, although he always enjoyed the support of Aex Ferguson. He made a total of 16 league appearances, although he was only a member of the starting line up on 11 occasions.
