60.name: McClair
pages: * Brian McClair is an institution at Old Trafford. The Scot is now the club's veteran, and, although his appearances in the side are now more sporadic, he remains with the club as a player of great charisma. As a man who enjoys the full trust of manager Alex Ferguson his presence in the dressing room is more important than at first it might appear. Few people can pass on to the younger players the spirit needed to keep a club like United at the top. And, when he does get into the action he more than demonstrates his outstanding football skills and years of experience.

* Brian McClair is an outstanding and very versatile team player remaining an untiring worker. He scores goals regularly, almost always by surprising defenders on their blind side. He can play in a number of positions in midfield, but is at his best when he links up between the forward line and the midfield. Technically good, he reads the game well while being an accurate passer and striker of the ball. 
* A player who gives every game everything he's got, his hard work is appreciated by his teammates. He defends with tenacity and is always available in support of the attack while his vast experience at the highest level of competitio is  something which has given him plenty of know how and intelligence to apply in every game.

* Scottish League Championship winners medal 86. 
* Scottish Cup winners medal 85. 
* English League Championship winners medals 93, 94, 96 and 97.
* F.A. Cup winners medals  90 and 94. 
*  League Cup winners medal 92. 
*  European Cup Winners Cup winners medal 91. 
* Charity Shield medals  90, 94 and 97. 
* "Scottish Player of the year" 1991.

* 30 full international appearances for Scotland, with 2 goals to his credit. He made his debut in November 1986 against Luxembourg at Hampden Park.
* One "B" international appearance. 
* 8 under-21 international appearances.

* Although in July 1979 he joined Aston Villa as an apprentice, Brian McClair never got to play a first team game simply because the Birmingham  based club never offered him a professional contract. At 18 years of age he returned to his native Scotland and signed for Motherwell. He made his debut on 21st August 1981 in a game against Kilmarnock. 
* After two seasons he was transfered to Glasgow Celtic for £100,000. He signed for the then Celtic manager Billy McNeill on 1st July 1983, and in his first season at Celtic Park scored 23 goals in 35 league games. The titles and the full international debut were soon to follow. 
* In July 1986, Mark Hughes left Manchester United to move to Barcelona. One year later on 30th July the Old Trafford club signed Brian McClair for £850,000. On 15th August of that same year, he made his league debut in a match against Southampton. 
* In 1990 he won an F.A. Cup winners medal against Crystal Palace. The following year he was a member of United's losing side against Sheffield Wednesday in the League Cup final (0-1). Soon after nevertheless, he took part in the victorious European Cup Winners Cup  final against Barcelona (2-1).
* He has scored two hat tricks during his career, one of those against Derby County (4-1). 
* From 1995 onwards, he was no longer an automatic first team choice with United. Towards the end of the 95-96 season, there were constant rumours surrounding his imminent departure, but it was McClair himself who decided to stay at Old Trafford.

* For the first time in a lengthy playing career, Brian McClair ended last season without a goal to his name. However, the real story is that he was given only very limited opportunities, especially in the first part of the season. He made 19 league appearances but only on 4 occasions did he make the starting line up. Nevertheless, he demonstrated that his know how and experience can still prove to be useful to Manchester United, even though the goals might have dried up.

61.name: Butt
pages: * In a very short space of time Nicky Butt has convinced critics, supporters and manager Alex Ferguson that he was the ideal home made replacement for Paul Ince. A product of United's prodigious youth system this Manchester born lad has deservedly won himself a place in United's first team and has become one of the most outstanding members of the group of players known as "Fergies Babes". Together with Beckham, the Neville brothers and Ryan Giggs, Nicky is destined to become part of another era at Old Trafford, an era which promises to be another glorious one.

* Nicky Butt generally lines up as a defensive central midfield player, although he does possess the ability to get the team's attacks going from the back. He plays in front of the defence where he wins plenty of possession making the most of his stamina, bravery, determination and, if he needs it, agression. He keeps going throughout the ninety minutes, becoming a constant focal point for his teammates, who, through his own hard work, releives of some of their defensive duties. Once he has won possession he plays the ball around quickly and always makes himself available allowing the team to keep the ball and the game moving. He has good vision, although he doesn't pose much of a threat in the opposing penalty area, an aspect of his game he could try to improve.

* League Championship winners medal 96 and 97. 
* F.A. Cup winners medal 96. 
* Charity Shield medals 94 and 97. 
* F.A. Youth Cup winners medal 92.

* 2 full international appearances for England, he made his debut on 29th March 1997 in a friendly against Mexico at Wembley. 
* 7 Under-2 international appearances. 
* 7 youth international appearances.

* Born in Manchester, Nicky Butt began his career in the youth ranks at United. A fully qualified member of the "Fergie Babes" he made his first team debut on 21st November 1992 in a game against  Oldham. Nicky was 17 years old. He turned professional shortly afterwards on 29th January 1993.
* During the 94-95 season he appeared more regularly in the side. He scored his first goal in a United first team game on 31st December 1994 against Southamptonat The Dell (2-2). 
* When Paul Ince left Old Trafford to join Italian giants Inter Milan, many of the club's supporters protested against the departure of the England international midfielder who was one of the side's standard bearers. Alex Ferguson had full confidence in Nicky Butt's ability to replace him who responded to this confidence with some magnificent  performances quietening the critics. He scored his first goal of the 95-96 season against Liverpool, although that took very much second place since it came in the game that marked the return of Eric Cantona following his suspension for his infamous antics at Selhurst Park against Crystal Palace. 
* Captain of the England Under-21 side. 
* In september 1996 he renewed his contract with Manchester United for another five years.

* As was the case with the Neville brothers Nicky Butt renewed his contract with Manchester United for another five years. A few weeks earlier he had scored an outstanding goal against Newcastle United in the Charity Shield. At the end of the season he'd played in 26 league games, 24 of those as a member of the starting line up. He managed to hit the back of the net on five occasions, the best goals-tally of his short professional career. During the course of the season he suffered two injuries, the latter of which, a sprained ankle, causing him to miss six games. Once he had recovered however, he soon got back to his best form and was eventually named captain of the Under-21 side. He rounded off his extraordinary progress by making his debut, under the guidance of Glenn Hoddle, for the full England side.

62.name: Cole
pages: * Luck hasn't been on Andy Cole's side since his arrival at  Old Trafford from Newcastle United. This striker has suffered serious injuries, illnesses, poor form and problems in adapting to team play. This unfortunatley has prevented him from reproducing the form he showed at  St. James' Park. The competition for a place up front at United is getting more   intense all the time. Solskjaer, Scholes and Teddy Sheringham are all fighting with him for a place in the starting line up. Andy Cole will be hoping that the 1997-98 season will bring better luck. If it's with him, it won't be a surprise to see him lining up in the 1998 World Cup Finals in France.

* A centre forward with a real eye for a goal, Andy Cole is a fine striker, although last year he found that he needed to adjust his aim a little. Blessed with outstanding physical attributes, his change of pace over a short distance is spectacular. A right footed player he is always quick to get in shots on goal and is a specialist at getting on the blind side of defenders. He loses his markers quickly and opens up plenty of gaps for his teammates. His shooting is powerful and he is useful in the air. He is occasionally inconsistent however. He has very fragile confidence and seems to depend too much on good spells rather than consistent performances. Even so, he is an excellent striker who has all the qualities he needs to make himself, year after year, one of the top scorers in the Premier League.

* League Championship winners medals 96 and 97. 
* F.A. Cup winners medal 96. 
* "Young Player of the Year" 1994. 
* First Division winners medal 93.

* 2 full international apearances for England. 
* 2 "B" international appearances, scoring once. 
* 8 Under-21 international appearances, scoring three times.
* 20 youth international appearances, with six goals.

* Born in Nottingham into a Jamaican family. Since he was a young boy Andy Cole and sports have gone hand in hand. He became a real football fan towards the end of the 1970's when he regularly watched the great Nottingham Forest side which won the European Cup two years in succession. 
* When he was 14 years old he joined the FA School of Excellence at Lileshall later signing as an apprentice with Arsenal. Andy settled down with his sister Jackie close to his family in London. His brother Desmond also played football. 
*A professional since 18th October 1989 he made his debut for Arsenal on 29th December of that same year against Sheffield United. 
* Opportunities for the "Gunners" were fleeting so he was sent out on loan to London neighbours Fulham on 5th September 1991. Cole made a decisive contribution to the club helping them remain in the Third Division.
* On 12th March 1992 he was transfered to Bristol City for £500,000. There he suddenly began to score goals and, one year later, was very much a sought-after player. 
* Kevin Keegan became so interested in signing him that he even asked if he could borrow the Newcastle chairmain's private plane in order to go and watch Bristol City play. He was impressed by what he saw and, following a cup game against the Luton Town, Andy received the Magpies' offer while on his way back to the dressing room. 
* He became a Newcastle player on 12th March 1993. The transfer fee was set at £1,750,000.  Andy won a First Division winners medal, and as a result, was now in the Premier League. During the 93-94 season he was top scorer in the Championship with 34 goals, becoming one of the most popular players at St. James' Park. 
* His transfer to Manchester United on 12th January 1995 sparked a storm of controversy at Newcastle. The fee came to £7,000,000 and included the departure of Keith Gillespie from Old Trafford, valued at £1,000,000, moving to the Magpies as part of the deal. Keegan personally took responsibility for Cole's departure, a sale that was never really understood by a large section of the Newcastle supporters to whom Andy Cole was a hero. 
* He made his debut for the "Red Devils" on 22nd January 1995 in a 1-0 victory over  Blackburn Rovers at Old Trafford with Eric Cantona sole goal-scorer. On 27th February he scored his first goal for United against Aston Villa, also at  Old Trafford (1-0). 
* During the 95-96 season he shared the striker's position in the side with Paul Scholes.  Cole scored 11 goals in the league and 2 in the Cup.
* During his career he has scored 8 hat tricks. The first of those came on 25th August 1992 against Cardiff. Since then Barnsley, Leicester, Notts County (2), Liverpool, Coventry and Ipswich have all suffered from his goalscoring ability. Against Ipswich Town he didn't just settle for three goals but went on to hit the net five times on 4th March 1995. 
* During the 96-97 season he suffered a fracture of both tibias following a tackle by Neil Ruddock in a reserve game.

* During the pre-season there was a lot speculation surrounding his possible transfer to Blackburn Rovers to cover the gap left by Alan Shearer's departure to Newcastle United. Of the sides, Everton were said to be interested in signing him. Although pneumonia prevented him from playing in a number of games at the start of the season he finally decided to remain at Old Trafford. Justs beginning to get back his form injury struck again, and then, more bad luck followed when in a reserve game against  Liverpool at Anfield he was left with fractures to both tibias following a tackle from Neil Ruddock. He returned to the side in December beginning the new year with goals and good form, building up a good attacking partnership with the Norwegian Solskjaer. After so much frustrations, his hard work and effort was finally rewarded when he was called up to the England squad for "Le Tournoi" in France during the summer.

63.name: Keane
pages: * Roy Keane's commitment to Manchester United is total. The Irish midfielder is a genuine idol at Old Trafford. The fans appreciate his passion and undying will to win. He has the complete confidence of Alex Ferguson who considers him "the heart of the team". For that reason he will once again be an automatic first team choice during the 97-98 season as long as he steers clear of the ever present threat of injury which has kept him out in the past.

* A strong, hard running midfielder Roy Keane is also able to pass the ball well constantly making himself available to his teammates when they are looking for someone to keep the ball moving. Backed up by his powerful physique he wins an enormous amount of possesion and never hesitates to go in hard if he feels it to be necessary. His effectiveness though, is there to be seen in both penalty areas as he loves to break through from the midfield to get quickly forward into the attack letting fly with a powerful right foot shot. He is also more than competent in the air. 
* Above all, Roy Keane is a complete footballer. His versatility also allows him to play at right back, although it is in midfield where his all-action style of play really stands out. His only weak point lies in his volatile character, which occasionally sees him lose his head and become excessively physical.

* League Championship winners medals 94, 96 and 97.
* F.A. Cup winners medal 94 and 96.
* Charity Shield medals 93 and 97.
* Zenith Data Systems Cup winners medal 92.

* 36 full international appearances for Eire with one goal to his credit. He made his debut on 22nd May 1991 in friendly game against Chile in Dublin. He was a member of the Irish squad for the 1994 World Cup Finals in the United States. He was a member of the starting line up in the three games that Ireland played, against Italy, Mexico and Norway.
* One "B" international appearances.
* Four Under-21 international appearances.
* Youth and Schoolboy international appearances.

* Born in the Republic of Ireland, it was here in his native country where Roy Keane began his football career. He was playing for Cobh Ramblers when Nottingham Forest signed him on 12th June 1990 for £10,000. 
* Brian Clough - Forest's manager - gave him his debut on 28th August that same year against no less a side than Liverpool, then reigning champions. In his first season at the City Ground he played in 35 league games, made his debut for  the Irish national side and played in the F.A. Cup final against Tottenham Hotspur although Forest lost 1-2. 
* During the 91-92 campaign, the side reached 2 finals: they beat Southampton 3-2 in the final of the Zenith Data Systems Cup but lost to Manchester United in the League Cup final. Previously, a goal by Keane against  "Spurs" in extra-time of the game at White Hart Lane had taken Forest to Wembley.
* On the 22nd July 1993 he was sold to Manchester United for £3,750,000.  He made his debut for the "Red Devils" on 15th August away at Norwich City,  United winning by two goals to nil. Three days later Keane made his first appearance at Old Trafford and scored his first goal for United against Sheffield United (3-0). 
* During the 94-95 season, he suffered a serious injury in a Cup game against Crystal Palace, although his amazing powers of recovery helped him back into action before the end of the season. 
* He has one of the worst disciplinary records in the Premier League. Up to the end of the 94-95 season he was booked 35 times and sent off once, a record that places him firmly among the top ten in the list of Premier League  "Bad Boys". 
* Peter Reid, manager of Sunderland stated that Roy Keane was the best midfielder player in England after the Irishman's sensational performance against Reid's own side. 
* After the 1996 F.A. Cup final when Manchester United beat Liverpool 1-0 Keane was voted "Man of the Match". With that cup final win, United clinched the second league and cup double in the club's history. 
* On the 22nd August 1996 the Irishman extended his contract with Manchester United for another four years at a moment when Barcelona were taking an interest in him. Just a few days earlier Keane had undergone surgery on a knee injury .

* Roy Keane kicked off last season by extending his contract with Manchester United for another four seasons. As a result he put an end to the rumours suggesting an imminent move to Barcelona, a signing apparently personally requested by the then Barcelona manager Bobby Robson. During the first half of the season he suffered several different injuries including one to his knee. As a result he was unable to get the continuity he needed to show-off his best form. Fortunately, he recovered in time to make a vital contribution to his and the club's third league title triumph in four years.

64.name: Giggs
pages: * The appearance of Ryan Giggs among the elite of English football was in many ways the first recognition of Alex Ferguson's work at Manchester United. It was, in fact, Ferguson himself who showed all the confidence in the world in Giggs and gave him the opportunity to make his debut at the tender age of 17. Since then, everything has happened very quickly in the life of the young Welshman, chosen "Young Player of the Year" in England for two consecutive seasons, an automatic choice for his country while still very young and elevated to hero worship status by the Old Trafford fans. Last season Ryan took another step up with an outstanding performances against Oporto in the Champions' League. He is now being compared to George Best; not a bad comparison at all for one of the most exciting players in the Premier League.

* Ryan Giggs is an outstanding left winger. He generally likes to pick the ball up in the midfield area to go at defenders at speed, backed up by superb pace and technique, usually reaching either the by-line or the opponents' penalty area. Although he is very much a left footed player, hardly using his right, he possesses genuine quality. His change of direction when in full flights renders him a very difficult man to stop as he dummies to go one way past a defender but then zips past on the other side, demonstrating an array of faints and tricks, his speed simply finishing the job off.
* With space to go at in front of him, Giggs can often prove to be the difference between the two sides. He possesses good shooting ability, always with his left foot, is an accurate passer of the ball, and also takes free kicks and corners. He has occasionally played down the right but has always proven more effective on the left. Nevertheless, there is no doubt that with all the technical quality he possesses, Ryan Giggs is an outstanding footballer.

* League Championships winners medals 93, 94, 96 and 97. 
* F.A. Cup winners medals  94 and 96. 
* League Cup winnes medal 92. 
* Charity Shield medals  93, 94 and 97. 
* European Super Cup winners medal 91. 
* F.A. Youth Cup winners medal  92. 
* "Young Player of the Year" in 1992 and 1993. 
* "Trofeo Bravo" as the best under 21 in Europe , 1991.

* 20 full international appearancs for Wales, with four goals against his name. He made his debut on 16th October 1991 in a game against Germany. Ryan Giggs was just 17 years and 332 days old, making him the youngest player ever to play for the Welsh national side. 
* One Under-21 international appearance.

* The son of Brian Wilson, an ex-international rugby player, Ryan adopted his mother's surname following his parents' separation. In fact, as a youngster he played in an England juniors' side under the name of Ryan Wilson, although as a mark of respect to his mother, he decided to play for Wales as Ryan Giggs. 
* At eleven years of age, Ryan was playing for the team at Salford College. Dennis Schofield, a scout for Manchester City took him along to Maine Road where spent three years at City. Nobody seemed to notice him.  Alex Ferguson was suitably impressed by the quality that Giggs showed. That afternoon was the change young Ryan's life compeltely. 
* He became part of the Old Trafford youth set up in February 1988, before graduating as a "trainee" in July 1990. On 1st December that same year he turned professional and went on to make his first team debut on 2nd March 1991 at Old Trafford as a substitute against Everton. Giggs was then 17 years and three months old but was unable to break Duncan Edwards' record as the youngest ever player to play for Manchester United at 16 years 182 days old.
* 1991was the year Ryan Giggs broke through into the forefront of English football. In October he made his debut for the Welsh national side becoming the youngest player ever to play for Wales. He was chosen "Young Player of the Year" in 1992 by the Professional Footballers Association, and honour which came his way again in 1993. On top of this the prestigious Italian magazine "Guerin Sportivo" named him as the best player in Europe, under 21 years of age. 
* The influence of Alex Ferguson in Giggs' career has been fundamental in the  player's development. Under Ferguson's careful guidance, the young Welshman slowly but surely developed his game and matured as a person until he became a regular member of the side in the 91-92 season. 
* In October 1996 he extended  his contract with Manchester United for another five years.

* Ryan Giggs had his most outstanding moment of last season against Oporto in the quarter finals of the Champions league. At Old Trafford, against the Portuguese champions, Giggs gave an authentic exhibition which was compared to George Best's famous performance against Benfica in 1976. The contribution made by Giggs, who in October extended his contract with Manchester United, was fundamental in United clinching the title, especially in the second half of the season, when he was able to put together an unbroken run of appearances without injuries.

65.name: May
pages: * During the course of last season Manchester United searched high and low for a central defender. There was talk of the imminent arrival at the club of the Spanish pair Miguel Angel Nadal and Roberto Rios, but negotiations with  their respective clubs eventually came to nothing . Finally Alex Ferguson went in for the Swede Henning Berg from Blackburn Rovers. His arrival could have a big influence on David May's future at  Old Trafford. Both players were teammates at Ewood Park, but now they will be fighting tooth and nail to get into Alex Ferguson's side.

* In recent season it has become a common sight to see David May linning up as a central defender although his natural position is right back. May is a quick, strong, hard running footballer, who shows versatility. His one down-side is his frequency not to move forward to support the attack as often as perhaps he should. Excellent in the air, he needs to improve his touch on the ball in order to be able to bring it out from the back and lay it off more accurately. Perhaps his greatest asset is his positional play, getting back to cover quickly and seldom allowing forwards to get in front of him to gain an advantage. His contribution to the attack is limited to the occasions when he moves forward for set pieces, where his ability in the air should really see him scoring more goals each season.

* League Championship winners medals 96 and 97.
* F.A. Cup winnes medal  96.
*Charity Shield medals 94 and 97.
x

* He took his first steps in football playing for Blackburn Rovers' schoolboy team. He arrived at Blackburn in October 1984 and, after coming through the youth ranks, eventually signed professional on 16th  June 1988 once he had finished his education. His debut took place on 1st April 1989 in a game against Swindon. 
* At the beginning of the 89-90 season he put together a fine series of performances which was eventually and unfrotunately interrupted by injury. Once he had recovered from his injury problems however he returned to win back his place from Andy Hill going on to play in 18 of the last 19 games of the season. 
* In October 1991 he could only watch as he lost his first team place to Kevin Moran. May played in just two games up to the end of the season.
* On 1st July 1994 he was transfered to Manchester United for £1,400,000. He began the season playing as a replacement for Paul Parker, who had been playing right back, although he did get a few opportunities to play in his favourite central defensive position. At the end of his first seasosn at Old Trafford he suffered another injury. 
* The absences of Bruce and Pallister allowed him to play in 16 games during the 95-96 season, all of those appearances coming at the heart of the defence.

* David May played in a total of 29 games last time out, playing from the start in 28 of those. His scored three goals in the Premier League plus another in the Champions League against Oporto in what was probably the performance of the season by Alex Ferguson's men. He had the misfortune however to in advertantly grab the headlines for the wrong reasons against Turkish club Fenerbahce when the ball rebounded off him into the back of his own net thus robbing United of their proud record of having remained unbeaten at Old Trafford during 40 years of European competition. Despite that hiccup he had a very positive season adding another title to his personal role of honour and being called up to the England squad by Glenn Hoddle for a friendly - in which he didn't play - against Mexico.

66.name: Scholes
pages: * On more than one occasion Alex Ferguson has made it quite clear how highly he rates "The Ginger Prince".  For many Paul Scholes is the successor to the legendary Kenny Dalglish. Obviously, the young United player still has a long way to go to reach the dizzy heights that Liverpool's famous Scotsman did, but there is no doubt that the tributes that have come his way have been a real boost. For the moment he has managed to make his debut for the full England side, and if he maintains his progress he will no doubt be one of the chosen few for the 1998 World Cup Finals in France.

* Paul Scholes is a goalscoring forward who stands out for the intense level of performance he maintains throughout the 90 minutes. A quick player with the ability to beat men, he has a powerful shot from distance, is reasonably good in the air and, when he finds himself in the area, doesn't need telling twice to have a go at goal. He keeps opposition defenders under constant pressure, closing them down and showing good controlled aggression, doing an effective job as the team's first line of defence. 
*  He can also play as a midfielder, where his appetite for hard work is a great source  of support for his midfield colleagues. Still very young he has plenty of time, as well as ability, to go on to become one of the best goalscorers in England.

* League Championship winners medals 96 and 97.
*F.A. Cup winners medal 96. 
* Charity Shield medal  97.

* 3 full international appearances for England, scoring once.
* England youth international.

* Paul Scholes is yet another product of Manchester United's prolific youth system. He took the inital step up to the first team in January 1993. He didn't get to make his debut however until 24th September 1994 in an away game at Ipswich Town. Although the Red Devils were beaten 3-2 Paul gave a glimpse of his goalscoring instinct by scoring the side's second goal.
* Andy Cole's arrival at Old Trafford however was to signify a dip in Scholes' contribution to Manchester United's progress. 
* In the 95-96 season Paul proved to be decisive in getting United to the F.A. Cup Final - which they won - when he scored the goal against Sunderlandkeeping United in the competition. Scholes went on to play just a few minutes at Wembley coming on for Andy Cole. 
* Alex Ferguson once said of Scholes : "You only see a player like him once in your life".

* It didn't prove to be easy for Paul Scholes to force his way into the side and, in fact, although he started the first league game of the season, he didn't appear from the start of a game again until the end of October. He went on to find his best form of the season however during the months of December and January when he scored several important goals both in the Premier league and in the Cup. In February he was forced to undergo a cartilage operation, but, once recovered came back to show more excellent form. He was called up for "Le Tournoi" competition in the summer of 1997 by England and managed to find the back of the net with a superb goal against Italy.

67.name: Beckham
pages: * David Beckham is already one of the best footballers in Europe. The Manchester United midfielder possesses outstanding talent as he has more than demonstrated in recent seasons. He scores outstanding goals, is able to beat men in almost impossible situations and seems to stamp his class on everything he does. Now an automatic choice both for club and country David sets out on the 1997-98 season with his eyes very much set on the 1998 World Cup Finals in France where he could undoubtedly become one of the stars of the tournament.

* David Beckham is a genuine class midfielder, possessing superb technique and great vision. He is an accurate passer of the ball and packs a powerful shot. He generally plays tight on the right touchline where he can make the most of his speed and ability to beat men, and deliver dangerous crosses into the area. He can also play as a midfield organizer distributing the ball thoughfully, showing himself capable of dictating the pace of the game. Beckham is a player of real talent and surprising maturity, a maturiry which is backed up by the confidence he shows when he has the ball at his feet. He is also a free kick specialist, a situation where his superb technique is clearly on show. He can also score goals from distance and is useful with his head. A young but complete player, his progress seems to be unstoppable, destined as he apparently is, to become a real star.

* League Championship winner medals 96 and 97. 
* F.A. Cup winners medal  96. 
* Charity Shield medal 97.
* F.A. Youth Cup winners medal  92. 
* Voted "Young Player of the Year" 1997.

* 9 full international appearances for England. He made his debut in September 1996 against Moldova (0-3).
* 9 Under-21 international appearances.
* 4 Youth international appearances.

* One of the key members of the generation of players known as "Fergie's Babes", David Beckham won a competition for schoolboys organized by Bobby Charlton in the mid-1980's. As a prize he took part in a trip to Barcelona, where he met Terry Venables, then manager of the Catalan club. 
* Born and bred in London, but a boyhood Manchester United supporter he rejected an offer from Tottenham to join their youth set upas he wanted to play for the Old Trafford club. He finally got to play for United's youth sides standing out in the teams that won the F.A. Youth Cup twice. Even before winning his second F.A. Youth Cup title however, he had already turned professional, doing so on 29th January 1993. 
* On 28th February 1995 he went out on loan for three months to Preston North End, where he made his debut in the league on 4th March in a game against Doncaster Rovers. 
* Once back at Old Trafford, Alex Ferguson was suitably impressed by the progress Beckham had made, and, as a result of the injuries and suspensions at the club, Beckham got the opportunity to make his first team debut at Old Trafford on  2nd April 1995 against Leeds United (0-0). During that same season, he scored an outstanding goal against Turkish club Galatasaray in the Champions League. The fact that he was English helped him to get into the team for European competitions. 
* It was during the 95-96 season when Beckham finally settled down in the first team at United, covering the gap left by Andrei Kanchelskis following the Russian's departure to Everton. He played in 33 league games and  7 cup games, scoring a total of 8 goals between both competitions. Particularly important was the goal he scored against Chelsea in the F.A. Cup semi-finals which took United through to the final at Wembley, which they also went on to win. 
* Although he was never included in the England squad under Terry Venables, Glenn Hoddle had no hesitation in naming him in his first squad as England manager. England, with Beckham in the side, defeated Moldova away (0-3).
* He scored the goal of the season for 96-97: an extraordinary shot from his own half against Wimbledon.

* Without any doubt David Beckham last season proved to be not just one of the best players in England but in the whole of Europe.This was recognised by his fellow professionals in England who named him as "Young Player of the Year" 1997. David began his league campaign by scoring an incredible goal - possibly the best of the season - against Wimbledon in the opening game: He picked the ball up in his own half, looked up to see the keeper off his line, and connected with an accurate shot which flew over a startled goalkeeper before nestling in the back of the net. A few days earlier he had scored another extraordinary goal against Newcastle in the Charity Shield.  As a result he was voted "Player of the Month" for August. His great performances and extraordinary progress didn't go unnoticed by Glenn Hoddle, who promoted him to the full England side.

69.name: James
pages: * In March 1997 David James made history when he became the first black goalkeeper to play for the full England side. David celebrated the occasion by keeping a clean sheet. At Liverpool he has the full backing of manager of Roy Evans and not even a series of well publicised mistakes towards the end of last season caused the Red's boss to think twice about James' position as first choice in goal for the Anfield club, although he will be expected to get back to his best for the 97-98 season. Maybe then he will start thinking about the 1998 World Cup Finals in France.

* David James is a goalkeeper whose mere presence intimidates opposing forwards due to his amazing stature and physique. Something of an extroverted personality, though not to the extent of his predecessor Bruce Grobbelaar, James is slowly but surely becoming one of the side's most charismatic players. When he is playing well, he spreads a real sense of security, a fundamental quality in a goalkeeper. Agile and athletic, he still alternates all too often between spectacular saves and basic mistakes that he should really be trying to eliminate from his game. His outstanding physique and his ability to outjump opponents allows him to come off his line with confidence and make this an aspect of his game in which he is generally quite secure. That security will be fundamental if Liverpool are to bring the glory days back to Anfield.

* League Cup winners medal  94-95. 
* F.A. Youth Cup winners medal 88-89.

* One full international apperance for England. James made his debut on 29th March 1997 in a friendly game against Mexico at Wembley (2-0). 
* He has made 1 "B" international appearance.He came on as a substitute for Kevin Pressman in a game against Eire in December 1994. 
* 10 under-21 international appearances.

* James made his debut for Watford on 25th August 1990 against Millwall. 
* For a transfer fee of £1,000,000 he moved from Watford to Liverpool. 
* He arrived at Liverpool as the successor to the controversial Bruce Grobbelaar.
* Up to the end of the 94-95 season James had kept a clean sheet in 55 league games. Up to that stage of his career he had an average on 1.86 goals against per game.
* He has only been sent off once in the whole of his playing career. 
* He was included in the Premier League's ideal team, by his fellow professionals, for the 95-96 season.
* In March 1997 James became the first black goalkeeper to play for the full England side. His full international debut came at Wembley in a friendly game against Mexico.

* David James was Liverpool's first choice goalkeeper, throughout the whole of the 96-97 season. He played in all 38 league games although his form was on the inconsistent side. He put together a great run of performances during the first half of the season, making some outstanding saves. He impressed Glenn Hoddle who in March gave him his full international debut in a friendly agsainst Mexico. David responded by keeping his goal intact.. 
* During the run in to the season however, he had a series of poor games, heavily criticised for some of the goals he conceded, especially against Coventry and  Manchester United, goals which eventually saw the title slip away from Anfield. He was also especially unfortunate in the European Cup winners Cup semi-final first leg, away, against Paris St. Germain. Liverpool lost the game 3-0, burying almost all hope of reaching the final.

70.name: Warner
pages: * Born in Liverpool and a product of the Anfield youth system, Anthony Warner has the privilige of playing for his home town club. He is yet to get the opportunities he needs to be able to show his true ability as a goalkeeper. For the moment he will have to settle for trying to learn everthing he can from David James, who he seems unlikely to dislodge from side during the 97-98 season.

* In the few games in which he's played Warner has shown himself to be a quick and agile goalkeeper. Although he possesses a slightly less imposing physique than James he demonstrates his outstanding athleticism when called into the action. It remains to be seen how he develops and progresses before the clubs can decide just how good he is. His youth should give him the patience he needs to show while he waits for his chance.
* League Cup winners medal 94-95.
* He signed professional for Liverpool on 1st January 1995.
* Anthony Warner went through another season without the chance of a Premier League debut. Not even David James' poor form at the end of the season could allow him into Roy Evans' line up.

71.name: Kvarme
pages: * Bjorn Tore Kvarme arrived at Liverpool as replacement for the veteran John Scales, transfered to Tottenham Hotspur. The Anfield crowd were quick to appreciate what a good signing he had been. The Norwegian defender adapted perfectly to Evans side's way of playing and from day one, forced his way into the side as a regular member of the starting line up. He made such an inital impact that many even dared to compare him to the legendary Mark Lawrenson. It certainly wasn't a bad start at Anfield for a player who had declared himself an ardent Liverpool fan as a young boy in Norway.

* Kvarme generally plays at right back although he can also do the same job down the left hand side. He can also play at the heart of the defence. Kvarme possesses tremendous fighting spirit, never giving a ball up for lost and keeps up a fantastic pace throughout the ninety minutes. He likes to make progress down the flank getting involved in the attacks although he lacks a powerful shot and is not a threat in the air although he crosses the ball well. His great positional sense allows to him get back to cover quickly and efficiently.

* Norwegian League Championship winner medals, 92, 93, 94, 95 and 96. 
* Norwegian Cup winners medals 92 and 95.

* Kvarme began his profesional careeer in 1991, at Rosenborg. 
* He completed his contract with the Norwegian club and signed for Liverpool on 17th January 1997, although he had offers from several other clubs among them Glasgow Rangers. His contract with the "Reds" expires in June of the year 2000.
* Kvarme made his Premier League debut on 18th January 1997 in a game against Aston Villa at Anfield (3-0).
* He has been a Liverpool fan since he was a young boy.

* Kvarme arrived at Liverpool in January after winning a Norwegian League championship medal with Rosenborg. Even on the day of his debut at home against Aston Villa he showed his extraordinary ability to adapt to the pace of the game in the Premier League. Roy Evans was suitably impressed by his performance and from that point on played him in every league game up to the end of the season.

72.name: Bjornebye
pages: * After so long in the treatment room fighting to get back into action, last season Stig-Inge Bjornebye's smile finally returned. The Norwegian international was at last able to enjoy a long, injury free period which he took full advantage of to show the Anfield fans that Liverpool hadn't made a mistake in signing him. His main ambition now is to win something in England, and along the way, win himself a place in the Norwegian squad for the 1998 World Cup Finals in France.

* An attack minded left back, Bjornebye is constantly moving forward in support of the attack. Blessed with excellent left-footed ball control he likes to get down the line and hit long deep passes to the strikers. He also has the ability to occasionally get on the scoresheet himself. He is guilty however of occasionally neglecting his defensive duties, not getting back to cover quickly enough. If he gets his positional play right then he is a very difficult player to beat for speed, while he he has plenty of defensive know how and tricks which allow him to stop his opponents. However, at times, he doesn't seem fully recovered from the injury he suffered during the 94-95 season, something which has logically had an effect on his confidence and form.

* Norwegian League Championship winners medal 92. 
* Norwegian Cup winners medal 92. 
* League Cup winners medal 94-95.

* 54 full international appearances for Norway, scoring once. 
* A member of his country's squad for the 1994 World Cup Finals in the United States Bjornebye played in all three of Norway's games as a member of the starting line up.

* Bjornebye began his playing career with Kongsvinger. 
* Transfered to Rosenborg in 1992  he helped them win the Norwegian league and cup double in his first season there. He rounded off a superb campaign by scoring one of his side's three goals in the cup final against Lillestrom.  
* An automatic choice for Norway's international side, he played his part in Norway's qualification for the 1994 World Cup Finals in the United States after eliminating among other teams, England. Norway hadn't been in the World Cup Fianls since 1938.
* On 18th December 1992 he signed for Liverpool for £600,000. He made his league debut the following day against Coventry.

* Bjornebye was chosen "Player of the Year" 1994 by the Liverpool fans. The Norwegian defender played in all 38 league games scoring 4 times with 2 of his goals coming in the European Cup Winners Cup. Without any doubt he's completed his best season at Anfield since he arrived  in December 1992. He took charge of the left hand side of the park and, at last, was able to show his class without having to worry about injuries.

73.name: McAteer
pages: * Since his arrival at Liverpool in September 1995  Jason McAteer has made himself a regular member of the line up. The Irish international has a fiery character and shows courage and bravery in everything he does. As a result he has become an automatic first team choice both for Liverpool as well as for the Republic of Ireland international side. A few years ago it was said of him that he lacked confidence in his own ability, a criticism which nowadays nobody can hold against him.

* Jason McAteer is a fine footballer. Blessed with superb physical attributes and excellent tactical awareness. He can do a job either as a full back or in midfield, though always down the right hand side. At Bolton he generally played in midfield although Roy Evans prefers to use him as an attacking full back making the most of his ability to take men on. A technically correct player he should try to make more use of his physical strength to get in and around the area more often and should try to get in more efforts on goal, possessing as he does a powerful shot in his right foot. Only an occasional goalscorer, he could contribute more to the side's attacking play.

* League Cup runners up medal with Bolton Wanderers (94-95). 
* F.A. Cup runners up medal with Liverpool (95-96).

* 22 full international appearances for the Republic of Ireland. 
* He played in the 1994 World Cup Finals in the United States.
* One "B" international appearance.

* A member of a family of boxers, his uncles Les and Pat were both British Champions.
* He arrived at Bolton Wanderers from Merseyside club Marine where the club's manager decided that McAteer wasn't good enough to hold down a place in the modest Northern Premier League. 
* His move to Bolton cost the club just £500.It was the club's manager at the time, Dave Ramsden, who discovered him and who showed more confidence in McAteer's ability than Jason did himself.
* Made his debut for Bolton on 28th November 1992 against Burnley in a First Division game.
* He scored against Wolverhampton Wanderers at Molineux in a play off game for promotion to the Premier League, a goal which proved decisive in getting Bolton up to English football's top flight.
* During his time at Bolton Wanderers he was booked 11 times, though he was never sent off.
* During the 1994 World Cup Finals in the United States he executed an outstanding marking job on the Italian Roberto Baggio which brought him international recognition and increased his valuation in the transfer market. 
* On 6th September 1995 he was transfered to Liverpool for £4,500,000. He made his debut on 16th of that same month in a game against Blackburn Rovers at Anfield (3-0).
* McAteer scored his first goal for the Reds on 24th March 1997 at Highbury against Arsenal, being first to the rebound after David Seaman saved a Robbie Fowler penalty.

* McAteer was one of the side's most regular performers during the course of last season. He played in 37 of the 38 league games maintaining excellent form for both club and country. He also managed to score his first goal in a Liverpool shirt after knocking in the rebound from David Seaman's save from Robbie Fowler's now famous "penalty he didn't want" against Arsenal at Highbury.

74.name: Babb
pages: * The final run in to the season was a difficult time for Phil Babb. Used to being an automatic first choice both for Liverpool as well as the Republic of Ireland national team he lost out to his colleagues in both sides. At club level the arrival of the Norwegian, Kvarme relegated him in no uncertain terms to the substitutes bench. Phil will be out to get his place back during the 97-98 campaign and show that what happened last year was an  accident. If he doesn't manage this then he could be facing an uncertain future at Anfield.

* Phil Babb is a player who is perfectly at home playing either as a central defender or at left back. He is a quick, forceful defender who anticipates forwards' intentions well and is at all times a very decisive player. He never shirks a physical challenge and times his tackles well when he slides in to win the ball. Probably one of his greatest strengths is his ability to cover across the back as the last man in the defence. He has a good touch on the ball with his left foot and likes to bring the ball out from the back. Occasionally he will play it long, backed up by the power he possesses in his left foot. He is safe in the air at the back but should try to make more of his ability in the air by moving forward more frequently to support the attack. Nevertheless he has scored a few goals during the course of his career.
* League Cup winners medal 95.

* 21 full international appearances for the Republic of Ireland. 
* He played in the 1994 World Cup Finals in the United States 1994. 
* 2 "B" international appearances.

* After coming through the ranks at Millwall, Babb turned professional in August 1989. He never got the opportunity to make his debut for the first team.
* On 10th August 1990 he signed for Bradford City. His league debut came on 8th September 1990 in a game against Reading.
* His move to Coventry (27th Junly 1992 ) was valued at half a million pounds.
* On 1st September 1994 Liverpool paid £3 ,600,000 to sign him, which at the time made him the club's record signing. Weeks earlier Babb had been one of the Republic of Ireland's most outstanding players during the World Cup Finals in the United States.

* Last season left something of a bitter taste in the mouth for Phil Babb, who began the season as an automatic choice and ended it on the substitutes bench. The change in Babb's fortunes came about as a result of  both the arrival at the club of the Norwegian defender Kvarme, as well as Roy Evans' new defensive system reducing the number of central defenders from three to two. From May through to the end of the season Babb failed to make a first team appearance in the league while he also lost his place in the Republic of Ireland side.

75.name: Jones
pages: * Rob Jones has a difficult task ahead of him trying to win back his first team place at Liverpool; he has to fight for a place against two players - Jason McAteer (Irish international) and Stig Inge Bjornebye ( Norwegian international). Neverthless, everything could change if Rob manages to get back to the outstanding form he showed a few seasons ago taking him into the full England side. This was suddenly cut short by an apparently never ending run of injuries. At the moment, a place in the England squad for the 1998 World Cup Finals in France would seem to be an impossible dream, although stranger things have happened.

* Rob Jones is a player who stands out for his pace, a quality which makes him a very  difficult defender to beat. His excellent physical attributes means that opposing forwards have to show a real touch of skill to get away from his tight marking. His speed also makes him a very decisive player when he is covering across the back. Though not a particularly spectacular player he is undoubtedly an effective defender. Throughout the majority of his career Jones has played at right back, although at Liverpool, following the arrival of McAteer, he has been forced to play a number of games out on the left where he doesn't feel quite so comfortable. Under Roy Evans he finds himself playing slightly further forward helping out the midfield from a position where he gets less time on the ball to measure his crosses. On the right Jones looks much more at home showing a good touch on the ball as well as the ability to get forward in support of the attack.

* League Cup winners medal 1992. 
* League Cup winners medal 1995.

* 10 full international apperances for England. He made his debut in a friendly France at Wembley, a game which ended in a 2-0 victory for England. 
* 2 under-21 international appearances. 
* 2 youth international appearances, scoring once. 
* Welsh schoolboy international.

* His debut for Crewe Alexandra, where David Platt also played came on 9th April 1988 at Crewe's Gresty Road ground against Darlington shortly before he signed as an apprentice.
* He played in the Foruth Division and enjoyed the experience of Crewe's promotion to the Third Division.
* His move to Livepool on 4th October 1991 cost the Anfield club £300,000. Liverpool's manager at the time was Graeme Souness who had no choice due to injuries to give him his debut in a game against Manchester United at Old Trafford. Jones marked Ryan Giggs.
* Jones made his full England debut on the same day as Alan Shearer. 
* Injury kept him out of the 1992 Euroepan Championships in Sweden . 
* Another injury kept him out of action for the majority of the 96-97 season 
* Robert Jones is the grandson of Bill Jones who played right back for Liverpool in the 1950 F.A. Cup final at Wembley against Arsenal.
* Injured for the majority of the season, Rob Jones managed to play in just 2 league games - those against Sunderland and Everton - both of those appearances coming towards the end of the season.

76.name: Matteo
pages: * It's proved to be a difficult task for Dominic Matteo to settle down in the Liverpool first team. Fortunately for him, after four years of hard work on the training ground and plenty of frustration, last season he finally got his chance to prove himself. He won the confidence of Roy Evans and was able to battle away with his colleagues for a place in the first team. During the  97-98 season he will no doubt get more chances to measure his progress against the best strikers in England.

* Matteo gives a good account of himself both at the heart of the defence, as well as in the left back position and can even do a good job when he is pushed further forward. Although he still needs to improve technically he is slowly but surely gaining experience singularly in getting out of tight situations in defence. His height allows him to dominate in the air, although it is rare to see him move forward into the attack. Though he possesses great abillity he obviously still needs more experience of competition at the highest level.

* 3 under-21 international appearances. 
* 1 youth international appearance.

* After coming through the ranks at Anfield Dominic Matteo signed as a professional with Liverpool on 27th May 1992.
* He made his debut on 23rd October 1993 in a game against Manchester City.  
* Since the opportunities weren't coming his way at Anfield he was sent out on loan to Sunderland, although he made just one appearance in a Sunderland shirt.
* It was the 96-97 season onwards when he began appearing regularly in the side, making 38 appearances for the Reds out a possible total of 52.

* Last season finally saw Dominic Matteo make the breakthrough. The Liverpool defender began the season as a member of the starting line up, his good form allowing him to put together a run of 14 consecutive starting appearances. He proved himself to be well capable of playing in a competition as tough as the Premier League and was even called up by Glenn Hoddle to the full England squad although he didn't get to make his debut. The arrival at the club of Kvarme saw him pushed into the background a little, though in no way did it take the shine off a great season.

77.name: Wright
pages: * Mark Wright is now very much the club's veteran, but when he's out on the park he still shows the application and commitment of a much younger player, fighting for every ball and inspiring the same sort of spirit in his teammates. Now 34 years old, Mark is enjoying his second youth at Anfield. Roy Evans will be trusting in him to once again direct things at the back with the much sought after league title very much in their sights

* A strong and forceful central defender Mark Wright is a lot quicker than he might first appear. Good in the air he frequently gets forward for corners and free kicks. He has vast experience behind him, something which is reflected in the composure evident in his possession and safety aspects of his short passing game. At the very beginning of his career he played as a centre forward proving to be clinical in front of goal, expecially with his head.

* F.A. Cup winners medal 91-92. 
* Charity Shield medal 92.

* A full international on 45 occasions, Mark Wright made his debut on 2nd May 1984 against Wales played at Wrexham. His first and only goal for England came in the 1990 World Cup finals in Italy against Egypt on 21st June 1990 at Cagliari. That goal put England into the quarter finals. 
* One England "B" international appearance. 
* Four under-21international appearances.

* Mark Wright signed for Oxford United on 26th August 1980 after having played for the club's youth side. 
* He made his league debut on 17th October 1981 in a game against Bristol City.
* His move to Southampton involved a swap deal between the "Saints" and Oxford. Wright and Keith Cassels moved to The Dell in exchange for Trevord Hebberd and George Lawrence. He signed on 25th March 1982 for £80,000. 
* In 1986 a broken leg suffered in an F.A. Cup Semi-final against Liverpool prevented him from going to that year's World Cup Finals in Mexico. 
* After an incident involving Wright and Lawrie McMenemy he was transfered from Southampton to Derby County, on 27th August 1987, together with Peter Shilton. His fee had gone up t £760,000. Derby County managed to finish fifth in the league but were unable to remain amongst the big boys. 
* Wright took part in the 1988 European Championships in Sweden where England lost all their games. 
* The following season (90-91) Derby County were relegated to the Second Division. At the end of the season the side was hammered 1-7 at Anfield. Strangely it was a game that pointed to Mark Wright's future. Graeme Souness was watching him closely, and shortly afterwards on 15th July 1991 he signed for the Reds in exchange for £2,200,000.
* Wright quickly settled down at Liverpool as a regular member of the side, although an injury in a UEFA Cup tie against Genoa kept him out of action for a while.
* He played in the 1992 F.A. Cup final against Sunderland. Following the match he went up to collect the trophy from the Queen without removing the Liverpool cap that he was wearing at the time.
* Graham Taylor left him out of the England side after refusing to attend the training sessions prior to a friendly against Hungary, preferring as he did to remain in Liverpool to celebrate the F.A. Cup triumph. 
* Liverpool manager Roy Evans publicy accused him of not being commited enough to the  the Liverpool cause during the 96-97 pre-season games when the team suffered a number of defeats on their Scandinavian tour.

* Mark Wright was a member of the starting line up in all 33 of the games in which he played last season making him the most used player at the heart of Roy Evans' defence. He showed great consistency throughout the season although he was unable to realise his dream of returning to the England side. In the return leg of the European Cup Winners Cup against Paris St. Germain at Anfield Mark connected with a fabulous header bringing the score to 2-0, giving the Reds fresh hope of turning the tie around on it's head. But, unfortunately for Liverpool, there were to be no more goals on the night.
* At the end of the season he was included in the Premier League ideal team, voted for by his fellow professionals.

78.name: Harkness
pages: * In direct competition for a place with Jason McAteer and Rob Jones for a place at right back, Steve Harkness, initially, would seem to have little chance of making the position his own. Nevertheless, throughout his career, Steve has done more than enough to show that he possesses a real fighting spirit, never more so than a few seasons ago when he managed to keep Rob Jones out of the side. He will once again be fighting tenaciously during the 97-98 season although the competition would seem to be stiffer than ever.

* Although he could be described as a midfielder, the truth is that his most natural position is at full back. His aggressive approach and lack of inclination to push forward make him a player more at home in defensive positions. In fact, he made his debut in the 91-92 season at right back. Harkness is undoubtedly a player with a future in the Premier League. His technical limitations however seem destined to make it difficult for him to settle down at one of the really big clubs.
* 13 youth international appearances for England, scoring twice.

* Harkness made his debut for Carlisle United's schoolboy side in March 1987.
* On 23rd March 1989 he signed as a professional, having already made his debut on 18th February in a 3-0 victory against Hereford.
* Liverpool signed him on 17th July 1989, for £75,000. 
* He was loaned out to Huddersfield on 24th September 1993, and to Southend United on 3rd February 1995.
* During the 95-96 season in a game against Coventry, he suffered a badly broken leg and was kept out of action for several months.

* During the 95-96 season  Steve suffered a serious injury which forced him to miss the majority of the 96-97 season. Around mid-March he fought his way back into the side and put together a run of 5 consecutive games as a member of the starting line up. However he didn't have the time to get back to the form he showed before his injury.

79.name: Carragher
pages: * Jamie Carragher is another product of the apparently never ending supply of young talent currently around Anfield. He made his first team debut at just 19 years of age and slowly but surely has began to win the confidence ofmanager Roy Evans. During the 97-98 season, he will be hoping to take another step in his career and become a more regular member of the Liverpool side. All he seems to need is a minimal amount of luck, and a little time.

* Carragher can play either in midfield or at the heart of the defence. In either position he is a dynamic player who shows physical power and strength. A forceful ball winner, he also distributes the ball effectively and moves forward to support the attack at set pieces where he can make the most of his heading ability. Still a young player, he is very much the typical promising young footballer of the future.
* F.A. Youth Cup winners medal 96.

* Four under-21 international appearances for England .
* An England youth international.

* A product of the Anfield youth system, Jamie Carragher signed professional for Liverpool on 9th October 1996.
* He made his Premier League debut on 11th January 1997 in a game against West Ham at Anfield (0-0). Carragher came on for Neil Ruddock in the 45th minute.
* He scored his first league goal on 18th January 1997, against Aston Villa at Anfield. It was also the first game in which Jamie had played from the start (3-0).

* Although he played in just 2 league games, Jamie Carragher made a fine impression on the Anfield  fans. He scored a good goal against Aston Villa - a header from a Bjornebye corner. It was the first time that Carragher had made a starting appearance. He didn't manage to get back into the first team, but certainly proved that he is on the right tracks. Proof of that is his regular inclusion in the England under-21side.

80.name: Murphy
pages: * Danny Murphy is, together with Michael Owen, one of the Liverpool fans' big hopes for the future. Roy Evans had been on the player's trail for several years. Faced with the possibility of him landing up at one of the other big clubs Evans decided to go in with an offer which neither Crewe Alexandra nor the player could refuse. With patience and hard work Danny could well go on to reach the top. Very soon, both Liverpool and the England side could have an exceptional player on their hands.

* Danny Murphy is a very skillfu young midfielder with a great attack-minded approach to the game. He can do a fine job playing either as a midfield organizer, or playing just behind the main strikers from where he can show his ability to make powerful runs into the box, or create chances for others. He also manages to get on the scoresheet regularly himself. A player for the future, he possesses all the qualities he needs to go on to become a great success: class, strength and dedication.
x

* An England under-20 international, he played in the 1997 under-20 World Cup in Malaysia.
* England youth and schoolboy international.

* A product of Crewe Alexandra's youth system, Daniel Murphey made his first team league debut on 11th December 1993 in an away game against Colchester United. In his second appearance six days later, he scored his first goal for the club against Preston North End.
* In 1997 he played a decisive part in a play-off game for promotion to the First Division. Crewe managed to overcome Brentford at Wembley. 
* At the end of the 96-97 season his fellow professionals included him in the Second Division's ideal team.
* He has been a Liverpool player since 8th July 1997. His transfer fee was set at £3,000,000.
* As well as Liverpool, Tottenham Hotspur have also shown a great interest in signing him.

* Danny Murphy was one of last season's revelations. His fine performances and his goals (10), helped take Crewe up to the First Division. Danny played a decisive part in the victory over Brentford in the play off final at Wembley. His excellent season was recognised by the Professional Footballers Association who voted to include him the Second Division's ideal team for 96-97.

81.name: Leonhardsen
pages: * In Oyvind Leonhardsen, Roy Evans has found the ideal substitute for John Barnes. In signing Leonhardsen Liverpool have taken on a fine footballer, who though still relatively young will no doubt prove to be an excellent reinforcement for the midfield. At Anfield, Oyvind will be sharing the dressing room with his compatriots Bjornebye and Kvarme; at the same time he has also managed to make one of his boyhood dreams come true: to wear the same shirt that was worm years earlier by Kevin Keegan and Kenny Dalglish.

* Basically an attack-minded midfielder, Leonhardsen was one of the most talented footballers at Wimbledon. Blessed with a great touch on the ball he takes charge of organising the team's attacks although while at Wimbledon this occasionally clashed with the team's style, more inclined as they were to play the long ball into the heart of the area. He is a very dangerous payer from free kicks and other set pieces. He poses a real threat when he has a go at goal from distance. He is a regular goalscorer and is a genuine focal point for the side. He does a good job either as a central midfielder or pushed out wide preferably down the right hand side. In whichever position he plays, the Norwegian always shows tremendous effort and, above all, talent.

* Norwegian league championship winners medals 92-93 and 93-94. 
* Norwegian Cup winners medal 92-93.

* 53 full international appearances for Norway, with 5 goals to his name. He made his debut in 1990 in Egil Olsen's first game as Norway's manager. Norway defeat Cameroon by an emphatic six goals to nil.

*  Leonhardson began his career at modest Norwegian club Clausengen, before being  transfered to Molde in 1987. 
* He was the scorer of the first goal, in the Norway-England game, in Oslo in 1993, a game which the Scandinavian side won 2-0.
* His transfer to Rosenborg in 1992 for £9,000 was the most expensive in the history of Norwegian football. 
* He was voted Player of the Year by the Norwegian Sports Writers. 
* He went out on loan to Wimbledon in November 1994. On his debut against Aston Villa on 2nd November, he scored in the 90th minute of the game, clinching a 4-3 victory for the Dons. 
* At the end of the 94-95 season, Wimbledon decided to exercise their option to buy Leonhardsen, and signed him for £650,000.
* After two and a half years at Wimbledon where he became one of the Selhurst Park supporters' most popular players he was transfered to Liverpool on 2nd June 1997 for £4,000,000. He signed a four year contract.
* Leonhardsen has declared that he has been a Liverpool fan since he was a boy. His boyhood idols were Kevin Keegan and Kenny Dalglish.

* Leonhardson was one of the most regular performers at Wimbledon throughout the whole of last season. He played in a total of 27 league games, all of those as a member of the starting line up, scoring five goals. Some of his goals were particularly important, such as the ones scored against Liverpool, Newcastle and Nottingham Forest. His will to win and untiring fighting spirit made him one of the most appreciated players at Selhurst Park.

82.name: Ince
pages: * Paul Ince has returned to England. Following his adventures in Italy the international midfielder is back in the Premier League. But this time he is in the red not of Manchester United but Liverpool. Though the shirt is different, the commitment and strength he has shown down the years will no doubt be the same. The Anfield supporters have the opportunity to watch one of the most charismatic of English players. With him in the side Liverpool can certainly begin to dream of big things, while Paul Ince, without any doubt, will be dreaming of even winning the World Cup with England.

* A real battling midfielder, tremendously strong, he posseses a great shot and seems to have the knack of getting onto the end of rebounds and parries from goalkeepers. He stands out for the work he does in winning back possession for his team, a job in which he shows himself to be forceful, solid and occasionally hard. He likes to get forward to support the attack although he is not quite as effective when he has the responsibility of directing the team's pattern of play himself. Nevertheless his drive, energy and will to win are qualities which are well appreciated by the rest of the side.

* Two English League Championship winners medals with Manchester United (93 and 94).
* Two F.A. Cup winners medals with Manchester United (90 and 94). 
* One League Cup winners medal with Manchester United (92). 
* One European Cup Winners cup winners medal Manchester United (91). 
* One European Super Cup winners medal with Manchester United (91).

* 30 full international appearances for England. 
* Ince made his debut on 9th September 1992 against Spain in Santander. The game, which ended in a 1-0 victory for Spain, with a goal from Goyo Fonseca, also marked  Javier Clemente's first game in charge of the Spanish national side.
* The most emotional moment of his career came in June 1993 when he became the first black player to captain England. It was in a friendly game against a United States team, who ruled Ince's big day, by surprisingly winning the game by two goals to nil.
* He also played in the 1996 European Championship in England .

* Ince had a childhood which was full of problems, and only football seemed to be able to keep him on the straight and narrow. The player himself has acknowledged that if it hadn't been for sport, he could now well be either in prison or on the dole. His family broke up when he was just 8 years old when his father walked out and his mother had to move to Germany to find work. In the meantime Paul was involved in a series of problems which, on more than one occasion, saw him paying a visit to the local police stations in the East End of London. Thankfully however, everything changed when John Lyall, manager of  West Ham United saw him in action and took him on to play for the club's youth teams, a decisive moment in the life of Paul Ince. 
* His strong character and personality, developed throughout his childhood, helped him to overcome his worst moments. However this side to his nature has also caused him a problem more than once during his playing career. During the 94-95 season, for instance, he had to explain his actions to a magistrates court after a Crystal Palace supporter reported to the police that he had been attacked by Ince. Finally the incident remained as no more than an anecdote, although he could quite easily have had the same luck as Frenchman Eric Cantona, who was banned  for almost a year, following a similar incident.
* He played his first full game for West Ham on 30th November 1986, against Newcastle. Paul scored one of the Hammers' goals in their 3-1 win. 
* During the 88-89 season he went through one of the worst moments of his career, as West Ham were relegated to the Second Division. Liverpool and  Manchester United battled it out for his signature, although it was finally the Reds of Manchester who he joined. His decision to leave West Ham didn't go down well with the East London club's supporters, who gave him a hostile reception when he went back to Upton Park for the first time as a Manchester United player. He himself has acknowledged that he will never forget, or forgive, the reception he was given.
* Inter Milan paid £7,500,000 for Ince in 1995. 
* He will go down in footballing history as the first black player to captain the full England side.
* As well as the logical problems of adpting to the style of football played in the "calcio", he also had to take on board the reluctance of his wife Claire to change country. Proof of that was the attack of nerves that she suffered during her husband's official presentation as an Inter Milan player. 
* Golf and snooker are his two great passions outside of football. 
* He is known as O. J. Simpson for his resemblance to the ex American Football star.
* Bryan Robson and John Lyall are his two biggest idols. 
* His two favourites actors are Al Pacino and Kim Bassinger . 
* He is a big fan of the music of Montell Jordan.
* Although his contract with Inter didn't expire until June 1998, he was transfered to Liverpool on 18th July 1997. The transfer fee was fixed at £4,200,000.

* In what was a relatively mediocre season for Inter last time out, Paul Ince was one of the team's best players. The club's British coach, Roy Hodgson , lined him up in 24 league games. Ince scored 6 goals, a good return for a a basically defensive midfield player like him, and especially so in a championship as competitive as the Italian serie "A".
