83.name: Berger
pages: * Although the very beginning of his Liverpool career was quite simply spectacular (4 goals in 3 games), during the majority of his first season in England, Patrick Berger suffered from a logical lack of adaptation to the style of the game in the Premier League. In spite of this, the Czech international gave glimpses of his undoubted talent and showed the Anfield supporters that he is a player that they can have plenty of confidence in as one for the future, a future that looks brighter all the time, thanks to young players of the talent of Robbie Fowler, Jamie Redknapp, Michael Owen, Danny Murphy and Patrick Berger himself.

* An attacking midfielder, Berger can stand out playing as a wide midfield man, or playing just behind the forwards. He is quick and skillful and blessed with exquisite technique, all of which makes him a very difficult player to contain when he is at the top of his game. He possesses tremendous vision, which together with the accuracy of his passing makes him a key man going forward. He has a powerful shot from distance, which is how he scores a lot of his goals. A left footed player he is also a specialist at free kicks and set pieces while he is also an expert penalty taker.
* Despite his youth, Berger is a player who shows great maturity in everything he does. Given his quality and the decisive attacking contribution he makes to the attack, he rarely does much defensively, although he more than makes up for that with his creativity and the array of abilities he shows going forward. Still with plenty of time ahead of him to improve, Berger is well on the way to becoming a very compelete footballer.

* German Bundesliga winners medal 1996. 
* 1996 European Championships runners up medal, with the Czech Republic.

* 26 full international appearances for Czech Republic, with 11 goals to his credit, Berger made his debut on 17th August 1995 in a friendly game against France, played in Bourdeaux (2-2). He scored his first international goal on 6th September of that same year in Ostrava, against Malta (6-1). A member of his country's squad for the 1996 European Championships in England, he made 6 appearances, playing from the start in 3 games including the final. It was Berger who scored the Czech Republic's goal (from the penalty spot) in the final game, although it wasn't enough to give his side the trophy. 
* 2 full international appearances for the now defunct Czecoslovakia. He made his debut on 24th March 1993 against Cyprus in Limassol (1-1).

* Berger began his career with Sparta Prague's amateur team. He made his debut however in the top flight of Czech football with the city's other big club, Slavia Praga.
* Transfered to Borussia Dortmund, Berger helped the club to win the Bundesliga in his first season in Germany. 
* He was his country's top scorer during the qualifying games for the 1996 European  Championships, scoring 6 goals in 9 games. 
* During the European Championships in England, he made an appearance in all 6 of the Czech Republic's  games. A member of the starting line up in the final, he scored from the penalty spot, to put his side one goal to nil up against Germany. However after drawing 1-1 after ninety minutes, Bierhoff scored the golden goal in extra-time that gave the trophy to the Germans. 
* On 2nd August 1996 he was transfered to Liverpool for £3,250,000 although he was initially faced with some problems to join the club, due to the difficulties he encountered in getting a work permit.
* He made his Premier League debut on 7th 1996. Liverpool went on to defeat Southampton at Anfield by two goals to one.
* On 15th September 1996 against Leicester, at Filbert Street, Berger scored his first two goals in a Liverpool shirt.

* In his second Premier League appearance, Berger put two goals past Leicester City on their own ground. In the following game he scored another two this time against Chelsea, blasting his way into Roy Evans' side on a regular basis. Slowly but surely however, he began to slip down the pecking order, going on to spend a good many games on the bench. By the end of the season he had played in 23 games, 13 of those as a member of the starting line up and had managed to find the back of the net on 6 occasions.

84.name: Thomas
pages: * Liverpool's signing of Michael Thomas in 199 was not well received by some sections of the Anfield supporters who had bitter memories of Thomas' goal depriving them of the league title in the last minute of the last game of the season. Just to add salt to the wounds, the match was played at Anfield. However, his work rate out on the pitch combined with his efforts in defence of the famous red shirt have won him the recognition of the club's supporters. Although each time a new season starts he seems candidate to be left out of the squad, he eventually ends up a regular member of the side. He is a player who, though he may have his off days, always guarantees wholehearted commitment right to the end of the ninety minutes - something which both Roy Evans and the Anfield crowd know and appreciate.

* Michael Thomas is a midfielder who covers every inch of the pitch, blessed as he is with tremendous physical attributes allowing him to maintain an intense work rate throughout the whole game. He makes up for his technical limitations with his untiring effort in support of his teammates. He plays more often than not slightly towards the right, from where his runs into the opposing penalty area can pose a real threat. Although he is not a prolific goalscorer, he knows how to get into dangerous positions often getting on the end of rebounds and parries, and occasionally finding the back of the net. 
* A very dinamic footballer Thomas wins plenty of possession, constantly helping out both in defence and attack. Although he doesn't possess great vision his contribution to the team is significant due to the amount of ground he covers, a tremendous help for his fellow midfielders.

* League Championship winners medals 88-89 and 90-91. 
* F.A. Cup winners medal 91-92. 
* League Cup winners medal 86-87 and 94-95. 
* Charity Shield  medal 89 and 91.

* 2 full international appearances for England. He made his debut on 16th November 1988 in a friendly against Saudi Arabia in Riyadh (1-1). His final appearance for the national side came on 13th December 1989; England defeated Yugoslavia 2-1 at Wembley.
* 6 "B" international appearances. 
* 12 under-21 international appearances, scoring 3 times. 
* 22 youth international appearances.

* During the summer of 1996 there was specualtion regarding Michael's possible departure to Italy. There was even rumour of interest from Atalanta and even talk about a move to Reggiana. The negotiations however, which seemed to be reaching a conclusion, were finally broken off and Thomas began the 96-97 at Liverpool.
* His career began at Arsenal, where he arrived as a schoolboy in July 1982 going on to sign professional for the club on 31st December 1984. 
* He was loaned out to Portsmouth on 30th December 1986, making his league debut on New Years Day 1987 in a game against Reading, playing at left back.  
* Back at Arsenal, he began to settle down in the right back spot a suspended Steve Williams pushed him forward to midfield.
* He played in the 1988 League Cup Final against Luton Town at Wembley which Arsenal lost 3-2. On a personal note however, Thomas ended the season as the Gunners' second top scorer.
* The 88-89 season saw him enjoy the best moments of his career. In the final game of the season Arsenal visited Anfield needing a win by two clear goals to snatch the title from Liverpool. Arsenal were leading 1-0, not enough to give them the title, when, in injury time, up popped Michael Thomas to score the goal that took the championshi, and the glory that goes with it back to Highbury.
* The following season, Arsenal were knocked out of the European Cup by Benfica while Thomas saw his form dip significantly. The arrival of the Northern Irish player David Hillier saw him relegated to the substitutes bench, or occasionally, even the reserve side.
* He was transfered to Liverpool on 16th December 1991 for £1,500,000. It was very much a personal signing on the part of then Liverpool boss Graeme Souness, who took him to Anfield  to replace the outgoing Steve McMahon. 
* Thomas scored a superb volley in the 1992 F.A. Cup final against Sunderland which opened the way up for the Reds to go on to lift the trophy.

* From the start of the season Thomas won himself a place in the starting line up. He put together a few outstanding performances at the start of the season, creating plenty of chances for the Liverpool strikers. He scored 3 goals in 31 league games, one of those proving to be decisive, clinching a victory for the Reds against West Ham.

85.name: McManaman
pages: * Steve McManaman is currently one of the best players in Europe, possessing so much talent that just a couple of glimpses of his skill is often enough to change the course of a match. For that very reason, Barcelona, under the guidance of Dutch coach Louis van Gaal, tried to sign him at the beginning of the 97-98 season. Fortunately for the Liverpool supporters, Steve will be staying at Anfield. His presence at the club is absolutely fundamental for a side that has genuine hopes of lifting a title that has eluded them for too long. His presence will no doubt also prove fundamental for the England side which has high hopes of going far in next year's World Cup Finals in France.

* Steve generally operates down the right hand side of the park either as a winger or more as an orthodox right sided midfielder, although he also often moves over to the left hand side where he can cut inside to get in shots on goal. Wherever he plays his outstanding mobility makes it an extremely difficult job for those defenders who are given the task of trying to mark him. Blessed with outstanding pace he carries the ball forward with it apparently tied to his rigft foot. He shows himself to be a skillful player who takes full advantage of his ability to beat men. Equally, he possesses superb technique and vision, allowing him to pick out his best placed teammates with ease. For his ability to take on and beat the opposition defence and to accept responsibility when the team finds itself in the tightest of situations,  McManaman comes very close to the perfect profile of a genuine star. His weak point is his shooting which is something he should work on to increase the number of goals he scores each season, although in his defence, he lays on an incredible amount of chances for his teamamates. Though he could do more to help the side out defensively, that would perhaps be asking too much of a young man who has become a truly outstanding footballer.

* F.A. Cup winners medal 92. 
* League Cup winners medal 95.

* 18 full international appearances for England.
* He made his debut on 16th November 1994 in a friendly against Nigeria  at Wembley (1-0).
* 7 under-21 international appearances scoring once. He made his under-21 debut against   Wales.
* 2 youth international appearances.

* McManaman has always been an Evertonian, something he never hides. As a boy he was a regular at Goodison Park.
* He had his first trial as a footballer with Everton but was turned down. 
* He then went to have a trial with Liverpool whose coaching staff decided to take him on. On 19th February 1990, he signed as a professional with the Reds.
* Everton tried to sign him, a few years after his original trial, but this time it was  Steve who turned down the Blues.
* He made his debut on 15th December 1990 in a game against Sheffield United.
* He was chosen as "Man of the Match" in the 1992 F.A. Cup final in which Liverpool beat Sunderland. McManaman, who was coming back from injury, was chosen as replacement for John Barnes, who was also injured. 
* The team's poor 92-93 season saw Steve booed by a section of the crowd in a number of games at Anfield. He was on the point of a transfer.
* On 2nd April 1995 he scored both goals which saw Liverpool win the League Cup against Bolton Wanderers at Wembley.
* Chosen by U.E.F.A. in the 1996 European Championship ideal team following the tournament, in which he played from the start in all five of the games that England played.
* At the end of August 1997 Barcelona were actively interested in signing him, to the point where McManaman even travelled to the Spanish City. The deal wasn't finally pushed through however, since Barcelona opted for the Brazilian Rivaldo.

* Steve McManaman's performances were slightly inconsistent over the course of last season. Following the exhibition he gave during the 95-96 season, which came to a peak with his excellent performances in the European Championships in England, the Liverpool man gave the impression of being worn out after playing so much football in recent seasons. Despite that, he played in every Premier League game except one. Nevertheless, as he seems to be every year, he was involved in some of the team's most exciting football creating any number of scoring chances combining with both Robbie Fowler and Stan Collymore. He chipped in with 7 goals.
* Although he wasn't at his best, he was included in the Premier League ideal side, voted for by his fellow professionals.

86.name: Redknapp
pages: * Redknapp is one of the best representatives of the new generation of English football, a generation that seems destined to mark a new era. The son of Harry Redknapp, ex-West Ham, Bournemouth and Brentford player and current manager of the Hammers, Jamie and football have gone hand in hand since he was a young boy, while his early development suggested he could explode onto the scene. If he can steer clear of injuries he could go on to perfectly represent the new breed of British midfield player capable of combining physical power and an exquisite touch on the ball. He will be out to make the 97-98 season the one when he finally announces his arrival in the big time. The 1998 World Cup Finals in France offer him the perfect stage upon which to do just that.

* Redknapp is one of the best passers of the ball in English football. Blessed with   exceptional technique, he stands out for the accuracy of his crossing. He is capable of playing anywhere in the midfield although his favourite position is in the centre of the park where he can get on with the job of directing the team's play. His great mobility often sees him move out wider, especially towards the left hand side. He possesses great vision, as well as a powerful shot which he never hesitates use whenever the opportunity arises. He has in fact scored some spectacular long distance goals. Redknapp is also something of free kick expert. For all of the qualities he possesses, as well as the significant defensive contribution he makes in each game, Jamie Redknapp is one of the most complete players in the Premier League.
* League Cup winners medal 94-95.

* 8 full international appearances for England. He made his debut on 6th September 1995 in a friendly game against Colombia at Wembley (0-0). 
* One "B" international appearance. 
* 18 under-21 international appearances, scoring 5 times. 
* 2 youth international appearances.

* Jamie began as a schoolboy at Tottenham in September 1987. When he left school he moved to Bournemouth, then managed by his father, signing as an apprentice.
* He made his league debut for Bournemouth on 13th January 1990 against Hull City when he he was 16 years and 6 months old. 
* On 15th January 1991 he signed for Liverpool, following the interest show by Kenny Dalglish, then the Reds' manager.
* He made his debut for the Anfield club in  the UEFA Cup against French side Auxerre while his league debut came against Southampton at The Dell, a game in which he managed to score Liverpool's equalizer. 
* Once scored a hat trick in an under-21 international game. . 
* During the early stages of his Liverpool career he found himself watching a lot of games from the bench - Jan Molby blocking the path to a place in the first team.

* Injuries and Michael Thomas' good form prevented Redknapp from making himself a regular in Roy Evans' side. Everything changed however in mid-January. Jamie got back to his best form and put together a run of 14 consecutive games in the first team, forming an outstanding partnership with John Barnes. He scored two league goals and one in the league cup demonstrating that if he stays clear of injury then he is sure of a place in the team.

87.name: Thompson
pages: * David Thompson is considered by many experts as one of the most promising young players in England but he is yet to gain the full confidence of Liverpool manager Roy Evans. His appearances in the side are as sporadic as they are fleeting; in fact up to the beginning of the 97-98 season he had seen just eight minutes of action in the Premier League - far too little for a young man who now needs to take the step up to the first team.

* Thompson is a midfield player with a real ability to find the back of the net. He moves forward from the midfield to get quickly into the attack. Blessed with good basic technique, he proved to be one of the most outstanding players in England  at youth level. He makes up for his lack of physical power with speed and ability and  is a very clever player when it comes to getting himself into positions from where he can get in shots on goal. Given his youth, he is a player who still has plenty of aspects to his game he can improve, as well as plenty to learn.
* F.A. youth Cup winners medal  96.

* 2 under 21 international appearances for England.
* England youth international.

* A product of Liverpool's youth system, he turned professional on 8th November 1994.
* He made his Premier League debut on 19th August 1996 in a game against  Arsenal at Anfield (2-0). Thompson came on for Stan Collymore in the 86th minute.

* Last season saw David Thompson make his Premier League debut. His contribution however was minimal. He enjoyed only eight minutes of action, all of those at Anfield, three against Arsenal and five against Sunderland.

88.name: Owen
pages: * Michael Owen is probably the most promising young footballer in England. Despite his youth he has already given more than a glimpse of the class he possesses. He has talent, character and ambition; three of the key ingredients that make a star. It is essential however that both Roy Evans and the Anfield supporters protect and look after a player who is real diamond, waiting to be finally polished up. For him to go on to fulfill his true potential, the club will need to show patience and try not to rush everything along too quickly. Nevertheless the 97-98 season could prove to be an excellent foundation upon which to build and go on to really show what he can do.

* A young striker, he moves and plays right along the forward line. Very quick to lose his markers and skillful with the ball at his feet, he doesn't think twice about taking on defenders in one on one situations. He has a great change of direction, vision, and above all, tremendous self confidence, all of which makes him an outstanding prospect. He is a young player who possesses that special instinct that separates the stars from the merely good.
x

* An England under-20 international, he played in the 1997 World under-20 Championships in Malaysia.
* Youth and schoolboy international.

* The son of Terry Owen, who once played for Everton, Michael always dreamed of wearing the Blue shirt of the Goodison Park club.
* His reputation as a goalscorer precedes him. At Deeside District Primary School he shattered the record for the number of goals scored in one season, setting it at 97.  Years earlier the legendary Ian Rush had scored 72. 
* Despite being an Everton supporter, Michael began to learn his trade in the youth ranks of bitter local rivals Liverpool.
* He made his debut for the first team on 6th May 1997, in the penultimate league game of the season against Wimbledon at Selhurst Park.  He came on in the 57th minute in place of Patrick Berger,and, in the 74th minute scored his first goal. Unfortunately, Liverpool lost 2-1.
* Together with teammate Danny Murphy Owen was one of the sensations of the world Under-20 championships played in Malaysia during the summer of 1997.

* Michael Owen was one of last season's revelations. His breakthrough into the Premier League in the penultimate league game of the season couldn't have been better, in a personal sense; he scored against Wimbledon barely 20 minutes after coming on as a substitute for Patrick Berger. An England under-20 international, the young Owen became one of the stars of the World Under-20 championships in Malaysia.

89.name: Riedle
pages: * To cover Stan Collymore's departure to Aston Villa, Liverpool needed a centre forward of prestige and experience. Karl Heinz Riedle, as well as meeting both requirements, is very much a player who could become a great success in England as was demonstrated just a few seasons ago by his compatriot Jurgen Klinsmann during his spell at Tottenham Hotspur.  Riedle arrives at Anfield with just one aim in mind: to help Liverpool win the league championship, something which has eluded Roy Evans' team for too long. For the title to return to Anfield the German striker will need to get among the goals.

* Karl Heinz Riedle possesses all the qualities of a classical centre forward. Strong and intelligent inside the penalty area, he has the knack of getting the better of defenders to get in powerful efforts on goal, preferably with his head. Riedle is a brave player, who never shirks a physical challenge with defenders and who also knows how to make the most of his vast experience . He is a quick player who also links up intelligently with the team's general build up play. He will have a go at goal with either foot and, whenever he is in and around the penalty area, danger lurks. Without doubt however, his greatest strength above his other qualities is his heading ability helped by his tremendous ability to get up above defenders.

* World Cup winners medal in Italy 1990.
* European Cup winners medal 97.
* German League Championship winners medals, 88, 95 and 96.
* Bronze medal winner in the Seul Olympic Games, 1988.

* 42 full international appearances for Germany, with 16 goals to his name.  
* 4 under-21 international appearances, scoring once.

* Karl Heinz Riedle's career began in 1974 in the ranks of modest TSV Ellhofen. After a spell with  SV Weiler he arrived at Augsburg, a team in a German regional league, in 1982.
* During the 85-86 season he scored 22 goals and was included in the German under- 21 side. Shortly afterwards he was transfered to Second Division club, Blau-Weiss Berlin.
* In 1987 he was signed by Werder Bremen. In his first season in the First Division he won a German championship winners medal and made his debut for the full German national side, scoring against Finland. 
* In 1990 he was transfered to Italian side Lazio for £5,500,000, making him one of the most expensive signings in Europe. At the Rome based club he teamed up with Paul Gascoigne.
* At the end of the 1990 World Cup Finals in Italy he announced his retirement from international football, tired as he was of being permanently in the shadow of Klinsmann and Voeller.
* He returned to Germany in 1993, this time moving to Borussia Dortmund where he went on to win two league titles and a European Cup. In the Champions League final against Juventus in the Olympic stadium in Munich, Riedle became the hero of the hour scoring two of his side's three goals. 
* Although he had a contract with Dortmund until June 1998 he was transfered to Liverpool on 30th July 1997 for £1,800,000. Just days earlier Riedle had received a tempting offer, financially, from Italian side Perugia.

* The high point of last season for Riedle came in the final of the Champions League, in the Olympic Stadium, Munich on 28th May 1997. Two goals from the German striker put Borussia Dortmund ahead. The German side eventually ran out 3-1 winners against Juventus. Little did it seem to matter at the time, that, up to the final, both Riedle as well as Dortmund, managed by Omar Hitzfield, had had a fairly mediocre league campaign, finishing in third place, eight points behind champions Bayern Munich.

90.name: Fowler
pages: * For a number of years people speculated about who would eventually go on to succeed Ian Rush at Liverpool. As things stand today, nobody is in any doubt as to the fact that Robbie Fowler is destined to mark his own era at the club, leading the Reds back to the forefront of the international game. Fowler, as well as proving himself to be a superb footballer, has also demonstrated a tremendous sense of professional honesty. The young English goalscorer represents, together with McManaman, Redknapp and Owen, the new wave at Anfield, an outstanding generation of footballers, representing the future of both Liverpool and the England national team. There is no better opportunity than the World Cup Finals, in France in 1998, to weigh up Robbie Fowler against the best defenders in the world.

* Above all else, Fowler is a goalscorer. He is capable of making the most dificult job in football, scoring goals, look quite simple. He is not a player who should be considered a classic English centre forward, who remains static in the middle of the penalty area waiting for the ball to come in, generally in the form of crosses that he can get his head to. On the contrary, the Liverpool striker stands out for the constant movement he shows throughout  the whole of the attacking third of the field. He is well capable of picking the ball up deep and going past defenders before striking the ball home. Blessed with good speed and an exquisite touch in his left foot, as well as his opportunism, he also has excellent vision which allows him to pick out his unmarked teammates apparently at will. He also has a powerful shot. All of these qualities together with his knowledge of the game and his astuteness make him a young man with a splendid future ahead of him. At present his progress seems to be unstoppable.

* League Cup winners medals 94-95. 
* European under 20 Championship winners medal after beating Turkey 1-0 in the final.

* 6 full international appearances for England. He made his debut on 27th March 1996 in a firendly against Bulgaria at Wembley (1-0). 
* One "B" international appearance. 
* 18 under-21 international appearances, scoring five goals. 
* 2 youth international appearances.

* Born in the Toxteth district of Liverpool, as a boy he was a supporter of Everton,  Liverpool's bitter local rivals. 
* He began playing footbal for his school team, St. Patrick's. In November 1990 at just 15 years of age, he joined the F.A. School of Excellence, instead of joining the youth ranks at Liverpool. In July 1991 he joined the Anfield club as an apprentice.
* During those early years, his passion for Everton was such that he used to wear an Everton shirt under his training top. However he later turned down an offer from the "toffees" to stay with Liverpool. According to Fowler himself the decision was strictly a professional one.
* He sigend professional for Liverpool on 23rd April 1992. 
* During the 92-93 season he was called up to play in a game against Tottenham, although finally he didn't play. He had to wait until 12th September 1993 to make his debut and, at the same time, go down in the history of the club. It was in a League Cup game against Fulham which ended in a 5-1 win for Liverpool. Fowler scored all five goals, something only previously achieved by Kenny Dalglish, Ian Rush and Dean Saunders.
* Thirteen days later on 25th September he made his Premier League debut against Chelsea replacing Nigel Clough. In his second league game, against Oldham, he struck his first goal for Liverpool and in his third against Southampton managed to hit his first hat trick.
* The Professional Footballers' Association voted him young player of the year 1995.
* He ended the 94-95 season as the second top scorer in the Premier League,behind Alan Shearer. Fowler managed to score a total of 25 goals. He celebrated his 23rd goal of the season in the strangest of ways, by turning his shirt back to front displaying the number he wears on the back to the fans; the number was of course, 23.
* With 18 goals to his credit, he was once again the side's top scorer, for the 96-97 campaign. He was also included by his fellow professionals in the Premier League's ideal team.
* On 24th March 1997, Robbie Fowler's name went right around the world. Liverpool were playing at Highbury against Arsenal when, following a clash between Fowler and  Seaman,the referee gave a penalty. Fowler, in a show of genuine professional honesty, acknowledged that the Arsenal keeper hadn't commited a foul and appealed to the referee not to award the spot kick, without success. Seconds later up stepped Fowler himself to take the penalty, but it was saved by Seaman. Jason McAteer was on hand to ram home the rebound.

* During the course of last season, Robbie Fowler was once again one of the Premier League's most outstanding players. He scored 18 goals in 32 league games, making  him Liverpool's top scorer for another season. He was included in the Premier League's ideal team and managed to round off a superb campaign with his return to the England side. But, apart from his goals, Robbie also stood out for his professional integrity. An example of that was the honest attitude he showed at Highbury when he appealed to the referee not to give a penalty - against Arsenal!
* Unfortunately for Liverpool Robbie missed the last three league games of the season after being sent off against Everton, his presence in the side obviously missed.

91.name: Martyn
pages: * Last season the Elland Road fans had the good fortune to be able to watch Nigel Martyn in action throughout the whole of the campaign. His excellent performances didn't go unnoticed by England manager Glenn Hoddle who gave him the opportunity to get back into the national squad. The now veteran goalkeeper sets out on the 97-98 season optimistically, hoping that his performances with Leeds United prove to be good enough to earn him a place in the England squad for the World Cup Finals in France.

* A keeper with tremendous experience, he has plenty of know how and possesses surprising agility for a man of his size and stature. He stands out for his ability in the air, an aspect of the game in which he is both  safe and decisive. His presence out on the park earns him the respect of opposing forwards, although, on occasions, he is over eager when he comes off his line. With his good positional sense, professionalism and experience, Martyn remains one of the best keepers in England.

* First Division winners medal 94.
* Third Division winners medal 90.
* Full Members Cup winners medal 91.

* 4 full international appearances for England. He made his debut on 29th April 1992 in Moscow against the Community of Independant States in a game which ended in a 2-2 draw. In June 1993 he was a member of England's  squad for the U.S. Cup, where he played in the side's final game which they lost against Germany in Detroit (1-2).
* 6 "B" international appearances.
* 11 under-21 international appearances.

* He came through the ranks at modest St Blazey, before signing professional for Bristol Rovers on 6th August 1987.
* After more than 100 league games for Bristol Rovers he was transfered to Crystal Palace for 1 million pounds on 21st November 1989.
* In the summer of 1994 he suffered a series of injuries and was forced toundergo a hernia operation. During the course of the 94-95 season he suffered a broken index finger which ended broke a run of 150 consecutive games. That season Crystal Palace were relegated to the First Division.
* During the summer of 1996 he was transfered to Leeds United for 2,250,000   pounds. He made his debut in the league on 17th August of that same year away at Derby County.
* At the end of his first season with Leeds he was voted the club's Playerof the Year by the Elland Road supporters.

* Without any doubt, Nigel Martyn was Leeds' best player throughout last season . He played in every game except one, the visit to Derby County in February. His outstanding performances also allow him to win back his place in the full England side, playing in a friendly against Mexico.  He ended the season with the honour of being the goalkeeper with most clean sheets to his name for the 96-97 season. As a result nobody was surprised when he was voted Player of the Year for the Elland Road club.

92.name: Beeney
pages: * Mark Beeney is Leeds' second choice goalkeeper. When John Lukic left Elland Road, everything seemed to suggest that it would be Beeney who would take over as number one in goal for Leeds. However, the signing of Nigel Martyn once again signalled a bleak future for Mark Beeney. Now in the shadow of the international goalkeeper, Mark will be hoping that he can take full advantage of the first opportunity that comes his way. Nevertheless he has a far from easy task on his hands.

* Despite his size, Mark Beeney is a very agile goalkeeper, which, together with his good reflexes, allows him to get to some very dificult balls, especially when he finds himself positioned on the goal line. Nevertheless, he is a keeper who likes to come out to try to get to crosses into the box, although he occasionally takes too much of a risk, leaving his goal completely unguarded. He needs more ganes to be able to settle down in the first team, and if he gets more experience under his belt, he could go on to become a good goalkeeper.

* After coming through the ranks at Gillingham, he made his league debut on New Years Day 1987 in a game against Walsall. 
* Maidstone United signed him on 31st January 1987 at a time when Beeney wasn't signed up with any club. In March 1990 he was loaned out to Aldershot. 
* On 28th March 1991 he was transfered to Brighton & Hove Albion for 30,000 pounds. 
* He took the step up to the Premier League on 20th April 1993, when Leeds United paid out 350,000 pounds to take him to Elland Road.
* Up to the 94-95 season he had kept a total of 37 clean sheets in the league. His average of goals conceded per game, up to that point was to  1.281. 
* He has been sent off 3 times during the course of his career, the last of those coming at Old Trafford in April 1996. Curiously, he was replaced in goal by defender, the Southafrican Lucas Rabede.

* Mark Beeney spent almost all of last season on the substitute bench. In fact, he played in just one league game, replacing the injured Nigel Martyn. His colleague's excellent performances denied him any chance of establishing himself in the Leeds side.

94.name: Molenaar
pages: * Although he arrived in England halfway through last season, Robert Molenaar didn't take long to adapt to the pace of the game in the Premier League. In his first game at Elland Roadé the Dutchman showed the supporters that George Graham had got it right when he decided to bring him to the club. Now, in the 97-98 season, he will be trying to consolidate himself as one of the best defenders in the Premier League.

* A central defender with great physical presence, he is very forceful in everything he does. At times hard, he has plenty of know how when it comes to winning possession for the side. Dominant in the air he also stands out for the intelligence and composure he shows in playing his way out of tight situations.
x
x

* After 6 seasons with Dutch club Volendam, Robert Molenaar was transfered to Leeds United on 11th January 1997 for 1 million pounds.
* He made his Premier League debut on 11th January 1997, in a game against Leicester City at Elland Road (3-0). He was chosen as Man of the Match in that particular game.
* He scored his first goal in England on 8th March 1997 in a 1-0 victory for Leeds against Everton at Elland Road.

* He arrived at leeds in January and immediately forced his way into George Graham's side. Despite being unknown in England, he didn't take long to win over the Elland Road supporters, and on the day of his debut was, in fact, voted Man of the Match. He scored a vitally important goal against Everton at Elland Road, clinching three points for the Whites.

95.name: Halle
pages: * Although, at the beginning of last season, he declared that 96-97 would be his last campaign in England, the truth is that Gunnar Halle was unable to resist the temptation of playing in the Premier League, once again, this time in the ranks of Leeds United. The Norwegian player had been hoping to return to Norwey to end his career there. However, George Graham now has him in his ranks at Elland Road, where he forms an important part of the managers plans. For the time being Gunnar Halle will have to postpone his journey home.

* A hardrunning right back, he stands out for his strength and pace. Halle constantly gets up and down the flank, making a tremendous physical effort and maintaining a tremendous work rate. He generally sets off  on runs from deep positions, making the most of his pace and direct approach to get himself to the edge of the opposition penalty area. Defensively he is an effective player, who is more practical than spectacular. He creates plenty of danger both when he pushes forward into the attack as wel as at set pieces situations.
x

* 54 full international appearances for Norwey.
* He was a member of Norway's squad in the 1994 World Cup Finals in the United States where he played in the games against Mexico and Ireland.

* He arrived in England in February 1991 from Norwegian club Lillestrom. 
* He made his league debut on 2nd February 1991, in a game against Oxford United. On 22nd August 1992 he scored his first goal in the English league against Nottingham Forest.
* He was on the point of being transfered to Leeds in September 1996. However Howard Wilkinson's sacking as manager saw the deal fall through. Nevertheless, in December of that same year he became George Graham's first signing since taking over in charge at the Elland Road club. The fee was set at 400,000 pounds.
* He made his debut for the Whites on 14th December 1996, in a game against Tottenham Hotspur at Elland Road (0-0).

* He began the season at Oldham Athletic, although it wasn't long before he received an offer from Leeds United. However the deal collapsed when Howard Wilkinson was sacked as manager of the club. It was December when George Graham authorized his signing, and he was immediately included in  the side. Due to his good performances he was able to make himself a regular right through to the end of the season.

96.name: Robertson
pages: * George Graham turned to David Robertson whe he was looking for someone to cover the gap left by Tony Dorigo's departure to Italian club Torino. The Scottish international possesses experience in top level competitions, something which was well valued by the Leeds United manager. Initially everything seems to suggest that Robertson will be a first team regular at Elland Road. All he needs is a touch of luck to help him out in his first year in England.

* A quick attack minded left back, he constantly pushes forward into attacking positions from where he gets over good crosses into the area. His international experience gives him plenty of know how which he makes the most of to play himself out of tight situations. Althouhg he is now a veteran player, he retains all of his pace as well as, most impotantly, his will to win.
* Scottish League Championship winners medals 92, 93, 94, 95, 96 and 97.

* 3 full international appearances for Scotland.
* An under-21 international.

* He began his professional career in 1986 with Aberdeen.
* In 1991 he was transfered to Glasgow Rangers, who he helped to win six consecutives league titles.
* On 13th May 1997 he was transfered to Leeds United for 500,000 pounds. His arrival at Elland Road coincided with the departure of Tony Dorigo to Italian club Torino.

* He played in 24 league games for Glasgow Rangers scoring 4 goals, the best total of his career. Once again he won a Scottish league championship winners medal with the club and retained his place in the side as first choice left back.

97.name: Haaland
pages: * Like many other Scandanavian footballers, Alf-Inge Haaland arrived in England in the hope of making a name for himself in one of the strongest championships in Europe. Last season proved that he has fully adapted to the Premier League, although his tremendous performances were sadly  overshadowed by the poor season that his side Nottingham Forest went through, eventually ending up relegated. Now he is setting out on a new adventure at Elland Road with a club, Leeds United, who have their sights set on the very top.

* A versatile player, he can play in a number of different positions. Although his natural qualities as a footballer make him a perfect right back, his well developed defensive ability allows him to do a good job at the heart of the defence, or, ocasionally in midfield. A good ballwinner, he has excellent positional sense. He is quick, hard,  dominant in the air and always gives 100%. However, he makes only a very limited attacking contribution and seldom gets involved in set pieces.
x
* 23 full international appearances for Norway.

* Alf-Inge Haaland began his football career in the ranks of Byrne SK, in his native Norway. After a brief spell with Swiss club Young Boys Berne, where he played alongside his compatriot Lars Bohinen, he was transfered to Nottingham Forest on 25th January 1994. Just one month earlier Bohinen had also arrived at the City Ground.
* He made his debut in the First Division on 6th February 1994. Forest won the game, at home, against Leicester City, 4-0. Few months later the club were celebrating their return to the Premier League. However in his first three seasons in England he was unable to make himself a regular member of the starting line up.
* In the 96-97 season he was part of the Nottingham Forest side that was relegated to the First Division. .
* On 12th June 1997 he was transfered to Leeds United for 1,600,000 pounds.

* Despite Nottingham Forest's disastrous season, which culminated in   relegation to the First Division, Alf-Inge Haaland showed some tremendous form both in midfield as well as in defence. The Norwegian international  scored 6 goals in 35 league games, including 2 against Arsenal in Stuart Pearce's first game as player-manager.

98.name: Jackson
pages: * Last season Mark Jackson demonstrated that, despite his youth, he has more than enough ability to look after himself in the Premier League. He is a part of George Graham's plans, and looks set to be given plenty of opportunities during the course of the 97-98 season. In fact it would be a surprise if he wasn't.

* A cental defender who stands out in the air, he can also play in midfield, where he makes the most of his good distribution. Still very young, he needs more time to become the finished article and acquire the experience needed in the Premier League. For the moment he remains one for the future. The club will need to see him play more regularly before they make a final decision.
x
x

* Born in Leeds and the product of the Elland Road youth system, Mark Jackson made his Premier League debut on 30th March 1996. Jackson came on for John Pemberton in the 80th minute of a game against Middlesbrough at Elland Road (0-1). He didn't get to play again all season.
* During the 96-97 season he played in 17 league games for the first team, winning the confidence of manager George Graham.

* Last season was the best so far of Mark Jackson's short career. The young defender, who came through the ranks at Elland Road, won the confidence of George Graham, who played him in 12 consecutive games, in which he  proved himself to be one of the most promising young players at Leeds United.

99.name: Harte
pages: * Born in Drogheda, the home town of teammate Gary Kelly, Ian Harte would no doubt be happy to go on to have as good a professional career as that of his uncle and club colleague at Leeds. For the moment he has given some excellent performances wich have demonstrated to both the coaching staff and the supporters that he is a player who could, at any time, take the step up to the first team.

* He can play in several different positions at the back, although his natural position is left back. A left footed player, he possesses good technique, is a good marker, and has tremendous pace which makes him a  very difficult player to beat for speed. He is dominant in the air and is capable of bringing the ball out from the back. He needs to gain more experience, although when he has played in the side he has always given an excellent account of himself.
x

* 11 full international appearances for the Republic of Ireland.
* 2 under-21 international appearances.

* He is the nephew of Garry Kelly, his club colleague at Leeds.
* He made his debut at Elland Road on 13th January 1996, coming on in place of Tomas Brolin in the 76th minute of the game against West Ham (2-0). Brolin had earlier scored both Leeds' goals.
* His first starting appearance came against Arsenal on 6th April 1996. Leeds were beaten 2-1 at Highbury and Harte was shown his first yellow card in the Premier League.

* He was one of the season's more pleasent surprises. He was given his chance by both Howard Wilkinson as well as George Graham, and the young defender took full advantage. He even allowed himself the luxury of scoring 2 league goals. He also firmly established himself in the Republic of Ireland side for which he is now almost an automatic choice.

100.name: Kelly
pages: * Garry Kelly is one of the most promising young Irish players around at the moment. Year after year, the young Leeds United player confirms  himself as one of the best right backs in the Premier League, putting together performances which have made him a regular in the Republic of Ireland side. He made his debut in the top flights at just 17 years of age, and this season sets out on his seventh at Elland Road. He has the experience and know how of a veteran, despite still being a very young player.

* A very strong, mobile full back. Although he needs to improve the technical side of his game, he is a magnificent defender, who it is very difficult to get the better of. Blessed with tremendous speed,  he is excellent at coming to the aid of is defensive colleagues when he covers across the back line as the last man in defence, while he has the pace to quickly get back into his own position. He doesn't generally make a decisive attacking contribution, an aspect of his game on which he needs to work. Consistent and a good marker, he keeps up a tremendous level of performances throughout the ninety minutes. Despite his youth he is an experience player who has great positional sense out on the park. Garry Kelly is, in short, a fine footballer who has a great future ahead of him.

* 21 full international appearances for the Republic of Ireland scoring once. He was a member of Ireland's squad in the 1994 World Cup Finals in the United States.
* 4 under-21 international appearances.

* He arrived at Leeds from modest Irish club Home Farm, not long after his 17th birthday on 24th September 1991. Shortly after he made his debut for the club in a league cup game against Scunthorpe. His league debut came on 22nd December 1991 against Nottingham Forest at the City Ground.
* He scored his first goal in the Premier League on 23rd November 1996, in a game against Southampton at The Dell (0-2).

* For the fourth consecurive season Garry Kelly was one of Leeds' most consistent players. He played in 36 league games making 32 starting appearances and managing to score his first 2 goals in the Premier League. Surprisingly, despite his excellent performances, he found himself left out of the Irish side n several occasions.

101.name: Wetherall
pages: * After 6 years at Elland Road, David Wetherall established himself as one of Leeds United's most important players. Season after season he tries to improve his game, working on both his weaknesses as well as  his strengths. Following the arrival of Robert Molenaar he had to make a real effort to keep his place in the starting line up. However, nobody is in any doubt that his presence in the side will be of great importance during the course of 97-98 season.

* A central defender in the classic English style, he stands out for his power in the air in defence as well as in attack. A hard player, he often has problems when he comes up against quick skillful strikers. He is much more comfortable when he is faced with forwards who rely more on physical power, a situation in which he can hide his weaknesses and lack of speed on the turn. Technically limited, he often has problems when he has to control the ball and lay it off to his teammates, preferring, in general to keep things simple and hit the ball long as quickly as possible. On the other hand, he posses a real threat for the opposition when he moves forward for free kicks and corners, situations where he scors plenty of goals due to the power of his heading ability. Physically fit, his contribution for Leeds would be greater if he improved the technical side of his game, something which, given his youth he could well achieve.

* Born in Sheffield, he began his career with one of the city's two big league clubs, Sheffield Wednesday. On 1st July 1989, he took the step up to Wednesday's first team squad, although he never made a league appearance for the club.
* On 15th July 1991 he was transfered to Leeds United together with John Newsome in a deal which totalled 125,000 pounds. His debut came at Elland Road on 3rd September 1991, in a game against Arsenal (2-2). He failed to make another appearance all season.
* Up to the end of the 94-95 season he had been booked 12 times.

* The arrival of the Dutchman Robert Molenaar in January added extra competition for a place at the heart of the defence. Until then David Wetherall had enjoyed regular first team football under both Howard Wilkinson as well as George Graham. As it turned out, he remained a first choice in the side for Graham, going on to play in a total of 29 league games.

102.name: Ribeiro
pages: * The absence of Lee Sharpe due to injury forced George Graham to look for a replacement who could be guaranteed to do a job. He found that guaratee in the figure of Bruno Ribeiro, a complete unknown for the Elland Road supporters. Nevertheless, Riberio, a Portuguese under-21 international, is confident that he will soon be known all over England.

* An attack minded midfielder, he generally operates down the left hand side. He possesses good vision and a good touch on the ball, and has the ability to beat a man. However he needs to acquire more experiece in order to make the most of his natural ability.
x
* Under-21 international for Portugal.

* He came thorugh the youth ranks at Vitoria Setubal, where he made his debut in the Portuguese First Division.
* On 6th August 1997 he was transfered to Leeds United for 500,000 pounds. The deal was rushed through as a result of the serious injury suffered by Lee Sharpe: ruptured cruciate ligaments.
* He spent last season with Boavista, who ended the season in Portugal near the foot of the Portuguese First Division.

103.name: Hopkin
pages: * David Hopkin is Leeds United's most expensive signing for the 97-98 season. Scottish international was one of outstading players in the First Division last season, and, thanks to a goal by him, Crystal Palace are now playing in the Premier League. He is still young and, above all, ambitious, a quality which George Graham values very highly in his players. He will be a player to watch out for next year, as he seems sure to be a member of Scotland's squad for the 1998 World Cup Finals in France.

* Hopkin generally plays on the right hand side of midfield, although he can play in other positions down the same flank or in the centre of the midfield. A hard working player, he wins plenty of possession and  is constantly helping out the defence, although he is a tremendously attack minded player who is well capable of finding the back of the net. He has a good shot with either foot, although he is stronger on the right.  He puts good accurate service through to the forwards, creating plenty of goalscoring opportunities. He is also effective in the air when he surprises defenders by coming late from deep positions.
x
* 2 full international appearances for Scotland.

* He signed for Morton in 1989 from amateur club Port Glasgow. He made his debut on 27th March 1990 against Forfar Athletic.
* He was transfered to Chelsea in September 1992 and played his first gamefor the club against Liverpool on 10th February 1993.  He scored his first goal as a professional on 3rd May 1995 against Everton.  *In July 1995 he was signed by Crystal Palace in exchange for 850,000 pounds. He made his debut on 12th August 1995 against Barnsley and scored his first goal against Oldham Athletic on 2nd March 1995.
* David Hopkin was the scorer of the goal that took Crystal Palace up to the Premier League in 1996. The goal came in the 90th minute of the play off final at Wembley.
* He was transfered to Leeds United on 21st July 1997 for 3,250,000 pounds.

* David Hopkin eneded the season being voted Player of the Year by the  Crystal Palace supporters. An automatic choice for the London side, his  goals and tremendous form were key factors in the clubs return to the Premier League following their victory over Sheffield United in the play off final at Wembley. Hopkin scored the winning goal in the 90th minute of that decisive game.
* Last season also saw the Scot make his debut for the national side, a deserved reward for one of the most outstanding players of the 96-97 season.

104.name: Maybury
pages: * Alan Maybury made his Premier League debut at just 17 years of age. With five Leeds players suspended, three on international duty in the African Nations Cup and Tomas Brolin ruled out by the manager, Maybury was given the opportunity to make his debut in the top flight of English football. However, Leeds were hammered by Aston Villa a Maybury quickly return to the reserve side, although, given his youth that is nothing for him to get worried about. Sooner or later he is bound to enjoy more opportunities.

* A defensive midfield player, he can play in a number of different positions in the centre of the park. He still needs to continue his development in the reserve side before taking the step up to the Premier League. Still very much in a learning proccess, he needs to be given time before a decision is reached as to how good he really is.
x
x

* Still a very young player, and a product of the club's youth system, he made his debut in a defeat against Aston Villa at Villa Park on 3rd February 1996 (3-0). He played from the start before being substituted by Mark Tinkler at half time.
* Last season he failed to make a first team appearance in the Premier League.

105.name: Blunt
pages: * Jason Blunt's first appearance at Elland Road, shortly after Leeds' defeat at Wembley against Aston Villa in the 1996 League Cup final, was a real breath of fresh air for the club's supporters. The side were losing 0-1 with their goalkeeper having been taken off injured. However, Blunt gave the supporters the impression that he was capable of turning the game around. He won a penalty and did everything he could. Leeds eventually lost the game but benefitted from the emergence of three young players: Harry Kewell, Mark Jackson and Jason Blunt.

* Jason Blunt is an attacking midfielder, very quick and with good techical ability. He distributes the ball intelligently and, in fact, stands out for his passing ability. A skillful player, he cuts through opposing defences with apparent ease, creating plenty of goalscoring chances. Blunt is an adventurous player who always tries to come up with something unexpected. He combines both youth and quality, and, if he maintains his progress, seems to be guarantee a bright future.
x
x

* After playing in the juniour sides at Elland Road, he was included in the first team squad for the 94-95 season, although he didn't get the opportunity to make his debut.
* His first game came at home on 30th March 1996, against Middlesbrough (0-1). Blunt came on in the 46th minute of the game after goalkeeper John Lukic had to go off due to a head injury. Blunt was immediately involved in the action, winning a penalty which was unfortunately missed by Gary McAllister. In the same game, defender Lucas Radebe took over in goal from Lukic. 
* During the 96-97 season he played in just one game: George Graham's first as manager of Leeds.

* He played in just one first team game, against Coventry, which was also George Graham's first in the hot seat at Elland Road. He spent the rest of the season in the reserve side, where he gave some tremendous performances.

106.name: Kewell
pages: * Harry Kewell is a footballer who, at just 18 years of age is still learning the game. Howard Wilkinson gave him his first opportunity during the 95-96 season, making his debut alongside Jason Blunt and Mark Jackson in Leeds' first game following the defeat in the League Cup final against Aston Villa. It was a way of showing the Elland Road supporters that the club's future players were coming through the youth ranks. One of those players is Harry Kewell. Everything now just seems to be a matter of time.

* An attack minded midfielder, Kewell also has the ability to play up front. Technically good he is quick and decisive when he pushes forward into the attack. His youth encourages him to play without inhibitions against veteran defenders, although occasionally he is let down by his lack of experience. With time and hard work he could go on to become an excellent footballer.
* F.A. Youth Cup winners medal 1997.
* Under-20 international for Australia.

* Born in Australia and a product of the Australian Sports Academy, he arrived at Leeds United in December 1996. He made his first team debut on 30th March 1996 in a game against Middlesbrough at Elland Road (0-1. Kewell was replaced in the 80th minute by Rod Wallace. Harry played in the game due to the absence through injury of goalscorer Tony Yeboah.   %% 
* On 3rd April he made another starting appearance at Elland Road, this  time against Southampton. Leeds won the game 1-0.

* He made just one first team appearance all season. That came with a brief few minutes of action against Tottenham in December. He spent the rest of the season alternating between the reserves and the youth team. However, he was called up once by Terry Venables to the Australian national Squad.

107.name: Gray
pages: * When Andy Gray made his league ebut in January 1996, he was just 19 years old. However, the Elland Road supporters soon realised that he had an awareness about him that was beyond his years. He quickly made himself a regular member of the side, and, although the team didn't have a brilliant season, Gray did an excellent job whenever he was called upon by the then Leeds manager Howard Wilkinson. If he maintains his progress he could well become a player who carves out a brilliant career for himself with the Elland Road club.

* He can play in several different positions in the midfield. He has reasonable basic technique, although he needs to improve that side of his game. He stands out, above all, for his defensive contribution, although that doesn't prevent him from moving forward at set pieces. Still very young, perhaps his greatest asset at the moment is the maturity he shows out on the park. Due to the physical and technical attributes he possesses, Andy Gray is a promising young footballer.
x
x

* He is the son of Frank Gray and nephew of Eddie Gray both ex-professional footballers.
* He came through the youth ranks at Leeds, making his first team debut on 13th January 1996, in a game against West Ham United at Elland Road.  (2-0). Gray came on in the 76th minute, replacing Rod Wallace.

* Andy Gray was dogged by bad luck throughout last season. He was called up 3 times for the Scottish under-21 squad but was forced to withdraw on each occasion due to injury. Fortunately, during the run in to the  end of the season he managed to make a handful of first team appearances for Leeds, enough to show the ability he possesses.

108.name: Sharpe
pages: * Lee Sharpe arrived at Elland Road in the summer of 1996 from Manchester United. Having had a taste of glory on more than one occasion during his time at Old Trafford, he will now be hoping to bring the same sort of  success to Leeds. In his first season at the club he didn't have too much good luck, however, in his second campaign, under the guidance of George Graham, he will be out to get back to his best form and help to try to put his teammates on the road to sucess.

* During his playing career, Lee Sharpe has played in a number of different positions, from left back to left winger, and even playing on both sides of the midfield. In the earlier stages of his career, he played well forward, almost as a left winger where he made the most of his speed and ability to take men on. With time, and, following the emergence of, amongst others, Ryan Giggs, he dropped back to play down the left hand side with the Welshman. He has excellent basic technique, which makes him a very valuable player for any side that basis its game on touch and pasing ability. A very mobile player, he helps out both in defence as well as in attack, getting forward quickly and finding the back of the net regularly. He also puts good crosses over into the penalty area for his teammates, helped out by his ability to reach the byline.
* A versatile player, he can even due job on the right hand side of the midfield, although he is not helped in that position by the fact that he is very much left footed. As a full back he has occasional lapses in concentration in defence, although he tries to make up for them with his tremendous physical attributes and harworking unselfish attitude. Lee Sharpe is a phenomenal player, who is still young and with a fine future ahead of him.

* League Championship winners medals 92-93,93-94 and 95-96. 
* F.A. Cup winners medals 93-94 and 95-96. 
* League Cup winners medal 91-92. 
* Charity Shield medal 94. 
* European Cup Winners Cup winners medal 91. 
* Voted Young Player of the Year by the Professional Footballer's Association 91.

* 8 full international appearances for England. He made his debut on 27th March 1991 against the Republic of Ireland at Wembley (1-1), in a qualifying game for the 1992 European Championships in Sweden. 
* 1 "B" international appearance. 
* 8 under-21 international appearances.

* After coming through the youth ranks at Torquay United, he made his debut for the first team on 3rd October 1987 against Exeter. However he didn't sign as a professional until 31st May 1988. 
* After an outstanding career in the Fourth Division he was transfered to Manchester United on 10th June 1988 for 185,000 pounds. 
* 1991 was a glorious year for Lee Sharpe: he won a European Cup Winners Cup winners medal beating Barcelona in the final (2-0), he also made his full England debut and rounded the season off by being named Young Player of the Year.
* The following season a serious injury kept him out of the side for several months.
* He stood out in the Champions League in the 94-95 season, scoring important goals against Gothenburg and Barcelona. Against the Spanish side, at Old Trafford, he scored a spectacular goal with a backheel. An ankle ligament injury put a halt to his progress during that season.
* On occasions he has shown a very peculiar way of celebrating his goals, taking hold of the corner flag, as though it were a microphone, and singing into it whilst imitating the king of rock, Elvis Presley.
* In August 1996 he was transfered to Leeds United for 4,500,000 pounds, making him the most expensive signing in the history of the club.
* He made his debut for Leeds on 17 August 1996, in an away game against Derby County (3-3).
* On 26th August 1996 he scored his first goal in a Leeds shirt, at Elland Road against Wimbledon (1-0).

* Injuries prevented Lee Sharpe from showing his best form for Leeds during his first season at Elland Road. In fact, he was unable to play at all during the months of January and February, a crucial time in any seasons. Despite that he was a first choice player whenever he was available, and gave glimpses of his undoubted clas, such as the fantastic goal he scored against Wimbledon in August.
