109.name: Radebe
pages: * When Lucas Radebe arrived at Elland Road, virtually nothing was known in Europe about South African football. In a short space of time, the English supporters have discovered that Radebe, as well as his compatriots Masinga and Williams, are capable of doing a good job at a high level of the game. Last season Radebe revealed himself to be one of the best man markers in the Premier League. Now in his fourth seasons in England, Radebe will be out to complete his adaptation to the game in Europe and make a contribution in the fight to get Leeds back to the top of the league.

* He can do a job as a central defender, although he is at his best when he plays as a midfielder just in front of the back four. Technically good, he takes on the responsibility of distributing the ball, a job he does very intelligently. He gets forward into the attack, help out by his  tremendous physical attributes, and is capable of quickly getting back into his defensive position. He needs time to fully adapt to English football, although, in the meantime, he shows touches of tremendous quality which make him a player to keep an eye on in the future.
* African Nations Cup winners medal 1996.
* 25 full international appearances for South Africa, host nation and winners of the 1996 African Nations Cup, with Radebe forming part of the winning side.

* On 17th April 1996, Leeds United were playing a league game at Old Trafford when goalkeeper Mark Beeney was sent off in the 18th minute. With no substitute goalkeeper on the bench for Leeds, Radebe pulled on the number one jersey and took up his position between the sticks. He made some excellent saves and kept his goal intact until, in the 72nd  minute, Roy Keane struck the winning goal for Manchester United 1-0.
* He had previously played in goal during the early stages of his career in South African. Later, playing for South African club Kaiser Chiefs, he developed his career as an outfield player.
* On 5th September 1994 he was transfered to Leeds for 250,000 pounds. One month earlier, his compatriot, Philomen Masinga, had also signed for the Elland Road club. Radebe made his league debut on 26th September of that same year at Hillsborough, coming on in the 64th minute in place of Mark Tinkler in a 1-1 draw between Leeds and Sheffield Wednesday .
* In March 1995 he suffered a serious injury to his cruciate knee ligaments, an injury from which he has now completely recovered.

* The 96-97 season was the most complete one yet in the career of Lucas Radebe. The South African defender finally settle down in the Leeds side and put together some sensational performances against strikers of the calibre of Cantona, Zola and Ravanelli. Radebe demonstrated that he is an outstanding marker and a player of real quality. As a result Leeds' board of directors decided to renew his contract for another three years.

110.name: Bowyer
pages: * Lee Bowyer is one of the best young players in England, and, as a result, Leeds were willing to pay out a tremendous amount of money in order to make him part of the squad in 1996. In just one season in the Premier League, Lee has justified his transfer fee. He has even been  knocking on the doors of Glenn Hoddle's England team. George Graham has full confidence in his ability to bring the glory days back to Leeds. The Elland Road fans are waiting for him to do just that.

* Bowyer shows class in everything he does.  He stands out in any midfield position, although his natural position is as a midfield playmaker. Blessed with outstanding technique he intelligently distributes the ball With apparent ease, making himself the focal point of the team's attacking play. Out on the park he shows a maturity beyond his years, dictating the pace of the game and spreading the ball around accurately. He has  natural leadership qualities as well as the ability to go on to become one of the best midfielders in the Premier League. It seems to be just a matter of time.

* 8 under-21 international appearances for England.
* A youth international.

* At just 17 years of age Lee Bowyer signed his first professional contract with Charlton Athletic, on 13th April 1994. He made his debut in the league cup against Swindon, and, shortly after, made his league debut against Watford.
* On 5th July 1996 he was transfered to Leeds United for 2,600,000 pounds, making him the most expensive teenager in England.
* He made his Premier League debut on 17th August 1996, in an away game against Derby County (3-3). Bowyer scored Leeds' third goal.
* In March 1997 he was named captain of the England under-21 side.

* During his first season at Elland Road Lee Bowyer made a tremendous impression. He scored on his debut, in the first game of the season, and soon made himself an automatic member of the side. Unfortunately he suffered a serious eye injury during the game against Manchester United in September. Once he had recovered he came back into the side and was even called up into the full England squad. Still very young, he was appointed captain of the England under-21 side in March. In short he was a great season for a highly promising young player.

111.name: Lilley
pages: * Derek Lilley was one of the surprise signings in the run in to the end of last season. He arrived at Elland Road with the reputation of being a fantastic goalscorer, something he had earned during his time with Morton. Nevertheless, he will need time to adapt to a competition as demanding as the Premier League, where defenders don't think twice about going in to win the ball and where they certainly don't give newcomers the benefit of a settling in period.

* A strong, quick strike, his presence in the penalty area always posses a threat for the opposition although he doesn't possess tremendous technical ability, his power, bravery and finishing ability make him a real nightmare for opposing defenders. He is good in the air and has a powerful shot with either foot, although he lacks the experience of competition at this level of the game.
x
* A Scottish Youth international.

* He came through the ranks at modest Everton Boys Club, but, in August 1991 he moved on to Scottish league club Greenock Morton.
* He was Morton's top goal scorer in 3 consecutive seasons.
* On 27th March 1997 he was transferd to Leeds United for 500,000 pounds . 
* He made his Premier League debut on 7th April 1997,in a game against Blackburn Rovers at Elland Road (0-0).

* He arrived at Leeds at the end of March with the reputation of being a genuine goalscorer. He made his debut in April against Blackburn Rovers and was given five other first team opportunities by George Graham.  However his appearances in the side weren't enough to see Lilley open His goalscoring account for Leeds United.

112.name: Hasselbaink
pages: * An inhability to find the back of the net was one of Leeds United's main problems during the course of last season. Manager George Graham new perfectly well what he needed fot the 97-98 season: a strong, goalscoring centre forward. He found exactly what he was looking for in the shape of Jimmy Hasselbaink, who arrived at Elland Road with the intention of setting out on a prolific goalscoring career in the Premier League.

* A classic centre forward, who stands out for his finishing ability. Strong, brave and decisive, he fights for every ball that finds its way into the opposition penalty area. His power allows him to get in attempts on goal from almost any position; with his head or with either foot. He holds the ball up well as he waits for his teammates to come through in support from the midfield. He is also very dangerous when he controls the ball and turns to go at defenders. Still very young, he could go on to make even more of the natural ability he possesses.
* Portuguese Cup winners medal 97.
x

* Born in Surinam in 1995 he made his debut in the Portuguese First Division, playing for Campomaiorense.
* In the summer of 1996 he was transfered to Boavista. In his first season at the club he made himself the team's top scorer with 27 goals and won a Portuguese Cup winners medal beating Benfica 3-2 in the final.
* On 12th June 1997 he was transfered to Leeds United for 2,000,000 pounds.

* Last season he scored 27 league goals for Boavista, just one less than the total scored by Leeds United in the Premier League. He stood out in the Portuguese cup final in which Boavista beat Benfica 3-2.

113.name: Wallace
pages: * In 1987, Rod Wallace's appearance in the top flight of English football created a sense of great expectations. The supporters found in Wallace a short but tremendously quick and spectacular footballer. Added to these qualities was his natural ability to find the back of the net, a talent possessed by only a chosen few. Nevertheless, for a number of different reasons, despite his ability he never really took off and, a player who could have gone on to become a genuine star, remained just a good footballer. He fell once step short of becoming a full international, something which may well have given his career the final push that it needed. However, the Elland Road supporters known, that, just when it is least expected, Rod is capable of going off on an electrifying run which he will frequently end with a goal.

* A very quick forward, he plays as a winger, operating out wide tight  on either touchline. Small, but full of quality, he makes the most of his pace to go past opponents, showing his tremendous ability to throw defenders off balance. He has a good shot and creates goalscoring opportunities with apparent ease. When he played alongside Tony Yeboah, they formed one of the fastest attacking partnerships in the Premier League. Wallace is a very complete footballer, whose only weakness is his lackof power in the air, something which is quite understandable given his height. When the main strikers drop deep, Wallace is able to find space in which he can make the most of his direct style of play. He is often at his most dangerous in the second half of games when his speed often proves to be decisive.

* League Championship winners medal 91-92. 
* Charity Shield medal 92.

* 1 "B" international appearance for England. 
* 11 under-21 international appearances scoring twice.

* A member of a footballing dynasty, at Southampton he played alongside his brother Danny his cousing Ray. He joined Southampton as schoolboy in December 1983 and became an apprentice in July 1986. He made his first team debut on 26th September 1987 against Newcastle at St James' Park. In his second game as a professional he scored a goal at Anfield giving Southampton a point against Liverpool.
* During the 89-90 season he formed part of an outsanding forward line at Southampton alongside Alan Shearer and Matt Le Tissier.
* On 7th June 1991 he was transfered to Leeds for 1,600,000 pounds. An automatic first choice during his first seasons at the club, he had his best campaign in 1994 when he was Leeds' top scorer with 17 goals.
* Wallace was highly rated by previous manager Howard Wilkinson, who rejected an offer from Southampton of 1,500,000 pounds in an attempt to take him back to The Dell.

* He was Leeds' top scorer last season, reserving his best performances for the F.A. Cup and the League Cup. In a league Cup he scored 3 times, as he also did in the Premier League, while he scored twice in F.A. Cup. His goals in the F.A. Cup against Crystal Palace and Arsenal were particularly spectacular. However, Rodney Wallace was an inconsistent performer, alternating his good games with a number of poor performances.

114.name: Given
pages: * In Seamus John Given Newcastle have captured the services of one of the best keepers in the Premier League.  Although last season he hardly played, Kenny Dalglish has shown a lot of faith in Shay Given, who despite his youth has more than demonstrated the extraordinary progress he has made. He is a serious candidate to dislodge either Shaka Hislop or Czech Republic international Pavel Srincek from the first team. Very sure of himself and aware of his potential, Given knows that establishing himself in the Premier League is just a matter of time, and may happen sooner rather than later.

* Despite his youth and logical inexperience Shay Given has already shown signs of being an extraordinary keeper as well demonstrating a surprising level of maturity. He possesses enviable reflexes which allow him to make some incredible stops, backed up by his excellent positional sense. Dominant in the air and effective in one on one situations, he looks every inch a brave safe keeper, very complete and, above all, has a promising future ahead of him.
* First Division champion's medal 96.

* Nine full international appearances for Eire. 
* Under 21 international. 
* Youth international.

* A full international for the Republic of Ireland, Shay Given seemed destined to become a regular in goal for Glasgow Celtic where he had played youth team football. The Scottish club however allowed him to leave and on 8th August 1994 Given became third choice keeper at Blackburn Rovers. At that time Tim Flowers and Bobby Mimms were the two first team goalkeepers. 
* Unable to dislodge Tim Flowers one of the best keepers in England from the goalkeeping spot, Blackburn sent the young Shay Given out on loan to Swindon Town on 4th August 1995. There he played in five games, conceding just one goal.
* On 19th January 1996 he went out on loan once again, this time to Sunderland. In the space of just 17 games he became one of the idols of the Sunderland fans, his tremendous performances proving to be a decisive contribution in the club's promotion to the Premier League. Shay had such a spectacular impact on the sidethat there was speculation that he might move to the "Rokerites" on a permanentbasis. However, the departure of Bobby Mimms to Bradford City meant that he became an automatic second choice as Blackburn keeper, in the shadow of Tim Flowers.
* He has been a Newcastle player since 31st May 1997. A tribunal set his transfer fee at £1,500,000. Given signed a four year contract with the Saint James' Park club.

* Given played in just 2 league games all season. In both of those games he showed himself to be a class act in goal. Unfortunately for him, manager Tony Parkes decided to trust in the experience of Tim Flowers in the fight to avoid relegation. Not getting regular first team action for Blackburn, Shay lost his place as the Republic of Ireland's first choice goalkeeper.

115.name: Hislop
pages: * The signing of Shay Given has made matters much more complicated for Newcastle's goalkeepers in the fight to make the goalkeeping jersey their own. Shaka Hislop who last time out was Kenny Dalglish's first choice has seen his priviliged position come under real threat. The giant keeper remains determined to make it all the way to the full England side and also hopes to one day get a league title triumph under his belt. With these aims in mind, it seems certain that a player with the ambition of Shaka Hislop will no doubt relish the battle with Given and Srnicek for a place in the team.

* Shaka Hislop, at 1.98m tall is a very safe keeper in the air. His size together with his extraordinary leaping ability allows him to dominate the situation catching balls that would be practically impossible for many other keepers. Despite his great physical presence, Hislop stands out for the speed and agility of his movements, all of which goes to make him a very complete all round keeper. However, he does occasionally commit errors which he should try to put right.
* Authoritative in the area, he knows how to position his defenders, and is also capable of showing tremendous coolness in tight situations, a characteristic which must be taken into account. Despite the short period of time that he has spent competing at the highest level, Hislop has quickly learned from the experience he now has underhis belt and currently, is well established as a fine competent keeper.
* Second Division Championship winner medal 1994.
x

* An engineer by profession before dedicating himself to professional football he worked for NASA at Cape Kennedy. 
* He signed for Reading on 9th September 1992 from a university team in the United States ( Howard University). He went on to become an undisputed first team choice during the 1993-94 and 94-95 seasons, playing in 46 league games.
* Chosen as Reading's player of the year by the club's supporters for the year 1995 he was also chosen as the First Division's best goalkeeper by the Professional Footballer's Association.
* On 10th August 1995 he was tranfered to Newcastle United for £1,575,000, despite interest being shown by a number of other clubs.
* He made his Premier League debut in the first league game of the 95-96 season on 19th August 1995. The "Magpies" defeated Coventry by 3 goals to nil at St. James' Park. In December he suffered an injury which kept him out of action for four months.
* In 1995 Hislop turned down the opportunity to become a full international for Trinidad and Tobago, feeling confident that one day he would go on to play for England.
* He is the brother of Kona, a striker who signed for Hartlepool United in September 1996.

* During the course of last season Shaka Hislop played in a total of 16 league games, all of those as a member of the starting line up. Although missing from the Charity Shield, he was in goal for the first league game of the season. He paid the price however for Newcastle's defeat against Everton and was replaced by Srnicek the following game. He returned to the team for the final game of the year, a 7-1 thrashing of Tottenham, and managed to keep his place until flu prevented him playing in the final four league games of the season..

116.name: Srnicek
pages: * These are not easy times for Pavel Srnicek at Saint James' Park. The Czech goalkeeper, a very popular figure with the Newcastle faithful has seen how the signing of Shay Given has greatly affected his chances of winning back his place in the first team. Kenny Dalglish now has at his disposal three goalkeepers of recognised quality, a situation which could well mean that one of the three won't finish the season at the club. In the wake of the rumours that were doing the rounds last season, Pavel Srnicek seems the likely favourite to leave Saint James' Park.

* A very agile keeper, Pavel Srnicek shows extraordinary reflexes between the posts, a quality which enables him to make some incredible saves. His game lacks consistency however, his preformances being something on the erratic side alternating between tremendous moments and calamitous errors. Srnicek is a keeper who goes through different spells. When he puts together a run of good performances he is well capable of proving a difficult man to beat. More comfortable when asked to get down to low shots he is still capable of polishing up his errors and improving his overall game.

* First Division championship winners medal 1993.
* European championship runners up medal 1996.

* 8 full international appearances for Czech Republic.
* Srnicek made his debut on 12th October 1994 in a game against Malta in LaValetta (0-0).
* A member of his country's squad for the European Championships in England 1996 he couldn't manage to get into the side.

* Whilst playing for Banik Ostrava one of the most important clubs in the now defunct Czecoslovakia Newcastle's interest in signing him was finally formalized when he joined the English club on 5th February 1991. The fee was £350,000.
* He made his league debut on 17th April 1991 in a game against Sheffield Wednesday.
* Little by little Srnicek forced his way into Newcastle's first team line up, managing to become an undisputed first choice during the 1994-95 season, a campaign which also saw him make his international debut for the Czech Republic. The arrival however of Shaka Hislop in August 1995 saw him once again relegated to the reserves. Only a serious injury suffered by Hislop in December in a game against Chelsea allowed him to return in goal for the "Magpies". But almost as soon as he had taken up his position in goal at Stamford Bridge he could only watch as the Rumanian Petrescu hit the ball past him and into the back of the net.

* He kept up a constant battle with Shaka Hislop for the first team goalkeeping spot, with Srnicek making more appearances (22). He lost his place however after a defeat against Blackburn at Ewood Park. He failed to win the backing of new manager Kenny Dalglish, givibg rise to rumours regarding Pavel's possible departure from the club.

119.name: Griffin
pages:
* Signed for Newcastle during the 97-98 season.
* Andrew Griffin is a product of the well-groomed Stoke City youth squad, a squad that has produced a lot of interesting players in recent times.  His great performance last year aroused the interest of some Premier League clubs. A man for the future but who is already a reality.  His progress, if all goes well, could bring him to the England team one day.  He has already played for the England youth team.

* Griffin is a young player who occupies the position of left back.  He is very solid and complete when doing his job, never getting in a fret and always keeping calm, notable facets in a player so young.  He pushes up his touchline well, playing one-twos with a team-mate and he gets into dangerous positions in the rival box as he has shown on several occasions.
x
x

* Originally from the lower ranks of Stoke City, Griffin signs as a professional on the 5th of September 1996.  His debut occurs on the 26th of October against Portsmouth and he scores his first goal against Grimsby town, his only goal to date for the team, on the 5th of March.

* Griffin had a sensational first season at Stoke City, bursting into the first team aged just 17.  After taking the place from Nigel Worthington, he settled into the side and his raids down the left wing brought a lot of danger and he even scored a goal.  In total he played 34 games and scored 4 goals.

120.name: Hamilton
pages: * Des Hamilton is a promising young footballer. He arrived at St. James' Park inMarch 1997, immediately sparking rumours of the possible departure of Frenchman David Ginola. Months later, Ginola was signing for Tottenham while the doors to the Newcastle first team were opening up for Hamilton. Nevertheless it won't be easy for him to force his way into Kenny  Dalglish's line ups. He has all the time in the world on his side, although his lack of experience will be a factor clearly working against him.

* Hamilton's natural position is as a right-sided midfielder although he can also do a job down the opposite flank. His speed allows him to take on rival defenders getting to the by-line from where he delivers accurate crosses to the strikers. A very consistent performer he is capable of a high level of effort, mainting it throughout the ninety minutes. He works hard in defence, aggressively keeping opponents under pressure. He possesses a good touch on the ball and reasonable dribbling skills, although on occasion he can to do too much on his own. A very promising young player Hamilton needs to develop more confidence in front of goal and, above all, get more experience under his belt.
x
* One under 21 international appearance for England.

* After coming through the ranks at Bradford City he finally signed as a professional in June 1994. His first team debut on 3rd May 1994 could have been better, managing to find the back of the net against Barnet. 
* He has been a Newcastle player since 3rd March 1997. His transfer fee was  set at £1,500,000.

* Hamilton was one of the season's revelations in the First Division. An automatic choice for Bradford City, he became the perfect foil for the team's strikers creating inumerable goal chances for his teammates. His magnificent performances took him to the England Under-21 side for whom he made his debut against Poland. Transfered to Newcastle on the final day before the transfer deadline he didn't manage to make his Premier League debut.

121.name: Pearce
pages:
* Stuart Pearce is one of the most charismatic players in English football. At 33 he remains a key member of the national side which he's captained. At the City Ground he was genuine idol. His love of Nottingham Forest saw him take on the job of manager at a very difficult time for the club. Stuart was unable to save Forest from the drop, but once again he gave everything he had right to the very end..
* Kenny Dalglish decided that the ex-Forest man's experience would prove to be of great value to Newcastle so he took him on a free transfer. Now only time will tell whether or not the Magpies' boss made the right decision.

* Pearce plays at left back, standing out for his power, aggressive style of play and tight marking. He continually gets forward down the flank making the most of his speed, showing great accuracy in his crossing. As time has gone by however he has lost some of his mobility and has tended to play too many long balls, often not particularly thoughtfully. What undoubtedly has remained intact is the power and accuracy of his left foot when shooting at goal, something which makes it almost impossible to miss penalties, making him a real threat from free kicks around the edge of the box.
* In recent times Pearce has also lined up as a central defender, a position where he feels comfortable given that the physical effort required is less than that demanded of a fullback. As a central defender his experience also allows him to calmly take care of tight situations.

* League Cup Winners medals 89 and 90. 
* Full Members Cup Winners medals 89 and 92.

* 76 full international appearances for England, scoring five times he made his debut on 19th May 1987 at Wembley against  Brazil (1-1) in a game which formed part of the Rous Cup tournament. He scored his first goal on 25th April1990; England defeated Czecoslovakia at  Wembley (4-2).
* As a member of England's squad in the 1990 World Cup Finals in Italy he was a member of the starting line up in all games, against Eire (1-1), Holland (0-0), Egypt (1-0), Belgium (1-0), Cameroon (3-2) and Germany (1-1). In the semi-final against Germany Pearce missed his spot kick in the penalty shootout and England were eliminated. 
* In the 1992 European Championship in Sweden in 1992 Pearce played in the three first phase games against Denmark (0-0), France (0-0) and against the host nation (1-2). England couldn't manage to make it through to the quarter final stage.
* As captain of the England side during the 1996 European Championships staged in England he was a member of the starting line up in the five games which Terry Venables side played. Up until they were eliminated by Germany (1-1) England had played against Switzerland (1-1), Scotland (2-0), Holland (4-1) and Spain(0-0).
* One Under 21 international appearance.

* Stuart Pearce began his career with Wealdstone, a club he joined as a youth team player in 1978. His father, a Queens Park Rangers supporter, endevoured to get his son to play for the West London Club, and as a result, Stuart spent a number of months on trial at Loftus Road.
* On 20th October 1983 he signed for Coventry for £l25,000. He made his league debut on 12th December 1983 in a game ironically against Queens Park Rangers. From that moment on he was an automatic first team choice for the wholeof the 20 month spell he had at Highfield Road.
* On 3rd June 1985 he was surprisingly transfered to Nottingham Forest together with Ian Butterworth in exchange for £200,000. He made his debut on 17th August of that same year in Forest's visit to Luton Town. 
* Pearce was known as "Psycho" amongst the City Ground faithful, for the commitment, determination and physical effort he puts into every game. Withouth doubt, he went onto become the club's greatest idol since Duncan McKenzie.  
* A league cup winner in both 1989 and 1990, it was unfortunately also in 1990 when he experienced one of the worst moments if his career. Pearce missed from the spot in the penalty shoot out of the 1990 World Cup Semi final in Italy against Germany, a miss which saw England eliminated from the competition..
* In 1992, with Forest, he won the Zenith Data Systems Cup after beating Southampton 3-2 in the final.
* As captain of both Nottingham Forest and the England side during Terry Venable's time as manager, Pearce encapsulated one of the representative images of the 1996 European Championships, staged in England. In the quarter finals the England team's passage through to the semi-finals was hanging by the thread of a dramatic penalty shoot out against Spain. This time Stuart was on target and his gesture of defiance and determination went out on T.V. screens right around the world.
* On 20th December 1996 he was named player manager of Nottingham Forest. He took over from Frank Clark who had resigned two days earlier. At that time Forest were well down the table in the relegation places to the First Division. Despite Pearce's efforts, Forest were unable to stay in the Premier League..
* With his time at the City Ground having come to an end he signed for Newcastle on 18th July 1997.

* It was a special season for Stuart Pearce. In December following the resignation of manager Frank Clark he was named player manager of Nottingham Forest. In January he was voted "Manager of the Month". Despite the technical help of Dave Bassett however  Pearce was unable to avoid the club being relegated. It was a real blow forPearce, a member of the starting line up in all 33 of the league games in which he played. He scored five goals two of those coming from the penalty spot.
* Despite the problems at Forest, England manager Glen Hoddle continued to show faith in Stuart, considering him a key member of the squad in England's battle to qualify for the World Cup Finals in France in 1998.

122.name: Pistone
pages: * At just 22 years of age, Alessandro Pistone decided to take an important step in his short professional career and accepred Newcastle's offer. In this respect Pistone, one of the most promising young players in Italy, is following the example of some of his home country's most prestigious footballers; men like Zola, Di Matteo, Vialli Carbone who are all enjoying great success in the Premier League. Kenny Dalglish is trusting in Pistone to cover the departure of Robbie Elliott. With his signing Newcastle have undoubtedly been given an injection of both youth and quality.

* Despite being right footed his natural position is at left back. Nevertheless he can also operate down the opposite flank. He is very quick and effective at the back, but is totally attack minded. He has acceptable technical ability and can cross the ball with reasonable accuracy. What stands out most about Pistone is his tremendous speed, something which makes him very difficult to beat for those opponents he plays directly against. He is capable of creating problems for opposing midfield players who see themselves forced to cover the many forward runs he makes.
* European Under-21 Championship Winners medal with Italy in 1996.

* Five Under-21 international appearances for Italy. In Barcelona '96 he was a member of the victorious Italian side.
* Two appearances as an Olympic International. He played in the 1996 Olympic Games in Atlanta.

* Pistone was born in Milan and grew up in a street called Via Capecelatro which, ironically, leads to the Piazzale de San Siro, the name of course of the famous home of Milan's two clubs.
* He first played football for Alcione, from there moving onto Milan's youth teams. He was later sent out on loan to Aldini a club which is closely linked to Milan.
* He made his debut for Inter on 29th November 1995 against Lazio in an Italian Cup match which ended 1-1.
* Despite being right footed, he has lined up down the left hand side ever since Luciano Zecchini, his coach at Solbiate, played him in that position. 
* His signing for Inter produced a conflict of emotions, remembering that he had always declared himself to be an A.C. Milan supporter. 
* In 1997 he was a member of the starting line up in both legs of the U.E.F.A. Cup final. Inter lost against German side Schalke 0-4 in the penalty shoot out.
* He has been a Newcastle player since 27th July 1997. His transfer fee was set at £4,300,000.

* In his first full season with Inter, Alessandro played in 26 League games. He was first choice in the majority of those games, although on occasions manager Roy Hodgson played the Argentinian Zanetti  in his position, or even the Frenchman Angloma. Lining up in the U.E.F.A. Cup final against Schalke 0-4, he was unable to prevent Inter from going down in the penalty shoot out.

123.name: Albert
pages: * It's more than possible that Philippe Albert ends his playing career with Newcastle. At Saint James' Park he has found the ideal place to show off his elegant style of play. Perfectly adapted to the Premier League and well loved by the clubs supporters, Philippe is confident that he will continue to be given the opportunity to show off his talent in the stadiums of England. Newcastle fans as well as Kenny Dalglish will also be hoping this is the case.

* A left footed player his good technical ability allows him to play in a number of positions, although with Newcastle he generally lines up at the heart of defence. Calm and collected when required to do a containing job, he is very solid when going in to win the ball thanks to his positional play and his sense of anticipation. Backed up by his excellent physique he is dominant in the air in both penalty areas while his presence in the attack is a real source of danger. His basic defensive ability and speed also allow him to play as aleft back.
* He has played a good many games in midfield where he can make the most of his ability to get forward into the penalty area. His distribution is thoughtful and accurate and he also possesses a powerful shot in his left foot. A good penalty taker, he regularly gets on the scoresheet. Albert is a very complete footballer, capable of doing a number of different jobs, and remains disciplined and hardworking throughout the ninety minutes. With plenty of experience under his belt showing genuine leadership qualities the Belgian has a wide range of attacking and defensive qualities which make him avery valuable player for his club.

* Belgian League Championship Winners medals 88-89, 92-93 and 93-94. 
* Belgian Cup Winners medal 93-94. 
* Belgian footballer of the year 91-92.

* 42 full international appearances for Belgium scoring five times. 
* Albert made his full international debut on 29th April 1987 against Eire in a qualifying  European Championship game against Germany, played in Dublin.
* He scored his first goal for the national side against France in Paris (3-3).
* A member of his country's squad in the World Cup Finals in Italy in 1990 and in the United States in 1994. In the second of these tournaments he was a member o fhis country's starting line up and managed to score the goal that beat Holland.

* Philippe Albert was born in Bouillon, a Village in the Ardennes, a French speaking region of Belgium. He took his first steps in the world of football with Standard Bouillon, later signing his first professional contract with Charleroi.
* After making his full international debut at the age of 19 under the guidance of then national manager Guy Thys, he had to wait another year and a half before being called up again.
* In the summer of 1989 he was transfered to KV Mechelen but injuries prevented him from finding his best form. Even so he managed to recover and get back to his best in time for the 1990 World Cup in Italy.
* His extraordinary progress immediately won over Paul Van Himst, who had succeeded Guy Thys as manager of the Belgian national side. Under Van Himst he was an automatic choice, to the point of being named captain of the nationalside.
* At the end of the 91-92 season he was transfered to Anderlecht, one of the most powerful clubs in Belgium.
* His tremendous performances in the World Cup in the United States didn't go unnoticed by the Newcastle coaching staff. On 10th August 1994 he signed for the Magpies for four seasons in exchange for £2,650,000. He made his debut on 21st of that same month in a 1-3 victory away at Leicester City. He scored his first goal in a Newcastle shirt on 16th October that same year against Manchester United.
* In December 1994, while he was training, he suffered ruptured knee ligaments which kept him out of acion for a number of months.
* He is known to the Newcastle fans as "Prince" Albert.
* On 25th July 1996 he extended his contract with the St. James' Park club until the year 2000.

* Last season Albert played in 27 league games, all of those as a member of the starting line up. He scored 2 goals in the 5-0 thrashing of Manchester United. It wasn't an easy campaign for the Belgian international who saw himself out of the side on too many occasions; sometimes due to injury, other times for tactical reasons. In March he was forced to undergo a knee operation which prevented him from returning to the side until the run in to the season.

124.name: Watson
pages: * Despite his youth Steve Watson is setting out on his seventh season in Newcastle's first team squad, and everything seems to indicate that he will go on to defend the colours of Newcastle United for plenty of years yet, especially after extending his contract in March 1996 for another four years. Watson, who made his debut at just 16 years of age, has already become a very mature footballer, secure, and above all, versatile. Kenny Dalglish has full confidence in him, something which would seem to indicate that he will continue to be a first team regular throughout the 97-98 campaign.

* The principle characteristic of Steve Watson's game is his versatility. He can play either at right back, in the heart of the defence as a right sided midfield player, or even on occasions as a striker. Strong, with tremendous reserves of stamina, he fights for every ball in defence and never hesitates to go in hard. When he has the ball his distribution is thoughtful backed up by good basic technique. His game however lacks a little creativity, which if added to his range of ability would make him a less predictable footballer then he currently is.
* Despite not being a natural goalscorer - on the occasions when he has played up front - he has managed to get on the scoresheet, thanks to his powerful shooting.
x

* 12 under-21 international appearances for England, scoring once. 
* 13 times an England youth international.

* Steve Watson's career history includes a record; he was the youngest player ever to make his debut in the League for Newcastle. He did so on 10th November 1990 in a game against Wolverhampton Wanderers. Watson was 16 years and 223 days old.
* A product of Newcastle's youth system, he signed as a professional on 6th April  1991.
* He scored his first goal on 29th February 1992 against Port Vale. 
* In the 94-95 U.E.F.A. Cup he found the back of the net against Belgian side Royal Antwerp.
* An England Under-21 international, in 1995 he had the honour of playing against Eire in front of his home supporters at St. James' Park.

* Once again Steve Watson produced more evidence of his tremendous versatility. Although  he played most of the games at right back he had no problem in adapting to line up at the centre of defence, in midfield, or even along the forward line if considered necessary. He proved that he was a progressive footballer managing to keep the clubs other right back,  Warren Barton, firmly on the bench. A memberof the starting line up in 33 of the 36 league games in which he played, he scored just once - unusually low for him - in a game against  Coventry. In March he renewed his contract for another four years.

125.name: Howey
pages: * Steve Howey is a well loved player at Newcastle, it not being anycoincidence that he has spent the whole of his playing career with the "Magpies".During the course of his career he has experienced promotion from the Second to theFirst Division, the club's breakthrough into the Premier League and theirestablishing themselves as one of the best teams in England. A classical defender inthe purest British Style, his progress has taken him as far as the England side, andalthough luck seems to have deserted them over recent seasons Howey remainsconfident that the side will soon be winning a trophy with which they can toast the St. James' Park faithful.

* Althougn at the moment he is currently playing in the centre of the defence,a position  where he does an excellent job, at the beginning of his career he started out as a centre forward. A player with a tremendous physical presence, he stands out for his ability in the air in either penalty area. He generally proves to be very consistent in his defensive duties showing good positional sense and responsibility never hesitating to go in hard in he feels he has to, although he i occasionally guiltyof the odd calamitous error. Technically limited he only very rarely gets involved inthe attacking side of the game, although he will move forward for corners and freekicks where his size allows him to get his head to the ball and occasionally find the backof the net.
* Steve Howey has suffered a number of injuries which have put back his progress. Even so, he has gone on to become a fine defender, though he still has plenty of room forimprovement.
* First Division championship winners medal 92-93.

* Four full international appearances for England.
* He made his debut on 6th November 1994 in a friendly against Nigeria atWembley (1-0). He didn't return to the national side until more than a yearlater in another friendly, also at Wembley, against Portugal (1-1). Initiallycalled up by Terry Venables to play in the 1996 European Championshipsin England, an unfortunate injury just a few days before the start of thecompetition forced him to miss out.

* The younger brother of  Sunderland striker Lee, Steve Howey is a product of the Newcastle youth systeem. He made his first team debut on 13th May 1989 in a game against Manchester United. He was then just 17 years old and still hadn'tturned professional. He later signed professional terms on 11th December that same year.
* After failing to make an appearance during the whole of the 89-90 season,little by little he managed to force his way into the team, until he became anautomatic first team choice during the 92-93 season, when he was a key memberof the team that won  promotion to the Premier League.
* A full international since November 1994 his appearances with the national sidehave been sporadic. Although included in England's squad for the 1996 EuropeanChampionships, injury forced him to miss the tournament. 
* During the 1996-97 season injuries prevented him from playing in no more than the opening 8 games of the season.

* Throughout last season Steve Howey was constantly dogged by bad luck.He started the first 8 games of the campaign but was kept out of action for the rest of the season by injury. He was in fact forced to undergo surgery on two separateoccasions before he could finally get back into training in March 1997.

126.name: Peacock
pages: * Since his arrival at St. James' Park in 1994, Darren Peacock became a key member of the Newcastle United line up. Unmistakeable with his long pony tail trailing behind he has suffered more than most the disappointments which the club has experienced in recent years. Nevertheless, Darren will be hoping that lady luck will smile on him and that he will soon get the opportunity to get a real taste of glory.

* Strong and aggressive, Peacock is a classical central defender, hard working and well equipped to get out of the tightest of situations against rival forwards. Though good in the air he has problems when coming up against more skillful strikers who he tries to stop by outwitting them, backed up as always by his physical power. On occasions a hard  player, he never hesitates to go in witha tackle.
* In an attacking sense, Peacock's contribution is limited, needing as he does to improve his ball control and the accuracy of his passing. Although he generally moves forward to get his head to the ball at dead ball situations, it is very rare to see him get on the scoresheet.
* Welsh Cup Winenrs medal 1990.
x

* Peacock took his first steps in the football world with Bristol Rovers, a club he joined as an apprentice in September 1983. In August 1984 he had a trial with modest Welsh outfit Newport County with whom he eventually made his league debut on 14th September 1985 against Plymouth. Despite having made his debut he would have to wait until 11th February 1986 before turning professional.
* In October 1986 he suffered a serious injury preventing him from getting back into action until April 1988. 
* After becoming a free agent he signed for Hereford United on 23rd March 1989.
* His outstanding performances opened up the doors to the top flight of English football and on 22nd December 1990 he was transfered to Q.P.R. for £200,000.
* After 126 games and 6 goals for the West London Club, he was transfered to Newcastle on 24th March 1994. The St. James' Park club paid £2,700,000 for his services. He made his league debut on 29th March in a home game against Norwich Citywhich ended in a 3-0 victory for the Magpies.
* He scored his first goal or Newcastle on 3rd May 1995 in a game against Tottenham Hotspur at St. James' Park (3-3).
* Up to the end of the 94-95 season he had been booked on 23 occasions although he had  never been sent off.

* Although he missed the first three league games of the season Darren put together a run of 35 consecutive league games as a member of the starting line up becoming the club's most frequent performer throughout the season. Solid and efficient in his defensive duties, there was talk of his possible inclusion in the Welsh national side. Manchester United were on the receiving end of the only goal he managed to score all season.

127.name: Barton
pages: * It took Barton a lot of hard work to finally get to play for a team that had aspirations of winning the Premier League. In 1995 the English international defender, was for a few days the most expensive signing in Newcastle's history, with the prospect of a trophy filled future at  Saint James' Park beckoning. However, after two seasons in the team he is yet to achieve everything he might have hoped when he signed. Now under the guidance of Kenny Dalglish he will be fighting to make himself an automatic first team choice, and along the way pick up the first medals of his career.

* Warron Barton can play either as a right back or in midfield down the same flank, although it is at the back where he has shown his best form. A very mobile player, Barton fits the description of a modern full back or wing back appearing along the whole of the right hand side and getting involved as much up front as he does at the back. Fast and disciplined, Barton is a difficult defender to beat for speed, brave when going into tackles with opposing forwards. Although technically sound in possession he doesn't stand out for the accuracy of his passing. Nevertheless his hard work and constant supporting of the side's attacks gives him the chance to enjoy plenty of opportunities to put dangerous crosses into the Penalty area.
x

* 3 full international appearances for England.
* He made his debut in 1995 in a game against Eire.
* 3 B international appearances.

* Barton signed for Maidstone United from modest Leytonstone on 28th July 1989. His price: £10,000. An automatic first team choice in his first season he made his debut on 19th August 1989 in a game against Peterborough United.  
* On 7th June 1990 he was transfered to Wimbledon for £300,000. His transfer was carried out personally by Bobby Gould who was sacked the day after his signing. Nevertheless Gould's replacement Joe Kinnear had full faith in Barton. His first game for the "Dons" came at Highbury against Arsenal, although Barton didn't play from the start of the game.
* An England international since 1995, his first appearance was memorablefor all the wrong reasons. His first game in an England shirt was the infamous game in Dublin which had to be abandoned due to incidents in the crowd. 
* Barton was transfered to Newcastle on 5th June of that same year for £4,500,000, making his debut in the first game of the season (19-8-95) against Coventry at St. James' Park, in a 3-0 victory for the "Magpies".

* A disappointing season for Warren Barton who could only watch as Steve Watson made the right back spot his own for a large part of the season. Barton's situation improved with the arrival of Kenny Dalglish in the Newcastle hot seat. Under Dalglish he played in 14 games as a member of the starting line up. In one of those games, against Liverpool at Anfield, Warren scored his first goal as a Newcastle player.

128.name: Robinson
pages: x
* A very young footballer, he can play as an attacking midfielder or as a forward.  Very skilful, he shows great promise.
x
x
* Signed for Newcastle in March 1998.
* The manager didn't count on him much and only aligned him in three games.

129.name: Speed
pages:
* Speed was transfered to Newcastle in February 1998 for 5.500.000 pounds. 
* Gary Speed's Everton dream turned sour at the start of his second season at the club. The club he supported as a boy were not reaching the expectations Speed wanted, so he asked for a transfer. At Newcastle Speed will be re-united with his old Leeds team-mate David Batty.

* Speed is an attacking midfielder who plays down the left hand side of the park, aided by the quality of his left foot. He is a player who gives 100% in every game he plays with both his club and the Welsh national side. He combines his tremendous work rate with good basic technique. He is good in the air in both penalty areas, and gets forward to join the attack quickly and dangerously. A player who combines talent and hard work,  he makes an important contribution to the side.

* League Championship winners medal  91-92.
* Charity Shield medal  92.
* Second Division winners medal  89-90.

* 42 full international appearances for Wales, with 3 goals to his name. He made his debut on 20th May 1990 in a game against Costa Rica.
* 3 under-21 appearances, scoring twice.

* He learnt his trade in the youth ranks at Leeds United, where he arrived as a schoolboy in January 1995, and began training with the club in July 1986. On 13th June 1988 he signed professional and made his debut in the penultimate game of the 88-89 season. That was on 6th May 1989 at Elland Road, against Oldham (0-0). 
* Up to the end of the 94-95 he had been booked 18 times. .
* In July 1996 he signed for Everton, who paid Leeds United 3,500,000 pounds to take him to Goodison Park. He made his Premier League debut for Everton on 1st August 1996 at Goodison Park against Newcastle (2-0). Speed had an excellent game and scored Everton's second goal in the 40th minute of the game.

* In his first season at Everton, Speed won over the Goodison Park fans from the very first game. In the 37 games in which he played he was constantly one of Everton's most dangerous players, both outside and inside the penalty area. He scored 9 goals, amongst them a hat trick against Southampton at Goodison Park. On his debut, against Newcastle, in the first league game of the season, he managed to find the back of the net with perhaps his best goal since the one he scored that clinched the league title for Leeds in 1992.

130.name: Tomasson
pages: * At the end of last season Jon Tomasson was one of the most sought after players in Europe. His extraordinary quality and potential have made him a star at a very young age. Top scorer in the Dutch league and an international for Denmark, his presence at Newcastle represents an injection of youth and quality for Kenny Dalglish's side. If he manages to adapt quickly to the demands and style of the Premier League then Tomason could turn out to be one of the 97-98 season's pleasant surprises.

* Despite his youth, Jon Tomasson is already a very complete footballer. He plays tucked in behind the main strikers, a position which allows him free reign of his tremendous imagination. He possesses extraordinary vision which he uses to slide accurate passes through to the forward line, whilst he is also adept at playing one-twos with intelligence and opportunism. He posses the ability to score regularly, but above all creates numerous goalscoring chances for his teammates. He is blessed with excellent individual technique, possesses good dribbling skills and a change of pace, as well as showing real character out on the park. Very quick, he is a maestro in one on one situations with the goalkeeper. Given his youth and the qualities he possesses, Jon Tomasson has everything he needs to go on to become a player which every manager would want in his team.
* Top Scorer in the Dutch League  96-97.

* Three full international appearances for Denmark.
* Although present in the 1996 European Championships in England he didn't manage to get into the action.
* Twelve under-21 international appearances scoring five times.

* Tomasson began his career with Koge BK, a modest Danish Second Division side.
* He broke into the First Division at 17 years of age signing for F.C. Copenhagen.
* In 1994 he was transfered to SC Heerenven, a Dutch First Division club .In his first season he scored five goals in 16 games. In his second campaign he ended the season as the club's leading scorer, with 14 to his credit. 
* As leading goalscorer in the Dutch League during the 1996-97 campaign he was voted "Talent of the Year" by the prestigious magazine "Voetbal". 
* He was chased by several of Europe's most improtant clubs such as Ajax, Barcelona, Sampdoria, and Atletico Madrid. The Dutch coach Louis Van Gaal recommended his signing both for Ajax and Barcelona. Tomasson finally accepted Newcastle's offer.
* He has been a Newcastle player since 31st May 1997. His transfer fee was fixed at £2,500,000 while his contract doesn't end until the year 2002. 
* He has been compared on many occasions to his countryman Michael Laudrup. In Denmark he is considered as the successor to the Great Dane, who is now with Ajax.

* Jon Dahl Tomasson was one of the European revelations of last season. He ended the season as top scorer in the Dutch League, an extraordinary achievement for a midfielder and even more so taking into account the fact that he was playing for a relatively small club such as Heerenven. For that reason, nobody was too surprised when a number of Europe's most important clubs became interested in signing him as the season progressed.

131.name: Barnes
pages: * John Barnes will go down as one of the greatest players to have emerged from English football in recent times. During his time at Liverpool Barnes defined another successful era in the history of the famous Anfield club whose red shirt he wore proudly for 10 years. When the veteran captain left Anfield offers weren't slow in coming his way. Tottenham were actively interested in taking him while West Ham manager Harry Redknapp prematurely announced that Barnes would be signing for the Hammers. John however prefered to move to Newcastle United where he linked up once again with Kenny Dalglish, another British football legend. Together they will be hoping to provide the character and experience needed to take the Saint James' Park club on to Premiership and European Glory.

* A footballer of pure talent, Barnes is one of the best players in England. He began his career as a forward, particularly down the left hand side backed up as always by the exquisite touch of his cultured left foot. At that time he was genuinely quick with the ability to get on the end of crosses and through balls, scoring as he did a significant number of goals each season. Nowadays, having lost that explosive pace he generally lines up in midfield normally just in front of the defence. From this deeper position which he now finds more to his liking he can dictate the way the team plays making the most of his extraordinarily accurate passing and tremendous vision. He is a free kick specialist making the most of the subtle touch his left foot still possesses. Although now at the veteran stage of his career he still has more than enough class to score the occasional brilliant goal, something which has been a constant feature of his playing career.

* League Championship Winner medals 87-88 and 89-90. 
* F.A. Cup Winners medal 88-89. 
* League Cup Winners medal 94-95. 
* Charity Shield Medals  88, 89, 90 and 92. 
* Football Writers Player of the Year 1988 and 1990.
* Professional Footballers Association Player of the Year 87-88. 
* F.A. Youth Cup Winners medal  81-82.

* 79 full international appearances for England. He made his debut on 11th May 1983 in a game against Northern Ireland in Belfast (0-0). 
* One England "B" international. 
* Two England under-21 international appearances scoring once.

* Son of a Jamaican diplomat he has sometimes been injustly accused of not possessing a real passion for the white shirt and three lions of England. 
* He signed his first professional contract for Watford on 14th July on 1981 moving from Sudbury Court. He made his debut on 5th November of that same year against Oldham.
* On 10th June 1984 John Barnes carved out a place for himself in the history of world football. At the legendary Maracana stadium in Rio de Janeiro Barnes scored one of the most memorable goals of modern times: He picked the ball up in the middle of the park and carried it at high speed toward the Brazilians' penalty area. After going past one Brazilian defender after another he finally rounded the keeper before calmly rolling the ball over the line and into the back of the empty net. A similar goal to another, equally as famous, scored by Maradona against England in the World Cup finals in Mexico. Two amazing goals that only players of exceptional quality are capable of scoring.
* On 19th June 1987 he signed for Liverpool. The transfer fee was set at £900,000.
* In 1988 he received a number of tempting offers from Italian clubs but prefered to stay on at Liverpool. 
* He has scored 3 hat tricks during his career, one of which was rounded off with a spectacular back heel in a cup tie against Crewe Alexandra. 
* He played in the World Cup Finals in Mexico in 1986 and Italy 1990 where England reached the semi-finals. Injury kept him out of the 1992 European Championships in Sweden.
* At the end of 96-97 season he reached the end of his contract with Liverpool. He received offerts from Tottenham and West Ham but Barnes prefered to sign for Newcastle, led of course by his ex-Liverpool colleague and manager Kenny Dalglish.
*  He has been a Newcastle player since 13th August  1997.

* A member if the starting line up in 34 of the 35 legaue games in which he appeared for Liverpool last season, John Barnes was, once again, one of the Reds' most regular performers. Now well established in the midfield, he directed Liverpool's game with class and intelligence, imposing his touch, vision and experience on games. He scored four times in the Premier League and added another three in theEuropean Cup Winners Cup, a competition in which he helped to take Liverpool through to the semi-finals.

132.name: Lee
pages: * Following the departure of Peter Beardsley, Robert Lee is the new captain of Newcastle, and is, without doubt, the perfect man for the job. Now a veteran with character and real leadership qualities he is appreciated and respected by both colleagues and rivals. Now at the peak of his career, Lee will be confident in his ability to guide Newcastle towards the Premiership title that has eluded them over the last two seasons.

* A hardworking player but also blessed with good technical ability Lee can comfortably occupy any position across the midfield area. He generally plays down the centre from where he can not only organise the teams attacks, but where he can also get heavily involved in defensive duties. A good short passer of the ball he is also accurate over longer distances when he attempts to open the game up. Powerful and quick he is also very difficult to stop when he moves in on goal. He possesses a good touch on the ball and a powerful shot with either foot which is how he scores mos tof his goals. Lee is also an expert penalty taker showing great confidence from the spot. Added to all these qualities he is also a fine header of the ball.
* Robert Lee is a very complete player who is a key man for his team. If he is in good physical condition then he makes his presence felt all over the field.
* Division One championship Winners medal 1992-93.

* 13 full international appearances for England.
* He made his debut on 12th October 1994 at Wembley against Rumania (1-1) with Lee scoring England's goal.
* One "B" international appearances for England. 
* Two under-21 international appearances.

* Lee began his career with modest Hornchurch. He signed as a free agent for Charlton Athletic on 12th July 1983 although he didn't make his first team debut until 10th March 1984 in a game against Grimsby Town
* Charlton's financial problems forced them to sell Lee to  Newcastle for £700,000. He signed for the Magpies on 22nd September 1992. Soon after on 26th September he made his debut for the club against Peterborough. He scored his first goal for Newcastle on 21st November 1992 against Watford. 
* His tremendous start to the 94-95 season saw the doors to the full England side open up for him. He made his debut in October 1994 against Rumania with Lee scoring England's only goal in a 1-1 draw. A tremendous run of form with plenty of goals along the way, was broken by injury.
* Disappointed by his absence from the European Championships in England in 1996 Lee was later called up by England's new manager Glenn Hoddle following the departure of Terry Venables.

* Last time out Robert Lee occupied a more defensive position in Newcastle'sline up, something which affected his ability to get on the scoresheet compared to previous years. Nevertheless his extraordinary performances didn't go unnoticed by national team boss Glenn Hoddle who regularly called him up to the England squad. He played in 34 Premier League games, scoring 4 times in the League andonce in the Cup against his old club Charlton Athletic.
