133.name: Batty
pages: * David Batty has become a key man for Newcastle and has developed into one of the best players in England. Through hard work and determination he has won the trust of two prestigious managers in the shape of Kenny Dalglish and  Glenn Hoddle. He was one of last season's stars, as was recognised by his fellow professionals. He has managed to tone down his temperamental character and has polished up many othe raspects of his game. At present he is going through one of the best spells of his career. With David Batty performing as he is at the moment Newcastle will no doubt be heavily involved in the chase for honours.

* David Batty is a central midfielder at his best playing just in front of the defence. In that central midfield position he can get heavily involved in helping to contain the opposition's main creative players as well as helping to build up attacks from the back. At times the creative side to his game is hidden by the tremendous physical effort he puts into every game and which allows him to win so much possession for his team. However, when he has the ball his distributionis both thoughtful and accurate, making him a real focal point for his team and key part of their approach work. 
* Batty is a player who is always involved in the game, switching from one side to the other, supporting his teammates and getting forward to help out in attacks. He possesses a good shot from distance although he doesn't score many goals. He is an ideal partner for a classy midfielder as was the case when he partnered Sherwood at Blackburn Rovers. Occasionally for tactical reasons he has been asked to play tight on the touchline, particularly down the left. When pushed out wide his influence on the game is clearly diminished.

* League Championship Winners Medal 91-92 (Leeds Utd.). 
* Second Division Championship Winers medal 89-90. 
* Charity Shield Medal 1992.

* 25 full international appearances for England. He made his debut on 21st May1991 in a friendly against Russia at Wembley. Batty came on as a substitute for Dennis Wise with England going on to win by three goals to one. He was a member of England's squad for the 1992 European Championships in Sweden in1992 where he played in two games.
* For "B" international appearances. 
* Six under-21 international appearances.

* David Batty came through the ranks at Leeds United his hometown club. He arrived at Leeds as a schoolboy in November 1983 going on to become an apprentice in August 1985.  He signed his first professional contract on 3rd August 1987. His league debut came just months later on 21st Novemberr in a game against Swindon Town at Elland Road..
* After making his international debut in 1991 and winning the league title in 1992 he was transfered to Blackburn Rovers on 26th October 1993 for £2,750,000.
* He made his league debut for Blackburn on 30th October 1993 in a victory at Ewood Park against Tottenham Hotspur (1-0). The scorer of the goal was Alan Shearer.
* He ended the 93-94 season having to undergo surgery on a broken bone in his foot. However, the result of the operation was not satisfactory and he was forced to have two more operations before reappearing towards the end of the 94-95 season. Although Blackburn managed to win the title Batty was unable to add this to his own personal honours list since he had only played in five games.
* During the 95-96 season Blackburn were involved in the Champion's League with Batty involved in a regrettable incident with Graeme Le Saux, with the two players coming to blows during the game in Russia against Spartak Moscow. This incident together with Batty's unhappiness with his new position out wide on the left hand side brought about a hasty departure from the Ewood Park club.
* On 2nd March 1996 he was transfered to Newcastle United for £3,750,000. He made his debut two days later at St. James' Park against Manchester United and, despite Newcastle's 0-1 defeat was chosen man of the match. In April, during Newcastle's visit to Ewood Park, and in front of his old Ewood Park fans, he managed to put one past Rovers keeper Tim Flowers, although Newcastle went on to lose 2-1.

* David Batty was one of  Newcastle's most regular performers throughout last season. He delivered masterly performances as the side's midfield organizer spreading the ball around, always prepared to get stuck in at the back. He scored the "Magpies" first league goal of the campaign against Wimbledon, although he didn't manage to find the back of the net throughout the rest of the season. He was sent off once against Chelsea at Stamford Bridge. despite this it was a very positive season for David Batty, something which was confirmed when his fellow professionals named him in the Premier League's ideal team.
* His excellent performances for Newcastle saw him force his way into Glenn Hoddle's England squad. He especially stood out in the qualifying game for the '98 World Cup finals against Georgia in November, after which he was named man of the match.

134.name: Andersson
pages: * After the departure of Tino Asprilla to Italy, Newcastle's manager, Kenny Dalglish, looked for a new strike partner for Alan Shearer.  And he found him in the Swede Andersson, a player who the Scottish manager had been keeping an eye on for a few years and who will maybe find more luck in England than he did in Milan.

* He plays as a centre forward, although he operates in the whole of the attacking zone and it is normal to see him drop back almost to the midfield to receive passes.  Very strong physically, quick despite his stature, and with a notable technique, Andersson has a powerful shot on goal and a built in instinct to connect with a shot as soon as he gets the ball. He will also initiate the pressure on the rival defenders to hinder the free circulation of the ball.  His biggest problem is his lack of experience at an international level, something that will get corrected with the passage of time.  For the time being he just has to rely on raw talent.

* Swedish League title with Gothenburg (96). 
* Top scorer in the Swedish League in 1996.

* A full international for Sweden 14 times. 
* He made his debut on the 25th of February 1996, in a game between Australia and Sweden (0-2) played in Brisbane.  He played the full ninety minutes and scored two goals for his team.

* He started playing football for Folval, before moving onto Tidahom. 
* He made his debut as a professional in 1994, playing for Degerfors. 
* Towards the end of 1995 Benfica showed interest in acquiring his services and he even made the trip to Lisbon to sign the contract, but the operation didn't come to its fruition. 
* AC Milan paid almost £1.5 million for him.  His contract was until the 30th of June of the year 2001. 
* He made his debut in the Serie A on the 28th of September 1997 in a game between Milan and Vicenza (0-1). 
* He asserts that football isn't the most important thing in his life. 
* He was the sixth Swedish footballer to don the AC Milan shirt.  Before him, Nordhal, Liedholm, Gren, Hamrin and Blomqvist had done so also. 
* On the 27th of January 1998 he was transferred to Newcastle for £3 million pounds.

* Before moving to Milan, Andersson had scored thirteen goals in eight games played for Gothenburg in the Swedish League.  As had been the case in the previous season he was a reference point for all of the attacking moves of his team and a decisive man in the squad.

135.name: Rush
pages: * Ian Rush is one of  English football's most recent legends, one of those exceptional players whose greatness goes beyond the boundaries of football. The Premier League's top honours winner arrived at Newcastle together with John Barnes, both called to the club by Kenny Dalglish. The three of them, old colleagues, will be out recapture at Saint James' Park the glory days they knew together at Liverpool. So, Rush sets out on a new chapter in a glittering career, although nobody will be ready to predict whether this is likely to be his final destination.

* One of the best centre forwards in the history of English football, and one who retains his goalscoring instinct. Although physically he is not what he was a few years ago, he is well capable of making the most of his intelligence and know how to find gaps in the opposition defence. Obsessed with goalscoring, over the years his speed of movement and ability to lose his marker have been enough for him to find the back of the net with astonishing regularity. He scores the majority of his goals from close in, generally with either foot. Although he can score with his head, this is far from his most potent weapon. As well as the goalscoring efficiency which has characterized his career, Rush has also added a great deal of style to the game. His winning mentality allows him to maintain his concentration throughout the 90 minutes. A tremendously experienced player, his presence is a constant threat to opposing goalkeepers.

* European Champions' Cup Winners medal 1983-84. 
* League Championship Winners Medals, 81-82,82-83,83-84,85-86 and 89-90. 
* F.A. Cup Winners Medals 85-86,88-89 and 91-92. 
* League Cup Winners Medals 80-81,81-82,82-83 and 94-95. 
* Charity Shield  Medals 82,83,84,86,88,89 and 92. 
* Golden Boot Winner 1984. 
* Footballer of the Year 83-84. 
* Professional Footballers' Association Player of the Year, 83-84. 
* P.F.A. Young Player of the Year, 1983.
* European Champions' Cup Runners-up Medal 1984-85.

* 73 full international appearances for Wales, 28 goals.
* He made his debut on 21st May 1980 against Scotland, in a gamewhich Scotland won by one goal to nil.
* Two under 21 international appearances, scoring once.

* The ninth of eleven brothers, he arrived at Chester City in March 1977 as aSchoolboy. An apprentice since August 1978, he made his league debut on 28th April 1979 against Sheffield Wednesday. On 25th September of that same year he signed his first professional contract.
* In his second season at Chester he was top scorer with 14 goals. Shortly after on 1st May 1980 he was transfered to Liverpool  for £300,000. 
* The early stages of  his Anfield career were not particularly brilliant, to the point where Rush suggested to manager Bob Paisley that a move to another club might be a good idea - an idea which Paisley rejected. His first great performance for Liverpool came against Leeds, where he hitt the back of the net twice. It was the beginning of a triumphant career, although he had to fight for a place with players of the calibre of Steve Heighway, David Fairclough and David Johnson. It was eventually Rush however who forged such a fantastic partnership withKenny Dalglish. 
* On 26th January 1982 he scored his first hat trick in a game against Notts County.
* As a member of Liverpool's triumphant European Cup Final team of 1984, he scored from the spot in the penalty shoot out, a goal which helped clinch the trophy against Roma after the scores had finished level at 1-1 after ninety minutes.
* In June 1987 he left for Juventus of Turin who paid £3,200,000 for his services. However Rush never really adapted to the Italian League. It was Pescara who suffered at the hands of his best performance in Italy, Rush scoring four times against them in an Italian Cup game.
* On 23rd August 1988 he returned to Liverpool in excahnge for £2,800,000. 
* After overcoming Roger Hunt's record, he became the top goalscorer in Liverpool's history, doing so after strangely failing to score in the first 9 games he played for the Reds.
* He is the top scorer in the history of the F.A. Cup and is the only man in history to have scored in five different F.A. Cup finals. 
* Rush is also the top scorer in the history of the Welsh national side. As a schoolboy he even managed to score 14 times in two consecutive games. 
* In his final game at Anfield Rush went off on a lap a honour around the pitch and threw his shirt into the crowd while "You'll Never Walk Alone" rang around the famous stadium. It was one of the most emotional moments of the season.
* During his career in England he has scored 14 hat tricks, a total matched by no other player still in the game. The last of those came on 30th November 1994 in a League Cup tie against Blackburn Rovers.
* One of the games real gentlemen he has only been booked 13 times throughout the whole of his glittering career and has never been sent off. 
* On 25th May 1996 he signed for Leeds United where he spent the whole of the 1996-97 season.
* He has been a  Newcastle player since 16th August 1997. His signing coincided with the injury to the side's goalscorer-in-chief Alan Shearer. At St. James' Park he has been reunited with Kenny Dalglish and John Barnes, both ex-colleagues at Liverpool.

* During his one and only season with Leeds United he played in 36 league games, 34 of those appearances coming as a member of the starting line up. He scored just 3 goals, a poor return for a player with his goalscoring record. However, he was unableto do much more playing for a team that was going through a real crisis and at a club where manager Howard Wilkinson had been replaced by George Grahamat the beginning of the season.

136.name: Gudjonsson
pages: * Bjarni Gudjonsson arrived in England with the dream of setting out on a brilliant Premier League career. It won't be easy for him to force his way into the side in hisfirst season at Newcastle, but Kenny Dalglish will be trying to make sure that he learns everything he can, keeping one eye on the future. For such a young player to receive the advice of a legend with the charisma of Dalglish is already an honour in itself.

* As a striker Gudjonsson makes the most of his speed and ability to lose his marker in order to demonstrate his goalscoring instincts. He strikes a ball well and is quite clever when it comes to getting in front of opposing defenders. As a prospect for the future he still has plenty of time to improve and polish up the weaknesses that come hand in hand with lack of experience.

* Icelandic League Championship Winners medals 95 and 96.
* Icelandic Cup Winners medal 96.
* A full  Icelandic international.

* A product of the youth system of  IA Akranes, the most important club in Iceland, Bjarni took the step up to the first team in 1995. In his first season he played in just 2 league games, coming on as a substitute on both occasions.
* In 1996 he won both league and Cup winners medals and made his debut with Iceland's national side.
* He has been a Newcastle player since June 1997. His transfer fee was £500,000.

* In 1996 Gudjonsson won an Icelandic League Championship winners medal for the second year in succession. He was also celebrating a double triumph as his team carried off the cup just for good measure. To round off an extraordinaryseason for him, he made his debut for the national side.

137.name: Ketsbaia
pages: * Following his magnificent performance at Wembley with the Georgian national side a number of different clubs expressed an interest in Ketsbaia. Taking advantage of the fact that he was coming to the end of his contract with AEK Athens, Kenny Dalglish recommended the player to the Newcastle board. With the Georgian midfielder in their ranks Newcastle can count on a harworking player, experienced and versatile capable of guaranteeing a fine job in a number of different positions. It seems sure that Dalglish will be giving him plenty of opportunities to show his quality in the Premier League.

* A strong midfielder with good reserves of stamina, he can play in a number of different positions, although he generally plays on the right hand side of the midfield. He carries out a tremendous amount of work throughout the whole of the ninety minutes. He helps out with defensive duties and makes decisive runs forward to support the attack making the most of his speed, power and shooting ability. Good in the air, he is also more skillful with the ball at his feet than he might at first appear.
* Greek Cup Winners medal, 1996.
* A full international for Georgia.

* In 1994 he signed for three years for Greek First Division club AEK Athens.
* Having finished his contract with the Greek club, he signed for Newcastle Unitedon 17th July 1997. He has a contract with the "Magpies" until the year 2000.
* Ketsbaia attracted the attention of the English clubs as a result of his excellent performance in a qualifying game for the 1998 World Cup Finals in France between Georgia and England at in spring 1997.
* He made his Newcastle debut on 9th August in a game against Sheffield Wednesday.

* Once again Ketsbaia proved to be one of AEK Athens best players. The team finishedsecond in the league championship and managed to carry off the Greek Cup, beating Panathinaikos in the final. By the same token he remained a key member of the Georgian national side. He specially stood out in the qualifying game for the 1998 World CupFinals in France at Wembley, although he was unable to prevent the English from winning 2-0.

138.name: Gillespie
pages: *  Little by little Keith Gillespie has forced his way into Newcastle's line upon a regular basis, although it has turned out to be a far from easy task. A product of Manchester United's youth system, during his time at United he was constantly compared with Ryan Giggs. His arrival at Saint James' Park coincided with the departure of Andy Cole to Old Trafford, a deal which at the time caused a great deal of contreoversy. Game by game Gillespie has managed to justify his place in the team. He has won the confidenceof Kenny Dalglish and is now an automatic choice for Northern Ireland. Now he is dreaming of picking up some major honours.

*  Speed and ability are the basic characteristics of Keith Gillespie's game. Equally at home either in midfield or pushed further forward but always hugging the touchline he likes to get forward quickly and directly. Although he is primarily right footed he can do equally as good a job down either flank. Playing down the left he likes to cut inside to get in shots on goal with his stronger right foot. If he is operating down the right he will more probably try to reach the by-line from where he can send over dangerous crosses to his teammates.
* Technically sound he possesses excellent dribbling skills, especially on the run. With the ball apparently tied to his feet he can be very difficult for defenders to tackle cleanly, constantly shielding the ball from them; something he does very well. On occasions his ability sees him attempting to do too much on his own, apparently enjoying himself on the ball and failing to see the pass which would put a teammate through on goal. Without being a real goalscorer he is capable of finding the back of the net regularly especially when he plays as a more orthodox left winger. Still very young, he is a very promising footballer.
* Charity Shield medal 1994.

* 17 full international appearances for Norther Ireland, with one goal to his name.
* One under-21 international appearances.

* A product of Manchester United's youth system he signed professional on 3rd February 1993.  He went through 2 seasons without making his first team debut.
* Gillespie went out on loan to Wigan Athletic on 3rd September 1993 and made his league debut the following day against Doncaster.
* On his return to Old Trafford he was given his Premier League debut against Sheffield Wednesday at Hillsborough. Manchester United lost 1-0. 
* He caught the public's attention in a league game against Newcastle in which he scored a beatiful goal, rounding off an excellent solo run with a powerful shot from the edge of the area.
* On 12th january 1995 he was transfered to Newcastle for £1,000,000. His arrival on Tyneside formed part of the costly operation which took the ex-"Magpies" striker Andy Cole to Manchester United. Moving in the opposite direction Gillespie ended up at St. James Park and made his debut on 24th of that month, once again at Hillsborough against Sheffield Wednesday. This time things at least went a little better; the final score was a goalless draw. 
* In his first season at Newcastle he scored twice in a Cup tie against Manchester City at St. James' Park. His first league goal came on 13th May 1995: Newcastle and Tottenham Hotspur drew 3-3, again at St. James' Park.

* Although at the beginning of the season he hardly got a look in as a member of the starting line up, from the end of September onwards Gillespie managed to force his way into the side on a regular basis. Gillespie showed that he had made real progress on the defensive side of his game, allowing him to occupy deeper positions. He continued however to be much more effective in an attacking role where his speed can prove to be deadly. He made 32 league appearances, 23 of those as a member of the startingline up. He scored just once, that goal coming against Liverpool at Anfield.

139.name: Shearer
pages:
* The pre-season brought terrible news for Newcastle. Alan Shearer, the best goalscorer in England, the successor to Gary Lineker had been seriously injured. The estimated period for a full recovery was given as eight months meaning that the England international striker was likely to miss more or less the wholeseason. A serious set back for Kenny Dalglish who was counting on Shearer as Newcastle's standard bearer in both the Premiership and the Champions League.
* Shearer's injury also meant that life would be more complicated for England, already heavily involved in the battle to qualify for the 1998 World Cup Finals in France. Nevertheless the player himself seemed confident that, on the one hand, his England teammates would stamp their passport to the World Cup Finals and, on the other, he would be ready in time to be the first choice centre forward in Glenn Hoddle's team.

* Alan Shearer is all about goals. He possesses that special instinct which all great goalscorers have and which allows them to always seem to be in the right place at the right time. Blessed with tremendous technique he is a superb striker of the ball, either with his head or with either foot - although he probably shows greater accuracy with his right. He also has the virtue of scoring a high percentage of  his goals with his first touch, that way denying rival defenders even the slightest opportunity of closing closing him down. He is quick, opportunist, intelligent and shows great mobility right across the front line. He can pop up to surprise defenders, can get up at the far post or manoeuvre himself into position to gain the advantage over defenders. Above all he never hesitates and will have a go at goal if he is offered even the slightest opportunity.
* Shearer is a player who can go through long spells without touching the ball, but with his first touch is capable of finding the back of the net. He does however like to get involved in his team's build up play, pulling out wide to allow team mates to comethrough the middle, or dropping deep to pick the ball up, shielding it until support comes through from midfield or the flanks. He won't normally try to take defenders on - this not being his strong point. He battles constantly however with defenders and in his team's first line of defence keeping his rivals under pressure at all times.The complete all round striker, he is dangerous from free kicks and rearely misses from the penalty spot. In short he is an extraordinary footballer.

* League Championship winners medal 1994-95. 
* Winner of the Golden Boot 94-95 and 95-96. 
* Footballer of the Year 1994. 
* Professional Footballers' Association Player of the Year 1995. 
*Top scorer in the Premier League 94-95 with 34 goals; in 95-96 with 31 and 96-97 with 25.
* Top scorer in the 1996 European Championships in England.
* Voted into 3rd place in FIFA'S World Footballer of the year 1997 rankings.

* 35 full international appearances for England with 11 goals to his credit. He made his debut on 19th February 1992 in a friendly at Wembley against France. England won 2-0 with Shearer striking the first himself and setting up the second for Gary Lineker.
* He was a member of England's 1992 European Championship squad in Sweden where he played in just one game, against France in Malmo.
* He was top scorer in the 1996 European Championships in England with five goals. He was a member of the starting line up in the five games that England played before losing to Germany 1-2 in extra time in the semi-finals. Shearer scored England's goal.
* In September 1996 he was named captain of England by national team boss Glenn Hoddle.
* One "B" international appearance. 
* Twelve under-21 international appearances, scoring thirteen times. 
* Five youth international appearances, with one goal.

* At the time of Alan Shearer's transfer to Newcastle it was the most expensive in the history of world football. On 29th July 1996 the St. James' Park club paid Blackburn Rovers £15,000,000. Shearer had always shown adesire to play for Newcastle, his home town club.
* Curiously,  Alan Shearer began his career with Newcastle but was rejected by the club's coaches who decided that he didn't have enough ability to go on to be a success. Referring to Alan, Peter Kirkley one of his coaches at the time has said, "he had good technique but we didn't think that he would go on to play in what was then the First Division".
* In September 1984 he joined Southampton as a schoolboy and in July 1986 became an apprentice. He made his First Division debut on 26th march 1988 in a game against Chelsea, coming on in place of Danny Wallace. Shortly after on 9th April he made his first appearance as a member of the starting line up againstArsenal. Southampton won 4-2 and Shearer notched his first hat trick becoming in the process the youngest player ever to score three in one game. All the signs indicated he was about to sign his first professional contract, which he did on 14th April 1988.
* Despite his extraordinary breakthrough into the elite of the English game Shearer wasn't immediately a first choice at Southampton. Both Matthew Le Tissier and Rodney Wallace kept him out, and Alan went through long spells in the reserves.
* During the course of the 89-90 and 90-91 season he began to get more regular tastes of first team football although by no means did his goalscoring potential stand out in the league games he played. Nevertheless in 10 cup games he managed to find the net 8 times.
* Wallace's departure for Leeds opened up the doors to success during the 91-92 season. Despite the ultra defensive style of play employed by manager Ian Branfoot, Shearer was Southampton's top scorer with 13 goals and took the club through to the Zenith Data Systems Cup final where they lost 3-2 against Nottingham Forest.
* During the summer of 1992 several clubs such as Chelsea, Crystal Palace, Manchester United and Liverpool made enormous offers in an attempt to secure his signature. However, attracted by the project that Kenny Dalglish had mapped out fo rBlackburn, Shearer decided to sign for the Lancashire club, recently promoted to the topflight of English football. The transfer was closed on 24th July 1992 with the fee beingset at £3,600,000 pounds.
* He began the 92-93 season by scoring 12 goals in 12 games, lifting the Ewood Park club to lofty heights in the table. However on 26th December 1992 a hard tackle by Chris Fairclough caused him to suffer a rupture in the cruciate ligaments of his right knee. He was operated on by doctor David Dandy and that was the end of the season for Alan Shearer.
* He has been the top scorer in the Premier for three consecutive seasons (94-95, 95-96 and96-97). In the first two of these seasons he also received the"Golden Boot" award as the top goalscorer in Europe. 
* He was the first player to reach 100 goals in the newly established Premier League, which opened up in 1992-93.
* On 30th July 1996 he was transfered to Newcastle for £15,000,000 making him the most expensive footballer in the world. A few weeks later this record was broken when Ronaldo signed for Barcelona.
* He made his debut for the Magpies in the Charity Shield, while his league debut came on 17th August 1997 in an away game against Everton. Four days later he marked his home debut at St. James' Park by scoring against Wimbledon (2-0).
* In 1997 he came third in the voting for "European Footballer of the Year". He occupied an identical position in FIFA'S  "World Player of the Year" award.
* During the 97-98 pre-season he suffered a serious injury which is likely to keep him out of action for at least eight months.

* For the third consecutive year Alan Shearer was top scorer in the Premier League. He scored 25 goals (including 3 penalties) in the 31 league games in which he played. He would undoubtedly have increased on this total had he been able to steer clear from injury. In his first season at Newcastle he did more than enough to show that he is one of the best players in the world. He opened his account with a goal from a direct free kick in his first game at Saint James' Park in the "Magpies" colours and he also closed it at home in the final game of the season against Nottingham Forest. He formed an outstanding partnership with Les Ferdinand, and ended the season being voted "Player of the Year" by his fellow professionals. A new honour to add to his list which was also lengthened by two prestigious third places, in the voting for the "European Player of the Year" and in the voting for FIFA'S  "World Player of the Year" award.
* His presence in the England side also proved to be crucial. In September he was named captain of the national team by Glenn Hoddle and wore the captain's arm band for the first time against Moldovia.

140.name: Oakes
pages: * In the shadow of Mark Bosnich, Michael Oakes is waiting to become the first choice keeper at Aston Villa. Last season he stepped in perfectly when the Australian was absent and showed the crowd at Villa Park that he can be trusted. In principle, it seems that it will be hard to play as first choice keeper, but the whole world knows, Brian Little included, that it won't be long before he finds a place in the Premier League.

* A young goalkeeper with excellent ability making rapid progress. Oakes dominates his area and is safe in all his actions. He needs time and experience to develop his qualities and polish out his defects.
x
* 6 under-21 appearances for England.

* He is the son of Alan Oakes, ex Manchester City player who has the record for the number of games played for this club. 
* From the Aston Villa "juniors" he turned professional on the 16th of July 1991. Loaned to Third-Division Scarborough on the 26th of November 1993, he has only played one game -a 1-2 defeat at the hands of Torquay United-.
* He maked his League debut with the Aston Villa first team on the 17th of August 1996, with a defeat at Hillsborough by Sheffield Wednesday (2-1).

* Injuries to his team mate Mark Bosnich allowed Oakes to defend the Villa goal in 20 games, 18 from the start. He showed that he is able to play in the Premier League and, above all, showed that Bosnich has a worthy goalkeeper as understudy.

141.name: Bosnich
pages: * Bosnich's presence does not go unnoticed in the grounds. Without doubt, Bosnich is one of the best goalies in the Premier League, but he is also one of the most acclaimed showmen.

* A young goalkeeper, but already consolidated in the Aston Villa goal, he stands out for his great reflexes and agility. Quick and decisive, he comes out well to make the interception.  Despite being young he looks as if he has got a lot of experience, transmitting a lot of tranquility to his team mates. In the last few seasons he has notably improved his game with the ball at his feet. Left-footed, he is exeptionally cold-blooded in difficult situations, his intent always being to pass the ball safely. A great goalkeeper with a brilliant future ahead of him.
* League Cup Champion in 93-94 and 95-96.
* 9 full international caps for Australia.

* Bosnich started his career in the Australian team Sydney Croatia before signing for Manchester United on the 5th of June 1989, although he hardly had any playing chances at the Old Trafford club. 
* In the summer of 1991 he was forced to return to Australia due to problems with his English work permit. He signed however for Aston Villa on the 28th of February 1992. On the 24th of April of this same year he makes his debut with the "Villains" against Luton Town. 
* During the 94-95 season various illnesses and injuries in succession kept him out of the team temporarily, although he turned in a good season.
* Until the end of the 94-95 season the average number of goals conceded was 1.139.

* A persistent knee injury prevented Bosnich from defending the Aston Villa goal at the start of the season. Four games after he reappeared he suffered a relapse which kept him out for more than a month until Christmas. The run of injuries did not stop there; Mark was forced to visit the physio once more after a game with the Australian national team. He played a total of 24 games, in half of those managing to keep a clean sheet.

142.name: Grayson
pages: * Simon Grayson is one of the few reinforcements which Aston Villa have made going into the 97-98 season. The ex Leicester City player arrived at Villa Park alongside Stan Collymore. For his part manager Brian Little hopes that Grayson can maintain the level he showed last season ending up with the conquest of the League Cup.

* A very fast right back who covers a lot of ground, Grayson is also able to act as a midfielder. A good marker, he likes to push up with the ball close to his feet, although at times he forgets his defensive duties. He has a good shot on goal, but hardly scores.  All his actions are very correct. Not a brilliant footballer, he is however, efficient, disciplined and does what is asked of him. He makes up for his technical limitations with hard work and sacrifice.
* League Champion in 97.
x

* A product of the Leeds United youth squad Simon Grayson turned professional on the 13th of June 1988.  He made his debut in the league in the 87-88 season, when he played in two games. Despite playing with the Whites for the four following seasons however he did not appear with the first team again.
* On the 13th of March 1992 Grayson was transferred to Leicester City for £50,000. Two weeks later his team mate Mike Whitlow arrived at Filbert Street 
* In 1994 Leicester win promotion to the Premier League and Simon Grayson is voted "Player of the Year" by the club's supporters. 
* Grayson has enjoyed a place in the starting line-up with three successive managers: Brian little, Mark McGhee and Martin O'Neill. 
*  Voted "Player of the Year" by the fans at Leicester City. On the 26th of June 1997 Grayson was transferred to Aston Villa for £1,350,000.

* The 96-97 season was one of the most brilliant in Grayson's career, up to the point where he was voted as the best player of the year at Leicester City. The injury to the Swede Pontus Kaamark allowed him to settle at left back in the team managed by Martin O'Neill. He played 36 League games, all of these from the start. What's more he scored 2 goals in the League Cup, a competition in which his team was proclaimed champion after defeating Middlesborough in the final.

143.name: Nelson
pages: * Fernando Nelson needed just one game to earn the confidence of Brian Little. The Portuguese defender adapted rapidly to the British style of play and justified the price of his transfer with some great performances. Going into the 97-98 season Nelson faces a double challenge: to become one of the best right backs in the Premier League and to recover his place in the Portuguese national team.

* A right wing back who covers a lot of ground Nelson is particularly outstanding in the defensive game. Thanks to his speed and resources rival forwards find him hard to get passed. Technically sufficient, he passes the ball well in short and uses his team mates for quick one-twos to set an attacking move in motion. Although he joins in the attack on his wing skilfully, he needs to improve the accuracy of his crosses to the heart of the box to increase his effectiveness. Disciplined, he falls back to his defensive position quickly and is always well placed. At times however, he lacks the forcefulness needed to cut out the rival counter-attack.

* Portuguese Cup Champion 93-94. 
* Portuguese Supercup Champion 95.

* 5 full international caps for Portugal. 
* He made his debut on the 3rd of June 1995 in a game against Latvia played in Porto (3-2).

* Born in Porto, Nelson began his career in the lower teams of the town's main club. 
* Transferred to Sporting Lisbon in 1991, he had to wait until the 93-94 season before finding a fixed place in the starting line-ups. 
* An international since 1995, the Portuguese manager Antonio Oliveira did not call him up for the European Championship in England in 96. 
* With a contract lasting until 1998, he is transferred to Aston Villa in the summer of 1996 for £1,750,000. 
* He made his debut in the Premier League on the 24th of August 1996 against Derby County at Villa Park (2-0).

* In his first season in England, Fernando Nelson managed to find a place for himself in the starting line-ups of Aston Villa. The Portuguese defender started the Championship on the substitutes' bench, but from the moment of his debut in the third game of the season he became a fixed feature in Brian Little's teams. He played 34 League games, 33 of these as a starter, but despite the ease with which he joins in the attack, he did not score a single goal.

144.name: Charles
pages: * After a season without playing Gary Charles hopes to regain the level he showed two years ago. It will not be at all easy to find a gap in Brian Little's line-ups however as there are men around such as Fernando Nelsno and even Simon Grayson who have better chances of playing in the starting eleven. Gary will have to work harder than ever. It is the unjust price that he has to pay for so many months of inactivity.

* Gary Charles is a right back whose most striking feature is his extraordinary physical condition which allows him to take part in the attacking game. He operates along the whole of the wing regaining his position quickly for defensive tasks. A good marker, he judges distances well when making interceptions. His career suffered a minor set-back after his appearance with the national team when he was 21. In his return to the Premier League however he has showed the level required for this category.
* League Cup Champion 95-96.

* Full international two times. His debut came on the 8th of June 1991 in Wellington in a friendly game against New Zealand (0-2). 
* 4 under-21 appearances.

* Gary Charles started his football career as a Schoolboy at Nottingham Forest in May of 1995. After passing through the lower ranks of the club, he turned professional on the 7th of November 1987. 
* Made his debut with Forest at the City Ground against Arsenal on 6th of November 1988. 
* Loaned to Leicester on the 16th March 1989. 
* On returning to Nottingham Forest he forced his way into the starting line-up little by little against fierce competition with Brian Laws. 
* Played in the final of the League Cup in 1992.  Nottingham Forest lost to Manchester United. 
* He plays in and loses the final of the F.A. Cup in 1993 against Tottenham Hotspur.. 
* On the 29th of July 1993 he was transferred to Derby County, then in the Second Division, for £750,000. 
* He has been with Aston Villa since the 6th of January 1995.  His signing coincided with the departure of Earl Barrett, also right wing back - to Everton. 
* At the end of the 95-96 season he suffered a serious injury when he broke his ankle, and therefore missed out completely on the whole of the 96-97 season.
* Recovering from his serious ankle injury, he did not recover in time to play a single game.

145.name: Ehiogu
pages: * Despite his youth Ugo Ehiogu is already one of the best defenders in England. Brian Little has always had a blind faith in him. Ugo has responded to this faith by taking the responsibility of playing in the first team. Together with Gareth Southgate he forms one of the most solid partnerships in the centre of defence in the country, and no-one would be surprised if, one day, they formed the defensive axis of the England team. With every day that passes Ugo Ehiogu makes a stronger claim for a place in the national team.

* At the beginning of his career he played at right back, but it has to be said that Ehiogu is one of the best central defenders in the Premier League. Blessed with a good technical quality he feels comfortable with the ball at his feet and he distributes it with good judgement.  His heavy build and physical power make him a hard player to get by. He is good in the air in both areas and he will usually push up for the set-plays. Hard at times he usually comes out on top in a man-to-man marking situation. As well as his technical virtues Ehiogu has a strong personality, able to infect his team mates with a winning spirit.  Young and ambitious, he still has plenty of room for improvement. His presence in the national team seems inevitable.
* League Cup Champion in 93-94 and 95-96.

* 1 full international cap for England. 
* He made his debut in 1996 in a game against China. 
* 1 international B appearance. 
* 15 under-21 international appearances. 1 goal.

* Ehiogu started as a youth player at West Bromwich Albion before starting to train on the 13th of July 1989. 
* His league debut occured on the 22nd of September 1990 at Boothferry Park, Hull City's ground. 
* On the 12th of July 1991 he joined Aston Villa for £40,000. His signing was contraversial - Aston Villa did not pay West Bromwich Albion the training rights of Ehiogu. 
* On the 24th of August 1991 he made his debut for Aston Villa as right back in a game at Villa Park against Arsenal. 
* In the 94-95 season he received his call-up to the England squad, although he did not get to make his debut. Up to the end of this season he recieved 8 yellow cards and was sent off once. 
* 1996 sees Ugo Ehiogu's debut with the full national team in a friendly against China.

* Ugo Ehiogu had an extraordinary season, playing from the start in the 38 League games.Helped by the departure of Paul McGrath, Ugo shared the centre of defence with Southgate, Tiler and Staunton and played to a very high level. He scored 3 League goals - one in the Cup - but, above all, he showed his progress had still not reached its limit, not by a long way.

146.name: Wright
pages: * Year after year Alan Wright has consolidated his status as one of the best left backs in England. So much so that many critics and fans demanded his presence in the team trained by Glenn Hoddle. With Aston Villa he is still an undisputed starter, more so since his team mate Steve Staunton began to occupy positions more in the centre of the pitch.  If luck goes his way in the 97-98 season he could make the definitive jump to the English national team.

* Wright is one of the best left backs in the Premier League. He has excellent ball control and his capable of passing. Blessed with an extraordinary turn of speed his work is felt both in attack and defence. He has the ability to play as a winger, even at times in the midfield as left half. Quick when making interceptions - and a good marker - he should improve his shot on goal. A great footballer making constant progress.

* F.A Cup Champion 95-96. 
* Charity Shield Medal 94.

* 2 under-21 international appearance for England. 
* 10 youth international appearances.

* Trained in the lower ranks of Blackpool Wright became the youngest player ever at the club making his debut at Bloomfield Road on the 2nd of May 1988 against Chesterfield.  Wright was 16 years and 217 days old. 
* On the 13th of April of 1989 he turned professional with Blackpool.
* Kenny Dalglish signs him for Blackburn Rovers. The operation costs £400,000, completed on the 25th of October. 
* The arrival of Graham Le Saux at Blackburn in 1993 forced him onto the substitutes' bench and after having a hernia operation is transferred to Aston Villa on the 10th of March 1995 for £1 million. 
* Up until the end of the 94-95 season he has been shown 6 yellow cards.

* For the second season running Alan Wright played in all the league games (38) as a starter, an honour only shared with his team mate Ehiogu. The defender kept up a very consistent level for the whole of the Championship and his fantastic goal against Wimbledon was the icing on the cake.  His level of understanding with the forward Dwight Yorke should also be underlined.

147.name: Southgate
pages: * Gareth Southgate is one of the axes about which Aston Villa's game rotates. Aged 27, the player from Watford has reached the necessary level of maturity to lead the defence of his club and England. Going into the 97-98 season Gareth will try, on the one hand, to win a major title with Aston Villa and, on the other, participate in the England team which hopes to be among the teams that go the World Cup in France.

* Although he started his career at right back he has played in midfield many times,and in the last few seasons he has settled into the centre of defence, both with Aston Villa and with the national team. Technically better than he actually looks, he is a footballer who stands out for his defensive security and the tranquility with which he operates on the pitch. Quick, he makes interceptions without thinking twice. In attack, he is particularly dangerous in the set-plays. Southgate infects his team mates with his competitive spirit.

* League Cup Champion 95-96 with Aston Villa. 
* First Division Champion 93-94.

* 19 full international caps for England. 
* He made his debut on the 12th of December 1995 at Wembley against Portugal (1-1). 
* He is selected for the European Championship in England, and was a starter in the five games that the team played.

* Schoolboy and apprentice at Crystal Palace, the club where he arrived in October 1986, he signs as a professional on the 17th of Janaury 1989.
* Makes his debut at Anfield on the 23rd of April 1991. Crystal Palace are defeated 3-0 by Liverpool. 
* Southgate scored the Crystal Palace goal in the famous match played at Selhurst Park when Eric Cantona, the Manchester forward, assaulted a spectator in the 94-95 season. At the end of that Championship, Crystal Palace was relegated. 
* He was the Palace captain and fought hard to prevent the club from making the drop in 1995, just before signing for Aston Villa. 
* On the 23rd of June 1995 he's transferred to Aston Villa for £2,500,000 making his debut on the 19th of August 1995 against Manchester United at Villa Park. 
* Playing for England in the European Champion of 96 Gareth had the bad luck to miss a decisive penalty in the shoot-out with Germany in the semifinals. The German goalkeeper Kopke stopped both his shot and England's hopes of reaching the final collapsed.

* Although he didn't start the season in very good form, as the games went by Gareth began to regain the level of the previous season, an injury however keeping him out for several weeks. In total he played 28 League games all of these from the start, and scored a goal against Blackburn Rovers in Aston Villa's home debut. Southgate continues to figure in Glenn Hoddle's plans for the England team.

148.name: Staunton
pages: * Steve Staunton is one of the most charismatic players at Aston Villa, the reason he was named captain of the 94-95 season. His strong leadership has allowed him to produce moments of brilliance such as the goal he scored against Manchester United at Old Trafford. His insistence and perserverance are an example for the younger players at the club.

* For a large part of his career Stephen has played both as a wing back and as a wide midfield player, always on the left. In recent times however he can often be seen in the centre of the defence, a position where he operates well. Very left-footed, he is noted for his capacity to join in the attack and take advantage of his powerful shot. He needs to improve his technique to connect better with the forwards. Even so, his strong personality means that he competes with feeling, never giving up a ball for lost and never shirking his responsibility in difficult situations.

* League Champion 89-90 with Liverpool. 
* F.A. Cup Champion 88-89 with Liverpool. 
* League Cup Champion 93-95 and 95-96 with Aston Villa.

* 68 full international appearances for The Republic of Ireland. 5 goals.
* He made his debut on the 19th of October at home against Tunisia.
* 1 international B appearance. 
* 3 under-21 appearances.

* Originally from the modest Irish team Dundalk, Stephen arrived at Liverpool on the 2nd of September 1986. His transfer was set at £20,000.
* After a run of 14 months without play he was loaned to Bradford City in November of 1987. His league debut occurs the following day against Sheffield United. 
* On his return to Liverpool Stephen makes his debut at Anfield on the 17th of September 1988 against Tottenham Hotspur coming on as a substitute in the second half. 
* An international for The Republic of Ireland. Stephen does not manage to settle into the left back position at Liverpool, and so on the 7th of August 1991, he moved to Aston Villa for £1 million. 
* He makes his debut in the Hillsborough Stadium, where Aston Villa beat Sheffield Wednesday 2-3. Staunton scores the winning goal. 
* In the 94-95 season he suffers from several injuries, one of which was damage to knee ligaments keeping him out for several games. Even so, he was made the "Villains" captain.

* Recovered from past injuries Steve Staunton started the 96-97 season with a place in the starting eleven. The tactical disposition of Brian Little who includes three central defenders pushed him out to the left of the central of the defence where he adapted without problem.  Only further injuries kept him out of the team, although he only missed eight League games.  He scored 2 goals, the first of these against Coventry which gave the "Villains" victory. Steve continued to accumulate caps with the Irish national team, where he has an undisputed place.

149.name: Scimeca
pages: * Riccardo Scimeca is one of the young players of worth from the Villa youth squad.  His extraordinary progress however seems to have stagnated a little in the last few seasons, so he hasn't managed to find his way into the line-ups fielded by Brian Little. The 97-98 season will be a challenge for him. If he does not meet it, it seems likely he will be transferred to another team where he can start again.

* A heavily built defender who can even play as a forward. Quick and strong, and technically blessed and with good playing vision, he just needs a few minutes at competitive level to show his footballing qualities.
* League Cup Champion 96.
* 5 times under-21 international for England.

* Originally from the club's youth squad, Scimeca signed for Aston Villa on the 7th of July 1993. 
* He made his league debut on the 17th of August 1995 against Manchester United at Villa Park (3-1).

* Last season Scimeca played eleven league games as a starter, a number somewhat less than he would have hoped.  As if this wasn't enough he was often ommited from the squad.  Brian Little used him as a central defender in several games, a position which he is not completely adapted to. To finish off a disappointing season, an injury kept Scimeca out for the last month of the Championship.

150.name: Draper
pages: * Since his arrival in Birmingham the progression of Mark Draper has taken a radical turn.  Not only has become an essential man in the plans of Aston Villa but he has also managed to attract the attention of Glen Hoddle for the World Cup in France. It is a safe bet that Mark is not going to let this one slip him by and so we will have to pay careful attention to his progress during the 97-98 season, possibly the most important of his career.

* A right-footed midfielder with an excellent technical foundation. A class player, he masters the ball perfectly, an aspect which is complemented by his good playing vision.  e adapts perfectly to the position of centre half, where he carries out the task of linking the defensive line with the forward line. In recent times he has been used in deeper positions allowing him to try out his powerful shot on goal.
* League Cup Champion 95-96.
* 3 time under-21 international for England.

* On the 12th of December 1988 he signed as a professional for Notts County, the club where he trained. 
* After 5 seasons with Notts County he was transferred to Leicester on the 22nd of July 1994 for £1,250,000, the most expensive of that summer.
* His contract with Leicester included a clause which allowed freed him to move should the club be relegated.  Draper signed for Aston Villa in August of 1995 for £3,250,000. 
* He made his debut with the "Villains" on the 19th of August 1995 in a game against Manchester United at  Birmingham. Aston Villa won 3-1. Draper scored the second goal.

* Draper was one of the best players at Aston Villa during last season. He played 29 League games, 28 of those from the start.  Only injury could keep him out the team. He accepted the responsibility of organising the team's play, and did so well. His work was noticed by Glenn Hoddle the national trainer, who included him in the squad for the game against Moldavia. He never got the chance to make his debut.

151.name: Taylor
pages: * Little by little Ian Taylor has found his place amongst the figures of the Premier League.  Although he cannot be considered a star, he is the type of footballer who is necessary in any team. Being multi-faceted, disciplined and efficient it has has meant that he enters into the Villa starting line-ups and providing that his form keeps up and he remains injury free, he will continue to be a starter in the 97-98 season.

* A right-footed midfielder of an attacking cut, Taylor is a centre half with an ability to score goals. He is also well adapted to playing in the centre of the defence however or even as wing back. In his game strength takes precedence over technique preventing him from taking on too much responsibility in the attack. His eye is always on the opponents goal, making him much appreciated by the trainers. He should improve his mastery of the ball. Combining this with his great pace and vercatility would make him unstoppable.
* League Champion 95-96.

* Taylor started his career in the modest Moor Green from where he moved to Port Vale on the 13th of July 1992 for £15,000. 
* His debut occurs on the 15th of August 1992 in a game against Fulham.
* On the 12th of July 1994 he is transferred to Sheffield Wednesday for £1 million. 
* On the 21st of December 1994 he signs for Aston Villa in an exchange taking Guy Whittingham to Sheffield Wednesday. 
* In his first game at Villa Park he scores a goal against Chelsea.
* In the final of the League Cup of 1996, against Leeds United, he is the scorer of the second of the three goals the "Villains" score (3-0).

* A good season produced by Ian Taylor in which he once more gave signs of his versatility, playing both as a centre half and in the centre of the defence. He suffered several injuries which kept him out for a few games, but all the time received the confidence of Brian Little.  He played 34 League games, 29 of them from the start. He scored 2 goals in the League and 1 in the League Cup.

152.name: Hendrie
pages: * Lee Hendrie  still hasn't made an appearnace at Villa Park. Now aged 20 and with footballing blood coursing through his veins, Lee hopes to beat the world but at times he is a little temperamental which means that on the pitch he is betrayed by his own character.  No-one doubts that sooner or later however he will find a slot for himself in the Premier League - and Paul Hendrie, his father and ex-footballer, will smile.

* A very fast forward who can play on either side. He takes advantage of his speed to go past defenders with a long-range good turn and scurry to the by-line from where he puts over a cross. Technically good, he is too individualistic at times and has quite a few small defects due to lack of experience. Very impulsive, his winning character could by a nasty but salutary shock for the team, although sometimes he oversteps the mark.
x

* 1 under-21 international appearance for England. 
* Youth international.

* A member of a footballing family he is the son of Paul Hendrie the ex Birmingham player. Cousin John Hendrie plays for Barnsley. 
* A professional since the 18th of May 1994, he made his debut in the Premier League on the 23rd of December 1995 at Loftus Road, in a game that Villa lost to QPR 1-0. Hendrie came on as a substitute for Mark Draper in the 33rd minute and was then sent off in the 90th, receiving his second yellow card.

* It was not a good season for Hendrie who hardly figured in the plans of Brian Little. In fact, he only played one game from the start, a statistic which says a lot. Called up for the English under-21 squad once, he did not play.  A season to forget.

153.name: Davis
pages: * Seemingly it is getting harder for Neil Davis to be successful at Aston Villa  He has more than passed the age when a footballer can be catalogued as promising and now needs to demonstrate that this promise is something real; for this he needs some chances. Brian Little for the moment does not seem to be giving him many and it is unlikely that his situation will change in the near future, so a transfer seems on the cards.

* A very fast forward who operates in the whole of the attacking zone, he is particularly difficult to stop when he has the ball under control on the run. His versatility is notable, and he always looks for the rival goal, although at times he precipates too much.  A good finisher, he needs some continuity to let his game settle down.
x
x

* Trained in the modest Redditch, he was transferred to Aston Villa on the 4th of May 1995 for £25,000.  However, he has to wait until the 19th of March 1996 to make his debut in a game against Middleborough played at Villa Park (0-0).  Davis comes on as a substitute for Julian Joachim in the second half. 
* Without any chances for getting a game at Villa, he is loaned for three months to Wycombe Wanderers of the Second Division on the 25th of October 1996.

* As Brian Little showed little inclination to use him Neil Davis was loaned for three months to Wycombe Wanderers. He met up again with John Gregory who had been his trainer years before.  Although he did not score his work was valued positively in the 13 games in the Second Division that he played.

154.name: Collymore
pages: * At times football produces surprises that are hard to understand. Stan Collymore was destined to mark an epoch at Liverpool, but now he won't. In principle he had everything going for him at Anfield, including the support from the terraces, but he failed. He has arrived at Birmingham with the label of a star, ready to return Aston Villa to the glory days of bygone times. The fans welcomed his signing with great hopes. Perhaps this time Stan will be successful.

* Collymore is a powerful goalscoring forward, one of those players able to make the difference. Helped by an impressive physique and a good technical foundation, he is a constant threat to rival defences. He has plenty of resources to solve complicated situations.  He shields the ball well with his body and makes good passes to his team mates. With his power, he drifts over to the wing and from there creates chances for his team mates. His strength when on the run makes him almost unstoppable. To all this he has an excellent shot on goal from outside the area. We are looking at a fantastic player, who needs a bit of consistency to become a star.  Given his youth, he has plenty of time ahead of him.
* 2 full international appearances for England.

* His first team was the modest Stafford Rangers. Prviously he had a trial at Walsall in June of 1988 and then at Wolverhampton Wanderers in March of 1989 without success. Graham Turner, the manager of Wolves offered him a contract but Stan didn't accept. 
* In the 90-91 season with Stafford he scored 9 goals in 10 games.
* On the 4th of January 1991 he was transferred to Crystal Palace for £100,000. 
* He made his debut on the 16th of February 1991 against Queens Park Rangers. 
* On the 20th of November 1992 he signed for Southend United.  He scored 15 goals in 30 games. 
* He moved to Nottingham Forest on the 5th of July 1993.  His price: £2 million. Forest were in the Second Division at the time and with the arrival of Collymore the club managed by Frank Clark returned to the Premier League.
* In August of 1995 Liverpool pay £8,500,000 to sign him. It is the most expensive signing in the history of the Anfield club. 
* He makes his debut for Liverpool scoring a great goal against Sheffield Wednesday at Anfield. 
* In his professional career he has scored 1 hat-trick and 1 own goal. Up to the end of the 94-95 season he has received 12 yellow cards and been sent off once. 
* On the 13th of May 1997 he is transferred to Aston Villa for £7 million becoming the most expensive signing in the history of the club.

* More was expected of Stan Collymore at Anfield.  In his second and final season at Liverpool, Stan "The Man" couldn't reach the level of adaptation that was expected of him and his name appearance too often on the list of substitutes. He played 30 League games, 25 from the start scoring 12 goals, but he always gave the impression that he could have done better.

155.name: Milosevic
pages: * It remains to be seen how what effect the arrival of Stan Collymore will have on the situation of Savo Milosevic at Aston Villa.   Until now the Yugoslavian international has been an undisputed starter in the team managed by Brian Little despite his performance not being as good as hoped last season. The arrival of Collymore however adds a bit of competition for places in the forward line. Milosevic who arrived at Birmingham with the label of star should rise up to the challenge posed by a man with the charisma of Collymore.

* An extraordinary forward, one of the best in the Premier League. To his impressive physical strength - which makes him a very hard player to stop - he has enviable technique. Although left-footed he can use both feet, capable of turning past his rival on either side and running quickly at the defence. He shoots well from a distance, hard and well placed. His strength and heavy build makes his presence felt in the area and he is able to make a gap for the shot both with his feet and head, an area also outstanding. He is a very complete footballer, young with a great future ahead of him. Although he looks clumsy at first sight, when he is watched more closely his quality can be easily seen.

* Yugoslavian League Champion 93-94. 
* Champion of the Yugoslavian Cup 94-95. 
* League Cup Champion in 95-96 with Aston Villa. 
* Top scorer in the Yugoslavian league in 93-94 and 94-95.

* 18 full international appearances for Yugoslavia. 10 goals. 
* He was the scorer of the first goal that Yugoslavia scored after their readmission by the FIFA, in a game played against Uruguay.

* Of Serbian family, Savo Milosevic was born in Bosnia. Aged 14 he moved to Belgrade, where he began to train in the lower ranks of Partizan.
* Champion of the Yugoslavian league in 1994, he scored three goals in the Cup final of the same season against Spartak Subotica (6-1). His team did the double. 
* Top scorer in the Yugoslavian league for two seasons running, in both he finished above Darko Kovacevic. In the 93-94 season he scored 20 and in the 94-95 season - 30. 
* In August 1995 he was transferred to Aston Villa for £3,500,000 making him the most expensive in the history of the club. The Italian team Parma and Athletico Madrid were interested in signing him. 
* It was said of Milosevic that in time he would be the "Best centre forward in Europe".

* Miloseviv didn't play his first game until the fourth week, but in his second appearance he scored two goals against Arsenal at Highbury. Since then he passed through a long goal drought which didn't stop until the end of the season. He scored 9 goals in 30 League games, not performing as well as was hoped.  n the other hand, Savo still entered in the Yugoslavian squad although he did not play as a starter with his national team. Even so, in October he scored a hat-trick against the Faroe Islands in a classification for the World Cup in France in '98.

156.name: Joachim
pages: * The departure of Tommy Johnson to Celtic could favour the Joachim's aspirations of playing regularly with the first team. Although the manager Brian Little was very keen on signing him, it has to be said that since he arrive at Villa during the 95-96 season, the under-21 international has hardly had chances to show his worth.

* Julian Joachim is a very fast forward, who can also operate as a midfield on the right. We are looking at a player with a lot of talent, a good turner who gets into good positions.  Skilful, he likes to participate in the build-up. Very young, he needs to take full advantage of his excellent ability.

* League Cup Champion in 95-96. 
* Under 20 European Champion with England. 
* Third Place in the Youth World Cup in Australia in 1993.

* 9 under-21 international appearances with England. 
* 8 youth international appearances.

* He joined Leicester City as a schoolboy and turned professional on the 15th of September 1992. 
* In the 94-95 season he scored his first goal for Leicester in the Premier League against Newcastle. This same season, he saw the club relegated to the First Division. 
* At Leicester he coincided with Brian Little, the manager who recommended his signing by Aston Villa half-way through the 95-96 season. 
* His transfer fee was set at £1,500,000.  He makes his debut this same day in a game at home against Wimbledon (3-3).

* In his second season at Villa Park, Julian Joachim continued to be a regular sight on the substitutes' bench.  He played 15 League games but only played from the start in 3 of these.  Scorer of 3 goals with the first team, he showed his effectiveness in front of goal in his performances with the reserve teams.

157.name: Yorke
pages: * Dwight Yorke has become on his own merits one of the idols of the fans at Villa Park. The Trinidad and Tobago international combines all the qualities needed to be a star: class, talent and charisma. Yorke produces goals, impossible runs and details of subtilty with the new Aston Villa. With him, the fans dream of repeating past glories.

* Yorke is one of the fastest forwards in the Premier League. He is very good at finding space making it easier for his team mates to pass to him and taking advantage of his speed to get to the opponent's goal. Last season he showed himself to be a good goalscorer, clever in the area and with a good header  If he keeps up his progress he will be one of the best footballers in England.
* League Cup Champion 93-94 and 95-96.
* 15 full international caps for Trinidad and Tobago. 7 goals.

* The former manager of Aston Villa Graham Taylor noticed Yorke during a tour of Trinidad and Tobago. Taylor set his sights on signing the player who was playing for the local team Signal Hill. The signing was realised for £120,000 on the 19th of December 1989. 
* His debut occured on the 24th of March 1990 against Crystal Palace.
* After the Check Jozef Venglos finished his spell as manager of Aston Villa, the arrival of Ron Atkinson saw Yorke's career take off. 
* In the 94-95 season Yorke renouced the opportunity to play in the Pan-American Championship so that he wouldn't lose his place at Aston Villa.
* Yorke was top scorer at Aston Villa in the 95-96 and 96-97 season at Aston Villa. 
* Athletico Madrid were interested in signing him in the summer of 1996.

* For the second season running Dwight Yorke was the top scorer at Aston Villa scoring 17 goals in the 37 League games that he played.  Even though he didn't start the season on top form, as the weeks went by the Trinidad and Tobago international tuned his game. He scored a hat-trick against Newcastle at Saint James' Park and although he never reached the same level as in the 95-96 season Yorke was still one of the best players at Aston Villa.
