158.name: Manninger
pages: * With the arrival of Alex Manninger at Highbury, there are now four goalkeepers on the Arsenal payroll. Given that David Seaman will be continuing as the club's first choice in goal, Alex will have to settle for learning everything he can from the England goalkeeper and battling for a place on the bench with the other two substitute goalkeepers, John Lukic and Vince Bartram. He was signed with one eye on the future by Arsene Wenger, who saw in the young Austrian a very promising goalkeeper.

* Still a young man, he possesses all the physical qualities he needs to go on to become a great goalkeeper: physical presence, agility and speed. However he still has a logical  lack of experience in competitive football at the top level.
x
* He has represented Austria at Under-21 level.

* He broke through into Casino Salzburg's first team squad during the 95-96 season. During that same campaign he made his debut in the Austrian First Division although his one and only apperance came as a substitute. 
* During the summer of 1996 he was transfered to Casino Graz. 
* He has been an Arsenal player since June 1997.
* He spent last season with Casino Graz, a club who finished in fifth place last season in the Austrian League.

159.name: Lukic
pages: * John Lukic is a player who comes and goes. He has spent the whole of his playing  career with Leeds United and Arsenal, having had two different spells with each club. He is now playing out the final years of his career at Highbury, in the shadow of David Seaman, widely regarded as the best keeper in the Premier League. Just as he was last season John Lukic will be ready and waiting if he is needed to take his place in the Arsenal line up. However he will also be aware that during the 97-98 season the competition for a place in Arsene Wenger's side will be even more intense than before.

* Despite his extraordinary physical stature John Lukic is a spectacular goalkeeper, blessed with great reflexes and capable of making some astounding saves. Safe in the air, Lukic stands out for his consistency . A player with vast experience behind him, this is evident  in the tremendous positional sense he shows when he is out in the action. On the other hand, he has a weakness when he has to come out to go down at the feet of strikers, a situation  which exposes his lack of speed.

* League Championship winners medals 1989 and 92. 
* League Cup winners medal 1987. 
* Charity Shield medals  89, 90 and 92.

* 1 "B" international appearance for England. 
* 7 under-21 international appearances. 
* 10 youth international appearances.

* Born to Yugoslav parents, John Lukic took his first steps in the world of schoolboy football in the ranks of his hometown club Chesterfield in Derbyshire. In October 1975 he joined the youth set up at Leeds United, under the watchful eye of David Harvey, John's boyhood hero. He finally turned professional on 16th December 1978. Nevertheless he didn't get to make his debut until 13th October 1979 in a game against Brighton. 
* Lukic set a new record in the history of Leeds when he played in a total of 146 consecutive league games, blocking the route to the first team of keepers of the quality of Henry Smith, a Scottish international, and ironically David Seaman.
* At the end of the 81-82 season Leeds were relegated to the Second Division although  Lukic stayed with the club for another year.
* After losing his place in the first team for Harvey, he was transfered to Arsenal for 50,000 pounds on 25th July 1983. In his first season with the Gunners he made just 4 appearances, being kept out of the side by a keeper of the stature of Pat Jennings. Slowly but surely he settled down in the first team and went on to play a key role in the club's league Championship triumph of 1989, playing in every league game.
* On 14th June 1990 he returned to Elland Road. George Graham had announced his interest in taking David Seaman to Arsenal and so Lukic decided to return to Elland Road. Leeds paid 1,000,000 pounds to sign him and Lukic was able to enjoy regular first team. football. Two years after his return to the club, the  "Whites" won the league title, with Lukic, once again, an ever present in the side.
* His average of goals conceded per game, up to the end of the 94-95 season was 1.075
* He began the 95-96 season as a regular member of the starting line up, though he later lost his place following a poor game against Sheffield United. Despite getting back into  the side, and playing in the League Cup final which the club lost to Aston Villa, at the end of the season he became a free agent.
* Having realised the situation he was in at Leeds, Arsenal decided to sign him again, six years after leaving the club ( June 1996). At the time Lukic was 35 years old.
* During the course of his career he has played in every game in eight separate league seasons  (80-81, 81-82, 87-88, 88-89, 89-90, 90-91, 91-92 and 94-95).
* He is known by the nickname "Big Johnny Goal Kick".

* A back injury to teammate David Seaman, allowed John Lukic to make 15 league appearances last season for Arsenal, following his return to Highbury six years after he left the club. John demonstrated that he reamins a very  dependable keeper. Proof of that came in the month of March when his tremendous performances saw him manage to keep three consecutive clean sheets against Everton, Nottingham Forest and Southampton, giving new hope to the Gunners' title aspirations.

160.name: Seaman
pages: * Upon David Seaman's broad shoulders falls the dual responsibility of keeping not  just Arsenal's goal intact but also that of the England side, though it is a responsibility which never seems to affect him. In fact, quite the opposite seems to be the case, the England international goalkeeper always giving the impression of having everything under control, radiating composure and security in everything he does. Far from possessing the extrovert and occasionally crazy character that the majority of goalkeepers around the world seem to have, Seaman moves around out on the park with an aura of ice cool composure around him. Some experts have commented that the best goalkeepers are those who are as elegant when they concede a goal as they are making a save. Seaman is one of those. Whether that particular theory is true or not, what nobody doubts is that Seaman is an extraordinary goalkeeper, one of the best in the world. And, what is even more important is that David Seaman is, for the whole country, England's number one. The World Cup finals in France await him.

* Regarded by many critics as one of the best goalkeepers in the world, David Seaman stands out for his security, speed, agility and consistency although undoubtedly the most outstanding characteristic in his game is the extraordinary composure he maintains at all times. He rarely, if ever, loses his head during the course of a game and is capable of spreading this sense of security to his defensive colleagues, who always have full confidence in the goalkeeper they have behind them. Seaman is a player who is capable of sorting out even the tightest of situations with apparent ease. He is also good with the ball at his feet, and has no hesitation in taking the ball around opposing forwards if he feels he needs to. 
* Now a veteran, with vast experience at the highest of international levels behind him, as time has gone by he seems to have simply got better. For all of these reasons David Seaman is a keeper who is a real guarantee in goal for any side.

* European Cup Winners Cup winners medal 94. 
* European Cup Winners Cup runners up medal 95. 
* League Championship winners medal 91. 
* F.A. Cup winners medal 93. 
* League Cup winners medal 93.

* 36 full international appearances for England. He made his debut on 16th November 1988 in a friendly against Saudi Arabia in Riyadh (1-1). 
* In the 1996 European Championships in England, he was a member of the five games that his country played, before being knocked out in the semi-finals by Germany. Seaman played against Switzerland, Scotland, Holland, Spain and the Germans.
* 7 "B" international appearances. 
* 10 under-21 international appearances.

* Seaman began his career with Leeds United, who he joined as an apprentice in March 1980. On 22nd September 1981, he took the step up to the first team, though, seeing how opportunities were few and far between he decided to accept an offer from Peterborough United, of the Fourth Division, who paid l4,000 pounds to sign him. He moved on 13th August 1982. He quickly made himself the club's first choice in goal and made his debut on 28th August 1982 against Stockport County  (1-1).
* His next destination was Birmingham City, who he joined on 5th October 1984 in exchange for 100,000 pounds. His spell at the club proved to a brilliant one, even to the point of keeping 13 consecutive clean sheets which helped the club win promotion to the Second Division finishing the campaign in second place behind Oxford United. In the two seasons he played in goal for Birmingham he played in 75 league games, 5 F.A. Cup games and 4 League Cup games.
* On 7th August 1986 he was transfered to Queens Park Rangers for 225,000 pounds. During his first season at the club he played in every game except one. In the game he missed, QPR lost 7-1 against Sheffield Wednesday, a statistic which explains all by itself the quality of the keeper that Rangers had in their squad. His excellent spell with Rangers, where he played in 141 league games, 17 in the F.A. Cup and 13 in the League Cup allowed him to take the step up to one of the biggest clubs in the country, and so, he moved across London to Arsenal.
* On 18 May 1990 Seaman was at the centre of the most expensive transfer involving a goalkeeper in the history of English football. George Graham, then manager of  Arsenal had no hesitation in paying 1,300,000 pounds to take him to Highbury . At the end of his first season at the club Arsenal lifted the league title.
* An automatic choice in the England side, both under Graham Taylor and Terry Venables, surprisingly Seaman didn't play in the 1992 European Championships in Sweden. After an error he made in a game against Czechoslovakia, Taylor decided not to call him up for  the tournament, naming Nigel Martyn and Chris Woods in his squad. It was Woods who was first choice, but the England side went on to have a very mediocre tournament. A few months later Seaman returned to the national side.
* After winning a European Cup Winners Cup winners medal in 1994, in the same competition the following season, Seaman was elevated to heroe status by the Gunners supporters when he played in the ties against Auxerre and Sampdoria with a broken rib. On top of this, in the semi-final against Sampdoria, in Genoa, his brilliant performance in the penalty shoot out took Arsenal through to the final for the second year in succession. However,  Seaman was unable to do anything about Nayim's goal from the halfway line in  the last minute of extra time which gave the trophy to Spanish side Real Zaragoza. 
* During the 95-96 season he once again showed just how safe a keeper he is in the 1996 European Championships in England, saving a penalty from Scotland's Gary McAllister in the first phase of the tournamentand another one from Spain's Miguel Angel Nadal in the penatly shoot out in the quarter finals. Although the semi-final against Germany also went to penalties Seaman was unable to save any of Germans' spot kicks. Nevertheless the acclamation that came his way was in recognition of the quality he had shown throughout the tournament. A few days later, when he appeared at the Wimbledon tennis championships to watch a match at the prestigious tournament, he was given a spontaneous and thundering ovation from the publie which went on to last for several minutes.

* Despite injury problems, David Seaman demonstrated over the course of last  season that he remains the best goalkeeper in England. He played in 22 league games, all of those as a member of the starting line up, and proved to be in particularly oustanding form in the run in to the season, helping Arsenal to eventually finish third in the table, level on points with both Newcastle and Liverpool.
* The season brought David Seaman plenty of great moments; being acclaimed, as he was, in numerous stadiums thanks to his performances in the 1996 Euroepan Championships. As a result he was able to see for himself that his work had been well appreciated by supporters all over the country.

161.name: Upson
pages: * Matthew Upson was signed by Arsenal with one eye on the future. The young central defender, signed from Luton Town, barely has any experience of football at the top level, and it seems unlikely that he will get any during the 97-98 season. Nevertheless, the coaching staff at Highbury, with Arsene Wenger at the head, have plenty of confidence  in him which means it wouldn't be a great surprise to see him given the opportunity to make his Premier League debut during the course of the season.

* Still a very young player, he generally operates at the heart of the defence. Dominant in the air and good with the ball at his feet, he remains composed when he is called upon to  play the ball around. A good passer of the ball he needs to get more experience behind him  to make the most of his tremendous natural ability.
x
x

* A product of the Luton Town youth system, he made his first team debut on 31st August 1996 in a home victory against Rotherham United (1-0), although he wasn't to make another  appearance all season. At the time Matthew was just 17 years old.
* On 10th May 1997 he was transfered to Arsenal for 2,000,000 pounds although several  other Premier League clubs were also interested in signing him.

* As captain of the Luton Town youth team he took the side to the semi-finals of the F.A. Youth Cup. He also managed to make his first team debut during the course of last season in August against Rotherham United; although it was an appearance as a substitute. Nevertheless his progress didn't go unnoticed by the Arsenal coaching Staff, who, in May, exercised an option that they already had, to sign the player.

163.name: Hughes
pages: * Steve Hughes demonstrated last season that he was a player who could be trusted to do a job in the first team. Not only did he give a good account of himself whenever he was thrust into the action, but also, thanks to the touches of class he showed, he had the Highbury fans wondering what else he might have in store for them. He is already an England under-21 international and, although he will have a tough task on his hands trying to get into the side during the course of the 97-98 season, nobody is in any doubt that he is going to become one of Arsenal's star men in the next few years. All he needs to do is maintain his outstanding progress.

* A young midfielder who generally plays tight down the left hand side, he has extraordinary basic techniqye, is skillful with the ball at his feet and can beat a man with apparent ease. He likes to cut in from the flank to put accurate crosses over for the strikers. He has a good shot in his left foot which he doesn't hesitate to use when given even the slightest opportunity. A player for the future he will need to keep working at his game if he wants to get even better.
* F.A. Youth Cup winners medal  94.

* 4 under-21 international appearances for England.
* A youth and schoolboy international.

* A product of the Arsenal youth system, in 1994 he won an F.A. Youth Cup winners medal.
* He made his Premier League debut on 26th December 1994 in a game against Aston Villa (0-0); although he didn't get to make another first team appearance  throughout the rest of the season. In the following season, the 95-96 campaign, he again made just one Premier League appearance .
* The arrival of Arsene Wenger in the hot seat at Arsenal in the 96-97 season saw the doors to the first team open up for him. As a result, in January 1997 he managed to score in a Cup game against Sunderland, opening his account for the club, while on 15th March 1997 he scored his first goal in the Premier League against Southampton at The Dell.
* He was captain of the England under-21 side during the 1996-97 season.

* Last season saw Steve Hughes make the breakthrough into the Premier League. Arsene Wenger gave him opportunities in the side and the youngster took full advantage of them. He played in 14 league games, 9 of those as a member of the starting line up, and managed to find the back of the net once, against Southampton at The Dell. He also managed to find the back of the net in a cup game against Sunderland, but, above all, proved himself to be a player of real quality. He replaced Paul Merson on several occasions, and showed some tremendous form both for Arsenal and for the England Under-21 side, which he was captain of. Without any doubt, Steve Hughes was one of the more pleasent surprises of the 96-97 season.

164.name: Petit
pages: * Emmanuel Petit's career has always followed a steady rate of progress. The French international showed at Monaco that he is the perfect club man, disciplined and effective. He made his debut under Arsene Wenger at Monaco and soon moved on to play  for the full national side. Now manager at Arsenal, Wenger has turned to Petit's services once again, as he tries to bring the title to Highbury. All the indications are that Petit is likely to become a key man in the side during the 97-98 season. He has a   more difficult job on his hands if he wants to get into the French squad for the 98 World Cup Finals, since at present he doesn't figure in the plans of French manager AimÚ Jacquet.

* Versatility is Emmanuel Petit's most outstanding quality. The Frenchman is a genuine jack of all trades, capable of playing in a number of different positions either in defence or in midfield. A good technical player he possesses good vision and is an accurate passer of the ball. He brings the ball out well from the back, under control, and passes it around thoughtfully. Defensively he is disciplined and has good positional sense. However, he makes only a limited contribution in an attacking sense and seldom finds the back of the net.

* French League Championship winners medal 1997.
* French Cup winners medal 1991.

* 15 full international appearances for France
* He made his debut on 15th August 1990, in a game against Poland (0-0).

* After coming through the youth ranks at Monaco, he made his first team debut on 18th March 1989 in a league game against Sochaux (0-0). Monaco's coach at the time was Arsene Wenger.
*He scored his first goal for the club on 28th July 1990 in an away game against Auxerre (0-1).
* At the beginning of the 96-97 season he was being chased by Tottenham Hotspur, although finally the London club failed to reach an agreement with Monaco, which would have allowed the transfer to go through. That same season Monaco went on to win the French league title.
* He has been an Arsenal player since 4th June 1997. He arrived at Highbury together with his countryman Gilles Grimandi, at the request of manager Arsene Wenger.

* Last time out Emmanuel Petit helped Moncaco to win the French title. Throughout the whole of the campaign Petit demonstrated his versatility  and became a key man in coach Jean Tigana's side. He played in a total of 29 games.

165.name: Marshall
pages: *  At the end of the 95-96 season Scott Marshall was included on the Arsenal  transfer list. He was even offered to a number of Spanish clubs, but, finally, he remained at Highbury. His appearances in the side are very limited and in fact, he is only called upon when one of the first choice central defenders ahead of him in the queue is either injured or suspended. The outlook is bleak for the Scot, who, if he was able to enjoy more regular first team football could even find himself challenging for a place in the Scotland squad for the World Cup Finals in France in 1998.

* Scott Marshall is very much a modern central defender, capable of playing a short passing game to bring the ball out at the back,  setting up the team's attacks. He is dominant in the air and is a tight marker, who doesn't hesitate to go in hard if he feels he needs to, although he always goes for the ball. He is also a dangerous player in the opposing penalty area when he moves forward for set pieces to try and get his head to the ball. He possesses the youth and the natural ability he needs to go on to become a fine player. The few errors he makes can generally be put down to his lack of experience.
x

* 5 under-21 international appearances for Scotland. 
* 3 youth international appearances.

* The son of ex -professional Gordon Marshall, and the brother of Celtic keeper  Gordon junior, Scott Marshall learnt his trade in the youth ranks at Arsenal. He has been a professional since 18th March 1991, making his league debut on  6th May 1993, in a game against  Sheffield Wednesday.
* In December 1993 he was loaned out to Rotherham United, while on 25th August 1994 he went out on another loan spell, for three months, to Sheffield United. At the Bramall Lane club he covered for the absence of the injured Paul Beesley forming a defensive partnership with Brian Gayle, playing in every game the side played during his spell at the club. 
* Back at Highbury for the 95-96 season he scored his first goal for the Gunners, a header, against Newcastle United on 23rd March 1996, in a  2-0 victory. Despite playing in 11 games, at the end of the season he was placed on the transfer list by  Arsenal and was even offered out to several Spanish clubs.

* It wasn't easy for Scott Marshall to force his way into the Arsenal line up during the course of last season. In fact, before the start of the season he had been placed on the transfer list by the club. The presence of three central defenders of the calibre of Bould, Keown and Adams, all of them internationals, prevented him from making more than 8 appearances. Nevertheless on the 8 occasions he did play Scott gave a good account of himself.

166.name: Keown
pages: * After a number of years away from Highbury, in 1993 Martin Keown returned to Arsenal, where he came through the ranks. The Arsenal defender returned to the club with the prestige of having made his debut for the full England side and his own personal reputation intact following England's failure in the 1992 European Championships in Sweden. He is now captain of Arsenal, in the games in which Tony Adams doesn't play, and more importantly has won over the supporters. The way in which the Arsenal supporters chant his name before each home game is the best possible reward for a player who, despite being at the veteran stage of his career, seems to make a greater contribution to to the Gunners' cause. Now well settled down in Arsene Wenger's side, his next challenge is to force his way into Glenn Hoddle's squad for the World Cup Finals in France.

* Although throughout his career Martin Keown has played both in midfield and at  right back, it is at the heart of the defence where he is at his best. An outstanding man to man marker he is quick, strong, on occasions hard, forceful and possesses plenty of character. Good in the air he moves forward to get his head to the ball at set pieces, although it is very rare to see him find the back of the net. Technically limited, he stands out for his stamina which allows him to keep up a tremendous level of performance throughout the ninety minutes, during which time he shows tremendous fighting spirit.

* European Cup winners Cup runner up medal 95. 
* Charity Shield medal 93.

* 15 full international appearances for England, scoring once. He made his debut on 19th February 1992 in a game against France at Wembley. He scored his first international on 25th March of that same year against Czechoslovakia in Prague (2-2).
* A member of the England squad in the 1992 European Championships in Sweden he played against Denmark (0-0), France (0-0) and in the game which England lost 2-1 against the host nation.
* One "B" international appearance. 
* 8 under-21 international appearances. 
* 4 youth international appearances.

* Martin Keown began playing football as a young boy in his home town of Oxford. In. October 1980 he joined the youth ranks at Arsenal, where he learnt his trade before taking the step up to the first team squad on 2nd February 1984. Shortly after, on 23rd February, he made his debut in a game against Manchester City.
* One year later on 15th February 1995 he was loaned out to  Brighton & Hove Albion, who were then in the Second Division. 
* On 9th June 1996, after failing to agree on a new deal with Arsenal, he was transfered to Aston Villa for 200,000 pounds. He immediately made himself an automatic first team choice and remained so for the three years he spent at the club.
* On 7th August 1989 he signed for Everton, who paid 750,000 pounds to take him to Goodison Park. His superb performances for the Merseyside club opened up the doors to the full England side. He formed a partnership at the heart of the England defence with Des Walker and, surprisingly, managed to score a scpectacular goal for the national side against Czecoslovakia in Prague. 
* One of the best man to man markers in England, Martin Keown is especially remembered for the marking job he did on  Ruud Gullit in an international game, while the Dutchman  was still an  A.C. Milan player.
* His return to Highbury came on 4th February 1993, six years after he originally left the club. His valuation in the transfer market had risen to 2,000,000 pounds. On 3rd December 1994 he scored his first goal in an Arsenal shirt. That day the Gunners drew 2-2 at the City Ground against Nottinghma Forest.
* Up to the end of the 94-95 season he had been booked 24 times, been sent off 3 times and had scored 5 own goals.
* During the 95-96 season he was named captain in the absence of Tony Adams. Injuries to Adams himself and Steve Bould saw Keown forming a central defensive partnership with Andy Linighan. Keown went on to make himself one of the most popular players with the Highbury faithful.

* If, during the 95-96 season Martin Keown had been one of the best players in the side, then his performances last season were even better. An automatic first choice in defence for Arsene Wenger he played in 23 league games. Keown became a real tower of strength for Arsenal, who ended the campaign with the best defensive record in the Premier League.  His form was such that Glenn Hoddle granted him the occasional return to the England side.

167.name: Bould
pages: * For a long time now, Steve Bould has formed a partnership with Tony Adams at the heart  of the Arsenal defence. Both men are now coming to the end of their playing careers, although they continue to perform to an extraordinary level. The arrival of Arsene Wenger at the club  has been no problem for the veteran defenders. They both have the full support of the manager, a confidence which doesn't look as though it is going to waver during the 97-98 season. As a result, both Steve Bould and Tony Adams will be out to make sure that the Arsenal back line is once again the toughest to break down in English football.

* Steve Bould is a classic central defender. He has great physical presence, and strength, he is  extremely dominant in the air in both penalty areas but is not the most comfortable of players when he is asked to play a short passing game to bring the ball out from the back. He moves forward to support the attack at set pieces, where his heading ability brings him the occasional goal. He is a specialist in flicking the ball on at the near post, something which always creates danger in the opposing goalmouth. Defensively he is safe and forceful and is decisive when he has to cover across the back as the last line of defence. He makes up for his technical weaknesses with all the know how of the experienced player that he now is.

* European Cup Winners Cup winners medal 94. 
* League Championships winners medals 89 and 91.

* 2 full international appearances for England. 
* 1"B" international appearance, scoring once.

* Born in Stoke-on-Trent, Steve Bould went on to join the youth ranks at Stoke City. A professional from 15th November 1980, he made his first team debut on 26th September 1981in a game against Middlesbrough. 
* Not being presented too many opportunities, he was loaned out to Torquay United on 19th October 1982. 
* From the 1983-84 season onwards he began to make himself a regular in the side at Stoke City, who were relegated to the Scond Division, during the 84-85 season.
* On 13th June 1988 he was transfered to Arsenal for 390,000 pounds. He arrived at  the club together with Lee Dixon, and at the end of their first season at Highbury the Gunners lifted the league title. Together with Tony Adams he forms one of the best central defensive partnerships in English football.
* After winning a European Cup Winners Cup winners medal in 1994, in the same competition the following year, he became one of the stars of the semi-final against Italian club Sampdoria, scoring twice in the game at Highbury. However an accumulation of yellow cards prevented him from playing in the final in Paris, against Spanish side Real Zaragoza.

* Free from injury, Steve Bould was able to go on to complete an outstanding season. He adapted  perfectly to Arsene Wenger's style of play which included a three man defensive line up. Together  with Tony Adams and Martin Keown, Steve Bould made a decisive contribution to Arsenal's  strength at the back which gave them the best defensive record in the Premier League. He played in a total of 33 league games, all of those as a member of the starting line up.

168.name: Winterburn
pages: * Although, at the beginning of each season, there are plenty of voices who announce that the time has come for Nigel Winterburn to step down, the truth is that the veteran defender remains immovable in his position. The arrival of Arsene Wenger in the hot seat at Arsenal has brought no change in the player's situation, a player who, year after year has demonstrated that he possesses two fundamental requirements; a superb left foot, and a genuine Gunners' spirit. For these reasons, while the club are happy that there is no siutable candidate to replace him, he will remain a regular member of the first team.

* His natural position is left back. where, defensively, he is vey comfortable. Tenacious and a real fighter, he wins plenty of possession which he uses well, playing off either short passes or long balls into the area looking for a teammate to connect with a header. Very much a left footed player, he likes to keep the ball on his stronger foot, though he occasionally lacks accuracy. At times a hard player, Nigel Winterburn is not a brilliant footballer, but does a good efficent job.

* European Cup Winners Cup winners medal 94. 
* European Cup Winners Cup runners up medal 95. 
* League Championship winners medal 89 and 91. 
* F.A. Cup Winners medal 93. 
*Charity Shield 89, 91 and 93.

* 2 full international appearances for England. He made his debut on 15th November 1989 replacing Stuart Pearce in a friendly game against Italy at Wembley (0-0).
* His final international appearance took place on 19th June 1993. Winterburn replaced Lee Sharpe in the England-Germany game which formed part of the United States Cup. England lost the match 1-2.
* 4 "B" international appearances. 
* 1Under-21 international appearance. 
* 1 youth international appearance.

* Birmingham City was where Nigel Winterburn learnt his trade, and was also the club who gave him his league debut. He signed professional terms for the Blues on 14th August 1981, while he made his debut on 27th August 1983 in a game against Bolton Wanderers. However, shortly after this first appearance he was released by Birmingham.
* On 22nd September 1983 he signed for Wimbledon, then in the Third Division. Nigel enjoyed the club's promotion seasons to the Second and First Divisions, playing in the top flight of  English football during the 86-87 season.  
* Voted Player of the Year at Wimbledon for four years in succession, he was transfered to Arsenal on 26th May 1987 for 407,000 pounds. He took over from Kenny Sansom, and made his debut for the Gunners on 21st November. That same season he was a member of the Arsenal side that lost the League Cup final against Luton Town, a game in which he also missed a penalty. In his second season with the north London giants he won a League Championship winners medal. Shortly afterwards he made his debut for the full England side. 
* However, he has never made a starting appearance for England .

* Nigel Winterburn managed to steer clear of injury for the second consecutive season. This allowed him to go on to bnecome the only player at the club to play in all 38 Premier League games. The arrival of Arsene Wenger in place of  Bruce Rioch, meant no change for Nigel Winterburn, who kept up his consistent form right throughout the season. At the end of the season he was awarded a well deserved testimonial game against Glasgow Rangers, in which the Highbury fans were able to show their appreciation for his ten faithful years at the club.

169.name: Dixon
pages: * After ten years at Highbury, Lee Dixon has gone on to become one of the most charismatic players at the club. In every game he plays, the veteran defender shows the same fighting spirit which has made him an example for all the young players in the Gunners's youth set up. He has been a first team regular for all of the managers who have occupied the Arsenal hot seat over the last ten years and nothing would seem to suggest that the 97-98 campaign is likely to be any different .Arsene Wenger and the whole of Highbury have complete faith in him.

* An attack minded right back, Lee Dixon likes to get forward to help out the attack, getting down the flank to put crosses over into the penalty area, although occasionally his lack of technical ability is evident when he gets into the attacking third of the field. Nevertheless he is a very consistent player who is capable of keeping up a good level of form throughout the whole of the season. Fast, and with good positional sense he is a very difficult defender for opposing forwards to beat.
* His strong character makes him one of the pillars of the side, passing his own will to win on to his teammates. An experienced player, his defensive qualities have improved with the years. He is good in tight situations and keeps his cool well he is under pressure, as he also does from the spot in penalty shoot outs.

* European Cup Winners Cup winners medal 94. 
* European Cup Winners Cup runners up medal 95. 
* League Championship winners medals 89 and 91. 
* F.A. Cup winners medal  93. 
* Charity Shield  medals 89, 91 and 93.

* 21 full international appearances for England, scoring once. He made his debut on 25th April 1990 in 4-2 friendly victory over Czechoslovakia at Wembley.
* He scored his only international goal on 27th March 1991 against the Republic of Ireland in Dublin (1-1) in a qualifying game for the 1992 European Championships in Sweden.
* 6 "B" international appearances.

* Born in Manchester and brought up through the youth ranks at Burnley, Lee Dixon turned professional for the Turf Moor club at 18 years of age on 21st July 1982. Almost one year later, on 10th May 1983 he made his league debut against Queens Park Rangers.
* He became a free agent after playing just 4 games for Burnley, proving unable to force his way into the plans of manager John Bond. On 16th February 1984 he joined Chester City where he also proved to be unable to make much of an impression. Once again a free agent he moved on Bury on 15th July 1985.  
* In his one and only seasaon at Bury, he played in 45 games, scoring 5 times. His peformances didn't go unnoticed by  Stoke City, who signed  him for 40,000 pounds on 18th July 1986.
* His progress was unstoppable and Dixon was soon knocking on the doors of the top flight of English football. As a result on 29th January 1988 he signed for Arsenal, who paid 400,000  pounds to take him to Highbury.
* In his second season with the Gunners he won a league championship medal, a feat he went on to repeat two seasons later. Shortly after he went on to become an England international and win European honours at club level. Dixon shows his will to win in every game he plays, and doesn't hide from the responsibility of taking spot kicks in penalty shoot outs.
* An occasional captain of the side, only injuries prevent him from taking his place as a member of the starting line up.

* For yet another season Lee Dixon was an automatic choice in the Arsenal defence, which proved to be the most miserly in the Premier League. The arrival of Arsene Wenger at the club allowed him to enjoy more attacking freedom. Dixon went on to play in 32 league games, scoring twice. One of his goals, against Newcastle at St. James' Park, was an especially valuable one giving the Gunners a 1-2 victory after playing for more than an hour with 10 men.

170.name: Boa Morte
pages: * Luis Boa Morte is one of the numerous signings that Arsenal have made with a view to the 97-98 season. The Portuguese midfielder arrived in England as a complete unknown, although many people thought, as a result of the physical similarity, that it was just a thirteen years younger version of Ian Wright. Initially it would seem that he has a difficult task on his hands trying to get into Arsene Wenger's  side, taking into account the tremendous competition that exists at Highbury. But, he will no doubt get his chance eventually, and will have to make sure that he is ready to take full advantage of it when it does eventually come along.

* A very young midfielder he can operate down either flank, although it is down the left where he is at his best. Fast, brave and skillful, he possesses the ability to beat a man on the run, and doesn't need to be asked twice to have a go at goal. Despite his youth he shows glimpses of genuine class which time and experience can only improve.
* Portuguese Youth Championship winners medal 1996.
x

* A product of the youth set up at Portuguese club Sporting Lisbon, he stood out especially during the 95-96 season when he was a member of the side that won the Portuguese Youth title, a competition in which he scored 10 goals. 
* Without having made his league debut for the Lisbon based club, he was signed  by Arsenal in June 1997.
* He bears a striking resemblance to England international striker Ian Wright.

* Luis Boa Morte spent last season playing for Sporting Lisbon's youth side in Portugal. Although there was speculation that he could soon be taking the step up to the club's first team, the move didn't eventually come about.

171.name: Méndez
pages: * The signing of Alberto Mendez  was one of the big surprises of the season. Not only was a he complete unknown in England, neither were there any references about him from Germany, the country from where Arsenal signed him. As a result Mendez represents something of a risk on the part of Arsene Wenger. It remains to be seen whetheror not the French manager has got it right.

* Alberto Mendez is an attack minded midfielder, who generally plays pushed out towards  the left hand side. Skillful with the ball at his feet, he gets forward whenever he gets the slightest opportunity, making the most of his passing ability and his powerful shooting. He needs to develop more security in his defensive duties, showing certain tactical weaknesses, due mainly to his lack of experience of compeition at the highest level.
x
x

* Born in Germany of Spanish parents he could qualify for dual nationality.  
* He came through the youth set up at FC Nuremberg, where he played in the youth team, although never managed to make a first team appearance for the club.
* He was discovered by a friend of Arsene Wenger, who recommended him to the Arsenal manager after seing him stand out in a German regional league, in the ranks of  modest FC Feucht. In fact in his last season at the club Mendez scored 19 goals in 34 games.
* He signed for Arsenal in June1997. On 8th July 1997 he played his first game in a Gunners shirt in a friendly against St. Albans.

* He spent last season in the ranks of FC Feucht, a modest club in a German  regional league where he was the team's star player. Mendez scored 19 goals in 34 league games, a performance which helped his team to win promotion. He also showed his tremendous goalscoring ability in the Cup, a competitionin which he hit 7 goals in 6 games.

172.name: Grimandi
pages: * Gilles Grimandi made his debut in the French First Division, under the watchful eye of Arsene Wenger, in 1991. Almost seven years later the French coach has turned to him again to reinforce the Arsenal defence. Grimandi is setting out on a new stage in his career, in a new country, and in a league as competitive as the Premier League.

* He generally plays at the heart of the defence although he can do a job in other poistions along the back line. He is a forceful, defensive player who likes to keep thing as simple as possible. He possesses good technical ability and is safe in the air. Though not a brilliant footballer Grimandi is a practical and effective performer.
* French League Championship winners medal 97.
x

* After coming through the youth ranks at Monaco, he made his league debut for the  first team on 30th November 1991 in an away game against Nancy: Monaco won 1-4. Monaco's coach that day was Arsene Wenger.
* He scored his first league goal on 21st May 1994 against Nantes (1-0)
* After winning a French League Championship winners medal he was signed by Arsenal on 4th June 1997 together with his teammate Emmanuel Petit. Both of them were personally requested by Arsene Wenger, who had both players under him during his time as manager of Monaco.

* Gilles Grimandi won the first major honour of his career last season, lifting the French league title with Monaco. He played in 24 league games, scoring once. Although he was never an automatic choice, he was a regular member of French coach Jean Tigana's side.

173.name: Garde
pages: * Remi Garde's arrival at Arsenal came just weeks before Arsene Wenger took up the Gunners' hot seat for the first time. The French coach had recommended his countryman's signing even before he had taken over as manager of Arsenal,  clearly demonstrating the faith he had in Garde's ability. However, injuries and his teammates' good form prevented him from forcing his way into the side, though all of that could change during the 97-98 season. As Remi Garde will no doubt be hoping it does.

* A defensive midfielder who is now something of a veteran, Garde's principal characteristic is his appetite for hard work, something which his teammates benefit from. He can also play as a free man at the back, a position where he demonstrates excellent positional sense. Technically weak, he helps out with ball winning responsibilities; although he is a reasonable passer of the ball. He makes only a very limited attacking contribution, although one season he did manage to find the back of the net nine times.
x

* 6 full international  appearances for France. He made his debut on 21st January1990 in a friendly against Kuwait. The French won1-0. 
* 3 "B" international appearances.

* He began his career in the French Second Division, in the ranks of Lyon. He made his league debut on 21st July 1989 in a game against Marseille (1-4). A regular member  of the side, he made a contribution to the club's promotion to the French First Division.During his time with Lyon he played in two U.E.F.A. Cup games scoring once.
* During the summer of 1993 he was transfered to Strasbourg, a club he helped to reach  the 1995 French Cup final, although they went on to lose 0-1 to Paris St. Germain.
* His contract with Strasbourg expired in June 1996. Shortly afterwards on 14th August, his move to Arsenal was announced, a signing made with the personal recommendation of Arsene Wenger, who had still not taken over as the Gunners' manager.
* He made his Premier League debut on 26th October 1996, in a 3-0 victory over Leeds at Highbury. Garde came on as a substitute for Ian Wright in the 81st minute.

* Injury prevented Remi Garde from making more appearances during his first season in England. In fact he played in just 11 league games, and made only 7 appearances as a member of the starting line up. Nevertheless he did enough to demonstrate the qualities he possesses; composure, accurate passing and forcefulness at the back.

174.name: Parlour
pages: * Ray Parlour is an easily identifiable player out on the park. His flowing red hair seems to pop up all over the place, amidst a flurry of dynamic acitvity and stamina. Nevertheless Ray is yet to go on to produce the performances that so many people expected of him, after arriving at Highbury with the job of taking over from Michael Thomas. Fortunately for him time is still on his side. Still young, the 97-98 season could see him finally explode onto  the scene.

* An aggressive midfielder with plenty of pace, Parlour plays down the right hand side of the midfield, although on occasions he will adopt a more central position. He works hard to win back plenty of possession for his side and creates goalscoring opportunities for his teammates. However his own shooting at goal is not particularly effective, rarely finding the back of the net. A good passer of the ball, though not technically brilliant, his stamina allows him to cover plenty of ground and help out in the team's approach play. At times he is too hurried in his actions, something he should try to improve as he goes on acquiring experience.

* European Cup Winners Cup winners medal 94. 
* European Cup Winners Cup runners up medal 95. 
* F.A. Cup winners medal  93. 
* League Cup winners medal 93.
* 12 Under-21 international appearances for England.

* Ray Parlour, unmistakeable with his long, curly hair, is a product of the Arsenal youth system. He signed his first professional contract on 6th March 1991 and made his league debut on 29th January 1992, in a 2-0 defeat against Liverpool at Anfield, a game in which he gave away a penalty. Everything seemed to indicate that Ray was destined to go  on to cover the gap left by Michael Thomas' departure to Liverpool.
* F.A. Cup and League Cup winners medals came his way in 1993, although he didn't play in the 1994 European Cup Winners Cup final against Parma. However he did line up in the final of the same competition the following year against Real Zaragoza in Paris. Arsenal lost the game 2-1 in the final minute of extra-time.
* During the course of a club tour of Asia, Parlour was involved in an incident with a taxi driver in Hong-Kong, which saw him hauled up in court.

* He was a member of the starting line up in 17 of the 30 games in which he appeared last season, although he never gave the impression of having made himself a regular memeber of the side. Nevertheless he showed courage and enthusiasm in every game he played, showing that although he may not be a star he is a fantastic club man. He scored two goals; one of those a truly spectaculareffort against Sunderland.

175.name: Vieira
pages: * Patrick Vieira was one of Arsene Wenger's signings, the French coach trusting his compatriot to give Arsenal a new style of play. From his central midfield position Viera attempts to pull the strings and impose a more elaborate short passing game rather than the more traditional long ball approach. In his first season in England he demonstrated class, talent and professionalism. In his second campaign in the Premier League he will be out to win the title.

* His natural position is in the centre of the midfield, a position in which his ability to win the ball and set up new attacks stands out. He also possesses tremendous physical atributes, concentrations, intelligence, tactical awareness, visions and technical ability which allows him to play accurate long passes. Added to this is his untiring defensive work, which is helped out by his superb positional sense. Viera also possesses a maturity beyond his years, and due to the character he possessess, is a real leader for his teammates. His only real weakness is his fragile physique, something he should try to work on if he wants to avoid the risk of injury.
x
* 5 full international appearances for France.

* Despite having veen born in Senegal and identifying with Cape Verd, Vieira possesses French nationalilty having moved to France with his family when he was still just a young boy. He was already playing football in Senegal for a club called Trappes, while, in France, he began by playing for the local club, where he lived, Dreux. However he soon moved on to join the youth ranks of Tours. 
* He arrived at French First Division club Cannes, during the 93-94 season. Tours were going through serious financial problems and decided to cash in and sell the young Vieira. He made his debut in the top flight of French football at just 17 years of age, under the watchful eye of coach Luis Fernandez, on 20th November 1993, in a 0-0 draw between Nantes and Cannes. During that season he played in just five games, although in the following campaign he made himself a regular member of the side.
* At just 19 years of age, with the Bosnian coach Safet Susic in charge, he became captain,  something which explains for itself the tremendous charisma, quality and personality that Vieira possesses.. 
* He began he 95-96 season in the ranks of  Cannes, although he later moved on to A.C. Milan, during the "Calciomercato" the period in the season during which new signings are permitted in the Italian Championship, once the season is underway.
* His transfer to Silvio Berlusconi's club was full of controversy and expectation given the excellent reports that the club had of the still young Vieira. The Cannes President, Francis Borelli had reached an agreement for the player's transfer to Paris Saint Germain, although the size of the offer from Milan, and the player's own desire to play in Italy resulted in him joining the Italian giants. At the time the deal went through, Cannes were near the foot of the French championship. 
* In order to help him adapt to Italian football, and get back to full futness, Vieira began his time at Milan in the reserves. His first team debut came on 28th November in 1995 against Bologna, in the first leg of the Italian cup quarter finals, a game which ended 1-1. Vieira played the full game and formed one of the trio of foreign players, along with Boban and Weah. It was in fact Weah, together with Desailly, who helped him most during his early days In Italy, due to the fact that as a result of the language barrier they were the only two members of the side he was able to communicate with. As time went on, he became friendly with Panucci and Simone, two of the younger members of the squad.
* Vieira never really managed to adapt to Italian football and, as a result, and despite the   contract which tied him to Milan until the year 2000, he was transfered to Arsenal on 14th August 1996 for 3,500,000 pounds. 
* He made his Premier League debut on 16th September 1996 in a victory against Sheffield Wednesday at Highbury (4-1). Vieira came on for Ray Parlour in the 27th minute.
* He scored his first goal for Arsenal on 7th December 1996 against Derby County, at Highbury.

* From the moment he made his debut for Arsenal halfway through september, Patrick Vieira showed an extraordinary ability to adapt to English football. With Arsene Wenger in charge, he managed to make himself a regular member of the side and went on to complete a good first season. His first goal, against Derby County, was, quite simply, superb, and allowed Arsenal to save a point at home. Vieira was, in short, one of the season's more pleasent surprises, thanks to his efforts in giving his side a new, more elaborate, more European style of play.
