177.name: Wreh
pages: * Christopher Wreh arrived in England as much on the strength of being a relative of George Weah than for his career in French football nevertheless the Liberian striker has the full backing of manager Arsene Wenger, and nobody should forget that it was the French coach who was the first to show confidence in the ability of George Weah, today an international star. Perhaps Christopher may well go on to repeat the experience and become one of the top goalscorers in the Premier League. Only time will tell.

* A very strong striker, he makes up for his technical limitations, with his aggressive style of play and physical power. A good striker of the ball he knows how to get in front of rival defenders in order to get in efforts on goal. He creates plenty of danger when he pulls out wide to the flanks, and takes advantage of his pace to get on the blind side of defenders. Still very young, he has plenty of time to get better.
x
* A full international for Liberia.

* He is the cousin of George Weah, A.C. Milan striker and one of the best players in the world.
* Born in Liberia, he took his first steps in French footbal in the ranks of Monaco. He made his First Division debut on 25th March 1994 in a 0-1 home defeat against Auxerre.
* During the 94-95 season he failed to make a league appearance of any kind. 
* On 26th August 1995 he scored his first two goals in the French league in an away game against Bourdeaux. Monaco won the game 2-4.
* Once the 95-96 season was over he moved on to join Guingamp, signing a one year contract.  He ended the  96-97 season as the club's leading scorer with 10 goals against his name.
* He has been an Arsenal player since 7th August 1997, although he had already been training with the London club for a number of weeks before signing. His move was set at 300,000  pounds, and came at the personal request of manager Arsene Wenger, the first coach to  have shown full confidence in the ability of George Weah, according to Weah himself. At Highbury Christopher Wreh tamed up with Petit and Grimandi, who he had played alongside at Monaco.

* Last season was Christopher Wreh's one and only at Guingamp. The French club had a mediocre league campaign, although the Liberian striker was one of the side's most outstanding performers, to the point of ending the season as leading scorer, finding the target 10 times in 33 games. Guingamp were on the verge of winning the French Cup although, after drawing in the final against Nice (1-1), they finally lost on penalties.

178.name: Anelka
pages: * Nicolas Anelka is something of a diamond that just needs to be polished up. At least that's what Arsene Wenger thought halfway through last season when he decided to sign him at all cost, despite being so young. Now Wenger has the time he needs to put the finishing touches to him and turn him into a star. At Arsenal Anelka will be able to learn plenty from men like Ian Wright and Dennis Bergkamp, while the fans at Highbury will have a new heroe to acclaim. The final word is with Arsene Wenger.

* Anelka is a young striker who is still developing his game, both physically and technically. A player who can operate in different attacking positions, he is skillful with the ball at his feet and has no hesitation in taking on opposing defenders. A very quick player, he is especially dangerous when he finds himself in space, and is also adpet at getting on the blind side of defenders. He is a good finisher but still needs the experience that would allow him to keep his cool in order to make the most of all the chances that come his way. Nevertheless he is a player blessed with exceptional natural ability, who has a very promising future ahead of him.
* French Youth Championship winners medal 96.
* A French under-21 international.

* He came through the youth ranks at Paris Saint Germain. He made his first  team debut on 7th February 1996 in a 1-0 defeat away at Monaco. That same year he won a French Youth Championship winners medal with PSG.
* He began the  96-97 season with PSG, but on 6th March 1997 he was transfered to Arsenal for 500,000. The deal was sealed following a disagreement between the London club and Paris Saint Germain, who were reluctant to release the player who had not yet reached 18 years of age. Finally, Anelka signed a six year contract with the Gunners.
* He made his Premier League debut on 5th April 1987 against Chelsea at Stamford Bridge. Anelka came on for Ian Wright in the 85th minute. Arsenal won the game 0-3.

* He began the season at Paris Saint Germain, where he scored once in 8 league games.  In March, despite a disagreement between the French club and Arsenal, he was transfered to Highbury. He made his debut against Chelsea at Stamford Bridge and, from then until the end of the season, he went on to make 3 more appearances. Although none of those appearances came as a member of the starting line up, and despite not getting more than just a few minutes of action under his belt, he didn't need much time to show at least of couple of glimpses of the class he possesses.

179.name: Overmars
pages: * The presence of Dennis Bergkamp in the side was one of the deciding factors that finally saw Marc Overmars sign for Arsenal. The Dutch international wasn't short  of offers, but he finally decided to play in England alongside his good friend Bergkamp, who he had already teamed up with both at club level with Ajax as well as for the Dutch national side. With his acquisition, Arsene Wenger has signed a genuine matchwinner, one of the top players in the world at the moment, and a good reason why the Highbury fans can start dreaming of major honours, while Arsenal is undoubtedly a fine club which can  help Overmars add to his honours list. All this, and the World Cup Finals in France just around the corner.

* Speed and skill are the two most outstanding characteristics in Marc Overmars' game. He generally operates tight on the left hand touchline, from where, once he picks the ball up, danger is guaranteed. He possesses a quite simply outstanding ability to beat a man, while in full flight, and takes full advantage of his speed to get to the byline, to thread accurate passes and crosses though to the forwards. On other occasions he will look to cut inside to connect with a powerful shot on goal. He has such refined technique that he can take free kicks abnd corners with either foot. Despite his age he is already an experienced player in terms of competitive football at the highest level, something which adds even more value to the extraordinary quality he already possesses.

* European Cup winners medal 95.
* Intercontinental Cup winners medal 95.
* European Super Cup winners medal 96.
* Dutch League Championship winners medals 94, 95 and 96.
* Dutch Cup winners medal 93.

* A full international for Holland. He made his debut on 24th February 1993 in a victory over Turkey in a friendly game played in Utrecht. That same day he scored his first goal for the national side, in the 5th minute. 
* A member of the Dutch squad in the 1994 World Cup Finals in the United States, he was  a member of the starting line up in all five of the games that Holland played, against Saudi Arabia, Belgium, Morroco, the Republic of Ireland and Brazil.
* A serious knee injury prevented him from playing in the 1996 European Championships in England.

* He began his playing career with Willem II, one of the more modest sides in the Dutch First Division. In his first season he played in 31 league games and put together some outstanding performances before signing for Ajax. Overmars was 19 years old at the time.
* During the 92-93 season, in which he made his debut for Ajax, he played in every  minute of every league game, somthing which nobody had done for the club for more than 27 years. He also managed to score a goal against Turkey just five minutes into his full international debut with the Dutch national side.
* In the Dutch Cup final in 1993, Ajax defeated Herenveen 6-2. Overmars found the back of the net twice.
* In 1994 he helped Ajax to the Dutch league title and played in all of Holland's games in that years World Cup finals in the United States. 
* With coach Louis van Gaal in charge, Ajax won the 1995 Euroepan Cup, beating Fabio Capello's A.C. Milan side in the final.
* During the 95-96 season he suffered a serious knee ligament injury which kept him out of the 1996 European Championships in England.
* Sought after by several of the most important clubs in Europe, among them Barcelona, he was transfered to Arsenal for 7,000,000 pounds on 17th July 1997 signing a five year contract with the Gunners. At Highbury he teamed up with fellow Dutchman Bergkamp, whom he had already played alongside both at Ajax and for Holland.

* Once he had recovered from the serious knee injury he had suffered the previous season, Overmars won back his place in Louis van Gaal's starting line up. However it took him some time to get back to full fitness and especially to recover the blistering place that he had shown in previous years. Ajax finished the season in fourth place in the Dutch league and were unable to get past the Champions League semi finals where they were eliminated by Juventus.

180.name: Bergkamp
pages:
* A few years ago, when he was still a young man, Dennis Bergkamp was tagged  right across Europe as the successor to Marco Van Basten , as the Arsenal man showed tremendous class in everything he did, just as his predecesor in the Dutch national side did. Although, for a number of different reasons, he was never really a great succes in Italy, his signing for the Gunners in the summer of 1995, was still one of the big attractions of the 1995 pre-season. From the moment he arrived at the club, the Dutch striker won over the Highbury faithful, especially the club's younger supporters, who see in Bergkamp the player they would all like to be.
* Bergkamp is now a star of the world game, a footballer of exceptional status and quality. Still a young player, he seems destined to symbolize a new era at Arsenal, with a new competitive team being built around him. As with all the great players of the past, the blonde, Dutch striker is one of those footballers who is capable of lighting up a relatively dull game with one unforgettable moment of class and skill.

* Dennis Bergkamp is a superb athlete, a perfectionist in his job and a footballer with an  outstanding talent for finding the back of the net. He can play as a centre forward as well as operating just behind the main striker, linking up with the midfield, doing a superb job in either position. He possesses all the qualities that can be asked for in a goalcorer; technique, opportunism and imagination. He is good in the air, has a powerful, accurate shot with either foot, while his long, powerful stride allows him to get into the opposition's penalty area ahead of defenders, giving him the time and space to finish the job off.  He has plenty of  tricks up his sleeve which he uses when he comes face to face with opposing goalkeepers, while he shows incredible coolness when he is putting the ball away. An expert in one on one situations, Bergkamp is, currently, one of the best players in world football.
* It is difficult to find a weakness in Dennis Bergkamp's game, although at times he can be his own worst enemy. His own character can sometimes see him disappear from games, having a negative effect on the side's performance. Nevertheless, he is a player who, at any moment, can win a game with just one glimpse of his enormous talent.

* European Cup Winners Cup winners medal 1987. 
* U.E.F.A. Cup Winners medals  92 and 94. 
* European Cup Winners Cup runners up medal 88. 
* Dutch League Championship winners medal 90. 
* Dutch Cup winners medals 87 and 93.

* 55 full international appearances for Holland, with 32 goals to his name. He made his debut on 26th September 1990 in a friendly game between Italy and Holland played in the La Favorita Stadium  Palermo. Italy won 1-0 with a goal by Roberto Baggio. Bergkamp came on in the 70th minute of the game in place of Frank de Boer.
* A member of the Dutch squad for the 1992 European Championships in Sweden, he played in 4 games, scoring 4 times, against Scotland, Germany and Denmark (2). The only game in which he failed to find the back of the net was the one against the Community of Independant States (CIS). 
* In the 1994 World Cup Finals in the United States, where he played in all 5 of Holland's games, and in all 450 minutes of action, he found the target 3 times: once against Morroco in the first phase, once against the Republic of Ireland in the last sixteen, and one against Brazil in the  quarter finals.
* During the 1996 European Championships in England, he started all four of Holland's games, against Scotland, Switzerland, England and France.He scored his side's second goal against Switzerland, (2-0) Holland's only victory of the tournament.

* As did both Johan Cruyff and Van Basten, he learnt the game in, and came through, the youth ranks of Ajax of Amsterdam, a club he joined at the age of 12. He took the step up to the first team in  March 1987, under the watchful eye of Johan Cruyff. Before that date he had already made his Dutch First Division debut on 14th December 1986 in a game between Roda and Ajax. By the end of that season he played in 14 games and scored twice. 
* In his third season in the first team (88-89), at just 19 years of age, he played in 30 games, finding the net 13 times. Nevertheless he began the following season in the club's second string, a decision taken by Kurt Linder. Finally Van Basten's transfer to A.C.Milan saw him return to the first team squad.
* During this period of his career he received his first big offers from Feyenoord, and from no less a club than Real Madrid. The club rejected both approaches sensing the best Bergkamp was yet to come, over the next three seasons. With 55 goals in 91 games he went on to become considered one of the best goalscorers in Europe. 
* As top scorer in the Dutch league, in 1991 with 25 goals (level with the Brazilian Romario) in 1992 with 24 and 1993 with 26 ( 4 more than PSV Eindhoven's Brazilian star), Dennis became the target of some of the biggest clubs in Europe: A.C. Milan, Barcelona, Real Madrid, Juventus, Inter  Milan... , all of them came in for him, but it was Inter who accepted all of his conditions, and took Wim Jonk to italy with him.. 
* Regarded in Holland as the successor to other Dutch footballing legends such as Abe Leenstra (before the Second World War ), Coen Moulinj (the 1960'), Johan Cruyff (1970') Marco Van Basten  (1980'), Dennis Bergkamp has the reputation of being an extremely cold and calculated man  in all aspects of his life. It has even been said that he has problems getting on with people and making friends, something which has given him some difficulties in adapting to new countries.
* Bergkamp has acknowledged that his boyhood idol was Glenn Hoddle and has also expressed his admiration for English football. After two seasons at Inter Milan the Dutch striker never really settle down to the lifestyle in Italy and, as a result, on 3rd July 1995 he was transfered to Arsenal for  7,500,000  pounds, making him the most expensive player in the history of the club. His acquisition sparked off an outbreak of euphoria amongst the club's supporters.
* He made his debut at Highbury on 20th August 1995 in a game against Middlesbrough (1-1). On 23rd September of that same year he scored his first two goals for the Gunners, making a contribution to Arsenal's 4-2 home victory against Southampton (4-2).
* He is a player who is genuinely terrified of flying. For this reason, he has a clause writen into his contract which gives the right to refuse to travel by plane.

* With 12 league goals to his credit, including 3 peanlites, Dennis Bergkamp was Arsenal's top scorer, beaten only by Ian Wright. Although an injury he picked up in September forced him out of the side for a number of games, he was an automatic choice in the side when he was fit. He showed that his understanding with Ian Wright was getting better all the time, and also allowed himself the luxury of scoring a few extraordinary goals. Among those was the one he scored against Sunderland,lifting the ball over the keeper after beating two defenders in a space where there was barely enough room to turn.

181.name: Adams
pages: * Tony Adams' charisma, both at Arsenal and in the England side makes him an automatic choice for both sides. Out on the park he is very much the manager's right hand man, ordering his teammates around and directing defensive operations with authority and efficiency. A very popular player with both his teammates as well as the Gunners' supporters, throughout his career Tony has been an example of professional honesty. The 97-98 season presents a double challenge; on the one hand another treasured  league title triumph; on the other the fight for glory in the World Cup finals in France, with which the whole of England is dreaming, Tony Adams included.

* Tony Adams is a tremendously efficient central defender, who has all the qualities needed to play at the heart of the defence. An exceptionally tight marker, he is almost impossible to beat in the air and frequently moves forward for corners and free kicks, where he poses a real threat. Although technically limited, he is aware of his weaknesses , and generally keeps his passing short, looking for his nearest teammate, keeping things as simple as possible. He makes up for his  lack of pace with positional sense and anticipation.
* His experience and leadership qualitities make him an extremely important player, bringing tremendous confidence and security to the side.

* European Cup Winners Cup winners medal 94. 
* European Cup Winners Cup runners up medal 95. 
* League Championship winners medals 89 and 91. 
* F.A. Cup winners medal 93. 
* League Cup winners medal 87. 
* Charity Shield medals 89, 91 and 93. 
* Voted Young Player of the Year by the Professional Footballers' Association.

* 47 full international appearances for England, scoring 3 times. He made his debut in a 2-4 victory against Spain, on 17th February 1987, in the Santiago Bernabeu stadium in Madrid. His first goal came on 11th November of that same year. That day England beat Yugoslavia 1-4 in Belgrade. 
* A member of England's squad in the 1988 European Championships in Germany 1988, playing in 3 games as a member of the starting line up, against the Republic of Ireland Holland and the Soviet Union; a game in which he managed to find the back of the net.
* In 1990, following his problems with the British Criminal Justice system he was left  out of the England side for two years.
* Back in the England squad for the 1996 Euroepan Championships in England, he played as a member of the starting line up in the 5 games that the national side played, against Switzerland, Holland, Scotland, Spain and Germany. England were beaten in the penalty shoot out in the semi-final against the Germans.
* Adams has captained the England side on a number of occasions. 
* 4 "B" international appearances, scoring once. 
* 5 Under-21 international appearances, with one goal to his credit. 
* 18 youth international appearances, scoring six times.

* He has spent the whole of his playing career at Arsenal, a club he joined as a youth team player in November 1980. He made his first team debut on 5th November 1983, in a game against Sunderland at Highbury, barely two months after signing his first professional contract on 30th January 1984. 
* At the end of the 86-87 season he was voted "Young Player of the Year" by the Professional Footballers' Association.
* His charisma within the squad and his quality as a footballer soon made the youngest captain in the history of the club. With a brilliant professional career already behind him, out on the park he is a real example of honour and commitment in defence of the Arsenal cause.
* However, his career suffered a serious setback during the 90-91 season, when he had to spend three months in prison for drink driving. As a result he was out of the England side for two years and caused great indignation in many sectors of British society. Nevertheless the Arsenal supporters quickly forgot about the incident and welcomed him back with open arms on the day he made his comeback. Even so, he had to put up with plenty of stick from rival.
* As a member of the England squad during the European championships in 1988 in Germany in 1988 and in England in 1996, he has captained the side in the absence of other more regular captain such as his current clubmate David Platt.
*In September 1996, Adams publicy recognised that he had a new drink problem, which came  about as a result of England's elimination in the semi -finals of that year's European Championships. Tony declared that the disappointment the suffered following the defeat against Germany was such that he once again fell victim to the lure of alcohol, and made an appeal for the support of his  teammates and the public. A brave gesture which again proved the character and personality of the man.

* Although a knee injury prevented him from taking up his place in the side until the end of September 1996, Tony Adams once again put together some extraordinary performances During the course of last season. The veteran defender overcame his personal problems and won the complete confidence of both his teammates as well as manager Arsene Wenger. He was a member of the starting line up in 27 of the 28 games he played in, scoring 3 times, one of those goals coming against Arsenal's arch-enemies, north London rivals Tottenham Hotspur. Once he had got back to his best form, England manager  Glenn Hoddle called him up to the national squad. At the end of the season he was included in the Premier league's ideal team, voted for by his fellow professionals .

182.name: Platt
pages: * The 1997-98 season ends with the World Cup finals in France. David Platt, ex-captain of the England national side, will be hoping that he is included in the squad for what is likely to be the last big international competition of his playing career. In order to make sure his name goes down on the list, he will have to put together a good season with Arsenal, and hope that injury problems don't get in his way. Glenn Hoddle has already shown he has great faith in the player, while those who know him are sure that David Platt will get exactly what he is after.

* Clever, skillful, and with an eye for a goalscoring chance, David Platt does a superb job as a link up man in the centre of the park, from where he sets off at speed, with the ball under control, to break through the opposition defence. He is quick, has exceptional ball control, vision, organizational ability and is a tremendous finisher with both feet as well as his head, all of which makes him a very dangerous player when he makes his late runs into the penalty area. A basically right footed player, he can also do a job when he is used in deeper midfield positions, although, when he is asked to play further from the opposition's goal, then he loses some of his effectiveness.
* Platt also possesses tremendous leadership qualities and vast international experience, both greatly valued by teammates and managers alike. In short, the Arsenal midfielder is, above all else, a magnificent fooballer.

* U.E.F.A. Cup winners medal 93.
* Italian Cup winners medal 94.
* Voted  P.F.A. Player of the Year 1990, by the Professional Footballers' Asssociation..

* 62 full international appearances for England, scoring 27 times. He made his debut on 15th November 1989, in a friendly game against Italy at Wembley (0-0).
* He scored his first goal for England in the 1990 World Cup finals in Italy, a goal that  clinched a victory for England over Belgium on 26th  June (1-0). He appeared in all 6 games that England played, scoring 3 times, against Belgium, Cameroon and Italy (the game against Italy was the third place play off which England lost 2-1).
* A member of  England's squad in the 1992 European Championships in Sweden , he was a member of the starting line up in the 3 games that England played. Against Denmark, France  and the host nation against whom he found the back of the net once.
* Called up again to the national squad for the 1996 European Championships in England he played in 4 of the 5 games that the side played. However he only played from the start in the quarter final against Spain and in the semi-final against Germany.
* 3 "B" international appearances.
* 3 under-21 international appearances.

* He began playing football for his school team, Chadderton Boys,  from where he joined Manchester United as an apprentice in July 1984. Once at the club, Ron Atkinson, one of the most prestigious managers in English football, decided to release him, and so, as a result, he saw himself moving on to Fourth Division Crewe Alexandra. Platt's dream of making the grade with Manchester United had disappeared.
* He signed for Crewe on 25th January 1985. In four seasons at the club he played in 152 games, scoring 62 goals. His progress attracted the attention of Graham Taylor, then manager of Aston Villa, who signed him for 200,000 on 2nd February 1988.
* He showed some tremendous form for his new team and soon went on to make his debut for the full England side. He confirmed himself as an international footballer in the 1990 World Cup Finals in Italy, where he was England's best player. Especially important was the goal he scored, in such agonising circumstances, against Belgium, a goal which took England through to the quarter finals.
* In the three and a half seasons in which he played for Aston Villa, he played in 121 league games (50 goals), 4 F.A. Cup games (2 goals ) and 14 League Cup games  (10 goals). Those statistics and his excellent performances in the World Cup Finals in Italy were enough to see the president of Italian club, Bari, Vicenzo Matarrese, determined to sign him.
* On 20th July 1991 he was transfered to Bari for 5,500,000 pounds. It was an offer which was well in excess of that put forward by Olympique Marseille, who were also interested in signing the English midfielder.
* His Italian League debut came on 1st September 1991, in a game between Bari and Torino, which ended in a 1-1 draw. Platt spent one season with the Southern Italian club, playing in 29  league games, scoring 11 goals. A good return but not enough to save the club from being relegated to serie "B". 
* Although the club went down Platt's transfer valuation didn't, and he moved on to Juventus, one of the biggest clubs in Italian football. He didn't have too much good fortune in Turin either,   having to battle against injuries as well as the club's other foreign players,  Julio Cesar, Kohler and Muller, who were all ahead of the Englishman in the coach Giovanni Trapattoni's list of preferences. Trapattoni left Platt kicking his heels on the bench on numerous occasions. During his only season with Juve, he played in just 16 league games, scoring 3 times.
* David Platt was named captain of the England side during the 92-93 season, for a game against San Marino (6-0). He celebrated by scoring four times in the game, but missed a penalty that would have allowed him to join the legendary Malcom McDonald, who remains the only player to have scored five times for England in a full international.
* Although in 1993 he still had two years left of his contract with Juventus, the Turin based club decided to sell him, something which alerted the interest of clubs such as Monaco, Borussia Dortmund, Lazio,  Parma and Blackburn Rovers, although it was finally Sampdoria who managed to win his signature. With the Genovese club David became a key player and finally was able to feel as though his Italian adventure had been a success.
* On 14th July 1995 he was transfered to Arsenal for 4,750,000 pounds. The acquisition of both Platt and the Dutchman Bergkamp, saw the Gunners' fans going into a state of near euphoria.  Platt made his debut at Highbury on 20th August 1995 in the first league game of the season against Middlesbrough (1-1). At the end of his first season at the club he played for his country in the 1996 European Championships, played on home soil in England.

* Once he had recovered from the injuries that he was carrying as a result of the 1996 European Championships in England, David Platt soon won the confidence of Arsene Wenger and became a regular member of the starting line up. The veteran midfielder initially took up a more defensive midfield role, although as the season went on his opportunities to get forward into the attack became more frequent. He hit his best run of form in April, when he scored three goals in three consecutive games against Chelsea, Leicester and Blackburn Rovers.
* England manager Glenn Hoddle included him in a number of his squads, but didn't finally put him in the side.

183.name: Wright
pages: * Ian Wright is a real symbol at Arsenal and is one of the best centre forwards in the history of English football. Although now a veteran he shows no signs of having entered the final stages of his career. In fact quite the opposite seems to be the case, apparently having an even keener eye for a goascoring chance and more ambition as each season goes by. The 1997-98 season offers an even greater motivation for that ambition; the World Cup Finals in France. Ian Wright is sure not to let anybody down.

* Ian Wright is a fabulous striker, blessed with exquisite technique and an outstanding ability to find the back of the net. Quick and skillful, he is decisive when he takes on defenders, and when he is in full flight, is a very difficult player to stop. He knows exactly where the goal is and doesn't need to be asked twice to have a go when he gets even the slightest opprtunity, even from the most acrobatic of positions. He has a hard, accurate shot in either foot, although he is also capable of rounding off moves with the subtlest of touches. He is also a good header of the ball, helped by his ability to get up high above defenders, while he remains cool and composed when he steps up to take spot kicks.  All of this makes him a real matchwinner, a quality to which he also adds the spectacular grace with which he decorates so many of his goals.
* Wright is a player who always gives 100%, although he is occasionally guilty of being a little too fiery, and has at times gone into tackles harder and more recklessly than he should. Nevertheless his presence out on the park is a real threat for any opposing team, and he remains a player who,  when it is least expected, is capable of striking a a goal out of nothing.

* European Cup Winners Cup winners medal 94. 
* European Cup Winners Cup runners up medal 95. 
* F.A. Cup winners medal  93. 
* League Cup winners medal 93. 
* Charity Shield  medal 93. 
* "Golden Boot" 1992.

* 27 full international appearances for England with 7 goals to his credit. He made his debut on 6th February 1991 in a friendly game against Cameroon at  Wembley (2-0).
* He scored his first goal for the full England side on 29th May 1993 in a qualifying game for the 1994 World Cup Finals in the United States. England drew 1-1 with Poland.
* 3 "B" international appearances.

* Ian Wright grew up in the same district of London as David Rocastle. Years later both of them would go on to play for Arsenal. He signed for modest Greenwich from school side Ten Em Bee. His quality didn't go unnoticed by the talent scouts of Crystal Palace and on 2nd August 1985 he signed for the London club, who didn't have to pay out a penny to take him to Selhurst Park. 
* He made his league debut on 31st August of that same year in a game against Huddersfield.
* In six seasons at Selhurst Park he formed a sensational goalscoring partnership with Mark Bright; between the two of them they managed to strike over a hundred goals.
* During the 88-89 season he scored  24 goals in 42 games, and was a fundamental factor in  Palace winning promotion to the First Division. The following year he suffered a broken leg although he recovered in time to play in the 1990 F.A. Cup final against Manchester United. Wright came on in the second half, scored twice and forced the game to go to a replay. Although Crystal Palace lost the game, Ian Wright had done enough to confirm himself as an outstanding footballer. 
* In 1991 he made his full international debut for England. His progress was now unstoppable and, on 24th September of that year he was transfered to Arsenal for 2,500,000 pounds. He made his debut in the League Cup against Leicester City, managing to find the back of the net. On his league debut, he went even better and hit a hat trick against Southampton at The Dell. 
* In Ian Wright's second season at Highbury the side lifted both the F.A. Cup and the League Cup.
* In the 1994-95 European Cup Winners Cup competition, Wright gave some outstanding performances that helped Arsenal lift the trophy. However, an absurd yellow card in the semi-final against Paris Saint Germain prevented him from playing in the Final. At the end of the semi-final the Gunners striker was unable to hold back the tears. Weeks later in the final, his teammates defeated Parma and Wright was able to pose with them and the trophy; although he was, of course, wearing a suit at the time. 
* In the 94-95 season Arsenal defended their European trophy. Wright scored nine times , finding the back of the net in every round, except in the final in Paris against Spanish club Real Zaragoza. The Gunners, with Wright failing to hit the target, went down  2-1 in extra time.
* An extraordinary goalscorer he has scored 13 hat tricks during the course of his career, a total bettered only by Ian Rush. The first time he scored 3 in a game was on 3rd November 1987, the victims being Plymouth Argyle. Since then, Brimingham, Southend, Wimbledon, Southampton (three times), Everton, Yeovil, Huddersfield, Sheffield Wednesday andIpswich (twice) have all suffered from Ian Wright's deadly touch in front of goal.
* As well as for his goals, Ian Wright is known for his fiery temperament. He is in fact one of the top five players in England, in terms of yellow cards.
* At the end of the  95-96 season there was speculation surrounding his possible departure from Highbury, something which sparked the protests of the Highbury faithful.
* In September 1997 he became the top scorer in Arsenal's history after beating the record that Cliff Bastin set of 150 goals for the club.

* With 23 goals in 35 games, Ian Wright was the second top scorer in the Premier League, beaten only by Alan Shearer (25). As a result he managed to reach the 100 league goals mark for Arsenal. He also scored 7 goals in other competitions to go on to complete an extraordinary season. He developed a tremendous understanding with Dennis Bergkamp while his presence out on the park was a constant source of danger for opposition defenders.
* He was deservedly called up by Glenn Hoddle for the national side. He made four appearances and made a key contribution to the country's fight to quality for the 1988 World Cup Finals in France.

184.name: Grodas
pages: * Grodas' signing was an emergency solution adopted by Chelsea to counteract the injury crisis that descended on the club at the beginning of last season. The Norwegian international arrived as a loan player to substitute for Hitchcock, but his chance quickly came and he took it.  Gullit decided to extent his contract, but the arrival of Ed De Goey at Stamford Bridge casted a shadow of doubt over his future. Grodas signed for Tottenham in January 1998.

* A veteran goalkeeper, he is noted for his security between the posts. He is an effective and level-headed keeper, but little given to spectacular actions, although at times he makes pretty serious mistakes, especially when coming for crosses and when using his feet.
* FA Cup Champion 97.
* 31 full international appearances for Norway.

* He started his sporting career at the modest Mossen BK, and from there moved to the Swedish team Gothenborg.
* In 1988 he was transferred to Lillestrom, the Norwegian club whose colours he defended for eight seasons.
* In September 1996 he was on the point of signing for the Austrian team Sturm Graz.  However the goalkeeper coach at Chelsea, Eddie Niedzwiecki, convinced him to come to Stamford Bridge as a loan player.
* He signed for Chelsea on the 21st of September 1996, as the London team only had one keeper available in their squad (Kevin Hitchcock) after the injuries to Dmitri Kharine and Nick Colgan.
* He made his debut for the Blues on the 25th of September 1996 in a League Cup tie against Blackpool.
* His first appearance in the Premier League took place on the 16th of November 1996 at Ewood Park against Blackburn Rovers (1-1).
* Satisfied with the performance of Grodas, the manager at Chelsea, Ruud Gullit, decided to sign him definitively during the course of the 96-97 season, a season which ended with Grodas playing in the Chelsea goal in the FA Cup final where the Blues beat Middlesbrough (2-0).

* His incorporation was hurried through in September due to the injuries to Dimitri Kharine and Nick Colgan, leaving Kevin Hitchcock as the only keeper in the squad.  He arrived on loan from Lillestrom and made his debut in November, playing several games on the trot as the first choice, before returning to the substitutes' bench.  However, an injury to Hitchcock's elbow allowed him back into the team until the end of the season.  His performance was satisfactory, so much so that Ruud Gullit gave the green light to his definitive move to Stamford Bridge.  He finished the season on a high note, as he was the first choice keeper in the FA Cup final against Middlesbrough.

185.name: Baardsen
pages: * Espen Baardsen arrived at White Hart Lane aged just 18 to step into the shoes of Erik Thorsvedt, his fellow countryman, one of the best goalkeepers in the history of Norwegian footballer and who played for nearly eight years at Spurs.  Given his youth and inexperience, he is a firm candidate to be sat firmly on the substitutes' bench.  What's more, nobody doubts that Ian Walker should be the first choice keeper for the team.  Even so, Walker shouldn't get over confident because in the few games the Norwegian got to play last season he showed that he has the talent to be a first choice keeper.
* A very young keeper, with great reflexes and extraordinary physical conditions.  His performances in top-level competition will have to be watched to evaluate his playing characteristics.
x
* Norwegian youth international.

* Norwegian international at the youth level, Espen Baardsen spent the 95-96 season in the ranks of the San Francisco All Blacks, a team in the United States league.
* In the summer of 1996 he signs for Tottenham Hotspur to cover for the absence of his fellow countryman, Erik Thorsvedt, the reserve keeper who was finishing his sporting career.
* He made his debut in May against Liverpool at Anfield (2-1).  Baardsen stepped on the pitch in the second half due to an injury to Walker.

* The 96-97 season was Baardsen's first at Tottenham.  He made his debut in the Spurs goal against Liverpool in May, a game in which he showed a lot of self confidence and caused a great impression on the Tottenham supporters. Espen stepped onto to the Turf in the second half due to an injury to Walker, and managed to stop the Liverpool forwards from scoring with three magnificent saves.  Later he played a full game, showing once more that he was a worthy replacement for Walker.

186.name: Walker
pages: * Walker has already seen both sides of football, the successful side and and that of defeat, and he is aware that he can't rest on his laurels. When he made it to the England team he had what was perhaps his best moment, but the goal that Zola scored at Wembley and a couple of hard defeats brought him back to reality.  Walker recovered from this bad moment and no-one doubts that he will be the first choice at Tottenham, though he shouldn't be too complacent as behind him he has Baardsen waiting for his chance.

* Agile and with great reflexes, he stands out for his extraordinary positioning between the posts.  On the other hand, he needs to improve his game when he comes out to the feet of rival forwards.  He has an acceptable individual technique, and doesn't aim to complicate matters when he has to get rid of the ball.  He has a strong character allowing him to show a calmness not often seen in someone his age.  Still very young, he has a plenty of room for improvement which will make him, without doubt, into an excellent goalkeeper.

* European Under-20 champion with the England team.
* Charity Shield Medal in 91.
* Youth Cup Champion 89-90.

* 3 full international appearances for England.  He made his debut on the 18th of May 1996 in a friendly game against Hungary played at Wembley (3-0). Present in the 96 European Championship in England, although he doesn't play a single minute.
* 9 times under-21 international.  He made his debut on the 5th of February 1990 against Wales (0-0).  European under-20 champion, he formed part of the team that beat Turkey 1-0.
* 16 times youth international.

* He is the son of Mike Walker, who was the goalie at Reading, Swindon, York, Charlton and Colchester between 1963 and 1983.  What's more, he managed Norwich between 1992 and 1994 in the Premier League.
* Ian started his career at Tottenham, as an apprentice to Ray Clemence, the best teacher possible.  He joined the first squad on the 4th of December 1989, but this season he didn't get to play a single game.  Loaned to Oxford, he makes his debut at Manor Ground on the 29th of September 1990 against Wolverhampton (1-1).  He only played two league games with this team and one League Cup tie.  On returning to White Hart Lane, his dream of making his debut for Spurs comes true.  This was in April 1991 against Norwich.
* At this time he hardly had any chances to play as the Norwegian Erik Thorsvedt was having the best of his career, keeping him out of the team. Little by little, Walker found his way into the side, alternating with the Nordic goalkeeper.
* The arrival of the manager Gerry Francis in November 1994 was Walker's passport to the team, playing regularly as the first choice keeper, a situation which remains the same today.
* A full international since May 1996, he takes part in his country's tour of Asia and plays in a game against China.  Shortly afterwards, the manager Terry Venables includes him in the 22-strong squad for the European Championship in England.
* Up until the 94-95 season he had managed to keep 20 clean sheets.  The average number of goals conceded per game was 1.511.
* He was the first choice keeper in the game England played against Italy at Wembley (0-1).

* It was a somewhat irregular season for Walker who was unable to repeat the excellent season he had in 95-96 when he was pressing David Seaman hard for his place in the England team.  The thrashings received from Newcastle (7-1) and Bolton in the Coca-Cola Cup (6-2) as well as the goal conceded against Italy in the classification game for the World Cup in France made him the object of criticisms and the supporters turned against him.  However, little by little and thanks to his temperament, Walker regained his form and finished the season producing some good performances.

187.name: Vega
pages: * In his first full season in England Ram¾n Vega will try to demonstrate that he has a place among the best central defenders in the Premier League. For this the injuries will have to keep away.  The arrival of the manager Christian Gross, who he overlapped with at Grasshoppers in Switzerland, should guarantee him a place in the starting line-up.

* A very big central defender, he is particularly noted for his firmness and security in the aerial game.  Quick and experienced, he can solve apparently complicated situations with ease.  He joins in the attack in set-plays, trying to take full advantage of his header.

* Swiss League Champion 91, 95 and 96. 
* Swiss Cup Champion 94.
* 20 full international appearances for Switzerland.  He made his debut on the 26th of January 1993 with a win over Hong Kong in a friendly (3-2).

* Born in Switzerland, but with Spanish family, he started playing football in the modest Trimbach, before moving to Grasshoppers in the 90-91 season. 
* With Grasshoppers he won three league titles, two of them under the orders of the manager Christian Gross. 
* He was one of the most outstanding players in the Swiss team in the England 96 European Championship. 
* In the summer of 1996 he signed for Cagliari, then in the Italian Serie A.  However, in January 1997 he was transferred to Tottenham Hotspur for £3.7 million. 
* He made his debut in the Premier League on the 12th of March 1997, with a home defeat against Manchester United (1-2).

* He started last season at Cagliari, but never really adjusted to playing in the Italian League.  At Tottenham since January, his presence was a noticeable reinforcement for the Spurs' defence.  However, injury prevented him from playing more than 8 league games for the club.

188.name: Clemence
pages:
* The surname Clemence has played a big role in the success of English football in recent years, above all at the end of the seventies and the beginning of the eighties.  Ray Clemence, Stephen's father, is considered, together with Shilton, to be one of the best keepers in English football in the last thirty years.  Ray marked an era at Liverpool, winning several European Cups and had plenty of success in the England team.
* Just as with his father, Stephen will also have the privilege of defending the Tottenham colours, the team in whose youth squad he has trained and grown as a footballer.  Francis trusts him and it is likely that he will be the first choice left back.  The surname Clemence extends its history in English football.

* Clemence is a left back who promises a lot.  He pushes up decisively along his touchline and doesn't get frightened when he has to fight for the ball with stronger, more experienced players.  He is still lacking a little bit of consistency in his game to remedy difficult situations, but we are looking at a player with a splendid future.
x

* 8 schoolboy international appearances.
* 13 under-16 international appearances.
* 6 youth international appearances.

* He is the son of the mythical Ray Clemence.
* This is his first season in the first squad at Tottenham and in the Premier League.
* He played in the lower ranks of Tottenham and in the reserve team, where he disputed several games.

189.name: Scales
pages: * This is his second season at White Hart Lane, arriving from Liverpool. The games he disputed last season with the Spurs' shirt helped him win the confidence of Gerry Francis and the team-mates and so Scales may be on of the regular starters this season.  Experienced and secure in his game, John will bring consistency to the Tottenham defence.

* Normally, Scales plays in the centre of defence.  He is a good defender, strong and safe; but his level drops a lot when he has the ball at his feet, due to his limited technique.  He doesn't join in the attack much, leaving this to other people.  In contentious tasks he is noted for his good positioning.  A right-footed player, he has played at right back at times, and even in the midfield.  In any position, Scales is an imposing presence and brings a lot of security, working hard in defence.

* English FA Cup Champion 87-88 with Wimbledon.
* League Cup Champion 94-95 with Liverpool.
* Charity Shield Medal 88.

* He has been a full international three times.
* Two times B international.

* He started out as an apprentice at Leeds United, but he signs his first professional contract on the 11th of July 1985 with Bristol Rovers.
* He makes his league debut for Rovers on the 7th of September 1985, the team losing 3-0 to Newport County.
* He left the Bristol club due to the financial problems they were having and signed for Wimbledon on the 16th of July 87 for just £70,000.
* At Wimbledon, he was second choice to the experienced Eric Young, the undisputed starter with the Dons until the arrival of Scales.
* He signs for Liverpool on the 2/9/94.  His price: £3.5 million.
* Until the end of the 94-95 season he had received 13 yellow cards and one red one.
* In December 1996 he is transferred to Tottenham Hotspur.  His move to Spurs is surrounded by controversy as the player had made a commitment to Leeds United earlier.  However, Scales pleaded "sporting reasons" to explain his decision to move to White Hart Lane instead.

* Although he started to play in the centre of the Liverpool defence, the arrival of Wright didn't benefit him and he was unable to retain his position.  With a bleak outlook at Anfield, Scales decided to move to Tottenham, the team where he played the first two games as a substitute for a team-mate.  His first full game for Tottenham was played on the 1st of April at White Hart Lane against Nottingham Forest just after recovering from an injury.  After this, his security in the air and his efficiency at making interceptions led him to share defensive duties with Vega and Campbell.

190.name: Carr
pages: * He starts the season with the comforting thought that he played 26 games last season and left behind a good impression.  Even so, he will not find it easy to get on the teamsheet, but he will be one of the first that Francis will turn to when injuries and sanctions affect his usual defenders.

* He can occupy several positions in the defensive axis.  Quick and solid, his speed with the ball at his feet and his ability for marking are his best qualities.  He should still try and polish out some faults, but we could be looking at one of the first-choice defenders for the Republic of Ireland team.
x
* 3 times under-21 international for Ireland.
*  He is a professional at Tottenham Hotspur since August 1993, although he has been there a lot longer in the lower categories of the club.

* Looking at the figures, last season was easily Carr's best season at Tottenham.  He took part in 26 games, compared with just 1 in the three previous seasons.  He had some great performances, of which his marking job on Cantona and Shearer were outstanding, earning him respect and boosting his confidence.

191.name: Austin
pages: * He is not in the starting line-up, but Francis is aware that Austin is a player who can lend a hand at any time.  His ability to push up along his band and create danger, as well as his defensive qualities, make him a useful player for the team.

* A skilful right back with attacking presence, Dean Austin is secure when passing the ball to his team-mates.  He joins in the attack easily, although he normally limits himself to crossing.  It isn't often that you see him shoot at goal.  In any case, he offers his best in defensive tasks, as he is a player who is hard to beat for speed and who doesn't shy away from the collision.  If it is necessary, he is tough when tackling.  Still very young, he should try and improve his attacking contribution, increasing his presence around the box.
x
x

* He arrived at Southend United on the 22nd of March 1990 from St. Albans, a regional team.  On the 10th of April of this year he makes his debut as right back in a game against Burnley.
* He formed part of the historic Southend Team who, after finishing second in the Third Division, took part in the play-offs for promotion to the Second Division.
* After a lot of speculation about his future he is transferred to Tottenham Hotspur on the 4th of June 1992 for £375,000.
* In November 1994, the arrival of Gerry Francis to the club is a shot in the arm for Austin, who was going through a bad patch at the club, as he had lost his place in the team managed by the Argentinean Ardiles.

* The injuries had a negative effect on him when he was trying to reach his top form.  What's more, the presence of Scales and Ramón Vega, as well as the good form of Carr, were another obstacle which he had to confront. This meant that at times there were rumours of his departure from the club.  However, Austin is a player who, even though he doesn't play from the start, is held in high esteem, and so when he wasn't playing he was a regular on the substitutes' bench.

192.name: Edinburgh
pages: * Edinburgh is going into his ninth season with Tottenham and it looks like it won't be the last, as he has renewed his contract and will be tied to the White Hart Lane club for three more seasons.  He is one of the few players who is left from the team who won the FA Cup in 91 and Justin is dreaming of lifting another trophy wearing the Spurs shirt.  He will fight with Clemence for the position of left back with the team.

* Justin Edinburgh is a left back with a clear attacking vocation, so much so that, at times, he has played at left half.  He joins in the attack easily, taking part in the game helped by his good ball control with his left foot and his safe passing.  The arrival of Gerry Francis at the head of the coaching body brought a notable increase in his contribution to the team, showing that he is a footballer with a lot of confidence in his abilities and, above all, a versatile player, capable of playing in several positions.  He can play in several positions and takes on responsibility, both in defence and in attack.  He has a good shot with his left, although he doesn't try it out as often as he should.  However, his main virtue is his spirit and enthusiasm, always willing to push the team on in search of the win.

* FA Cup Champion 90-91.
* Charity Shield Medal 91.
x

* Trained in the Southend United youth squad, he signs as a professional on the 5th of August 1988.  On the 23rd of September he makes his debut against Cardiff City.
* On the 30th of July 1990 he is transferred to Tottenham Hotspur, the club where he had had a loan spell shortly before, though he hadn't got to make his debut.  Spurs paid £150,000 to acquire his services.  At the beginning he played some games, alternating with Pat Van den Heuwe and Mitchell Thomas.  
* He plays in the final of the FA Cup in 1991 against Nottingham Forest, the last title won by Tottenham Hotspur with the help of an own-goal by Des Walker.
* He renewed his contract at the end of the 95-96 season for three years, despite rumours of a possible move.

* He managed to figure in the manager's plan more or less regularly.  He started the season as first choice for his position and left the starting line-ups when he was affected by injury and suspension.  He normally played at left back, but several times Francis played him on the right.

193.name: Calderwood
pages:
* To reach the top of English football Colin Calderwood had to follow a long hard path, full of seasons in lower divisions waiting for a contract with one of the big teams.  However, the persistent work of the Scot has born its fruits as he signed for Tottenham first, then made his debut for the Scotland team.  An international at 30, he had the privilege of taking part in the 1996 European Championship and will probably savour the exciting experience of playing in the World Cup, as he is one of the regulars in the Scotland line-ups.
* Calderwood has won the confidence of Gerry Francis and everything seems to point towards him being one of the first choice central defenders.

* Calderwood is a very strong central defender, bulky and excellent in the air.  An extraordinary defender with leadership qualities, he is the leader in the Tottenham defence, ordering people about constantly.  A right-footed player and a good marker, he is not comfortable in constructive tasks, the reason why he failed as a midfielder when the former manager, Ossie Ardiles, played him there.  The Scottish defender has a broad experience which he uses to make up for his lack of technical resources with the ball at his feet.He doesn't push up much, although his consistency in the aerial game allows him to score the odd goal.
* Fourth Division Champion 85-86.

* 20 full international appearances for Scotland.  He made his debut on the 29th of March 1995 against Russia, in a classification game for the England European Championship played in Moscow (0-0).  His only goal as an international came on the 26th of April 1995 in Serraville against San Marine (2-0).  Present in the 96 England European Championship, he played three games from the start for his country.
* 2 B-international appearances.

* Originally an amateur with Mansfield, he makes his debut in the league with this team on the 13th of March 1982 in a game against Crewe. Six days later he signs as a professional.
* After 100 games he is transferred to Swindon Town for £30,000.  This was on the 1st of July 1985.
* At the end of the 92-93 season Swindon's relegation precipitates his transfer to Tottenham Hotspur for £1,250,000.  He signs for Spurs on the 22nd of July 1993.
* In March 1995, already aged 30, his chance to play for his country comes along.  Aged 31 he defends his country's colours in the England European Championship and he takes on his former team-mates Sheringham and Anderton in the second game Scotland played against England.
* Up until the end of the 94-95 season he had received 15 yellow cards and been sent off 4 times.  In this same period his statistics reflected 2 own-goals.

* He was an essential player both for Gerry Francis and for the Scotland manager.  He formed a partnership in the centre of defence with Campbell and led the Tottenham defence well.  He also made use of his height at set-plays.  A safe passer, he continued to show his ability to read the games and his gritty nature, playing almost all of the season with knee problems.
