194.name: Mabbutt
pages: * One of Tottenham's flagships in recent years, Gary Mabbut starts this season from scratch as he has just recovered from a serious injury that affected him in the first part of the 96-97 season.  A player with a lot of character and very much liked at the club.  Team-mates, manager and fans will be happy to see this charismatic central defender make a comeback and try and bow out gracefully with some title or other for Tottenham.

* A very hard and experienced central defender, Mabbutt is the axis of the Tottenham defence and his impetus and character mark the team's game. Excellent in the aerial game, it is hard to get anywhere by bombarding the area with high balls, as he imposes his presence well.  This dominance also allows him to join in the attack dangerously and he scores goals with a certain regularity, almost always with his head.  He infects the rest of the team with his enthusiasm and his presence is a guarantee in the defence.  Technically discrete, he takes advantage of his experience to remedy difficult problems and, if he doesn't see a clear-cut solution, he doesn't hesitate to punt the ball away.  In any case, the best definition of his characteristics are summarised in two words: good defender.

* UEFA Cup Champion in 1984.
* FA Cup Champion 90-91.
* Charity Shield Medal 82 and 91.

* 16 full international appearances for England.  He made his debut on the 13th of October 1982 at Wembley, in a friendly where the England team lost 1-2.
* He scored his first and only goal as an international on the 12th of November 1986 at Wembley.  England defeated Yugoslavia 2-0.  His last appearance for his country was on the 25th of March 1992, in a game against Czechoslovakia played in Prague.
* 10 B-international appearances.
*  5 under-21 international appearances.
* 11 youth international appearances.  2 goals.

* He is member of a family of footballers.  His father played between 1956 and 1971 for Bristol Rovers and Newport County.  His brother Kevin played for Bristol City, Bristol Rovers and Crystal Palace between 1976 and 1985. 
* Following in the steps of his father, he starts at Bristol Rovers, one of the clubs of his hometown, making his debut on the 16th of December 1978 against Burnley.  Mabbut was 17.  Shortly afterwards, on the 9th of January 1979, he signs his professional contract for the Eastville club.
* A diabetic, he needs to control his sugar levels tightly though this obviously doesn't stop him from playing football.
* On the 11th of August 1982 he is transferred to Tottenham Hotspur for £105,000.  He makes his debut for Spurs in a game against Luton Town and scores a goal.
*  In 1984 Spurs were proclaimed UEFA Cup Champions after defeating the Belgian team Anderlecht in the penalty shoot-out.
* On the negative side of his European experience is the tie with Real Madrid.  In the first leg at White Hart Lane, Mabbut scores the only goal of the game in his own net.  In the second leg played in the Santiago Bernabéu (0-0), he was sent off after a hard tackle on Jorge Valdano.
* In 1987 Tottenham loose the FA Cup final against Coventry City by 1-2 with another own-goal from Gary Mabbutt.
* His is compensated four years later (1991) when the team win the FA Cup beating Nottingham Forest 2-1.
* He is the Spurs' captain.
* Up until the end of the 94-95 season he had only received 3 yellow cards in the whole of his career, less than the number of own-goals: 4.
* He suffered a serious injury in the first game of the 96-97 season which kept him out for a year.
* An injury in the first game of the championship kept him out for the entire season, and Mabbut could only play that fateful game against Blackburn.

195.name: Campbell
pages: * Today, Sol Campbell is the most sought after Tottenham player both in England and abroad.  With some innate ability for playing football and some amazing enthusiasm to continue improving, the English international is perhaps in the most important season of his career.  With the French World Cup looming in the background, Campbell has the obligation to maintain or even improve on the excellent performances of last year.  If he manages to do so and confirm his role as a star in the Finals, a lot of the big English and European clubs will be calling at Tottenham's door to try and acquire his services.

* Sol Campbell is one of the most versatile players in the Premier League. With an extraordinary physique, he can adapt to several positions, and has played as a centre back, left back, midfielder and even forward.  In any position, Campbell puts in a lot of work.  Left-footed, his strength and resistance manifest themselves on the pitch.  He is untiring which, combined with his pace makes him an important man during the 90 minutes.  Hard to beat when he is defending, he is powerful in the air, characteristics which lead him to often play as a centre back.  He has an acceptable technique, something fundamental when joining in the attack.  However, his youth means that he makes some mistakes for being over eager, which he should correct.  In any case, we are looking at a footballer with an extraordinary future, and who, given time, could become a star of the Premier League and one of the regulars in the England line-up.
* European under-20 Champion with England in 1993.

* 9 full international caps for England.  He made his debut on the 18th of May 1996 at Wembley, in a friendly against Hungary (3-0).  Present in the England 96 European Championship, he only played in the first phase game against Scotland (2-0), substituting for the injured Jamie Redknapp in the 84th minute.
* 1 international B appearance.
* 11 under-21 international appearances.  1 goal.
* 3 youth international appearances.

* Raised in the Tottenham youth squad, he signs as a professional on the 23rd of September 1992.  In this same year he makes his league debut on the 5th of December against Chelsea.  Despite scoring a goal, this was the only league game he played that season.
* European under-20 Champion, he doesn't make his debut for the full team until May 1996.  He is called up by Terry Venables for the final phase of the European Championship, but only plays 6 minutes in the whole of the championship, after substituting for the injured Jamie Redknapp in the England-Scotland game played at Wembley.
* Up until the end of the 94-95 season he had received 3 yellow cards. 
* His value has gone through the roof and several times there were rumours of a move to Liverpool, or to one of the big teams of the continent, Real Madrid being the main candidate.

* His versatility meant that Campbell even played as a forward.  In his natural position he showed himself to be a player who has made giant leaps and has increased his security and self-confidence.  He played all of the games during the championship and became one of Hoddle's regulars in the England defence.  He was a key part in England's classification for the France World Cup in the game in Rome which led to England's qualification.

196.name: Wilson
pages: * He never starts the seasons as a regular in the line-ups, but Wilson always ends up playing a lot of games.  He is a veteran wide defender who despite never having played for his country, has a lot of respect within English football.  This season he will have to compete with Clemence, and the son of the mythical goalkeeper should not be complacent because Wilson is still a footballer with a lot to offer.

* Although he has, at times, played as a midfielder, Wilson offers his best performances at left back.  He is a very quick footballer who joins in the attack frequently and quickly.  He pushes up his touchline decisively to help out in midfield and in the team's attack, although he doesn't often get shots in.  Experienced and with resources, he does his defensive duties effectively despite not being very bulky.  A good marker, he is hard to get by in a one-on-one.  On the other hand, due to his physical conditions he is not so good in the air.  In any case, Clive Wilson is an excellent wide defender who could still make a good contribution to Tottenham's cause.
* Second Division Champion 88-89.
x

* A native of Manchester, he made his first steps in the footballing world in one of the big clubs of the city, Manchester City.  Originally from the junior category, he signs for the first squad on the 8th of December 1979.  However, he has to wait two years to make his debut in the league, a debut which takes place at Maine Road on the 28th of December 1981 against Wolves. 
* Lacking opportunities he is loaned to Chester City on the 16th of September 1982.  This loan allows him to acquire the experience necessary to find a slot in the team on returning to Maine Road.
* On the 19th of March 1987 he is transferred to Chelsea for £250,000.  The 88-89 season sees the Blues proclaimed Second Division Champions.
* Queens Park Rangers sign him on the 4th of July 1990 for £450,000.  In the 90-91 season he plays as a midfielder.  The manager, Gerry Francis, who has been managing QPR since June '91, decides to play him at left back. 
* He starts the 94-95 season badly, being sent off after 7 minutes of the first half of the first game of the league.  It was at Old Trafford and Manchester United beat QPR 2-0.
* At the end of the 94-95 season his contract finishes and Gerry Francis, now at Tottenham, signs him in August.  He makes his debut in the league in the third match of the season, on the 26th of August, with a 3-1 defeat for Spurs against Liverpool at White Hart Lane.
* He played his five-hundredth game at the top level in the month of October against Sunderland.

* He had a job finding a gap in the first team due to injuries and the presence of Carr, Scales and Ramón Vega.  However, in some of his appearances he showed his decisiveness when he pushed up along the touchline.  In total he played 26 games and scored a goal.

197.name: Saïb
pages: x

* The introverted character that Moussa shows in his private life is not reflected when the Algerian steps onto the pitch.  From this moment onwards, he becomes one of the main reference points, continually making himself available to receive passes and start his team's attacking moves.  He usually plays as a right half, although he will often play in the centre as a playmaker or as a link-man with the forwards, whether in the middle or on one of the wings.  He has a notable technical level and great playing vision.  His astute passes are full of precision.  He shoots powerfully and when he pops up in the rival box he will often find the back of the net.  However, perhaps he is a little irregular, which leads him to "disappear" during certain phases of the game.

* French League title with Auxerre (96).
* Two French Cup titles with Auxerre (94 and 96).
* One African Cup with Algeria (90).
* One Algerian League title with Kabylie (90).
* One African Clubs Championship title with Kabylie (90).
* One Afro-Asian Clubs Championship title with Kabylie (91).
* One Algerian Cup title with Kabylie (92).

* Full international for Algeria more than 70 times. 
* He made his debut in 1988. 
* He has participated with his national side in several African Cups.

* The eldest of nine brothers.  One of them, Ramzi, plays for Kabylie and is a cadet international for Algeria. 
* He has a reserved and introverted character. 
* When he won the African Cup with Algeria he was suspended for a year from taking part in his country's championship because he had signed for two teams (Tiaret and Tizi-Ouzou) at the same time.  He didn't get to play for the latter of these.  During this season he only played international games. 
* The Auxerre training body discovered him in a friendly game between Algeria and France played in August 1992.  One month later Sa°b signed for the French team. 
* His first season in France was very hard as he hardly got to play, but his manager, Guy Roux, was sincere with him and told him that the first season was one for adaptation and that his opportunities would come in the following season.  The confidence that Roux showed in him was enough to dissuade him from returning to Algeria. 
* In his second season at Auxerre, the departure of Dutuel, now with the Spanish club Celta, to Marseilles, paved the way to a regular place in the first team as right half.  Years later, the transfer of Martins to Deportivo (Spain) gave him the chance to operate in the playmaker role. 
* He has dual nationality, Algerian and French. 
* He made his debut in the French First Division on the 30th of October, 1992, in a game between Valenciennes and Auxerre (3-3). 
* Arsenal and Real Betis showed interest in signing him. 
* He is very good friends with Sabri Lamouchi, a French footballer originally from Tunisia, who he overlapped with at Auxerre. 
* Before starting the 95-96 season he had an offer from Marseilles, but Guy Roux didn't let him go. 
* He had problems with Guy Roux, the Auxerre manager, at the end of the 95-96 season.  In the last game of the season, before lifting up the trophy for winning the League, Roux called on all the players apart from Sa°b, something which didn't please the Algerian at all.  He had to be content with seeing the title award on the tele, as a few weeks earlier he had broken a rib.  Despite the injury, Moussa had accepted playing the weekend before in the final of the French Cup, and he expected a better treatment from his manager.The intentioned snub by Roux reduced him to tears in front of the set and he admits that in this moment he was thinking of returning to Argelia.  Despite all this, his importance in the team were such that Roux gave him the captain's armband for the games which Sabri Lamouchi couldn't play in the 96-97 season. 
* Real Sociedad (Spain) tried to sign him before he was signed by Valencia. 
* He has a contract until the 30th of June 2001. 
* He was the first community player not born in Spain signed by Valencia after the Bosman ruling. 
* He is the second Algerian to play for Valencia in the whole of the history of the club.  Before him Rabah Madjer played for the club. 
* He made his debut in the Spanish league on the 31st of August 1997, in a game between Mallorca and Valencia (2-1).  He was starter and was substituted by Javi Navarro in the 65th minute.

* Last season he played 33 games in the French league for Auxerre and managed to find the net eight times.  He was once again one of the team's best players, although his contribution wasn't enough to repeat the success story of the season before and Sa°b had be content with seeing his team finish mid-table.

198.name: Berti
pages: x

* He is an attacking minded midfield player, quick, who can distribute the ball well, though his game is a little erratic.  If he plays as he is capable of doing, he is as dangerous as any forward, and he makes good use of his speed and power to breakthrough rival defences, arriving from the midfield.Although he is not great technically, he makes up for this with his impressive physical condition, which allows him to push up into the attack constantly without affecting his defensive duties.  He sacrifices himself for the good of the team and battles hard.  Berti is a great headerer of the ball and shoots powerfully with his right foot.  If his performance were more consistent Berti would be a much better footballer than he currently is.

* One league Championship with Inter Milan (89).
* Two UEFA Cup titles with Inter (91 and 94).
* Third in the Italy '90 World Cup.
* Runner-up in the US '94 World Cup.

* 39 full international appearances and 15 under-21 caps.
* He made his debut on the 19th of October 1988 in a friendly game between Italy and Norway played in Pescara (2-1).
* He has taken part in the Italy '90 and United States '94 World Cup final stages.
* In the World Cup Finals played on American territory he played in all the games disputed by his side, including the 120 minutes of the final.  He played in seven games (467 minutes) and didn't manage to score a single goal.  Arrigo Sacchi had blind faith in him, despite the current of public opinion in Italy, which went against Berti's presence in the United States.

* He is a close friend of the Russian midfielder Igor Shalimov.  Berti always visited him whenever he could in the Swiss town of Lugano, whose team Shalimov was playing for until November 1995.
* He started his career at Visalso, a small team from his hometown, Salsomaggiore, a few kilometres from Parma.   The Brazilian, Maurizio Battistini, one of the men in charge of the lower teams of Parma, saw him him play, and suggested that he join the Parma club.  He finished his training there.  Nicola Berti was only 15 years old and was playing as a centre forward, perhaps the reason for his good finishing today.
* He made his debut in the Serie A on the 8th of September 1985 in a game between Fiorentina and Sampdoria (1-0).
* In 1988 the Florence club loaned him, without his consent, to Inter, a loan which ended up as a rather disputed transfer.  For this reason, every time Berti steps onto the pitch at Artemio Franchi he is greeted with plenty of jeers.
* Convinced of the view that Inter Milan with the Germans (Matthaus, Brehme and Klinsmann) and Ramon Diaz was a stronger team than the great AC Milan of the Dutchmen (Van Basten, Gullit and Rijkaard), Berti scored the most spectacular goal of his career in a game his team played against Bayern Munich.He ran 70 metres with the ball at his feet and finished off the run by slotting the ball away.  From that moment on, many people's opinion of Berti as a player improved considerably.
* In the 93-94 season he hardly played.  On the 8th of September 1993, during the course of a game between Inter and Cremonese (2-1), he suffered a very serious injury to his knee which kept him away from the football pitches until the 6th of March, when he reappeared in a game against Udinese.
* On the 3rd of February 1996 he ruptured his front crossed knee ligament, an injury which kept him out for the rest of the season.

* Last season he played 23 games, five of them from the start, and scored a goal.  He managed to overcome his physical problems which had haunted him in the last few years and he managed to play regularly, though almost always coming on as a substitute for a team-mate.  When he was on the pitch he used all his force, his winning mentality and battling spirit that have characterised him throughout his career.

199.name: Dominguez
pages:
* This is his second spell in English football after having played from March 1994 to June 1995 at Birmingham, the team which was proclaimed Second Division Champions and therefore earned promotion to the First Division.  After this success Sporting Lisbon decided to reclaim him for Portuguese football, and he did well in the two seasons he was at the Lisbon club.
* Gerry Francis had heard good things of Dominguez, a player he had already began to watch at Birmingham.  More mature than in his first spell in England, the Portuguese player is now an even more unsettling player for the opposition, and he could be a supersub for Ginola and who knows, finish the season in the starting line-up.

* Dominguez if a left-footed player with a devilish turn.  Quick and skilful, on an inspired day he is able to tie any defender in knots.  He is not timid about trying a one-on-one, although at times he is a little selfish. Always on the left, his exquisite left allows him to pass well.  In some games he pushes up to play as a winger.
* Second Division Champion with Birmingham in the 94-95 season.
* Under-21 international for Portugal.

* Dominguez arrived in English football for the first time in March 1994. On that occasion Birmingham paid Benfica £180,000 for him.
* After three seasons at Birmingham his progress didn't pass unnoticed by several Portuguese clubs, though it was Sporting Lisbon who brought him back to his native country.
* For the last two seasons at the Lisbon team, Dominguez hasn't stopped growing as a footballer, up to such a point that Tottenham didn't hesitate to pay £1,600,000 for him.
* He made his debut in the Premier League for Tottenham in a game against Coventry.  Domínguez came on as a substitute for Ginola.  According to some fans and reporters it had been a long time since someone caused such a good impression on his debut at Tottenham.
* He had an excellent season at Sporting Lisbon, which led Tottenham to insist on signing him.  He took part in 32 games and scored three goals.

200.name: Ginola
pages:
* Ginola is, without doubt, one of the biggest talents in European football in the last 10 years.  The heir of the French school which, in its day, produced players such as Fontaine, Kopa, Platini and Cantona, Ginola always gave the impression that he could be something better than he currently is.  The first time his name was heard strongly in Europe was after the UEFA Cup tie which Paris Saint Germain disputed against Real Madrid in the Santiago Berbabéu.  The Spanish team won 3-1, but the Spanish supporters have the twists and turns of Ginola engraved on their memories.
* It is not known if due to lack of motivation or due to his failed moves to Cruyff's Barcelona or Real Madrid, but David Ginola has not managed to equal that football which had Europe spellbound when he was playing at PSG.  Since he arrived in England, signed by Newcastle, only on a limited number of occasions has his prodigious right produced the football he has inside.  Now at Tottenham, and with the disillusion that he won't play in the World Cup played in his country, the only thing left is to recover the lost prestige, for his own good, that of Tottenham and all the fans who have, at some time or other, been captivated by his game and gone to the grounds with the knowledge that if Ginola was playing the spectacle was assured.

* When David Ginola receives a ball out on the touchline, generally the left, an attacking move is immediately underway.  Blessed with an extraordinary talent and an exquisite technique, the Frenchman is one of the most creative footballers in England.  He takes advantage of his speed to break through rival defences, stops and, suddenly, changes the rhythm again in a new twist.  Although he is right-footed, he can use both feet and is able to make goalscoring passes to his team-mates or try out his powerful shot on goal from a distance.  It has to be said he is not noted for his aerial game nor does he help out in defence, which, at times, creates problems for his team's backs.
* Ginola can also play as a link-man with the forwards, but he offers his best performance out wide.  A very complete player, he can shield the ball, control it with the chest or the feet, and when he is on song he is hard to stop without fouling him.  A good free-kick taker, the attacking capacity of the team drops when he doesn't enter much in the game.  It is his temperament that leads him into trouble at times, and his performance drops.  In any case, Ginola has always shown that he is a sensational footballer.

* French League Champion 94.
* French Cup Champion 93 and 95.
* Voted "French Footballer of the Year" in 1994, by the Footballers Association.
* Voted "French Footballer of the Year 94" by the magazine France Football.

* 16 full international appearances for France.  3 goals.  He made his debut on the 17th of November 1990 in Tirana against Albania.  Ginola came on in the 66th minute as a substitute for Tibeuf and the French team won 0-1.  He didn't return to the national team until the 26th of August 1992, in a game in which Brazil beat France 0-2 in the Princes Park in Paris.

* Aged 13, David Ginola was a lad suffering from his complex of being "shorty".  However, he had a passion for football and after class he would go and train in the park.
* Aged 17, his father tried to get Nice to sign his first professional contract, but he was rejected.  Ginola left for Toulon, who accept him into their training centre thanks to the interest of Mr. Pieri, Christian Dalger and Gaby Robert.
* He makes his debut in the French First Division in a game against Metz, coming on for Víctor Ramos for the last quarter of an hour.  Toulon won 2-0. 
* In the summer of 1988 he is transferred to Matra Racing Paris, where he plays two seasons.
* After finishing his first season at Brest (90-91) the team finished in twelfth position, but is punished for economic irregularities with relegation.  
* After starting the 91-92 season at Brest, Paris Saint Germain offer him the chance to return to the First Division.  With this club he wins titles and takes part in European competitions which bring him international recognition.  In total he played 27 games in the Champions League, Cup Winners' Cup and UEFA Cup, scoring 5 goals.
* Strangely, he usually has good games against Spanish teams.  With PSG the team knocked out Real Madrid twice from European competition and Barcelona from the Champions League in 1995.  In one of these games he scored an extraordinary goal on the volley against Real Madrid in the Princes' Park in Paris.  Míchel, a Madrid player, went over to congratulate him.
* His popularity in France dropped notably after a classification game for the 94 United States World Cup which France lost to Bulgaria, eliminating the team from the competition.  Ginola wanted to show off with the ball, lost it, and in the counter-attack, Kostadinov scored the Bulgarian goal. Many supporters turned against him after that, and the incident led to a strong argument with Eric Cantona and cost him his place in the team as a result of declarations he made after the game.
* In July 1995 he is transferred to Newcastle for £2,500,000.  He makes his debut on the 19th of August of this same year with a 3-0 win over Coventry at St. James Park.  He scores his first goal for the Magpies on the 27th of August at Hillsborough against Sheffield Wednesday.
* His absence from the French team during the 96 England World Cup provoked a big controversy in France, as a large sector of the press and the fans considered both his and Eric Cantona's presence necessary in the national team.  However, the selector, Aimé Jacquet decided not to call up either of them, remembering the bad relations that he had with both players in the past. 
* In the summer of 1996 there were persistent rumours about a move to Barcelona, but they didn't materialise.
* A great golf fan, one of his best friends is Phillipe Alain, a golf professional.
* The BBC awarded him two "goal of the month" awards in 96-97, something which no other player had achieved.
* His move to Tottenham Hotspur in July 97 cost the club £2,000,000.

* Despite rumours of a move to Barcelona, Ginola started the season at Newcastle playing as a left winger.  However, he didn't have a good season, and only came good on a few occasions such as in the UEFA Cup game against Halmstad when he made three goals, or two goals of his own against Manchester and the other against Ferencvaros, which were voted Goal of the Month by the BBC.
* These details didn't help to cover up a disappointing season in which Kenny Dalglish felt forced to relegate him to the bench due to his poor performance.  In total he played 24 league games and scored a goal.  These are not good number for a player who has the talent to come through in any team.

201.name: Nielsen
pages: * This is Allan Nielsen's second season at Tottenham and much is expected of him by the club at White Hart Lane.  Already last season he managed to earn the affection of the fans and this season he is one of the players who could be one of the keys Francis' scheme.  Nielsen is a player on whose shoulders a lot of attacking responsibility at Tottenham should rest when Francis decides to play him, above all for constructing and initiating the moves.

* Allan Nielsen has the characteristics that allow him to play in several positions on the pitch.  Blessed with an excellent technique and a good playing vision, he has the ability necessary to play as a centre half, although at times he drifts over to the wings.  He passes the balls quickly and with good judgement, offering himself constantly to his team-mates to redirect the play.  Well prepared physically, he his workmanlike in defence, although he offers his best performances when he is near the rival area.  He has a good long-range shot and finishes well.  A footballer still young, he needs to improve, but he has enough abilities to become an important player.
x

* 10 international appearances for Denmark.  2 goals.  He made his debut on the 16th of August 1995 in a game against Armenia (2-0), substituting for Jensen in the 45th minute, scoring a goal.  Present in the England in the European Cup, he only played one game against Hungary in Hillsborough. Denmark won 3-0 and Allan Nielsen scored the second.

* Before filling out the ranks of Brondby arriving from Copenhagen, he had a brief spell at the German team Bayern Munich, the team where he got to play one game.
* He scored a goal against Armenia on his debut for the Denmark side and scored another against Hungary in his first and only game played in the England European Championship.
* Tottenham tried to sign him for the 95-96 season, but couldn't.  The club at White Hart Lane had to wait until the 23rd of July 1996 before acquiring his services in exchange for £1,650,000.
* He made his debut for Tottenham in the league against Wimbledon (0-0) in London on the 4/9/96.
* He scored his first goal in the Premier League wearing the Tottenham shirt at White Hart Lane (1-0) on the 12/10/96 against Aston Villa.

* Allan Nielsen arrived at Tottenham from Brondby with the competition already underway.  An injury he suffered led to some doubts about his performance, but when he began to show his class and score goals, six, with his head, with his feet, from inside and from outside the area, all doubts about his game evaporated.  This made Allan one of the favourites of the fans.  He played 29 games.

202.name: Hill
pages: * He won't find it easy to find a play or even find a place on the substitutes' bench. He is a player who still isn't used until now and he should think about looking for another team where he will have more chance to show his qualities.

* A midfielder with good technique with both feet, Danny Hill can play in practically any position in the midfield.  A great passer, he usually plays the ball first time, with accurate crosses and a good playing vision.  He needs to improve his physical level to play in a competition as demanding as the Premier League.
x

* 4 under-21 international appearances for England.
* 1 youth international appearance.

* A professional since the 9th of September 1992, the date when he signs his contract for Tottenham, the club where he was trained.
* His debut in the League with the Spurs first team took place on the 20th of March 1993 in a game against Chelsea.
* He didn't play a single game, his contribution being non-existent.

203.name: Howells
pages: * David Howells is facing his fourteenth season at Tottenham, making him one of the most veteran players of the team.  Howells is, above all, a phenomenal club player, capable of adapting to different positions and systems.  For this reason, his presence in the squad is especially valuable and, although he isn't starting the season as a member of the starting line-up, it has to be said that during the course of the season he usually gets to play an important number of games.  And nothing seems to indicate that this season will be different: you don't have to be a superstar to play.

* Versatility. This is the word that best defines David Howells' characteristics.  Although he is considered a midfielder, it is true that he can play in any position in the middle and can even join in the defence. At times Gerry Francis plays him in front of the defence to start the attacking moves from there, helped by his good touch and his skill at distributing the ball.  Other times he plays as an attacking midfielder, where he takes advantage of his speed.  With the ball under control he is able to find gaps in the rival defence.  In any position Howells works hard in defence and attack, contributing with goals to the attacking capacity of Spurs.  Veteran, he has acquired a lot of resources thanks to his ample experience.  He is a good club footballer, though perhaps he is lacking a little bit of aggression in defensive tasks.

* FA Cup Champion in 90-91.
* Charity Shield Medal 91.

* 1 B-international appearance for England.
* 7 under-21 international appearances.  1 goal.

* Trained in the Tottenham youth squad, he moves up to the first team on the 28th of January 1985.  He makes his debut in a game against Sheffield Wednesday played on the 22nd of February 1986, and Howells puts away the winner (2-1).
* Up to the end of the 94-95 season he had received 8 yellow cards in the whole of his career.
* During the course of his extended career he has played in an infinite number of positions both in the midfield and the defence.

* He brought his experience and personality to the team, above all when players were missing who could also contribute with similar characteristics. The fans could see that his game was not so spectacular, but very effective.  He also got over diverse personal problems during the course of the season.He took part in 32 games and scored 2 goals.

204.name: Anderton
pages:
* Anderton is one of the young guns in the new British football, a very complete player with an extraordinary future.  In the 96 England European Championship he showed that we are looking at a phenomenal footballer, a regular in Terry Venables' line-ups and recently recovered from a serious injury.  The England selector must have had a lot of faith in his talent when he called him up, running the risk of severe criticism if Anderton didn't respond to the challenge.  However the Tottenham player not only recovered physically, but also became a fundamental man in the good tournament had by England. 
* A member of an extraordinary generation of players, Anderton's future, as well as that of the England side, looks very good indeed.  At Tottenham alongside Walker and Sol Campbell, amongst others, he is set to mark a splendid period.
* Once more he has to recover from lost form, as last season he was unable to play in a lot of games.  If he returns to his best level, Tottenham will have made one of their best "signings" for this season.

* Darren Anderton is a very complete player, an attacking midfielder who is quick, resistant, technically good and skilful.  Although he is right-footed he can operate perfectly on either side of midfield.  Over near the wing he offers his best repertoire of moves: he controls the ball, passes it accurately and turns effectively.  He is quick enough to get by rival defences and pass the ball between lines.  He also scores goals helped by a good shot from long-range and by his talent for finding space.  Without doubt, one of his best qualities is the intelligence he displays on the pitch, and intelligence that allows him to mark the games pace and, above all, read the game. 
* He collaborates constantly in defensive tasks, regaining his position quickly and pressurising intensely.  He looks fragile but the truth is he is a strong and resistant footballer, capable of keeping up a high rhythm of play for the full 90 minutes.
* Still very young, he could improve even more.  He is one of the best players in England for his versatility and talent.
x

* 16 full international caps for England.  5 goals.  He made his debut on the 9th of March 1994 against Denmark, in a friendly at Wembley (1-0).  He scores his first goal on the 17th of May of this same year, also at Wembley and against the Greece (5-0).  Present in the 96 England European Championship, he was a starter in all the games.
* 11 under-21 international appearances.  4 goals.
* 1 youth international appearance.

* Trained at Portsmouth, he signs as a professional on the 5th of February 1990.  This same year, the 3rd of November, he makes his league debut against Wolverhampton Wanderers.
* He was the star of the 91-92 season in England.  He led Portsmouth to the FA Cup semi-finals, playing against Liverpool.  The first game finished 0-0, and after the 90 minutes of the replay the score was tied again (1-1), and the game went into extra-time.  Anderton managed to put Portsmouth ahead, but in the end Liverpool drew level with a goal from Whelan and in the penalty shoot-out, Anderton's team didn't transform a single one.  And so the dream of a historic final between two Second Division teams, Sunderland was the other finalist, went up in smoke.
* His magnificent season for Portsmouth led to his transfer to Tottenham Hotspur for £1,750,000.  The date was the 6th of June 1992.
* During a Cup tie played at the Dell against Southampton in the 94-95 season the rival fans booed him continually remembering his past with Portsmouth, Southampton's eternal rival.  Anderton managed to silence the crowd with a magnificent goal.
* A complicated injury in the groan kept him out for the most part of 95-96. However, although he had been practically discarded for the European Championship, he recovered in time and on his reappearance he scored two goals against Hungary at Wembley.
* He was on the point of going down in history as the first footballer who scored a golden goal in the European Championship, but a shot of his in extra-time of the semi-final against Germany unfortunately smashed into the post. 
* The injury he suffered in the 96-97 season only allowed him to play in 16 games.
* He had a somewhat irregular season due to injuries.  He showed his quality on numerous occasions but he wasn't the player that we have seen before. He played in 16 games and scored 3 goals.

205.name: Fox
pages:
* He arrived at Tottenham with the 95-96 season already underway and quickly found a space for himself in the team's line-ups and in the hearts of the supporters.  The truth is that Ruel Fox is a special footballer, used to earning the affection of the fans with his constant effort.  Short of stature, his figure covers every square inch of the pitch.  He takes part in defensive tasks and helps out in attack.  He never gives up a ball as lost.  These qualities make him an important player for the team.  For this reason Gerry Francis has blindly placed his trust in him, and Fox has responded once again. 
* This faith that Gerry Francis placed in him has not been lost, but there were certain rumours of a possible move from the club because the manager prefers wing backs rather than pure wingers.  Even so, to get rid of a player of the quality of Fox is not easy and Francis knows that when Ruel is on form he is one of the best players in the Premier League.

* An attacking midfielder blessed with excellent technique and turn of speed.  He usually plays hugging the right touchline, where he receives the ball to make forays into the area or get to the by-line to give cross for his forwards.  He has also got a good turn, making the jobs of rival defenders more difficult.  At times he moves to the left flank, to take advantage of his shot with the right.  Physically powerful, he makes a constant contribution to the team's defence, giving his all during the game. His speed allows him to regain his position quickly and pressure the rival. He finishes well and usually scores several goals during a season, some with his head, surprising given his lack of height.  However, he makes up for this disadvantage with an extraordinary physical force and great positional skill.
x
* 2 times England B international.

* Trained in the Norwich City youth squad, he signs as a professional on the 20th of January 1986.  He makes his debut in the league on the 29th of November of this year in a game against Oxford.  He plays several years for Canaries, forming part of an excellent strikeforce with Chris Sutton and playing in the UEFA Cup in 93-94.
* On the 2nd of February 1994 he is transferred to Newcastle United for £2,250,000.  At St James' Park he becomes on of the most popular players among the fans.
* In the 94-95 season he scores a goal against Athletic Bilbao in the UEFA Cup.  Newcastle beat the Spanish team 3-2 in England, but are eliminated after loosing 1-0 in Bilbao.
* In October 1995 he is transferred to Tottenham Hotspur.  His price had gone up to £4 million.  He makes his debut for Spurs on the 14th of October in a game against Nottingham Forest played at White Hart Lane. Tottenham lost 0-1.
* He scores his first goal with the Spurs shirt on the 4th of November 95 at Highfield Road.  Tottenham beat Coventry 2-3.
* Despite being short he has scored several goals with his head, one of which was against Spurs when Fox was playing for Newcastle.
* Up until the end of the 94-95 season he had received 23 yellow cards.

* Ruel Fox was another of the important players at Tottenham who was affected by injury.  For this reason his game didn't have much continuity he was unable to reach his normal level of form.  His best game was the London derby against Chelsea.

206.name: Sinton
pages: * This is Andy Sinton's third season at Tottenham and there is little doubt that he is a profitable player for the club.  Last season he was one of the best in the team, becoming one of the main references in attack when injuries left Tottenham without some key players.  All this means that Sinton starts this season as one of the footballers who will almost always figure in Francis' plans, whether he plays from the start or comes on as a substitute.

* Sinton is an unpredictable player.  Both on the right and on the left, he is able to turn on a ha'penny, lift his head and create danger.  He moves quickly and is skilful in a one-on-one, an old style winger.  However, his lack of tactical discipline is inconvenient for a lot of managers, who prefer to align footballers who are not as brilliant or as talented as Sinton, but who stick to the proposed tactics.  Andy Sinton is a player who fights against the mechanical football played in many teams.  He moves around in all areas of attack, generally near the touchline, although it is on the left where he is most comfortable and finds a way through with his turn.  At times, Sinton is guilty of selfishness, as he tries for the individual plays without thinking of the good of the team.  And, at other times, he has rejected the decisions of some managers, who have played him in positions far removed from his natural tendency such as right back and even left back.  His lack of a scent for goal has denied him the chance to play more minutes for some teams.  What's more, his lack of leadership prevent him from taking the weight of the team on his shoulders, as he lacks a strong build and mentality, but certainly not talent.
x

* 12 full international appearances for England.  He makes his debut on the 13th of November 1991 in Potsdam against Poland (1-1).  Present in the 92 Sweden European Championship.
* 4 B international appearances.

* He takes his first steps in the footballing world at the modest Cambridge United in September 1980.  Two years later he plays as an apprentice at the same club.  On the 2nd of November 1982 he becomes the youngest player to make his debut for the club in a game against Wolverhampton.  Shortly afterwards he signs as a professional.  In almost four complete seasons with the team he plays more than 100 games.  He was still under 20.
* Despite his services Cambridge United drop from the Second to the Fourth Division.  He is transferred to Brentford on the 13th of September 1985 for £25,000.
* His quality doesn't pass unnoticed by his neighbours Queens Park Ranger, who don't hesitate to pay £350,000 to acquire his services.  On the 23rd of March 1989 Sinton made the jump from the Third to the First Division.  In his home debut he scores the winner against Aston Villa.  An undisputed starter in the 89-90 and 90-91 seasons.
* In the 91-92 season he appears on the international scene.  He is called up for the decisive qualifying game for the Sweden European Championship.  England, with Sinton, draw in Poland.  Later, in a friendly disputed in Moscow he plays at left back, and his performance doesn't earn him his ticket to Sweden for the 92 European Championship.  However, an injury to John Barnes returns him to the team.  England fail in the tournament and Sinton doesn't have much luck at right back.
* On the 19th of August 1993 he is transferred to Sheffield Wednesday for £2,750,000.  Injuries prevent him from gaining confidence and he hardly plays. 
* He starts the 95-96 season with the Owls before moving to Tottenham in January 96 for £1,500,000.  He makes his debut for Spurs on the 3rd of February at Anfield.  Liverpool and Tottenham draw nil-nil.

* Although he had some injury problems in the preseason, Sinton got over them and had a good season.  He was one of the few older players at Tottenham who helped them get through difficult times, such as the game against Manchester United, which, although it ended up in defeat for Spurs, Andy showed the form that, in his day, had brought him into the England team.  His statistics were: 33 games and six goals.

207.name: Klinsmann
pages: x

* He plays at centre forward, although his mobility means that he will take up different positions in the attacking zone during the course of a game.  Quick, with a plenty of technical quality, intelligent, physically strong and with a great finish both with his head and with his feet, Klinsmann has all the qualities necessary to decide a game.  He is a born goalscorer and knows better than anyone what positions he should look for in the area.
No data.
No data.

* He started his career at TB Gingen. The manager of this side was Werner Grass who said of Klinsmann "He cried if he didn't score two goals in a game".  When he was playing for this team he once managed to score 16 goals in one game, an unreachable figure for most footballers, even in lower categories.
* His following destination was SC Geislingen, then he moved onto Stuttgart in 1981, playing for the Stuttgart Kickers.  He made his debut with them in the Second Division.  He 1984 he moved to Stuttgart, where he stayed for five seasons, and scored 79 goals in 156 games.  His excellent strike rate made him into one of the most sought-after German forwards and in 1989 he moved to Inter Milan, where he never quite reached the level that was expected of him.
* He even had some run-ins with the manager Giovanni Trapattoni, who coincidentally went on to manage Bayern Munich the next season.  After three seasons with the Milan team, he moved to Monaco.  There he refound his goalscoring touch which he seemed to have lost on Italian soil.  Two exciting years with the French club and a magnificent performance in the United States World Cup aroused the interest of Tottenham who signed him. At White Hart Lane he produced his best form in recent seasons.
* He was voted "Player of the Year" by the British press and the Spurs fans didn't wait long before elevating to the status of idol.  However, at the end of the 94-95 league he left the club and returned to Germany, more exactly to Bayern Munich.  The Bavarian side only paid £1 million for him, the amount that was in his cancellation clause.  However, the club had to pay the forward another £1.5 million, as well as the £0.8 million salary that he draws per year.
* The most important title of his career is undoubtedly the World Cup that that Germany won in Italy '90.  To this honour the Bronze medal he won at the Seoul Olympics, an Italian Supercup (90) and one UEFA Cup (91) with Inter and another with Bayern Munich (96) should be added.
* He has 80 full international caps for Germany under his belt.  He has played in two European Championships (Germany '88 and Sweden '92) and two World Cup final stages (Italy '90 and United States '94).
No data.

208.name: Ferdinand
pages:
* The arrival of Alan Shearer at Newcastle hasn't forced his exit, but if the international striker wasn't there it is likely that the club at St. James' Park would have let him go so easily.  The offer that Tottenham put on the table was, in any case, irresistible, taking into account that Ferdinand is nearly 31.
* However, despite his advanced age Ferdinand is still a player capable of producing some good performances, and will try all the more harder as he will want to be included in the squad that goes with Hoddle to France in the coming summer.

* Les Ferdinand is, above all, a player for the box, whose performances is measured in terms of the number of goals he scores each season.  As such, his capacity to resolve chances is his biggest virtue.  Excellent in the aerial game, many of his goals bear the signature of his powerful header. Thanks to his extraordinary jump and sense of anticipation, Ferdinand is able to stay suspended in the air a instant longer that the rival defenders, making him hard to mark.  With the ball at his feet is not a technical footballer, but his is able to find space to get in his powerful shot with the right.  Physically strong, he never shies away from a challenge and has the necessary resistance to pressure the rival defence.  He doesn't take much part in the elaboration of moves, but is always well placed to finish them off.
* Turkish Cup Champion 93.

* 10 full international appearances for England.  3 goals.  He made his debut on the 17th of February 1993 in a classification game for the United States World Cup against San Marino played at Wembley.  The English team won 6-0 and the Ferdinand scored a goal.  Present in the 96 England European Championship, he didn't play a single minute.

* He started playing football at the modest team Hayes.  In March 1987 he receives an offer from Queens Park Rangers, an offer that he accepts after rejecting one for a job as a painter/decorator.  He signs for the London club on the 12th of March and makes his debut in the League on the 20th of April of this same year in a game against Coventry City.
* On the 24th of March 1988 he is loaned to Brentford and shortly afterwards he joins the Turkish team Besitkas.  In Turkey he needs a total of 53 games to score 21 goals and contributes decisively to the conquest of the Cup title and the runners-up title in the league.
* On returning to England, the presence of Gerry Francis at QPR allows him to figure a little more in the team's line-ups.  In 1994 the club extends his contract by two years.
* Ferdinand is QPR's top scorer for three seasons on the trot (92-93, 93-94, and 94-95).  During this time he scores 2 hat-tricks.
* Several clubs in the Premier League are interested in signing him, but in June 1995 he moves to Newcastle for £6 million.  His signing corresponds to the club's effort to cover for the absence of Andy Cole, transferred a few months earlier to Manchester United.  Ferdinand makes his debut on the 19th of August of this same year in a game against Coventry played at St. James' Park (3-0) and he finishes his first season at Newcastle as the third top scorer in the League behind Alan Shearer and Robbie Fowler.
* He is one of the players who has received the most number of yellow cards in the Premier League.  Up till the end of the 94-95 season he had received 23 yellow cards and had been sent off twice.
* He scored his fiftieth goal for Newcastle on the 11/6/97 in St. James' Park against Nottingham Forest (5-0).
* Tottenham pay Newcastle £6 million for his transfer in July 97.

* Contrary to what a lot of people thought, Ferdinand was able to form a deadly attacking partnership with Alan Shearer.  Ferdinand moved over towards the right a little and set up a lot of goals for Alan, at the same time scoring quite a lot himself, 16, six of these in consecutive games.  His performance led Hoddle to call him up to play against Poland and Georgia, scoring a goal against the latter of these.  Unfortunately, Ferdinand saw how an injury forced him out for some games.  Even so, when he recovered he once again reached his high level and scored his fiftieth goal for Newcastle.

209.name: Iversen
pages:
* The injury crisis that hit Tottenham Hotspur at the end of November 1996 precipitated the signing of Steffen Iversen.  The Norwegian forward was sought after by some of the most prestigious clubs in Europe, but the economic conditions and the presence of Espen Baardsen in the team led him to accept the Spurs offers.  Once his signing went through, Gerry Francis showed a boundless faith in him and announced his immediate presence in the team.  White Hart Lane now has a new idol to worship, a young 21-year old Norwegian. 
* Everyone expected a lot of Iversen because he is a player with a good future who, last season, showed some of the things he is capable of doing. He could form an excellent strike partnership with Ferdinand.  If this is the case Tottenham will be a team to be feared when the ball is near the rival goal.

* He plays as a centre forward, a position where he takes advantage of his efficiency in front of goal.  Quick and powerful, he is able to find space in the rival area.  He has a good header, his biggest virtue, and never runs away from physical contact with the defenders.  Despite his youth he is shows some of the resources of a veteran footballer.  He hardly takes part in the build up, but his ability to slip his marker allows him to finish off the moves from favourable positions.

* Norwegian League Champion in 95 and 96.
* Norwegian Cup Champion 95.
* 17 under-21 international appearances for Norway.  13 goals.

* Trained in the youth squad at Astor, Steffen Iversen joins Rosenborg as a youth player.
* In 1995 he makes his debut in the First Division and scores 8 goals in 25 games.  Rosenborg are proclaimed League and Cup Champions.  Iversen scores a goal in the final of the Cup competition, where his side defeat Brann 3-1.  
* At the beginning of the 95-96 season his great performances, both in the Norwegian league -where his team are once again champions- and in the Champions League awake the interest of several of the best clubs of the continent such as PSV Eindhoven, Liverpool, Ajax and Barcelona.
*  On the 2nd of December 1996 he is transferred to Tottenham Hotspur for £2,600,000.  However, two days later, he plays his last game wearing the Rosenborg shirt.  The Norwegian team knock the all-mighty Milan out of the Champions League after beating them 1-2 in San Siro.
* At White Hart Lane Iversen overlaps with his great friend Espen Baardsen, the second goalkeeper.
* He made his debut for Tottenham at Coventry (1-2) on the 7/12/96. 
* He scored his first goal for Spurs in the Premier League on the 26/12/96 at White Hart Lane against Southampton (3-1).  Iversen scored his first goal in the first minute, and his second in the sixtieth.

* It was, without doubt, the best season of his life, backed up by his performance in the San Siro stadium, in the game in which Rosenborg eliminated Milan from the Champions league.  This game caused the asking price for Iversen to go through the roof and several European clubs were interested in signing him.  Finally, it was Tottenham who managed to bag him in the month of December.  Once at White Hart Lane, Iversen quickly showed that this was a good inversion, producing some excellent performances, such as the time when he scored a hat-trick against Sunderland.  In total, he took part in 16 games for Spurs and scored 6 goals.

210.name: Armstrong
pages:
*  It was looking like the most expensive signing in Tottenham's history was one of those multi-million-pound transfers that don't fit in and end up sloping out the back door.  However, Gerry Francis' personal project started to bear fruit little by little and, goal by goal, Armstrong has managed to earn the respect of the followers in his first season.
* Armstrong, after an unfortunate last season, starts from square one and will try and return to the sort of form that dazzled in his first year at Tottenham.  His chances won't be lacking because Francis has a lot of faith in him.

* Chris Armstrong's game has progressed spectacularly in the last few years. A quick forward, with a great ability to find space, he knows how to get behind the rival defender.  Technically correct, he takes advantage of his good turn to force a one-on-one with the goalkeeper.  He scores goals easily, many with his head thanks to the power of his jump.  Right-footed, most of his goals come from inside the box.  And his long range shot is one of the aspects of his game that he should work on.
* He has an extraordinary physique, with a lot of power and resistance, allowing him to put a lot of pressure on the rival defence.  At the moment he is one of the best forwards in England, and when he is on form, he is practically unstoppable.
* First Division Champion 93-94.
* 1 B-international appearance for England.

* He started his training as a footballer at the modest Llay Welfare, before signing for Wrexham on the 3rd of March 1989.  He makes his league debut on the 4th of January 94 against Hartlepool.
* On the 16th of August 1991 he is transferred to Millwall for £50,000. 
* One year later his price had gone up notably.  Transferred to Crystal Palace on the 1st of September 1992 for £1 million, Armstrong saw his dream of playing in the Premier League come true.
* He sees Palace's relegation to the First Division in 1993 and, one year later, the return to the Premier League.  In the 94-95 season, despite scoring 3 goals in the last three games of the league, he is unable to prevent the club from going down again.
* When he signs for Tottenham in August 1995 he is the club's most expensive player ever at the time, the price: £4,500,000.  He makes his debut in the first game of the 95-96 season.  Tottenham draw 1-1 at Maine Road against Manchester City.  However, his first goal would have to wait until the tenth game (22/10/95), the equaliser in a game against Everton at Goodison Park.

* Due to an injury Armstrong was unable to compete for the honour of being among the Premier League's top scorers.  He could only play twelve games, in which he scored five goals, not a bad tally.  Armstrong was, without doubt, one of Francis' hopes to take Tottenham to the top but, just as happened with Anderton and Fox, injuries got in the way of the plan.

212.name: Forrest
pages: * Having lost his first team place at Ipswich Town to Richard Wright, Craig Forrest decided upon a change of scenery. In July 1997 he was transfered to West Ham, theoretically as a replacement for Ludo Miklosko. However, in a competition as tough and as demanding as the Premier League, sooner or later opportunities are bound to come along, and, Craig Forrest will no doubt be ready when they do.

* The Canadian is a very complete goalkeeper. With good reflexes and fine positional sense, he is also very safe in the air. A spectacular keeper, he likes to try to win over the supporters by over elaborating some of  his saves, something which occasionally sees him making some incredible mistakes. Despite that, his experience gives him the know how to get himself, and the team, out of tight situations with apparent ease.
* Second Division winners medal 1992.
* 37 full international appearances for Canada.

* Back in his native Canada he played ice hockey. 
* After coming through the ranks at Ipswich Town, he signed professional in August 1985. He made his league debut on 27th August 1988 against Stoke City. 
* In March 1988 he went out on loan for two months, at Colchester United. He made his debut on 4th March 1988 against Wrexham. 
* Understudy to Richard Wright at Ipswich, he went out on loan again, this time to Chelsea, on 26th March 1997. He made his debut for the Blues on 16th April of that same year in a 3-1 defeat against Newcastle at Saint James' Park. Forrest came on in place of the injured Grodas in the 36th  minute of the first half. 
* On 22nd July 1997 he was transfered to West Ham for 500,000 pounds.

* As Richard Wright's stand in at Ipswich Town, he was limited to just six appearances for the Portman Road club. In March he went out on loan to Chelsea, initially as the club's third choice goalkeeper. However, an injury to the Norwegian Grodas, in a game against Newcastle, allowed him to make his debut for the Blues. Satisfied with his performance, manager Ruud Gullit showed enough confidence in Forrest to play him in another two league games, both of which ended in victories for Chelsea.

213.name: Miklosko
pages: * Ludo Miklosko is one of the foreign players who has best adapted to the English way of life. Since his arrival in London, the goalkeeper has been very well appreciated by the Upton Park supporters, an appreciation which he has always publicly been grateful for. As a result, nobody was surprised when Ludo decided that he wanted to set up home in Essex once his career was over. The only problem is, given his tremendous form in recent seasons,(ask any Manchester United fan), nobody dares to predict the date of his retirement. While nothing happens to change the situation, Miklosko remains the best goalkeeper at West Ham, and one of the best in England.

* Ludo Miklosko is a goalkepeer with tremendous reflexes which allow him to make some incredibles saves. A well built man, he is dominant in the  air, safe in one on one situations and generates confidence amongst his defensive colleagues. Brave, and with tremendous character, he seems to grow in size and stature when the going gets tough, helped out by all the knowledge that his experience gives him. He is good with his feet, and stands out for his long goal kicks. Miklosko is, above all, a keeper who provides a genuine guarantee of security in goal.
x

* 42 full international appearances for Czechoslovakia.
* He made his last appearance for his country on 25th April 1990, at Wembley against England. The Czech lost 4-2.
* He was a member of his country squad in the 1990 World Cup Finals in Italy, although he didn't play.

* In 1995 Ludek Miklosko took up British Citizenship, with the intention of staying on in the country, together with his wife and child, once his playing career is over. 
* Known in England by the nickname Ludo, Miklosko spent a number of years playing in goal for Banik Ostrava in Czecoslovakia. In December 1989 he was given a trial by Lou Macari, then manager at West Ham. 
* On 18th February 1990, once he had sorted out his work permit problems, he made his debut for the Hammers in a Second Division game against Swindon. Ironically, just hours before the game, Lou Macari had left his job as manager of West Ham. 
* His transfer to West Ham, finalized on 19th February, cost the club 300,000 pounds. 
* In the summer of 1990 he was called up to the Czech squad for the 1990 World Cup Finals in Italy, although he failed to make an appearance. 
* During his first full season in England, (90-91), with Billy Bonds in charge at West Ham, he equalled Phil Parkes' record of 22 clean sheets. At the same time he was voted as Player of the Year by the Hammers' supporters, on the same day that the club won promotion back to the First Division.
* In the 91-92 season West Ham were relegated. Miklosko missed six games, four of which ended in defeat for the Hammers. Fortunately, one year later the Hammers were back in the Premier League. 
* During the 94-95 season he suffered eye and rib injuries. Even so he played in every league game and, in the final match of the season, against Manchester United (1-1), his extraordinary performances snatched the league title away from the Red Devils, handing it over to Blackburn Rovers. A victory for United  would have taken the championship trophy to Old Trafford.
* Up to the end of the 94-95 season is average of goals against per game was 1.122. 
* For three consecutive seasons (92-93, 93-94 and 94-95) Miklosko played in every one of West Ham's league games. On 1st January 1996 his absence du to a suspension, in a game against Manchester City, put an end to his outstanding run. 
* On 3rd May 1997 he played in his 300th Premier League match, in which West Ham defeated Sheffield Wednesday 5-1.

* Miklosko played in 36 league games as a memeber of the starting line  up during the course of last season with only an injury managing to kept him out on two occasions. He puts together some tremendous performances and was particularly outstanding in the games against Newcastle, Sheffield Wednesday and Liverpool. Towards the end of the season he made his 300th Premier League apeparances. That day West Ham trounced Sheffield Wednesday 5-1.

214.name: Ferdinand
pages: * The Upton Park coaching staff have very high hopes of Rio Ferdinand, a young player who, though still learning the game, seems to have a great future ahead of him. Last season he gave plenty of glimpses of the quality he possesses and earned himself a place in the England under-21 side. Logically, 97-98 should become the season in which he confirms himself as having genuinely arrived on the scene.

* His natural position is at the centre of the defence, although his versatility and positional sense allows him to do a good job at left back or even in midfield. Despite his youth, he shows great maturity out on the park. He has good ball control, good vision, is safe in the air and can be forceful when he needs to be. He has a very bright future ahead of him.
x

* 2 under-21 international appearances for England. 
* An England youth international.

* He is the cousin of Les Ferdinand, Tottenham Hotspur's England international striker.   . 
* After coming through the ranks at West Ham, he turned professional on 27th November 1995. 
* He made his Premier League debut on 5th May 1996 in the last game of the season against Sheffield Wednesday at Upton Park (1-1). 
* On 8th November 1996 he was loaned out to Bournemouth. 
* He scored his first goal for West Ham on 1st February 1997, in a game against Blackburn Rovers at Ewood Park (2-1).

* Last season was a good one for Rio Ferdinand, who went out on loan to %%Bournemouth, where he developed the confidence he needed to make the breakthrough into the Premier League. Under the guidance of Harry Redknapp, he more than demonstrated his versatility, adapting perfectly according to the needs of the team, and showing a maturity beyond his years. His outstanding performances were rewarded with his debut for the England under-21 side.

215.name: Pearce
pages: * Ian Pearce was one of the key men for Ray Harford, ex-manager of Blackburn Rovers. When Harford left the Ewood Park club, Pearce lost his main admired, and, as a result, it surprise nobody when he accepted an interesting offer from West Ham United. Under the guidance of Harry Redknapp, this forceful defender will be trying to get back to his best form, the form he show when he helped Blackburn Rovers to the league title in 1995.

* Ian Pearce is a very versatile footballer, who can do a job at the heart of the defence, as a full back, in midfield and, occasionally, has even played up front where he makes the most of his ability in the air. However, he is at his best when he plays in the centre of the defence, where he can show how effective he is as a man to man marker and demonstrated both his ability in the air as well as his good positional play. Quick once he gets into his stride, he needs to try to improve his change of pace when he is faced with skillful forwards. Young and with reasonable ability on the ball, with time he could go on to become one of the best central defenders in the country.
* League championship winners medal 1995.

* 3 under-21 international appearances for England.
* 10 youth international appearances for England scoring once.

* After coming through the ranks at Chelsea, Ian Pearce made his first team debut on 11th May 1991 against Aston Villa. He had just turned 17 at the time. Shortly after on 1st August he signed professional terms. 
* Ian never really settled down in the side at Stamford Bridge, although he made himself a regular member of the England youth side which finished third in the world youth championships in Australia in 1993. 
* On 4th October 1993 he was transfered to Blackburn Rovers for 300,000 pounds. Kenny Dalglish gave him his debut on 9th November in a league cup game against Shrewsbury Town, with Pearce scoring the side's winning goal in a victory for Blackburn (3-4). He had to wait until 15th January 1993 to make his first league appearance. That came against Sheffield Wednesday at Hillsborough in a game which Rovers won thanks to two goals by Alan Shearer(1-2).
* During the 94-95 season he won a regular place in the side, due, to some extent, to a fantastic marking job he did on Romario in a friendly against Barcelona. At the end of that season Pearce picked up a league championship winners medal. 
* Rovers' manager, Ray Hartford considered him to be the best young central defender in England. Firmly established in the side at Ewood Park, a serious ankle injury, which he suffered in November 1995, kept him out of action for a number of months. 
* On 18th September 1997 he was transfered to West Ham for 2,000,000 pounds.

* Ian Pearce got back into the action after a number of months out trough injury, only to realised that he hadn't fully recovered. As a result he returned to the treatment until March, when he came back into the side for the last seven league games. He did a reasonable job but fell well short of his best form.

216.name: Unsworth
pages: * The Upton Park supporters were happy to see David Unsworth to join West Ham. The ex-Everton player arrived at the club to cover the gap left by Danny Williamson, a player who, in recent times, had failed to make himself a key part of Harry Redknapp's plans. As a result, David Unsworth sets out on a new stage of his career with the same optimistic attittude as always, and one burning ambition: to get back into the England side.

* Unsworth central defender who stands out for his tremendous physical presence. A difficult player to get the better of in the air, he doesn't hesitate to go in hard when he feels he has to. On the other hand, his lack of speed on the turn, often gives him problem against more skillful forwards. A very fair player he never gives a ball up for lost. His strong character makes him a player his teammates luck up to, while he is also capable of passing on his own tremendous will to win. He needs to work harder on the technical side of his game if he wants to get back into the full England side. His youth and his strength are the two main qualities he possesses to help him do excatly that.
* F.A. Cup winners medal 94-95.

* 1 full international appearance for England.
* 7 under-21 international appearances.
* 14 youth international appearances scoring 3 times.

* He played in the World Youth Championships in Australia in 1993, %%   where England reached the semi-finals. 
* An Everton supporter since he was a boy, he made his debut for the club on 25th April 1992 against Tottenham (3-3). That day he came on as a substitute for Andy Hinchcliffe and managed to find the back of the net. At the time he had not yet turned professional. 
* He signed his first professional contract on 25th June 1992. He had been a member of the Everton youth set up since 1987. 
* After six seasons in the first team squad at Everton, on 14th August 1997, he was transfered to West Ham United in a swap deal which saw Danny Williamson move in the opposite direction.

* David Unsworth put together an excellent season for Everton. He played 34 league games and scored five goals, including two penalties. He develop a great understanding with Dave Watson, in spite of the fact that he was forced to play in a number of different positions along the back line. He was, without doubt, one of the best players in the side and got back to the form that won him a place in the national side in 1995.

217.name: Hall
pages: * Following the departure of Marc Rieper and Sloven Bilic, Richard Hall's future at Upton Park suddenly looks a lot brighter. The young defender is one of the candidates to hold down a place at the centre of the defence during the 97-98 season. If he can steer clear of injury and maintain his progress, Richard Hall could become a real pillar at the back for West Ham United in the not too distant future.

* A central defender with a tremendous physical presence, Richard Hall stands out for the way in which he dominates in the air in both penalty areas. He moves forward to get on the end of corners and free kicks, where his power and heading ability allow him to find the back of the net with some regularity. A good marker, strong and powerful he does a hard, effective job at the back. However, he needs to work on his touch on the ball in order to more effectively set up attacks from the back. Fully aware of his technical weaknesses, he keeps things as simple as possible when he finds himself in tight situations.
x
* 11 under-21 international appearances for England, scoring twice.

* In June 1987 Richard Hall joined his home town club, Ipswich Town, as a schoolboy. In July 1988 he moved on to become a trainee with Scunthorpe %% United. While still a youth team player he made his league debut on 26th December 1989 against Grimsby at Glanford Park. 
* A professional since 20th March 1990, he was a regular member of the side at Scunthorpe during the 90-91 season, although he didn't end the campaign at the club, as a result of being transfered on 13th February 1991 to Southampton for 200,000 pounds. That same week Neil Cox, another young Irons prospect, was transferd to Aston Villa. 
* He made his debut for the Saints in the last game of the 90-91 season, against Wimbledon, coming on in place of Neil Ruddock. 
* During the 91-92 season Hall found the back of the net during his first full starting appearance at the heart of the defence. In February, in a fifth round F.A. Cup tie against Bolton Wanderers, he scored twice with two identical headers, in the space of just four minutes. At the end of the season he was called up to the England under-21 side for the prestigious international Tournament in Toulon, France. 
* During the 93-94 season he suffered a serious injury which kept him out of the game for several months. 
* In July 1996 he was transfered to West Ham United for 1,400,000 pounds.
* He was injured in a pre-season friendly, preventing him from making his debut for the Hammers until 9th April 1997, in a home game against Middlesbrough (0-0).

* Richard Hall didn't have much luck during his first season with West Ham. He was seriously injured in a pre-season fiendly, and was unable to get back into action until April. He was a member of the starting line up in the last seven league games of the season.

218.name: Potts
pages:
* Steve Potts has dedicated the whole of his career to West Ham United. His genuine Hammers' spirit is a real example to all the young players in the junior teams at Upton Park. In recent times, the arrival at the club of others players has relegated him the role of substitute. However Steve always seems to find a way into Harry Redknapp's side. His secret consists of training hard, working hard and giving 100% out on the park. 
* Before all else, Steve Potts is a West Ham United supporter, and, it would surprise nobody if he remained at the club in some capacity once his playing days where over. Until that moment comes, he will carry on fighting to force his way into the manager's plans.

* Despite his slight physical stature, Steve Potts does an excellent job at the heart of the defence. His consistency, bravery and outstanding sense of anticipation, allows him to calmly play his way out of tight situations. Quick to cover across the back and decisive in the tackle, he is a genuine specialist in the art of winning possession and can also operate in midfield as well as at right back. In whatever position he plays he shows his defensive approach to the game, very rarely making an attacking contribution. In fact during the course of his now long professional career he has scored just one goal.
x
* 20 full international appearances for England.

* Born in the United States, when he was still a young boy his family settled down in Dagenham, Essex. 
* As a youth and schoolboy international for England, he is prevented from playing in the colours of the United States national side. 
* He began playing football with Barking and went on to play for the London boys under-16's side before joining the youth set up at West Ham United.
* Captain of the Hammers youth side, he turn professional on 11th May 1984. His first team debut came on 1st January 1985 against Queens Park Rangers at Upton Park. 
* His second opportunity came during the 85-86 season, when he came on as a substitute in place of Steve Walford in a 1-0 victory over Ipswich Town. However, for two years he had to settle for playing for the reserves.
* An injury to Ray Stewart allowed him to play a few games at right back under Lou Macari. However, when Billy Bonds took over at Upton Park he gave the right back spot to Tim Breacker. Later, injuries to Alvin Martin and Tony Gayle saw Bonds obliged to put in back in the side. 
* On 6th October 1990 he scored the only goal of his career. A long shot from Potts beat the Hull City goalkeeper at Upton Park. West Ham won the game 7-1. 
* As captain of the side, he played in every game during the 94-95 season. The supporters voted him Hammer of the year. 
* He is currently the longest serving player at West Ham. At the end of the 96-97 season he renewed his contract until the year 2000.

* He began the season on the substitute's bench, with Rieper and Bilic enjoying the full backing of manager Harry Redknapp at the heart of the defence. However, an injury to Tim Breacker in the second half of the  season allowed him to come back into the side at right back, a position where he gave a satisfactory performance.
