219.name: Dicks
pages: * Julian Dicks is not only captain of West Ham, but also represents  the heart and soul of the side. Now that criticism of his occasionally excessively aggressive style of play seems to have subsided, followers of the game in England are beginning to appreciated his ability. In fact, recently many have campaigned for his inclusion in Glenn Hoddle's England side. At the end of the day, it is certainly difficult to find full backs that possess Julian Dicks' ability to find the back of the net.

* A hardrunning left back, very often his aggressive and even dirty approach to the game has overshadowed his ability as a footballer. Very much a left footed player, he stands out for his strength and fighting spirit. In defence he goes about his work with tremendous passion, fighting for every ball and even intimidating opponents. Quick and mobile, he is decisive when he covers across the back, is consistent in the air and never shirks a physical challenge, an aspect of the game in which he is a genuine specialist.
* A effective defender, Julian Dicks' main quality is his ability to lead the side, something which is clearly evident when he moves forward to join the attack. Good in the air, he is an accurate passer of the  ball and has a tremendously powerful shot with his left foot. A free kick and penalty specialist, his goalscoring record is far superior to the majority of defenders.
x

* 2 "B" international appearances for England.
* 4 under-21 international appearances.

* Known by the nickname "Terminator" due to his aggressive approach out on the park, Julian Dicks is one of the most popular players in the history of West Ham United. 
* Also famous for his problems with referees, it is no coincidence that he has one of the worst disciplinary records in the Premier League. However, those who know him describe him as a calm, pleasent family man. 
* During the 92-93 season he was sent off three times and missed thirteen league games due to suspension, and, as a result, was actually on the verge of giving the game up. 
* After coming through the youth ranks at Birmingham City, he made his first team debut on 24th August 1985 against Chelsea. However, he didn't turn professional until 12th April 1986. With Gary Pendrey and Ron Saunders in charge, the young Julian Dicks generally played on the left hand side of the midfield. 
* On 25th March 1988 he was transfered to West Ham for 300,000 pounds, at the personal request of manager John Lyall. On 2nd April of that same year, he made his debut for the Hammers in a game against Sheffield Wednesday.
* In October 1990 he suffered a serious injury to the ligaments in his left knee. After a long hard battle, he managed to make his comeback fourteen months later. He quickly got back to some tremendous form, taking the captaincy of the side from Ian Bishop, and managing to win a call up from Graham Taylor to play two games for the England "B" side. 
* In 1992 he signed a new contract with West Ham for four years. However, on 17th September 1993 he was transfered to Liverpool in exchange for Mike Marsh, David Burrows and 1,500,000 pounds.
* After a year at Anfield, Dicks returned to West Ham on 20th October 1994. His valuation in the transfer market had dropped to 1,000,000 pounds. Two days later the Hammers were at home against Southampton at Upton Park. When Julian Dicks ran out onto the pitch, he was given an emotional ovation by the West Ham supporters. 
* In September 1995 Julian Dicks was sent off at Highbury. However, he wasn't shown another yellow card for the next twenty two games. At the  end of the 95-96 season he was voted Hammer of the year by the club's supporters, an honour he received again at the end of the 96-97 season.

* Julian Dicks was the best left back in England during the course of last season. As a result, it was no surprise when he was named Hammer of the year at the end of the campaign. Dicks made himself West Ham's second top scorer with six goals (five penalties). That record takes on even more significance when it is remembered that all but one of those goals clinched either a victory or a draw for the Upton Park club. He was especially outstanding in the game against Tottenham in February in which he scored twice to help West Ham win the game 4-3. Unfortunately  an injury prevented him from playing in the final weeks of the season.

220.name: Breacker
pages: * Tim Breacker has been dogged by bad luck in the last few seasons.  This brave right back has suffered numerous injuries which have prevented him from getting the continuity he needs in order to find his best form. During the 97-98 season Tim will be hoping that he can stay out of the treatment room, and show Harry Redknapp that he can have full confidence in him to help strengthen the West Ham defence.

* A very attack minded right back, Tim Breacker stands out for his power and physical strength, although he shows a few technical weaknesses when he moves forward to join the attack. A very quick player, he defends with plenty of energy, and wins plenty of possession due to his tremendous sense of anticipation. He likes to join in with the attack and puts some good long balls through to the forward line. Although he has a good shot with his right foot, he seldom makes uses of it and only very rarely finds the back of the net.
* League Cup winners medal 1988.
* 2 under-21 international appearances for England. He made his debut on 9th April 1996 against Italy in Pisa.

* He joined Luton Town as a schoolboy and played his way through all the ranks at the club before turning professional on 15th May 1983. He made his first team debut on 31st March 1984 against Ipswich Town. 
* An England under-21 international on two occasions, curiously, in both games Italy provided the opposition. 
* In 1988 he played in the League Cup final in which Luton beat Arsenal. One year later Luton reached the final again, after beating West Ham in the semi-finals, only to lose against Nottingham Forest. 
* On 12th October 1990 he was transfered to West Ham for 600,000 pounds, becoming the first signing of Billy Bonds spell in charge. He made his debut for the Hammers that same month, as s substitute in a game against Swindon Town. In his first campaign at Upton Park the club won promotion back to the top flight. 
* In December 1991 he was sent off for the first time in his career after being shown two yellow cards in a game against Everton.
* During the course of his career he has been beaten three times in the F.A. Cup semi-finals. Twice for Luton, against Everton (1985) and Wimbledon (1988); and once more with West Ham at the hands of Nottingham Forest (1991).
* In October 1994 he suffered a cartilage operation which forced him to miss a number of games. One year later he had to undergo a similar operation.

* Injuries prevented Tim Breacker from playing regularly throughout the season. Even so he puts together some superb performances amongst which stands out the marking job he did on David Ginola while the Frenchman was playing for Newcastle. Unfortunately, his season was brought to an early end, following an injury he suffered during West Ham's visit to Coventry.

221.name: Lampard
pages: * Frank Lampard junior is one of the brightest young prospects at Upton Park. At just 19 years of age he already knows what it is like to play in the Premier League. He has outstanding ability but needs time to put the finishing touches to the quality he possesses. Harry Redknapp has full confidence in his potential. Frank Lampard seems to be on the way to do even better than his father, who, as a matter of fact, is currently %%  second in command at West Ham.

* A very young midfielder, he stands out for his vision, control and accurate passing ability, qualities which make him a real prospect for the future. All he seems to need his time to develop his game and acquire maturity and experience.
x
* An England youth international.

* He is the son of Frank Lampard, currently assistant manager at Upton Park, and an ex-West Ham player. 
* After coming through the youth ranks at Upton Park, he turn professional on 1st July 1995. 
* On 6th October 1995 he went out on loan to Swansea City, where he played in nine league games scoring once. 
* He made his Premier League debut for West Ham on 31st January 1996, in a victory over Coventry City at Upton Park (3-2). 
* He formed part of the West Ham youth team that reached the 1996 F.A. youth cup final . 
* In March 1997 h suffered broken leg during a league game against Aston Villa.

* He was a member of the starting line up in the first league game of the season, although from that point on he alternated between the reserve side and sporadic appearances in the first team. Unfortunately, he broken leg in the visit to Aston Villa in March, an injury which forced him out for the rest of the season.

222.name: Impey
pages: * Andy Impey returned to the Premier League under the guidance of Harry Redknapp. The West Ham manager showed full confidence in the player's ability to bring extra strength to the midfield. With Impey, the Hammers have taken on a player who is commited, practical, experienced and, above   all, good value for money. Although something of an inconsistent player, he always gives 100% and is sure not to let anyone down.

* Andrew Impey is a midfielder with tremendous strength and pace, who generally operates down the right hand side, although he can also do a good job down the opposite flank. Enthusiastic and hard working, he makes up for his technical weaknesses with his fighting spirit and tremendous work rate, all of which makes him a valuable type of player for any side. Quick with the ball at his feet, he has good passing ability, and tries to get defenders off balance in order to create space to allow him to get dangerous crosses over into the opposition's penalty area.
x
* 1 Under-21 international appearance for England. He made his debut on 17th November 1992 against Turkey.

* QPR signed him from amateur club Yeading, for 35,000 pounds in June 1990. He made his league debut on 11th January 1992 against Coventry City. His first league goal, on 26th August 1992, clinched a victory for Rangers over the same club he made his debut against, Coventry City. 
* He was chosen as Player of the Year for the 94-95 season by the QPR supporters. 
* In April 1995 he was called up to the England squad by Terry Venables.
* On 26th September 1997 he was transfered to West Ham United for 1,200,000 pounds. Impey signed a four year contract with the Upton Park club.

* Last season wasn't a good one for Andy Impey. Injuries and suspensions prevented him from getting the continuity he needed to help him find his best form. Only towards the end of the season did he begin to look like the player of previous seasons. However, weeks earlier QPR had already lost all hope of getting back into the top flight.

223.name: Lomas
pages: * West Ham's signing of Steve Lomas in March 1997, was one of the surprises of last season. Lomas was a key member of the side at Manchester City, a club expecting to get quickly back into the Premier League. However, the Northern Ireland international prefered to take the quickest route back to the top flight, and moved on to West Ham where he quickly forced his way into manager Harry Redknapp's plans. Everything seems to suggest that he will be a regular member of the side throughout the 97-98 season.

* Lomas is a midfield player who is happier in a defensive role than when he is asked to make an attacking contribution. An untiring worker, he can play in a number of different positions; either just in front of the defence or anywhere in the midfield. Basically right footed, he has good technique which allows him to distribute the ball intelligently and efficently, preferably over short distance.
x

* 22 full international appearances for Northern Ireland, scoring once. He made his debut on 23rd March 1994 against Romania in Belfast. 
* 1 "B" international appearance. 
* A youth and schoolboy international.

* After coming through the youth ranks at Manchester City, he signed  professional in January 1991. 
* He made his first team debut in the league on 25th September 1993, against Sheffield United and scored his first goal on 8th October 1994, in a game against Nottingham Forest. 
* In 1996 he was a member of the Manchester City side that was relegated to the First Division. 
* Although he received an interesting offer from Wimbledon, he began the 96-97 season with City. But, surprisingly, he was transfered to West Ham on 26th March 1997 for 1,600,000 pounds. 
* He made his debut for the Hammers on 9th April 1997 in a game against Middlesbrough at Upton Park (0-0).

* He was a regular member of the side for each of the managers that took charge at Manchester City during the course of last season, something of an achievement in itself. He was sent off in the game against Reading, although, once he had completed his suspension he came back to make himself one of the best players in the side. Surprising, he was transfered to West Ham in March, where he was a regular member of the starting line up in the last few weeks of the Premier League season.

224.name: Berkovic
pages: * The first time that Graeme Souness saw him play, Eyal Berkovic was just 17 years old. Despite his youth the Scottish manager recognised that the slightly built young player, who had shown glimpses of tremendous quality, was well capable of going on to play in English football. Seven years later Souness signed him for Southampton in exchange for 1,000,000 pounds his breakthrough into the Premier League was such a surprise that it didn't take long for plenty of offers to come his way. Finally it was West Ham who won the battle for his signature, making him Harry Redknapp's side's most expensive signing for the 97-98 season.

* Eyal Berkovic is very much an attack minded midfielder. Despite his fragile appearance, which brought him his fair share of criticism in the early stages of his career, he does a tremendous job on the right hand side of the midfield. Skillful when he has the ball at his feet, he is a specialist at going past opposing defenders to reach the byline from where he puts over dangerous crosses into the heart of the penalty area. An occasional goalscorer, he has a good shot in his right foot which he doesn't need to be asked twice to use. However, his contribution to games is not always as effective as it is spectacular.

* Israeli League Championship winners medal 94.
* Israeli Cup winners medals 93 and 95.
* Voted Israeli Player of the Year 1994.
* 43 full international appearances for Israel.

* Born in Haifa, Eyal Berkovic made a name for himself with one of his home town clubs Maccabi Haifa. 
* After winning a cup winners medal in 1993, it was in the 93-94 season when he proved himself to be one of the best players in Israel. During  that season he won a championship winners medal, after playing in every league game, and, to crown a magnificent campaign, he was also voted as Israel's Player of the Year. The season was rounded off for Berkovic when he scored the goal that earned a draw for Israel against France in the Parque des Princes (2-2). 
* In 1995 he was a member of the starting line up in the cup final in which Maccabi Haifa beat arch enemies Hapoel Haifa, 2-0. 
* On 9th October 1996 he was transfered to Southampton for 1,000,000 pounds. He made his Premier League debut on 13th of that same month in an away game at Coventry (1-1). Berkovic came on for Gordon Watson in the 59th minute.
* On 26th October 1996 he scored his first two goals in a Southampton shirt against Manchester United at The Dell. The Saints beat the Old Trafford club by a resounding 6-3. 
* On 3rd June 1997 he was trasfered to West Ham for 1,750,000 pounds.

* He arrived at Southampton in October, under the guidance of Graeme Souness, and made a tremendous impression on his debut. His vision, the accuracy of his passing and his attitude out on the park made him one of the more pleasent surprises of last season, up to the point of competing on an equal footing for a place in the Saints' starting line up with Matt Le Tissier himself.

225.name: Lazaridis
pages: * Stan Lazaridis' signing for West Ham in September 1995 was a real surprise. The Australian international midfielder was a complete unknown in Europe, although the Upton Park coaching staff had received good reports about him during the course of the Hammers' tour of Australia. In his first season in England he didn't have too much luck, although last season, he showed glimpses of the quality he possesses. He will be hoping that, during the 97-98 season, Harry Redknapp gives him more opportunities to show what he can do.

* A hard working midfielder, he does a good job down the left hand side. Left footed, quick and consistent, he is not a match winning footballer, but, given his youth, he has plenty of time to improve the technical side of his game.
x
* 9 full international appearances for Australia.

* He came through the ranks of Australina club West Adeleide. Stan Lazaridis was transfered to West Ham United on 8th September 1995 for 300,000 pounds.
* He made his debut on 11th September of that same year in a defeat against Chelsea (1-3) at Upton Park. Lazaridis came on for Ian Bishop in the 71st minute. 
* In February 1996 he suffered a broken ankle dueing the course of a Cup tie against Grimsby Town. 
* He scored his first goal in England on 18th March 1997, against Wimbledon at Selhurst Park (1-1).

* Slowly but surely, he began to obtain the experience needed to be able to guarantee a good level of performances in the Premier League. He played in 22 league games, starting in 13. He did a satisfactory job, which he  rounded off with an excellent goal against Wimbledon in March, a goal which won a valuable point for West Ham.

226.name: Moncur
pages: * John Moncur is one of the classiest players in the Hammers' squad. He is also one of the most experienced, and, as a result has an ever increasing influence over the other players at the club. During the 97-98 season, he will, once again, alongside Ian Bishop, be responsible for orchestrating things in midfield for West Ham and making sure that the strikers get the quality services they need. West Ham will also need John Moncur, if they want to improve on last season.

* A talented midfielder blessed with tremendous passing ability, John Moncur is a very dangerous player when he gets the ball at his feet. He possesses tremendous vision and shows good intelligence when he is around the edge of the opposition penalty area. He knows how to dictate the pace of the game, pull the strings in midfield and is always available for his teammates to give the ball to. However, without doubt, his greatest asset is his  ability to make spectacular runs forward, with the ball apparently tied to his feet, going past defenders and opening up gaps for the strikers.
x
* 1 Youth international appearance for England.

* Before arriving at Tottenham as an apprentice in 1983, John Moncur had already stood out with his performances for non-league Harlow. 
* A professional since 22nd August 1984, his loan spell at Doncaster Rovers, beginning on 25th September 1986, allowed him to make his league debut two days later against York City. 
* Following that original spell out on loan, he set off on a genuine  pilgrimage from one team to another being loaned out by Spurs to Cambridge United (March 1987), Portsmouth (March 1989), Brentford (October 1989) and Ipswich Town (October 1991). 
* On 30th March 1992 he was transfered to Swindon Town for 80,000  pounds. with Glenn Hoddle as manager of the club he became an automatic first team choice and scored a vital goal in a play off game against Leicester City. Swindon won 4-3, clinching promotion to the First Division. 
* He has been a West Ham player since 24th June 1994. Although he was chased by a number of clubs, the fact that his father works in the offices at Upton Park finally swayed his decision in West Ham's favour. The Hammers paid out 900,000 pounds to take him to Upton Park. 
* His Hammers' debut came on 27th August 1994 in an away game against Norwich, which West Ham lost 1-0. On 2nd October of that same year he scored his first goal in a West Ham shirt against Chelsea.

* John Moncur found his best form towards the end of the season, proving to be a tremendous boost to West Ham, who, at the time were in some trouble. The veteran midfielder suffered several injuries at the beginning of the season, which saw him take longer than usual to get into his stride; however, he went on to complete his best season yet at Upton Park. He scored two goals in the league, both of those coming against Leicester. Those two goals earned six points for West Ham.

227.name: Abou
pages: * Samassi Abou's transfer was one of the main objectives of Peter Storie, the director of signings at West Ham.  His incorporation is a noticeable reinforcement for the "Hammers"' attack.  Everything seems to indicate that the under-21 French international will find a place in the team managed by Harry Redknapp.

* A fast, skilful forward, he usually plays out on the right of the attack, although he will drift over to the left at times.  He can also operate as a link-man between the forwards and the midfield, where he can pop up by surprise in the vacant spaces.  A good passer, he still doesn't resolve as well as he should in front of goal.
x
* Under-21 international for France.

* He started his sporting career in 1991 in the ranks of Martigues, a Second Division team at the time.
* In the summer of 1992 he is transferred to Lyon.  He makes his debut in the First Division on the 15th of August of this same year, with a 0-2 defeat at the hands of Nantes.
* He scored his first goal for Lyon on the 13th of December 1992 in an away game against Lens (0-3).
* On the 28th of October 1997 he was transferred to West Ham for £400,000.

* In his first season at Cannes, Abou didn't perform as well as was expected. In fact, he only scored 4 goals in the whole of the season, too small a tally.  Cannes finished the season in sixteenth spot.

228.name: Sinclair
pages: * Now one of the top names in Englsih football, Trevor Sinclair was the subject of many rumours regarding million pound offers from Tottenham Hotspur, amongst others, but, both he, as well as QPR rejected any approaches that were made. However, he was transfered to West Ham on the 29th of January 1998 for 2 million pounds.

* With all the qualities he needs to go on to become a genuine star, Sinclair basically plays as a left winger, despite being right footed, although he has also operated as both a right winger and as an out and out striker. A very quick player, he has tremendous acceleration, has a direct approach to the game and is constantly looking to take on opposing defenders with his pace and dribbling ability. In recent seasons he has managed to improve the quality of his crossing, managing to iron out a few minor faults in that aspect of his game. He has good vision and is an unselfish player when it comes to playing the ball off to his teammates  or whenever a colleague is in a better position than he is to have a shot on goal.
* Chosen in the First Division's ideal sie for the season 96-97.
* An England youth international he has also played for the under-21 side, making his debut  on 12th October 1993 against Holland.

* After graduating from the F.A. School of Excellence, Sinclair moved on to sign for Blackpool.
* He came through the youth ranks at Blackpool and eventually signed professional in August 1990. He made his league debut on 19th August 1989 against Wigan Athletic, and scored his first league goal on 10th November 1990 against Aldershot.
* He was transfered to QPR in August 1993 for £600,000. He made his debut on 18th August 1993 against Liverpool and scored his first goal for his new club on 1st September 1993 against  Sheffield United.
* He has been called up on a couple of occasions to the full England squad.  
* With the option of choosing between Blackburn Rovers and QPR,  Sinclair finally decided to join the London club.

* Despite the continual rumours surrounding his possible transfer to a Premier League club, Sinclair had a tremendous season, which was reflected by his inclusion in the First Division's ideal team. Full of strength and ability his contribution to QPR'S cause was greater than ever, putting together some outstanding performances for the club. In total, he played in 39 games scoring 3 times.

229.name: Hartson
pages: * John Hartson is the most expensive signing in West Ham's history. He made his debut for the Hammers on the same day as Paul Kitson in a game in which both players scored their first goals for the club. Together they look set to form a striking partnership in Harry Redknapp's during the course of the 97-98 season. With these two players up front, West Ham will be out to make sure that they are not struggling near the foot of the table, and, if luck is on their side, will be trying to get involved in the battle for a U.E.F.A. Cup place. To achieve that aim, they will need John Hartson to be regularly on target.

* An opportunist, goalscoring striker, John Hartson stands out for his effectiveness in the air, and his ability to get in first time efforts on goal. A player of great physical presence, he is better on the ball than he might at first appear to be. He holds the ball up well, waiting fo his teammates to come through in support from midfield. A classic striker, strong and brave, the Welshman is blessed with a natural ability to sniff out a goalscoring chance, although he lacks the quality to make a significant contribution to the side's approach play.
* European Cup Winners Cup runners up medal 95.

* 11 full international appearances for Wales, scoring once.
* 7 under-21 international appearances.

* John Hartson's move to Arsenal in January 1995 set a new record. The fee of 2,500,000 was the highest ever paid in Britain for a player under 20 years of age. 
* Before joining Arsenal, Hartson came through the ranks at Luton Town, where he turned professional on 19th December 1992. He made his debut in the league on 28th August 1993, against Nottingham Forest.
* He moved to Arsenal on 13th January 1995. That same day the club also signed Chris Kiwomya from Ipswich Town. The Gunners urgently needed a striker to cover for the injured Alan Smith, and, as a consequence, the following day Hartson made his debut against Everton at Highbury (1-1). He managed to score his first goal for the club in his second game, away at Coventry (0-1).
* Having settle down in the side at Arsenal, he played as a member of the starting line up in the 1995 European Cup Winners Cup final against Zaragoza and scored the goal that took the game into extra-time. However, in the extra period, Nayim's famous goal from the halfway line gave the trophy to the Spanish side. 
* He was transfered to West Ham on 14th February 1997 for 5,000,000 pounds, making him the most expensive player in the history of the club. He made his Hammers' debut on 15th February of that same year, in an away game  against Derby County (0-1). Paul Kitson also made his debut in that same match.
* On 24th February 1997 he scored his first goal for West Ham, against Tottenham Hotspur at Upton Park (4-3).

* He began the season as a first team regular at Arsenal, however manager Arsene Wenger was happy to let him move on to West Ham for a record fee. Hartson and Paul Kitson proved to be a revelation up front for the Hammers. Hartson scored five goals in the battle to avoid relegation, and also maintained his place as a regular in the full Welsh international side.

230.name: Kitson
pages: * Paul Kitson is a classic centre forward, powerful and good in the air. He arrived at Newcastle three months before Andy Cole left for Manchester United. However, despite the gap which Cole left, Kitson had neither the luck the opportunities to genuinely establish himself in the side. Alan Shearer's arrival at Saint James' Park kept the doors to the first team even more firmly closed, although it did help to open up the one that eventually saw him moving on to Upton Park. In just four months with West Ham, he made himself the club's top scorer. A fact which will no doubt work in his favour during the 97-98 season.

* A strong forward, he is constantly battling away with opposing defenders, although he is lacking in technical ability. Kitson's main strength is  his heading ability, which is how he scores the majority of his goals. A very hard working player, he keeps up a tremendous work rate throughout the ninety minutes, constantly making life very uncomfortable for rival defenders, never giving them a moments respite. A player with an eye for a goalscoring chance, he has the knack of finding space inside the penalty area, to allow him to get in shots on goal from apparently impossible positions. However, his limited contribution to the side's approach work, prevents him from playing a more significant role in the team's general pattern of play. Nevertheless, what nobody can deny, is the tremendous amount of effort he puts in to every game.
x

* 1 "B" international appearance for England.
* 7 under-21 international appearances for England, scoring three times.
* 4 youth international appearances.

* After coming through the ranks at Leicester City, he signed professional on 15th December 1988. He made his league debut on 13th September 1989, in a game against West Bromwich Albion. 
* On 11th March 1992 he was transfered to Derby County for 1,300,000 pounds.
* He began the 94-95 season with Derby County, but, on 24th September 1994 he was transfered to Newcastle United for 2,250,000 pounds. He made his debut on 12th October against Aston Villa at Villa Park, in a game which the Magpies won 0-2. In his first season at St. James' Park, he scored a hat trick in a cup replay against Swansea, although an injury to ligaments in his ankle, as well as a neck injury, limited his contribution. 
* On 7th February 1997 he was transfered to West Ham United for 2,300,000 pounds. He made his debut for the Hammers on 15th February of that same year in an away game at Derby County (0-1). 
* On 24th February 1997, he scored his first goal for West Ham against Tottenham Hotspur at Upton Park (4-3).

* Unable to break into the side at Newcastle due to the presence of strikers of the quality of Asprilla, Ferdinand and Shearer, Paul Kitson was transfered, in February, to West Ham. It was a deal which was heavily criticised in some quarters, due to the size of the fee involved. Nevertheless, Kitson managed to silence the critics by scoring goals. He became an automatic choice in the side and ended the season as West Ham's top scorer with 8 goals including a hat trick against Sheffield Wednesday.

231.name: De Goey
pages: * At the end of last season Ed De Goey could choose between a bundle of clubs who were fighting to acquire his services.  He finally opted for Chelsea.  Ruud Gullit had a lot to do with this decision.  The Chelsea manager persuaded the Dutch keeper to try his luck in the Premier League.  With this background, everything seems to indicate that De Goey will be the first choice keeper for the Blues during the 97-98 season. It looks as if he will have an impeccable sporting career at Chelsea and, above all, the faith the Gullit has placed in him.

* Ed De Goey is a veteran keeper with a broad international experience.  His imposing stature makes him a guarantee in the air, where he dominates with a lot of authority.  He is also an agile goalie, with good reflexes who moves quickly, helped by his slim build.  He always gives the impression of security and calmness and transmits this to his team-mates.  A complete keeper, the passage of time has just made him better.

* Dutch League Champion 93. 
* Dutch Cup Champion 91, 92, 94 and 95.

* 29 full international appearances for Holland.  He made his debut on the 16th of December 1992 in a game against Turkey played in Istanbul.  The Dutch team won 1-3. 
* He was the first choice keeper for Holland in the '94 United States World Cup for the five games played by his team. 
* Present in the '96 England European Cup, he didn't play a single minute.
* 17 times under-21 international.

* He started his career at Sparta Rotterdam in the 85-86 season. 
* In 1990 he was transferred to Feyenoord, the most important club in Rotterdam and the eternal rival of Sparta. 
* In seven seasons at Feyenoord he only missed eight games: six due to suspension and two due to injury. 
* After several years as the first choice keeper in the national team, he lost his place in 1995 to the Ajax goalie, Van der Saar. 
* At the end of the 96-97 season he receives offers for Dutch and Spanish clubs, but Ruud Gullit, who he had played with in the Dutch team, convinced him to sign for Chelsea.  He was transferred to the Stamford Bridge club on the 11th of June 1997 for £2,225,000. 
* He is, at 1.97 m, the tallest player in the history of Chelsea.

* For the seventh year running Ed De Goey was the first choice keeper at Feyenoord during last season.  The good performance of the international goalie was one of the keys to the good run the team had in the league, fighting to the bitter end with PSV Eindhoven for the title.  In the end Feyenoord managed to classify for the 97-98 edition of the Champions League.

232.name: Hitchcock
pages: * The presence in the Chelsea squad of Frode Grodas and, above all, of Ed De Goey, makes Kevin Hitchcock's inclusion in the team hard.  The veteran keeper starts off at a disadvantage in the fight between the team's keepers, which also include Dimitri Kharine.  However, Kevin is used to waiting and has made patience one of his main virtues.  In the 97-98 season he will continue to work to make sure that he is in good condition when Ruud Gullit calls on him.  Hitchcock knows, after all, the opportunities may arrive sooner or later, but they always arrive.

* Kevin Hitchcock is a goalie who is characterised mainly by his great reflexes.  Quick and agile, he is able to make extraordinary stops and usually is good in a one-on-one, where he often makes his experience count. In the games where he is particularly inspired he infects the rest of the team with his competitive spirit and constantly orders the defence around. A specialist penalty stopper, his weak point is the aerial game, where he doesn't always judge the distances well.
* FA Cup Champion 97.
x

* Because of the coincidence of his surname with that of the famous director of suspense movies, Kevin Hitchcock has had to put up with all the easy jokes during the course of his career.  "Hitchcock Thriller" is a normal critically reference to his game, whether it be positive or negative. 
* Originally from the modest team Barking, he arrives at Nottingham Forest on the 4th of August 1983 in exchange for £15,000, although he never gets to play for this team. 
* On the 1st of February 1984 he is transferred to Mansfield Town for £140,000.  He made his debut on the 10th of March of this same year in a game against Colchester. 
* After five seasons in the Fourth Division, he is transferred to Chelsea on the 25th March 1988 for £250,000.  At the Stamford Bridge club he doesn't have much chance to show his qualities and his only appearances are to cover for an injury to, first of all, Dave Beasant, and then Dmitri Kharine.
* On the 28th of December 1990 he was loaned to Northampton Town, the club that was playing in the Fourth Division at the time. 
* The injury to Kharine in the 94-95 season allows him to play in four Cup Winners Cup games. 
* In the 96-97 season another injury to Kharine once again lets him into the team.  But in this same season he suffers two different injuries; firstly to his elbow and then to his shoulder.  Curiously, both times the opponents were Manchester United.  He was operated on to treat his shoulder, leaving the place to Grodas.

* He started the season as the understudy to Dimitri Kharine, but when this keeper was injured at Hillsborough he was the guy who stepped into the Russian's shoes.  Hitchcock produced some good performances for the following seven games, and made a decisive contribution to Chelsea's win at Old Trafford, where Manchester United had gone a long time without loosing a league game.  Unfortunately for him, in this same game he injured his elbow, bringing about the Premier League debut of the Norwegian Grodas. He reappeared in February, but another injury, this time to his shoulder, and also, strangely enough, against Manchester United.  Kevin had to go to the operating theatre and left the place open to Grodas until the end of the season.

233.name: Kharine
pages: * Dmitri Kharine has not had much luck in the last two seasons, both marked by serious injuries.  Last season he had a crossed-ligament injury to his knee, an injury whose recovery time spread to months and months.  When he manages to recover completely he faces a new challenge: to get back in the Chelsea goal.  An almost impossible task if we take into account the fact that in the fight for a place he has ahead of him not only Hitchcock, but also international keepers such as Grodas and De Goey.

* A keeper with a plenty of personality and a strong temperament, he exercises an energetic dominance over the defence, ordering them about vehemently.  Kharine is noted for his agility and excellent reflexes, allowing him to make spectacular stops, especially in a one-on-one and in the penalty kicks.What's more, he is good with the ball at his feet, an important quality in a modern keeper. 
* On the other hand, he is guilty of too much irregularity and makes some mistakes unthinkable in a goalkeeper of prestige.  Many of his mistakes are a result of the great confidence that he has in his abilities, which leads him to take more risks than necessary.  Despite this, Kharine is a good goalie, one of the best in the Premier League.

* A League title with CSKA Moscow. 
* Gold medal in the 88 Olympic Games in Seoul.

* 34 full international appearances for Russia.  He made his debut in the 3-0 win over Hungary, the game played on the 28th of April 1993 in Moscow.
* Present in the 94 United States World Cup, he plays two games, against Brazil and Sweden, both ending in defeat for Russia. 
* Called up for 96 England European Championship, he only plays one game, against Germany.  Russia loose 0-3. 
* Kharine also made 15 international appearances for the now extinct Soviet Union and for the CIS (Community of Independent States).  His debut took place on the 21st of November 1988 in a friendly against Syria played in Damascus.  The USSR won 0-2. 
* Present in the Sweden 92 European Championship with the CSI, he played three games, against Germany, Holland and Scotland. 
* An Olympic international with the Soviet Union, he won a gold medal in the 88 Seoul games, after beating Brazil in the final.

* When Dmitri Kharine made his debut in the Soviet First Division aged just 17, many considered him to be the successor to the mythical goalie Lev Yashin.  The year was 1984 and he was playing in Torpedo Moscow. 
* In 1988 he is transferred to Dynamo Moscow and in 1991 he moves to CSKA, the club which wins the League championship and leading to international recognition for him. 
* On the 22nd of September 1992 he is transferred to Chelsea for £200,000. He makes his debut in the Premier League on the 27th of January 1993 in a game against QPR. 
* His strong character causes him a problem or too.  Once, he criticised his team-mates at Chelsea, saying that they weren't technically good enough to play in a big club.  Taken out of the team temporarily, he was allowed back in when he had apologised. 
* In January 1996 he suffered an injury to his shoulder in a Cup game against Newcastle played at Stamford Bridge which had a negative influence on his season.  Up until then he had been secure in the Chelsea goal and enjoyed the complete confidence of the manager at the time, Glenn Hoddle. 
* On the 7th of September 1996, in a League game against Sheffield Wednesday played at Hillsborough, he damages his crossed ligaments in his knee, one of the most serious injuries for a footballer.  Until then he had offered some extraordinary performances under the orders of Ruud Gullit. 
* He has been a full international with three different teams: the former Soviet Union, the CIS and Russia, where he alternates in goal with Cherchesov.

* He started the season on impressive form.  Undisputed first choice in Ruud Gullit's plans, he kept clean sheets for the first three games.  In the fifth Chelsea were playing at Hillsborough against Sheffield Wednesday. Bad luck crossed the path of the Russian keeper, who suffered damage to his crossed knee ligaments, a very serious injury that kept him out for the rest of the season.

234.name: Babayaro
pages: * With Celestine Babayaro's signing Chelsea have acquired one of the players who has made most impact in Europe in recent times.  He is only 19 and he has already been playing four years in high level competition.  A Nigerian international, his progress was followed by some of the most important clubs in Italy and Spain, but he finally signed for Chelsea for the next five years.  He has an impressive honours list for a player so young, but as he himself says "in Africa you are a man when you are 18".  Ruud Gullit has unbounded faith in his capabilities, almost as much as the expectation that his signing has aroused in England.  With Babayaro at the head the youth is coming through at Stamford Bridge.

* He usually plays at left back, although the amount of ground he covers allows him to perform satisfactorily as a midfielder on this side.  At times, he has played as a centre back, a position which allows him to take advantage of his notable attacking projection.  Despite his youth Babayaro is a mature footballer with a lot of experience in top competition.  He is technical, quick and brave.  He likes to push up along the left and create a lot of danger joining in the attack; in fact, he scores goals with a certain regularity.  His great resistance allows him to keep up a high rhythm during the ninety minutes.  He has works hard and makes sacrifices. For all these qualities, Celestine Babayaro is a footballer with a very promising future.

* Olympic Champion in Atlanta '96. 
* Belgian League Champion 94 and 95. 
* Belgian Cup Champion 95. 
* Voted best player in Belgium 94 and 95.

* 24 full international appearances for Nigeria.  2 goals. 
* Olympic International, he was in the team for the Atlanta Games in '96. He scored a goal in the final in which Nigeria beat Argentina.

* Born in Kaduna, a town of 150,000 in the North of Nigeria.  As a small boy he lived in the same street as Daniel Amokachi. 
* He has six brothers and two sisters.  One day he went to see his big brother, who was a keeper in a youth team, and they asked him to play with them.  That day, his meteoric career started. 
* Aged 14 he was already an under-17 international for Nigeria. 
* He was the youngest player in the under-17 World Cup in Japan in '92. There he was discovered by Anderlecht.  The Belgian club made an offer for him and Babayaro accepted although his parents were against the idea at the beginning. 
* Aged 15 he joined the lower ranks of Anderlecht.  One year later he was a regular in the first team. 
* Belgian champion in 1994 and 1995, he was one of the stars of the Olympic Games in Atlanta.  He even allowed himself the luxury of scoring a goal in the final, in which Nigeria overcame Argentina. 
* In 1997 he receives offers from Milan, Juventus and Deportivo de la Coruña, but he is finally transferred to Chelsea on the 21st of April of this same year for £2,250,000.  Up till then the London club had never paid so much for a player so young.  Babayaro signed a five-year contract. 
* He admits that the worst moment of his career was in the European Cup in 1994, when he was sent off for a tackle on the Steaua Bucharest forward Lacatus.  Babayaro was 16. 
* His greatest dream in his life would be to take his parents to one of Chelsea's game, according to his own declaration.

* Last season Babayaro was, for yet another year, an undisputed starter in Anderlecht's line-ups, both in the League and in the UEFA Cup.  Celestine showed his continued and unstoppable progress, although his contribution wasn't enough to bring the title to the Belgian club.  Anderlecht finished the league fourth, lost the Cup final to Ekeren and was knocked out of the UEFA Cup by Inter Milan.

235.name: Le Saux
pages: * Four years after his departure for Ewood Park, Graeme Le Saux returns to Chelsea.  In his spell at Blackburn he experienced the glory of a league title and misfortune in the form of injuries.  He was one of the big absentees in the England European Championship, but now Graeme doesn't want to think about it.  He now has all his hopes pinned on the '98 French World Cup, where, provided nothing untoward happens, he will be the first choice left back in Glenn Hoddle's team.

* A left back who covers a lot of ground, Graeme Le Saux is also able to play in the midfield.  A classy left-footer, he is noted for his decisiveness when joining in the attack and the speed with which he gets back in position to cut out the rival counter-attack.  He has an extraordinary technique in his left foot, allowing him to take free-kicks with a lot of precision. An explosive footballer, he is hard to get by on the run and to catch out of position.  Temperamental and ambitious, his presence is a guarantee for any team.  Without doubt, Le Saux is one of the best wide defenders in the Premier League.

* League Champion 95. 
* Charity Shield Medal 94.

* 20 full international appearances for England.  1 goal. 
* 2 B-international appearances. 
* 4 under-21 international appearances.

* A native of Jersey, he started playing football in the modest club of his home-town, St. Paul's.  His class didn't escape the notice of the coaches at Chelsea, and on the 9th of December 1987 he joined the side.  His debut in the League didn't take place until the 13th of May 1989, in a game against Portsmouth.  The game was pretty irrelevant, as Chelsea had already won the Second Division title, and Graeme didn't play from the start. 
* He had to wait until the 26th of December of this year before making his second appearance, once again as a substitute.  But this time Le Saux scored the last goal of the game at Selhurst Park (2-2). 
* Little by little he prised his way into the Stamford Bridge side, until on the 25th of March 1993 he was transferred to Blackburn Rovers. 
* In the 94-95 season he consolidates himself as one of the best left backs in the country, and Rovers are proclaimed League champions and he is voted a member of the Championship Dream Team.  On the 11th of June 1995 he scores an extraordinary goal against the Brazilian team at Wembley. 
* However, the 95-96 season brings its bad luck for Graeme Le Saux.  In September he suffers from a ligament injury and shortly after making his comeback he takes part in the lamentable incident in the Champions League game, fighting with his team-mate David Batty in Blackburn's visit to Spartak Moscow.  In December, he suffers a broken ankle and several tendons in a game against Middlesbrough.  This injury keeps him out of the side for the rest of the season and prevents him from taking part in the England European Championship, where, in theory, he had his chances of playing. 
* He reappeared at the end of October 1996 and quickly got his place back in the Blackburn Rovers side and in the England team. 
* At the end of the 96-97 season Le Saux makes public his desire to leave Ewood Park.  He had some interesting offers from clubs such as Arsenal and Athletico Madrid, though he finally decided to return to Chelsea. 
* On the 8th of August 1997 he was transferred to the London club for £5 million.  He signed for the Stamford Bridge club for four years.

* He returned to the competition at the end of October, almost a year after he suffered that very serious injury.  Despite having had a period of inactivity Le Saux offered an extraordinary performance right from the start.  He took over the left flank at Blackburn in the 26 League games he played.  In all of these he was a starter.  He even scored a goal against Sheffield Wednesday.  His work caught the eye of the new England selector, Glenn Hoddle, who gave him the opportunity to play as an international again.

236.name: Lambourde
pages: * By signing Bernard Lambourde Chelsea have noticeably reinforced their backline.  The French footballer, originally from Girondins of Bordeaux, is noted for his solid defensive game, and so is perfectly adapted to the needs of the team managed by Ruud Gullit.  At Stamford Bridge Lambourde will coincide with his fellow countryman Frank Leboeuf.  Although Bernard doesn't have a guaranteed place, sooner or later, he will have the chance to show what he is made of in the Premier League.

* He plays basically as a central defender, although he can also operate as a sweeper or even in the midfield.  He is dominant in the air and has an adequate touch.  He is physically very strong, quick and agile, and so rival forwards find him hard to beat.  He doesn't take part much in the attacking game, although he will push up at free-kicks and corners.
x
x

* He was born on the island of Guadalupe, but when he was two his family moved to France. 
* He started his professional career in the 91-92 season in the ranks of Cannes.  He made his debut in the French league on the 15th of November 1991 in a game Nantes-Cannes (1-0). 
* He scored his first goal on the 1st of September 1993 in an away game against Caen. 
* In the 94-95 season he plays on loan to Angers, in the Second Division.
* In 1996 he was transferred to Girondins of Bordeaux. 
* On the 14th of June 1997 he was transferred to Chelsea for £1,500,000.
* Last season, his first at Girondins of Bordeaux, he played 28 League games and scored 1 goal.  The team finished the league season in fourth place, so managing to classify for the 97-98 UEFA Cup.

237.name: Sinclair
pages: * Frank Sinclair is a footballer with a strong character and, at times, his personality has caused him a few problems since he arrived in the first team from the youth squad at Chelsea.  However, this same temperament has also helped him score some important goals and carry out some good marking jobs.Although he hasn't yet settled into the Blues starting line-up, the fans at Stamford Bridge have had plenty of occasion to applaud his game and also to see some set-backs.  Ruud Gullit hopes to bring some equilibrium to Sinclair' game which he needs before he can offer his best.  If he manages this the player's contribution to the team could be larger.

* His natural position is that of left back, although injuries to his team-mates have forced him to play in the centre of defence or even in the midfield.  Frank Sinclair's biggest virtue is his extraordinary speed.  He is probably the team's quickest player, and his forays down the touchline can create danger in the rival box.  This characteristic also allows him to make interceptions quickly and makes him a defender who is hard to beat. Brave, aggressive and strong, he doesn't hesitate to be tough if he thinks the situation demands it.  This combativity gives him the characteristics that allow him to play in the centre of defence, a position where, despite not being very tall, he is effective.  He makes up for his lack of height with a great jump.  Very hard-working, he joins in the attack enthusiastically at the slightest opportunity. 
* At times he is too aggressive and hard, bringing a lot of problems with the referees; something he should try and correct to avoid too many suspensions.
* FA Cup Champion 97.
* 1 youth international appearance for England.

* Frank Sinclair is a footballer trained in the lower ranks of Chelsea.  A professional since the 17th of May 1990, he made his debut with the first team at Stamford Bridge on the 6th of April 1991 in a game against Luton Town (3-3).  On the 12th of December of this same year he is loaned to West Bromwich Albion, where he plays 6 league games. 
* When he was at WBA he was sent off for attacking a referee in a game against Exeter.  Sinclair denied the act, although he couldn't avoid a 9-game suspension. 
* In the 94-95 season he scored 2 goals in the European Cup Winners' Cup.
* His abrasive character has let him down several times.  In October of 1995 he received an absurd red card after going after Brian McClair in a a game against Manchester United.  Chelsea were loosing 1-4 at Stamford Bridge.  Days later he suffered an injury in the fibula that needed surgical attention, so he had no other option but to be in dry dock for several months.

* Frank Sinclair found it hard to return to the Chelsea line-ups.  He played his first game in December.  In January an injury to his team-mate Duberry allowed him to find a gap in the backs of his team.  He reached a high level in a Cup tie against Wimbledon, where he was workmanlike and effective in defence.  As a reward for his work he was aligned in the FA Cup final at Wembley against Middlesbrough and he was able to savour the sweet taste of victory.

238.name: Lee
pages: * The 97-98 will be David Lee's tenth at Chelsea.  Lee is a product of the Stamford Bridge youth squad but, although he has been at the club for many years, his appearances for the first team are few and far between.  He had his best period when Glenn Hoddle arrived at the club's bench, but after the manager's departure, his role in the squad is merely testimonial. To make matters worse, last season he was seriously injured.  His future is uncertain, and the option of a transfer seems ever more likely.

* For the most part of his career David Lee has played as a central defender, but when Glenn Hoddle played him as a sweeper he performed well, as his qualities adjust well to this position.  He is a good short range passer and has a powerful and accurate long-range pass.  He is also good in the air, and can shoot powerfully from a distance.  His height helps him a lot in the aerial game both in the rival and his own areas.  However, he ought to score more goals, as he has the qualities to do so.  In defence, he is good at making interceptions although he is not exactly quick, and the fast and skilful forwards are the ones that cause him most problems in defence.
* Second Division Champion 88-89.

* 10 England under-21 international appearances. 
* 1 youth international appearance.

* Trained in the lower ranks of Chelsea, David Lee turns professional on the 1st of July 1988.  Months later, more exactly on the 1st of October of this same year, he makes his debut in the first team in a game against Leicester played at Stamford Bridge.  At the end of this season, the team returns once more to the First Division. 
* He has spent his whole career at Chelsea, however, he has gone on loan to three clubs.  On the 30th of January 1992 he goes to Reading and on the 26th of March he goes to Plymouth Argyle.  On the 12th of August 1994 Portsmouth is his destination. 
* Up till the end of the 94-95 season he had received 5 yellow cards and been sent off once.

* After his great performance during the 95-96 season, David Lee had gone into last season in a very positive mood.  However, last season developed contrary to expectations.  The signing of Lebouef forced him onto the substitutes' bench and he could only play one game at Stamford Bridge against Spurs when the Frenchman was out due to injury.  Lee scored a goal from the penalty spot against Ian Walker, but 28 minutes later he suffered a broken tibia and fibula in his right leg and had to say goodbye to the season.

239.name: Duberry
pages: * Michael Duberry is one of the most promising defenders in England.  The fans at Stamford Bridge have a lot of hope placed in him, and he has shown that he has more than enough talent to be successful in the Premier League. Michael has won the confidence of Ruud Gullit and, when he makes a full recovery from the serious injury he suffered last season, he will figure in the team once again.  His strength and quality will be of great worth in a season in which Chelsea aspire to everything, both in the English League and in the European Cup Winners' Cup.

* A central defender who stands out for his strength and speed, Michael Duberry not only carries out his defensive duties effectively, but also takes part in the attacking game.  Quick with the ball at his feet, he doesn't hesitate to bring it towards the rival area and, if given the slightest chance, try out his powerful shot on goal.  He is also dominant in the air helped by his extraordinary physical strength, an aspect which helps his game enormously.  He usually joins in the attack dangerously at set-plays.  A footballer with a great future ahead of him, on the pitch he shows a maturity and security not often seen in someone his age.
x
* 3 under-21 appearances for England.  He made his debut in August 1996, in a game against Moldavia.

* Trained in the lower ranks of Chelsea, he has been a professional since the 7th of June 1993.  He made his debut in the League on the 4th of May 1994 in a game that Chelsea lost to Coventry City at Stamford Bridge 1-2.
* After missing an entire season, he is loaned to Bournemouth on the 29th of September 1995.  He plays 7 games before returning to Chelsea.  This same season he scores his first two goals in an FA Cup game against Grimsby and he becomes one of the most eye-catching players of the season.  The radio station Capital Gold vote him "London Player of the Year". 
* In the 96-97 season he took up a regular place in Chelsea's line-ups under the leadership of Ruud Gullit, but in January 1997 he suffered a serious injury to his Achilles tendon which kept him out for the rest of the season.
* He scored his first goal for Chelsea on the 2nd of November 1996 at Old Trafford against Manchester United, managing to head past the outstretched Peter Schmeichel.

* A serious injury to his Achilles tendon in January put an end to his extraordinary progress.  Michael Duberry has managed to settle into the starting line-ups at Chelsea and usually played in the centre of defence alongside Frank Lebouef and Steve Clarke.  He had even given a sign of his powerful aerial game when he scored a goal with his head at Old Trafford against Manchester United and another for the England under-21 team against Georgia.  But bad luck came his way in a training session when he became injured and was out for the rest of the season.

240.name: Myers
pages:
* Andy Myers is one of the footballers most praised by the supporters at Stamford Bridge, who value highly the effort he puts into every game he plays at left back.  He made his debut in the first team when he was just 17.  Up until a few seasons ago he was considered a player with a great future ahead of him and was a regular in the lower categories of the national team.
* However, injuries have cut short his progress and haven't allowed him the continuity needed to make his mark as a footballer.  In any case, the fans still trust him.  He was voted the best young player of the team in the 95-96 season and last season earned the confidence of Ruud Gullit.  Now, Myers hopes to regain this confidence and that for once, luck is once again on his side.

* A left back who covers a lot of ground and who is very mobile, Myers is a footballer whose strength and tenacity are more important than his technique. He works untiringly along the whole touchline, taking part both in the attack and in defence.  Very quick and resistant, he is hard at times and doesn't hesitate to make a tackle on opposing forwards.  It is this determination that is one of his main characteristics, allowing him to overcome his technical limitations in his game, though, given his youth, he still has time to improve in this department. 
* He can also play as left half, although he needs to improve the accuracy of his passes and his shot on goal.
* FA Cup Champion 97.

* 4 under-21 international appearances for England.  1 goal.  In June 1995 he plays 3 games for the team in the Toulon international tournament.
* 11 youth international appearances.  1 goal.

* Andy Myers made the step up into the Chelsea first squad on the 6th of April 1991, the date of his league debut against Luton Town in game played at Stamford Bridge.  In that game Myers came on as a substitute for Damian Matthew and became the youngest player to make his debut for the team since Tommy Langley in 1974.  In any case, his record was surpassed one month later by another young footballer, Ian Pearce.  Shortly afterwards, on the 25th of July, Andy Myers signs his first professional contract for the Blues.
* In October 1991 he plays his first full game against Liverpool, helped by the absence of Dennis Wise.  Myers scored the second goal of the game (2-2).
* Injury prone, this has prevented him from playing more games.  He has had some injury or other in just about every season as a professional. 
* He was voted the best young player at Chelsea in the 95-96 season.

* He started the season as a member of the starting line-up, playing at left back to the detriment of Scott Minto.  Andy managed to keep his place in Gullit's teams until a back injury kept him out the team.  But before this he had managed to score his only goal of the season at Hillsborough against Sheffield Wednesday.  He played a total of 18 league games, 15 of those from the start; and although he didn't play a single minute of the FA Cup final at Wembley, he was able to include the title in his honours list.

241.name: Clarke
pages: * He arrived at Stamford Bridge in January 1987, and so he is currently the player who has been at Chelsea the longest.  A Scotland international, Steve Clarke has never been a star.  However, his constant effort and his great professionality are very much appreciated by the fans and are also noted by the coaches.  With Ruud Gullit on the bench he had to adapt to the position of centre back and not only managed this, but also became one of the footballers most used by the Dutch manager.  This is because Steve Clarke is a player who can be trusted.  He never disappoints.

* Although he played a large part of last season as a centre defender, it has to be said his true position is right back.  Technically discrete, he contributes with a lot of work and effort to the team's game.  He passes the ball well, something which has improved a lot in face of the demands of Hoddle and Gullit, two managers in favour of the passing game.  He will be tough if he thinks it necessary.  He hardly joins in the attack, but in contentious tasks he fulfils his mission effectively, helped by his broad experience.

* FA Cup Champion 97. 
* Second Division Champion 88-89.

* 6 full international appearances for Scotland.  He made his debut on the 9th of September 1987 in a game against Hungary played at Hampden Park.
* 3 B-international appearances. 
* 8 under-21 international appearances.

* His first steps in the footballing world were made at Beith Juniors in Scotland.  In 1981 his talent opens the doors to St. Mirren, with whose first team he makes his debut on the 4th of September 1982 in a game against Hibernian. 
* On the 19th of January 1987 he is transferred to Chelsea for £422,000.  In his second season in England he sees the Blues drop to the Second Division.
* Since 1989 he has to compete for the status of first choice right back with Gareth Hall, a Wales international. 
* His best season is 93-94.  At the end of it he is voted "Player of the Year" at Chelsea.  The following season he suffers from several injuries, but, even so, he is an important footballer for the team. 
* After the arrival of the Romanian Petrescu in the team in the 95-96 season, Clarke adapts his game and plays as a central defender on the left of the axis. 
* In the summer of 1996 he played a testimonial game between Chelsea and PSV Eindhoven as a recognition of his ten years of services to the club.
* During the 96-97 season he renewed his contract with Chelsea until 1999.

* Last season Steve Clarke was a starter in the 31 league games he played. Ruud Gullit made him responsible for forming a defensive line comprising three central defenders and the veteran footballer responded by offering a great level of performance.  In the Cup tie against Wimbledon he had to adapt to the left back position and also performed satisfactorily.  After ten years at the club he received the recognition of his loyalty when the team won the FA Cup at Wembley.  Months before he had played in his testimonial game against PSV Eindhoven in the pre-season, receiving the appreciation of the fans.

242.name: Leboeuf
pages: * Frank Leboeuf has needed just one year to become one of the idols of the fans at Stamford Bridge.  In this time the French defender has brought elegance and good play to the grounds in England.  His presence in the line-ups was one of the keys to the FA Cup title for Ruud Gullit's team and now, going into the 97-98 season, he has the responsibility of leading Chelsea in their journey through the Premier League.  And it could even be that the French selector Aimé Jacquet decides to call him up for the World Cup that will be played in his country, France.

* As a central defender or sweeper, Frank Leboeuf is a player who stands out for his extraordinary sense of positioning, allowing him to win back a lot of balls without committing a foul.  With better technique than appears at first sight, he plays the ball out from the back simple, looking for the support of his team-mates and, rarely does he have to resort to a punt to clear the ball.  He joins in the attack frequently, especially at set plays, and, considering his position, he scores a lot of goals.  Excellent in the air, he presence is felt in both areas.  Right-footed, thanks to his experience he is efficient in defence and also creates danger in attack, something much appreciated by the coaches.
* FA Cup Champion 97.

* 11 full international appearances for France.  2 goals.  He made his debut on the 22nd of July 1995 in a friendly against Norway played in Oslo (0-0).  On the 6th of June of this year, he scores his first two goals against the Azerbajan team.  The game was played in Auxerre and France won 10-0.
* Present in the 96 England European Championship, he doesn't get to make his debut.

* He started his career in the Toulon training centre, from where he moved to Meaux in 1987. 
* Transferred to Laval one year later, he makes his debut in the First Division on the 13th of August 1988, with a 1-0 defeat at the hands of Nice.
* In his first season at Laval he was unable to prevent the team from being relegated to the Second Division.  In November 1990 he signs for Strasbourg, who were playing in the Second Division at the time. 
* His good performances for Strasbourg, where he was an undisputed starter, didn't go by unnoticed by the big French clubs.  So much so he was on the point of being transferred to Monaco, whose coaches considered him an ideal substitute for Mendy. 
* In 1992 he is called up by his country for the Mediterranean games, but the competition was suspended in the end. 
* After playing more than 130 games in the First Division and scoring nearly 30 goals, a high number for a central defender, Lebouef had a pretty empty honours list.  His biggest success is runner-up in the Cup in the 94-95 season.  Strasbourg lost to Paris Saint Germaine in the final 1-0. 
* In the summer of 1996 he is transferred to Chelsea for £2.5 million.  Shortly before, Leboeuf had been called up by the French selector, Aimé Jacquet, for the England European Championship.  However, he doesn't get to play a single chance to play. 
* Since his arrival at Stamford Bridge he quickly forms a friendship with Dennis Wise. 
* He made his debut in the Premier League on the 18th of August 1996, in a game against Southampton played at the Dell (0-0). 
* He scored his first goal for Chelsea on the 24th of August 1996 in a game against Coventry disputed at Stamford Bridge (2-0). 
* He declared that he is an admirer of Ruud Gullit even before signing for Chelsea.

* Frank Leboeuf was one of the big surprises last season.  Since the start of the Championship he showed a great admiration for English football without renouncing his own style of play.  Ruud Gullit made him the leader in Chelsea's defence and Leboeuf responded perfectly.  He played 26 league games, all of those from the start; and scored 6 goals, one from the penalty spot.  He put the icing on the cake with a perfect performance in the FA Cup final against Middlesbrough in the mythical Wembley.

243.name: Petrescu
pages: * Dan Petrescu is one of the most profitable foreigners in the Premier League.  Since his arrival in England in 1994 the Rumanian international has given plenty of signs of his quality.  He was one of the regulars at the Chelsea managed by Glenn Hoddle and now, with Ruud Gullit on the bench at Stamford Bridge, he continues to enjoy his status as a starter.  For the 97-98 season Dan has set himself two objectives: to win another title with the Blues and to play an important role in the France World Cup.

* He can play equally well as right half or right back, supported by his good technique and his attacking nature.  He is quick, disciplined and defends effectively.  When he joins in the attack he passes accurately and moves quickly.  Blessed with a powerful shot on goal with his right, he usually scores several goals during a season.  His experience has allowed him to improve his contribution to the team's game using different resources, although at times his attacking nature makes him neglect a little his obligations in defence.

* Romanian League Champion 85, 86, 87 and 88. 
* Romanian Cup Champion 85, 87 and 88. 
* FA Cup Champion 97.

* 61 full international appearances for Romania.  9 goals.  He made his debut in his team's 1-0 win over Italy in a friendly played in Sibiu on the 29th of March 1989.  He scores his first goal for the team on the 5th of December 1990: Romania beat San Marino 6-0. 
* Present in the United States 94 World Cup, he played from the start the five games of his team, against Colombia, Switzerland, The United States, Argentina and Sweden, and what's more, he scored the winning goal against the host nation (0-1). 
* In the England 96 European Championship he played from the start in the three games played by Romania, who were knocked out in the first phase.

* He started his sporting career in Steaua Bucharest, the club related to the Romanian army, arriving in their first team in the 85-86 season.  He is loaned to F.C. Olt next season, but his extraordinary performances lead to is return to Romania's biggest club. 
* An international since 1989, an injury prevents him from playing in the Italy World Cup in '90. 
* In the summer 1991 he is transferred to the Italian team Foggia, the club has recently been promoted to the Serie A.  He makes his debut in the Calcio on the 19th of September 1991, against Inter in San Siro (1-1).  His career shows an appreciable progression and Petrescu becomes one of the best right backs on the continent. 
* In August 1993 he signs for Genoa, the club where he only stayed for one season. 
* On the 6th of August 1994 he is transferred to Sheffield Wednesday for £1,250,000.  His eruption in the Premier League couldn't be better.  He makes his debut on the 20th of this same month in a game against Tottenham Hotspur, and Wednesday win 3-1 with the help of a goal from Petrescu. 
* He arrives at Chelsea on the 18th of November 1995.  The club at Stamford Bridge paid £2,300,000 for his transfer.  He makes his debut this same day with defeat at the hands of Leeds at Elland Road (1-0).  He scores his first goal for the Blues on the 17th of December 1995: Chelsea beat Newcastle 1-0 at home.

* Dan Petrescu was one of the most outstanding Chelsea players last season. Ruud Gullit played him as a starter in 34 games in the Premier League, and he showed that he is one of the best wing backs in English football. Petrescu didn't take long to reach a good understanding with the Italians in the team (Di Matteo, Zola an Vialli) and to his usual solid defending he could add his efficiency in attack.  He scored 3 League goals and 1 in the League Cup.  He also continued to receive call-ups for Romania and finished off a phenomenal season when the team won the FA Cup at Wembley against Middlesbrough.
