244.name: Hughes P.
pages: * Last season allowed Paul Hughes to show that he has a place in the Premier League.  His arrival was quite simply spectacular, up to the point where he scored one of the best goals of the year.  He is young, talented, self-confident and is keen to be successful.  If he keeps up his progress, Paul Hughes is destined to form part of the Chelsea of the future alongside players of his generation such as Jody Morris and Mark Nicholls.

* He usually plays as a link-man between the forwards and midfield, where he takes advantage of his speed and turn to get into dangerous positions in the rival box.  Despite his youth he is a mature footballer, calm when dealing with difficult situations.  He is very mobile and has a good playing vision, allowing him to make a lot of scoring chances for his team-mates.
x
* Schoolboy international for England.

* Trained in the Chelsea youth squad he turned professional on July 19th 1994. 
* However, his debut in the Premier League didn't take place until the 18th of January 1997 in a game against Derby County disputed at Stamford Bridge.  Hughes came on as a substitute for Dennis Wise during half time and in the 85th minute he scored the last goal, establishing the final score of 3-1.

* Paul Hughes had a spectacular debut in the Premier League.  Forty minutes after stepping on the pitch as a substitute for Dennis Wise he scored an impressive goal: he picked the ball up in the left back position, played three one-two's with team-mates and, once in the area, finished with the calmness of a veteran.  His performance earned him the recognition of the fans at Stamford Bridge and from Ruud Gullit himself, who played him in another 11 league games, 8 from the start.  It was, without doubt, his best season in his short professional career.

245.name: Newton
pages: * The goal Eddie Newton scored at Wembley in the final of the 1997 FA Cup was just reward for his consistency.  Up till then, the Chelsea midfielder hadn't had much luck with injuries, which had eaten into a promising career.  Newton earned the confidence of Ruud Gullit and now, going into the 97-98 season, he hopes to regain his best level of play and help the Blues fight for all the titles possible.

* A midfielder who battles constantly and who is effective at winning the ball back.  Eddie Newton spends a lot of energy in each game.  He makes sacrifices for the good of the team, helping the work of his team-mates and equilibrating the team's game.  He has an acceptable technical foundation allowing him to distribute the fluidly and sensibly; and create danger when he joins in the attack, where he is quick and shows great determination when looking to get a shot in.
* FA Cup Champion 97.
* 2 under-21 international appearances for England.

* A product of the Chelsea youth squad, he turned professional on the 17th of May 1990. 
* In the 91-92 season he was loaned to Cardiff City, scoring 4 goals in 18 games for this team.  On returning to Stamford Bridge, he made his debut with the first team in the last game of the season against Everton.  Newton celebrated the occasion scoring a goal against Southall. 
* He played in the 1994 FA Cup final which Chelsea lost to Manchester United 4-0.  Newton gave away a penalty. 
* In the 95-96 season he broke his leg in a strong collision with his own goalkeeper. 
* Eddie Newton scored Chelsea's second goal in the 97 FA Cup final.  The Blues beat Middlesbrough 2-0.  In this way he made up for the 1994 final when he gave away that cursed penalty.

* After a serious injury in the 95-96 season, Eddie Newton returned to the team in October, although he wasn't a member of the starting line-up until December.  He strung together fourteen games on the trot as a starter and when he had reached his best level of play he saw how a new injury kept him out the team again.  Eddie damaged his knee in a warm up before the league game against Derby.  Fortunately, he could return to the competition before the end of the season and even had a centre-stage part in the final of the FA Cup when he scored the second and definitive goal for Chelsea against Middlesbrough.

246.name: Poyet
pages: * Gustavo Poyet is a personal signing on the part of Ruud Gullit for the 97-98 season.  The Uruguayan midfielder left behind his stamp of quality in Spanish football and he now hopes to also be successful in the Premier League.  To help him he has a broad experience in top competition and his style of play could fit in perfectly with Chelsea's scheme.  His arrival has awoken expectations at Stamford Bridge, almost as much as his sadness on leaving Saragossa.  Those who know him also know that he is a great signing.  And in the football of today it is not easy to get hold of footballers of his class without paying dearly for them.

* Although he doesn't have exquisite technical quality he is a very complete midfielder.  He usually plays as a link-man with the forwards and is given freedom to push up into the attack where he can take best advantage of his qualities.  He makes sacrifices in defence, collaborates in the construction of moves and, above all, scores goals.  The Uruguayan international seems to have a rare ability to score goals at the most crucial times, which seem to be the team's winners.  He has a terrifying shot with his right and a spectacular header, allowing him to score a lot in attack and clear balls in defence.  He isn't the classical finisher who waits in the centre of the area, far from it.  On the contrary his "surprise factor" is his best ally and he is used to popping up from deep positions with a lot of strength when the defence least expects it.

* Spanish Cup Champion in 94. 
* Cup Winners' Cup Champion 95. 
* Americas Cup Champion 95.

* 23 full international appearances for Uruguay. 
* He was the champion of the Americas Cup with Uruguay in 1995 and was voted the player of the tournament.

* His father was a pivot in the Uruguay basketball team in the Olympic Games in Helsinki and Tokyo. 
* Ildo Maneiro was the man who recommended him to Saragossa. 
* He arrived at the Arragon team as centre forward. 
* His signing cost £175,000. 
* He made his debut in the Spanish league on the 2nd of September 1990.
* He is the foreign player who has worn the Saragossa shirt most times in the history of the club. 
* Poyet swore allegiance to the Spanish constitution on the 24th of January 1997.  Since then he stopped taking up a foreigner's place in European football. 
* His contract with Saragossa expired on the 30th of June 1997, but already in May of this year he had reached an agreement with Chelsea.  At the time there were a lot of Spanish, Italian and Uruguayan clubs interested in signing him.  Before moving to Stamford Bridge, Poyet contributed with goals and good play to Saragossa's survival in the top level of Spanish football.

* In his last season in the Spanish league Gustavo Poyet was once again one of the most important players at Saragossa.  He played 38 league games, 37 of these from the start, and finished the season as the team's top scorer with 15 goals, the same as Fernando Morientes.  His goals and his play where crucial for the team destiny, managing to avoid the drop to the Second Division.  By way of thanks for so many years of service to Saragossa, the fans said goodbye with a long and emotional ovation.

247.name: Zola
pages: * Chelsea's project to construct a champion side needed a star and Ruud Gullit came up with Gianfranco Zola, who he had known in his spell in Italy, as the ideal candidate.  In his first season in England Zola became the new standard-bearer of the new Chelsea and a new idol for the fans at Stamford Bridge.  Supported by classy players such as Di Matteo, Vialli, Lebouef, Wise, Le Saux and Flo; and under the orders of a brave manager such as Gullit, the Italian international could take the Blues to the highest point of their history.

* A player of enormous talent, he can play both as a centre half or as a link-man with the forwards, or even as a born striker, and in all these positions he has produced an excellent level, touching on genius.  His extraordinary footballing vision allows him to set the rhythm of each move and chose the right option at the right moment.  His exquisite individual technique gives his the accuracy necessary to pass and the skill required to remedy complicated situations with apparent ease. 
* A complete footballer, he is quick to find space and unpredictable on the turn.  He finishes well and has powerful shot allows him to score a lot of goals per season.  He is also a free-kick master.  In fact, according to the statistics published in Italy, his success rate is greater that men of the calibre of Michel Platini, Diego Maradona and Ronald Koeman.

* UEFA Cup Champion 95. 
* European Supercup Champion 94. 
* Italian League Champion 90. 
* Italian Supercup Champion 90. 
* FA Cup Champion 97. 
* Voted "footballer of the year 97" in England.

* 33 full international caps for Italy.  9 goals.  He made his debut on the 13th of November 1991 in a game between Italy and Norway played in Genoa (1-1). 
* Present in the 94 United States World Cup, he only played 12 minutes in the game against Nigeria, as he was unjustly sent off. 
* In the England 96 European Championship he took part in the three games played by his team, against Russia (2-1), The Czech Republic (1-2) and Germany (0-0).  Only in the second game did he not play from the start.

* Son of the owner of a cafe on Sardinia, as a small boy he earned a great reputation as a footballer on the island.  He started to play for Nuorese and from there he moved to Torres, another Sardinian team where he stayed for three seasons, the team rising from the Serie C2 to Serie C1 in 1987.
* Zola remembers a white Renault 9 from this period which he used to make the journey from Oliena, his hometown, to Sassari, a car in which he covered thousands of miles.  At Torres he already gave signs of great things and the sporting director of the club, Nello Barbanera, told him that Luciano Moggi was following his progress. 
* In 1989 he made the definitive jump to the elite when he signed for Naples, where he formed a great friendship with Diego Armando Maradona, who had been his big idol.  Zola's game and his physical appearance were, furthermore, similar to that of Maradona, and so he soon became known as Marazola.  The Argentinean star himself said, when Zola introduced him to his parents, while holding up the number-10 shirt that "this will belong to your son soon".This anecdote showed the admiration that Diego had for Zola, both on a professional and personal level.  And it didn't stop there, as Maradona even gave up the number-10 shirt for a game against Pisa in the 90-91 season, thus giving Zola the responsibility of being the natural heir to the best player in the world at Naples. 
* His next destination was Parma, who he joined in 1993.  He was, with 18 goals, the top scorer at the club in his first season. 
* Although his contract wasn't going to expire until 1998, the signings of Hern and Crespo and Enrico Chiesa by the Parma side pushed through his move to Chelsea on the 8th of November 1996 in exchange for £4,500,000. At the English club managed by Ruud Gullit, Zola coincides with his fellow countrymen Roberto Di Matteo and Gianluca Vialli. 
* He made his Premier League debut on the 16th of November 1996 in a game against Blackburn Rovers played at Ewood Park (1-1); and scored his first goal for Chelsea on the 7th of December of this same year at Stamford Bridge against Everton (2-2). 
* At the end of this first season in England he was voted "Footballer of the Year" by the sports reporters of the country. 
* A great friend and profound admirer of Claudio Ranieri, his manager at Naples, Zola has declared that when he leaves football he will return to his small Sardinian village of Oliena.

* Gianfranco Zola was voted "Footballer of the year 97" by the sports reporters of England, a well-earned prize for the player who arrived at Chelsea in November and who gave signs of his quality straight away.  He didn't take long to show his class, taking part in some brilliant moves and scoring some spectacular goals; among which the ones against Everton, the first of them all, Manchester United and Sunderland were outstanding.  He was a starter in the 23 league games in which he appeared.  He scored 8 goals, the same number as Mark Hughes and one less than his fellow countryman Vialli. 
* In the Cup competition he also produced some sensational games, guiding the team to victory at Wembley with 4 goals in the ties leading up to the final. 
* Zola scored the goal that beat England in the World Cup classification game at Wembley.  The Italian forward escaped from Sol Campbell and beat Ian Walker's advance.  It was yet another classy detail from the best player in England.

248.name: Morris
pages: * Jody Morris is one of the shortest players in English football, but he is also one of the players with the most promising future.  He was captain of the national under-17 team last season and he has settled into the national under-21 side.  Despite his youth, Jody has shown that he has no fear of playing in a competition as demanding as the Premier League.  Ruud Gullit seems willing to give him more opportunities.  And Morris is sure he will know how to take them.

* Jody Morris is a very creative midfielder.  His playing style is very similar to that of his team-mate Dennis Wise.  Technical and skilful, he has a masterful turn and from the link-man position, gives measured passes to his forwards.  He plays well between lines helped by his great mobility. Quick and clever, he sees the space created by his team-mates clearly.  He should improve his strength as, although he isn't very bulky, he could get more from himself were he to work on his physique.  Very young, he has plenty of time ahead to progress both technically and physically.
x

* 3 under-21 international appearances for England.  He made his debut in October 1996, in a game against Poland. 
* Under-17 international.

* Born in London and raised in the Chelsea youth squad, Jody Morris signed his first professional contract on the 8th of January 1996.  His debut in the Premier League took place on the 4th of February of this same year in a game against Middlesbrough played at Stamford Bridge.  Morris came on as a substitute for John Spencer in the 70th minute, but couldn't prevent his team going down 0-5.  Six weeks earlier he had celebrated his 17th birthday.
* He was also captain of the England under-17 team. 
* He scored his first goal for the Chelsea first team on the 18th of September 1996 in a League Cup game against Blackpool played at Bloomfield Road.

* The overall balance of the season is clearly positive for Jody Morris.  The young Chelsea midfielder earned the confidence of Ruud Gullit, who didn't hesitate to align him as a starter in the second game of the league. Unfortunately, injuries kept him out at various points and even delayed his debut with the England under-21 team, which didn't happen until October.  In any case, he showed that soon he will be playing regularly in the Premier League.

249.name: Di Matteo
pages: * Although he arrived in England without the aura of a star that surrounded his team-mates Vialli and Zola, Roberto Di Matteo became one of the sensations of last season.  Ruud Gullit gave him the responsibility of directing Chelsea's player and the Italian international performed his duties to perfection.  Stamford Bridge discovered a footballer with exceptional class, capable of applying himself effectively in defensive and attacking tasks and stamping a more modern concept of football on the team.  With men such as Di Matteo in the squad, Chelsea can aspire to everything in England and in Europe.

* Di Matteo is one of the best centre halves in Europe.  He has a great technical quality and playing vision which allows him to direct the team with good judgement.  He has a broad range of passes and is able to set the rhythm of the game.  Very elegant, he works the ball well, organised the game of his team-mates and takes on a lot of attacking responsibility. What's more, he scores goals thanks to his powerful shot. 
* In defence he fights for every ball and doesn't shy away from body contact.  However, he is a little irregular, something he should try and put right, though he is young and has the chance to do so.  This irregularity is carried through to the team's overall performance; if Di Matteo plays well, the others play better as well. 
* An admirer of Baresi, he can also play as a sweeper, the position he occupied at the beginning of his sporting career.

* Swiss League Champion 92-93. 
* FA Cup Champion 97.

* 26 full international appearances for Italy.  1 goal.  He made his debut on the 16th of November 1994 in a game against Croatia played in Palermo. The Italian side lost 1-2. 
* Present in the England 96 European Championship, he was a starter in the games against Russia (2-0) and Germany (0-0), while he wasn't played in the game Italy lost to the Czech Republic.

* Born in Switzerland, but of Italian parents, Roberto Di Matteo could have been a Swiss international when the German, Uli Stielike, was managing the national team, but he renounced the chance with the intention of acquiring Italian nationality.  At times he has gone so far as to say that he doesn't like Switzerland, and there the people are very distant and cold, and he, like most Latin types, is very passionate. 
* He was trained in the club of his hometown, Schaffausen, in the Swiss Second Division.  He arrived in the first squad in the 88-89 season and stayed there until 1991, the year in which he signed for Zurich, one of the big clubs in Swiss football.  His excellent performances gave him star status in Swiss football. 
* However, Di Matteo, a lover of risky adventures decides to sign for Aarau, a modest club used to having problems to stay up.  The reason for the move is that he wants to play once again under the orders of Rolf Fringer, who prefers attacking football and who had been his manager at Schaffausen. The Italian preferred Fringer to the conservative Kurt Jara, a man with a more conservative outlook. 
* At Aarau he goes through, according to his own statements, the most important moment of his career when his team is proclaimed Swiss champion, a great performance for such a small club.  At the time he was playing as a sweeper and was considered as one of the best in his position, to such a point that there was speculation that he could be the replacement for the mythical Alan Geiger, the historical sweeper of the Swiss side.  But he renounced the chance. 
* In 1993, as a complete unknown in Italy, he signs for Lazio.  One year later he was making his debut for the national team under the leadership of Arrigo Sacchi.  In his first season he manages to displace Fabrizio Di Mauro from the side an becomes the team's playmaker. 
* A regular in the Italian side, he plays in the England 96 European Championship and is a starter in the schemes of the manager Arrigo Sacchi. Shortly afterwards he is transferred to Chelsea for £4,900,000.  In England Di Matteo faces a new sporting challenge. 
* He made his debut in the Premier League on the 18th of August 1996, in a game against Southampton at the Dell. 
* He scored his first goal for Chelsea when he made his home debut on the 21st of August 1996 against Middlesbrough (1-0). 
* He finished off his season in England scoring the first goal in the final of the FA Cup, where Chelsea beat Middlesbrough 2-0 at Wembley.  Di Matteo beat Roberts, the rival keeper, after 43 seconds, the fastest goal in the history of the FA Cup.  He was also voted "Man of the Match".

* To finish off an extraordinary season Roberto Di Matteo was voted the "Man of the Match" in the FA Cup final against Middlesbrough.  On that day the Italian midfielder scored the fastest goal in the history of the competition, 43 seconds after the referee blew the starting whistle. 
* Di Matteo had an impressive season.  He played 34 league games, 33 of these from the start, and scored 7 goals.  A man who enjoyed the full confidence of Ruud Gullit, he became the extension of the manager on the pitch; directing the team masterfully and showing that he is a very complete footballer.  Some of his goals were quite simply brilliant, among which the goal against Leicester City at Filbert Street in a Cup game stands out.  With the Italian team he also shone, and his presence on the pitch was one of the keys to Italy's win against England at Wembley.

250.name: Wise
pages: * The Chelsea captain is a slight man and very temperamental.  At times his strong character eclipses his talent.  He is capable of the best and, at times, the worst, but nobody can deny his class as a footballer.  Loved and respected in the changing rooms, on the pitch his game represents the spirit of the Blues.  For these reasons, nobody was surprised when he extended his contract last year with the London club till the year 2001. Dennis is capable of scoring spectacular goals and providing thousands of scoring passes to his team-mates.  He is an extraordinary footballer and an idol at Stamford Bridge.  Ruud Gullit knows this.

* Dennis Wise is a talented footballer.  His bad temper and his inspiration can cause anything to happen.  He usually plays as a midfielder or link-man with the forwards, generally over on the right, although he can start up from any position on the pitch and make a run towards the rival box.  He has an extraordinary technique, a good turn, skill, excellent playing vision and passes accurately.  So much so that in an international game against Nigeria the statistics showed a 95% success rate for his passes out of 50 interventions, a very high average.  A specialist at taking free-kicks, corners, and penalties, always very accurately. 
* Very temperamental, his character betrays him at times and when protesting, bad temper and toughness take over his game.  Even so, when he is concentrated in the game he is hard to stop.  Although he is right-footed, he can used both feet and can score from any position thanks to his powerful shot.

* FA Cup Champion 88 and 97. 
* Charity Shield Medal 88.

* 12 full international appearances for England.  1 goal.  He made his debut in a win over Turkey (0-1) in a classification game for the Sweden European Championship played on the 1st of May 1991 in Izmir.  Dennis Wise was the scorer of the only goal of the game. 
* A regular in the national line-ups during Terry Venables' reign, he was preselected for the England 96 European Championship but was finally discarded. 
* 3 B-international appearances.  1 goal. 
* 1 under-21 international appearance.

* Dennis Wise, one of the most temperamental players in England football, was trained in the lower ranks of Southampton.  However, the coaches at the Dell rejected him, and so he moved to Wimbledon on the 28th of March 1985. He made his debut in the league on the 11th of May of this same year, in the last game of the season against Cardiff. 
* He lives through Wimbledon's ascent to the First Division.  His progress continues and on the 3rd of July 1990 he is transferred to Chelsea for £1,600,000.  Months later he makes his debut for his country scoring the winner against Turkey. 
* A footballer with a strong character, Wise is one of the players who has received most suspensions.  Up to the end of the 94-95 season he had accumulated 37 yellow cards and been sent off 3 times. 
* His fiery nature also shows itself off the pitch.  A lamentable incident with a taxi-driver at the doors of a pub owned by Terry Venables and the later accusations by the driver brought him to the law courts.  He was also removed from the national team. 
* The Chelsea captain and in good form after his legal problems, he earns a place in Terry Venables team.  However, shortly before the start of the England 96 European Championship he is discarded from the final squad.
* In 1997 he renewed his contract with Chelsea until the year 2001.

* Although at the beginning of the season there were rumours of a possible conflict with Ruud Gullit, the veteran footballer started the season as a member of the starting line-ups.  On the pitch Wise fitted in perfectly with Chelsea's new signings (Lebouef, Di Matteo, Zola...) and made a decisive contribution to the FA Cup title, scoring 3 goals on the road to Wembley.
* In the League Wise played 31 games, 27 from the start, and scored 3 goals. And to finish of the season he renewed his commitment to Chelsea until the year 2001.

251.name: Nicholls
pages: * In recent years the youth squad at Stamford Bridge is producing footballers with great futures.  Mark Nicholls is one of them.  Perhaps he is not as talented as some of his team-mates such as Jody Morris or Paul Hughes, but he united qualities much appreciated by managers.  Last season Ruud Gullit decided to play him leaving a big star as is Vialli on the substitutes' bench.  An obvious indication of the Dutch manager's faith in this young player.

* A striker who scores goals, he shoots with either foot and heads well. Although he isn't so strong physically, he takes advantage of his speed to get behind rival defenders.  Still very young, he needs to gain experience to let his game settle.
x
x

* Trained in the youth squad at Chelsea, he turned professional in July 1995. 
* He made his debut in the Premier League on the 12th of October 1996 in a game against Leicester City played at Filbert Street (1-3).  Nicholls formed part of the starting line-up, but was brought off at half time, replaced by Gianluca Vialli in the 45th minute.

* He made his debut with the first team in a League Cup game against Blackpool, coming on as a substitute for Steve Clarke.  He produced a satisfactory performance, and so Ruud Gullit didn't hesitate to play him from the start in the Premier League game with Leicester City at Filbert Street, leaving the Italian Vialli on the bench.  At the end of the season Nicholls had played 8 league games, 3 as a member of the starting line-up.

252.name: Flo
pages: * Tore Andre Flo is one of the young stars of Norwegian football.  Once his move to Everton was frustrated in March 1997, Chelsea decided to enter the fray and signed him.  Flo had declared that he was a fan of English football and an admirer of Ruud Gullit.  The Dutch manager has the aim of constructing a team capable of challenging for the Championship and needs quality players to do so.  Flo is already one of them, and beside men such as Zola, Vialli and Mark Hughes he can learn all about how to become a star.

* Tore Andre Flo a classic centre forward.  Tall, strong and quick, his presence in the rival area is a synonym for danger.  He is masterful in the air, helped by his height and an extraordinary jump.  He also shoots well with both feet and, although he isn't so technical, he makes up for this with speed, anticipation and a scoring instinct.  Still very young, he has time ahead to improve his ball control, although he is already a fearsome striker.
x

* 15 full international appearances for Norway.  6 goals. 
* 28 under-21 international appearances.  15 goals.

* He started his sporting career at Sogndal IL, the Norwegian First Division club. 
* In 1995, in the ranks of Tromso IL, he was the fifth top scorer in Norway.
* In 1996, defending Brann's colours, he finishes the League as the third top scorer in this competition. 
* In March 1997 he was on the brink of signing for Everton, but the club, entangled in internal problems after Joe Royle's departure, didn't go through with the buy.  Shortly afterwards Flo scored his first hat-trick for the Norwegian team in a friendly against the United Arab Emirates in Dubai.
* On the 5th of May 1997 he was transferred to Chelsea for £300,000.  Flo had offers from Germany, Italy and other teams in the Premier League, but the presence of Ruud Gullit at Stamford Bridge swung the decision to sign for the London club.

* Last season Flo performed to a high level at Brann, the club where he arrived from Tromso.  The Norwegian forward finished the season as the third top scorer in the League, scoring 19 goals in 24 games.  He also continued producing good performances for the Norwegian team.  In a friendly against the United Arab Emirates played in Dubai Flo scored 3 goals.  Shortly before Everton had backed out of signing him.

253.name: Hughes M.
pages: * Mark Hughes is experiencing a second wind of youth at Stamford Bridge. The performance of the Welsh international gets better each year, as if he is reaping the reward for so much accumulated experience.  Ruud Gullit has been able to get the best out of Mark's game he has become a good example for young footballers in England.  In the 97-98 season he will have the chance to add to his already extraordinary honours list.

* Power and good finishing are the most outstanding characteristics of Mark Hughes, a battering-ram forward in his last playing years.  After his spell in Spain and Germany, he now plays more deeply to take greater part in the elaboration of the moves.  Well-built and strong, the Welshman is able to make use of his quality without shying away from collisions with rival defenders.  He drops back to receive the ball, controls it with his good technique and shields it skilfully waiting for his team-mates to join in the attack.  With the years, the rough play of his early days have given way to a more technical, intelligent game, and his contribution to the team is much greater today. 
* In the rival box he doesn't forgive.  He is dominant in the air helped by his powerful jump and bravery.  He is able to find space and shoot on goal with both feet.  But his speciality is always his spectacular volley. He is a master of this.  He sometimes resorts to acrobatics to shoot, hitting the ball very hard and scoring extraordinary goals.

* Cup Winners' Cup Champion 91. 
* European Supercup Champion 91. 
* League Champion 93 and 94. 
* FA Cup Champion 85, 90, 94 and 97. 
* League Cup Champion 92. 
* Charity Shield Medal 93 and 94. 
* Voted "Young Player of the Year" in 1985 by the Footballers Association.
* Voted "Player of the Year" 1989 and 1991.

* 65 full international appearances for Wales.  16 goals.  He made his debut on the 2nd of May 1984 with a 1-0 win over England played in Wrexham.  Hughes was the scorer of the only goal of the game. 
* 5 times under-21 international.  2 goals. 
* Youth and schoolboy international.

* "Sparky" is Mark Hughes nickname since his beginning in football, he arrived at Manchester United aged just 14.  A professional since the 5th of November 1980 and a finalist in the Youth Cup 1982, he didn't make his debut with the first team until the 21st of January 1984, when he substituted for a team-mate in a game against Southampton.  He scored his first goal shortly afterwards in a Cup game against Oxford. 
* Hughes himself tells how, one day when he was very young, he was visited in Manchester by a friend.  Both started to drink and the forward got drunk.  The following day, with a screaming hangover, he called the club to tell them he would miss the training session due to flu.  Nobody knows how, but shortly afterwards the managing body at the club suddenly started to pay him attention. 
* In May 1984 Wales play England in his hometown, Wrexham.  This day Hughes makes his debut for the national team and he scores the only goal of the game. 
* This same year Manchester United are proclaimed Cup Champions after beating Everton in the final with a goal from Norman Whiteside.  Little by little he forces his way into the team, displacing Alan Brazil and Whiteside himself, and also earns the respect of the fans, especially among the Strettford End crowd, the most passionate at Old Trafford. 
* In the 85-86 season United are on the way to the longed-for League title, and even go 10 points clear.  The crowd makes Hughes a hero and saviour of the team.  However, Manchester doesn't manage to keep it up and they miss out on the championship.  Shortly afterwards, on the 1st of July 1986, Mark Hughes is transferred to Barcelona for £2,500,000. 
* At Barcelona he coincides with Gary Lineker and Terry Venables, but Mark is unable to adapt to Spanish football and, at the end of his first season at Barça he is loaned to Bayern Munich.  His spell in Germany is not successful either and so, on the 20th of July 1988, he returns to Old Trafford in exchange for £1,500,000. 
* In 1989 Manchester win another FA Cup title, this time beating Crystal Palace and Hughes scores two goals in the first game (3-3).  He is also voted "Best Player in England" for the first time. 
* He played in the final of the Cup Winners' Cup in 1991 in Rotterdam against Barcelona, and scores United's second, United winning 2-1.  The Welshman had a sweet revenge against the Spanish team.  This same year he is voted "Best Player in England" by the Footballers Association. 
* In February 1995 he signs a new contract for two years with United but, surprisingly, on the 6th of July 1995, he is transferred to Chelsea for £1,500,000.  He arrives at Stamford Bridge at the same time as Ruud Gullit. He makes his debut at home on the 19th of August of this same year in a game against Everton (0-0).  On the 30th of this same month he scores his first goal against Coventry wearing the Blues shirt, and on the 13th of April he scores his first hat-trick for Chelsea, the fourth of his career.

* In his second season at Chelsea Mark Hughes performed to a high level. He forcefully defended his status as a starter and didn't have any problems to reach an understanding with Gianluca Vialli and Gianfranco Zola.  He played 35 league games, taking part from the start in 32 of these and scoring eight goals in the Premier League, one less than Vialli. 
* But the Welsh forward saved his best for the FA Cup competition, where he produced some memorable performances.  Not only did he score 5 goals, 2 in the semi-final against Wimbledon, but his effort was decisive for winning the title.  He was particularly outstanding in the game against Liverpool; Hughes came on after half-time with Liverpool winning 0-2 and after scoring a goal, led the Chelsea comeback, the London team eventually winning 4-2.

254.name: Vialli
pages: * The arrival of Gianluca Vialli at Stamford Bridge caused a commotion amongst the Chelsea fans.  The Italian forward was received as a star, a role which Vialli is already used to playing.  As the season went on his influence in the team grew; he was admired at home and feared away. But curiously, the signing of his fellow countryman Zola was negative for him, as he lost his place in the team after suffering an injury.  So bad was it that there was even talk of a new transfer.  However, Vialli will continue at Stamford Bridge and try to show Gullit that he is the best marksman in the squad.

* Vialli is a very quick forward, tremendously aggressive and a good finisher.  He moves a lot around the whole of the attacking zone to open up gaps for his team-mates, he drifts over to the flanks to receive the ball and take part in the construction of the moves.  Very hard-working, he never shirks on hard work when the other team has the ball.  Although he doesn't have exquisite technique, he makes up for this by his opportunism, intelligence and workmanship.  He is able to find the gaps in the rival box and doesn't hesitate to shoot in forced positions and finishes well in counter-attack moves, where he is like a fish in water.   A good marksman, when he is on form he is unstoppable.

* European Cup Champion 96. 
* Cup Winners' Cup Champion 90. 
* UEFA Cup Champion 93. 
* Italian League Champion 91 and 95. 
* Italian Cup Champion 85, 88, 89 and 95. 
* FA Cup Champion 97.

* 59 full international appearances for Italy.  He made his debut on the 16th of November 1985, in a Poland-Italy game played in Chorzow (1-0). Vialli came on as a substitute for Altobelli in the 78th minute. 
* In the team for several years, he took part in the Mexico 86 World Cup in Italy 90.  In 1995 he renounced his place due to differences with the Italian manager Arrigo Sacchi.

* Trained in Cremonese, a team of his hometown, he makes his league debut with the first team in the 80-81 season, when the club was in the Serie C1. After promotion to the Serie B, he played 3 seasons in this division of Italian football. 
* His magnificent progress didn't go by unnoticed by the big Italian clubs and so, in 1984, he is offered to Juventus, but Boniperti, the president of the Turin club, rejected him.  He signs for Sampdoria, forming a strike partnership with Mancini.  His understanding with him and the finishing was good that they were soon known as the "goal twins".  He was with the Genoa team for eight seasons, in which he scored 85 goals in 223 League games.  He consolidates himself as one of the top marksman in the Italian championship, winning titles and is an undisputed member of the national side. 
* In 1992 Sampdoria get to the European Cup final, but loose to Barcelona in Wembley.  It was one of his last games for Sampdoria. 
* Shortly after the "Wembley Disappointment" he is part of one of the most expensive signings in history when he signed for Juventus of Turin.  £12.5 million was the asking price.  Vialli was 28 years old.  His career with this team was marked by injuries and poor performances, not meeting the expectations placed in him. 
* In the 93-94 season, after a good pre-season, he is injured seriously in the second game of the League and hardly plays for the rest of the year, preventing him from playing the United States World Cup.  However, everything changes in the 94-95 season.  Vialli regains his best form and forms a devastating partnership with Ravanelli, capable of forcing the team's star, Roberto Baggio, into the background. 
* A temperamental footballer and with a strong personality, during the course of his career he has changed his image on several occasions.  His hair has been the direct victim of his moods and Vialli has not thought twice about dying it black, his natural colour, almost platinum blond, and recently he has had his hair shaved off, although this last choice could be due to a receding hairline. 
* In 1995 he renounces his place in the national side and offers himself to play in the Atlanta Olympic Games.  This decision is motivated by a consultation made by Arrigo Sacchi, on the eve of the game against Slovakia, with the regular players in the international side, who rejected the presence of Gianluca.  Afterwards, Sacchi declared that the internationals had changed their mind and accepted the return of the Juventus forward. This caused serious criticism from the player, who accused the manager of a lack of personality. "I didn't know that the call-ups where made by a vote" declared Vialli, who renounced a possible return to the Italian team. 
* In 1996 he plays in and wins the European Cup Final against Ajax of Amsterdam played in Rome.  Vialli, the team's captain and scorer of two goals in the semi-final, plays as a striker alongside Ravanelli, the Italian scorer in the final.  Months later both leave Italy to play in the Premier League.
* His contract with Juventus finishes, and Vialli accepts the offer from Chelsea and signs for the London club.  His arrival is greeted with satisfaction by the fans of the Blues, who consider the Italian the new hero of the team. 
* He made his debut in the Premier League on the 18th of August 1996 in a game against Southampton at the Dell (0-0).  On the 24th of August of this same year he scores his first goal for Chelsea against Coventry at Stamford Bridge.

* The announcement of his signing by Chelsea aroused a lot of expectation among that fans at Stamford Bridge.  He started the season playing from the start in Ruud Gullit's teams, and didn't wait long to show his marksmanship.However, an injury kept him out in December and afterwards it wasn't easy to regain his place, as Gullit was opting for the Hughes-Zola partnership.  In any case, Vialli finished the season as the team's top scorer with 9 -1 from the penalty spot- in 28 league games. 
* A substitute in the final of the FA Cup against Middlesbrough, he came on for his fellow countryman Zola two minutes before the end of the game.

255.name: Heald
pages: * It is not likely to prove to be an easy task for Paul Heald to win back his regular first team place at Wimbledon. Last season his colleague Neil Sullivan proved himself to be a fine goalkeeper and even made his full international debut for Scotland. Heald will have to work especially hard if he wants to dislodge him from the side, although he knows that during the course of the season, eventually, everybody gets a chance. He will be determined to make sure that he is ready to take his when it comes.

* Heald is a powerful goalkeeper with a dominant character, whose progress has been hindered by injury. Slightly inconsistent, his handling from powerful shots on goal lacks the security needed at this level of the game. However, he is a brave, agile goalkeeper who is noticeably improving as he gains in experience. His tremendous will to win guarantees that he will be doing everything he can to try to improve his game.

* After coming through the ranks at Sheffield United, he signed his first professional contract on 30th June 1987, although he didn't get to make his first team debut for the Blades.    %% 
* On 2nd December 1988 he moved on to become a Leyton Orient player, from where he went out on loan to Coventry in March 1992 and Swindon in March 1994. 
* A serious back injury kept him out of action for 18 months, although, on his return to Leyton Orient he put together a tremendous campaign in the 94-95 season.
* In August 1995 he was transfered to Wimbledon for 125,000 pounds as a replacement for Hans Segers. He made his debut at Selhurst Park on 19th of  that same month, making contribution in the Dons 3-2 win over Bolton Wanderers.

* The good form shown by teammate Neil Sullivan, prevented him from makinghimself a regular member of the side at Wimbledon. In fact, he played in just 2 league games, both appearances coming during the run in to the end of the season.

256.name: Sullivan
pages: * After a number of years waiting patiently to make himself first choice in goal at Wimbledon, Neil Sullivan finally got his reward last season. Joe Kinnear handed him the responsibility of taking over in goal and he let nobody down. He showed himself to be a very safe keeper and he kept  up a consistent level of form throughout the whole season, and even managed to make his debut for the full Scotland side. He is now aiming to force  his way into the squad for the World Cup Finals in France. That would be just reward for a man who has had to fight hard to make a name for himself at the top level of the game in England.

* A brave goalkeeper, he stands out for the determination he shows when he comes out off his line, either for crosses or to go down at the feet of opponents. Very safe in one on one situations, he keeps his cool when he is under pressure and is at his best when he is making saves on his goalline. Still young, he needs to acquire more experience in order to  improve his positional play. However, despite this, he is a goalkeeper who has enough quality to go on to play for a number of years in the Premier League.
* 1 full international appearance for Scotland.

* Although he turned professional on 26th July 1988, his league debut for Wimbledon had to wait until 20th April 1991, in a game against Aston Villa. 
* On 1st May 1992 he went out on loan to Crystal Palace, where he made just one appearance.
* During the 94-95 season he forced his way into the side due to the abscence of Segers and managed to keep a clean sheet in the 3 games in which he played. However, he had a stroke of bad luck, when, in the final game of the season, a clash with Nottingham Forest's Jason Lee, saw him ending up seriously injured, just when he seemed to have settle down as first choice in goal for the club where he learned his trade.

* Last season was the best of Neil Sullivan's career. Having established himself in goal for Wimbledon, he played as a member of  the starting line up in 36 of the 38 league games that the side played. He was the star performer in many games, making some spectacular saves, amongst which  can be included two saves he made from penalties against Sheffield Wednesday and Middlesbrough. His outstanding form saw him make his debut for the full Scotland side.

257.name: Roberts
pages: * The 97-98 season will see Andy Roberts make his Premier League debut. The Crystal Palace defender will get the opportunity to play against some of his teammates in the England under-21 side. This is the moment Andy has been waiting for right through his still short career, and, he seemed to be possibly the Eagles' happiest player when, in May 1997 at Wembley he achieved his dream of moving up into the top flight of English football.

* Although in the early stages of his career he played in midfield, at Crystal Palace he generally plays as a sweeper. He has outstanding positional sense which allows him to do a tremendous covering job behind the defence. He is a very accurate passer of the ball, both over short and long distance, helped out by his excellent technique. He has a good shot from outside the area, but, above all, he stands out for the composure he shows in tight situations.
* F.A. Cup winners medal 1991.
* 5 under-21 international appearances for England. He made his debut on 27th March 1995 in a game against the Republic of Ireland in Dublin.

* After coming through the youth ranks at Millwall, he signed professional in October 1991. His debut came on 4th April 1992 against Cambridge United and he scored his first goal for the club on 2nd October 1893 against Watford. 
* He was transfered to Crystal Palace in July 1995 for 2,300,000 pounds, making him the most expensive player in the club's history. He made his debut for the Eagles on 7th October 1995 against Sunderland, while he scored his first goal for the club on 27th May 1996 against Leicester City in the play off for promotion to the Premier League.
* He was chosen player of the year by the Crystal Palace supporters for the 95-96 season.

* Andy Roberts was Crystal Palace's most regular performer during the course of last season, playing in 45 league games. An automatic choice in the side, he made excellent progress throughout the whole season, culminating in an excellent performance at Wembley in the play off for promotion to the Premier League.

258.name: McAllister
pages: * Brian McAllister perfectly fits the description of a one club man. He came through the ranks at Wimbledon, and, although he has never been an automatic first team choice, every time he has been called up into the  side he has always done a satisfactory job. However, Brian has plenty of confidence in his ability and will continue battling to try and make himself, one day, a regular member of the side. Maybe he will do just that during the 97-98 season. Joe Kinnear has the final word.

* A strong central defender, he stands out for the power of his clearances, capable of setting up counterattacks by sending the ball the length of the field towards the oppositions penalty area. Technically limited, he keeps things as simple as possible in defensive duties, where he imposes his physical style of play, and takes full advantage of his effective clearances, both with his head as well as his feet. The qualities he possesses means he seldom makes an attacking contribution. A good marker, he rarely pushes forward into the attack, and never complicates matters when he finds the ball difficult to control, or when he is faced with an opposing forward.
x
* 3 full international apperances for Scotland. He made his debut on 27th May 1997 against Wales .

* After coming through the youth ranks at Wimbledon, he went on to form part of the first team during the 88-89 season. However, he had to wait until 13th January 1990 to make his debut in a game against Arsenal.
* During the 88-89 season he made 8 appearances while on loan at Plymouth. 
* He failed to make a league appearance during the 94-95 season.
* During the 95-96 season, after playing 2 games for Wimbledon, he went out on loan again, this time to Crewe Alexandra of the Second Division.

* He played in the first six games as a member of the starting line up, but suffered an injury which kept him out of the side for a number of weeks. Once he had recovered it took him a while to force his way back. He played in 19 of the final 27 games of the season and his excellent performances took him into the full Scottish international side, who he made his first appearance for in a game against Wales.

259.name: Pearce
pages: * Now at the veteran stage, in recent years Andy Pearce's career as taken a downward turn. He is not a key part of Joe Kinnear's plans, and, as a  result, it would be no surprise if he was eventually transfered to another club where he could demonstrate that he still has plenty of football left in him yet.

* Pearce doesn't stand out for the quality he shows with the ball at his feet. Technically limited, he is not a player who will get the crowd on their feet with outstanding moments of class. However Pearce is very much  aware that he is a defender and, as a result, he applies himself to defensive duties very effectively. He makes the most of his physical power to go into challenges with opposing forwards, knocking them off balance. In the air he is almost unbeatable, especially in defence, although from time to time he will find the back of the net at dead ball situations. He also possesses tremendous leadership qualities at the heart of the defence, positioning and directing his teammates. A good defensive player, he needs to work on his touch on the ball, and try to develop his ball control and passing ability, in an attempt to become more accurate and make more of an attacking contribution.
x
x

* His first club was Coventry, who he joined from modest Halesowen Town. Previously he had played for two amateur clubs, Wednesbury and Stourbridge. He joined Coventry together with two other teammates, Sean Flynn and Tim Clarke, although Clarke soon moved on to Huddersfield Town. His first division debut came on 9th March 1991 at Elland Road against Leeds where he replaced the injured Brian Kilcline. He kept his place in the side until the end of the season and even managed to score the goal that clinched a victory for Coventry at home against Luton Town. Following the departure of both Kilcline and Trevor Peake, he was able to establish himself as the leader of the Coventry defence.
* On 24th June 1993 he was transfered to Sheffield Wednesday for 500,000 pounds. He made his debut on 14th August of that same year at Anfield against Liverpool (2-0).
*  He was transfered to Wimbledon on 22nd November 1995 for 700,000 pounds, making his debut in a 1-0 defeat away at Manchester City on 22nd November 1995.
* Last season was the worst of Andy Pearce's career. He failed to make even the briefest of appearances in the Premier League.

260.name: Thatcher
pages: * Ben Thatcher is one of the most promising full backs in England. After a meteoric rise with Millwallhe was transfered to  Wimbledon for a substantial amount of money. If it hadn't been for an injury, Ben would have gone on to complete a magnificent season, however, his tremendous progress was cut short by stroke of bad luck. Nevertheless, when he is back to full fitness, he will be able to show the supporters that he has more than enough ability to go on to be a success in the Premier League.

* Although, at times, he has played as a central defender, where he has given a good account of himself, he is at his best at left back. Blessed with tremendous physical attributes, his aggressive style of play is a real nightmare for opposing forwards, who he allows no breathing space. Tremendously effective in his defensive duties, he is a spectacular player in the way he judges distances when he covers across the back with great speed. Although a good passer of the ball, he makes only limited attacking contribution. Young and enthusiastic, he just needs to polish up some aspects of his game. Nevertheless, Ben Thatcher is a highly promising footballer.
x

* 3 under-21 international appearances for England.
* An England youth and schoolboy international.

* A member of the Lilleshall School of Excellence. After coming through the youth ranks at Millwall, he signed as a professional on 8th June 1992. He made his debut in a defeat against Leicester City (4-0) on 28th August 1993. 
* His first league goal was truly sensational: A long distance volley against Charlton at The Den. 
* On 5th July 1996 he was transfered to Wimbledon for 1,840,000 pounds. He made his debut on 17th August of that same year in a league game against Manchester United at Selhurst Park (0-3). In November he suffered an ankle injury which kept him out of action until the end of the season.

* He began the season as an automatic member of Joe Kinnear's side and was even a regular member of the England under-21 squad. However, a serious ankle injury which he suffered in November kept him out of the side for the rest of the season. Up to that point, he had played in 9 games, playing as a member of the starting line up in each one.

261.name: Jupp
pages: * Duncan Jupp is one o the best players to have come through the youth ranks %% at Fulham in recent years. His move to Wimbledon represented a step forward in his professional career and there was even speculation surrounding his possible full international debut for Scotland. However, his first season at Selhurst Park was a disappointing one, being given very few opportunities by Joe Kinnear. Duncan will be hoping that the situation changes during the 97-98 seson, although dislodging Kenny Cunningham from the first choice right back spot is likely to prove to be a far from easy task.

* Although his natural position is right back, on occasions he has lined up at the centre of the defence where he is noticeably less comfortable. A player with good mobility, he constantly gets up and down the right flank, although his attacking contribution needs to improve. Quick and  with good vision, he is an intelligent passer of the ball and is always available for his teammates. As he gains more experience he develops his defensive know how, although he needs to also develop physically if he is to make a more significant contribution. Still very young, he has plenty of time to improve.
x
* 10 under-21 international appearances for Scotland.

* After coming through the ranks at Fulham, he signed professional on 12th July 1993. He made his debut in a 1-0 victory against Hartlepool on 14th August of that same year.
* A Scottish under-21 international, he was transfered to Wimbledon on 27th June 1996 for 125,000 pounds.
* He made his Premier League debut on 28th December 1996, in a game which Wimbledon won against Everton at Goodison Park 1-3.

* In his first season at Selhurst Park he was unable to make himself a regular in Joe Kinnear's side. Kenny Cunningham's good form prevented him from forcing his way into the line up, and, in fact, he went on to make just 6 league appearances all season, a poor total for a player more accustomed to playing every week.

262.name: Cunningham
pages: * Kenny Cunningham is one of Joe Kinnear's most important players. The Wimbledon manager values very highly the enormous amount of work that he does at right back and has no hesitation in naming him in the starting line up. He seems to get better year after year and has made himself one of the regulars in the Republic of Ireland side. If Ireland finally manage to qualify for the World Cup Finals, it would be no surprise to see Kenny on his way to France.

* A versatile player he generally plays at right back, although he has occasionally done a job down the left and has even played as a central defender. A player with a good touch on the ball, he generally chooses the right option when he is passing it on to his teammates. Although he hardly  ever finds the back of the net, he does create plenty of goalscoring chances for his colleagues.

* 10 full international appearances for the Republic of Ireland. 
* 2 "B" international appearances. 
* 4 under-21 international appearances.
* Youth international.

* He moved from modest Tolka Rovers to join Millwall on 18th September 1989. %% He made his debut on 17th March 1990 in a game against Norwich. 
* After 136 games and 1 goal for Millwall, he was transfered to Wimbledon on 9th November 1994. As part of the deal, valued at 1,250,000 pounds, another ex-Millwall player, Jon Goodman, was also on the move. 
* He made his Premier League debut on 15th November 1994, in a game against Newcastle at Selhurst Park (3-2).

* For the third consecutive season, Kenny Cunningham was Wimbledon's first choice right back, and was apparently unaffected by the arrival at Selhurst Park of Duncan Jupp. He played in 36 league games, all of those starting appearances, and, although he failed to score himself, he set up plenty  of goals for the rest of the side due to the quality of his passes from out on the flank.

263.name: Kimble
pages: * After a number of years toiling away in the lower divisions, Wimbledon offered Alan Kimble the opportunity to play in the Premier League. The Dagenham born defender hasn't let his big chances pass him by and has adapted perfectly to the "crazy gang's" style. Year after year the veteran full back earns himself the right to a first team place and nothing would suggest that the 97-98 season is likely to be aby different.

* He generally plays at left back, although he can also do a good job on the right. Technically limited, his strength and commitment are his main assets. A good marker, he has a very simple way of playing the game: win the ball and get it into the opposing penalty area as quickly as possible. He is a genuine specialist of the long ball game, although he also possesses a powerful shot from long distance.
* Third Division winners medal in 90-91 with Cambridge.

* After coming through the youth ranks at Charlton Athletic, he took the step up to the first team squad on 8th August 1984. His debut came on 16th April 1985 in a game against Sheffield United.
* On 23rd August 1985 he went out on loan to Exeter United. 
* He became a free agent in the summer of 1986. On 26th August of that same year he signed for Cambridge United, where he went on to win a Third Division Championship winners medal in 1991.
* On 27th July 1993 he was transfered to Wimbledon for 175,000 pounds. He made his debut on 14th August in a victory for the Dons away against West Ham United (0-2).
* During the 94-95 season he suffered a series of injuries which kept him out o the side.

* Once again Alan Kimble was first choice left back for Wimbledon. Although he began the season left out of Joe Kinnear's side, he didn't take long to win back his regular place in the manager's line up. At the end of the season he had played in 31 league games making 28 starting appearances .

264.name: Blackwell
pages: * Another product of the prolific Wimbledon youth system, Dean Blackwell's career has been affected by injury problems which have prevented him from reaching greater heights. Fortunately, last season he was able to go through a long spell without ending up in the treatment room. As a result he was able to show his best form. Dean has high hopes for the 97-98 season, and is confident that Joe Kinnear will continue to make him a regular member of the side.

* His natural position is at the heart of the defence. Technically limited, his strength makes him a dificult player to get the better of. He is less effective when he comes up against quick, skillful forwards. Blackwell's attacking contribution is limited to his participation at dead ball situations.
* 6 under-21 international appearances for England.

* He joined Wimbledon as a schoolboy in May 1985. On 7th July 1988 he turned professional, making his debut on 16th September 1989 coming on as a  substitute at Wimblendon's old home, Plough Lane, in a game against Manchester City.
* On 15th March 1990 he was loaned out to Plymouth Argyle.
* During the 91-92 season he underwent a hernia operation. 
* A persistent injury during the 94-95 season prevented him from making a Premier League appearance. He was unable to get back into action until February 1996.

* Last season Dean Blackwell did a satisfactory job for manager Joe Kinnear The central defender made a decisive contribution to Wimbledon's excellent season. He played in 27 games making 22 starting appearances.

265.name: Perry
pages: * Chris Perry seems to get better with each season. Under the guidance of Joe Kinnear, the coach who first showed full confidence in him, the Wimbledon player has become one of the safest defenders in the country. Many people think that the time has come for him to be given a chance in the full England side.

* Perry plays at the heart of the defence. A strong composed footballer, he is decisive when he needs to go in hard. Although he is not particularly tall, he is safe in the air, helped out by his positioning and his ability to get up above opponents. His weakness is his ball control, a basic technique he needs to work on. His competitive nature will help him to improve this aspect of his game and force his way into the elite of English football.

* He arrived at Wimbledon as a schoolboy in December 1987. He had to wait until 2nd July 1991 to turn professional, while his league debut came almost three days later on 4th April 1994 against Liverpool.   %% 
* He scored his first goal in the Premier League on 29th January 1997, in a game against Manchester United at Old Trafford: Wimbledon lost 2-1. %% 
* As he has repeatedly stated, he has been a Wimbledon supporter since he was a boy.

* Chris Perry had a magnificent season. He was very much the leader of the Wimbledon defence and managed to come out on top in the majority of his confrontations with the best strikers in England. He played from the start in 37 of the 38 league games and even allowed himself the luxury of scoring a goal at Old Trafford. His second goals of the season came at Gresty Road against Crewe Alexandra. Due to his tremendous performances during the course of the season, he has been mentioned as a possible member of the full England squad.

266.name: Reeves
pages: * Alan Reeves has lost a good part of the influence he once had in the first team squad at Wimbledon. He hardly played during the course of last season and there is very little to suggest that the 97-98 campaign will be any different. As a result, he would seem to be one of the prime candidates to be leaving Selhurst Park has soon as the opportunity comes along.

* He can play either at the heart of the defence or as a defensive midfield player, a position he played in during his first season at Wimbledon. He is a good short passer of the ball, although he occasionally lacks accuracy. He is more comfortable when he is asked to do a job in defensive positions, especially in the air. He needs to be more decisive in attack and take advantage of his ability to get up above opponents to get on the end of set pieces. At the same time he also needs to try to control his temperament so as to avoid going in too hard.

* Whilst playing for modest Heswall, he signed or Norwich City on 2nd September 1988. He went out on loan to Gillingham on 9th February 1989 making his debut two days later in a game against Bristol City.
* On 18th August of that same year he was transfered to Chester City for 10,000 pounds. He became a free agent in the summer of 1991, taking advantage of the fact by moving to Rochdale on 2nd July 1991.
* He took the definitive step up to the Premier League on 6th September 1994, when Wimbledon signed him for 300,000 pounds to cover the departure of John Scales. In his first few months with the Dons he had a number of disciplinary problems.
* He made his Premier League debut on 10th September 1994, at home against Leicester City (2-1). On 24th of that same month he scored his first goal in a Wimbledon shirt against QPR.

* He failed to make himself a regular part of Joe Kinnear's plans. He played in just 2 league games, coming on as a substitute twice towards the end of the season. Far too little action for a player who is now at the veteran stage of his career.

267.name: Solbakken
pages: * After two years on his trail, Joe Kinnear finally managed to sign Stale Solbakken. The Norwegian midfielder is one of the key men in the Norwegian national squad and played a decisive role in the Scandinavian country's  qualification for the World Cup Finals in France. His signing is an excellent reinforcement for the Wimbledon midfield which he will give greater attacking power. Solbakken will be hoping that he can go on to prove to be as much of a success in the Premier League as several of his colleagues in the Norwegian national side already have been.

* He can play in a number of different positions in the midfield. Wherever he plays Stale Solbakken shows tremendous attacking ability, regularly finding the back of the net. A very strong footballer, he also possesses good technique which allows him to distribute the ball effectively and orchestrate the side's attacking play.
x
* 37 full international appearances for Norway, scoring 4 times.

* He came through the ranks at modest Norwegian club Grue. His second club was Ham-Kam, where he played until he signed for Lillestrom in 1994. 
* He was Lillestrom's leading scorer in 1995, with 13 goals.
* On 13th October 1997, he was transfered to Wimbledon for 225,000 pounds. Solbakken asked Joe Kinnear to delay his move until he was sure that Lillestrom had finally avoided relegation.
x

268.name: Hughes M.
pages: * Oyvind Leonhardsen departure to Liverpool had left a difficult gap for Wimbledon to fill. The Dons' manager, Joe Kinnear, decided to sign Michael Hughes with the season already having got underway in order to cover the Norwegian's absence. As a result, it seems highly likely that the ex-West Ham player will get plenty of chances at Selhurst Park to show exactly what he can do.

* A quick, left footed winger, Michael Hughes generally plays tight down either touchline, although it is on the left where he is at his best. From that position he takes advantage of his speed off the mark to get to the byline, from where he puts over some dangerous crosses. Blessed with  an exquisite touch in his left foot, Hughes is a very skillful player, who can apparently go past players with ease and who also has a powerful shot. However, despite his ability he doesn't stand out for his goalscoring.
x

* 31 full international appearances for Northern Ireland, scoring once. He made his debut on 13th November 1991 in a 2-1 defeat against Denmark in Odense.
* He scored his first goal on 2nd June 1992, in a friendly game against Germany in Bremen (1-1).
* 2 under-23 international appearances.
* 1 under-21 international appearance.

* In october 1985 Michael Hughes joined the youth ranks at Manchester City. A trainee from July 1988 he turned professional on 17th August of that same year, shortly after his 17th birthday.
* He made his league debut on 15th october 1988, away against Plymouth. 
* In 1989 he was on the losing side in the F.A. Youth Cup final against Watford.
* A regular member of the side at Maine Road since September 1991, his progress didn't go unnoticed by Northern Ireland manager Billy Bingham, who gave him his debut in November against Denmark.
* At the end of the 91-92 season he was transfered to Strasbourg for 450,000 pounds. In France he was a regular member of the side for two complete seasons.
* On 29th November 1994 he was loaned out by the French club to West Ham. He made his debut on 4th December in a 2-1 defeat against Queens Park Rangers. 
* He is especially well remembered by Manchester United fans for his goal in the final game of the 94-95 season which snatched the title away from the Old Trafford club, handing it over to Blackburn Rovers. The game ended in a 1-1 draw.
* On 2nd October 1995 he went out on loan again to the Hammers from Strasbourg. Once he had completed his contract with the French club in June 1996, West Ham decided to sign him on a permanent basis.
* On 25th September 1997 he was transfered to Wimbledon for 1,600,000 pounds. With his signing manager Joe Kinnear was attempting to cover the gap left by the departure of the Norwegian Oyvind Leonhardsen to Liverpool.

* He began last season in outstanding form, scoring three goals in the first seven games. Although he wasn't able to maintain the same goalscoring rate throughout the season, he kept up his tremendous form during the course of the 33 league games in which he played. An automatic member of the side, he almost always played down the left, although at times the team needed him to perform down the opposite flank.

269.name: Hughes C.
pages: * Ceri Hughes is one of the few nes faces in the Wimbledon squad for the 97-98 season. The Welsh international perfectly fits the description of the type of player who could become a success with Joe Kinnear's side. He is competitive, forceful, brave and, occasionally, aggressive. As a result, many experts predict along and successful career for him at Selhurst Park.

* A talented midfielder, he holds nothing back as he goes about his defensive duties. Ceri Hughes is a strong, hardworking footballer, who is a good passer of the ball and who possesses tremendous shooting ability. However, all too often he is let down by his temperament, which causes him to get into trouble with referees.
x

* 6 full international appearances for Wales. 
* 2 "B" international appearances. 
* A Welsh youth international.

* A product of the Luton Town youth system, he made his first team debut during the 89-90 season.
* In November 1994 he suffered ruptured cruciate knee ligaments, which kept him out of action for a number of months.
* In June 1997 he joined Wimbledon for 400,000 pounds.

* For the first time in a couple of years, Ceri Hughes was able to enjoy a suspension free season and one with far fewer injuries than normal. As a result he became one o the most important players at Luton Town. He played from the start in all 36 of the league games in which he played, scoring 4 times. His tremendous performances allow him to get back into the Welsh international side, replacing Vinny Jones in a friendly game against the Republic of Ireland. Unfortunately, an injury kept him out of the final few games of the season, including the play-offs.

270.name: Ardley
pages: * A young player who has spent all of his career at Wimbledon,for Neil Ardley each week of the season represents a new battle to try to force his way into the side. When he manages to make an appearance he gives 100% in an attempt to help clinch a victory for his one and only club. Last season Joe Kinnear gave him the chance to settle down in the first team and Neil didn't let him down. The 97-98 season should see him finally establish himself.

* A defensive midfielder who generally plays in the centre of the midfield, playing tight to the right hand touchline. Although he is not a bad passer of the ball, his main asset is his strength, which makes him a very difficult player to get the better of and contain throughout the whole of the ninety minutes. He has an excellent shot at goal from distance, which makes him a very dangerous player from dead ball situations.
* 10 under-21 international appearances for England.

* Having been a member of the Wimbledon youth set up since 1988, he made his Selhurst Park debut on 20th April 1991, making a contribution to the Dons' 2-1 victory over Aston Villa. On 29th July o that same year he signed his first professional contract.

* Last season was the best of Neil Ardley's career. He managed to make himself a regular member of the side and showed his versatility by playing  in a number of positions both in midfield as well as at the back. He scored 2 superb goals. The first came direct from a free kick in a game against Leeds United, while the second flew past Chelsea keeper Kevin Hitchcock who could do nothing to stop Ardley's powerful shot from outside the area.

271.name: Earle
pages: * Although his breakthrough into the top flight came late in his career, Robbie Earle has managed to make a name for himself as one of the best midfield players in the Premier League. This veteran player seems to be capable of getting better with every year that goes by, and his now almost a legend in the history of Wimbledon football club. Such is his influence that it is almost unimaginable to think of Joe Kinnear's side taking the field without Robbie Earle.

* Either in the center of the midfield or playing behind the main two strikers, Earle is a tremendously attack minded player. He is a quick, strong footballer, who also possesses good technique. His pace allows him to beat defenders to the ball, he also makes good late runs from deep positions and is capable of appearing out of the blue at the far post. He has a good shot from distance, is a good header of the ball and has all the qualities he needs to do a good job as a centre forward. Although Robbie Earle has been something of a late developer, when he stays free from injuries and gets the regular first team football any player needs, he is capable of becoming a genuine matchwinner who could do a job for any side in the Premier League.

* As a youth team player with Port Vale, Earle moved up to the first team squad on 5th July 1982, at just 17 years of age. On 26th August of that same year he made his debut in a 1-0 victory over Swindon.
* He was a member of the Port Vale sides that won promotion to the Third and then to the Second Division. Following the departure of Andy Jones, he managed to average a goal every three games, a high scoring rate for a %%   midfield player.
* On 19th July 1991  he was transfered to Wimbledon for 750,000 pounds. 
* During the 94-95 season he suffered a series of injuries which kept him out of action. Up to end of that season he had been booked a total of 12 times. During the course of his career he has scored 1 hat-trick.

* For yet another season Robbie Earle successfully kept his place as a regular member of the side at Wimbledon. He scored 7 goals in 32 league games, which made him one of the top scoring midfield players in the Premier League. He also managed to score in every round of the F.A. Cup up to the semi-finals. Thanks to his outstanding performances, Robbie was on the verge of making his full England debut, although, eventually, Glenn Hoddle denied him that opportunity.
