272.name: Castledine
pages: * Stewart Castledine is another of the players to have come through the ranks at Wimbledon, and, as a result, learned all about the clubs very characteristic way of doing things at a very young age. When he steps on to the pitch the supporters instantly recognised that Castledine is very much a typical Wimbledon product. Unfortunately for him he has never managed to make himself a regular member of the side, and, during the course of last season, played more games for the reserves than he did for the first team. Nothing would suggest that the 97-98 season is likely to see his situation at the club change very dramatically.

* A defensive midfield player, he can play either in the centre of the park or pushed out wide towards the right hand side. Technically limited he keeps up a constant work rate, attempting to win back possession. An aggressive footballer and blessed with tremendous physical attributes, if he improved his touch on the ball, the team would no doubt benefit more from the vision he undoubtedly possesses.
x

* A product of the Wimbledon youth system, Castledine took the step up to the first team on 2nd July 1991. He had to wait until 25th April 1992 to make his league debut in a game against Norwich at Carrow Road.
* He was the scorer of Wimbledon's first goal of the 94-95 season, a goal which earned the Dons a draw against Coventry. Up to the end of that season he had never been booked.
* On 25th August 1997 he went out on oan to Wycombe Wanderers, where he made 7 league appearances scoring 3 times.

* He made just 7 first team appearances during the course of last season,  6 of those coming in the league. He scored with an outstanding volley against Leeds United in one of the last games of the Premier League season. He also managed to score on his only appearance in the League Cup, connecting with a powerful header which flew past a surprised Luton Town goalkeeper.

273.name: Fear
pages: * Like many of his colleagues, Peter Fear is a genuine Wimbledon product, having arrived at the club in 1987 at just 14 years of age. He obviously had to wait a number of years before making his first team debut with the Selhurst Park club. That day, Peter was finally rewarded for all the hard work he had put in, with his sights firmly set on a first team place. Now he is out to make that place his own week after week.

*  He generally plays as a midfielder, directing the teams attacks from the centre of the midfield or from a position out slightly wider on the left hand side. His main asset is his versatility, which allows him to also do a job at the centre of the defence an intelligent footballer, he has vision and good basic technique which he uses to hit accurate long passes. Capable of creating plenty of danger with the balls he plays through to his teammates, he needs more regular first team football in order to consistently force his way into the starting line up. Perhaps he would be more at home at a club which played a different style of football to Wimbledon's.
* 3 under-21 international appearances for England.

* A product of the prolific Wimbledon youth system, he took the step up to the first team squad on 2nd July 1992. He made his league debut on 10th February 1993 in a game against Arsenal.
* He scored his first league goal on 26th March 1994, against Leeds United at Selhurst Park (1-0).

* A member of the starting line up in 9 of the 18 league games in which he played, Peter Fear went through another season without managing to settle down in Joe Kinnear's side. He was the scorer of a very important goal in the league cup which knocked out Luton Town in extra-time, taking Wimbledon through to the next round.

274.name: Kennedy
pages:
* He was transfered to Wimbledon in March 1998 for 2.000.000 pounds. 
* The Anfield supporters had high hopes of Mark Kennedy. The Irishman has shown plenty of class, but is yet to be given the opportunities he needs to really demonstrate what he is capable of. He is now certainly approaching the age where he needs to develop from being simply a good prospect into becoming the real thing.

* Kennedy began his playing career as a centre forward. Blessed with plenty of talent and a prodigious left foot, slowly but surely he has gone on to play wider, operating now as a left winger, an area from where he creates plenty of danger. He is a very quick player with an easy change of direction and the ability to throw defenders off balance with his deft sway of the hips. He also possesses a powerful shot from outside the penalty area with his left foot. His class and youth would suggest that he has a highly promising future ahead of him.

* 12 full international appearances for the Republic of Ireland.
* 7 under-21 international appearances. 
* A youth and schoolboy international.

* After coming through the ranks at Millwall, he signed his first professional contract with the London club on 6th May 1992.
* In the 93-94 season he played in the final of the F.A. Youth Cup.
* On 21st March 1995, he was transfered to Liverpool in exchange for £1,500,000. 
* He made his Liverpool debut on 9th April 1995 in a Premier League game against Leeds United at Anfield. He didn't manage to find the back of the net but did hit the post. 
* During the 96-97 season he made eight first team appearances for Liverpool in official, competitive matches. In none of those games however did he play from the start.

* He made just five Premier League appearances during the course of last season coming on as a substitute in each of those games. As a result, his contribution to the side was never more than merely anecdotal.

276.name: Leaburn
pages: * Carl Leaburn was transfered to Wimbledon on the 8th of January 1998. He was Charlton's top scorer in the last two seasons.

* Carl Leaburn is a very strong forward who is able to hold onto the ball, waiting for his teammates to join in the attack. He is excellent in the air and so is very dangerous at set-plays due to his height and decisiveness when heading. Also with long balls, he usually wins them and lays them off for some other team member coming up from behind to collect.  He is not very skilful with the ball at his feet but in a 50-50 situation he almost always makes his strength and long legs pay. He uses the right better than the left, above all when distributing the ball although he normally receives and passes quickly.  When it comes to shooting, he doesn't think about it, letting fly from any position and whenever an opportunity presents itself. He is fairly quick.
* Top scorer at Charlton Athletic in the 95-96 and 96-97 seasons.
* Leaburn has been an English youth international.

* Trained in the youth squad at Charlton Athletic, he signed for this club in April 1987 as a professional footballer. His first game with their shirt on is on 24th March 1987 against Oxford United and he opens his account on 4th May 1987 against Newcastle United.
* Leaburn is loaned to Northampton Town in March 1990, making his debut on 24th March 1990 against Blackpool.

* Once again, Carl Leaburn was one of the most important men for Charlton, finishing up as top scorer for the second year running. However, the statistics weren't as good as in previous years and he finished with just 8 goals in 44 games, below his career average.

277.name: Euell
pages: * Jason Euell's breakthrough into the Premier League in 1995 was a spectacular one. Since then his appearances for Wimbledon's first team have been as sporadic as they have promising. Jason is ove of the best prospects at the club, and, if he maintains his progress, he could go on to become one of the stars of English football in the not too distant future.

* A striker blessed with outstanding speed and no lack of skill and ability, he stands out for his direct style of play, which makes him a player who is always looking to go for goal. A constant battler, he keeps rival defenders under constant pressure, making it difficult for the opposing side to set up counterattacks. Still very young, he has all the qualities of a complete centre forward, possessing, in addition to his fine technique, a real striker's eye for goal. If he maintains his progress, he could well become a player to watch in the next few seasons.
x
x

* After coming through the youth ranks at Wimbledon, he made his league debut %% on 28th October 1995 at Selhurst Park against Southampton. Although he managed to find the back of the net, he was unable to prevent the side from losing 1-2. However, his performance was highly praised in all the newspapers' sports pages.

* In his second season in the first team he managed to make 7 league appearances, although he only played from the start 4 times. Howeve, he demonstrated that he is continuing to make progress. He scored two goals, once against Liverpool in the second to last game of the season and once against Sunderland in the last match of the campaign, A goal which sent Peter Reid's side down to the First Division.

278.name: Clarke
pages: * Andy Clarke is now in his eighth season at Wimbledon. Although is appearances in the side are becoming less frequent, the veteran striker remains confident that he can continue to make a goalscoring contribution to help keep the club in the Premier League. He enjoys the backing of the Selhurst Park fans, being, as he is, one of the most popular players at the club.

* A competitive striker, he has great mobility and strength and has a good touch on the ball in both feet. He stands out for his direct approach, always looking to quickly go for goal, although he is at his best when he plays tight down the touchline, as an out and out winger. He has a tremendous shot from distance, which he never hesitates to use when he gets the slightest of opportunities. However, his defensive contribution is not what it could be, as he reserves his pace and energy for the attacking side of the game.
* GM Vauxhall Conference winners medal 90-91.

* He began his career at Barnet under the guidance of manager Barry Fry. Fry sent videos of Andy Clarke to some of the most important clubs in England and, eventually, it was Wimbledon who decided to sign him.
* He was transfered to Wimbledon on 21st February 1991 for 250,000 pounds. He made his debut for the Dons on 2nd March of that same year in a game against Norwich.
* During the 94-95 season, although he was generally a substitute, he managed to score two vitally important goals; one against Newcastle and another against Liverpool.

* Although he was a member of the starting line up in the first three games of the season, Andy Clarke was barely given a chance in the first team and, as a result, was a regular member of Wimbledon's reserve side. He played in 11 league games, making 4 starting appearances and scoring once, against West Ham at Upton Park.

279.name: Goodman
pages: * When Wimbledon decided to sign Jon Goodman and Ken Cunningham in 1994, Goodman was top scorer at Milwall. His move to Wimbledon represented, on the one hand, a step up to the Premier League, and, on the other, the  beginning of a battle for a place in the side with other quality strikers. However, he is yet to win the full confidence of Joe Kinnear. Jon will be hoping that during the 97-98 season his luck will change and that he can become more of an influence at Wimbledon.

* A strong, bustling striker with a genuine goalscorer's instinct, Goodman is an untiring worker, who fights for every ball and never shirks physical contact. As a result he is a real nightmare for the opposing defence. He is a good header of the ball, a quality he uses to good effect to score the majority of his goals. He occasionally plays as an attacking midfield player or as a winger, preferably down the right hand side. He makes a significant contribution defensively, keeping opponents under constant pressure, forcing them into mistakes. He is a player who was born to play for Wimbledon, due to his character and attitude out on the park.
* 4 full international appearances for the Republic of Ireland.

* After coming through the ranks at modest Bromley, he was transfered to Millwall on 20th August 1990 for 50,000 pounds. His debut came on 26th December of that same year in a game against Leicester.
* As top scorer at Millwall, he signed for Wimbledon on 9th November 1994 together with his teammate Ken Cunningham.
* He made his Premier League on 19th November 1994, in a game against Newcastle at Selhurst Park (3-2).

* It proved to be impossible for Jon Goodman to force his way into the forward line at Wimbledon on a regular basis with Joe Kinnear preferring to play Ekoku, Gayle and Holdsworth. He played in 13 league games, making 6 staring appearances. However, he did make his presence felt with the Republic of Ireland, playing for his country in a game against Wales in Cardiff.

280.name: Gayle
pages: * Although he didn't come through the ranks at Wimbledon, Marcus Gayle's style of play is very much in the Wimbledon mould. A real fighter, his goals are fast becoming a regular feature of matches at Selhurst Park and, if he maintains the progress he has shown over the last two seasons, he will once again be making an important contribution at a club where he has settled in perfectly.

* A strong striker, he is at his best playing on the left hand side of the attack. He has good technique in both feet which allows him to send accurate crosses over into the penalty area. However, his main characteristic is his constant battling throughout the ninety minutes. He never gives anything up as lost and keeps opposing defenders under constant pressure, preventing them from bringing the ball out as they would like. A good header of the ball, he regularly finds the back of the net. Still young he has plenty of time to improve.
* Third Division winners medal, 91-92, with Brentford.
* 1 England youth international appearance.

* His league debut for Brentford came on 22nd October 1988 in a game against Preston at a time when Marcus hadn't yet signed professional terms. He finally turned professional on 6th July 1989. 
* On 24th March 1994 he was transfered to Wimbledon for 250,000 pounds. 
* He made his Premier League debut on 26th March 1994, in a game against Leeds United.
* During the 94-95 season he played in 14 of the first 16 league games, however, an injury kept him out until February 1995.

* He was one of the best players at Wimbledon during the course of the season. He was an automatic choice for Joe Kinnear, and went on to make himself top scorer in all competitions. He scored 8 league goals, 3 less than a Ekoku, 3 in the League Cup and 2 in the F.A. Cup. Some of his goals were especially spectacular, such as the one he scored against Chelsea at Stamford Bridge and the header which knocked Manchester United out of the F.A. Cup.

281.name: Harford
pages: * Mick Harford is one of the most well travelled players in English football and is one of the best examples of the classic style of British centre forwards. After more than 20 years as a professional, Harford is bringing a dignified end to a tremendous career. He is a real example to all budding young footballers.

* A centre forward in the purest English style. His main strength is his power in the air, where he takes full advantage of his height and ability to get up above opposing defenders. He is not particularly skillful with the ball at his feet, although he is capable of holding it up and shielding it with his body as he waits for his teammates to come through in support. More experienced than most, Harford makes the most of his know how to get into good positions inside the penalty area and get in unexpected efforts on goal. He will occasionally pull out wide to creates space for his colleagues in the attack.
* League Cup winners medal in 87-88 with Luton Town.

* 2 full international appearances for England. He made his debut on 17th February 1988 in Tel Aviv in a game against Israel (0-0). On 14th September of that same year he made his second, and final, appearance for England against Denmark at Wembley (1-0).
* 1 "B" international appearance.

* During the course of his career he has scored 8 hat-tricks, a total which only 7 players still in the game have equalled. His first hat-trick came on 29th Febraury 1980 against Wigan. He scored his last one on 31st October 1990 against Sunderland, ironically his home town club.
* He came through the ranks at modest Lambton Street. On 6th July 1977 he signed for Lincoln City, where he made his debut on 10th October of that same year against Gillingham.
* His transfer to Newcastle was set at 180,000 pounds and went through on 24th December 1980. However, shortly afterwards on 24th August 1981, he moved on to Bristol City who paid out 160,000 pounds to take him to Ashton Gate. 
* On 26th March 1982 Harford was transfered again, this time to Birmingham City. His valuation in the transfer market had dropped to 100,000 pounds. 
* On 13th December 1984 he was transfered to Luton Town for 250,000 pounds.  
* On 18th January 1990 he was transfered again, this time to Derby County for 450,000 pounds.
* On 12th September 1991 he returned to Luton Town for 325,000 pounds. 
* On 13th August 1992 he moved to Chelsea for 300,000 pounds.
* On 18th March 1993 he was transfered to Sunderland for 250,000 pounds. 
* On 12th July 1993 he ended up at Coventry for 200,000 pounds. 
* On 18th August 1994 he was transfered to Wimbledon for 50,000 pounds. He made his debut on 20th August, in the first game of the season against Coventry at Highfield Road (1-1).

* He spent the majority of the season on the substitutes bench, but, whenever he was called upon, he showed himself to be an exemplary professional. He scored 1 goal in the 13 league appearances he made. A goal which, of course, he scored with a powerful header against West Ham at Selhurst Park.

282.name: Ekoku
pages: * Efan Ekoku has made a name for himself among the best strikers in the Premier League. The Nigerian international's goals have more than paid back the fee Wimbledon handed over to sign him, a sum which at the time was a club record. Efan has made himself a genuine idol at Selhurst Park and, if he maintains his outstanding form, it would be no surprise to see him playing for Nigeria in the 1998 World Cup Finals in France.

* A striker who generally operates down the right hand side, where he takes full advantage of his pace to go past opposing defenders. He is particularly dangerous on the break, and, when he is given space, he is a very difficult player to stop. He likes to go straight for goal, although, occasionally he is guilty of trying to do too much on his own. Despite not being  particularly skillful, on the run he can take men on with apparent ease. An opportunist striker, with a good shot, he is a regular goalscorer. Ekoku is very much a player to watch, and could probably do an even better job in a side which attempts to play a more sophisticated style of football.
* 5 full international appearances for Nigeria.

* Although born in Manchester, Ekoku retains the Nigerian nationality that has been passed on to him through his family.
* After coming through the ranks at modest Sutton United, he was transfered to Bournemouth on 11th May 1990 for 100,000 pounds. He made his league debut on 25th August of that same year against Brentford.
* On 26th March 1993 he moved on to Norwich City for 500,000 pounds. 
* He travelled to the 1994 World Cup Finals in the United States as part of the Nigerian squad, although he saw only a few minutes of action. 
* His move to Wimbledon on 14th October 1994 caused something of a surprise in English football. The Selhurst Park club paid out 900,000 pounds to take him to south London.
* Ironically, Ekoku's first goal in a Wimbledon shirt was enough to beat his previous club Norwich 1-0 at Selhurst Park. In February 1995 he suffered an ankle injury which prevented him from playing in a number of games.

* Efan Ekoku was, without doubt, one of Wimbledon's best players during the course of last season. He ended the campaign as the Dons' top goal scorer in the league, finding the back of the net 11 times. He formed a tremendous attacking partnership with Marcus Gayle. The Nigerian international scored one of the season's most outstanding goals, taking the ball past a number of defenders before sliding it home against West Ham at Upton Park.

283.name: Clarke
pages: * Matt Clarke's debut in the Premier League couldn't be worse.  In the last game of last season he was sent off nine minutes after coming on as a substitute for Kevin Pressman.  The Owls keeper didn't deserve the red card.  So long waiting for his chance to come, and when it does, he can't seize it.  In the 97-98 season he will return to Pressman's shadow, but this time his future looks a little more favourable.

* Matt Clarke is a goalkeeper with good reflexes.  His quality allows him to make some spectacular saves.  He is safe when trapping low shots, while in the air he plays with authority.  A keeper with a lot of potential, he has an exceptional natural ability and just needs to acquire a bit more experience at the highest level.  Without doubt, we are looking at a promising keeper whose future looks splendid.
x
x

* A product of the Rotherham United youth squad, he arrives in the first team on the 28th of July 1992 and plays 9 league games in his first season as a professional (92-93).
* Undisputed first choice since 1994, he is made the team's captain in the 95-96 season, leading Rotherham to a 2-1 win over Shrewsbury Town in the final of the Auto Windscreens Shield played at Wembley.
* On the 5th of July 1996 he is transferred to Sheffield Wednesday for £300,000.  In principle Clarke arrives at Hillsborough to cover for the departure of Chris Woods, Kevin Pressman's substitute.
* He made his debut in the Premier League on the 11th of May 1997 after coming on for the injured Kevin Pressman in a game against Liverpool at Hillsborough.  It was the last game of the season.  Nine minutes later he was sent off for handball outside the area.

* Matt Clarke had the worst season of his sporting career.  Without having played a single minute in the League, he had to come on as a substitute for the injured Pressman in the last game of the season.  Unfortunately, nine minutes later he was sent off for playing the ball with his hand outside the area.  A year to forget.

284.name: Pressman
pages: * Very much an institution at Hillsborough, Kevin Pressman goes into his thirteenth season as a professional with the hope of keeping his place in the Sheffield goal one season more.  It won't be easy as Matt Clarke is a very promising keeper and will fight hard to find a place in the team. On the other hand, Kevin Pressman's other dream of making it to the national team looks further away each day.

* secure between the posts and when intercepting, Pressman is a keeper with good reflexes and excellent positioning.  These two qualities help make up for the disadvantage of being a little overweight, something he should watch.  The aerial balls are where he has his biggest problems, as he doesn't make his presence felt both for the forwards and for his own defence.  Perhaps his biggest virtue is his regularity.  He doesn't often make amazing saves, but nor does he make unforgivable mistakes.
x

* 2 B-international appearances for England.
* 1 under-21 international appearance on the 13th of September 1988 in a game against Denmark played at Watford.  Pressman comes on for Nigel Martyn, the Crystal Palace goalkeeper.
* Youth and schoolboy international.

* His sporting life starts at Sheffield Wednesday.  He joins the club in November 1985 as an apprentice.  Almost two years later he makes his debut in the League on the 5th of September 1987 against Southampton.  The injury to the first choice keeper, Martin Hodge, allows him to play a total of 11 league games.  In that season maintains up a good level of play, except in the last game of the season where the team loose 5-1.
* However, he didn't have much continuity in the Sheffield goal, neither in this season nor in the following ones.  In the 88-89 season he was replaced by Chris Turner and only played 5 games from the start.  In the 89-90 season an injury he received at Hillsborough prevents him from enjoying the first choice status he had just reclaimed.   This same season Wednesday are relegated.
* In March 1992, given that he is a substitute, he is loaned to Stoke City although he only played in 4 games.
* Since the 93-94 season, Pressman becomes a member of the Wednesday first team to the detriment of a great international such as Chris Woods.  In the 94-95 season he plays 34 league games, although in April 1995,  a crushing home defeat at the hands of Nottingham Forest force him onto the bench for the rest of the season.

* For yet another season Kevin Pressman remained solid as the first choice keeper for Wednesday.  He played 38 league games, although in the last match of the season he had to leave the pitch due to an injury.  He kept 12 clean sheets but, above all, showed that he is still one of the best goalies in the Championship.

285.name: Barrett
pages:
* Signed for Sheffield Wednesday in March 1998. 
* The early days of Earl Barrett's career suggested that he was a real prospect who was  about to explode onto the scene. A versatile footballer capable of adapting to a number of different positions, he had the best spell of his career between 1990 and 1993 when he left behind a succesful Oldham Athletic side, moving on to Aston Villa, and also forming part of the England side.

* He began his career as a marker at the heart if the defence, but, when he moved on to Aston Villa, he changed his position and lined up at right back, with Paul McGrath well established in what would have been his spot at the centre of the back four. Playing out on the flank Barrett can take full advantage of his tremendous pace, although he is not a player who is particularly dangerous when he moves forward to join the attack. Nevertheless, he does a good efficient job at the back, and is a difficult player to beat. However, his progress has come to something of a standstill, and it would now seem as though he is entering a downward phase in his career.

* League Cup winners medal  93-94. 
* Second Division Championship winners medal 91-92.

* 3 full international appearances for England. He made his debut on 3rd June 1991 in Auckland, in a friendly game between New Zealand and England, (0-1). 
* 5 "B" international appearances. 
* 4 under-21 international appearances.

* After coming through the youth ranks as a trainee, he signed for Manchester City on 26th April 1985. 
* Sent out on loan to Chester City on 1st March 1986, he made his league debut three days later in a game against Mansfield. 
* Manchester City sold him to Oldham Athletic on 24th November 1987 in exchange for 35,000 pounds. 
* With Oldham he reached the 1990 F.A. Cup semi finals only to lose, after a replay, to Manchester United. The club also reached the League Cup final which they also lost at Wembley. That same season, Barrett helped Oldham to win promotion to the First Division. 
* On 25th February 1992 he was transfered to Aston Villa. His transfer valuation  had risen to 1,700,000 pounds. He played in the U.E.F.A. Cup,.losing to Intter Milan in the penalty shoot out. He began the season at right back, although the arrival of Gary Charles hastened his departure from the club.
* On 30th January 1995 he was signed by Everton for the same amount of money that Villa had paid for him three years earlier. 
* He was sent off in his first game in an Everton shirt. It was the first sending off of his career. 
* He was unable to play in the 1995 F.A. Cup final against Manchester United, as a result of being cup-tied following an appearance he made for Aston Villa in an earlier round of the competition.

* Without doubt he had his best season yet for Everton making a total of 36 appearances as a member of the starting line up. He was normally used as a right back, although in a number of games he played at the heart of the defence. His excellent season brought about  the end of Swiss player Marc Hottiger's Everton career.

286.name: Hinchcliffe
pages:
* Signed for Sheffield Wednesday in January 1998. 
* Only an injury prevented last season from being the best of Hinchcliffe's career. His full international debut for England and his magnificent start to the season, finally confirmed him as one of the best full backs in the British game.

* A hard running mobile left back, he gets forward quickly to support the attack, helped out by his fine touch on the ball. Capable of beating a man, he makes the most of his pace to take on opponents and get good crosses into the heart of the penalty area. However the most outstanding part of his game is his efficiency at set pieces, where he proves to be a real specialist. His left foot launches free kicks and corners with impressive power and extraordinary accuracy; the ball scribing a perfect arc, making Hinchcliffe a key member of the side. Defensively he does a good job, and is a fine player when he is covering across at the back as the last line of defence, where, when he needs to be, he can be a very forceful player.
* F.A. Cup winners medal 94-95.

* 3 full international appearances for England.
* 1 Under-21 international appearance.
* 8 youth international appearances, scoring once.

* He arrived at Manchester City as a schoolboy in July 1985. He signed as a professional on 17th June 1986.
* He made his league debut for Manchester City on 15th August 1987, in a home victory against Plymouth Argyle. The following year the club won promotion back to the top flight.
* Injury kept him out of the end of the 89-90 season.
* He was transfered to Everton on 17th July 1990 for 800.000 pounds, in a deal which also saw Neil Pointon move in the opposite direction to Maine Road. 
* He made his Goodison Park debut at against Leeds United on 25th August 1990.
* In his first season at the club Everton lost the Zenith Data Systems Cup final against  Crystal Palace at Wembley.
* Up to the end of the 94-95 season he had been booked 7 times.
* On 21st December 1996, he suffered a knee ligament injury which kept him out of the rest of the season. 
* Signed for Sheffield Wednesday in January 1998 for 3.000.000 pounds.

* Andy Hinchcliffe was having the best season if his career until a knee ligament injury he suffered on 21st December against Leeds United at Goodison Park put him out of action for the remainder of the season. Up to that moment he had been doing a job which was proving to be both effective and good to watch, and had attracted the attention of England manager Glenn Hoddle, who called him up for the game against Moldova.Andy gave a satisfactory performance which saw Glenn Hoddle keep him in the starting line up for the game against Poland.

287.name: Nicol
pages:
* To talk of Steve Nicol is to talk of one of the most emblematic British players of the 80s who, now a veteran, keeps the Wednesday defence in shape. To give an idea of Nicol's standing as a footballer, it would probably be enough to speak of the 14 seasons at Liverpool, although if this weren't enough, maybe it should be said that with Liverpool he was the European Champion in 1984, four times league champion and was voted best player in the English league by the Association of Sports Reporters.
* Now past 36 he still finds the motivation to train hard each week in the hope that he can add another game to his lengthy career.  For this reason alone, he will be a stimulus for the young players in the Hillsborough youth squad.

* Although he is right-footed, he started his career at left back.  His notable technique with both feet and his versatility made him one of the best wide defenders in England.  For many years, he changed sides constantly. He was very quick and attacking, and could break through defensive lines easily.  He is good in the air and has a powerful right.  Currently, he is playing more as a central defender, and although the passing of the years has led to a loss of speed, he makes up for this with excellent positioning, the fruit of accumulated experience in so many battles in grounds all around the world.

* European Champion 84.
* League Champion 84, 86, 88 and 90.
* FA Cup Champion 86, 89 and 92.
* Charity Shield Medal 89.

* 27 full international appearances for Scotland.  He made his debut on the 12th of September 1984 in a game against Yugoslavia.
* 14 under-21 international appearances.

* Steve Nicol's career is quite simply astounding.  He started at Ayr United, arriving in their first team in 1979.  On the 26th of October 1981, aged just 19, he was transferred to Liverpool for £300,000.  At the time, Nicol had already made his debut as an international, defending his country's colours at the under-21 level in a game against Sweden.
* He made his debut in the English First Division on the 31st of August 1982 against Birmingham City, but didn't manage to find a regular place in the side until the 83-84 season.
* With the Anfield club he won 4 league titles, and 3 FA Cup winners medals. But without doubt, the most important triumph of his sporting career was in the final of the European Cup in 1984, when Liverpool beat Rome in the penalty shoot-out.  Nicol missed his penalty, something that hasn't detracted from his honours list.
* At the end of his career at Liverpool he only played 4 games in the 94-95 season, and so he was allowed to go half-way through the season. Notts County took advantage of this to sign him on the 20th of January 1995.  However, his presence doesn't help the club to avoid relegation to the Second Division.
* On the 25th of November 1995 he arrives as Sheffield Wednesday on a free transfer.  He makes his debut for the Owls this same day against Everton at Goodison Park (2-2).  At the end of this season, his return to the Premier League, he had played 19 league games.

* Although he was a regular on the substitutes' bench during the course of the season, it has to be said that every time this veteran defender stepped onto the pitch his performance was satisfactory.  For yet another year he showed the value of experience and played well in different positions.  He took part in a total of 23 games in the Premier League, playing from the start in 19 of these.

288.name: Nolan
pages: * The fans at Hillsborough are fond of Nolan.  The Northern Ireland international has been one of Sheffield Wednesday's key players since he arrived at the club in 1994 and only injuries have prevented him from playing. His progress seems unstoppable.  He now hopes to continue the good work in the 97-98 season, and is optimistic that it will be a good year.

* Ian Nolan is a team player.  If there is a characteristic that defines him it is his capacity to adapt to the demands of the manager.  He has played as left back for most of his still short career, despite preferring his right foot and operating naturally on the right.  He is pretty defensively minded, but had to play in the midfield under the orders of David Pleat, the manager at the time.  Nolan is not a right back who covers a lot of ground, however, he is quick over a short distance and passes the ball safely, earning the confidence of his team-mates.  A good marker, he doesn't hesitate to use force if he thinks it necessary.  In any case, he should try and take more part in attack, which would increase his contribution to the team.
x
x

* Although he trained in the Preston North End youth squad, Ian Nolan arrived at Tranmere Rovers from Marine (an amateur team).  On the 2nd of August 1991 he signs for the Prenton Park club in exchange for £10,000.  There he coincides with the veteran Eire marksman, John Aldridge, although the two players are at opposite ends of their careers.
* Nolan makes his League debut on the 26th of October 1991 against Wolverhampton.  This season he plays 34 league games and scores a goal on the 31st of March 1992 against Bristol City.
* On the 17th of August 1994 he is transferred to Sheffield Wednesday for £1,500,000 and makes his debut three days later at home to Tottenham Hotspur (3-4).
* His first goal for Wednesday is in a mythical place, Anfield, although it doesn't help to prevent the team going down 4-1.  The date: 1st October 1994.
* An undisputed starter since his arrival at Hillsborough, in March 1996 he suffers a serious ligament injury which keeps him out for several months. 
* Despite being born in Liverpool, in the 96-97 season he made his debut for Northern Ireland.

* Ian Nolan and Kevin Pressman were the only Wednesday players who took part in every league game last season.  His extraordinary performance didn't pass unnoticed by the Northern Ireland selector, who included him in his teams regularly.  He put the finishing touch to an extraordinary season scoring a vital goal against Tottenham Hotspur.

289.name: Newsome
pages: * It is an honour for Jon Newsome to put on the Wednesday shirt.  Born in Sheffield and raised in the Hillsborough youth squad, he left that club in 1991 to return five years later.  Last year, he lost the status of starter, something he will try and regain in the 97-98 in the tough battle with Dejan Stefanovic.

* Technically discrete, he stands out for his dominance in the air in both areas, something which allows him to score goals, although not so often. His fighting spirit allows him to play in different positions, but he is most comfortable in the centre of defence.  However, in his spell at Leeds United he quite often played as right back.  He tries to make up for his lack of speed with good positioning and anticipation, although the rival forwards will try and draw him out to the wings, where his performance drops as he is not so agile.
* League Champion 92.
x

* Originally from the Wednesday youth squad, he signs as a professional on the 1st of July 1989.  On the 9th of September of this same year he makes his debut in the league against Arsenal.
* On the 1st of June 1991 he is transferred alongside David Wetherall to Leeds United for total cost of £250,000.  On the 2nd of November he plays his first league game for Leeds against Wimbledon.  Almost one month later in his second game for the team Newsome scores against Tottenham.
* This same season the injury to Mel Sterland allows him to play at right back and, depsite only playing ten games, he scores another goal.  This was the winner against Sheffield United (3-2) in the last-but-one game of season; a victory that hours later brought the title to Leeds when Manchester United were beaten by Liverpool.
* On the 30th of June 1994 he is transferred to Norwich City for £1 million. However, he doesn't have much luck at Carrow Road as, despite playing 35 games and scoring 3 goals in the season, he can't help prevent relegation to the First Division.
* His return to his roots was a surprise.  On the 16th of March 1996, just one day before the transfer deadline, Sheffield Wednesday decide to bring him back for £1,600,000.

* The 96-97 season was not a good one for Jon Newsome, who hardly got to play in the league.  He fought for a place in the team and once he managed to figure in the starting line-ups again, an ankle injury in a Cup tie against Wimbledon kept him out till the end of the season.

290.name: Atherton
pages: * Peter Atherton has needed just three seasons to make him one of the best representatives of the Owls spirit.  He was one of the team's most important players last season and Wednesday were able to jostle for the top places in the table thanks to men such as him.  Nothing would indicate that in the 97-98 season he will loose his influence at the club.

* We are not looking at a central defender with a wide range of technical resources, though he is perfectly aware of this.  He is therefore happy to do what he does well: position himself well and offer a solid aerial game. He might look a little slow, but he is really faster than he seems.  At times he plays at right back, however he doesn't cover a lot of ground and so doesn't usually join in the attack.

* 1 under-21 international appearance for England.  He made his debut on the 15th of October 1991 with a 2-0 victory over Turkey, both England's goals scored by Alan Shearer.
* Schoolboy international.

* Atherton's professional career starts at Wigan Athletic.  His league debut takes place on the 24/10/87 against Blackpool.  He plays for four seasons with the club scoring only one goal during this time against Sheffield United in October 1988.
* After 149 league games with Wigan, he is transferred in August 1991 to Coventry City for £400,000.  On the 24th of this same month he makes his debut against Queens Park Rangers.  He plays 134 games for the Sky Blues and doesn't score a single goal.
* In June 1994 he signs for Sheffield Wednesday for £800,000 and he manages to find a spot for himself in the starting line-ups.
* Peter Atherton won't forget the 27th of November 1994 easily.  On this day the Sheffield centre back scores a scorcher, his first for his current club.  It was a volley from 30 yards which silenced Villa Park and left Ian Walker, the Aston Villa keeper, speechless.  His goal was the equaliser.

* A key man in the Wednesday defence, Peter Atherton was a starter in the 37 games he took part in last season.  For another year he was one of the team's leaders, showing an unbreakable spirit in every game.  He scored two goals, one against Newcastle at St. James Park and the other against Tottenham at Hillsborough.

291.name: Walker
pages: * Walker's career could have been a lot different if things had gone his way in his Italian adventure.  In the summer of 1992, Sampdoria of Genoa acquire his services.  Sampdoria had just lost in the European Cup final to Barcelona.  Although in the Italian league the club had not been so successful the Genoese club were still very prestigious.  And prestigious clubs usually sign classy players.  This was the case with Walker, a defender who had had a brilliant career in the ranks of Nottingham Forest.  However, luck was not on his side and one year later he packed his bags and returned to England, finding himself at Sheffield Wednesday.  Although he is not captain, Des Walker is still very much a guarantee of safety in the Owls defence.

* Des Walker is one of the best central defenders produced by British football in recent times.  If we are talking about a defender, we are looking at a specialist.  Hard to beat, Walker clings like a leech to his rival; making use of his great speed to cut out the move.  Agile and powerful, and gifted for the aerial game, one of his biggest virtues is his safety, something fundamental in a defender.  He hardly ever looks to complicate life, robbing the ball and laying it off quickly.  Conscious of his technical limitations, he doesn't try to play the ball out of defence; this being perhaps his biggest defect.  Nor does he try and join in the attack at free-kicks or corners, and so it is not surprising that he hasn't scored a goal in the whole of his career.

* League Cup Champion 89 and 90.
* Full Members Cup Champion 89 and 92.

* 59 full international appearances for England.  He made his debut as a substitute for Terry Adams on the 14th of September 1988 in a game against Denmark played at Wembley (1-0).
* Present in the Italy 90 World Cup, he was a starter in the seven games played by the team.
* In the Sweden 92 European Championship he was a member of the starting eleven in the three games in which he played.
* 7 under-21 international appearances.  He made his debut on the 21st of May 1985 against Finland.

* He starts his career as an apprentice on signing for Nottingham Forest in November 1983.  He was 18.  However, Des' dream was to play for Tottenham, the club he supported and where he was on trial.  But Bill Nicholson, the coach of the lower-category teams throws him out for having his hair too long.  Walker, very disappointed, was encouraged by Keith Burkinshaw and John Moncur to have a trial for Forest.
* On the 13th of March 1984 he makes his debut against Everton.  From the 85-86 season onwards he is a regular in the starting eleven, and remains so until the 91-92 season.  In his last season at Forest he scores the only goal of his career.  The date: 1st of January 1992.  The opponents: Luton Town. 
* While he is at Forest the team is proclaimed League Cup Champion in 1989 and 1990 and FA Cup Runner-up in 1991 after loosing to Tottenham in the final with an own-goal from Walker.
* In 1988 he makes his full debut for the England team and two years later is one of the most outstanding players in the Italy 90 World Cup.
* He is transferred to Sampdoria in August 1992 for £1,500,000.  One year later, without having had much success in the Italian league, he returns to England.
* He signs for Sheffield Wednesday on the 22nd of July 1993 in exchange for £2,700,000 and makes his debut on the 14th of August of this same year with an away defeat at the hands of Liverpool (2-0).
* In the 95-96 season the manager David Pleat decides to relieve him of his captain's duties which he had been carrying out for some years.

* Last season Des Walker was once again one of Wednesday's most outstanding players.  He was a starter in the 36 league games in which he played and reached such good form that there was even talk of his return to the national side.  Even so, he didn't manage to add his name to the list of goalscorers.

292.name: Briscoe
pages: * A product of the Hillsborough youth squad, he is destined to be one of Sheffield Wednesday's pillars in the very near future.  However, last year his career suffered a setback as he was left out of the starting line-ups too often.  Now he will have to make an effort to regain his best form and fight on equal terms with his team-mates for a place in the starting line-ups.

* Lee Briscoe started off as a left winger or left half, but he converted into a left back little by little.  He is an attacking footballer, with a good turn, and quick, which help him to get a long way down the left.  However, thanks to his training as a forward, he sometimes neglects his responsibilities in defence too often, causing cracks at the back which can be used by rival forwards.
x
* 5 under-21 international appearances for England.

* Lee Briscoe comes from the Sheffield Wednesday youth squad. Professional since the 22nd of May 1994, in his first season with the first team he only played in his debut on the 5th of Febraury 1994 against Tottenham at White Hart Lane.  The Owls won 1-3.
* It's the 95-96 season when David Pleat begins to align him regularly, leading to his call-up for the England under-21 side.

* It was a disappointing season for Lee Briscoe.  He started the season carrying an injury and couldn't reappear until November.  Even so, he didn't manage to settle into the team and only towards the end of the Championship did he have a handful of opportunities.

293.name: Stefanovic
pages: * The arrival of Dejan Stefanovic at Sheffield Wednesday happened at the same time as the that of Darko Kovacevic.  In some ways it could be considered a double transfer where the star was his team-mate, one of the top marksmen in Yugoslavia and sought after by several continental teams.  After the forward's departure to Spanish football, Dejan had to show his worth, and he did just that.  Last season he unveiled himself as an extraordinary defender and aroused a lot of hopes for the Owls future.

* Although he is a right-footed player, for many games he has played at left back.  Even so, his versatility has allowed him to play as a marker in the middle and, at times, on the right, a position in line with his physical characteristics.  He moves quickly and likes to join in the attack, where he shows off his shot.  Effective when marking and excellent in the air, he has good ball control and passes well, although at times he seems to "go missing" from the game.  In any case, there is no doubt that one of Stefanovic's biggest asset's is his youth, making him a player with a brilliant future.

* Yugoslavian League Champion 95.
* Yugoslavian Cup Champion 95.
* 9 full international appearances for Yugoslavia.

* Stefanovic became known in the 94-95 season playing in the ranks of Redstar Belgrade.  With this historic club he managed the League and Cup double.In the league tournament he scored 9 goals in 30 games, an extraordinary haul for a wide defender.  He played in both legs of the final of the Cup against Obilic (4-0) and (0-0).
* 9 full international appearances, his attacking ability was exploited by Santrac, the Yugoslavian manager, to play him in the midfield against Uruguay.
* He is transferred to Sheffield Wednesday on the 4th of December 1995 along with Darko Kovacevic for a total of £4 million.  He makes his debut on the 26th of December with a defeat at the hands of Nottingham Forest at the City Ground (1-0).  Dejan comes on for Lee Briscoe in the 29th minute.
* Unlike Kovacevic, Dejan isn't very successful in his first season at Hillsborough.  According to the coaches, his lack of English prevented him from reaching a good understanding with his team-mates in the defensive line.

* Last season the fans at Sheffield Wednesday saw the true Dejan Stefanovic. The Yugoslavian international earned a place in the starting eleven to the detriment of Jon Newsome.  He scored 2 goals in 29 league games: the first was the equaliser at Stamford Bridge against Chelsea; the second sealed the win over Sunderland.  Dejan was, without doubt, one of the pleasant surprises in the championship.

295.name: Rudi
pages: * Petter Rudi was caught in the middle of a fierce battle between Sheffield Wednesday and Southampton.  Both clubs wanted desperately to sign him, although it was the player himself who chose the Owls offer.  With him at Sheffield club he brings youth, strength and quality to the midfield line. The only thing left is for Rudi to adapt quickly to a competition as demanding as the Premier League.

* A young midfielder with great playing vision.  He is particularly noted for the ease with which he creates scoring chances for his team-mates. He has an acceptable technique, moves about a lot and collaborates effectively in defence.  He also has a powerful shot which he doesn't hesitate to use at the slightest chance.
x
* Full Norwegian international.

* In 1995 he was voted best Footballer of the Year by the popular Norwegian paper "Verdens Gang".
* Liverpool tried to sign him in 1995 and 1996.  In 1997 Southampton and Sheffield Wednesday had a hard battle for him.  Finally the Norwegian midfielder opted for the Hillsborough club's offer.
* He is a Sheffield Wednesday player since the 2nd of October 1997.  The price of his transfer is set at £800,000.

* Although Molde didn't have a good season, Petter Rudi was one of the best players in the team again.  The Norwegian midfielder also played a decisive role in his country's battle to reach the 98 World Cup Finals.

296.name: Di Canio
pages: * Paolo Di Canio is the most expensive signing in the history of Sheffield Wednesday.  The Hillsborough club made a strenuous effort to sign the Italian footballer, who was one of the big stars of the Scottish league last season. The footballer's own desire to leave Glasgow and Celtic's interest in Regi Blinker helped the operation go through.  Now, Di Canio will have to live up to the expectations placed in him.  Beside him he will have his fellow countryman Benito Carbone.  Together, the two Italians will try and win the hearts of the Owls supporters.

* A right-footed link-man with the forwards, quick and very strong, who usually plays on the right of the pitch.  He makes up for his technical shortcomings with a tremendous amount of physical effort and speed to go past defenders looking for the rival box.  He has a good header, although he doesn't score many goals during the course of the season.

* UEFA Cup Champion 93.
* Italian League Champion 96.
x

* He was trained in the Lazio youth squad.  He owes everything to Mario Facco, the man who convinced him to dedicate himself to football professionally.  In the 85-86 season he arrived in the first team of the Rome club, although he didn't get to make his debut.
* In the 86-87 season he was loaned to Ternana, in the Serie C2.
* Di Canio's debut in the Serie A took place on the 9th of October 1988, in a game against Cesena-Lazio which finishes as a nil-nil draw.  From that moment till his move to Juventus he hardly missed a game, playing 54 games and scoring 4 goals in those two seasons.
* In 1990 he was transferred to Juventus, the club where he played three seasons.  He played 78 games and scored 15 goals.
* In the 93-94 season he was loaned to Naples.
* He started the 94-95 season at Juventus, but was transferred to Milan. 
* In 1996 he moved to Celtic for £l million.  He made his debut on the 24th of September of this year, with an away win over Kilmarnock (1-3). Di Canio scored the first goal of the game.
* In his only season in Scotland he was voted Footballer of the Year.  Despite this, Di Canio himself repeatedly announced his intention to change clubs.
* On the 6th of August 1997 he was transferred to Sheffield Wednesday for £3 million, making him the most expensive signing in the history of the club.  The operation included the Dutchman Regi Blinker's move to Celtic.
* He is hard to miss on the pitch due his golden boots he usually wears.

* The fans at Celtic welcomed Paulo Di Canio with open arms and he didn't disappoint.  He scored 12 goals in 26 league games, making him the third top scorer in the Scottish team behind the Portuguese Cadete and the Dutchman Van Hooijdonk.  Di Canio offered a great performance at Parkhead, although he often said he didn't feel comfortable in Glasgow.  At the end of the season he was voted the Player of the Year by the footballers themselves.

297.name: Magilton
pages: * Jim Magilton is one of Sheffield Wednesday's reinforcements for the 97-98 season.  The Northern Ireland international has the quality and experience needed to be successful at Hillsborough.  His contribution could be a great plus for a team which hopes not to have a nail-biting season.

* Magilton is a very hard-working midfielder who can play both as a defensive playmaker or at right half.  When playing just in front of the defence he acts as a link with the men further forward, joining in the attack frequently to try out his powerful right, the way he scores most of his goals.  A good passer, he doesn't try anything too flashy.  He wins back a lot of balls, helped by his good physical resistance.  This hard work makes him a valuable player for the team.  To these qualities his security from the penalty spot should be added.
x

* 36 full international appearances for Northern Ireland.  5 goals.
* 1 B-international appearance.
* 2 under-21 international appearances.

* Despite spending 5 seasons at Liverpool, arriving in their first team from the youth squad on the 14th of May 1985, Jim Magilton didn't get to make his league debut for the Reds.
* Transferred to Oxford United for £100,000 on the 3rd of October 1990, he makes his debut on this same day against West Ham.
* Southampton was the team that gave him the chance to play in the Premier League.  Signed on the 11th of February 1994 for £600,000, he makes his debut 3 days later at the Dell, strangely enough, against Liverpool. Southampton won 4-2.
* On the 6th of September 1997 he was transferred to Sheffield Wednesday for £1,600,000.

* Jim Magilton was one of the most outstanding players at Southampton during last season.  Thanks to footballers such as him the supporters at the Dell were able to celebrate the team's survival in the Premier League.  An undisputed starter, he took on the responsibility of leading the team in the absence of Matt Le Tissier.  He scored 4 goals in the League, 2 of them from the penalty spot.  The most important of these was against Nottingham Forest at the City Ground: his impressive blast from outside the area definitively saved Southampton's skin.

298.name: Carbone
pages: * It wasn't easy to fill the gap left by the departure of the mythical Chris Waddle at Hillsborough.  The Wednesday manager, David Pleat, resorted to Benito Carbone to bring imagination and creativity to the team's game. And the Italian footballer didn't disappoint.  In his first season in England he showed his quality, scored goals, played some wonderful passes, and above all, brought hope to the Owls supporters.  Benito hopes that in the 97-98 season he will settle definitively into the Premier League.

* A footballer with a lot of technical quality, he can play as a forward or link-man with the forwards.  He is very skilful, quick, and has a good turn and a lot of natural talent.  He is also creative, with an excellent playing vision and is dangerous when he is in the rival box.  To all this can also be added his youth, making him a player with a splendid future ahead of him. 
* Although he is not a born scorer, he does find the net a fair few times each season thanks to his powerful shot with the right and his skill at taking free-kicks.
x
* Italy under-21 international.

* Called Benito because of the great admiration that his father had for Mussolini, Carbone was a Juventus fan right from his childhood days.
* An under-21 international with Italy under the leadership of Cesare Maldini, his big idol is Roberto Baggio.
* Trained in the Torino youth squad, he moved up to the first team in the 88-89 season.  He made his debut in the Serie A on the 15th of January 1989 in a game against Pisa (0-0).
* He had a lot of problems to get a game at Torino due, perhaps, to his shortness and youth, although the arrival of Mondonico on the bench lead to a slight improvement in the situation.  After playing only 8 games in two years and going through relegation to the Serie B, Carbone played at a string of clubs on loan, starting at Reggina, then Casertana and then Ascoli, all in the Serie B.
* He returns to Torino in the 93-94 season.  He plays 28 games, 25 of those from the start and scores three games against Piacenza, Roma and Naples. 
* Naples was his next destination, although he only played for one year at this club.
* In the summer of 1995 he is transferred to Inter Milan.  In his first and only season at the club he takes orders from three different managers: Ottavio Bianchi, Luis Su rez and the Englishman Roy Hodgson.
* He starts the 96-97 season at Inter, but the arrival of Ivan Zamorano and Youri Djorkaeff shut him out of the team so, on the 14th of October 1996, he is transferred to Sheffield Wednesday for £3 million.
* He made his debut in the Premier League on the 19th of October 1996, in a game against Blackburn Rovers played at Hillsborough (0-0).  On the 18th of November of this same year he scored his first goal for the team against Nottingham Forest.

* He started the season at Inter, but in the middle of October he was transferred to Sheffield Wednesday.  He immediately found his way into the team and became one of the idols of the supporters at Hillsborough.  He scored 6 goals in 25 league games and, above all, left behind memories of his undisputed class.

299.name: Oakes
pages: * Scott Oakes, alongside his team-mate Mark Pembridge, was one of the men who David Pleat trusted most.  The manager signed him first of all for Luton Town and in 1996 he joined Sheffield Wednesday.  Now that Pleat has been removed from the bench the player's position at Hillsborough is a little more difficult.  But Oakes, used to battling things out, isn't going to give up in his attempt to be successful in the Premier League.

* Scott Oakes is a versatile footballer who can carry out several different functions on the pitch.  In fact, during the course of his career he has played as a forward, a midfielder and even as a wide defender.  He has excellent technique, and is noted for the accuracy of his passes which open up the wings and for his skilful turn.  Spectacular at times, he has a powerful shot on goal and won't hesitate to use it given the slightest chance.  He is also a free-kick specialist, scoring a reasonable number of goals in this way.
x
* 1 under-21 international appearance for England.

* He is the son of one of the members of Showaddywaddy, the famous British group from the 70's.
* Born in Leicester, he is trained in the Filbert Street youth squad.  A professional since the 9th of May 1990, he made his League debut in the 89-90 season.  However, in three seasons at Leicester he only played three matches. 
* On the 22nd of October 1991 he arrives at Luton Town in a free transfer. He quickly started playing in the first team managed by David Pleat and becomes one of the Hatters' most acclaimed players.
* He finishes the 93-94 season as Luton's top scorer with 13 goals, 8 in the League and 5 in the FA Cup.
* At the end of the 95-96 season Luton are relegated to the Second Division. In the last home game of the season the team whistle him off the pitch. 
* He is a Sheffield Wednesday player since the 1st of August 1996.  His move was set at £450,000.  Oakes coincides with David Pleat once again at Hillsborough, having already taken his orders at Luton Town.
* He made his debut in the Premier League on the 17th of August 1996 in a game against Aston Villa played at Hillsborough (2-1).  On the 23rd of November of this same year he scores his first goal in Sheffield Wednesday's visit to Sunderland (1-1).

* Scott Oakes played the first games of the Premier League last season. A regular on the substitutes' bench he only played 7 of the 19 games from the start.  Even so, he showed signs of his undeniable class, scored a goal against Sunderland and showed that he could be an interesting footballer in the near future.

300.name: Pembridge
pages: * Mark Pembridge's career runs parallel to that of David Pleat, who seems to have a particular liking for the Welsh midfielder.  The former manager of Sheffield Wednesday was his in charge at Luton when the player was there and years later he brought him to Hillsborough.  Now, with David Pleat no longer at the club, it remains to be seen if Pembridge will enjoy the trust of the new manager.

* Pembridge is a very strong player with an impressive physique.  He works hard, using his resistance to help him win back a lot of balls and supply oxygen to the midfield.  He has a good left, and doesn't hesitate to have a dig at the slightest opportunity.  He is also good at taking free-kicks; most of his goals coming from long-range free-kicks.  He usually plays as a midfielder on the left and even as a defensively minded playmaker, giving more freedom of movement to the more creative players who are more limited physically.
x

* 23 full international appearances for Wales.  3 goals.
* 2 B-international appearances.
* 1 under-21 international appearance.
* Schoolboy international.

* Pembridge is a player moulded in the Luton Town youth squad.  He turned professional at the club on the 1st of July 1989.
* 1991 was his first great year.  He made his debut in the league for Luton against Wimbledon on New Years Day, and then for the Wales under-21 team against Poland.  He scored his first league goal against Aston Villa and finished the season with 18 league games under his belt.
* In the following season (91-92) he plays 42 league games and scores 5 goals.  He also gets to make his debut for his country's first team against none less that Brazil.
* On the 2nd of June 1992 he is transferred to Derby County for £1,250,000. He played there for three seasons, taking part in 110 league games and scoring 28 goals.
* He becomes a Sheffield Wednesday player on the 19th of July 1995.  He is signed for £900,000 in a personal choice on the part of David Pleat who had been his manager at Luton.
* He makes his debut for the Owls on the 19th of August 95 with a 1-0 defeat against Liverpool at Anfield.  Four days later at Hillsborough, in a game against Blackburn Rovers, the reigning champions, Pembridge scores his first goal for Wednesday.

* Although he had to endure the criticism of a sector of the supporters at Hillsborough, Mark Pembridge responded with his best football, thus becoming a key player in the Wednesday and national sides.  He played 34 league games, 33 of them from the start; and scored 6 goals, the same number as Benito Carbone and David Hirst.

301.name: Hyde
pages: * The fans at Hillsborough consider Graham Hyde as one of their biggest heroes.  The midfielder, one of the few born in Yorkshire in the Wednesday squad, is an example of commitment and sacrifice for the good of the team. His contribution is much appreciated by the fans, by his manager and by his own team-mates, who see him as one of the main representatives of the club spirit.  Hyde will never be a star, but with him on the pitch a fight is guaranteed until the last minute.

* A midfielder who constantly offers support, Hyde moves the ball well over short distances.  He lends a helping hand when his team-mates are having problems and then plays the ball away with good judgement.  He is physically strong, and makes constant sacrifices in defensive tasks.  He is the lungs of the team and wins back a lot of possession in midfield.  However, he lacks a certain creativity and his contribution to attack is not often noticed, although the statistics indicate that he scores every now and again.
x
x

* Originally from the Sheffield Wednesday youth squad, he signs as a professional on the 17th of May 1988, but his debut with the first team doesn't take place until the 14th of September 1991 in a league game against Manchester City.
* In September 1992 he scores the first goal of his career against Nottingham Forest.
* He plays in the final of the League Cup in 1993 against Arsenal, coming on as a substitute for Phil King.  This same year, he plays both in the final and the replay of the FA Cup, also against Arsenal.  In neither of the games does he play from the start; in one he comes on for Viv Anderson and in the other for Danny Wilson.

* He started the season as a substitute, but little by little he began to find his way onto David Pleat's teamsheet.  Unfortunately an injury in an FA Cup tie against Wimbledon forced him to say an early goodbye to the season.

302.name: Humphreys
pages: * Richie Humphreys is one of the most promising footballers at Sheffield Wednesday.  A product of the Hillsborough youth squad, he is destined to be star at the club within a short space of time.  His great performances laden with goals in the reserves have not passed unnoticed by David Pleat. In fact, he was the first young footballer to be included in the Owls first squad by the former manager.  Richie now knows what it is like to play in the Premier League and has defended the England under-21 colours.  Born in Sheffield, he has everything in his favour to become the new idol of the fans.

* Although at times he has played on the left of midfield, Richie Humphreys is a born striker.  Skilful and with good playing vision, his great speed allows him to go past rival defenders with apparent ease.  But, without doubt, his biggest asset is his scoring instinct.  He can shoot on goal from just about anywhere, preferably with his left.  Despite his youth, he is very safe when it comes to finishing off one-on-ones with the rival keeper. Still very young, his talent announces the arrival of an extraordinary footballer.
x
* 3 times under-21 international for England.

* Born in Sheffield, Richie Humphreys was trained in the Wednesday youth squad.  After playing in all the lower categories and showing his devastating marksmanship in the reserves team, David Pleat gives him the chance to play with the first team.
* He made his debut on the 9th of September 1995 in a visit to Queens Park Rangers.  Humphreys comes on as a substitute for Donaldson in the 84th minute of a game Wednesday won 0-3.
* On the 17th of August 1996 he scored his first goal in the Premier League against Aston Villa at Hillsborough (2-1).  It was the first game of the 96-97 season.

* He started the season on extraordinary form, scoring three goals in his first four league games.  However, he couldn't keep up this level and he lost his place to David Hirst.  In any case, the overall impression for the season was very good for the young footballer, who also made his debut for the England under-21 team.

303.name: Booth
pages: * Andy Booth was the most expensive signing made by Sheffield Wednesday going into the 96-97 season and, to tell the truth, he was also the most profitable.  In his first season in the Premier League he became the team's top scorer and one of Hillsborough's biggest idols.  The 97-98 season should confirm his arrival at the top level, and if he keeps up his progress, he should start to receive call-ups from the England team.

* The header is possibly Andy Booth's biggest asset, a very effective centre forward in front of goal.  Opportunistic and brave, he is able to get goalside of rival defenders and, once he has a small advantage, he doesn't usually show any mercy.  Physically strong, he never shies away from a collision, although his natural instinct allows him to get in ahead of the defend and avoid the need for contact.  He scores most of his goals with a first-time shot, a characteristic which defines the great forwards.
x
* 3 under-21 international appearances for England.

* Born in Huddersfield, Andy Booth was trained in the Huddersfield Town youth squad.  He made his debut with the first team in the 91-92 season, although he doesn't turn professional until the 1st of July 1992.
* In the 94-95 season he scored 26 goals in the league, and was the team's top scorer.  Furthermore, his contribution was decisive in Huddersfield's promotion to the First Division.  Thanks to this he was included in the Second Division Dream Team by the professionals themselves.
* During the course of the 95-96 season there are several Premier League clubs who are interested in signing him.  Huddersfield even turned down offers of £1.5 million.  Booth was once more the team's top scorer with 16. 
* In July 1996 he was transferred to Sheffield Wednesday for £2,700,000. He made his debut in the Premier League on the 17th of August of this same year against Aston Villa at Hillsborough (2-1).  Three days later he scored his first goal for the club against Leeds (0-2).
* In his first season at Sheffield Wednesday he was the top scorer with 10 goals in the league and three in the Cup.
* He played as a goalkeeper for the last 10 minutes of the last game of the 96-97 season as Matt Clarke had been sent off after coming on as a substitute for Kevin Pressman.  Andy Booth let in a goal from a free-kick by Jamie Redknapp, the Liverpool midfielder.

* In his first season in the Premier League Andy Booth became one of the pleasant surprises in the top division.  Not only was he a deserved starter in the Wednesday line-ups, but he was also the team's top scorer with 10 goals in the League and three in the Cup.
* Booth also played his part in one of the year's anecdotes when he had to go in goal in the last game of the season against Liverpool.  Matt Clarke had come on as a substitute for the injured Kevin Pressman, but shortly afterwards was sent off.  With Andy Booth between the posts for the last ten minutes of the game Liverpool equalised, the game finishing with a 1-1 draw.

304.name: Whittingham
pages: * Guy Whittingham is one of the best marksmen in England in recent years, as he showed in the 91-92 season, when he scored 42 goals in 46 league games. He has also scored seven hat-tricks during his professional career, a figure only within range of a chosen few.  He is now playing out his last years of football at Sheffield Wednesday, although, having seen his excellent performance last year, it wouldn't be a surprise to see him extend his career for a while to come in the Premier League.

* Whittingham is a centre forward of the old school.  Brave and always ready to shoot, he is dominant in the air, with a powerful jump and the skill needed to anticipate the defenders.  He has a good shot with both feet from close range; he turns well, finds some space and shoots without thinking about it.  Quick, he slips his marker well and is clever in the area.  His generous effort should also be added to these qualities. He fights for every ball and pressures the rival defence.  Recently, David Pleat has been playing him in the midfield, where he has linked up with the forwards.
x
x

* He starts his career as an amateur at Yeovil Town.  On the 9th of June 1989 he sings for Portsmouth, making his debut on the 26th of August of this same year against Stoke City and scoring his first goal fourteen days later against Hull.  This season he scores 23 goals in 42 league games.
* The name of Whittingham is linked to the 92-93 season.  He manages to dazzle the footballing world scoring 42 goals in 46 games in the ranks of the modest Portsmouth.
* Nobody was blind to such effectiveness, although it was Aston Villa who acquired his services on the 1st of August 1993 in exchange for £1,200,000. It is hard to understand why he didn't find his way into the starting line-ups of the team managed by Ron Atkinson.  In fact, in February 1994 he was loaned to Wolverhamtpon Wanderers.
* He is a Sheffield Wednesday since the 21st of December 1994.  His move cost £700,000 forming part of an exchange which saw Ian Taylor go to Aston Villa.  However, Whittingham had already made his debut for the Owls on the 17th of December, with a home defeat at the hands of Queens Park Rangers (0-2).  One week later, the team travel to Goodison Park to play Everton and Whittingham scores two of his team's four goals (1-4).
* Although he had played as a forward for his entire career, David Pleat, the Wednesday manager, converted him into a midfielder in the 95-96 season. 
* During the course of his career he has scored 7 hat-tricks.  The first of them was on the 30th of December 1989, with Oldham Athletic on the receiving end.  The last was on the 5th of October 1994, in a League Cup game against Huddersfield Town in which Whittingham scored 4 times.  Between these dates, Bournemouth, Millwall, Bristol City, Luton Town and Bristol Rovers all conceded three goals from the forward.

* He was one of the players most used by David Pleat during the course of the season.  His contribution to Sheffield Wednesday's good performance was decisive.  He scored 5 goals, three in the league; but, above all, he created chances for his team-mates.  His most brilliant moment of the season: the goal he scored against Liverpool at Anfield which put the Owls 1-0 up.

305.name: Hedman
pages: * Hedman is a young goalkeeper who has already been present in the final stages of a World Cup (with Sweden, USA 94), although he didn't play a single game.  Strachan has said that he is very safe and given the age of Ogrizovic, who is not going to play for ever, Hedman could be a worthy successor.  Trained at AIK Solna with whom he won several titles in his country, Magnus will try and show why he reckons he can make the step up to a big club one day.

* Hedman is a goalkeeper with good reflexes who is particularly noted for his one-on-ones with the forwards.  It seems that his weakest point is the aerial game, but given his youth he still has time to master this aspect of his game.

* 1 Swedish League Champion title with AIK Solna in 1992. 
* 2 Swedish Cup titles in 1996 and 1997. 
* 1 Swedish youth champion title.
* 5 full international appearances for Sweden, Hedman was at the United States World Cup where his country finished third, but he didn't play a single game.

* He entire career in Sweden has developed at AIK, the team where he arrived aged 15 and who he managed to win the League and the Cup with. 
* Hedman was present in the United States World Cup in which Sweden finished third. 
* He played 127 games for AIK in the Swedish First Division. 
* Coventry paid £500,000 to sign him.
* He played for AIK Solna as first choice keeper.
