306.name: Ogrizovic
pages: * Steve Ogrizovic is the only survivor from that Coventry team that won the FA Cup in 1987.  Aged 40 he is still as a keen as when he arrived at Highfield Road twelve seasons ago.  The supporters continue to place their trust in "The Big Man", and no-one dares to predict the day of his retirement. With the record for the number of appearances with the Sky Blues' shirt on after going past George Curtis, Ogrizovic is a living legend at Highfield Road.

* A very bulky keeper, he is outstanding for his safety in the aerial game and when blocking the ball.  A man with a lot of experience, he inspires confidence in the defensive line, ordering them about continually.  He makes up for his lack of speed with a great sense of positioning, but is not so effective when a long way from the line.  His veteran status, an advantage in many respects, is a defect when it comes to clearing the ball with his feet.  In this type of action he shows his lack of technique.  Years ago, Ogrizovic didn't need to master this facet of the game.

* FA Cup Champion 87. 
* Charity Shield Medal 87.
* 1 B-international appearance for England.

* Up till the end of the 95-96 season Steve Ogrizovic had played 440 league games for Coventry, the biggest number for a goalkeeper at the club.  He has now gone past the record of George Curtis, who defended the sky-blue colours in 486 league games. 
* The son of a Yugoslavian immigrant who worked as a miner, Steve was a police cadet who practised his passion for football playing as keeper in team in a local league in Mansfield. 
* Know as "Oggy" or "The Big Man" among the fans, he started his professional career on the 28th of July 1977 in the ranks of Chesterfield. He made his debut on the 20th of August of this same year with a 3-1 win over Port Vale.
* On the 18th of November 1977 he was transferred to Liverpool for £70,000, but he only played 4 games in five years.  Ray Clemence stood in the way to a place in the first team. 
* Shrewsbury Town signed him for £70,000 on the 11th of August 1982, and was the undisputed first choice keeper. 
* He arrives at Coventry on the 22nd of June 1984 in exchange for £72,000 and, between 1984 and 1989 he plays all the league games disputed by the Sky Blues. 
* On the 25th of October 1986 he goes down in club history as the first goalkeeper to score a league goal.  This was the result of an enormous punt which found its way into the Sheffield Wednesday goal. 
* In 1987 they are proclaimed FA Cup Champions for the first time in their history beating Tottenham Hotspur 3-2 in the final with Ogrizovic defending their goal. 
* At the end of the 94-95 season he suffers a fractured ankle in a friendly against Northampton which keeps him out for several months.  Once recovered he regains his place in goal. 
* On Boxing Day 1996 he beat George Curtis' record as the player who had made most appearances wearing the Coventry shirt.  At the end of the 96-97 season Steven had already taken part in 550 games for the Highfield Road Club.

* Ogrizovic produced an excellent season in which he played in every game. He had games in which he was an insurmountable barrier for the rival teams. Steven was one of the reasons why Coventry City managed to stay in the Premier League.  Also, in the FA Cup, he was outstanding, stopping a a Sutton penalty and had an extraordinary game at Anfield which ended in a glorious victory for Coventry.

308.name: Nilsson
pages:
* Roland Nilsson belongs to the generation of Swedish footballers who dragged his country's football out of its lethargic slumber.  Ekstrom, Hysen, Nilsson, Ravelli, Thern, as well as the youngsters who were beginning to come through such as Brolin and Dhalin, managed to pull Sweden up to the first rank of world football, especially after the 94 World Cup. 
* Nilsson returns to England this season to start his second spell in the Premier League after a four season spell a while back at Sheffield before returning to his country.  Strachan has said of him that he "is 33 but that is not a problem.  Stuart Pearce is 35 and is still an England international.  He has a lot of experience, but we have signed him more for his quality than for his experience".

* Roland Nilsson is a defender who is noted above all for the elegance of his game, both when playing the ball out from the back and when making an interception.  He doesn't have the turn of speed nor the force that he had when he was at Sheffield, but he makes up for these shortcomings with his experience and his always perfect positioning.
x
* 86 full international appearances for Sweden.  1 goal.  He took part in the Sweden 92 European Championship and in the United States 1994 World Cup where the team finished third.

* Roland Nilsson was trained in the Helsinborg youth squad, from where he moved to Gothenburg. 
* In December 1989 he signs for Sheffield Wednesday who pay Gothenburg £375,000.  At plays four and a half seasons at Wednesday.  He leaves Hillsborough due his wish to be with his wife in Sweden and signs for Helsinborg.
* His return to England comes about due to Strachan's interest in him and Nilsson accepts because this time his wife and son will be with him for his entire stay at Coventry.  The Highfield Road club pay Helsinborg £500,000 for him.
* He played for the Swedish team Helsinborg, and was the reference point for this team in defence.

309.name: Breen
pages: * This is the Irish international's second season at Coventry.  Breen is considered as a defender with a brilliant future, an opinion which has been backed up by his performance in the games he played last season, his first in the Premier League.

* Gary Breen is a central defender with a lot of talent, not often seen in a back, and he knows how to take advantage of this.  He is quick for a man so well-built and has enough technique to allow him to get out of difficult situations, pushing up into the midfield although he will only leave the defence at set-plays.  He is also noted for his aerial game, the Irish defender is tough but, being so quick, he is often able to anticipate his rival without resorting to hard tackles.  With his characteristics he can also play in the midfield.
x

* 10 full international appearances for the Republic of Ireland. 
* Under-21 international for the Republic of Ireland.

* He signs for Maidstone United in March 1991 while he was in the Charlton Athletic youth team.  He makes his league debut on the 11/1/91 against Wrexham. 
* As a free agent he signs for Gillingham in July 1992, playing his first game on the 15/8/92 against Northampton Town. 
* He is transferred to Peterborough United in August 1994 for £70,000, making his debut on the 13/8/94 against Bristol Rovers.  His first goal as a professional is on the 11/3/95 against Crewe Alexandra. 
* Birmingham City sign him in February 1996 for £400,000.  His debut is on the 18/2/96 against Stoke City and he scores his first goal on the 20/4/96 against Derby County. 
* He becomes a Premier League player on the 1/2/97 wearing the Coventry shirt, making his debut at Sheffield Wednesday's ground (0-0).  The Highfield Road club had payed £400,000 to Birmingham for his transfer.

* Signed from Birmingham in the month of February, Breen was impressive on his debut for Coventry City in a game against Sheffield Wednesday despite injuring one of his arms.  He had some good performances in other games, but his mistakes against Manchester and West Ham cost him his place.  He took part in 9 games for Coventry, and had played 21 games for Birmingham before his transfer.

310.name: Hall
pages: * Born in Coventry, Marcus Hall, aged just 20, has managed the to make the dream of defending the Sky Blues colours come true, a dream shared with many of the young lads in the city.  Under Ron Atkinson the wide defender started to show that he has enough talent to play in the Premier League with full guarantee.  If he keeps up his progress he will become one of the most important footballers at the club in the near future.  His work has not gone by unnoticed by the selectors of the England team who have called him up five times for the under-21 side.

* His natural position is that of left back, although at times he has played as a central defender.  A promising footballer, with good mastery of the ball and who covers a lot of ground, he joins in the attack decisively and quickly, supporting midfielders constantly.  Despite his youth, Marcus moves along his flank naturally, regaining his position quickly, confident of his ability.
x
* 5 under-21 international appearances for England.

* A native of Coventry and trained in the Highfield Road youth squad, Marcus Hall has been a professional since the 1st of July 1994.  He makes his debut in the League on New Years Eve of this same year replacing Phil Neal in a home game against Tottenham Hotspur.  Coventry go down 0-4. 
* In the 95-96 season he manages to find a gap in the starting line-up of the Sky Blues due to the prolonged absence of David Burrows.

* A hernia suffered in the pre-season kept him out until after Christmas. When he reappeared his performance was acceptable, although he had problems to find a regular place in the side.  Even so, he was called up four times for the England under-21 side.

311.name: Daish
pages: * The arrival of Liam Daish at Coventry in February 1996 was a shot in the arm for the weakened defence of Ron Atkinson.  The Irish international left behind him a long career in the lower divisions and a lasting memory at Birmingham City.  This is his third season at Coventry and his chances of playing depend mainly on whether he has recovered from a knee injury which he suffered the season before.

* A very strong central defender, Liam Daish instils enthusiasm and power into every one of his actions.  In tasks of contention he is very hard to beat because he never shies away from physical contact, and is always efficient and, at times, tough.  A left-footed player, he is more skilful that he looks on first sight and he has good judgement when distributing the ball.  Good in the air, he is particularly dangerous at set-plays and he also has a powerful shot with his left.  A leader on the pitch he infects the rest of the team with his winning character.

* Second Division Champion 95. 
* Third Division Champion 91.

* 5 full international appearances for Eire. 
* 1 B-international appearance. 
* 5 under-21 international appearances.

* A product of the Portsmouth youth squad, the team of his hometown, Liam Daish turned professional on the 29th of September 1986. 
* On the 11th of July 1988 he signs for Cambridge United as, at Portsmouth, he had only managed to play one game.  After living through two successive promotions, Cambridge are relegated in the 92-93 season. 
* On the 10th of January 1994 he is transferred to Birmingham City for £50,000.  He made his debut the following day with a 2-1 defeat in the visit to Notts County. 
* Barry Fry, the manager at Birmingham, that the Daish could stop a bus. He was made the team's captain and at the end of the 94-95 season is voted a member of the Second Division Dream Team after leading the charge into the First Division. 
* A full international for the Republic of Ireland, it was Jack Charlton who gave him his chance to make his debut. 
* Signed by Coventry on the 24th of February 1996 for £1,500,000, he makes his debut this same day at home to Middlesbrough.  On the 9th of March he scores his first goal in the Premier League in a game against Everton played at Goodison Park. 
* An injury during a training session in January 97 keeps him out for the rest of the championship.
* An injury during a training session in the month of January kept him out of the team for the rest of the season.  Until that moment he had played 21 games and scored a goal against Sunderland.

312.name: Williams
pages: * After his extraordinary debut in the Premier League, Paul Williams goes into his third season at Coventry.  He puts in a lot of effort and never gives up the ghost.  He is always available for the manager, and does his job in any position and doesn't slope off when things are going badly.  Thanks to players like him, Coventry can puff out their chests with pride at being a Premier League team.

* Strong and firm, Paul Williams is a central defender with plenty of competitive spirit.  An iron marker, he has all the resources needed by a defender.  He is secure when making interceptions and workmanlike with aerial balls, oozing effort on the pitch.  He works untiringly for the full ninety minutes, and works hard to win back possession, although he should improve his distribution.  He has a powerful shot on goal from a distance and also joins in the attack at set-plays.
x
* 6 under-21 international appearances for England.

* A product of the Derby County youth squad, he is a professional since the 13th of July 1989.  Loaned to Lincoln City on the 9th of November of this same year, he defends their colours in three league games. 
* From the 91-92 season on he becomes a regular in the starting line-up at Derby.  In the 94-95 season he forms an excellent defensive partnership with Craig Short and, and after Gordon Cowan's departure to Wolves, he is made the team's captain. 
* On the 6th of August 1995 he is transferred to Coventry for £950,000, in an exchange operation that takes Sean Flynn to Derby.  At Coventry he coincides with Paul Williams, who leaves Highfield Road four days later to join Plymouth Argyle. 
* He makes his debut in the Premier League on the 19th of August 1995 in a game against Newcastle played at St. James Park.  Coventry loose 3-0.
* He scores his first goal for the Sky Blues on the 4th of November 1995 against Nottingham Forest at Highfield Road (2-3). 
* At the end of his first season at Coventry he is voted "Player of the Year" by the club's supporters.

* He played in midfield, where he was a good ball-winner and in the centre of the defence, being more comfortable when it was made up of three centre backs.  He had some great duels with Hughes and Bergkamp, who he marked impeccably.  Williams took part in 32 games and scored two goals.

313.name: Burrows
pages: * For years David Burrows has been considered as one of best the wide defenders in English football.  However, despite that fact that during his career he has been called up by his national team, he has never actually made his full international debut.  A man with strong character and used to fighting for titles in his spell at Liverpool, he is not just content with trying to keep Coventry up.  Aged 29 he hopes to reach new glories.  To do so he will give his all to Coventry, contributing with his experience and competitive spirit.

* A left back who covers a lot of ground, David Burrows can also operate well in the centre of defence and even as a midfielder.  Solid and hard in defensive tasks, helped by being quick and disciplined, he is very authoritative and doesn't hesitate to join in the attack at the slightest opportunity.  He has a powerful shot with his left from just outside the box, although he doesn't score many goals.  A temperamental man, his character betrays him at times, and the loss of concentration affects his performance.

* League Champion 90. 
* FA Cup Champion 92. 
* Charity Shield Medal 89 and 90.

* 3 B-international appearances for England. 
* 7 under-21 international appearances.

* A product of the West Bromwich Albion youth squad, David Burrows made his debut for the first team on the 22nd of April 1986.  He was just 17.  On the 8th of November 1986 he turned professional. 
* A Liverpool player since the 20th of October 1988, his transfer was set at £550,000.  In his second season at Anfield (89-90), Liverpool are proclaimed League Champions after playing 23 games and alternating at left back with Steve Staunton.  In August 1991 he scored his first goal for the Reds against Everton.  Months later he rounded off his season with victory over Sunderland (2-0) in the FA Cup final.  In this game David played at the heart of the defence alongside Mark Wright. 
* Julian Dicks signing for Liverpool was accompanied by Burrows departure to West Ham on the 17th of September 1993.  He made his debut the following day in a game which ended with a 2-0 win for the Hammers. 
* In the 94-95 season he plays for three different teams.  He starts off at West Ham, but on the 6th of September he is transferred to Everton for £1 million, the same amount paid by Coventry to acquire his services on the 2nd of March 1995. 
* He made his debut for the Sky Blues on the 4th of March.  Coventry and Southampton drew 0-0.  Burrows had been signed by Ron Atkinson to strengthen the defence to try to avoid relegation to the First Division, something successfully achieved. 
* A hernia get him out form October 96 till April 97.

* A hernia kept him out from October until April.  When he recovered he took up his position in the centre of the defence, and City appeared more solid at the back.  He had a great game against Liverpool, perhaps the best of the 18 he played.

314.name: Shaw
pages: * When Crystal Palace's relegation was confirmed in May 1995 Richard Shaw suggested the possibility of a transfer to a Premier League team.  Richard was one of the favourites among the Eagles' crowd, who had voted him "Player of the Year", but, after nine years he thought that the moment had come to start a new period.  However, his departure was delayed a few months.  In the meanwhile, he continued to play for Crystal Palace with the same spirit as always until he moved to Coventry in November.  His proven professionality made him into an important man at Highfield Road as well. The Sky Blues have got hold of a good footballer, but above all, a great professional who was voted second best player of the year by the fans at Coventry.

* He can play perfectly well both at centre back and at right back.  He makes up for his lack of height with great agility and quick movements, allowing him to anticipate his rival.  An extraordinary man-to-man marker, he is firm when regaining possession and he is hard to beat for speed.  On the other hand, his contribution to the attacking game is small; although he is able to pass the ball he doesn't push up much and you don't often see him have a go.
* First Division Champion 94.
x

* Trained in the lower ranks of Crystal Palace, he turned professional on  the 4th of September 1986.  He defended the Eagles colours for 10 seasons and saw their return to the First Division in 1990 followed by relegation then by promotion again. 
* On the 14th of December 1989 he was loaned to Hull City, where he played 4 league games. 
* In 1990 he played in the FA Cup final, Crystal Palace loosing 1-0 to Manchester United. 
* In the 94-95 season Shaw formed an extraordinary defensive partnership with Chris Coleman, although they couldn't prevent Palace from being relegated.  In any case, this year he is voted "Player of the Year" by the fans at the club. 
* Transferred to Coventry on the 17th of November 1995 for £1 million, Ron Atkinson lets him make his debut two days later in a game against Queens Park Rangers (1-1).

* The experienced Coventry defender had a good season, playing in different positions (wide defender, central defender and wing back).  As a marker he did some excellent work, his marking jobs on Kanchelskis, McManaman and Ian Wright being outstanding.  He was voted second best player of the team by the Coventry City fans.  He took part in 35 league games.

317.name: Soltvedt
pages: * Trond Egil Soltvedt is one of Coventry's most important signings for this season.  Coming from Rosenborg, the club where his asking price soared after the team knocked out Milan from the Champions League.  His arrival at Coventry could take some of the responsibility from McAllister's shoulders, and he could form an excellent partnership with him in the midfield.

* In the beginning of his career he played as a forward, but since his move from Brann to Rosenborg he has moved back a bit to act as a link-man between the forwards and the midfield.  Left-footed, although he can also use his right well, Sotvedt takes part constantly in the attacking game.  He likes to catch the defence by surprise and get in a shot.

* 2 Norwegian League Championships. 
* Norwegian Cup Champion once.
* Full Norwegian international.

* Trondt Egil Soltvedt had spent the whole of his career at Brann and Rosenborg, both Norwegian clubs, before signing for Coventry. 
* His performance for Rosenborg in San Siro against Milan (1-2) in the Champions League aroused the interest of several European clubs.  Soltvedt was voted the man of the match. 
* Coventry paid Rosenborg £500,000 for him.
* It was a great season for Soltved who saw how his asking price soared after his performance in the Champions League.  Soltved was Rosenborg's most dangerous and skilful player.

318.name: Huckerby
pages:
* In November 1995 Newcastle got in ahead of Manchester United and hurried through the signing of Darren Huckerby, despite the interest of Manchester United.  Signed to cover for the possible absence of Ferdinand, Huckerby had the chance to make his debut when Les was injured and, in just one game, earned the appreciation of the St. James Park crowd. 
* Signed by Gordon Strachan in the month of September, Huckerby produced an excellent season for the Sky Blues, earning the confidence of his team-mates and that of the fans.  His talent gave him an assured place in Strachan's teams.

* He can play both in the midfield and in the forward line, although it is up front where he is most comfortable.  A good finisher, his game is better when there is a pure centre forward in front of him.  A versatile footballer, he has an acceptable technique, distributing the ball with good judgement and covering a lot of ground, making him a complete player.  He is on the way to becoming a useful link-man, as he has a lot of attacking resources and pops up well in dangerous positions.  Still learning, he should work to polish out his defects and improve his virtues.  He has improved a lot in making goalscoring passes for team-mates.
x
* 4 under-21 international appearances for England.

* Professional since the 14th of July 1993, he makes his debut for Lincoln City, the club where he had trained, on the 1st of March 1994, in a game against Shrewsbury Town.  This same day he shows his marksmanship, scoring the team's second. 
* Sought after by a lot of Premier League clubs, among others, Manchester United, he is transferred to Newcastle on the 10th of November 1995 for £400,000. 
* He makes his debut in the Premier League on the 20th of January 1996 in a game against Bolton Wanderers.  Huckerby came on as a substitute for Kitson in the second half to take part in the team's 2-1 victory. 
* Unable to find a place in the line-ups of Kevin Keegan, the Newcastle manager, Darren is transferred to Coventry on the 22nd of November 1996. His transfer is set at £1 million. 
* He makes his debut for Coventry on the 23/11/96 at Highfield Road against Aston Villa (1-2). 
* He scores his first goal for the Sky Blues against the team where he had played, Newcastle, on the 17/12/96 in Coventry's ground (2-1).

* He arrived at Coventry in the month of November from Newcastle, after playing on loan at Millwall.  Huckerby made his debut against Aston Villa causing a good impression in the 16 minutes given to him.  His talent for setting up and scoring goals was important, especially in the games against Newcastle and Leeds.  He took part in 25 games and scored five goals, and was also called up for the under-21 team twice.

319.name: Boland
pages: * Willie Boland is one of the valuable young players at Highfield Road. Until now he has been a patient substitute waiting for his chance.  Perhaps this will be the season when he can launch his career.

* A midfielder with exquisite technique and an extraordinary passer, he operates perfectly as right winger.  Very secure with the ball at his feet, he can hold onto it waiting for support and pass it accurately.  Elegant when circulating the ball, he is a little irregular.  This lack of consistency has prevented him from earning the confidence of the managers. In any case, given his youth, the future looks promising.
x
* 9 under-21 international appearances for the Republic of Ireland.

* Originally from the Coventry City junior team, Willie Boland turned professional on the 4th of November 1992.  His debut with the first team took place on the 1st of May 1993 in a League game against Chelsea. 
* In his second season at Highfield Road, with Neal on the bench, he manages to play 27 League games, although in the 94-95 season his level dropped drastically. 
* Ron Atkinson, made manager in February 1995, hardly uses him.

* He hardly figured in Gordon Strachan's plans who only used him for a few minutes against Newcastle at St. James Park.  Even so, he is one of Ireland's most promising players, and was called up three times for the under-21 team.

320.name: Telfer
pages: * Telfer is facing his third season at Coventry and he is convinced of his chances of figuring on the team-sheets, as he was one of the players who appeared most last season.  He is competent in his position, and it is probable that he won't lack chances to play.

* A midfielder gifted for winning back the ball, Paul Telfer has the touch and vision necessary to distribute the game with purpose.  He operates on the whole of the right of midfield, although tactical considerations sometimes forces him to play on the left, where his performance drops. Predisposed to pushing up, he doesn't hesitate to have a dig at the smallest chance, showing the power and accuracy of his right.  A complete footballer, he defends effectively and attacks dangerously, but his main defect is his irregularity.  During the course of his career he has played some games at right back, and has done pretty well in this position.
x

* 1 B-international appearance for Scotland. 
* 3 under-21 international appearances.

* A Scot born in Edinburgh, Paul Telfer played in the lower ranks of Luton Town before turning professional on the 7th of November 1988, although he didn't get to make his debut for the first team until 1991 in a game against Everton. 
* From the 91-92 season onwards he starts to appear with a certain regularity in Luton's starting line-ups, but his career doesn't receive the definitive push until the arrival of David Pleat at the club in 1991. 
* In 1994, after recovering from injuries due to a traffic accident, he gets play in the semi-final of the FA Cup. 
* Luton Town's star in the 94-95 season, with 9 goals in 46 league games, he is transferred to Coventry on the 11th of July 1995 for £1,5 million.
* He made his debut for the Sky Blues on the 19th of August 1995 with defeat at St. James Park in a game against Newcastle (3-0).  On the 23rd of August, in his first appearance at Highfield Road, he scores his first goal in the Premier League. 
* During the 95-96 season there is speculation of a possible move to Blackburn Rovers in exchange for £3 million, but Coventry turn the offer down.

* He had a good season, playing on both sides of the midfield, and even as a wing back when Strachan changed the system, adapting well to the defensive aspects by not the attacking ones.  He took part in 34 games and didn't open his account.

321.name: McAllister
pages: * McAllister is the soul of Coventry and the Scotland team, as he was at Leeds.  A footballer with a lot of class and characters, in after a handful of games he was made captain.  This is his second season at Highfield Road and the fans hope that he will be the same player who dazzled at Leeds with his talent and sacrifice.

* He normally plays at centre half, the position in which he deploys his abilities masterfully to distribute the ball.  Helped by an exquisite technique, he is able to impose his rhythm on the game and create a lot of scoring chances for his team-mates.  Skilful and powerful physically, he helps his team-mates in defensive tasks and when he gets into dangerous positions in the rival box he is very dangerous, as he has a powerful shot on goal and doesn't hesitate to use it given the slightest opportunity. He is also a free-kick specialist and safe from the penalty spot. 
* A footballer with leadership capacity, both at his club and his national team, where his presence is a constant reference for his team-mates.  In every game he tries to infect the rest of his team with his winning spirit burning up calories on every square inch of the pitch.

* English League Champion 92. 
* Scottish First Division Champion 85. 
* Charity Shield Medal 92.

* 53 full international appearances for Scotland.  5 goals.  He made his debut on the 25th of April 1990 in a friendly with East Germany (0-1) disputed in Glasgow. 
* He scored his first goal on the 17th of October 1990.  Scotland beat Switzerland 2-1 in Glasgow. 
* Present in the Sweden 92 European Championship, he played from the start in the three games his side played against Holland (0-1), Germany (0-3) and the CIS (3-0).  In this last game he scored a goal. 
* Scottish Captain in the England 96 European Championship, he played from the start in his side's three games against Holland (0-0), England (0-2) and Switzerland (1-0).  McAllister missed a penalty in the game against the England side. 
* 3 B-international appearances. 
* 1 under-21 international appearance.

* He was trained in the Scottish team Fir Park BC, from where he moved to Motherwell in 1981.  He played for four and a half seasons in the team of his hometown, making his debut on the 1st of May 1982 in a game against Queen of the South and the team was proclaimed First Division Champion in 1985.
* On the 15th of August 1985 he was transferred to Leicester City for £125,000.  He adapted quickly to this team and on the 28th of September 1985 he made his debut in the English First Division against Ipswich Town. The following season he formed an attacking partnership with Alan Smith and Leicester dropped to the Second Division, something which didn't lower his asking price, in fact the opposite occurred.   Brian Clough was very interested in signing him for Nottingham Forest. 
* An international since April 1990, he didn't take part in the Italian World Cup where his side failed miserably, even loosing to Costa Rica. 
* On the 2nd of July 1990 he signed for Leeds, just promoted to the First Division.  His asking price had now risen to £1 million.  Together with David Batty and Gary Speed, McAllister led a great team that won the League title in 1992 and he earned the recognition of specialists and fans in Britain.
* After his outstanding performance in the Sweden 92 European Championship including a goal against the CIS, several Italian clubs are interested in signing him, but he stays at Leeds.  He was made the team's captain in the absence of Gordon Strachan and kept this position of responsibility until Strachan's return. 
* Scotland captain, Glasgow Rangers tried to bring him to the club several times, but without success. 
* In the England 96 European Championship McAllister once again showed signs of his class.  Known as Braveheart among the Scottish fans, he once again lead the national team.  However, in a game against the host nation, David Seaman saved a penalty of his which would have tied the game.  In the end Scotland lost 2-0 and were knocked out in the first phase. 
* Shortly afterwards he moves to Coventry City for £3 million.  His move creates a lot of disillusion at Leeds, as the Elland Road crowd considered him one of their best players. 
* He makes his debut for Coventry in the Premier League on the 17/8/96 at Highfield Road against Nottingham Forest (0-3). 
* He scores his first goal in the league for Coventry on the 21/8/96 at Upton Park against West Ham (1-1).

* You could always expect more form a player like McAllister but in general his first season at Coventry was acceptable.  He was made captain after three matches after the Sky Blues poor start to the season.  McAllister scored some important goals which helped keep Coventry in the Premier League, also showing his talent for taking penalties, corners and free-kicks. He was also a regular in the Scotland team which has now classified for the France 98 World Cup.

323.name: Johansen
pages: * Twin brother of the Bolton player, Michael Johansen, Martin will try and find success in a league as difficult as the Premiership.  To do so he will have to take full advantage of his qualities: speed and skill.  He won't have it easy because he will have to adapt to British football, but it is likely that Strachan will give him some opportunities.

* Martin is a quick slippery forward who can play on either side.  His stature makes his a difficult player for defenders as he doesn't stop moving about, trying to take advantage of his devilish turn.

* Danish League Champion in the 92-93 season. 
* Danish Cup Champion in 1995.
* 1 full international appearance for Denmark.

* Johansen has scored 39 goals in 143 games for Copenhagen. 
* Coventry didn't pay anything to sign Johansen and his contract is for two years. 
* His twin brother, Michael, plays for Bolton Wanderers.
* He played for the Danish club Copenhagen, where he was one of the main attacking references.  He took part in 26 games and scored two goals.

324.name: Haworth
pages: * Considered as one of the most promising Welsh players, Hayworth has already made his full international debut.  Trained in the Cardiff City youth squad his goals and skill led several Premier League clubs to take an interest in him.  Finally, it was Coventry who managed to get hold of this promising footballer who, if he produces what is expected of him, will play from the start in Strachan's teams.

* A young forward, quick and skilful, who usually creates problems for the rival defence.  He has a good shot on goal and he positions himself well. He is in excellent physical shape which helps him get on the end of free-kicks or to get away from his markers.

* 1 full international appearance for Wales.  He makes his debut against Scotland in May 97. 
* 3 under-21 international appearances for Wales. 
* Wales youth international.

* Trained in the Cardiff City youth squad, Coventry sign him on the 21/5/97 for £500,000. 
* The 97-98 season is his first season as a Premier League player.

* Last season was the one in which Hayworth's career took off.  He made it to the full Wales team and his goals caused his name to ring round the ground.  He started on the bench, but little by little, he made a gap for himself until he became one of the Cardiff players with the brightest future.

325.name: Dublin
pages: * Dublin has lost the captain's armband to McAllister, but he is still one of Coventry City's most emblematic players.  His goals have brought a lot of glorious afternoons to the fans at Highfield Park and these are never forgotten even when Dion is going through a bad patch.  Once more his finishing and his work will be indispensable for Strachan who will give him the number 9 shirt and the responsibility of scoring the majority of Coventry's goals.

* A classic centre forward, powerful and bone-crushing, Dion Dublin prefers to use force rather than technique, although he can sometimes surprise with an incredible ball control in the area.  An extraordinary header of the ball, he is able to get behind defenders and surprise them with his jump to head past the keeper.  Hard-working and with the spirit of a leader, he fights for every ball and doesn't give up till the final whistle, trying to infect his team-mates with his competitive spirit.  Resolute in front of goal, his presence in the rival box is a synonym for danger.

* Charity Shield Medal 94. 
* Third Division Champion 91.
x

* Coventry captain, he has been the team's top scorer in his first two seasons at the club. 
* Trained in the Norwich City youth squad, he turned professional on the 24th of March 1988, but didn't get to make his debut for the first team at Carrow Road. 
* On the 2nd of August 1988 he signed for Cambridge United.  On the 16th of December of this same year, with Chris Turner as manager, he made his debut in the League against Wrexham.  At Abbey Station his goals helped to team rise from the Fourth to the Second Division. 
* The coaches at Manchester United took notice of his progress and, on the 7th of August 1992, he was transferred to the Old Trafford club for £1 million.  However, Alex Ferguson hardly aligned him. 
* On the 9th of September 1994 he is transferred to Coventry for £2 million, becoming the most expensive signing in the history of the club. 
* He makes his debut the following day in the visit to Queens Park Rangers. Dublin plays from the start and scores the Sky Blues second goal.  In his first thirteen games with Coventry he scores 10 goals, finishing the season as the team's top scorer. 
* At the end of the 95-96 season he extended his contract for another four years, silencing the rumours of an imminent transfer.

* It was a somewhat irregular season for Dublin.  He lost the captaincy to McAllister and until the 11th game he hadn't scored a goal and was forced onto the substitutes' bench.  His return to the first team in December coincided with Coventry's best run.  Dublin managed to score four goals in four games.  He also played a few games in the defence, but returned to the front line in the last stage of the championship, scoring the winner at Anfield, and another goal against Arsenal before receiving a knee injury.

326.name: Ducros
pages: * There was plenty of talk at Highfield Road about Andrew Ducros, a young lad from the Coventry youth squad who has managed to make his debut in the Premier League.  In the five games he played last season he left behind some indications of being a good footballer and in is likely that he will play even more this season.

* Andrew Ducros' most notable feature is his extraordinary scent for goal. A classical centre forward, he is a true danger inside the box, although we need to see more of him in high-level competition to evaluate his characteristics.  At the moment he is promising footballer.
x
x

* A product of the Coventry youth squad, he arrives in the first squad in the 94-95 season, although neither in this nor in the following season does he makes his debut in the Premier League. 
* He makes his debut in the Premier League for Coventry on the 17/8/96 at Highfield Road against Nottingham Forest (0-3). 
* He plays his first game from the start on the 21/8/96 against West Ham at Upton Park (1-1).

* It was Andrews best season since arriving in the first squad as he managed to make his debut against Nottingham Forest.  Four days later he played as a starter for the first time, doing some good work out on the right.  He took part in three more games before receiving an injury that kept him out the team until almost the end of the season.

327.name: O'Neill
pages: * Injuries and problems in finding his ideal form left the Northern Ireland international without any chances to show his ability as a winger.  At Highfield Road everyone expects that O'Neill can be more useful than he has been until now.

* He usually plays as a midfielder on the right, a zone where he uses his good touch and talent for distributing the ball.  Michael O'Neill is a footballer with attacking tendencies, with a powerful shot on goal, allowing him to score goals regularly.  In fact, at times, he has played as a forward and also on the left of the midfield.
x
* 31 full international appearances for Northern Ireland.

* Michael O'Neill's professional career started in 1987 in the ranks of Newcastle.  After two years at St. James Park he was transferred to Dundee United.  In the 91-92 season he showed signs of his scoring ability when he found the net four times in eight league games. 
* A Northern Ireland international, in 1993 he signed for Hibernians, a Scottish Premier League club. 
* In the summer of 1996 he returns to England, arriving at Coventry City for £500,000.  In principle, the Northern Ireland player is to be the substitute for the veteran Gordon Strachan on the right.
* O'Neill didn't have much joy in his first season at Coventry.  He only played in the first half of the first game, spending the rest of the season either injured or in the reserve team.

328.name: Whelan
pages:
* On the 23rd of December 1996 the fans at Highfield Road were leaving the ground happy.  On the one hand, Coventry had beaten Everton.  But also, the winner had been scored by Noel Whelan, who was making his home debut. According to Ron Atkinson, the former Leeds forward is the sort of player that you have to sign at the first opportunity that presents itself, because if you don't, when you try again it will be too late. 
* Already as a youth Whelan had shown an extraordinary talent many times. An under-21 international, nobody doubts that, if he keeps up his progress, he will soon be playing for the national side.  Aged 22, "Snowy" has a sweet future ahead of him.  Ron Atkinson was right.

* Noel Whelan is a very complete forward, with class and an scent for goal. Dynamic, he moves around the entire attacking zone trying to help create space for his team-mates.  Technically good, he is outstanding for the apparent ease with which he resolves the one-on-one with the keeper, hiding his intentions until the moment of the final shot.  A specialist at chipping the ball over rival goalies, he scores most of his goals on the first touch.  He has an effective header, and is able to shield the ball well, and never runs away from a collision.  Still very young, Whelan is one of the most promising players in English football.

* European National Team Champion in the youth category. 
* English Youth Cup champion in 93.

* 2 under-21 international appearances for England.  He made his debut scoring the winner against the Republic of Ireland in a game played at St. James Park. 
* Youth international, in 1993 his side was proclaimed European Champion in 93.

* Born in Leeds, Noel Whelan is one of the products of the extraordinary generation of footballers to come from the Elland Road youth squad. In 1993 the Leeds United youth team, with Whelan among them, won the Youth Cup and this same year Whelan was also in the team that won the European Youth Championship. 
* Professional since the 5th of March 1993, he made his debut in the Leeds first team on the 4th of Mary of this same year, in a game against Sheffield Wednesday played at Hillsborough. 
* He scored his first goal on the 24th of August 1994 in the last minute of the game between Leeds and Arsenal at Elland Road (1-0).  Whelan had come on as a substitute during the game.  The Arsenal keeper was David Seaman. It was the first of seven that he scored in the first fourteen games of the 94-95 season. 
* He started the 95-96 season at Leeds, but on the 16th of December 1995 he is transferred to Coventry for £2 million.  Ron Atkinson, the manager of the Sky Blues, had full confidence in him and let him make his debut on the day he signed.  Coventry lost 4-1 in their visit to Aston Villa. 
* His home debut took place on the 23rd of December against Everton.  Whelan managed to scored the winner (2-1).  He finished the season as the second top scorer in the team with eight.

* It was a slightly frustrating season for Whelan as it was hoped that the strike partnership with Dublin would be more effective than it was.  In November things weren't going well for Noel as he had only scored one goal. Little by little he found his form until he produced his two best performances against Arsenal and Southampton.  Whelan took part in 35 games and scored six goals.

329.name: Jones
pages:
* The eternal understudy to Mike Stowell at Wolverhampton Wanderers, Paul Jones has shown that he is a keeper with talent and his performance last year was vital for Stockport County's successful promotion bid.  His great performances were rewarded with his international debut for Wales in a game against Scotland in May.
* His arrival at Southampton is, without doubt, a step forward in his career.  He will have to fight with Beasant and Taylor for the place, but given his quality, it wouldn't be a surprise to see him in the Southampton goal.

* A very big goalkeeper, Paul Jones is dominant in the air, taking advantage of his size.  He is a little irregular at times, capable of the best and worst.  He is a true specialist at stopping penalties.
x
* One international appearance for Wales, he made his debut at the top level in May 1997 against Scotland.

* Wolverhampton Wanderers sign him from the amateur club Kidderminster Harriers for £40,000 in July 1991.  His first game for Wolves is on the 3/11/92 against Sunderland.
* He was the hero of the 4th round Cup tie in the 94-95 season against Sheffield Wednesday, stopping a Chris Bart-Williams penalty in the first game at Hillsborough and then one from Chris Waddle in the replay.  Thanks to this Wolverhampton Wanderers went through.
* He is transferred to Stockport County on the 25th of July 1996.  His first game for the team is on the 17th of August against Crewe Alexandra. 
* Southampton pay Stockport £1.700.000 for him and Lee Todd in July 1997.

* Jones signed for County at the beginning of last season and ever since his arrival he caused an immediate impact, holding on to his place until the end of the season.  His performance was particularly outstanding in the last few weeks of the championship, keeping 7 clean sheets, and thus making a big contribution to the club's promotion.  He played 46 league games.

330.name: Moss
pages: * Although he had already managed to make his debut in the Premier League last season, playing three games, Neil Moss theoretically starts as the club's fourth keeper.  In front of him are Jones, Beasant and Taylor, who all have more experience than him.  He has to wait for an opportunity to play and continue his progress.

* A very young goalie, Moss is still a little inexperienced in top-level competition.  However, his future looks brilliant as, judging by his talent, he is one of the most promising keepers in England.  Very sure on his line, he needs some more minutes at the top level to confirm his progress.
x
x

* Until he arrived in Southampton in 1996, he had played exclusively for Bournemouth, the club where he signed as a professional on the 23rd of January 1993.  His league debut took place on the 15th of January of this same year in a game against Brighton & Hove Albion (3-3), after coming on for Vince Bartram.
* After Bartram's departure, Neil Moss shared the place in goal at Bournemouth with Ian Andrews, though he played less than him.
* The absence of Bruce Grobbelaar in the 95-96 season led directly to his signing by Southampton.  Grobbelaar moved to Plymouth.
* He makes his debut in the Premier League on the 4/9/96 at the Dell against Nottingham Forest (2-2).

* After arriving in December 95, Moss finally made his debut in the Premier League in the fourth game of the season against Nottingham Forest due to Beasant's absence.  Four games later he played in two more matches against Middlesbrough, where he kept a clean sheet, and against Coventry, where he let in a goal.

x

332.name: Beresford
pages: * If the departure of Robbie Elliott to Bolton seemed to leave the way open for John Beresford to make a first team place his own, the signing of the Italian Alessandro Pistone at the end of July added further uncertainly to Beresford's future at Newcastle. Nevertheless, John signed a new contract for two years at the end of last season which seemed to indicate that Kenny Dalglish had not lost faith in the full back. However he was transfered to Southampton on the 6th of February 1998 for 1.500.000 pounds.

* John Beresford is a left back who stands out for his ability to constantly get forward in support of the attack. Fast and with tremendous reserves of stamina he is untiring in his work. He keeps rival forwards under constant pressure and as soon as his team regains possession is ready to offer himself as an outlet on the left flank, often getting as far forward as the edge of the opponent's penalty area from where his crosses, looking to pick out the Newcastle forward line.
* In his defensive duties he is consistent and very safe in one on one situations. However his tendency to get forward at every opportunity to support his forwards means that he will now and again leave some spaces, which rival forwards can take advantage of.
* First Division Championship winners medal 1992-93.

* 2 "B" international appearances for England. 
* 26 youth international appearances scoring 3 goals.

* A product of Manchester City's youth system Beresford signed professional on 16th September 1983. After 3 seasons without being given the chance to make his first team debut, he became a free agent at the end pf the 85-86 campaign. On 4th August 1986 he was taken on by Barnsley and on 24th of that month he made his debut against Crystal Palace.
* On 23rd March 1989 he was transfered to Portsmouth for £300,000 where he became an automatic first team choice. 
* Transfered to Newcastle on 2nd July 1992 he helped the club clinch promotion to the Premier Leagueat the end of his first season at  St. James' Park.  
* Beresford was listed in the England squad for a game against Norway but didn't get the chance to make his debut.
* At the end of the 96-97 season he renewed his contract with Newcastle for two seasons. 
* Signed for Southampton on the 6th of February 1998.

* Throughout the whole season John Beresford and Robbie Elliott kept up a ding dong battle for the first team left back spot. He suffered an injury in January that kept him out of the side but once recovered showed excellent form. In total he played in 19 league games. In only one of those did he fail to make the starting line up.

333.name: Todd
pages: * Lee Todd starts his career in the Premier League after catching the eye of several teams last season with his game.  Todd has the chance of a lifetime as not everyone gets to play at the top level of English football.  He will have a job to find a gap in the starting line-up, but if they give him the chance and he plays as well for them as he did for Stockport he could become one of Southampton's revelations.

* Lee Todd makes up for his lack of height with a truly commendable fighting spirit.  He works incessantly at left back, joining in the attack quickly and with determination, and regaining his position in the defence rapidly.
x
x

* Originally from the Hartlepool United juniors, Todd signs as a professional for Stockport County on the 23rd of July 1990.  His debut for the club is on the 1st of September 1990 against Walsall and he scores his first goal as a professional against Wrexham on the 26th of December 1994.
* Southampton pay £1,700,000 for an operation which brought both him and Jones to the club.
* The 97-98 season is his first as a Premier League player.

* In his seventh season at the club, Lee Todd was once again one of Stockport's best players.  He took part in 41 league games and earned the applause and respect of the fans yet again.  His good performances caught the attention of Premier League teams, especially the danger he created in attack.

334.name: Palmer
pages:
* His signing by Southampton in the month of September was on the books, as the Leeds manager, George Graham, seemed to show little interest in him. This despite showing commitment and professionality in the three years he defended the Leeds colours.
* What Leeds have lost Southampton and their supporters will have gained. We are looking at one of the best central defenders in the Premier League.

* During the course of his career he has played in several different positions, both as a central defender or in front of the back four, where his performance is better.  A footballer in extraordinary physical condition, his presence in the midfield is a shot in the arm for the midfield, as he offers support in attacking tasks, but above all, when trying to win the ball back.He is an untiring ball-winner who makes up for his technical limitations by battling and with constant commitment.  A right-footed player who covers a lot of ground, he makes his presence felt in both areas. He joins in the attack easily, although he is not noted for his goals.  Despite his height, he is not excellent in the air.  He has a winning character and, often, takes the burden of the team on his shoulders. Authoritative, but generous, Palmer is an excellent team player who adapts to the demands of the manager, a necessary type of footballer in any team.
* League Cup Champion 90-91 with Sheffield Wednesday.

* 18 full international appearances for England.  He makes his debut on the 29th of April 1992 in a game against the Confederation of Independent States (CIS) played in Moscow (2-2).  His first and only goal for his country was on the 17th of February 1993 against San Marino, and a classification game for the United States 94 World Cup played at Wembley (6-0).
* 5 under-21 international appearances.
* 4 times youth international.  1 goal.

* He was trained at West Bromwich Albion, a club in his home town, signing for them on the 21st of December 1984.  His league debut takes place on the 16th of September 1985.  Palmer comes on for Robbie Denison in a game against Newcastle United.
* The manager Ron Atkinson took notice of him, and so he was transferred to Sheffield Wednesday on the 23rd of February 1989.  His price: £750,000. 
* In the 90-91 season Sheffield return to the First Division and Palmer only missed two games.
* Present at the Sweden 92 European Championship, he plays in the England-France (0-0) and the England-Sweden (1-2) games.
* On the 30th of June 1994 he is transferred to Leeds United for £2,600,000.  In his first season at Elland Road he takes part in 39 games and scores three goals.
* Up till the end of the 94-95 season he had received 30 yellow cards and two red ones.  In this same period he had scored two own-goals.
* On the 26th of September 97 Southampton pay Leeds United £1 million for his transfer.

* He played as a central defender and as a defensive midfielder, performing well.  However, the arrival of the new manager George Graham led to rumours in the press that Palmer was going to leave the club.  A few months later the rumours were confirmed and he moved to Southampton.

335.name: Lundekvam
pages: * By signing Claus Lundekvam, Graeme Souness hoped to reinforce Southampton's back line, a back line which had looked a bit shaky at the beginning of the the 96-97 season.  The Norwegian is a young footballer, but he already has international experience.  He is not an automatic choice for the starting line-up of his national side, but it is likely that he will be among the 22 players who go to the France 98 World Cup.

* A central defender with a lot of physical presence, his bulk makes him an insurmountable barrier in the air.  A strong footballer, he never runs away from a collision.  A good ball winner, his technical limitations prevent him from playing the ball out of defence decisively, and his contribution to the attacking game is practically zero.  Given his youth he has time ahead to improve his ball control.
x
* 4 full international appearances for Norway.

* Clasus Lundekvam started playing football as a schoolboy in the ranks of Selbjorn, although he soon moved to Austenvoll.
* He arrived at Brann while still in the youth category, and after a brief spell once again at Austenvoll, he makes his debut in the Norwegian First Division in 1993 defending the SK Brann colours.  In his first season he only played 3 league games, and in all of these he came on as a substitute. 
* In the starting line-ups since 1994, one year later he plays in the Norwegian Cup Final against Rosenborg, although his team lose in the replay (3-1). 
* In September 1996 he is transferred to Southampton for £400,000.

* He arrived at Southampton from the Norwegian team Brann, and quickly found his way into the first team.  His strength and ability to play the ball out from the back created a good impression among the supporters. He also showed his grim determination in a game against Sunderland where he carried on playing despite having a dislocated shoulder.  The last two games were crucial for Southampton to avoid relegation.

336.name: Dryden
pages:
* Few expected that in his first season in the Premier League, Dryden would manage to find a place in the first team.  Not only did he manage this, but he was also the third most used player at Southampton last season. 
* For this season the arrival of Palmer could act against him and force him onto the bench, though if this happens Dryden will continue to train as normal in case his chance comes.

* A classic central defender, well equipped for the aerial game, but not very sure of himself with the ball at his feet.  A good defender, his bulk and veteran status make him hard to beat, as his experience has brought him a lot of resources for resolving difficult situations.  He never life over complicated, and doesn't hesitate to punt the ball away if he doesn't see a clear outlet.  At times he can play as a defensive centre half, helping constantly to win back balls.  His contribution to attack is practically non-existent, although in his spell at Exeter City he scored goals with a certain regularity.
* Fourth Division Champion 1990.
x

* Trained in the Bristol Rovers youth squad, he signs as a professional on the 14th of July 1987, although he had already made his debut with the first team.
* On the 22nd of September 1988 he is loaned to Exeter City, who decide to sign him definitively on the 8th of March 1989.
* On the 9th of August 1991 Notts County pay £250,000 to acquire his services.  First choice for a season, during the 92-93 season he is loaned first to Plymouth Argyle on the 18th of November and then transferred to Birmingham City on the 19th of March 1993.  His price: £165,000.
* On the 16th of December 1994 he signs for Bristol City, the eternal rival of Rovers, the club where he trained, for £140,000.
* In the summer of 1996 Southampton offer him the chance to make his debut in the Premier League.  His transfer is set at £150,000.
* He makes his debut in the Premier League on the 18/8/96 at the Dell against Chelsea (0-0).
* He scores his first goal in the Premier League on the 4/9/96 at the Dell against Nottingham Forest (2-2).

* In his first season in the Premier League Dryden managed to settle into the Southampton first team.  He was one of the team's revelations because few people thought that someone who had spent most of their career in the lower leagues could perform to such a level.  He took part in 29 games and scored a goal against Nottingham.

337.name: Monkou
pages: * After eight years in England, Kenneth Monkou is one of the foreign players who has been longest in the Premier League, and it is hard to imagine him playing in another country.  A thoroughbred, his constant effort defending Southampton's colours has been recognised by the fans at the Dell who have great affection for him, so much so that they consider him the heart of the Saints.  97-98 will be Monkou's fifth at Southampton.  Although he is now 33, his retirement still looks a long way off, above all if you watch the effort, commitment and illusion with which he plays every game.  A player with so many assets that no-one doubts that Dave Jones will use him.  It isn't every day you find a player with his spirit.

* Despite not being native to Britain, Monkou's style of play is perfectly adapted to the classical British central defender: tall, strong and with total dominance in the aerial game.  Quick at making interceptions and hard at times, he is difficult to beat, as he never runs away from a collision and makes the rival forwards work difficult.  Technically limited, his participation in attack is restricted to corners and free-kicks, where he looks to get in a header and score the occasional goal.
* At times he goes a little over the top when going in for a tackle, which has cost him a lot of bookings during his career.  However, he compensates for this aggression with a strong personality, allowing him to act as a leader of younger team-mates, which works for the good of his side.
x
* 2 under-21 international appearances for Holland.

* Kenneth Monkou was born in Surinam, but, just as with many footballer from his country, he was recruited by a Dutch club, Feyenoord, where he started his career as a player.
* He arrived in England aged 24, transferred to Chelsea for £100,000 (2/3/89). His league debut takes place on the 1st of May 1989 in a game against Stoke City.
* After five seasons at Chelsea, he signs for Southampton on the 21st of August 1992.  His signing cost the club at the Dell £750,000.
* During the course of his career in England he has been sent off twice, been booked 24 times, and scored 3 own-goals.

* It was not a good season for Monkou who was kept out by and injury.  Once he had recovered, the signings of Lundekvam and Dryden acted against him as Souness preferred to play them.  Monkou took part in 13 games and didn't manage to find the net once.

338.name: Benali
pages: * Although he doesn't reach quite the same mythical status as Matt Le Tissier among the Southampton fans, Franny Benali is one of the most acclaimed players at the Dell.  This recognition of his hidden work by the crowd at the club of his hometown is, without doubt, the best prize the defender could hope for after eleven seasons with the Saints, seasons in which, though not playing brilliantly, he has worked hard and enthusiastically to keep the club in the Premier League.

* Franny Benali is an eminently defensive footballer.  Very left-footed, his natural position is at right back, however, he often abandons this position to follow the other team's best player.  An extraordinary marker, and times he is too hard, which has cost him several suspensions during his career. He doesn't complicate life at all, booting the ball away if he has problems to play it.  His contribution to attack is practically zero, letting technically better men do the work.  Untiring and tenacious, Benali is aware that his place is in the defence, and you don't often see him cross the half-way line.
x
* Schoolboy international for England.

* He is one of the footballers in the Premier League who has been booked most.  At the end of the 94-95 season he had accumulated 31 yellow cards, two red ones and more than 100 disciplinary points.
* A native of Southampton, he trained in the lower ranks of the club before signing as a professional on the 5th of January 1987.  However, he doesn't manage to make his debut in the League until the 1st of October 1988, in a game against Derby County.

* During the first part of the championship he was on the bench until he was aligned from the start in a game against Derby at the Dell.  Later, an injury kept him out the team before returning in the final stages of the championship.  He took part in 13 games and didn't score a single goal.

339.name: Dodd
pages: * Jason Dodd's versatility has made him one of the most useful players for Southampton.  A typical club player, Jason prefers to play at right back, but if injuries or suspensions affect the rest of the team he is the first man who the manager thinks of to remedy the problem.

* He usually plays at right back, but his ability also allows him to play in the midfield, from where he joins in the attack and, occasionally, scores goals.  A right-footed player, he is very quick and covers a lot of ground, and is noted for his excellent defending.  Hard to beat for pace, he judges distances well and makes interceptions efficiently.  He has a good shot with his right from outside the area, scoring most of his goals this way.  Still progressing, his performance gets better after each year that passes.
x
* 8 under-21 international appearances for England.

* His first steps in the world of football where made in the modest Bath City, the club of his hometown.  On the 15th of March 1989 he is transferred to Southampton for £50,000, and makes his debut in the League on the 14th of October of this year in a game against QPR.
* After he had managed to settle in the Saints first team, he suffers an injury to his ankle which keeps him out the game.  When he recovers he discovers that Jeff Kenna has taken over as first choice right back and Dodd has some difficult moments on the bench.  Later, Kenna's move to Blackburn Rovers leads to his return to the Southampton line-ups.

* He took part in 23 games, in which he was used as a right back and also as a central defender in the last few games of the championship.  His versatility served Southampton well when the team was fighting to stay up. What's more, Dodd scored a goal against Sunderland.

340.name: Robinson
pages: * After four seasons in the Southampton first team, Matt Robinson hopes that the arrival of Dave Jones to the bench at the Dell will allow him to show that he is a player with enough category to perform in the Premier League.
* He can play both as a winger or as a wing back, though always on the left. Quick and resistant, he has an excellent left, although his lack of experience in high competition is evident.
x
x

* Trained in the Southampton youth squad, he signed as a professional on the 1st of July 1993. 
* He made his debut in the first team in November 1996 in a game against Blackburn.  The Southampton trainer was Graeme Souness.
* For yet another year he had to be content with the role of substitute. However he did play from the start in three important games; against Liverpool, Middlesbrough and Newcastle.

341.name: Williams
pages: x
x
x
x
x
x

342.name: Richardson
pages: * Signed from Coventry, Richardson is a player how is recognised in England for his professionality and the impetus he puts into all his actions.  A footballer who helps balance the midfield, Richardson will give Southampton consistency and regularity.  His winning spirit will do the team good, a team which has suffered a lot in recent seasons to remain in the Premier League.

* Kevin Richardson is not only a hard working midfielder.  Although he can win back in infinite number of balls during a game, his good playing vision and acceptable technique allow him to also give some dangerous passes to his forwards.  An untiring fighter, he puts in a lot of effort during the ninety minutes.  He doesn't hesitate to go in hard and tries to drive his team-mates on.  However, he is guilty of not scoring many goals.  A veteran footballer, he tries to make experience count as an anecdote to his understandable loss of physical capacity.

* Cup Winners Cup Champion 85.
* League Champion 85 and 89.
* FA Cup Champion 84.
* League Cup Champion 94.
* Charity Shield Medal 84, 86 and 90.
* 1 full international appearance for England.

* Originally from the Goodison Park youth squad, Kevin Richardson turned professional for Everton on the 8th of December 1980.  Almost one year later, on the 21st of November 1981, he made his league debut against Sunderland. Howard Kendall was the manager that gave him his first chance.
* In 1984 Everton are proclaimed FA Cup champions after beating Watford in the final 2-0.  However, in the League Cup final of this same year, Everton are beaten by Liverpool 0-1.  The following season his honours list swells with two more titles, League champion and Cup Winners Cup champion, although Richardson didn't play in the final in which Everton defeated Rapid Vienna in Rotterdam (3-1).
* On the 4th of September 1986 he was transferred to Watford for £225,000. In his only season at the club he played 39 league games and scored two goals. His brilliant performance in the cup-tie with Arsenal, in which Watford came through 3-1, would mark his sporting future, as months later, he signed for the Gunners.
* His transfer to Arsenal took place on the 26th of August 1987.  His price: £200,000.  He quickly earned the trust of George Graham and found his way into the first team and contributed to the record 14 consecutive wins.  In 1989 he won the second League title of his career with the dramatic game against Liverpool at Anfield included.
* In 1990 Kevin Richardson starts a brief overseas adventure.  He signs for the Spanish team Real Sociedad on the 1st of July in exchange for £750,000. He coincided with John Aldridge and Dalian Atkinson, who he would play with at Aston Villa.  Strangely, when the Welshman, John Toshack is made the team's manager, one of his first decisions was to get rid of the foreigners. 
* He returns to England, signing for Aston Villa on the 6th of August 1991. His asking price had dropped to £450,000.  With Ron Atkinson as manager, the Villans win the League Cup in 1994, beating Manchester United in the final 3-1.
* He starts the 94-95 season at Aston Villa, but on the 16th of February 1995 he is transferred to Coventry for £300,000.  His signing was the first acquisition made by Ron Atkinson on taking charge of the Sky Blues.  He made his debut at Highfield Road on the 18th of February with a win over West Ham (2-0).
* The price for his transfer to Southampton has to be decided by a tribunal as Coventry and the club at the Dell don't reach an agreement.

* Once more, he was the steady player who did the hidden work that has to be done in every team.  He only missed five games for Coventry and showed his worth in the games against Newcastle where he set up two goals which gave Coventry the win.
