343.name: Oakley
pages:
* To make you debut in the Premier League at the age of 17 is a privilege that few footballers can boast of.  Oakley was able to enjoy this sensation in May 1995, and not only that, but months later his presence in the Southampton line-ups were becoming ever more frequent.  The young midfielder is eternally grateful to Dave Merrington, the team's former manager, for the trust he showed in him.
* Oakley now knows what it is like to play regularly in the Premier League and the manager isn't taking a risk by playing him.  His skill and quality guarantee him a good number of chances to confirm his progress of last season.

* A right-footed midfielder, Oakley's biggest asset is his capacity to constantly join in the attack and take part in dangerous moves.  Despite his youth, he has some extraordinary technical resources which are seen in accuracy of his passing.  He also has a good playing vision which makes him dangerous when he has the ball under control.  He is more comfortable near the touchline, where he will try and get to the by-line to put over a cross to the heart of the box looking for a striker, although he will often take up a more centralised position from where he can try out his powerful shot on goal with his right.
* A good footballer, with a big will to win, if he corrects the mistakes caused by his rushing thinks, mistakes natural in one so young, he could become an important footballer in the coming years.
x
* 1 under-21 international appearance for England.

* Trained in the Southampton youth squad, he went from apprentice to making his debut in the first team on the 6th of May 1995 in a game at Goodison Park, after coming on for Simon Charlton in a game against Everton (0-0). He was only 17 at the time.
* He scored his first goal as a Premier League player for Southampton on the 23/9/96 against Wimbledon at Selhurst Park.

* Oakley has his best season since he arrived in the first squad, despite being injured during February and March.  He took part in 23 games and scored three goals, opening his account in the Premier League.

344.name: Hughes
pages:
* A footballer much loved by the fans, in the few chances he has had to play he has been able to score beautiful goals.  However, he is given to injuries which keeps him out too often and prevents him from enjoying the necessary continuity to let his game settle.
* A Wales under-21 international, injuries were what prevented him from making his debut at the top level.  Hughes hopes that his luck will change and we can see the true ability of the player who was considered as one of the best to come out of the Southampton youth squad in many years.

* David Hughes is an attacking midfielder, so much so that he is perfectly capable of playing as a forward.  Technically good, and blessed with speed and skill, he is able to score spectacular goals, helped by his extraordinary shot.  An untiring worker, he is a footballer who covers a lot of ground with an enviable resistance.  He helps out a lot in defence, although he is more comfortable the nearer the rival box he is.  If he keeps up his progress and if he remains injury-free he could be a useful player in the Premier League.
x
* 1 under-21 international appearance for Wales.

* Despite being a professional at Southampton since the 2nd of July 1991, his debut in the first squad of the club where he trained didn't take place until the 5th of February 1994, in a game the Saints lost to Oldham Athletic 2-1.
* In the 94-95 season he scores some spectacular goals, but a back injury keeps him out.  Since then, various injury problems have prevented him from playing regularly.
* Once more injuries kept him out for a lot of games.  He played in six games and didn't find the net once.

345.name: Le Tissier
pages:
* Every time that Matt Le Tissier goes over to take a corner the fans at The Dell bow to him as a sign of the adoration they hold for him.  The fact is that Le Tissier is the incarnation of the Southampton spirit, and the supporters of the Saints are thankful for every game in which he stays with the club.  The position in the table and the result are unimportant, because Le Tissier is on the pitch and, at any time, everything can change if the magician shows us another trick from his inexhaustible supply.  Many of the best goals in recent seasons have been scored by him.
* Once more he will have to be Southampton's leader, the player who takes on the team's responsibility.  If the team is doing well, it is Matt who has to ensure they continue to win, and if the team is doing badly it is him who has to pull out every last stop to ensure the team stays in the Premier League.  Le Tissier is the soul of this team, his name is synonymous with that of Southampton, although he was on the point of moving to Tottenham. The fans would never have forgiven him for it and given time he probably wouldn't have forgiven himself either.

* Without doubt, Matt Le Tissier is one of the most talented players in the Premier League.  Playing just behind the forward, he is master of all aspects of the attacking game.  He appears in any position in attack and, from there, opens up a wide range of possibilities.  He dispatches long balls to his team-mates with enviable precision, changes wings in an opportune moment or tries the individual play, using his extraordinary turn.  He has also got an extraordinary playing vision, allowing him to use the appropriate technical resource at a given time.  A great passer, he sets up his team-mates as, not only does he see the pass, but he can carry out his intention.
* In a one-on-one he is very hard to defend against, as he can break to either side.  Le Tissier is a fantasy footballer, able to chip a defender, go past another and play the ball through the legs of another in the same play.As if this weren't enough, he has an excellent finish, scoring goals easily, many of them impressive.  He shoots well from a distance with both feet, as well as being a specialist at set-plays.  He takes free-kicks, corners and the penalties, and is a constant reference for his team-mates, who look to him to organise the team's attack.
* At times, he disappears from the game, this intermittence perhaps being his biggest defect.  However, he can reappear when he is least expected, produce a stroke of genius, and settle the game.  At times he is hard and protests in excess, faults that can be put down to his competitive spirit. 
* In short, Matt Le Tissier is an extraordinary footballer, and genius blessed with fabulous class, capable of bringing in the crowd single-handed.
* Voted "Young Footballer of the Year 89-90".

* 8 full international appearances for England.
* 6 B-international appearances.
* 1 youth international appearance.

* Southampton consider Le Tissier to be a home-grown man.  His entire sporting career has taken place at the Dell.  Coming from the club's youth squad, he makes his debut for the first team on the 30th August 1986 in a game against Norwich.  Shortly afterwards, on the 17th of October of this same year, he signs as a professional.
* On the 7th of March 1987 he scored the first of his 8 hat-tricks against Leicester.  The last came on the 19th of August 1995 at the Dell against Nottingham Forest (3-4), although two of his goals were from the spot. 
* After a phenomenal season he is voted "Young Footballer of the Year" in 1990 by the Player Association.
* Although, thanks to his technical characteristics, he plays up front, his strong character has led him to be one of the most booked players in the Premier League.  At the end of the 94-95 season he had received 32 yellow cards and been sent off once.
* He is the Premier League's second top scorer from the penalty spot with 34.  First place is taken up by Jan Molby with 39.
* Up until the beginning of the 97-98 season he had scored 149 goals for Southampton.

* It wasn't a particularly good season for Le Tissier who saw how his team were on the verge of being relegated and how the press blamed him for England's defeat at Wembley against Italy.  Even so, his personality and talent allowed him to shine once more.  He refound his form, and is very possible that without him Southampton would be a First Division team this season.  Le Tissier took part in 31 games and scored 13 goals.

346.name: Basham
pages: * Aged just 20, Steven Basham is one of Southampton's promising players. The young forward his shown an extraordinary goalscoring capacity in the reserves and he now hopes to maintain this efficiency in a competition as tough as the Premier League.

* A centre forward in the classical mould, Steven is strong and heavily built, shoots on goal with both feet and is dominant in the air.  He is also able to hold up the ball while waiting for his team-mates to join in the attack.
x
x
* Trained in the Southampton youth squad, he made his debut with the first team in 1996, in a game against Chelsea.

* Although he took part in the opening game of the season against Chelsea, he hardly had any more opportunities during the course of the season.  In fact, his only appearance from the start was in the game against Manchester United played at Old Trafford.  Steven was on for the full 90 minutes but Southampton lost 2-1.

347.name: Johansen
pages: * Stig Johansen has followed in the footsteps of his team-mates Ostenstad and Lundekvam.  In Norway he played for Bodo Glimt, where he was their star player.  A forward with a considerable goalscoring capacity and an international for Norway, if he adapts to English football Southampton won't have to depend on Le Tissier's goals so much.
* Above all Stig Johansen is a marksman, a player for the box who is always looking for the loose ball.  He is good in the air and his power and speed make him hard to stop.
x
* 3 full international appearances for Norway.
* Johansen signs for Southampton on the 5/8/97 after a series of problems with his former team, Bodo Glint.  He arrived as a free agent.
* He played in the ranks of the Norwegian team Bodo Glint, and reaffirmed himself as one of the best players in Norway.

348.name: Davies
pages: * A very talented player, Kevin Davies has a great chance to show that he could be a valid player for the Premier League.  Until he signed for Southampton he had played for Chesterfield, where his performances had caught the eye of many teams for the Premier League.  It was finally Southampton who acquired his services, and they won't regret it if Davies can live up to the expectations placed in him.

* A young forward with exquisite technique, Kevin Davies operates well on the right of the attack.  Despite his youth, his game shows some details that point to a great footballer; his first-time balls and good turn.  He is also in good physical shape.  These qualities together make him an interesting prospect for the future.
x
x

* Kevin Davies had spent the whole of his career at Chesterfield, the team in whose first squad he has been for the last four seasons until in May when he signed for Southampton, although he couldn't make his debut.
* Southampton paid £750,000 to sign him.
* The 97-98 season was Kevin Davies' first as a Premier League player.

* His good season with Chesterfield, where he played 34 games and scored three goals prompted Southampton to sign him.  At Chesterfield, he had been on of the main references for the team in attack, and was a constant danger in the other team's box.

349.name: Bowen
pages: * This will be Bowen's first season at Southampton after having played beforehand at Swansea and Birmingham.  A Wales international, Bowen is reckoned to be an interesting player, either playing from the start or coming on as a substitute if the team is behind.

* Bowen is a footballer who can play both as an attacking midfielder, a forward or a winger.  A good finisher, he shoots well with either of his feet.He dribbles well and he likes to do individual plays, trying to dribble past defenders to then have a go or set someone up.  For these reasons he is, at times, a bit selfish.  He is also quick of feet and mind, thinking in split seconds what he has to do next.
* Top scorer at Swansea City 93-94.
* A youth, under-21 and full international for Wales twice.

* Originally from the lower ranks of Swansea City, he signs as a professional in July 1990.  He makes his debut in the league on the 26/2/91 against Exeter City, scoring his first goal on the 5/2/93 against Burnley.
* He is transferred to Birmingham City in the summer of 1995 for £275,000. He makes his league debut on the 12/8/95 against Ipswich Town, coming on as a substitute for Richard Forsyth and scoring 5 minutes from the end. Birmingham won 3-1.
*  Southampton pay Birmingham City £500,000 to bring him to the Dell. 
* The 97-98 season is his first in the Premier League.

* The brilliant start that Jason Bowen had to the season caught the eye of the Wales selector who called on him for the game against Holland.  However, his inconsistency meant that he was on the verge of being transferred to Huddersfield.  Even so, his quality didn't pass unnoticed by Southampton, who decided to sign him.

350.name: Hirst
pages:
* At the end of 1991 David Hirst was a forward with a higher asking price than Alan Shearer.  Three years older than Newcastle's marksman, Hirst aroused great expectations among the British fans, who saw in him one of the aspirants to take over the throne left vacant by Gary Lineker.  However, all these hopes were mown down by a series of injuries that cut short his progress and prevented him from settling into the national team.
* His signing by Southampton was a big surprise and a nasty one at that for the fans at Sheffield.  Now at the Dell he can form an explosive partnership with Le Tissier in which talent and finishing could go hand in hand.

* Hirst is an aggressive forward, with a good shot from 20 yards and an excellent aerial game.  Left-footed, he is hard to stop when he is heading for the opponent's goal and is good in a one-on-one with the keeper.  Very secure from the penalty spot.  He is quick and clever in the area, and can find space to have a go, preferably with his head.  He has a good turn and a scent for goal, though is too given to injuries, which has prevented him from enjoying the continuity necessary to reach his best form.  In recent times he is slightly overweight which he should watch, as it takes the edge the reaction times which were very quick in times gone by.
* League Cup Champion 91.

* 3 full international appearances for England.  1 goal.  He made his debut on the 1st of June 1991 with a 0-1 win over Australia in a friendly played in Sydney.  One week later he scored his first goal for his country against New Zealand at Wellington.
* 3 B-international appearances.  2 goals.
* 7 under-21 international appearances. 1 goal.
* 11 youth international appearances.  10 goals.

* He starts his career as an apprentice at the club in his hometown, Barnsley.  A professional since the 8th of November 1985, he is transferred to Sheffield Wednesday on the 11th August 1986 in exchange for £250,000.
* On the 23rd of August 1986 he makes his league debut for the Owls in a game against Charlton Athletic.  Two days later he scores his first goal against Everton, the same club who were on the receiving end of his 100th goal almost ten years later.
* Hirst has the privilege of having been the team's top scorer for five seasons on the trot, from 88-89 to 91-92, regaining this status in the 95-96 season.
* League Cup Champion 1991, he came on for Danny Wilson in the final of the the same competition that Wednesday lost in 1993 to Arsenal.  He also played in the FA Cup replay of the same year; also loosing to the Gunners. 
* On the 27th of April 1996 he scores his 100th goal in the league for Wednesday, though his team still lose to Everton.  Months before this game there had been some rumours of a possible move to the club at Goodison Park. 
* In October 97 Southampton pay Sheffield Wednesday £2,000,000 for his transfer.

* For yet another year, David Hirst was Sheffield Wednesday's top scorer with 13 goals (4 penalties).  He played 30 league games and only in the first of these, the first game of the season, did he come on as a substitute. However, a lot of his season was marked by rumours of a transfer to Everton, rumours which turned out to be unfounded.

351.name: Ostenstad
pages:
* Nobody at the Dell now doubts that Ostenstad has been one of Southampton's best signings in recent years.  His goals and those of Le Tissier were what kept Southampton in the Premier League.  His goal against Sunderland is stuck in the Southampton's fans' memories, a goal that was crucial for Southampton, as was his contribution to the 6-3 win over Manchester United at the Dell.
* Ostenstad starts the season with peace of mind of receiving recognition from everyone, something essential for a forward whose signing was questioned at the time.  If he reaches the level he showed last season the name of Ostenstad could take on a mythical quality.

* Efficient finishing is the most noted characteristic of Egil Ostenstad, a centre forward with a scoring instinct.  Quick and powerful, he is hard to stop when he gets into the rival box with the ball at his feet on the run.  He has a powerful shot on goal with both feet and is brave in the aerial game.  Although he isn't particularly skilful with the ball at his feet, his effectiveness in front of goal makes him a very dangerous player.
* Norwegian League Champion 91.
* 5 full international appearances for Norway.

* In his time as a youth, Egil Ostenstad played in the ranks of Torvastad, a modest Norwegian club.
* In 1990 he makes the step up to Viking Stavanger and plays 10 League games in his first season in the First Division.
* In 1991 Viking are proclaimed league champions, but Ostenstad only played one game from the start.
* Viking's top scorer in 1993 and 1995, he has played 25 times for Norway in the lower categories.
* The extraordinary progress in his game was noticed by Graeme Souness, the Southampton manager.  And so, on the 2nd of October 1996 he was transferred to the English club for £900,000.
* He makes his debut as a Premier League player on the 23/9/97 in Wimbledon's ground losing (3-1) to the local team.  He scores his first goal for the Saints on the 26/10/96 at the Dell against Manchester United (6-3).

* The Dell won't easily forget what Ostenstad did.  The Norwegian forward was perhaps, along with Le Tissier, responsible for Southampton remaining in the Premier League.  Voted "Player of the Year" by the Saints fans, Ostenstad scored the goal against Sunderland that spared the Saints the drop which would have condemned them to First Division football this season. Another of Egil memorable performances was the one against Manchester United (6-3), in which he scored a hat-trick.  He was also a key player in Norway's classification for the France 98 World Cup.

352.name: Poom
pages: * "I swore to myself that I would return, but I didn't think it would be so soon. This time I will do better," declared Mart Poom shortly after signing for Derby County. The Estonian, who had already played for Portsmouth, had to leave England due to problems with his work permit. Now, with a new work permit in his pocket and once more with Jim Smith at the helm, he faces the challenge of showing his class in the Premier League.

* Despite his great height and bulk, Mart Poom boasts an extraordinary agility. He is a young keeper, but with an extensive international experience behind him, allowing him to operate with a lot of safety in difficult situations.  Very good with aerial balls and with quick reflexes, he needs to improve his game with his feet, and his effectiveness in a one-on-one.
x
* 54 full international caps for Estonia.

* Originally from the Estonian club FC Wil, Mart Poom arrived at Portsmouth on the 4th of August 1994, under the orders of Jim Smith.  His transfer was set at £200,000. 
* He made his debut in the First Division on the 12th of August 1995, in a home game against Southend United (4-2). 
* In 1996 his work permit was not renewed, forcing him to leave England and return to his country to play in the ranks of Tallin. 
* On the 26th of March 1997 he was transferred to Derby County for £500,000 on the request of Jim Smith, the current Rams manager. He made his debut in the Premier League on the 5th of April, in a game against Manchester United played at Old Trafford. Derby County came through 2-3. 
* At the moment he is studying at university for a degree in Economics.

* The manager, Jim Smith, received very good reports about Mart Poom after a great game for Esthonia against Scotland. Shortly afterwards, the Derby manager gave the green light for his signing. The Estonian goalie made his debut in the Premier League on a good note, as the Rams defeated the almighty Manchester United at Old Trafford at the beginning of April. From then till the end of the Championship he played 3 more games in the league, although a shoulder injury prevented him from notching up more games.

353.name: Hoult
pages: * Mart Poom's signing casts a shadow of doubt over the future of Russell Hoult at Derby County. The manager, Jim Smith, has already shown his preference for the Estonian keeper, so it looks like Hoult is condemned, in principle, to the reserves. However, Russell is a young keeper and he should have some patience and wait for his chance.

* Despite being heavily built Russell Hoult is an agile goalie between the posts and is quick when coming out. However, his biggest virtue is his dominance in the aerial game, where he uses his height and strength to good effect to grasp the ball securely. Energetic in the area, he constantly orders his defence around.

* A native of Leicester, Russell Hoult was trained in the youth squad at Filbert Street. On the 28th of March 1991 he made the jump to the first squad at Leicester City, although he would have to wait to make his debut.
* On the 27th of August 1991 he was loaned for the first time to Lincoln City, repeating on the 12th of August 1994. In the mean time he was loaned to Bolton Wanderers (3rd November 1993) and defended the Leicester goal on various occasions. 
* On the 17th of February 1995 he arrived at Derby County as a loan player. However, shortly afterwards the club at the Baseball Ground went through with the buying option and paid £300,000 for him.  He made his debut at home on the 26th of February with a 2-1 win over Bolton Wanderers. 
* He started the 95-96 season as the understudy to Steve Sutton, but in October 1995 he takes over in goal. Months later, Derby County are promoted to the Premier League.

* He started the 96-97 season on great form, with some eye-catching performances.  However, as the championship progressed his performance went into decline, speeded up by the six goals he conceded against Middlesborough, and by the very serious error he made against Newcastle at St. James' Park. At the end of the season he lost his place to Mark Poom, although an allowed him to regain his place momentarily.

354.name: Laursen
pages: * That Derby County managed to stay in the Premier League at the end of last season was due largely to Jacob Laursen. The Danish defender had a phenomenal championship, adapting rapidly to English football and fitting in perfectly with Jim Smith's schemes. It is to be expected that in the 97-98 season he will continue along similar lines. The fans at Derby would appreciate it.

* Versatility is the characteristic that best defines him, as although he normally plays as a central defender, in the Danish team he plays as a wide defender. At the start of his career however he played as a midfielder in front of the defensive line  Despite not being excessively tall, he is dominant when it comes to clearing high balls. Strong, quick and with a good shot with his right, he is comfortable in defensive tasks, but does not take part much in the attacking play. To do so he ought to work on his individual technique.
* Danish League Champion 94.

* With 12 full international caps for Denmark he made his debut on the 8th of January 95 in a game against Saudi Arabia at Riyadh. The Danish team won 2-0. 
* Present in the European Championship in England in 96, he only played in the second half of the game against Croatia. Laursen came on as a substitute for Helveg at half time.  Denmark lost 3-0. 
* Olympic international, he took part in the 92 Barcelona Olympic Games.

* Laursen started his career at Vejle Bk, a modest club in his native Denmark. In 1992 he was transferred to Silkeborg, one of the classic Danish teams, who he wins a league title with in 1994. 
* It was Bo Johansson, the Silkeborg manager, who decided to play him further back in the defence. Thanks to this change of position Laursen found a place in the national team. 
* Before the European Championship in England there were several clubs interested in signing him. In the summer of 1996 he is transferred to Derby County, just promoted to the Premier League, in exchange for £500,000.
* He made his debut in the Premier League on the 17th of August 1996, in a game against Leeds United (3-3).  He scored his first goal with the Rams on the 4th of September of the same year against Manchester United.

* In his first season in the Premier League Jacob Laursen managed to find a spot in the defence of the starting eleven at Derby County. He occupied several positions during the course of the season, performing to the satisfaction of the manager. In September he scored a superb goal from a direct free-kick against Manchester United, but it was the only time he did find the target in all of his 35 league appearances.

355.name: Carsley
pages: * Lee Carsley is one of the young products of the Derby County youth squad and one of the most valuable players for Jim Smith. The English manager has full confidence in him and, although he still hasn't managed a definitive place in the starting elevens, it has to be said that he is getting more and more chances. Therefore, it wouldn't be a surprise if he manages to definitively settle down in the team in a competition as difficult as the Premier League.

* Lee Carsley is a versatile footballer, able to player in several positions in the midfield and as a wide defender on either side. Physically strong, he fights for every ball and doesn't hesitate to use force in defence if he thinks it necessary. Very hard-working, he likes to lend support to the attacking play and can score the odd goal every now and again thanks to his powerful long range shot. In any case, we are looking at a eminently defensive player whose ideal position is that of right back, where he makes use of his ability to double up along the touchline.
x
* 1 under-21 international appearance for the Republic of Ireland.

* Originally from the Derby County youth squad, Lee Carsley joins the first squad on the 6th of July 1992.  He makes his league debut on the 11th of September 1994 with a draw at Swindon Town's ground (1-1). Two days later he scores his first professional goal against Bristol City. 
* In February 1995 he suffers an injury to his knee ligaments in a game against Bolton, an injury that kept him away from the playing fields until the end of the season. Once recovered, he entered into the starting line-up for the 95-96 season.

* Thanks to his tenacity, Lee Carsley was able to find a gap for himself in the Derby County line-ups in the second half of last season. He played 24 league games, 15 of these from the start. For yet another year he showed signs of his versatility, playing competently in different positions.

356.name: Stimac
pages: * Igor Stimac is very much an idol for the supporters of Derby County. No-one forgets that when the Croatian arrived in October 1995, the team was hovering near the bottom of the table and that, months later, it was celebrating promotion to the Premier League. The Croatian is a natural leader both on and off the pitch. For this reason nobody was surprised when he was made captain.

* A solid central defender with great leadership qualities, Igor Stimac has got a good technical foundation and fully dominates the back line. His conditions allow him to perform to a high level as sweeper. Effective at making interceptions, he is calm in dangerous situations and takes advantage of his vision to start attacking moves. He hardly ever joins in the attack and is often the player furthest back in his team, although at times he surprises with the power of his shot on goal.  Very hard to beat in a one-on-one, and thanks to his height he is authoritative in the air. All in all Stimac is a very complete defender.

* World Youth Champion 1987. 
* Yugoslavian League Champion 91. 
* Croatian League Champion 95. 
* Croatian Cup Champion 95.

* 23 full international caps for Croatia - 2 goals. He made his debut on the 22nd of December 1990, in a friendly between Croatia and Rumania (2-0). Stimac came on for Celic in the 66th minute. 
* He scored his first goal on the 3rd of September 1995. Croatia beat Esthonia 7-1 in a game played in Rijeka. 
* Present in the 96 European Championship in England, he played three games from the start against Turkey (1-0), Denmark (3-0) and Germany (1-2). This last result meant Croatia's elimination in the quarter-finals. 
* Youth international for Yugoslavia, he won the World Championship at this level in Chile in 87, beating Germany in the final.

* In 1987 Igor Stimac was part of the Yugoslavian youth team alongside players such as Brnovic, Pavlicic, Jarni, Boban, Suker, Prosinecki and Jerkan, who are stars today. That team won the World Championship in Chile.
* Trained in the youth squad of Hajduk Split, he has spent almost all of his sporting life with this club. In 1992 he signed for Cadiz together with his fellow countryman Varvodic. His performance was exceptional but he could not prevent the Andalusian team from being relegated to the Second Division and, in the following season, to the Second Division B. 
* At the beginning of the 94-95 season he returns to Hajduk, where he lives some of the best moments of his career when his team reaches the quarter- finals of the Champions League. 
* The delicate economic situation of the Croatian team and its premature elimination from the European Cup forced him to try his luck elsewhere half-way through the 95-96 season. On the 31st of October 1995 he signed for Derby County.  His arrival was decisive, as on joining the club, Derby was eighteenth in the table.  At the end of the season the Rams finished the season with promotion to the Premier League. 
* On the day of his debut, the 4th of November 1995, Stimac scores the only goal of his team on their visit to Tranmere Rovers, but Derby County is given a sound 5-1 thrashing.  However, from that moment on, the Rams string together 20 games without loosing. 
* A hardened badge collector, Stimac enjoys a lot of success among the women of his country, where he is compared to Richard Gere, Igor's favourite actor. He is currently married to an ex Miss Yugoslavia and tries not to miss a single film of Kim Bassinger's. 
* He is currently the captain of the Croatian and Derby County team.

* In some ways, injuries and suspensions were centre stage in Igor Stimac's season. He played 21 league games, all of them from the start. For the second year running the manager, Jim Smith, showed that he has a lot of confidence in the Croatian defender's game, who carried out authoritatively his role as team leader.

357.name: Yates
pages: * Dean Yates career is sadly laden with bad luck. Injuries have broken the career of a defender who promised a lot, but who has been all too often in the physio rooms. An idol of the Derby County followers, he gave his all to help push the team to promotion in 1996.  And he succeeded, also being the best player of the season. However, last season, his first in the top flight, bad luck returned once again. Let's hope it was the last time.

* A central defender with a sense for organising the game, he can also play as a sweeper, a position where he can get the most out of his excellent positioning. Tall and powerful, he dominates the aerial game in both areas, and is dangerous at free-kicks and corners.  Despite not being a marker, he is firm and workmanlike when intercepting. He is a leader among his team mates due to his calmness under pressure.
x
* 5 under-21 international appearances for England.

* A product of the youth squad at Notts County, Dean Yates turned professional on the 14th of June 1985, when he was only 17 years old. Before then he had already played 8 games with the first team at Meadow Lane. 
* A undisputed starter from the 85-86 season onwards, he became an under-21 international.  In 1990 he saw Notts County relegated to the Second Division, and one year later, the promotion to the First. However, his progress was cut short by a serious injury which kept him out for two years.
* Physically recovered, he started the 94-95 season at Notts County, but on the 26th of January 1995 he was transferred to Derby County for £300,000. He made his debut on the 11th of February with an away defeat at the hands of Reading (1-0). On the 26th of February, the day of his debut at the Baseball Ground, he scored his first goal for the team, the winner against Bolton Wanderers. 
* Very quickly Yates formed a partnership in the centre of the defence with Craig Short, also an ex Notts player, although a relapse of his knee injury prevented him from playing the last games of the season. 
* In the 95-96 season, free of injuries, Yates becomes one of the pillars of the Rams team, who earn promotion to the Premier League.

* Dean Yates didn't have much luck last season. He played in the first game of the season, but an injury to his Achilles tendon kept him out of the team for two months. In a game against Wimbledon played in January he once again became injured, and this time his recovery period is prolonged to almost the end of the season. In total, he could only play 10 league games, 8 of these as a starter.

358.name: Chris Powell
pages: * Chris Powell's signing by Derby County half-way through the 95-96 season was a personal bet on the part of Jim Smith. Despite the initial criticisms about the operation, time has proved Jim Smith right. The older of the Powell brothers is an example of good behaviour on the pitch, both in the sporting and disciplinary sense. Chris is a footballer who always plays fairly and who has shown that he has a place in a competition as demanding as the Premier League.

* A left back who covers a lot of ground, Chris Powell takes advantage of his speed to dominate the flank authoritatively. Efficient in defensive tasks, he his hard to beat for speed.  He has a great sense of positioning and it is not very common to see him badly placed.  Technically correct, he is able to put across dangerous passes to the heart of the rival area for the arrival of his team mates. However, he doesn't have much of a shot on goal and he dedicates himself to undoing the play of the other team rather than constructing that of his own.
x
x

* Older brother of Darryl, his team mate at Derby County, Chris Powell started his career at Crystal Palace, arriving in their first team on the 24th of December 1987 from the lower ranks. 
* On the 11th of January 1990 he was loaned to Aldershot, where he made 11 appearances. 
* At the end of the 89-90 season Chris Powell became a free agent, and Southend United took advantage of this to incorporate him into their squad. A Shrimpers' player since the 30th of August 1990, he immediately found a place in the starting line-ups. 
* Southend captain for several seasons, he was transferred to Derby County on the 31st of January 1996 for £750,000. His transfer takes place on the request of the Rams coach Jim Smith. He coincides with his brother Darryl at the Baseball Ground, who arrived at the club in July 1995. 
* Debuts on the 3rd of February in an away game against Grimsby town. The teams draw 1-1 with Derby's goal coming from Darryl Powell.  At the end of this season the Rams earn promotion to the Premier League.

* During last season Chris Powell was one of the set features of the Derby County line-ups.  He played as a starter in the 35 league games that he played, showing that he has more than enough quality to play in the Premier League with full guarantee.

359.name: Rowett
pages: * Two years after signing for Derby County no-one doubts that Gary Rowett has been a profitable player. During this time, the English defender has found an undisputed place for himself in the team's line-ups. The 97-98 season gives him the chance to settle into the Premier League and, if he keeps up the good work, may be able to make the jump to the national team.

* Rowett can play both in the centre of defence and at right back, although his vision and sense for distributing the ball means he can play as sweeper and even as centre half.  Rowett is, then, a versatile footballer; dominant in the air and a hard marker, but with enough technical capability to start attacking moves from the back. Young and with class, he shows a maturity not often seen in someone so young, and is therefore considered as one of the great promises of English football.
No data.
No data.

* Rowett began his professional career at Cambridge United on the 10th September 1991, once he had finished his training in the lower ranks of the club. Gary Johnson was the coach who gave him the chance to play in the First Division in the 92-93 season, although at the end of the season the team were relegated. 
* Loaned to Everton in 1994, he made his debut in the Premier League on the 2nd of April in a game at Hillsborough against Sheffield Wednesday. However it wasn't a happy day: Everton lost 5-1. Shortly afterwards, on the 21st of May, Rowett made the definitive move to the Toffees for £200,000. 
* Unable to find a spot on the teamsheets first of Mike Walker, then, of Joe Royle, he is loaned to Blackpool on the 23rd of January 1995. 
* He is a Derby County player since the 20th of July 1995. The price of his transfer was set at £300,000.  He made his debut on the 13th of August at the Baseball Ground, with a goal-less draw against Port Vale. At the end of his first season with the Rams the team is promoted to the Premier League.

* Fully identified with the playing scheme of Jim Smith, Gary Rowett was one of the most brilliant players for Derby County during last season. He appeared in  25 league games, all of them from the start, performing to an excellent level in the centre of defence. Proof of this were his several nominations for "Man of the Match".  What's more, Gary played for the second consecutive year without injuries, allowing him to maintain a good level of form for the whole of the championship.

360.name: Delap
pages: * Signed for Derby County in February 1998.
* Young attacking midfielder. Delap has an admirable playing vision and stands out particularly for his precise long passes and the power of his shot on goal from a distance.
* AMC Champion in 1997.
* 3 under-21 international appearances.
x
* Last season Delap took part in 32 games and scored four goals. His versatility allowed him to figure regularly in the plans of the manager, whether it was as forward or on the right.

361.name: Solis
pages: * Solis arrived at Derby County in March 1997 and in his first season his understandable lack of adaptation to English football was evident. His presence was eclipsed by the brilliant arrival of his fellow countryman Wanchope in the Premier League. In principle, he will be condemned to the role of substitute in the 97-98 season, but he should be prepared to take advantage of the first chance that comes his way.

* He can play both as left half or left back. Skilful and well endowed technically, he is noted for the accuracy of his passes. However, he is a little indolent and fragile in defensive tasks and needs to adapt to the demanding rhythm of English football.
x
* 29 international appearances for Costa Rica.

* Originally from the Costa Rican club Heridiano, he arrived at Derby County on the 27th of March 1997 alongside his fellow countryman Paulo Wanchope. Solís' transfer was set at £600,000. 
* He made his debut in the Premier League on the 12th of April 1997, with a home win over Aston Villa (2-1). Solís came on as a substitute for Asanovic in the 79th minute.
* Solís arrived at Derby County in March alongside his fellow countryman Wanchope, but he only made two appearances in the league, both times as a substitute.

362.name: Hunt
pages: * After the disappointment he suffered last season, when he hardly counted for Trevor Francis, the coach at Birmingham City, Jonathan Hunt hopes to start a new stage in his career in the ranks of Derby County. Although, in principle, he will condemned to the substitutes' bench, Jonathon could find a place in the team if he regains the extraordinary level of play he reached two seasons ago.

* The power and accuracy of his shot with either foot are the most eye-catching feature of Jonathan Hunt's game, a midfielder with a lot of presence in the attack. Intelligent on the pitch, he is effective when passing, although he doesn't take many risks. He has an acceptable technique with both feet, is quick on the run and dangerous near the area.

* Second Division Champion 94-95 with Birmingham City. 
* Associated Members Cup Champion 95.
x

* Originally from the lower ranks of Barnet, he made his league debut on the 12/12/91 against Mansfield Town. 
* As a free agent he signed for Southend United in July 1993.  He made his debut in the league on the 15/8/93 against Nottingham Forest, scoring his first goal on the 3/11/93 against Watford. 
* Transferred to Birmingham City for £50,000 in September 1994. He made his debut on the 18/9/94 against Peterborough United. 
* He was the top scorer at Birmingham in the 95-96 season, finding the net 11 times in the league, twice in the FA Cup and once in the League Cup. This same season he was voted "Player of the Year" by the fans at the club.
* He is a Derby County player since the 11th of May 1997. His arrival at the Rams saw the departure of Darren Wassall to Birmingham in an operation set at £500,000.

* Hunt suffered a serious injury to his knee in a game against Ipswich Town played in October, which prevented him from reaching his best form. When he recovered, the manager, Trevor Francis, had already decided to opt for Anders Limpar, Andy Legg and Martin Grainger and forced Jonathan to the reserves team. Hunt could only play a total of 12 league games in the whole of the season, although in half of these he didn't play in the starting eleven.

363.name: Eranio
pages: * Now in his thirties, Stefano Eranio has decided to start a new stage in his sporting career.  Derby County gives him the chance to play in the Premier League, a competition where some of the best Italian footballers are grouped. With the signing the Italian international, Jim Smith is bringing an illustrious veteran to the team, whose experience will be a very important contribution to the Pride Park team in the 97-98 season.

* Eranio plays at inside right, although he can also act as wide defender on this side.  Although he is not a very technical footballer, he is very dangerous when he joins in the attack, taking advantage of his speed and strength.  Eranio is a veteran player, who is able to make good use of his resources and contributes a lot of experience. An untiring worker, he will sacrifice himself for the good of the team.

* Italian League Champion in 93, 94 and 96. 
* European Champion in 94.
* European Supercup Champion 95. 
* Italian Supercup Champion 93 and 94.

* 18 full international caps for Italy. 
* He made his debut on the 22nd of December 1990, gainst Cyprus (0-4) played in Limasol.  It had been thirty years since a Genoa player had donned the "squadra azzurra" (Blue Squadron) shirt, a truly praiseworthy statistic for Stefano Eranio. The last person to do so was Buffon on the 13th of March 1960.

* Eranio started playing football in his school team, Molassana, where he played as a playmaking centre half.  A year later, Scoglio became right half. In his position he made the jump to the lower ranks of Genoa, his home town. He trained with this player and performed for the first team for the first time when he was just 16. 
* He made his debut in the Serie A on the 27th of August 1989 against Lecce which finished as a one-all draw. 
* Eranio has had a lot of trainers during the course of his career (Cuttica, Morelli, Maselli, Perotti, Capello...), but he will never forget the man who allowed him to make his debut in the Serie B in the 84-85 campaign, Burgnich, ex interational and Inter Milan wide defender who scored a goal in the Mexico 70 semi-final against Germany. 
* He is a great admirer of the ex Italian international Tardelli, and has said that he would like to be like him. 
* Eranio had a serious accident in 1988 which almost brought him to the point of retirement from football, although it was not much more than a big fright and Stefano recovered completely from this mishap. 
* At the end of the 96-97 season Milan decide not to renew his contract. On the 21st of May 1997 he signed for Derby County for three seasons.

* In a disastrous season for Milan, in which they didn't even qualify for the UEFA Cup, Stefano played 21 league games and scored 2 goals. His presence in the line-ups increased when the Uruguayan coach Óscar Washington Tab rez was thrown out in favour of the Italian Arrigo Sacchi.

364.name: Dailly
pages: * Christian Dailly's arrival in England was preceded by reports of his great footballing talent, one of the best in Scotland. In his first season at Derby County Dailly only confirmed these references and didn't delay in showing his ability. A full Scottish international, he is still very young, and so he has a lot of time ahead of him to improve. If he keeps up his progress it wouldn't be a surprise if he were to draw the attention of the big clubs of the country.

* A technical midfielder, he usually plays on the right. A good passer, he supplies balls to the forward line. He has a strong shot on goal, although he doesn't try it out so often. Despite a weak physical condition, he helps out effectively in defence. Still very young, he needs to improve some aspects of his game, with a view to acquiring a greater regularity and consistency.
* Scottish FA Cup Champion in 94.

* 3 full international caps for Scotland Dailly  made his debut on the 27th of May 1997, in a friendly game against Wales. On the 1st of June of this same year he scored his first goal in a friendly against Malta. 
* 1 international B appearance. 
* 34 under-21 international appearances for Scotland. In 1996 he played in the final phase of the European Championship in Barcelona. The Scottish team was beaten in the semi-final by Spain. 
* Schoolboy international.

* A native of Dundee, he turned professional in the ranks of United, one of the two important clubs of the city, and made his debut for the first team in the 90-91 season. 
* After six seasons in the Scottish league and being an under-21 international, he receives an offer for Celta of Vigo in the summer of 1996. However, in July he is transferred to Derby County for £1 million. 
* He made his debut in the Premier League in the inaugural game of the 96-97 season on the 17th of August. Derby County and Leeds United draw nil-nil at the Baseball Ground. 
* He scored his first goal on the 21st of this same month, away to Tottenham Hotspur.

* In his first season in England Dailly played 36 league games, 31 of these from the start. He started off playing in the midfield, but an injury to Igor Stimac obliged him to drop back to the defence. His excellent form did not go by unnoticed by the Scottish selector, Craig Brown, who didn't hesitate to let him make his debut for the full team in a friendly against Wales.  Satisfied with his performance, Brown let him add two more games to his international tally.

365.name: Darryl Powell
pages: * Darryl Powell is one of the players who enjoys the trust of Jim Smith. The Derby coach was also in charge of him in his spell at Portsmouth and didn't hesitate to incorporate him into the Rams' squad looking for promotion to the Premier League. And Darryl has not disappointed.  He can play in a variety of positions and do well in all of these. Still very young, his future looks very rosy.

* Capable of distributing the ball well, Darryl Powell took on the role of playmaking centre half in Jim Smith's scheme. Left-footed, dynamic, and blessed with great physical resistance, he covers a large area of ground, wins back a lot of balls and is charged with initiating the attacking moves. Technically good for the short pass, he offers himself constantly as a reference for his team mates. Although he needs to improve his long range passes, his youth and enthusiasm announce a promising footballer. 
* Versatility is one of his biggest virtues. Despite acting as a the team's axis at Derby County, at other times he has done well in other positions in the midfield.
x
x

* Darryl Powell is two years younger than his brother Chris, his team mate at Derby County. 
* Born in London but raised in Portsmouth, he is a product of the youth squad at Fratton park. He reached the Portsmouth first team on the 22nd of December 1988, just turned 17.  Alan Ball was the manager who gave him the chance to make his debut this same season. 
* The arrival of Jim Smith as manager allowed Darryl to find a place in the starting line-up. 
* When Jim Smith is made the manager at Derby County he takes Darryl Powell with him. He signs for the Rams on the 27th of July 1995, in exchange for £750,000, although Portsmouth try to barter him for Van der Laan. 
* In the starting line-up in his first season, he makes his debut at the Baseball Ground on the 13th of August 1996, with a draw against Port Vale (0-0). On the 21st of November of this same year he scores his first goal for the Rams against Birmingham City. 
* In January 1996 he sees how his brother Chris joins the squad at Derby County. Months later both are celebrating the club's promotion to the Premier League.

* In his first season in the Premier League, Darryl Powell appeared in 33 games, 27 of those from the start. He showed signs of his versatility performing to a good level in the different positions where he was played by Jim Smith, although his repeated changes in position had a negative effect on his goalscoring efficiency. He only scored once, against Arsenal at Highbury (2-2).

366.name: Wanchope
pages: * On the day that he made his debut in the Premier League, Pablo Wanchope was a complete unknown for almost all the fans. At the end of the game the score showed Derby County's first win against Manchester Untied at Old Trafford in the last thirty years. The orchestrator of this triumph was none other than Wanchope. The Costa Rican forward set up the first goal for Ashley Ward and scored the second against a surprised Peter Schmeichel. He immediately won the reverence of the fans of the Rams.

* Pablo Wanchope is a young forward, very tall and a little graceless. However, despite appearances, he is skilful with the ball at his feet and turns effectively. He can also play as a link-man. Quick and strong, rival defenders find him hard to mark, as he uses his body well to protect the ball. Brave, decisive and charming, he always looks to take someone on one-on-one.
x
* 17 full international caps for Costa Rica.

* Originally from Heridiano, a club of his native Costa Rica, Pablo Wanchope signs for Derby County on the 27th of March 1997. In the same operation his fellow countryman Mauricio Solís is also transferred. The price of each transfer is set at £600,000. 
* Before signing for Derby County he had been on trial at QPR, but the club at Loftus Road rejected him. 
* Wanchope made his debut in the Premier League on the 5th of April 1997 against Manchester United at Old Trafford. Derby County win 2-3 and Wanchope produces a great performance, even scoring Derby's second. It had been thirty years since Derby last won at United's ground.

* His debut in the Premier League could not be better. Derby County beat the all-powerful Manchester United at Old Trafford and Wanchope not only scored his team's second goal, but also served up the first on a tray for his team mate Ashley Ward. In just two months - arriving at Derby at the beginning of March - he won the favour of the fans. He played 5 league games and was a starter in 2 of these.

367.name: Van der Laan
pages: * Robin Van der Laan is a much loved footballer at Pride Park, and it was him who scored the goal that clinched promotion for Derby County to the Premier League. The Dutch midfielder, who has had the honour of wearing the captain's band, allows works generously in every game, one of the reasons why he is so appreciated by his team mates and the coach Jim Smith. Although he has now lost the status of undisputed starter, everyone knows that if his presence is required on the pitch, he wont let his side down.

* An all-terrain midfielder, he is noted for his combativity. He works constantly for the full ninety minutes, fully exhausting his physical reserves. A good ball-winner, he joins in the attack dangerously in set-plays with a view to getting a header in. He makes up for his lack of technique with commitment and fighting spirit. When he is on form he is a true engine for the team. However, his performances drops sharply if he is not on top physical form.
* Associated Members Cup Champion 93.
x

* Dutch forward, he signed for Port Vale on the 21st of February 1991, from Wageningen, a club in his native country.  His transfer was set at £80,000. 
* On the 2nd of August 1995 he was transferred to Derby County for £675,000. He made his debut with the Rams on the 13th of August of the same year, at home against Port Vale (0-0).  At the end of the season, Derby earned promotion to the Premier League thanks to a goal of his against Crystal Palace.
* At the beginning of the 96-97 season he suffered an ankle injury. On the 11th of October 1996 he is loaned to Wolverhampton Wanderers for two months. He was on the brink of being transferred to the Moulinex club, but no agreement was made and he returned to the Derby County squad.

* Last season did not begin too well for Robin Van der Laan as he suffered an ankle injury which kept him out the side. In October he accepted a deal which took him to Wolverhampton Wanderers on loan. He played 7 games in the First Division and even thought about moving to Moulinex, but no agreement was reached. On returning to Derby County he managed to find a place in Jim Smith's line-up, and he contributed to the his team successful fight to avoid relegation with two goals: one against Tottenham and the other against Aston Villa.

368.name: Baiano
pages: * Francesco Baiano is, alongside Stefano Eranio, one of the star reinforcements for Derby County going into the 97-98 season. The Italian forward arrived with an exemplary career behind him at Fiorentina and with his country's team. With his signing, Jim Smith is bringing a prestigious player to the club, whose experience and quality will be vital to achieving the Rams objective of settling into the Premier League.

* Baiano is an exceptional forward, very quick and skilful with the ball at his feet. He understands football as a very vertical game and is very dangerous when he has the ball under control near the rival area. He usually operates on the right, although his mobility allows him to appear in any part of the forward line, always looking for the weak point of the rival defence and opening up gaps for his team mates. To his unpredictable game is added good finishing.

* "Guerin d'Oro" in 1991.
* Italian Cup Champion in 96. 
* Italian Supercup Champion in 96. 
* Serie B Champion in 96.

* Full international for Italy. 
* He made his debut on the 13th of November 1991, in a game between Italy and Norway corresponding to the classification for the 92 European Championship in Sweden. The game was played in Genoa; the result a goal-less draw.

* He made his debut in the Serie A aged 17 on the 14th of December 1985, in a Sampdoria-Naples game (2-0). 
* In 1990 he was transferred to Foggia. 
* In the team with the red and black striped shirt, then in the Serie B, he coincided with Zdenek Zeman as manager and had Giuseppe Signori as a team mate, with whom he formed one of the most feared striking partnerships in Italy. 
* He is a great admirer of Francesco Graziani, the Italian forward in the 82 World Cup in Spain. 
* In the 93-94 season a very serious injury kept him out for several months.
* In the final stages of the 95-96 season he suffered a fractured fibula, which forced him to miss the first games of the following season. 
* He states that Zdenek Zeman is the manager who has most influenced him in his career and he would like to play under him again. 
* He has some excellent memories of Diego Maradona, with whom he coincided at Naples when he was 17. 
* He is a great admirer of Batistuta and says that for his finishing ability, the Argentinean is the heir of Van Basten in the Serie A. 
* On the 31st of July 1997 he was transferred to Derby County for £650,000 for three seasons.

* Baiano started the season out of the team, recovering from a fractured fibula which he suffered at the end of the previous season. But little by little he started to figure in Claudio Ranieri's line-ups.  He played 21 league games and only scored 2 goals, less than his usual tally. A mediocre season in line with that produced by Fiorentina as a whole, incapable of managing a place in the UEFA Cup.

369.name: Burton
pages: * Deon Burton is still a promising player. Although last season he didn't perform to the level expected by the Portsmouth trainers, the expectations this young forward has created are still intact. Now he has been signed by Derby County, Burton has made one more step in a short career and explodes into the Premier League. He will be one of the players to watch in the 97-98 season.

* A young forward, he stands out for his finishing. Very quick, he is able to leave his marker behind and take advantage of the spaces behind the rival defenders. He has a good turn and can shoot on goal with either foot.
x
* Full international for Jamaica.

* Originally from the lower ranks of Portsmouth, he signed as a professional in February 1994. 
* His league debut took place on the 26th of April 1994 against Leicester City. 
* He scored his first goal on the 17th of April 1995 against Watford.
* On the 24th of December 1996 he was loaned to Cardiff City, in the Third Division, whose colours he defended in 5 league games. He scored 2 goals on his debut against Torquay United. 
* On the 8th of August 1997 he was transferred to Derby County for £1 million.

* He started the season in the starting line-up but soon lost his place in favour of Lee Bradbury. In December he was loaned to Cardiff City, in the Third Division, and in his first game scored two goals against Torquay United. On returning to Fratton Park he was favoured by an injury to his team mate Mathias Svensson, allowing him to regain the place he had lost towards the end of the season.

370.name: Willems
pages: * Ron Willems is playing out the last years of his career at Derby County. Although his appearances in the starting eleven are ever more scarce, it has to be said that the Dutch footballer always offers good performances when his presence is required on the pitch. A hard-working man, he never gives up a ball as lost and tries to infect his team mates with his winning spirit. His experience should help him to do some good things in the Premier League.

* Willems usually plays as a link-man, just behind the forwards. Technically good, he controls, shields and moves the ball efficiently, distributing sensibly. He moves around the entire attacking area and, although he doesn't finish well, he doesn't hesitate to shoot if given the chance. A very professional footballer, he can also play as a forward. He has a good header and is sure when taking penalties.

* Dutch League Champion 90. 
* Swiss League Champion 95. 
* Swiss Cup Champion 94.
x

* Ron Willems' sporting career begins in the 83-84 season with PEC Zwole, a modest club in his native Holland. 
* Signed by Twente at the beginning of the 85-86 season, he is transferred to Ajax in 1988.  Although he never plays as a starter in the most prestigious club in Holland, his presence in the squad allows him to add to his honours list. 
* With no chances at Ajax, he arrives at Grasshopers in Zurich in the 93-94 season. After winning the League title in 1995 he is transferred to Derby County on the 28th of July of this year for £300,000 pounds. 
* He makes his debut as a member of the starting line-up on the 19th of August 1995, with an away defeat at the hands of Reading (3-2).  On the 1st of October he scores his first goal for the Rams against Millwall at the Baseball Ground. (2-2).
* He spent most of the season on the substitutes' bench. In fact, of the 16 games he played in, only seven were from the start.

371.name: Sturridge
pages: * Dean Sturridge showed last season that he doesn't have to envy most of the forwards in the Premier League. The Derby player allowed himself the luxury of scoring an extraordinary goal against a goalie of the standing of Peter Schmeichel at the mythical Old Trafford. His goals were vital for the Rams effort to avoid the drop, and everything seems to indicate that in the 97-98 season he will be one of the regular features in Jim Smith's line-ups.

* A very quick forward, he usually operates on the right of the attack. Powerful, he is hard to stop without fouling him if on the run. He takes on the rival defenders and finishes well.  Sufficiently skilful with the ball at his feet, he has a good jump allowing him to head comfortably. He has various resources in attack, and is able to turn in the area to get a shot in. When he is confident in his own abilities he is a very effective goal scorer. A young promise, his progression in the last year has been astounding.
x
x

* The younger brother of Simon, player at Stoke City, Dean Sturridge signed as a professional at Derby County on the 1st of July 1991, after having played in the lower ranks of the club. He made his debut at the end of the 91-92 season in a game against Southend. 
* On the 16th of December 1994 he was loaned to Torquay United as part of a transfer deal which bought Paul Trollope to Derby County. In two months at the Plainmoor Ground he showed his class scoring 5 goals in 10 games.
* He finishes the 95-96 season as Derby County's top scorer, with a tally of 20, and helps take the Rams to the Premier League. This same year he is voted a member of the First Division Dream Team by the other players.
* In the 96-97 season he is once more the team's top scorer, with 11 goals in 30 league games. 
* An admirer of John Barnes, Peter Beardsley and Romario, Dean Sturridge has a superstition: he likes to be the last out onto the pitch.

* For the second successive year Dean Sturridge was the top scorer at Derby County, finding the net 11 times in 30 league games. The Rams forward was the scorer of some of the most spectacular goals of the season, of which the ones against Manchester United and Arsenal at Old Trafford and Highbury respectively particularly stand out. Sturridge confirmed that he is a complete footballer and in full progression.

372.name: Arphaxed
pages: * After a trial period during the summer Pegguy Arphaxed convinced MartinO'Neill that he was a  goalkeeper with enough quality to cover the loss of Kevin Poole. The frenchman put in some good performances in the pre-seasongames against  Preston and Northampton and, just as importantly showed interestand a desire to play in England. He eventually signed for Leicester just before the U.E.F.A. Cup transfer deadline, maintaining Leicester's tradition of having a promising young keeper in the squad. Nevertheless it seems unlikely, for the moment at least, that he will be dislodging Keller from the first team.

* A young keeper he stands out for his agility, bravery and reflexes, though he still lacks experience. However, Arphaxed has shown that he possesses real ability which can only improve with time and trainign. A little unsure when going up for high balls and not particularly dominant in the air, he nevertheless has a whole career ahead of him to improve in these areas.
x
* 7 times a French uncer-21 international.

* A product of the youth system of French side Brest, in 1991 he was transfered to Lens of the French First Division.
* He made his league debut on 27th April 1996, in a game against Montepellier (2-1).
* During the 1996-97 season he was loaned out to Lille, where he made 19 appearances.
* He has been a  Leicester player since 13th August 1997, after signing a one year contract.
* After signing he confessed he had always dreamt of playing in the English League.

*  After failing to get an opportunity at Lens, he was sent out on loan to French First Division side Lille. However he played in just 19 games. At the end of the season he became a free agent as Lens failed to renew his contract.

373.name: Keller
pages: * In Kasey Keller Martin O'Neill has found the perfect man to defend the  Leicester City goal. The American took just a couple of games to win over the Filbert Street faithful. He spreads confidence and security to his defensive colleagues and demands the respect of opponents. An automatic first choice ingoal for United States and at Leicester, Kasey Keller is one of the best keepers in the Premier League.

* A keeper with great reflexes, Keller stands out for his security between the posts and his ability to cut out shots from distance. A specialist at saving penalties he possesses extraordinary speed of reaction which also allows him to show his effectiveness when he is forced to come off his line. With more experience under his belt, his game has become more consistent. His improvement is especially noticeable at corners and set pieces where he has managed to turnhimself into a dominant goalkeeper around the penalty area.
* League Cup Winners medal 1997.
* 35 full international appearances for the United States.

* A full international for the United States Kasey Keller signed for London club Millwall on 20th February 1992 from Portland University. 
* An automatic first team choice from the 1992-93 season onwards in 1995 he was the star of a cup tie against Chelsea. In the replay at Stamford Bridgehis brilliant performance in the penalty shoot out saw the "Blues"crash out of the competition.
* On 14th August 1996 he was transfered to Leicester City, recently promoted to the Premier League, for£ 900.000. He made his debut on the 17th of that same month in a home game against Sunderland (0-0).

* He arrived at Leicester just before the start of the league season and saw himself enjoying first team football inmediately. He had some tremendous games amongst which stands out the game against Newcastle at Filbert Street in which his saves assured a famous victory for the "Foxes". Above all his presence in goal was one of the keys to Leicester's triumphin the Legaue Cup. Both at Wembley as well as in the replay at Hillsborough Keller showed his tremendous ability. Once the trophy was won he joined upwith his national side in the battle for a place in the 1998 World Cup Finals in France.

374.name: Elliott
pages: * Matthew Elliott proved to be one of last season's sensations. A number of Premier League  clubs had been following his progress for a while though finally it was Martin O'Neill who decided to sign him to reinforce the centre of the defence. Elliot's transfer was a new record fee for the Filbert Street club, but given the player's performancesit could even be considered to be cheap. Safe at the back and effective in attack Matt has done more than enough to show that he has a place in the top flight.

* Elliott is a right footed central defender. A strong player he is a good marker and despite his size shows good speed of movement. Excellent in the air he dominates his area with authority creating danger when he gets forward to support the attack at dead ball situations, scoreing goals with some regularity. However with the ball at his feet he shows some technical weaknesses which means he generally chooses to play the ball long sending passes through to the forwards more in hope than with any real thought.
x
x

* Charlton Athletic signed him from amateur club Epsom & Ewell in September 1988 for £5,000. 
* He was transfered to Torquay United for £10,000 in March 1989, making his debut on 27th March 1989 against Stockport County. He scored his first goal as a professional against Carlisle United on 3rd May 1989, a goalwhich gave his side the points.
* Scunthorpe United signed him in March 1992 for £50,000. His debut came on 31st March 1992 against Chesterfield and scored his first goal on 2nd May 1992 against Carlisle United.  * He was signed by Oxford United in exchange for £150,000 in November 1993. He played his first game for the club on 6th November 1993 against Millwall while his first goal came 7 days later against Derby County. 
* He was chosen as Oxford United's player of year by supporters for the 1995-96        season.
* He began the 96-97 with Oxford but on 18th January 1997 was transfered to Leicester for £1,600,000, making him the most expensive player in the history of the club. He made his Premier League debut with a 1-0 win over Wimbledon.
* On 2nd February 1997 he scored his first goal for Leicester. It came at Saint James' Park although it wasn't enough to stop his side going down 4-3 to  Newcastle.

* When Matt Elliot left Oxford United in January he left an enormous gap in the centre of the defence. On the other hand Leicester City didn't take long to realise that the £1,600,000 they had spent to sign him was money well spent. Martin O'Neill included him immediately in the starting line up and he went on to keep his place until the end of the season. He played in a total of 16 league games for the Filbert Street club. He also scored four goals, a very respectable total for a central defender..

375.name: Kaamark
pages: * Everything points to Pontus Kaamark becoming one of Leicester's key men during the 1997-98 campaign. The swedish defender possesses vast international experience that could prove to be of real value to a club who hope to put together a good performance in the UEFA cup. For that to happen he will need to see a change in his fortune given that since his arrival in England he has spent more time on the treatment table than he has out on the training field. Pontus has already proven himself to be an excellent footballer, and if further proof is needed just ask Juninho.

* He generally plays as a right back although he can also operate in midfield. Kaamark is a complete defender: fast, disciplined and strong in the tackle. A specialist man to man marker he goes about his job fairly without commiting too many fouls. With the ball at his feet he is more than capable, showing intelligent and accurate distribution with either foot. Although he doesn't stand out for his goal-scoring ability he does possess a powerful shot which he never hesitates to use given the slightest opportunity. This Swedish international is also a very experienced footballer which provides him with plenty of know how and expertise both at the back and in attack.

* Swedish League Championship winners medals, 91, 93, 94 and 95.
* Swedish Cup Winners medal 1992.
* League Cup Winners medal 1997.
* 29 full international appearances for Sweden.

* A Swedish international, the majority of Pontus Kaamark's career has been spent with Gothenburg one of the most impotant clubs in Sweden. A four time league championship winner, he went on to become captain.
* On 2nd November 1995 he was transfered to Leicester City for £840,000 making his league debut three days later in a 3-2 victory against West Bromwich Albion. However, he was struck down by injury in his second appearance for the "Foxes", in a League Cup game against Bolton. Two months later he underwent surgery on ruptured cruciate knee ligaments which meant he had to say goodbye to the rest of the season.

* Once he had recovered from the serious knee ligament injury that he had suffered during the 95-96 season, Pontus Kaamark returned to the side in December. However, bad luck dogged his progress again just as he was beginning to get back to his best form. In March he broke his arm in a cup game against Norwich. Fortunately soon after everything changed and the Swedish defender went on to become one of Leicester's heroes. Kaamark controlled the threat of Middlesbrough's Brazilian star Juninho, both at Wembley and in the LeagueCup final replay. His performance was a key factor in helping the Filbert Streetclub win the trophy for the first time in their history.

376.name: Prior
pages: * At Filbert Street Spencer Prior has found the perfect team in which his style of play can shine. Martin O'Neill gave him the chance to return to the Premier League last season and the defender went on to fully repay the faith shown in him by the manager. With Prior, Leicester have become more secure at the back and above all in the air. Few forwards in England are capable of beating Prior inin the air. If he carries on the way he is going it will very difficult for Martin O'Neil to leave him out, something for which the manager will no doubt be enormously grateful.

* Despite his size Spencer Prior is a footballer who stands out for his mobility and dynamic style of play. He generally plays as a left sided central defender, and even on occasions as a full back down the same flank. He possesses powerful heading ability something which makes him a dangerous player at set pieces. He carries out his defensive duties with great security. His power makes it tremendously difficult for opposing forwards to go about their work. Occasionally his eagerness to attack sees him neglecting his ball winning responsibilities, a flaw in his game which needs some polishing. However he still has time on his side for that.
* League Cup Winners medal 1997.
x

* Born in Southend, Spencer Prior formed part of Southend United's youth set up before turning professional on 22nd May 1989. He made his league debut at the age of 17 although he didn't become an automaticfirst team choice until the 1991-92 season.
* On 24th June  1993 he was transfered to  Norwich City for £200,000. His first appearance in the Premier League came on 1st September 1993 at Hillsborough against Sheffield Wednesday (3-3).
* The arrival of  Jon Newsome at Norwich in 1994 saw him relegated to the bench for many games although his outstanding performances during the 1995-96 season saw him being chosen "Player of the Year" by the club's supporters. 
*In the summer of 1996 he was transfered for £600,000 to Leicester City, recently promoted to the Premier League.
*He made his debut for the "Foxes" on 17th August 1996 against Sunderland.

* In first season at Filbert Street, Spencer Prior won himself a place in the first team. His security at the back was won over Martin O'Neill who trusted in him throughout the whole of the campaign. In March an injury kept him out of the side and he later suffered knee trouble which prevented him from playing in every game. Fortunately for Leicester he recovered in time to play in the League Cup Final where he gave a tremendous performance, in total he played in 34 league games, only one of those appearances not coming as a member of the starting line up

377.name: Walsh
pages: * The 16th of April 1997 proved to be one of the most emotional days ofSteve Walsh's life. Leicester overcame Middlesbrough 1-0 in the League Cup final replay, played at Hillsborough. As captain of the side Steve had the honour of lifting the trophy. It was a deserved reward for a player who had given everthing for Leicester over the last eleven seasons. A fitting prize for a man who embodies the real spirit of the "Foxes".

* A central defender, as a left footed player he is at his best on the left handside of the defence. Steve Walsh is a leader out on the park and does exactly that job. He is dominant in everything he does, orders his teammates about while his mere presence spreads a sense of security to the rest of the team. An aggressive marker he never gives an inch to opposing forwards whilehe fights tenaciously for every ball. His dominance in the air turns him into a real defensive wall at the back and a real threat in the opposition's area.In fact, taking into account the fact that he is a central defender he has an excellent goalscoring record. Although not a technical footballer his influence upon the team's play allows him to overcome his own limitaions.

* Associated Members Cup winners medal 1985.
* League Cup winners medal 1997.
x

* Steve Walsh's playing career began in the youth teams at Wigan Athletic. After coming through the ranks he turned professional on 11th September 1982 and managed to make a regular place his own during the course of his first seasonwith the first team.
* He has been a Leicester player since 24th June 1986. The Filbert Street clubpaid £100,000 for his signature.
* In 1994 he became a genuine heroe for the Leicester fans. On 30th May atWembley he scored the two goals in the play off final against  Derby County that took Leicester up to the Premier League (2-1).
* Unfortunately, a few months after his big moment he suffered a serious knee ligament injury which kept him out of action for a long period. That same season (94-95) Leicester went back down to the First Division. 
*As the club's longest serving player he played a key role in the transitional period between the departure of Mark McGhee and the arrival of the new manager Martin O'Neill. In March 1996 he became captain and made a decisive contribution to Leicester's return to the Premier League two months later. 
* He was voted man of the match in the 1997 League Cup final. Leicester carried off the trophy after defeating Middlesbrough.

* Steve Walsh's season was interrupted by injuries.The first of those came in a League Cup tie against Manchester United. He first underwent a hernia operationand later another, this time on his knee. After getting back into the side he suffered a series of other problems which prevented him from finding his best form. Nevertheless he was back in time to play in the League Cup final againstMiddlesbrough. He was deservedly chosen man of the match in the replay at Hillsborough. A great way to put an end to a highly successful campaign for Leicester.
