378.name: Watts
pages: * The arrival of Matt Elliott at Leicester halfway through last season meant that Julian Watts was to lose the regular first team spot he had been enjoying. Nevertheless that didn't mean that manager Martin O'Neill had lost faith in the Sheffield born player, quite the opposite in fact. Nobody is in any doubt that Watts will be given chances to get into the action as the 97-98 campaign goes on. Even more so remembering that the team will be facing a competion extra:the UEFA Cup. When he gets the opportunity he will no doubt show what he can do.

* Despite his youth and his inexperience, Julian Watts shows a surprising coolness in tight situations. Always at the heart of the defence he dominates his penalty area with authority using his physical presence and his close marking ability. Safe when the ball is in the air he is slightly more limited with the ball at his feet. He keeps his passing simple although he should try to improve his accuracy. He goes forward for set pieces where his heading ability always makes him a threat for the opposition.
* League Cup Winners medal, 1997.
x

* Julian Watts took his first steps in football with humble Frecheville C.A., later turning professional whilst in the ranks of Rotherham United, on 10th July  1990.
* His league debut took place on 13th October 1990 in a game against Huddersfield Town at Rotherham's Millmoor ground.
* On 13th March 1992 he returned to his native City of Sheffield to sign for Wednesday for £80,000. However, he never became a first team regular at Hillsborough and went out on loan to Shrewsbury Town  in Decemberof that same year.
* Sheffield Wednesday's signing of John Newsome hastened his departure to Leicester City, who paid £210,000 for him on 29th March 1996. 
* He made his debut on 30th March in a 0-2 defeat against Sheffield United at Filbert Street. On 27th May he was a member of the starting line up in the play off final for promotion to the Premier League, at Wembley, a game in which Leicester beat Crystal Palace by two goals to one.
* He scored his goal for the "Foxes" on 12th October 1996 against Chelsea at Filbert Street.

* Last time out Julian Watts played in a total of 26 league games, 22 of those from the start. He began the campaign as a key man in Martin O'Neill's line up but the signing of Matt Elliot saw him relegated to the bench for a number of games. He was unable to force his way into the side for either of the two games that it took to decide the League Cup final, although it would have been fully derserved if he had made the side. Nevertheless, it was a good positive season form him which saw him hit his first goal in a Leicester shirt, in the league against Chelsea.

380.name: Campbell
pages: * Stuart Campbell is one of the brightest prospects at Leicester. The young midfielder won the faith of Martin O'Neill by never letting the manager down when he chose to play him, even at difficult places like Old Trafford and Anfield. If he maintains this progress he won't take long to settle down in the Premier League. At the moment his future couldn't be brighter.

* A young midfielder he generally plays down the right hand side. His tremendous defensive work also allows him to play as a full back. A player with great stamina he keeps up a fantastic work rate throughout the ninety minutes.
* League Cup Winners Medal 1997.
x

* A product of Leicester's youth system he made his league debut for the first team on 30th November 1996 in a game against Manchester United at Old Trafford. Leicester lost 3-1.
* Although born in England his family ties could allow him to play for Scotland.

*  Last season saw Stuart Campbell make his debut for Leicester's first team. It was in a League Cup tie against Scarborough. His convincing performance won-over Martin O'Neill who chose him to line up from the start against all powerful Manchester United at Old Trafford. In total he played in a total of 10 league games. An extraordinary season for such a young player.

381.name: Wilson
pages: * The Filbert Street faithful have high hopes for Stuart Wilson. In his few appearances for the first team, Stuart has already shown some lovely touches in his game. It is to be expected then that as the 1997-98 season unfolds he will begin to figure in the side on a more regular basis, a real source of pride for the Leicester born lad.

* An attack minded midfielder he has shown himself to be a very mature player despite his youth. He likes to get down the flank to the by-line from where he gets over extraordinarily accurate crosses.
x
x

* A product of Leicester City's youth system he made his debut on 22nd February 1997 in a home victory over Derby County (4-2).
* On 11th May 1997 in the final league game of the sason, he scored his first goal as a professional, against Blackburn Rovers.

* The month of January saw Stuart Wilson make his debut for Leicester'sfirst team. It came in a cup tie against Southend United. Martin O'Neill later lined him up against Chelsea, also in a cup tie, before giving him his bowin the league. He couldn't have ended the season any better scoring his first goal against Blackburn Rovers in the final game of the season.

382.name: Ullathorne
pages: *  Robert Ullathorne didn't get off to a very good start with the "Foxes. In his first game for the club he suffered a fractured ankle and was unable to get back into action for the remainder of the season. After such an unfortunate start, following a fleeting spell in Spanish football Robert was just trusting that his luck hadn't deserted him completely and that he could again show that he was a player who had enough about him to play in the Premier League. Nevertheless, the signing of Guppy added competition to the fight for the leftback spot.

* Although his natural position is that of left back he can also play as a left-sided midfielder. Fast, hardworking and disciplined he gets forward dangerously to support the attack. He has a good change of direction on the run and sends dangerous crosses into the opposition penalty box. Despite his slight physical build he never hesitates to battle it out with his opponents.
x
* England youth international.

* A product of Norwich City's  youth system, he took the step up to the first team during the 1989-90 season.
* In the summer of 1996 he decided to make the move to Spanish football and signed a three year contract with Osasuna, in the Spanish Second Division.Previously  Ullathorne had signed an agreement to join Crystal Palace, however, Michael Robinson and Sammy Lee, both ex- Osasuna players, convinced him to join the Spanish club.
* On 18th February 1997 he was transfered to Leicester for £600,000. In his first game for the "Foxes" (the League Cup Semi-Final against Wimbledon) he suffered a broken ankle.

* 1996-97 wasn't the best of seasons for Robert Ullathorne. His experience in Spain ended in disappointment although the internal situation at Osasuna didn't help, with the club submerged in a fight to avoid relegation and with the manager being sacked at the beginning of the season. Neither was his return to England particularly fortunate, ending up seriously injured (broken ankle) in his first game in a Leicester shirt, against Wimbledon in the League Cup.

383.name: Parker
pages: * Throughout his distinguished playing career Garry Parker has shown himself capable of overcoming the most difficult of moments. The last two seasons at Leicester have been particularly hard ones for him. In the first of those he lost the captaincy after having a run in with manager Martin O'Nell, whilst he began last season on the bench. However on both occasions Parker fought back to become a first team regular once again. On top of that he became a genuine leader for the team, reserving his best performances for decisive games. He went on to lead Leicester to the first league cup triumph in the club's history and the third of his own career.

* Throughout the majority of his career Garry Parker has played as a right sided midfield player. However, at Leicester he lines up as the team's midfield organizer playing in front of the defence in a deeper more central position. A hardworking footballer with good vision and accurate passing ability, he distributes the ball intelligently and efficiently. He possesses a powerful shot at goal from outside the area and is a geniuine free kick and penalty specialist, from where he scores most of his goals. Although in recent seasons he has lost some of his physical strength he retains the fighting spirit which has made him one of the team's leaders out on the park.
*  League Cup Winners Medal 1989, 90 and 97.

* One England "B" international appearance. 
* 6 under-21 international appearances. 
* Youth international.

* Garry Parker took his first steps in the world of football in the youth ranks at Queens Park Rangers, a club where he arrived as a schoolboy in September1980. In June 1982 he moved on to become an apprentice at Luton Town before finally turning professional on 5th May 1983. 
*  He made his league debut on 9th May 1983 in a game against Manchester United. Nevertheless, he never managed to make a first team spot his own at Luton.
* On 21st February 1986 he was transfered to Hull City for £72,000. He immediately became a first team regular at Boothferry Park, finally breaking into the England Under-21 side.
* As the target of some of the top clubs in the country he signed for Nottingham Forest on 24th  March 1988. The fee was £260,000. 
* In 1989 he won a League Cup Winners medal after defeating Luton Town in the final  (3-1). A year later he won another winners medal in the same competition defeating Oldham Athletic at Wembley (1-0).
* However, in 1991 Garry Parker's Nottingham Forest side would go on to lose the League Cup Final to Tottenham Hotspur (2-1). 
* In the first weeks of the 1991-92 season Parker lost his first team spot to Scott Gemmil although he managed to win it back just a few weeks later. Despitethat he was transfered to Aston Villa on 29th November 1991 for £650,000. A first team regular in Ron Atkinson's line up, he lost his place after Atkinson was replaced by  Brian Little in 1994.
* Parker arrived at Leicester City on 10th February 1995 in exchange for £300,000. He made his debut, ironically, against  Aston Villa at Villa Park (4-4). On 5th April he scored his first goal in a "Foxes" shirt. However his presence wasn't enough to prevent the club from being relegated to the First Division.
* During the  95-96 season Garry Parker maintained a series of confrontations with manager Martin O'Neill, who had just been appointed manager of Leicester. As a result the midfielder saw himself lose the captaincy. However the Northern Irish manager continued to call on Parker's ability and Parker became one of the stars in the play offs to the Premier League scoring twice including one in the final at Wembley against Crystal Palace (2-1). He wasn't only chosen as man of the match but also as the Filbert Street faithfuls' Player of the Year for 1996.

* Although he began the season as a substitute, little by little he managed to force his way into the side. Garry overcame some family problems and hit some fantastic form which culminated in his superb performance in the League Cup final. He made a total of 31 league appearances, 22 of those from the start, scoring twice both times from the penalty spot.

384.name: Taylor
pages: * Scott Taylor's first campaign in the Premier League wasn't everything he might have hoped it would have been. The knee injury that he carried throughout the season didn't allow him to give the best of himself, losing his first team spot as a consequence. Nevertheless logic would dictate that once he has recovered from the surgery he has been forced to undergo, Scott will once again be forcing his way back into the plans of Martin O'Neill, a manager who has always shown plenty of faith in him.

* A right sided midfielder Scott Taylor is a player who is attack minded in everything he does. He generally plays as a link up man with the main strikers, a position from where he can make the most of his ability to surprise defenders by coming from deep with late runs. Quick and skillful with the ball at his feet he likes to take on defenders going past them on either side. Dangerous when he has the ball under control in the area he is also an excellent passer of the ball and possesses a fierce shot in his right foot. Without being a goalscorer he generally gets at least a few goals each season.

* League Cup winners medal 1997.
* Second Division Championship winners medal 1994.
x

* A product of Reading's youth system he has been a professional sinceJune 1989. During the 1994-95 season he completed his 200th leaguegame, becoming the youngest player in the history of the club to reachthat figure. 
* On 12th July 1995 he was transfered to Leicester City for £500,000. He made his debut in an away victory at Sunderland (1-2) on 12th Augustof that same year.
* He scored his first goal for the "Foxes" on 21st October 1995: Leicester defeated Sheffield United at Bramall Lane (1-3).
* Months later Scott Taylor was celebrating promotion to the Premier League after playing as a member of the starting line up against Crystal Palace (2-1).

* It wasn't a particularly good season for Scott Taylor. Although he began the season as first choice, it wasn't long before he lost his place to Garry Parker. Scott later suffered knee trouble which prevented him from getting back to form. He was a substitute in the League Cup final at Wembley and was unable to take any part in the replay at Hillsborough as his troublesome knee saw him forced to undergo surgery. He played in a total of 25 games, 20 of those from the start and for the first time in a number of years went right through the season without finding the net.

385.name: Lennon
pages: * Neil Lennon is one of the most popular players amongst the Filbert Street faithful. The red haired Northern Irishman has won over the supporters with his mixture of fighting spirit and commitment, while not being short of a touch of skill whenever when it is needed. Neither has his progress gone unnoticed by some of the most important clubs in the Premier League who have been tracking the development of this dynamic professional whose fiery temperament can sometimes let him down. Despite that, Martin O'Neill has full confidence in him to lead Leicesterthrough the 1997-98 season.

* Neil Lennon is a hard running midfielder who stands out for the energy he uses up in every game he plays. He covers every blade of grass making the most of the physical qualities which allow him to win agreat deal of possession for his side. But as well as his defensive qualities Lennon is also comfortable on the ball. He has a good change of direction in possession and is an accurate passer of the ball. He possesses a tremendous shot in his right foot and has the strength to get into the penalty area after starting off from deep positions. His lack of height doesn't allow him to get involved in arialbattles, but with this one exception, he is a very complete footballer with tremendous attributes..
* League Cup winners medal 1997.

* 15 full international appearances for Northern Ireland. 
* 3 "B" international appearances. 
* 1 under-23 international appearance. 
* 2 under-21 international appearances. 
* Youth international.

* Neil Lennon's career began at Manchester City. Although he turned professional on 26th August 1989, in three seasons at Maine Road, he played just one game forthe first team
* On 9th August 1990 he arrived at Crewe Alexandra on a free transfer. In 1994 he made a decisive contribution to the clubs promotion to the Second Division.
* He was included in the ideal team for his division by his fellow professionals in three consecutive seasons. In 1994 in the Third Division, in 1995 in the Second Division, and in 1996, now at Leicester, in the First Division.  
* He was transfered to Leicester on 23rd February 1996. He made his debut the following day as a substitute in the "Foxes" visit to Reading.
* On 27th  April 1996 he scored his first goal as a Leicester player in a home game against Birmingham City. One month later he was at Wembley celebrating the club's promotion to the Premier League.
* During the 96-97 season he became an undisputed first team choice at Leicester and rounded off a fine campaign by helping the club lift the League Cup at Middlesbrough

* In his first full season at Filbert Street, Neil Lennon became one of Leicester's most important players. He played in a total of 35 league games, all of those as a member of the starting line up, and his influence on the team's play grew as the season went on. He played out the final weeks of the season with a broken toe in his foot, something which didn't prevent from being one of the most outstanding performers in the League Cup Final..

386.name: Izzet
pages: * In a short space of time Muzzy Izzet went from being a complete unknown to becoming one of the idols of the Filbert Street faithful. After three years at Chelsea without being given the opportunity to make his first team debut Izzet was called upon by Martin O'Neill to reinforce Leicester City. The Northern Irish coach was so impressed by the player's performance that he wasted no time in making an offer to sign him on a permanent basis. Today Muzzy Izzet is a key member of the line and has demonstrated that he has everything he needs to have a successful career in the Premier League.

* A midfielder with a fragile look about him, Izzet generally plays down the right hand side or sometimes as a link man between the midfield and the forwards. A skillful player with extraordinary vision, he does more damage around the edge of the penalty area than he does inside it, coming, as he does, on the run from deep positions with the ball tightly under control. A player blessed with excellent technique, he stands out for the accuracy of the passes he sends through to the forward line. A very dynamic footballer he puts in a tremendous amount of work throughout the ninety minutes and he often proves to be especially effective in the closing minutes of games when his ability against tired defenders can turn out to be decisive.
* League Cup Winners Medal 1997.
x

* Son of a Turkish father, but born in England, Muzzy Izzet has turned down the opportunity to play for the Turkish national side simply because, if not, he wouldhave had to complete his Turkish National Service. 
* Although he came through the youth ranks at Chelsea, and he became a professional on 19th May 1993, he never came to make his League for the "Blues".  
* On 28th March 1996 he was sent out on loan to Leicester City. However on the day of his debut (30th March) the "Foxes" were defeated at home against Sheffield United (0-2).
* He scored the first goal of his career on 5th May 1996 during Leicester's visit to Watford (0-1).
* At the end of the 95-96 season once promotion to the Premier League had been clinched Leicester decided to sign Izzet on a permanent basis.The cost of his transfer reached the £650,000 mark.
* During the course of the 96-97 season he became an automatic first team choice at Leicester and rounded off a tremendous season by helping to lift the LeagueCup.

* As was to have been expected after his magnificent run in to the 95-96season, the 96-97 campaign saw Muzzy Izzet really establish himself as a footballer. The Leicester midfielder was a starter in all but one of the 35 games in which he played, becoming one of the focal points of Martin O'Neill's team. He scored 3 goals in the League and in the League Cup, putting the final touch to a tremendous season by helping to beat Middlesbrough in the League Cup final replay.

387.name: Cottee
pages: * Afer a spell in the exotic world of Malaysian football Tony Cottee has decided to return to England under the guidance of Martin O'Neill. The Northern Irish coach has placed a lot of faith in this goalscoring forward, an experienced performer with plenty of hard fought battles behind him aswell as a spell in the England side. Although initially it is difficult to see him making a place in the side his own, Tony will be ready and waiting for whenever he may be called into the fray. Without an doubt, his signing is undoubtedly an excellent reinforcement for Leicester.

* A veteran striker he can play either straight through the middle or pull out wider to either of the flanks. Fast and with plenty of tricks up his sleeve, he is especially dangerous when he gets holds of the ball inside the penalty area and knows how to get in front of rival defenders to get in efforts on goal. Although as time has gone by his physical attributes have diminished he still possesses the ability to make the most of his experience.
x

* 7 full international appearances for England.
* He made his debut on 10th September 1986 in a game against Sweden in Stockholm (0-1). He made his last appearance for England on 27th May 1989 against Scotland in Glasgow (2-0).
* 9 under-21 international appearances, scoring twice.
* 4 youth international appearances, with four goals.

* Born in West Ham, London, Tony Cottee began his career with the "Hammers", moving up to the first team squad in September 1982.
* He made his league debut on 1st January 1983 in a game against Tottenham Hotspur, scoring once.
* During his first spell with the Hammers he formed an outstanding partnership with Frank McAvennie. Together they helped to take the club to third place in the league, the best finish in West Ham's history.
* In 1986 came his full England debut whilst he was also chosen "Young Player of the Year".
* Cottee played in every league game West Ham played for three consecutive seasons (85-86, 86-87, 87-88).
* On 2nd August 1988 he was transfered to Everton for £2,300,000. In his first season at the club the side reached the F.A. Cup final only to be beatenby Liverpool (3-2).
* Once he had finished his contract with Everton he returned, to West Ham United, on 7th September 1994. In exchange The "Toffees" received David Burrows from West Ham.
* On 4th February 1995 he scored his 100th goal in the League. It came at Filbert Street in a game against Leicester City.
* He ended the 1994-95 season as West Ham's leading scorer with 15 goals.. 
* He began the 1996-97 season with West Ham, but, in October decided to leave to join Selangor, a Malaysian League club
* He has been a Leicester play since 13th August 1997. His transfer fee was £500,000.
* Up to the end of the 1996-97 season he had scored 11 hat tricks during the course of his career. The first of those came on 25th October 1983, in a League Cup tie against Bury. He hit his last hat trick on 17th December 1994 against Manchester City.

* He began the season at West Ham as a substitute. He went on to play just 3 league games, two of those from the start before he decided to move in October to Selangor, one of the most important clubs in Malaysia. But before leaving he had to score his final league goal for the "Hammers" in a League Cup game against Barnet.

388.name: Guppy
pages: * It was by no means easy for Steve Guppy to make it all the way to the Premier League. Just a few years ago he was on the verge of making his top flight debut but was never given the opportunity by Kevin Keegan, then manager of Newcastle. However, his outstanding performances fo rPort Vale saw him quickly moving on to  Leicester, where  Martin O'Neill gave him his debut at left back, Guppy responded to the faith shown in him by producing some tremendous form. Well used to battling for his place it is not going to be easy for anybody to dislodge him from the spot he seems to have made his own.

* Although his natural position is as a left sided midfielder he can also do a good job down that flank as a full back. A wholehearted player he gets forward to support the attack and works hard to get back and help with defensive duties. Very much a left footed player he is an accurate crosser of the ball and packs a powerful shot. He is a free kick and corner specialist and makes up for his lack of speed with the quality he possesses in his left foot.
* GM Vauxhall Conference winners medal 1992-93.
x

* A product of Southampton's youth system he was never given the opportunity to make his first team debut for the "Saints".
*  In the 89-90 season he signed for Wycombe Wanderers.
* In the 92-93 season he won a  GM Vauxhall Conference winners medal with Wycombe, taking the club up to the Third Division. He managed to score on his Third Division debut on 14th August 1993 against Carlisle United. 
* In August 1994 he was transfered to Newcastle United for £150,000. 
* He never got to make his league debut for the Saint James' Park club and was transfered to Port Vale for £25,000 in November 1995. He made his debut on 13th August 1995 against Derby Countythough he didn't strike his first goal until 7th October 1995 in a game against Huddersfield Town.
* He began the 1996-97 season with Port Vale but on 28th February 1997 he was transfered to Leicester for £850,000. He made his Premier League debut on 1st March in an away victory against Wimbledon (1-3).

* Guppy began the season at Port Vale where he made 34 appearances scoring 6 goals. His tremendous form didn't go unnoticed by the Leicester coaches and in February they made him part of their squad. Injuries to a number of colleagues saw him making his debut at left back where he did a competent job until the end of the season. He played in a total of 13 games and only in one of those was he not a member of the starting line up.

389.name: Fenton
pages: * After Alan Shearer's departure from Newcastle many thought that Graham Fenton would go on to force himself into the Blackburn Rovers forward line. But lady luck wasn't on Graham's side as injury prevented him from hitting peak form. At Filbert Street and under the guidance of Martin O'Neill he will be trying to get back to his best to help a Leicester side which has attracted the attention of everybody in England and is also due to play in the UEFA Cup.

* A strong,aggressive and fast striker Graham Fenton can also play in the midfield although it is around the opponent's penalty area where he is at his best. His power in the final few yards can prove to be decisive and while he doesn't stand out as a technical player he is capable of winning plenty of balls simply through his physical power. A player with an eye for goal he has a powerful shot and also knows how to protect the ball. He is neither a brilliant nor an elegant footballer, but is hardworking and highly effective in front of goal.
* League Cup Winners Medal 1994.
* One under-21 international appearance for England.

* After coming the youth system at Villa Park, Graham Fenton finally turned professional with Aston Villa on 13th February 1992. However, when he finally got to make his league debut on 12th January 1994 against Leicester,Fenton was wearing a West Bromwich Albion shirt, a club where he had arrived on loan just two days earlier. On 1st February of that same year he scored his first goal as a professional against Grimsby Town.
* Once back at Villa Park he made his first appearance in the first team on 22nd February, although Aston Villa could do no more than draw 0-0 against Manchester City.
* An England under-21 international since November 1994 he began the95-96 season with Aston Villa, but on 7th November 1995 he was transfered to Blackburn Rovers for £1,500,000. He made his debut at Ewood Park on 16th December against Middlesbrough coming on for the seriously injured Le Saux, in the 54th minute of the game. Rovers won 1-0 thanks to a goal by  Alan Shearer. 
* On 23rd December 1995 Graham Fenton made his first starting appearance for Blackburn.
* In April 1996 Newcastle came to  Ewood Park with a large part of their title hopes resting on the game. Ex- Rovers star David Batty opened the scoring for the "Magpies" in the 76th minute. However Fenton, who had come on in the 71st minute, scored two goals in the final five minutes of the game to keep Kevin Keegan's side's dreams of glory very much on ice.
* He has been a Leicester player since 9th August 1997. His transfer fee was set at £1,100,000.

* An unfortunate injury kept Graham Fenton out of action for several months. For that reason the ex-Blackburn Rovers man was hardly able to break into the first team. He played in 13 games, 8 of those from the start, including the first game of the season against Tottenham Hotspur.

390.name: Savage
pages: * After making a decisive contribution to Crewe's promotion to the First Division, Rob Savage took the step up to the Premier League. Leicester City gave him the chance to line up against the best teams in England. However he will have to wait patiently before he is given his opportunity and needs to be aware of the fact that there are players ahead of him in the squad who are going to be very difficut to dislodge from the first team.

* Although he began his career as a striker, in recent seasons Rob Savage has been converted into a midfielder, a position which also makes the most of his attack-minded attitude to the game. An untiring worker he puts in a tremendous amount of effort throughout the ninety minutes. Still very much in the learning process with regards to Premiership football, his technique and his eye for a goal make him a player to keep an eye on in the future.
x

* 5 full international appearances for Wales. 
* 5 under-21 international appearances for Wales. 
* Youth and schoolboy international powers.

* A product of Manchester United's youth system, he never got to make his debut for the first team.
* On 22nd July 1994 he signed for Crewe Alexandra. He made his league debut on 10th September that same year in a game against Wrexham. Three days later he scored his first goal as a professional against Oxford United. 
* A first team regular since the 95-96 season, in 1997 he celebrated Crewe's promotionto the First Division for the first time in the club's history. 
* He has been a Leicester City player since 19th July 1997. His transfer fee was set at £400,000.

* Rob Savage's unstoppable progress continued during the course of last season. Now well settled as a midfielder, he missed just 8 games throughout the whole championship,and his contribution to Crewe Alexandra's promotion to the First Division for the first time in their history was decisive. By the same token Rob consolidated his place in the Welsh national side, an automatic choice for national squads.

391.name: Marshall
pages: * Despite having passed the 30 years of age barrier Ian Marshall has managed to find himself a place in the  Premier League in the ranks of Leicester City. His versatility and goalscoring ability are a great help to Martin O'Neill who has no hesitation in lining him up at the heart of defence if needed. Ian puts in tremendous effort, commitment and work rate in every game he plays while his never say die attitude makes him an invaluable player for any side. If that wasn't enough then the Filbert Street faithful give him all the support he needs to keep battling minute bay minute.

* Although at the begining of his career, he generally only lined up as a central defender, in recent years Ian Marshall has become a goa-lscoring centre forward and, on exceptional occasions has even occupied a position in the middle of the park. He possesses a physical power which is quite out of the ordinary, something which makes him very difficult for rival defenders to stop. Fast and intuitive he is good at getting into position inside the penalty area and never hesitates to get in a shot on goal when given the slightest opportunity. He stands out for his power in the air in either penalty area, where he manages to impose himself using his powerful leaping ability. With the ball at his feet he is more capable than at first he might appear to be. He has good vision and above all a real eye for a goal. He battles away with opponents and puts pressure on the opposition as they try to bring the ball out from the back. But, perhaps the real key to his success has been the way in which he has known how to get the very best out of the attributes he possesses.

* Charity Shield  Medal 1986.
* Second Division Championship  winners medal 1991.
x

* Born in Liverpool and a product of Everton's youth system, Ian Marshall turned professional on 23rd March 1984. He made his league debut on 20th August 1985 taking over from the injured Derek Mountfield in a game against West Bromwich Albion at Goodison Park.
* Without really getting a look in at Everton due to the presence in the side of Kevin Ratcliffe and Dave Watson he was transfered to Oldham Athletic on 24th March 1988 for £100,000. He was initially taken on a two week trial period but following that period the club decided he was the ideal replacementfor Andy Linighan.
* He began playing as a central defender but wanted to convince manager Joe Royle that he had what it takes to become an effective striker. During the 1989-90 season he played in several cup games as a member of the forward line and even scored in the semi-final against Manchester United. Unfortunately an injury prevented him from playing in the final against Nottingham Forest. 
* He hit a hat trick in the first game of the season against Wolverhampton Wanderers in the first week of the 90-91 season. He scored two of his goals in the last five minutes. Oldham won the game 3-2 and Marshall had finally convinced Joe Royle of his ability to play as a striker. As it turned out he ended the season as the team's top scorer with 17 goals and Oldham were promoted to the top flight.
* On 9th August 1993 he was transfered to Ipswich Town for £750,000. Curiously, he made his debut on 14th August in the visit to Oldham Athletic. Ipswich won 0-3 with Marshall hitting the all-important opening goal. He ended the season at Portman Road as leading scorer with 10 goals to his credit. 
* During the 94-95 season Marshall was plagued by injury. At the end of the season Ipswich were relegated.
* He ended the 95-96 season as Ipswich's leading scorer with 19 goals. On 29th August 1996 he was transfered to Leicester for £1,800,000 becoming the most expensive signing in the history of the club
* He made his debut for Leicester on 2nd September 1996 in 2-1 defeat against Sheffield Wednesday at Hillsborough. On 22nd of that same month he hit his first goal for the "Foxes" against Tottenham Hotspur.
* On 2nd February 1997 he hit a hat trick against Derby County in just 27 minutes.

* Marshall began the season at Ipswich Town but on 31st August he was transfered to Leicester. Although tactical reasons forced him to play a number of games as a central defender, he played the majority of the season as a centre forward forming part of the forward line together with Heskey and Claridge. With eight goals in 28 games he was the "Foxes" third top scorer and just for good measure hit a hat trick against Derby County in just.27 minutes.

392.name: Robins
pages: * Since Martin O'Neill has been in charge at Leicester Mark Robins has hardly enjoyed a taste of the action. However, despite his limited opportunities, the English born striker has put in satisfactory performances every time he has been called upon to get into the action. During the course of last season he was loaned out toa Danish club but, upon his return had time to help the "Foxes" to lift the League Club. As the 97-98 approaches his chances of being a first team regular are remote, although nobody is in any doubt that, if he is called upon, then Mark Robins will be fully prepared.

* A right footed forward he occasionally plays deeper behind the two main strikers. However it is inside the area where Robins best exploits his qualities as a goalscorer. An intelligent footballer with good speed of movement, he knows how to get in front of opposing defenders and turns quickly giving him the opportunity to make the most of his powerful shooting. Not a particularly strong player, neither does he stand out for his heading ability, although he is capable of making the most of any potentially dangerous situation.

* European Cup Winners Cup Winners medal 1991.
* European Supercup Winners medal 1991.
* F.A. Cup Winners medal 1990.
* League Cup Winners medal 1997.
* 6 under-21 international appearances for England.

* Robins joined Manchester United's youth set up at just 14 years of age in February 1994. After working his way through all the various youth teams he finally turned professional on 23rd December 1986, not long after his 17th birthday.
* He had to wait until 22nd October 1988 to make his league debut, in an away game against Wimbledon.
* In 1990 he became one of the stars of that season's F.A. Cup. He scored the goal that knocked out Nottingham Forest and struck another in the fifth round against Newcastle, (3-2). Although he wasn't a member of the starting line up against Oldham in the semi-final he came on in the second half and it was his goal that took Manchester United through to the final. At Wembley the "Red Devils" defeated Crystal Palace.
* In 1991 Manchester United lifted tje Cup Winners Cup as well as the EuropeanSuper Cup although Mark Robins failed to make the side for either final, against Barcelona and Red Star Belgrade respectively. Brian McClair and Mark Hughes formed the striking partnership.
* On 14th August 1992 he was transfered to Norwich City for £800,000 and, in his first season at Carrow Road, scored 15 goals in 37 games.
* He has been a Leicester player since 16th January 1995. On the day of his debut 25th January he scored the goal that gave the "Foxes" victory over Manchester City at Maine Road (0-1).
* During the 1996-97 season he had a spell out on loan to FC Copenhagen, a Danish First Division club.

* Not getting many first team opportunities at Leicester Mark Robins was sent out on loan to FC Copenhagen, a Danish First Division club where he managed to score a few goals. Back at Filbert Street he put together some tremendous performances although he didn't enjoy too many opportunities. He scored two spectacular goals one in the League Cup against Ipswich Town and another, an extraordinary volley in the league, against Wimbledon. As a reward for his work he was chosen to play in the League Cup final at Wembley as well as in the replay.

393.name: Heskey
pages: * Emile Heskey is one of the most brilliant young stars in English football. He has taken just two years to show that he is not just a bright young prospect but already a real force to be reckoned with. His progress seems to have no end and already a number of clubs have got him at the top of their shopping lists. At Filbert Street he is a real idol, and it is fairly sure that he soon will be all over the country, seeing that he is already knocking hard on the door of the full England side.

* A player who can do equally as good a job either in the forward line or slightly behind the two main strikers. A man of great physical power and speed he is extremely difficult to stop when he goes at defenders on the run with the ball under control. Good on the ball with either foot he also possesses extraordinary strength for such a young player and shows good intelligence out on the park. However, possibly his greatest quality is his ability in the air. His powerful leaping ability allows him to get in headers with amazing ease. Heskey is a striker with tremendous natural attributes. Blessed with a goalscorer's instinct, if he maintains his progress and works on his technique he could go on to become a real star.
* League Cup winners medal 1997.

* Four under-21 international appearances for England.
* Youth international.

* Born in Leicester and a product of the Filbert Street youth system Emile Heskeymade his first team debut on 8th March 1995 not long after his 18th birthday: Leicester were beaten in their visit to Queens Park Rangers (2-0). On 3rd October of that same year he scored his first professional goal. 
* He was a revelation for Leicester during the 95-96 season and was a member of the starting line up in the play off for promotion to the Premier League. His impressive progress led to the supporters choosing him as their "Young Player of the Season".
* He rounded off an excellent 96-97 season by helping to lift the League Cup. That same season he made his debut for the England under-21 side. 
* He is known as "Bruno" amongst the Filbert Street fans due to his physical similarities to Frank Bruno.

* Last season Emile Heskey simply confirmed everything that had been expected of him since the 1995-96 campaign. An undisputed first choice in Martin O'Neill's line up his presence out on the pitch proved to be a real threat toany defence. His goals, (10 in 35 league games and 2 in the League Cup); and his attacking play delighted supporters and coaches alike. Proof of that was his debut with the England U-21 side. Heskey also scored Leicester's goal in the firstgame of the League Cup final at Wembley against  Middlesbrough (1-1). Ten days later he was once again one of the outstanding performers in the replayed final at Hillbrough which ended in a 1-0 victory for the Filbert Street outfit.

394.name: Cox
pages: * Neil Cox's game has seen a noticeable improvement in the last two seasons. For this reason the Bolton training body recommended his signing.  Cox wanted to carry on playing in the Premier League and didn't hesitate to accept the Wanderers offer.

* A right back who covers a lot of ground, Neil Cox's characteristics are very much in line with the modern wing-back.  He covers the whole of the touchline, helping out in defence and joining in the elaboration of the attack.A footballer with a lot of attacking projection, at times he neglects his defensive zone, which rival forwards can take advantage of.  In any case, Cox's speed allows him to regain his position quickly and he is effective at making interceptions.  Physically strong and with good playing vision, he can score the odd goal or two.

* League Cup Champion 94. 
* First Division Champion 95.
* 6 under-21 international appearances for England.

* Neil Cox, known as "Coxy" by the fans, took his first footballing steps at Scunthorpe United, the club of his hometown.  He arrives in the first team on the 20th of March 1990 and on the 6th of October of this same year he makes his debut in a game against Halifax.  Although he is sporting the number seven he plays at right back. 
* After played only 17 games in the Fourth Division he is transferred to Aston Villa, one of the big clubs in England, at the express wish of the manager Richard Money who he had known at Scunthorpe.  The operation was completed on the 12th of February 1991.  The Villa Park club paid £400,000 to sign him.  However, Cox never manages to find a place in the first team.
* On the 19th of July 1994 he is transferred to Middlesbrough for £1 million, making him the club's most expensive signing up till then.  He makes his debut on the 13th of August in the opening game of the season against Burnley at Ayresome Park.  Boro win 2-0 with both goals scored by Hendrie. At the end of this season Middlesbrough are proclaimed First Division Champions and are promoted to the Premier League.  Nigel Cox is voted as the right back for the division's Dream Team by the professionals themselves. 
* On the 25th of November 1995 he scores against Liverpool 120 seconds after kick-off, probably one of the fastest goals scored by a defender in English footballing history. 
* Bolton paid Middlesbrough £1.5 million for him.
* He played in 35 games, in which, just as with the rest of the Middlesbrough team, he didn't reach the level needed to keep the team in the Premier League.

395.name: Fish
pages: * Mark Fish is one of the best players of South Africa, the team that won the African Nations Cup.  This led to an increase in his asking-price and several European clubs were interested in signing him.  It was Lazio who finally managed to do so, though his spell in Italy hasn't been so good.   Even so, he is a quality player who could bring a lot of security to Bolton and allow them to play the ball out from the back.

* He is a central defender with a lot of physical strength, good positioning and elegant when intercepting.  He is a hard man to get by, and he can also play the ball out from the back.  Furthermore, he is powerful in the air, both when clearing the ball or looking to get a header in on the rival goal from a set-play.
* 1 African Nations Cup title 1996.
* 26 international appearances for South Africa, 2 goals.  He made his debut in 1993 against Mexico.

* Mark Fish achieved a name for himself when South Africa won the African Nations Cup in 1996.  At the time important European clubs such as Manchester United tried to sign him.  However, Lazio was the club who got him to put his signature on the dotted line. 
* Bolton have paid Lazio £2 million for the move.

* He played for Lazio, but didn't manage to perform to the level that was expected of him.  In the South African national side he had, however, much better luck, contributing to his country's classification for the France 98 World Cup.

396.name: Whitlow
pages: * Premier League Champion with Leeds, Whitlow arrives at Bolton from Leicester, the club for whom he has played these last six seasons.  Experienced and with a winning mentality, Whitlow will contribute professionality and know-how to the Bolton defence.

* Whitlow is a left back who likes to join in the attack at the slightest opportunity.  Very left-footed, he has a powerful shot on goal and so will get to take a lot of free-kicks.  In fact, during his career he has scored a lot of goals this way.  Also, his accuracy with his left foot makes him a specialist at corner kicks.  In defence he is a disciplined and efficient defender, although not brilliant.  He is decisive at making interceptions and tough at times.  However, his attacking nature has led him to neglect his defensive responsibilities at times.

* League Champion 92. 
* Second Division Champion 90.
x

* Mike Whitlow arrived at Leeds United on the 11th of November 1988 from the modest team Witton Albion.  His transfer fee was set at £10,000.  He played 20 games in his first season at Elland Road, and at the end of the second, celebrated the team's promotion to the First Division. 
* Although he was transferred to Leicester City on the 27th of March 1992, Mike Whitlow had contributed with one goal in 10 games to the League title won by Leeds in the 91-92 season. 
* In 1994 Leicester are promoted to the Premier League.  However, in the following season, with Whitlow plagued by various injuries, the team is relegated once again to the First Division. 
* In the 95-96 season he scores three league goals, the highest number of his career.  Leicester return to the Premier League after beating Crystal Palace in the final of the promotion play-offs (2-1). 
* In November 96 he received an injury to his ligaments which kept him out for 4 months. 
* Bolton pay Leicester £500,000 to bring him to the club on the 19/9/97.

* A ligament injury in the month of November cut short his spectacular start to the season.  He returned to the team at the end of March, playing a series a games in which he showed details of a good player.  In total he took part in 17 games.

397.name: Elliot
pages: * After going through a true injury nightmare, Robbie Elliot saw the light at the end of the tunnel at the end of the 95-96 season, when he managed to take the left back position away from John Beresford and earn the recognition of the fans at Newcastle.  Since then his progress has been good, so much so that last season he became one of the best left backs in the championships. The £2.5 million paid by Bolton for him will be an excellent investment if he performs to the same level as the previous season.

* Rob Elliot is a very versatile player, able to occupy several positions. In fact, during his career he has played on the left wing, at centre back and left back.  In this last position he has offered his best performance, helped by his stamina, allowing him to cover the whole of the touchline and take part in defensive missions and in attack.  He is quick and skilful, and has an acceptable technique, passes well and shoots powerfully.  He pushes up constantly supporting the forwards and regains his position quickly when his team is on the defensive. 
* He usually played at left back for the under-21 side as well.  At Newcastle he has played in the midfield at times to take advantage of his creativity.  He has also played in the centre of the defence, and has done his job thanks to his good aerial game.  Elliot is, at the end of the day, a very versatile footballer.
x

* 2 under-21 international appearances for England. 
* 1 youth international appearance.

* A product of the Newcastle youth squad, Robbie Elliot makes his debut for the first team on the 12th of March 1991 in a game against Middlesbrough. Shortly afterwards, on the 3rd of April, he signs his first professional contract. 
* He has to wait till the 94-95 season to score his first goal.  It was on the 21st of August 1994 in the first game of the season against Leicester in the City Stadium.  Newcastle won 1-3. 
* His short professional career has been plagued by injuries, some of them as serious as a broken tibia and broken ligaments. 
* Up till the end of the 94-95 season he had received 5 yellow cards and he had been sent off once. 
* In July 97 Bolton pay Newcastle £2.5 million for his move.

* Despite the problems he had at Newcastle at the beginning of the season, Elliot had one of his best seasons since arriving in the Premier League. He scored 7 goals, one of them direct from a corner and his incorporations into the attack was one of Newcastle's attacking options.

398.name: Bergsson
pages: * A solid and aggressive footballer, Gudni Bergsson performs the role given to him by his manager perfectly without complicating things.  He is noted above all in defensive aspects although he usually brings danger at set-plays.

* A defender who can play both at right back and in the centre of defence, he is very good in set-plays thanks mainly to his height, powerful jump and aggression when looking for the ball as he doesn't wait for the ball to come to him but rather looks for it decisively.  He is quick in both positions, going in strongly for the ball.  When he plays at right back he doesn't usually push up into the attack as he is not so skilful at dribbling past his opponents and his crosses are pretty mediocre.
x

* He has been an Iceland international in the youth, under-21 and full categories, in the last of these 74 times, making him the player who has made most appearances for the Nordic country and is also captain.

* He is signed by Tottenham Hotspur from Valur Reykjavik for £100,000 in December 1988.  He makes his debut in the league on the 26/12/88 against Luton Town and his first goal is in the London derby against Wimbledon on the 23/3/91. 
* He is transferred to Bolton Wanderers for £65,000 in March 1995 although he was there on trial with the reserves and once his transfer had gone through, the first time he is called on is to play the League Cup final against Liverpool, coming on as a substitute for Scott Green, although his team lost the game.  His league debut is on the 5/4/95 against Swindon Town and he scores his first league goal on the 22/8/95 against Newcastle United.
* He took a year out from playing football to finish his studies in law.

* Although he started the season on the bench, Bergsson became on of the most regular players in the manager's line-ups.  He played as a wide defender on both sides and as a central defender, bringing a lot of danger in set-plays. He took part in 33 games and scored 3 goals, two of them against Swindon Town.

399.name: Salako
pages: * Signed for Bolton in March 1998. A few years ago John Salako was one of the most promising players in England.  A native of Nigeria, in 1991 his talent carried him into the England team managed Graham Taylor.  His progress was spectacular until he became injured in a game at Selhurst Park.  From that moment on, his life has been a constant battle to make up for lost time and to reach the same level.  Little by little he seems to be managing to do so.  Although for now he has only offered glimpses of the great footballer he was, at Highfield Road much is expected of him.  He goes into his third season at Coventry with the hope of becoming the best signing made by the Sky Blues.  To do so he will have to try to forget that Autumn night at Selhurst Park.  Perhaps this year, John Salako, 28, will once again become one of the most promising players in England.

* A very quick left wing and very technical, John Salako is outstanding for the ease with which he makes very accurate passes.  Hugging the touchline, he takes advantage of his excellent ball control with both feet to provide chances for the forward line.  A footballer who covers a lot of ground, his turn is able to tie even the firmest defenders in knots, but he doesn't score so many goals.  Although he has lost some of his speed after the lengthy period of inactivity caused by a very serious injury, Salako still shows signs of being a good footballer.  However, he needs to take more part in the team's game, as his performance is a bit irregular at times.
* First Division Champion 94.
* 5 full international appearances for England.  He made his debut on the 1st of June 1991 with an England victory over Australia in Sydney (0-1). Salako came on as a substitute for David Hirst.

* A native of Nigeria, John Salako arrived in England aged 10.  Four years later he joined Crystal Palace.  A professional since the 3rd of November 1986, he made his league debut three days before turning 18 in a home game against Barnsley.
* In the 86-87 season he only played four games, all of them as a substitute, but in the following years he formed part of the best Crystal Palace team in history, a side which also boasted Ian Wright, Mark Bright, Andy Gray and Geoff Thomas among others.
* In 1989 the team is promoted to the First Division.  On the 14th of August of this same year he is loaned to Swansea city, the team for who he played 13 games.  In 1990 he plays in the final that Crystal Palace loose to Manchester United.
* In June 1991 he makes his debut for the England team under the command of Graham Taylor.  But in October of this same year he suffers from a very serious injury to his knee ligaments in a game against Leeds United played at Selhurst Park.  Crystal Palace send him to Los Angeles, where he received a tendon implanted from a deceased person.
* Shortly afterward making his reappearance in the 92-93 season he has a relapse and goes to the States once again to receive more treatment.
* Salako returns to the playing field in the 93-94 season and makes a decisive to Crystal Palace's return to the Premier League.  In October 1994 he scores two goals against Arsenal to help the Eagles to the first win at Highbury in their history.
* On the 7th of August 1995 he is transferred to Coventry for £1,500,000. He makes his debut on the 19th of August with a defeat in St. James Park against Newcastle.  On the 9th of December he scores against Blackburn Rovers at Highfield Road, his first goal for the Sky Blues.

* Salako took part in 24 games and scored a goal.  Injuries prevented him from performing more, although in the games in which he appeared to be on form, he showed that he is one of the most skilful wingers in the Premier League, especially in a game in Highfield Road against Leeds, where he scored a great goal after starting the play from his own half.

400.name: Taylor
pages:
* Loaned to Bolton in March 1998. During his time at Bristol City, Bob Taylor was one of the most promising strikers in the lower divisions, and was even spoken about as a possible  England striker for the 1994 World Cup Finals in the United States. However  a dip in his form hindered his progress and caused the big clubs to lose interested in him. 
* An automatic first choice in previous season, he took advantage of this to score a respectable number of goals. However the arrival of Paul Peschisolido saw him lose his place in Alan Buckley's starting line up. The situations hasn't change under Ray Harford although Taylor will always have an important contribution to make either coming off the bench or replacing an injured or suspended teammate.

* Bob Taylor is a penalty area player and is a fine finisher with either foot as well as his head whenever he gets the slightest opportunity, a player who regularly finds the back of the net. A hard worker, he keeps opponents under constant pressure. Physically he is very strong and fights for every ball with rival defenders. He holds the ball up well waiting for his teammates to come through in support. Good in the air, he gets onto the end of long balls which he lays off perfectly to team mates coming through from deeper positions. However technically he is quite basic and doesn't get involved in the build up, prefering to wait to finish the moves off.

* Top scorer at Bristol City in seasons 89-90 and 90-91. 
* Top scorer at WBA in seasons 92-93, 93-94 and 95-96.
x

* Taylor began his playing career with amateur club Horden Colly, signing professional in January 1986 with Leeds United. He made his league debut on 12th April 1986 against Millwall, scoring his first goal on 16th August 1986 against Barnsley. 
* In March 1989he was transfered to Bristol City. He made his debut in the local derby against Bristol Rovers on 25th March 1989. Taylor had a good end to his first season at the club, scoring 8 goals in 12 games. 
* He was transfered to WBA In January 1992 for £300,000, managing to score on his league debut on 1st February 1992, against Brentford.

* In general Taylor didn't enjoy a particularly good season as a result of injuries and loss of form. Even so he managed to end the campaign with 10 goals to his name, several of which proved to be very important for the Baggies. The arrival of Peschisolido didn't help him even though he managed To make a total of 32 appearances during the course of the season.

401.name: Gunnlaugsson
pages: * An Iceland international, Gunnlaugsson is a player who, according to Todd should progress a little more to get to play some more.  Even so, if things are going badly for Bolton he might come on as a shot in the arm.

* Gunnlaugsson is a typical forward who finishes well, is in good physical condition and who tries to shoot at all costs.  He is still a player who needs to improve as he has shown details of being a good footballer.
x
* Full international for Iceland.
* Trained in Akranes, Bolton have paid £100,000 for his transfer.
* He played for Akranes, for whom he scored 15 goals in 18 goals, and arousing the interest of several teams.

402.name: Holdsworth
pages: * This is Holdsworth's first season at Bolton, after having spent the last few years of his career at Wimbledon where he has left behind a good impression.  At Bolton he is hoped to be the man who puts away the chances that come Bolton's way.

* A great centre forward, blessed with an excellent technique and great strength.  He was Wimbledon's best marksman, easily able to find space to get in one of his good shots.  Clever, he usually makes good use of hanging balls to the box.  Right-footed, at times he drifts over to the left to take advantage of his hard well-placed drive, although he performs best when he is in front of the goal.  He is a football with a good finishing instinct, this nuance which distinguishes great marksmen from good forwards.
* Third Division Champion 91-92 with Brentford.
* 1 international-B appearance for England.  1 goal.

* Raised in the Watford youth squad, he turns professional on the 12th of November 1986, but his league debut doesn't take place until the 12th of December 1987 in a game against Luton. 
* As a Watford player, he is loaned to four different teams in the year, 1988: Carlisle United in February, Port Vale in March, Swansea in August and Brentford in October. 
* Finally, he is transferred to Brentford on the 29th of September 1989 for £125,000. 
* Brentford's and the Third Division's top scorer in 91-92, his step-up to the Premier League was disputed between several teams, among them Manchester United, although finally it was Wimbledon who managed to sign him on the 20th of July 1992 for £720,000. 
* During the course of his career he has scored 4 hat-tricks, the first of which was on the 6th of January 1990 against Rotherham United and the last on the 20th of April 1994 against Oldham. 
* In the 94-95 season there are constant rumours of a transfer to another club which, together with his constant injuries, negatively affected his performance: only 2 goals in 11 games at the beginning of the season.  Up till the end of this season he had received 40 yellow cards in his career, though he had never been sent off.

* Gayle and Ekoku's form prevented Holdsworth from enjoying the continuity that he had enjoyed in previous seasons.  Even so, in the games in which he did appear he showed his character, scoring some important goals for Wimbledon.  He played 25 games and scored 5 goals.

403.name: Blake
pages: * A classical centre forward with enormous power, Nathan Blake is a player who usually guarantees a good number of goals during the course of the season.  A little selfish when near the goal as he only sees the goal and not his team-mates who might be unmarked.  As well as the great power of his shots he also is good in the air thanks to his strength and height, but his header is not one of the best.  Last season was an excellent one for him and a lot is expected of this player.

* A powerful centre forward, it is hard to get the ball off him or bring him down.  When he has the ball in his possession he goes in search of the opponents' goal, finishing with a powerful shot although the quality leaves something to be desired.  But try enough times and you will succeed, so he usually scores a fair few goals.  He is technically rather weak, and can't dribble out of tight spaces, using force in everything he does.  His important assets are his constant battling for the ball and the pressure he puts the other defenders under.

* Welsh Cup Champion with Cardiff City 1992 and 1993. 
* Third Division Champion 1993 with Cardiff City. 
* Top scorer at Cardiff City 93-94. 
* Top scorer at Sheffield United 94-95.
* Wales under-21, B and full international, with six appearances in the latter of these categories.  He made his debut on the 9/3/94 in Cardiff against Norway.

* Originally from the Chelsea juniors, although he ends up signing as a professional for Cardiff City.  He makes his league debut on the 24/3/90 against Bristol Rovers and his first two league goals help his team to victory over York City on the 13/10/90. 
* Sheffield United sign him in February 1994 for £300,000, making his league debut with the team on the 22/2/94 against Ipswich Town and scoring his first goal against Tottenham Hotspur on the 5/3/94. 
* He is transferred to Bolton Wanderers in January 1996 for £1.5 million. He makes his debut on the 19/12/95 against Tottenham Hotspur and scores his first goal against Middlesbrough on the 17/2/96.

* Last season was, without doubt, one of Blake's best since turning professional.  He scored 19 goals, a figure he had never reached in the Premier League, and appeared in 42 games, being one the automatic choices for the manager.

404.name: Jaaskelainen
pages: * Colin Todd, Bolton's manager, has always been in favour of having a squad which includes three good goalkeepers.  For this reason he has decided to sign Jussi Jaaskelainen, a very young keeper from Finland with a lot of talent and a sparkling future ahead of him.
* A young keeper, he has an amazing physical condition.  He is noted for his effectiveness in the aerial game although, logically, he needs to acquire the resources that will come with experience.
x
* An under-21 international for Finland.

* The Bolton manager, Colin Todd, decided to bring him to Bolton for a trial period after seeing him in a game played between the Finnish and Norwegian under-21 teams.
* He signed for Bolton on the 11th of November 1997.  His price: £100,000.
x

405.name: Branagan
pages: * Keith Branagan is a level-headed keeper, who always does what's asked of him without much ado.  He is a true life insurance for his team and never let's them down.  He is also very brave and decisive when coming out to the forwards' feet.  His debut in the Republic of Ireland first team the previous season has given him plenty of confidence in his abilities.

* A very complete keeper, with good reflexes, excellent positioning and dominant in the aerial game.  He complies with an fundamental requisite in any goalie, and that is he never lets in stupid goals.  In other words, he doesn't make incredible saves to then concede absurd goals.
* Runner-up in the League Cup 94-95 with Bolton Wanderers.

* 1 full international appearance for the Republic of Ireland. 
* B international.

* Originally from the lower ranks of Cambridge United, he signs as a professional in August 1983.  He makes his debut on the 14/1/84 against Carlisle United. 
* He is transferred to Millwall in March 1988 for £100,000, making his debut in the league on the 13/1/90 against Nottingham Forest. 
* He is loaned to Brentford in November 1989 but only plays 2 games, the first of which is on the 25/11/89 against Northampton Town. 
* He is loaned once again, this time to Gillingham in October 1991 for just one game played on the 12/10/91 against Halifax Town. 
* His contract with Millwall ends and he signs for Bolton Wanderers in July 1992, and plays his first game for the club on the 15/8/92 against Huddersfield Town. 
* He was one of the heroes of the play-off in May 1995 when he saved a penalty from Stuart Lovell, the Reading player, when his team were losing 2-0.  From that moment on, Bolton recovered and ended up winning the game 4-3 in extra-time.

* Branagan won't easily forget the 96-97 season, when he at last managed to make his debut for the Republic of Ireland.  He made some spectacular saves and left no doubt as to who should be first choice to defend the Bolton goal.

406.name: Fairclough
pages: * Chris Fairclough is a quick central defender who is, above all, very aggressive, something which has created more than a problem or two in the clubs where he has played.  He is a player who always gives 100%, sweating blood on the pitch in every game.  He also has a great personality which, together with his aggression, make him a central defender who sticks close to his man and who is difficult to get the better of.

* A strong aggressive central defender, he is very good in the air and is dangerous at set-plays.  With the ball at his feet he is not so comfortable and prefers to release it without making things complicated.  He only joins in the attack for set-plays and won't push up even if he takes the ball off the rival forward, passing it to the closest team-mate.  He has lost some of his speed but is still hard to beat in this respect.  He is a hard player when going in for the ball.

* 2nd Division Champion 89-90 with Leeds United. 
* First Division Champion 91-92 with Leeds United. 
* Charity Shield Medal 92 with Leeds United.

* He has been a B and under-21 international, making his debut in the latter of these categories on the 13/11/84 against Turkey in an England team which included David Seaman, Paul Bracewell and Barry Venison to mention just a few.

* Originally from the lower ranks of Nottingham Forest, he signs as a professional in October 1981.  He makes his league debut against Liverpool and scores his first league goal against Tottenham Hotspur on the 29/11/86.
* Tottenham Hotspur sign him in July 1987 for £387,000.  He makes his league debut on the 15/8/87 against Coventry City and his first goal in the winner in the London derby against West Ham United on the 19/9/87. 
* Transferred to Leeds United in March 1989 for £500,000, he makes his debut in the league on the 25/3/89 against Portsmouth, in a game in which he scores his team's equaliser. 
* He is finally transferred to Bolton Wanderers in the summer of 1995 for £500,000 making his debut on the 19/8/95 against Wimbledon.
* He formed an excellent partnership with Taggart in the centre of the defence.  He was very secure and also scored some decisive goals to help Bolton return to the Premier League.

407.name: Johansen
pages:
* A footballer who has earned himself a lot of prestige recently, Michael Johansen was seen as one of the most creative players in the Danish league. He even took part in the 6-2 thrashing of Bayern Munich by Copenhagen in the 91-92 season although he came on as a substitute. 
* Last season was his first in English football, adapting well to the style of football, and making himself one of the favourites among the Bolton fans.

* The Danish player is a very quick left wing who always plays hugging his touchline, which prevents him from scoring many goals.  Despite playing on the left, he is right-footed, and he will often cut infield.  He is a good passer and with good playing vision as well, supplying his forwards with some excellent balls.  His crosses are not so consistent, some being good and others bad.  He has a good first-time touch, looking for one-twos and triangular moves to penetrate the other team's defence.
* Danish League Champion with Copenhagen in 1993.

* 3 full international appearances for Denmark. 
* He has played in the Danish Olympic team alongside Per Frandsen, who is now his team-mate at Bolton Wanderers.

* After being in teams such as Kjobenhavns Boldklub, B 1903 and Copenhagen, Johansen moves to Bolton Wanderers in August 1996 in exchange for £1.25 million. 
* He made his debut for Bolton in the First Division on the 17/8/96 against Port Vale (1-1).

* In his first season at Bolton, Johansen quickly managed to establish himself in the first team.  He was a skilful winger, able to open up tight defences.  He took part in 33 games and scored 5 goals.

408.name: Sheridan
pages: * For a player who has represented his country 32 times, who has participated in two World Cup final stages and one European Championship, it can't be easy to get used to seeing the game from the bench.  Desperate to play, last season John Sheridan chose to leave the Premier League to try and return with Bolton, something he managed.

* Sheridan is a classy midfielder.  Blessed with good ball control and playing vision, he is used to make passes with extraordinary accuracy over thirty or forty metres.  With an exquisite right foot, he is particularly good at taking direct free-kicks and penalties.  As he is rather short and not so strong, he is more reliant on his technique to control the ball and pass it on safely.  On the other hand, he doesn't help out so much in defence, something which has cost him his place in the side many times.
* League Cup Champion 91.

* 34 full international appearances for the Republic of Ireland.  He made his debut on the 23rd of March 1988 in a preparation game for the 88 European Championship against Romania in Dublin. 
* He is included in the squad that plays in the Germany 88 European Championship, but doesn't play a single minute. 
* In the Italy 90 World Cup he come on for John Aldridge in the quarter-final between Ireland and Italy.  He doesn't have much time to impress, as there were only 13 minutes left till the end. 
* Present in the USA 94 World Cup, he is first choice in the four games played by his team against Italy (1-0), Mexico (1-2), Norway (0-0) and Holland (0-2). 
* 1 B-international appearance. 
* 2 under-23 international appearances. 
* 2 under-21 international appearances. 
* Youth international.

* He started his career in the Manchester City youth squad.  He also found a gap in the Republic of Ireland team at this level. 
* On the 2nd of March 1982 he signs for Leeds United as an apprentice to make his debut in the league on the 20th of November of this same year against Middlesbrough.  In December Oldham Athletic are on the receiving end of his first goal. 
* After seven years at Elland Road John Sheridan is transferred to Nottingham Forest on the 3rd of August 1989 for £650,000. 
* Only three months later (3rd November), and without having played a single minute in the league, Brian Clough decides to transfer him to Sheffield Wednesday for £500,000. 
* By chance, his league debut for the Owls takes place against Nottingham Forest on the 4th of November and in March 1990 he scores his first goal in a game against Derby County. 
* Probably the happiest day of his career at Sheffield was the day of the League Cup final in 1991.  Sheridan scored the winner against Manchester United.  However, he couldn't repeat the feat in the FA Cup replay in 1993 against Arsenal, nor in the League Cup final in this same year, also against the Gunners. 
* In February 1996 he is loaned to Birmingham City and there was even talk of his definitive transfer.  However, on returning to Hillsborough in March the Wednesday crowd gave him a rousing ovation.

* Unable to find a place in the Sheffield team, he chose to go on loan to Bolton in November.  His performances were pretty good and so the club decided to make the move definitive.  He took part in 20 games and scored 2 goals.

409.name: Frandsen
pages: * This is Fransen's second season at Bolton, where he arrived from Copenhagen. It seems as if he has adapted well to English football, although he will now have to prove himself in the Premier League.

* A midfielder with a lot of strength and quality, Frandsen is also a good ball-winner.  The Danish player has a good presence on the pitch as he always asks for the ball.  He passes the ball effectively, both over short and long range, and always to the most suitably placed player.  He is better with his right that his left and it is hard to get the ball off him thanks to his bulk.  If this weren't enough, he has a great shot from about 25 yards, both powerful and well placed.

* Danish League Champion with Copenhagen in 1995. 
* Top scorer at Copenhagen in 1995 alongside Lars Nielsen with 12 goals.
* 13 full international appearances for Denmark.

* Originally from the Danish team Copenhagen, Frandsen signs for Bolton Wanderers in the summer of 1996 for £1.25 million. 
* He scored his first goal for Bolton against Manchester City.

* Just as with Johansen, Frandsen quickly found a place for himself in the first team.  His powerful shot and playing vision helped him earn the confidence of the manager, who aligned him 41 times.  Frandsen scored five goals.

410.name: Phillips
pages: * Jimmy Phillips is basically the type of footballer who is considered a club player, doing his job efficiently without many complications, but being firm in his game, trying to do the things he knows how to do.  He is a true defensive specialist, making things difficult for the other team's forwards but hardly making a noteworthy contribution to the attack.

* A very consistent left back, he doesn't usually leave his position in the defence to push up but when he does so his crosses are good.  He is not quick, so will not try the individual play much, preferring to pass the ball.  He is defensively very solid, not spectacular in his actions but it is hard to get the better of him.  He passes the ball efficiently and you rarely see him make mistakes.  In the aerial game he is OK but not outstanding.
* League Cup Runner-up 94-95 with Bolton Wanderers.
x

* Originally from the lower ranks of the club, he signs as a professional in August 1983.  He makes his league debut on the 7/4/84 against Gillingham and scores his first league goal on the 29/3/85 against York City. 
* Glasgow Rangers sign him in 1987 for £95,000 and he makes his debut against the Old Firm in the derby against Celtic. 
* He is transferred to Oxford United in August 1988 for £110,000, and makes his league debut on the 27/9/88 against Leeds United and scores his first goal against Shrewsbury Town on the 1/10/88. 
* He is transferred to Middlesbrough in March 1990 for £250,000.  He plays his first game for the club against Blackburn Rovers on the 17/3/90 and scores his first goal against Leicester City on the 29/9/90. 
* Finally Bolton Wanderers sign him again in July 1993 for £250,000, and he makes his debut in the league on the 4/2/95 against Wolverhampton Wanderers and scores the first goal of his new spell at the club in the same game.

* Phillips once again had a regular season, contributing with good defending. %He was available for selection for just about every game, and played in most of the games, and was a true pillar of the Bolton side.
