411.name: Taggart
pages: * Gerry Taggart became the most expensive signing in the history of the club in October 1995.  However, he didn't live up to expectations created by such a talked about signing.  A professional and tough player, these are the main characteristics of one of the key players in Todd's plans.

* A very powerful central defender, he is a player who always tries to make his strength count when taking on rival forwards.  He is dangerous at set-plays more for the attention paid to him creating more room for his team-mates than for his own header.  He is nothing special with the ball at his feet, almost always playing the long ball or the short pass to the midfield if he has the time and space to do so.  He is not quick but has a good sense of placement which helps him in difficult situations.  He is very tough when going in for the ball, making use of this tremendous physical power.
x

* Northern Ireland international in the youth, under-21 and full categories. He made his debut in Belfast on the 27/3/90 against Norway.  In total he has played 42 times for his country and scored 6 goals.

* A player originally from the lower ranks of Manchester city, he signs as a professional in July 1989.  He plays his first league game on the 4/2/89 and scores his first goal against Chelsea on the 18/3/89. 
* He is transferred to Barnsley in January 1990 for £75,000.  On his league debut he scores against Brighton & Hove Albion, the date: 13/1/90.
* Bolton Wanderers sign him in October 1995 for £2.3 million, and he makes his debut for the team on the 9/9/95 against Middlesbrough and scores his first league goal against Sheffield Wednesday on the 1/1/96. 
* Taggart has the honour of being the most expensive player in the club's history.
* He formed a defensive axis alongside Fairclough and became one of the cornerstones on which the Bolton promotion bid was founded.  He took part in 43 games and scored 3 goals.

412.name: Thompson
pages: * A player who has an enormous quality but has certain character problems, above all if things don't go his way.  Proof of this was when he was sent off in the under-21 game against Portugal at the end of 1995.  Now in the Premier League again, Thompson will try to repeat the good things he showed last season.

* A left winger with a very high quality left foot, his forays down the left bring a lot of danger with them both for his good crosses and his shot, powerful and well-placed.  He is quick and before starting off a move he has everything pre-recorded and so doesn't improvise much.  At times he has played successfully as a centre half such as in the playoff game against Reading, where he showed his good playing vision and calmness when directing the team's play.
* Runner-up in the League Cup 94-95 with Bolton Wanderers, scoring the team's only goal against Liverpool.
* He is an England youth and under-21 international, making his debut in this latter category in the Toulon international tournament on the 7/6/95 against Latvia.

* Originally from the lower ranks of Newcastle United, he signs as a professional in March 1991.  He makes his league debut on the 2/11/91 against Swindon Town.  However, the arrival of Kevin Keegan as manager at St. James Park forced him onto the bench, and he only played two games in the 92-93 season.
* In July 1993 he is transferred to Bolton Wanderers for £250,000, in an attempt to revitalise his career.  He plays his first game on the 14/8/93 against Grimsby Town and scores his first goal on the 26/9/93 against Nottingham Forest. 
* His goal from the penalty spot in the opening game of the 95-96 season against Wimbledon was Bolton Wanderer's first in the Premier League.
* He was voted "Man of the Match" in the play-off game against Reading in May 1995.

* He was, without doubt, one of Bolton's best players and one of the key pieces in their promotion to the Premier League.  His goals and quality led teams such as Nottingham and Leeds to take an interest in him.  Thompson took part in 34 games and scored 10 goals.

413.name: Sellars
pages: * Scott Sellars is one of the best left-footers in English football, but also one of the most irregular.  That's the way he is, sometimes brilliant, other times mediocre.  He is so inconsistent that when he is on form he likes to direct the team and take on the responsibility but when he is off form he has vast deserts in his play, and he disappears from the game.

* In recent years he was a left wing with a magnificent left foot which gave accurate passes and put over precise crosses for the forwards.  But after a serious injury to his knee he has lost speed, and now plays in the midfield, playing with good touch and playing vision.  He is also a true free-kick specialist.  He is not so strong physically but doesn't need to be as he always tries to avoid contact with his opponent if it is possible but he is not timid, he just tries to make use of his skill.
* First Division Champion 92-93 with Newcastle United.
* Under-21 international for England, he makes his debut on the 22/3/88 against Scotland in Nottingham, coming on for Paul Gascoigne.

* Originally from the lower ranks of Leeds United, he signs as a professional in July 1983.  He makes his league debut on the 2/5/83 against Leicester City, scoring his first league goal on the 31/12/83 against Middlesbrough.
* He is transferred to Blackburn Rovers for £20,000 in July 1986.  He plays his first game against his former team, Leeds United, on the 23/8/86.  His first goal in the league is the winner seven days later in a game against Shrewsbury Town. 
* He returns to Leeds United once again in July 1992 in exchange for £800,000 and makes his debut in the league on the 13/9/92 against Aston Villa.
* Kevin Keegan had always had confidence in his abilities and so he signed him in March 1993 for Newcastle United for £700,000, and he was a key player in the Magpies' promotion to the Premier League.  He makes his debut in the league competition on the 10/3/93 against Charlton Athletic and scores his first goal against Barnsley on the 7/4/93. 
* A serious knee injury keeps him out for several months in the 94-95 season. 
* Bolton Wanderers sign him for £750,000 in December 1995, and he makes his debut in the league on the 9/12/95 against Liverpool and scores his first goal seven days later against QPR.
* Sellars had one of his best seasons, taking part in 42 games and scoring 8 goals.  He was dangerous when taking free-kicks.  His presence was vital for Bolton's return to the Premier League.

414.name: Todd
pages: * Although he is the manager's son, Andy Todd is a footballer who is there on his own merit.  What's more, when he was signed by Bolton, the manager wasn't his father but Roy McFarland.  Transferred from Middlesbrough, Bryan Robson didn't use him and the competition for a place in the defence was very strong.  In any case, he is a team player who fights hard and has a good future ahead of him.

* He is playing as a midfielder for Bolton Wanderers.  A physically strong player, he wins back a lot of balls, and joins in the attack quickly.  He shots well with either foot.  He also distributes the ball effectively and with good judgement.  He is good in the air despite not being so tall.  Finally, it should be mentioned that doesn't stop working for the team.
x
x

* Originally from the lower ranks of Middlesbrough, he signs as a professional in March 1992.  He makes his debut in the league on the 18/12/93 against Notts County. 
* He is loaned to Swindon Town in February 1995, and plays his first league game on the 1/3/95 against Millwall. 
* He is signed by Bolton Wanderers in the summer of 1995 for £250,000 and makes his league debut on the 23/9/95 at Anfield against Liverpool, where he also scored his first goal as a professional.  He couldn't have picked a better place for it.
* He took part in 15 games in which he showed that he is a player who can be counted on at any time.

415.name: Ward
pages: * Gavin Ward is a goalie who basically has the function of stepping in for the first choice keeper when he is injured or suspended, a job he does well. He was bought from Bradford City to cover for the absence of the injured Branagan, something that had also happened at Leicester City with his team-mate Kevin Poole.  In general, he is a player who does his job without spectacular performances and for this reason he doesn't usually play a lot.

* A very secure goalkeeper with the aerial balls, he has good reflexes and his positioning is excellent but he isn't a keeper who is able to win games on the strength of his performance, that is to say, he is not decisive. Nor does he commit serious mistakes.

* Third Division Champion 1993 with Cardiff City. 
* Welsh Cup Champion 1993 with Cardiff City.
x

* He is signed from the Aston Villa juniors by Shrewsbury Town in September 1988 when his contract with the Birmingham club expires. 
* After his contract expires he signs for WBA in September 1989. 
* He signs for Cardiff City in October 1989, and makes his debut on the 7/10/89 against Huddersfield Town. 
* He is transferred to Leicester City in July 1993 for £175,000 and makes his debut in the league on the 14/8/93 against Peterborough United.
* In the summer of 1995 he signs for Bradford City for £400,000, a price which included Nicky Mohan and Ian Ormondroyd.  He makes his debut on the 12/8/95 against Bournemouth. 
* He is finally transferred to Bolton Wanderers in March 1996 for £500,000, making his debut on the 30/3/96 against Manchester City.

* Ward didn't have many chances during the course of the season due to the good performances of Branagan, the first choice goalie, only making 11 appearances in the whole of the league.  In short, his role was to watch how Branagan settled ever more firmly into the team, without being able to to do anything about it.

416.name: Ismael
pages: * With the season already underway, Ismael arrives at Crystal Palace in order to bolster the defence of the London team.  An under-21 international for France, he hopes to relaunch a still short career with a success story in the Premier League.
* He usually plays at centre back.  He is strong and firm and, at times, hard.  He is dominant in the aerial game, but he squanders some chances in attack.
No data.
* French under-21 international.

* Trained in the Strasbourg youth squad, he made his debut for the first team on the 15th of January 1994, in a game between Cannes and Strasbourg (1-1).
* He was transferred to Crystal Palace on the 15th of January 1998 for £2,750,000.
* He was one of the players most used by the Strasbourg manager.  He played in 33 league games and scored a goal.

417.name: Fullarton
pages: * In a bid to reinforce the defensive line of Crystal Palace, the manager Steve Coppell didn't hesitate to push through the signing of Jamie Fullarton.  The Scottish footballer guarantees hard work and security, qualities that might help him find a gap for himself in the Premier League.
* A very powerful central defender, he is particularly noted for his sound aerial game.  Discrete technically, he doesn't look to make things too complicated when playing the ball out form the back.
x
x

* Before signing for Bastia in 1996 he had worn the shirts of two Scottish clubs: Motherwell and Saint Mirren. 
* In February 1998 he was transferred to Crystal Palace.
* He played in 17 league games for Bastia.

418.name: Smith
pages:
* Signed for Crystal Palace in October 1997.
* Despite his youth, James Smith was a key man in Mark McGhee's plans, with his continuous movement up and down the flank, where he shows tremendous pace and enthusiasm. He has just completed his best season yet with Wolverhampton Wanderers and now he will have a great opportunity in the Premier League.

* The young Wolves full back possesses a tremendous, attacking approach to the game, although one of his defects is his carelessness when he chooses to go forward. He possesses effective, though not particularly orthodox, dribbling ability, and, when the ball moves infield from the left hand side, he accelerates forward into the space created, looking to get away from his markers and get onto the end of a long through ball. A difficult player to beat for speed, his crosses have noticeably improved in recent times although he still needs to refine some some of his weak points, above all his crossing while on the run. He is not a player who is inclined to have a shot at goal, generally prefering to put crosses over into the strikers.
x
x

* After coming through the youth ranks at Wolverhampton Wanderers, he signed professional in June 1993. He played his first league game for the club on 13th August 1994 against Reading. 
* He was chosen as Wolves' Young Player of the Year for 94-95. 
* He has been called up to the England Under-21 squad on a number of occasions but is yet to be given the chance to make his debut

* A sensational season for this young product of the Wolverhampton Wanderers youth system, who went on to play 38 games during the course of last season. His attacking contribution got better as the season drew on, and he even managed to open his goalscoring account for the club in the play-off game against Crystal Palace, although it wasn't enough to get Wolves up into the Premier League.

419.name: Hreidarsson
pages: * After coming through a trial period, Herman Hreidarsson was finally able tp sign for Crystal Palace. During the 1997-98 he will no doubt get the chance to make his debut in the Premier League for Palace, an excellent way to start going about the task of making a name for himself in English football.

* A strong, forceful central defender, he stands out for his ability in the air. Nevertheless he has very little experience of high level competition, which makes him something of an unknown quantity.
x
x
* He arrived at Crystal Palace in the summer of 1997 from Icelandic club IVB, although he had already played a number of games for Palace's reserve side during the 96-97 season.
* He had two separate trial periods with Crystal Palace and played a number  of games for the club's reserve side.

420.name: Emblen
pages: * Neil Emblen is one of Crystal Palace's reinforcements for the 97-98 season. A defender, he was signed from Wolverhampton Wanderers, who, last season, fell just short of winning promotion to the Premier League. With Steve Coppell in charge, Neil will no doubt get the opportunity to make his debut in the top flights of English football.

* A strong, quick midfielder, he does an important ballwinning job for the side. A good marker, he regularly gets forward into the attack, above all for dead ball situations, where he can make the most of his ability in the air.
x
x

* He was signed by Millwall from amateur club Sittingbourne for 175,000 pounds in November 1993, making his debut on 20th November 1993 against Tranmere Rovers. 
* He was transfered to Wolverhampton Wanderers in July 1994 for 600,000 pounds. He played his first game for the club on 13th August 1994 against Reading and scored his first goal in a Wolves shirt on 30th August 1994 Against Watford. 
* On 11th August 1997 he was transfered to Crystal Palace for 1,800,000 pounds.

* He was a member of the starting line up in 27 of the 28 league games in which he played. Once again, injuries prevented him from playing more regularly. As a result he had something of an inconsistent season. In March he went through some problems with his knee, and, although he reappeared one month later, he was unable to recapture his best form.

421.name: Linighan
pages: * Now 35 years of age, Andy Linighan is bringing a tremendous career to a dignified end. However, his excellent form during the course of last season, means that nobody is willing to predict when he will finally call it a day. He signed for Crystal Palace to help the club get back into the Premier League, which he managed to do. Although very much at the veteran stage, he seems to have plenty of good performances left in him yet.

* Andy Linighan is a classic central defender, who dominates in the air in both penalty areas and is a hard and forceful player at the back. His main strength is his ability to clear the ball long, away from his own penalty area. His clearances occasionally serve to set up counterattacks. Technically limited, he makes up for his lack of ability on the ball with his commitment, concentration and experience.

* European Cup Winners Cup winners medal 1994.
* European Cup Winners Cup runners up medal 1995.
* F.A. Cup winners medal 1993.
* League Cup winners medal 1993.
* Charity Shield medal 1993.
* 4 "B" international appearances for England.

* A member of a footballing family, is father Brian played for Darlington while his brothers David and Brian are also professionals with Blackpool and Sheffield Wednesday respectively. Andy Linighan set out in the world of football at modest Henry Smiths Boys Club. 
* As a free agent, he signed for Hartlepool United on 19th September 1980, although he didn't make his league debut until 28th March 1981, against Stockport. 
* On 15th May 1984 he was transfered to Leeds United for 20,000 pounds. The Elland Road club were, at the time, in the Second Division. 
* Linighan took the step up to the top flight of English football on 4th March 1988, when he moved on to Norwich City for 350,000 pounds. He was signed as cover for the departure of Steve Bruce. After three seasons at Carrow Road, the club received a tempting offer from Arsenal. Shortly after On 4th July 1990, Andy ended up at Highbury in exchange for 1,250,000 pounds. He made his debut as a substitute in a game against Chelsea on 15th September 1990. 
* Andy Linighan went down in Arsenal's history when he scored with a powerful header in the last minute of the 1993 F.A. Cup final replay against Sheffield Wednesday which took the trophy back to Highbury. However, he never really settle down as a regular in the Gunners' side. 
* He began the 96-97 season with Arsenal, but, on 27th January 1997 he was transfered to Crystal Palace for 150,000 pounds. He made his debut the following day in a 2-1 defeat away against Southend United. 
* On 4th March 1997 he scored his first goal for the Eagles against Bolton Wanderers.

* Tony Adams' abscence through injury allowed him to play from the start in the first few games of the season, while he also enjoyed a number of opportunities during the months of November and December. At the end of January Arsenal agreed to his transfer to Crystal Palace, where he showed that he remains a good footballer, helping the Eagles to win promotion to the Premier League.

422.name: Quinn
pages: * Robert Quinn sets out on the 97-98 season with the dream of making a name for himself in the Premier League. Last season he made his first appearances for the Republic of Ireland under-21 side, and game glimpses of the quality which suggests he could go on to be a fine footballer. Still very young, the experience of lining up against the best players in England could prove to be a great help for him in the new future.

* Quinn is a very disciplined central defender who shows good positional sense out on the park. A quick player, he stands out for his reading of the game and his ability to do an effective man to man marking job. Efficient in the air at the back, he very rarely moves forward to support the attack. He is occasionally played in midfield, where he is generally less effective.
x
* 2 under-21 international appearances for the Republic of Ireland.

* A product of Crystal Palace's youth system, Quinn signed as a professional in March 1995. His first team debut came on 5th May 1996, in a game against Norwich City in the final weak of the 95-96 season.

* Last season was a good one for Robert Quinn, who played in 24 games for the first team, 21 of those appearances coming in the league. He was also given the opportunity to make his debut for the Republic of Ireland under-21 side. He scored his first goal for Crystal Palace in a League Cup game against Bury.

423.name: Boxall
pages: * Danny Boxall is one of the latest prospect to emerge from the youth system at Crystal Palace. Young defender begins the 97-98 season hoping to get the opportunity to make his Premier League debut. If he maintains his progress, nobody is in any doubt that Steve Coppell will give him his chance. Danny will have to make sure that he is ready to take full advantage.

* Boxall is a very solid right back, safe when he has to cover behind the defence and is a player with good positional sense, who can also do a job in the midfield. He possesses good technique which allows him to past the ball accurately. Young, quick and disciplined, he has a tremendous future ahead of him.
x
x

* After coming through the youth ranks at Crystal Palace, he made his debut for the Eagles on 5th May 1996 against Norwich City, although the team were already automatically qualified for a place in the play off for promotion to the Premier League. 
* In the 96-97 season he suffered ruptured cruciate knee ligaments.

* Just when he was beginning to settle down in the first team Danny Boxall suffered ruptured cruciate knee ligaments, an injury which involved surgery and a long recovery period. Fortunately, he was able to reappear to get a few minutes of action in the final game of the season.

424.name: Tuttle
pages: * David Tuttle is back in the Premier League, where he played a few years ago, first of all for Tottenham and later with Sheffield United. During that time David matured as a footballer and is now a player who can guarantee consistently good form throughout the full season. During the 97-98 campaign he will get the opportunity to measure the progress he has made by lining up against the most dangerous strikers in England.

* Tuttle is a solid central defender who keep things as simple as possible when he finds himself in tight situations. Quick and a very tight marker, his main strength is his ability to dominate in the air in both penalty areas. However, he has more difficulties when the ball is played along the ground and when he comes up against more skillfull strikers. Occasionally  a very hard player, his aggressive approach has sometimes seen him run into problems with referees.
* F.A. Youth Cup winners medal 1990.
* An England youth international.

* After coming through the ranks at Tottenham Hotspur, he signed professional in February 1990. He played his first game for Spurs on 1st December 1990 against Chelsea.                            * He went out on loan to Peterborough United in January 1993, making his debut on 22nd January 1993 against Birmingham City. 
* Sheffield United signed him for 350,000 pounds in August 1993. He made his debut on 14th August 1993 against Swindon Town, and scored his first goal as a professional against Watford on 20th January 1996. 
* He moved on to Crystal Palace, together with Carl Veart, in the swap deal which took Gareth Taylor to Sheffield United in March 1996. He made his debut on 9th March 1996 against WBA, and scored his first goal seven days later against Grimsby Town.

* David Tuttle had an excellent season. He was an automatic choice in the side at Crystal Palace until an injury which he suffered in March, forced to miss a few games. He was one of the best players in the play off final at Wembley which gave him the opportunity to line up against, and beat, his previous club Sheffield United.

425.name: Edworthy
pages: * The 97-98 season offers Marc Edworthy the opportunity to make his debut in the Premier League. Yhe young Crystal Palace full back has made excellent progress over the last few years and is currently an automatic choice in the Eagles' defence. It remains to be seen how he performs against the best strikers in the country.

* Edworthy can play at right back, as a sweeper or even in midfield. A very attack minded player, he makes the most of his pace to get down the flank and put dangerous crosses over into the heart of the penalty area. An excellent passer of the ball, and with excellent vision, he is a player who is very comfortable with the ball at his feet. However, on the other hand, he lacks a certain amount of tactical awareness, and, as a result, is often found out of position.
x
x

* After coming through the youth ranks at Plymouth Argyle, he signed professional in March 1991. He made his league debut on 31st August 1991 against Millwall and scored his first goal for the club on 22nd October 1994 against Stockport County. 
* Transfered to Crystal Palace in May 1995 for 350,000 pounds, he made his debut for the Eagles on 12th August 1995, against Barnsley. 
* Unfortunately, it was Edworthy who commited the penalty which eventually meant that Leicester were promoted to the Premier League in 1996, with Crystal Palace being forced to remain in the First Division for another year.

* He was one of the best players at Crystal Palace during the course of last season. He missed just one game in the Eagles' race to the Premier League, and, although he didn't managed to find the back of the net in the league, he did score his first goal for Crystal Palace in the League Cup game against Bury.

426.name: Gordon
pages: * Dean Gordon was a teammate alongside Jamie Redknapp, Trevor Sinclair and Robbie Fowler in the England under-21 side. After two years in the First Division, Dean returned to the Premier League to once again put himself to the test against the best teams in England. If things go well for him he could even find himself lining up alongside his ex-under-21 colleagues in the full England side. It is, after all, free to dream.

* Dean Gordon is an attack minded left back, who continually gets forward into the attack, sending dangerous crosses over into the hard of the penalty area. A real battling footballer, he is occasionally too forceful for his own good, although he always goes in fairly. He has a good shot at goal from distance both in open play as well as from dead ball situations.
* Chosen in the First Division's Ideal Team for 95-96.

* 13 under-21 international appearances for England. 
* He made his debut in the Toulon International Tournament on 30th May 1994 against Russia.

* After coming throuth the youth ranks Crystal Palace, Gordon made his first team debut on 22nd December 1991 against Tottenham Hotspur. He scored his first goal for Palace on 24th August 1993 against Nottingham Forest.

* He was unable to begin the season with the rest of his teammates, due to an injury he picked up the previous season. Once he has recovered he once again made himself a regular member of the starting line up and played in the last 30 games of the season.

427.name: Curcic
pages:
* Signed for Crystal Palace in February 1998. 
* When Sasa Curcic signed for Aston Villa in August of 1996 the fans at Villa Park welcomed him like a star. The Yugoslavian international had shone at Bolton Wanderers, the club which had given him the chance to play in England but in his first season with the Birmingham club Sasa was disappointing. Not only did he fail to reach the expected level, but he even lost his status as starter.

* An attacking midfielder blessed with exceptional technique capable of playing in any position in the midfield, Curcic is a footballer with a lot of talent, allowing him to be inventive, constantly surprising his rival. He has an extraordinarily tight turn and with the ball under control he is very hard to stop; he can start up from the midfield and dribble past opponents to shoot powerfully at goal or make a weighted passed to a team mate.  A good passer, he usually looks for the one-two to get nearer to the area offering constant details of great class; back-heels, balls through opponents legs...Very young with a lot of physical resistance, he keeps up a high level of play for the full ninety minutes. His profile means he operates best as a link-man with the forwards. Freed of defensive tasks he is a constant source of danger. Still learning, he is destined to be one of the best footballers in Europe in the near future.
x
* 12 full international appearances for Yugoslavia.

* Originally from Partizan Belgrade where his excellent progression brought him to the Yugoslavian national team he arrives at Bolton Wanderers on the 28th of October 1995 for a transfer fee of £1,500,000.  His signing is the most expensive in the history of the "Trotters".
* He makes his debut with Bolton at Burnden Park two days later (30/10/95) with a win over Arsenal (1-0).
* He scored his first goal in England on the 22nd of November 1995 at Stamford Bridge in a game which Bolton lose against Chelsea by 3-2. Despite the result, Curcic manages a spectacular goal going past several defenders and sliding the ball underneath the Russian goalkeeper Dimitri Kharine. 
* Although in the last few months of the season Sasa Curcic repeated his desire to continue with Bolton Wanderers, even if the team where relegated to the First Division. Once the drop became a stark fact many of the Premier League clubs were interested in him. And so, on the 14th of August his move to Aston Villa was confirmed for £4,000,000, the most expensive in the history of the club.
* His transfer was the fruit of personal interest that Brian Little put into his signing. He admitted to have been after him for months and he met with Colin Todd the manager of Bolton Wanderers, to convince him of the importance of his move.
* He made his League debut with the "Villains" on the 24th of August 1996 against Derby County at Villa Park (2-0).

* Much was expected of Sasa Curcic at Villa. The player who had worked wonders at Bolton however did not appear at Villa Park in the whole of the season. He played 22 League games, 17 of these from the start, never reaching his top form.  So much so that for the first time in his career he couldn't manage to score a single goal in the whole of the season.

428.name: Warhurst
pages: * Paul Warhurst is setting out on a new stage of his professional career. The serious injuries he has suffered in recent years have, logically, affected his performance, although, at Crystal Palace he will be trying to reestablish his reputation, at a club who are returning to the Premier League with high hopes.

* A footballer with good technique, vision, skill and pace, Paul Warhurst is a versatile player whose progress has been hindered by injuries. He is at his best when he plays in the centre of the midfield just in front of the defence, where he can demonstrate his ability to distribute the ball and orchestrate the teams attack. Nevertheless, his ability also allows him to play at the heart of the defence and even at right back. A good footballer and the fine passer of the ball he has the imagination to play his way out of tight situations and show his class when he moves forward into the attack. All he needs now to get back to his best form is regular first team football.
* League Championship winners medal 1995.
* 8 under-21 international appearances for England.

* The son of ex-Sheffield United, Birmingham, Manchester City, Crewe and Oldham player of the 40's and 50's, Roy Warshurst, Paul Warhurst began his career in the youth ranks at Manchester City. After turning professional on 1st July 1988, he was unable to break through and make a first team appearance for the Maine Road club. Shortly after signing professional terms, on 27th October he was transfered to Oldham Athletic for 10,000 pounds. 
* After three years at Boundary Park he got the opportunity to play in a top flight of English football when he was signed by Sheffield Wednesday on 17th July 1991 in exchange for 750,000 pounds. At Hillsborough he played as a centre forward during the Premier League's inaugural season, replacing the injured David Hirst. His goals took the Owls to the F.A. Cup and League Cup finals although Wednesday lost in both games against Arsenal. Although called up into the full England squad, he didn't get the chance to make his debut. 
* At the end of the season he attracted the attention of Blackburn Rovers. Negotiations between the clubs broke down when Wednesday failed in their attempt to sign Brian Deane. Finally further talks resulted in Warhurst moving to Blackburn Rovers for 2,700,000 pounds on 17th August 1993. Paul made his debut on 12th September in a defeat against Liverpool at Anfield (1-0).
* Following his arrival at Ewood Park he went through an incredible run of bad luck. In his first season with Rovers he suffered a broken leg in a game against Swindon. After a long, hard fight back to full fitness he broke his other leg during a training session. Months later, during the 95-96 season, he suffered a series of illnesses and injuries, although he did manage to play in a number of games. However in his first league apperance of the season he suffered a broken rib. 
* On 24th July 1997 he was transfered to Crystal Palace for 1,500,000 pounds.

* Although he began the season as a member of the starting line up in three of the first four league games, he soon disappeared from the Blackburn Rovers side. He scored his only two goals on the season against Manchester United, one at Old Trafford and another at Ewood Park.

429.name: Lombardo
pages: * The signing of Attilio Lombardo represented an injection of quality to Crystal Palace's first team squad. The ex-Juventus player is one of the best footballers to have come out of Italy in recent years. A full international and with a fistful of honours to his name, Lombardo arrives in England hoping to become one of the leaders of the Eagles' side, and one of the idols of the Selhurst Park crowd.

* He is one of the best right sided midfield players in the league and a very quick player. A tremendously valuable member of the side, Lombardo is capable of dominating the whole of the left flank, where he goes past opponents with apparent ease and also does a tremendous job defensively. In full flight he is practically unstoppable, possessing great speed as well as fantastic ball control and strength. He also has a fierce right  foot shot. A real battler and a very unselfish player, one of his weaknesses is his heading ability. He makes much less of a contribution when he is move away from the right hand side of the park, an area where he is a truly spectacular player to watch.

* One Italian League Championship winners medal with Sampdoria (91).
* One Italian Cup winners medal with Sampdoria (94). 
* One European Cup Winners Cup winners medal with Sampdoria (90). 
* One Italian Super Cup winners medal with Sampdoria (91). 
* One European Cup winners medal with Juventus (96).

* 15 full international appearances for Italy. 
* He made his debut on 22nd December 1990, against Cyprus in a qualifying game for the 1992 European Championships. The game ended 0-4 with Lombardo scoring one of Italy's goals.

* He is known in Italy as Popeye. 
* He is a great joker and has a tremendous sense of humour. 
* He didn't have an easy start to his career. Despite being a good goalscorer for his school team, he was unable to find a club to take him on in the youth ranks. As a result he had to work as a waiter and as a mechanic before managing to sign for Pergocrema, in the Italian Serie C2. 
* While with Cremonese, coached by Emiliano Mondonico, he took advantage of an injury to regular right back Vigano to force his way into the side on a regular basis. 
* In 1989 he signed for Sampdoria. Paolo Mantovani, then president of the Genovese club, was the man mainly responsible for his move to Sampdoria. After seeing Lombardo in action for Cremonese, he was greatly impressed by what he had seen and, from that moment on did everything he possibly could, until he finally saw Lombardo wearing a Sampdoria shirt. 
* He made his Serie A debut on 27th August 1989, against Lazio, a game which ended in a 0-2 victory for Sampdoria. 
* Shortly after signing for Juventus, he suffered a fractured shin bone, as a result of a tackle from Borussia Dortmund left back, Reinhardt. That injury kept him out of action for a number of months. 
* In the summer of 1996 he was on the verge of signing for Sheffield Wednesday. 
* On 1st July 1997 he was transfered to Crystal Palace for 1,600,000 pounds.
* During the course of his career he has played in 3 European Cup Finals. In 1992 and 1997, he lost against Barcelona and Borussia Dortmund, Respectively. In 1996 he got his hands on the trophy when Juventus defeated Ajax.

* It didn't prove to be easy for Lombardo to force his way into the Juventus side during the course of last season. In the final of the Champions' League, although he didn't start the game, he did a good job when he was called into the action. He didn't have an injury free campaign, and, as a result, was unable to find his best form. Even so, he managed to add three more medals to his personal roll of honour: the Intercontinental Cup, the European Super Cup as well as the Italian Championship.

430.name: Brolin
pages: * After a very brief spell in Italy, Thomas Brolin returns to England with the hope of relaunching his career, which has been marked by injuries in the last few seasons.  Crystal Palace have given him the chance to regain his prestige in a competition as demanding as the Premier League.

* He is a very skilful and quick forward, with a great turn.  He is very effective in front of the rival goal.  In any case, his position has evolved during the course of time and he now plays more as a link-man between the midfield and the forwards, where he is, perhaps, more dangerous.  A right-footed player, he has exquisite technique which allows him to go past defenders, shoot accurately on goal and help out his team-mates.  This is another of his virtues, he will often drop back to the midfield to receive the ball with more space and take advantage of his capacity for helping out his team-mates.

* Italian Cup Champion in 92.
* Cup Winners' Cup Champion in 93.
* European Supercup Champion in 94.
* UEFA Cup Champion in 95.
* Third in the United States World Cup '94 with Sweden.

* 42 full international appearances for Sweden.
* He made his debut on the 25th of April 1990, in a game between Sweden and Wales (4-2).  In this game Brolin scored two goals, something that he repeated in the following game with his team (6-0 against Finland).
* He was present in the Italy '90 World Cup and in the United States '94 World Cups.
* In the United States World Cup, in which Sweden managed to come third, Brolin was one of the most outstanding players and was a member of the tournament's dream team.  He played every possible minute of the championship (660 over the course of seven games) and scored three goals, one against Russia from the penalty spot, another against Romania in the quarterfinals and the third one against Bulgaria in the consolation play-off.

* He grew up in the one of the coldest towns in Sweden and more or less had to learn his football on ice.  His goalscoring instinct was already evident when he was twelve, as he scored 15 goals in a game.  It is not surprising that he made his debut in the First Division when he was just seventeen years old.
* Although he was never outstanding as a schoolboy, he had a stroke of luck when Anders Gronhagen, the manager of IFK Sundsvall, took notice of him in 1987.  He combined his football with an accounting job.  His spectacular progress lead to his call-up for the Swedish under-21 side.
* He played three years in Sundsvall and in 1990 moved to IFK Norrkoping, one of Sweden's big teams where players such as Gunnar Nordahl, Harry Bild, Henry Kallgren, Ove Kindvall and Benny Wendt had played.  When Brolin arrived the team's marksman was Jan Hellstrom, a good forward who had the misfortune to injure himself shortly before the big game against Gothenburg.  The manager played Brolin, who scored three goals in his team's crushing 6-0 win.
* Once the Italian World Cup had finished he signed for Parma, who had just managed a historic promotion to the Italian Serie A.  He made his debut on the 9th of September 1990, in a game between Parma and Juventus (1-2).
* On the 16th of November 1994, during the course of a game between Sweden and Hungary, he ruptured the ligaments of his left ankle, an injury which kept him out for several months.
* In November 1995 he was transferred to Leeds for £4,500,000, the most expensive signing in the history of the club.  On the 25th of this same month he made his debut in St James' Park against Newcastle.  He came on in the 81st minute as a substitute for Mark Ford.  Leeds lost 1-2.
* At the beginning of the 97-98 season he was on the verge of signing for Sampdoria, but the doctors at the Genovan club advised against the operation because they weren't sure that he could recover completely from his physical problems.
* Fond of his racing, he owns a couple of thoroughbreds called Hyper and Peach Valley.
* He loves to play golf, a very quiet sport which fits well with his character.  He also likes a spot of pool and tennis.
* At the age of 16 he had to choose between football and ice-hockey, his other great passion.
* In the 96-97 season Leeds loaned him twice, once to the Swiss team Zurich Grasshoppers and the second time to the Italian Parma.
* In January 1998 he signed for Crystal Palace.

* He had difficulties adapting to the rhythm of English football, very different from Italian football.  Little by little he started to find his way into the team, though he never seemed produce the football that he was capable of.  He played 19 games, 17 as a member of the starting line-up, scored four goals, a low number for a player of his category, but this is understandable in a way, as he wasn't really fully recovered from his injury.  He also had problems adapting to the Premier League.

431.name: Jansen
pages: * Signed for Crystal Palace in February 1998.
* A fast forward and with an excellent future, Jansen is able to change the course of a game with his presence on the pitch.
* AMC Champion in 1997.
* Youth international for England.
x
* Last season he took part in 19 games, four of those from the start scoring one goal. Jansen displayed his quality showing a glipse of a brilliant future.

432.name: Bent
pages: x
* Bent lines up either as a right winger or a centre forward and stands out for his speed and ball control, qualities which, due to his youth, still need to be polished up a little.
x
x
x

* Last time out he played in 34 games with 29 of those appearances as a member of the starting line up. He managed to find the back of the net on 3 occasions. He wasn't hindered by his lack of experience and despite his youth he became one of the teams most outstanding performers.

433.name: Padovano
pages: * In England Michelle Padovano is setting out on a new stage in his  career. At 31 years of age, and with plenty of honours against his name, the Italian striker is following in the footsteps of some of his most illustrious compatriots, attempting to give a good account of himself in the Premier League. At Crystal Palace he will have the help of a couple of players who he knows well: Attilio Lombardo and Ivano Bonetti. He will be hoping that luck is on his side.

* He is a goalscoring centre forward, in the classic mould. Very strong and brave, he is a tremendous header of the ball, and possesses more technique and ability than many supporters think. He moves intelligently along the front line and is continuously opening up gaps for his colleagues, doing a tremendously useful job.

* European Cup winners medal 96. 
* Intercontinental Cup winners medal 97. 
* European Super Cup winners medal 97. 
* Italian League Championship winners medal 97.
x

* Ironically, Padovano was always a supporter of Torino, the local rivals of the Vecchia Signora, Juventus. As a boy he dreamt of emulating Pulici a hero of his when he played for "Toro". 
* He began his career in the youth ranks at Barcanova, where he had Borghetto as coach. He later moved on to Ravenna and, in 1983, he joined the apprentice at Varese, where he spent a year before signing for Asti Torretta Santa Caterina. 
* In 1990 he almost signed for Fiorentina as a replacement for the Argentinian Oscar Dertycia, who was having a very poor spell.
* At Reggio Emilia he was a very popular player with the club's supporters who even appealed to Italian national team boss Arrigo Sacchi to include him in the full Italian side. However, Michele didn't just have admirers among the Reggiana supporters, but also among the managers in Italy at the time, such as the Romanian Mircea Lucescu, who once said that the ideal striker partnership for Italy at full international level would be Padovano playing alongside Casiraghi. 
* A graduate in Geometry, Michele Padovano made his name as a goalscorer with a hat-trick he scored in a game between Pisa and Cesena, in Serie A. Although he had previously managed to score four times in a game between Asti and Entella, the importance of scoring three timesin the top flight saw his name in the headlines following that game in the 90-91 season.
* He made his Serie A debut on 9th September 1990, in a game between Bolonia and Pisa (0-1). 
* On 12th November 1997 he was transfered to Crystal Palace for 1,700,000 pounds.

* A good season for Padovano who, although he wasn't an automatic choice in the side, managed to add another three titles to his roll of honour: The Intercontinental Cup,the European Super Cup and the Italian League Championship.

434.name: Rodger
pages: * Of all the players at Crystal Palace, Simon Rodger is the one who has spent most time with the London club. In recent years, injuries have often prevented him from finding his best form, althouhg last season he was one of the main man in Steve Coppell's side during the final decisive run in to the end of the season. As a result he can look forward with optimism to the 97-98 season.

* Simon Rodger is a left footed midfield player who generally plays down the left hand side of the park. He is a hardworking player in his part of the pitch due to his tremendous reserves of stamina. He puts 100% into every game, and never gives anything up as lost. A good passer of the ball, he likes to keep his distribution simple and uncomplicated.
* First Division winners medal with Crystal Palace in 93-94.
x

* Crystal Palace signed him from amateur club Bognor Regis in July 1990 for 1,000 pounds. He made his league debut on 5th October 1991 against Sheffield Wednesday and scored his first league goal on 2nd February 1993, clinching a victory for Palace against Blackburn Rovers. 
* During the 95-96 season he suffered a back injury, which kept him out of action for a long spell. 
* During the 96-97 season he had two different loan spells: with Manchester City in October 1996 and Stoke City  in February 1997. Back at Crystal Palace, he playd in the play-off final for promotion to the Premier League, at Wembley against Sheffield United.

* He began last season injured, but managed to end it at Wembley, celebrating Palace's promotion to the Premier League. In between he went out on loan twice, first of all to Manchester City and later to Stoke. Once back at Selhurst Park he enjoyed the full confidence of Steve Coppell, who played him in all three play-off games.

435.name: Pitcher
pages: * If he manages to make a full recovery from the serious injury he suffered last season, Darren Pitcher could become one of the most important playersat Crystal Palace in the club's return to the Premier League. With Pitcher in good form, Steve Coppell will have in his ranks an effective, experienced player.

* Pitcher is an attack minded midfield player. A tenacious battler, he keeps opponents under constant pressure and wins plenty of possession. His qualities allow him to adapt perfectly to the right back position,  although he seldom makes an attacking contribution. He limits himself, though very effectively, to winning the ball an laying it off to his nearest teammate.
x
* An England youth international.

* After coming through the youth ranks at Charlton Athletic, he signed professional in January 1988. He made his debut on 25th August 1990 against Swindon Town and scored his first league goal on 29th September 1990 against Barnsley. 
* He was transfered to Crystal Palace in July 1994 for 700,000 pounds, although his debut couldn't have been worse, when, in the first game of the 94-95 season the Eagles were beaten at home by Liverpool by six goals to one.
* During the 96-97 season he sufferd the serious injury, rupturing his cruciate knee ligaments.

* Pitcher was hit by a stroke of bad luck with the 96-97 season having only just got underway. An injury to his cruciate knee ligaments wich he picked up in a game at Huddersfield put an end to his season in the first team. On regaining his fitness he only had time to reappear for the reserves.

436.name: Shipperley
pages: * Neil Shipperley is back in the Premier League. He left Southampton October %% 1996, but in the space of just a few short months at Selhurst Park he demonstrated that he is a player for the top flight of the game. In his new spell in the Premier League, Crystal Palace will need players like Neil to be on top of their game if the club's aim of remaining in the top flight is not to become an almost impossible task.

* A strong, powerful centre forward, he stands out for his heading ability. One of his greatest assets is his ability to hold the ball up while he waits for the midfielders to come through in support of the attack. A very hardworking player, he keeps the opposing defence under constant pressure. He creates plenty of danger as a result of his outstanding mobility and is always attempting to pull defenders out of position. Still very young, he has plenty of time to improve.
x
* 7 under-21 international appearances for England.

* He is the son of David Shipperley, who played for several teams during the 1970's. 
* He came through the ranks at Chelsea, signing professional for the London club in September 1992. He played his first game on 10th April 1993 against Southampton and scored his first goal as a professional two days later against Wimbledon. 
* He went out on loan to Watford in December 1994. He made his debut on 10th December 1994 against Grimsby Town, while his first goal for the club came on 26th December 1994 against Portsmouth. 
* He was transfered to Southampton in January 1995 for 1,250,000 pounds, making him the most expensive player in the club's history. He made his debut for the Saints on 14th Janaury 1995 against Leeds United and scored his first goal in a Southampton shirt on 15th March 1995 in a game against West Ham. 
* Crystal Palace signed him in exchange for 1,000,000 pounds on 24th October 1996. He played his first game for the Eagles on 26th October 1996 against Grimsby Town, and, three days later against Bradford City, scored his first two goals for Palace.

* He began the season with Southampton, where he played in 12 games, although he found the back of the net just once. In October he was transfered to Crystal Palace where he didn't take long to demonstrate his ability in front of goal. He ended the campaign having scored twelve goals for the Selhurst Park club. His presence in the side was a great help in finally winning promotion to the Premier League.

437.name: McKenzie
pages: * Leon McKenzie is a very promising footballer. He is a player who is making good progress and is obtaining the experience he needs in order to be able to make his Premier League debut. Despite his youth, nobody  doubts that he will more than likely get the chance to see how he measures up against the best teams in the country during the 97-98 season.

* McKenzie is a strong, mobile centre forward who puts everything he has got into every game he plays. A clever player, he is always looking to lose his marker and get on the blind side of defenders. He has good vision and is decisive in everything he does. He likes to get in first time shots  on goal, with either foot, and, although he is not very tall, he is good with his head.
x
x

* He is the son of Clinton McKenzie, an ex-British boxing champion, and is %%  the nephew of Duke McKenzie who was a world champion at three different weights. 
* He came through the youth ranks at Crystal Palace, to make his debut for the first team of 3rd October 1995 against Southend United. 
* He scored his first league goal on 15th March 1997, in a game against Norwich City at Selhurst Park (2-0).

* Despite his youth, during the course of last season Leon McKenzie revealed himself to be an excellent striker. Although he was generally used as a substitute, Leon won the full backing of the Crystal Palace coaches and showed a number of touches which suggested that he has a fine future ahead of him.

438.name: Dyer
pages: * Last season Bruce Dyer began to justify the fee that Palace paid out to bring him to Selhurst Park. When the young striker arrived at the club from Watford he was considered to be a real prospect for the future. Last season he was the side's top scorer and now, during the 97-98 season, he will be out to try to beat the top goalkeepers in the country as often as he can.

* Bruce Dyer is a vey quick striker who has to pull out wide to the flanks, from where he sets up new attacks making the most of his pace. He holds the ball up well when he receives it with his back to goal. He is also capable of turning quickly and getting in a shot on goal with either foot. A typical goalscoring centre forward, he keeps his cool extremely well in front of goal.
* First Division winners medal 93-94 with Crystal Palace.
* 9 under-21 international appearances for England. He made his debut on 30th May 1994 against Russia, later being replaced by Robbie Fowler.

* After coming through the youth ranks at Watford, he signed as a  professional in April 1993. He made his league debut on 17th April 1993 against Birmingham City and scored his first goal against Middlesbrough on 10th October 1993. 
* He was transfered to Crystal Palace in March 1994 for 1.25 millions pounds. He made his first appearance for the club on 12th March 1994 against WBA Scoring his first goal in a Palace shirt against Manchester City. 
* He was Crystal Palace's top scorer in the 96-97 season, with 17 goals.

* Bruce Dyer ended last season as top scorer at Crystal Palace, with 17 goals including 2 penalties. His excellent performances allowed him to make  more appearances for the England under-21 side as well as representing the First Division in the annual game against a representative side from the Italian Serie B.

439.name: Nash
pages: * Carlo Nash arrived at Crystal Palace almost unnoticed, with the dream of making a name for himself in the First Division, although he found himself in the shadow of Chris Day. Slowly but surely, he won the confidence of both coaches and supporters, up to the point of being first choice in goal at Wembley in the play-off final. Undaunted by the setting and the atmosphere, he managed to keep a clean sheet. Now, as a result, he will be spending the 97-98 season in the Premier League.

* Despite his youth and lack of top level experience, Carlo Nash is a safe, reliable goalkeeper. Dominant in the air, he is decisive when he comes offhis line, making the most of his excellent judgement. Nash is capable of apparently remaining composed in even the tightest of situations, spreading tremendous confidence to his defensive colleagues.
x
x

* Signed from modest club Clitheroe, he arrived at Crystal Palace on 16th July 1996 in exchange for 35,000 pounds. 
* He made his First Division debut on 21st September 1996, in a 6-1 victory against Reading at Selhurst Park. 
* He was first choice in goal for Crystal Palace in the final of the play-offs for promotion to the Premier League at Wembley in May 1997. The Eagles defeated Sheffield United 1-0, winning promotion to the top flight of English football.

* He made his Crystal Palace debut in September against Reading, in a game which ended in a resounding 6-1 victory for the London club. During the course of the season he managed to dislodge Chris Day from the number one spot in goal, and, in fact, played in the last 18 games of the season,  culminating with the side clinching promotion to the Premier League after beating Sheffield United at Wembley.

440.name: Miller
pages: * After an exceptional season with Watford, Kevin Miller now has the opportunity to make his debut in the Premier League. The Crystal Palace goalkeeper will be trying to settle down in a demanding competition, where even the slightest of errors is usually punished. However, Kevin has a tremendous will to win which could prove to be a great help in allowing him to get over the occasional difficult moment.

* Kevin Miller is a goalkeeper who dominates his penalty area, giving tremendous confidence to his defensive colleagues. Energetic, authoritative, and with plenty of character, even on the worst of days he retains his intense will to win. Excellent in the air, his main weakness is evident when he has the ball at his feet.
* Fourth Division winners medal 1990.
x

* After coming through the ranks at modest Newquay, he signed for Exeter City on 9th March 1989. 
* In 1990 he was part of the Exeter side that won promotion to the Third Division. 
* He was transfered to Birmingham City on 14th May 1993 for 250,000 pounds, but, in August 1994 he was sold to Watford for an identical sum of money.
* In 1996 he suffered the disappointment of Watford's relegation to the Second Division. 
* He was chosen as the best goalkeeper in the Second Division for the 96-97 season. Shortly afterwards he was transfered to Crystal Palace, recently promoted to the Premier League, for 1,500,000 pounds.

* Kevin Miller's season for Watford could easily be described as outstanding, going on to be named as the Second Division's top goalkeeper. He was a member of the starting line up in 42 league games, and was chosen as the club's Player of the Year by the Vicarage Road supporters. His performances attracted the attention of a number of Premier League clubs.

441.name: Tinkler
pages: * After a brief stay in the Italian Serie A, Eric Tinkler arrived in England with the intention of finding a place for himself amongst the stars of the Premier League. His signing by Barnsley is a result of the favourable impression that his play had on Danny Wilson, who saw him play with the South African national side in May of 1997 in a game against England at Old Trafford. Every thing seems to point to him being included in the starting eleven, at least in the first stages of the championship.

* A defensive midfield player, he usually plays in front of the line of defenders. He is strong and has a lot of physical resistance, and tries to compensate for his technical limitations with commitment and constant battling. He pressurises the rival footballers untiringly and is outstanding for his ball-winning capacity. He hardly takes part in attacking moves, although he has a very powerful shot on goal with his right. At times, he can play as a central defender.
* African Champion with South Africa in 1996.

* Full international for South Africa. 
* He made his debut on the 8th of June 1994. 
* He played in the African Cup in 1996, which took place in his country. He played the full ninety minutes of the six games disputed by his country including the final against Tunisia.

* Tinlker started playing his football with Wits University in Johannesburg.
* He soon left South Africa to try out his luck in Portuguese football. His team, Vitoria de Setúbal, won the Second Division Championship in 1993.
* Once his contract finished with the Portuguese club, he signed for three years with the Italian team Cagliari. 
* He was included in the 1996 African Cup Dream Team in 1996. 
* In June of 1997 he is transferred to Barnsley for £650,000 pounds having already been on trial in England in 1989 with Coventry City. 
* Tinkler has Portuguese nationality, so he does not occupy a foreign player's place in the Premier League.

* Last season Eric Tinkler was playing in Cagliari, a team in the Italian Serie A. He did not have much luck and did not manage to produce the expected level of play, which paved the way for his move to Barnsley at the end of the season.

442.name: Bosancic
pages: * Jovo Bosancic goes into his first season in the Premier League with the hope of regaining a place in the starting line-up at Barnsley, something that he was loosing little by little as the championship progressed last season. In principle, everything seems to point towards Danny Wilson using him as a substitute, so the Croatian footballer should try and take advantage of the first opportunity that comes along.

* A midfielder with good technique and playing vision, he usually plays hugging the right-hand touchline. A good passer, he does not shirk away from a bit of hard work when the team is defending. He burns an extraordinary number of calories every game and never gives up.
x
* Under 21 international for Yugoslavia.

* Bobby Robson, the former England manager, advised Danny Wilson to buy Jovo Bosancic. Robson was greatly impressed by the performance of the Yugoslavian footballer in the Portuguese league. 
* He is a Barnsley player since the 2nd of August 1996. He made his league debut on the 17th of this same month with an away win over West Bromwich Albion (1-2).

* In his first season in England, Bosanic turned in a high level of play at Barnsley; especially in the first third of the championship. However, as the season went on his name began to disappear from the teamsheet. Jovo showed an unbreakable winning character and fighting spirit, not often seen.His only goal came from the penalty spot against Manchester City.

443.name: Marcelle
pages: * Clinton Marcelle was one of the most interesting novelties of the 96-97 league. He adapted immediately to English football, which allowed him to earn himself a place in the line-ups of Danny Wilson and collaborate decisively in the promotion to the Premier League. Clinton showed that he was one of the quickest footballers in the First Division. He now has the chance to measure the progress in his game against some of the best defences in England.

* Speed is the characteristic that stands out most in Clinton Marcelle. Playing in the middle of the pitch, he joins in the attack constantly looking for the shot, taking advantage of his power and physical capacity. He has a good shot on goal and scores goals regularly.  Furthermore, he is a footballer who helps out in defence as well, facilitating the work of winning back the ball for his team mates.
x
* 6 full international caps for Trinidad and Tobago.

* Arriving from the Portuguese team Felgueiras, Barnsley signed him for two seasons in the summer of 1996. 
* His signing was recommended to Danny Wilson by the former England manager Bobby Robson. Marcelle turned down offers from various Portuguese clubs.
* He made his debut with the "Tykes" on the 17th of August of 1996, in an away game against West Bromwich Albion. Barnsley won that game 1-2 and Marcelle scored the first goal.

* In his first season in England Marcelle made a favourable impression. Danny Wilson included him in the squad in 40 league games, 26 from the start. He scored 8 goals, not a bad figure for a midfield player. Marcelle was also the player who opened Barnsley's account in the league championship.

444.name: Redfearn
pages: * Nobody has ever given any thing to Neil Redfearn, the Barnsley captain, for free. Since he arrived at the Oakwell Ground in 1991, this brave player has become one of the idols of the fans. The trainer Danny Wilson has also showed that he has full confidence in him. Now 32 years old, Neil has seen one of his most cherished dreams come true: to play in the Premier League.

* A midfielder with attacking tendencies, he joins in the attacking moves dangerously. He has a very powerful left-foot shot, and he does not hesitate to unleash it if given the slightest opportunity. Blessed with a an almost unnatural physical resistance, he is able to keep up a frenetic playing rhythm for the full ninety minutes. Thanks to his leadership capabilities and the ease with which he scores goals, Neil Redfearn is a very important footballer for any team. He is also a true penalty specialist.
* Second Division Champion with Oldham Athletic in the 90-91 season.
x

* Redfearn received his training in the lower ranks of Nottingham Forest.
* In June of 1982 he signed for Bolton Wanderers, but did not make his debut in the league until 19th February 1983, in a game against Rotherham United.
* In March of 1984 he is transferred to Lincoln City for £8,250 and makes his league debut on the 31st of this same month against Exeter City. His first goal for the club does not arrive until the 14th of April against Wimbledon. 
* Signed for Doncaster Rovers in August of 1986 and made his league debut on 23rd August 1986 against Mansfield Town and his first goal arrives seven days later against Brentford. This same season Redfearn ends up as the top goalscorer of the team. 
* Crystal Palace sign him in July of 1987. He makes his debut in league competition on 15th August 1987 against Huddersfield Town and scores his first goal against Huddersfield town on the 5/9/87. 
* He is transferred to Watford in November of 1988. He plays his first game with the club on the 26th November 1988 against Hull City and his first goal comes against Portsmouth. 
* January of 1990 sees his departure to Oldham Athletic. He makes his debut on the 13th of this same month, against Swindon Town. His first goal, against Bournemouth, does not arrive until the 20th of March. 
* He has been a Barnsley player since the 5th of September 1991. The Tykes pay £150,000 to bring him to the club. He made his league debut two days later in a game against Derby County. On the 17th of September Leicester City conceded the first goal that Neil Redfearn scored wearing the Barnsley shirt, a goal scored from the penalty spot. 
* He is currently the Barnsley captain.

* For Neil Redfearn the 96-97 league was the best one of his life. Not only was he the team's top scorer with 17, six of these from the penalty spot, but he also established himself as the leader of the team. His drive and vitality made him one of the players most appreciated by the fans at the Oakwell Ground. It is a shame that he missed a few penalty kicks. If he had scored these he would have surpassed the 20-goal barrier for the season.

445.name: Sheridan
pages: * The youngest of the Sheridan brothers has become an important piece in Barnsley's scheme of things. Although he can not boast of the same class as his brother John, Darren is a good example of a hard-working player, who sacrifices himself a lot and who toils away.  For this reason he has triumphed at the Oakwell Ground, and for this reason also, he deserves to play in the Premier League.

* Sheridan is a multi-faceted player who can play both as wing back or as left half. Very left footed, he stands out for the precision of his passes and playing vision: although he will not take on much risk when it comes to distributing the ball. Blessed with a good technical foundation, he does not run away from body contact nor shirk on ball-recuperation work. He has a good shot on goal in set-plays, although he hardly scores any goals.
x
x

* He is the brother of John Sheridan, the Irish international who has worn the shirts of Leeds, Nottingham, Sheffield Wednesday and Bolton.
* He arrived at Barnsley in August of 1993 from the modest team Winsford United; the asking price, £10,000. 
* He made his league debut on 4th April 1994, against Notts County, and scored his first goal against Stoke City.

* For the third consecutive year Darren Sheridan was one of the regulars in the Barnsley line-ups. The Irish midfield player played in 41 league games, and was a starter in 39 of these. He only scored 2 goals, but the first of those, against Reading at the Oakwell Ground, was quite simply spectacular.

446.name: Markstedt
pages: x
x
x
x
x
x

447.name: Barnard
pages: * Darren Barnard was the fifth signing by Danny Wilson going into the 97-98 season. In fact, his incorporation at Barnsley occurred a little before the start of the championship. With Barnard, the Tykes have made a notable reinforcement to their left flank and the player returns to the elite after a not-too-successful stay at Chelsea years ago.

* His natural position is at left back, although he can also play in the midfield. Barnard is a skilful player, blessed with good technique, and with a capacity to go past rival defenders and cross accurately. He is also a specialist at taking penalties and direct free-kicks, where he takes good advantage of the power and placement of his shot with the left.
x
* Schoolboy international with England.

* He started his career at Wokingham Town, but in July of 1990 he was signed by Chelsea for £50,000. He was 18 at the time. 
* His debut with the Stamford Bridge occured during the 91-92 season.
* In November of 1994 he was loaned to Reading. 
* On the 6th of October 1995 Barnard was transferred to Bristol City for £175,000. He made his debut one day later, in an away game against Swindon Town. One week later he opened his account at Ashton Gate against Hull City.
* BArnard has been a Barnsley player since the 6th of August 1997. He cost £750,000. Curiously, some days before signing for the Tykes, he had renewed his contract with Bristol City for three more years.

* The 96-97 season was the best one in the career of Darren Barnard. He settled into the starting line-up of Bristol City, played in 44 league games and finished the season as the second top scorer of the team finding the net 11 times, with seven from the penalty spot. For these reasons he was voted "Player of the Year" by the fans at Ashton Gate.

448.name: Krizan
pages: * Born in Slovenia, Ales Krizan is one of the new players for Barnsley in the 97-98 season. He is a left sided defender who will be competing with Neil Thompson and Scott Jones for a regular place in Barnley's line up.

* He normally plays as left wing back, although he is also able to perform in the centre of the defence.  Strong, hard and solid, he hardly participates in the teams attacking game.  Notwithstanding, in defensives tasks he is a very safe player and very hard to beat.
* Slovakia Cup Champion in 94.
* Full international for Slovakia.
* He is a Barnsley player since July of 1997.  He arrived from the Slovakian team Maribor Branik, the club where he had developed his entire sporting career.
* One season more, Ales Krisan had an undisputed place in the line-ups of Maribor Branik.

449.name: Thompson
pages: * Two years after leaving the Premier League, Neil Thompson returns to the top flight of English football, but this time defending different colours: those of Barnsley.  And no-one doubts that his experience will be an inestimable contribution to a team in need of guides in its first stroll alongside the big clubs.

* Thompson is a class left back, but he can also operate in the midfield. He is hard when it comes to fighting for the ball and does not fold when faced by the opposition. He has a very powerful shot on goal, a shot whose speed has been clocked at 135 km/h. He takes corners effectively, looking for his team mates on the near post. From a throw-in he can reach the six-yard box.  Experienced - with a winning attitude - he is a true penalty specialist.
* Second Division Champion in 91-92 with Ipswich Town.
x

* Originally from the lower ranks of Nottingham Forest, he moved to Hull City in November of 1981 when his contract with the Nottingham team expired. He maked his league debut on 13th February 1982 against Tranmere Rovers.
* In August of 1983 he signs for the amateur club Scarborough. Three years later, his team earns promotion to the next division, thus becoming a professional team. During this time, he even leaves football for a while, working as a salesman. 
* He is transferred to Ipswich Town for £100,000 in June of 1988 with his  league debut on 19th August 1989 against Barnsley. His first goal in the league, from the penalty spot, gives his team the win over Watford on  31/10/89.
* Once his contract with Ipswich Town had run its course, he signed for Barnsley on 14th June 1996. He makes his debut on the 17th of August of the same year in a game where his team overcome West Bromwich Albion away (1-2).

* Although he had various injuries during the course of the season, it has to be said that Neil contributed a lot of experience and quality for the 24 games that he played. In all of these he was in the starting line-up. What's more, he scored 5 goals, including two against Ipswich Town at the Oakwell Ground. He was also made the team's penalty taker, taking over from Neil Redfearn.
