450.name: Appleby
pages: * Once he has recovered from the injury which prevented him from finishing last season, Matt Appleby will have to fight to earn himself a place in the plans of Danny Wilson again. The trainer at Barnsley has already placed his faith in him to take the team to the Premier League, so in principle, Matt will have the chance to show his progress as a player amongst the elite of English football.

* Appleby fulfilled the function of sweeper in the Barnsley side although he can also perform as a midfield player. He is a player who reads the game very well, knows what rhythm to impose on the game and almost always makes the right choice. He has good technique, which allows him to play the ball out of defence. He is efficient in defensive tasks, and his passing ability is one of his biggest virtues.
x
x

* Matthew Appleby is the older brother of Richie Appleby, a Swansea City player. 
* Originally from the lower ranks of Newcastle United, Appleby signed as a professional in May of 1990. He plays his first game with the Magpies on 27th October 1990 against W.B.A. 
* Loaned to Darlington in November of 1993, he made his debut for them on 27th November 1993 against Bury, even managing to score a goal for his team.
* His is freed of contractual obligations with the club at St. James Park and so moved on to Darlington in June of 1994. He made his debut for them on 13th August 1994 against Preston North End. He scored a goal against this same team in his second spell with the club on 17th September 1994.
* He is voted player of the season 95-96 by the fans at Darlington.
* He is transferred to Barnsley on 19th of July 1996 and makes his debut on the 17th of August of this same year with an away win over West Bromwich Albion (1-2).

* Undisputed starter for a large part of the season, a serious injury to his ankle ligaments kept him away from the playing fields for the last three months of the championship.  Until then he had played 35 games in the league, and in all of these he was in the starting eleven.

451.name: Jones
pages: * A product of the youth squad at Barnsley, for Scott Jones it is a great honour to have the chance to play in the Premier League. However, despite evidence of his progress and the confidence that Danny Wilson has placed in him, everything seems to indicate that in the 97-98 season he will have to get used to experiencing the game from the substitutes' bench and wait for the trainer to give him the chance to measure up against the best forwards in England.

* Scott Jones corresponds to the profile of a classical left back. He is a hard marker and efficient when it comes to winning the ball back. He hardly takes part in the attacking play of the team, although he has an undoubted skill for passing the ball with good sense and accuracy. Physically strong, he needs some time to polish up his game.
x
x
* Trained in the youth squad at Barnsley, Scott Jones signed as a professional in February of 1994. His debut with the team took place on 9th March 1996 against Ipswich Town.

* Although he did not figure on the teamsheet until the middle part of October, Scott Jones had chances during last season to demonstrate his progress. Danny Wilson aligned him on the left flank 24 times, although in only 16 of these did he form part of the starting eleven. In any case, Scott gave clear signals that his career is only just beginning.

452.name: Eaden
pages: * The position of right back at Barnsley has had a name on it for the last four years - that of Nicky Eaden. The player from Sheffield is a faithful definition of reliability in the world of football. His performance is always constant making him into an essential part of Danny Wilson's scheme of things. It will have to be seen if Nicky is capable of keeping this up in a competition as hard as the Premier League.

* Nicky Eaden occupies the position of right back with a dependability which should be underlined.  He is quick and disciplined, hard to get by and dangerous in attack.  He pushes up his wing easily and crosses accurately to the area.  In recent times, he has also given signs of the enormous power of his shot from long range.
x
x

* Originally from the lower ranks of Barnsley, Eaden signed as a professional in June of 1991.  He makes his league debut on 1st May 1993 against Brentford and scores his first goal for the team against Southend United on 5th February 1994.

* For the second season running, Nicky Eaden was in the starting line-up of the 46 games played in the league championship. He also figured in the goal-scoring statistics of Barnsley, contributing 3, not a bad number for a right back. His goals against Wolves were particularly important and also against Norwich, allowing his team to come away with decisive points in the promotion bid.

453.name: De Zeeuw
pages: * Arjan De Zeeuw was considered as one of the best defenders in the First Division.  The Dutchman is fully adapted to playing football in England. Having been successful at Barnsley he now has his chance to shine in the Premier League. A complete challenge for a footballer with a lot of quality and one of the axiis about which the schemes produced by the trainer, Danny Wilson, rotate.

* De Zeeuw is a very tall central defender, left-footed, strong, powerful and very difficult to get by. A specialist in the aerial game, he joins in the attack at corners and free-kicks to take advantage of his heading ability. A good passer, he can bring the ball out of defence in a controlled fashion and, despite his bulk, move quickly. A good footballer without a shadow of a doubt.
x
x

* Barnsley sign him from the Dutch team Telstar on 3rd of November 1995. The price for the transfer was set at £250,000. 
* He made his league debut on 4th November 1995 against Wolverhampton Wanderers and scored his first goal for the side against Ipswich Town on 22nd December 1995.

* Last season Arjan De Zeeuw played in 43 league games, all of which he was on from the start. The Dutch defender showed that he was one of the best in his position in the whole of the division, offering security and efficiency in the defensive line of Barnsley. He scored two goals in consecutive games, both, of course, coming from a header.

454.name: Moses
pages: * Last season the fans at the Oakwell Ground were pleased to note the evolution in the game of Adie Moses. He went from being a substitute to the national under-21 team in the period of months and showed himself to be a player who will have to be watched from now on. Now that he has acquired confidence in his abilities his progress will have to be carefully observed. If this is kept up at the same rate as in the previous season, nobody would be surprised to see him settle into competition at the level of the Premier League.

* A young central defender, he stands out for his safety in the aerial game and the solidity with which he carries out his defensive duties. Physically strong and with quick movements, he has made a lot of progress in the technical aspect of the game, making him a more complete player. As he has gained experience he has shown himself to be a footballer with a promising future.
x
* 1 under-21 international appearance for England.

* Originally from the lower categories of Barnsley, he signed as a professional in July of 1993, making his debut in the league on 14th January 1995 against Luton Town, scoring his first goal for the club against Wolverhampton Wanderers on 8th April 1996.

* At the beginning of last season Adie Moses was not important for Danny Wilson's plans.  However, the injury to Steve Davis gave him the chance to figure in the team line-ups. And Moses did not waste the chance - the defender from Doncaster showed an extraordinarily high level of play, up to the point where he received his call-up for the England under-21 team. A great finishing touch to a season which invites plenty of optimism.

455.name: Fjortoft
pages: * Jan-Aage Fjortoft is a typical club player, battling and enthusiastic. His combative spirit is always well appreciated in the stands, who applaud his impossible runs, and every one of his efforts to get a shot in. His effort has led him to a very active participation this season with Sheffield United, the club where he made an immediate impact and where he enjoys the trust of the coach, Nigel Spackman. Whether he plays from the start or comes on as a substitute, the crowd at Bramall Lane will support his actions with the same enthusiasm as before.

* A born finisher in the box, although Fjortoft doesn't have the bulk of a battering-ram-type forward, his playing style reminds us of the classic centre forwards. He has a good header, is able to anticipate the rival defences in the danger area. Technically he is discrete, though he shields the ball effectively with his body while he waits for team-mates to join him. A true battler, he never gives up a ball or a game as lost. He oozes enthusiasms in every move and tries to infect the rest of the team. For these reasons his performances surpass his technical limitations on many occasions.
* Top scorer in the Norwegian League in 1988.

* 69 international appearances for Norway.
* Present in the 94 United States World Cup, he was a starter in the first two games played by his team against Mexico (1-0) and Italy (0-1).
* After the 94 World Cup he is made captain by the national selector, Olsen.

* In 1987 Fjortoft scored 10 goals at Hamerkameratene, a modest club in his native town.  His brilliant progress brought him to Lillestrom, one of the most important teams in Norway. In 1988 he becomes the top scorer in the First Division with a tally of 14.
* Halfway through the 89-90 league Lillestrom are on the way to a League title, however, Fjortoft turns his back on this and moves to Rapid Vienna. The Norwegian forward scored a goal in his first appearance in the Austrian championship and finished the season as the team's top scorer with a tally of 17.
* On the 29th of July 1993 he is transferred to Swindon Town for £500,000. He makes his debut on the 14th of August with a defeat at the hands of Sheffield United (3-1).
* After five months at Swindon without scoring a single goal, the forward is on the verge of returning to Norway. However, he has an impressive run of goals starting in a Cup game against Ipswich Town. He ends the season as the team's top scorer with 12 goals, although this doesn't prevent their relegation.
* He starts the 94-95 season at Swindon, with whom he is proclaimed the top scorer in the First Division (including all competitions), in front of John Aldridge and David Kelly. Three of these goals are against Middlesborough, the club where he moves to on the 31st of March 1995 for £1,300,000. 
* He makes his debut on the 1st of April with an away win against West Bromwich Albion (1-3). Sixteen days later he scores his first goal against Sheffield United while defending Middlesborough's colours. Shortly afterwards, "Boro" are promoted to the Premier League.
* Fjortoft has been the Norwegian captain since 1994.
* At the beginning of the 96-97 season he received offers from an Indonesian club, but Fjortoft decided to continue in English football. After all, since his youth he has always expressed his desire to play in England.
* He is transferred to Sheffield United during the 96-97 season for £700,000. His first game with the Blades is on the 1st of February against Swindon Town and he scores his first goal for the club against Bolton Wanderers two weeks later.

* With the arrival of Ravanelli and company, Fjortoft saw how his opportunities at Middlesborough became very few and far between, playing only five games. In view of this he decided accept the offer from Sheffield United and move the Blades. After a discrete debut, Fjortoft scored 8 goals in 8 games, including a hat-trick against Grimsby Town and was a key player when the club reached the play-offs for promotion to the Premier League, where the club were defeated by Crystal Palace with a goal almost in injury time.

456.name: Ten Heuvel
pages: * Laurens Ten Heuvel is a promising forward who has hardly had any chances to play with the first team. The Dutch footballer has always been around, waiting for the slightest continuity which he still has not achieved. In any case, the arrival of Georgi Hristov does not exactly seem to favour the aspirations of Ten Heuvel, as the Macedonian is another goalscorer to add to the competition. If things do not change much, it would not be surprising if Laurens were to end up trying out his luck away from the Oakwell Ground.

* Laurens Ten Heuvel is a young forward, opportunistic and with a great goalscoring efficiency. Technically good, he likes to take part in the elaboration of the team's attacking moves, dropping back to midfield to look for support from his team mates. The ease with which he finishes makes him a constant danger for the rival defences.
x
x

* Heuvel arrived at Barnsley on 12th March 1996 from the Dutch team Den Bosch. The price of his transfer was set at £75,000. 
* He made his debut with the first team on 27th April 1996. Barnsley beat Luton Town 2-0 at the Oakwell Ground.

* Ten Heuvel only had the chance to play a few minutes with the first team during the whole of last season. In fact, he only intervened in three games, and in all of these he came on as a substitute. However, with the reserve team where he was top goalscorer, he produced some great performances.

457.name: Hristov
pages: * In Macedonia, Georgi Hristov is considered as the successor to Darko Pancev, the mythical forward who played for, amongst others, Inter Milan. In the Balkan country they are convinced that Hristov will be the best ambassador they could possibly have in England.  For this, it will be enough if the young footballer, who left a great impression on Danny Wilson months ago, maintains the goalscoring average that he has shown in his short, but intense, professional career.

* Georgi Hristov is a classical centre forward.  He is blessed with a well developed goalscoring instinct, and shows a great finishing capacity, both with his head and with both feet. He has a strong winning character and does not get nervous in any situation. On the playing field he behaves as would a mature footballer, despite his youth. His presence in the attacking axis of the team makes him a constant reference for his team mates. He is quick and strong, but above all, Hristov is a goalscorer.
* Champion of the Yugoslavian League in 96 and 97.

* 12 full international caps for Macedonia. 
* He made his debut in May of 1995, in an away game against Armenia (2-2). Hristov scored a goal.

* A Partizan player and in the Macedonia national side, his class did not go by unnoticed by the trainer of Barnsley, Danny Wilson, who was impressed in a game played against the Republic of Ireland in April of 1997 on British territory. Macedonia won 2-3 and Hristov scored the winning goal.
* In June of 1997 he is transferred to Barnsley for £1,500,000 pounds, thus becoming the most expensive signing in the history of the club.

* For the second year running, Georgi Hristov and Partizan won the Yugoslavian championship. The Macedonian forward contributed with goals to the conquest of the title.  Similarly, Hristov also demonstrated his ability to find the back of the net with the national selection, where he kept an undisputed place.

458.name: Ward
pages: * Taking full advantage of his roving character, Ashley Ward was transferred to Barnsley shortly after the start of the 97-98 season. In eight years as a professional, Ashley has worn eight different shirts. So much instability might indicate that the forward, a native of Manchester, never quite settles down at any club. But if we look at the quality of his performances, we will come to the conclusion that he is a very useful footballer. Ward could mark an epoch at the Oakwell Ground... provided that they don't transfer him first.

* A heavily-built forward with goalscoring instinct, he has a wide variety of technical resources available which makes him an unpredictable player. Able to control the ball in difficult situations, Ashley Ward shows that he also has the skill to shield it. Intelligent and opportunistic, although not so quick, he knows how to slip his marker and find a bit of space in the rival box to get in a shot. He moves around the whole of the attacking area, is dominant in the air, skilful with both feet and finds the back of the net easily.
x
x

* A native of Manchester, Ashley Ward was raised in the youth squad at Maine Road. On the 5th of August 1988, at the age of 17, he turned professional with Manchester City, although he only got to play one game with the first team. 
* On the 10th of January 1991 he was loaned to Wrexham as a preliminary step to his transfer to Leicester City on the 30th of July of this same year. His price: £80,000. 
* On the 21st of November 1992 he is loaned once again, this time to Blackpool. On the 1st of December he signed for Crewe Alexandra, for the same price as before. 
* In his second season at Crewe he scores 13 goals in 25 games. In the third, after recovering from breaking both his legs and from a back injury he manages to score 10 goals in his last 6 games with the shirt of the "Railwaymen". So, Norwich decide to acquire his services on the 8th of December of 1994 for £500,000. 
* He scores 2 goals against Chelsea at Carrow Road in his debut match for Norwich (10th of December 1994). 
* He starts the 95-96 season at Norwich but, surprisingly, is transferred to Derby County on the 19th of March 1996 for £1 million. Despite this, Ward finishes the season as Norwich City's top marksman. 
* He makes his debut for Derby on the 23rd of March and, strangely enough, the team lose 1-0 to Norwich City at Carrow Road.  He would have to wait till the end of the season to score his first goal for the "Rams", although it didn't prevent Derby from loosing away to West Bromwich Albion. Fortunately, shortly afterwards the team lead by Jim Smith made it to the Premier League.
* On the 4th of September 1997, with the season already underway, he is transferred to Barnsley for £1,300,000; the second highest amount paid by the club for a player.

* A hernia operation prevented Ashley Ward from playing in the first two games of last season.  Once he had recovered, he was a regular feature of of the forward line of Derby County together with Dean Sturridge, who he formed an interesting strike partnership with.  He played 30 league games, 25 of them from the start. He scored 8 goals, six of them in eight consecutive games in the months of March and April.

459.name: Hendrie
pages: * At the beginning of the 96-97 season John Hendrie was playing for Middlesborough, a team which at the team aspired to everything in the Premier League. At first sight his departure for Barnsley seemed to mark a downturn in his career. However, months later, the Scottish forward was celebrating the Tykes' promotion to the Premier League and receiving the accolade of the fans at the Oakwell Ground. At the same time Middlesborough were lamenting their relegation. You can bet that John could not hold back an ironic smile.

* John Hendrie is a very intelligent forward, who knows how to get the best from his abilities and find the defects of the rival defences, getting behind the backs efficiently to create his own opportunities. A good finisher, he is very level-headed and sure of himself in front of goal. Despite his veteran status, he still has a fair turn of speed in the final few metres. He has a very powerful header and takes advantage of his experience to anticipate his rivals and finish off the move.

* Third Division Champion with Bradford City in the 84-85 season.
* Second Division Champion with Leeds United in the 89-90 season.
* First Division Champion with Middlesborough in the 94-95 season.
* 3 times youth international for Scotland.

* Originally from the lower ranks of Coventry City, Hendrie signed as a professional in May 1981. He makes his league debut for the club on 5th December 1981 against Tottenham Hotspur and scores his first goal as a professional against Stoke City. 
* He is loaned to Hereford United in January of 1984, playing his first game on 21st January 1984 against Peterborough United. 
* He completes his contract and departs for Bradford City in July of 1984. He makes his debut on 25th August 1984 against Cambridge United and manages his first goal on 23rd October 1984 against Preston North End. 
* He is transferred to Newcastle United in 1988. His first game for the Magpies is on 27th August 1988 against Everton and his first goal is against Liverpool on 1st October 1988. 
* Leeds United sign him in exchange for £600,000 in June of 1989. He plays his first game with the team at Elland Road on 19th August 1989 against Newcastle United, his former team, and manages to score his first goal against Brighton & Hove Albion. 
* In July of 1990, Hendrie ends up signing for Middlesborough for £550,000. He makes his debut with the team against West Ham United and he scores his first goal against Leicester City. 
* He has been a Barnsley player since the 11th of October 1996, his transfer set at £250,000.  He made his debut the following day at home against Crystal Palace (0-0). On the 29th of this same month he scored his first goal for the Tykes, in an away game against Port Vale (1-3).

* In his first season at Barnsley John Hendrie was voted "Player of the Year" by the fans at the Oakwell Ground. He arrived in October from Middlesborough and quickly found himself a place in the starting eleven. He played 36 games and scored 15 goals, the second highest figure for the club, only surpassed by Redfearn.

460.name: Liddell
pages: * The arrival at the Oakwell Ground of Paul Wilkinson and John Hendrie forced Andy Liddell from the starting line-ups. However, the Scottish forward does not give in and continues to work intensely to regain his place. Whenever the trainer Danny Wilson required his services, Andy responded faithfully. For this reason, despite the signing of goalscorers of of the mark of the Macedonian Hristov, Liddell will continue to fight with the hope of making his debut in the Premier League and showing his worth.

* Intelligence and skill are the two most outstanding qualities of Andy Liddell.  Despite is small stature, the Scottish forward battles untiringly against the rival defences. Andy has a great scent for goal, although often he is forced to carry out the dirty work to provide chances for his team mates. He shoots with both feet and in all of his actions he shows himself to be a fast and decisive footballer.
* Top goalscorer at Barnsley in the 94-95 season.
* 11 under-21 international caps for Scotland. He made his debut on the 16/11/93 against Malta.
* From the lower ranks of Barnsley, Liddell signs as a professional in July 1991. He made his league debut against Portsmouth and scores his first goal for the club against Notts County.

* Although he started the season in the starting line-up, the arrival of John Hendrie forced him onto the substitutes' bench.  Notwithstanding, his goals at the beginning of the season gave Barnsley the impulse needed to allow them to dream of promotion to the Premier League. He played a total 38 games, 25 of them from the start, and scored 8 goals.

461.name: M. Bullock
pages: * Martin Bullock is a young footballer. The trainers reckon that he has a splendid future ahead of him. However, last season his progress suffered a setback, as he hardly figured in the Barnsley starting line-up. In any case, Martin has shown that he has a great capacity for adapting to the needs of the team and he could make his comeback to the line-ups at any time. Time is on his side.

* Bullock plays on the wing and takes good advantage of his speed to get by the opposing defenders. Right-footed, he likes to hug the touchline and run at defenders using his good turn and dribbling. He can also play as a link-man, just behind the forwards. In any position he is a generous footballer, a good passer and with an acceptable shot from outside the area.
x
x
* Barnsley sign him from the amateur club Eastwood Town in September 1993 for £15,000 pounds. He makes his league debut against Reading and scores his first goal against Leicester City.

* Last season Martin Bullock played in 28 league games. However, only in 9 of these was he a starter, a disappointing figure for a footballer making a lot of progress. Even so, he was included in the under-21 First Division team which took on a team from the Italian Serie B. A nice touch in a season that was somewhat frustrating for him. His only goal in the whole of the season was against Oldham Athletic in a Cup game.

462.name: Leese
pages: * Arriving from the Bundesliga, Lars Leese arrives in the Premier League with the hope of making it in English football. In principle, although he has hardly played in recent seasons, everything seems to suggest that the German goalkeeper will play occupy the Barnsley goal to the detriment of David Watson. But he can not be sure, as his team mate showed last season that he has the ambition of playing in the top division. In any case, the arrival of Leese will be an important reinforcement for the trainer Danny Wilson.

* A very big goalkeeper, he stands out for the safe way he comes to meet crosses. He is authoritative, energetic and dominant in his area and knows how to order about his defensive line. However, he needs to improves his game with the feet and his effectiveness in a one-on-one situation.
x
x
* Originally from the German team Bayer Leverkusen, he arrives at Barnsley in June of 1997 in exchange for £250,000 pounds.
* Without any chance of entering in the first team, Lars Leese spent last season on the substitutes' bench.

463.name: Watson
pages: * The arrival of the German Lars Leese puts David Watson's place in the team in danger.  However, the English goalkeeper has shown signs of his extraordinary progression last season and possible has earned an opportunity to play in goal for his team in the Premier League. A worthy reward for a man who made a decisive contribution to the Barnsley's arrival in the elite for the first time in their history.

* A young goalkeeper, but, even so, experienced, his progress has been evident. Agile and sure of himself between the posts, he his made a notably improvement in his aerial game, his weak point in previous campaigns. Also, he is surer of himself when the ball is at his feet, allowing him to pass to team mates with greater calm and precision. In this way Watson has been rewarded for his hard work in the training sessions.
x

* 5 under-21 international caps for England. 
* Youth international.

* Trained in the lower ranks of Barnsley, he signs as a professional in July 1992. On the 10th of February 1993 he makes his debut with the first team in a game against Derby County. 
* Undisputed first choice since the 94-95 season, Watson was the goalkeeper of the team that achieved promotion to the Premier League at the end of the 96-97 season.

* The good season that David Watson had was vital in Barnsley's successful promotion bid.  Watson played in the 46 league games and managed to keep a clean sheet in 18 of these.  His playing level saw a noticeable improvement, thus allowing him to earn the confidence of the manager Danny Wilson.

464.name: Beasant
pages:
* Signed for Nottingham Forest in the 97-98 season. 
* An England international twice and voted Southampton's best player in the 95-96 season, Beasant is faced with the challenge of showing that he is still a valid goalie in the First Division.

* One of the most veteran footballers in the Premier League, Dave Beasant has managed to take advantage of this experience to become a great keeper. A player with a lot of physical presence, he is dominant in the air and places himself well on the line, but he is not comfortable coming out to strikers' feet.  His veteran status has given him the resources to remedy difficult situations, although he still hasn't adapted to using his feet, a requirement for modern keepers.  Some critics say he is an eccentric keeper and irregular.  It is true he usually offers his best performances in the final stages of the season, and he is used to having it all to play for in the last game of the season, whether it is for promotion or relegation at stake.

* FA Cup Champion 88-89. 
* Second Division Champion 88-89. 
* Fourth Division Champion 82-83.

* 2 full international appearances for England.  He made his debut on the 15th of November 1989 in a friendly against Italy played at Wembley (0-0). He came on for Peter Shilton.  His second game was on the 13th of December of this same year on the same stage.  England beat Yugoslavia 2-1 and Beasant came on for Shilton once again. 
* 6 B-international appearances.

* His first team was the modest Edgware Town, from where he moved to Wimbledon for £1000.  He made his league debut on the 12th of January 1979 in a game against Blackpool. 
* In his 9 seasons at Wimbledon he lives through the continual rise in category from the Fourth to the First Division. 
* On the 13th of June 1988 he is transferred to Newcastle for £800,000, although he didn't play a full season for the club at St James Park. 
* He arrives at Chelsea on the 14th of January 1989 for £725,000 and, at the end of the season, he celebrates the club's promotion to the First Division.  This same year he makes his debut with the England team in a game against Italy played at Wembley (0-0). 
* He starts the 92-93 season at Chelsea, but during its course he is loaned to Grimsby Town first (24/10/92), and then to Wolverhampton Wanderers (12/1/93). 
* On the 4th of November 1993 he is transferred to Southampton for £300,000. One month later he makes his league debut for the Saints in a game in which Southampton loose against Everton (1-0) at Goodison Park. 
* Until the end of the 94-95 season his goals-conceded average was 1.333 per game and he had managed to keep 131 clean sheets. 
* In eight seasons of his extensive career he managed to play in all the league games, a record he shares with John Lukic and Peter Shilton.

* Despite starting the season on a high after having been voted the player of the year 95-96, Beasant saw how first Neil Moss and then Woods, took over in goal.  He started as the first choice keeper, but the arrival of Taylor forced him onto the bench.  He played in 14 games, a low figure for a keeper such as Beasant.

465.name: Pascolo
pages: * Marco Pascolo is one of  Nottingham Forest's reinforcements for the current season, in which Dave Bassett's side will be out to get back into the Premier League. His magnificent performances in the European Championships in England and the quality he showed as first choice in goal for Switzerland were enough to convince Dave Bassett to take him to  the City Ground. A slightly inconsistent keeper, Pascolo is as capable of hitting real heights  as he is of making schoolboy errors. However he seems likely to become Dave Bassett's regular keeper ahead of  Steve Crossley.

* He is basically a very safe keeper who is dominant in the air and has good international experience, although he can, at times, be inconsistent,as he demonstrated while playing in the Swiss league with Servette. He combines incredible saves with some equally incredible lapses in concentration and mistakes. This uncertainty can be passed on to his defensive colleagues who can never be quite sure whether Pascolo is there to be relied upon or not. Despite his height, he has no problem when he is required to use his feet, something which he frequently finds himself doing when he is playing for the Swiss national side. Among his weaknessess is his eagerness to come off his line, something which can become, at times, a real handicap for his side.

* One Swiss League title with Servette (94).
* He was chosen as second best goalkeeper in Switzerland for 1996, behind Philip Walker of Lugano.

* He has made 40 full international appearances for Swirzerland
* He made his debut on 23rd January 1992 in a friendly game in Dubai, between the United Arab Emirates and Switzerland  (0-2).
* He wasa a member of Switzerland's squad for the 1994 World Cup Finals in the United States where he played the full game in all four of his country's matches, against the host nation, Romania, Colombia and Spain.
* He also took part in the 1996 European Championships in England where he played in all three of Switzerland's games, against England, Holland and Scotland.

* He began his career at Sion, from where he moved on to Neuchatel Xamax, coached at the time by Roy Hodgson, who later gave him his full international debut for Switzerland. 
* He is married with two daughters, Megan and Melanie.
* Throughout his career he has had to put up with a great deal of criticism from journalists and and supporters, having a go at him for his inconsistency. 
* This lack of consistency saw him lose his place in the side on more than one occasion while he was with both Sion and Neuchatel. His place in the side at Sion went to Stephan Lehmann, while at Neuchatal he was replaced by Joel Corminboeuf. Ironically both boalkeepers are now theoretically Pascolo's replacement at in theSwiss national side. 
* He is of Italian origin. 
* Before the 1996 European Championships in England he was known as "Flopolo" due to his mistakes, but his good performances in the tournament saw his nickname change to "Topolo". 
* When he is on holiday, he generally visits the vineyards that his brother-in-law has in the Swiss region Valais.
* He was only the second foreign goalkeeper to play in the Italian serie A. Before him the only foreign keeper in the entire history of the Italian championship had been the Brazilian Claudio Taffarel.
* Nottingham Forest signed him after paying Cagliari 750,000 pounds during the summer of 1997.
* Pascolo spent last season with Italian club Cagliari in Serie A.

466.name: Crossley
pages: * A product of the youth team set up at the City Ground, Mark Crossley is now seeing how the repurcussions of his mistakes are overshadowing his ability. However nobody had been able to dislodge him from the side. Although logically last season was a sad one due to the team's  relegation to the First Division, personally it was a particularly sweet one for Crossley when his good work over the years was finally recognised when he was selected for Wales, despite having previously declared himself available for Scotland. A fairly consistent keeper, he will be out to help as much as possible in the task of getting Forest back into the Premier League, despite having Marco Pascolo ahead of him in the fight for a place in the first team.

* Although on many occasions what has most stood out in Mark Crossley's game  has been his mistakes and his inconsistent form, the truth is that his performances have shown good progress in recent years. A reflex goalkeeper, he is very comfortable when he is on his line where he shows good handling when he is making saves from long shots. He is a specialist in one on one situations, where he is exceptionally good at making opposition strikers hesitate. The Forest keeper's weak spot is when he comes out for high balls, an aspect of the game in which, despite his obvious progress, he needs to keep working on.
x
* 3 under-21 international appearances for England.

* Known as "Norman" among the supporters, due to his physical similarity to the  ex-Manchester United player Norman Whiteside, Mark Crossley is a product of the  Nottingham Forest youth system. He has been a professional since 2nd July 1987.  He didn't make his league debut on 26th October 1988 in a 2-1 victory against Liverpool at  the City Ground. That day Mark replaced the injured Steve Sutton. 
* Although three days later he put together another good performance in a game against  Newcastle (1-0), he had to wait until the 90-91 season to make himself a first team  regular.
* Throughout his career he has been involved in some strange goals. One which is  especially remembered is the one he conceded after throwing the ball towards his own goal. 
* During the 89-90 season he was loaned out to Manchester United, although he didn't get to make a league appearance for the Old Trafford club.
* An indisputed first team choice at Forest since the 90-91 campaign, his performances  improved noticeably during the 93-94 season, following the arrival at the club of the Northern  Ireland international Tommy Wright.
* Although he has made three under-21 international apperances for England in 1996 he  commented on the possibility of playing for Scotland at full international level, eligible due to  the fact that he has a Scottish grandmother. However up to now he hasn't been called up  by Scotish manager Craig Brown. 
* In 1996 rumours about a possible move to Leeds grew more intense, but in May he put an end to  speculation by signing a new four year contract with Forest.

* Once again Mark Crossley was Nottingham Forest's first choice goalkeeper, making 33  appearances for the club. Although he was unable to prevent Forest from being relegated  to the First Division, he personally had an excellent season, even getting the opportunity  to make his full international debut for Wales, despite having previously stated that he  would have liked to have played for Scotland..

468.name: Hjelde
pages: * Jon Olav Hjelde is very much a personal signing for this season on the part of  Nottingham Forest manager, Dave Bassett. His fine performances for Norwegian club  Rosenborg reached a peak last season when they knocked Italian giants Milan out of the  Champions League. Hjelde had been the target of a number of Italian clubs, but finally  it was Forest who won the day, and signed a player who could really be one to keep  an eye on and prove to be vital in the fight to get back in the Premier League.

* Hjelde is a Norwegian defender who shows great versatility at the back, able to play either  at the heart of the defence or at full back, almost always down the right hand side. His  height allows him to dominate in the air, while he is a dangerous player in the opposition's  area at  free kicks and corners. He is a quick player and also shows some good  touches of skill.
x
x
* Nottingham Forest signed him in the summer of 1997 after paying out 600,000 pounds  to his previous club, Norwegian outfit Rosenborg.
x

469.name: Rogers
pages:
* A product of the excellent and almost never ending Trannmere Rovers youth  system Alan Rogers is the lates jewel to emerge from the modest Merseyside club,  Rodgers is a 20 year old left back who seems to have a tremendous future ahead of  him. His most outstanding quality is the great maturity he has shown for such a  young player, which allowed him to make himself a regular at Tranmere. His ability  and his confidence in himself has allowed him to come a long way in a short time, and  if he maintains his progress he could well have a future in the left back slot in the England  side.
* After coming through at a modest club like Tranmere Rovers, he went on to become a  major signing for Nottingham Forest during the pre-season. With his signing Forest have tied  up one of the best young footballers in the English game, and one of those who seems to  have the brightest of futures ahead of them. Rogers was an automatic first team choice at  Tranmere Rovers and, despite having moved to a much bigger club, he will no doubt be a  regular for Nottingham Forest, if he can steer clear of injury.

* Alan Rogers is a very competent left back who, for his age, shows tremendous maturity.  He is an attack minded player, continually going on the overlap in support of the attack, getting  in good crosses from the byline. He is comfortable with the ball at his feet, and is good passer  of the ball over both short and long distance. Very much a left footed player, he basically uses  his right for standing on, while he likes to keep things simple at the back, hitting the ball long  when he has to. A hard player when he goes in for the ball, he is also very quick which allows him  to immediately get himself involved in counter attacks. His combination of pace and toughness  makes him a very difficult player to beat.
x
x

* After coming through the ranks at Tranmere Rovers, he signed as a professional in July  1995. He made his league debut on 25th November 1995 against Grimsby Town , while  his first goal as a professional came on 2nd April 1996 against Millwall. 
* Nottingham Forest signed him in the summer of 1997, after splashing out 2 million pounds.

* Despite being sent off in the first game of the season against Southend United, Alan Rogers' form  for Tranmere Rovers was always excellent. He became a key member of John Aldridge's side,  managing to maintain his tremendous progress. He played in a total of 31 games.

470.name: Chettle
pages: * Steve Chettle is one of the few local born players to have played in Forest's first  team in the last decade. It has become almost impossible to think of Forest taking   the field without Steve Chettle's name in the side. He has been a regular  under the  various different managers that have passed through the City Ground. It was Brian  Clough who gave him his first opportunity, which, clearly, he took with both hands. He  was an automatic choice last season for Frank Clark,  and remains so this time out under  Dave Bassett. He will be hoping that he proves to be a key member of the side that, at the  end of the season,  will hopefully find itself back in the Premier League.

* He normally plays at the heart of the defence, although he can also do a job as a right  back. Solid and consistent, he has good positional sense and is also an excellent tight  marker . he is dominant in the air at the back, but, although he moves forward for corners  and free kicks, he rarely finds the back of the net. Not a particularly quick player, he tries  to make up for his lack of pace by using the know how he has picked up over the years.Even so, he does sometimes have problems against quick, explosive forwards.
* League Cup winners medal 1990.
* 12 under-21 appearances for England.

* Born in Nottingham, Steve Chettle is a product of Forest's youth system.On 28th 1986 he signed professional terms, but he was forced to wait until 5th  September 1987 to make his debut, in a 4-3 defeat against Chelsea.
* A regular member of the side from the 1987-88 season onwards, he has made more  than 400 official appearances for the club.
* In 1990 he formed part of the Forest side that won the League Cup final, although  one year later, he saw the F.A. Cup  snatched away from Forest in the final against  Tottenham Hotspur. 
* For a long time he formed a defensive partnership with Des Walker. However the  signing of Carl Tiler relegated him to the bech, and it was only Walker's departure  to Italian club Sampdoria that allowed him to get back into the side. 
* In 1993, following the arrival of Colin Cooper at the City Ground, he went on to form  an outstanding partership with  Cooper at the heart of the Forest defence. 
* During the 95-96 season he scored against Bayern Munich, in Germany, in the first leg of  a U.E.F.A. cup tie. In the return leg the German side won 1-5.

* Chettle enjoyed another consistent season with Nottingham Forest, forming a good  partnership with Colin Cooper at the centre of the defence. Unfortunately his outstanding  performances couldn't prevent the club from being relegated to the First Division.  Chettle played in a total of 32 games.

471.name: Cooper
pages: * Colin Cooper is a player who as time has gone by, has proven himself to be a  tremendously important player for Nottingham Forest, forming a solid central defensive  partnership with Steve Chettle. He has been the subject of rumours surrounding  his  possible departure, but, the most important thing for him remains staying in the side as one  of  Dave Bassett's regulars. He had the misfortune to be hit by a slight injury during the  pre-season, which proved to be enough to allow the recently arrived Hjelde to take his  place in the Forest side. A player who has a lot going for him, Cooper will get his chance  to stake a claim for a starting place in Dave Bassett's side, as the season draws on.

* Blessed with great leadership qualities and a tremendous will to win, Colin Cooper  pushes the team on from his central defensive poisition. Dominant in the air, a tight  marker and a hard tackler, he is a tremendously difficult obstacle for opposing forwards  to get past. He possesses a well developed positional sense, although he won't shy away   from using physical contact to make sure that he wins possession for his side. Although   he is not a skillful player with the ball at his feet, his moves forward into the attack for  set pieces cause plenty of danger. In fact he has scored a fair number of goals, the majority   of those coming with his head.
x

* 2 full international appearances for England. He made his debut on 8th June 1995  against Switzerland.
* 8 under-21 international appearances.

* After coming through the youth ranks, he signed professional terms with Middlesbrough  on 17th July 1984, although he didn't get to make his debut until 8th March 1986. That day  Middlesbrough took on Crystal Palace in a Second Division game. 
* In 1988 he won promotion to the First Division with Boro, although one year later the club  went straight back down.
* On 25th July 1995 he was transfered to Millwall for 300,000 pounds. He quickly made a  first team place his own. 
* His move to Nottingham Forest came on 21st June 1993. The fee : 1,700,000 pounds .  He made his debut on 15th August in an away game at Southend United (1-1). On 19th December  he scored the first of the seven goals he went on to score that season. Strangely, that day Forest  were playing Southend United in the second of that season's two league clashes between the  clubs, though on this ocassion the game took place at the City Ground.
* At the end of his first year at Forest the club returned to the Premier League. Colin was included  in the First Division's ideal team. 
* During the 94-95 season Cooper put together a tremendous campaign in defence with teammate Steve Chettle.  At the end of the season Terry Venables gave him his full England debut. 
* Though a temperamental player, in the abscence of  Stuart Pearce, he is Forest's captain.

* Colin Cooper was one of  Nottingham Forest's most consistent players in a season which saw  the club relegated to the First Division. Although he began the season at full back, he ended  up back at the heart of the defence, a position where he feels much more comfortable. In total  he played in 36 games, managing to score twice.

472.name: Lyttle
pages: * In 1992, when he was sharing his time between his job as a bricklayer, and his passion  for football as a player with Worcester City, it would have been difficult for Des Lyttle  to imagine that  he would soon be playing for one of the most prestigious clubs in  in English football, Nottingham Forest. Although he has never been a star, the full back  has demonstrated on plenty of occasiones that he has the ability to play in the top flight  in England, as he did for a number of years before the club was eventually relegated  to the First Division. He was one of the first signings of former manager Frank Clark,  and has gone on to become one of Forest's bargain buys. He is an undisputed first team  choice for Dave Bassett, although his position in the side can also be filled by the  Norwegian Hjelde.

* A mobile, hard running full back, Des Lyttle does a tremendoous amount of defensive  work during the ninety minutes. His pace and his excellent physical attributes allow him  to cleanly win the ball off opponents. A very fair player, he seldom resorts to commiting  fouls to stop opposing forwards. Efficient and untiring in his defensive duties, he is less  effective when he moves forward in support of the attack. Although his runs down the  flank help out the midfield, he shows technical weaknesses in his control and passing  as well as when he has a shot at goal.
x
x

* Released by Leicester City, where he learnt his trade, for a while Des combined his job  as a bricklayer with the games he played in the ranks of  Worcester City. 
* On 9th July 1992 he was transfered to Swansea City for 12,500 pounds, and, shortly  after, on 15th August, he made his league debut, against Burnley. 
* He needed just one good season at Swansea City to attract the attention of Nottingham  Forest. On 27th July 1993, he signed for the Reds in exchange for 375,000 pounds, becoming  one of Frank Clark's first signings.
* He made his debut for Forest on 15th August 1993 in the visit to Southend United, while  he scored his first goal for Forest on 1st January 1994 against Charlton Athletic at the City  Ground. At the end of that season the club returned to the Premier League.

* Lyttle compelted a good season for Nottingham Forest, playing in 32 games, scoring  once, the third of his career, against Sunderland. He gave a good account of himself operating  either as a traditional full back or as a wing back in a five man defence, a system which  Forest used quite frequently. In short, he was one of Forest most consistent players.

473.name: Thomas
pages: * Five years ago the name of Geoff Thomas was being put forward as a possible  signing for one of the big clubs in English football, with a 2 million pound price  tag oon his head. At that time he was even a full England international and was enjoying his best years as a professional footballer.   * In 1993 he was surprisingly  transfered to Wolverhampton Wanderers and, since that time, his contribution has  been minimal, due to the numerous injuries that he suffered during his time with The  Molineux club. Despite these continuous setbacks, last season Thomas once again  gave glimpses of his quality, which finally convinced Dave Bassett to sign him for  the current season. He could well prove to be an important acquisition, due to the  vast experience he possesses. Which may turn out to be a deciding factor in the fight  to win promotion to the Premier League.

* A left footed player, he is a strong, dynamic performer, and is a  hard player when he goes  in for the ball, something which has at times caused him some problems with referees.  A good ball winner in the middle of the park, he makes good strong runs forward, although  he is technically limited. Nevertheless he is a dangerous player when he gets on the end of things  in the box, getting in efforts on goal, either with his left foot or his head. He is a dangerous  player in the air when he moves forward for dead ball situations where his height and decisiveness  allow him to get up and get in some dangerous headers.
* Zenith Data Systems Cup winners medal with Crystal Palace in the 90-91 season.

* Thomas has played for England as a "B" international and as a full international  on 9 occasions. His full international debut came in a qualifying game for the 1992  European Championships in Sweden on 1st May 1991 in Izmir against Turkey. The  game ended in a 1-0 win for England, the goal coming from Dennis Wise who was  also making his debut. His final international appearance came on 19th February 1991,  against France at Wembley, in a game in which Alan Shearer made his England debut.  Thomas missed a great scoring opportunity when French keeper Frances Rousset came  well off his line. Thomas tried to lob the advancing goalkeeper, only to see his lobbed effort come  to a halt near the coner flag.

* He completed his contract with amateur club Littleborough, and moved on to Rochdale in August 1982. He made his league debut on 30th October 1982 against Hereford United,  while he struck his first goal as a professional in a league game against Crewe Alexandra  on 14th January 1984, a goal which clinched victory for Rochdale.                 * He became a free  agent and signed for Crewe Alexandra in March 1984. He played his first game for the club  on 31st March 1984 against Aldershot and managed to open his account for them on 28th   April against Tranmere Rovers.
* He was transfered to Crystal Palace in June 1987 for 50,000 pounds. He made his debut   on 15th August 1987 against Huddersfield Town whle he struck his first goal for the Eagles  on 1st September 1987 against Middlesbrough.
* Wolverhampton Wanderers signed him in June 1993 for 800,000 pounds. He made his debut  on 14th August 1993 against Bristol City. His first goal for Wolves came 8 days later against  Birmingham City.
* Thomas completed his contract during the summer and moved on to Nottingham Forest. 
* In the Zenith Data Systems Cup final, Thomas scored the first goal of the game, in extra-time,   for Crystal Palace against Everton.

* The former England international wasn't a key man in the Wolverhampton Wanderers  side  until the month of November when Wolves were going through something of a crisis. During  that period Thomas stood out and managed to pull the club out of their freefall to the foot of  the table. Unfortunately, from January onwards, he lost his place and was only able to get back in   as a result of Emblem's injury. Despite playing in just 22 games, with 3 goals to his credit,  he once again gave glimpses of the player who made such an impact a few years earlier.

474.name: Johnson
pages: * A new product of the Norwich City youth system, he has  tremendous natural,  physical qualities to make him a footballer, and is not lacking in ability and technique  either. His contribution at Norwich City proved to be an important one over recent   years and eventually attracted the interest of Nottingham Forest. This interest finally  resulted in Johnson becoming one of Forest's biggest signings in recent seasons, when  he moved to the club during the summer. Normally a first team regular for Dave Bassett,  he will have a key job to do if Forest are to get back into the Prmier League.

* Johnson is a player who possesses incredible physical strength. He is a good ballwinner and  is a very uncomfortable oppenent in the middle of the park where he keeps his rivals  under constant pressure. He is good passer of the ball, although he is not a midfield playmaker.  He has good pace which he takes advantage of, continually moving forward in support  of the attack, making him an important extra option for the side in counterattacks, and  breakaways, where he also makes the most of his ability to get into the penalty area. He  occasionally allows himself to become too aggressive, too easily, something which sees him  picking up plenty of yellow cards or even sendings off. He is a good header of the ball,  though not because of his height but for his enthusiasm and determination.
x
* He has played for England as a schoolboy international.

* After coming through the ranks at Norwich City, he signed as a professional in  March 1992, He made his debut in the league on 20th April 1992 against  Sheffield Wednesday, while he socred his first goal against Middlesbrough on 8th May 1983. 
* He was involved in a curious incident when he was sent off at Upton Park, home of    West Ham United. Due to their similar hairstyles he was mistakenly sent off in place of  teammamate Spencer Prior.
* He was transfered to Nottingham Forest during the summer of 1997 for 2,200,000 pounds.

* Johnson had a disappointing season, occasionally being forced out of Mike Walker's plans  at Norwich City due to injury. Nevertheless, whenever he managed to get on the scoresheet,  curiously, the side never lost. His tremendous run at the beginning of the season raised everybody's  expectations of him, although these were never quite fulfilled as the season progressed. In total  he played in 27 games, scoring 5 goals.

475.name: Allen
pages: * Chris Allen is a player of whom Nottingham Forest have had high hopes,  ever since Frank Clark's time as manager of the club. It was Clark who signed  him and who had tremendous faith in his ability. Nevertheless, Allen didn't  manage to make himself a regular in the side,although he made a good impression  on the supporters and the club's coaching staff. He is a player who possesses  tremendous talent, but will need to put it into practice if he is going to force his way  into Dave Bassett's plans and manage to play in games from the start.

* Speed and ability are Chris Allen's most outstanding qualities. A left footed player  he can operate either as a winger or as a left sided midfield play. A skillful player  with the ability to beat a man, he is very difficult to stop when he is in full flight,  without fouling, and he does, in fact, win plenty of penalties. A good passer  of the ball, his crosses into the box from the byline create plenty of chances for the  strikers, while his strength allows him to battle away with defenders. Still very young  he is well on his way to becoming an outstanding footballer.
x
* 2 under-21 international appearances for England.

* Chris Allen is a product of his hometown club Oxford United's youth system. He turned  professional on 14th May 1991, although he didn't make his league debut  until the following  season.
* In February 1995 he scored in a game between an English First Division select side and  their counterparts from the Italian Serie B. In the summer of that same year, Allen made his  debut for the England  under-21 side in the Toulon International Tournament. 
* On 24th February 1996 he arrived at Nottingham Forest on loan. He made his debut   as a substitute on 2nd March, at Hillsborough against Sheffield Wednesday. The Reds  ran out 1-3 winners. On 16th of that month he made his first starting appearance at the  Riverside Stadium, where he also scored his first goal in the Premier League against  Middlesbrough (1-1). 
* At the end of the 95-96 season Frank Clark decided to make his move to Forest a permanent  one. However Oxford United and Forest couldn't come to an agreement on the transfer fee  and negotiations broke down. Finally Clark's interest in signing the player imposed itself   and Allen signd for the club on 20th June 1996. His move to the City Ground finally cost   Forest 450,000 pounds.

* Chris Allen didn't have as consistent a season as he no doubt would have liked,  having to be content wth just sporadic appearances in the side. However he did show  glimpses of his natural footballing ability. He eventually made a total of 24 appearances  for Nottingham Forest.

476.name: Woan
pages:
* Following the outstanding performances he put together during the 95-96 season,  nobody was surprised when Frank Clark turned down Everton's approach to take  Ian Woan to Goodison Park. The left footed midfielder wasn't just Forest's top scorer,  but also layed on more chances for his teammates than any other member of the side.  There was even speculation surrounding his possible inclusion in the England squad, even  though he had never been included in an England squad at any other level. 
* Nevertheless, Woan had a slightly disappointing season which, along with Steve  Stone's injury, was one of the reasons why Nottingham Forest were unable to maintain  their Premier League status. At present, under the guidance of  Dave Bassett, Woan  is not even in the side, and it wouldn't be a surprise if a change of club soon happens,  in an attempt to relaunch the career of a player who would no doubt like to  once again become as decisive for Nottingham Forest as he once was.

* A classy midfielder, Ian Woan is comfortable playing anywhere down the left hand  side. Left footed, with an exquisite touch, he possesses enough talent to add a brilliant  finish to any move. Woan is a creative player, an outstadingly accurate passer of the ball  and elegant when carries the ball forward. Blessed with a prodigious left foot, Woan  has the ability to beat a man, while he also possesses a powerful shot. He is, in fact,  something of a specialist in having a go at goal from distance, either in open play  or from free kicks, which is how he scores the majority of his goals.
x
x

* Ian Woan signed for Nottingham Forest on  14th  March 1990 from modest  Runcorn. The transfer fee was set at 80,000 pounds. Nevertheless he had to wait  until 2nd January 1991 to make his debut in a 6-2 victory over Norwich City. 
* A regular in the side from the 91-92 season onwards, although it was in the 95-96 campaign  when he started to show what he is genuinely capable of. During that season he scored  twice from free kicks in a game against Tottenham Hotspur,  and once in a UEFA Cup game  against Swedish club Malmo. He went on to become Nottingham Forest's top scorer with a total  of 12 goals in official competitions. 
* Some comments he made to the press in 1996, in which he criticised the quality   of the Forest squad, saw the club take disciplinary action against him, and there  was even talk about his possible departure from the City Ground. Nevetheless  Frank Clark turned down an offer of 3,000,000 pounds from Everton.

* After having a superb season during the 95-96 campaign, Woan proved to be unable  to maintain his tremendous form and carry it on into the following the season. He was  unable to get back to his best either on the left hand side of the midfield or at the heart  of things in the centre of the park. His disappointing performances were, without doubt,  one of the reasons why Nottingham Forest were eventually relegated to the First Division.   He played in a total of 32 games scoring once.

477.name: Stone
pages:
* Steve Stone represents, like few other players, a triumph for perseverance, overcoming a   number of injuries during his short playing career. In a short space of time he suffered three  serious injuries and even considered hanging up his boots. Fortunately for Forest, the midfilder's  desire to succeed knows no limits, and, supported by the coaching staff, Steve vowed to fight to  %%         effectively begin all over again. 
* Unfortunately for Steve, he was struck by another serious injury, after completing the best season  of his professional career, during which he managed to make his full international debut. At present,  having recovered from this serious blow, he is once again an automatic choice for Forest, now under  Dave Bassett, although a recent minor setback has once again delayed his full reintegration into  Nottingham Forest's starting line up. However, he should go on to become one of the most  important players in the First Division during the course of this season.

* He plays as a right sided midfielder and stands out for his speed, power, stamina and aggresive  approach to the game. A player with better technical ability than it might at first appear, he is  constantly moving up and down the flank, getting involved in the attack and helping out with  defensive duties, giving everything he's got, physically speaking. He makes the most of his  excellent shooting ability and the dangerous forward runs he makes into the opposition penalty  area allow him to score a good number of goals each season. He also creates plenty of goalscoring   chances for his teammates. He gives 100% in every game he plays, a quality which is  well appreciated by his manager.
x

* Nine full international appearances for England with 2 goals to his name. He made his debut  on 11th October 1995 in a friendly against Norway in Oslo (0-0). He scored his first goal for  his country on 15th November of that same year. England defeated Switzerland 3-1 at Wembley.  * He was in the England squad for the 1996 European Championships, in England. He  played in three games coming on each time as a substitute. In the first phase of the tournament  he played against Switzerland and Scotland, while in the quarter finals, he came on as a  substitute in extra-time against Spain, replacing Darren Anderton.

* As a boy, in his hometown  of Gateshead, Steve Stone went to the same school as  Paul Gascoigne, although the Forest midfielder is four years younger. In 1989 he   joined the youth set up at the City Ground and on the 20th May of that same year he  signed professional terms with the East Midlands club.          * Since his arrival at Forest  he has been dogged by bad luck. In fact, during the course of his career he has suffered  three broken legs, and, on more than one occasion, has seriously though about the  possiblity of retiring from the game. However, first of all Brian Clough and then FrankClark clough convinced him to press on with his career.
* Given the nickname of "Bulldog" for his tough, aggressive approach to the game he made his  debut in the league on 2nd May 1992 in a game against West Ham United. 
* At the beginning of his career, he played at the centre of the midfield although he later discovered that his most natural position was out on the right hand side of the midfield. 
* In October 1995 he became the star man in English football. That month he made his debut  for the full England, side, scored a superb goal that gave Forest a victory against Tottenham  Hotspur at White Hart Lane and was also the socrer of the goal that knocked Auxerre  out of the U.E.F.A. Cup. Months earlier Stone had been voted "Player of the Year, 1995"  by the City Ground supporters. 
* Shy and reserved when he is speaking to the press, Steve is married to Judith, his childhood  sweetheart. He has two daughters:  Carlyann and Robyn.
* After the 1996 European Champioships in England, where his contribution was merely  anectodal, he suffered another serious injury which he took a long while to get over.

* Steve Stone had an unfortunate season last time out. Having settled down in Forest's  first team, and as a regular member of the England squad, a serious knee injury in just the  fifth game of the season put him out for the rest of the campaign. His abscence from the side  was a key factor in Forest eventually being relegated to the First Division.

478.name: Gemmill
pages:
* The surname Gemmill is a well respected one around the City Ground.  Nobody forgets that Archie Gemmill was one of the heroes who brought the  glory days to Forest at the end of the 1970's and, years later, had a a brief spell  as a coach at the club. His son Scot is a product of the Reds' youth team set  up and is also one of the most promising Scottish players around at the moment.  Despite his background he hasn't always had an easy ride at the club. He  formed a tremendous partnership with Roy Keane which was eventually broken  up by the Irishman's departure to Manchester United. 
* Neverthless, Gemmill is a young player who could prove to be tremendously  valuable to the side, as he has done in previous years. Having been made a  first  team regular by Dave Bassett, he should now go on to become a key man in Forest's  return to the Premier League.

* He can play either at the heart of things in the centre of the park or out on the right  hand side of the midfield. In either position he stands out for his good vision and the  thoughtful way in which he plays the ball around. A very dynamic footballer, he fights  for every ball, helped out by his excellent strength and stamina. He creates plenty of danger  in and around the penalty area with his powerful right foot shot. Although not a brilliant  player, he is an efficient performer in the middle of the park. However, his weakness is his  inconsistency, as he alternates between some fantastic performances and disappointing games  where he often disappears from the action.
* Full members Cup winners medal, 1992.

* 11 full international appearances for Scotland. He made his debut on 21st May 1995 in a game against Japan, played in Hiroshima (0-0).
* He was a member of his country's squad in the 1996 European Championships in England,  although he didn't get to make an appearance.

* The son of Archie Gemmil, who was a member of the Nottingham Forest sidethat won the European Cup in 1979 and 1980, Scot arrived at the club as an apprentice  in March 1988. His father, at the time a Forest coach, was primarily responsible for his  signing, and was the man who directed the early years of his career. 
* Although a member of the first team squad from the 5th January 1990 he didn't make his  debut until 30th March 1991 in a game against Wimbledon.
* During the 91-92 season he made himself a regular in the side and formed a midfield  partnership with Roy Keane which relegated Gary Parker to the bench. 
* During the 94-95 season he suffered a series of injuries and illnesses which kept him  out of the team. He later saw how the Norwegian Lars Bohinen took his place in the side  from him. Nevertheless, Bohinen's dparture to Blackburn Rovers in October 1995 allowed  him to come back in, and, months later, he was called up to the Scotland squad for the 1996  European Championships in England, although he didn't get to make an appearance in the  tournament.

* Last season has an inconsistent one for Scott Gemmill, who didn't get his best run  of games until the month of March, when he made himself a regular until the end of the  season. In total, he played in 25 games for Nottingham Forest.

479.name: Bart-Williams
pages:
* Ex-Forest manager Frank Clark was the manager who gave Chris Bart-Williams  the chance to make his debut in the league, when the Sierra -Leone born player  had only just turned 16 years of age. That was the beginning of a meteoric rise  that took him from Leyton Orient to Sheffield Wednesday and even to the England  "B" side in a short space of time. 
* His transfer, was, at the time a record for a Nottingham Forest player. A player with  enormous potential, Bart-Williams should go on to become, as the regular first  team player he is at the moment, an important member of the side in the battle to get  back into the Premier League at the first attempt.

* Chris Bart-Williams' versatility allows him to do an effective job in a number of different   positions. In fact during the course of his career he has played as a striker, as a wide midfield   player down both flanks, as well as in the centre of the midfield. At Forest Frank Clark played   him just in front of the defence, where he can take advantage of his excellent touch on the ball, although   he is less dangerous. His natural physical attributes allow him to cover plenty of ground and make a  constant contribution to the side's efforts to win back possession. A dynamic and competitive  player who shows touches of real class,  Chris Bart-Williams is a very complete footballer.
x

* One England "B" international appearance.
* 16 Under-21 international appearances, scoring once.
* 12 youth international appearances, with two goals to his name.

* Born in Sierra Leone, though of British nationality, Chris Bart-Williamswas discovered by Frank Clark during his time as manager of Leyton Orient.
* Clark gave him his debut in the league at just 16 years and 4 months of age, making  him the youngest player in the history of  Leyton Orient. He made his debut on 3rd October  1990 in a game against Grismby Town.
* A professional since 18th July 1991 he was transfered to Sheffield Wednesday on 21st  November of that same year in exchange for 275,00 pounds. He was very much a personal  signing on the part of the "Owls" manager Trevor Francis. 
* He made his debut for Wednesday against Arsenal, then league champions. The maturity  of his performance saw manager Francis eventually go on to to make him a first team  regular. In fact he was a regular member of the side during most of the time he spent at  Hillsborough.  He was a member of the side that played in the 1993 F.A. Cup Final at  Wembley and make his debut for England at under-21 and "B" international level. 
* Bart-Williams won the admiration of the Sheffield Wednesday supporters who celebrated  the player's goals with their own peculiar song, complete with its own special dance. 
* A Forest player since 1st July 1995, he was signed as a personal request of then manager  Frank Clark, who had no hesitation in paying out 2,500,000 pounds for him. His first  appearance in a Forest shirt came in the first leg of a first round U.E.F.A. Cup tie against  Swedish club Malmo.
* He made his league debut on 17th September 1995. Forest defeated Everton 3-2 at the  City Ground.

* Playing in a more advanced position than he is used to, Bart-Williams didn't have a very  fortunate season at Nottingham Forest, although he gave glimpses of the reasons why the  club signed him from Sheffield Wednesday. In total he played in 16 games, scoring just once.

480.name: McGregor
pages:
* Paul McGregor is one of the best young players to have emerged from the youth ranks  at Nottingham Forest in recent years. An insatiable goalscorer with the youth side,  he has   demonstrated a surprising amount of know how during his appearances with the first team,  and has not been overawed by the higher standard of football. 
* Unfortunately for him, during the course of  last season he hardly came into the plans of the  club's coaching staff, while he also suffered an ankle injury. On top of this, the team were  going through a spell when what counted was experience, preventing young players like  McGregor from staking a claim for a place in the side. At the beginning of this league season,  he is yet to force his way into the plans of manager Dave Bassett, though that is a situation  he will no doubt be out to change in the not too distant future.

* Although in the club's junior sides he played as a striker, in the first team he generally   lines up as a right sided midfield player. Blessed with a well developed goalscorer's instinct,  his presence in and around the penalty area is a guarantee of danger. A good passer of the  ball, he makes the most of his speed to go past his rivals and send good, quality crosses overto the strikers. He also works hard to keep opposing defenders under constant pressure, forcing  them into mistakes.
x
x

* Paul McGregor is one of Nottingham Forest's top scorers at youth team level. After  coming through the youth system at the City Ground, he took the step up to the professional ranks  on 13th  December 1991. However, he didn't make his first team debut until 10th December 1994,  in a home victory against Ipswich Town (4-1). Days later, on 31st December, he scored his first  goal in Forest's visit to West Ham United (1-3). 
* In the 95-96 season he scored the goal that gave Forest victory in the U.E.F.A. Cup against  Lyon.

* Paul McGregor had a slightly disappointing season last time out, especially taking into account  the good performances he had put together during the previous campaign when he showed good  potential and forced his way into manager Frank Clark's plans. Last season wasn't the best moment   for the youngster to try to settle down in the Forest side, taking into account the delicate position that  the club found themselves in for the majority of the campaign. McGregor was limited to making   just five appearances, all of those coming as a substitute.
