481.name: Van Hooijdonk
pages:
* Pierre Van Hooijdonk is the most expensive signing in the history of Nottingham  Forest, and is Dave Bassett's main weapon in the battle to get back into the Premier  League, the Dutchman leading the fight from the front line. Although he didn't have  The immediate impact that might have been expected of him, managing to keep Forest  in the Premier League, nobody should be thinking that Van Hooijdonk will let people   down this time round; his ability is there for everybody to see, game after game. 
* A player whose character caused a few problems during his time with Glasgow Celtic,  he has had no problem adapting to life at Nottingham Forest. He will be hoping he can   build on this to become one of the best players in the First Division and help Forest return  to the Premier League.

* Van Hooijdonk is a naturally powerful man, with an incredible amount of physical  strength and a power in the air which few other players can match. However he is not  just a big powerful centre forward who remains rooted in the penalty area waiting  to get in efforts on goal. The Dutch striker has more ability than that, and technically  speaking is quite a complete player. He holds the ball up superbly well, waiting for his  teammates to come through from midfield. He is a dangerous player inside the area,  showing tremendous ability to get in efforts on goal, and find the target, as he has more than demonstrated over recent years, and will no doubt go on to do this season.
* Top scorer for Glasgow Celtic during the 95-96 season.
* Van Hooijdonk has played for Holland as an under-21 international and has made 8  full international appearances, scoring twice.

* Glasgow  Celtic signed him on 7th Januray 1995, after paying out 1,200,000 pounds to his  club, Dutch outfit NAC Breda . 
* After going through some turbulent spells with the hierarchy at the Scottish club, Van Hooijdonk  signed for Nottingham Forest on 11th Match 1997 for 4,500,000 pounds, setting a new record for a  Forest player, and breaking the record previously established when the club signed fellow Dutch  winger Bryan Roy. His debut for the club came on the same day as he signed against Blackburn  Rovers, although he had to wait for his first goal until his sixth game for Forest, finding the  back of the net against Leeds United on 19th April.

* In terms of goalscoring Van Hooijdonk had a superb season, scoring 14 goals in just 21  21 games for Glasgow Celtic. Nevertheless, differences of opinion between the board of  .directors and the coaching staff at the Scottish club saw him eventually being transfered  to Nottingham Forest. At Forest he didn't have the impact he might have, managing to find  the net just once in 8 games, being unable to prevent the club from being relegated to the  First Division.

482.name: Moore
pages:
* It's no coincidence that the young ex -Tranmere Rovers' striker has been tagged  "Golden Boy". A footballer with a tremendous future ahead of him, Ian Moore is one  of the jewels at Nottingham Forest, and could be one of those who goes on to shine most  brightly in the future. Signed as one for the future by Stuart Pearce during his brief spell   in charge at Forest, he is regarded as a player to keep an eye on at the City Ground club, due   to the tremendous ability he possesses. 
* At present he is out on loan at another club, allowing him to get games under his belt and to get   back the goalscoring instinct that last season he seemed to have lost, but will surely no doubt  quickly recapture. He is not a regular in the side, but his contribution could prove to be important,  taking into account the length of the league campaign and the inevitable crop of injuries that  will no doubt occur.

* Moore is not a particularly strong striker, though he makes up for that with explosive pace,  capable of taking defenders on for speed, helped out by his good dribbling ability. He has a good  change of direction, and scores some quality goals, though not in great quantities. He is good with   either foot, although his right is the stronger of the two. Despite having a tremendous ability to  get on the blind side of defenders, he is also dangerous when he picks the ball up in and around  the penalty area, not only due to his class and ability put also for his vision.
x
* An England Under-18 international, he scored a hat-trick on his debut against Denmark..

* After coming through the youth ranks at Tranmere Rovers, he made his debut in the league  on 30th April 1995 against WBA. His first goals came on 26th August 1995 against Huddersfield Town. 
* He was loaned out to Bradford City on 13th September 1996. He made his first appearance  for the club against Oxford United the following day.
* Nottingham Forest signed him on 15th March 1997 for 1,000,000. His debut came on 22nd  March against Sunderland.

* Last season was a disappointing one for Ian Moore, a young striker who has a fine  future ahead of him but who, nevertheless, was almost incapable of finding the back  of the net between the months of October and February. Apart from the 21 games he played  with Tranmere Rovers, he also played for Bradford City, where he made 6 appearances. He  was finally signed by Nottingham Forest, although he made just 5 appearances for his new club.

483.name: Campbell
pages:
* Kevin Campbell was one of the signings Frank Clark made in an  attempt to cover the departure of Stan Collymore to Liverpool. It was great opportunity  for one of the best striking prospects in English football at the beginning of the 1990's but   who has failed to go on to live up to the expectations that everybody had of him. 
* Injuries have also taken their toll on this still young player, preventing from getting  the continuity he would no doubt have liked. Nevertheless, despite what has been said  about him Campbell remains a genuine penalty area predator, while it is not recomendable  to give him the chance to demonstrate whether he reamains the prospect he once was  because he is not a player who generally fails to take a chance. Harshly criticised by the  City Ground supporters, he is a regular member of Dave Bassett's side, alternating up front  With Dean Saunders, although, more often than not, it is  Campbell who gets the vote  to partner Van Hooijdonk in the attack.

* His power in the air is Kevin Campbell's most outstanding quality. A real battling centre  forward he is blessed with outstanding physical attributes. An explosive player he uses his   power to get the better of opposing defenders inside the penalty area, whilst he attempts to   make up for his technical limitations with speed and strength. He is a very difficult player   to stop when he is in full flight although he doesn't always make the right decisions when   it comes to finishing off moves. Nevertheless his mobility opens up gaps that can be taken   advantage of by teammates. Unfortunately inconsistency and, as a result, a lack of confidence   often become his own worst enemy.

* European Cup Winners Cup winners medal 94.
* League championship winners medal 91.
* F.A. Cup winners medal  93. 
* League Cup winners medal 93.
* Charity Shield medals 91 and 93.
*  F.A. youth Cup winners medal 88.

* One "B" international appearance for England.
* Four Under-21 international appearances for England, with 1 goal to his credit.

* Born in London, he formed part of the Arsenal youth set up before he signed his first  professional contract on 11th February 1988. His league debut came on 7th May 1988   against Everton. 
* That year he won an F.A. Youth Cup winners medal after helping the Arsenal youth side  to beat their Doncaster Rovers counterparts in the final. In the first leg of the final he played as a  left back, something which didn't stop him from scoring a hat trick in 45 minutes, as a result  of some magnificent individual runs.     * With Paul Merson and Alan Smith forming the  Arsenal front line, his appearances were limited, and so, as a result he went out on loan  to Leyton Orient, where the manager was Frank Clark, on 16th  January 1989. On 8th November  of that same year, he had another loan spell, this time at Leicester City.    * During the 90-91  season  he scored 9 goals in 22 league games for Arsenal,  helping the club to lift the championship.  From that season onwards he became a regular in George Graham's side. In May 1994 he was a  member of the starting line up in the side that won the European Cup winners cup by beating Italian  side Parma in the final in Copenhagen (1-0). * In February 1995, an injury brought his season  to an early end.  * On 1st July 1995 he was transfered to Nottingham Forest for 30,000 pounds.  His signing was at the personal request of manager Frank Clark, and was made as cover for the  departure of Stan Collymore to Liverpool.
* He made his debut on 19th August in a victory away at Southampton,  (3-4). On 29th of that  same month he scored his first goal in a Forest shirt, ironically against  Arsenal, at Highbury   However, in general, he didn't have a very satisfactory first season at the City Ground.

* Campbell began the season explosively, scoring a hat-trick against Coventry City in the first  game of the league campaign. However shortly afterwards an injury forced him out of the side,  until November. From then on he wasn't the same player although he ended the season as the  side's top scorer, though that was with just six goals to his name. In total Campbell played in  17 league game for Nottingham Forest.

485.name: Roberts
pages: * Ben Roberts is a keeper raised in the Middlesborough youth squad, and who is one of the big hopes for the club in this important position.  His contribution to the team's efforts have been increasing steadily and his good performances have even lead to his inclusion in the England under-21 team.  He will have a hard job to displace Mark Schwarzer but time is on his side.

* Roberts is a promising goalkeeper who has great virtues as a goalie.  His overall game is notable, being very steady in every aspect, dominating in the aerial game, his strong point.  He will make mistakes but this is due more to his inexperience than lack of ability.

* Runner-up in the League Cup in 1996.
* Runner-up in the FA Cup in 1996.
* One under-21 international appearance for England at the under-21 level.

* A product of the Middlesborough youth squad, Roberts signs as a professional on the 24th of March 1993.  His first game with the club has to wait until the 18th of January 1997 against Sheffield Wednesday.
* Roberts has been loaned to several teams before making his debut for Middlesborough.  These teams were Hartlepool United, Wycombe Wanderers and Bradford City.

* Roberts started the season on loan to Bradford City, the club where he played two games.  On returning to Middlesborough, his participation increased with the rotation of players practised by Bryan Robson so that they wouldn't play too many games.  The position between the posts was mainly occupied by Steve Walsh and also by Schwarzer.

486.name: Schwarzer
pages: * Mark Schwarzer became a man who had the trust of Bryan Robson last year when he had defended the Middlesborough goal after being signed from Bradford city.  Coming from German football, his figure brought a lot of security and confidence to the Boro defence and he has managed to settle into Robson's first teams this year.

* Schwarzer is a very complete goalkeeper who is dominant in almost every aspect of the game.  His mastery of the aerial balls is excellent due to his height and excellent judgement.  The reflexes of the Australian international allow him to make almost impossible saves.  To sum up, a fault free keeper for Boro.

* Runner-up in the League Cup in 1996.
* FA Cup Runner-up in 1996.
* 4 international appearances for Australia.

* He is signed by Bradford City on the 22nd of November 1996 from the German club Kaiserslautern in exchange for £350,000.  His first game for the Bantams is on the 23rd of this same month against Charlton Athletic.
* His great performances lead Bryan Robson to pay £1.5 million for him on the 26th of February 1997.  He makes his debut on the 1st of March against Sheffield Wednesday.
* Schwarzer has dual nationality due to his descent, these nationalities being German and Australian.

* Schwarzer's season was marked by different and radical changes of course, moving from one team to another in the space of months due to his sensational performance.  After signing for Bradford City, his qualities so impressed Robson that the Middlesborough coach signed him almost immediately.  Unfortunately, injuries prevented Schwarzer from producing his best for a long time.

487.name: Festa
pages: * Gianluca Festa was one of the best signings last year by Bryan Robson, bringing a lot of defensive security to Middlesborough, something that Middlesbrough had lacked, this being one of the reasons why Middlesbrough made the drop.  His figure is essential for the club, and thanks to his contributions he will certainly be a starter this year.

* Festa is a specialist in defensive tasks, and is very complete in this aspect with an outstanding ability to dominate in the air.  He is tough when going in for the ball and doesn't fold against a rival or in a difficult game thanks to his enormous concentration during the games.  He is no wonder in the technical aspect but is acceptable.  His is not noted for his attacking contributions except in corners and free-kicks but he has hardly scored any goals during the course of the years.

* League Cup Runner-up in 1996.
* FA Cup Runner-up in 1996.
x

* After playing for Cagliari and Inter Milan amongst others, he signs for Middlesbrough from Inter on the 18th of January 1997 for £2,7 million. His debut for Boro takes place this same day against Sheffield Wednesday, and he also scores a goal.

* Festa's signing brought a great deal of defensive security to the team which didn't exist before his arrival.  His impact was immediate and he even managed to score a goal on his debut despite not being a prolific man in front of goal.  However, his outstanding first campaign in England could not prevent the team from being relegated to the First Division.

488.name: Kinder
pages: * A Slovakian international, Vladimir Kinder is an international quality player at Middlesborough. Great things are expected of him this year, as last year he couldn't manage to adapt to English football.  He is a regular in Bryan Robson's schemes and his firmness on the left flank will be important for the team during the course of the league.

* Kinder is a wide defender who can play on either side but who usually plays on the left despite being right-footed.  He is OK in the technical aspect, passing and crossing acceptably.  His speed is average and thus has problems against very quick wingers.  However, his lack of speed is compensated for by close hard marking; not one inch of advantage is given to the rival.

* Runner-up in the League Cup in 1996.
* Runner-up in the FA Cup in 1996.
* Kinder has been an international for the former Czechoslovakian team once. Currently he has played 27 times for the Slovakian team, and scored a goal.

* Kinder was signed by Middlesborough on the 18th of January 1997 in exchange for £1 million.  His first game for the club was on the 1st of March against Sheffield Wednesday. His first goal came four days later against Derby County.

* Kinder's first season in English football was not as good as he might have hoped as he found it hard to adapt to the style of play. However, in the games he played he showed that he has quality and that he could make some useful contributions to the side managed by Bryan Robson. In total he played 6 games and scored a goal.

489.name: Blackmore
pages: * The figure of Bryan Robson has been a continuous reference in Clayton Blackmore's career. He coincided with him at Manchester United, both sharing changing rooms and titles. Robson, captain of the Reds, collected the Cup Winners' Cup trophy in 1991 after a final in which Blackmore played an outstanding role.  When the time came for the Welshman to leave Old Trafford, Robson didn't hesitate to bring him to Middlesborough, where he was player-manager and although last season he hardly had any opportunities, Blackmore is hoping that, in any moment, his former team-mate will ask one more thing of him. Even so, the Welshman has just had one of his best seasons, so it wouldn't be a surprise to see him in the team as the league progresses.

* A very versatile player, Clayton Blackmore can play is several positions both in the midfield and in the defence. In fact, during the course of his career he has played at left half, left back and in the centre of the defence. He has an acceptable technique and a good playing vision, as well as a very powerful shot on goal.  A specialist at taking free-kicks, he has scored many goals this way.  A veteran footballer, Blackmore uses his broad experience as a resource to make up for the inevitable loss of speed with the passing of the years. In recent times he has gained a bit of weight, something he should be careful about for the good of his game.

* European Cup Winners' Cup Champion in 91.
* League Champion in 93.
* FA Cup Champion in 90.
* Charity Shield Medal in 90.
* First Division Champion 95.

* 38 full international caps for Wales. 1 goal. He made his debut on the 5th of June 1985 in a game against Norway played in Bergen. Blackmore replaced Hopkins.
* 4 under-21 international caps. 1 goal.

* At the end of the 70's and the beginning of the 80's Clayton Blackmore was one of the most promising young Welsh footballers. Trained in the youth squad at Manchester United, he made it to the first team on the 28th of September 1982. At Old Trafford he coincided with Bryan Robson, one of the stars of the England team who, months before had played in the Spanish World Cup, and who, years later, would be his coach at Middlesbrough.
* Blackmore made his debut in the League on the 16th of May 1994 against Nottingham Forest. However, his appearances as a starter were still few and far between.
* FA Cup Champion in 1990, in the following season he settles into a regular place in the team, plays 35 games and scores 4 goals. However, his biggest success is on the 15th of May 1991 when he plays in the starting eleven of the team that beat Barcelona (2-1) in the Cup Winners' Cup Final played in Rotterdam. Blackmore had an outstanding game, and in the last minute of the game he cleared a shot off the line by the Dane Michael Laudrup. The captain of that Manchester United was Bryan Robson. Clayton had also been one of the most important men in the previous rounds.  He scored a goal against Pecsi MSC in the first round and another from a direct free-kick in the quarter-finals against Montpellier.
* From the 92-93 season onwards Blackmore lost his status as a regular starter and in the following season he didn't play a single game. As a free agent he signed for Middlesborough on the 11th of July 1994.  At Boro he overlapped once again with Bryan Robson, who recommends his incorporation into the team from his new position as player-manager. He maked his debut alongside 4 other new players on the 13th of August, with a 2-0 home win over Burnley.At the end of his first season with Middlesborough the side was proclaimed champions of the First Division and earnt automatic promotion to the Premier League.
* Loaned to Bristol City during the 96-97 season, playing 5 games and scoring a goal.

* Clayton Blackmore started the season on loan to Bristol City until he was once again needed by Middlesborough, the club where he had his best spell as a professional, playing his best football in years and finally being included once again in the Welsh national side.  He played 16 games and scored a spectacular goal against Everton, one of Boro's best goals of the season.

490.name: Fleming
pages: * A footballer tremendously appreciated by the fans at the Riverside Stadium, Curtis Fleming has just had a tremendous season which was tainted by relegation to the First Division.  Unthreatened by Chris Morris, Fleming has settled definitively as a wide defender at Middlesborough and once again figures in the plans of the Irish selector.

* Curtis Fleming is a wide defender who stands out for his spectacular style. Although he normally plays on the left, the arrival and inclusion of Kinder has forced him over to the other side where he plays a good role. He is dominant along the whole of his flank, fighting for every ball bravely not hesitating to go in hard. Once possession is regained he joins in the attack very quickly and, helped by a technically good left foot, passes accurately to his team-mates. A specialist at recovering impossible balls, Fleming is a valuable team player who doesn't give an inch to his rivals and who is also very generous, pushing hard in attacking tasks.

* Irish League Champion in 90.
* First Division Champion 95.

* 7 full international appearances for the Republic of Ireland.  Fleming made his debut on the 24th of April 1996 in a friendly against the Check Republic played in Prague. The Republic of Ireland lost 2-0.
* 1 international B appearance.
* 6 under-21 international appearances.

* Born in Manchester, but with Irish nationality, Curtis Fleming began as a footballer in the ranks of St Patricks, the club where he arrived after a trial at Swindon Town (March 1989) and Manchester City (August 1990). With St Patricks he is proclaimed champion of the Irish league in 1990.  A regular in the lower categories of the Irish teams, his performances did not go by unnoticed by the English clubs.
* On the 16th of August 1991 he is transferred to Middlesborough for £50,000. On the 24th of this same month he makes his debut in a game against Ipswich Town and plays 28 league games in his first season at Boro, making a decisive contribution to the team's promotion, which was able to compete in the first edition of the Premier League.
* Curtis Fleming is one of the best-loved players at Middlesborough. His enthusiastic playing style has struck a resonant chord with the spectators who attend the ground regularly, especially those who occupy the Holgate End at Ayresome Park.
* On the 13th of April 1996 he scores his first goal in English football against Wimbledon, although Middlesborough loose at home 1-2. Days later Fleming makes his debut for the full Republic of Ireland team.

* Fleming had his best season in the Middlesborough first team, playing in 30 games and being an integral part of the team in its doomed fight to avoid relegation and its League and FA Cup runs, both ending with a defeat at Wembley.  What's more he was once again called up by his the Republic of Ireland side for one of their games.

491.name: Pearson
pages: * Nigel Pearson is a central defender with a lengthy experience in English football who has a lot of prestige in this sport. He is now very much a veteran but is valuable for the security and solidness he brings to Middlesborough, attributes invaluable for Bryan Robson.  Together with Gianluca Festa he forms a very stable partnership which the club hopes will serve as a platform to launch their bid for a rapid return to the Premier League.

* Thanks to this lengthy experience, Nigel Pearson has a lot of resources he can call on in his duties as a central defender. He stands out for his firmness in aerial balls, a facet of his game where he is unbeatable when fighting for the ball with which he creates danger in attack.Technically limited, he brings the ball out more by brute force than by use of skill, but even so, he is very level-headed in difficult situations, surprising with his security. An intelligent footballer, he can read the games tactically, and so is very much valued by coaches. His presence is a continual reference for his team-mates. All in all, Nigel Pearson is a great team player.

* League Cup Champion in 91.
* First Division Champion 95.
* Runner-up in the League Cup in 1996.
* Runner-up in the FA Cup in 1996.
x

* Known by the fans as "Captain Fantastic", his ample experience and model career have lead him to be named captain of Middlesbrough in his first season at the club.
* Trained in the modest Heanor Town, he was transferred to Shrewsbury Town on 12th November 1981 for £5,000. On the 28th of August of 1982 he made his debut in the league against Oldham Athletic. An undisputed starter for his entire spell at Shrewsbury, only injuries could keep him out the team. In fact, he missed the entire 84-85 season due to a serious physical problem. 
* After six years in the Second Division, Sheffield Wednesday give him the chance to play in the top category of English football.  And so, on the 16th of October 1987, Nigel Pearson was signed by the Owls in exchange for £250,000.
* In the 90-91 season he was part of the team that win the League Cup and that are also relegated to the Second Division, although the following season Sheffield Wednesday regain their place in the top division.
* On the 19th of July 1994 Pearson is transferred to Middlesbrough for £500,000. His signing was greeted with a certain amount of suspicion by the fans, because, amongst other reasons, Pearson had had two broken legs during the course of his footballing career. He made his debut on the 13th of August with a 2-0 home win over Burnley.  On the 11th of September he scored his first goal for the team lead by Bryan Robson. At the end of the season the club celebrated promotion to the Premier League.

* Although he couldn't play more than 18 games during the whole of the league, Pearson was once again one of the biggest sources of inspiration for Middlesbrough from his position in the heart of the defence, helping the team in their bid to win the League and FA Cup in one of his best seasons at the club. Without doubt, he was one of Boro's best players.

492.name: Vickers
pages: * When Steve Vickers signed for Middlesbrough in 1993, there were many critics who questioned his capability for playing in a team which were aspiring to return to the Premier League. However, the player responded to these criticisms with a satisfactory performance, earning the confidence of the manager and supporters. Currently he is a very valuable player for Bryan Robson, vital in the last two seasons but the arrival of Festa has led to a reduction in his chances, as Robson opted for Festa and Pearson as central defenders. In any case, his figure will be seen as the league advances.

* A classic central defender, Steve Vickers stands out for his firm aerial game, which allows him to join in the attack dangerously in set-plays. Aggressive and hard at times, the rival forwards find it hard to get by him.  He is conscious of his technical limitations, and doesn't take any risks when in possession and never complicates things when playing the ball out.  Sober in his actions, he is effective rather than brilliant.

* First Division Champion 95.
* Runner-up in the League Cup in 1996.
* Runner-up in the FA Cup in 1996.
x

* On the 11th of September 1985 Steve Vickers arrived at Tranmere Rovers from modest Spennymoor United. On the 4th of April 1986 he made his debut, in a Fourth Division game against Northampton.
* From the 86-87 season he settled down as a starter in the ranks of Tranmere. In 1989 he saw promotion to the Third Division and in 1991 to the Second Division. One year later, the restructuring of English football and the creation of the Premier League placed them in the First Division.
* Surprisingly, on the 3rd of December 1993 Vickers was transferred to Middlesbrough for £700,000 after a decision made by Lennie Lawrence. On the 4th of December he maked his league debut away against Bristol Rovers (0-0), although Steve didn't play from the start, something which would happen one week later.
* In the 94-95 season Middlesbrough was promoted to the Premier League and 12 years later, Steve Vickers is voted "Player of the Year" by the Boro fans.

* Steve Vickers was one of the main components of the defensive machine of the team during last season. His prize as the best player of the year two years earlier was repeated last year and he made some great contributions once again to Middlesbrough, including an important goal against Liverpool in the League Cup knocking out the Reds. Vickers took part in 30 games during the course of the League.

495.name: Maddison
pages:
* Signed for Middlesbrough in October 1997. 
* Neil Maddison spent the whole of his sporting career defending Southampton's colours.  A regular in the Saints line-up since the 92-93 season, only untimely injuries have kept him out the team and he has even scored some important goals.  Last season, he lost his status of automatic starter, but he has enough quality to be called on by the manager in any moment.

* He usually plays as a midfielder down the left, although he has also played in attack.  He is a hard-working player, blessed with a lot of strength and physical resistance which allows him to keep up the rhythm for the full ninety minutes.  His constant commitment takes the work burden off the more technical players such as Matt Le Tissier, with whom he has a perfect understanding.  Technically limited, his contribution to the attacking game is limited, although he doesn't hesitate to push up into the area if he sees a gap in the rival defence.  Not particularly brilliant, and times he has been undervalued, but the team looses defensive balance in the games when he doesn't play, as his presence guarantees a lot of ball recuperations per game.
x
x

* Neil Maddison is a true Southampton product, and his entire career has been spent at the club at the Dell.  He signed as a professional for them on the 14th of April 1988 after training in the lower ranks. 
* He makes his debut in the league on the 25th of October 1988 in a game against Tottenham Hotspur. 
* In total he has been booked five times during his career and has never been sent off. 
* He was transfered to Middlesbrough in October 1997 for 250.000 pounds.

* Although he wasn't regular member of the starting line-up, he participated in 18 games, doing what was asked of him.  In the game against Newcastle his goal provoked his team's reaction.  They were loosing 2-0, and after his goal Le Tissier scored the equaliser.

496.name: Ormerod
pages: * Anthony Ormerod is one of the novelties at Middlesbrough going into this season coming up as he has from the lower ranks.  However, despite having a technical base, he has the tendency to disappear from the games, something that will be corrected as he gains experience.

* Ormerod is a midfielder who occupies the right of the pitch, applying his entire strength and enthusiasm on this flank. He is quick and has good technical quality, to which an outstanding capacity for sacrifice on his part should be added.
x
x
* A product of the Middlesbrough youth squad, Ormerod signs as a professional with Middlesbrough in 1997.
* Promoted from the lower ranks of Middlesbrough, Ormerod didn't play a single game for the club last year.

497.name: Townsend
pages: * Andy Townsend is a veteran player but has become a personal bet on the part of Bryan Robson for this season. Without doubt he is a very good signing for Middlesbrough given that this sensational midfielder will be vital for Middlesbrough's attempt to return to the Premier League. A regular for Robson and also the Irish team.

* A very strong midfielder who covers a lot of ground. He operates on the left of midfield, helping out a lot defensively with strokes of class. His mastery of the pass is complemented by his profound knowledge of the game. His good vision allows him to read the movements of his team-mates quickly. Furthermore, he has an excellent shot from long range, hard and well placed. The arrival of Ian Taylor saw Townsend play a little deeper to help out in defence.  Although his physical performance is dropping, he makes use of his veteran status to help sort out difficult situations.
* League Cup Champion in 93-94 and 95-96.

* A full international for the Republic of Ireland 54 times - 5 goals. He made his debut in February of 1989 in a friendly against France. He took part in the 90 Italian World Cup and the 88 European Championship in Germany. 
* International B on one occasion.

* The son of Don Townsend, player for Charlton and Crystal Palace between 1959 and 1965.
* After playing in the modest teams Welling and Weymouth, Townsend is transferred to Southampton on the 15th of January 1985 for £35,000.
* He made his league debut on the 20th of April 1985 in a game against Aston Villa, playing at right back.
* On the 31st of August 1988 he signs for Norwich City.  His price had risen to £300,000. In his first season with the Canaries he reaches the semi-final of the FA Cup.
* He is transferred to Chelsea on the 4th of July 1990 for £1,200,000. 
* He is transferred to Aston Villa on the 26th of July 1993 for £2,100,000.  
* Finally his signing for Middlesbrough comes through in the summer of 1997 for £500,000.

* Townsend had yet another consistent season for Aston Villa, taking part in almost all the league competition games and scoring his usual number of goals, including one against his former team, Chelsea.

498.name: Merson
pages:
* Once he had got over his personal problems, Paul Merson became once again the player who dazzled England seasons ago to such an extent that he was voted "Young Player of the Year" in 1989. However, everyone was surprised when Arsenal transferred him to Middlesbrough after many successful years with the Gunners. It is rumoured that his relationship with Wenger had deteriorated in recent times which has finally lead to his transfer to Boro.
* In Bryan Robson's team, he will occupy the position left vacant by Juninho and, from the start, he will be an important component in the team that hopes to return to the Premier League. His great start to the season has lead to reports that he will be called up once again by Glenn Hoddle, the England manager.

* Although at the beginning he usually played as a forward, in recent times Merson has converted into a link-man between the forwards and midfield who generally operates on the left. From this position, he takes advantage of his good turn on the run to make dangerous forays and supply passes to the forward line or try out his shot on goal. Quick, and a good finisher, he is not a born goalscorer, but he creates a lot of chances for his team-mates. Right-footed, he takes the direct free-kicks effectively and usually takes the corners. With good playing vision and ball control, Paul Merson is a great footballer, creative, with a very attacking nature.

* European Cup Winners Cup Champion 94.
* European Cup Winners Cup Runner-up 95.
* League Champion 89 and 91.
* FA Cup Champion 93.
* League Cup Champion 93.
* "Young Player of the Year" in 1989, according the Professional Footballers Association.

* 14 full international appearances for England - 1 goal.  He made his debut on the 11th of September 1991 in a friendly against Germany played at Wembley.  Merson came on as a substitute for Salako during the game.
* He scored his first goal on the 25th of March 1992 in a game against Czechoslovakia played in Prague (2-2).
* Present in the 92 European Championship in Sweden, he was a starter in the games against Denmark (0-0) and the host nation (England defeated 1-2). 
* 3 international B appearances - 2 goals.
* 4 international under-21 appearances.
* 3 youth international appearances.

* As a young lad, Paul Merson began his career at Brent, one of the many clubs in London.  After being rejected by Chelsea, Queens Park Rangers and Watford he arrives at Arsenal in April 1982, aged just 14. He starts his journey through the lower ranks of the club until he sings his first contract as a professional on the 1st of December 1985. However, his debut with the first team didn't take place until the 22nd of November 1986 in a game against Manchester City at Highbury (3-0). Merson came on as a substitute for Nial Quinn during the game.
* As he wasn't a starter he was loaned to Brentford on the 22nd of January 1987. Merson plays 7 games in the Third Division.
* His explosion as a footballer occurs during the 88-89 season, when he becomes a regular in the team's line-up, scoring 13 goals in 37 games making a decisive contribution to the League title won by Arsenal. Thanks to his extraordinary season he is voted "Player of the Year" by the English footballers. 
* George Graham, the Arsenal manager at the time, and Paul Merson had a tense relation for a time. When they made peace, a new nickname was given to Merson, "George's son".
* International since 1991, Paul Merson's career was on the brink of falling apart in 1994 due to his addiction to gambling, cocaine and alcohol. Luckily, the footballer made his problems public and could receive the necessary help. The English Federation decided not to suspend him and Merson entered a rehabilitation plan far away from the footballing world.  Weeks later he reappears to an emotional ovation from the fans at Highbury. That day, Arsenal was fighting for the European Supercup against Milan.
* In the 95-96 season he played in all of the league games and Hoddle's appointment as the manager of the national side fuels his hopes of returning to the England side.
* He is transferred to Middlebrough during the 1997 season for £5 million.

* Last season was another outstanding season for Paul Merson who once again became one of the most important men for Arsene Wenger in his position as attacking midfielder. His statistics reflect this, 32 games played and six goals for his tally.

499.name: Liddle
pages: * Bryan Robson, the manager at Middlesbrough, guides the first steps of Craig Liddle in the footballing world, trying to protect him. The midfielder has already enjoyed chances to show his conditions in the Premier League and he has performed satisfactorily. Although he still has a lot to learn, without doubt things will always be easier with Robson at his side. His opportunities in the top category of English football haven't led him to a place in the team but this season he hopes to be able to make the definitive breakthrough.

* A defensively oriented midfielder, Craig Liddle is noted for his versatility as he can play in the centre of the defence and even at right back. He is physically strong, and makes the interceptions decisively, winning back most balls. Good in the air defensively, his contribution in attack is still limited. Liddle is a clear example of a club footballer, workmanlike but not brilliant. In any case, his youth gives him ample margin for improvement.
x
x

* Craig Liddle started with Middlesbrough on the 12th of July 1994 coming from the modest team Blyth Spartans. He normally plays in the reserve teams, and made his debut in the first squad in the last game of the 94-95 season, playing on the 7th of May 1995 at Prenton Park against Tranmere Rovers (1-1). 
* On the 4th of November 1995 he makes his first appearance in the Premier League.  Middlesbrough draw 1-1 at home against Leeds United on the day of Juninho's debut in English football.

* The arrival of several stars at Middlesbrough limited the number of chances Liddle had to play, taking part in only 5 matches with the team. His appearances were basically due to suspensions or injuries during the course of the league. He performed adequately.

500.name: Hignett
pages: * In the 96-97 season, Craig Hignett's career seemed to have finished at Middlesbrough due to the enormous number of foreign stars who had arrived at the club.  Even so, this brave footballer tried to overcome the adverse situation and stay at the club, accepting a reduction in his fees. The result was spectacular as Robson once again used him and he became an important man for the team during the league. Once again this year his situation is not favourable but it is certain that Hignett will get over this obstacle and play once again for Boro.

* A true specialist at taking penalties and direct free-kicks, Craig Hignett is an attacking midfielder who can play perfectly well in the forward line, preferably hugging the left touchline.  A skilful and quick footballer, he turns effectively and his crosses to the box bring a lot of problems for the rival team. He also has a scent for goal, which makes him a complete and useful player.

* First Division Champion 95.
* Runner-up in the League Cup in 1996.
* Runner-up in the FA Cup in 1996.
x

* After playing in the prestigious youth squad at Anfield, Liverpool let Craig Hignett go in 1988. And so, on the 11th of May of this year Crewe Alexandra, then in the Fourth Division, acquired his services. Months later on the 8th of October, he was making his debut against Wrexham, although he didn't play for the rest of the season.
* From the 89-90 season Hignett settled into the team, but the club is continually promoted and relegated between the Third and Fourth Division. 
* On the 30th of April 1991 he scores his first hat-trick of his career against Rotherham.  On the 14th of November 1992 he scores 4 goals in a Cup game against Wrexham.  Shortly afterwards, on the 27th of November, he is transferred to Middlesbrough for £500,000.
* Once their first season in the Premier League comes to a close (92-93), Boro drop to the First Division.
* On the 21st of September 1993 he scores 4 goals against Brighton.
* Hignett fought his way into Bryan Robson's plans the hard way during the course of the league. In total this battling midfielder played 22 games and scored 4 goals.

501.name: Stamp
pages: * Considered by the fans at Boro as the most brilliant young footballer in the side, Phil Stamp showed a good level of play last season aged only 20. Bryan Robson has blind faith in the possibilities of this genuine youth squad product and has seen how Stamp has eased his way into a place in the team making his future even more promising. His great enthusiasm has led to him playing from the start this season.

* Although Phil Stamp is a midfielder much valued for his defensive aptitudes, it would be unfair not to consider his creativity in the attacking moves, something to which his powerful long-range shot should be added. He moves the ball around effectively and makes good passes to his team-mates. In defence he stands out for his aggression, his constant battling, and for the determination he puts into each and every every action.  A very dynamic player who covers a lot of ground, he just needs time to hone his magnificent talent.
x
* 4 times youth international for England.

* Born in Middlesbrough, Philip Stamp is one of the most promising products of the Boro youth squad. After passing through all of the lower categories at the club, he turned professional on the 4th of February 1993.
* His debut in the League occurs on the 10th of October 1993 in Middlesbrough's visit to Watford, with a 2-0 home win.
* After the promotion to the Premier League in 1995, Stamp scores his first goal on the 9th of December of this same year in the Riverside Stadium.

* During last season, Stamp managed to double the number of appearances in the League competition for Middlesbrough, settling down as a regular in the team.  His season in all of the Cup competitions was one of the of the reasons for their extended runs which ended with defeats in the finals. In total he played 24 games and scored a goal.

502.name: Mustoe
pages: * Robbie Mustoe is one of the players the fans at the Riverside Stadium most acclaim.  Lacking brilliance, the supporters at Middlesbrough recognise the constant effort of the midfielder defending Middlesbrough's colours, appreciating his fighting spirit. For several seasons he has been one of the most used players by the club's managers.  The arrival of the Portuguese Emerson, a man with similar characteristics, didn't put his place in danger as he acted as a complement to the recent signing. Both are two defensive barriers for Middlesbrough in the midfield.

* Blessed with some extraordinary physical conditions, his great resistance allows him to keep up a high playing rhythm for the full ninety minutes.  A good passer, he plays as a midfielder, generally on the right, putting in a lot of effort in defence and also participating in the attacking game of the team.  An all-terrain footballer, he covers a large area of the pitch and his work relieves others of their defensive duties. Enthusiastic and generous, he never gives up a ball as lost and tries to infect his team mates with combative spirit. His unconditional commitment is a guarantee for any manager.

* First Division Champion 95.
* Runner-up in the League Cup in 1996.
* Runner-up in the FA Cup in 1996.
x

* Trained in the Oxford United youth squad, he has been a professional since the 2nd of July 1986.  On the 29th of November of the same year he makes his debut in the league in a game against Norwich.
* In 1988 he sees the club promoted to the Second Division, and in this category he settles into the first team.
* On the 5th of July 1990 he is transferred to Middlesbrough for £375,000, immediately becoming a regular in the team's line-ups.

* Mustoe had an inspired season in which he could lead Middlesbrough for a large number of games despite being surrounded by world class players. He even took on the captaincy of the team during the forced absence of Pearson. In total he played 31 games and scored 3 goals.

503.name: Branca
pages: * The signing of Marco Branca is in response to the interest that Middlesbrough have shown in reinforcing their forward line going into the 97-98 season.  The Middlesbrough fans have placed their hopes in the Italian footballer in the bid for their team's speedy return to the Premier League.  And Branca hopes that he will have more luck than his fellow country-man Ravanelli, who saw the team relegated at the end of last season.

* A forward with a good finish and an acceptable technique.  Branca is a born goalscorer, a man who has the goal coursing through his veins. Skilful, strong and with an excellent header, he has a good shot with his good foot, the right, and is an expert at taking penalties.  Although his physical condition isn't that of years gone by, his experience allows him to take full advantage of his resources and know when he should attack the rival backs.

* Italian League Championship with Sampdoria (91). 
* Italian Cup with Sampdoria (88). 
* UEFA Cup Champion with Parma (95).
* Runner-up in the UEFA Cup with Inter (97).

* He has been an Olympic international three times. 
* He played in the Atlanta '96 Games.
* He made his debut in the Serie A on the 14th of September 1986 in a game between Udinese and Juventus (0-2).

* Last season he played in 21 games, 16 as a member of the starting squad, and managed five goals.  He looked like the guy destined to play at centre forward, by the excellent performance offered by Maurizio Ganz, the presence of Zamorano and the performance of Djorkaeff as the second striker made him the last in the pecking order established by the coaches.  Despite this lack of confidence, Branca responded very professionally and when he was called upon he scored some important goals.

505.name: Armstrong
pages: * Alun Armstrong signed for Middlesbrough during the 97-98 season. He hopes to be an important man in the battle to promotion.

* A young forward, he appears to be, however, a mature footballer.  He has an innate scent for goal, as well as being mentally and physically strong.  He is good in the air.  Given his youth, he has a ample margin for improvement and his future looks rosy.
* Top scorer at Stockport County in the 94-95 and 95-96 seasons.
x

* Originally from the lower ranks of Newcastle United, he signs as a professional in October 1993.  However, he never gets to play for the Magpies. 
* He is transferred to Stockport County in June 1994 for £50,000.  His debut takes place on the 13th of August 1994 against Cardiff City, scoring a goal.

* This young and hard-working forward had a great season for Stockport County.  His role in the successful promotion bid to the First Division was outstanding.  His beginning to the season was spectacular, scoring in almost every game, but towards the end of the league, he had a drought which left him with just 9 goals in 39 games.  Even so, in general terms it was a very good season.

506.name: Moore
pages: * After two seasons in which he has converted himself into one of the most important players at Middlesbrough, the recent years have been a true nightmare for the Irish international.  A very skilful player with a lot of talent, his chances should increase after Juninho's departure.  He has the capability to open up the game.

* Moore can play both as a wide midfielder or left wing. Hugging the wing, he takes advantage of his speed to get to the by-line or turn inwards to have a go with his left. Skilful with the ball at his feet, he has a nose for goal.  He doesn't hesitate to shoot at goal from anywhere, sometimes scoring some very spectacular goals. On the other hand, he is guilty of a certain irregularity in his game, as, at times, he disappears from the game. Without doubt, this lack of continuity is the main defect this young Irish player should correct.

* First Division Champion 95.
* Runner-up in the League Cup in 1996.
* Runner-up in the FA Cup in 1996.

* 5 full international appearances for Ireland. He made his debut in a friendly against the Check Republic on the 24th of April 1996 in Prague. His team lost 2-0.
* 6 times under-21 international, scoring 1 goal.

* A native of Dublin, Alan Moore trained in the Middlesbrough youth squad. A professional since the 5th of December 1991, he didn't make his debut with the first team until the 10th of April 1993 in a game against Everton. 
* He started the 93-94 season scoring two goals against Notts County in the first week of the league. At the end of the season he is, with 10 goals, the third top scorer of the team, beaten only by Wilkinson and Hendrie.

* Despite his important contribution to Middlesbrough's promotion to the Premier League in 1995, Alan Moore hardly counted in Bryan Robson's plans as he only played 17 games in the whole of the league. Even so, in his appearances he showed an undoubtable talent and almost always did well.

507.name: Beck
pages: * The signing of Mikkel Beck was one of Middlesbrough's reinforcements last year although he had less impact on the supporters than the well-known Ravanelli and Emerson. His scoring capability was not so good but he formed a strike partnership with the Italian international. Now, with the departure of Ravanelli and without his long shadow, Beck has the chance to make a name for himself in English football, having as team-mates players of the talent of Paul Merson, his new team-mate in the attack. He is a starter for Bryan Robson.

* He is a very quick footballer with an acceptable technical quality, who doesn't usually waste the chances that present themselves in the box. Tremendously aggressive, he won't fold in front of any defender, however hard he may be. A good finisher with his head, and opportunistic, he doesn't take much part in the elaboration of the moves, but he knows how to get goalside of the defenders. Given his youth, Mikkel Beck is a footballer with a good future ahead of him.

* Runner-up in the League Cup in 1996.
* Runner-up in the FA Cup in 1996.

* 13 full international caps for Denmark, scoring 3 goals. He made his debut on the 31st of May 1995 with a 0-1 win in a friendly against Finland played in Helsinki. Beck came on as a substitute at half-time for Peter Rasmussen and scored the only goal of the game in 74th minute.
* Present in the 96 European Championship in England, he played two games. He was a starter against Portugal (1-1) and in the came against Croatia he came on as substitute for Vilfort in the 58th minute.

* Trained in the Danish club B 1909, Beck was transferred in 1993 to the modest Fortune Cologne, a German Second Division team. A full international since 1995, he played in the 96 European Championship in England, although his performance in the two games he played was as discrete as Denmark's overall performance.
* After the European championship, as a free agent, he signed for Middlesbrough.

* One of Middlesbrough's incorporations last season, Beck eased his way into the side as the season progressed, forming a partnership with Fabrizio Ravanelli. He scored 5 goals in 25 games in his first year on English soil.

508.name: Pollitt
pages: x

* A very big goalkeeper, Michael Pollitt has good reflexes, self confidence and youth.  However, despite only being 25 years old he already has a lengthy career behind him, a career in which he has shown plenty of signs of his quality.
x
x
x
* Michael showed that he is an excellent goalie in the few games in which he took part. His excellent performance with the reserves team was the reason why the coach placed his confidence in him.

509.name: Pérez
pages: * Lionel Pérez was one of the new faces appearing at Sunderland going into the 96-97 season. Despite being virtually unknown, his work was recognised by the supporters who praised his great season after he replaced the injured Tony Coton.  If last year he started at a disadvantage, this year is the opposite as he is first choice for defending the Rokerites' goal.

* Lionel Pérez is a goalkeeper who is noted for his extraordinary reflexes between the posts, a quality which allows him to stop a lot of difficult shots. A relatively short keeper, he is quick coming out to forwards' feet and decisive when using his feet to clear. However, he has problems with high balls, an aspect of his game where he is vulnerable.
x
x

* The sporting career of Lionel Pérez began in the ranks of Nimes, a French Second Division side, arriving in their first team in the 89-90 season.
* At the end of the 90-91 season Mimes are promoted to the First Division. On the 20th of July Pérez made his debut in the top flight of French football in a game against Sochaux endeding a one-all draw. 
* Nimes, with Pérez as the first choice keeper in the 92-93 season, finished bottom of the table and returned to the Second Division.  However, the keeper was transferred to Girondins Bordeaux and he could stay in the First Division. 
* An understudy to Huard at Girondins, he signs for Laval going into the 94-95 season, but only plays two games in the Second Division. 
* On the 19th of August 1996 he is transferred to Sunderland for £200,000 to be, in principle, understudy to Tony Coton. His debut occurs on the 19th of October against Southampton.

* Last season Lionel Pérez began as the second choice at Sunderland but took advantage of an injury to Tony Coton to take over, producing some great performances for the club. At the end of the season, he was voted player of the year by the fans as a recognition of his merits. In total he played 29 games.

510.name: Coton
pages:
* Tony Coton arrived at Sunderland in order to reaffirm his status as one of the best goalies in English football.  Unfortunately, in a collision with the Southampton striker, Egil Ostenstad, he broke his leg and missed the rest of the season. 
* Now recovered from this fifth fracture, Coton is considering the possibility of regaining his place in the Sunderland team, a place lost to Lionel Pérez, who is currently the worthy occupant of the place. His experience could be important to help the team in its bid to return to the Premier League.

* A very experienced keeper, Tony Coton dominates all aspects of the game between the posts. He is an unspectacular goalkeeper, but very effective. He is sure of himself with the diagonal ball, also when coming out for aerial balls. With good reflexes, he reacts quickly to close-range shots and is outstanding for the effectiveness with which he stops powerful shots from a distance. Perhaps his weak point is coming out to strikers' feet, although his veteran status allows him to read the development of every ball and anticipate rival forwards.
x
* 1 international B appearance for England.

* Originally from the modest Mile Oak Rovers, a club of his native town who were playing in an amateur league, Tony Coton arrived at Birmingham City on the 13th of October 1978.  The goalie was centre-stage in his debut game, when he stopped a Sunderland penalty in a home game on the 27th of October 1980. 
* He had to fight firstly with Jeff Wealands and then with Jim Blyth to find a place in the first team, a place which he made his from the 82-83 season onwards. 
* Birmingham City had a disastrous start to the 84-85 season, and couldn't win any of their first seven games conceding 15 goals. This circumstance accelerated Tony Coton's move, who became a Watford player on the 17th of September 1984 in exchange for £300,000. 
* At Watford, Tony immediately replaced Steve Sherwood and became one of the most appreciated footballers at Vicarage Road. He  was voted "Player of the Year" three times. 
* Economic problems at Watford precipitated his transfer to Manchester City.  On the 20th of July 1990, the Maine Road club paid £1 million to acquire his services. 
* As a substitute for Andy Dibble in his first season at City, he only missed 4 games in the entire championship. 
* Coton was voted the safest goalie of the First Division in the 91-92 season and was called up for the England team in March 92. He never made his debut. Both Chris Woods and David Seaman stood in the way of his selection for the national team. Not even Graham Taylor, the manager who he had been under at Watford, gave him the chance to defend the England shirt. 
* In January 1996 Tony Coton was transferred to Manchester United for £500,000. Always in the shadow of Peter Schmeichel, he didn't play a single game for the Reds. And so, in the summer of 1996 he signed for Sunderland, recently promoted to the Premier League for £350,000. 
* His first game for the club is on the 17th of August against Leicester City.

* Coton started the league as the first choice at Sunderland in front of the Frenchman Pérez but in an unfortunate incident broke his leg, missing out on the rest of the championship. He had only played 10 games.

511.name: Summerbee
pages:
* Signed for Sunderland during the 97-98 season.
* Nicky Summerbee was very much a regular member of the starting line up at Maine Road,  either as a wide midfield player, or at full back, and is one of the few players who has followed in the footsteps of his father and his grandfather, who were both professional footballers.

* A skillful, wide midfielder, he shows great mobility down the right hand flank, getting up and down the line untiringly, finishing his runs off with a cross which looks to pick out rhe sides strikers. He is basically a right footed player with great speed and great reserves of stamina. Not being a good finisher he prefers to lay the ball off to better placed teammates to finish the job off. He works hard to win the ball back for the team and is continually to be found dropping back to help out his full back. In his early days at Swindon Town, when his manager was Glenn Hoddle, who is probably the man who has shown most faith in Summerbee, he  played nominally as a right back. However, in reality, he played more like a right sided midfield player, since Swindon operated eith 3 central defenders. During his time at Manchester City he has basically played as a natural right sided midfield player who finishes off his runs with a cross into the box. This, in some ways has hindered his progress, since, in previous seasons, he liked to occasionally get down the line and try something on his own, take on a defender or play a one two to get into a position from where he could then get in a telling final ball. In recent times at City he has basically been used to high balls into the opposition's penalty area, something which worked well when Niall Quinn, now at Sunderland, was the target man he was looking to pick out.
x

* International for England at "B" and under-21 level, he made his under-21 debut in the Toulon International Tournament on 7th June 1993, against the Portuguese under-21 side. He has made a total of 3 under-21 international appearances.

* He came through the junior ranks at Swindon Town to sign professional in July 1989. He made his debut on 3rd September 1989 against Wolverhampton Wanderers and scored his first goal in the professional game in a league game on 16th October 1992 against Notts County. 
* Manchester City signed him for £1,500,000 in June 1994, making his debut on 20th August 1994 against Arsenal. He scored his first league goal against Liverpool on 14th April 1995. 
* He is the son of ex-Manchester City star and England international Mike Summerbee. He gave his famous father a nasty shock when, as a youngster, he declared that he was a fan of Manchster United. Arch enemies, of course, of Manchester City.

* Summerbee completed a satisfactory third season at Manchester City, creating plenty of danger down his side of the pitch. Nevertheless the team's poor form also had a knock on effect on Summerbee's own performances although he continued to make an active contribution. His season got better following the arrival of Frank Clark, who asked him to make his presence felt more in the opponents penalty area. This advide helped him to go on to complete a good season personally. He played in a total of 44 games, scoring on 4 occasions.

512.name: Craddock
pages: x

* A central defender, Craddock usually occupies the right side of the defense. He has an acceptable individual technique allowing him to play the ball out of defence. Powerful when going for aerial balls he joins the attack at corners and free-kicks allowing him to score the occasional goal.
x
x
x

* Despite missing the start of the season due to injury, as the weeks went by Craddock found his way into the starting line-up. His performance was excellent allowing his inclusion in the Dream Team for the division, causing various clubs from higher divisions to take an interest in him. He scored his first goal on the 12th of April against Hartlepool.

513.name: Makin
pages: * Chris Makin is a young player who, last year, ventured out onto French territory, more exactly Olympic Marseilles, but has returned to England looking for some chances at Sunderland, the club who became interested in the progress of this footballer who was an under-21 international for his country not so long ago. Makin brings a lot of firmness to a team which needs to make a come-back after a somewhat irregular start to the league season. A starter for Peter Reid.

* Makin is a man who plays in defence but he can also play on either of the flanks although he is currently being aligned on the right. He is tough and always guarantees sensational defensive work. However, in attack he doesn't stand out much, limiting himself to protecting his zone.
x
* Makin has been an international for England at the under-21 level five times, as well as at the youth and schoolboy levels.

* Before moving to Olympic Marseilles, Makin played for Oldham Athletic and Wigan Athletic. 
* He returned to England, more exactly to Sunderland in the summer of 1997.
* Chris Makin played for Olympic Marseilles during the course of last season in the French First Division.

514.name: Ord
pages:
* A few years ago Richard Ord was one of those players who seemed to have a brilliant future ahead of him.  Richard had some great technical conditions which pointed to a complete footballer. These qualities led him to the England under-21 team. However, his performance dropped markedly, which in a short space of time shattered the expectations that had been placed in him.
* The arrival of Peter Reid to the Sunderland bench was an injection of optimism for Ord's career. The manager showed right from the start that he wanted to use this central defender and the player responded to his confidence with good play. One of the most consistent players in the last few seasons for the Rokerites, Ord will be a basic piece in Sunderland's attempt to reach the Premier League.

* A central defender who is very solid and consistent, Richard Ord is effective in all aspects of the defensive game. He is dominant in the aerial game, hard when tackling, and tough when marking. Despite his extraordinary bulk he is masterful with the ball at his feet.  Notwithstanding, he doesn't join in the attack much, something that he should work on given his undeniable qualities.
* First Division Champion 96.
* 3 times under-21 international for England.

* A product of the Sunderland youth squad, Richard Ord turned professional on the 14th of July 1987 and, on finishing his first season, he saw his team promoted to the Second Division. Ord was one of the most promising youngsters at the club and even defended the colours of the England under-21 side three times. 
* On the 22nd of February 1990 he was loaned to York City, where he played three games. 
* At the end of the 95-96 season Sunderland are proclaimed champions of the First Division and are automatically promoted to the Premier League. 
* Richard Ord is voted "Player of the Year" by the fans at the club. Even though there are rumours of his transfer to Manchester United, it never came to pass.

* Last season Richard Ord was one of the most regular players for the team eventually relegated to the First Division. Even so, his ability for playing at the highest levels of English football was demonstrated though he couldn't do anything about the fatal destiny. In total he played 33 games and scored 2 goals.

515.name: Williams
pages: * Darren Williams was a personal signing on the part of the Sunderland manager, Peter Reid, who bought him last year for very little money taking into account the enormous potential this player has. His maturity on the pitch is outstanding, important for a player so young. He is very hard-working and no one gave him any concessions when trying to enter the Sunderland team. He is there on his own merit. Williams hopes to be fundamental in his side's return to the Premier League.

* Williams is a man who plays in the midfield, right in the middle of all the action as he himself quoted when speaking of his preferences. Even so, he has also been aligned on the right of midfield and even at right back before the arrival of Chris Makin. He is hard-working and places himself into some dangerous positions, as has already been seen.
x
x

* Originally from the lower ranks of York City, Williams signs as a professional on the 21st of June 1995.  His first game was on the 26th of December 1994 against Blackpool. 
* Transferred to Sunderland for £50,000 on the 18th of October 1996.  His debut with the team is on the 11th of January 1997 against Arsenal. He scores his first goal as a professional against Leicester City.

* Although he had only played one game as a substitute, Sunderland had seen enough to sign him from York City. The beginning for this player was not easy but towards the end of the season he found a space for himself in the starting line-ups fielded by Peter Reid.  Williams ended the season with 11 games under his belt and 2 goals for the Rokerites.

516.name: Johnston
pages:
* Allan Johnston is a Scottish winger who has earned a name for himself in British football due to his great skill which has earned him great praises.After a brief spell in French football, Johnston joined Sunderland towards the end of the league but couldn't prevent the drop. 
* Johnston was the last player to score a goal at Roker Park, the team's old ground, before moving to the Stadium of Light. Reid hopes that with players such as Scott, Sunderland can turn the tables and return to the Premier League quickly.  Johnston is a regular either in the starting line-ups or on the bench.

* Johnston is a quick, vertical winger with a goalscoring instinct, these qualities in combination making him a dangerous opponent. He can also play in the midfield on one of the flanks. He has enough technical quality to beat the rival, producing some dangerous plays based on these characteristics.
x
x

* Trained at Hearts, Allan Johnston received the nickname "Magic" after a hat-trick scored against Glasgow Rangers at Ibrox in 1996. He was later transferred to the French team Rennes in the summer of 1996. 
* Reid signs him in April of 1997 for £550,000. His first game with the team is on the 5th of April against Newcastle United and he scores his first goal for the club against Everton on the 3rd of May, the last league goal scored at Roker Park. 
* His brother Sammy plays for Glenavon in Northern Ireland.

* After playing for the French side Rennes for the first part of last year, Johnston joins Sunderland, producing a good performance for the Rokerites in a vain attempt to prevent the team from relegation to the First Division. In total he played in six games and scored one goal.

517.name: Smith
pages: * Martin Smith was, in his time, a player who the whole world thought would become a regular in the English side. However, despite having had an outstanding season with Sunderland, he has never been able to meet the tremendous expectations placed in him.  Currently, he is being picked by Peter Reid to occupy the post of centre forward helped by Alex Rae, a position in which he can operate well thanks to his ability. For his youth and quality he should be important for Sunderland in their bid to get promoted to the Premier League on the first attempt.

* Martin Smith is a player who can play in several different positions. Hugging the left touchline in the midfield, he is skilful and quick enough to get by opposing defenders. He can also play as a forward, using these abilities together with his very powerful shot on goal and his ability in the air.
* First Division Champion with Sunderland in the 95-96.
x

* Originally from the lower ranks of Sunderland, Smith signs as a professional on the 9th of September 1992. His first game is on the 20th of October 1993 against Luton Town, scoring his first goal as a professional in this very same game.
* Smith had a somewhat disappointing season due to the low number of chances given to him, playing only 11 games during the league season.

518.name: Clark
pages: * Despite his youth, Lee Clark was one of the players who had been at Newcastle the most time, the club for which he has a true passion. However, the enormous amount of talent at the Magpies and the arrival of David Batty have shut the doors to the first team and so he asked for a transfer, a transfer which finally came about during the summer when he signed for Sunderland. With a lot of quality, Clark hopes to become a leader for the Rokerites in their bid to return to the Premier League.

* Lee Clark is a midfielder with a good playing vision, capable of distributing the ball fluidly and with good sense. Technically correct, he usually plays in front of the defence as a defensive centre half, although at times he plays nearer the wing. Clark helps out in defence in tasks of contention and, once the ball is regained, he offers himself as the first reference in the construction of the attacking play. However, his play is often too predictable, as he doesn't alternate a short ball with a long one. Clark hasn't scored as many goals as he is used to, due, in part, to the fact that he is playing in deeper positions.
* First Division Champion in 92-93.

* 11 under-21 international appearances for England. 
* 8 youth international appearances.

* A true Newcastle supporter, Lee Clark has often said that he couldn't play for another club.  However, after the 94-95 season there were rumours of a possible move, although he finally signed another contract with the club at St. James Park. 
* Raised in the Newcastle youth squad, Clark signed as a professional on the 9th of December 1989.  He makes his debut with the first team on the 27th of September 1990 in a game against Bristol City. Shortly afterwards (10/11/90) he scores the first goal of his career against Wolverhampton Wanderers.
* In 1994 he suffered a serious injury which kept him out the team for several months. After reappearing with the 94-95 season already underway he was outstanding in a game against Blackburn Rovers scoring the winner in a Cup tie replay. 
* A starter in the 95-96 season the arrival of David Batty led to his disappearance from the line-ups in favour of the ex Blackburn player. 
* He is known as "Jigsaw" by the fans at St. James Park. "Nash" and "Nasher" are other nicknames. 
* Clark is transferred to Sunderland in the summer of 1997 for £2.5 million.

* Once again the enormous amount of talent at Newcastle United closed the doors to the first team for Lee Clark, this circumstance limiting his appearances. He played 25 games, most of them coming on as a substitute. In the second part of the league he played some games from the start but the run didn't last long.

519.name: Gray
pages: * Two seasons ago there were three footballers with the surname Gray in the squad at Sunderland but only one, Micky, played all of the games of the championship. Micky, was chosen to represent the English First Division against an Italian selection and also figured in the the diaries of the big clubs in England. The reason: Micky Gray is a very talented player who will soon play in a bigger club. But until this moment comes, the fans at Roker Park will enjoy his performance as Sunderland try to return to the Premier League.

* Micky Gray is a very skilful midfielder, hard to stop when he has the ball at his feet. He usually plays hugging the left touchline, where he takes advantage of his turn where he covers a lot of ground. Quick - a battler - he doesn't shirk his defensive duties helping out the wide defender on his side. He fights for every ball and, once won back, distributes it with good judgement. Although he has a good shot on goal however he doesn't finish so well.  A very young footballer, he has an ample margin for improvement making him an interesting footballer for the future.
* First Division Champion 96.
x

* Born in Sunderland, Michael Gray was trained in the youth squad at Roker Park. He made it to the first team on the 1st of July 1992 and, in his first season, scored two goals in 27 league games. 
* In the 95-96 season his brilliant performances awakened the interest of Premier League clubs and he is chosen for the friendly game between a selection from the English First Division and another one from the Italian Serie B. However, once Sunderland earned promotion, he stays with the Rokerites.

* He operated in his usual position on the left-hand side of midfield for most of the campaign, but switched to left back following the arrival of Chris Waddle. Gray scored the club's first goal of the season away at Nottingham Forest and other important strikes at Newcastle and at home against Manchester United.

520.name: Melville
pages: * The good performance of Andy Melville during the last two seasons has forced Peter Reid to change his plans, incorporating him in the Rokerites' line-ups alongside Richard Ord and forming a very solid partnership in the defensive axis of Sunderland. Once more he will be important in the attempt to return to the Premier League.

* A central defender who is outstanding for his dominance in the aerial game, the presence of Andy Melville in the rival box is the forerunner of danger, as the Sunderland player is a specialist at scoring goals with his head at set-plays. In defensive tasks Melville is solid, but the quick skilful forwards cause him problems due to his lack of pace. With the ball at his feet on the other hand he is comfortable and shows good judgement when distributing it.

* Welsh Cup Champion 89. 
* First Division Champion 96.

* 27 full international caps for Wales. 
* 1 international B appearance. 
* 2 times under-21 international.

* A Welsh international, Andy Melville was trained in the youth squad at Swansea City, the main team of his hometown, where he turned professional on the 25th of July 1986. 
* In 1989 the team was proclaimed Welsh Cup Champion. 
* An undisputed starter since the 86-87 season, he was transferred to Oxford City on the 23rd of July 1990 for £275,000. 
* A player at Sunderland since the 9th of August 1993, he made his debut in the League on the 14th of August with a 5-0 defeat against Derby County. He would have to wait until the 6th of April 1994 to score his first goal for the Rokerites, although it didn't help prevent the team falling to Millwall (2-1).

* Melville started the season with a fixed place in the side, forming a sensational partnership with Richard Ord.  He was almost always available for selection except for an injury towards the end of the championship. In total he played 30 games and scored 2 goals.

521.name: Scott
pages: * Martin Scott is one of the biggest idols of the fans at Sunderland, a good example for the young footballers at the club. Since his arrival in December 1994 "Scotty" has always played from the start except when injured; as was the case last year, this time around he will be an undisputed starter. His absence was much felt last season, and now recovered, he will be a key player in Sunderland's bid to return to the Premier League.

* A left back who covers a lot of ground who has a great attacking presence, Martin Scott is generous with his physical effort during the ninety minutes. Solid in defence, he is characterised by his anticipation when halting the progress of the rivals. A good marker, he makes constant incorporations into attack, supported by the power of his left foot. He is also dangerous when taking direct free-kicks and takes on the responsibility for taking the penalties. A few misses haven't effected his confidencel.

* First Division Champion 96. 
* Fourth Division Champion 89.
x

* Martin Scott was trained in the youth squad of Rotherham United and made his debut with the first team in the 84-85 season. However, he would not become a professional until the 10th of January 1986. After dropping to the Fourth Division in 1988, he took part in the campaign to return to the Third, although he never got to enjoy the status of an undisputed starter. 
* On the 5th of December 1990 he was transferred to Bristol City for £200,000 and since his arrival has played regularly in the team. 
* He is a Sunderland player since the 23rd of December 1994. The club at Roker Park paid £750,000 for the best left back the team has had since the days of Joe Bolton. 
* He made his debut at home on the 26th of December 1994 where underland and Bolton Wanderers drew 1-1. 
* In the 95-96 season Scott became the third top scorer of the team with six goals, four of them coming from the penalty spot. Sunderland are promoted to the Premier League for the first time in their history.

* Martin Scott was the first choice left back at Sunderland during last season but a series of set-backs limited him to just 15 games in the league. Obviously, his absence was felt by the team which finally were relegated to the First Division.
