522.name: Aiston
pages:
* Sam Aiston is one of the most promising footballers in his age group in England. He just needed a few appearances in the Premier League to be considered as one of the stars of the future. His sparks of class announce the explosion of an extraordinary player. There are even people who compare him with the selfsame Chris Waddle. 
* Even so,  he has a difficult road ahead although he has the ability to leave his mark on the Rokerites and, who knows, even get to the English national team. He is not a starter but he will have his chances as the League progresses.

* A midfielder who covers a lot of ground, Sam Aiston can play just as well on either of the flanks, although he tends to operate on the left.  He is a very quick footballer who likes to take on rival defenders and beat them for speed thanks to his extraordinary dribbling ability.  With an exquisite technique, he is outstanding for the accuracy of his passes and his attacking nature. His capacity for breaking through allows him to create a lot of chances for his team-mates, but he should improve his goal contribution, as he doesn't finish so well. Still very young, he has the talent to be a great player is his able to maintain his astounding progression.
* First Division Champion 96.
x

* A native of Newcastle, Sam Aiston was trained in the youth squad of St. James Park, although there were several clubs interested in him, amongst them Everton, Ipswich, Wimbledon and Swindon. 
* At Newcastle Sam combined his studies with games in the team coached by Colin Suggett, a former Sunderland player. After Suggett's departure Chris McMenemy took charge of the team and showed that he was prepared to align Aiston, but only if he dedicated himself completely to football. 
* And so Sam was claimed by Sunderland and accepted their offer immediately. On the 14th of July 1995 he joined the team at Roker Park and started to play for the youth team. 
* He made his first team debut on the 2nd of September 1995, with a 3-0 defeat at the Ipswich Town ground. His debut was a surprise. 
* A student of English Literature, History and Theology, he received offers from several universities and even had the opportunity to study at Boston in the United States with a grant. However, he signed a new contract with Sunderland in November 1995 and his rapid rise to the first team led him to plumb for a sporting career. 
* On the 21st of February 1997 he was loaned to Chester City, playing his first game for the club one day later against Mansfield Town.

* Aiston couldn't figure in Reid's plans last season, only player in two games as a substitute.  Fortunately, he was given the opportunity to go to Chester City as a loan player, where he became on of the supporters' idols. In total he played 14 games for this club.

523.name: Phillips
pages: x
* An opportunist striker, with a real eye for goal, he knows how to get on the blind side of defenders inside the penalty area. His intelligence makes him a very difficult player to mark.
x
x
x

* Last season he played in 16 games, making 13 starting appearances, scoring four goals. He was one of the most popular and well appreciated players with the culb's supporters, despite the fact that injuries prevented him from playing  more regularly.

525.name: Rae
pages:
* Alex Rae was one of the novelties in the Sunderland squad going into the 96-97 season.  However, the midfielder, who arrived after a successful spell of a few years at Millwall, wasn't able to make the impact that was hoped for by a team that needed goals. 
* This year a serious opportunity is being given to Rae, playing as a second forward just behind Smith. In this more advanced position, Reid hopes to remedy the goal drought that the Rokerites are suffering. It could be the most important year of his spell at Sunderland. He hopes to crown it with promotion to the Premier League.

* Alex Rae is a midfielder who stands out for his scoring efficiency although he can also play as a second striker but playing deeper than the centre forward. The power of his right-foot shot creates a lot of problems for the rival keepers both in play and at set pieces, where he is a true specialist.Rae is also characterised by constant battling during the course of the game, allowing him to help out in winning the ball back. His crosses create a lot of chances for his team-mates. However, his performances are guilty of a certain irregularity, although at any time he can connect with one of his awesome shots and score a goal.
x

* 2 times international B for Scotland. 
* 8 times under-21 international.

* A native of Glasgow, Alex Rae was trained in the ranks of Bishopbriggs before moving to the Scottish team Falkirk in 1987. From the 88-89 season onwards he became an undisputed starter. 
* His transfer to Millwall went through on the 20th of August 1990. The price: £100,000.  Under the management of Bruce Rioch first, then later Mick McMarthy, Rae always enjoyed a place in the starting line-up and became the team's top scorer two seasons running (94-95 and 95-96). In both seasons he was included in the First Division Dream Team by his fellow professionals.
* In his last season with the Lions he was made captain in the absence of Keith Stevens. 
* In the summer of 1996 he is transferred to Sunderland, recently promoted to the Premier League, for £750,000.  His first game with the team is on the 4th of September against Newcastle United. He scores his first goal in the Premier League against Middlesbrough from the penalty spot on the 14th of October.
* Alex Rae didn't have many opportunities at Sunderland last year. His campaign was limited to 23 games scoring only 2 goals.

526.name: Hall
pages:
* For nearly ten years Gareth Hall belonged to the Chelsea squad. His start at Stamford Bridge announced an arrival of a great footballer who even managed to make his debut for the Welsh team at a very tender age. However, the hopes placed in him were never fully met and little by little he was forced onto the bench at Chelsea. 
* His spell at Sunderland has helped him re-launch his career a little which in recent times had fallen away. Last year he became a fundamental player for Peter Reid and played 30 games with the Rokerites. Unfortunately, he has been unable to keep up this magnificent run this year.

* Although his technical characteristics are perfectly adapted to the position of right back, in recent times Gareth Hall has tended to play on the left of the defence. In any case, versatility is one of his biggest virtues, as he can also play at centre back or even in midfield.  A good marker, he joins in the attack decisively at the slightest opportunity to try out his powerful shot from a distance.

* Second Division Champion 89. 
* First Division Champion 96. 
* Full Members Cup Champion 90.

* 9 full international appearances for Wales  He made his debut on the 23rd of March 1988 in a game against Yugoslavia. 
* 1 under-21 international appearance. 
* Schoolboy international.

* Gareth Hall is a product of the Chelsea youth squad, joining in September of 1984.  A professional since the 25th of April 1986, he had the chance to make his debut in the league with the first team against Wimbledon on the 5th of May 1987. 
* A full Welsh international since March 1988, he was one of the members of the Chelsea squad that won the Second Division title in 1990, although his appearances were few and far between. 
* His limited appearances in the first team cut short his progress, and only injuries to team-mates allowed him to enter into the Blues' team. 
* On the 20th of December 1995 he was loaned to Sunderland. However, in the first few days of 1996 Peter Reid decided to incorporate him into the Rokerites permanently. 
* He made his debut for Sunderland on the 23rd of December 1995, with a 3-1 defeat against Derby County.

* Hall started last season as the first choice right back at Sunderland, performing his role perfectly.  What's more, his versatility allowed him to continue in the starting line-up although most of his appearances were on the right. In total he played 30 games for the Rokerites.

527.name: Agnew
pages: * Steve Agnew is a player who has not had time to show off his undoubted qualities. His presence was felt by Sunderland in the year in which they were promoted to the Premier League as well as his absence last year, when they returned from whence they came. He is not a starter at the moment but his presence will be important to fulfil the anxious desire of the Rokerites' supporters to return to the Premier League, supporters who have always appreciated Agnew's work.

* A midfielder with a powerful stride and attacking presence, Steve Agnew usually plays on the right of midfield. He has good playing vision and a particular gift for the diagonal ball. He can play both in short or long range balls and is a very dangerous man near the goal. He also participates in the defensive work, winning back a lot of balls thanks to his physical effort.
* First Division Champion 96.
x

* Agnew started his career as an apprentice at Barnsley in 1992 and signed his first professional contract on the 10th of November 1983 on his eighteenth birthday. He made his debut in the league as a substitute against Charlton Athletic played at Oakwell on the 14th of April 1984. 
* In the 85-86 season he suffered a very serious injury that almost put an end to his sporting career. However, he made a successful reappearance in the following season taking up a place in the midfield leaving his original position as a forward. 
* For four consecutive seasons he was one of Barnsley's most important players. 
* On the 25th of June 1991 he was signed by Blackburn Rovers for £700,000. After playing two league games however, the midfielder suffered a very serious injury to his ankle which kept him out of the game until the end of the season. 
* After a brief loan spell at Portsmouth in November 1992, Steve Agnew was transferred to Leicester City on the 9th of February 1993 for £250,000. In the summer of 1994 they celebrated the club's promotion to the Premier League.
* Agnew started the 94-95 season at Leicester, but on the 11th of January 1995 he was once again on the move, this time to Sunderland, for £250,000. He made his debut on the 14th of January during his team's visit to Oldham Athletic (0-0) and on the 25th of February he scored his first goal against Southend United. 
* In the 95-96 season he scored two goals against Manchester United in an FA Cup tie, although in the end Sunderland were knocked out in the replay. As a compensation, the Roker Park team finished the league as First Division Champions with automatic promotion to the Premier League.

* Once more injuries got in the way of Steve Agnew, who saw his season limited to 16 games and two goals. Therefore, his contribution in rescuing Sunderland was minimal, unfortunate for the Rokerites who felt his absence.

528.name: Ball
pages: * The Sunderland captain is also one of the fans' biggest idols.  His commitment to the club's colours mean that he offers the best of himself each matchday. For "Bally", the nickname by which he is known, there are no impossible games. For this reason he tries to instil his untouchable spirit into his team-mates. Whether in defence or in the midfield, he takes on the responsibility of dragging the team to victory. Peter Reid has full confidence in him. In fact, he acts as an extension of the coach on the field. He is respected by the players and adored by the people in the terraces. Nobody felt Sunderland's relegation more deeply so it is to be expected that he will give his all to lead the team back to the Premier League.

* Although his usual position is that of centre back, when Kevin Ball has played in midfield his performance has been satisfactory.  A man with plenty of character, he burdens himself with the responsibility of pulling the rest of the team along. An extraordinary marker, hard when tackling, dominant in the air and someone who rival forwards find hard to beat, he oozes energy in every minute of the game. He steals balls, makes interceptions, aids his team-mates and joins in the attack decisively, creating danger with his attempts. A tenacious footballer, he never gives up a game as lost nor a ball unreachable. His presence on the pitch is always an extra injection of courage for the team.
* First Division Champion 96.
x

* Originally from the Coventry City junior team, Kevin Ball signed as a professional for Portsmouth on the 6th of October 1982 and in 1987 contributed to the club's promotion to the First Division. However, they returned to the Second Division one year later. 
* Ball has been a Sunderland player since the 16th of July 1990 for whom the club paid £350,000. His arrival was well received by the fans, who saw him as one of the best representations of the "Rokerite" spirit. Years later he would be made captain of the team and in 1996 the team could, at last, celebrate promotion to the Premier League with Peter Reid at the helm.
* Despite producing a typical season in his usual line at Sunderland, Ball couldn't avoid the team's drop to the First Division. In total this brave footballer played in 32 games.

529.name: Quinn
pages:
* Niall Quinn was the most expensive signing Sunderland made going into the 96-97 season.  With his incorporation it was hoped to reinforced the forward line with an effective and recognised goalscorer with a broad experience in the Premier League. 
* Unfortunately - though his spell at the club started very well - a very serious injury kept him out the team until the end of the season, denying the club a man who was supposed to mark their attacking game. His absence was sorely felt and the club was eventually relegated to the First Division.

* The header is the most notable feature of Niall Quinn's game. A battering ram type forward, very large and very strong, he takes advantage of these qualities to open gaps in the rival area coming through powerfully from the back. Although he has some technical failings, he is able to protect the ball efficiently when he drifts over to the wings to receive and he can hold onto it while he waits for his team-mates to join in the attack. Blessed with good chest control, he uses his corpulence to hide the ball away from rival defenders. A brave fighter, he makes up for his limitations with full commitment and his presence near to the rival goal creates a lot of danger.

* League Cup Champion 87. 
* Charity Shield Medal 89.

* 60 times full international for the Republic of Ireland. 12 goals. He made his debut as a substitute on the 25th of May 1986 against Iceland. 
* 2 times international B - 3 goals. 
* 6 times under-21 international - 1 goal.

* Born in Dublin in 1966, Niall Quinn was rejected by Malcolm Macdonald, the manager at Fulham, before joining Arsenal.  A professional since the 30th of November 1983, he made his debut in the league on the 14th of December 1985 against Liverpool at Highbury. He scored a goal and Arsenal won 2-0.
* From the 86-87 season on he settled into George Graham's young team, but couldn't finish the season with a league title despite the fact that Arsenal were at the top of the table for a good part of the championship. 
* In 1987 Arsenal were proclaimed League Cup Champions after beating Liverpool in the final 2-1. However, the signing of Alan Smith in the summer of this year forced him onto the substitutes' bench the following season.
* On the 21st of March 1990 Quinn was transferred to Manchester City for £800,000, making his debut at Maine Road against Chelsea (1-1) and, months later, represented Ireland in the Italian World Cup, scoring a goal against Holland. 
* In the 90-91 season he scored 20 league goals. 
* In November 1993 he suffered a serious crossed ligament injury which almost brought about his retirement.  As a consequence he failed toattend the United States World Cup. 
* He reappeared in the first game of the 94-95 season with a 3-0 defeat at the hands of Arsenal at Highbury. With the signing of Uwe Rosler and the presence of Paul Walsh Quinn was forced onto the bench at Maine Road. At the end of the season there were rumours of his departure from Manchester City - even receiving an offer from Sporting Lisbon for £1,800,000. 
* In May 1996 Manchester City's relegation to the First Division is confirmed. Months later Niall Quinn is transferred to Sunderland, recently promoted to the Premier League, for £1,300,000.  At Roker Park he coincides with Peter Reid, his old manager at Maine Road. 
* Quinn suffers a serious injury to his knee at the beginning of the season. His debut takes place on the 17th of August against Leicester City. He scores his first two goals against Nottingham Forest a week later.  He doesn't reappear until the 5th of April against Newcastle United.

* Niall Quinn started last season very well at Sunderland, scoring three goals in 7 games but then a serious injury to his ankle meant that he missed all league games until April, when he reappeared and gave the team a reference in the rival box. Unfortunately for the Rokerites, it didn't help them avoid the drop. In total Quinn played 12 games and scored 2 goals in league competition.

530.name: Bridges
pages: * Michael Bridges is one of Sunderland's big hopes for the near future. It is true that little by little he is progressing and his game is adapting to the stresses of the upper divisions of English football. He figures fairly often in Reid's plans although most often as a substitute. It will only be a question of time before he makes his definitive breakthrough into the Rokerites starting eleven.

* Blessed with the scoring instinct of the great strikers, Michael Bridges is a very complete forward. Quick, powerful, with good ball control, he shows a maturity in his game out of proportion with his youth. A great finisher, he doesn't often forgive in the box, making him an interesting player for the future.
* First Division Champion 96.
x

* Michael Bridges is a product of the Sunderland youth squad. After impressing with his extraordinary goalscoring capacity in the lower ranks of the club, he turned professional on the 9th of November 1995.  His debut with the first team took place on the 10th of February 1996, after a substitution in a home game against Port Vale (0-0). 
* He scores his first goal in the First Division on the 27th of February 1996 in the Rokerites' visit to Southend United.  Months later, Sunderland celebrate promotion to the Premier League.

* Bridges was able to continue his progress during last year as well as figuring fairly often in Peter Reid's schemes at Sunderland. One of his best games was against Everton, managing to score two goals against the Toffees in his team's 3-1 win. In total he played 25 games and scored 3 goals.

531.name: Scully
pages:
* Signed for QPR in March 1998. 
* Tony Scully, who learnt his trade in the youth ranks at Crystal Palace, is a player whose quality hasn't gone unnoticed by the Republic of Ireland's coaching staff who have already given him his chance with the under-21 side and who will certainly have him very much in mind for the future with regards to the full international team. He has so far had very few opportunities to show what he can do and has had to change clubs in order to try to make the breakthrough. His latest destiny is Manchester City who signed him in the hope of him being able to help the the club win back their top flight status.

* A midfielder who operates down the right hand side, Tony Scully has a great future. A basically attack minded player, he links up well with the forwards and manages to get plenty of good service through to them. However he can also create plenty of danger of his own, making decisive runs from deep positions, although this potential threat is yet to be transformed into goals.
x
* A Republic of Ireland Under-21 international.

* A product of the youth set up at Crystal Palace, he signed as a professional in December 1993. He made his league debut on 26th August 1995 against Charlton Athletic.
* He was loaned out to Bournemouth in October 1994, making his debut on 15th October 1994 against Brentford.
* Manchester City signed him in the summer of 1997.

* There is very little that can be said about Tony Scully's campaign, given that the young Irishman made just one league appearance all season, and that only came in the final minute of the game between Crystal Palace and Barnsley. Nevertheless he did have an outstanding season for the reserves.

532.name: Kulcsar
pages:
* Signed for QPR during the 97-98 season.
* George Kulcsar is a man who, despite being born in Hungary, has been raised almost completely in Australia, the country for who he is an international, and furthermore, he was a regular feature of the line-ups of Terry Venables, the national coach. His work is not always very much appreciated but he is important for the team, above all, when it comes to defending. He will have his opportunities during the course of the league to find a place in the starting eleven.

* Kulcsar is a midfielder of defensive cut, who doesn't stop running for the full 90 minutes and who is very much appreciated by his coach due to his enormous capacity for work. He usually joins in the attack, supporting his teammates but he is not a born goalscorer.
x
* Kulcsar has represented the Australian team 3 times.

* Coming from the Belgian club Royal Antwerp, George Kulcsar signs for Bradford City in March 1997 after his transfer fee, set at £100,000, had been paid. His first game with the team takes place on the 8th of March against Grimsby Town.

* After playing 17 games with Royal Antwerp, Kulcsar is signed by Bradford City, where he is good in the contentious tasks in midfield, earning the appreciation of the fans during the nine games that he plays for the Bantams.

533.name: Rowland
pages:
* Keith Rowland was transfered to QPR on the 29th of January 1998.
* Harry Redknapp had a special liking for Keith Rowland. The Hammers' boss was, in fact, the man who discovered him and who gave him his first big opportunity. As a result, although, during his time at West Ham, he did not enjoy too much regular first team football.

* Although, during the majority of his career, he has played at left back, last season Rowland demonstrated that he can adapt perfectly to the left hand side of the midfield, a position where he is helped out by his superb left foot. A versatile player, he is a good passer of the ball, and creates plenty of goalscoring chances for his teammates, although he himself doesn't stand out for his ability to find the back of the net. He likes to get forward into the attack, although, occasionally, he is slow to get back into his defensive position, something he needs to try and work on.
x

* 12 full international appearances for Northern Ireland. He made his debut in September 1993 in a game against Latvia. 
* 2 "B" international appearances. 
* A youth international.

* The development of Keith Rowland's playing career has a lot to do with Harry Redknapp, the man who discovered him in the youth ranks at Bournemouth, and who gave him his league debut as well as taking him to West Ham a few years later. 
* A professional with Bournemouth since 2nd October 1989, he played his first league game on 17th August 1991, against Darlington. 
* A first team regular since 91-92, he was loaned out to Coventry City on 8th January 1993, going on to play in two Premier League games.
* Harry Redknapp, Billy Bonds assistant at West Ham, was instrumental in taking him to the Hammers. The transfer fee for the deal, which was finalized on 6th August 1993, was set at 110,000 pounds. 
* He made his debut at Upton Park in the first game of the 93-94 season. West Ham lost against Wimbledon 0-2. 
* Rowland found it difficult to force his way into the side, with David Burrows establishing himself as the man to replace Julian Dicks in the left back spot. 
* In April 1994 Keith was left with a broken leg as a consequence of a clash with John Ebbrell of Everton. 
* Julian Dicks'return to Upton Park in October 1994 represented another obstacle that Rowland was faced with in order to get into Harry Redknapp's side.
* He scored his first Premier League goal on 16th November 1996, against Newcastle at Saint James' Park (1-1).

* It was difficult for Rowland to make himself a regular member of the side, although when he did play he did a satisfactory job. He played in eleven games from the start, and in one of those, against Arsenal in January, was named Man of the Match, despite the fact that West Ham lost. He also made a number of appearances for Northern Ireland and managed to score his first goal in the Premier League against Newcastle in November.

534.name: Graham
pages: * Mark Graham is one of the young players who has come through the ranks at QPR in recent years, and of whom great things are expected. He has everything he needs to go on to be a success, and is also a very versatile player. His good performances last season saw him playing in the side quite often, and even won him an international call up to play a few games for  Northern Ireland's "B" team. A player for the future, he will no doubt gaet his chances as the season progresses.

* Graham is a young product of the QPR youth systeam who can play in a number of different positions all over the park. At the beginning of his carrer he played as a winger, although he has been converted into a right back with some success, and on occasions, has even played as a midfielder. A hard player when he goes in to win the ball, he also shows some good touches when he is in possession.
x
* Graham has represented Northern Ireland as a schoolboy international, as a youth international, and has made 3 "B" appearances, the first of those appearances coming against Portugal.
* After coming through the youth ranks at QPR, Graham signed as a professional on 26th May 1993. He had to wait for his debut until 21st September 1996 against Swindon Town.

* Graham made 18 appearances for QPR during the course of last season, the majority of those coming at right back, a position that, at the time, was new to him. His good peformances gave the club's coaching staff high hopes for the player in the future, and also saw him achieve international recognition, with Northern Ireland's "B" team.

535.name: Peacock
pages:
* After a number of inconsistent years with Chelsea, Gavin Peacock's failure to force his way into the plans of Blues' manager Ruud Gullit has seen him move on to carve out a future for himself elsewhere. Although Gullit had said at the start of the season that all the players in his squad would get their chance, Peacock became the the forgotten man of Stamford Bridge, even to the point where he wasn't even given a squad number for the season.
* Realising that he was unlikely to get even the slightest of chances to show what he could do at Chelsea, Peacock moved across London to join QPR. At the club he teamed up with his ex-Chelsea teammate John Spencer to form an excellent striking duo. Following the acquisition of Mike Sheron, Peacock will presumably take up a deeper position, playing as a link up man between the midfield and the two man strikers. He is an automatic choice for Stewart Houston.

* Gavin Peacock is an attacking midfielder, to the point where he can also play as a striker. He possesses a good powerful shot with his left foot and, technically speaking, is a very correct footballer. He makes good runs into the box from deep positions which take defenders by surprise. He is a good passer of the ball, showing thoughtful and efficient distribution. However, he makes only a very limited defensive contribution.
* First Division winners medal 92-93.

* One "B" international appearance for England.
* 6 youth international appearances.
* Schoolboy international.

* The son of ex-Charlton Athletic  player Keith Peacock, Gavin came through at Queens Park Rangers where he signed his first professional contract on 19th November 1984. However he had to wait until 29th November 1986 to make his debut in a game against Sheffield Wednesday.
* On 5th October 1987, he was transfered to Gillingham for £40,000. He immediately made himself a regular in the side.
* His next destination was to be Bournemouth. The transfer deal was sealed on 16th August 1989. The fee: £250,000.
* On 30th November 1990 he arrived at Newcastle United in exchange for £150,000. While with the St. James' Park club, he helped the Magpies win promotion to the Premier League.
* He became a Chelsea player on 12th August 1993 and two days later made his debut in a 1-2 defeat at Stamford Bridge against Blackburn Rovers, with Peacock scoring the Blues' only goal  of the game. He ended his first season at Chelsea as the club's top scorer with 14 goals  (8 in the league and 6 in Cup competitions).
* During the 94-95 season, he was named captain of the side, in the absence of Dennis Wise.
* On 4th February 1996 he scored his first hat trick for Chelsea, the third of his Career, in a game against Middlesbrough at Stamford Bridge. Six years had gone by since a Chelsea player had managed to score three times in one game. The last to do so had been Kerry Dixon in May 1990.
* He was transfered to QPR on 22nd 1996. His debut came on 23rd of that same month against Reading, while he opened his goalscoring account for Rangers on 7th December.

* Completely absent from Rudd Gullit's line up at Chelsea, Peacock had to find himself a new club where at least he would be able to get regular first team football. After having a month on loan at QPR, he finally joined the west London club on a permanent basis and had an immediate impact, forming a partnership with another ex-Chelsea player , John Spencer. In total he made 27 appearances, scoring 5 goals..

536.name: Murray
pages: * A very young player, Murray has already played as an under-21 international for England, and is a player with a very promising future ahead of him, above all taking into account the tremendous performances he put together at Carlisle United before being transfered to QPR. Initially he didn't get too many opportunities with the Londoners, but during the course of last season he managed to break into the side and did enough to make himself a regular member of the starting line up. At present he remains in the side and certainly doesn't seem prepared to give his place up.

* Murray is a midfielder who can do a job either as a right sided midfield man, or at the heart   of things in the middle of the park. A fast, dynamic player who makes good forward runs into the penalty area, he also possesses a powerful shot. However when he plays in the centre of of the midfield his ability to get forward is restricted, taking on the responsibilities of directing operations from the middle of the park, a job he does with composure, keeping the game flowing, always apparently picking out the right pass at the right time. Physically, he lacks the strength to always come out on top in clashes with opponents, although he will never shirk a challenge.
x
* Murray has played for England as a youth international and has also made 2 appearances for the Under-21 side.

* After coming through the youth ranks at Carlisle United, Murray signed as a profesisional in June 1994. His first game for the club came on 27th December 1993 against Darlington while he opened his goalscoring account on 9thDecember 1995 against Hull City.
* He was transfered to QPR in March 1996 for £300,000, making his debut on 5th May 1996 against Nottingham Forest, in the final game of the 95-96 season.

* Murray enjoyed a sensational season with QPR, his first full campaign with Stewart Houston's side. He played in 32 games, and found the back of the net 5 times. In every game he played he showed tremendous ability and outstanding composure for such a young player. He made his debut for the England under-21 side.

537.name: Barker
pages:
* For his leadership qualities and his presence out on the park, Simon Barker is the heart and soul of QPR. Ray Wilkins showed tremendous faith in him, something which made him very much the manager's man out on the park, a situation which hasn't changed with Stewart Houston in charge. He became a much better player under the guidance of the ex -England international, Wilkins, an improvement has seen him develop into an almost constant presence, popping up all over the park.
* His tremendous performances made him almost irreplaceable for the side, although at present he is not a regular member of Stewart Houston's side. However, now in the final year of his contract, and, perhaps, nearing the end of his time at QPR, Simon Barker would be a very satisfied footballer if the club were to gain promotion back to the Premier League.

* Barker is a player who operates in midfield from where he pulls the strings for QPR, moving all over the park and picking the ball up in all kinds of positions, playing the ball off to his teammates with his efficient, simple, short passing game. He has a powerful shot in his right foot while he is also a very forceful player when he goes in to win the ball, winning a tremendous amount of possession back for the side.
* He was top goalscorer for Blackburn Rovers during the  86-87 season.
* He has made 4 Under-21 international appearances for England, making his debut against Israel in Tel-Aviv on 27th February 1985

* A player who came through the ranks at Blackburn Rovers, where he signed professional in 1982. He made his league debut on 2nd October 1983 against Oldham Athletic, and scored his first goal for the club against Newcastle United on 26th January 1983.
* He was transfered to QPR in July 1988 for £400,000. He made his debut for his new club on 27th August 1988 against Manchester United, while he scored his first league goal on 31st December 1988.

* In his ninth season at the club Simon Barker has proved himself to be an almost irreplaceable  member of the side for his manager. For the fourth year in succesion he played more than 30 games for the club, making, to be more precise, 38 appearances, scoring 5 goals. His presence in the side was always well appreciated by his teammates for whom he was always a positive influence.

538.name: Jones
pages:
* Signed for QPR in March 1998.
* A real character, Vinny Jones' career has been full of all sorts of anecdotes and incidents. He is, without doubt, the hardest player in the  history of English football and, with Wimbledon, he has found the perfect home for his peculiar personality. He is such a symbolic figure at the club, that, at the beginning of the 94-95 season he was named captain. Of Welsh descent, Jones is now trying to instill the same spirit into the Welsh international side, attempting to bring to the side his own particular  blend of pride and passion.

* Vinny Jones' game is more about fighting spirit than quality. Either at  the heart of the defence or in midfield, Jones shows his hold repertoire of tackles, physical challenges and even wild lunges, with just one aim: to win the ball from the opposition. His attacking contribution is limited to his participation at dead ball situations, where he tries to make the most of his physical power to get in efforts on goal. He also stands out for his incredibly long throw-ins which are practically like corners. His aggressive style of play is evident in everything he does. He is, undoubtedly, a player who will never stop battling and will never give anything up as lost.

* F.A. Cup winners medal 1987-88.
* Second Division winners medal 1989-90.
* 9 full international appearances for Wales.

* Whist playing for Weakstone, Dave Basset moved in to sign him for Wimbledon on 20th November 1986. The fee: 10,000  pounds. 
* He made his debut at the City Ground in a game between Nottingham Forest and Wimbledon on 22nd November 1986. In his second game for the Dons, Vinny Jones scored the winning goal against Manchester United.
* In his first eight games in the First Division he scored four goals. 
* In 1988 he was an ever present in Wimbledon's F.A. Cup run which ended with the south London club lifting the trophy after beating Liverpool. From that moment on Wimbledon became known as The Crazy Gang. Photographs of Wimbledon's outrageous victory celebrations, with Vinny as the ring-leader, were splashed across England's newspapers.
* On 20th June 1989, Vinny Jones surprised everybody when he moved to Leeds United. His valuation in the transfer market had risen to 650,000 pounds. 
* On 13th September 1990 he was transfered to Sheffield United for 600,000 pounds. One year later, on 30th August 1991, Chelsea paid out 575,000 pounds to take him to Stamford Bridge. In the fifth round of the Cup,  Chelsea played against his previous club Sheffield United, a game in which Jones was shown the yellow card after just three second, leaving ex-England international Stevens with a permanent injury.
* As a Chelsea player, he published a book called "Soccer Hard Man", a collection of tricks for defenders to use in order to put opponents off their game. Amongst other things, Vinny "advised" defenders to poke their fingers in the eyes of opponents, and to grab them by the testicles. Publication of the final "work" sparked tremendous controversy in England, And resulted in Vinny being punished by both his club as well as the Football Association. 
* He has the worst disciplinary record in the Premier League. Up to the end of the 94-95 season he had been shown 53 yellow cards and sent off 5 times.  
* A very popular personality in England, Vinny Jones has presented his own TV programme.

* Once again Vinny Jones was in charge of representing the genuine spirit of Wimbledon. He played from the start in the 29 league games in which he appeared and his presence at the back was fundamental in helping the Dons to enjoy such a tremendous season. He scored 3 league goals, the best of which was the one he scored against Arsenal at Highbury. On the disciplinary side, by his standards he had a quiet season. He dedicated some of his time to speaking at university conferences and presenting his own television programme. Once again he was one of the pillars of the Welsh international side.

539.name: Ruddock
pages:
* Loaned to QPR in March 1998. 
* Neil Ruddock has a reputation as one of the hardest players in English football. During his career he has been involved in a number of incidents many of them a direct result of his style of play. Nevertheless Neil is a well respected player for the commitment he shows out on the pitch. He always gives everything he's got and never hides when the going gets tough. Although he is now a less regular member of the side, he still has the strength and ability to show Roy Evans that he can do a job, whenever he is needed.

* Neil Ruddock is a superb marker. Physically powerful he is a very difficult player to beat with strength alone, forcing opposing forwards to show a little bit of extra skill and ability if they have to get away from him. Ruddock never shirks away from the physical side of the game and is forceful in everything he does, occasionally taking his aggresion right to the limit. He commands the respect of his opponents, especially when he moves forward for corners and set pieces where his physical presence allows him to open up gaps and get in powerful headers on goal. Technically limited, he keeps things simple when he has the ball at his feet, laying it off to his nearest team-mate or sending it long, away from the danger area.
* League Cup winners medal 94-95.

* One full international appearance for England. 
* One "B" international appearance. 
* 4 under-21 international appearances. 
* 10 youth international appearances.

* Neil Ruddock signed his first professional contract on 3rd March 1986 with Millwall. Since  October 1983 he had previously played for the club as an associated schoolboy, and as an apprentice from June 1984. 
* On 14th April 1986, little more than a month after signing for Millwall he moved on to Tottenham Hotspur in exchange for £50,000. 
* Ruddock made his league debut on 18th April 1987 in a game against Charlton Athletic at White Hart Lane. 
* He returned to Millwall on 29th June 1988. 
* He moved to Southampton on 13th February 1989, for £250,000.
* A Southampton he replaced Kevin Moore, at the heart of the central defence.
* On 29th July 1992 he returned to Tottenham: the fee £750,000. 
* On 22nd July 1993 he signed for Liverpool who paid £2,500,000 to take him to Merseyside.
* His first goal for the Reds came in a game against Aston Villa. 
* During the course of his career he has scored 4 own goals. 
* In the 96-97 season, during a reserve team game against Manchester United at Anfield, United striker Andy Cole suffered fractures in both legs following a clash with Ruddock.
* He is known as "Razor Ruddock", in a play on words with the famous boxer.

* The good form shown by the rest of the Liverpool central defenders meant that Ruddock was unable to get into the starting line up until the middle of November against Leeds United. He gave a good performance and even managed to find the back of the net, the launching pad for a run of eleven consecutive games in the side. He then however disappeared from the side and was unable to get back in until May when he played in the final three games of the season.

542.name: Morrow
pages:
* Steve Morrow was involved in one of the strangest incidents in English football in recent times when he was seriously injured while celebrating a goal with his team mates in the League Cup Final. That incident made this product of the Arsenal youth system known around the world although finally the tremendous competition he was up against while with the Gunners forced him to move on to QPR.
* He has formed a partnership together with Steve Yates, following the departure of the apparently eternal Alan McDonald from the club, and has now settled down in manager Stewart Houston.'s line up. Very much a team man, he will have an important job to do to try to strengthen the Rangers defence and take them once again back to the Premier League.

* A very versatile player, Steve Morrow can play either at the heart of the defence, a left back or even in the midfield. Left footed, and very much a defensive player, he stands out for his tight marking and is a genuine specialist man-to-man marker. A hard tackler, he is good in the air, proving to be very difficult to beat for opposing forwards. Technically limited, he clears the ball decisively and seldom makes an attacking contribution.

* European Cup Winners Cup winners medal, 1994. 
* European Cup Winners Cup runners-up medal 1995. 
* League Cup winners medal 1993. 
* F.A. Youth Cup winners medal 1988.

* 19 full international appearances for Northern Ireland, scoring once. 
* One "B" international appearance. 
* 3 Under-21 international appearances.

* It wasn't easy for Steve Morrow, a product of the Arsenal youth system, to get the opportunity to make his debut for the Gunners' first team. A professional since 5th May 1988, he spent more than two seasons without making a first team apparance until, loaned out to Reading on 16th January 1991, he played his first game as a professional three days later, against Exeter. 
* In August 1991, he went out on loan again, this time to Watford, and, later, in October that same year he returned to Reading for a second spell. His spells out at other clubs didn't end there, with him having another loan spell, starting on 4th March 1992, this time at Barnet.
* It was during that same season 1991-92 that he finally got to make his first team debut for Arsenal. Although he never enjoyed the privilige of being a regular member of the side he played in Arsenal's League Cup triumph in the 1992-93 season although in the final against Sheffield Wednesday he incredibly suffered an injury while he was celebrating teammate Tony Adams' goal.  
* A Northern Ireland international at all levels, he is currently captain of the country's full international side.
* He was transfered to QPR on 27th March 1997 for £1,000,000. His debut for the club came on 5th April against Bolton Wanderers, a game in which he also managed to find the back of the net, although he was unable to prevent Rangers losing to the eventual First Division champions.

* Morrow made 14 league appearances for Arsenal last season before being transfered to QPR, on the same day as the trransfer deadline ended in March. His presence in Stewart Houston's side proved to be very positive, taking over from veteran Alan McDonald and forming an excellent partnership with Steve Yates. Morrow had a spectacular debut, managing to score a marvellous goal against Bolton Wanderers. In total he played in 5 games for Rangers, scoring once.

543.name: Rose
pages: * Matthew Rose was captain of that marvellous side that won the F.A. Youth Cup in 1994, and seemed destined to become Arsenal's centre half. Nevertheless, as always seems to be the case, the tremendous competition that exists for a place in the Gunners' side saw him asking for a transfer when he realised that he was unable to force his way into the plans of Gunners' boss Arsene Wenger. With a great future ahead of him, Rose will get his chance with QPR, where, as a member of the starting line up, he will be out to help the club win promotion back to the Premier League.

*  A player who can do equally as good a job at the heart of the defence as he can at left back, although he has also been used down the right hand side. Matthew Rose stands out for his distribution and his touch on the ball, showing himself to be comfortable with the ball at his feet always maintaing his composure when he finds himself in possession. Fast and disciplined in defence, he has good positional sense and knows how to choose his moment well when he is looking to push forward down the flank in support of the attack. Young and talented, he needs to gain more experience of competitive fotball at the highest level.
x
* Last season Rose made his debut for the England Under-21 side, playing in games against Georgia and Italy.

* Captain of the Arsenal side that won the F.A. Youth Cup in 1994, Matthew Rose has been a professional since 19th July of that same year.
* He made his first team debut on 2nd March 1996. Arsenal drew 1-1 with Quenns Park Rangers at Loftus Road, with  Rose coming as a half time subsitute in place of Steve Morrow. Three days later he made his first starting appearance, against Manchester City at Highbury.
* He was transfered to Queens Park Rangers during the summer of 1997, for £500,000.

* Little can be said about Matthew Rose's season last time out, since the young defender made just one appearance all season for Arsenal, taking the place of the injured Martin Keown. He had an unfortunate time of things during his only game, managing to put through his own goal, attempting to get in the way of a header from West Ham United's Slaven Bilic. His job last season was basically limited to turning out for the reserves.

544.name: Bardsley
pages: * David Bardsley is one of the side's veterans and, undoubtedly, has a tremendous amount of feeling for the blue and white hooped shirt of Queens Park Rangers, after having defended  the club's colours over the past eight seasons. He is a player who does an outstanding job for the side, above all in an attacking sense, a side to his game which saw him make a couple of appearances for England at full international level under Graham Taylor though he was later forgotten by Taylor's successor, Terry Venables. He is very well respected by his teammates and by the club's supporters. His contribution at QPR is a crucial one, although first of all he will have to get over his serious achilles tendon problem  which has kept him out for a long spell..

* Bardsley is a very attacking right back, who will accept the slightest of opportunity to get forward in support. He puts over good quality crosses, of which ex-QPR striker Les Ferdinand took full advantage to score plenty of goals for the club. He also possesses a tremendous shot from distance in his right foot. If all of that wasn't enough, he is also a very hard tackler when he goes in to win the ball from opponents. However, he is not the most difficult of defenders to take on and beat, and occasionally leaves his defensive position unguarded when he moves forward to support the attack, sometimes without thinking.
* F.A. Cup runners-up medal with  Watford 1984
* He has represented England at youth international level and on two occasions as a full international. He made his debut on 9th September 1992 against Spain in Santander, replacing Lee Dixon.

* After coming through the ranks at Blackpool, he signed as a professional in November  1982. He made his league debut on 18th May 1982 against Bury. 
* He was transfered to Watford in 1983 for £150,000. His debut came on 26th November 1983 against Luton Town, while he managed to find the back of the net twice against Chelsea on 5th May 1986.
* He was transfered to Oxford United in September 1987 for £265,000, making his debut on 19th September 1987 against his current side QPR. He scored his first goal for the club on 16th March 1988 against Norwich City. 
* He was transfered to QPR in September 1989 for £500,000. He played his first league  game for the club on 23rd September 1989 against Aston Villa, and opened his goalscoring account in the London derby against Tottenham Hotspur, seven days later.
* Bardsley missed the whole of last season due to an achilles tendon injury which prevented him from making an appearance throughout the whole of the campaign.

547.name: Dowie
pages: * The Upton Park supporters had taken Iain Dowie on board as one of their idols. The Northern Ireland strikers has never hidden his love of West Ham. He is a genuine example of pride and fighting spirit in defence of the club's colours. However he was transfered to QPR on the 29th of January 1998.

* A powerful, brave centre forward, who is excellent in the air, Iain Dowie is a real threat when he is inside the oppositions penalty area. A good header of the ball, he makes the most of his stature to get the better of opponents and show off his ability as a goalscorer. Technically limited, despite his obvious weaknesses in possession, he makes up for this with his constant work rate throughout the ninety minutes. He never gives a ball as lost and keeps opposing defenders under constant pressure. When he receives the ball with his back to goal, he is adept at protecting it with his body, as he waits for teammates to move up in support. Once he has laid the ball off he will quickly make his way into the opposing penalty area to try to get on the end of crosses into the box.
x

* 44 full international appearances for Northern Ireland, scoring 11 times. 
* 1 under-23 international appearance.
* 1 under-21 international appearance.

* A professional since the age of 23, Iain Dowie had time to study for a degree in mechanical engineering and work for British Aerospace before turning to football on a full time basis. 
* A boyhood Hammers'supporter, it was a dream come true when he first signed for West Ham in 1991. 
* A physically powerful man, curiously he was allowed to leave Upton Park for Southampton, as a schoolboy, being considered to be too small.
* Dowie developed his game with non-league clubs such as Cheshunt, St. Albans, Bishop's Stortford and Hendon, before joining Luton Town on 14th December 1988. The Hatters paid out 30,000 pounds for him to his club at the time, Hendon . 
* He made his league debut on 28th March 1989, in a game against Tottenham Hotspur. 
* His first spell with West Ham began on 22nd March 1991, when he signed  for the Hammers in exchange for 480,000 pounds. By signing Dowie, manager Billy Bonds was attempting to cover for the absence of the injured Trevor Morley. He made his debut on 23rd March in an away game against Hull City. At the end of that season the Hammers were celebrating their return to the top flight. 
* However, shortly after, on 3rd September 1991, he was transfered to Southampton for 500,000 pounds. 
* A first team regular at The Dell for three seasons, on 13th January 1995 he signed for Crystal Palace in exchange for 400,000 pounds. On 21st  January he made his debut in a 3-1 defeat against Everton at Goodison Park.
* On 8th September 1995 he returned to West Ham United, who paid 500,000 pounds to take him back to Upton Park. Three days later Harry Redknapp put him in the side for a league game against Chelsea. The supporters gave him a tremendous ovation, a sure sign of the excellent impression he made during his previous spell at Upton Park before moving to Southampton four years earlier. 
* He was named captain of Northern Ireland in 1997, an honour he celebrated by scoring twice against Albania.

* Last season wasn't a good one for Iain Dowie. He failed to find the net throughout the whole of the league season, and, as a result, lost his place in the side once Hartson and Kitson had arrived at West Ham. Fortunately, he managed to hold onto his place in the Northern Ireland side, and, was even named captain.

548.name: Sheron
pages:
* The magnificent form that Mike Sheron showed during his time at Manchester City saw him become considered as one of the most promising young prospects in English football. His signing for Norwich City initially seemed to be a good move for the player, becoming as he did the player the Canaries looked to most to find the back of the net.
* However, injuries prevented him from finding the form that was expected of him and as a result was transfered to Stoke City, where he managed to make a tremendous impression. His form last season saw him chosen for the First Division's ideal side, and full value for the £2,750,000 which QPR paid out to bring him to the club during the summer. One of the best goalscorers, in the division, if Sheron can maintain the form he showed last season, then  QPR will have a serious chance of getting back into the Premier League.

* Mike Sheron is a quick, clever centre forward, who possesses excellent vision which allows him to play accurate long balls through to his teammates, or play sharp incisive one twos. Technically he is a very complete footballer and is decisive when the opportunity comes along to try and open up an opportunity on his own. He is good with both feet and although stronger on his right, he never hesitates to have a go with right or left. He is an extremely quick player, both inside and outside the area. He is a good header of the ball, due to his ability to get in front of rival defenders. One of his greatest assets is his ability to hang on the last defender, just remaining onside, to break through the back line and take on and beat the keeper.

* Top scorer at Stoke City, 1995-96 and 96-97.
* Chosen in the First Division's ideal side for the 96-97 season.
* An England Under-21 international on 16 occasions, he made his debut on 28th May 1992 against France together with such players as Ian Walker, Ugo Ehiogu and Paul Kitson.

* After coming through the youth ranks at Manchester City, he signed as a professional in July 1990. He made his league debut on 17th September 1991 against Everton and scored his first goal for the club on 6th October 1991 against Notts County.
* He went out on loan to Bury in April 1991. He played his first game on 6th April 1991 against Preston North End, managing to score the winner for the club in a game against Tranmere Rovers.
* He was transfered to Norwich City in August 1994 for £1,000,000. He made his league debut for the club on 31st August 1994 against Sheffield Wednesday and scored his first goal in a Norwich shirt on 22nd October 1994.
* Stoke City signed him in November 1995, in a swap deal which saw Keith Scott travelling in the opposite direction to Norwich City. He made his debut on 18th November 1995 against Portsmouth, and opened his account for the club on 16th December 1995 against Crystal Palace.
* He was transfered to QPR for £2,750,000 in July 1997.

* Sheron began the league season in outstanding, making himself the First Division's top scorer. Unfortunately, a neck injury towards the turn of the year in December, saw a dip in his fitness, which affected his performances. Nevertheless he completed a sensational season, scoring 19 goals in 41 games for Stoke City. His tremendous performances saw him chosen for the First Division's ideal side.

549.name: Spencer
pages:
* John Spencer had to leave Scottish football in order to get the opportunity to really show what he was capable of. While at Chelsea, although not always a regular member of the side, he put together some tremendous seasons. What really motivates John Spencer is the thought of ending the season as Rangers leading scorer.
* Following the arrival of Hughes and Vialli, Gullit barely gave Spencer a chance in the side and, as a result, decided to accept the offer that QPR made for the player last year. A player blessed with tremendous pace and a real killer's instinct inside the penalty area, Spencer is an automatic choice at Rangers and forms a striking partnership with the club's new signing,  Mike Sheron, undoubtedly one of the most feared partnerships in the whole of the First Division.

* A skillful player with an eye for a goal, John Spencer takes advantage of his dribbling ability to get into the area and get in efforts on goal. With the ball apparently tied to his foot he is a very difficult player to stop, going past defenders with his fantastic change of pace. An intelligent player, he knows how to get into position to latch onto any rebounds or deflections that might come his way around the penalty area. He will occasionally pull out wide to the flanks, where he will try to get to the byline and from where he will pull the ball back to an incoming teammate. He can also do a job as a linkman, doing a good job complementing a strong centre forward.

* Top scorer at Chelsea in the season 94-95 and 95-96.
* Top scorer at QPR in the season 96-97.

* 12 full international appearances for Scotland. He made his debut on 16th November 1994  in a game against Russia, played in  Glasgow (1-1), coming on as a substitute for McGinley. He was a member of Scotland's squad in the 1996 European Championship in England. He  played in all three of Scotland's matches, against Holland, England and Switzerland, although his only starting appearance came against the host nation.. 
* 3 Under-21 international appearances, scoring once. 
* A youth and schoolboy international.

* Spencer joined the ranks of Glasgow Rangers at 14 years of age, and took the step up to the first team squad in 1986. Without managing to make a first team appearance he went out on loan to Morton on 4th March 1989.. That same day he made his league debut in a game against Partick Thistle.
* During the 88-89 season he had an altogether new experience when he ended up playing in Hong-Kong. On his return to Rangers he saw how he was still unable to force his way into the coaching staff's plans for the side.
*  On 1st August 1992 he was transfered to Chelsea for £450,000. In November 1994 he scored possibly the best goal of his career. In a European Cup Winners Cup game against Austria Vienna he picked the ball up in his own penalty area and carried it the  length of the field, before connecting with a decisive shot that took the ball into the back of the net.
* Up to the end of the 94-95 season he had been booked 12 times and sent off once during the course of his Premier League career. 
* During the 95-96 season he sufferd the consequences of an outrageous kick in the head from West Ham's Julian Dicks. In that same game and, up until that moment, Spencer had scored twice.
* He was transfered to QPR on 22nd  November 1996 for £2,500,000. The following day he made his debut against Reading, managing to strike his new club's winning goal.

* Last season was one of two very different halves for John Spencer. The first of those was with Chelsea where he couldn't break into the side due to the presence of Hughes and Vialli. Fortunately for the Scottish international, he moved to QPR where he had an immediate impact. In fact despite only playing for the club from November, he ended the season as Rangers' top goalscorer with 17 goals in 25 games. In short, it was a magnificent season for John Spencer.

550.name: Gallen
pages:
* The young QPR striker is one of the most promising young players at the west London club, although last season he had the misfortune to pick up a serious injury just when it seemed that everything was going well for him. A very complete player, and a genuine  goalscorer, at least at youth level, he is yet to live up to the expectations that the QPR supporters had of him, and which promised an outstanding future, even bringing comparisons with other goalscoring legends of English football such as Jimmy Greaves and Gary Lineker.
* At present Gallen is not a regular member of manager Stewart Houston's side, due to the signing, since his injury, of John Spencer, and, during the summer, Mike Sheron. Although he possesses tremendous ability, he will have to show every ounce of it this season if he wants to get back in Rangers' side on a regular basis.

* Kevin Gallen is a magnificent penalty box player, with great strength and the ability to get away from defenders. He strikes a ball well with either foot and is brave when he goes up to win the ball, never afraid to put his head in where it hurts. He lacks the technical ability of Robbie Fowler, but, despite not having made the same progress as his Liverpool counterpart, is still very young and has his own future very much in his own hands.
* He holds the record for the number of goals scored by one player in a season for Queens Park Rangers' youth team, with 78 goals.

* He made 8 appearances for England as a youth international, scoring 3 times.
* He has played 3 times for the England Under-21 side.

* After coming through the youth ranks at QPR, he signed professional in September 1992. He made his debut in the first game of the 1994-95 season on 20th August 1994 at Old Trafford against Manchester United, making a tremendous impression and scoring a goal that was unfortunately disallowed. Nevertheless, he managed to open his account just 4 days later against Sheffield Wednesday.
* Gallen has been regarded as the new Gary Lineker and compared to Jimmy Greaves. At 17 years of age he broke Greaves' 37 year record when he scored 60 goals for QPR's youth team. His record however didn't last long, the following year he beat it himself when he went on to find the back of the net an incredible 78 times.
* He didn't spend the usual season or two in the reserve side, after taking the step up to the first team squad, but went straight into the Premier League from the youth side.
* At the beginning of his career he played at right back, but, as time went on, he moved further forward until he eventually ended up playing as a centre forward.
* His brother Joe and Steve are both professional footballers playing for Shrewsbury Town and Doncaster Rovers respectively, and are both Irish internationals. However Kevin decided to play for England, and not Ireland, which is where his parents were born.

* Bad luck crossed Kevin Gallen's path last season, just at a moment when it seemed as though everything was going right, after an explosive start to the campaign. After scoring three times in just two games, Gallen suffered a serious knee injury in the second league game of the season and was forced to miss the rest of the campaign..

551.name: Maddix
pages: * A safe, tight marking central dedfender, Danny Maddix brings great defensive security to the side and is a player who would prove to be a real pillar at the back for any team. However, his lack of technical ability has surely prevented him from taking the step up to one of the big clubs in English football, and his place in the side at QPR is now under threat from the emergence of Steve Yates. At the moment Maddix is clinging on to his first team place, which he has won back for this season and is forming a partnership at the back with Steve Morrow.

* One of the quickest central defenders in English football, he is a difficult, not to say  impossible player to beat for pace. As a result he is undoubtedly one of the best markers around in his position. Despite not being particularly tall for a central defender, he is good in the air, and is a very good covering player across the back line. Nevertheless he is technically very weak, and, as soon as he is pressured when in posession, will send the ball long.
x
x

* Maddix came through the youth ranks at Tottenham Hotspur signing professional in July 1985.
* He went out on loan to Southend United in November 1986 for 2 games, the first of those against Orient on 4th November 1986.
* He completed his contract with Tottenham Hotspur and signed for QPR in July 1987. He made his league debut for the club on 28th November 1987 against Sheffield Wednesday with his first goal giving the club victory in the London derby against West Ham United on 15th October 1988. 
* He was kept out of action for 17 months by a serious knee injury which he suffered at the beginning of March 1993.

* Although Maddix didn't make his first starting appearance of the season until the month of December, he did make a number of appearances as a substitute. Nevertheless from December onwards he became a regular member of Stewart Houston's line up playing in 25 games.

552.name: Quashie
pages: * This still very young player is one of the pearls in Stewart Houston's squad, and is a product of the club's youth system. A hardworking midfielder with plenty of quality about his game, he is considered to be a real star of the future both for QPR and in English football in general. From his very first appearances he made himself a favourite with the fans who have supported him right from the beginning, even though he had more than his fair share of bad luck during his first two seasons. A player who is very much one to keep an eye on for the future, at the beginning of this current season he has been very much a regular for his manager.

* Nigel Quashie is a left sided midfield player with an excellent left foot capable of hitting good accurate passes over long distance. A player with a deft touch on the ball, he also packs a powerful shot in his left foot, proof of which was the goal he scored against Chelsea in the cup. He is a hard worker in his area of the pitch, and is always willing to help out the defence.
x
* An England youth international, he has also made one Under-21 appearance, against Poland in May 1997.

* A product of the Queens Park Rangers youth system. He made his league debut on 30th December 1996 against Manchester United, at just 17 years of age and had a superb match against Alex Ferguson's side.

* Suffering from the consequences of an illness which kept him out of the end of the 95-96 season, Quashie played in six games as a member of the starting line up in September, but a new injury went on to keep him out of action until March. He forced his way back into Stewart Houston's plans and managed to go on to make his debut for the England under-21 side against Poland, in May. In total he played in just 13 games, but showed plenty of promise.

553.name: Ready
pages: * A player who stands out for his versatility, Karl Ready is virtually more of a luxury stand in at QPR, than a regular member of the side. Although he has a difficult task in making himself a first choice in the team, his performances last season allowed him to apparently finally settle down at Rangers, doing a good job in a number of different positions. His progress also saw him called up to the Welsh national side, making his debut in February.He is not an automatic choice, but is certainly one of Stewart Houston's first options on the bench.

* A player who offers Houston a real range of posibilities, Ready is a man who can operate in any of the defensive positions. A player who is comfortable with the ball on either foot, he passes the ball simply without making things too complicated. Good in the air he also stands out for his ability to think ahead of opposing forwards. Nevertheless, all things being normal, he is generally at the back of the queue when first team places are being handed out.
x

* 5 under-21 international appearances for Wales, scoring once. He made his debut on 19th May 1992 against Romania. 
* 3 "B" international appearances for Wales.
* 1 full international appearance for Wales.

* After coming through the youth ranks at QPR he signed professional in August 1990. He made his league debut on 1st February 1992 against Wimbledon while his first goal for the club was the equaliser against Blackburn Rovers on 24th April 1994.

* Ready began the season as the team's right back, a position he managed to hold onto for a few games before picking up an injury. On his return he hit his best form playing at the heart of the defence, but he was struck down by an injury once again, which kept him out for the rest of the season. In total he played in 29 games.

554.name: Harper
pages:
* Lee Harper was playing for an amateur side when, in 1994, he caught the eye of the Arsenal coaching staff who signed him for £150,000. However, the competition at the club was enormous and Harper had to bide his time on the  bench trying to dislodge a keeper like David Seaman, one of the best in the world in his position.
* Harper had to wait until last year to make his debut for the Gunners, making a good impression. Stewart Houston, manager of QPR, and a man who had spent a number of years at Highbury, had good reports about Harper and, during the summer, decided to sign him on. Harper has gone on to put in some fine performances and has settled down as Rangers' number one goalkeeper.

* Harper is a young goalkeper with a powerful build and physique although that doesn't stop him from making some great saves. He has good reflexes and is a very secure figure in goal. He is also safe in the air.
x
x

* Harper signed for Arsenal from amateur club Sittingbourne on 16th June 1994 for £150,000. He had to wait for his Gunners debut until 15th Match 1997, when he took over in goal against Southampton due to the absences of both Seaman and Lukic. He had an outstanding debut managing to keep a clean sheet.  
* He was signed by QPR during the summer of 1997.

* Harper was only able to make just one appearance for Arsenal throughout the whole of the season. His moment came when the side was going through a poor spell which saw the club call upon his services who at the time was playing for the reserves. He had a sensational debut, showing glimpses of real quality and managing to keep a clean sheet against Southampton.

555.name: Roberts
pages: * A real luxury to have on the bench for QPR, Tony Roberts is an explosive player who is capable of real highs and lows, not being too consistent a player for the rest of his team. The arrival of Jurgen Sommer has seen him relegated to the bench, and as a result it wouldn't be a surprise to see him soon looking for a fresh start elswhere, although his good performances last season suggest that he may well even turn the situation around. At the present moment he is also the Welsh number two behind the great Neville Southall. At QPR meanwhile he is in a battle for the number one spot which is currenly held by Lee Harper.

* A very spectacular keeper, he makes plenty of saves which clearly reflect his power and agility. An inconsistent performer he concedes some absurd goals as a result of trying to be   over elaborate, while he is often guilty of poor judgement when he comes off his line, another of his weaknesses.
x

*  A Welsh international at youth, under-21 and "B" levels, he has also made 2 full international appearances. He made his debut on 17th February 1993 in Dublin against the Republic of Ireland, replacing the apparently eternal Welsh goalkeeper, Neville Southall.
* After coming through the ranks at QPR, he signed professional in July 1987. He made his league debut on 18th December 1987 against Coventry City.

* The Welsh keeper began the season as Stewart Houston's second choice in goal for Rangers. Taking advantage of the departure of Sommer to play for the United States, Roberts took over as number one in goal, only to later lose his place again to the American. At the end of the season he once again benefited from Sommers' absence due to international duty to take over for the last five games of the season, in which he managed to keep three clean sheets.

556.name: Yates
pages: * Steve Yates is one of the least spectacular players at QPR, but one of the most secure when it comes to defending. He may never go on to become a great central defender, but, what he does, he does well, without any frills, leaving that side of the game for those who know how. After a slightly hesitant start to the season Yates settled down and his form picked up to the point where there was no doubt about him deserving his place in the side.

* A real example of consistency, Steve Yates is a difficult player to beat both on the floor and in the air. A composed player he does his job with the minumum of fuss, keeping things as simple as possible. With the ball at his feet he leaves a lot to be desired as do the team's other central defenders. He possesses good positional sense but seldom moves forward for set pieces, prefering to stay back, covering his defensive  position.
* Third Championship winners medal with Bristol Rovers in 89-90.
x

* Yates came through the ranks at Bristol Rovers, and signed professional for in July 1988. He made his league debut on 3rd March 1987 against Darlington.
* He was transfered to QPR in August 1993 for £650,000. He made his league debut on 18th August 1983 against Liverpool, and scored his first league goal [which was also his first as a professional], on 14th January 1995, against Aston Villa.

* Yates began last season, partnership Alan McDonald at the heart of the QPR defence. Unfortunately, an injury in September, kept him out of action until February, going on to play just 3 games from his return to the end of the season. Not a bad season but a disappointing one due to the injury that kept him out for so long. During the course of the league season Yates played in a total of 16 games scoring once.

557.name: Sommer
pages: * Jurgen Sommer is a keeper who has really stood out since his arrival from Luton Town, where  he didn't make such a good impression. One of the tallest keepers in the English league, his ability is confirmed by his international status with the United States. He has a good future ahead of him and was the number one choice in goal for Rangers, although, for the moment Lee Harper has established himself as Stewart Houston's number one.

* A very complete goalkeeper, he stands out for his dominance in the air and for excellent positional sense. A very composed character, he always seems to remain unaffected by hostile atmospheres. He covers his angles well in one on one situations, making it very difficult for opposing forwards to beat him. He is also a very authoritative keeper who has tremendous confidence in his own ability..
x

* A United States international he made his debut at Wembley against England on 7th September 1994 replacing Brad Friedel while the score was 2-0 for England, both coming from Alan Shearer. 2-0 was how the game finally ended.

* He signed for Luton Town in September 1991. 
* He was sent out on loan to Brighton & Hove Albion for one game on 16th November 1991 against Cambridge United.
* He was also loaned out to Torquay United in October 1992, making his debut in the league on 31st October 1992 against Gillingham. 
* He finally made his debut for Luton Town on 14th August 1993 against Watford.
* He was transfered to QPR for £600,000 in November 1995 while he made his league debut for the club on 4th November 1995 against Southampton.

* Sommer was once again QPR's  number one choice in goal throughout the whole of last season, missing games only when he was away on international duty, making him unavailable for Stewart Houston. He played in a total of 33 games for Rangers.
