558.name: Slade
pages: * Steve Slade is a striker who has had to move away from Tottenham Hotspur to try to carve out a future for himself due to the tremendous difficulties he found in breaking through into the Spurs' attack with players of the calibre of Sheringham and Armstrong blocking the way. He is still a young player who could yet go on to become a good footballer and a valuable member of the side, although neither is he likely to have an easy time of things at QPR, following the arrival of players like Peacock, Spencer, Sheron and Gallen.

* A quick incisive forward he works hard to open up gaps for himself and to try to help other players to come through in support. In this new stage in his playing career, he needs to dispell a few doubts that exist in his game, above all surrounding his apparent lack of a goalscoring instinct that any forward in the professional game must have. Despite his lack of weight and physique, he is an intelligent player who has good technique.
x
x

* Slade came through the youth ranks at Tottenham Hotspur, making his debut for the club on 2nd March 1996 against Southampton. 
* QPR signed him for £300,000 in July 1996. His debut for the club came on 28th August against Wolverhampton Wanderers while he scored his first goal as a professional on 20th October against Tranmere Rovers.
* He was loaned out to Brentford during the 1996-97 season.

* Slade began the season as a key member of Stewart Houston's plans, playing  in several games and scoring goals that won points for Rangers. However following the arrival of John Spencer he could only watch as his chances of getting into the side became more remote all the time, eventually going out on loan to Brentford. He finally returned to QPR towards the end of the season. In total he made 17 appearances for the London club, scoring 4 times.

559.name: Bishop
pages:
* Signed for Manchester City in March 1998.
* Considered by the majority of the Upton Park supporters as the best passer of the ball at the club, Ian Bishop is setting out on his ninth season at West Ham. Although a few years ago the club's directors placed him on the transfer list, the truth is that the Liverpool born midfielder as managed to win the full confidence of the club's managers year after year with Harry Redknapp in charge since 1994, Ian Bishop's game has improved  noticeably, to the point where he is now the manager's right hand man out on the park. Nothing would suggest that the 97-98 season is likely to be any different.

* Ian Bishop is a classical midfield playmaker, with a good touch on the ball and the ability to orchestrate matters from the centre of the park. An excellent passer of the ball, his influence is noticed right throughout the side, as he takes on the responsibility of picking the ball up from the defence and playing it through to the strikers. He also helps out defensively, winning plenty of possession and maintaining a tremendous work rate throughout the ninety minutes. An experienced player, he is well capable of dictating the pace of the game. Perhaps his main weaknesses is his lack of a presence in and around the penalty area, although he sets up plenty of chances for his teammates.
x
* 1 "B" international appearance for England, which came in May 1991, against Switzerland at Walsall.

* During the course of his professional career, Ian Bishop has played in all four divisions of the English football league.
* Born in Liverpool, he took his first steps in the football world in the youth ranks at Everton, before turning professional on 24th May 1983. 
* He went out on loan to Crewe Alexandra on 22nd March 1984, and made his league debut five days later in a game against Darlington.
* Unable to force his way into the plans of Howard Kendall, Everton's manager at the time, Bishop was transfered to Carlisle United on 11st October 1984 for 15,000 pounds.
* Harry Redknapp signed him for Bournemouth on 14th July 1988 for 35,000 pounds.
* One year later, on 2nd August 1989, Manchester City signed him for 465,000 pounds. In one of his best games for the Maine Road club, City defeated Manchester United for 5-0. Shortly after, Mel Machin was sacked as City manager and Howard Kendall's arrival hastened Bishop's departure from the club. 
* On 28th December 1989 he was transfered, together with Trevor Morley, to West Ham for a fee of 500,000 pounds, in a deal which also saw Mark Ward moved in the opposite direction to Maine Road. Two days later, on 30th December, Bishop and Morley made the debuts in a game against Leicester. 
* In December 1992 he was placed on the transfer list by West Ham, together with a number of teammates, although, eventually, he remained at Upton Park.

* He missed the beginning of the season due to injury, although, once he was fit, he quickly made himself a regular member of the side. He played in 29 league games making 26 starting appearances. He scored an outstanding goal against Derby County in November, winning the ball in midfield and moving forward with it under control before unleashing a ferocious drive from outside the area.

560.name: Pollock
pages:
* Signed for Manchester City in March 1998. 
* After a brief spell in Spanish football, Pollock returned in November 1996 to Bolton.  His arrival was positive for the team, who were reinforced with a player with character, able to instil spirit into his team-mates.

* Pollock is a right half who covers a lot of ground during the games.  His game is very aggressive which means that he concedes a lot of free-kicks, something that cost him dearly in Spain, where the referees do not allow the type of game that is played in England.  He is technically limited.
x
* An under-21 international for England three times.

* Trained in Middlesbrough, in the 96-97 season Osasuna, a Spanish team, signed him.  But he didn't adapt well to Spanish football, and so returned to England.
* The Spanish club didn't have to pay for Pollock's move thanks to the Bosman ruling as his contract with Middlesbrough had expired, although his asking-price in England was £3 million.
* Aston Villa and Leeds United were also interested in acquiring his services, but Pollock wanted to have a bit of a Spanish adventure.
* Bolton paid Osasuna £500,000 for his move.

* After his spell at the Spanish club Osasuna, were things didn't go so well, Pollock decided to return to England.  His arrival was a shot in the arm of the team who appreciated his battling in the midfield in the 20 games in which he played.  He also scored four goals.

561.name: Crooks
pages: x
x
x
x
x
x

562.name: Wiekens
pages: * Gerard Wiekens is a player who was signed from Dutch football by Frank Clark as one of this season's reinforcements for Manchester City. Having realised that he was not attracting the attention of any of the big clubs in Holland such as Ajax, PSV, Feyenoord, or the more modest Groningen, Wiekens decided to accept a move to English football, flattered as he was by the interest shown from Manchester City, although he also stated that he had been preparing himself for three years to take such a step. Under the Bosman ruling, Wiekens is not considered a foreign player with the Maine Road club and lines up at the moment as an automatic first team choice for Frank Clark.

* Wiekens is a player who, during his time in Dutch football, always played as a sweeper, a position where he showed quality and forcefulness. Capable of bringing the ball out at the back under control he uses his good vision to distribute it accurately and thoughtfully to his teammates. However, at Manchester City he is playing as a midfield organizer, though slightly withdrawn, with one of his duties being to cover for his more attacking midfield colleagues. He is capable of getting forward though, and his presence in the penalty area is often translated into goals or chances created for others.
x
x
* Wiekens was signed from Dutch club Veendam in the summer of 1997.
x

563.name: Brannan
pages:
* Another product of Tranmere Rovers' youth system,  Gerald Brannan is a player who does an important ball winning job in midfield, as well as having the ability to get forward to support the attack with enthusiasm and strength. He knows how to get onto the end of things in the box as his goalscoring record might suggest, although his goals tally in recent seasons has tailed off slightly.
* As he was coming to the end of his contract, which was due to expire at the end of the season, Tranmere Rovers moved quickly to get something back on the player they had brought through, realising that sooner or later he would move on anyway. Although the fee Tranmere received for the player was below his real value, Frank Clark was quite happy in the knowledge that he had secured a fine player who will play an important part in Manchester City's season this time round.

* Brannan is a strong player in the middle of the park, a man who wins a tremendous amount of possession for his isde. He can play in midfield, his best psition, or at full back on either flank although he prefers the right. A powerful player he is always willing to work hard for his teammates. When he plays at full back he likes to continually get down the flanks, something he does decisively and at speed, putting over some excellent crosses.
x
x

* After coming through the youth ranks at Tranmere Rovers, he signed professional in July 1990. He made his league debut on 22nd October 1990, against Mansfield Town, and opened his goalscoring account as a professional on 12th January 1991 against Stoke City.
* He was transfered to Manchester City on 12th March 1997. His debut came on 15th March against Grimsby Town while his first goal for the Maine Road club came on 5th April against Charlton Athletic.

* Brannan had an outstanding season last time out as a regular member of theTranmere Rovers line up, proving to be a tremendously competent peformer both at the back and in midfield. He continued his excellent form at Manchester City after arriving at the club in the month of March, going on to become one of the key men in Frank Clark's line up. In total, between both clubs, he played in a total of 45 games, finding the target on 7 occasions.

564.name: Brown
pages: * A product of Manchester City's youth system, Michael Brown hasn't had the opportunities he needs in order to be able to continue his progress. His limited first team chances means he has been unable to force his way into the plans of the numerous managers who have passed through Maine Road in recent years, including the latest of those, Frank Clark. After a meeting with the club's chairman, Francis Lee, Michael Brown knows that the only way he is going to force his way back into the  manager's plans is by getting his head down and being consistent in his work. Still a young player he has everything to go for in the future.

* Brown is a player who operates down the left hand side of the midfield. A very hard working player who especially stands out for the help he gives to the Manchester City defence, showing the qualities which also allow him to play at left back. A hard tackler. he never stops getting up and down the line, although he rarely proves to be a decisive player in attack. Technically he is nothing out of the ordinary and, despite being a right footed player he is more at home on the left. He is not a player who looks to take on opponents, limiting himself to laying the ball off the to one of his midfied colleagues. He is not a particularly good crosser of the ball, a responsiblity he will generally pass on to colleagues, as he also tends to do when it comes to getting in shots on goal.
x
* An England uner-21 international, he made his debut on 23rd April 1996 against Croatia. He has now made a total of 4 under-21 international appearances.

* A player who came through the club's youth ranks, he made his debut for Manchester City's first team on 26th August 1995 against Queens Park Rangers.  
* He was loaned out to Hartlepool United on 27th March 1997. He made his debut for the club on 29th of that same month against Colchester United. He also managed to score his first goal as a professional during his spell at Hartlepool, on 9th April against Darlington.

* Michael Brown began the season well playing in 6 of the first 7 games, but he later  suddenly disappeared from the line up. His performances were sporadic ones from that momento on, and he was even loaned out to his home town club, Hartlepool United, who he helped save from relegation. With City he made 11 appearances plus another 6 which he made during his spell out on loan, when he also managed to score his first goal as a professional.

565.name: Jobson
pages:
* Signed for Manchester City in March 1998. 
* In recent seasons Richard Jobson's career has been affected by injuries. As a result Leeds United was unable to get the best out of this excellent footballer who is now in the final years of his career.

* A central defender, he has an exquisite touch on the ball, which allows him to also do an excellent job in the midfield. He is very comfortable in possession, and distributes the ball intelligently, making him a player who is well capable of setting up the side's attacks. Quick with the ball at his feet, he is very elegant in everything he does although he makes things more complicated than they need to be.Strong in the air in both penalty areas, he is a good header of the ball and has, in fact, scored plenty of goals during the course of his career.
* Richard Jobson is a fine footballer, although the serious injury he suffered in 1994 put the brakes on his progress. Althouhg he is now at the veteran stage, his quality and experience allows him to do an effective job out on the park.
* Second Division winners medal 91.
* 2 "B" international appearances for England.

* He began his career with modest Barton Athletic, from where he was  transfered to Watford for 22,000 pounds on 5th November 1982.
* On 7th February 1985 he signed for Hull City, his home town club who paid out 40,000 pounds to take him to Humberside. 
*He was transfered to Oldham Athletic on 30th August 1990 for 460,000 pounds.
* Ex-England manager Graham Taylor once described Jobson as the best defender in Britain, in terms of technique and ball control. 
* In November 1994, an ankle injury kept him out of action for 6 moths. He underwent two successive operations.
* In October 1995 he was transfered to Leeds United for 1 million pounds. He made his debut on 28th of that month at Elland Road against Coventry (3-1) and scored his first goal for the Whites on 9th December against Wimbledon. It was a goal that clinched a point for Leeds (1-1).
* During the 95-96 season he suffered ruptured cruciate knee ligaments, a very serious injury which prevented him from playing during the large  part of the 96-97 season.

* Richard Jobson was dogged by bud luck during the course of last season. Just when he began to enjoy regular first team football in the side at Leeds United, he suffered a recurrence of the serious knee injury which had kept him out for a large part of the previous season. As a result he was forced to put an end to his season earlier than he would have liked.

566.name: Vaughan
pages: * One of the brightest prospects at Ipswich Town, Tony Vaughan is a player who can bring a lot to the side, with his youth and enthusiasm. After completing an outstanding season, Vaughan was offered the opportunity of a new contract at Portman Road, but he decided to make a fresh start, a decision which finally saw him signing for Mancgester City during the summer. He is one of City's reinforcements for the coming season but is likely to have a tough time on his hands as he tries to break into the side. Nevertheless, his versatility, strength and know how out on the park could soon see him knocking on the doors of the first team.

* A left back who can also play at the heart of the defence, he is a very dangerous player when he moves forward for dead ball situations, where he makes the most of his physical presence and power. He is a very solid defender who is difficult to get past. When he plays as a full back he likes to get forward into the attack, giving tremenodus support to the midfielder playing in front of him.
x
x

* After coming through the youth ranks at Ipswich Town he signed as a professional in July 1994. His league debut came on 23rd October 1994 against Chelsea and he scored his first goal in the league, which proved to be the winner, against Derby County on 2nd April 1996.
* He was signed by  Manchester City in the summer of 1997.

* Tony Vaughan had an outstanding season, managing to find the back of the net in the first few games, somthing which gave him a real confidence booster. An injury kept him out of action for a short while, although he managed to come back in time to contribute to a run of five consecutive games in which Ipswich Town's rivals failed to score a goal against the East Anglian club. He made a total of 32 appearances, scoring 32 goals.

567.name: Beesley
pages: * An experienced central defender, Paul Beesley was very much one of Frank Clark's  personal signings, knowing the player from a previous spell they had together at Leyton Orient. Since his acquisition the City defence has been more solid and secure. He was also signed very much with one eye on this current season in which City will be all out to make it back to the Premier League.

* He generally plays as a central defender although occasionally, such as when he was playing at Sheffield Wednesday, he lines up at left back. He is a quick player who gives 100% in every game he plays, making up for his technical weaknesses. A good marker, he also makes the the most of his experience to get his team out of tight situations. He is not a particularly dangerous player when he moves forward in support of  the attack since he is not as dominant with his head as other central defenders. Paul Beesley is not a brilliant footballer, but is certainly an effective performer for the side.

* Paul Beesley began his career at modest Merseyside club Marine, in the Northern Premier League before signing for Third Division Wigan Athletic on 22nd Deptember 1984. His debut came along on 3rd October of that same year in a game against Reading.
* When he was in his sixth season with Wigan, he was transfered to Leyton Orient on 20th October 1989 for £175,000. He played 32 games for the club and was voted "Player of the Year". His excellent progress opened up the doors to the First Division, still then the top flight of English football in pre- Premier League days. Sheffield United paid out £300,000 to sign him. With the Blades he played in the first two seasons of the newly formed Premier League, although in 1994 the club were relegated to the First Division.
* At the begining of the 94-95 season he suffered a knee ligament injury which kept him out action, although on his return to the side he was even madecaptain in the absence of Brian Gayle.
* In August 1995,Leeds United paid £250,000 to take him to Elland Road. 
* He made his League debut for Leeds in the first week of the 95-96 season. Beesley came on as an 8th  minute substitute for Carlton Palmer at Upton Park as Leeds managed to overcome West Ham by 2 goals to one.
* He was transfered to Manchester City during the 1996-97 season.

* Although he made 12 appearances for Leeds United, Beesley played his best football of the season for Manchester City, adding security to the Maine Road club's defence from the moment he arrived. Unfortunately an injury against Birmingham City, brought his season to a premature end after just 6 appearances for his new club

568.name: Hiley
pages:
* Scott Hiley is a player who brings a touch of quailty to Manchester City, not only in an attacking sense but also defensively, showing great security  in everything he does. However it remains to be seen how he comes through the serious injury which he suffered last season and which kept him out of the side when the season had only just got underway.
* Nevertheless he does possess tremendous class, and if he manages to make a full recovery, he will no doubt get a chance to make a contribution to the Maine Road club's season.

* A very classy attacking full back, he loves to get forward whenever the opportunity presents itself. His crossing into the penalty area is top quality, as was well appreciated firstly by Niall Quinn and now by Uwe Rosler. As well as all these qualities he is also well capable of operating down either flank, equally as effectively. Defensively he is quite safe and covers well, while his speed makes him a very difficult player for opposing forwards to take on and beat. When he moves forward, not only does he move up the line and get into positions to receive the ball, but he also possesses the ability to carry the ball forward himself.

* Fourth Division Championship winners medal with Exeter City in 1990. 
* Player of the year 1991-92 with Exeter City.
x

* A player who came through the junior ranks at Exeter City he signed profesional in August 1986. He made his league debut on 17th October 1987, against Burnley, scoring his first goal as a professional on 19th March 1988 against Hereford United.
* He was transfered to Birmingham City for £100,000 in March 1993, making his first appearance for the Blues on 13th March 1993 against Bristol City. The arrival of Gary Poole limited his first team opportunities at Birmingham City and as a result, he moved, on loan, to Manchester City in February 1996, meeting up once again with his ex-manager at Exeter City, Alan Ball. 
* On his debut he put over a cross which allowed Niall Quinn to hit the back of the net against Newcastle United. Unfortunately he broke a bone in his foot against Bolton on 30th March, although that didn't prevent his move to Maine Road from Birmingham City being made permanent, just 2 days later.

* The season began well for Scott Hiley, making himself a first team regular at Manchester City, although he later went on to suffer an injury, similar to that suffered by striker Niall Quinn who by now had moved on to Sunderland, which kept him out of action for the rest of the season. He managed just 3 appearances before being struck down by injury.

569.name: Brightwell
pages: * Ian Brightwell, is a one club man, Manchester City being the only club where he has plied his trade. After spending the whole of his career at Maine Road he is one of the side's most committed players, something which has occasionally caused him disciplinary problems, as his desire to win leads to an excessively physical approach to the game. He has, though, made an invaluable contribution for all the managers who have passed through Maine Road, right through his career, men such as Alan Ball as well as current manager Frank Clark.

* Brightwell is not a player who stands out in any aspect of the attacking side of the game, although he is a real specialist at doing a man to man marking job and stifling the opposition's danger man. He can play in midfield, operating just in front of the defence, as a full back on either side or even as a central defender. He is not a quick player but puts plenty of heart into everything he does. In summing up, he is a player whose job is basically to stop the other team from playing, barely making a contribution in an attacking sense.
x

* An England international at schoolboy, youth and under-21 level. He made his under-21 debut on 13th September 1988 at Watford's Vicarage Road ground against Denmark in a game which ended in a 0-0 draw. The English side included amongst its ranks Paul Merson and David Hirst while the Danish line up included Marc Rieper of West Ham United and ex-Liverpool star Jan Molby.

* After coming through the youth ranks at Manchester City Ian Brightwell signed as a professional in May 1986. He played his first game for the only club of his career on 23rd August 1986 against Wimbledon and opened his goalscoring account in the league on 14th February 1987 against Norwich City. 
* He is the only remaining member of the "Famous Five", when he played with Lake, White, Redmond and  Hincliffe, in the City side that won the F.A. Youth Cup in 1985. Shortly afterwards each one of those players went on to play in the first team.

* Once again Brightwell was one of Manchester City's most regular players, making a total of 37 appearances during the course of the season and managing to find the back of the net twice. He gave a particularly brilliant display with the marking job he did on Fabrizio Ravanelli in a cup game against Middlesbrough, completely nullifying the Italian International striker's threat.

570.name: Edghill
pages:
* The young Manchester City right back is a player who brings great enthusiasm and energy to everything he does. His qualities didn't go unnoticed by the coaching staff at Arsenal, who, in the past, made enquiries about possibly taking the player to Highbury. Edghill has also made himself a feature of the England under-21 side, and has shown more than enough ability to suggest he could well go on to become a first team regular for the Maine Road outfit.
* A serious knee injury has momentarily put the block on what had previously been a meteoric rise in the career of this young player who in recent seasons has seen very little action. However, if he manages to make a complete recovery, then City will once again find themselves with a real star amongst their ranks in their struggle to get into the Premier League.

* An extremely quick right back, he is a very difficult player to beat for speed. He doesn't mess about when the ball is there to be won, always prepared to go in hard if need be. He regularly gets forward into the attack, supporting the man in front of him, although he is not a player who provides the best of service to the front men.
x

* An England "B" international, as well as having played for the under-21 side. He made his debut on 8th March 1994 against Denmark. The game ended in a 1-0 win for an English side which included Jamie Redknapp, Chris Bart-Williams and Ray Parlour. England's goal was scored by Trevor Sinclair.
* After coming through the youth ranks at Maine Road, he signed professional in July 1992. He played his first game for the club on 20th September 1993 against Wimbledon.

* Despite having recovered from a serious knee injury Edghill never became part of the plans of the various managers who occupied the Maine Road hot-seat last season, remaining, as he did, wrapped up in cotton wool.

571.name: Clough
pages: * An elegant and now veteran midfielder, Nigel Clough played the best football of his career at Nottingham Forest, where he enjoyed a number of fine seasons which saw him eventually make the full England side. Unfortunately the players form dipped alarmingly during his time at Liverpool, until, eventually, he left Anfield  to sign for Manchester City. His contribution, up to now, has not been what either he or the club might have expected. As a result, he currently finds himself out on loan, and, free to move, as far as the board of directors are concerced. With Frank Clark at the helm, Clough will be hoping to get a final opportunity to revitalise a fine playing career, which he would no doubt love to round off by getting at least one more honour up against his name.

* For many seasons Clough proved his quality as an intelligent and skillful striker capable of setting up plenty of goalscoring chances for his fellow strikers. In recent years his position has become a more withdrawn one, first of all playing just behind the two main strikers and eventually as a midfielder. He is a player with tremendous vision who is capable of playing accurate balls through to the strikers, or who can even drive forward himself, playing  a one-two or surprising defenders with runs from deep positions. He has lost some of his speed and in that aspect of the game is not as dangerous as he once was. His job at City is to basically provide support for Georgi Kinkladze, who has more freedom of movement as he attempts to prompt City into action up front.

* Top scorer at Nottingham Forest, in 85-86, 86-87 with Garry Birtles, 87-88, 88-89, 90-91 and 92-93.
* League Cup Winners medal with Nottingham Forest in the 88-89 season, scoring twice against Luton Town in the final, one coming from the penalty spot. Forest went on to retain the trophy the following year, against Oldham Athletic, with Clough picking up his second winners medal.
* F.A. Cup runners up medal with Nottingham Forest in 1991 after losing in the final against Tottenham Hotspur.
* League Cup Runners up medal with Nottingham Forest in 1992, losing the final against Manchester United.

* Has represented England at "B", under-21 and full international levels. He made his debut for the full side on 23rd May 1989, against Chile at Wembley, in a game which was watched by the lowest ever attendance for a England home game, just 15,628. He has made a total of 14 full international appearances for his country.

* Nigel Clough completed his contract with amateur Heanor Town, moving on to join Nottingham Forest in September 1984. He made his league debut on 26th December, 1984, against Ipswich Town while his first goal in the league clinched a draw for his side, on 4th May 1985 Watford.
* After scoring more than 100 goals for Forest, he was transfered to Liverpool for £2,275,000. On his debut for the Anfield club he scored the two goals that brought the Reds a home victory against Sheffield Wednesday on 14th August 1993.
* He was transfered to Manchester City in January 1996 for £1,500,000, making his debut on 31st January 1996 against Southampton. His first goal for the club came just 3 days later on 3rd February 1996 against Queens Park Rangers.
* He was loaned out to his original club Nottingham Forest during the 96-97 season. His first game was on 21st December against Arsenal while just one week later, against Leicester City, he managed to score his first goal, in his second spell at the City Ground.

* A regular member of the starting line up at the beginning of the season for Manchester City, he was unfairly criticised during the month of November, hastening his departure, on loan, to his ex-club Nottingham Forest. Forest at the time were in the process of trying to save themselves from relegation to the First Division. With Forest he played in 13 games and scored once before returning to City. For the Maine Road club he played in a total of 23 games finding the target twice.

572.name: Goater
pages: * Shaun Goater signed for Manchester City in March 1998.

* Speed is Shaun Goater's biggest strength. Thanks to his speed the Bermudan international is capable of going past even the fastest of defenders with apparent ease. A good striker of the ball, his progress seems to be endless while his finishing is improving all the time.
* Associated Members Cup Winners medal 1996.
* 8 full international appearances for Bermuda.
x

* Last season he played in a total of 42 games, 39 of those as a member of the starting line up and managed to score 23 goals. He was the teams top scorer, a focal point of every attack and undoubtedly the squad's genuine match winner.

574.name: Horlock
pages: * Kevin Horlock was one of the signings that Frank Clark made at the end of last season, when he signed him from Swindon Town. Above all though he was asigning made very much with a view to the present season in which Clark will be expecting, from the team in general, a great improvement on last season and, from Horlock in particular, at least as good a campaign as the one he had last time round. A player who fits in perfectly with the style of football that Frank Clark likes to play, he will no doubt have a fundamental role to play in the battle for promotion to the Premier League. He is likely to be an automatic choice for his manager.

* Playing tucked in behind the main strikers, he manages to surprise opposing defenders by coming forward late from deep positions. A very complete player, he is a good striker of the ball with either foot, although he prefers his left. He is also useful with his head. In one on one situations he keeps his cool well, generally making the most of the opportunities that come his way.
* Second Division Championship winners medal , 95-96 with Swindon Town.
* A Northern Ireland international he made his debut on 26th April 1995 against Latvia.In total he has made 9 appearances for his country.

* Afte coming through the ranks at West Ham United, he signed professional in July 1991.
* He became a free agent and moved on to Swindon Town in August 1982. He made his league debut on 10th October 1992 against Portsmouth, scoring his first goal in the  competition 7 days later against  Notts County.
* He was transfered to Manchester City on 31st January 1997 in exchange for £1,250,000. His first game for the club was against Oxford United on 2nd February, while he opened his goalscoring account for City against his ex-club Swindon Town on 22nd February.

* Horlock enjoyed an outstanding season, both at Swindon Town where he scored 8 goals in 28 games as well as with Manchester City for whom he had a tremendous debut, in a televised game against Oxford United. He did a fine job in in whichever position Frank Clark asked him to play, his unselfish attitude and eye for a goalscoring chance always remaining key elements in his game.

575.name: Bradbury
pages: * Lee Bradbury had the sort of season he could only have dreamed of. Not only did he spectacularly increase his number of appearances with Portsmouth but he also became the club's leading scorer with 15 goals to his credit. His fine performance last season was rewarded when, during the summer, Manchester City splashed out the incredible sum of  £3,500,000 to take him to Maine Road, and make him the club's most expensive signing ever. With the pressure of such a large fee, added to the already difficult task of living up to the expectations of a much bigger club than Portsmouth, Bradbury will be out to show that the faith shown in him was not misguided. For the beginning of the season at least, he has to be an automatic first team choice for Frank Clark.

* Bradbury is a very combative striker who is continually on the move looking to find space and get on the blind side of defenders. A very quick player he is always ready  to have a shot on goal, his shooting being one aspect of his game that improved immensely last season. Good in the air he gets in powerful, decisive headers. An enthusiastic worker when it comes to keeping the opposition defence under pressure, he is also capable of holding the ball up as he waits for support to come through from midfield, or equally he can play the ball out to the flanks, picking out the team's wide men.
* Top scorer at Portsmouth during the  96-97 season.
x

* Portsmouth signed him in August 1995 from amateur club Cowes. He made his debut on 30th August 1995 against Leicester City.
* He was loaned out to Exeter City in December 1995. His first game for the club came on 2nd December 1995 against Doncaster Rovers, while his first two goals for the club came a week later against Leyton Orient.
* He was transfered to Manchester City during the summer of 1997, for £3,500,000 establishing a new club record fee for the Maine Road.

* Bradbury proved to be Portsmouth's cutting edge last season, ending the campaign as the club's top scorer and forming a tremendous partnership with Mathias Svensson. His work was recognised with his inclusion in a First Division under -21 side which was chosen to face a similar side from Italy's serie B. His end of season statistics were, 42 games played with 15 goals to his credit.

576.name: Dickov
pages: * Paul Dickov learned his trade in the youth ranks at Arsenal, however, his limited opportunities with the Highbury giants saw him move on to forge out a career elsewhere. What he wanted was regular first team football, something he was unlikely to get with the north London Club. His arrival at  Manchester City  has relaunched his career and he has seen how, with hard work, the opportunities have finally come his way. He has been a regular member of the first team under Frank Clark, but he will have to be on his toes to make sure that Uwe Rosler doesn't take his priviliged position away from him.

* A striker of great confidence and determination he fights for every ball and is, basically, a player who gives his all for the sake of the team, if need be sacrificing the chance of some personal glory. An aggressive player, he keeps the oppostition defence under constant pressure. Though not particularly quick, his intelligence around the edge of the area allows him to put through clever passess which set up goalscoring chances or he may occasionally work out a shooting chance for himself. A good penalty taker he can also play tucked in just behind the main strikers from where he can make the most of his excellent vision.
*  European Cup Winners Cup winners medal for Arsenal, in  93-94, although he failed to play in the final.
* A Scottish schoolboy, Youth and under-21 international, he made his debut for the Under-21 side on 29th May 1992 against Yugoslavia and went on to make a total of fourappearances.

* After coming the youth ranks at Arsenal, he signed as a professional in December 1990 making his league debut on 20th March 1993 against Southampton. He scored his first goal for the Gunners on 8th May 1982 in the London derby against  Crystal Palace.
* He was sent out on loan to Luton Town for 3 months in October 1993. He madehis first appearance for the Hatters on 9th October 1993, and managed to open his account for his new temporary club seven days later against Notts County, clinching a victory for his side.
* He was loaned out to Brighton & Hove Albion in March 1994, making his debut on 26th March against Exeter City. His first goal came on 30th March 1994 against Plymouth.
* His move to  Manchester City came in August 1996 for £1,300,000. He made his first appearance in a City shirt on 24th August 1996 coming on for Kavelashvili, in a game against Stoke City.

* Dickov didn't have a very easy season last time out. After moving to Manchester City from Arsenal, he could only watch as the man who had signed him, Alan Ball, then left the club. Nevertheless he carried on fighting and working hard to try to work his way into the plans of the next succession of managers who had spells in charge. With the arrival of Clark, he was initially ignored, but his commitment to the cause eventually saw him back in the team, and he managed to go on to complete what turned out be a satisfactory season, personally speaking. He played in 29 games, and managed to hit the target on five occasions.

577.name: Creaney
pages: * As he himself has stated, Gerry Creaney's performances at Manchester City since his arrival from Portsmouth, have been disappointing. A striker who would be capable of breaking his way into most sides, his inconsistency is his worst enemy, hitting the heights one minute and virtually disappearing from the action the next. At present he finds himself at something of a crossroads, trying to sort out his future. However it wouldn't be a surprise if he finally decides that his days at Maine Road are over, if he eventually fails to force his way into Frank Clark's plans.

* An intelligent player inside the area where he is always quick to react, getting in shots on goal with either foot as soon as he gets the space to do so. He is good in the air, above all when he makes the most of his anticipation to get in front of defenders. At times he seems to be disinterested, drifting out of the game when things aren't going his way, while on other occasions the killer instinct, necessary in every goalscorer, seems to desert him.
x
* A Scottish under 21 international, making his debut on 16th October 1990 against Switzerland, scoring once. He made a total of eleven appearances at under-21 level.

* A player who learnt his trade in the youth ranks at Glasgow Celtic he signed as a professional in May 1987. He played his first game for the Celts on 24th March 1990 against Dunfermline Athletic while his first goal for the club was the equalizer against Dundee United on 21st April 1990.
* Portsmouth signed him in January 1994 for £500,000. He made his league debut on 5th February 1994 against Notts County, while his first goals came in the form of a hat trick on 19th February 1994, against Grimsby Town.
* He was transfered to Manchester City in September 1995 for £1,000,000. He managed to open his account on his league debut, against Newcastle United, hitting the back of the net just once on this occasion.
* Not managing to really make a place in the forward line his own he went out on loan to Oldham Athletic in March 1996. He played his first game for the club on 30th March 1996 against Reading and struck his first goal at Southend United on 27th April 1996.
* He had another spell out on loan, this time at Ipswich Town, arriving on 25th October 1996. His first game for the club came on 26th of that same month against Tranmere Rovers. His first and only goal for Ipswich Town came against Swindon Town on 19th November.

* Once again Gerry Creaney had a disappointing season being unable to make more than just five appearances, of which the majority came as a substitute. He scored just one goal. His time at Ipswich Town, where he went out on loan produced similar statistics.

578.name: Ingram
pages: * Rae Ingram is another example of the young prospects that have emerged from the Manchester City youth set up in recent years. However, as is the case with his young colleagues that have come through at City, he has seen how opportunities to show what he can do in the first team have been few and far between. A promising left back, Ingram will no have a difficult job on his hands to force his way into Frank Clark's plans, but the season is long and he may well eventually get his chance.

* A player who operates down the left hand side, above all as a full back, he shows good speed when he gets involved in the action. Despite his speed though, he is not a player who shows a great ability to beat a man when he moves forward into the attack, nor is he a particularly great crosser of the ball. At the back he occasionally has lapses in concentration, failing to anticipate the strikers to try to prevent tight situations developing for his fellow defenders.
x
x
* After coming through the youth ranks at Manchester City, he made his debut for the Maine Road club on 30th August 1995 against Everton.

* It turned out to be a strange season for Rae Ingram. One minute he was apparently a key man in the side making a number of appearances, while the next he was suddenly relegated to the reserves. With the arrival of Frank Clark at Manchester City, he was given another opportunity but, finally, he had to give way to the signings that the manager made as the club approached tthe run in to the season, and the final effort in the fight to stay in the First Division. He made a final total of 18 appearances.

579.name: Symons
pages: * One of the defensive pillars of the side, Kit Symons is a central defender who is surprisingly good with the ball at his feet. He brings enormous defensive stability to the team, making an invaluable contribution and proving to be a real rock at the back. In short he is a player who does a fine, competent job, bringing a real touch of quality to the defence. He will no doubt be an automatic first team choice this season for Manchester City.

* A central defender who possesses great technique, he is able to bring the ball out from the back, showing great composure, and playing the ball off quickly and efficiently. Excellent in the air he formed a great partnership at the heart of the Manchester City defence with his ex-colleague Keith Curle, now at Wolverhampton Wanderers. One of his greatest qualities is his co-ordination, which is magnificent for such a tall player, and allows him to covet across the back line quickly, showing anticipation and consistency.
x

*  A player who has represented Wales at youth, "B", Under-21 and full international level, he made his debut in Dublin in February 1992 against the Republic of Ireland. In total he has made 22 full international appearances for the Welsh national side.

* He came through the youth ranks at Portsmouth, signing professional terms in December 1988. His first game came against Leicester City on 14th January 1989 while he opened his goalscoring account as a professional on 2nd May 1992 against Barnsley.
* He was transfered to Manchester City for £1,600,000 in August 1995. His debut came against Tottenham Hotspur on 19th August 1995 while his first league goal for the club came on 3rd February 1996 against Queens Park Rangers.

* Symons was one of Manchester City's best players during a season which can only be described as disastrous for Frank Clark's men. Symons' contribution was crucial in keeping the club in the First Division. In total he played in 44 games, though he failed to find the back of the net, despite a number of good opportunities coming his way.

580.name: Phillips
pages: * Martin Phillips is a winger who is yet to be given enough opportunities to properly show off his direct, go for goal style of play, since his arrival at Manchester City. It was said of Phillips in some quarters that he would go on to become the first 10 million pound player, although, clearly, that was before Alan Shearer's move to Newcastle United was completed, as well as several others around the world that have since followed. He certainly has the ability to stake a claim for a regular place in Frank Clark's side, although the question is when will he finally take the definitive  step up from reserve team football to finally establish himself in the first team. Although still very young, in no way can be afford to relax if he wants to carve out a future for himself at Manchester City. The league season is a long campaign and he ahs to have a chance of making the breakthrough, although it wouldn't be a surprise if he was eventually loaned out to another side where he would have a better chance of getting some first teamexperience behind him.

* Phillips can play wide on the right although he is a natural left winger, who, while comfortable with the ball on his right, is very much a left footed player. Being a very slim player he needs to put on a little more weight and muscle, since he often has problems when he comes up against physically powerful defenders. A very skillful player, he is a good crosser of the ball and shows good vision. He needs to develop more confidence in himself and try to improve his speed, not being tremendously quick, especially for a winger. Nevertheless he possesses a superb body swerve and dribbling skills, something which invites comparisons with players like Chris Waddle or John Robertson, the ex-Nottingham Forest and Scottland winger. Neither of these two fantastic player were exceptionally quick but were always incredibly difficult to dispossess. If this  comparison hadn't already said enough, Phillips' ball control and balance are also magnificent.
x
x

* Phillips came through the youth ranks at Exeter City, signing as a professional in June 1994. He made his league debut on 9th January 1995 against Wigan Athletic and opened his account on 26th November 1994 against Scarborough.
* He was transfered to Manchester City early in 1996 for £500,000, making his league debut against West Ham United.

* Although he played in just a few games last season Martin Phillips showed that the ability is there. What he needs is to be given the opportunity to get  some experience behind him, to be able to go on to show just exactly what he is capable of. In total he made 4 appearances for Manchester City.

581.name: Rosler
pages: * A bustling centre forward who is also quick and decisive. He possesses real character and never allows himself to be overawed by the opposition, as hard as they might be in their attempts to deal with him. Even when things aren't going too well for him, he will still give 100% in every game he plays. All of these qualities make him one of the favourites with the Manchester City fans. His spell at the club has had its ups and downs, during which he has been an automatic choice one minute and on the bench the next. His quality is not in doubt, but, for the moment, Frank Clark is sticking with the attacking duo formed by Dickov and Bradbury. However Rosler's ability will, sooner or later, surely see him back in the team. If things go normally, he will no doubt have a part to play in the battle to get back into the Premier League.

* A real battler who fights for every ball, both in the air and on the ground. One of his greatest strengths is his ability to get on the blind side of defenders, taking them by surprise and often finding himself in one on one situations with opposing goalkeepers. He strikes the ball well with either foot and is also a powerful header of the ball. He struck up a fine understanding with ex-colleague Niall Quinn, who is now at Sunderland, while he is also a favourite target for the incisive passess slotted through by Kinkladze.
* Top goalscorer for Manchester City in season 94-95, 95-96 and 96-97.
* He made 5 appearances for the old East German national side.

* Manchester City signed him from German club Dinamo Dresden in March 1994 for £750,000. His league debut came on 5th March 1994 against Queens Park Rangers, while he scored his first goal in English football on 29th March 1994 against Ipswich Town.

* Uwe Rosler's season had two very different parts to it. During the first part of the season, the German striker could hardly find the back of the net, and rumours went around that his poor performances would soon see him off to another club. However following the arrival of Frank Clark and some new signings, his form improved dramatically, and he once again became the dangerous striker that he had previously been.His end of season statistics of 15 goals in 44 games made him City's top scorer in the league.

582.name: Kinkladze
pages:
* Georgian  midfielder, Georgi Kinkladze is very much the star man at Manchester City, and, at the same time is one of the players currently most sought after by the big Premier League clubs. However City's chairman Francis Lee, has stated that Kinkladze is going nowhere. Kinkladze is a real diamond of a player, who can only get better and will undoubtedly prove to be a key man if City are to eventually regain their top flight status.
* His first season in the First Division didn't prove to be an easy one. The team weren't playing well and that seemed to have a knock on effect on the Georgian's peformances. On top of this he was given special attention by defenders, being subjected to some really tight and at times aggressive marking with opponents not wanting to give him an inch of space. However, his class told, and he went on to have an outstanding season which was recognised by his fellow professionals when he was chosen for the First Division's ideal team. His contribution will be crucial for Manchester City's attempt to win promotion back to the Premier League. However, for that to happen there will need to be some stability at the club, something which has certainly been lacking over the last two seasons, with the continuous changes in manager at Maine Road.

* Above all, what stands out in Georgi Kinkladze's play is his dribbling, proving as he does, time after time, to be a very difficult player to dispossess without fouling. He is capable of getting in shots on goal almost always with his left toot, showing a genuine goalscoring instinct. Much stronger than he might at first appear, his balance sees him able to work his way out of the tightest of situations. Perhaps he should try to do more of his best work nearer to goal, for the side to get the full benefit of his ability, either to score goals himself or to set up chances for his teammates. Alan Ball  played him in every possible midfield position but was still unable to get the best out of this fabulously gifted player, who, if he can be criticised for anything, it would be for his tendency to drift out of games.
* Chosen in the First Division's ideal team for  96-97.
* The Manchester City midfielder has made 23 full international appearances for Georgia, scoring 5 goals.

* He was signed from Dinamo Tiblisi in the summer of 1995 for £2,000,000. His first game came against Tottenham Hotspur on 19th August 1995, while he scored his first goal in English football on 25th November 1995 against Aston Villa.

* The fine season that Georgi Kinkladze had last time out was one of the few good things that emerged from the disastrous campaign that City went through last season. Even so, despite having an outstanding season, Kinkladze can do better. Perhaps dropping down a division didn't help him to maintain his form, although he did manage to round off the season by being named in the First Division ideal team. In total he played in 39 games, scoring 12 times, half of those coming from the penaly spot.

584.name: Wright
pages:
* Tommy Wright has been described, in the words of Portuguese national manager Artur Jorge, as one of the best goalkeepers in European football. The prestigious Portuguese coach's words are not said without some justification, since Wright is without doubt a fine keeper whose acquisition has been a real boost for Frank Clark and Manchester City. The fact that he plays for a relatively low profile national side like Northern Ireland has meant that he has had a problem in gaining the recognition in footballing circles that his performances have deserved.
* Now a veteran, he hasn't had an easy career, having had a number of spells out on loan at different clubs, apparently unable to settle down at with one  particular side. He will be hoping he can settle at Maine Road, and, at the same time, try to get up into Premier League.

* Wright is, above all, a great goalkeeper. The qualities he possesses make him capable of making some fantastic saves. His reflexes are truly seansational and, as a result, so are some of the stops he manages to pull off. He is safe in the air and is more than steady when the time comes to use his feet to clear the ball. One of the main charasteristics of his game is the very few errors he makes, something which makes him a very consistent performer.
x
* Wright has made 28 international appearances for Northern Ireland.

* Newcastle United paid Linfield £30,000 to sign him on 27th January 1988. His first game for the Magpies came on 14th January 1989 against Aston Villa. 
* He went out on loan to Hull City in February 1991.
* He was transfered to Nottingham on 24th September 1993 for £450,000. He made his debut on 1st March 1994 Against Aston Villa.
* He was loaned out to Reading on 4th October 1996. His first game for the club came on 5th October against Wolverhampton Wanderers. 
* He went to Manchester City on loan on 17th January 1997. His move to Maine Road was made permanent on 3rd March 1997 for £450,000. His debut came on 18th January against Huddersfield Town.

* Tommy Wright had an outstanding season last time out, although not for Nottingham Forest, but for the teams where he had his loan spells, Reading and Manchester City. After making just one appearance for Dave Bassett's men, he had the first of his loan spells, moving to Reading where he played  in 17 games in a run of unbroken appearances until his loan spell was over. At City, his arrival brought extra security to the side. He went on to make 13 appearances and saw his good form rewarded with a permanent move to the Maine Road club.

585.name: Margetson
pages: * Though a member of the first team since 1990, as the years have gone by, Martyn Margetson has had very limited opportunities to show what he can do. However, although such distinguished goalkeepers as Andy Dibble, Tony Coton amd Eike Immel, have passed through Maine Road during that time, the club's coaching staff have never given up hoping that one day, sooner or later, he would break through to become a first team regular. Last season he managed to do just that, coming in to do a good job. However, his most important step forward has come this season, managing to take over from Tommy Wright, who began the season as favourite to retain his number one spot. On this occasion Margetson will be trying to make sure that the opportunity doesn't pass him by.

* One of Martyn Margetson's main assets is his youth, although, obviously, that is not the only thing he has going for him. He is a very complete keeper, who rarely makes mistakes. He is very sure in most trhings he does and is also shows good ability when he us called upon to use his feet. He is also good in the air and possesses good reflexes and possession.
x
* A schoolboy, young and under-21 international for Wales, having made 7 appearances for the Under-21 side.

* After coming through the youth ranks at Manchester City, Margetson signed as a professional on 5th July 1990. His first game for the Maine Road club came on 4th May on 1991. In the local derby against Manchester United. 
* He was loaned out to Bristol Rovers on 8th December 1993, where he played his first game on 18th December against Bournemouth.
* He has also had spells out on loan at Luton Town and  Bolton Wanderers, although he never made a first team appearance with either side.

* Margetson finally got his chance last season after a long spell without making  an appearance for Manchester City. After replacing Andy Dibble in one game he made the place his own and didn't do a bad job, taking into account the team's poor season in general. His appearance were much more limited, following the acqusition of Tommy Wright in January, hardly getting another first team chance all season. In total he made 17 apperances.

586.name: Purse
pages:
* Signed for Birmingham during the 97-98 season.
* Although Darren Purse began his career at Leyton Orient and was even named captain at just 17 years of age, many have hinted that his form hasn't been up to the level expected of him, playing as he has at right back when his more natural position is at the heart of the defence. Last year Purse became Oxford United's most expensive signing, and at no time did he disappoint anybody, putting together some tremendous peformances for such a young player.

* Purse is a central defender who is dominant in the air, taking full advantage of his height and physical presence. He is also very quick and shows a great ability to read his opponents' intentions. For a young defender he is forceful in everything  he does, due to his physical power. A very agile player, sometimes his lack of experience is evident although he has shown himself to be a very quick learner. Despite being technically sound, he prefers to keep things simple when he brings the ball out of defence.
x
x

* Purse learnt his trade in the youth ranks at Leyton Orient, signing as a professional with the East London club in February 1994. He made his league debut on 19th March 1994, against Brighton & Hove Albion. His first goal for the club came against Birmingham City on 13th August 1994 
* He was transfered to Oxford United in the summer of 1996 for £100,000.

* In his first season at Oxford United, Purse made a number of genuinely impressive performances for such a young central defender, making very few errors, which in the main, could be put down to his lack of experience.

589.name: Charlton
pages:
* Signed for Birmingham City in January 1998. 
* Simon Charlton is one of those footballers whose unspectacular game is more appreciated by managers than the crowd.  An untiring worker, in his seasons at Southampton he has always ended up playing in an important number of games per season, although at times, as in the 94-95 season, injuries and suspensions kept him out the team for several weeks.

* Although his natural position is that of left back, Simon Charlton has played in midfield many times.  A left-footed player, he is noted for his defensive game and the way he wins back the ball, helped by his extraordinary physical capacity.  Technically good, he doesn't take part in attack much, and so doesn't get too many chances to try out his shot.  Not very spectacular, Charlton is content to do his defensive duties effectively, working hard.
x
x

* A native of Huddersfield, he soon started to train at Huddersfield Town, turning professional on the 1st of July 1989.  However, his debut didn't take place until the 3rd of March 1990 in a game against Crewe.
* Transferred to £250,000 to Southampton on the 8th of June 1993, he makes debut at the Dell on the 14th of August of this same year in the first game of the league against Everton.  Southampton lose 0-2.  He scored his first goal for the Saints on the 16th of October against Coventry City (1-1). 
* Up till the end of the 95-96 season he had been shown 7 yellow cards, and been sent off once. 
* Signed for Birmingham City in January 1998.

* Simon Charlton adapted to the position of wing back and forced Benali, who in principle should have been first choice, onto the bench. However, an injury forced him out for the last seven games when Southampton where fighting to save their skin.

590.name: Grainger
pages: * Martin Grainger is a player who puts everything he's got into the game, although neither is he a footballer lacking in ability, or technique, as he proves when he steps up to show his masterly touch from free kicks. After a number of good years with Brentford, he became one of Barry Fry's last signings for Birmingham City and was one of the players that Trevor Francis found at the club when he took over. The Blues manager has continued to show his faith in Grainger and he is likely to become aregular member of the ex-England international's line up.

* Grainger is a player who basically operates down the left hand side of the field, either as a midfielder, or in defence, though it is at the back where he plays in the majority of games. Reasonably good on the ball, he has a very selfless attitude and fights for the team throughout the whole of the 90 minutes. One of his greatest strengths is his defensive ability, an aspect of his game which is well appreciated by the manager. He is also a real danger for the opposition from free kicks whilst he is also the team's penalty taker, rarely missing from the spot.
x
x

* After coming through the ranks at Colchester United, he signed professional on 28th July 1992. His first League game came on 19th December 1989 against Torquay United, while he opened his goalscoring account as a professional on 8th January 1992 against Doncaster Rovers. 
* He was transfered to Brentford on 21st October 1993 for £60,000, making his debut for the club on 23rd October against York City and scoring his first goal against Cambridge United on 26th march 1994. 
* Finally, he was transfered to Birmingham City on 25th March 1996 in exchange for £400,000. His first game for the Blues came on 30th March against Grimsby Town and he hit his first goal for the midlands side on 29th March 1997, clinching  victory against Crystal Palace.

* As the season wore on, things gradually got better for Martin Grainger .He missed the first part of the season due to a knee injury although he came back to become a key member of the side. In total he made 23 appearances.

591.name: Wassall
pages: * Darren Wassall is a veteran defender who finally seems to have found the opportunity he has been looking for at Birmingham City, following a numberof seasons at Derby County where he never managed to make himself a regular member of the starting line up. During his time out on loan with the Blues, manager Trevor Francis was suitably impressed and decided to make his move to the midlands a permanent one. A regular member of the side last season, Wassall can now be considered almost an automatic choice either as a central defender or at full back.

* Wassall is an experienced defender who has shown great ability as a man to man marker, taking care of the opposition's danger man. He is also a versatile player who can play either at the heart of the defence as he did when the injuries piled up last season, or at right back. Technically sound he is comfortable bringing the ball out of defence. He rarely moves forward to get involved in the attack and is often at his best in a five man defence.
x
x

* After coming through the ranks at Nottingham Forest, Wassall signed professional terms on 13th February 1988, making his debut against Southampton. 
* He went out on loan to Hereford United on 21st October 1987 and played his first game for the club on 23rd October 1987 against Scarborough. 
* Wassall also went to Bury on loan in March 1989. He made his debut for the Shakers on 4th March against Gillingham and ten days later scored his first, and to date only, goal as a professional. It came against Sheffield United, but was enough to avoid Bury being beaten.
* He was transfered to Derby County on 15th June 1992 for £600,000. His first game for the Rams came on 15th August against Peterborough United. 
* He had yet another loan spell, at Manchester City moving on 11th September. He made his debut for the Maine Road club on 14th September against Crystal Palace.
* Birmingham City was his next destination, on loan again. He arrived at St. Andrews on 26th March 1997, but this time, his loan spell became apermanent move, on 17th May, in exchange for £100,000. His first game for the Blues came on 29th March against Crystal Palace.

* Wassall was unable to force his way into the Derby County side, a situation which brought about his move on loan to Manchester City and later Birmingham City. He made a total of 23 appearances, and was an important member of the side at both clubs although finally it was Birmingham City who signed him on permanently.

592.name: Johnson
pages: * Michael Johnson last season became the joker in Trevor Francis' defensive pack. Doing a fine job in every game and in every position he was asked to play in, Johnson was one of the Blues' most regular performers, something he will be out to repeat this season. Although he hasn't started this season as a member of the starting line up, Johnson is sure to get his chance as injuries come along, a chance he will no doubt take to do his usual competent job.

* Johnson is a player who possesses great physical power as well as exceptional pace, somthing which makes him very difficult to beat for speed. For a defender he shows good touch on the ball. He has good vision and his passes into the midfield area generally find their target. He shows good anticipation in everything he does, making the most of his speed and power. He is good in the air and reasonably comfortable on either foot. He can play in the midfield, as a left sided midfielder or even as a left back.
x
x

* After coming through the ranks at Notts County he signed as a professionalin July 1991. He made his league debut on 26th October 1991, against Arsenal.
* He was transfered to Birmingham City in the summer of 1995 for £300,000 making his debut on 2nd September 1995 against Barnsley.

* Last time out Michael Johnson once again went about his work with discipline finishing the season as one of the players most called upon by Trevor Francis, making a total of 25 appearances in any defensive position in which he was required to play, covering the gaps left by the injuries to Steve Bruce or Gary Abblett.

593.name: Bruce
pages:
* Steve Bruce proved himself to be one of the key men in the resurgence of Manchester United during the 1990's piling up the honours during his time with the Red Devils. A man of great experience and with tremendous leadership qualitities out on the park, Alex Ferguson's club felt that his best years were now behind him and allowed him to leave to join Birmingham City. 
* Although he is now at the veteran stage of his career, his signing proved to be a masterstroke by Trevor Francis, who in Bruce acquired a player who could not only help the team but also advise the club's youngsters in their progress and development. Steve Bruce is an automatic choice for Francis, and, except for injuries, will always be found at the heart of the Birmingham defence.

* Bruce is a very consistent central defender although as the years have gone by he has lost some of his speed something he now makes up for with his tremendous positional play, gained from his years of experience. However when he finds himself pulled out of his position his much more vulnerable, not being a player who is particularly quick on the turn. A very precise, clean tackler he shows a great ability to judge distances. He is a dangerous player form free kicks and corners where he uses his power to get up high and demonstrate his heading ability. A primarily rightfooted player when he is put under pressure he generally sends tha ball long, not being too comfortable in possession, although he is a specialist penalty taker.

* Premier League Championship winners medals with Manchester United in 92-93, 93-94 and 95-96.
* F.A.  Winners medal with Manchester United in 1994.
* F.A. Cup runners up medal with Manchester United in 1995.
* League Cup Winners medal with Norwich City in 1985.
* League Cup Winners medal with Manchester United in 1992.
* European Cup Winners Cup Winners medal with Manchester United in 1991, defeating Barcelona in the final.
* European Super Cup Winners medal with Manchester United in 1991. 
* Manchester United's top scorer together with Brian McClair in 90-91, scoring 13 times, though 7 of those came from the penalty spot..
* Youth and B international for England.

* After coming through the youth ranks at Gillingham. He signed as a professional in October 1978. His debut came on 18th August 1979 against Blackpool while he opened his goalscoring account as a professional on 23rd October 1979 against Oxford United.
* He was transfered to Norwich City in August 1984 for £125,000. He made his debut on 25th August 1984 against Liverpool and scored his first goal for the club against Chelsea on 14th May 1985.
* He joined Manchester United in December 1987 for £800,000 making his debut on 19th December 1987 against Portsmouth. His first goal in the Red Devils' colours came on 13th February 1988 against Chelsea.
* He became a free agent in the summer of 1996, when he signed a two year contract with Birmingham City.

* Steve Bruce brought to Birmingham City exactly what was expected of him when signed; experience, know how, leadership and consistency at the heart of the Blues' defence. He was the team's key man and saw his contribution recognised when the club's supporters voted him most valuable player. In total he played in 32 games..

594.name: Bass
pages: * Jonathan Bass is a player who, despite his youth, has shown that he can keep his cool in tight situations. He hasn't been given too many opportunities at Birmingham City but the qualities he possesses make him a genuine prospect for the club's future. Things are likely to be far from easy although he will no doubt get a chance to show what he can do.

* Bass is a right back with basically a defensive attitude to the game. He shows great maturity for such a young man, above all showing that he can keep his cool in one on one situations with opposing forwards. Quite safe in possession, he prefers to pass the ball short, though it is rare to see him move forward into the attack, except when a clear opportunity presents itself.
x
x

* After coming through the youth ranks at Birmingham City he signed as a professional in June 1994. His league debut came on 17th February 1996 against Stoke City.
* He was loaned out to Carlisle United  in October 1996. His first game for the club came on 12th of that same month against Rochdale.

* Bass made a total of 13 appearances for the Blues during the course of the season bringing extra consistency to the side and making an active contribution to the Blues' run of 10 games without defeat. During a loan spell at Carlisle United he made 3 appearances.

595.name: Ablett
pages: * Gary Ablett is a veteran defender who spent the best years of his career with Liverpool and Everton. Now though he has proved to be a fine acquisition for Birmingham City and has formed a solid central defensive partnership with Steve Bruce. This central defensive pairing brought a great deal of experience to the club last season, and this season will once again prove to be one of the keys to Trevor Francis's sides hopes during the current league campaign.

* For a number of years Gary Ablett had operated as a left back but during the last few seasons has alternated between the left back slot and the central defensive position. Very safe in possession it is very rare to see him give the ballaway. Despite being very much a left footed player, basically using his right to stand on, he is an accurate passer of the ball, both over long and short distances. One of his favourite moves when he gets forward is to play one-twos and go of fon a run towards the penalty area. He is still a quick player and the quality of his crossing remains more than acceptable. It is unusual to see him have a shot at goal although his shooting is certainly powerful enough. Good in the air he poses a threat when he moves forward for dead ball situations.

* League Championship Winners medals with Liverpool 1988 and 1990. 
* F.A. Cup Winners medal with Liverpool in 1989. 
* F.A. Cup Winners medal with Everton in 1995. 
* F.A. Cup runners up medal with Liverpool in 1988.

* An England "B" and under-21 international, he made his debut on 27th April 1988 against France. The game ended in a 2-2 draw, with Paul Gascoigne hitting one of the English goals while the two French goals came from the boots of Eric Cantona.

* After coming through the youth ranks at Liverpool he signed professional in November 1983.
* He went out on loan to Derby County in january 1985 making his debut on 30th January 1985 against Bournemouth.
* He had another spell out on loan at Hull City in September 1986 making his debut on 13th September 1986 against Sunderland.
* He made his debut for Liverpool on 20th December 1986 against Charlton Athletic, scoring his only goal for the Reds on 28th April 1987 against Nottingham Forest.
* He was transfered to Everton in January 1992 for £750,000. He made his debut on 19th January 1992 against Nottingham Forest and hit his first goal for the club on 29th February 1992 against West Ham United.
* He went out on loan to Sheffield United in 1996 making his debut on 2nd March 1996 against Birmingham City.
* In the summer of 1996 he was signed by Birmingham City for £350,000. His first game for the midlands club came on 18th August 1986 against Crystal Palace while he scored his first goal for the Blues on 26th February against Swindon Town .

* As a central defender he became Steve Bruce's permanent partner at the heart of the Birmingham defence bringing all of his know how and experience to the side. He played in a total of 42 games, scoring once.
