599.name: Adebola
pages: * Dele Adebola was Crewe Alexandra's goal man. His sensational season last time out gives the side genuine hope in their First Division adventure. A product of the Crewe's youth system, he has made great progress and is showing signs of maintaining that development this season. However, he was transfered to Birmingham City during the 97-98 campaign.

* A left footed player, he generally plays down the left hand side of the attack, a position from where he likes to make the most of his powerful shooting. He possesses an outstanding change of pace, and shows great mobility, while his height allows him to get in plenty of headers on goal. Given his youth, Adebola has a very promising future ahead of him.
* Top goalscorer for Crewe Alexandra 96-97.
x

* After coming through the youth ranks at Crewe Alexandra he signed professional in June 1993. His first game for the club came on 15th August 1992. He scored his first goal as a professional on 19th November 1994 against Bradford City.

* An outstanding season for Adebola who finished the campaign with his best end of season statistics since he broke into Crewe's first team. He ended up as the club's top scorer and was the side's most decisive player in a campaign which saw them win promotion to the First Division.

600.name: Hughes
pages: * Bryan Hughes is a midfielder with a promising future ahead of him whhas even been compared to Bryan Robson, currently in charge at Middlesbrough. Although these comparisons haven't helped him, he is a player whose magnificent performance against his current club in the cup, saw Trevor Francis determined to sign him for his club. Now in his first full season with Birmingham City, Hughes looks set to to be an automatic choice for his manager, and a player who can become a real success in the First Division.

* A talented midfielder Hughes can perform equally as well in the central midfield position or pushed wider out on the right. He stands out for his one touchstyle of play, as well as his determination and his poweful shooting from outside the penalty area. He is also a palyer who gets forward into dangerous positions although he is yet to turn this into goals.
* Chosen in the Second Division's ieal team for  96-97.
x

* After coming through the youth ranks at Wrexham, Hughes made his debut on 2nd January 1992 against Cambridge United. He had to wait for his first goal for the Welsh club until 15th October 1994 against Hull City. 
* He was transfered to Birmingham City on 12th March 1997. His first game for the Blues came on 16th March against WBA.

* Hughes was a vitally important member of Wrexham's team last season, above all in his ex -club's fantastic run in the F.A. Cup, reaching the quarter finals. He later moved on to Birmingham City, making 11 appearances for the Blues in the First Division.

601.name: Ndlovu
pages:
* Peter Ndlovu is a player who has been dogged by bad luck in recent seasons,at the very time when it was being rumoured that Liverpool were highly interested in signing him, following a game against the Reds at Anfield. However bad luck, as well as a change in position at Coventry City, saw his form dip.
* In the summer of 1997 and after a multitude of problems trying to pass the medical, the African born player signed for Birmingham City, hoping to relaunch his once highly promising career. He could go on to become a very interesting signing for Francis, but only time will tell if he has got it right. He has started the current campaign as a member of the starting line up which, if he can stay clear of injuries, can only help him regain the form he showed when he first burst onto the scene.

* He can do a good job as a striker, as a left sided midfielder or tucked in behind the two main strikers. Although he is basically right footed he is comfortable on eitherfoot. A hard running mobile player, he is physically strong and puts in a tremendous amount of work throughout the whole of the ninety minutes. He keeps rival defenders under constant pressure never allowing them to bring the ball out at the back unchallenged. Technically good he makes the most of his speed to take on defenders and go directly for goal. He has a good shot with his right foot, and when he has the ball under control in the penalty area, he is not a player who tends to pass up goalscoring opportunities.
x
* 29 full international appearances for Zimbabwe, with 11 goals to his credit. He made his full international debut at just 15 years of age in a game against Mozambique.

* Bobby Gould discovered Peter Ndlovu in the mid 1980's during a trip to Zimbabwe. There Peter and his brother Adam were combining their careers with Highlanders, the most important club in the country, with their jobs as salesmen in a Hi-Fi store.
* During the 1990 pre-season both of them were invited to have a trial with Coventry City.  Adam failed to make the grade although Peter managed to impress the Sky Blues' coaches. He was transfered to Coventry for £10,000 on 16th August 1991. He made his debut on 24th August of that same year against Queens Park Rangers.
* In 1992 he was voted "Sportsman of the Year" in Zimbabwe. He was the first footballer to receive the award since 1958.
* During the 93-94 season he was the club's top scorer with 11 goals. 
* He scored a goal in a Cup tie against West Bromwich Albion which was voted goal of the month for January 1995. On 14th March of that same yea rhe scored a hat trick against Liverpool at Anfield. It had been 33 years since a visiting player managed to score three against the Reds at Anfield.

* Ndlovu had a disappointing season, taking into account the quality that he possesses. After getting injured while he was playing for Zimbabwe, he didn't reappear until October. He failed to make a regular first team place his own, and made the majority of his appearances as a substitute. He played in a total of 20 games, scoring once.

602.name: Furlong
pages: * As the most expensive signing in the club's history Paul Furlong still has to show that the money laid out to bring him to St. Andrews was money well spent.This classical centre forward this season has the chance to get back to his best as a regular member of Trevor Francis' side, this after a series of disappointing seasons. Both Paul and the club will be looking for him to reach somewhere near the twenty goalsmark this time round..

* Furlong is a centre forward of great physical power, who, as is to be expected, is a superb header of the ball with a tremendous ability to get up above defenders. Very much a left footed player he has good ball control, which allows him to get the time and space he needs to get in shots on goal, or hold the ball up waiting for his teammates to get up in support. He always gives 100% out on the pitch and is an untiring worker, selfless and always working for the team, never throwing in the towel when things go wrong. He is quick and has great power which allows him to constantly keep rival defenders under pressure. With the ball at his feet he is not ove-rblessed in the skill department while as a left footed player he is always looking to get the ball onto his left to have a shot at goal.
* Top Scorer at Watford in the 92-93 seasons and in 93-94.
x

* Although Paul Furlong began his career at amateur club Enfield,Coventry City signed him in July 1991. He made his debut for the Sky Blues on 17th August 1991 against Manchester City while he opened his goalscoring account as a professional 4 days later, against Luton Town.
* He was transfered to Watford in July 1992 for £250,000. His debut came on 15st August 1992 against Millwall scoring his first goal for the club one week later against Grimsby Town. * Chelsea splashed out £2,300,000 to sign him in May 1994. His debut for Blues could hardly have been better, managing to find the back of the net against Norwich City on 20th August 1984. 
* He was transfered to Birmingham City in the summer of 1996 for £1,500,000. He made his bow for the Blues of Birmingham on 18th August against Crystal Palace while his first goal in a Birmingham shirt came in the very next game when he found the target against Sheffield United.

* He put together a fine first season at Birmingham City although he might consider his goals return to be on the disappointing side. However his commitment out on the park won him the support of the club's fans and only a touch of bad luck prevented him from adding to his goals tally. He made a total of 43 appearances, finding the target on 10 occasions.

603.name: Poole
pages: * After a number of successful years defending Leicester City's goal, KevinPoole was forced to give way to the arrival at Filbert Street of Kesey Keller, who made the first team place his own, except for on the few occasions when he was either injured or away on international duty. Now, in the summer of 1997, Poole has seen himself move on to Birmingham City, with the opportunity to fight with Ian Bennett for the first team goalkeeping spot representing a new challenge. Nevertheless, if he doesn't make the position his own, he will still be providing the Blues with quality goalkeeping cover if injury problems should strike.

* The extraordinary reflexes that Kevin Poole possesses make him a really spectacular keeper. He reacts with great speed, anticipating the strikers' intentions. He also stands out for the safety of his handling and for the determination he shows when comes off his line to claim high crosses. An experienced campaigner, he is also a confirmed specialist when it comes to saving  penalties.
x
x

* Kevin Poole learned his trade in the youth ranks at Aston Villa. A professional since 26th June 1981, he had to wait until the 84-85 season before making his debut for the Villa Park based outfit after first going out on loan for a spell at NorthamptonTown, in November 1984.
* On 27th August 1987 he moved to Middlesbrough on a free transfer, but, in four seasons at the club, managed to make just 34 league appearances. On 27th March 1991 he went out on loan, once again, this time to Fourth Division Hartlepool United where he made 12 appearances.
* On 30th July 1991, he was transfered to Leicester City for £40,000, making himself the regular first choice goalkeeper in his first season at Filbert Street.
* In 1994, as second choice, he experienced the club's promotion to the Premier League. But, in the following season, now a first team regular once again, Leicester went straight back down. Nevertheless Poole was chosen by the fans as the club's "Player of the Year"; for 94-95.
* In the 95-96 campaign he confirmed himself as a first team regular, despite the club's signing of a new keeper, the Australian international  Zeljko Kalac. Poole's phenomenal performance in the promotion play-offs was a key factor in the "Foxes" return to the Premier league, after they overcame Crystal Palace 3-2 in the final game of the season.
* He was transfered to Birmingham City in the summer of 1997.

* Kevin Poole was unable to prove as much of a key member of the side as in previous seasons at Leicester City, due to the rise of Kesey Keller. The veteran English keeper saw his first team opportunities reduced to the point of him making just seven appearances all season. Nevertheless, despite only playing when Keller was either injured or away with the United States, Poole did the job that was expected of him in the games he did appear in.

604.name: Bennett
pages: * Ian Bennett's tremendous goalkeeping qualities make him one of the most outstanding keepers in the First Division and one of the most sought after outside the Premier League.  Together with Alan Kelly of Sheffield United, he is one of the best goalkeepers in the division, and is a key man for Birmingham City, where he is an automatic first team choice despite the recent acquisition of Kevin Poole. If he shows the form he is capable of then Birmingham City could well have a chance of winning promotion to the Premier League, though it remains a difficult task, given the intense competition.

* Bennett is a very complete keeper who has all the attributes necessary to make him what he is, one of the best in the First Division. He possesses exceptional reflexes, which allow him to make some incredible saves. He is also tremendously agile which, added to his already mentioned reflexes, make him a very difficult keeper to beat. His positional play is excellent, while he rarely makes an error of judgement when he comes off his line for high balls, either in the six yard box or in the rest of the penalty area. He always gives a real sense of security which he spreads on to the rest of the defence, safe in the knowledge that behind them they have a keepr of genuine quality.
* Chosen in the Second Division's ideal team while with Birmingham City, inthe 94-95 season. * Second Division Championship winners medal, 94-95 with Birmingham City.
x

* Bennett arrived at Newcastle United in 1989 from Queens Park Rangers juniorsides.
* He failed to make an appearance for the Magpies first team and moved on to Peterborough United in March 1991. His debut came on 8th April 1992 against Bournemouth, where he played through until the end of the season. 
* He was transfered to Birmingham City in December 1993 for £325,000, making his debut in the local derby against West Bromwich Albion, on 28th December 1993.

* Bennett was an automatic first team choice for Trevor Francis at Birmingham City, where he made 40 league appearances. He had an excellent season which, perhaps, was only bettered by that of Alan Kelly of Sheffield United, who carried off the honour of being named in the First Division's ideal team. Bennett had a spectacular end to the season managing to keep a clear sheet in 7 of the last 9 games.

605.name: McCarthy
pages: * Together with Paul Furlong Jon McCarthy is the most expensive signing in Birmingham's history. An extremely quick winger who is also dangerous inside the box, he first caught the eye of Blues' manager Trevor Francis the season before although McCarthy's club, Port Vale, turned down his offer. However when Francis went back a second time in September he was more successful and the player moved on to Birmingham City, a club with genuine hopes of reaching the Premier League. McCarthy is one of the first pieces in the jigsaw of a team that Francis is attempting to put together very much in the way he wants. As the season draws on he may well prove to be the key man.

* A right winger, McCarthy is a constant source of danger when he gets forward. As a result he is a player who receives special attention from rival defenders, who watch over him with especially tight marking. He carries the ball well, apparently tied to his foot, while his dribbling causes real panic amongst opponents. He stands out not for the quality of his crossing but his ability to run withthe ball, looking for the opportunity to play a decisive through pass or to get in a shot on goal.
x
* A Northern ireland international on four occasions plus one appearance as a "B" international.

* A product of Hartlepool United's youth system he signed as a professionali n November 1987, making his debut in the league on 7th May 1988 against Hereford United.
* He was transfered to York City in March1990, making his first appearance on 29th September 1990 against Gillingham. He scored his first goal as a professional on 5th February 1991 against Doncaster Rovers. 
* He moved on to Port Vale in August 1995 for £450,000 pounds. He made his bow for the Potteries club on 13th August 1995 against Derby County opening his account for the club on 7th October 1995, against Huddersfield Town. 
* His next destination was Birmingham City who splashed out £1,500,000 for his services in September 1997.

* McCarthy was one of Port Vale's key men throughout last season playingin 45 out of 46 games, scoring four times in the process. Not only did he have a successful season at club level but he was also called up into the Northern Ireland squad and was given the opportunity to make his debut.

606.name: Robinson
pages: * Steve Robinson is one of the brightest prospects among Birmingham City's young players, and his contribution last season saw him thrust into the spotlight for both the club's supporters and the coaching staff. The club have plenty of faith in him and gave him a two year extension to his contract, a real vote of confidence for any young player. He began the season as a member of the starting line up, but following the acquisitionof Jon McCarthy, a player who takes up a similar position to his own, he saw himself temporarily relegated to the bench. Although at present not everything is in his favour, his tenacity and determination will no doubt see his opportunity given during the course of the season.

* Robinson is a player who basically operates down the left hand side of the park, doing a great containing job and standing out in general for his defensive contribution. His selfless attitude knows no limits and when he is go in to win the ball, he more often than not comes away with it.
x
x

* A product of Birmingham City's youth system, he signed as a professional on 9th June 1993. His debut for the Blues didn't come his way until 4th March1995, against Hull City.
* He went out on loan to Peterborough United on 15th March 996. His first game for the club came on 16th March 1996 against Crewe Alexandra.

* Last time out Robinson could only sit and watch as an inexplicable illness forced him out of the beginning of the season, seriously limiting his first team opportunities.He eventually made a total of 9 appearances for Birmingham City.

607.name: O´Connor
pages: * Last season Martyn O'Connor became a key man for Trevor Francis' Birmingham City, following his arrival at the club from Peterborough United, where he never quite settled down.This powerful midfielder's contribution is expected to be fundamental for the club's hopes of winning promotion to the Premier League.

* As well as being an excellent midfield organizer, Martyn O'Connor also possesses an acute goalscoring instinct, something which managers appreciate in any midfield player. A footballer with plenty of character he never shirks the responsabilies of keeping the team ticking over; a responsability which allows him to show his extraordinary creative ability. His selfless attitude is also well appreciated, an attitude which, combined with his ability, makes him a very complete player.
x
x

* Crystal Palace signed him from amateur club Bromsgrove Rovers on 26th June 1992. His first game for the Eagles came on 20th November 1993 against Barnsley.
* He was loaned out to Walsall on 24th February 1993, although finally the move was made permanent. On 14th February 1994, in exchange for £40,000. His debut for the club came against Shrewsbury Town on 27th March 1993, while he opened his goalscoring account against Darlington on 6th April. 
* He was transfered to Peterborough United on 12th July 1996 for £350,000. He made his first appearance for the club on 17th August against Bristol Rovers and, just a week later scored his first goal in Peterborough's colours against Crewe Alexandra.
* Birmingham City paid out £500,000 for his services on 29th November 1996. Just one day later he made his debut for the Blues against Norwich City, and enjoyed the satisfaction of striking the winning goal.

* Martyn O'Connor had something of a Jeckyll and Hyde season, starting off with Peterborough United, where, during his short stay, he never quite settled down. He made 18 appearances scoring 3 times before being transfered to Birmingham where he did manage to make a place in the side his own, becoming almost irreplaceable for Trevor Francis. With the Blues he played in 24 games scoring four times.

608.name: Holland
pages: * Chris Holland is a midfielder with a tremendous future ahead of him although the tremendous competition at Newcastle United saw him first sent out on loan to Birmingham City before that move was made permanent. He had a good season but the Blues will be hoping that this young player can go on to fullfill the expectations that everybody has of him, and which, at one time saw him compared to the brilliant Paul Gascoigne. Howeve,r things will be far from easy for him this season given the club's acquisition of Jon McCarthy.

* Holland is a midfielder of tremendous class and who has an even better future ahead of him. Blessed with excellent technique, he carries the ball well, apparently tied to his foot, though he does prefer his right to his left. He has excellent dribbling skills and a real change of pace which allows him to get away from tight marking. He is an excellent passer of the ball, showing great accuracy over both long and short distance. A player of great vision he is a quick thinker and is capable of creating danger with just one pass. Quite a fast player, he is a good crosser of the ball, able to pick out his best placed  teammate, putting top quality service in to the strikers. He also packs a powerful shot in his right foot.
x
* 10 under-21 international appearances for England, he made his debut in theToulon International Tournament on 7th June 1995 against Letonia.

* After coming through the ranks at Preston North End, Holland made his debut in the league for Preston on 16th October 1993 against Wigan Athletic. 
* He was transfered to Newcastle United for £100,000 in January 1994 and made his first appearance for the Magpies on 23rd March 1994 against Ipswich Town.
* He went to Birmingham City on loan in September 1996. 
* His move to Birmingham City was finally made permanent in October 1996 for £600,000 pounds.
* Holland had his chance to show what he can do during his first season at Birmingham City, making 32 appearances, though he didn't manage to hit the back of the net.

609.name: Legg
pages: * Andy Legg was an important member of Trevor Francis' side last season with his quick runs down the flank, and he will hoping to provide more of the same this season to try to help Birmingham City into the top flight of English football, the Premier League. He will have a real fight on his hands to make himself a first team regular, following the acquisition of a man like Peter Ndlovu, bearing in mind that the Zimbabwean international plays in the same position.

* Legg is a midfielder who generally operates down the left hand side of the park,showing himself to be an attack minded player from that position, getting forward to support the attack as soon as the opportunity presents itself. He has good dribbling skills, is quick and likes to go off on solo runs, taking on defenders before putting over a cross to pick out the strikers. An enthusiastic player he helps out with defensive duties and can even do a job as a left back. He has a good shot in his left foot, although he doesn't make use of it too often.

* A Welsh cup winners medal with Swansea City in 88-89, 90-91.
* Top scorer for Swansea City in  92-93, together with Colin West.
* Legg has made 4 full international appearances for Wales, the first of those on 24th Aptil 1996, against Switzerland, when he came on in place of Gary Speed.

* Swansea City signed him from amateur club Britton Ferry in August 1988. He made his debut on 1st October 1988 against Bristol City and opened his goalscoring account, as a professional, on 10th March 1990, a goal which clinched victory for his side.
* He was transfered to Notts County in July 1993 for £275,000 pounds and made his debut for the club on 14th August 1993 against Middlesbrough, his first goal coming on 22nd January 1994 against Bristol City.
* He signed for Birmingham City in February 1996, making his first appearance on 2nd March 1996, against Sheffield United. His first goal came seven days later in a game against Tranmere Rovers.

* Legg was one of Trevor Francis' most important and most frequently used players during the course of last season, playing in 35 games scoring 4 times. 
His excellent form was translated onto the international scene, playing in two matches for Wales against Holland in a qualifying game, and against the Republic of Ireland.

610.name: Tait
pages: * At present Paul Tait is Birmingham City's longest serving player. Last season was one of his best at the club and one which could prove to mark the start of a new era of his now lengthy career with the Blues. Although he has not been an integral part of Trevor Francis' plans so far this season, last year's form would suggest that he can repeat what was a fine campaign personally speaking, and once again become a key man for the Blues manager.

* Tait is an attack minded midfielder, a player who has previously played as a striker. He has good technique and a real sense of opportunism in front of goal, being a player who makes good runs into the box, getting onto the end of crosses either with his head or his feet, always apparently popping at just the right time. He is also a very combative player in his part of the pitch, winning plenty of possession. He has great strength and outstanding reserves of stamina. Good with both feet, he is, in short, a very complete player.
x
x

* A product of Birmingham City's youth system, he signed professional terms in August 1988. He made his league debut on 6th May 1988, against LeedsUnited, and hit his first league goal on 26th September 1989, against Walsall. 
* He is remembered for having scored two important goals. The first of those clinched the Autoscreen Trophy for Birmingham City against Carlisle United on 23rd April 1995 while the second against Huddersfield brought the club the Second Division championship crown.

* Last season was one of Paul Tait's best for Birmingham City, putting together some great performances which saw him make a total of 26 appearances throughout the season. The only black spot to the season was his inability to find the back of the net.

611.name: O´Connor
pages: * Derek O'Connor was signed during a trip to Ireland by the Huddersfield Town coaching staff who were suitably impressed by the Irishman's ability. His opportunities to break into the side have been zero, but this hasn't stopped the young Irishman from making progress through the Irish national team's youth set up. He made the squad to take part in the Under-17 World Cup in Malaysia. His contribution to the Irish side proved to be decisive. O'Conner was first choice in goal and helped his team reach third place in the competition. His role at Huddersfield Town for the moment is to go on learning from Francis and wait patiently for his opportunity.

* Derek O'Conner is a keeper whose qualities have made him a first choice at several different levels for the Republic of Ireland. He possesses all the attributes he needs for the job: good reflexes, positioning, the ability and inclination to use his feet as modern keepers need to as well as the obligatory dominance in the air, despite not being the most physically overpowering of goalkeepers.
x
* He has reperesented the Republic of Ireland at a number of different levels, currently playing for the under-21 side.
* Huddersfield Town signed him from Irish club Crumplin United in 1995.
x

612.name: Francis
pages: * An undisputed first team choice since arriving at the club from Reading in 1993 Francis has played more than 40 games in each of the 4 seasons in which he has been with the Terriers, demonstrating the reasons why he was signed, as well as the fact that Brian Horton got it spot on when he decided to bring him to the club. A very safe keeper who can also make spectacular saves, if nothing out of the ordinary happens he should go on to be Huddersfield's regular keeper this season, if nobody manages to unnerve him. He will have under him the young prospect from Irish football, Derek O'Conner, a young goalkeeper who he will be out to help to go on to become a fine professional himself.

*  A goalkeeper with enormous experience behind him, one of his main virtues in his positional play which helps him enormously when called upon to make spectacular saves. Despite not being a particularly tall keeper he is excellent in the air. He always thinks before coming off his line, never doing so in a reckless manner. He occasionally hesitates when coming out, but when he is undecided he will generally prefer to stay on his line. He possesses great reflexes which together with his positional sense makes him a very safe keeper. As if all these attributes weren't enough, he is also a specialist when it comes to saving penalties.
x
* An England youth international.

* After coming through the youth ranks at Chelsea, he signed professional  in April 1982 making his league debut on 14th November 1981 against Oldham Athletic.
* He was transfered to Reading in February 1987 for £20,000, playing his first game for the club on 28th February 1987 against Shrewsbury Town. 
* Huddersfield signed him in August 1993. He made his debut against his old club Reading on 14th August 1993.

* A man who was practically irreplaceable for Brian Horton throughout the whole of the season, Francis played in 42 games and only lost his place to Tony Norman for a matter of a few games, although he quickly won back his number one spot.

614.name: Facey
pages:
* Delroy Facey last season became the fifth youngest player in the history of Huddersfield Town to make his league debut when he made his bow against Portsmouth. His enthusiasm out on the park has won him the admiration of the Terriers' faithful who see him as an important player in the futureof the club, and also one for the current season.
* His tremendous potential was underlined when in May 1997 the club offered him a new contract for 3 years to keep him at his home town club. A striker with a brilliant future ahead of him, he will no doubt get a chance this season to show what he can do.

* Facey is a player who is a natural centre forward and is always a source of danger when he is involved in the action. He is good in the air, despite not being too tall, and, when he goes up for the ball, he often proves to be a real handful for the defenders around him. His fighting spirit seems to know no limits as he gives it absolutely everything he's got out on the park. These attributes hide the technical weaknesses in his game, although he has all the time in the world to improve them.
x
x
* After coming through the ranks at Huddersfield Town Facey signed as a professional on 13th May 1997. His first game for the Terriers came on 15th March against Portsmouth.

* Delroy Facey's contribution last season was limited to just 3 games with Huddersfield Town although in those games it was easy to see what this young striker had to offer Huddersfield Town, an unselfish attitude and unequalled enthusiasm.

615.name: Beresford
pages: * David Beresford is one of the most promising players to have come through the ranks at  Oldham Athletic in recent times. Nevertheless, his transfer to Huddersfield Town will give him more of a chance to get a taste of success, playing for a more competitive side like the Terriers. A quick skillful winger, a lot is expected of him and this year he will be hoping to force his way into Brian Horton's team on a regular basis.

* A player who prefers to play as an orthodox right winger, he can also do a job down the other flank. Beresford possesses a devilish turn of pace and is an explosive player in everything he does. He has good dribbling skills both on the run as well as from a standing start. His crossing is excellent, arrowed in at the forwards, often with plenty of  swerve on the ball. He has a powerful shot in his right foot and while he prefers his right, his left is far from useless. He is not physically strong, which means he loses out in physical challenges with defenders, but he is a clever player and tries to avoid these physical clashes whever he can. He is also willing to get back and help out the full back playing behind him with his defensive duties.
x
* Beresford has represented England at under-15, 16, 17 and 18 levels.
* A product of Oldham Athletic's youth system he made his Latics debut on 2nd May 1995 against Barnsley. His first league goal came on 21st October 1995 against Reading.

* Berersford was a first team regular at Oldham Athletic where he made a total of 33 appearances, becoming a key member of Graeme Sharp's team. Before the transfer deadline in March, he moved on to Huddersfield Town, a team where he also became a first team regular, playing in 6 games and scoring one against Southend United.

616.name: Payton
pages:
* Andy Payton was one of the players who arrived at Huddersfield Town as a result of the money that the club obtained following the sale of Andy Booth to Sheffield Wednesday. His departure from Barnsley surprised just about everybody and saw the Terriers snap up a real bargain for an insignificant amount of money.
* A complete goalscoring striker, his signing was an extremely good one for the side and as well as representing the incorporation of a fine player, he also linked up exceptionally well with Marcus Stewart. Together they formed a really intimidating partnership, striking up a tremendous understanding which guarantees plenty of goals for the Terriers. Without doubt, Brian Horton got it 100% right.

* Andy Payton is a centre forward with a tremendous knack of finding the back of the net, thanks to his ability to always be in the right place at the right time. He shows splendid ball control when in goalscoring situations, and is a quick player with tremendous ability. He often moves parallel to the central defenders trying to get ontheir blind side. He has a good shot with either foot although he prefers the right, and is also a magnificent header of thanks to his anticipation and ability to get in frontof defenders. A very brave player he fights for every ball.

* Top goalscorer for Hull City seasons 89-90 and 90-91.
* Top goalscorer for Glasgow Celtic 92-93.
* Top goalscorer for Barnsley 93-94 and 95-96.
* Top goalscorer for Huddersfield Town 96-97.
x

* After coming through the ranks at Hull City Andy Payton signed as a professional in July 1985 making his league debut on 4th April against Stoke City while he scored his first goal as a professional against Leeds United on 3rd January 1988.
* He was transfered to Middlesbrough for £750,000 in November 1991.His debut couldn't have been better, scoring in the game against Bristol City on 23rd November.
* He signed for Glasgow Celtic in August 1992. He played his first game for the club on 15th August 1992 against Dundee United and scored his first goal in the famous green and white hooped shirts on 29th September 1992 against Airdire.
* Barnsley signed him in November 1993 in exchange for Wayne Biggins who moved to the Scottish club. He made his debut on 27th  November 1993 against Bolton Wanderers while his first goal came on 11th December 1993 against Peterborough United.

617.name: Stewart
pages:
* Marcus Stewart is Huddersfield Town's jewel in the crown. Signed initially as cover for Andy Booth, the young English striker has become a fine footballer and one of the most outstanding attackers outside the Premier League. If everything goes well and he suffers no setback the Premier League is where he could well end up in the not too distant future.
* Last season, in his first season at the club, he was unable to find the form he would have liked, and which was expected, due to injuries. However, this year free from any physical problems then the best should be seen of Marcus Stewart, a real star in the making. He is an automatic first team choice for Brian Horton.

* Stewart is a centre forward who can also play just behind the two main strikers as a link up man between the forwards and the midfield. With the ball apparently tied to his feet the English striker possesses fine dribbling skills and is capable with either foot although he feels more comfortable on his right. He can shoot with either foot from distance. In side the area he is very quick to react while he is cool enough to work out quickly what needs to be done in tight situations, never losing his nerve in front of the opposing goalkeeper. Sometimes he will drop back and play the ball around with passes played with either the outside or the inside of either foot. He will also pull out wide to the flanks to open up gaps into which his midfield colleagues can come through.
x
x

* After coming through the youth ranks at Bristol Rovers he signed professionalin July 1991. His debut for the club couldn't have been better, scoring against Ipswich Town in a game played on 17th August 1991. 
* He was transfered to Huddersfield Town in July 1996 for £1,240,000.

* Last season was a disappointing one for Marcus Stewart, after all the expectation that had surrounded his signing for the club. The disappointment was not however, because his form had failed to live up to expectation, but because that he was limited to making just 20 appearances for the Terriers although that didn't prevent him from becoming second top scorer. In only his second game for the club he managed to hit a hat-trick against Wrexham in the Coca-Cola Cup.

618.name: Richardson
pages: * One of the most talented players who has ever played for Oldham Athletic in their history, Lee Richardson has finally left for Stockport County this summer, and he hopes to be able to perform as well as he did for the Latics, where he was, without doubt, a sensational player.  He is the team's reference and his the club's fortunes will depend, to a large extent, on his contribution.

* Lee Richardson is the team's playmaker, moving the ball about with both feet.  He has a very powerful shot with his right, almost like a missile, and with his left he will also have a go though he is not as good with this foot.  He gets into some good positions and his header can be useful.  He is able to set moves in motion from the back and get into a dangerous position with a powerful run.  He can pass both in short and over long range and has a great presence in the midfield.  He is a great penalty taker.

* Top scorer for Oldham Athletic in the 95-96 season.
* Voted best player in the First Division in the 95-96 season by the press.
x

* Originally from the lower ranks of Halifax Town, he signs as a professional in July 1987.  He makes his league debut on the 15/8/87 against Darlington and scores his first goal as a professional on the 7/5/88.
* In February 1989 he is transferred to Watford for £175,000.  He makes his debut on the 25/2/89 against Brighton & Hove Albion and scores his first goal on the 16/12/89 against Bradford City.
* He is transferred to Blackburn Rovers in exchange for £60,000 and Andy Kennedy in August 1990.  He plays his first game on the 25/8/90 against Bristol City and scores his first goal on the 8/9/90 against Ipswich Town. 
* In the summer of 1992 he is signed by Aberdeen in exchange for £150,000. He makes his league debut on the 19/9/92 against Partick Thistle and scores his first goal in the League on the 7/11/92.
* Oldham Athletic sign him in July 1994 for £300,000, scoring two goals on his league debut against Charlton Athletic on the 13/8/94.
* With Aberdeen he plays in the FA Cup an League Cup finals in the 92-93 season but the team loses both games to Glasgow Rangers.
* The best player at Oldham Athletic in the 95-96 season as voted by the fans at the club.
* His next team is Stockport County, the team he joins in the summer of 1997.
* Before the start of the 97-98 season, his record for taking penalties was 100%, 27 goals from 27 attempts.

* Richardson had a very outstanding season for Oldham Athletic last year, once again being one of the best men and shining in a team which finally was relegated to the Second Division.  Despite missing the end of the league due to a hernia which needed surgical intervention, Richardson managed to play in 31 games and score 4 goals.

619.name: Browning
pages: * Despite being a target for Wimbledon, Marcus Browning finally signed forHuddersfield Town, who tempted the player from the Premier League club. A Welsh international, his fine performances for Bristol Rovers and now with the Terriers has seen him become a regular in the Welsh squad. The strong man in the middle of the park, a lot is expected of him this season.

* A midfield player blessed with plenty of physical power, Marcus Browning is every inch an athlete. He stands out for his ball winning ability and the way in which he gets forward to support the team's attacking  play, lending the weight of his considerable physical power, however, he is not a player who gets on the score sheet with any real regularity.
x
* 2 full international appearances for Wales.

* After coming through the junior ranks at Bristol Rovers, Browning signed as a professional on 1st July 1982. His debut came on 28th January 1990 against Bolton Wanderers while his first goal as a professional came against Cambridge United on 18th December 1992, a goal which clinched the match for his team.
* He went out on loan to Hereford United on 18th September 1992. He played his first game for the club on 18th September against Barnet and scored his first goal for them on 3rd October against Wrexham.
* Finally, he was transfered to Huddersfield Town on 17th February 1997. His first game for the Terriers came on 22nd February against Bolton Wanderers.

* Last season was an important one for Marcus Browning, once again proving himself to be a key man for Bristol Rovers. He played in 26 games and scored twice before being transfered to  Huddersfield Town where he immediately made himself an automatic choice right through to the end of the seasn. He played in a total of 13 games for the Terriers though he is yet to open his goalscoring account for the club.

620.name: Baldry
pages: * A product of Huddersfield Town's squad and born in the city, Simon Baldry is an extremely quick left winger although in recent seasons he has been unable to force his way into the Terriers' line up on a regular basis. He is still young enough to improve though and force his way into Brian Horton's side. The club have also offered him a new contract to keep him at Huddersfield for another 2 years, a real vote of confidence. Time will tell if Baldry is capable of taking advantage.

* Simon Baldry is a player who basically plays down the left hand side of the field, hugging the touchline, and trying to make the most of his sensational pace which is without doubt his greatest strength. He is not a footballer lacking in ability either, although he is not a player who poses too much of a goalscoring threat, something he leaves to the Terriers' strikers.
x
x

* Simon Baldry was only able to make 7 appearances for the Terriers last season, basically coming into the action off the substitutes bench. Logically he was unable to make a significant contribution.

621.name: Edwards
pages: * Rob Edwards is a midfielder who has a special killer instinct in front of goal, a priceless ability which he converts into an important number of goals. After shining at Crewe Alexandra, Edwards has seen how his form has dipped since signing for the Terriers although this can be put down to the fact that he is more tied down to one position rather than his being less effective or dangerous, something which Stewart and Payton would underline. He is likely to be a key figure in Bryan Horton's side.

* Edwards is a left footed, left sided midfielder who generally operates without straying too far from his position. He scores a significant number of goals with his head or with either foot, though he prefers his left, which he uses to good effect to shoot from distance. A quick player, his crossing is good, while he is always willing to get back and help out with defensive duties.
x
x

* A product of Crewe Alexandra's youth system, he signed professional in July1988, making his debut on 12th December 1987 against Cardiff City while he scored his first goal against Peterborough 6 days later. 
* He was transfered to Huddersfield Town in March 1996 for £150,000. His debut was as good as he could have hoped for, scoring the winning goal against Luton Town on 13th March 1996.

* Although the season wasn't as spectacular as his start to his new career with Huddersfield Town, Edwards still showed himself to have a goalscorer's instinct and made a decisive contribution to the fine goalscoring records of  both Payton and Stewart. In total he played in 33 games scoring 3 times.

622.name: Makel
pages: * Lee Makel wasn't given much of a chance to show what he could either at Newcastle United or Blackburn Rovers. He has had to wait until meeting up with Huddersfield Town manager Brian Horton to find the man who would be able to get the best out of him and prove that he is an excellent footballer. After really taking off last seson he now has the task of improving on that and settling down in the Terriers' side. Without him in the team Huddersfield lost a real focal point of their play something which indicated that Lee Makel is finally establishing himself as a fundamental member of Brian Horton's Terriers side.

* Makel is a constructive midfielder who is capable of directing the way the team plays, moving the ball around playing basically a short passing game, always accurately and efficiently always seemingly capable of picking up the pace of the game when necessary. He is more at home on his right foot than his left, and although he is not a powerful attacking force when he does get into the attack he does so by picking the ball up from one-twos and then lifts his head to look for Stewart and Payton. He is not a physically powerful player something which means his ball winning ability is not what it could be. Depending on the way the team lines up, he can play either in the centre of midfield or pushed out a little wider on the right hand side. He possesses excellent basic technique, which makes him something of a free kick speciallist.
x
x

* A product of Newcastle United's youth system he signed as a professional in February 1991. He made his debut on 4th May 1991 against WBA, and scored his first league goal on 7th December 1991 against Port Vale. With the arrival of Kevin Keegan in the "Magpies" hot seat he saw himself very much kept in the shadows.
* In July 1992 he was transfered to Blackburn Rovers for £160,000, making his debut on 2nd May 1994 against Coventry City. 
* The competition for a place in Blackburn Rovers' midfield proved to be intense and as a result he moved on to Huddersfield Town in the Autumn of 1995 for £300,000. He made his debut for the Terriers on 14th October 1994 against Reading and scored his first goal for the club against Luton Town on 23rd December 1995.

* Last season was an outstanding one for Lee Makel at Huddersfield Town. During the  period in which he made himself the team's midfield focal point he was an automatic first team choice. In the 19 games in which he played he managed to find the back of the net on 3 occasions, making the most of his ability from free kicks. Unfortunately injury later kept him out of action, and in his absence the Terriers lost their way.

623.name: Dalton
pages: * In his third year at Huddersfield Town, Dalton will be out to consolidatethe good form he has shown since his arrival at the Yorkshire club. A talented footballer capable of producing moments of real skill he is also on occasions somewhat inconsistent drifting out of games and barely making a contribution. He will normally make the starting line up playing down either flank, although the competition is stiff as was demonstrated last season when a large proportion of his appearances came as a substitute.

* Dalton is a wide midfield player who, being equally comfortable on either foot, can do a good job down the left or down the right. He has talent, good vision and reasonable dribling ability. He likes to go down the flank at speed, going past defenders on the run looking to get crosses over for the forwards to get their heads to. He is also a dangerous player when he lines up to take free kicks.
* Hartlepool United's top goalscorer during the 91-92 season.
x

* Dalton found it difficult to settle down as a regular in Brian Horton's side due to the enormous competition for places. A good proportion of his 29 appearances were as a substitute, nevertheless he did manage to make a contribution, finding the back of the net on four occasions.

628.name: Morrison
pages: * Following the sale of Andy Booth to Sheffield Wednesday, Huddersfield Town decided to invest a part of the money they received in the acquisition of Andy Morrison, a defensive midfield player who can also play as a central defender ifrequired . In defence he shows the same qualities, and is also a tight marker and good in the air, despite not being particularly tall. He is basically a right footed player.

629.name: Cowan

Since his arrival from Sheffield United, Tom Cowan has been a real tower of strength at the back for Huddersfield Town and has also been a real threat for the opposition at dead ball situations due to his power in the air. Very much a part of Horton's plans the Terriers' left back is unlikely to let him down .

* A very sold left back, though favouring his left foot he is also comfortable on his right. A good passer of the ball either short or long, he is an attack minded fullback who gets forward as soon as the opportunity presents itself. However, he is not the quickest of players and can have problems when he comes up against quick wingers though he generally sorts out any problems he might have by going in hard for the ball, showing strength, determination and anticipation. Though an aggressive player he always goes in fairly to win the ball. In attack he possesses a good long throw-in with which he can reach the penalty spot. Despite not being particularly tall he is good in the air thanks to his jumping power and the determination he shows when going up to win the ball.

631.name: Gray
pages: * At just 25 years of age Kevin Gray shows great maturity and composure out on the park. Although he has all the qualities he needs to play in his position, he needs to continue building on what he started last season when he finally managed to make a place in the Terriers' first team his own, improving at the same time some of the weaker aspects of his game. The great job he had done in recent years was however marred by his tackle on Gordon Watson, which saw the Bradford City man forced out of action for a lengthy period. It was also a tackle which eventually lost Gray his place in the team. Nevertheless, he islikely to prove to be a key man at the back for Huddersfield this season.

* Although a central defender Gray is a player who is very secure on the ball, always seeming to be comfortable in possession. Despite his ability on the ball though he rarely ventures upfield, prefering to pass it on to the midfield men. He will go forward for dead ball situations although he is not a player who poses a great threat. Defensively he is not outstanding in the air and is not to be wholly relied upon, lacking authority in this aspect of his game. He is basically a right footed player.
x
x

* After coming through the youth ranks at Mansfield Town he signed professional in July 1990. He made his league debut on 6th May 1989 against Chesterfield and opened his professional goalscoring account on 1st February against Cambridge United.
* He was transfered to Huddersfield Town in July 1994 for £20,000 and played his first game for the club on 3rd September 1994 against OxfordUnited. His first league goal for the club came on 13th September 1996 against Oldham Athletic, a goal which proved to be the winner.

* Kevin Gray put together a sensational campaign last time out doing a great job and making one of the central defensive spots his own. However, towards the end of the season as a consequence of a tackle which left Bradford City's Gordon Watson seriously injured he lost both his form and his place in the side. In total he played in 39 games for the Terriers, managing to find the back of the net once.

632.name: Bracey
pages:
* Lee Bracey was one of the most popular players with the Bury supporters from the moment he signed for the club. His hard work and charisma won him the admiration of both fans and teammates alike. Nevertheless in recent seasons things hadn't gone quite so well, with Bracey barely making an appearance in the last two league campaigns. 
* Faced with the same situation Bracey saw the opportunity to move on to Ipswich Town as reserve goalkeeper behind Richard Wright. In these circumstances he accepted the offer and, given his quality and experience, proved to be an excellent signing on the part of  George Burley. His opportunities to get into the side were limited during the course of last season to the games in which Wright wasn't available, though it proved impossible to dislodge the young Blue's keeper from his place in the side.

* Lee Bracey is an experienced keeper, with plenty of know how. The sense of security which he spreads to his teammates is well appreciated, while he hardly ever lets them down when he is called into the action. A charismatic figure, he was always well loved by the fans at his previous club Bury.
* Welsh Cup Winner medal with Swansea City, 1989.
x

* After coming through the youth set up at West Ham United, Lee Bracey signed for the Hammers as a professional on 6th July 1987. However he didn't manage to make a first team appearance for the East Londoners.
* He became a free agent and signed for Welsh club Swansea City on 27th August 1988. His first appearance for Swansea, and his first as a professional, came on 26th November against Blackpool.
* Transfered to Halifax Town on 17th October 1991 in exchange for £47,500, his debut followed on 19th of that same month against  Chesterfield.
* Finally he moved on to Bury, on 23rd August 1993 for £20,000, making his debut for the Shakers five days later against Crewe Alexandra. 
* He had a spell out on loan at Ipswich Town during last season, although he didn't manage to make a first team appearance. Nevertheless, in the summer of 1997, the suffolk club decided to pay out £50,000 to make his move to Portman Road a permanent one.

* Although having spells at two different clubs, Bury and Ipswich Town, Bracey was unable to force his way into the first team at either club during the course of the season, having to settle for a place on the bench and wait for an opportunity that unfortunately didn't come his way.

633.name: Wright
pages:
* Richard Wright is one the brightest young goalkeeping prospects in English football. He shows great security in everything  he does and demonstrates a surprising calmness for a young man who is barely 20 years of age, a maturity which inspires confidence in his teammates. Craig Forrest was the first victim of the rise of Wright, the Canadian being first relegated to the bench and later transfered to West Ham United 
* Wright has already had a taste of what it is like to train with the full England side which is where he could well end up in the not too distant future if he maintains his almost unstoppable progress.

* A very agile young man, this ability allows him to make outstanding saves. Still very young his performances still show a little inconsistency, occasionally showing rather too much confidence in his own ability. His ability in the air is acceptable, though one of the faults in his game which he needs to iron out is his judgement of distances when he comes off his line, a fundamental part of the game for goalkeepers in English football.
x
* He has reperesented England at both youth and schoolboy level.

* A product of Ipswich Town's youth system, he signed professional in January 1995 making his league debut on 6th May 1995, against Coventry City and played out the end of the season, although Ipswich had already been relegated to the First  Division.

* Wright was always first choice in goal for Ipswich Town, and went on to complete a sensational season. Not only did he see off Forrest's challenge for the first team spot, but he also managed to consolidate himself as the club's undisputed number one. Only a few back problems managed to prevent him from playing in every league game. He had a spectacular end to the season, managing to keep a clean sheet in five consecutive games. In total Wright played in 40 matches.

634.name: Venus
pages:
* In the summer of 1997, Mark Venus saw himself involved in one of the biggest transfer deals between two First Division clubs, forming part of the deal  which took Steve Sedgley to Wolverhampton Wanderers, with Venus plus £350,000 moving in the opposite direction to Ipswich Town. Mark Venus is a player who tries to make up for his lack of technical ability with his great enthusiasm and his competitive attitude, giving absolutely everything he's got all over the pitch, whether he is playing either at right back or in midfield.
* His arrival at the club represents one of George Burley's attempts to strengthen the side in the face of this season's attempt to win promotion to the Premier League. Acquiring a man of Venus' experience can only help the club's cause. He can play in a number of different defensive positions offering his manager a touch of versatility.

* Venus generally lines up as a central defender and played slightly towards the left hand side of the 5 man defence that Mark McGhee employed at Wolves. He is strong in the air, both in defence as well as in attack. Very much a left footed player he only rarely brings the ball out from the back, prefering to play it short or, when he is under pressure, clearing his lines and sending it long. He has a good shot in his left foot, both from free kicks as well as in open play. He can do a job in midfield but always in a defensive role.
* Third Division Championship Winners medal with Wolves in 88-89.
x

* Mark Venus came through the youth ranks at Hartlepool United to sign professional in March 1985. He made his debut in the league on 8th April 1985 against Bury. 
* He became a free agent and moved on to Leicester City in September in 1985. He played his first game on 31st March 1986 against Aston Villa, while his first goal in the league came on 7th November 1987 against Swindon Town, a goal which turned out to be the winner. 
* He was transfered to Wolverhampton Wanderers in March 1988. He made his debut on 12th march 1988 against Carlisle United, opening his account on 30th Septmeber 1989 against Portsmouth. 
* During the 94-95 season he played at least one game in every shirt except the number one and number nine. 
* Ipswich Town signed him in the summer of 1997 in a player plus cash deal which took Steve Sedgley to Wolves, plus another £350,000 going to Ipswich Town.

* Few people expected Mark Venus to become one of the regulars in Mark McGhee's  Wolverhampton Wanderers side. His total of 40 games made him one of McGhee's most used players playing in a number of different defensive positions, but always doing the job expected of him.

635.name: Cundy
pages:
* After several seasons at big clubs, Jason Cundy never really managed to settle down and establish himself in the Premier League. During the 90-91 season he saw plenty of action for Chelsea, at the time appearing to be at the start of a promising career. However, little by little, that early promise faded and he now finds himself at Ipswich Town bringing solidity and defensive security to the Portman Road Club. 
* Unfortunately bad luck has dogged Jason Cundy's progress. Just when it seemed that he had made a place in the team his own, he was diagnosed as suffering from cancer. The most important battle of this brave player's life was only just beginning, and it was a battle which he would go on to win, even managing to force his way back into George Burley's plans for the current season. After getting over the worst, Cundy should now try to look forward optimistically and attempt to relaunch his career. After everything he has gone through, he will now surely feel confident of overcoming anything.

* A central defnder who stands out for his ability in the air, undoubtedly his greatest strength. He moves forward to support the attack from dead ball situations, making the most of his power in the air. Though technically limited, he brings experience to the heart of the defence. If he could improve his touch on the ball, then he would be able to make more of a contribution in an attacking sense.
x
* 3 under-21 international appearances for England, with 1 goal to his credit.

* Jason Cundy learnt his trade at Chelsea where he signed professional on 1sr August1988. He would have to wait until 1st September 1990 to make his first team debut, in a game against Queens Park Rangers.
*  After a spell playing for Tottenham on loan, he finally made his move to White Hart Lane a permanent one on 26th March 1992, in exchange for £750,000. 
* Transfered to Ipswich Town in October 1996 for £200,000, he made his Blues' debut on 9th November against Southend United while his first goal in an Ipswich shirt came a week later against Bradford City.

* Once again Jason Cundy was barely given a chance to make a contribution to Spurs season. His participation at Tottenham Hotspur was limited to training sessions and reserve team football. He was later loaned out to Bristol City and Ipswich Town, who finally took him on permanently. He had a better time of things with the Blues getting 13 appearances under his belt, something he hadn't managed to do at his previous club.

636.name: Stockwell
pages: * Mick Stockwell is a player whose only club has been Ipswich Town. A permanent fixture at the club over its last ten years of history. Always ready to go out and do a job for the side, wherever he is asked to play, he is a real tower of strength and still a top class performer. He is one of  Ipswich Town's automatic choices, and once again, this season will no doubt prove to be one of the most popular players with supporters.

* A fast, attacking right back, Stockwell is an expert at playing one-twos to make his way up the flank. He can play as a wide midfield player, or even as a emergency striker. He is good solid tackler and is a difficult opponent to get the better of, and is thoughtful and efficient passer of the ball.
* Second Division Championship winner's medal with Ipswich Town in 1992.
x

* A player who is a product of Ipswich Town's youth system, as a youngster he also had trials with Leyton Orient. He signed professional terms in December 1982 and played his first game in the league for Ipswich on 26th December 1985 against Coventry City. He had to wait until 5th December 1987 to hit his first goal which came against Bradford City. 
* In the 95-96 season he had a testimonial match, the opposition being provided by Oporto, then managed by ex-Ipswich boss Bobby Robson. 
* He was voted player of the year for 1993 by the Ipswich Town supporters.

* Stockwell began the season as Ipswich Town right back, proving to be irreplaceable for George Burley. However, following the return of Uhlenbeek to the first team, Stockwell moved forward into midfield. From that position he was able to push forward much more, something which allowed him to achieve his best goals tally in a season, finding the net on 7 occasions.

639.name: Dyer
pages: * Keiron Dyer is one of the products of the revitalized youth policy that Ipswich Town have been carrying out in recent years. At just 18 years of age he has managed to break through into the first team on a regular basis and, as a result, great things are expected of him in the future. His professional career has only just begun, and he seems to have everything in his favour. George Burley has been showing plenty of faith in him, though we will have to wait and see if this young player manages to stand up to the rigours of the First Division and go on to make his mark on the team.

* Dyer is a young player whose main strength is his versatility, able to play in a number of positions in midfield or even as a full back in a five man defence, working away untiringly up and down the line. However he has more than just versatility to his game, as he also possesses a real quality touch on the ball, basically with his right foot, as well as the ability to go past opponents. As if all those previous qualities weren't enough he is also a fine passer of the ball.
x
* Dyer is an England youth international.
* After coming through the club's youth system, Dyer signed as a professional with IpswichTown on 3rd January 1997. His first game for the first team came on 26th December against Crystal Palace.

* Dyer turned out to be a pleasant surprise for Ipswich Town last season when he managed to break through into the first team, playing in a total of 13 games and demonstrating spectacular potential for such a young player.

640.name: Holland
pages: * Matt Holland  is one of the players Ipswich Town have signed with a view to putting together a squad of players who can take them up to the Premier League. A footballer of great strength and quality his versatility will prove to be invaluable for George Burley during the coming season due to the inevitable problems of injuries and suspensions, which will no doubt see Holland called upon to do a job in whatever position he is required to cover. He is likely to be a first team regular for the Blues.

* Although Matt Holland is a quality midfielder with the ability to get into the opposition's penalty area, he can also do a fine job playing as the free man behind the defence. He possesses a great shot at goal from distance and never hesitates to make the most of it when the opportunity presents itself. He is also decisive at the back, a quality which, added to his other strengths, makes him a very complete player.
x
x

* After coming through the ranks at West Ham United, Holland signed as aprofessional on 3rd July 1992. However he never got the opportunity to make his first team debut for the Hammers. 
* Holland signed for Bournemouth on 27th January 1995, his debut coming one day later against Huddersfield Town. His first goal came later against Leyton Orient on 1st Apri. 
* He was transfered to Ipswich Town during the summer of 1997 in exchange for £800,000.

* Matt Holland did a fantastic job last season. Not only did he put in some tremendous, performances from his position in the middle of the park but, when required, showed that he could drop back and do a job in defence. His performances brought great solidity to the side. By the end of the season he had made 45 appearances and scored 7 goals.

641.name: Petta
pages: * A product of the youth system at Dutch club Feyenoord, Bobby Petta is trying to make a place in the first team his own at Ipswich Town, a club who moved in to sign him and for whom he put in some good pre-season performances. However, his inability to keep up with the frantic rhythm of the English game saw him watching the majority of the games from the stands. This year, after having gained more experience in England with Ipswich, a lot more will be expected of Bobby Petta. He may well become a first team regular due to the quality he possesses, though everybody will have to wait and see if he manages to force his way into George Burley's starting line up.

* A quick left winger, Petta prefers to operate down the left, but can also give a good account of himself in other areas of the pitch, although always in attacking positions. He is basically left footed, though he possesses great technique. A skillful  player he likes to knock the ball about playing short accurate passes. He has good vision which allows him to put good passes through to create situations of real danger.
x
* Holland under-18 and under-21 levels.

* Bobby Petta completed his contract with Rotterdam based club, Feyenoord and signed for Ipswich Town in May 1996. The Dutchman has signed a 3 year contract for the Blues. 
* His debut came on 16th August against Manchester City.

* It wasn't the sort of season that Bobby Petta would have hoped for at the beginning of his career in English football. He began the season in the starting line up but his inconsistency saw him dropped first to the bench, then later to the stands, becoming the forgotten man of  Ipswich Town. In total he played in 6 games.

642.name: Mason
pages:
* Last season Paul Mason became one of  Ipswich Town's most influential players,  completing his best season at the club since his arrival at the club from Aberdeen in, 1993.  The Blues top goalscorer, he was the team's focal proint and a constant source of danger. 
* Fortunately for the club the transfer request that Mason put in the season before was long forgotten, and now all he has to look to is the future and to try to make as big a contribution as possible to help Ipswich achieve the ultimate prize of promotion to the Premier League. He will no doubt be an automatic choice for George Burley.

* A wide midfielder who can operate down either flank, he is a quick player, although technically weak. He makes up for this weakness however with his enthusiasm which sees him constantly getting up and down the flank. He is a player with the ability to get into the opposing penalty area, surprising defenders to get in efforts on goal with either foot. He prefers to play out on the flank from where he can cut inside and have a strike at the target.

* Scottish League Cup Winners medal 89-90, for Aberdeen defeating Glasgow Rangers in the final. 
* Scottish Cup Winners medal 89-90 with Aberdeen against Glasgow Celtic.
* Scottish Cup runners up medal 92-93 with Aberdeen, losing against Glasgow Rangers. 
* Ipswich Town's top goalscorer 96-97.
x

* Signed from Dutch side Groningen by Scottish club Aberdeen in August 1988 for £200,000  he made his league debut on 20th August 1988 against St. Mirren, scoring his first goal against Dundee United on 12th November 1988.
* Ipswich Town signed him in June 1993 for £400,000, scoring on his league debut against Oldham Athletic on 14th August 1993. 
* He scored both goals for Aberdeen in the 1989-90 Scottish League cup final, the Dons winning by two goals to one.

* In his most prolific season since he arrived at Ipswich Town, Paul Mason proved to be the Blues' most decisive player throughout the whole season, ending the campaign as the club's top scorer, with 12 goals in 43 games. He was a key man for George Burley's side, making a crucial contribution in a fantastic season which unfortunately ended in disappointment when they were eliminated in the promotion play offs.

643.name: Williams
pages: * Geraint Williams is a player who is almost always available for his manager and one who does an invaluable ball winning job, an unglamourous one which is not always given the recognition it deserves. His presence in the side is almost totally guaranteed, due to the amount of good work he has done for the club down the years. He is an automatic choice for George Burley and is currently the Ipswich Town captain.

*A midfield player who plays just in front of the defence, doing a basically destructive job, he has the rare ability to carry the ball away with him from the majority of physical clashes which he goes into. He is a good ball winner, who, once he has achieved his objective, plays the ball off quickly, without making things too complicated,  laying it off short to a teammate.
* Second Division Championship winners medal, 86-87 with Derby County.

* A Welsh international level at youth and under-21 level, he made his full international debut on 11th November 1987 against the now defunct Czecoslovakia in a qualifying game for the 1988 European Championship finals in Germany, a game which was vital for for the Welsh side's hopes of qualifying although they eventually lost 2-0. In total he has made 13 full international appearances for Wales.

* After working his way through the junior and youth sides at Bristol Rovers, he signed professional in January 1980. His league debut came on 18th October 1980 against Sheffield Wednesday, while he scored his first goal in the league on 8th November 1980 against Shrewsbury Town.
* He was transfered to Derby  County in March 1985 for £40,000, making his debut on 30th March 1985 against Brentford. His first goal came on 2nd November 1995 against Rotherham United, a goal which earned his side a draw.
* Finally he signed for Ipswich Town in July 1994 for £650,000 with his first game for the club coming on 14th August 1993 against Oldham Athletic while he hit the back of the net for the club for the first time against Leeds United on 1st November 1994.

* Geraint Williams put together a fine season and was almost always available for  manager George Burley, doing great work in the midfield. His first goal for the club came against Oldham Athletic, Williams being the first to react to a shot from Uhlenbeek that came back off the post. A the end of the season he was even named captain, in place of Steve Sedgley.

644.name: Milton
pages: * Despite now being at the veteran stage of his career Simon Milton still retains great energy in his game, which makes him still very much a key man in George Burley's line ups. Nevertheless Ipswich Town will no doubt be looking for a replacement to take over from him when the time comes. In the meantime though, he still has a place in the side and must importantly of all, still has plenty of football left in him yet. He will be an important player for Ipswich Town this season in their attempt to get into the Premier League.

* Simon Milton is a strong midfielder who posess good basic technique. He gets into the penalty box well and strikes a good ball  with either foot. In excellent condition for his age, this allows him to continue making constant runs forward in support of the attack. He showed his versatility during the course of last season playing both in the middle of the park as well as pushed out wide on the right.
* Second Division Championship winners medal 91-92 with Ipswich Town.
x

* Ipswich Town signed him in July 1987 from amateur club Bury Town, for £5,500. His league debut came on 28th December 1987 against Swindon Town while his first goal for the club proved to be the winner on 7th May 1988 against Bradford City. 
* In November 1987 he went out on loan to Exeter City, managing to find the net twice in his first league game on 21st November 1987, against Stockport County. 
* He went out on loan once again, but this time to Torquay United, in March 1988. His debut came on 5th March 1988 against Hartlepool United and, 6 days later, he struck his first goal, the winner, against Crewe Alexandra.
* Voted Ipswich Town player of the year 1995-96. 
* He is a Cambridge university graduate in industrial electronic engineering.

* Injuries dogged Simon Milton throughout last season, preventing from making himself a regular in the side. His 23 appearances came almost exclusively as a substitute. As a result he was also unable to make the goalscoring contribution he had done in previous seasons.

645.name: Uhlenbeek
pages: * After putting together a fantastic season with Ipswich Town, Gus Uhlenbeekturned out to be one of the club's best buys of recent seasons. He is a player who is a key man in George Burley's line up and will no doubt prove to be fundamental  in the club's fight to win promotion to the Premier League. A player of great speed and good technical ability he may soon be looking to make the step up to the international scene with the Dutch national side. But for the moment Dutch national boss Guus Hiddink is yet to call him up, which means Uhlenbeek will have to just keep working hard to try to force his way into his plans.

* The Dutchman is a right sided midfield player who possesses great speed, getting forward into the attack with real danger, capable of taking on defenders down the flank and get over excellent crosses. He gets into the penalty area dangerously, surprising defenders with his speed while his strikes on goal are well directed into the corners. He possesses good skill which he uses to get out of tight situations, either with a clever backheel or by playing a one-two with a teammate.
x
x

* Ipswich  Town signed him from Dutch club SV Tops in August 1995 for £100,000, his league debut coming on 12th August 1995 against Birmingham City, while he opened his goalscoring account against Watford on 16th September 1985.
* He played for Ajax as a youth team player.

* Although last season wasn't as impressive as his first season wiith the club. Uhlenbeek once again demonstrated that he is a vital member of the Ipswich side. His problems began in the pre-season when he picked up an injury which prevented him from returning to his natural position until December, when he made the position his own. He played in a total of 38 games.

646.name: Mowbray
pages:
* Tony Mowbray is a man who shown enormous bravery both on and off the pitch. Out on the park he is a real tower of strength for the defence, and a real leader for the rest of the team, with the younger players in particular benefitting from his presence. Off the field, he is a man who has managed to overcome personal tragedy following his wife's death from cancer in the first few days of January 1995. 
* A real example for all young players Tony Mowbray is all all about courage and is a key piece in the jigsaw that George Burley is attempting to put together to take Ipswich into the Premier League. Neverthless it would initially appear that Tony's first team opportunities are likely to be limited.

* A central defender, he is excellent in the air, and likes to go in hard, but always fairly, to try to win the ball for his side. A very difficult player to overcome physically, it is when he comes up against quick skillful forwards that he has problems, never having been a particularly agile player himself. He is, of course, a real threat in the air from set pieces, but, apart from these situations, never ventures upfield.
x
* 2 "B" international appearances for England.

* A product of Middlesbrough's youth system, he signed professional in November 1981. His league debut came on 8th September 1992 against Newcastle United, while  his first goal, which also proved to be the winner, came on 20th April 1984 against Carlisle United. 
* He was transferd to Glasgow Celtic in November 1991 for £1,000,000. He played his first game against Aberdeen on 9th November 1991, while his first goal north of the border came on 28th December 1991, against the same team he made his debut against, Aberdeen. 
* Ipswich Town signed him in October 1995 for £300,000, making his debut against Wolverhampton Wanderers on 7th October 1995. It was also against Wolves that he opened his goalscoring account in Ipswich Town's colours.

* An injury which initially it was thought could be cured on the spot, went a long way in determining what type of season Tony Mowbray had last time out. He suffered two recurrences of the same injury, which caused him to miss the majority of the club's matches. When he managed to get back to full fitness, Swailes and Vaughan were in such good form that he was limited to just 8 games.
