650.name: Scowcroft
pages: * James Scowcroft is a young striker who has managed to make himself a regular in George Burley's side. His enormous strength and the danger he causes in the air have deservedly attracted the attention of some of the powerful Premier League clubs, such as Liverpool,  who were said to be very interested in Scowcroft, and in Craig Forrest, now a West Ham United player. Scowcroft has a promising future ahead of him, and it is  now up to him to carry on attracting the attention of the elite of English football.

* A strong centre forward, good in the air, technically he lacks the quality that would allow to challenge the club's first choice strikers, such as Alex Mathie. He works hard to keep the opposition defender under constant pressure.
x
x

* A player who has learned his trade in the youth ranks at Ipswich Town, he made his league debut on 7th October 1995 against Wolverhampton Wanderers. His first goal on 10th February 1996 against  Stoke City.

* Following the departure of Ian Marshall, James Scowcroft won himself in Ipswich Town's starting line up, going on to compelete a very promising season. He played in a total of 40 games scoring 9 times, including two against Bolton Wanderers which inflicted the first defeat of 1997 on the team who would eventually go on to win the First Division and gain automatic promotion to the Premier league. He even managed to find the back of the net in a play off game against Sheffield United, but it wasn't enough to prevent Ipswich Town being eliminated.

651.name: Taricco
pages: * Mauricio Taricco last season became one of  Ipswich Town's best players, creating plenty of danger down his left hand side of the pitch. After a dubious beginning to his career in English football, the Argentinian has made himself a regular name on the Ipswich Town teamsheet. This season the club will, at least, be expecting from him contribution which helps to get the team up almongst the front runners, in the fight for promotion to the Premier League.

* A left winger despite being naturally right footed, he is a very attack minded player, who has good ability to beat players, although his crossing needs to improve. Defensively he is quite weak, although he seemed more settled when the side played with three central defenders.
x
* He is an Argentinian under-23 international.

* Ipswich Town signed him from Argentinos Juniors in September 1994, for £175,000. His English league debut came on 2nd September 1995 against  Sunderland, when he came on for Tony Vaughan. He scored his first goal on 24th August 1996 against Reading. 
* His father played for both Turin clubs, Juventus and Torino.

* Mauricio Taricco proved to be  Ipswich Town's most solid perfomer last season, earning him the honour of being voted the club's player of the year. He had confortably his best season yet in English football, and was a key man in the Blues' excellent season. In total he played in 41 games scoring 3 times.

652.name: Tanner
pages: * A player who is very much one to be watched for Ipswich Town, Adam Tanner  isn't just a hard worker in the midfield but also possesses enviable technique. Playing generally out wide on the right, from there he is well capable of sending long accurate passes through to the strikers. He hasn't yet had enough opportunities to be able to make a first team place his own due to the tremendous competition that exists at Portman Road. He will also have to wait and see what is the outcome of the incident which occured last year when he tested positive for cocaine and was suspended for three months. The supporters and the directors have stood by him but, only time will tell how he progresses in the wake of these events.

* A player who possesses a great shot with either foot, as a central midfielder he also displays a good touch on the ball, playing a neat short passing game, as well as showing a willingness and ability to get forward quickly in support of the attack. His longer passing is also accurate thanks to his great technique and vision. On top of these qualities he also wins plenty of possession for the side.
x
x

* A product of the youth system at Ipswich Town, he signed as a professional in July 1992. In his debut in the league, on 2nd January 1995 against Leicester, he scored a goal which went on to be voted as the goal of the season by the clubs supporters. 
* Twelve days later he scored another with a tremendous left foot effort, but this time the setting was Anfield against Liverpool. His goal gave Ipswich Town a victory at Anfield for the first time in the club's history after 34 visits to the famous stadium.

* Once again Adam Tanner's opportunities last season were most noticeable by their absence. He managed to make just 16 appearances all season. His best run came in December when he managed to form part of the team on a regualr basis, although was playing at the heart of the defence. He took on the responsability of taking the club's penalties, in the absence of Steve Sedgley. His season was ruined however when he tested positive for cocaine. He was suspended for three months by the league's executive Body.

653.name: Mathie
pages:
* A centre forward of great elegance and technique, Alex Mathie didn't enjoy too many opportunities to show his quality at his previous clubs. However, given the chance of  regular first team action at Ipswich Town, he has demonstrated that the club certainly didn't make a mistake when they decided to sign him, making an excellent contribution, showing good form and, above all, scoring goals. 
* Last season saw something of a halt in the almost unstoppable progress of the scot, who is now among the best strikers in the First Division. Now back and ready to compete following a serious injury, he will no doubt become one of the men in which George Burley places his trust in his attempts to get Ipswich Town back in the Premier League once again.

* A striker of real class, he has good dribbling skills and can score goals from all kinds of positions with either foot. He has plenty of tricks up his sleeve and, when he is fully fit, is very quick. Another of his virtues is the way he can hold the ball up, waiting for midfield men to come through and pick it up from him .
* Top scorer for Morton in the 91-92 and 92-93 seasons.
x

* After coming through the youth ranks at Celtic, he signed professional in May 1987. His league debut came on 11th February 1989 against Motherwell.
* Not enjoying  too many first team opportunities, in August 1991 he was transfered to Morton for £100,000. He scored his first goal for the club on his league debut against Partick Thistle on 10th August 1981.
* He was loaned out to Port Vale in March 1993, making his debut on 3rd April against Reading. 
* Transfered to Newcastle United in July 1993 for £285,000, he scored in his first appearance for the Magpies against Sheffield Wednesday on 13th  September. 
* Given the tremendous competition for a place in the forward line at St. James' Park, he decided to accept the first offer of a move that came his way. As a result he moved on to Ipswich Town in February 1995 for £500,000. He had an excellent debut for the club, managing to find the back of the net in the game against Southampton on 25th February 1995.

* Alex Mathie had a sensational start to the season, taking on the club's goalscoring responsibilities, following the departure of Ian Marshall, in the best way possible, with goals. He became a real cutting edge in the Ipswich attack. However, an unfortunate injury against Crystal Palace, a dislocated shoulder, represented the end of what was a highly promising season. In all he made a total of 12 appearances, finding the back of the net on 4 occasions.

655.name: Ndah
pages: * George Ndah is another product of the Crystal Palace youth system, whose progress has too often been hindered by jnjuries. Despite this he had the full confidence of the club's coaching staff, who, in November 1996 decided to extend his contract for another three years. However, Ndah signed for Swindon in November 1997.

* He generally plays as a centre forward, a position whoich allows him to take adavantage of his imposing stature to dominate in the air. He can also play tight down the left hand touchline, where he creates danger with his speed in possession. A left footed player he has an excellent shot at goal.
* First Division winners medal with Crystal Palace 93-94.
* An England youth international.

* He is the brother of Jamie, who is a professional with Barnet. 
* After coming through the youth ranks at Crystal Palace, he signed  professional in August 1992. He made his league debut on 28th November 1992 against Liverpool at Anfield in a 5-0 defeat. He scored his first goal for the Eagles at Leicester City on 14th January 1995. 
* In November 1996 he renewed his contract with the Eagles for another three years. 
* Signed for Swindon in November 1997.

* George Ndah played in 26 league games during the course of last season, although he started in just five. Despite this the Crystal Palace coaches once again showed plenty of confidence in him, giving him a three year extension to his contract.

656.name: Hay
pages: * Christopher Hay is the only new signing of note for Swindon going into the new season. It looks like he could turn out to be one of the bargains of the First Division. His impact at the Robins has been devastating, leading the team from the front as a marksman, being compared with the great Welsh striker, Ian Rush, by his own manager. He is unusually calm and has an amazing capacity for scoring goals. If he manages to keep up his sensational start to the season, Swindon Town could go far.

* Hay is a player who, in his spell at Glasgow Celtic played as a midfielder but since his arrival at Swindon has played a more forward role, or more exactly, a link-man with Allison. He has an amazing scent for goal, and has already shown that he is very cold-blooded when finishing chances. He has outstanding technique and is very quick.
x
x
* Originally from Glasgow Celtic, Hay signs for Swindon Town during the summer of 1997 for £330,000.
* Hay played 14 games for Glasgow Celtic during last season, showing a scent for goal, scoring 4 times in this limited number of appearances.

657.name: Allison
pages: * Wayne Allison is a brave footballer, a continual torment for rival defenders. A hard-worker, he doesn't shirk when it comes to defensive play. He responds to the model of a classic centre forward, a powerful player with a lot of strength but somewhat limited technically. A regular for Steve McMahon, he is forming an excellent partnership with Chris Hay, both reaching a great understanding together.

* A very strong centre forward, he is excellent in the aerial game and has a great header. He shoots with both feet without thinking about it, although for moving the ball about he is better with his left. He has a medium range shot to be reckoned with. However, he is technically rather weak and when he can't shoot, he is content with passing the ball. You don't often see him try the individual play.

* Second Division Champion 95-96 with Swindon Town. 
* Top scorer with Bristol City in the 91-92, 93-94 and 94-95 seasons.
* Top scorer with Swindon Town in the 95-96 and 96-97 seasons.
x

* Originally from the lower ranks of Halifax Town, he signs as a professional in July 1987, scoring on his league debut against Wolverhampton Wanderers on 17th March 1987. 
* He is transferred to Watford in July 1989 for £250,000, making his debut in the league on 14th October 1989 against Brighton & Hove Albion.
* In August 1990 Bristol City sign him for £300,000, making his debut against Swindon Town.  His first goal comes against Port Vale on 27th October 1990. 
* He is finally transferred to Swindon Town for £475,000 in the summer of 1995. His league debut takes place on 12th August 1995 against Hull City. His first league goal is scored against Oxford United on 30th August 1995.

* Allison finished the season as the top scorer at Swindon once again, but his campaign had two distinct phases. In the first half of the season he played well, scoring 10 goals before Christmas, but from then on, his game dropped off considerably, scoring only 3 times after Christmas. In total he played 44 games and scored 13 goals.

658.name: Kerslake
pages: * In his day, David Kerlsake was considered to be one of the brightest prospects in English football, but his inability to make an impression either at Leeds United or Tottenham Hotspur, has meant that his career has taken something of a nosedive. However, that doesn't mean that he can no longer prove to be an important player for the club he is playing for.

* David Kerslake generally plays at right back although his mobility allows him to also play in midfield down that same flank. Kerslake is a player who is always looking to get forward and is quick to get forward into the attack, in support of the midfielders and strikers. Though not over blessed technically he gets into good shooting positions and gets on the scoresheet with some regularity. As the years have gone by he has lost a little of his pace, making him more vulnerable at the back, and also one of the reasons why he faded out of the first team reckoning at Tottenham.
x

* Two "B" international appearances for England. 
* One Under-21 international appearance. 
* 27 youth international appearances scoring 8 goals.

* After coming through Queens Park Rangers' youth system, he signed professional on 1st June 1983. However, the opportunity to make his league debut didn't come until 13th April 1985, against Newcastle United. 
* On 24th November 1989 he was transfered to Swindon Town for £110,000. 
* His spell at Leeds United turned out to be a brief one. Signed for £500,000 on 11th March 1993, after making just 8 appearances he was transfered to Tottenham Hotspur on 24th of that same month. The fee was £450,000. 
* He went out on loan to Swindon Town in November 1996 and played his first game for the club on 23rd November 1996 against Birmingham City. 
* He became a free agent form Spurs and signed for Ipswich Town in the summer of 1997.

* The 96-97 season wasn't a particularly positive one for David Kerslake, once again finding himself out of Gerry Francis' plans for Tottenham Hostpur. Practically the only positive note came when he was loaned out to Swindon Town where he was at least able to make 8 appearances, the only games he played in throughout the whole campaign.

659.name: Borrows
pages:
* Signed for Swindon on the 13th of November 1997.
* Despite his veteran status, Brian Borrows is still maintains the defensive consistency that has allowed him to play for many years at the top level of English football. Born in 1960, he spent fourteen season at Coventry. Swindon is the next stop in his long career.

* Consistency is the most notable characteristic of Brian Borrows, a workmanlike right back, disciplined, a good passer and secure making interceptions.  His mastery in defensive tasks allows him to play at centre back or even on the left.  An extraordinary marker, he has a well-developed sense of positioning.  His broad experience at the top level have provided him with various defensive resources, although, on the other hand, his contribution to the attack is small.  In recent years he has lost some speed, due in part to successive injuries, but he still shows that he is an able marker of the rival forwards.
x
* 1 B-international for England.

* A native of Liverpool, he trained in the Everton youth squad.  After going through the junior levels he turns professional on the 24th of April 1980, although his debut with the first team doesn't happen until the 13th of February 1982, in a game against Stoke City played at Goodison Park.
* His second team was Bolton Wanderers, arriving at this club on the 24th of March 1983 in exchange for £10,000.  In his two years at the club he was an undisputed starter.
* On the 6th of June 1985 he is transferred to Coventry City for £80,000. 
* In 1987 the Sky Blues win the FA Cup at Wembley, but Brian, injured one week before, couldn't play in the final.
* Voted "Player of the Year" by the fans in 1995, in September of this year he celebrates his 500th league game at Coventry.

* The veteran Coventry defender was not one of the regulars in the line-ups of Strachan, above all after the first third of the season, when his appearances started to be fewer in number.  What's more the use of wing-backs meant that he played most of his games as a central defender.

660.name: McDonald
pages: * An institution at QPR, Alan McDonald was a true idol for the crowd at Rangers, virtually the only team in his sporting career. Surprisingly, the club's manager decided to let him go this summer and opt for the younger players in the London club's squad. This left McDonald with no place to go for the first time, though he didn't take too long to sign for Steve McMahon, who was looking for an experienced man to play in the heart of the Robins defence.

* A very experienced central defender, his positioning is practically perfect, and you don't often see him make mistakes. He is not so quick, but he makes up for this using his physique to get the better of his opponent. He is a tough but fair defender. Dangerous at set-plays. He is the leader in defence. He doesn't complicate life when he has the ball at his feet and when pressured lets go quickly with a punt upfield.
x

* He has been a youth international with Northern Ireland and also with the full team 50 times, scoring three goals. He made his debut on 16th October 1985 against Romania in Bucharest. 
* He played in the Mexico 86 World Cup with Northern Ireland.

* Originally from the lower ranks of QPR he signs as a professional in August 1981 making his league debut on 24th September 1983 against Wolverhampton Wanderers scoring his first goal on 26th December 1984 against Chelsea.
* He is loaned to Charlton Athletic in March 1983 and makes his debut in the league against Crystal Palace. 
* His contract ends and signs for Swindon Town in the summer of 1997.
* Alan McDonald had a sensational season in the centre of the QPR defence. He was the manager's first choice for holding the backline together. In total he played 39 games and scored 2 goals.

661.name: King
pages: * Phil King is a veteran player who is trying to get over a bad spell he has experienced in recent times. A new opportunity presented itself when he joined Swindon Town where he had already once played, hoping to figure in the Steve McMahon's plans. Although he is not a regular starter, his experience could be important in a long season. He could be influential at the Robins who have a lot of young players willing to learn the tricks of the trade from a veteran.

* He can play both as a central defender or left back, although at times he has even played as a forward or even on the right. Therefore, versatility is one of his biggest virtues. Very left-footed, he has an acceptable technique, which combined with his speed makes him a useful footballer. His level of performance has dropped in recent years. Even so, his quality is a guarantee which could help him regain the form he showed at Wednesday.

* League Cup Champion 90-91 with Sheffield Wednesday. 
* League Cup Champion 95-96 with Aston Villa.
* 1 B-international appearance.

* His footballing career started at Exeter City, where he played as a schoolboy and apprentice before turning professional on 7th of January 1985. Shortly after he makes his debut in the League against Halifax on 23rd of February. 
* The presence of Keith Veney at left back for Exeter forces King's transfer to Torquay United on 14th of July 1986 for £4,000. 
* On the 6th of February 1987 he signs for Swindon, the club which is promoted to the Second Division during his stay. His transfer was set at £155,000.
* The step up to the First Division occurs on 30th of November 1989 when Sheffield Wednesday pay £400,000 to acquire his services. At Wednesday, he wins the League Cup in 1991 beating Manchester United in the final.
* He scores his first goal as a professional against Wednesday's big rival, Sheffield United. 
* The Owls fans vote him best player at Sheffield in the 92-93 season.
* On 22nd of October 1993 he is loaned to Notts County. 
* On 1st of August 1994 he is transferred to Aston Villa for £250,000. He makes his debut on 20th of August against Everton at Goodison Park (2-2).
* Up till the end of the 94-95 season he had received 7 yellow cards.
* He is loaned to West Bromwich Albion on 30th of October 1995, making his debut at home with a defeat against Leicester City (2-3) on 5th of November. A ligament injury puts an end to his season. 
* He is signed by Swindon Town on 26th of March 1997 without any transfer fee involved. His first game for the Robins is played against Norwich City.

* After suffering a serious injury two seasons ago, Phil King couldn't manage to figure in Brian Little's plans for Aston Villa and so was freed of his contractual obligations signing for Swindon Town in March. He played 5 games for the Robins although he arrives in the middle of a team re-shuffle. He hardly plays a game for his new team.

662.name: Elkins
pages: * The ex England youth international had been ostracised by Wimbledon in recent times. His signing for Swindon Town could be a breath of fresh air for his sporting career.  With the Robins, at least the chances arrive, whether he plays at left back or in the centre of the defence. He has a new mentality now, and Elkins goes into this season hoping to be of some use to Swindon Town, either as a regular starter or as a replacement in times of injury.

* Gary Elkins is a left back who, despite not being very quick, has good positioning and his veteran status makes him hard to beat. He can use his right decently for a left-footed player, he attacks when he has the chance, putting over quality crosses. He isn't technical enough to break through defences so he will usually cross if he receives the ball. He is comfortable with the ball at his feet, passing effectively both in short and long range looking for spaces. Despite not being very tall, Elkins is good in the air, joining in the attack at set-plays. He can also play at left-half or even as a third central defender in Swindon's three-man centre-back system, taking up the position on the left.
x
* He has been an England youth international.

* Trained in the Fulham youth squad, Elkins signs as a professional in December 1983. He makes his debut on 22nd September 1984 against Middlesbrough and scores his first goal - the winner - on 27th August 1988 against Cardiff City. 
* Loaned to Exeter City in December 1989, he plays his first game on 26th december 1989 against Aldershot. 
* Wimbledon sign him for £20,000 in August 1990. He plays his first game on 17th November 1990 against Chelsea and scores his first goal for the Dons on 25th April 1992 against Norwich City. 
* He is transferred to Swindon Town in September 1996 for £100,000, making his debut on 21st September 1996 against QPR. His first goal comes on 1st of February 1997 against Sheffield United.

* Hoping to revitalise his career, Elkins moved to Swindon Town, where he took advantage of Drysdale's injury to find a place in the team. Even so, his run didn't last long, as he had to compete with other players for the left-back position. In total he played 23 games and scored 1 goal.

663.name: Darras
pages:
* Frederick Darras has the honour of being the first European Community player. The French defender was on trial in Swindon's tour of Finland for two weeks. His performance convinced Steve McMahon that he was a useful man and that he could make an interesting contribution to his team. 
* Relatively unknown, his great versatility could be his biggest plus point when it comes to playing for Swindon. He can play in all of the positions in the back line and in the midfield as well although always defensively minded. He will be a regular in Steve McMahon's line-ups.

* A right back who with defensive leanings, Darras doesn't make crazy runs as he is more concerned with defending and then, if he can, he will push up. In fact, he only pushes up to cover for someone else. He is quick, and good in the air. He is comfortable with the ball at his feet, passing accurately both over long-range to initiate a counter-attack, or over short range. In attack, his crosses are not so good as he is more a man who props up the defence.
x
x

* His contract with Bastia finishes and he signs for Swindon Town. He makes his debut for the Robins on 17th August 1996 against Norwich City.
* Before joining the Bastia squad, he played both at Auxerre and at Sochaux.

* Darras had a satisfactory first season at Swindon Town, with versatility his best weapon. He has managed to play in almost every position apart from goalkeeper or striker. In total the Frenchman has played 35 games.

664.name: Culverhouse
pages: * Ian Culverhouse was the first signing made by Steve McMahon after being named team manager, the only signing who has really lived up to expectations playing an outstanding role in defence. Named a member of the Second Division Dream Team the year before last, he is always level-headed and calm when he has to play the ball. He used to be a right back but has changed to a central defender, playing on the right of the heart of the three-man Swindon defence. He brings a lot of security to the defence, one of the regulars in the team.

* A quick player, he is secure when making interceptions and doesn't leave his position in the defence for any reason.  He is not so tall and so he has to anticipate the rival forward in aerial balls. He is right-footed and passes the ball accurately to the midfield, without making life too complicated. He has a good playing vision and occasionally pushes up, but never really crosses the half-way line.
* Second Division Champion 95-96 with Swindon Town.
* Youth international with the England team.

* Originally from the lower ranks of Tottenham Hotspur, he signs as a professional in September 1982.  His league debut comes on 21st February 1984 against Notts County. 
* He is transferred to Norwich City in October 1985 for £50,000, and makes his league debut on 12th October 1985 against Carlisle United. His first goal wearing the Norwich shirt and, until now, his only goal as a professional, comes in a game against Everton on 21st March 1994. 
* Swindon Town sign him in December 1994 for £250,000, and he plays his first game on 10th December 1994 against Tranmere Rovers.

* Culverhouse didn't have as distinguished a season as in the year in which the club was promoted to the First Division, his progress being hindered by injuries and suspensions. In total he played 31 games.

665.name: Digby
pages:
* After playing more than 400 games for Swindon Town, Fraser Digby has been an undisputed starter since he has been at the club, providing great service to the club. He has thus earned the right to a testimonial game being with Swindon for more than ten seasons, a game played against his former club, Manchester United, last summer. 
* Despite the both the club's economic problems and his own physical problems, Digby has once again shown that he is the best goalie at Swindon. It looks like things will continue for the coming season, provided that Talia doesn't end up taking his place away from him.

* A pretty complete keeper, he is very safe in the air and doesn't try and catch difficult balls, preferring to parry. He has some good reflexes although he is a little inconsistent when stopping long-range shots as he is not very sure of himself when he has to block this type of attempt.
* Second Division Champion 95-96 with Swindon Town.

* Digby has been an international with the England team in the schoolboy, youth and under-21 international categories, making his debut in the latter of these against Spain in Burgos, with a 2-1 win for the England team thanks to goals from Rocastle and Cottee. In total he has played 5 games for the under-21 team.

* Originally from the lower ranks of Manchester United, he signs as a professional in April 1985. He didn't get to play a single minute for the Old Trafford team. 
* He is transferred to Swindon Town in September 1986 for £32,000, making his debut as a professional on 27th September 1986 against Rotherham United.

* An understudy to Frank Talia for the first three months of competition, Digby regained his place after this period and kept it for the rest of the season. McMahon's enormous faith in him is demonstrated by the fact that despite the disastrous results against Bolton and Oldham, he didn't blame the keeper but rather other areas of team. He played 31 games.

666.name: Drysdale
pages: * After several years at Swindon Town, where he was affected negatively by the magnificent performance of Paul Bodin, Jason Drysdale goes into this season with plenty of hope. Over the last two seasons injuries have limited him to a handful of appearances. Although he will have to compete with Elkins and King for a place, Drysdale should be the first choice left back for the Robins.

* Drysdale is a classical wide defender, very sure in his zone. With the Swindon Town system, in which the wide defenders are projected into the midfield, he can push up into attack when he has the chance. Very left-footed, he doesn't dribble well and finds it hard to go by rival defenders. He prefers to put over crosses to the penalty spot, looking for Wayne Allison's head.

* Youth Cup Champion with Watford in 1989. 
* Second Division Champion in 95-96 with Swindon Town.
x

* Originally from the lower ranks of Watford, he signs as a professional in September 1988.  His league debut comes on 31st October 1989 against Ipswich Town with his first goal coming on 26th december 1991 against Millwall.
* He is transferred to Newcastle United in August 1994 for £425,000. However, Kevin Keegan doesn't give him a single opportunity. 
* Swindon Town sign him for £340,000 in March 1995. He makes his league debut on 25th MArch 1995 against Charlton Athletic. 
* His father played more than 300 games for Bristol City.
* For the second year in a row, bad luck hung over Drysdale, limiting him to just 13 games due to an injury in a League Cup tie in the month of September.

667.name: Finney
pages: * One of Swindon's pleasant surprises during the season when they earned promotion to the First Division, Stephen Finney was a player who had Steve McMahon's full confidence.  Unfortunately, due to an incident in that season in which he broke leg, he hasn't been the same and hasn't managed to perform to the same level. He is therefore relegated to the bench. It will be hard to get back in the side; he needs time to regain his confidence and then maybe he will be seen once again in the line-ups.
* A very clever player, he is quick both inside and outside the box being ablw to shoot with either foot. He is good in the air, anticipating the rival defenders.
* Second Division Champion 95-96 with Swindon Town.
x

* Originally from the lower ranks of Preston North End, he signs as a professional in May 1992. His league debut is on 18th January 1992 against Exeter City and scores his first goal on 2nd May 1992 against Bury. 
* His contract finishes and he joins Manchester City in the summer of 1992. However, he is completely marginalised and doesn't get a single chance.
* As a free agent he signs for Swindon Town in the summer of 1995. His league debut comes on 12th August 19995 against Hull City, scoring the winner.
* He was voted young player of the year 95-96 by the fans at Swindon Town.

* Finney didn't have a good season, playing in 20 games, only scoring 2 goals. He started the season as Wayne Allison's partner but couldn't find his place on the pitch and was relegated to the substitutes' bench. From this moment on, he only appeared as a substitute or stepping in for an injured team-mate.

668.name: Bullock
pages: * Just three years ago Bullock was playing in amateur football. Since then, the progress of this English midfielder has been so impressive that some of the top clubs have shown an interest in him. Finally, Swindon Town became his next destination, although for the moment, he hasn't made the desired impact at the Robins. He is currently not a regular in the team.

* Bullock is a very strong midfielder who works very hard in the midfield. He is a great ballwinner, very hard when fighting for the ball. He can be given the job of marking the brains of the rival team if it is considered necessary. He is quick and has a good physical reserve. Technically however, he is not so good. He is right-footed and has a great shot from long range.
x
x

* Huddersfield Town sign him from the amateur club Nuneaton Borough in November 1993 for £55,000. He plays his first game on 22nd November 1993 against Blackpool and scores his first goal for the Terriers on 12th February 1994 against Wrexham. 
* He is transferred to Swindon Town on 24th of February 1997 for £400,000. His debut cones on the 26th against Birmingham City, scoring the team's first goal.

* A regular in Brian Horton's plans for Huddersfield Town, Bullock played 27 games for the Terriers and scores a goal before moving to Swindon Town at a time when McMahon's men needed someone like him in the midfield after Kevin Horlock left to go to Manchester City.  His impact on the team was not what was hoped although he did score on his debut, playing 13 games for the Robins.

669.name: Leitch
pages: * Scott Leitch is a man with a tremendous personality on the pitch, constantly demanding the ball to initiate an attacking move. After playing before as a loan player, his performance as a substitute for Steve McMahon demonstrated his talent. He is an irreplaceable member of the team.

* A left-footed midfielder with a lot of quality, Leitch plays in front of the three centre backs, moving the ball quickly, over both short and long distances. He is the axis the team revolves around, always the guy responsible for playing the ball out from the back. He can also join in the attack but remains on the edge of the box to have a go with his left, looking for rebounds. He is physically strong.
x
x

* The Scottish player was trained at amateur team Shettleston Juniors but when his contract finished with the club, he signs for Dunfermline in April 1990. He plays his first game on 8th September 1990 against Aberdeen and scores his first goal on 23rd February 1991 against Hearts. 
* Signing for Hearts in August 1993 he makes his league debut on 28th August 1993 against Dundee United and scores his first goal for the new club against Motherwell on 15th december 1993. 
* He is loaned to Swindon Town in March 1996, playing his first game on 30th March 1996 against Bristol City. 
* Finally Swindon Town pay £15,000 for him in the summer of 1996. His debut for the Robins comes on the 17th of August against Norwich City.
* Leitch was one of Swindon's most regular players during last season, only missing 10 of the 46 possible league games due to suspension and injury.

670.name: Watson
pages: * Nothing good could come from Kevin Watson's continued presence at Tottenham Hotspur as he was kept firmly out the team. Faced with an obscure future at White Hart Lane he decided to try his luck at Swindon. Taking into account his performance last year, without doubt, he will have a lot of good moments in the years to come.

* Watson is a midfielder who is blessed with a good right, and who also dribbles well. He joins in the attack constantly but doesn't find the net so often, as is shown by his record. He is the playmaker and the perfect complement to Leitch. He has a good shot with his right and is a good passer and doesn't often try the long ball. Physically he is not so strong, so he is not really a ball-winner.
x
x

* Trained in the Tottenham Hotspur youth squad, he makes his debut for the London team on 27th September 1992 against Sheffield Wednesday. 
* He is loaned to Brentford in March 1994. He plays his first game for the club on the 26th March 1994 against Cambridge United. 
* He is loaned to Bristol City in December 1994, and makes his debut on 3rd December 1994 against Grimsby Town. 
* He is also loaned to Barnet in January 1995, playing his first game for the side on 24th January 1995 against Carlisle United. 
* Finally, he signs for Swindon Town when his contract expires with Spurs in the summer of 1996.  He makes his league debut on 17th August 1996 against Norwich City and scores his first goal for the Robins and his first as a professional on 31st August 1996 against Southend.

* A satisfactory first season for Kevin Watson at Swindon Town. He played in 27 games and scored a beautiful goal from 20 yards with a fierce drive. Despite coming on as a substitute in most of his appearances, he showed signs of the good player he could become.

671.name: Walters
pages:
* Mark Walters hasn't had much luck after his return to English soil, taking into account the magnificent performance he produced for Glasgow Rangers where he won quite a few titles. His arrival at Liverpool aroused great expectations at the club. However, Walters couldn't deliver the goods except in the 92-93 season which was a great one for him at Anfield, playing from the start and finishing as the team's second top scorer. Later he became unsettled at the club and was loaned to a series of clubs until his contract expired. He then signed for Southampton, where he didn't have many chances either.
* Swindon have signed him and bring an experienced footballer to the side. The former England international has his somewhat irregular performances against him, and much depends on how the first few minutes go. If they go well he takes active part in the game, if not he tends to disappear. His value as a player is well reflected when he has to hide the ball while the opposing team tries desperately to get it off him. Without doubt, Mark Walters is very valuable for a team like Swindon and great things are expected of this talented but irregular footballer by the Robins.

* A veteran left winger, he has great technique and a good turn of speed. Although he plays on the left he can use both feet well, mainly the right. He usually plays hugging the touchline, trying to dribble past defenders in two ways: cutting to his left or right after trying to catch the rival defender off balance, then look for the cross. At times, after cutting past the defender, instead of putting over the cross, he looks to move in field diagonally to then try out a shot, which is usually good from about 25 yards. To go past defenders he will often try the "bicycle" which he executes pretty well.  Although Walters plays on the left he can also play on the right wing.

* Youth Cup Champion 1980 with Aston Villa. 
* European Supercup Champion with Aston Villa in 1980 after beating Barcelona 3-0 in the return game. 
* Scottish League Champion 1989, 90 and 91 with Glasgow Rangers.
* Scottish League Cup Champion 1989, beating Aberdeen on 23rd October 1988, and in 1991 beating Celtic on 28th October 1991. 
* Runner-up in the Scottish Cup on the 20th of May 1989 loosing to Celtic.
* FA Cup Champion in 1992 when Liverpool beat Sunderland on 9th May 1992 although he doesn't play. 
* Top scorer at Aston Villa in the 85-86 season alongside Simon Stainrod.
* Top scorer at Glasgow Ranger in the 90-91 season.

* Walters has played for England at the schoolboy, youth, under-21, B and full level, the latter only once. His debut came on 3rd June 1991 in the Mount Smart Stadium in Auckland, New Zealand, against the host nation. England won 1-0 with a goal from Gary Lineker. Walker is a starter but is brought off to be replaced by John Salako.

* Originally from the lower ranks of Aston Villa, Walters signs as a professional in May 1982.  He makes his league debut on 28th April 1982 against Leeds United, substituting for Tony Morley. He scores his first league goal on 26th February 1983 against Watford. 
* He is transferred to Glasgow Rangers in December 1987 for £500,000, making his debut against the Old Firm on 2nd January 1988.  His first goal for the Scottish team comes on 13th February 1988 against St. Mirren. 
* He signs for Liverpool in August 1991 for £1,25 million, and plays his first game for the Reds against Oldham, coming on as a substitute for Steve McMahon, currently his manager at Swindon. He scores his first goal in league competition on 7th September 1992 [the winner] against Notts County from the penalty spot. 
* Loaned to Stoke City in March 1994, his debut comes on 26th March 1994 against Crystal Palace and he scores the winner against Sunderland on 16th April 1994. 
* He is also loaned to Wolverhampton Wanderers in September 1994, making his debut on 10th September 1994 against Tranmere Rovers, his first goal comes three days later against Southend. 
* His contract finishes and he signs for Southampton in January 1996, making his league debut on 20th January 1996 against Middlesbrough. 
* Free of contractual obligations he signs for Swindon Town in August 1996.  e plays his first game on 17th August 1996 against Norwich City.
* In the final of the 1991 League Cup against Celtic, he scores a goal for Glasgow Rangers.

* Mark Walters had an outstanding season at Swindon Town, being spectacularly effective in the first half of the season before a recurrent muscle problem put an end to his league in the month of February. In total he played 27 games and scored 1 goal.

672.name: Gooden
pages: * After some promising seasons, but without being able to play regularly, Ty Gooden is one of the most important players at Swindon Town. He has talent and can play well both out wide and in the middle of the pitch. Surprisingly McMahon is using him this season, giving the young player a chance to let his game settle and to play regularly in the Robins' starting elevens.

* Left half, he has a good shot with either foot, though he is really left footed. He is skilful, putting over accurate crosses both to the near and far post. He moves the ball about well, is quick and can go by players.
* Second Division Champion 95-96 with Swindon Town.
x

* His contract with Wycombe Wanderers finishes and he signs for Swindon Town in September 1993.  He makes his league debut on 5th March 1994 against West Ham United and he scores his first league goal on 19th March 1995 against WBA.
* Gooden had a disappointing season as he hardly had chances to play for Swindon Town, having to be content with playing in the reserves team. In total he played 13 games and scored a goal.

673.name: McMahon
pages: * See profile in the manager's section.

* A midfielder who still keeps some of the great strength although not as much as in his time at Liverpool.  He is the man who moves the rest of the team. He prefers his right foot, and he can move the ball over long range or in short, depending on the circumstances. He has an excellent long-range shot. He is not as good a ball winner as he was in years gone-by but he is still acceptable in this department.

* League Champion 85-86, 87-88 and 89-90 with Liverpool. 
* FA Cup Champion 85-86 and 88-89 with Liverpool. 
* Second Division Champion 95-96 with Swindon Town.

* An England under-21, B and full international, making his debut in the latter category in a game in Tel-Aviv  against Israel on 17th February 1988 (0-0). In total he made 17 full international appearances, including the Germany 88 European Championship and the Italy 90 World Cup.
* See manager's anecdotes.

* Since the beginning of the league he had announced that his sporting career was over.  However, McMahon played three more games in the Championship producing a more than dignified performance and being named man of the match in some of them. Even so, his appearances were becoming ever more few and far between.

674.name: Murray
pages: * The Swindon Town midfielder hasn't had many chances in the seasons that he has been with the Robins. His options for playing appear limited. If he wants to play he should work on his technical foundation, as this is his most noticeable weakness.

* A very strong midfielder, he has a good shot from a distance. He is a player who is very enthusiastic in everything that he does but who is technically rather weak. A dynamic footballer, he can play on either side and is quick.
* Second Division Championshiop 95-96 with Swindon Town.
x

* Originally from the lower ranks of Swindon Town, he signs as a professional in July 1991.  He makes his debut in the league on 5th March 21991 against Oxford United and scores his first goal for Swindon on 26th August 1995.

675.name: O´Sullivan
pages: * A very hard-working footballer, Wayne O'Sullivan covers every square inch of the pitch during the game. Although he has shown that he has the talent to be in Steve McMahon's starting eleven, the presence of Leitch has shut him out of the team, so he has to be content with being a team player, coming on as a substitute or stepping in for a suspended or injured player.
* An attacking minded midfielder, he gets into some good positions and surprises rival defences quite often. He is very quick and has a lot of stamina, allowing him to run from box to box.
* Second Division Champion 95-96 with Swindon Town.
* An Ireland international in the under-21 category, making two appearances.

* Originally from the lower ranks of Swindon Town, he signs as a professional in May 1993.  He makes his debut in the league on 14th August 1994 against Port Vale and scores his first goal against Brentford on 2nd September 1995.

* Displaced from his position by the recent arrival Scott Leitch, O'Sullivan had to be content with the role of team player, stepping in when others were injured or suspended. In total he played 25 games.

676.name: Robinson
pages: * Mark Robinson has been a very important player for Swindon Town since his arrival from Newcastle United in 1994, being especially important in the season when Swindon were promoted two years ago. He is a regular in McMahon's plans and always performs well for the Robins. At the moment he is not a starter but this will change soon.

* A very attacking right back, he is quick and consistent in his game. At times he has played as a central defender, performing well. He crosses pretty well and imposes with his presence in the rival box. He can go past players helped with his dribbling ability and strength. He is a fearsome adversary.
* Second Division Champion 95-96 with Swindon Town.
x

* Originally from the lower ranks of WBA, Robinson signs as a professional in January 1987. He makes his league debut on 22nd April 1986 against Sheffield Wednesday. 
* His contract finishes and he signs for Barnsley in June 1987. His debut takes place on 22nd August 1987 against Millwall, scoring his first league goal on 19th March 1989 against Leeds United. 
* Newcastle United sign him for £450,000 in March 1993, playing his first game for the Magpies against Charlton Athletic. 
* He is transferred to Swindon Town in July 1994 in exchange for £600,000. He makes his debut against Port Vale and scores his first goal for the Robins on 13th September 1995 against Bradford City.

* Mark Robinson had an impressive season with Swindon Town last year, becoming one of the best men at Steve McMahon's disposal.  He basically played at right back although he also operated at centre back when it was necessary with good results. In total, he played 43 games and scored 1 goal.

677.name: Seagraves
pages: * A player who has a lot of experience at all levels, including in the First Division with Norwich City and Manchester City, Mark Seagraves is one of the fundamental men in Steve McMahon's line-ups as he always brings a lot of firmness and safety to the Swindon defence. He is not a starter at the moment but the manager sleeps more easily knowing he is available for selection.

* A classic central defender, he is a tough player who is good in the air, taking good advantage of his height. He is also dangerous in the set-plays. He is not good technically and doesn't complicate things when he has to play the ball out from the back.

* League Cup Runner-up in 94-95 with Bolton Wanderers, loosing in the final against Liverpool. 
* Second Division Champion 95-96 with Swindon Town.
* He has been an England international in the schoolboy and youth categories.

* Originally from the lower ranks of Liverpool, he signs as a professional in November 1983.  However, he doesn't get to play a single game for the Anfield club. 
* He is loaned to Norwich City in November 1986, making his debut on the 22nd November 1986 against Coventry City. 
* He is transferred to Manchester City in September 1987 for £100,000. His debut takes place on 26th September 1987 against Leeds United. 
* Bolton Wanderers sign him in September 1990 for £100,000. He plays his first game on 28th September 1990 against Wigan Athletic. He scores his first goal as a professional on 2nd May 1992 against Stoke City. 
* He is finally transferred to Swindon Town for £300,000 in the summer of 1995, making his debut for his new team on 12th August 1995 against Hull City.
* Seagraves had a strange season due mainly to his lack of understanding with his new team-mates in the backline of Swindon Town after the departure of his centre-back partner Shaun Taylor.

678.name: Talia
pages: * Frank Talia's first steps in English football weren't too promising, as Blackburn Rovers hardly gave him a chance to show his class. The same can be said for his spell at Hartlepool and at Swindon Town. However, despite being a good keeper, his mistakes have cost him his place in the Robins goal, currently being the understudy to Fraser Digby.

* Frank Talia is a goalkeeper with extraordinary reflexes allowing him to make some sensational saves. He is very complete, both when going for crosses or playing the ball with his feet outside the area. Possibly his biggest defect is that he tries to be too flashy on occasions, and his lack of height, as he sometimes has problems against tall forwards. 
* However, the Australian keeper is very brave and risks a lot in some dangerous situations with rival forwards. Also, in the one-on-ones he is hard to beat thanks to his reflexes and speed, and his positioning makes him hard to go round in these situations.
* Second Division Champion 95-96 with Swindon Town.
x

* Blackburn Rovers sign him from the Australian team Sunshine George Cross in the summer of 1992. He can't get to play, kept out by Tim Flowers, Bobby Mimms and Shay Given. 
* He is loaned to Hartlepool United in December 1992, making his debut in the league on 28th December 1992 against Fulham. 
* Swindon Town sign him for £150,000 in September 1995 and makes his debut on 9th September 1995 against Chesterfield.

* The Australian goalie was the first choice keeper at Swindon Town for the first months of the competition but a disastrous performance against WBA where he presented them with goals and the points on a plate, put an end to his season, and from this moment on Digby was the man who defended the Swindon goal.

679.name: Cowe
pages: * Stephen Cowe is a very young player who had a job to figure in Brian Little's plans at Aston Villa and so he had to move to Swindon Town, the team where he had chances and has shown that he is a footballer who can be counted on for the future and in the present as well. It is possible that he could come through and take up a place in the Robins, though there is a lot of competition.

* Cowe is a very quick forward who is constantly moving about, looking to get free of his marker and get goalside of the defence, always waiting for a pass. He has good technique and this is combined with his good ball control and dribbling. Although Cowe isn't strong he is intelligent and pulls the rival to where he wants him. Basically right-footed, he can use both feet to shoot on goal without thinking about it. Thanks to his skill, if he is given some space in or near the box he can cause problems. He is not so good in the air and if he does connect it is thanks to his anticipation.
x
x

* Originally from the lower ranks of Aston Villa, the stiff competition at his club leads to his loan to Swindon Town in March 1996, and just one week later the loan becomes permanent for £100,000. He makes his debut in the league on 23rd March 1996 against Peterborough United, scoring on 23rd April 1996 against Chesterfield.

* A good season for Stephen Cowe, who showed that he has the ability to play in the Swindon Town attack. Despite starting the league as second choice to Finney, this player's inconsistency gave Cowe his chance, forming an attacking partnership with Allison until the end of the league. Unfortunately he didn't score so many goals though he had a fair number of chances. In total he managed to play in 38 games, scoring just 6 goals.

* An England youth international.
* Loaned to Bradford City in March 1998.

* Last season Sinnott made a total of 30 league appearances for Huddersfield, including 29 starting appearances. He brought all his experience and know how to the side, although he was unable to prevent the team from finishing the season near the foot of the table.

681.name: McAnespie
pages: * Steve McAnespie signed for Fulham in November 1997. In March 1998 he was loaned to Bradford City.

* A quick footballer but not such a good marker, he leaves a lot of gaps in his zone of the pitch.  He doesn't join in the attack dangerously and his crosses are not very accurate and lack quality, and are often not very controlled

* Scottish First Division Champion with Raith Rovers 94-95.
* Scottish League Cup Champion with Raith Rovers, beating Celtic 94-95.
x

* Raith Rovers sign him from the amateur Scottish team Vasterhaurine in the summer of 1993 and he makes his debut on the 25/1/93 against Motherwell. 
* Signed by Bolton Wanderers in September 1995 for £900,000, he makes his league debut on the 30/9/95 against QPR. 
* Signed for Fulham in November 1997.
* He wasn't used much by the manager, and he only made 13 appearances. McAnespie spent most of the season on the substitutes' bench, only coming on if a team-mate was injured or suspended.

683.name: Wilder
pages: * Chris Wilder is every inch a leader on the pitch and was a good signing on Chris Kamara's part going into last season, and he promises a lot going into this one, where he has found a place in the team at the expense of Richard Liburd. Last year his contributions to the team were correct but he did not dazzle, but the difficult situation that Bradford City were going through should be taken into account. This season he could be an important man for the Bantams.

* Chris Wilder is a true free-kick specialist, something not often seen in a right back.  However, his versatility allows him to play effectively as a sweeper or even in the midfield.  He has an acute positional sense and broad experience, but, above all, he is noted for the power of his long-range shot.
x
x

* Originally from the lower ranks of Southampton, Wilder signs as a professional on 26th of September 1985. However, he never got to play for the team at the Dell.
* As a free agent he signs for Sheffield United on the 20th of August 1986. His debut takes place on the 26th of January against Shrewsbury Town and his first goal has to wait until the 29th of October 1988 against Bury. 
* He is loaned to Walsall on the 2nd of November 1989, playing his first game for the club on the 4th of November against Bristol City.
* He is loaned to Charlton Athletic twice, the first time during the 90-91 season and the second during the 91-92 one. He plays his first game against Watford on the 20th of October 1990.
* Leyton Orient is his next stop, also as a loan player on the 27th of February 1992. He makes his debut days later against Shrewsbury Town and his first goal comes on the 24th of March against Bury.
* Finally his transfer to Rotherham United takes place after going there on many occasions as a loan player. The date: 30th of June 1992, the price: £50,000.  His first game with the club is on the 15th of August against Exeter City and he scores his first goal against Hartlepool United on the 30th of January 1993.
* Notts County sign him on the 2nd of January 1996 for £150,000, and he makes his debut for the team on the 20th of January against Wrexham.
* His latest team is Bradford City who pay £150,000 for him in March of 1997. The first game he plays for the Bantams is on the 29th of March against Portsmouth.

* Wilder was fundamental for Notts County throughout the season. He played 37 of the 39 possible games and then left for Bradford City, the team where he was also a set feature in the starting line-up, playing 7 games. In total, 44 league games for Chris Wilder.

684.name: Dreyer
pages: * A footballer with a lengthy experience in sport, John Dreyer arrived at Bradford City to contribute with his veteran's experience and consistency. The money paid for his transfer turned out to be a sensational investment, as he helped considerably in Bradford's efforts to stay in the First Division. His constant appearances in the heart of the defence were a boost for the Bantams. He will once again have a fixed place in Chris Kamara's plans.

* Although his natural position is that of left back, Dreyer can play in the centre of defence at times. His experience allows him to order his team mates in the defensive line. His presence in attack is limited to set-plays, where his dominance in the air is imposing. As he is not a quick player, he tries to compensate this shortcoming with his excellent sense of positioning.
* League Cup Runner-Up 89.
x

* Originally from the modest Wallingford Town, John Dreyer arrives at Oxford United in January 1985. He made his league debut on the 11th of October 1986, in a game against Coventry City, and scored his first goal on the 28th of March 1987, curiously against Coventry.
* In December 1985 he is loaned to Torquay United.
* March 1986 sees him loaned to Fulham till the end of the season. 
* Transferred to Luton Town in June 1988 for £140,000, he made his debut on the 27th of August of this same year in a game against Sheffield Wednesday. He had to wait until the 14th of May 1989 to score his first goal, and the victim was, once again, Coventry.
* When his contract expired in the summer of 1994 he signed for Stoke City. On the 13th of August he made his league debut in a game against Tranmere Rovers.
* Loaned to Bolton Wanderers in March 1995, he made his debut with this team on the 17th of April 1995, against Sunderland.
* He is transferred to Bradford City in November 1996 for £25,000. His first game with the Bantams is on the 8th of November against Huddersfield Town, scoring one of his team's goals in this game

* He had only played 12 games for Stoke City when John Dreyer surprisingly moved to Bradford City, to the desperation of some who thought that he was playing some of his best football as a professional. From the moment he arrived he was an automatic choice for Chris Kamara who aligned him in 28 games. He made his debut in the best possible way, scoring a goal for the Bantams against Huddersfield Town.

685.name: Moore
pages: * Darren Moore has been bought by Bradford City to reinforce the defensive aspect of the team coached by Chris Kamara. A true leader in the defence, his spell at Doncaster Rovers has left its mark on that team, something he hopes to be able to repeat at Bradford City. His games with the team will, in principle, be very limited, but Kamara believes that he could be a very interesting investment for the team in the future.

* Moore is a central defender who stands out for his ability to dominate in the air, a facet in which he is a true titan. He will often take advantage of this is set-plays, whether these are corners or free-kicks. A good marker, he stays close to the man and doesn't let his man breathe for for a moment. Technically, he should improve, but he is very young, so this department will be the one to dwell on in future training.
x
x

* Originally from the lower ranks of Torquay United, Moore signed as a professional on the 18th of November 1992. His first game with the club was on 25th of April against Bolton Wanderers, a game where he also manages to do well.
* He is transferred to Doncaster Rovers on the 19th of July 1995. He makes his debut with the team on the 12th of August against Scarborough and scores his first goal against Barnet on the 4th of November of this same year. 
* During the summer of 1997 he is transferred to Bradford City in exchange for £310,000.

* Once again a great season for Darren Moore at Doncaster Rovers, where his his presence was of vital importance for the team to function due to his know-how. In total he played 41 games and scored 5 goals.

686.name: Liburd
pages: * Richard Liburd is a young wing defender whose chances at Middlesborough were very few and far between, and so he decided to accept the offer from Bradford City, team where he has been able to show his qualities on the pitch. However, the good performances that he produced last year haven't done him much good as Wilder has taken the position of right back relegating Liburd to the substitutes' bench. The season is long and Liburd will have his chances.

* Liburd is a right back who can play on the other side in the case of an emergency. An attacking minded player, he joins in the attacks regularly and the defence has to be wary of him. He crosses accurately first time, better with the right than the left.  He is very quick and drops back when his team looses possession. He shoots with both feet. He is hard when making tackles but always fair, making good use of his great strength and anticipation.  He is good in the air and joins in the attack at set-plays.
x
x

* Middlesborough signed him from Eastwood Town for £20,000 in March of 1993. He made his debut in the league on 14th AUgust 1993 against Notts County and scores his first goal against Crystal Palace on 1st May 1994.
* The arrival of Bryan Robson to the bench at Middlesborough provokes his move to Bradford City in July 1994 for £200,000. He plays his first game for the Bantams against Leyton Orient and scores his first goal for the club on 1st December 1994 against Cambridge United.

* After signing a new contract with Bradford City, Richard Liburd showed more firmness in his game, being one of the regular features on Chris Kamara's team sheet last year in the First Division. His forays as wing back were dangerous and numerous so he was one of the most consistent men in the team during the 96-97 season. In total he played 36 games and scored a goal.

687.name: Jacobs
pages: * For the second successive year, the participation of Wayne Jacobs has been decisive for the future of Bradford City, first in earning promotion and then in the fight for survival in the First Division. An omnipresent man in Chris Kamara's schemes, the position of left wing back belonged almost legally to him as no-one in the team came anywhere close to forcing him from it. If he produces a season as complete as the previous, Bradford City will have a chance of staying up.

* A very powerful left back, he is a player with an attacking character who joins in the attack at the slightest opportunity, doubling on the wing thanks to the tactical placement used by Kamara.  His crosses are pretty good, always with the left foot. He is a good passer both in short or long distance. He takes the corners with a great restraint. He is a specialist at taking direct free-kicks. He does not have problems with the ball at his feet as he is very safe and calm.
x
x

* Trained in the youth squad of Sheffield Wednesday, he signed as a professional in January 1987 and makes his league debut on 18th February 1987 against Oxford United.
* He is transferred to Hull City in March of 1988 for £27,000. He plays his first game on 26th March 1988 against Leicester City and scores his first goal as a professional on 2nd December 1989 against the same team as in his debut, Leicester City.
* As a free agent he signs for Rotherham United in August 1993. He makes his debut in the league on 14th August 1993 against Wrexham and scores his first goal on 19th February 1994 against York City.
* Once his contract had finished he signs for Bradford City in August 1994.

* Jacobs was one of the important men in Chris Kamara's plans last year, as he produced some truly sensational performances during the 37 games that he played, scoring 3 goals, goals very important to earn a draw, Bradford's main source of points when the team was in a difficult situation. Thanks to his great season he was voted player of the year be the fans of the Bantams.

688.name: Pepper
pages: * The signing of Nigel Pepper has been a true bargain for Bradford City as they only paid £100,000 for a player vital to their final stages of the championship. An attacking midfielder, if he manages to maintain this sensational rhythm he will be a man who figures regularly in Chris Kamara's plans.

* Pepper is a midfielder who works hard in his position, carrying out the dirty work that is almost always ignored by the fans. His battling for the ball is constant and he is a specialist in regaining possession. Notwithstanding, one of his biggest virtues is the ease with which he scores goals, arriving from deep positions, scoring a reasonable number of goals during the course of the league.
x
x

* Originally from the lower ranks of Rotherham United, Pepper signs as a professional on 26th of April 1986. His first game for the side is on the 8th of March 1986 against Wolverhampton Wanderers and he scores his first goal against Shrewsbury Town on 25th of November 1989.
* Pepper is signed by York City when his contract finishes on 18th of July 1990.  His first game with the team is on the 25th of August of this same year against Maidstone United and he scores his first goal against Scarborough on 5th of January 1991.
* He is transferred to Bradford City on 28th of February 1997. His debut with the Bantams takes place on 1st of March against Manchester City and he scores his first goal against Wolverhampton on 22nd of March.

* Pepper was having his best season from the individual view point with York City, as he had scored 12 goals in 29 games but the club proceeded to transfer him to Bradford City, where his attacking game, full of heart, quickly pleased the training body who used him for a lot of games till the end of the league. With Bradford City he played 11 games and scored 5 goals.

689.name: Murray
pages: * Shaun Murray's career has been very well known throughout the world, i.e., the young player who has an enormous potential but who has never quite reached the expected level due to inconsistency preventing him from being successful with the teams where he has played. His role after the departure of Chris Waddle had a lot of merit, as he was one of the players who took on most responsibility going into the final phase of the league. At the beginning of this season, Kamara is using him, and if his inconsistency doesn't get in the way, he will have a regular spot during the course of the season.

* Murray is a midfielder who operates on the left of the pitch and whose enormous skill with the ball makes him the perfect playmaker for the team's attacking moves. He has good playing vision and, in recent times, has shown himself to be more ready to fight for the ball, something which wasn't one of virtues.
x
* Murray has been a youth international for England.

* Trained in the youth squad of Tottenham Hotspur, Murray turned  professional in December 1987.
* He is transferred to Portsmouth in June 1989 for £100,000 and made his debut in the League on 19th September 1990 against Brighton & Hove Albion. He scores his first goal for the club against the same team on 16th April 1991, also his first goal as a professional, and the winner for the Pompeys. 
* He signs for Scarborough in November 1993.  He plays his first game against Wycombe Wanderers and scores his first goal for them on 27th November 1993 against Torquay United.
* Transferred to Bradford City for £200,000 in August 1994, he makes his league debut against Chester City and scores his first goal for the Bantams on 30th October 1994 against Cardiff City.

* Although he only played 17 league games, Shaun Murray produced a great season, stepping in for Chris Waddle who left for Sunderland in the month of March and played a more than dignified role. What's more, he also managed to score a goal.

690.name: Ramage
pages: * During the summer Craig Ramage was let go by his previous team, Watford, but there was no shortage of teams interested in him, so Chris Kamara quickly signed him for the present season. A former England under-21 international for England, this midfielder who pops up well in the box could be a useful incorporation for the team as he scores quite a few goals, one of Bradford's failures last year.

* A link-man who scores a lot of goals, Craig Ramage's game sparkles particularly when he plays just behind the forwards. Even so, he can play as a playmaking midfielder or even as a centre forward at times. Skilful, strong and with playing vision, he is able to take advantage of the space between lines left by the rival team.
x
* Ramage has made 3 under-21 international appearances for England.

* Originally from the lower ranks, Craig Ramage signed as a professional with Derby County on the 20th of July 1988. His first game for the team is on 2nd December 1989 against Charlton Athletic and he scores his first goal against Coventry City on 30th December of this same year.
* Before his debut with Derby County, Ramage is loaned to Wigan Athletic on 16th February 1989. He makes his first appearance for the club on 11th March against Northampton Town and his first goal has to wait until the 27th against Chester City.
* Transferred to Watford on 21st February 1994 for £90,000, his debut takes place four days later against Charlton Athletic. He scores his first goal on 15th October of this same year against Notts County.
* Ramage is loaned to Peterborough United on 10th February 1997 where he plays his first game on the 11th of February against Wrexham.
* His contract with Watford expires and he signs for Bradford City in the summer of 1997.

* Ramage had the bad luck to start the season with a knee injury which cost him a place in the team at Watford.  To get some games, he was loaned to Peterborough United, where he played 7 games. After returning to Watford, he was played as a centre forward, and he responded with goals but was sent off in a key game against Chesterfield.

691.name: Lawrence
pages: * With the doors to the Leicester City first team practically closed, Lawrence has decided to opt for Bradford City to try and find a gap for himself in Chris Kamara's team sheets. Although in the pre-season he was plagued by injuries and so did not appear much, his coach has given him the opportunity and he is in the first team at the start of the league.

* A fast hardworking midfielder, Jamie Lawrence usually plays on the right, although he also adapts to the opposite flank. At times, he has played as a wing back a five-man defence.  He is a skilful footballer, with plenty of speed and capable of putting over dangerous crosses to the heart of the box. However, despite constant battling in defensive tasks, he is guilty of a lack of consistency in his attacking game. Perhaps he needs more consistency to let his footballing talents bloom.
x
x

* Sunderland was the first professional club Jamie Lawrence played for. Originally from modest Cowes, he signed for the "Rokerites" on 15th October 1993 and made his debut two days later with an away defeat at the hand of Middlesborough (4-1). He didn't finish the season at Sunderland.
* On 17th March 1994 he was transferred to Doncaster Rovers for £20,000. 
* Lawrence has been a Leicester City player since the 6th of January 1995. His transfer was set at £125,000.
* He made his debut on 14th January with an away defeat at the hands of Crystal Palace (2-0). On 1st April he scores his first goal in the Premier League against Wimbledon.
* He is transferred to Bradford City in the summer of 1997 for £50,000.

* It wasn't the season that Lawrence might have hoped for, because, of the 15 games that he played for Leicester City, in most of these he came on as substitute and he could not find a place in the Foxes' starting line-ups.
