693.name: Sundgot
pages: * Ole Bjorn Sundgot formed an attacking partnership with Solskjaer in the Norwegian team Molde, a partnership that scored a lot of goals for the Norwegian side. Their paths separated a few years ago when Solskjaer signed for Manchester United. Last year it was Sundgot's turn to leave for English football, more exactly, for Bradford City after an unsuccessful trial with Oldham Athletic. He has still not settled into a regular first team place with the Bantams but this state of affairs may soon change.

* Sundgot is a very strong centre forward who has scored a magnificent number of goals in Norwegian football and has, therefore, the reputation of being a goalscorer. He is very strong in the air and in this type of play he usually comes out on top. He is not so skilful with the ball at his foot but shields it well, waiting for his team mates to join in the attack.
* Top scorer at Bradford City in the 96-97 season.
* Sundgot has made one international appearance for Norway.

* After scoring 65 goals in 110 matches with the Norwegian team Molde, Sundgot signs for Bradford City on the 1st of November 1996. His first game with the team is on 2nd November against Oldham Athletic, the club where he was on trial for a while but no contract materialised. He scored twice against Ipswich on the 16th of the same month.

* Sundgot was the Bradford City player who was luckiest in front of goal, finishing as the Chris Kamara's team's top scorer. His position was a constant reference during the twenty games he played, and in which he scored 6 goals. An unfortunate hernia kept him out at the end of the season.

694.name: Edhino
pages: * Edon do Amaral Neto, better known as Edhino, is a Brazilian who has been successful in Portuguese football, being recognised as one of the best foreigners in that league. With this prestige behind him, this forward hopes to be successful at Bradford City and be a crucial player for the team, as he showed last year. The team is faced with the lack of goals, and due to his own scoring record, Edhino will be certainly be picked by Kamara.

* Edhino has the classic technical quality worthy of a Brazilian footballer, and this allows him to create a lot of dangerous situations single handed. He will constantly try to free himself of his marker and offer himself for the pass. As a good forward, he has a good scent for goal, amply demonstrated in his years spent in the Portuguese league, and he is a man who does not forgive in the area. His speed, skill and killing instinct make him very hard to mark.
x
x

* Edhino has spent the two seasons prior to his incorporation at Bradford in Portuguese football, where he has shown his worth as a goalscorer. Both with Chaves and Vitoria Guimaraes he has found the net more than a dozen times. 
* Edhino is transferred to Bradford City on the 6th of February 1997 for £250,000. His first game for the Bantams is on 8th February against Crystal Palace and he scores his first goal on English soil against Oldham Athletic two weeks later.

* Although he only played 15 games with the Bantams, Edhino was a key figure in the fight to remain in the First Division, because after his arrival, the danger created by the Bradford City forwards increased. This Brazilian footballer also managed to score 5 goals for the club.

695.name: Steiner
pages: * Robert Steiner spent last year as a loan player at Bradford City, his great performances leading Bradford to negotiate with his club to make his move permanent. After the negotiations with the Swedish team Norrkoping, Steiner returns to the Bantams' team, where the fans appreciated his effort last year. However, a not-so-good pre-season has meant that he starts the season on the substitutes' bench, although his opportunities will come during the course of the league.

* Steiner is a tall and well-built centre forward, but something more than the classic centre forward who waits in the area for the lofted balls to arrive from his team mates.  His intensity on the pitch earned him the applause of the followers who appreciated his aggressive style during the matches. Despite appearances, Steiner is a competent player with the ball at his feet, knowing what to do at every moment, and not trying to do things he is unable to do.
x
* Steiner has made 4 appearances for the Swedish team, scoring a goal.

* Originally from the Swedish team of Norrkoping, Steiner was loaned to Bradford City during the 96-97 season. His first appearance for the club is on 2nd November against Oldham Athletic and his first goal arrives the following game against Huddersfield Town.
* Steiner was transferred to Bradford City in the summer of 1997 when both clubs agree to a price of £500,000.

* Steiner was an excellent acquisition for the club during last season, when he played as a loan player. His best performances were in important league games or in the Cup tie against Everton. In total, the Swedish international played 15 matches and scored 4 goals.

696.name: Blake
pages: * Robert Blake is a young forward, who many of the top clubs have got their eye on, and whose future could be brilliant. After a spell at Darlington where he was one of the best players, his first season at Bradford City was fairly discrete but the important jump in divisions made by the footballer should be taken into account, as well as the difficult situation the Bantams where in, fighting to avoid the drop and in need of his goals. The pressure was too much for him, but this season he has shown signs of being a great forward who could form a dangerous partnership with the Brazilian Edhino.

* A young footballer, despite his inexperience he already shows signs of being a good forward. He has a built-in instinct for scoring goals, is intelligent with good playing vision, characteristics which make him a promising striker. What is more he works hard for the team and is not someone who hides himself away when it comes to pressuring the opposition and defending.
x
x

* Originally from the lower ranks of Darlington, Blake signs as a professional on 1st July 1994. His first game for Darlington takes place on 4th March 1995 against Colchester United and he scores his first goal against Exeter City on 20th January 1996.
* Blake is transferred to Bradford City on 27th March 1997 and makes his debut with the Bantams on 29th March against Portsmouth.

* Once again, Robert Blake was one of the most important men at Darlington as he scored 10 goals in 30 games, being one of the team's top scorers. His great season lead Bradford City to pay £300,000 for him to reinforce their attack but his performances for the Bantams was somewhat discrete and he could not meet the expectations placed in him in the five games that he played for the club.

697.name: Watson
pages: * Gordon Watson is a centre forward who is outstanding for the enormous amount of hard work he puts in on the pitch and who can be an interesting proposition for Bradford City.  However, this brave player suffered a serious injury in his third game with the Bantams which will keep him out for a long time and so he will have to fight to work his way back into the team. Gordon Watson will have to rely on his fighting spirit to help him recover from injury and then battle for a place on Chris Kamara's team sheet.

* A battling forward who operates throughout the attacking zone. Right footed, he is not noted for his technical foundation, although he guarantees constant pressure on the rival defenders. At times he drops back to act as as link-man with the midfield and to initiate the Southampton's attacking play from there.  As he is not a goalscorer, his presence in the forward line-up has the aim of helping his team mates who resolve better. A quick footballer, he is more efficient against open teams, as he needs space to operate in the rival penalty area.
x

* 2 under-21 international appearances for England - 1 goal.
* 1 youth international appearance.

* Trained in the youth squad at Charlton Athletic, Gordon Watson turned professional on 5th April 1989. On the 19th of August he made his league debut in a game against Derby County.
* On the 20th of February 1991 he is transferred to Sheffield Wednesday for £250,000.
* Four years later, half-way through the 94-95 season, Watson is transferred to Southampton for £1,200,000. He makes his debut for the "Saints" the day after his signing, the team losing to Nottingham Forest at the City Ground (3-0).
* In his home debut against Southampton he scores a goal against Newcastle United (3-1).
* Watson was transferred to Bradford City in the month of January 1997 for £550,000. His debut is on the 18th of January against Swindon Town, and he scores his first goal for the club in the following game against Port Vale.

* Watson didn't have many opportunities with Southampton as the new coach at the time Graeme Souness, opted for other players until Watson's good moment came and he played some games. However, with Berkovic and Ostenstad settled in their positions, he departed for Bradford City. Bad luck followed him as after only playing three games, he suffers a double fracture in his leg, thus causing him to miss the rest of the league.

698.name: Zabica
pages: * Robert Zabica is a goalkeeper who has been an Australian international more times than any other and he provides Bradford City with a substitute for Prudhoe with experience in the position and, what's more experience at international level. Now at the end of his sporting career, he has decided to accept the club's offer and try his luck in European football, more exactly in English football, where he hopes to produce some dignified performances. His role will be limited to cover for the first choice goalie if he should get injured, but he is a man who knows how to do his duty.

* Robert Zabica is a veteran goalkeeper who has a great ability to trap the balls that arrive aerially, taking advantage of his height and good positioning. He is also safe when he appears and doesn't usually make mistakes. However, his problems appear with low shots as he has a back problem which prevents him from giving 100%.
x
* Zabica has made 39 international appearances for Australia.
* Bradford City sign him during the summer of 1997 from the Australian team Perth Glory, paying £150,000 for his services.
x

699.name: Prudhoe
pages:
* Mark Prudhoe has been a wanderer of English football as he has played in a host of teams, but always leaving behind a good memory due to his keeping ability. It looked like he had found some peace at Stoke City but little by little he was forced out of the team and his chances were few and far between.
* Chris Kamara has been a man much taken by his virtues since he took over at Bradford City, making continual efforts to sign him. After several negotiations from the end of the league during the course of the summer, Prudhoe has become one of the signings to face the championship, giving the Bantams a solid keeper to defend their goal.

* Mark Prudhoe is a very formidable goalkeeper in the air and has a good positioning which allows him to make some great saves. He has good reflexes with shots from point-blank range, which together with his placement, make him a more than passable keeper.  However, his clearest defect is that he finds it hard to get down for the low shots.
x
x

* Originally from the lower ranks of Sunderland, Prudhoe signed as a professional in September 1981, making his league debut against WBA.
* Loaned to Hartlepool United in November of 1983, he played his first game against Hereford United.
* Prudhoe is transferred to Birmingham City in September 1984 for £25,000. He makes his debut with the Blues against Sheffield United.
* Walsall sign him in February 1986 in exchange for £20,000 and he plays his first game on 28th February 1986 against Newport County.
* Loaned to Doncaster Rovers in December 1986 to cover for the injury to first choice keeper Andy Rhodes, he makes his debut against Middlesborough. 
* Loaned to Grimsby Town in March of 1987 he plays his first game with the club on 28th March 1987 against Shrewsbury Town.
* He is loaned to Hartlepool United in August 1987. He makes his debut against Darlington.
* Loaned to Bristol City in November 1987 he plays his first game against Aldershot.
* He is loaned then transferred to Carlisle United in December 1987 in exchange for £20,000. He makes his league debut against Swansea City.
* Signed by Darlington in March for £25,000. In the only period in his life when he enjoys a certain amount of stability, he plays his first game with the club on 18th March 1989 against Peterborough United.
* Stoke City sign him in June 1993 for £120,000, and he makes his debut on 4th August 1993 against Millwall.
* In September 1994 he is loaned to Peterborough United. He makes his debut against Cardiff City.
* In November 1994 he is also loaned to Liverpool but he doesn't get to make his debut for the Anfield team.
* His transfer to York City comes together and he moves on 14th February 1997. His first game with the club is on the 15 of February against Gillingham. 
* In the summer of 1997 and after diverse upsets, Prudhoe joins Bradford City for £70,000.

* Mark Prudhoe's season was disappointing as he had very few chances to defend the Stoke City goal and on Macari's decision he was often relegated to watching the game from the terraces. His spell at York City brought a couple of appearances.

700.name: Bright
pages: * Mark Bright's golden period is linked to Crystal Palace.  In this team he had the good fortune to coincide with Ian Wright, one of the most talented players in English football.  Together they formed an exceptional strike partnership which carried the Eagles to the FA Cup Final in 1990 and to the Third spot in the 90-91 season.  Where Wright used his talent, Bright boasted of his scent for goal.  Their understanding was such that between them they scored 90 goals in the League in just two seasons (87-88 and 88-89).  There can be no doubt that Bright is a lucky man.  Years earlier, at Leicester City, he shared the same changing room as Gary Lineker.  Although he didn't get to play very many minutes with him, he surely was able to learn a lot from him.

* Bright is a great centre forward.  His powerful header is outstanding, where he makes use of his great jump and his skill at placing himself in exactly the right spot to get the better of the defender.  He is also helped by his extraordinary athleticism.  Very intelligent in the area, he can make the most of any play.  He shoots well with both feet, his shots being powerful and penetrating, usually from near the goal-line. He is a specialist at controlling the ball in difficult situations, and he knows how to shield it with his body while he waits for his team-mates to join him.  Although he is now somewhat veteran, he uses his experience to counteract the logical reduction in his physical capabilities.
x
x

* His professional career started on the 15th of October 1981 at Port Vale, arriving from the modest club Leek Town.  His league debut doesn't take place until the 1st of May 1982, when he comes on as a substitute for Neville Chamberlain in a game against York City.  However, he doesn't earn the favour of his trainer, John Rudge, until the 83-84 season, in which he plays 26 games and scores 9 goals, the first of which is against Wimbledon. 
* On the 19th of July 1984 he is transferred to Leicester City, the club which had among its players Gary Lineker and Alan Smith.  The price, £33,000.On the 25th of August of this same year he makes his debut in a game against Newcastle.  However, his spell at Filbert Street wasn't very successful.  Two full seasons and only six goals. 
* On the 13th of November 1986 he moves to Crystal Palace in exchange for £75,000 and pairs up with Ian Wright, which had arrived in the team one year earlier.  In his first game, on the 15th of this month, he scores a goal against Ipswich Town.  In little more than 200 games he would score 89 goals. 
* He plays in the final and the replay of the FA Cup in 1990, against Manchester United.  He leaves the club in September 1992, a year after Wright, his strike partner. 
* Sheffield Wednesday paid £1.375.000 to acquire his services on the 11th of September 1992.  He makes his debut on the following day against Nottingham Forest, and his first goal with for the Owls is against Tottenham Hotspur fifteen days later. 
* In 1993 he plays in and loses both the League Cup final and replay, both against Arsenal with Ian Wright.  He finishes the 94-95 season as Wednesday's top scorer, but the 11 goals he put away were a far cry from the numbers he reached in his golden days at Crystal Palace. 
* In the 95-96 season he scores the third hat-trick of his career in a League Cup game against Crewe Alexandra. 
* After a spell on loan to Millwall, he signed for the Swiss team Sion in January 1997.  However, on the 4th of April of this same year he signs for Charlton Athletic.

* In December he was loaned to Millwall, started a spell of wandering from team to team.  In January he moved to the Swiss team Sion and in April he signed for Charlton Athletic, who he scored two goals for in six league games.

703.name: Mendonca
pages:
* After fighting for more than a year with an injury caused by a traffic accident which many thought would be the end of his sporting career, Clive Mendonca manages to overcome adversity and perform and important role for Grimsby Town although he can't prevent the team from relegation to the Second Division.
* His name has been linked with West Ham during the summer but it was Charlton Athletic who showed the clearest intentions, managing to sign him after paying the largest sum in the club's history. Despite being the team's most expensive signing, Mendonca will put in a lot of effort and will be vital for the Addicks' aspirations during this season.

* Mendonca is a very quick forward, both inside and outside the box. He dribbles well and his sparkling reactions in the box allowing him to score goals regularly, despite not being a born goalscorer. He works hard, opening up spaces for his teammates and for himself.
* Top scorer at Grimsby Town in the 93-94 and 96-97 season.
x

* Originally from the lower ranks of Sheffield United, Clive Mendonca signed as a professional in September 1986. He made his league debut on 2nd May 1987 against Brighton & Hove Albion and his first league goal is the winner in a game against Hull City on 3rd October 1987.
* In February 1988 he is loaned to Doncaster Rovers, making his debut against Grimsby Town.
* In March 1988 he is transferred to Rotherham United for £35,000. He plays his first game on 26th March 1988 against Bristol City and scores his first goal on 4th April 1988 against Fulham.
* Sheffield United capture him again for £110,000 in July 1991. He makes his debut on 28th August 1991 against Coventry City and manages to scores his first goal on 21st September 1991 against Arsenal.
* In January 1992 he is loaned to Grimsby Town, making his debut on 11th January 1992 against Oxford United, scoring his first goal with the team on 8th February 1992 against Blackburn Rovers.
* Once again he is loaned to Grimsby Town in March 1992, and the loan turns into a definitive transfer for £85,000 in August 1992.
* In the summer of 1997, Charlton Athletic pay £700,000 for his services, setting a new record for a transfer fee for the club.

* Mendonca was one of the best players at Grimsby Town, topping the score sheet and contributing great things to the team. After a season full on injuries which could have forced him to retire, Mendonca played 45 games and scored 17 goals.

704.name: Jones
pages:
* After several disappointing seasons at West Ham United in which he hardly got a game, Steve Jones decided to join a team like Charlton Athletic which is on the step just below the Premier League, where he can consolidate his progress and make himself as a footballer.
* Despite the fact that his statistics have not been spectacular in his short spell with the Addicks, this season he has found his way into the team and hopes to form a devastating partnership with the new signing Clive Mendonca. It will be a great opportunity to show his ability and prove Harry Redknapp wrong in not giving him many options.

* A strong forward with a scoring instinct, Steve Jones is a very dangerous player in the rival penalty area. Quick and powerful, he uses his strength to make up for his lack of skill, and he is hard to stop when running at rival defenders. However, his biggest virtue is his capacity to shoot from any position. He has a powerful shot and doesn't hesitate to use it at the slightest opportunity, although at times he is guilty of rushing things too much.
x
x

* Trained in the modest Billericay Town, Steve Jones signed for West Ham on 16th of November 1992 in exchange for £22,000.
* Without finding a place in the Hammers' starting line-ups he was transferred to Bournemouth on 21st of October 1994 for £150,000.
* In a short space of time Jones becomes one of the Cherries' supporters' heroes. He was also the team's top scorer for two seasons in a row (94-95 and 95-96).
* On the 16th of May 1996 he is signed by West Ham again. Bournemouth receive Mark Watson and £200,000 in exchange for Jones, as well as another £100,000 if the player takes part in a set number of games.
* He is transferred to Charlton Athletic on the 14th of February 1997 for £400,000. His first game with the club is on the 15th of this month against Barnsley.

* It was a somewhat disappointing season for Steve Jones as he hardly was used by Harry Redknapp, the manager of West Ham, and he played only eight games. His statistics with Charlton Athletic didn't get much better and he only made two appearances wearing the Addicks' shirt.

705.name: Allen
pages:
* Bradley Allen is a classy forward and a complete player in almost all aspects of his game.  His signing by Charlton Athletic could bring a useful player to the club, whose contribution could be significant. It will be important for this unfortunate player to have a season uninterrupted by injuries so that he can settle down at the club.
* His evident quality could open all the doors to the first team aligned by Alan Curbishley although the signing of Clive Mendonca makes things more complicated. Whether he is a starter or substitute his contribution will be appreciated.

* Bradley Allen is a very complete forward in every way. He is skilful, has a good turn and moves and thinks quickly, knowing exactly what to do at every moment. He doesn't think twice before shooting, with either of his two feet or with his head. He is basically right-footed, and he likes to drift over to the wings from where he can create chances for other people, with good passes to the midfielders who come up from behind.  What's more, he makes runs to open things up for a teammate. When he receives the ball with his back to the goal, he turns quickly and shoots powerfully.
x
* England under-21 international, he makes his debut on 12th May 1992 against Hungary.  That day the English team had players such as Andy Cole and Ugo Ehiogu among them.

* Originally from the lower ranks of QPR, he turned professional in September of 1988. His debut was on 14th January 1989 against Wimbledon, and he scores his first league goal on 10th April 1991 against Aston Villa.
* He is transferred to Charlton for £400,000 in March 1996, scoring a goal on his debut against Norwich City on 30th March 1996.

* With the Addicks, his bad luck returned once again as injuries limited him to 18 games with the team, in which he scored 4 goals. To make matters worse, he had to visit the surgeon due to an injury, missing the end of the league.

706.name: Petterson
pages: * For the first time since his arrival from Luton Town, Andy Petterson was able to call the Addicks' goal his, managing to find a place in the team after the injury to Salmon. From this moment we saw the best of Andy Petterson, who was the most valuable player in the team in the opinion of the fans. The best moment of the season was the save he made against Crystal Palace, compared with the one Gordon Banks made against Pele in the Mexico World Cup of 1970. If nothing changes, he will be the first choice of Curbishley to defend Charlton Athletic's goal.

* Petterson is a very agile keeper for someone of his height and build, being able to stop shots which would be impossible for other goalies. He is fearless when leaving his line and one of his virtues is his ability to play with the ball at his feet. In general terms, a very complete keeper.
x
x

* Signed by Luton Town in December 1988, he made his league debut on 15th August 1992 against Leicester City, playing the first 14 games of the competition.
* Petterson is loaned to Ipswich Town in March 1993, only playing one game, on 8th May 1993 against Nottingham Forest.
* Charlton Athletic sign him in 1994 for £85,000. He makes his debut for the Addicks on 17th September 1994 against Swindon Town.
* He is also loaned to Bradford City in December 1994, making his debut on 10th December 1994 against Leyton Orient.

* Petterson's season can be divided into two parts as up to the end of the year he was always on the bench or in the stands. Then a chance came along due to an injury to Salmon and Petterson took over the position in the Charlton goal. Since then, the place was his and his great contribution was rewarded by the fans who voted him the player of the season.

707.name: Salmon
pages:
* Mike Salmon is a very experienced goalie who was the first choice at Charlton Athletic until last year. In every game he is very consistent and this has earned him the respect of the fans, who see him as a true life insurance for the Addicks.
* Despite finishing his best season for the club, Salmon lost his place when he was injured, allowing Petterson to have his chance and defend the goal of Curbishley's men until the end of the league. This year he will try to ensure that things resort back to how they were before his injury although this will not be easy due to the sensational performances of Petterson.

* Salmon is a very complete keeper, with almost no defects in his game, and who has excellent positioning. He is brave when coming out, using his physique in 50-50 balls.  Very good in the air, he judges distances well and is a true insurance for his team in this aspect. Always well placed on the pitch, he is hard to catch unawares.
x
x

* Originally from the Blackburn Rovers juniors, Mike Salmon signed as a professional in October 1981. However, he only played one game, that played on 15th May 1982 against Chelsea.
* He is loaned to Chester City in October 1982 for 4 months, making his debut on 30th October 1982 against Swindon Town.
* His contract finishes and he leaves for Stockport County in August of 1983, playing his first game on 27th August 1983 against York City.
* He is a free agent once again and signs for Bolton Wanderers in July 1986, his debut coming on 23rd August 1986 against Swindon Town.
* He is transferred to Wrexham in March 1987 for £18,000, making his debut on 7th March 1987 against Cambridge United.
* Finally he signs for Charlton Athletic in July 1989, playing his first game with the Addicks on 18th September 1990 against Oldham Athletic.

* Last season can be considered in two parts for Mike Salmon as for Andy Petterson but the other way round. For the first part of the league, Salmon was the first choice keeper at Charlton Athletic but an injury led to an exchange of positions and it was Petterson who finished the campaign in the Addicks' goal. In total, Salmon played 25 games during the season.

708.name: Youds
pages:
* He was transfered to Charlton in March 1998 for 550.000 pounds. 
* Despite an unfortunate season in which injuries prevented him from playing any game with Bradford City in the league, Eddie Youds hoped to return to the team as if he were one of the Bantams' new signings.

* Youds is a classic central defender, outstanding in the aerial game thanks to his height and aggression when looking for the ball. Hard when making tackles, he makes good use of his physical strength. Very dangerous at set-plays, he only pushes up in these circumstances.  Technically he is nothing out of the ordinary but the most important thing is that he knows this and won't try anything that is beyond him. He can also play in the midfield as a defensive centre half.
x
x

* Youds was trained in the lower ranks of Everton, signing as a professional in June of 1988.  He made his league debut on 22nd December 1990 against Norwich City coming on as a substitute for Martin Keown.
* He is loaned to Cardiff City in December of 1989, playing only one game against Bolton Wanderers on 20th January 1990.
* He is also loaned to Wrexham in February 1990 and stays there till the end of the season.  His first game is against Hereford United and he scores his first league goal as a professional against Peterborough United.
* Youds is transferred to Ipswich Town in November 1991 for £250,000. He makes his debut with the team on 16th November 1991 against Derby County and his first and only goal for the club is the winner in a game against Blackburn Rovers on 27th November 1993.
* Bradford City acquire him as a loan player in January 1995 and eventually the loan becomes a transfer with the price set at £175,000 in March of this same year. He makes his league debut gainst Shrewsbury Town and his first two goals in the competition are against Peterborough United on 18th February 1995.
* A series of injuries prevented Eddie Youds from playing any league games last year for Bradford City, playing in only 3 reserve games at the end of the league.

709.name: Mills
pages:
* Signed for Charlton Athletic in March 1998. 
* Also from the Canaries youth squad, Danny Mills is a very young player who didn't notice the change in category at all. Although he is a man who is noted for his contributions to attack, in defence he is a true life insurance and is very hard to beat in any way.

* Mills is a left back who originally played on the right but who has managed to adapt perfectly to this position, though he uses his right foot better than his left. He is basically a defensive man who doesn't usually join in the attack. In his area of the pitch he is very safe, hard to get by and very quick and tough. He is good in the air. He is comfortable with the ball at his feet, a good passer and can receive it without danger of giving away possession.
x
* A youth international for England.
* Trained in the Norwich City youth squad, Mills signs as a professional in November 1994.  He makes his league debut on 13th August 1995 against Luton Town.

* Danny Mills was an automatic choice to the detriment of Carl Bradshaw when deciding who should fill the left-back spot at Norwich City. His, at times, impetuosity brought him some nasty shocks but this was part of the learning process for Mills. In total, he played 32 games.

710.name: Bowen
pages:
* After playing more than 300 games for Norwich City, Bowen was signed by West Ham United when his former club couldn't offer him a new contract. His contribution to the Hammers was limited to a few games so he decided to take advantage of the opportunity to sign for Shimizu in the Japanese League, and try out his luck.
* However, after the Asian experience, Bowen has decided to return to English football, more precisely, to Charlton Athletic, the team which have acquired his services going into this season. His contribution could be important in the coming season, thanks to his experience and know-how on the pitch.

* Right-footed, Mark Bowen has adapted perfectly to the position of left back, although during the course of his career he has played both as a midfielder and in other defensive positions. He is noted for the ease with which he joins in the attack, with an efficiency in the rival box not often seen in a left back thanks to his great shot. Technically discrete, he counteracts these shortcomings with strength, speed, experience and, above all, enthusiasm; virtues that make him a hard man to beat for rival forwards.
x

* 37 full international appearances for Wales.
* 3 under-21 international caps.
* Youth and schoolboy international.

* Mark Bowen arrived at the Spurs youth squad in October 1978, when he was almost 15.  In June 1980 he became an apprentice and on the 1st of December 1981 he turned professional. However, his debut with the first team did not happen until 29th of August 1983, in a game against Coventry City.
* A full international for Wales since 1986, he never found a place for himself in the Tottenham team loaded with stars, and so moved to Norwich City on 23rd July 1987 for £97,000.
* In the 88-89 season he settled definitively into the left-back position, although he is right-footed. His games helped contribute to the spectacular start to the season made by Norwich, who were even top for several weeks. 
* In the 89-90 season Bowen ends up top of the scorers' list with seven. 
* In the 91-92 season Bowen looses his place as starter to Colin Woodthorpe, although he is aligned in distinct positions and takes part in the FA Cup semi-final against Sunderland. The Canaries lost a historic chance to reach a Wembley final.
* Despite being a defender he leaves Norwich as one of the top ten scorers in the history of the club in the top division.
* At the end of the 95-96 season Norwich decide not to renew his contract. Shortly afterwards he signs for Harry Redknapp's West Ham. His first game for the Hammers is on the 21st of August against Coventry City and he scores his first and only goal for the club against Nottingham Forest on 21st September.
* He then moves to the ranks of the Japanese club Shimizu S-Pulse, where he plays for about six months.
* Finally in the middle of September 1997 he reaches an agreement with Charlton Athletic, when he signs for the club and comes back to English football.

* It wasn't the season that Mark Bowen was dreaming about on arriving at West Ham United as the left back position was occupied by Julian Dicks, and Bowen had to be content with playing when and where he could. Later, when his contract with the Hammers expired he tried his luck in Japanese football. At West Ham he scored one goal in 17 appearances.

711.name: Poole
pages: * The signing of Gary Poole by Charlton Athletic stirred up a great controversy between the footballer and his previous club Birmingham City, but this didn't stop this right back from finding a place in the starting eleven of Alan Curbishley, putting his non-sporting problems behind him and concentrating on making the biggest contribution possible to the Addicks' season. At the start of this season Poole has been relegated to the stands due to the great performances of Brown, the player who occupies the same position as Poole. Even so, this right back will try and return and figure in his manager's plans again.

* Poole is a right back who can also play as right half. In defence he is very sure with an ability for cutting out runs thanks to his anticipation and skill when tackling. Quick, and with an attacking vocation, when he gets the chance he joins in the attack doubling up on his wing. He is not a prolific scorer. He is good in the air but is not dominant, either in his area nor in the rival box.
* Second Division Champion with Birmingham City in the 94-95 season.
x

* Poole signed for Tottenham Hotspur after being turned down by the Arsenal schoolboys.
* After three frustrating seasons at Spurs, he signed for Cambridge United in August 1987 when his contract with the London club expired. He made his league debut on 1st September 1987 against Cardiff City.
* He is transferred to Barnet in March 1989 for £3,000. He plays his first game on 24th August 1991 against Mansfield Town and scores his first goal on 19th October 1991 against Blackpool.
* Poole signs for Plymouth Argyle as a free agent in June 1992. His debut occurs on 15th August 1992 against Mansfield Town and his first goal comes seven days later against Bradford City.
* Southend United sign him in July 1993 for £350,000, and he makes his debut on 18th September 1994 against Peterborough United.
* He is transferred to Birmingham City alongside Jonathan Hunt, in exchange for David Regis and Roger Willis who go to Southend.
* Finally on the 13th of November 1996 he is transferred to Charlton Athletic for £250,000.  His debut with the Addicks is on 16th November 1996 against QPR, where he also opens his goal account with the club.

* Poole played 10 games with Birmingham City before signing for Charlton Athletic last year.  The move produced controversy at the club managed by Trevor Francis. His debut could not have been better, when he scored a nice goal against QPR in November. Competing with Steve Brown for the right-back position, Poole played 16 games and scored that goal.

712.name: Barness
pages:
* After three forgettable years, Anthony Barness returns to Charlton Athletic, the club where he took his first steps in professional football. His spell at Chelsea was so bad that he only played 12 games in all the the time he was there.
* His return to The Valley was spectacular as he was a basic part of Alan Curbishley's sides, where he was played on the left of defence for the whole of the league, and was one of the most outstanding men. The Chelsea years forgotten, Barness hopes to be able to settle definitively into the left back position, something he was unable to do at Stanford Bridge.

* Barness is a footballer who occupies the position of right back, playing his part very solidly.  However, despite being right-footed, he has been used basically as a left back, but he can play in any of the positions in the defence. He is pretty quick, not as attacking as Jamie Stuart on the other side, but when the chance presents itself, he pushes up on his wing. He crosses well with his right, and is also a good passer, above all with short balls, and tries to give support to the midfield when playing the ball upfield. He is good in the air and is not at all nervous with the ball at his feet when faced with pressure from the rival.
x
x

* Barness trained as a footballer in the youth squad of Charlton Athletic, the club where he turned professional in March 1991. His first game with the team is on 17th September 1991 against Sunderland while he scores his first goal as a professional on 18th January 1992 against Newcastle United. 
* Barness is transferred to Chelsea in September 1992 in exchange for £350,000. His first game with the London team is on 12th September 1992 against Norwich City.
* He is loaned to Middlesborough in August 1993 but he doesn't get to play a single game.
* He is loaned once again, this time to Southend United in February 1996, playing his first game for the club on 3rd February 1996 against Millwall. 
* Finally, he returns to Charlton Athletic in the summer of 1996 for £150,000. He makes his debut on 17th August against Huddersfield Town and scores his first goal on the 30th of November against Oxford United.

* Anthony Barness' was magnificent as he only missed one of the games that his side played, and was a basic piece in Alan Curbishley's schemes. From his position at left back, Barness played 45 games and scored 2 goals in his return to The Valley.

713.name: Stuart
pages: * Jamie Stuart is a very young player from the Charlton Athletic youth squad who has a pretty promising future ahead of him. He shows a surprising maturity for one so young although he is still somewhat inexpert, he loses his concentration at times leading to difficult situations.  However, the injuries lead to a loss of form and, subsequently, the loss of his place in Alan Curbishley's eleven, currently occupied by Barness. Without a shadow of doubt he will have problems to regain his position but he has the ability to be successful.

* Stuart is a left back with a with a large attacking presence, pushing up constantly along the touchline to lend support to the attack. He is quick and powerful. His crosses are pretty good and he is workmanlike with the ball at his feet, he always sweats blood on the pitch.  He joins in the attack at set-plays, trying to connect with a header, something he manages often but without finding the back of the net much as shown by his record. He will try his shot with the right, which is his better one, although he is capable of using his left as well.
x
* Youth international for England.

* Originally from the lower ranks of Charlton Athletic, he signed as a professional in January 1995. He made his debut on 5th February 1995 against WBA and scored his first league goal against Huddersfield Town on 2nd September 1995, a goal which turned out to be the winner.

* Last season was very irregular for this left back as he started the season as first choice for Alan Curbishley in this position. However, a loss of form due to injury lead to him loosing his privileged position, with few opportunities right up to the end of the season. In total he played 10 games and scored a goal.

714.name: Rufus
pages:
* Richard Rufus is an extraordinarily talented central defender who has a great future ahead of him, provided that his progress isn't interrupted by an injury. He has been an under-21 international for England and could make the full team one day if his play continues to improve, something that is happening at the moment.
* Rufus is a person much sought after by the Premier League clubs, who are very interested in him, although at the moment Charlton Athletic is blocking an transfer due to the loss of their great star Lee Bowyer to Leeds United. Currently, in the team who will not be able to count on the leadership of Bowyer in the midfield, Rufus could be very important thanks to the charisma that he might bring to the Addicks in the future.

* Richard Rufus is a central defender who has some excellent characteristics for playing this sport. He is physically strong, which he takes advantage of when going in for the ball, though he does so fairly. Very quick, he is hard to beat in this respect and has a great ability for making up the distance between him and the rival forward if he makes a mistake. He is very calm under pressure and is sure of himself with the ball at his feet, pushing up easily, although he doesn't do so often. He is good in the air, and takes part in the set-plays although he is not particularly dangerous as shown by his goalscoring record, he still hasn't opened his account. He has a great sense of positioning and, at times, appears to be everywhere at once in the defence. Thanks to his speed and positioning on the pitch, he is excellent at making interceptions, making good use of his anticipation.
x
* English under-21 international for England five times. His first game was against Croatia on 23rd April 1996 against Sunderland, where the Balkan team won 1-0.
* Trained in the Charlton youth squad, he signed as a professional in July 1993. His league debut took place on 29th October 1994 against Derby County.
* Richard Rufus continued the progress of the year before, showing that the great expectations placed in him are fully justified. In total, he played 34 games for Charlton Athletic.

715.name: Chapple
pages:
* Phil Chapple is a consistent centre back who is in his fifth season with Charlton Athletic, turning in a series of masterly performances. Unfortunately for Chapple, his league in the year 1995 was cut short prematurely due to a serious knee injury and he couldn't continue with the excellent form he had show up until that moment. Fortunately the rehabilitation was good and he didn't have any problem in returning to the plans of Alan Curbishley. 
* The veteran back has a great rivalry with Balmer for a place in the centre of the Addicks' defence as the other place is almost obligatorily given to Rufus. Although he is at a certain disadvantage with respect to Balmer, Chapple, thanks to his leadership and know-how, could return to a place in the starting eleven in the team. Wherever he plays, his contributions to the side will be appreciated.

* Chapple is a player who operates in the centre of defence, taking almost perfect advantage of his height in the aerial game, both in his own box and in that of his rival, where he is pretty dangerous. He is fairly quick and agile for a man of his height, has excellent placing and is very sure when making interceptions, trying to get in front of the forwards. He does not get very philosophical when making tackles, where he is tough.
* Third Division Champion with Cambridge United in the 90-91 season.
x

* Trained in the lower ranks of Norwich City, he signed as a professional in July 1985.
* As a free agent he signed for Cambridge United in March 1988.  He plays his first game for the side on 4th April 1988 against Rochdale and scores his first goal on 2nd May 1988 against Stockport County.
* Chapple is transferred to Charlton in August 1994 for £100,000, scoring on his his debut, a goal which is the winner, against Birmingham.

* Phil Chapple managed to recover from a serious knee injury in 1995 and once more was an important man for Alan Curbishley, whether as a substitute who was injured or even as a starter. His statistics improved with respect to the 95-96 season, playing 26 games and scoring 2 goals.

716.name: Brown
pages: * Steve Brown is a defender from the Charlton Athletic youth squad who has managed to perform efficiently in all of the positions in the defence. He does not disappoint at any time despite playing in a variety of different positions. Last year his versatility was much appreciated, and he played in a significant number of games. Competing with Gary Poole for the place at right back, for the time being he is the first choice and it doesn't look like he will give it up except in the case of injury or loss of form.

* Steve Brown is a versatile footballer who can play in a multitude of positions although his natural one is right back. He is very strong with his right which he takes advantage of for long balls, looking for the counter attack or looking for the head of Leaburn or Whyte in a static attack. He crosses pretty well first time from the right. He is fairly quick and consistent although he doesn't usually join in the attack very often.
x
x

* Originally from the lower ranks of Charlton Athletic, he signed as a professional in July 1990.  He made his debut on 21st September 1991 against Watford and scored his first goal from the penalty spot on 30th August 1994 against Sheffield United.

* Brown was a regular feature in Alan Curbishley's teamsheets, performing well wherever he was put. Of the 27 games that he played for Charlton Athletic, there was one where something strange happened. In one of them, he stepped in for the first choice keeper Salmon who was injured in a game against Wolverhampton Wanderers. No goals were conceded.

717.name: Balmer
pages:
* Trained in the youth squad at Glasgow Celtic, Stuart Balmer never had the chance to play for the first team of the Scottish club and show his ability.  To find that chance had to leave for English football, more precisely, to Charlton Athletic.
* With the Addicks, he formed a magnificent partnership with Richard Rufus, the very young centre back, with whom he seems to have a telepathic link, forming an almost insurmountable barrier. Once again in this season he will be a starter provided he isn't forced out by injury, but the presence of Chapple will make him work hard to keep his place.

* Balmer is a footballer with a lot of experience behind him and who can play both at right back and at centre back, his natural position. He is very authoritative in defence, knowing exactly what to do at every moment. He is excellent in the air, dominating in this aspect. As a good Charlton defender, he is safe with the ball at his feet, being able to pass it effectively.  He is dangerous at set-plays. Physically very strong, he is excellent at making interceptions due to his placing which makes him seems faster than he actually is.
x
x

* Trained in the Glasgow Celtic youth squad, he didn't get to play for the team.
* Balmer is transferred to Charlton for £120,000 in August 1990. He played his first game for the team on 15th September 1990 against Brighton & Hove Albion and he scored his first goal against Tranmere Rovers on 9th January 1993.

* Stuart Balmer was a regular feature in Alan Curbishley's schemes last year, until an injury kept him temporarily out of the team. However, on returning he produced high quality football, contributing firmness to the Addicks' defence. His partnership with Richard Rufus was very consistent. In total, he played 32 games and scored two goals.

719.name: Holmes
pages: * After an ill-fated season at Blackburn Rovers in which he didn't get to play a single league game, Matty Holmes hopes that he will have more opportunities at Charlton Athletic to show his footballing qualities. He could be an interesting incorporation for the Addicks as he works very hard and is versatile in the midfield.

* A very hardworking midfielder, Matty Holmes gives his all in every game. His constant effort is notable in ball-winning tasks, although he doesn't delay in joining in the attack at the slightest opportunity. Left-footed, and with a lot of physical resistance, he usually plays at left half. His acceptable technique with his good foot allows him to take free-kicks accurately.Holmes is, above all, a team player, who allows sacrifices himself for the good of the team.
x
x

* Matty Holmes started in the footballing world in the Bournemouth youth squad, and turned professional with on the 22nd of August 1988. Loaned to Cardiff City on the 23rd of March 1989, he makes his league debut two days later against Aldershot.
* On returning to Bournemouth, he sees the team relegated to the Third Division in 1990. On the 19th of August 1992 he is transferred to West Ham for £40,000 and, in his first season at Upton Park, he takes part in the team's promotion to the Premier League.
* Surprisingly, on the 15th of August 1995, he moves to Blackburn Rovers in exchange for £1,200,000. In principle, Holmes arrives at Ewood Park to cover for the temporary absence of Jason Wilcox. He makes his debut on the 23rd of this month, with a 2-1 defeat at the hands of Sheffield Wednesday at Hillsborough. Three days later he scores his first goal for the Rovers against Bolton.
* In the summer of 1997, Matty Holmes joins Charlton Athletic for a reduced price of £250,000.
* It is hard to say much about Matty Holmes' season last year as he didn't get to play a single game for the Rovers in the whole of the league. The opportunities, therefore, shine by their absence.

720.name: Kinsella
pages:
* Originally from a the Third Division team Colchester United, Charlton Athletic sign Mark Kinsella to cover, in part, the departure of their sensational midfielder Lee Bowyer at Leeds United, which happened at the end of the 95-96 season. The performance of this player was sensational and fully met the expectations placed in him. It could be said that it was to be expected that Kinsella would not take long to make the jump to a higher division due to his magnificent characteristics and his battling spirit. What is surprising is the extraordinary maturity that this young Irish international shows, who doesn't seemed to have noticed much the change in level.
* With a great future ahead, Kinsella will set Charlton Athletic's course again this season and is waiting for his probable call-up to the full Ireland team, something which could happen shortly.

* Kinsella is a player blessed with great technique, making him a skilful footballer, but who is also very combative on the pitch. He plays as a midfield playmaker, a role which he carries out splendidly, passing both in short and using the long ball very acceptably. At Colchester United, he even got to play as a sweeper and he didn't look out of place in this position. He uses both feet well and shoots with both of them easily. He is fairly quick and has an outstanding physical strength.
* Voted a member of the Third Division Dream Team in the 95-96 season.
* Kinsella has been a youth and under-21 international for Ireland eight times.

* Originally from the Irish team Home Farm, when his contract expires he moves to Colchester United in August 1989. His first game with the club is on 26th August 1989 against Halifax Town and his first goal comes on the 21st August 1992 against Barnet.
* Kinsella was voted the best player at Colchester United in the 95-96 season by the fans at the club.
* He is loaned to Charlton Athletic in September 1996 but he finally gets to stay when the club lead by Alan Curbishley decide to keep him in October of this same year. His debut with the Addicks takes place on the 28th of September against Oldham Athletic and he scores his first goal against Oxford United on the 26th of October.

* Kinsella was a key piece in Charlton Athletic's plans after they acquired him from Colchester United. His importance was so great that he didn't loose his place until September, the date of his definitive transfer. He was one of the most consistent men in the team during the course of the season, playing in 37 games and scoring 6 goals.

721.name: Robinson
pages:
* With the passing of time John Robinson has become an essential man at Charlton Athletic due to his versatility and danger in attack. What's more he works hard in defence, helping out his team mates without any complexes. 
* Thanks to his fighting and winning character, he has even caught the eye of the Welsh selectors, who have used him, and will do so again if nothing untoward happens in the coming years. In short, a man who has earned his place in the team and whose role will be very important this coming season for the Addicks.

* Robinson is a player who normally plays on the left despite being right footed although he can also operate on the right when Newton is not available. He always give 100% and goes in hard. He works hard in defensive tasks, being almost inexhaustible.  Robinson is skilful, bringing the ball along close to his feet and continually swerving to the left or right, giving his forwards good service. He has a good shot on goal with his right, shooting whenever he can. He is quick and doesn't stop pushing up along his wing, working hard. He can also play as a wide defender in times of emergency.
x

* Robinson has been an under-21 international for Wales, making his debut on 19th May 1992 against Romania.
* He has also played as a full international for Wales, his first game being against Switzerland on 24th April 1996 in Lugano. In total, he has played 3 games with the team.

* Trained in the youth squad at Brighton & Hove Albion, he turns professional in April 1989.  He makes his debut on 16th August 1990 against Portsmouth and scores his first goal as a professional against Portsmouth on 31st August 1991.
* Robinson is transferred to Charlton Athletic for £75,000 in September 1992. He makes his debut on 18th October 1992 against Millwall, scoring his first league goal six days later against Derby County.
* He is voted player of the year at Charlton Athletic by the fans of the club during the 95-96 season.

* In general terms John Robinson had a very notable role at Charlton Athletic last year, playing 42 games and scoring 3 goals, which did not go by unnoticed by the coaches of the Welsh national team, who gave him the chance to show his quality in the team, something that he took advantage of to perfection.

722.name: Newton
pages:
* Shaun Newton is a footballer who has a lot of class and who is one of Charlton's big stars.  This super-young player was trained in the youth squad of the Addicks and was one of the team's reference points last year, when the team was on the brink of making it to the Premier League in the 95-96 season, together with team mates such as Lee Bowyer and Richard Rufus.
* Although he is, at times, somewhat inconsistent in his performances, disappearing from the game, he has enough capacity to improve and be a very important player for Charlton Athletic's future. One of the fastest players in the First Division and with the best ability to break through defences, he will be a certain starter in the team aligned by Alan Curbishley.

* Newton is a player who almost always plays hugging the right touch line, where, thanks to his speed, he is very hard to stop for the rival defenders. He dribbles well and his speed, together with this skill, let him come away from double-marking situations to which he is almost always subjected. He is very technical and has excellent ball control. With the ball at his feet he is very competent and has vision and ability to make good crosses. He is basically right-footed although he can use the left acceptably. He has a good header when at the far post, taking the defence by surprise. What's more he has a good shot with both feet, and pops up dangerously from deeper positions and is resourceful. Physically, he is strong, and he will usually come off best in a collision. He has the power to set moves in motion from the back. He can also play at right back.
x
* Newton has made 3 international appearances for England at the under-21 level.

* Trained in the Charlton Athletic youth squad, he signs as a professional in July 1993. He makes his league debut on 1st May 1993 against Derby County and scores his first goal against Tranmere Rovers on 24th August 1993.

* With 43 appearances last year, Shaun Newton reached the highest number of games in his still short sporting career, showing that he has a great future ahead of him as a footballer.  He even got to score 3 goals for the Addicks, apart from drawing gasps with his electrifying game.

723.name: Mortimer
pages:
* In his second spell at Charlton Athletic, Paul Mortimer is the perfect complement to the youthful nature of the team, not due to his age but because he is a footballer with a lot of experience. He is a team player and doesn't hide away when it comes to taking on responsibility. For this reason, he is the official penalty and free-kick taker with his left.
* Unfortunately injuries have followed him during the last few seasons, including a very serious injury to his Achilles tendon, preventing him from playing for the Addicks. He could form an interesting partnership with Mark Kinsella but it remains to be seen if Alan Curbishley will play him from the start, although he has the aptitude to do so.

* Mortimer is a very complete midfielder who operates on the left of the pitch. He works hard for the benefit of the team but is not devoid of a great individual technique, together with a good playing vision and ball control. He is very strong physically and, therefore, it is hard to get the ball off him.  He shoots well from long range, very powerfully. He gets into good positions thanks to his strength and he takes advantage of this to surprise the rival defence.
x
* An English under-21 international, he makes his debut in the Toulon international tournament on 7th June 1989 against Senegal, scoring two goals.

* Mortimer's contract with Farnborough Town comes to an end and so he joins Charlton Athletic in September 1987. He makes his league debut against Norwich City and scores his first goal on 1st October 1989 against this same team.
* He is transferred to Aston Villa in July 1991 for £350,000, playing his first game for the Villains on 17th August 1991 against Sheffield Wednesday. His first goal for the Birmingham team is scored on 5th October 1991 against Luton Town.
* Crystal Palace sign him in 1991 for £500,000. He makes his debut on 19th October 1991 against Coventry City and he scores his first goal in the league against Manchester United.
* He is loaned to Brentford in January 1993, making his debut on 23rd January 1992 against Portsmouth.
* He is finally transferred to Charlton in July 1994. He makes his debut on 13th August 1994 against Oldham Athletic and manages to open his account for them in the league on 3rd September 1994 against Bristol City.

* Unfortunately injuries get in the way of Paul Mortimer last year, preventing this skilful midfielder from forming a playmaking partnership together with Mark Kinsella. In the few games that he did play, he was not at his best. He played in 11 matches and scored a goal.

724.name: Jones
pages:
* Keith Jones is a player with a lot of experience and is a leader in the Charlton midfield, acting as a pivot for Charlton's moves. He gives an opening for the ball, always giving it to the best placed team mate and carrying out defensive tasks efficiently.  He is also consistent during the course of the games, not dazzling with his brilliance but not making stupid mistakes either.
* Last season he couldn't reach his best form due to the injuries which followed him although in this season, now free of these problems, he won't have any difficulty occupying the position of conductor of the Addicks orchestra. Although there are men such as Mortimer who could make an excellent partnership together with his complement, Mark Kinsella, Jones is a man who will probably play as a starter in Alan Curbishley's teams.

* Keith Jones is Charlton Athletic's playmaker, directing operations from the midfield. His game is usually a short ball to the team mate in the best position, a game which he plays efficiently. He uses the right better than the left although his left is also acceptable. He has the ability to regain possession, and is a hard tackler. Technically he is complete, a good passer and crosses well.  He moves quickly and is a fairly strong player.
x
* England schoolboy and youth international.

* Originally from the lower ranks of Chelsea, he signs as a professional in August of 1983.  He makes his league debut on 26th March 1983 against Barnsley and his first two league goals are scored on 3rd November 1984 against Coventry City.
* Jones is transferred to Brentford in September 1987 for £40,000, scoring on his league debut against Rotherham United on the 5/9/87.
* In October 1991 Southend United sign him for £175,000. He plays his first game on 19th October 1991 against Watford and scores his first goal for them against Newcastle United on 1st January 1992.
* Finally, Jones is transferred to Charlton Athletic in September 1994 for £150,000. His first game with the Addicks is on 17th September 1994 against Swindon Town and he scores his first goal for the team on 17th December 1994 against Oldham Athletic.

* Keith Jones produced a good season with Charlton Athletic although injuries did not allow him much continuity in the team. He played 19 league games for the Addicks during the course of the league. After his injury in September against Reading, Jones returned to play some sensational games for his club.

725.name: Roberts
pages: * Iwan Roberts has become the most noticeable signing made by Norwich City going into the present season, adding a man with experience and proven goalscoring record to the squad managed by Mike Walker. A classic centre forward, his enormous power and danger in the rival box make him a sure bet for a place in the Canaries team, forming a good partnership with Robert Fleck.

* A very strong centre forward, the main virtues of Iwan Roberts are his magnificent aerial game and his enormous enthusiasm which oozes from every one of his actions. The Welsh player pressures rival defenders constantly, and technically, he is not so good but rather raw.  Despite his great bulk, he is fairly quick. An instinctive finisher, he usually controls the ball effectively when he receives it in a shooting position and then lets fly. He can shoot with both feet but he is better with the right. With his head, he is able to lay off a lot of long balls for Steve Bull or the quick midfielders to pick up on the run .

* Top scorer at Huddersfield Town in the 90-91, 91-92 and 92-93 seasons together with Phil Starbuck. 
* Top scorer at Leicester City in the 93-94, 94-95 and 95-96 seasons.

* Roberts has been a Welsh international at the schoolboy, youth, B and absolute level, making his debut in the latter on 11th October 1989 against Holland at Wrexham. In total he has 7 full international caps.

* Originally from the lower ranks of Watford, Iwan Roberts signed as a professional in July 1988. He makes his league debut on 29th March 1986 against Ipswich Town and scores his first goal as a professional against Manchester United on 16th September 1986, the winner for the Blues. 
* He is transferred to Huddersfield Town in August 1990 for £275,000. He makes his debut on 25th August 1990 against Southend United and scores his first goal on 8th September 1990 against Bolton Wanderers. 
* Leicester City sign Roberts for £100,000 in November 1993. His first game with the Foxes couldn't be better as he finds the net twice against Wolverhampton Wanderers on 27th November 1993. 
* Iwan is finally transferred to Wolves for £1 million in the summer of 1996. He makes his league debut on 17th August 1986 against Grimsby Town and scores his first goal on 10th September 1996 against Oxford United. 
* Five days later, his team wins the Black Country Derby against WBA and Roberts scores a hat-trick. Roberts is the first Wolves player to score three goals in one game at the Hawthorns, the West Bromwich Albion stadium, in the history of the team in these derbies, and the first player to score a hat-trick at this level since 1963. If this weren't enough, his goals helped Wolves to their first win over WBA since 1989. 
* In the summer of 1997 Norwich City sign him after paying Wolverhampton Wanderers £1 million.

* Roberts' spell at Wolverhampton Wanderers didn't start too well but shortly afterwards he scored that hat-trick against WBA in the derby. Unfortunately a domestic accident forced him out of the team for a while and when he returned, he had to fight with Don Goodman for a place in the attack alongside Steve Bull. Even so, he finished with 33 games and 12 goals, and was the second top scorer at Wolves behind Steve Bull.

726.name: O'Neill
pages: * A product of the almost inexhaustible youth squad at Norwich City, Keith O'Neill is a winger who seems set to be a star in a short space of time. A man who is enormously skilful, quick and aggressive, if the injuries stay away and things go well, he could leave his mark on the team and in his national team, where he has made his debut and promises to be a regular player both for Ireland and for the Canaries. The partnership he formed with Darren Eadie is overwhelming but to take up his place once again he will have to figure in Mike Walker's plans, although, given time, he will do so.

* O'Neill is a left winger with an amazing turn of speed, whose runs down his wing create a lot of danger thanks to the speed and good dribbling. He pushes up and drops back untiringly, covering for his team mate who pushes up. Despite his youth, he is very tough, aggressive and never folds. He has a good shot with his left and is very left-footed. He looks for one-twos and is capable of doing them with a lot of precision. He has great technique and the ability to make magnificent deep passes to the forwards.
x

* O´Neill has been an International for the Republic of Ireland at the schoolboy, youth, under-21 and full level. 
* He makes his debut at the absolute level on 29th May 1996 against Portugal in Dublin. 
* He scores his first goal on 2nd June 1996 against Croatia.

* Trained in the Norwich City youth squad, Keith O'Neill signed as a professional in July of 1994. He played his first game for the club on 2nd November 1994 against Southampton and scores his first goal for the team on 16th March 1996.

* When Keith O'Neill formed a partnership last year with Darren Eadie, it seemed as if the Norwich City players where unstoppable for their opponents. His season was very good but injuries and diverse problems prevented him from playing more during the course of the league. In total, he played 26 games and scored 6 goals.

727.name: Eadie
pages:
* Right from his debut a few years ago for Norwich City, it could be seen that Darren Eadie was one of the most promising wingers in the English League with an enormous amount of room for improvement. A very complete player, it won't be long before he plays again in the Premier League, whether it is with the Canaries or with some other club from this Division. 
* Last season was the one of confirmation for this sensational footballer, who dominated rival defences during the course of the season and was on amazing form. Leicester City were looking to sign him, trying every trick in the book at the beginning of last season although Eadie has said that he wants to stay at least one more year at Norwich City. It could be one of the last chances to see Eadie with the Norwich shirt on, so the supporters will try and takes as much advantage as possible. Despite being injured at the beginning of the league, Eadie is an undisputed starter for Walker, and he will be, without doubt, one of the great stars of the First Division.

* Eadie is a left winger who has an almost supersonic turn of pace and who is able to make runs from his own half and arrive in the rival box with the force necessary to put over a good cross or have a dig himself. Very left-footed, he is not fragile despite his physical appearance, being strong and fighting courageously for the ball. Up till last season he had problems when it came to finishing off his chances, but once solved, we are talking about a player almost without limits. He has a good shot from 20 metres. He moves easily in between lines and has enough playing vision to give his forwards some incredible passes. 
* This season he is being used as a link-man between the midfield and the forwards, and here, with his speed and verticality, he is making the team very happy. Sometimes he is a little selfish but most times, his extraordinary moves compensate for this small defect.
* Voted a member of the First Division Dream Team in the 96-97 season.
* Eadie has been under-21 international for England.  He made his debut on 31st MAy 1994 against France after coming on as a substitute for Peter Fear.
* Originally from the Norwich City youth squad, his debut couldn't be better as he scores a goal against QPR on 18th September 1993.

* Last year was Eadie's best, without doubt, for Norwich City. His performance was so extraordinary that he even became the team's top scorer and was named as a member of the First Division Dream Team by the footballers themselves. In total, he played 44 games and scored 17 goals.

728.name: Walton
pages: x

* A very experienced keeper, Walton is safe and decisive when he decides to come off his line. While his kicking is also powerful and accurate he keeps his concentration well even though he may be out of the game for long periods. He consistenly performs to a high level.
x
* One under-21 international appearance for Wales.
* He was loaned to Norwich City in March 1998.

* Walton was involved in one of the surprises of the season when, after 18 months out of   the professional game, he was suddenly back in goal and making a fine job of things. He played in a total of 28 league games, all of those appearances as a member of the starting line up. Taking into account that it took him until February to make himself a regular in the side he's played a considerable number of games,

729.name: Marshall
pages: * Aged just 21, Andy Marshall is one of the most promising goalies in English football and is destined to do great things for his country and team. Last season he managed to oust Bryan Gunn from the first team towards the end of the league, and has settled into the position at the beginning of this. His future is brilliant and now he just needs to go on improving little by little to catch the eye of Glenn Hoddle.

* Marshall is a tremendously promising keeper who acts as if he were a veteran. He is excellent in the aerial game, making full use of his height and has some sensational reflexes, making truly worthy saves. However, a small defect he has is that with the shots at goal he doesn't block them, but rather pushes the ball away, which can cause a nasty surprise for the defence.
x
* England under-12 international, he made his debut in the Toulon tournament against Malaysia on 8th June 1995.

* Originally from the lower categories of Norwich City, his first chance to play for the first team comes on 27th January 1994 against Nottingham Forest due to an injury to Bryan Gunn and the sale of the other goalkeeper, Scott Howie, to Motherwell. 
* His first full game is 4 days later against Newcastle United and he produces a powerful performance. In this season (94-95), he plays 21 games and despite his good work, Norwich City are relegated to the First Division.
* During the 96-97 season he is loaned to Bournemouth and Gillingham.

* Possibly, this was the most important season for Andy Marshall because it seemed to be the start of his change to first choice keeper. He started the league as always, that is, as understudy to Bryan Gunn but after being loaned to different teams, he showed that he was ready to occupy the position between the posts for the Canaries, something which he did at the end of the season.

732.name: Forbes
pages: * Adrian Forbes is one of the talented players who has come out of the youth squad at Norwich City in the last few years, and who has caused a true impact with his contribution to the Canaries on the pitch. A true raw diamond, he is similar physically to another former team player Ruel Fox, currently at Tottenham Hotspur. He has taken advantage of the gap on the left of the pitch left by Ian Crook to find a place in the team. He is a player who will have to be watched in the future.

* Adrian Forbes is a man who plays on the left of the pitch but is not exactly a winger. He battles a lot but he is not weak technically, and this combined with a lot of skill and playing vision allow him to make some truly wonderful passes.
x
* Youth international for England.
* Originally from the lower ranks of Norwich City, Forbes signs as a professional on the 21st of January 1997. His debut takes place on the 31st of August against Wolverhampton Wanderers.

* Forbes completed a sensational first season in the Canaries first team. His tenacity and skill with the ball brought delight to the followers at Norwich City, who saw how, given some playing time, the midfielder made had great performances, appearing a lot more experienced than he actually is due to his aplomb and consistency. In total, he played 10 games.

733.name: Grant
pages: * Peter Grant has been another of Norwich City's incorporations for this season. The former Glasgow Celtic player has played 20 or more games per season for the Scottish team in the last 12 seasons, in which he showed signs of his worth and durability. He brings a touch of experience to the young and promising team and brings with him capacity for sacrifice and work. He will be a certainty in Mike Walker's line-ups.

* Grant occupies the position of defensive centre half, and is a true specialist in this function and is excellent when breaking down the rival's game. He is very tough and has no complexes when going in for the ball, but he does so fairly. His privileged physical condition allows him to play full throttle for the full 90 minutes. He is technically correct but this aspect of his game is nothing to make a song and dance about.
x
* An international for Scotland in the youth, under-21 and full categories two times.
* After 15 seasons at Glasgow Celtic, Peter Grant signs for Norwich City during the summer of 1997.
* Grant played for Glasgow Celtic last season, and was one of the most consistent men in the Scottish team during the course of the league, clocking up 23 appearances.

734.name: Adams
pages: * The figure of Neil Adams on the right for Norwich City is almost vital for the Canaries, who have taken advantage of his good crosses and forays down the right over the years. As well as being a man who contributes a lot in attack, he does not hide away when it comes to defending. Furthermore he is fresh from a season in which he has scored 15 goals, being one of the best finishers in the team managed by Mike Walker. He will be one of the men who the coach uses although he hasn't started the league as a member of the starting squad.

* Adams is a footballer who basically operates on the right, where he plays an excellent role.  He has a great ability to cross well whether first time from a pass from a team mate, or after dribbling by a rival. Many goals are the result of passes of his.  He shoots well with the right.  He has good dribbling which allows him to make good individual plays. He always operates hugging the touchline from where he can make deep passes for the midfielders who arrive from the midfield. Despite his contribution to the attack, he doesn't shirk on his defensive duties and helps out a lot.

* League Champion with Everton in the 86-87 season. 
* League Cup Runner-up with Oldham Athletic in the 89-90 season.
* Adams has been under-21 international for England, making his debut on 9th September 1986 against Sweden.

* Originally from the lower ranks of Stoke City, Adams signed as a professional in June 1985.  He made his league debut on 21st September 1985 against Charlton Athletic and scored his first goal as a professional against Middlesborough. 
* In July 1986, Howard Kendall pays Stoke City £100,000 to acquire his services and bring him to Everton. He makes his debut in the league on 30th August 1986 against Coventry City and doesn't score a single goal for the Goodison Park team in his twenty appearances. 
* In January 1989 he is loaned to Oldham Athletic, the team with which he makes his debut on the 14th of this month against Manchester City. In view of his good performance, Joe Royle pays Everton £100,000 for him in August 1989. His first league goal comes on 26th December 1989 against Swindon Town.
* He is finally transferred to Norwich City in February 1994 for £250,000. His debut occurs on 19th February 1994 against Swindon Town and he scores his first goal for the Canaries on 8th October 1994 against Leeds United, a goal that is the winner.

* Adams had one of his best seasons as a professional, scoring the highest number of goals in 10 years finding the net 15 times and being one of the best examples of consistency that can be found at Norwich City. He only missed one game in the whole of the league due to flu.
