736.name: Segura
pages:
* Víctor Segura is a youngster who trained in the youth squad of Saragossa, but who finally wasn't exploited by this team, and he had to earn a living in other teams. Taking advantage of the Bosman Ruling, Segura has emigrated to England looking for chances that have eluded him in Spain, as well as looking for experience in a competition very different from the Spanish league. 
* In Mike Walker's team he will basically play as a defender and has even had the chance to play quite often at the beginning of the league due to injuries. He could be a valuable player for the Canaries taking into account the length of the English championship.

* Segura is a defender whose biggest virtue is his adaptability as he adapts perfectly to centre back, left back and can even play in the midfield as a pivot in the contentious tasks. This means that he can be an important man in any team.
x
* Segura has been a Spanish international in the under-16, under-17 and under-18 categories.
x
x

737.name: Jackson
pages: * After not managing to figure in the plans of different coaches at Everton , he is loaned to various clubs in the First Division. Then Jackson leaves finally for Norwich City, where he as made a great impact in just one season with the Canaries. His future is brilliant and he could have plenty of chances during the course of the season although he has started the year as a substitute.

* He usually plays at right back, although he can also fill the centre of the defence.  In both positions he is very mature and complies perfectly. His first touch is very good, although where he stands out most is in defensive tasks. When he plays as a wide defender, he offers constant support for the midfielders when trying to regain possession. In attack, does not catch the eye, something he could improve helped by his excellent aerial game. Given time, he could become a great footballer.
* FA Cup Champion 94-95.

* 11 under-21 international appearances. 
* 1 youth international appearance.

* Originally from the Luton Town juniors, Jackson signed his first professional contract on 4th July 1990. 
* He is loaned to Preston North End on 27th March 1991, and makes his debut for this club on 30th March against Crewe Alexandra. 
* On returning to Luton he makes his debut against Arsenal on 27th August 1991. On 4th September he plays his first full game at home against Southampton. 
* On 18th October 1991 he is transferred to Everton for £600,000. In February 1992 he scores his first goal for the Toffees in a game against Leeds United (1-1). 
* Jackson is loaned to QPR and then Birmingham City during the 96-97 season.
* Finally, his transfer to Norwich City takes place on 24th December 1996 for £450,000. His debut with the Canaries is on the 26th of this same month against QPR and his scores his first goal for the club against Portsmouth on 1st January.
* Unable to keep his place in the Everton team, Jackson was loaned both to QPR and Birmingham City before finally moving to Norwich City, the club where he produced some great performances.

738.name: Fleming
pages: * Craig Fleming is one of the best markers in English football and he has become another of Norwich City's reinforcements alongside Roberts, Grant and Segura going into the present season.  After a season where he was as solid as a rock, Fleming hopes to find a place in the Canaries starting line-up although, at the moment, he is not appearing on Walker's teamsheets. His opportunity will come sooner or later.

* Fleming can play both at right back, his preferred position, or as a central defender, marking the most dangerous and strongest rival forward. He is very good in the air. When playing as a wide defender he pushes up along the touchline frequently but he doesn't dribble well so he doesn't get by his opponents using skill but rather force. His crosses are acceptable and he even takes the free-kicks that are on the right. He is tough but fair, trying always to anticipate. Right-footed, Fleming is an acceptable passer who isn't uncomfortable with the ball at his feet.
x
x

* Trained in the youth squad at Halifax Town, Fleming signed as a professional in March 1990. He plays his first game on 2st January 1989 against Scunthorpe United. 
* After nearly 60 appearances for Halifax Town, he is transferred to Oldham Athletic in August 1991 for £80,000. He makes his league debut on on 24th August 1991 against Norwich City and scores his first goal as a professional against Everton on 7th March 1992. 
* Norwich City sign him in the summer of 1997 for £600,000.

* Fleming was as solid as ever in his position in the Oldham defence, only missing two games during the entire league. However, his good performance couldn't prevent his former team from being relegated to the Second Division. In total, he played 44 games.

739.name: Sutch
pages: * Daryl Sutch is blessed with a lot of talent for playing football, and is very acceptable technically. What's more, his versatility gives him the advantage of being able to play in several positions while other team mates can only do so in one. A product of the Norwich City youth squad, he has needed 6 seasons to reach the 150-game mark for the Canaries. His status as starter is almost certain but the signing of Fleming brings some stiff competition.

* Sutch is a very fast and strong player, who can play as a wide defender or a wide midfielder on the right. He is an excellent passer of the ball and is very safe when doing so, normally over short or medium range. Thanks to his speed, he normally joins in the attack, putting over good crosses but he doesn't usually finish the moves that he starts. He is good in the air and hard when tackling.
x
* Sutch has been a youth and under-21 international for England, making his debut in the latter category on 30th March 1993 against Turkey.

* Originally from the lower ranks of Norwich City, he signs as a professional in July 1990.  He makes his league debut on 26th December 1990 against Manchester United at Old Trafford and scores his first goal against Middlesborough on 31st October 1992.

* Finally Daryl Sutch enjoyed a season without injury problems, and was one of the certainties in Mike Walker's teams during the league. He played 44 games, one of the highest numbers in the team and, what's more, created danger in front of goal scoring three times, his best tally for Norwich City.

740.name: Milligan
pages: * Mike Milligan is the man who does the dirty work on the pitch, and is basically a team player, who doesn't mind working hard for the good of the team. His presence is almost essential for Mike Walker who has played him alongside the new signing Peter Grant in the midfield, forming a very intimidating defensively oriented partnership. His place in the team is almost a sure thing for the Canaries.

* A defensively minded midfielder, he is the man who covers the backs of the other midfielders. For this reason he does not often push up. Evidently, he is a good ball-winner, hard and very competitive. His, at times, excessive aggression cause him some problems with the yellow cards. When it comes to distributing the ball he is discrete, almost always doing so over short range.
* League Cup Runner-up with Oldham Athletic in the 89-90 season.

* An under-21, B and full international for Ireland, he makes his debut in the latter category on 29th April 1992 against the United States in Dublin, this being his only game for his country to date.

* Mike Milligan started his sporting career in the lower ranks of Manchester City, but it was Joe Royle's Oldham Athletic who he offered to sign for in February 1985. He makes his league debut on 12th April 1996 against Sheffield United and his first goal comes on 5th May 1986 against Carlisle United.
* In August 1990 he is transferred to Everton for £1 million. His debut for the Toffees is on 25th August 1990 against Leeds United and his only goal with the Merseyside team is on 16th March 1991 against Southampton. 
* After not managing to make an impact with his game, he returns to Oldham Athletic for £600,000, and is an undisputed starter with the Latics.
* After playing nearly 300 league games for Oldham, he is transferred to Norwich City in June 1994 for £850,000. His first game with the Canaries is on 19th September 1994 against Ipswich Town and his first goal comes on 15th october 1994 against Aston Villa.

* A tremendous season for Mike Milligan who was one of the stalwarts of the team during the league. His 37 games show the importance of this player in Mike Walker's schemes and, what's more, he scored a goal to crown a sensational season.

741.name: Polston
pages: * John Polston has been a classic figure in the centre of the Norwich City defence in recent years, contributing his enormous firmness and elegance to Mike Walker's team. Without him, the Canaries defence lowers its performance although he doesn't miss many games. His injury last year which kept him out for three months was one of the reasons why the team didn't get closer to the promotion places, although of course, it would have been difficult anyway. He is permanent in Mike Walker's teams.

* Polston is an excellent central marker who is hard enough to overcome for the opponent, helped by good positioning he anticipates the strikers well. Magnificent in the air in his own area, he is not a man blessed with a scent for goal in the set-plays in the other area. He moves elegantly, passing well and is comfortable with the ball at his feet although he doesn't usually venture into the rival half, preferring to pass the ball to the midfield. He is fairly quick.
x
* English youth international.

* Originally from the lower ranks of Tottenham Hotspur, a back injury almost forced him to give up football, but once recovered he signs as a professional in July 1985. He makes his league debut for Spurs on 15th November 1986 against Coventry City and scores his first goal for the London club in his best season with them (89-90), appearing thirteen times and scoring his first goal on 10th March 1990 against Charlton Athletic. 
* In July 1990 he is transferred to Norwich City for £300,000, quickly adapting to the team and becoming a key piece in the defensive line. He makes his league debut on 25th September 1990 against Sunderland and scores his first goal on 22nd December 1990 against Everton.

* Last season was one of John Polston's best, where he was an automatic choice for Mike Walker during the league. His absence was felt when an injury kept him out of the Canaries team for three months although he quickly regained his place. In total, he played 31 games and scored 2 goals, the first time he found the back of the net in 3 seasons.

742.name: Van Heusden
pages: * Arjan Van Heusden is, at the moment, the club's second choice goalkeeper behind  Musselwhite. At present his prospects don't look too bright given that the Englishman seems to be well settled in as the club's number one choice in goal. However his tremendous pre-season performances last year gave him an opportunity which he was unable to take. Worthy of note is the fact that he has been given the chance to carry on at Port Vale this season, to try to continue his interesting progress. A keeper who has a promising future ahead of him, he will no doubt be out this season to turn the situation around and make himself a regular in the side.

* The gigantic Port Vale keeper makes the most of his height when he goes up to catch high balls into the box. He shows great confidence in everything he does, which, together with his natural ability makes him a very complete goalkeeper.
x
x
* Van Heusden was signed from Port Vale in August 1994 for £4,500 from Dutch side Noordwijk.

* After having a superb pre-season, Van Heusden made himself Port Vale's number one choice in goal at the start of the season. Unfortunately a disastrous run of results saw Musselwhite win back his place which he managed to keep until the end of the season. He eventually played in a total of 13 games.

743.name: Musselwhite
pages: * Without any doubt, when John Rudge thinks about who is going to play in goal for Port Vale, then the name of Paul Musselwhite appears on the teamsheet almost automatically. He is a regular in goal for the side and is a player who shows great character out on the park. However the Englishman will have to be careful to make sure that Dutch signing Arjan Van Heusden doesn't take his place off him, this season as he did at the beginning of the previous campaign. In normal circumstances, he will be the Valiants' regular keeper.

* Musselwhite is, above all, a keeper who is very safe on high balls and one who shows good positional sense in his goal area. One of his greatest strengths is his ability to keep his cool when he is faced with opposoing forwards in one on one situations, holding them up superbly well trying to make them lose their nerve, something he frequently achieves.
x
x

* A player who came through the youth ranks at Portsmouth, he signed professional terms in December 1986. Neverthless, he didn't get the chance to make his first team debut for the club. 
* In March 1988 he was transfered to Scunthorpe United, making his league debut on 27th August 1989, against Hereford United. 
* In July 1992 he was signed by Port Vale in exchange for £20,000. He made his debut on 12th August 1992 against Exeter City.

* Musselwhite began the season as second choice behind Van Heusden, when it came to deciding who would take charge of Port Vale's goal. Taking advantage of a poor run of results, the Dutch keeper was dropped, with Musselwhite winning back his place as the side's number one goalkeeper. From that moment on he made the position his own, and went on to make a total of 33 appearances.

744.name: Snijders
pages: * Mark Snijders is one of John Rudge's big signings for this season. A versatile player, his signing for the club wasn't a straightforward one but, fortunately, everything was eventually sorted out. His performances during the pre-season have made him an automatic choice for the manager, who has lined him up in the midfield. Time will tell if he adpats to English football quickly enough to be able to hang on to his place in the side, although for the moment, at least, he has proved to be irreplaceable for John Rudge.

* Snijders is a good all round footballer who can do a good job in a number of different positions. His normal position is at the back either in the centre of the defence or at right back. However he can also do a job on the right hand side of the midfield. He has good pace and, thanks to his height, is dominant in the air, while he is also technically sound.
x
x
* Port Vale signed Mark Snijders in the summer of 1997.
x

745.name: Carragher
pages: * Matthew Carragher was one of Port Vale's pre-season signings. An attacking right back, he had a disappointing time at Wigan Athletic last season, unable to reproduce the sensational form he had shown in previous seasons. He became the youngest player  in the history of the club to play in a total of 100 League game, as result, despite still being a young player, he is certainly not lacking in experience. However the competition for a place in the side that exists at Port Vale, is very stiff, and the jump up of two Divisions that Carragher has made in joining the club could be decisive in limiting the opportunities he gets to show what he can do.

* A young right back, he stands out for his attacking approach to the game. A tight marker, he is constantly moving forward in support of the attack. Despite still being young, he has plenty of experience behind him, something which sees him making fewer errors than might be expected in a player of his age. His weakness is the defensive side of his game, occasionally neglecting his duties at the back when he moves forward, an aspect of his  game he needs to try to improve.
* Third Division Championship winners medal with Wigan Athletic in the 96-97 season.
x

* After coming through the youth ranks at Wigan Athletic, Carragher signed as a professional on 25th November 1993. His first game for the club came on 2nd October 1993 against Chester City.
* He signed for Port Vale during the summer of 1997.

* Carragher had a disappointing campaign compared to previous seasons when he was an important member of the  side for Wigan Athletic. His 18 appearances meant he was deservedly awarded a medal for the clubs achievement in clinching theThird Division championship last time out.

746.name: Stokes
pages: * A player who hasn't enjoyed too many opportunities at Port Vale, Dean Stokes has nevertheless shown that he is a player who the club can count on whenever the team is hit by injuries. A regular member of Port Vale's  reserve team, he managed to force his way into the first team, in place of Tankard, for a few games last season. In normal circumstances Stokes won't be a player who finds himself in the starting line up, except when injuries allow, although he will make appearances as a substitute.

* A basically defensive left back, Stokes is a player who covers well across the back, while he is also a powerful tackler. However he lacks the technical ability of Tankard that would allow him to get forward more effectively in support of the Port Vale attack.
x
x
* After coming through the ranks at Halesowen Town, he made his league debut on 18th December 1993, against Burnley.

* Stokes saw himself limited to just 10 league apperances throughout the whole season, 9 of those as a member of the starting line up. Unfortunately an injury in a game against Sheffield United in March allowed Tankard to come in and win back his plade, which he held onto until the end of the season.

747.name: Griffiths
pages: * Gareth Griffiths has been a regular member of John Rudge's line up since his arrival at Port Vale from Welsh club Rhyl, and has responded to the confidence shown in him by doing a fine job at the heart of the Valiants' defence. He was also a regular in the side last season, although his run of apperances was brought to an end by a knee injury. As a result of that injury, he was forced to undergo surgery in order to sort out the problem for good. At present, although he has managed to get over his knee problem, he is not currently in the side, although he  will be fighting every inch of the way in order to get back the place in the side which he had made his own personal property in recent seasons.

* Although Griffiths is excellent in the air, he still doesn't take full advantage of his considerable height, Not a particularly strong player, he  needs to  learn to develop the physical side of his game, using his arms to knock opponents off balance. Proof of that was the goal conceded against Leeds United in an aerial dual with Gary McAllister. He is not too comfortable with the ball at his feet though this is more due to a lack of confidence than a lack of ability.
x
x

* He was signed from amateur club Rhyl in February 1993 for £1,000 and was given the opportunity to make his debut in the league on 12th February 1994 against Stockport County. His first goal came on 12th April 1994 against Rotherham United.

* Griffiths had an up and down time last season. He did a good job up until the month of January, and was a regular in John Rudge's side. Unfortunately an injury kept him out for almost the whole of the remainder of the season, managing to come back into the side only for the final league game of the season against Crystal Palace. He eventually made a total of 26 appearances.

748.name: Glover
pages: * An elegant central defender, Dean Glover possesses the ability to play the ball around which is lacking in many defenders. He is also a very experienced player who has plenty of tricks up his sleeve when he comes up against opposition forwards. Last season proved to be another fine one in a long and successful career which has now reached the 500 league appearances mark. However, so far this season Glover hasn't made himself a regular member of John Rudge's side although he certainly possesses the ability to win back his place in the Valiants' starting line up.

* Glover is Port Vale's best footballing central defender, capable of bringing the ball out of defence into the midfield area, although he seldom moves forward towards the opposition penalty area except for dead ball situations, such as corners and free kicks. He is not a quick player but he shows tremendous positional play out on the pitch, which is a great help to him when he comes up against fast strikers.
x
x

* After coming through the youth ranks at Aston Villa, Dean Glover signed as a professional in December 1981. He made his league debut on 19th January 1985 against Coventry City.
* He was loaned out to Sheffield United in October 1986, making his debut for the Blades on 18th October 1986, against Huddersfield Town. 
* In June 1987 he was transfered to Middlesbrough for £25,000. He played his first game for the club on 15th August 1987 against Millwall and scored his first goal  in the league on 4th November 1987 against Manchester City. During that season he was used as a right back while in the following campaign he played as a striker. .
* Port Vale signed him for £200,000 in February 1989. He made his debut on 4th February 1989 against Blackpool, while he scored his first goal for the club on 19th August against Bradford City.

* Last season proved to be an excellent one for Dean Glover. He missed the first four league games of the season,but then went on to play right through to the end of the season, making himself an automatic first choice, bringing tremendous security to the Valiants' defence. He found the back of the net twice during the course of his 42 games. He had one of his best seasons, in an attacking sense, not only for his goals but also for the danger he caused.

749.name: Aspin
pages: * Beginning his ninth season at the club, Neil Aspin is a permanent fixture at the heart of the Port Vale defence. He is a strong, courageous central defender who always gives 100% out on the park. His absences are very few and far between, but when he is not in the side, his presence at the back is sorely missed by the Valiants. However, under normal circumstances, Aspin will continue to captain the side and will no doubt remain an automatic choice for John Rudge.

* The veteran Port Vale man can play either as a central defender, or as a full back, although it is at the heart of the defence where he is most comfortable. He is not a particularly quick player, something he tries to make up for by taking advantage of his powerful physique to impose himself on opposing strikers, anticipating their intentions or going in hard to win the ball. Though not outstanding in the air, he does a competent job.
x
x

* After coming through the youth ranks at Leeds United, he signed as a professional in October 1982. He made his debut for the Elland Road club at just 16 years of age on 20th February 1982 against Ipswich Town. His first goal as a professional came on 17th March 1984, against Grimsby Town. 
* He was transfered to Port Vale in July 1989 for £200,000. He made his debut on 19th August 1989, against Bradford City. He scored his first goal for Port Vale on 19th January 1991, against Portsmouth.

* As seems to be the case every year with Neil Aspin, he had a sensational campaign last  season, becoming the team's leader out on the park. His abscences were significant in that the team clearly missed his leadership and presence in the defence, although  fortunately he wasn't absent on too many occasions. In his eighth season atthe club, Aspin played in a total of 33 games.

750.name: Tankard
pages: * Allen Tankard is Port Vale's regular left back, a player who poses a real threat, in and around the opposition penalty area with his shots and crosses. If  that wasn't enough, he is also a genuine free kick specialist, taking full advantage of his fine left foot. In this new season, Tankard will be out to hold on to his place, in the face of the challenge presented by club colleague Dean Stokes, who only manages to get into the side when Tankard is injured, but who will also be hoping that this season proves to be his big opportunity.

* Tankard is a full back who also poses a threat when he moves forward in support of the attack,  normally helping out left winger, Steve Guppy. He stands out for his crossing, which he puts over with real quality usually to far post. He seldom uses his right foot which is much weaker than his left. When he moves forward with the ball, down the flank, and is unable to pick out a pass or opportunity to cross the ball, he will let a powerful shot go from distance.
x
* He has represented England at youth international.

* After coming through the youth ranks at Southampton, he signed as a professional in May 1987. He made his league debut on 26th April 1986 against  Sheffield Wednesday.
* In July 1988 he was transfered to Wigan Athletic. He made his debut on 27th August 1988 against Bristol Rovers, while his first league goal proved to be the winner, against Bristol City, on 29th April 1989. 
* He was transfered to Port Vale in July 1993 for £87,500, making his debut on 14th August 1993 against Burnley. He scored his first goal for Port Vale on 15th January 1995 against Tranmere Rovers.

* Tankard was once again an automatic first choice at left back for Port Vale, missing  just a handful of games throughout the whole of the season. His contribution was well appreciated by the rest of the side, as he continued to put in tremendous peformances. He played in a total of 39 games, and scored once, his fourth goal in the years he has been at the club.

751.name: Hill
pages: * Andy Hill brings great experience and know how to the Port Vale side, qualities which the club will no doubt need as they could well face themselves with a battle to stay in the First Division. Last time out he barely misses a game except for a a small injury and a suspension. He proved to be a real pillar at the back for a team which was eventually on the verge of reaching the play-offs. Whether as a central  defender or at right back, his contribution will be fundamental for the Valiants, despite now being very much a veteran who has now played in a total of 500 games during the course of his career.

* Hill is a player of great experience and one who very seldom leaves his defensive position to move forward in support of the attack. Though not a quick player, his positional sense is almost perfect, making him a very difficult man to catch either off guard or not following the way the play is unfolding. Nevertheless when he is faced with a quick winger he can have problems, not being blessed himself with tremendous pace. He can also play at the heart of the defence when Port Vale are struck by injury problems.
x
* An England youth international.

* A product of Manchester United's youth system, he signed professional in January 1983. However he wasn't given the opportunity to make his debut for the Red Devils.
* In July 1984 he was transfered to Bury. He played his first game for the club on 25th August 1984 against Darlington, and hit his first goal as a professional on 6th October 1984 against Southend United.
* He was loaned out to Manchester City in December 1990, although his loan spell became a permanent move when he was transfered to the Maine Road club two months later for £200,000. He made his league debut on 5th March 1991 against QPR, while his first goal for City came on 10th Spril 1991 against Leeds United.
* Port Vale signed him for £150,000 making his debut on 27th August 1995 against Stoke City.

* Hill made the right back spot his own during the course of last season, missing very few games. His solid campaign was one of the reasons why Port Vale were on the verge of winning a  place in the play-offs. In total, he played in 39 games, managing to score once.

754.name: Jansson
pages: * Jan Jansson is a player who in his day was an international player for Sweden and who now finds himself at Port Vale as one of the club's signing for the current season. His career has been plagued by injury, which has prevented him from being more successful for the Swedish national side. He was, in fact, on his way back from another injury which had kept him out of action for quite some time when he went out on loan to Port Vale. The good form he showed convinced John Rudge to try to sign him on permanently during the summer, something which the Port Vale manager finally achieved. Though he is not currently a regular member of the starting line up, he will no doubt get his chance as the season progresses.

* Jansson is a midfielder who possesses the ability to go on to become the man who directs operations from the centre of the park. He is a good passer of the ball, helping to relieve pressure in the midfield, while he has enough imagination to play his football in even the tightest of midfields. He makes good forward runs into the box, although he is not a regular goalscorer, though he lays on plenty of good chances for his teammates.
x
* Jansson has represented Sweden at Under-21 level and also as a full international on 7 occasions.

* Jansson went out on loan to Port Vale on 4th November 1996 from Swedish club Norrkoping. His first game for the club came on 9th November against WBA, while he scored his first goal in English football on 29th January 1997 against QPR.
* During the summer of 1997, Norrkoping and Port Vale struck a deal for a permanent  move, with the player being valued at £150,000.

* Jansson contributed to Port Vale's season while on loan at the club from Swedish outfit Norrkoping. He showed some good form, and, when he was in the side, showed his ability to organise even the most congested of midfields. In total he played in 11 games, and managed to score once.

756.name: Corden
pages:
* Wayne Corden is a young player who has come through the youth ranks at  Port Vale who hasn't had an easy time trying to force his way into John Rudge's side, due to the presence in previous seasons of players like Guppy and McCarthy, who were blocking his way into the Valiants' first team. 
* Fortunately, opportunities finally came his way last season when Guppy was transfered to  Leicester City. He broke through into the first team, and went on to show some outstanding form. Manager John Rudge saw enough to convince himself to give Corden a 3 year extension to his contract. As a result, Corden's confidence is obviously sky high, even  more so, taking into account the fact that this season he has been a regular member of the starting line up. Nevertheless, he will have to work hard to make sure that all of this success doesn't go to his head, and that he remains in the Port Vale side.

* Wayne Corden is a player who operates down the left hand side of the field as a left winger, despite being a basically right footed player. He is at his best when he cuts inside to get into the penalty area, posing a real threat to the opposition, backed up by his speed and his stronger right foot. He has also played a number of games playing behind the two main strikers, a position from where he can make the most of his direct style of play.
x
x
* After coming through the youth ranks at Port Vale, Wayne Corden signed as a professional  on 20th September 1994. His first game for the club came on 7th May 1995 against Notts County.

* Corden played in 12 games during the course of last season, managing to increase his number of appearances following the departure of Steve Guppy toLeicester City. His form proved to be good enough for the club to offer him a new 3 year contract.

757.name: Porter
pages: * Andy Porter is a player who does a lot of the work which the supporters never see, and which is seldom given the credit it deserves;  the crucial job of winning possession in the middle of the park. As well as standing out for his defensive work, the English midfielder also contributes to Port Vale's cause with goals, although he is not an outstanding goalscorer. This time around Porter will be out to put together as fruitful a campaign as he did last season, and will undoubtedly be a key man for his manager John Rudge. His importance for Port Vale over the years has been such that he has now managed to put together a total of 350 games for the club during the course of his career, something which clearly illustrates the tremendous job he has done. Obviously, he is an automatic choice for theValiants.

* A midfielder of great strength, he is the man who does much of the spade work in Port Vale's midfield engine room. He is an excellent ball winner, and stands out for the constant support he gives to the defence. He is a player who goes in hard for the ball, is an untiring worker and occasionally gets forward into the attack, although he seldom finds the back of the net.
x
x

* He came through the ranks at Port Vale, signing professional terms in June 1987. He made his league debut on 28th February 1987 against Blackpool, while he scored his first goal for the club in the league on 6th May 1989 against Southend United.

*  Andy Porter had another fantastic season to add to the ones he had previously put together for Port Vale. He played in 44 out of a possible 46 games and had an immense influence in midfield, thanks to the strength and fighting spirit he showed out on the park. He also managed to find the back of the net on four occasions.

758.name: Talbot
pages: * Stuart Talbot is a young player who does a tremendous ball-winning job in midfield for Port Vale. Nevertheless that is not all he gives the team, showing himself to be well capable of playing a good short passing game. This time out he will be looking to make more starting appearances and not be spending too much time on the substitutes bench, hopefully going on to put together a season which proves to be at least as fruitful as the previous campaign, in which he made a total of 30 appearances. He has seen his performances last season rewarded by being included by John Rudge as a regular member of the starting line up.

* A strong midfielder, Talbot possesses a fine right foot with which he sprays around long accurate passes although he is a player who is not uncomfortable when he is asked to knock the ball about in a possession based game, a job he does efficiently. He can also play at left back where he gives a good account of himself, although he is not helped by his relative lack of speed.
x
x
* Talbot signed for Port Vale from amateur club Moor Green, and made his debut on 29th April 1995 against Charlton Athletic.

* Talbot enjoyed his best season at Port Vale since his arrival at the club. Last season had two very different sides to it for Stuart Talbot; home games and away games. At Vale Park, Port Vale's home ground, he made his main contribution as a substitute coming off the bench and providing more steel in midfield. Away from home it was a different story, with the team playing with just one striker, he played more of an attacking role, which was well appreciated by the rest of the side, as he managed to chip in with 4 goals. He went on to make a total of 30 appearances during the course of the season.

759.name: Ainsworth
pages: * This September Gareth Ainsworth became the most expensive signing in Port Vale's history. He was signed just moments after Jon McCarthy joined the club from Birmingham City. A right winger with an eye for goal, he could well become the bargain of the season for the Valiants, who managed to get in before a number of other clubs to sign Ainsworth who has signed a four year contract. An automatic choice for John Rudge, time will tell how much he notices the change in division, although he certainly possesses enough ability to go on to be a success for the Valiants.

* Ainsworth is a right winger who is constantly involved in the side's attacks. Quick, with a good eye for a goalscoring chance, a quality which, on more than one occasion, has seen his manager line him up as a centre forward, although it is not his normal or natural position.

*  Lincoln City's top scorer during the 96-97 season. 
* Chosen for the Third Division's ideal side 96-97.
x

* Ainsworth signed for Preston North End on 21st January 1992 from Northwich Victoria, after having previously had a spell in the youth team set up at Blackburn Rovers. His first game for Preston came on 11th January against Shrewsbury Town.
* He became a free agent and moved on to Cambridge United, where he signed on 17th August 1992. He made his debut on 17th October against Bristol City, and managed to score his side's second goal of that particular game. 
* Once again a free agent he returned to Preston North End on 23rd December 1992. He played his first game of his second spell at the club on 28th December against Exeter City. His first goals came on 21st August 1994, finding the back of the net twice against Scarborough. 
* Lincoln City signed him after paying out £25,000 on 31st October 1995. His debut came one day later against Mansfield Town while he opened his goalscoring account for the club on 18th November, scoring twice against Torquay United.
* Port Vale signed him in September 1997 for £500,000.

* Ainsworth had undoubtedly his best season as a professional, ending the campaign as Lincoln City's top scorer with 22 strikes. His involvement in the game was always a sign of danger and he was his sides best player through the season. He made a total of 44 appearances.

760.name: Bogie
pages: * The man around whom Port Vale's game revolves, Ian Bogie is one of the pillars of the side and is a genuine leader out on the park. Although his contribution to the side is basically as a attacking player, he is not one who finds the back of the net with any real regularity, prefering to allow others to take on the responsibility of putting the ball in  the back of the net. The great season he had last time out saw him renewing his contract for another 3 years, which will keep him at club until the year 2000. Although at the moment he finds himself on the substitutes bench, he will no doubt go on to make another important contribution for Port Vale this season.

* Ian Bogie is the playmaker at Port Vale, the man who pulls the strings in midfield. He possess superb control, carrying the ball forward apparently tied to his feet. He likes to play a short passing game, laying the ball off to his best placed teammates and is always available to help out colleagues when they are under pressure. He has excellent vision although he seldom  plays long passes, while he is a very difficult player to dispossess.
x
* Bogie has played for England as a schoolboy international.

* After coming through the youth ranks at Newcastle United, Bogie signed professional in December 1985. He made his league debut on 30th August 1986 against Luton Town, with both Paul Gascoigne and Peter Beardsley as teammates.  
* In February 1989 he was transferred to Preston North End for £100,000 plus Gary Brazil who moved to Newcastle United. He played his first game for the club on 11th February against Bristol Rovers, while his first goal came on 4th April 1989 against  Aldershot.
* Millwall signed him for £145,000 in August 1991. He made his debut for the London club on 17rh August 1991 against Middlesbrough.
* In October 1993 he was loaned out to Leyton Orient although his move later became a permanent one in December of that same year. He made his debut on 16th October 1993 against Reading, scoring his first goal for the club on 12th February 1994 against Bradford City.
* He was transfered to Port Vale in March 1995 for £50,000, making his debut on 28th March 1995 against Burnley. He scored his first goal for Port Vale against Millwall on 5th April 1995.

* Ian Bogie had an excellent season and was one of the main reasons why the Valiants were able to climb the table, almost to the point of getting into the play-offs for promotion to the Premier League. His teammates were able to take full advantage of his creative midfield play. He was rewarded with 31 first team appearances and 1 more goal to add to his career statistics with Port Vale.

761.name: Foyle
pages: * A very popular player with the Valiants' supporters, Martin Foyle is a very complete striker who provides the side with plenty of goals. In fact Foyle is widely regarded as one of the best goalscorers in the lower divisions in England. However last season he was almost exclusively limited to a substitute's role coming off the bench as a sort of secret weapon. This season he is fighting with Naylor and Mills to tie down one of the two striking places in the side, although occasionally John Rudge has lined up all three together.

* A very complete centre forward, despite not being very tall he is good in the air. He strikes a ball well with either foot, preferably with the right, and is a good header of the ball, getting the better of defenders thanks to his speed and positioning. He has the rare quality of apparently always being in the right place at the right time to get in efforts on goal, almost always on target. He has good control and sets himself up well when he gets hold of the ball inside the penalty area. Given his ability to get away from his markers he is a very dangerous player on the counter attack. He has a good touch on the ball and lays the ball off well to his teammates when they move forward in support of the attack.

* Oxford United's top goalscorer, in 1988-89. 
* Port Vale's top scorer, 91-92, 93-94 and 94-95.
x

* After coming through the youth ranks at Southampton, Foyle signed professional terms in August 1980. He made his league debut on 15th January 1983 against Coventry City, scoring his first goal for the club on 9th April 1983 against Manchester United.
* Martin Foyle was transfered to Aldershot in July 1984 for £25,000, opening his account for the club on his debut on 25th August 1984 against Chesterfield.
* Oxford United signed him in March 1987 for £140,000, covering the departure of John Aldridge to  Liverpool. He made his league debut on 28th March 1987 against Sheffield Wednesday, against whom he also managed to score his first goal for the club.
* He was transfered to Port Vale in June 1991 for £375,000, and managed to find the  back of the net twice on his league debut on 27th August 1991 against his ex-club, Oxford United.
* Foyle was voted Port Vale's Player of the Year, for 94-95, by the club's supporters.

* In terms of goalscoring Foyle had one of his poorest seasons since his arrival at Port Vale. Nevertheless, there is an explanation, since he made 30 of his appearances in the side as a substitute, depriving him of the action he would have needed to maintain his normal goalscoring record. In total he made 37 appearances, finding the back of the net 3 times.

762.name: Naylor
pages: * Since his arrival at Port Vale from Crewe Alexandra, Tony Naylor has become one of the side's figureheads, making the centre forward position his own and being a man who has the full backing of manager John Rudge, for whom he is one of the first names down on the teamsheet. His reputation amongst theValiants' supporters was reaffirmed when he managed to end the season as the club's top scorer. He will once again have an important role to play if Port Vale are to have a good season this time around, and avoid getting caught up in a relegation battle.

* A very quick centre forward, Naylor continuously causes plenty of problems for opposing defenders with his pace and mobility. He is constantly pulling out wide to the flanks, opening up gaps for the midfield players to come through into. The space he creates can also be taken advantage of by his striking partner Martin Foyle, with whom he has developed a tremendous understanding. Inside the area he doesn't think twice about having a go at goal whenever he gets the opportunity.

* Crewe Alexandra's top scorer in seasons 91-92 and 92-93.
* Top scorer at Port Vale in seasons  95-96 and 96-97.
x

* Naylor signed as a professonal in March 1990, moving to Crewe Alexandra from amateur club Droylsden. He made his league debut on 28th April 1990 against Mansfield Town while he scored his first goal as a professional on 21st September 1990 against Tranmere Rovers.
* He was transfered to Port Vale for £150,000 in July 1994. He managed to score on his debut on 20th August 1994 against Oldham Athletic.

* In terms of goalscoring, the Port Vale striker enjoyed his most prolific season since turning  professional, completely the opposite to teammate Martin Foyle who managed to hit the target just three times. Naylor scored 17 goals which made him the club's top scorer and almost took the Valiants into the play offs for promotion to the Premier League.

763.name: Mills
pages: * Lee Mills is very much an example of what is known as a classical centre forward, tall and powerful in the air, though not particularly good technically speaking. Nevertheless this doesn't prevent him from demonstrating tremendous enthusiasm out on the pitch and contributing with a good goals return each season. These qualities will once again see him doing an important job for Port Vale, either coming on as a substitute or playing from the start, alternating between the two as he has done in recent seasons. At present he is battling with Foyle and Naylor for a place in the starting line up, although in a few games the three of them have all played together.

* Mills is a centre forward of great strength and power, with his main weapon being his power in the air, an area of the game in which he often proves to be dominant. He has a good shot from distance, either from free kicks or in open play. He is constantly moving around the attacking third of the field, and is a difficult opponent to contain, not for his skill but for his enormous power.
x
x

* Signed from amateur club  Stocksbridge, he began his professional career at Wolverhampton Wanderers. He made his debut in the league on 7th September 1993 against Watford, and scored his first goal as a professional on 2nd April 1994 against Tranmere Rovers.
* In February 1995 he went out on loan to Derby County, a loan spell which became a permanent move in March 1995, for the sum of £400,000. He scored his first goal for the Rams on his debut against Bolton Wanderers on 26th February 1995.
* Port Vale signed him for £200,000 pounds in August 1995. He played his first game for the club on 13th August 1995 against Derby County, while he scored his first goal for his new club on 2nd September 1995 against Norwich City.

* Mills managed to reach double figures in the goal stakes last time out for Port Vale ending the season with 13 goals to his credit despite not being John Rudge's first choice striker. He hit his best form in March when he managed to strike 7 goals in 6 games, which eventually made him John Rudge's number one striker in away games, even nudging ahead of Naylor as  Port Vale played with just one man up front in their matches away from Vale Park. In short, it was a magnificent season for Mills.

766.name: Thomson
pages: * Andy Thomson is one of the central defenders upon whom Terry Fenwick will be depending this season at Portsmouth. In the two years that he has been at the club he has been a regular member of the side and has more than demonstrated to the manager that he is a player who is well worth his place in the Pompey back line. His good performances  last season have seen him stake a powerful claim for a place in the side, although, at the  moment, he is not an automatic first team choice.

* Thomson is a player who operates at the heart of the defence bringing to the side, consistency and security. His height allows him to dominate in the air, something which he takes good advantage of when he moves forward to get on the end of corners and free kicks around the edge of the opposing penalty area. A hard player when he goes in for the ball, he is also  an aggresive, tight marker. He likes to play the ball long up to the forwards, something he does quite thoughtfully. Though not particularly comfortable with the ball at his feet, he keeps things simple. Never trying to attempt to do something he is not accustomed to doing.
x
x

* After coming through the youth ranks at Swindon Town, Thomson signed as a professional on 1st May 1993. His debut came on 7th May against Leeds United.
* He was transfered to Portsmouth on 29th December 1995 for 75,000 pounds. He played his first game for Pompey on 27th January 1996 against Millwall. He scored his first goal as a professional against Crystal Palace on 17th January  1997.

* Thomson didn't begin the season as a first choice at the heart of the defence, but, following an injury to Russell, he was given an opporunity to stake his claim for a place in Terry Fenwick's side. From that moment on, he made a tremenodus contribution, playing in 28 games, scoring once, his first goal for Pompey. The goal he scored was asignificant one for more reasons than the three points it clinched  for Portsmouth. It gave Portsmouth their first victory over Crystal Palace at the Eagles' Selhurst Park home, for more than 30 years.

767.name: Whitbread
pages:
* Adrian Whitbread is a player who became a victim of the tremendous competition that exits for a place at the heart of  West Ham United's defence. As a consequence  he spent most of last season out on loan at Portsmouth a move which was finally  made permanent at the beginning of the current season. 
* He arrived at Upton Park with the reputation of being a very dominant player in the air although time has demonstrated that he hadn't improved enough to force his way into the side ahead of Bilic and Rieper, who played together at the heart of the East London club's defence. Fortunately for Whitbread, Portsmouth took an interest in him and finally signed him. He has had more opportunities with Terry Fenwick's side, and has managed to convince the ex-England international to have the faith in his ability to give hima place as a first choice at the heart of Portsmouth's defence.

* Whitbread is a central defender who stands out for his ability in the air , something which also makes hima very dangerous player when he moves forward for dead ball situations. He keeps things simple when he is put under pressure by opponents, playing the ball long without thinking twice about it. This side of his game is a direct result of the fact that he is far from comfortable with the ball at his feet, and prefers to play the ball on to a teammate,rather than keeping hold of it himself for too long. He is a good, hard, tight marker, who constantly attempts to impose his physical presence upon his opponents. He is quite a quick player, is very disciplined in his part of the pitch, and possesses good positional sense.
x
x

* After coming through the ranks at Leyton Orient, Whitbread signed as a professional in November 1989. He made his debut in the league on 3rd December 1984 against Brentford, while he opened his goalscoring account on 11th February against  Wigan Athletic.
* He was transfered to  Swindon Town in July 1993 for 500,000 pounds. He made his league debut on 14th August 1993 against Sheffield United, and scored his first goal for the club  on 22nd January 1994 against Tottenham Hotspur, a goal that clinched victory for the Robins.
* West Ham United signed him in exchange for 650,000 pounds.  He made his first appearance for the Hammers on 20th August 1994 against Leeds United. 
* He was loaned out to Portsmouth in November 1995 for three months. His first goal for Pompey came on 11th November 1995 against  Huddersfield Town. 
* Portsmouth signed him on a permanent basis in October 1996 for 250,000 pounds.

* Whitbread eventually became a Portsmouth player in October, after the club finally agreed a deal for a permanent move. Without a place in the side at  West Ham United, the player moved on and formed part of an excellent defensive line up at Pompey, and was a key man in the club's tremendous season. He finally made a total of 24 appearances.

768.name: Perrett
pages: * Russell Perrett is a central defender who is currently in his second spell at Portsmouth, hoping that this time he will be able to take advantage of any opportunity he gets to show what he can do. Proving to be much more of a succes than he was during his first spell at the club, Perrett has made himself a regular member of Terry Fenwick's starting line up. The turning point was, undoubtedly, Guy Butters' transfer to Gillingham, which opened upthe door to the first team for both Perrett and Whitbread, giving them the chance to step into the gap his departure left. At present Perrett forms the central defensive duo together with Whitbread at the heart of the Pompey defence.

* A central defender of great physical strength, he is a player who is dominant in the  air, and is always dangerous at dead ball situations, moving forward to help out the attack whenever he gets the opportunity to do so. A hard tackler when he goes in to win the ball, he always tries to impose his superior physical power on rival forwards. Technically acceptable, he is a good passer of the ball and is safe in possession, although he prefers  to keep things as simple as possible and not keep hold of the ball for too long. He can also  do a job as an emergency right back, although when he does play in that position he only rarely moves forward, prefering to remain back in  defensive positions.
x
x
* Perrett was signed by Portsmouth from AFC Lymington in September 1995. He made his debut on 4th November 1995 against Sheffield United.

* Perrett was one of the players who benefitted most from Butters' departure in October.  He didn't fail to take advantage of his opportunity, and formed a solid partership with Awford throughout the season, bringing tremendous security to the Portsmouth defence. In total he played in 32 games, scoring once.

769.name: Awford
pages:
* Andy Awford is a young central defender who has been dogged by injury problems in recent seasons and whose progress, as a consequence, has been hampered. After  suffering a broken leg, he came back last season only to suffer another injury whichkept him out of action for a long spell. 
* However, it seemed that things started to get better for him last season, when he took over the captaincy of the side following an injury to Martin Allen. He showed some excellent form and became one of Pompey's most outstanding performers. This season however things have turned a little sour again, and he can now only watch from the bench as Whitbread and Perret make the central defensive positions their own.

* Awford is a left footed dentral defender who plays on the left hand side of the heart of the defence although he can also do a job as an emergency left back. A very intelligent player he also reads the game well, managing to anticipate his opponents' intentions. He also possesses the ability to bring the ball out from the back, always choosing his moment well. A hard player when he goes into tackles, he has a great capacity to win the ball without  commiting fouls. He is quite a quick player and is excellent in the air, although he is not a particularly dangerous player when he moves forward for set pieces.
x

* Awford has been an England schoolboy and youth international, and has made 9  appearances for the Under-21 side, making his debut on 8th September 1992 against Spain, England winning 1-0, with a goal from Darren Anderton. In the the England side that day were Ian Walker, Ugo Ehiogu, Steve Watson and Chris Sutton.

* After coming through the youth ranks at amateur club Worcester City, Awford completed his contract and then signed for Portsmouth in July 1989. He played his first game for the  club on 15th April 1989, against Crystal Palace.

* Awford became a source of inspiration for his teamamtes from his position at the heart of  the defence, taking over the captaincy of the side in the absence of Martin Allen. He had a magnificent season, playing in 39 league games during the course of the campaign, and helped Pompey to slowly but surely become much tighter as the season went on.

770.name: Pethick
pages:
* During the years that he has been at Portsmouth, Robbie Pethick has become a key man for Pompey, due to his speed and the attacking contribution he makes to the side.
* Last season was yet another example of Pethick's importance to the side, a vital member of the line up due to the tremendous amount of work he puts in all over the park. One of Fenwick's most important men, he is an automatic choice as Portsmouth's right back.

* Pethick is a right back with an attack minded approach to the game, moving forward  down the flank whenever he gets the chance. He puts over good quality crosses, providing good service for the strikers. He shows a good turn of pace, when he is going forward as well as when he is patrolling his area of the pitch or getting back to defend against a fast counterattack. Predominantly right footed, he is a skillful player and has plenty of tricks up his sleeve. He is a good tight marker, while his speed makes him a dificult player for opponents to try to beat for pace. Basically he is a very complete performer, who can also be relied upon to bring the ball out from the back.
x
x

* He joined Portsmouth on October 1993 from amateur club Weymouth, in exchange for £30,000. He made his debut in the league on 2nd October 1993 against Nottingham Forest and scored his first league goal on 28th September 1994 against  WBA.

* Pethick was a constant member of the Portsmouth defence throughout the season, making a tremendous contribution in the 35 games in which he played at right back. He even got an unexpected chance to play in goal, when keeper Flahavan was sent off in the first game of the season. Portsmouth went on to lose 3-1 against Bradford City.

771.name: Russell
pages: * Lee Russell is a player who has come through Portsmouth's youth system and is one who brings a touch of versatility to Terry Fenwick's side. A very consistent performer, he never disappoints anybody and is an important player for his manager. This season, he will be out to improve on the previous campaign which was a far from positive one for him, failing as he did to settle down in the side and make himself a regular. He will no doubt be hoping he can prove that he is more than worth his place for Fenwick and for Pompey.

* Russell is a good all round defender, who can play at left back, his natural position, at right back or even as a central defender. Backed up by a good left foot, he is a good passer of the ball, and is comfortable with the ball at his feet, all of which makes him a player who can be entrusted with the task of building up the side's attacks from the back. Excellent in the  air, he moves forward for dead ball situations, although, in terms of goalscoring, he is not a particularly dangerous player. Physically very strong, he is a hard player who stands out for his tackling ability.
x
x

* After coming through the youth ranks at Portsmouth, Russell signed as a professional in July 1988. He made his league debut on 24th September 1988 against Crystal Palace, and opened his goalscoring account on 13th April 1991 against Hull City.
* He had a spell out on loan at Bournemouth in September 1994, making his first appearance for the club on 16th of that same month against Stockport County.

* It wasn't a particularly great season for Lee Russell for the second consecutive season. He made a total of 20 appearances during the course of the league campaign. He began the season as a member of the starting line up, but around the month of October, a combination of injuries and his teammates' good form limited him to just one more starting appearance throughout the remainder of the season. In short, for Lee Russell, it was a season to forget.

774.name: Hillier
pages:
* Hillier was a product of Arsenal's youth system, who looked to be a real prospect for the future, but who has been unable to maintain the early progress he showed. He has though become a good team player, which is perhaps what he  may well have turned into in any case..
* Nevertheless, his fine ability, above all defensively, hasn't been enough to guarantee him a place at Highbury, and he has seen himself having to move to a club like Portsmouth, where he has become an important member of the side for Terry Fenwick. His excellent first season at the club confirmed to the Pompey coaching staff, that they had got it right when they decided to sing him. He is an automatic choice in Portsmouth's starting line up.

* Hillier is a midfielder who generally plays just in front of the defence, where he does basically a containing job. He brings the ball out well from the back, playing a short passing game, opening the game up by playing the ball out to the flanks, always choosing the right pass at the right moment, hardly ever playing the ball long. Very safe with the ball at his feet, he is not particularly uncomfortable when placed under pressure by opponents. Not very quick, he seldom moves forward in support of the attack, prefering to hold back to help the defence. A good ballwinner, he goes in hard, backed up by his physical strength.

* F.A. Youth Cup winners medal in 1988 with Arsenal. 
* Charity Shield winners medal in 1991 with Arsenal. 
* League Championship winners medal, 1991, with Arsenal. 
* European Cup Winners Cup runners up medal, 1995 with Arsenal.
* Hillier has made one appearance for England as an Under-21 international.

* After coming through the ranks at Arsenal, he signed professional in February 1988. He made his league debut on 29th September 1990, against Leeds United, while he scored his first goal as a professional against Liverpool. 
* Hillier was transfered to Portsmouth in November 1996 in exchange for £250,000. His first appearance for the club against Oldham Athletic on 10th November 1996, wasn't a very fortunate one. He was sent off for stamping on Oldham's Nick Henry. His first goal for Pompey came on 22nd February against WBA.

* In general Hillier had a good season, although he made just 2 appearances for Arsenal. His debut for Pompey couldn't have been worse, being sent off against Oldham Ahtletic. From that moment on, he became a vital part of the side, giving regular demonstrations of his strength and fighting spirit. His end of season statistics with Portsmouth; 21 games played with 2 goals to his name.

775.name: Allen
pages:
* Martin Allen is a veteran midfielder who possesses a tremendous temperament when he is out in the thick of the action, something which makes him a tremendous example for all the young players who make the breakthrough into the Portsmouth first team. Although he is not a player who stands out for his technical ability, he is a man who does a tremendous amount of work for the rest of the team.
* His good performances during his short spell on loan at the club, were enough to convince Terry Fenwick to immediately make his move to the club a permanent one. Though last season was a poor one due to injuries,  Allen is now back to full fitness and will be hoping to force his way back into the side, although for the moment he is not a key part of the manager's plans.

* A powerful midfielder, Allen runs and works throughout the whole ninety minutes, always giving 100%. He is good ballwinner, helped in his job by his hard tackling. He doesn't stand out technically, although he is a dangerous player when he gets into the opposing penalty area, coming from deep positions to surprise defenders. He packs a powerful shot in his right foot, a quality which has seen him strike several spectacular goals.
x

* Allen has played for England as a youth, "B", and, on two occasions, as an Under-21 international. His debut for the Under-21 side came on 9th September 1986 against Sweden. Allen came on in place of Franz Carr. In the England side that day, amongst others, were Tony Adams, Paul Parker and Des Walker.

* After coming through the youth ranks at QPR, he signed professional in May 1983. He made his league debut on 22nd March 1985 against Luton Town, while he hit his first goal on 1st January 1986 against Oxford United.
* In August 1989, he was transfered to West Ham United, for £660,000. His first game for the Hammers on 26th August 1989 against Plymouth Argyle, managing to find the back of the net on his debut.
* He was transfered to Portsmouth in the summer of 1995 in exchange for £500,000. He made his debut on 12th September 1995 against Sunderland, and opened his goalscoring account for the club on 28th October 1995 against Watford. 
* His father, Dennis Allen, played for Charlton Athletic, Reading and  Bournemouth.
* He is a cousin of Paul and Bradley Allen, both still playing professionally, and also of Clive Allen, a much travelled ex-profesional, and now a commentator with Sky Sports.

* Allen had a season which he will no doubt want to forget quickly. A combination of injuries and his teammates' good form limited him to just 4 appearances throughout the whole season. However his presence on the bench added experience to Pompey's squad during their final battle to try to win a place in the play-offs for promotion to the Premier League.

776.name: McLoughlin
pages: * Alan McLoughlin is an automatic choice in midfield for Portsmouth, and is a player, without whom, Portsmouth would no doubt have a real task on their hands in their battle to stay in the First Division. His importance to the side was clearly demonstrated last season when he was Pompey's most outstanding player, and played a large part in ensuring that the club would be enjoying another season in the First Division. However, despite such tributes, at the start of the current season, McLoughlin has not been a regular member of the side, although nobody is in any doubt that that is a situation which will soon be changing.

* McLoughlin is a very dynamic midfielder, physically strong, and a player who wins a great deal of possession. He is Portsmouth's playmaker, due to his excellent technique and short passing game which sees him constantly involved in the game. He supports the attack constantly and has a powerful shot from 20 to 25 yards out. He also makes dangerous forward runs into the box, and is capable of finishing moves off with either foot or with his head, either way getting some fine efforts in on goal.
* He was Portsmouth's top scorer for the 95-96 season, together with Paul Hall.

* He has represented Ireland at "B" and full international level on 23 occasions. He made his full international debut on 2nd June 1990, against Malta.  
* McLoughlin scored the goal that took the Republic of Ireland to the 1994 World Cup Finals in the United States. The goal came on 17th November 1993 against Northern Ireland, with just 14 minutes remaining.

* McLoughlin came through the youth ranks at Manchester United, where he signed professional in April 1985. However, he never got the chance to make his first team debut for the Red Devils. 
* He completed his contract and moved on to Swindon Town in August 1986. His first game for the Robins came on 31st August 1986, against Notts County, while he scored  his first goal for the club on 5th February 1989, against Oxford United.
* He went out on loan to Torquay United in March 1987. He made his league debut for the club on 14th March 1987 against Scunthorpe United and hit his first goal on 20th April 1987, against Exeter City.
* He went back to Torquay United for a second loan spell in August 1987. 
* In December 1990 he was transfered to Southampton for £1 million. He made his debut for the Saints on 15th December 1990 against Aston Villa, and hit his first goal for the club on 30th March 1991 against Manchester City. 
* Portsmouth signed him in February 1992 in exchange for £400,000. He played his first game for Pompey on 22nd February 1992 against Wolverhampton Wanderers and had to wait just one week for his first goal, which came against Tranmere Rovers.

* Once again Alan McLoughlin had another sensational season for Portsmouth. He wasn't as prolific in front of goal as in previous seasons, but his presence in the attack was always felt, and he posed a real threat for opposition defences. In total he played in 36 games scoring 5 times.He managed to crown a fine campaign when he was voted Irish "Player of the Year" ahead of men like Dennis Irwin and Roy Keane.

777.name: Simpson
pages:
* Fitzroy Simpson is an aggresive midfielder, a team player who does a tremendous amount of work for the side, putting the team before himself. He had an uncertain future ahead of him at Manchester City, made even more so by the acquisition of Georgi Kinkladze, who plays in the same position.
* Simpson did what he had to for the sake of  his career and moved on to Portsmouth, where he has managed to force his way into the side and become an important part of Terry Fenwick's plans. This season he will be out to make sure he keeps his place and will be doing everything he can to make sure that Portsmouth are not battling to avoid relegation. However, at the moment, he is not a member of Terry Fenwick's starting line up, making just the occasional appearance.

* Simpson is a powerful midfielder with a good left foot which allows him to pass the ball around accurately. A player with great reserves of stamina, left doing an enormous amount of work for the side, preferably down the hand side. He possesses a powerful shot in his left foot and is a mobile player who covers a tremendous amount of ground. He is not a player who holds back when he is required to put his foot in to win the ball, showing himself to be a hard tackler. Simpson is a player who will never hide, and is also an excellent crosser of the ball.
x
x

* After coming through the youth sides at Swindon Town, Simpson signed professional  in July 1988. He made his debut on 3rd December 1988 against Shrewsbury Town, and scored his first goal as a professional on 7th October 1988 against Hull City.
* He was transfered to Manchester City in March 1992 for £500,000. He made his league debut on 7th March 1992 against QPR, and scored his first league goal for the club on 25th April 1992, against Notts County. 
* He went out on loan to Bristol City, where he made his first appearance on 17th September 1994 against Southend United.
* Portsmouth signed him in August 1995 in a deal which took Simpson and Griffiths, both valued at £400,000, to Pompey, while Kyt Symons moved in the opposite direction, to Manchester City, in exchange for £2,000,000. He played his first game for the club on 19th August 1995 against Grimsby Town. He scored his first goal in Portsmouth's colours on 17th October 1995 against Oldham Athletic, a goal which brought Pompey level.

* Simpson was a key man in Terry Fenwick's side throughout the main part of last season, in which he played in 41 games scoring 4 times. He did most of his work down the right hand side, where he put in a tremendous amount of work, showing some great form.

779.name: Thorp
pages: * Hamilton Thorp is just one of the Australian signings to have arrived at Portsmouth during the summer, together with his compatriots Aloisi and Foster. Physically powerful, Thorp will have to adapt to the pace of the game in England if he wants to be a success with Pompey. However for that to happen he will have to prove himself capable of dislodging some of the regular members of the first team as well as his fellow Australian Aloisi. Nevertheless he has already made a number of appearances for the side and has given glimpses of the ability he possesses.

* Thorp is a centre forward who has a fine goalscoring record in Australian football. His height makes him extremely dangerous in the air, as he has already shown in a couple of games, and is, without any doubt, very much his main asset. A physically powerful man, he also holds up the ball well as he waits for his teammates to come through in support from midfield. He needs to work on the technical side of his game.
x
x
* Portsmouth signed him in the summer of 1997 from Australian club West Adelaide Sharks .
* Thorp had an outstanding season in Australian football, scoring 11 goals in 18 games for his ex-club West Adelaide Sharks.

780.name: Svensson
pages: * An ex-car salesman, Mathias Svensson went on to become one of Terry Fenwick's best value for money signings last season. He formed a fairly prolific partnership with Bradbury towards the end of the season and only injury kept the Swedish player out of the side. This season, following the departure of Bradbury to Manchester City, he will be partnering Portsmouth's new signing, John Aloisi.

* Svensson is a real bustling centre forward, who never takes a rest for even a moment of any game. A quick player, his pace allows him to get into the opposition penalty area from deep lying positions. Dangerous when he comes into the box late, he is also technically good, although his game is based upon the advantage he gets from his physical strength. He has a good eye for a goalscoring chance, and scores a good number of goals each season.
x
x

* Svensson signed for Portsmouth in December 1996 from Swedish club Elfsborg, for £200,000. He couldn't have made a better start to his career in England, scoring twice on his debut against Huddersfield Town on 14th December. Just 3 minutes separated his two strikes.

* Svensson had an excellent first season at Portsmouth, playing in 19 league games, and finding the target on 6 occasions. His form got better as the season went on, and he became an important member of the side for Terry Fenwick, who chose him to partner Bradbury in the Portsmouth attack.

781.name: Aloisi
pages: * John Aloisi has become Terry Fenwick's big signing for the 97-98 season. An Australian international, Aloisi is a player who arrives at the club backed up by the experience of having played in the Italian league with Cremonese. He is a good striker who can guarantee a good goals return each season and is the man charged with the task of replacing Bradbury, who has moved on to Manchester  City, depriving Portsmouth of their top scorer from the previous season. An automatic choice for Fenwick, he will be hoping he can maintain his fantastic start to the season throughout the rest of the campaign, making himself an irreplaceable man up front for Pompey.

* Aloisi is a centre forward of enormous power who makes the most of his  physical advantage to impose himself upon opposition defenders. He is a dominant figure in and around the penalty area, getting in efforts on goal with his head or with either foot. His great strength doesn't hide his good technique, which, though still in need of some refinement, is improving with every game he plays.
* A runners up medal in the 1992-93 European Cup Winner Cup with Amberes, losing to Parma in the final.
* A full international for Australia.

* After having played for Ingel Farm and Adelaide City, he joined Standard Liege's youth set up at just 16 years of age. 
* He left the club one year later to sign for Amberes, where he managed to get regular first team football, and maintain a good goals per game average.  
* He moved on to Italian club Cremonese, leaving the Italian side in the summer of 1997 to join Portsmouth. He scored on his debut for Pompey against Manchester City.
x

782.name: Turner
pages:
* Andy Turner is a young left winger who came through the ranks at Tottenham Hotspur, where he was given very few opportunities to show his undoubted ability. When Tottenham finally decided to sell him, it was Portsmouth who won the  battle to sign him, following Huddersfield Town's failure the previous season to come up with an offer that matched Tottenham's valuation. 
* The young Irish under-21 international will finally get the opporunity to show that the Tottenham coaching staff made a mistake when they allowed him to leave White Hart Lane. He will be out to continue the progress that looks likely to  make him a regular, in the future, for the Republic of Ireland national side. Turner has so far been a regular in the Portsmouth side at the beginning of this season, just as he was throughout the previous campaign.

* Turner is a very quick left winger, skillful with tremendous dribbling ability and able to put tremendous crosses into the box. Though very much a left footed player, he has great technique and plenty of tricks up his sleeve. His crossing ability allows him to put over some fantastic balls into the box from tight situations in which he has very little space to work however he is a strong player who never shirks a physical challenge. If he were a little more selfish in certain positions, he may well get onto the scoresheet more himself. Basically Turner is a creative player who rarely finds the back if the net himself.
x
* Turner has made 7 appearances for the Republic of Ireland at under-21 level.

* Turner came through the the ranks at Tottenham Hotspur to sign professional in April  1992. He made his debut on 15th August 1992 against Southampton, while he struck his first goal as a professional on 5th September 1992 against Everton, a goal which clinched a victory for the Londoners.
* He was loaned out to Wycombe Wanderers in August 1994, making his debut for the club on 27th August 1994 against Bristol Rovers.
* He had another loan spell, this time at Doncaster Rovers in October 1994. His first game for the club came against Scarborough on 15th October 1994, while he opened his account for them on 5th November 1994 against Exeter City.
* Another loan spell was agreed to in November 1995. This time he went to Huddersfield Town, where he played his first game on 2nd December 1995 against Port Vale, and scored his first goal on 16th December 1995 against WBA. 
* Southend United was his next loan destination, March 1996. He made his debut for the club on 30th March 1996 against Tranmere Rovers.
* Finally he was transfered to Portsmouth in September 1996. He played his first game for Pompey on 7th of that same month against Port Vale and scored his first goal in a Portsmouth shirt on 2nd November against WBA.

* Turner had an up and down season last time out. He began the season well, but, after playing in 23 consecutive league games, in 12 of which he was substituted, a loss of form saw him spend the rest of the season on the bench or playing in the reserves. His end of season statistics were: 24 games with two goals to his name.
