783.name: Hall
pages: * One of the first names down on Terry Fenwick's teamsheet at Portsmouth, Paul Hall was one of the main reasons why Pompey finally managed to end last season on a high note, finishing in a position which almost qualified them for a place in the play-offs for promotion to the Premier League. His contribution is likely to be crucial again for the team, while his direct style of play and the danger he creates when he goes forward, seen sure to make him a regular member of the starting line up for Pompey.

* Hall's normal poistion is a right winger although he has played plenty of games as a centre forward, above all during the course of last season. Nevertheless, it is out on the right hand side where he is at his most dangerous, making the most of his speed and ability and proving to be a very difficult player to stop if he is given room to turn and accelerate. A good crosser of the ball, he is also quite complete technically and has great ball control. Despite being basically right footed, he is also excellent on his left, and possesses outstanding vision. He puts over plenty of good crosses for the strikers to turn into goals, and is also a good finisher himself, in and around the penalty area.
* Top goalscorer at Portsmouth during the 95-96 season together with  Alan McLoughlin.
x

* He came through the ranks at Torquay United, signing professional in July 1990. He made his league debut on 14th November 1989, against Gillingham, and scored his first goal as a professional on 26th December 1991, against Fulham.
* He was transfered to Portsmouth in March 1993 in exchange for £100,000. He played his first game for Pompey on 17th August 1993 against Charlton Athletic, and just four days later, opened his goalscoring account for the club against  Luton Town, with a goal that clinched victory for Portsmouth.

* Paul Hall had his best season yet for Portsmouth, playing tucked in behind the two main strikers and creating plenty of danger for Terry Fenwick's side. He was the club's second top scorer, with 13, and was an automatic choice throughout the campaign, making 42 appearances.

784.name: Carter
pages:
* During his time at Portsmouth Jimmy Carter has managed to regain the form he showed while he was at Millwall, and which won him a move to Liverpool in  1991. Since then, the player who was one of Kenny Dalglish's last signings at Anfield before he left, failed to justify the money that had been spent to take him to the Mreseyside giants, and later found himself virtually ignored by Dalglish's successor Graeme Souness.
* His time at Arsenal was a little better, although he was still unable to reproduce the sort of performances he had put together at Millwall. At present Carter is doing a good job at Portsmouth, which, over the last two seasons, has made him a regular  member of Terry Fenwick's starting line up. However, so far this season he is yet to force his way into Terry Fenwick's plans, although during the course of the season he will no doubt get his chance to force his way into the side.

* Carter can play either as a right winger, or in midfield, although his normal position is out wide on the right. He is very decisive in everthing he does, and is an untiring worker throughout the whole game. He has a good shot in his right foot which he doesn't need to be asked twice to make use of. Carter has a good change of direction, and likes to push the ball past defenders to run onto, taking full backs on for pace, creating space which he can use to put over good crossses into the penalty area. On occasions he is too individualistic, trying to sort things out on his own, when it would be easier to bring a team mate into play. He has good vision and possesses fine individual technique.
x
x

* After coming though the youth ranks at Crystal Palace, Jimmy Carter signed professional in November 1983, although he was never given the opportunity to make his first team debut for the Eagles.
* He completed his contract and moved on to QPR in September 1985, although he was again unable to make a league appearance for the club.
* He was transfered to Millwall for £15,000 in march 1987. He made his professional league debut on 14th March 1987 against Oldham Athletic, while his first goal came on 18th April 1987 against Brighton & Hove Albion. 
* He was transfered to Liverpool in January 1991 in exchange for £800,000. He proved to be one of Kenny Dalglish's last signings before resigning as the Red's manager. He made his first appearance for the club on 12th January 1991 against Aston Villa.
* Graeme Souness' arrival as manager of Liverpool, didn't help his career at Anfield, and, as a result he was transfered to Arsenal in October 1991 for £500,000. He made his debut for the Gunners on 8th December 1991 against Nottingham Forest. He scored his first two goals in the league for Arsenal against Southampton on 20th March 1993; two goals which clinched victory for the Gunners.
* He was loaned out to Oxford United in March 1994, making his debut on 26th March 1994 against Grimsby Town . 
* He went back to Oxford United, again on loan, in December 1994.
* He became a free agent and signed for Portsmouth in the summer of 1995. His first game for the club came on 12th August 1995 against  Southend United and opened his account for Pompey on 28th October 1995, against Watford. 
* Carter was nicknamed the "Peanut" as a result of having the same name as the ex-President of the United States, Jimmy Carter, who owned a peanut factory.

* Carter began the league campaign as a member of Terry Fenwick's starting line up, and did a good job until the month of November when he was struck by  injury and was forced out of action for a while. After getting over his injury, he found it impossible to get back into the side, with Paul Hall in a rich vein of form, and the manager unwilling to change a side which was beginning to produce good results. He finally returned in April, to go on to complete a season in which he played in 27 games, scoring once.

785.name: Igoe
pages: * Another product of Portsmouth's youth system. Sammy Igoe is a young midfielder who has already shown glimpses of the ability he possesses, which suggest that he is a player to keep an eye on with regard to the future. The fantastic season he had last time out made him an automatic choice for Terry Fenwick, who has seen the faith he has shown in this young player well rewarded: A young player who, although talked about as one for the future, is very much a player who is already making his presence felt as a regular member of the Portsmouth side, at the start of the current season.

* Igoe is an attack minded midfielder and a player with a tremendous fighting spirit who gives 100% in every game he plays. He is at his best when he moves forward in support of the attack, showing himself to be a player who is best suited to that side of the game, possessing as he does good individual technique. However, he is not an outstanding goalscorer, standing out more as a provider of chances for others rather than as a finisher himself. He makes the most of his excellent vision and passing ability to lay on plenty of chances for his teammates.
x
x
* After coming through the youth ranks at Portsmouth, Igoe played his first game in the club's first team on 7th May 1995 against Oldham Athletic in the final game of the 94-95 season.

* Igoe made himself a vital member of the side last season, playing in a total of 40 games, and scoring twice. Despite having made just 4 starting appearances for the club, Igoe saw Fenwick give him the chance that every young player needs to gain confidence and show what they can do.

786.name: Durnin
pages: * John Durnin is an attack minded midfielder, who, during the years he has been with Portsmouth, has shown that he does a tremendously important job for Terry Fenwick's side. Although he is not a player who stands out for his technical qualities, his enthusiasm and ability to find the back of the net have made him almost indispensable in the side's attacking play. Last time out Durnin made most of his appearances coming off the bench as a subsitute, his place taken by Mathias Svensson. At present he is covering for the team's two strikers, Svensson himself and John Aloisi.

* An attacking midfielder, Durnin can also be used as an out and out striker. He possesses great strength and battles away throughout the whole of the game. Technically he is quite weak, although he keeps things simple, passing the ball on quickly, and moving into the attack looking for the chance to get in a shot on goal. Durnin has demonstrated his ability to find the back of the net over the years, and remains a good finisher, never thinking twice when he gets the opportunity to have a shot on goal.
* Top scorer at Oxford United during the 89-90 and 92-93 Season.
x

* John Durnin completed his contract with amateur club Waterloo Dock and signed for  Liverpool in March 1986. However he was unable to make a league appearance  for the Reds.
* He went out on loan to WBA in October 1988. He made his league debut for the club on 22nd October 1988 against Bradford City and scored his first goal as a professional four days later Manchester City.
* In February 1989 he was transfered to Oxford United for £250,000. He played his first game for the club on 11th February 1989 against Portsmouth, while his opening goal for the Manor Ground club proved to be the winner, against  Walsall, on 27th March 1989.
* Finally he was transfered to Portsmouth in July 1993 in exchange for £200,000. He made his debut on 28th August 1993 against Crystal Palace, and hit his first goal in Portsmouth's colours on 4th September 1993 against Stoke City.

* Durnin made most of his appearances last season coming off the bench as a substitute. This situation wasn't helped following the arrival of Svensson in December, making his opportunities even more limited. Nevertheless he proved himslef to be a fine substitute for either of the two main strikers whenever he was required. In total he played in 34 games, scoring 3 times.

787.name: Flahavan
pages: * A goalkeeper who came through the youth system at Portsmouth, Aaron Flahavan has proven himself to be capable of dislodging Alan Knight from the first team goalkeeping spot at Portsmouth. Knight, a genuine institution at Pompey, has seen himself replaced by a young keeper, who, before making himself a regular had not made a starting appearance for the club. For many the club's future goalskeeper, Flahavan has the ability to make himself an automatic first team choice and become one of the best in the First Division. Just as he was last season, he remains, at least at the beginning of the current campaign, a first choice in goal for Terry Fenwick.

* Flahavan is a keeper who, despite his youth and logical lack of experience, has already shown himself to possess tremendous ability. One of his weaknesses is his ability in the air, lacking real dominance and occasionally misjudging crosses into the  box. However he makes up for this defect in his game with his tremendous agility, and the speed he shows when he is force to come out at the feet of forwards, covering his angles well as he does so.
x
x

* After coming through the youth ranks at Portsmouth, Flahavan played his first game for Pompey on 17th August 1996 against Bradford City, although he didn't have a particularly fortunate debut, being sent off.

* Flahavan began the season as Portsmouth's first choice goalkeeper, although he didn't  enjoy a successful debut, being sent off along with central defender Andy Awford. He remained in the side until a bad run and a loss of form saw Alan Knight win back his place in the side. In total he played in 24 games.

788.name: Knight
pages:
* Very much a fixture at Portsmouth, Alan Knight has spent the whole of his playing career as a professional at Fratton Park. A player who has seen it all during his career with Portsmouth, he has managed to break the record set by Peter Bonetti for the number of games played by a goalkeeper for one club and now has just Jimmy Dickinson ahead of him as the holder of the record number of appearances for Portsmouth.. 
* Despite having played more than 750 games for Portsmouth, Knight continues to show tremendous form, and remains a fine goalkeeper. His star pupil, Aaron Flahavan has learnt well from the maestro and is, for the moment, Terry Fenwick's number one choice in goal. Last season Alan Knight's campaign got better as it went on, and he will no doubt be hoping for a repeat performance this time round.

* Knight is a very complete goalkeeper who has all the attributes he needsto be competent in all aspects of a goalkeeper's job. He has tremendous reflexes that allow him to make some tremendous saves, while he is very safe when he goes up for high balls, showing himself to be dominant, the safety he shows spreading a great sense of security through the whole of the defence knowing as they do that he is unlikely to let them down. He has fine positional sense and keeps his cool and covers his goal well in one on one situations. Not as quick as he once was, this can prove to be a handicap when the ball is played ball either over or through the defence, Knight not being as efficient in these situations as he once was.
x

* An England youth international, he has also made 2 under-21 appearance for his country He made his debut on 29th March 1983 against Greece, in an England team which included, among other, Paul Bracewell, Steve McMahon and Mark Hateley.

* A product of Portsmouth's youth system, Knight signed as a professional in March 1979.  He made his debut for Portsmouth in the final game of the season against Rotherham United., with the club already having been relegated to the Fourth Division.

* While Aaron Flahavan began the season as Portsmouth's first choice goalkeeper at the beginning of the season, it was Knight who reclaimed his number one spot, following a dip in the youngster's form. He made a crucial contribution to the club's tremendous run of form which took them to the edge of the places that would have qualified them for the play offs to promotion to the Premier League. However, eventually Pompey just missed out. During the course of the season Knight made a total of 22 appearances.

790.name: Davies
pages:
* Signed for Reading December 1997. 
* Steve Coppell's presence in charge at Crystal Palace didn't help Gareth Davies to force his way into the side.

* Davies is a quick central defender who is hard and forceful in everything he does. Excellent in the air, he likes to get forward to support the attack at dead ball situations. A very uncomfortable opponent for strikers, he is a very tight marker while his agility and speed make him a very difficult player to get the better of.
x

* 8 under-21 international appearances for Wales. 
* He made his debut on 30th March 1993 against Belgium.

* After coming through the youth ranks at Hereford United, he signed professional in 1992. He made his debut on 7th April 1992 against Scarborough, and scored his first goal as a professional against Halifax Town.
* Crystal Palace signed him in June 1995 for 120,000 pounds. He played his first game for the Eagles on 22nd November 1995 against Wolverhampton Wanderers and scored his first goal for the club on 9th December 1995 against Oldham Athletic. 
* On 21st February 1997 he went out on loan to Cardiff City.

* Last season wasn't a good one for Gareth Davies, who spent most of his time in either the reserve side or on the treatment table. Manager Dave Bassett sent him out on loan to Cardiff in February, but when Steve Coppell Arrived to take over at Crystal Palace, he was able to make a few appearances in the side in the final games of the season.

791.name: Primus
pages: * Linvoy Primus is one of the best central defenders in the lower divisions of English football whose rise to a bigger club was only a matter of time. His performances for his former team, Barnet, were so eye-catching that last year the scouts went running to Underhill, the club's stadium, to see him play.  Reading has been quick to tie the player to the club and hope for great things from him this season and in the coming ones.  He is a starter for Bullivant, who also overlapped with him at Barnet and who knows him perfectly.

* Primus is a man who occupies the position of central defender, contributing an enormous amount of security to the team, an important thing taking into account his youth.  He is fairly quick for a central defender and controls the ball well, playing it out from the back.  His positional sense on the pitch is excellent and he has a praiseworthy elegance in his movements.
x
x

* Originally from the lower categories of Charlton Athletic, he signs as a professional on the 14th of August 1992.  His debut occurs on the 1st of November of this year against Birmingham City.
* As a free agent he signs for Barnet on the 18th of July 1994.  He plays his first game with the club on the 20th of August against Scarborough and scores his first goal as a professional against Colchester United on the 13th of January 1996.
* He signs for Reading in the summer of 1997.

* Primus was a fundamental piece in Barnet's machine last year, not missing a single game in the entire championship.  His presence in the back line was one of the reasons why Barnet was so powerful in defence.  Obviously, he played in the 46 games of the championship and scored 3 goals, two of of them with headers.

792.name: Swales
pages: * Steve Swales is a young wide defender who hasn't had so much success since he arrived at Reading from Scarborough in 1995.  In the last few seasons he has not been seen much and his chances shine by their absence.  Up till this season he hadn't enjoyed the confidence of the coaches but this has changed with the signing of Terry Bullivant, who hasn't aligned him from the start but he is a regular on the Royals' subs bench, so his outlook is a lot more rosy.  It is up to him to take advantage of his situation or else he will be waiting for a chance that will probably never come.

* Steve Swales is a defender who normally plays at left back although in emergencies he can play on the other wing.  He is quick and skilful but he lacks consistency in his performance which would help him find a place in the starting eleven.  He is tough when going in for the ball, not thinking about it too much.  He is not so good in the air due mainly to his lack of height.
x
x

* Originally from the lower ranks of Scarborough, Swales signs as a professional on the 3rd of August 1992.  His debut takes place on the 10th of March 1991 against Wrexham and he scores his first goal for the club against Scunthorpe United on the 25th of February 1995.
* He is transferred to Reading on the 13th of July 1995 for £70,000.  He plays his first game for the team on the 19th of August against Derby County.

* Swales had a disappointing season only playing in three league games in the whole of the championship, all of these in December and not making another appearance in the teams fielded by the managers at the time, Gooding and Quinn.

793.name: Booty
pages: * Martin Booty is one of the players that Reading hope to use to build their future as he has the ability to be an important man for Terry Bullivant. He has shown that he is mature and consistent in his actions, facets which will help him figure in Reading's plans again, this time with the new manager.  He is not a member of the starting line-up but he does count for the manager of the Royals.

* Booty is a wide defender who occupies the right of the pitch and who has the ability to figure on the teamsheet.  He distributes the ball well, passing it to the best-placed team-mate and he has good technique.  He makes up for his lack of height with aggressive marking of his opponents, not letting them get a moment's peace.
x
x

* Originally from the lower ranks of Coventry City, he signs as a professional in May 1989.  He makes his debut on the 2/11/91 against Chelsea.
* His contract finished as he signs for Crewe Alexandra in October 1993. He plays his first game on the 9/10/93 against Hereford United and his first goal in league competition in the winner against Chester City on the 27/11/93. 
* He is transferred to Reading in January 1996 for £75,000, making his debut on the 20/1/96 against Stoke City.  His first goal comes on the 27/2/96 against Luton Town.

* Although Booty only played 17 league games during the course of the championship.  This is due mainly to a very bad run of injuries which kept him out for most of the season.  However, when he did play, he gave the impression of being a useful player for the future.  He was the Royals' captain towards the end of the league.

794.name: Hunter
pages:
* Barry Hunter is a central defender with enormous physical power and who is fairly competent technically.  His qualities made him a good organiser of the Reading defence, the team to which he moved last summer and where he was irreplaceable.  Unfortunately, an injury prevented him from finishing the season with his team-mates and made him loose his place in the Royals' starting elevens.
* What's more, the arrival of Linvoy Primus has momentarily shut the doors to the first team and, if the truth be told, he will have a job to oust Primus if he lives up to the expectations placed in him.  Even so, he could make an interesting contribution to the team when the injuries hit the defence, guaranteeing a good performance for the team managed by Terry Bullivant.

* Hunter is a very powerful central defender who tries to make his strength count continually on the pitch.  He is very tough and dominates in the air with his great height although this dominance hasn't, as yet, been converted into danger in the rival box.  A good distributor of the ball which is rarely seen in a player as tall as he is, as is his security with the ball at his feet.  He is even quick for someone of his physique.
* Welsh Cup Champion with Wrexham in 1995.
* Hunter has been youth, B and full international six times for Northern Ireland, making his debut on the 26/4/95 in Riga against Latvia.

* Wrexham pay the amateur club Crusaders £50,000 to acquire his services in August 1993.  He makes his debut in the league on the 28/8/93 against Blackpool and he scores his first goal for the team against Reading on the 5/3/94, a goal that turns out to be the winner.
* He is transferred to Reading in the summer of 1996 for £400,000.  His debut occurs on the 17th of August against Sheffield United and he scores his first goal with his new side against Ipswich Town just a week later.

* Since his arrival at Reading, Barry Hunter became a leader at the back, and was a true example for the rest of his team-mates in terms of consistency and commitment on the pitch.  Unfortunately an injury got in his way and prevented him from playing from March onwards.  Until this moment he had played 27 games and scored 2 goals.

795.name: Wdowczyk
pages: * The now veteran central defender Dariusz Wdowczyk is a true life insurance policy for Reading, a man who brings a lot of experience and security to the Royals backs. The team missed him last year during his prolonged absence although his substitutes did pretty well.  There was a certain worry amongst the coaches at Reading for his Achilles tendon but it seems that he has fully recovered and his renewed presence will be as valuable as in previous years. He is not a starter but has a place on the substitutes' bench.

* This Polish defender plays in the heart of the Reading defence, forming an almost insurmountable barrier. He is not very quick but his positioning is almost perfect and tries to anticipate the forward's moves. He is good in the air, taking advantage of his stature. Very comfortable with the ball at his feet, he is able to join in the attack with the ball under control, dispatching it with good sense. From the rear-guard he is able to make passes of 30, 40 and 50 metres, opening up the wings very accurately. He organises the defence well and reads the games accurately, knowing when he should, or should not, opt for the long ball, the short one, or play it himself.

* Scottish FA Cup Runner-up with Glasgow Celtic in 89-90.
* Scottish League Cup Runner-up with Glasgow Celtic in 90-91.
* Wdowczyk has made 51 international appearances for Poland, including ten as captain.

* Originally from Legia Varsovia, the team for whom he plays more than 220 games, he signed for Glasgow Celtic in November 1989 for £400,000. He makes his debut in the Scottish league on 14th November 1989 against St. Mirren and his first goal comes on 9th December 1989 against Hibernian.
* His contract expires and signs for Reading in August 1994. His first game with the Royals is on 13th August 1994 against Wolverhampton Wanderers.
* Last year, the Polish defender had the bad luck to be injured for a large part of the league, something which did not help his team. His appearances, therefore, were limited to just 8 matches.

796.name: McPherson
pages: * Keith McPherson is a central defender who is very consistent and calm, making him a defender hard to beat. His presence is vital for Reading, the club where he has been almost an undisputed member of the starting eleven except when there have been injuries. He currently forms a defensive partnership with the team's new signing Linvoy Primus.

* McPherson occupies the position of central defender in the Royals' back line. His good positioning allows him to make interceptions without having to expend much energy. He is good in the air and takes good advantage of his physique in collisions, where he usually comes out on top. A very sticky marker, he bothers the rival forwards but doesn't usually join in the attack. He is very consistent but it's not often that he's seen to make a mistake or have a bad game. Fairly complete, he is OK with the ball at his feet although he doesn't usually complicate life too much.
* Second Division Champion with Reading in 1994.
x

* Originally from the West Ham United youth squad, he signs as a professional in September 1981 with his only game coming on 20th May 1985 against Liverpool.
* He is loaned to Cambridge United in September 1985. His debut for the club and first goal comes on 2nd October 1985 against Preston North End. 
* Northampton Town sign him in exchange for £15,000. He also manages to score on his debut on 17th October 1986 against his former club, Cambridge United.
* He is transferred to Reading in August 1990 for £100,000. He plays his first game against Exeter City on 25th August 1990 and scores his first goal for the Royals on 6th October 1990.

* Despite suffering a few injuries at the beginning of the league, McPherson managed to come back to regain his place in the Royals' starting eleven. His great performance during the course of the season meant that he finished the season as the second best player, second only to Trevor Morley. In total he played 39 games and scored 2 goals.

797.name: Bodin
pages:
* After several years at Swindon Town, Paul Bodin left because the club wanted to build its future with players younger than the Welsh international. 
* Even so, his great experience and contribution to the attack have led him to sign for Reading, a team that were looking for a man of these exact characteristics.
* Currently, it seems that the Royals are thinking exactly the same way as his former team as he has been loaned and other players are occupying the position he held last year. The prospects aren't exactly rosy for Bodin but he will try and make known that Bullivant is wrong and figure once again in the plans of the coach - a difficult task.

* Paul Bodin is a left back who covers a lot of ground on his wing, constantly pushing up quickly and decisively. He is an acceptable passer, not uncomfortable with the ball at his feet and master of both the short and long ball. His crosses are of a high quality. In the defensive aspect he is a little weak and neglects his defensive duties because he pushes up so much. He has a good shot with his left and is a safe penalty taker.

* Second Division Champion 95-96 with Swindon Town.
* Voted a member of the Second Division Dream Team in the 95-96 season.
* He has made 23 international appearances for Wales.

* Originally from the lower categories of Chelsea, his contract expires and moves to Newport County in January 1982.
* As a free agent again he joins Cardiff City in August 1982. He makes his debut on 28th August 1982 against Wrexham and his first two goals bring his team the win against Manchester City on 29th September 1983.
* He then switches to amateur football, playing for Bath City.
* He is transferred to Newport County in January 1988 for £15,000. He plays his first game on 29th Jnuary 1988 against Stockport County, scoring his first goal on 13th February 1988 against Crewe Alexandra.
* Swindon Town sign him in March 1988 for £30,000. On his debut for the Robins on 12th March 1988 against Oldham Athletic, he scores a goal.
* Transferred to Crystal Palace in March 1991 for £550,000, he makes his debut on 17th April 1991 against Tottenham Hotspur.
* He is loaned to Newcastle United in December 1991, making his debut on 7th December 1991 against Port Vale.
* He returns to Swindon Town in January 1992 in exchange for £225,000. Like his first spell, he scores on his debut on 18th January 1992, against Leicester City.
* Freed of contractual obligations he signs for Reading in July 1996. His debut occurs on 17th August against Sheffield United and he scores his first goal against Crystal Palace on 23rd April.

* Last season Bodin had a satisfactory season at Reading, his first with the club after leaving Swindon Town. However, a loss of form and the arrival of young blood from the youth squad led to a gradual reduction in his number of appearances as the league progressed. Finally, he played in 27 games and scored a beautiful goal on the volley against Crystal Palace.

798.name: Bernal
pages: * This Australian defender has found a place for himself in the starting line-ups since his arrival from his country of birth. In general, Andy is a defensive-minded back who gives his all on the pitch, the main reason why he is a regular in the team.

* Although Andy Bernal's normal position is that of right back, he can play in all defensive positions with equal effectiveness. Technically very discrete, he is pretty quick and sticks close to the player he is marking. A tough back, he collects a lot of yellow cards.  He is good in the air but doesn't usually join in the attack, not even for set-plays. On his wing he doesn't usually push up, and is basically a defensive player.
x
* He has been an Australian international 18 times.

* He signs for Ipswich Town in September 1987, making his debut in the league on 8th November 1987 against Birmingham City.
* He moves to the Australian team Sydney Olympic, where he stays for five years.
* He is transferred to Reading in July 1994 for £30,000. His first game is on 13th August 1994 against Wolverhampton Wanderers.

* Last year Andy Bernal had a pretty complete season in which he was made team captain, sent off three times, played in the midfield and even made some sensational saves after Mihailov was sent off in a game against Ipswich Town. In short, an outstanding season for Bernal who played 41 games for the Royals during the course of the season.

799.name: Crawford
pages:
* Signed for Reading in March 1998. 
* Jimmy Crawford was on the verge of being transfered last season, but eventually remained at the club and under Kenny Dalglish was even given the chance to make his first team debut. Nevertheless his future at Newcastle is anything but clear. Unless there is a radical change it would seem that Jimmy could soon be out the door at St. James' Park.

* A skillful midfield player, Crawford shows good touch on the ball as well as good vision. A player with potential he needs to get more experience under his belt and improve his consistency and positional play. A player with natural ability. Whether or not he settles down in the Premier League will depend on how quickly he can progress and develop.
x
x

* James Crawford is the first player born in the United States to play for Newcastle. A player of Irish descent he has already been called up for the Irish under-21side.
* Signed from Irish League side Bohemians he arrived at Newcastle on 23rd March 1995. However he didn't get to make his first team debut until 10th March 1997 in a game against Liverpool at Anfield (3-4).
* Previously, in September 1996 he was sent out on loan to Rotherham United where he played 11 games. He almost joined the Yorkshire side on a permanent basis but the deal fell through after the clubs failed to reach an agreement.

* With no opportunity at Newcastle Crawford went out on loan to Rotherham United in September and was even on the point of being transfered to the Yorkshiremen. The clubs however failed to agree terms and was forced to return to Saint James' Park. Kenny Dalglish gave him the opportunity to make his first team debut in the Premier League in the daunting setting of  Anfield. He made 2 appearances for the Magpies, on both occasions coming on as a substitute.

801.name: Houghton
pages:
* One of the best players who have passed through English football in the last decade, Ray Houghton has been an excellent midfielder who still has a lot to offer.
* Although he is now 34 years old, he still has the enthusiasm of youth, giving his all on the pitch. Houghton has a winning character which is transmitted to the rest of the team.
* In the last years of his sporting career, Houghton has made an active contribution to training the talented players at Crystal Palace and to their promotion to the Premier League last year. His spell at the Eagles finished so he decided to join Reading, a club which needs someone with his experience and class to get through the season without any nasty shocks. Still with a lot of strength left, he has time to continue to make the fans happy, now the Royals' fans.

* Ray Houghton is a midfielder who, despite the years, is still very physically strong. His zone of the pitch for Palace was the midfield, though during his career he has played at right half. However, this doesn't prevent him from expressing his freedom of movement, popping up on one side then the other, surprising the defences. He is still quick, though not so much so as before, but with a good turn of speed. He has a good shot from long range - powerful and well placed. Always attentive he tries to surprise the opponent at the slightest opportunity, taking free-kicks quickly or looking to slip his marker. He is good at one-twos, whether receiving the ball or acting as the pivot.

* League Champion with Liverpool in the 87-88 and 89-90 seasons.
* FA Cup Champion with Liverpool in the 88-89 and 91-92 seasons.
* FA Cup Runner-up with Liverpool in the 87-88 season.
* League Cup Champion with Oxford United in the 85-86 season.
* FA Cup Champion with Aston Villa in the 93-94 season.

* 66 appearances for Ireland. He makes his debut on 26th March 1986 in Dublin against Wales with a 1-0 victory for the away side, the goal scored by Ian Rush. The game was also the first played with the Irish manager Jackie Charlton in charge.
* Houghton took part in the '88 European Championship in Germany, in which he scored the goal that beat England in both teams' opening game, and in the 90 Italy and 94 United States World Cups, where he scored a goal in Ireland's first game, again the winner, this time against Italy.

* Trained in the youth squad at West Ham United, he signs as a professional in July 1979.  His only game with the Hammers is on 1st May 1982 against Arsenal, coming on as a substitute for George Cowie.
* As a free agent he signs for Fulham in July 1982. He makes his debut in the league on 28th August 1992 against Rotherham United and scores his first goal as a professional against Bolton Wanderers.
* He is transferred to Oxford United in September 1985 for £147,000, making his debut on 14th September 1985 against Liverpool. He scores his first goal for the team on 26th October 1985 against Watford.
* In October 1987 he is signed by Liverpool in exchange for £825,000. He plays his first game for the Reds on 24th October 1987 against Luton Town and scores his first goal for the Anfield club against Wimbledon on 4th November 1987.
* Aston Villa sign him for £900,000 in July 1992. He makes his debut on 15th August 1992 against Ipswich Town and scores his first goal for Villa on 28th Novemeber 1992 against Norwich City.
* His next destination is Crystal Palace, arriving in March 1995 in exchange for £300,000.  He makes his debut on 1st April 1995 against Manchester City and scores his first goal for the Eagles against Blackburn Rovers on 20th April 1995.
* In the summer of 1997, Houghton moves to Reading to combine playing duties with a position in the coaching body.

* Houghton didn't have the season that he had hoped for at the beginning. His season was marred by injuries and suspensions which limited him to just 23 games during the course of the league competition. As a sign of his strong character, Houghton "went missing" despite being captain, during the handing over of the trophy which certified the Crystal Palace's promotion to the Premier League.

802.name: Williams
pages:
* Signed when his contract with Luton Town expired, Martin Williams couldn't find much playing time during his first year with the Royals, appearing sporadically. There was even talk of a possible transfer to Peterborough United which didn't come through in the end.  However, despite the rumours, this young centre half is a man who battles for every ball, and is very popular amongst the fans.
* His outstanding season last year has elevated him definitively to the starting eleven, playing in a position further forward than he is used to, almost as a second striker alongside Carl Asaba. These two have formed a good partnership and it seems that William's explosion at Reading has come about at last. He has all the time in the world to keep the club in the First Division without any problem.

* Williams is a player who operates as a right half. He is very quick and every time he has the ball tries to go past the defender to get to the by-line and put over a cross, although these aren't the best in the world. He helps out in the defence when the rival wing back pushes up. He has the tendency to drift infield looking for a one-two to bring him into the box. Thanks to his good dribbing, he is always thinking about attacking but doesn't score so many goals.
x
x

* Williams is from the Leicester City junior team. However, he finished his contract and moved to Luton Town in September 1991. He makes his debut in the league on 21st March 1992 against Southampton and scores his first goal as a professional on 13th April 1993.
* He is loaned to Colchester United in March 1995, making his debut on 11th March 1995 against Hartlepool United.
* Free of contractual obligations he signs for Reading in July 1995.  He makes his debut on 12th August 1995 against Stoke City, his first goal coming on 30th April 1996 against Wolverhampton Wanderers.

* Williams had a very important season which saw him settling into the Royals' team, improving in every aspect of his game, leading him to become a regular in the Reading line-ups. In total he played 29 games and scored 3 goals.

803.name: Parkinson
pages: * In this his sixth season at Reading, Phil Parkinson has shown in absolute terms why he remains one of the starters at Reading. His fighting spirit and great defensive work have made him a worthy recipient of the affection of the fans and have earned him the respect of his team-mates. Thanks to his inestimable work and prolonged career at the club, Parkinson is one of the men that Bullivant uses most when making up the teamsheet.

* Parkinson is a midfielder who does the dirty work on the pitch for Reading. He is brave, always sticking out a leg in the 50-50 balls. He can play as a central defender in times of emergency and even as a forwards. In attack, he contributes little, being mainly defensive.  He is quick and can be placed as the marker of the opposing team's organiser.
* Second Division Champion with Reading in 1994.
x

* Trained in the Southampton youth squad he signs as a professional in December 1985 but doesn't get to play for the Saints.
* He is transferred to Bury in March 1988 for £12,000. He scores against Brentford in his debut in the league on 12th March 1988.
* Reading pay £37,500 for him in July 1992. He plays his first game for the Royals on 15th August 1992 against Hartlepool United and scores his first league goal on 28th November 1992 against Exeter City.

* Despite missing part of the season due to a dislocated shoulder, Parkinson was once again a basic part of the Reading team in the 24 games that he played. In many of these games he had the honour of being captain of the Royals. He even managed to score a goal during the course of the league.

804.name: Meaker
pages: * Michael Meaker is a player who hasn't had many opportunities at QPR nor has he had much luck in his spell at Reading, not finding a regular place in the Reading starting line-ups.  Even so, he is still young but he lacks consistency. Terry Bullivant is currently playing him from the start.

* Meaker plays on Reading's right, showing off his great speed. He likes to hug the touchline and push up along it, trying to go past the rival defenders to then put over a cross. He is basically right-footed but he can shoot with either foot. However, he doesn't finish too well, either with his shot or in individual actions, being better at making goals rather than scoring them. A battler, he helps the defenders and pushes up constantly into the attack.
x
* Meaker has made 2 under-21 international appearances for Wales.

* Raised in the QPR youth squad, he signs as a professional in February 1990. He makes his debut in the league on 1st December 1990 against Manchester City and scores his first goal as a professional against Leeds United on 29th December 1993.
* He is loaned to Plymouth Argyle in November 1991, making his debut on 23rd November 1991 against Sunderland.
* Reading pay £500,000 for him in the summer of 1995. He plays his first game on 19th August 1995 against Derby County.

* Meaker once again had a season that can be classed as disappointing as he didn't have the consistency necessary in his intervention to get into the starting line-up on a regular basis. He played 24 games and scored a goal in the last game of the season. Once again however, hints of a good player were seen, but all too seldom.

805.name: Fleck
pages:
* Signed for Reading in March 1998.
* Robert Fleck is a centre forward who had a very bad time in his spell at Chelsea, and he was even thinking of retiring. He returned to Norwich City, the team to whom he had given his all for a good part of his sporting career. He was also a man very much appreciated by the fans at Carrow Road.

* Fleck is a very quick centre forward who has the ability to take defences by surprise after breaking the offside trap. He is good in the air, above all because of his anticipation and positioning as he is not so tall. Intuitive, this Scottish player is able to position himself well in almost all the moves. He is not at all selfish and doesn't mind if a team mate, who is in a better position than him, scores. Although he is right-footed, he shoots with either. Fleck also works hard pressuring the rival defences.

* League Champion with Glasgow Rangers in the 86-87 season. 
* League Cup Champion with Glasgow Rangers in the 86-87 season. 
* League Cup Champion with Glasgow Rangers in the 87-88 season. 
* Top scorer at Norwich City in the 88-89 and 91-92 seasons and in the 95-96 season together with Ashley Ward.

* Fleck has represented Scotland at youth, under-21 and full level four times, making his debut in this latter category on 28th March 1990 against Argentina with a 1-0 victory for Scotland. 
* He took part in 2 Italy-90 World Cup games, against Brazil and Sweden.

* Born in Glasgow, Robert Fleck is drawn to one of the greats of the city, Glasgow Rangers.  He makes his debut with the club on 7th April 1984 against Hearts at Ibrox, the Rangers ground, and his first goal comes on the 7/8/85 against St. Mirren. The 86-87 season is his best with the team, coinciding with the arrival of Graeme Souness. He scores 19 goals in 40 games, including three hat-tricks along the way. 
* In December 1987 Fleck is transferred to Norwich City for £580,000. He makes his league debut on 18th December 1987 against Wimbledon and scores his first goal 8 days later against Derby County. 
* Chelsea pay £2.1 million for him in August 1992 although Fleck doesn't manage to adapt to the playing system of the London team, only scoring 2 goals in the whole of the season, the first of these on 2nd September 1992 against Aston Villa. The arrival of Glenn Hoddle at Stamford Bridge forces him into the background. 
* He is loaned to Bolton Wanderers in December 1993, the club where he plays his first game on 18th December 1993 against Grimsby Town. He scores a goal on 1st January 1994 against Notts County. 
* In the 95-96 Season Fleck is first loaned then transferred to Norwich City for £650,000.

* Robert Fleck completed a somewhat disappointing season as he only managed to score 4 goals in the 36 games he played for Norwich City. It seems that his once devilish speed is not what is was, something that might explain his low tally. Even so, he helped some the new players to establish themselves, players such as Darren Eadie, Keith O'Neill and Craig Bellamy amongst others.

* Hodges is a centre forward who scores a lot of goals. He has a very accurate left foot and shoots powerfully. Intelligent, he makes good runs off the ball.

* England youth international.

* He did his duty as a link-man bridging the gap between the midfield and the forwards perfectly. At times he didn't reach the level expected of him, but he recovered and finished with a good season.

809.name: Roach
pages: * Neville Roach is a young centre forward who comes from the lower ranks at Reading who has a very promising future ahead of him. He has been at the club since he was 10 years old, a graduate of the prestigious School of Excellence. His opportunity arrived last year after scoring more than 40 goals for the Royals youth and reserve teams. Roach's progress appears to be unstoppable but it will have to be seen how his second year with the club goes. It will be difficult for Roach to become an undisputed starter due to the presence of record-setting Carl Asaba.

* Roach is a centre forward who moves with purpose in the attacking zone. He has a scent for goal as has been amply demonstrated by his record in the lower categories and has the resources to score a lot of goals. In short, a valuable player for the future.
x
x

* From the Reading youth squad, Neville Roach signs as a professional on 10th May 1997.  He makes his debut on 19th April against Grimsby Town and scores his first goal as a professional against Oldham Athletic just one week later.

* Neville Roach created a great impression among the fans at Reading and the training body in just three games with the first team. His best moment came when he scored his first goal against Oldham Athletic with a sensational lob over the rival keeper.

810.name: Asaba
pages:
* Carl Asaba has been the most expensive player in the history of Reading, the club paying £800,000. This label shouldn't prevent Asaba from producing a satisfactory season with the Royals as he has shown what he is capable of against Brentford during the course of last year when he was one of the best players in the Second Division.
* He is a starter and, what's more, due to the row that has accompanied his signing, he will have to score as many goals as possible while the first choice centre forward, Trevor Morley, is out.

* A strong centre forward, powerful and a good finisher; his presence on the pitch announces danger. Quick and resistant, he never gives up a ball as lost, but he should work more on his technique. He has polished up his one-on-ones with the goalkeeper as is shown by his scoring record. He is a man who takes advantages of his chances.
* Top scorer at Brentford in the 96-97 season.
x

* Carl Asaba was originally from Dulwich Hamlet. On 9th August 1994 he signs as a professional with Brentford. His debut for this team takes place on 9th September 1995 against Rotherham United and he scores his first two goals against Bournemouth on 4th May, the last game of the season.
* He is loaned to Colchester United on 16th February 1995, playing his first game on 18th February against Barnet, scoring the winning goal.
* He is transferred to Reading during the summer of 1997 for £800,000, the highest amount paid by the club for any player in its entire history.

* Last year was the one when Carl Asaba finally exploded on the scene at Brentford, finishing the league as the team's top scorer with 23 goals in 44 games. His most brilliant performances were at the beginning of the season when he scored 11 goals in 11 games and in a game against Shrewsbury he scored a hat-trick in 7 minutes. As a reward he was voted as a member of the Second Division dream team.

811.name: Lambert
pages: * A man from the youth squad, James Lambert has shown irrefutably his good technical qualities, making him an interesting player for the future. His technical details betray a bit of individualism however, but if he erases this defect he could be a very useful player. As well as polishing his skill, he will have to settle into the first team a bit more, though last year was his best since he moved up to the first squad. His ability has made him a starter in the team at the beginning of this season.

* Lambert is a quality left winger, skilful with the ball at his feet. As he is not so quick he likes to hug the touchline and take advantage of his skill to go by defenders. Very left-footed, he uses his right almost only as support. He is a little selfish because, at times he tries to do too much but he has scored some excellent individual goals. He has the ability to put over good crosses and supply good deep balls.
x
x

* Originally from the lower ranks of Reading, he signs as a professional in July 1992 after leaving school at 18. He makes his debut in the league on 16th September 1992 against Rotherham United and scores his first goal against Chester City on 12th December 1992.
* Lambert made it to the front page of some English newspapers when he trained with the French team Monaco for 3 days in December 1992.

* Lambert had one of his best seasons at Reading but once more he lacked consistency on the pitch. He had some good and bad moments but it has to be said that, little by little, he has found a slot for himself in the team managed both by Gooding and Quinn. In total he played 31 games and scored 5 goals.

812.name: Caskey
pages:
* The still young English midfielder Darren Caskey has not had many chances to play over the years he was at Tottenham Hotspur, the club where he trained as a footballer.
* Caskey, however, has not compensated for the amount of money spent on his transfer. His irregular spell at Reading is one of the worst moments of his professional career. He is young and strong and possesses the quality which might help to turn this situation around and make him a useful player for the Royals.

* Caskey is a strong midfielder, right-footed, and a man who fights hard in the midfield although he is lacking in technique. An acceptable passer, he doesn't usually join in the attack too much but has a noteworthy shot from long range. Hard but fair when going in for the ball.
* European under-18 champion in 1993 with the England team.
* Schoolboy and youth international for England.

* Originally from the lower ranks of Tottenham Hotspur, Caskey signs as a professional in March 1992. He makes his debut in the league in the London derby against Arsenal on 16th August 1993 and his first goal for Spurs is the winner against Everton on 3rd October 1993.
* Transferred to Reading in March 1996 for £600,000. His first game is on 2nd March 1996 against Watford, scoring his first goal for the team on 23rd March 1996 against Tranmere Rovers.
* In the final of the European under-18 championship against Turkey, Caskey scored the winning goal for the England side. In the same team were, amongst others, Robbie Fowler, Gary Neville, Sol Campbell, Paul Scholes and Kevin Gallen.

* Caskey had a good season in general, but only really took off after the halfway point. Before this mark he didn't play regularly. After, he became the team's axis, his accurate passes in depth much appreciated by his team-mates. In total he played 35 games.

815.name: Mautone
pages: * Steve Mautone is an Australian goalkeeper who wasn't presented with many opportunities when he arrived on English soil at West Ham United where he was the understudy to Ludek Miklosko. He has had to look outside the club for chances to be successful in English football. His performance while on loan was so good that Reading decided to sign him in the summer. It hasn't just stopped there for Mautone - he is now the first choice keeper.

* Mautone is a keeper who takes good advantage of his height to dominate in the aerial game, conceding few mistakes. He is very agile for a man of his build. This allows him to make some great saves. Competent at stopping penalties.
x
x

* West Ham United sign him in 1996 for £30,000 from the Australian team Canberra Cosmos. His debut with the Hammers is delayed until 21st September 1996 in a game against Nottingham Forest.
* He is loaned to Crewe Alexandra on 6th September, playing his first game for the team on 7th September against Bournemouth.
* He is loaned to Reading on 17th February 1997, in the end staying with the Robins. He plays his first game for the club on 22nd September against Southend United.

* Steve Mautone played with three different teams last year despite remaining a West Ham player. In the team managed by Harry Redknapp he was the understudy to Miklosko and hardly got to play except for one game during the whole of the league, a game in which he kept a clean sheet. At Crewe Alexandra he was on loan but, despite playing well, he had to return to the Hammers to guard Miklosko's back. Finally, he moved to Reading as a loan player but was finally transferred after a series of good performances for the Royals.

816.name: Hammond
pages:
* Nicky Hammond is a goalkeeper who hasn't had very many playing minutes during the course of his career, never really settling down regularly in any of the teams in which he has played.  It is probable that this is due to his lack of consistency, as he is capable of the best and the worst on the pitch. 
* Bad luck has been added to this collection of circumstances, a serious back injury almost leaving Hammond out of the league. He made a satisfactory return. Mautone is the current first choice keeper.

* Hammond is capable of making truly great saves but also equally capapble of letting in stupid goals. He is pretty secure in the air though his judgement on distances is poor, the area where most ofhis mistakes are made. His biggest virtues are his reflexes and his bravery in 50-50 balls, not even thinking about the possible damage to himself. He moves quickly in the box.
x
x

* Hammond started his sporting career in the Arsenal youth squad, signing as a professional in July 1985. He didn't get to play for the Gunners however. 
* He is loaned to Bristol Rovers in August 1986, making his debut on 27th September 1986 against Blackpool.
* As a free agent he signs for Swindon Town. His first game comes on 31st October 1987 against Manchester City.
* Transferred to Plymouth Argyle for £40,000 in August 1995, making his debut on 12th August 1995 against Colchester United.
* He is transferred to Reading in January 1996 for £40,000. His first game comes against Sunderland.

* A serious back injury limited Nicky Hammond to just one league game last year - a 2-0 defeat at the hands of WBA. His recovery was going well at the end of the season and he could even manage to play a couple of games for the reserves.

817.name: Morley
pages:
* Trevor Morley is an experienced centre forward who has managed to return by literally sweating blood, scoring goals for the team which had put its faith in him after he was rejected by other clubs. After a first season at the club when he had a true nightmare, Morley was justly rewarded with one of his best years as a professional.
* Unfortunately, the spell of this very brave forward at Reading suffered a terrible episode when he was seriously injured for 6 months in a game against Barnsley. After his return, which will happen, Morley will once again figure in the plans of Bullivant despite the acquisition of Carl Asaba.

* Trevor Morley is forward at home in the box, being very dangerous in this zone. He has the rare ability to find himself in the right place at the right time. He shoots from any position and with either of his feet although he moves the ball about better with his right. He doesn't dribble well, but this doesn't matter as he is a good finisher. He is good with his head thanks to his good positioning and anticipation, despite his lack of height. Despite his age, he is still quick in the box and surrounding area but can't arrive from deep positions. He rarely helps out in defence.

* Fourth Division Champion with Northampton Town in 1987.
* Top scorer at Northampton Town in the 87-88 season alongside Tony Adcock and Paul Culpin.
* The top scorer at West Ham United in the 90-21, 92-93 and 93-94 seasons. 
* Top scorer at Reading in the 96-97 season.
x

* Morley was in the Derby County youth squad although he later moved to the amateur club Corby Town. From there he moved on to Nuneaton Borough. 
* In June 1985 he is transferred to Northampton Town for £20,000. He made his debut in league competition on 17th August 1985 against Burnley, managing to score a goal.
* He is signed by Manchester City in January 1988 for £175,000. He makes his debut on 23rd January 1988 against Aston Villa and scores his first goal for the Maine Road team against Ipswich Town on 5th March 1988.
* West Ham United sign him in 1989 for £500,000. He plays first game against Leicester City and scores his first goal on 2oth January 1990 against Hull City.
* He is finally transferred to Reading in the summer of 1995. He plays his first game on 12th August 1995 against Stoke City and scores his first goal for the Royals on 19th Agust 1995 against Derby County.

* Morley had one of his best seasons as a professional, scoring 22 goals in 37 games, the best average in the whole of his career, his presence in the area a synonym for danger. His effort was rewarded with the prize, Player of the Year, chosen by the club's supporters.  Unfortunately, bad luck caught up with Morley once again, receiving a serious injury in a game against Barnsley in March. He could be out for six months.

818.name: Lovell
pages: * A young player from the Reading youth squad, Stuart Lovell, has not had much luck in the last two years as injuries have hardly given him a breathing space to keep playing regularly.  Despite not being a veteran, Lovell has played more than 200 league games for Reading.  Very much loved by the fans at the club, he is a player with an ability for scoring goals and who, if good luck goes with him, could play despite the presence of men such as Asaba, Nogan and Morley.

* Lovell is a forward who scores a lot of goals. He works for the team and is not selfish in situations where there is a team-mate in a clearly better position than him for scoring. He doesn't mind working hard, looking for some space and pressuring the opposing defenders.  He is very quick and can arrive powerfully from deeper positions. He is good in the air thanks to his good anticipation. A good finisher, he moves about intelligently.
* Second Division Champion with Reading in 1994.
x

* Trained in the Reading youth squad, he signs as a professional in July 1990. He makes his debut in the league on 3rd November 1990 against Stoke City and scores his first goal - the winner - as a professional in his first game on 1st December 1990.
* A penalty miss of his in the playoff for promotion to the Premier League in May 1995 when his team were winning 2-0 against Bolton Wanderers provoked a reaction in this team, with Reading finally losing 4-3 in extra-time.
* Lovell started the season on the Reading bench but thanks to his sacrifice he started to figure in the plans of Gooding and Quinn. In total he played 26 games and scored 5 goals.

820.name: Francis
pages:
* Signed for Oxford during the 97-98 season.
* Kevin Francis is the tallest player in all four divisions at 2.01 metres tall and represents a real nightmare for defenders when high balls are sent in, generally coming out on top in ariel battles.

* Being a tall man and having such an ability to win the ball in the air, Francis is a player whom his teammates will generally seek to find with long balls which he will usually win and nod down to his fellow strikers or oncoming midfield men. He is also a powerful header of the ball and shows great bravery in everything he does. Although a hard player he always goes in fairly. However, he is quite limited, technically speaking, although he possesses a powerful but often inccurate shot which he doesn't hesitate to use. He occasionally strikes some spectacular goals, though he also gets his fair share of deffections. He has an enormously long stride, and is genuinely quick, as well as enjoying the advantage of having such long legs which also help him to win the ball in tackles and challenges with defenders. Defensively he makes an important contribution, dropping back to pick up opposing defenders when they move forward for deadball situations.

* Top scorer at Stockport County in the seasons 92-93 and 93-94.
* Second Division Championship Winners medal with Birmingham,94-95.
x

* After becoming a free agent at amateur club Mile Oak Rovers, he signed for Derby County in February 1989. All the appearances he made with the Rams came as a substitute, the first of those being on 20th January 1990 against Nottingham Forest.
* He was transfered to Stockport County in February 1991 for £45,000 making his bow in the league on 23rd February 1991 against Lincoln City. His first goal came on 9th April 1991 against Northampton Town.
* He signed for Bimingham City for £800,000 pounds in January 1995. He made his debut against his ex-club Stockport County on 4th February 1995 while his first two goals for the club came against York City on 18th February 1995.

* Francis had a dreadfully unlucky season with regards to injury. An ankle problem kept him out until the month of January. Despite finding the net in one of his first games of the season, he barely entered into Trevor Francis' plans. In total he played in 19 games scoring just that one solitary goal.

821.name: Banger
pages: * A striker who saw opportunities come his way at Southampton following the departure of Alan Shearer to Blackburn Rovers. Although he had a few outstanding moments for the Saints he was never really able to settle down in the side. His spell at Oldham proved to be an up and down one, alternating between highs and lows. Finally the Latics decided it was time for him to move on, and, as a result, he became oneof Oxford United's most important acquisitions for the current season, as striking cover for Jemson and Aldridge. His contribution will no doubt be well appreciated by the club.

* A very quick forward, he is good with either foot, although he is more at home when he is playing down the right hand side. His constant movement, looking to get away from defenders, makes him a very difficult player to cover. He is a good striker of the ball and is always quick to react inside the area. He is not a genuine goalscorer though he does find the back of the net fairly regularly. A clever player he is always looking to get on the blind side of defenders, and also possesses excellent vision. On occasions he is guilty of trying do too much on his own.
x
x

* After coming through the ranks at Southampton, he signed as a professional in April 1989. He made his league debut on 8th December 1990 against Norwich City, although he had to wait until 29th August 1992 for his first goal, against Middlesbrough. 
* He was loaned out to Oldham Athletic in October 1994, a deal which became a permanent one for £250,000. He made his debut on 8th October 1994 against Portsmouth, and scored his first two goals for the club on 25th February 1995 against Sheffield United. 
* He was transfered to Oxford United in the summer of 1997.

* Banger began the season as a first team regular at Oldham Athletic, but after playing in the first 15 games of the season, 12 of those appearances coming as a member of the starting line up, he was inexplicably left out of the side. As a result his appearances in the side became very few and far between. The goals he scored, several of them clinching victory for the Latics, didn't prove to be enough to earn him a regular place. He went on to make a total of 23 appearances.

822.name: Murphy
pages: * A player who arrived at Oxford United from amateur football, Matt Murphy is a striker who has now completed five seasons at Oxford United, and has always made a good impression, though without managing to really settle down as a regular in Denis Smith's line up. Despite being technically limited, he is a decisive player with plenty of character, always trying to go straight for goal whenever he gets possession, Since his arrival at the club he has become the joker in the pack for the manager, coming off the bench as a substitute, doing a fine job whenever he is called into the action. In total he has made more that 50 appearances as a substitute. He looks likely to be in the same position this season.

* Murphy is a very strong striker. Though he is lacking in terms of skill, he is a real bustler who fights for every ball, makes life uncomfortable for defenders, and is constantly on the move looking for spaces. A basically right footed player, he doesn't need to be asked twice to have a go at goal. He occasionally tries to do too much on his own, though these occasions are few and far between. A hardworking player, he keeps defenders under constant pressure.
x
x

* Oxford United paid £20,000 to sign him from amateur club Corby Town. He made his debut in the league on 6th May 1993 against Newcastle United and scored his first goal in the professional game against Cardiff City on 10th December 1994, a goal which gave Oxford all three points.
* Matt Murphy remained the joker in the pack for the Oxford United manager, making a number of appearances after coming off the bench. He played in a total of 30 games, scoring 3 times.

823.name: Aldridge
pages: * Martin Aldridge is a young striker who had an immediate impact on his arrival at Oxford United from Northampton Town, where, in recent seasons, not too much confidence had been shown in his ability. A genuine goalscorer, he is something of an inconsistent performer, a problem he will have to try to put right if he wants to make himself a regular in Denis Smith's line up. At present he is partnering Jemson in the Oxford attack, forming a good striking duo, scoring plenty of goals. His position as a regular member of the side is almost assured, unless Banger proves to be capable of taking that privilige from him..

* As was his namesake, John Aldridge, who is no relation to him, Martin is a genuine  goalscorer. He possesses a great ability to find the back of the net and is capable of getting in efforts on goal from any position, in any way he can. A quick player, his pace helps him to make up for his lack of strength and power. His speed allows him to play between the midfield and the forwards, doing a job as a link up man. He is an intelligent player who is a good passer of the ball.
x
x

* After coming through the youth ranks at Northampton Town, Martin Alridge signed professional in July 1991. He made his league debut on 4th April 1992 against Barnet and scored his first goal on 10th October 1992 against Scarborough. 
* In October 1995 he went out on loan to Oxford United. He made his debut on 26th December 1995 against Bournemouth, and scored his first two goals for the club on 13th January 1996, against Brentford, clinching a victory for Oxford.

* Aldridge fought for the right to partner Nigel Jemson in the attack with Paul Moody,  emerging as the winner in his private battle with his teammate. He played in 30 games and ended the season as the club's second top scorer, with 8 goals to his name, his total only being bettered by Jemson. The highlight of the season for Martin Aldridge was the hat-trick he scored against Sheffield United, in the space of just 15 minutes.

824.name: Gray
pages: * As is usually the case, although Martin Gray's presence in the Oxford defence wasn't particularly eye catching for the supporters, the containing and ballwinning job he did was, as ever, a tremendous one. Given the unspectacular nature of the work he does for the side, he is not one of the supporters' most popular players, and, occasionally, is not given the credit he deserves. However Denis Smith decided on a change and, as a result, has not yet made Gray a regular this time out. Nevertheless, the league campaign is a long one, and he will no doubt get his opportunity to stake a claim for a place in the starting line up.

* Gray is basically a defensive player who goes in hard to win the ball. Despite being a midfielder, he can also do a a job as an emergency full back, down either flank, although he is a right footed player. He seldom moves forward in support of the attack, almost always staying back to help out the defence. He is a very uncomfortable opponent for his midfield rivals.
x
x

* Martin Gray came through the youth ranks at Sunderland, signing professional in February 1990. His first game for the club came on 29th April 1992 against Blackburn Rovers, while he hit his first goal on 1st May 1993 against Portsmouth. 
* He was loaned out to Aldershot in January  1991, making his debut on 12th January against  Scunthorpe United.
* He also went out on loan to Fulham in October 1995, playing his first game for the London club on 21st October 1995 against Chester City.
* He was finally transfered to Oxford United in March 1996 for £100,000. His debut came on 2nd April 1996 against Wrexham.

* In his first season at Oxford United, Gray was one of Denis Smith's most regular performers, playing in 43 games and scoring 2 goals. During the course of the season he even came to captain the side, demonstrating once again that he is a genuine leader out on the pitch, proving himself to be fully deserving of his brief spell as captain.

825.name: Lewis
pages: * Mickey Lewis is a player who has made himself extremely popular with the crowd at the Manor Ground, through the impressive performances he has put together patrolling his area of the pitch. He has been at Oxford United for a number of years and has always responded to the faith shown in him by putting in a tremendous amount of work out on the park. However last season he failed to make even the briefest of first team appearances and will have to make up all of that lost ground if he wants to force his way back into Denis Smith's plans.

* Lewis is the strong man in the Oxford United midfield, a player of tremendous strength and power which allows him to win plenty of possession for his side. Though a hard tackler,when he goes in to win the ball, he always does so fairly. He is not a player who is blessed with the ability to operate as a midfield playmaker, nor does he move forward in support of the attack, being a basically defensive player, although that doesn't mean that he doesn't do a key job for Oxford United.
x
* England youth international.

* After coming through the ranks at WBA, he signed professional in February 1982. He made his debut on 26th December 1981 against Coventry City.
* In November 1984 he was transfered to Derby County for £25,000. His debut in the league came on 24th November 1984 against Wigan Athletic.
* Finally he was transfered to Oxford United in a swap deal that took Trevord Hebberd to Derby County. He played his first game for the Manor Ground club on 27th August 1988 against Leeds United, and opened his goalscoring account as a professional on 13th January 1990 against Watford.
* Mickey Lewis failed to get a taste of the action throughout the whole of last season at  Oxford United .

826.name: Massey
pages: * After a number of years in the English amateur game, Stuart Massey took the step up to professional football with Crystal Palace, from where, not getting too many opportunities, he moved to Oxford United. Not a particularly skillful player, although a real fighter, he does an important defensive job for his side. His enthusiasm and the character he shows out on the pitch make him a very popular player with the Manor Ground supporters. Very much a team man, he is a regular in Denis Smith's side, either coming off the bench as a substitute or as a member of the starting line up.

* Massey is a player who does a fine job down the right flank. He is a hard worker and is an excellent ball winner. Though not over blessed with skill, his appetite for hard work makes him an almost indispensable member of the side. He is a good crosser of the ball and will occasionally pose a threat, making late runs into the box from deep positions, although he is not a regular goalscorer. He can also do a job as a right back, whenever Les Robinson is not available.
x
x

* Crystal Palace signed him from amateur club  Sutton United in July 1992 for £20,000. He played just two games for the Eagles, the first of which was on 5th September 1992 against  Aston Villa.
* He completed his contract in July 1994, and moved on to sign for Oxford United. His first game for the club came on 13th August 1994, and he struck his first goal in an Oxford shirt on 30th January 1996 against Burnley.

* Stuart Massey wasn't a regular member of Denis Smith's side, at least from the start of games. The majority of his appearances came as a substitute. He was limited to 29 appearances, scoring 3 times.

827.name: Angel
pages: * After a couple of years in which Mark Angel was unable to do himself justice at Sunderland, he signed for Oxford United after completing his contract. He won himself his move to Oxford virtually on the strength of an outstanding performance in the pre-season games. His good form throughout the league campaign and his explosive runs down the left flank assured him the admiration of the club's supporters and the backing of manager Denis Smith. Whether it is as a member of the starting line up or coming into the action off the bench, Mark Angel will no doubt be taking an active part in Oxford United's 97-98 campaign.

* Mark Angel is a very quick left winger who takes full advantage of his pace to take on opposition defenders. A left footed player, he can also operate down the opposite flank, thanks to the good touch he shows in his right foot, although his natural position is down the left hand side. He has good dribbling skill, and is difficult to disposses as he keeps the ball under tight control, apparently tied to his foot. He also has good vision and is an  excellent passer of the ball. His weakness is his crossing which is not consistently up to the standard he, or the strikers, would like it to be. When he moves forward he likes to look for one twos to continue making progress down the flank.
x
x

* A product of Sunderland's youth system he was never given the opportunity to make his debut for the Roker Park club. 
* He became a free agent and signed for Oxford United in August 1995. He made his league debut on 12th August 1995 against Chesterfield, while his first goal for the club came on 4th November 1995 against Bristol City.

* Mark Angel began the season on the bench but, slowly but surely, became a player in whom Denis Smith showed full confidence. This quick left winger played in a total of 24 games, scoring twice, one of which was a beautiful header, that from a player not known for his ability in the air.

828.name: Beauchamp
pages:
* The arrival of Joey Beauchamp at Oxford United could be termed as something like the return of the prodigal son. After a number of seasons away from his spiritual home, in which he didn't really live up to the expectations that many people had of him, Beauchamp is now back at the ground where he began his playing career, and where he originally showed the form that won him a move to Swindon Town. 
* Although nobody can doubt his undeniable quality, what he can be criticised for is his occasional lack of character, which all too frequently sees him disappearing from games. As well as this, opposing defenders have learnt their lesson and very often put two men onto the task of tying down this skillful winger. He will no doubt be making an important contribution this season after striking up a partnership with Bobby Ford.

* A left footed midfielder, Beauchamp plays out wide, tight on the touchline, down either the left or right hand side of the field. He has good dribbling ability and is able to twist and turn his way out of trouble with apparent ease. He possesses the strength and speed to set off on runs from deep positions, cutting inside to go straight for the opposition's goal. Good with his right, for a basically left footed player, he also has a powerful shot and  keeps his cool well to finish off the chances that come his way. He uses his excellent vision to good effect, playing accurate passes all over the park, and is also a fine crosser of the ball.
x
x

* After learning his trade in the youth ranks at Oxford United, he signed professional in May 1989. He made his league debut in the final game of the 88-89 season on 13th May 1989 against  Watford. His first league goal came on 28th December 1991 against Sunderland. 
* In October 1991 he was loaned out to Swansea City. He made his debut on 1st November 1991 against Wigan Athletic and scored his first goal for the club 4 days later against Leyton Orient. 
* His fantastic form saw West Ham United splash out £1,000,000 to take him to Upton Park. 
* However, just two months later, without having played in an official competitive game for the  Hammers, he was transfered to Swindon Town in exchange for £850,000. 
* Finally Oxford United signed him for £300,000 in October 1995. He made his first appearance on 7th october 1995 against Stockport County, while on 2nd March 1995, against Bournemouth, he scored the first goal of his second spell at the Manor Ground.

* Joey Beauchamp had a more complex season than the total of 45 appearances might suggest. He began the season in superb form, and was an automatic choice for Denis Smith. However in the final third of the campaign Beauchamp saw more action as a substitute than as a member of the starting line up, a spell which also coincided with a poor run for Oxford United. He managed to find the back of the net on seven occasions.
