829.name: Smith
pages: * Since he signed for Oxford United, David Smith has made himself a key member of the side for namesake and manager Denis Smith, during the course of his three seasons at the Manor Ground. A basically defensive midfielder, he perhaps lacks the confidence to try to take more risks in the attacking side of the game. In just a few seasons this solid midfielder has managed to make 130 apperances for the club, and looks very much set to go on adding to this total during the course of the current campaign.

* A player who basically does a containing job, Smith is a good ballwinner who generally operates just in front of the defence. Following Bobby Ford's injury he was pushed further forward into a more attacking position which allowed him to get into the opposition penalty area more frequently. Smith plays a good short passing game and shows excellent positional sense in his part of the pitch.
x
x

* A product of Norwich City's youth system, he signed as a professional in July 1989. He made his league debut on 21st April 1990 against Derby County. 
* He was transfered to Oxford United in July 1994 for £100,000. He made his debut on 13th August 1994 against Hull City and scored his first goal in the league on 21st October 1995, against Wycombe Wanderers.

* David Smith had another superb season for Oxford United last time out and was virtually irreplaceable in the starting line up for manager Denis Smith. He missed just one league game all season and was, at all times, a real focal point of the side, both in defence and in midfield. He failed to find the back of the net, although he did come close once or twice.

830.name: Davis
pages: * Signed for Oxford United in March 1998.

* Davis is a very good marker from his position in the centre of the defence. He stays very close to the rival forwards, and is hard to play against. He shows himself to be hard when fighting for the ball, but always fair. His sense of anticipation, his dominance in the air and his solidity are his biggest virtues. Dangerous in set-plays due to the effectiveness of his headers, he does not complicate life when he has the ball at his feet.
x
* Youth international for England.

* Originally from the youth squad at Stoke City, he becomes a free agent and signed for Crewe Alexandra in August of 1983.  He makes his debut in the league on 27th August 1983 against Rochdale. 
* He is transferred to Burnley in October of 1987 for £15,000. He plays his first game on 3rd October 1987 against Scarborough and scores his first goal on 31st October 1987 against Stockport County. 
* Barnsley sign him in July of 1991 for £180,000. He makes his debut on 17th August 1991 against Plymouth Argyle and opens his account with a goal against Charlton Athletic on 20th August 1994. 
* In January of 1997 he suffers a broken leg after a collision with John Spencer in a game against Q.P.R. played in the Rangers Stadium.

* For the second season in a row, injuries kept Steven Davis away from the team when he was completely settled into the starting line-up put out by Danny Wilson. Davis broke his leg in a game against Q.P.R. after crashing John Spencer (would finish the game with a hat-trick). This happened in the month of January, and he didn't have time to recover to savour the sweet taste of promotion to the Premier League.

834.name: Remy
pages: * Christophe Remy is a player who has spent the whole of his playing career with Auxerre in his native France, although he seldom managed to force his way into the side on a regular basis. Last year he wasn't signed up by any club and was dogged by bad luck, even managing to break his shoulder blade. Things got at little better towards the end of the season when he had a spell on trial with Derby County, although he didn't finally manage to win himself a move to the Rams. Oxford United have shown plenty of faith in him and have offered him a 2 year contract. The best response to that faith that Remy has come up with, is to win himself a place in Denis Smith's starting line up.
* Remy is a player who plays at the back, occupying the left hand side of the pitch. A technically good player he gets down the flank often to support the attack, putting over some fine crosses.

* French  League Championship winners medal 1996.
* French Cup winners medal 1996.
x
* A product of the youth system at French club Auxerre, Remy had always played for the club since turning profesional. His debut came on 19th May 1990, against Nantes. The game ended 0-0.
* Last season he found himself without a club and also had the added misfortune of breaking a shoulder.

835.name: Whelan
pages: * After a number of seasons at Middlesbrough where his first first team opportunities were very few and far between, during the summer Phil Whelan decided to accept Denis Smith's offer to join Oxford United. Taking into account the length of the league season, this tall central defencer could become a very important player in the side, and will no doubt get the opportunity to justity his signing.

* An impressively powerful central defender, Phil Whelan makes the most of his height to dominate in the air in both penalty areas. He is virtually unbeatable in the air at the back and, despite his appearance brings the ball out comfortably from the defence, backed up as he is by a surprising turn of pace for a man of his size. In attack he is a dangerous player when he moves forward to get his head to the ball at dead ball situations. Still a young player, he needs to improve his touch on the ball if he wants to become a more complete player.
x
* Three Under-21 international apearances for England, scoring once.

* After coming through the club's junior sides, Phil Whelan moved up to Ipswich Town's first team squad on 2nd July 1990. His debut took place on 4th April 1992, in a game against Southend United. He came on for David Linighan, who was injured, and managed to score the side's winning goal in a 2-1 win. 
* It was from the 92-93 season onwards that the tall central defender made himself an automatic first team choice at Portman Road.
* In the final home game of the 93-94 season he suffered a serious ankle injury. Although the doctors announced that he wouldn't be back in action until 1995, Whelan made an amazing recovery and reappeared in  November 1994.
* On 3rd March 1995 he was transfered to Middlesbrough for £300,000 although he failed to make a first team appearance of any kind during his first season at Boro. His debut eventually came on 20th August 1995 after coming on for Jamie Pollock in the 85th minute of  Middlesbrough's 1-1 draw against Arsenal at Highbury. On 28th October of that same year he made his first full starting appearance, in a 2-0 defeat against Manchester United at Old Trafford. His first goal for Bryan Robson's side came on 8th April 1996; and earned Middlesbrough a point in a 1-1 draw in their visit to  Tottenham Hotspur.
* He was signed by Oxford United in the summer of 1997.

* Whelan went through a disappointing season with Middlesbrough, only being able to make 9 league appearances all season. Apart from not being in the best of form, Whelan also had to compete for a place in the side with more prestigious big name player such as the Italian Festa, as well as those who were already at teh club. As a result he made a much more limited contribution to Middlesbrough's season.

836.name: Gilchrist
pages: * Despite being quite young, the ability that Phil Gilchrist possesses suggest that he has a promising future ahead of him, providing he can steer clear of injury. His formed dropped noticeably when Matt Elliott moved on to Leicester City, but he managed to get back to his normal form when he teamed up with Darren Purse currently his regular partner at the heart of the Oxford United defence. He is one of Denis Smith's key men.

* A left footed central defender, Gilchrist is excellent in the air and dangerous at dead ball situations, where he attempts to benefit from the attention defenders pay to other players. He plays the ball around well, and, due to his good basic technique is a safe player when he has to bring the ball out at the back. Physically strong, he is a hard player when he goes in to win the ball, while in physical challenges he generally comes out on top.
x
x

* After coming through the junior ranks at Nottingham Forest, he signed professional in December 1990.
* He completed his contract and moved on to Middlesbrough in January 1992.
* Once again he saw out his contract and signed for Hartlepool United in November 1992. He made his debut on 19th December 1992 against Stoke City.
* He was transfered to Oxford United for £100,000 in February 1995. He made his debut on 18th February 1995 against Bristol Rovers and, one week later, he scored his first goal, which proved to be the winner, against Chester City.

* Gilchrist had another outstanding season and was one of the regulars in Denis Smith's starting line up. He noticed the absence of Matt Elliott when he signed for Leicester City, but he formed a good partnership with the men who subsequently replaced his ex-defensive colleague. His form was especially outstanding at the beginning of the season when he made a key contribution in helping Oxford to keep a number of clear sheets during that period.

837.name: Robinson
pages: * Les Robinson made the right back spot at Oxford United his own, almost from the day he arrived at the club, bringing security to the side from the full back position as well as moments of occasional danger when he moves forward to support the attack. A very difficult man to beat, he forms part of an Oxford United defence which has proved to be one of the most solid in the First Division. Once again, this season, he will almost certainly be operating on the right hand side of the defence.

* Robinson is a solid, compact right back with good speed, who is very difficult to take on for pace. A hard player when he goes in to win the ball, he shows great determination in everything he does. A good marker, he likes to get forward to support the attack whenever he gets the opporunity to do so. He is a good crosser of the ball and passes the ball accurately, very rarely giving away possession. He is basically a right footed player.
x
x

* A product of Chesterfield's youth system, he was released by the club and moved on to sign professional with Mansfield Town in October 1984. He made his league debut on 23rd March 1985 against Hereford United. 
* He completed his contract and signed for Stockport County in November 1986. He made his debut on 28th November 1986, against Hartlepool United, while he struck his first goal for the club on 2nd March 1987, against Orient.
* In March 1988 he was transfered to Doncaster Rovers for £10,000. He played his first game for the club on 2nd April 1988 against Port Vale, while his first goal came on 30th April 1988 against Brentford.
* He was tranfered to Oxford United in March 1990 for £150,000. His league debut came on 5th May 1990 against Port Vale, and he opened his account for the club on 21st August 1993 against WBA.

* Robinson almost made the Oxford United right back spot his own, missing games only through injury, and bringing great consistency to the side throughout the 38 appearances he made  during the course of the season.

838.name: M. Ford
pages:
* Now in his tenth season at Oxford United, Mike Ford has always shown himself to be a very valuable player in his poistion, playing in plenty of games each season and proving himself to be a very competitive full back. In defence he shows great character, and is constantly urging on his teammates.
* A genuine leader out on the park, he is respected by teammates and supporters alike, for the enthusiasm he shows for the game. After so many seasons at the club he has seen how, for the moment both Gilchrist and Purse have taken over as the central defenders in Denis Smith's side, although the veteran captain certainly won't be giving up and will fighting all the way to win back his first team place.

* Mike Ford currently holds down the left back spot at Oxford United, and is a real leader at the back, and retains enough of a turn of pace to make life difficult for opponents. Though not particularly tall, he is excellent in the air, is an accurate passer of the ball and can be trusted when he is in possession. His ability as a marker prevents him from moving forward to support the attack frequently, although when he does he shows himself to have a powerful shot in his left foot.
x
x

* After coming through the youth ranks at Leicester City he signed professional in February 1984. He didn't get the opportunity to make his debut for the Foxes, and moved on for a short spell with amateur club Devizes Town.
* He completed his contract and signed for Cardiff City in September 1984. He made his debut on 29th December 1984 against Leeds United, and scored his first goal in a Cardiff shirt against Barnsley on 23rd April 1985. 
* In June 1988 he was transfered to Oxford United for £150,000. He made his debut on 14th January 1989 against Sunderland and scored his first goal for the club on 6th May 1989 against Plymouth Argyle.

* Mike Ford completed another sensational season, and also managed to find the back of the net on 3 occasoins in the games he played during the course of the season. He played in a total of 42 games, during which he once again showed tremendous consistency at the heart of the Oxford United defence, making him an irreplaceable player for Denis Smith.

839.name: Jackson
pages: * A product of Oxford United's youth system Elliott Jackson is regarded as the man who will take over as Oxford United's goalkeeper in the not too distant future. His fine performances during the course of last season have confirmed the expectations that the club have of him. Nevertheless it seems that his waiting period is now over, as he is currently Oxford United's first choice in goal. He will be out to make sure that the position remains his throughout the current season, although with Whitehead waiting in the wings he is likely to have a real fight on his hands.

* Jackson is a keeper who shows great security in everything he does and has an outstanding ability to keep his composure for someone so young. He is dominant in the air, shows excellent judgement when he is called upon to come off his line. An agile keeper, he has outstanding reflexes.
x
x
x

* Jackson came into the side last season when Phil Whitehead was struck down by injury. He did a fine job on his debut, managing to keep a clean sheet against Tranmere Rovers. His total number of appearances was limited to just 3, following Whitehead's recovery which saw him kept out of the side for the remainder of the season.

840.name: Whitehead
pages: * Phil Whitehead is a keeper who has played for a number of clubs and whose quality hasn't gone unnoticed by Denis Smith. Very consistent, he is constantly ordering his defence around and, more importantly, spreads a great sense of security to the rest of the defence, something which is vital for any team. Despite this, Oxford United's present first team goalkeeper is young Elliott Jackson who is out to make sure that he remains in goal for the side.With great experience on his side Whitehead will be trying to turn things around and make himself number one in goal at Oxford..

* Whitehead is a very complete goalkeeper who shows great positional sense and an understanding with his defence. Good in the air he takes advantage of his height and judges well when he has to come off his line. Thanks to his good reflexes and his positional play he is a very difficult keeper to beat.
x
x

* After coming through the ranks at Halifax Town, he signed as a profesional in June 1988. He made his league debut on 27th September 1986 against Burnley. 
* In March 1990 he was transfered to Barnsley for £60,000. His first game for the club came on 17th August 1990 against Plymouth Argyle.
* He was loaned out to Halifax Town in March 1991, he made his debut on 9th March 1991 against Chesterfield. 
* In November 1991 he was loaned out to Scunthorpe United, where he played his first game on 30th of that same month against York City.
* He had another loan spell at Scunthorpe United in September 1992. 
* Two months later he was loaned out to Bradford City, where he made his debut for the Bantams on 9th January 1993 against Stockport County.
* In September 1993 he went out on loan to Oxford United, making his debut on 2nd October 1993 against Grimsby Town. His loan spell finally became a permanent move two months later for £75,000.

* A great season for Phil Whitehead during his first year in the First Division. The security of the Oxford United defence helped him to concede just one goal in six games during one of the team's best spells. However towards the end of the season the defence changed a lot and as a result Whitehead had to pick the ball out of the back of the net much more frequently. Nevertheless this didn't prevent him from being voted the club's Player of the Year by the supporters.

841.name: Devlin
pages:
* Signed for Sheffield United in March 1998. 
* A Birmingham City fan for a number of years, Paul Devlin returned to his birthplace, to play for one of the City's most important clubs. Devlin has gone on to become the side's goalscorer in chief and with Paul Furlong could well begin to form a striking partnership that should average a fair number of goals each season. Although originally a midfielder, playing further forward has been beneficial both for himself and the team.

* Devlin can perform either as a right winger, his more normal position or as a striker or even in midfield. Good with either foot, he has good pace and operating down his flank gets well involved in the game. He is always ready to receive the ball and is not afraid of responsibility. He has good dribbling ability and is a difficult player to contain once he has got the ball under control and is in a position to go at defenders. He puts over quality crosses and is, in short, a very complete winger. Very often he will try to cut inside onto his left to try and hit the target with his powerful and accurate left foot shot, a quality which sees him find the back of the net on a fairly regular basis. He also packs a fine shot in his right foot.

* Top Scorer at Notts County in 94-95.
* Top Scorer at Birmingham City in 96-97.
x

* Notts County signed Paul Devlin from Stafford Rangers in February 1992 for £40, 000, making his debut on 11th April 1992 against Coventry City and opening his goalscoring account on 27th February 1993 against Grimsby Town. 
* He was transfered to Birmingham City on 28th February 1996 and made his debut in the league on 2nd March 1996 against Sheffield United. He scored his first two goals for his home town club three days later against Wolverhampton Wanderers.

* Devlin lived up to all the high hopes that people had of him last season in the best possible way; by scoring goals. He averaged almost a goal every two games, ending the season as the club's leading scorer and won the recognition of the club's supporters being voted the club's Player of the Year. In total he played in 38 games, scoring 16 goals in the process.

842.name: Saunders
pages:
* Signed for Sheffield United in December 1996.
* A veteran of a number of clubs, among them Liverpool, where he failed to do the job he was  signed to do, score goals, Saunders  is now perhaps spending the final years of his career at Sheffield United, trying to be as effective as possible as the club try to get back in business  by returning to the Premier League.

* A battling centre forward, blessed with a great ability to get in first time efforts on goal, Dean   Saunders is especially dangerous when he has a few yards of space in which to move into. His speed  and change of pace often prove to be decisive in these moments. The Welshman also possesses  good shot in his right foot, and is a fine header of the ball. He always gives his best in every  game, and chases every ball, making it tremendously difficult for defenders to bring the ball out  from the back. He is an experienced player, more effective than brilliant, but capable of creating a  goal out of nothing.

* F.A. Cup winners medal  1992. 
* League Cup winners medal 1994.
* Charity Shield medal 1992.
* 58 full international appearances for Wales, with 20 goals to his credit. He made his debut  on 26th match 1986 in a game against the Republic of Ireland in Dublin.

* He is the son of Roy Saunders who played for Liverpool and Swansea between 1948 and 1963.  He began his career with hometown club, Swansea City. After coming through the youth ranks at  the club he turned professional on 24th June 1982. He had just turned 18 years of age. 
* He made his league debut on 22nd October 1983 in a game agaisnt  Charlton Athletic and went  on to score 9 goals in 30 games in the 1984-85 season.
* In March 1985 he went out on loan to Cardiff City, and on 7th August of that same year he signed   for Brighton & Hove Albion, as a free agent. During two consecutive seasons  (85-86 and 86-87)  he played in every game for the club.                       * On 12th March 1987 he was transfered to  Oxford United for 60,000 pounds, but in 1988 the club was relegated to the Second Division. 
* He signed for Derby County in 28th October 1988 for 1,000,000 pounds. In 1989 he scored the first  hat trick of his career in a League Cup game against Cambridge. The second came in March 1991,  the victims this time being Newcastle United.           * On 19th July 1991 Dean Saunders became  the most expensive signing in Liverpool's history. He cost 2,900,000. The deal became an especially   expensive one due to the interest of other clubs, particularly Everton.              * At Anfield he teamed up with his compatriot Ian Rush, with whom he formed the forward line   for the Welsh national side. Although Saunders ended the season as Liverpool's top scorer, he failed  to show the form that was expected of him. Even so he played as a member of the starting line up in  the F.A. Cup final which Liverpool won 2-0 against Sunderland.   * At the beginning of the 92-93  season Liverpool decided to transfer Saunders in order to finance the deal that took the Norwegian  Bjornebye to Anfield. Liverpool accepted the 2,300,000 pounds that the then Aston Villa manager   Ron Atkinson offered for the Welshman. He was a Villa player from 10th September 1992 and two  seasons later he went on to win a League Cup winners medal with the Villains.                    * Saunders ended the 94-95 season as Villa's top scorer with 15 goals in 39 games. In the summer of 1995 he decided to  move to Turkish club Galatasaray, managed at the time by Graeme Souness, his ex boss at Liverpool.              * Health problems surrounding his daughter Louisa, who suffers from asthma, saw him looking   for a return to England, at the end of his first season in Turkish football.
* On 27th June 1996 he signed for Nottingham Forest. The transfer fee was set at 1,500,000 pounds.

* Last season was, without any doubt, not one fo Dean Saunders' best in English football, and  more precisely at Nottingham Forest, scoring just 3 goals in 34 goals, apparently affected by  the team's poor run which eventually ended with Forest being relegatd to the First Division.

843.name: White
pages:
* At the beginning of the 90's, David White was one of the most outstanding forwards in English football, whose scent for goal even allowed him to get to make his debut for his national team, his only game at this level.
* However, after leaving Manchester City and his signing for Leeds United, his progress ground to a halt and he now hopes to re-launch a, what was in its time, promising career at Sheffield United. White's contribution at Sheffield has been good but the new coach of the Blades has placed his money on other players, only letting this player intervene in a sporadic fashion. Despite this, White has the quality to return to the starting line-ups and help the team get promoted to the Premier League, the place where they belong on the basis of their class.

* White can play both as a forward and as a link-man with the forwards, supporting the man furthest forward. He is very direct in his actions, trying to get to the goal as quickly as possible. Basically right-footed, he is not very elegant in his actions but effective. His enormous speed allows him to pop up in the box from very deep positions and he is hard to stop once he is on the run.  He has a good shot on goal from long range. He also heads the ball well, powerfully and well placed. He works hard and constantly pressurises the rival defence.
* Top scorer at Manchester City in the 91-92 and 92-93 seasons.

* White has been a youth and under-21 international with England before making his debut for the first team against Spain in Santander, his only appearance for his country. This game was the debut of Javier Clemente as the Spanish manager.  In this first and only game, White had a game to forget, wasting two clear chances against the goal defended by Andoni Zubizarreta, the Spanish keeper. Paul Ince also made his debut in this game.

* Originally from the lower ranks of Manchester City, White signs as a professional in November 1985. His league debut takes place on 27th September 1986 against Luton town after coming on for Neil McNab. His first goal comes on 13th December 1986 against West Ham United. 
* He moves to Leeds United in an exchange that sees David Rocastle go to Manchester City. He plays his first game for the club on 29th December 1993 against QPR, scoring his first goals on 4th April 1994, also against the London team. 
* He is finally acquired by Sheffield United in December 1994 for £500,000. He makes his debut on 18th November 1995 against Sunderland, opening his scoring account on 23rd December 1995 against Stoke City.

* White had a disappointing season when his performance in previous seasons is taken into account. He jousted with Ward for a place in the starting eleven and never managed to reach his best form during the course of the season. In total he played 37 games and only scored 6 goals.

844.name: Taylor
pages:
* Gareth Taylor is a classic centre forward who works well for the team and who is not selfish in his actions, being basically a team player. Despite the fact that after his arrival from Crystal Palace he had a bit of a dry spell, he had a good understanding with Andy Walker which could be important in the future. 
* His good role with Sheffield United in seasons gone-by has helped him to keep his place in the Welsh national team, increasing his number of international appearances. He promises to be an important player for his country in the future. 
* Although he might not be a starter in the Blades' attack due to the presence of men such as Katchouro, Deane and Fjortoft amongst others, his opportunity will come during the course of the season and it is certain that Taylor will try not to waste it, showing that he can be a player who Nigel Spackman make use of.

* Taylor is a very hard-working forward who stands out for his aerial power, and rival defences can't afford themselves the luxury of not picking him up as he finishes very well.  He is a team player who works well pressurising the rival defence and holding on to the ball while waiting for players to arrive from the midfield. He shoots with either foot without thinking about it, although his right is better. In the technical aspect, he doesn't stand out at all, and should try and improve in this respect  He is hard to mark when he receives the ball with his back to the goal, as he is able to shield it and pass to the best placed team-mate. Fairly quick and tenacious. he works the spaces well to create space for other players.
* Top scorer at Sheffield United in the 96-97 season together with Katchouro and Walker.

* Under-21 international for Wales seven times, he makes his debut against Albania on 15th November 1995 in a classification game for the 96 European Championship. In total he has played three games for the first team.
x

* A starter at the beginning of the league before Katchouro was signed, from this moment on his name disappeared from the teamsheet although he continued to figure in Howard Kendall's plans. At the end of the league he had played 34 games and scored 12 goals, making him joint topscorer with Walker and Katchouro.

845.name: Walker
pages:
* Signed from Glasgow Celtic to solve the problems that the team was having up front, the contribution of Andy Walker was vital for the team to avoid the drop to the Second Division two years ago and for the team to finish in a comfortable position in the final classification. 
* Almost a personal signing on the part of the club's ex-coach, Howard Kendall, his acquisition was very positive for the club, bringing a very intelligent footballer who had a perfect understanding with his team-mates. In principle he could be one of the men to fill the places in the Sheffield forward line although at the moment Spackman prefers to choose between Katchouro, Deane and Fjortoft.

* Walker is a centre forward of a very high quality who, thanks to his speed and skill on the turn, can come out of difficult situations or create scoring chances for himself. Very intelligent, he has a good playing vision and good first-time control of the ball setting himself up perfectly for the shot. Good in the air despite not being tall, he is quick in the area and has a special sense of opportunism, something which brings him a lot of goals. He shoots with both feet although his right is better.

* League Champion with Glasgow Celtic 87-88. 
* Cup Champion with Glasgow Celtic 87-88. 
* Runner-up in the League Cup with Glasgow Celtic 94-95. 
* Top scorer at Motherwell in the 86-87 season together with Steve Jirk.
* Top scorer at Glasgow Celtic in the 87-88 season. 
* Top scorer at Bolton Wanderers in the 91-92 and 92-93 seasons.
* Walker has made three full international appearances for Scotland and one at the under-21 level.

* Motherwell sign him from the amateur club Baillieston Juniors in the summer of 1984. He makes his league debut on 1st December 1984 against Meadowbank Thistle and he scores his first league goal on 20th March 1985 against Airdrieonians. 
* Walker is transferred to Glasgow Celtic in the summer of 1987, scoring two goals on his debut on 8th August 1987 against Morton. 
* He is loaned to Newcastle United in September 1991 but only plays two games, the first of them on 21st September 1991 against Millwall. 
* He is loaned to Bolton Wanderers in January of 1992 and his transfer comes through a month later for £160,000.  He manages to score on his debut against Exeter City on the 11th January 1992. 
* Celtic sign him in the summer of 1994, and he scores his first goal in this second spell at the club against Falkirk on 13th August 1994, the equaliser. 
* He is transferred to Sheffield United in February 1996 for £500,000. He makes his debut for the Blades on 24th February 1996 against Barnsley and his first goal comes 6 days later against Birmingham City.

* Despite being on the Blades' substitute bench for a lot of time, Walker managed to find a regular spot for himself in the teams fielded by Howard Kendall. His good performances made him one of the key players at the club. In total he played 37 games and scored 12 goals, equalling Katchouro and Taylor as the team's top scorers.

846.name: Hamilton
pages:
* Signed for Sheffield United in March 1998.
* Despite being a very consistent player and always fitting in with the needs of the team he didn't finally arrive on the scene until a couple of seasons ago and, since then, he had become an important member of the Baggies' side. He had put in such complete performances that he had gone on to make himself one of the side's most outstanding players. As a result it certainly wouldn't be a surprise to see him out on the park in a WBA shirt.

* Ian Hamilton can do a job in all the positions in the midfield, although he is principally a right sided midfield player. An intelligent player, he has the ability to play the right pass at the right time, a quality which allows him to set up plenty of goalscoring chances for his teammates, while he is also a player who never strays too far from his position, always remaining well placed. Defensively he makes a good contribution, while he also possesses a good shot in his right foot, although it is something he doesn't use too frequently.
x
x

* A product of Southampton's youth system, he signed professional in December 1985. Nevertheless he failed to make a first team appearance for the Saints during his time at the club. 
* In March 1988 he was transfered to Cambridge United in exchange for £20,000. His debut for the club couldn't have been better, finding the back of the net against Darlington on 1st April 1988. 
* Scunthorpe United signed him in December 1988 for £15,000. He made his first appearance in a Scunthorpe shirt on 26th December 1988 against Hartlepool United and opened his account for the club on 2nd January 1989, against Halifax Town. 
* In June 1992, he was transfered to WBA for £170,000. He made his debut on 15th August 1992 against Blackpool, while his first goal for the club came on 2nd September 1992 against Stockport County.

* A very complete season for Ian Hamilton, who made his usual darting runs from the midfield causing plenty of danger for WBA's rivals. His performances were very much to the liking of both of the club's managers during the course of last season, Alan Buckley and later Ray Harford, proving to be a fundamental part of the plans of both men. In total he played in 39 games, scoring 5 times, as well as being voted Albion's Player of the Year, by the Baggies' supporters.

848.name: B. Ford
pages:
* Signed for Sheffield United during the 97-98 season.
* Bobby Ford is a player who possesses tremendous quality and has a very bright future ahead of him. His performances in the Second Division demonstrated just why everybody has such high hopes of him. A player of enormous class, he has the ability to dictate the pace at which the team plays. The games he played in the First Division went further in confirming these expectations.

* Ford is a good midfield organizer and a fine passer of the ball, having the ability to create a clear goalscoring chance with just one pass. He is more at home as a link up player between the forwards and the midfield than as a right sided midfielder. An intelligent footballer who is helped out by his excellent dribbling ability, he has good ball control in both feet. Though fairly strong, he more often than not loses out in physical challenges. In one on one situations with the goalkeeper he shows his quality and keeps his cool well to finish the job off. Though he makes a limited contribution defensively, he is an outstanding player at set pieces.
x
x

* After coming through the youth ranks at Oxford United, he signed professional in October 1992. He made his league debut on 10th October 1993 against Stoke City, and struck his first goal on 26th December 1994 against Peterborough United.

* An outstanding season for the young product of Oxford United's youth system, he had an important role to play for the side throughout the whole campaign. His best moments came when he was given a free role in the midfield, posing a real threat to the opposition. He played in a total of 33 games but, unfortunately, was unable to crown a fine season by finding the back of the net.

849.name: Stuart
pages:
* Signed for Sheffield United in November 1997.
* Graham Stuart is another talented product of the Chelsea youth system, and is a player who seems to get better with each season. His class decorated Everton's play with skill, imagination and, of course, work rate. A key member of the side, he had a knack of scoring in big games. His progress seems to be continuous, something for which both Sheffield United and their fans are thankful.

* A very complete footballer, Stuart plays down the right hand side of the midfield, although for the amount of ground he covers he sometimes appears to be playing as a winger as well. He has exquisite technique, good ball control and can play the ball around accurately with either foot. A great passer of the ball, he stands out in the attacking side of the game for his ability to improvise as well as his excellent vision. He rarely gives the ball away, while his ability on the ball allows him to calmly sort out the most complicated of situations and play a quick one touch game. He scores plenty of goals as a  result of his good positioning and powerful shooting. He is, with all the qualites he possesses,  an exceptional footballer.
*  F.A. Cup winners medal 94-95.

* 5 under-21 international appearances for England, with 2 goals.
* 5 youth international appearances, scoring once.

* He arrived at Chelsea in March 1985, when he was just 15 years old. A graduate of the F.A. School of Excellence, he signed for the Stamford Bridge club on 15th June 1989.
* He made his league debut at Stamford Bridge against Crystal Palace (3-0) on 16th  April 1990  with Stuart scoring one of the goals.
* The following season he scored 4 goals in 19 games, two of those coming against Arsenal and Liverpool, that season's two main title challengers.
* On 19th August 1993 he was transfered to Everton for 850,000 pounds..
* He was one of the stars of the 1995 F.A. Cup semi-final against Tottenham, scoring the second of Everton's four goals. He was a member of the starting line up in the final against Manchester United.
* Signed for Sheffield United in November 1997.

* He made 35 appearances and was one of the key men in Joe Royle's side. He found the back of the net on five occasions, although, like the rest of the side, he had something of an inconsistent campaign.

850.name: Quinn
pages: * Recently promoted from the lower ranks of Sheffield United, Wayne Quinn is reckoned by many to be a player who could become one of the Blades' stars in next to no time. His great technique and composure on the pitch have justly earned him the status of starter in the teams fielded by Nigel Spackman. With a great future ahead of him, Quinn hopes to help the club attain promotion to the Premier League.

* Blessed with a sensational left with which he can do true marvels, Quinn can play at several positions on the pitch although always out on the left. In the lower ranks he played in the midfield but since his arrival in the first squad, his position has basically been that of left back, where he performs very well. He has all the resources to become a great player.
x
* Quinn is an England under-21 international.
* From the Sheffield United youth squad, he makes his debut on the first day of the 97-98 season against Sunderland.
x

851.name: Ebbrell
pages: * A product of the Everton youth squad, John Ebbrell was one of the most promising players at the club, as was shown by his making international appearances in the lower categories. However, his progress was not as good as was hoped and the injuries he suffered never allowed him to reach his best form. With the doors to the Everton first team firmly shut, Ebbrell decides to join Sheffield last season although his contribution to the Blades effort has been minimal. Waiting for a run of good luck, Ebbrell is holding out for his chance.

* A defensively minded midfielder, Ebbrell usually plays in front of the backs and tries to distribute the ball for the attacking moves, helped by his good vision. A hard-working footballer, he is noted for winning the ball back. In his incorporations into the attack he can surprise with his powerful shot from a distance. He has the capability to contribute somewhat more to the team.
* FA Cup Champion in 94-95.

* 1 B international appearance. 
* 14 times under-21 international. 
* 2 youth international appearances - 1 goal.

* Originally from the lower ranks where he was a trainee, he signs as a professional for Everton on 7th November 1986. 
* He makes his league debut on 4th February 1989 in a game against Wimbledon, coming on as a substitute. 
* In the second half of the 94-95 season he suffers several injuries which keep him out the team and prevent him from playing in the Cup final against Manchester United. 
* Up till the end of the 94-95 season he had received 26 yellow cards.
* Transferred to Sheffield United during the 96-97 season for £1 million pounds. His first and only game for the Blades is on the 29th of March against Reading.

* An unfortunate season for John Ebbrell who saw how he was the captain against Manchester United one day and the next he would be a substitute. What's more, an injury limited him to 7 games for Everton. Howard Kendall, the manager at the time at Sheffield United and future manager at Everton, signed him but another injury limited him to one appearance for the Blades.

852.name: Hutchison
pages:
* Nobody doubts that Don Hutchison is a man with a lot of quality but due to continual problems with his character and his inconsistency on the pitch, he is a player who has not met the expectations that people had placed in him. 
* When he was playing at Liverpool, Hutchison became a very promising player but his difficult character, at times violent for no apparent reason, made the club at Anfield loose interest in him. Now with his arrival at Bramall Lane, he hopes to make up for lost time and show that he is still an interesting player for any important team in the Premier League. While he is waiting, he hopes to be able to collaborate as much as possible from the substitutes' bench in order to help his team earn promotion to the top flight of English football.

* Hutchison is a midfielder who can also play as a forward, his position when he turned professional. He has a lot of physical power and is quick, also being a man with good technique which allows him to set up a lot of goals. He is noted for getting into dangerous positions, and is basically an opportunistic man who is in the right place at the right time. He is good in the air which makes him dangerous at set-plays. He doesn't have a good turn but in the area he is able to get by, being a very quick player with a goal instinct. He is tough in his zone, a man who fights hard.
x
* Hutchison has played once for the Scotland B team.

* Trained in the lower ranks of Hartlepool United, he signs as a professional in March 1990.  He makes his league debut on 7th October 1989 against Scunthorpe United and scores his first goal just 10 days later against Torquay United. 
* He is transferred to Liverpool for £175,000 in November 1990. His first game with the Reds is on 31st March 1992 against Notts County and his first league goal is Liverpool's winner against Sheffield Wednesday on 3rd October 1992. This season is his best with the Anfield side. 
* West Ham United sign him in 1994 for £1.5 million. In his league debut for the Hammers, he scores a conciliation goal in a game against Newcastle United on 31st August 1994, the final score is 1-3. 
* He is finally transferred to Sheffield United in January 1996 for £1.2 million. His first game for the Blades is on 13th January 1996 against Tranmere Rovers and exactly one month later he scores his first goal against Millwall. 
* At the time, he was the most expensive signing, both for West Ham and for Sheffield United.

* Hutchison mixed moments of brilliance when he played in the midfield and joined up with the forwards with others a lot less memorably where he hardly contributed at all to the Blades. He had problems with suspensions, accumulating too many due to his difficult character. His season was also marred by an injury in the decisive game against Crystal Palace, which in the end saw the Eagles promoted to the Premier League. In total, he played 41 games and scored only three goals.

853.name: Spackman
pages: * See manager's profile.

* Spackman is a midfielder of a defensive cut and is a great ball winner. He plays in front of the defence as a pivot and covers perfectly for the centre backs when they push up into the attack. He is also noted for his interceptions helping out the wide defenders. Very intelligent, he reads the games perfectly. He is a good passer, always in short where it is almost impossible to see him loose the ball. He has great physical strength and positioning allowing him to cover a lot of ground without wearing himself out. He is still quite quick despite his age.

* Second Division Champion with Chelsea in 1984. 
* League Cup Runner-up with Liverpool in 1987. 
* First Division Champion with Liverpool in 1988. 
* Scottish League Champion with Glasgow Rangers in 1990, 1991 and 1992.
* Scottish Cup Champion with Glasgow Rangers in 1992.
x

* Spakman's contract with the amateur club Andover ends and he signs for Bournemouth in May 1980. He makes his league debut on 16th August 1980 against York City and scores his first goal as a professional against Doncaster Rovers on 6th December 1980. 
* He is transferred to Chelsea in June 1983 for £40,000. He plays his first game for the London team on 27th August 1983 against Derby County scoring the first goal of the game. 
* Liverpool sign him in February 1987 for £400,000. He makes his debut on 28th January 1987 against Southampton. 
* He is transferred to QPR in February 1989 in exchange for £500,000. He disputes his first game on 4th February 1989 against Millwall and scores his only goal for the London team on 8th April 1989 against Wimbledon. 
* In November 1989 his move to Glasgow Rangers comes through for £500,000. He makes his debut in the Scottish league on 2nd December 1989 against Hearts and he scores his only goal with the club against the Old Firm, that is, in the derby against Glasgow Celtic, on 2nd January 1990, a goal which turns out to be the winner. 
* He is transferred to Chelsea in September 1992 for £485,000 with his first game played on 12th September 1992 against Norwich City. 
* His contract expires and he signs for Sheffield United in the summer of 1996, with his debut for the Blades coming on the 17th of August against Reading. 
* In the summer of 1997 he is made the manager at Sheffield United, stepping into Howard Kendall's shoes, who moves to Everton.

* Constantly bothered by an injury, Spackman manages to produce some great games at Sheffield United, his best one being the final game of the play-offs against Crystal Palace where his veteran know-how was important for the Blades but not enough to prevent them from being defeated. In total he played 23 games.

854.name: Whitehouse
pages:
* Dane Whitehouse is a key man for Sheffield United on the left, from where he produces a lot of danger, working hard for the Blades. After the arrival of Howard Kendall as manager at Bramall Lane, he was one of the few who kept his place after the revolution made by the coach. 
* Very consistent in his actions, he is a player who gives his all on the pitch and who fights constantly, making him a valuable player for the team. The great firmness in his game makes him essential for the club and this season he should occupy his position once again on the left, hoping to make up for a somewhat disappointing season. After the departure of Kendall, the situation with Spackman will not change, he will continue to figure in the Blades' starting eleven.

* Whitehouse is a left winger who not only helps out a lot in attack but also in defence, and is an untiring worker on his wing in both tasks. Very left-footed, he as a great vision which allows him to pass well. He has a good individual technique, having a good turn and putting over some good crosses. He is outstanding in attack where he gets into dangerous positions and his forays bring with them a lot of danger, surprising the defence by popping up from deep positions. When he enters the box he looks for the far post well, finishing well with both his head and his feet. He has a good medium and long range shot.
x
x

* Originally from the lower ranks of Sheffield United, he signs as a professional in July 1989.  He makes his league debut on 15th October 1988 against Blackpool and scores his first league goal against Bradford City on 3rd MArch 1990.

* Whitehouse had a spectacular season despite an injury that kept him out for a month. On returning, he recovered his place in the team and ended the league as one of the Blades' most consistent players, taking part in 30 games and scoring 6 goals.

855.name: Katchouro
pages: * Petr Katchouro has been one of the best signings made by Howard Kendall since he took up the reigns at Bramall Lane. A very complete forward and very promising, his actions during last season, despite not making a good start to the season, have showed that the club made a good signing when they bought him from Dynamo Minsk and for a cheap price. He has as a reference his performance last season and his important appearances for the Bielorussia team, making him, in principle, one of the men to occupy the attacking positions alongside Deane and Fjortoft.

* Katchouro is a very complete centre forward who has almost everything. He is physically very strong and it is hard to get the better of him in a collision, which is combined with great pace and verticality. He dribbles well, has good control and heads well. He is not selfish in front of goal and passes in these situations if there is a team-mate better placed. He finds space well, opening up the wings and allowing the midfielders to come through into the gap. He has good technical resources and a good playing vision. He has a good shot on goal with his right, and will use it without thinking about it.
x
* Petr Katchouro has made 18 international appearances for Bielorrussia.
* Sheffield United signed him in the summer of 1996 for £600,000.

* The start of his spell in English football was not that good for Katchouro who started as a substitute and was even substituted when on as a substitute. However, things didn't take long to change for the Bielorrussian international and his great season was finished off when he was awarded the prize of best player at the club as voted by the fans, a season where he also finished joint top scorer for the Blades alongside Taylor and Walker.

857.name: Sandford
pages:
* Lee Sandford returns to Sheffield after a short spell in Reading.
* Lee Sandford is a left back who was a Stoke City player for his first seven seasons as a professional before moving to Sheffield United, a club which had already shown an interest in him.  However, things did not go as Sandford would have liked and he didn't get to play much in the Blades' starting elevens.  Finally, he decided to move to Reading.

* A left-footed defender, he is very versatile, able to play as left back, central defender or even sweeper.  Solid and safe in his actions, he doesn't join in the attack much, rather dedicating himself to defence.  He is good in the air and a tough but fair tackler, and a true leader.  He is always very attentive of the game's development and it is hard to take him by surprise.
x
* English youth international.

* Trained in the Portsmouth youth squad, Sandford signs as a professional in December 1985.  He makes his league debut on the 26/10/85 against Millwall and his first goal is on the 26/9/87 against Wimbledon. 
* He is transferred to Stoke City in December 1989 for £140,000.  He plays his first game on the 26/12/89 against Newcastle United and scores his first goal for the club on the 13/1/90 against Portsmouth, his former team.
* Sheffield United sign him in the summer of 1996 for £450,000.  His debut for the Blades is on the 17th of August against Reading and he scores his first goal for the club against Oldham Athletic on the 7th of September.
* He is transferred to Reading during the summer of 1997.

* Sandford was the first choice left back at Sheffield United at the start of the league but lost his privileged place after the acquisition of Holdsworth and the arrival of Nilsen on the left.  From this moment on, he hardly returned to the starting line-up except when necessary due to suspension or injury, but producing good performances.  In total he played 30 games and scored 2 goals.

858.name: O'Connor
pages:
* Signed for Sheffield United February 1998. 
* A product of the Everton youth system, O'Connor had to wait almost three years before he was given the opportuniry to make his debut in the Premier League, doing so against no less an opponent than Ryan Giggs, one of the best players in the championship, and at Old Trafford.

* He is considered basically as a central defender, where he is most comfortable, although he has occasionally lined up as right back. An authoritative player, he orders his fellow defenders about, and shows good pace and discipline at the back although he rarely moves forward in support of the attack. Still very young, he needs to be given time to confirm his quality and work on his weaknesses.
x

* 3 under-21 international appearances for England.
* England youth international.

* After coming through the youth ranks at Everton, he signed professional on 28th October 1993. He made his league debut in a defeat, on 21st February 1996, against Manchester United at Old Trafford (2-0). O'Connor was given the job of marking Ryan Giggs. 
* Signed for Sheffield United February 1998.
* He failed to make a first team appearance throughout the course of last season.

859.name: Derry
pages: x

* He is one of the most interesting talents at Notts. Several teams from higher divisions have been watching him and it is possible that in the not too distant future he will make the jump.  He is an excellent passer and can also play as a midfielder.
x
x
x
* Despite being known as a right back, Derry played for most of the season in the midfield.  He caused a good impression and his play caught the eye of several teams.

860.name: McGrath
pages: * Paul McGrath is one of the most veteran players in all of English football. But he is also one of the players with the most brilliant career, both at the clubs where he has played and with the Irish team, where he was almost an institution. His continual knee-injuries have not managed to put an end to a model career. McGrath goes into yet another season in England with the same illusion as in the first. Currently he is playing at Sheffield United, the club he chose after he considered himself personally insulted by West Ham United who wanted him to go through a trial period. With the Blades, his impact is immediate and the presence of the veteran central defender could be a positive point for the team trying to reach the Premier League.

* A strong, well-built centre back, a great defender. His stature allows him to dominate the aerial game in defence, although he also creates danger in attack at set-plays. In the last few years he has lost speed, although his positioning is better. We are looking at a good footballer in the twilight of his career, although his veteran status and experience could still allow him to perform acceptably for Sheffield United.

* FA Cup Champion 84-85 with Manchester United. 
* League Cup Champion 93-94 and 95-96 with Aston Villa. 
* Charity Shield Medal 85. 
* Voted Player of the year 92-93 by the Footballers' Association.

* 76 full international caps for the Republic of Ireland. He made his debut against Italy on the 5th of February 1985 in Dublin. Present in the 88 European Championship in Germany and in the 90 World Cup in Italy and the 94 World Cup in the United States. 
* 1 B international appearance. 
* 1 under-21 international appearance.

* Despite being born in England, McGrath was discovered by Manchester United while playing in the modest Saint Patricks in the Republic of Ireland league. He is transferred to the Old Trafford club on 30th April 1982 for £30,000. 
* His debut occurs on the 13th of November 1982 in a game against Tottenham Hotspur. 
* In the 85-86 season he is second in the vote for the "Footballer of the Year" behind Gary Lineker. 
* In the 87-88 season, an injury keeps him out of the team for several games, although he recovers in time to play in the European Championship in Germany. 
* On the 3rd of August 1989 he is transferred to Aston Villa for £400,000.
* He is considered the best defender in the history of the Republic of Ireland. 
* Once the 96-97 season is underway, he is transferred to Derby County for £100,000. His debut for the Rams is on the 12th of October 1996 against Newcastle United. 
* His contract with Derby County expires and in the summer of 1997 he signs for Sheffield United.

* Last season McGrath joined Derby County from Aston Villa. Despite being very much a veteran, his capability is still intact and he can play solidly during the course of the season as was demonstrated last year. In total he played in 24 games.

861.name: Marker
pages: * Nicky Marker is one of Sheffield United's most experienced players, used to battling hard in the lower ranks of English football and rub shoulders with the best footballers in the country during the course of his spell at Blackburn Rovers. Signed during the summer by the Blades, his veteran status is one of his biggest plusses when it comes to finding a spot in the starting eleven put out by Nigel Spackman, something he has managed at the beginning of this season.

* A veteran central defender, hard and a good marker, Nicky Marker can also play effectively as a defensively oriented midfielder. A disciplined and versatile footballer, he is cut from the same cloth as the rough backs, physically strong, dominant in the air and technically limited. Therefore, his contribution to the attacking game is limited and he channels all his efforts into winning the ball back.
x
x

* Nicky Marker started in the footballing world at Exeter City, the biggest club in his native town. Trained in the youth squad, he made his debut for the first team aged just 16 on 17th October 1981 against Burnley. He had to wait until 4th May 1983 to turn professional, the day before his 18th birthday. 
* After several seasons in the Third and Fourth Divisions he is transferred to Plymouth Argyle on 31st October 1987, with the price set at £95,000. Undisputed starter, his performance caught the eye of Kenny Dalglish, who brought him to Blackburn Rovers on the 23rd of September 1992. His price had risen to £500,000, although part of the operation was financed by an exchange of the players Keith Hill and Craig Skinner. Three days later he made his debut as a substitute at Ewood Park against Oldham Athletic. 
* The defensive firmness of Kevin Moran and Colin Hendry prevent Marker from enjoying many chances during the 92-93 season, although his situation changed slightly the following year. Unfortunately, he missed the 94-95 season completely due to a ligament injury and could not take part in the Rovers' league title. 
* The forced absence of Colin Hendry in several games of the 95-96 season once again opened the doors to the first team temporarily. And so, on the 30th of December he scores his first goal in the Premier League against Tottenham Hotspur (2-1). 
* He is signed by Sheffield United during the summer of 1997.

* Present for almost all of the season in the reserves team of Blackburn Rovers, Marker was one of the first options to step in when the injuries affected the first choice defenders.  Always solid in his performance, he was never disappointing during the 7 games he played.

862.name: Holdsworth
pages:
* After playing more than 300 games for Watford, David Holdsworth put an end to years of speculation over his next club when he signed for Sheffield United in the summer of 1996. 
* A very consistent central defender, he doesn't make mistakes. His signing was made to reinforce a back-line at Sheffield United which wasn't exactly short of men but which welcomed a man of his capability. In fact, his impact was instant with the Blades, being one of the best men and captain as the league progressed. Currently, completely settled at the club, he forms a defensive line together with McGrath and Tiler which will be essential in their attempt to earn promotion to the Premier League.

* A very solid defender, Holdsworth is a very quick centre back for his weight and stature, but outstanding above all for his aerial power, which also makes him dangerous at set-plays. Very agile and a good marker, he sticks close to his man and makes the rival forward uncomfortable. He is always attentive and reacts quickly to mistakes of his or of a team-mate. He has an acceptable technique but he doesn't complicate life too much. Despite usually playing as a centre back, he is also being aligned as the team's sweeper by Spackman.
x

* An English youth and under-21 international once, making his debut on 7th February 1989 against Greece coming on as a substitute for Steve Redmond, currently at Oldham Athletic. In this English team were Paul Merson, Stuart Ripley and Lee Sharpe amongst others.

* Originally from the lower ranks of Watford, he signed as a professional in November 1986.  He made his debut in the league on 29th August 1988 against WBA and scored his first goal on 28th February 1989 against Barnsley.
* He is transferred to Sheffield United in September 1996. His debut with the Blades is on 12th October against Tranmere Rovers and he scores his first goal for the team at Bramall Lane against Swindon Town on 1st February.
* He is the twin brother of Dean Holdsworth, former Wimbledon forward and now at Bolton Wanderers.

* Holdsworth had an amazing season at Sheffield United in his first year at the club. After recovering from an injury, Holdsworth was a regular for Howard Kendall in the Blades defence, forming a sensational partnership with Michel Vonk. His leadership qualities were recognised when he was made captain to the detriment of Mark Patterson. In total he played 37 games and scored a goal.

863.name: Vonk
pages:
* Michel Vonk is a central defender who was much appreciated by his former manager, Howard Kendall, as he was under his orders at Manchester City and the manager was very insistent in signing the player to help in the  effort for promotion to the Premier League last year. Unfortunately, the team's performance dropped when Vonk was out after the month of November and the Blades' aspirations were about to go to ground, though in the end they made it to the play-offs. 
* After his injury he is now recovered and Vonk hopes to figure in the plans of the Sheffield United trainer, currently Nigel Spackman, to help as much as possible in the promotion bid to the Premier League. Even so, this will be difficult due to the sensational form of Tiler, McGrath and Holdsworth in the defence, although he will have his chance during the course of the league.

* Vonk occupies the position of central defender very effectively and is outstanding for his battling in the air where he is a specialist, and is also dangerous for the rival team in set-plays. He his tough when fighting for the ball but always fair. He moves the ball well, passing in short quickly and simply, not complicating things unnecessarily. A good marker, he tries to read the moves, taking advantage of a good turn of speed, something surprising in a man as bulky as he. He doesn't usually leave the defence except when there is a free-kick or corner for his team.
x
x

* He is signed by Manchester City in November 1992 for £500,000 from the the Dutch club SVV Dordrecht. He makes his league debut on 21st March 1993 against Nottingham Forest and scores his first goal on English soil on 29th August 1993 against Oldham Athletic. 
* He is loaned to Oldham Athletic during the course of the 95-96 season. He plays his first game on 18th November 1995 against Wolverhampton Wanderers. 
* Sheffield United sign him for £350,000 in December 1995. He makes his league debut on 23rd December 1995 against Stoke City.

* Vonk started the season where he finished off the previous season, that is to say in the starting line-up and he had some truly sensational games with Sheffield United.  Unfortunately an injury to his knee put an end to this run in December, and he then had problems getting back into the team. In total he played 17 games and scored a goal.

864.name: Short
pages:
* Brother of the Everton player, Craig Short, Chris is a right back who hadn't had many chances at Notts County in recent times and decided to accept the offer from Sheffield United in the month of December. 
* He wasn't wrong in his move, as since then he has played as a starter on the right flank and showed that he has plenty of ability. After getting over a season in which injuries limited his performance, Short will try and find a slot for himself on Nigel Spackman's teamsheet this season.

* Short is a very attacking right back, who pushes up when he has the chance without thinking it over much. His incorporations into the attack usually finish with a good cross. A man who covers a lot of ground, he is also powerful and quick, a good marker and anticipates his rivals well. He is tough when fighting for the ball and in the air is acceptable.  He can also play as a central defender in times of emergency.
x
x

* When his contract with the amateur club Pickering Town finishes he moves to Scarborough in July 1988.  He makes his league debut on 29th April 1989 against Darlington and scores his first goal in the competition against Halifax Town on 27th September 1989. 
* He is transferred to Notts County in September 1990 for £100,000. He plays his first game for the club on 30th October 1990 against Charlton Athletic and scores his first goal against Newcastle United on 6th April 1991.
* He is loaned to Huddersfield Town in December 1994, making his debut on 26th December 1994 against Hull City. 
* Sheffield United sign him in December 1995 in an exchange that sends Paul Rodgers to Notts County. He plays his first game for the Blades on 13th January 1996 against Tranmere Rovers.

* Despite having a season where the injuries were centre-stage, Short never disappointed Howard Kendall in his performance on the pitch. His bad luck even went with him to the play-offs as, before the game against Crystal Palace, in which he was going to be present in the team fighting for promotion to the Premier League, he twisted his ankle and missed the game. During the league he played 24 times.

865.name: Nilsen
pages:
* During the years that he has been at Sheffield United, Roger Nilsen, a Norwegian international has shown that professionalism and versatility are his biggest virtues when it comes to finding a place in the team which was managed by Howard Kendall and current is lead by Nigel Spackman. 
* The great consistency that this player boasts of mean that you rarely see him make a mistake.  His know-how have made him essential for the Blades and have allowed him to regain his place in the national side as a recognition of his good performance for the English club.

* Nilsen is a very solid defender who can play in several positions though his best one is left back, but he can also occupy the centre of defence or even operate as a sweeper.  He is pretty quick and hard when tackling. His lack of height prevents him from dominating in the air. He has a good shot with his left but has, as yet, been unable to open his account for the Blades. He has good technique and is comfortable with the ball at his feet, being a good passer, both in short and over long range although his speciality are balls that switch sides.  He only joins in the attack when he sees a clear cut situation and normally stays as a rearguard. Although he is technically good, he never unduly complicates things. Finally, he has a powerful throw-in.
x

* Nilsen has made 28 international appearances for Norway. 
* Travelled to the 94 United States World Cup but didn't play a single game.

* Sheffield United sign him from the Norwegian team Viking Stavanger in November 1993 for £550,000. The Norwegian international played his first game for the Blades on 6th November 1993 against Norwich City.

* After Gary Abblett's move to Birmingham City, Nilsen occupies the position of centre back until the arrival of Holdsworth, allowing him to move back to his normal position, the left flank. His form was consistent during the course of the league, playing 33 games and regaining his place in the Norwegian side.

866.name: Tracey
pages:
* Signed from Wimbledon in 1988, Simon Tracey has shown his undoubted quality during the course of the years that he has been at Sheffield United. However, the arrival of Alan Kelly has meant that this keeper appears more sporadically with the Blades, taking advantage of the few games when Kelly is injured. 
* From this moment on he has been at a succession of teams but Tracey has always been a loan player, although last season he showed that he is still a valuable keeper for Sheffield United. Even so, to become the first choice again he will not only have to battle with Alan Kelly but also avoid injury problems that have cut short some of the good runs that might have made him a regular in the first team. 
* In the present season, this charismatic player, respected by the crowd at Bramall Lane, will have the chance to try and oust Kelly from his position, something he has managed at the beginning of the league. An opportunity that Tracey hopes not to miss.

* Tracey is a complete goalkeeper and very brave and decisive in the 50-50 balls. His great reflexes and speed make him hard to take by surprise in an isolated move. It should also be said that, at times, he is somewhat irregular, sometimes brilliant and sometimes insecure, above all in aerial balls. He positions himself well between the posts allowing him to make a lot of saves he wouldn't otherwise manage.
x
x

* Trained in the Wimbledon youth squad, he signs as a professional in February 1986. He makes his debut in the league on 27th August 1988 against Arsenal in the first game of the 88-89 season where the team is thrashed 1-5. He doesn't play for the Dons again. 
* Sheffield United sign him in October 1988 for £7,500. He makes his debut on 11th March 1989 against Huddersfield Town. 
* He is loaned to Manchester City in October 1994 to cover for the injuries to the first choice and understudy, Tony Coton and Andy Dibble, respectively. He plays his first game on 29th October 1994 against Coventry City.
* He is also loaned to Norwich City in December 1994, his only game coming on 25th January 1995 against Coventry City.

* Once again Simon Tracey's season has been limited to a few games, more exactly seven, during the whole of the season due to the extraordinary form of Alan Kelly. His appearances were due basically to injuries to the first choice keeper of the Blades although he didn't disappoint with his performances in these games.

867.name: Kelly
pages:
* Alan Kelly is possibly the best goalkeeper currently in the English First Division. A very complete keeper, it can be said that he doesn't have a weak point and, furthermore, has great concentration during the games. 
* As well as being the undisputed first choice in the Irish side, he could be the heir to Pat Bonner and if injuries don't get in the way, he will keep his place for many years to come, being a true bastion for the Irish team.
* In short, Alan Kelly is a true life insurance for the Blades and a man who can be relied upon in the bid to reach the Premier League. Despite his extraordinary capability Kelly is not the first choice although he could make it with his quality at the highest level of English football.

* Kelly is a very complete goalie who is always focussed on how the game is going, and it is hard to take him by surprise with long balls thanks to the attention he plays and his great speed. Taking advantage of his great height, he is dominant in the area, very secure in this type of play. He positions himself well and great reflexes, it is not often that he is seen making a mistake in anything he does. In a one-on-one he covers the space well and always seems calm. The confidence he inspires in his team-mates is so great that they will use him as an extra player as he has good ball control and can boot it very hard, never complicating matters unduly. His long kicks are very powerful and well directed.
* Voted as a member of the First Division Dream Team in the 95-96 and 96-97 season.

* Alan Kelly has been an Irish international at the youth, under-21, under-23, B and full levels, making his debut in the last of these on 17th February 1993 in Dublin against Wales, the Irish winning 2-1. 
* 94 United States World Cup but didn't play. 
* He has played 18 games for his country.

* Trained in the youth squad at Preston North End, he signs as a professional in September 1985. He makes his league debut on 8th March 1986 against Crewe Alexandra. 
* He is transferred to Sheffield United in July 1992 for £150,000, making his league debut on 2nd September 1992 against Tottenham Hotspur. 
* His father, Alan Kelly, played in the FA Cup Final for Preston North End on 1964.

* Once again Alan Kelly showed the reason why he is possibly one of the best keepers in the whole of English football, making some brilliant performances during the season. He only missed seven games in the whole of the league finishing up with 39 great games under his belt. The work of Kelly was recognised, as he was voted a member of the First Division Dream Team.

868.name: Tweed
pages: * Steven Tweed has been one of the latest incorporations made by Stoke City going into the new season, on trial with the team just a week before the championship started.  His great performances during the course of the league and the magnificent partnership he forms with Sigurdsson have made him into one of the bargains of the category as his transfer from the Greek team Ionikos didn't cost a penny.  He has Bates' full confidence and is a starter with the Potters.

* Tweed is a player who operates basically as a central defender although, at times, he can play as a wide defender but only at times of emergency.  He is good in the air, both in defence and attack, causing a lot of problems for the rival backs.  He is quicker than he looks and his very solid in his actions.
x
x
* After playing in teams such as Hibernian and the Greek Ionikos, Tweed signs for Stoke City in the summer of 1997.
x

869.name: McNally
pages: * Mark McNally was an important signing for Ronnie Whelan during the two years he was at Southend United, the club where he showed his innate ability for this sport.  However, Stoke City has been his next destination, signing last year and becoming an outstanding figure within the Potters' squad.  Although at the moment he is not playing from the start, McNally could easily find a gap pretty soon in the team as he as quality and is versatile.

* McNally is a central defender who is pretty complete in the technical aspect.  He has the ability to play the ball out from the back mainly using his right foot and pass it to the wings, looking for the wings, whether it be to find some breathing space or start a counter-attack.  He is quick.  However, despite being good technically, he tries to avoid making life too complicated in difficult situations.  He joins in at set-plays but is not a goalscorer, not finishing well.  He is pretty good in the air.
x

* A Scotland under-21 international, he makes his debut against Bulgaria on the 26/3/91.  In this Scottish team were Gerry Creaney, Eoin Jess and Alan McLarren amongst others.  In total he has played 2 games for his country at this level.

* Originally from the lower ranks of Glasgow Celtic, he makes his debut on the 6/11/90 against Motherwell.  His first professional goal is on the 5/10/91 against Hearts. 
* He is transferred to Southend United in December 1995 for £50,000.  His first game for the club is on the 26/12/95 against Norwich City, scoring his first goal almost a month later on the 20/1/96 against Portsmouth. 
* He is transferred to Stoke City on the 27th of March 1997 for £120,000. His debut takes place on the 31st of March against Bradford City.

* McNally was one of the outstanding men at Southend United last year, producing an important season for his team as a wide defender and even as a centre back.  His good performance pushed Lou Macari into signing him.  He played 3 games for Stoke City from his signing to the end of the league. In total he played 37 games.

870.name: Pickering
pages: * Ally Pickering is a player with an enormous experience at the top level of English football, playing, for example, with Coventry City in the Premier League.  His contribution to the attack is always appreciated although at times he has defensive lapses.  Notwithstanding, and despite loosing his place last year towards the end of the league, he has the so much talent that it is unthinkable that he is not a starter for this season, something which is finally beginning to happen.

* Pickering is a very attacking right back who joins in the attack whenever he gets the chance, however small it may be.  He crosses pretty well and he is technically respectable, passing well both over long and short distance.  However, he is not so quick and he neglects his defensive duties at times when he pushes up like a man possessed.
x
x

* The amateur club Burton transfer him to Rotherham United in February 1990 for £18,500.  He makes his debut on the 6/3/90 against Cardiff City and scores his first goal as a professional against Preston North End on the 21/11/92, a goal which was also the his team's winner. 
* Coventry City sign him in November 1993 in exchange for £80,000.  His first game for the team is on the 25/2/94 against Liverpool. 
* He is transferred to Stoke City in the summer of 1996 but the price of the transfer has to be set by a tribunal.  The amount finally decided on is £280,000.  His debut takes place on the 17th of August against Oldham Athletic.

* Pickering had a very noteworthy season for Stoke City last year, his first at the club.  His good performances allowed him to make 40 appearances during the course of the season but he lost his place towards the end of the campaign.
