871.name: Sigurdsson
pages: * The cousin of Todd Orlygsson, the Oldham Athletic player, the arrival on the scene of Larus Sigurdsson was a true surprise at Stoke City, showing himself to be a very complete player in defensive aspects and who usually makes some attacking contributions, although he is not a man who scores a lot of goals.  An Iceland international, he looks like someone who can produce some good seasons both for his country and for Stoke City.  His good performance and undisputed status as a starter at the club have caused Newcastle United to sit up and take notice, although nothing has so far come of the supposed interest the Magpies have in him.

* Sigurdsson is a central defender who, despite not being very tall, is good in the air and is quick.  The Iceland back is a specialist individual marker, and is hard to beat as he always sticks very close to his rival, trying to anticipate the man he is shadowing.  When he steals the ball, he joins in the attack, and is able to make good deep passes to the forwards.
x
* Sigurdsson has been an Iceland international both at the youth and under-21 levels.

* Stoke City pay £150,000 for the Icelander Thor.  He makes his debut in the league on the 30/11/94 against Portsmouth and scores his first goal against Watford on the 4/4/95, a goal which is the Potters' winner.

* Sigurdsson had another magnificent season at Stoke City, continuing his impressive performance for the Potters in the seasons he has been at the club.  He presence was very important he almost played in all 46 games of the league, only missing one.

872.name: Wallace
pages: * Ray Wallace is the least known of the Wallace brothers and is the twin of Rodney, the Leeds United player.  He hasn't had as a much luck as his other brothers and has to move to a First Division team to earn a living. Thanks to his good performance in the last two seasons he continued to be an integral part of Lou Macari's teams, and he could have a good chance of remaining in the starting line-up in the teams that Macari's successor, Chic Bates, puts out.

* Ray Wallace is a player who can operate in different positions both in the midfield and as a wide defender on either side although last year he was playing in the midfield.  He is quick and works very hard for the team in this area of the pitch.  A good marker, he is technically weak, passing the ball rapidly and looking for long balls to the strikers. To make up for this defect, he doesn't stop running the whole game thanks to his enormous physical reserve.
x

* Under-21 international for England, he makes his debut in the Under-21 International Tournament of Toulon on the 5/6/89 against Bulgaria alongside his brother Rodney.  Playing in the England team were, amongst others, Neil Ruddock, Carlton Palmer, David Batty and David Hirst.

* Trained in the youth squad at Southampton, Wallace signs as a professional in April 1988.  He makes his debut in the league on the 22/10/88 against Sheffield Wednesday, this being the first time in 68 years that three brothers (Danny, Rodney and Ray Wallace) were played in the same team in the First Division.  Such an event hadn't been seen since William, John and George Carr played together for Middlesbrough. 
* He is transferred to Leeds United in May 1991 alongside his twin brother Rodney for £200,000.  His debut takes place on the 18/12/92 against Nottingham Forest. 
* Loaned to Swansea City in March 1992, he makes his debut on the 28/3/92 against Bradford City. 
* He is loaned to Reading in March 1994.  He plays his first game for the club on the 12/3/94 against Plymouth Argyle. 
* Stoke City sign him when his contract finishes in the summer of 1994.  He makes his debut on the 13/8/94 against Tranmere Rovers and his first goal as a professional comes on the 2/10/94 against WBA. 
* He is loaned to Hull City in December 1994, making his debut on the 17/12/94 against Oxford United.

* Although his season wasn't as complete as the 95-96 one, Wallace was one of the most courageous players on the pitch, whose contributions were almost priceless for the Potters.  In total he played 44 games and scored 2 goals for them.

873.name: Whittle
pages:
* Justin Whittle is a young central defender who Lou Macari hadn't used much, playing in only a handful of games in the last two years at Stoke City.  It was Macari himself who bought him for Glasgow Celtic from the Navy when he was the Scottish team's manager.  However, this hasn't helped give him more opportunities. 
* But finally it was Whittle who showed to Macari that he had in his squad a player who was valid and competent and he had his chances last year to show his ability.  His partnership with Sigurdsson was very solid and he earned the respect of the fans.  Even so, this year the situation is complicated once more for him due to the acquisition of Tweed, and the position of central defender is once again closed to him although he is almost always on the bench, waiting for the slightest opportunity.

* Whittle is a central defender who is almost perfect in the air, taking good advantage of his considerable height and bulk.  He is not so good with the ball at his feet, and limits himself to what he can do.  His great determination in the games and the enthusiasm he injects allow him to come out of some difficult situations, going in hard for the ball but always being noble at all times.
x
x

* Originally from the Navy, he signs for Glasgow Celtic at the end of the 93-94 season.  However he doesn't manage to find a place in the Scottish team.
* His contract finishes and he signs for Stoke City in October 1994.  His first game for the Potters is on the 11/11/95 against Southend United.

* Whittle finally made it into Lou Macari's team, showing a lot of serenity in his interventions during the course of the league.  His consistency allowed him to participate in 37 games and he formed a good partnership with Larus Sigurdsson.

874.name: Southall
pages:
* Signed for Stoke City in March 1998. 
* Now turned 38 years of age,  Neville Southall was one of the oldest players in the Premier League. He had spent almost the whole of his playing career at Everton, where he had become an institution. Everton supporters will never forget the game Southall had in the 1995 cup final at Wembley, when he made a series of incredible saves that finally clinched the trophy for the Toffees.

* Neville Southall is above all an extraordinary goalkeeper. His positional  sense makes him a very difficult keeper to beat, and, due to his positioning and his agility, he quickly closes down all the angles for opposition forwards, to whom he seems to grow in size as they bear down on goal. He also possesses incredible reflexes, but, perhaps his greatest quality is the character and personality he shows in goal. Experience allows him to anticipate the intentions of rival forwards while his intelligence and the way he reads the game, make him an example of the goalkeeper of the future. His only weakness is evident when he comes off his line although that  hasn't prevented him from becoming one of the best keepers in the second half of this century. The only thing  missing in his career has been the opportunity to prove his ability in one of the major international tournaments, in order to have gained  more internation recognition.

* League Championship winners medal 84-85 and 86-87. 
* F.A. Cup winners medals  83-84 and 94-94. 
* Eurooean Cup Winners Cup winners medal 84-85.
* Charity Shield medals  84 and 85.

* He has made 91 full international appearances for Wales. He made his debut on 27th May 1982 against Northern Ireland at Wrexham. Wales won 3-0. 
* 1 "B" international appearance.
* 1 Under-21 international appearance.

* After coming through the ranks at modest Winsford Town, he signed for Bury on 14th June 1980 in exchange for 60.000 pounds. He made his league debut on 20th   September 1980 in a 3-1 defeat for Bury, against Wigan.
*On 13th July 1981 he was transfered to Everton for 150,000 pounds. In November 1982, the veteran Jim Arnold took his place from him in the side. On 27th January 1983 he was  loaned out to Port Vale.
* Between 1984 and 1987 Everton won 2 League Championships, 1 F.A. Cup and one European Cup Winners Cup with Southall as a member of the starting line up in all of the important games.
* In 1985, he was voted "Footballer of the Year" in England.
* He was, at one time, on the point of making 200 consecutive appearances for Everton.
* He was on the losing side in the 1986 and 1990 F.A. Cup finals against Everton's arch enemies Liverpool.
* Up until the end of the 94-95 season, he had managed to keep 192 clean sheets, his average number of goals conceded per game was 1.135, while he had been booked 6 times and been sent off 3 times.
* In the first game of the 96-97 season egainst Newcastle at Goodison Park (2-0), Southall played his 700th game in an Everton shirt.

* Once again the Welsh international goalkeeper was first choice in goal for Everton despite the fact that there was a spell in the season when his performances were questioned by Joe Royle, who left him on the bench for three games. That decision sparked off a protest on the part of Everton supporters who consider Southall to be the best keeper in the world. However, following that poor run, he returned to the side  and managed to regain the trust of the manager, as well as his place in the side. Southall played in a final total of 34 games..

875.name: Morgan
pages: * Phil Morgan is a young goalkeeper who, since his arrival at Stoke City two seasons ago, still hasn't been able to make his debut for the Potters. The presence of Prudhoe and Muggleton shut the doors the team but the departure of the first of these left him as understudy to Muggleton, a man with a lot of experience and who has his place assured.  Even so, it could be a good opportunity for Morgan as, during the course of the league, the position could become vacant and he will be able to show his mettle.

* Morgan is a keeper with talent for the position.  He has good reflexes and saves a lot.  He is brave in all his actions and he is not frightened of leaving his area when danger approaches.  What's more, he is very sure of himself with the ball at his feet, making long, accurate passes.
x
x

* Originally from the lower ranks of Ipswich Town, he signs as a professional on the 5th of July 1993.  His first and only game for the club is on the 29th of April against Leicester City. 
* As a free agent he signs for Stoke City on the 6th of July 1995 although he still hasn't made his debut for the Potters. 
* He is loaned to Chesterfield on the 14th of October 1996, playing his first game for them on the 15th of October against Notts County.

* Morgan couldn't make his debut for Stoke City last season despite this being his second season at the club but he did get to play for Chesterfield where he went as a loan player for the month of October.  In total he could only play two games.

876.name: Muggleton
pages: * The signing of Carl Muggleton was almost a personal bet on the part of the former manager Lou Macari, who knew him from his time at Glasgow Celtic and who trusted the goalie's abilities.  His security could be confirmed last year when he defended the Potters goal for a good part of the league. If his position didn't seem safe enough, the departure of Prudhoe made it even more so, with only the young Morgan as substitute trying to learn as much as possible to take Muggleton's place away from him.

* Muggleton is a goalkeeper who is dominant in the area and judges the distances well when making aerial interceptions or cutting out long balls. He is excellent at stopping penalties and his great athletic ability allow him to make some wonderful saves from shots from his rivals.
x
* Muggleton has made one under-21 international appearance for England.

* Trained in the youth squad at Leicester City, he signs as a professional in September 1986. 
* He is loaned for 4 months to Chesterfield in September 1987.  He makes his league debut on the 12/9/87 against Port Vale. 
* He is loaned to Blackpool in February 1988.  He plays his first game for the club on the 13/2/88 against Notts County. 
* He is loaned to Hartlepool United in October 1988, making his debut on the 29/10/88 against Hereford United. 
* He finally manages to play a game for his team, Leicester City, against WBA on the 21/1/89. 
* In February 1990 he is loaned to Stockport County.  He makes his debut on the 2/3/90 against Colchester United. 
* He is loaned to Liverpool but doesn't get to play a single game. 
* In October 1990 he is loaned to Stoke City, making his debut on the 10/19/93 against Oxford United. 
* He is loaned to Sheffield United in November 1993 although he doesn't get to play a single minute for the Blades. 
* In January 1994 he is transferred to Glasgow Celtic for £150,000 to cover for the injured Pat Bonner.  His debut with the Glaswegian team is on the 22/1/94 against Dundee. 
* He returns to Stoke City but this time he is transferred in July 1994 for £200,000.  He plays his first game for the Potters on the 13/8/94 against Tranmere Rovers.

* Muggleton was the undisputed first choice at Stoke City for most of last season, showing once again his has more than enough talent for the position. Unfortunately for him, in a run in which he let in 32 goals in 18 games, he was replaced by Prudhoe, although at the end of the season he once again recovered his place.  In total he played 33 games.

877.name: Devlin
pages: * Mark Devlin is a valuable young player who has come from the youth squad at Stoke City and who has always had a regular place in the team in all these years he has been at the club when Lou Macari was the trainer and, now, with Chic Bates.  He has talent to be a good player for the Potters although his future is not so clear as he hasn't reached an agreement with the club about his contract.

* Devlin is a versatile player who can play both in the midfield or in the defence but almost always on the left.  He doesn't join in the attack much and his contribution in this respect should be improved it he wants to have more impact at the club.  Although in friendlies he has scored goals, he doesn't finish very well.
x
x

* Trained in the Stoke City youth squad, Mark Devlin signs as a professional on the 6th of April 1991.  His debut takes place on the 2nd of February 1991 against Chester City and he scores his first goal as a professional against Crewe Alexandra on the 13th of March of this same year.

* Devlin played in the not insignificant number of 21 games for the Potters but unfortunately, in most of these, he came on as a substitute, and he was unable to find a regular spot in the starting line-ups fielded by Lou Macari.

878.name: Stewart
pages: * After an unfortunate spell at Liverpool Paul Stewart's career seemed to go into an irreversible decline.  Loaned to club after club, the man who was one of the best forwards in England at the beginning of the 90's seemed to be heading for early retirement.  The trust that Peter Reid, the Sunderland coach, has helped the player to show his talent once again and, what is more important, to regain his confidence.  After a good spell at this club, Steward declared that he was leaving for personal reasons.  Stoke City is the team that has acquired his services, without paying a penny, getting their hands on a player with a lot of experience who could contribute a lot to the Potters.

* A centre forward in the first years of his professional career, currently Paul Steward has converted into a midfielder.  A very strong man, he is able to take advantage of his power to steamroller his rivals.  He wins back a lot of balls, although he doesn't always distribute the ball effectively. On the other hand, he can shield the ball with his body while waiting for team-mates to join him in attack.  Well equipped for the aerial game, he has lost a lot of his scent for goal, but his presence near to the rival box announces danger.

* FA Cup Champion in 91. 
* Charity Shield Medal in 91. 
* First Division Champion in 94 and 96.

* 3 full international appearances for England.  He made his debut on the 11th of September 1991 with defeat at the hands of Germany in a game played at Wembley (0-1). 
* 5 times international B.  1 goal. 
* 1 under-21 international appearance.  1 goal. 
* 2 youth international appearances.

* A native of Manchester, Paul Steward arrived at the Blackpool youth squad in 1981 from the Associated Schoolboys which he had joined in December of 1978.  He became a professional on the 13th of October just before he made his league debut on the 10th of February 1982 in a game at Bloomfield Road against Rochdale. 
* At the start of his career Paul was a forward who scored a lot of goals and these made a decisive contribution to Blackpool's promotion to the Third Division. 
* In the 86-87 season he scored 21 goals in 32 games.  His outstanding performance accelerated his transfer to Manchester City, which took place on the 19th of March 1987 in exchange for £200,000. 
* He scored 24 goals in 40 league games in the 87-88 season, including two hat-tricks.  On the 21st of June 1988 he was transferred to Tottenham Hotspur for £1,700,000.  However, an injury delayed his debut for Spurs until the month of October.  Finally, he appeared as a substitute at White Hart Lane in a game against Manchester United.  But unfortunately he missed a penalty when it was two all. 
* His career at Tottenham Hotspur brings him as a far as the England team in September 1991. 
* He signs for Liverpool on the 29th of July 1992 in exchange for £2,300,000 and in his first season at Anfield he plays 24 league games.  However, his appearances became ever more few and far between and he entered into a phase of going from club to club as a loan player.  Crystal Palace (January 1994), Wolverhampton Wanderers (September 1994), Burnley (February 1995) and Sunderland (August 1995) were his successive destinations. 
* However, luck is not on his side at either of these clubs.  He made his debut for Wolves on the day that Billy Wright died, one of the club's legendary players, and at Burnley he was sent off once and received several yellow cards which negatively affected his performance. 
* On the 5th of March 1996 he signs as a Sunderland player, although his debut for the Rokerites had taken place on the 30th of August 1995, in a period when he was on loan at Roker Park.  Despite injuring himself after playing just two games for Sunderland, Peter Reid showed his trust in the player and pressed for his signing. 
* His contract comes to an end at Sunderland and he signs for Stoke City during the summer of 1997. 
* During the course of his career he has scored 4 hat-tricks.  The first of these was on the 24th of March 1984 against Chester.  Port Vale, Huddersfield and Millwall, the last of these in April of 1989, were the other victims of his marksmanship.

* He was one of the top goalscorers at Sunderland but with just 4 goals in his tally.  This reflected the poor effectiveness of the team in front of goal.  Stewart played a dignified role, playing in 24 games, most of them as a lone striker.

879.name: Kavanagh
pages: * Graham Kavanagh is a young midfielder who has great talent for playing football but after the arrival of lots of stars at Middlesbrough he was forced to look elsewhere, arriving at Stoke City.  His ability is not unknown to Chic Bates, who his finding a slot for him in the starting team, to help him show that the confidence deposited in him was not wasted.

* A very capable midfielder, he is physically strong and covers a lot of ground thanks to this.  Very touch and battling, he boasts, however, a great technique allowing him to pass well, supplying the forwards with quality balls either in short or long.  Positionally he is good, always well-placed.  He has a great personality and is very intelligent.  Quick and excellent ball-winner, he has a good shot from medium range with his right foot although he can use the left better.
x
* Kavanagh has been an Irish international in the schoolboy, youth and under-21 categories.

* An Irishman born in Dublin, Graham Kavanagh was playing at Home Farm when he was discovered by the Middlesbrough scouts.  On the 16th of August 1991 he signs for Boro, but doesn't make his debut with the first team until the 21st of October 1992, in a game against Nottingham Forest. 
* On the 25th of February 1994 he is loaned to Darlington, a Third Division club where he plays five league games. 
* On the 18th of December 1993 he scores first two goals for Middlesbrough in a home game against Notts County (3-0).  However, he doesn't manage to settle into the team during this season nor in the coming ones. 
* He is transferred to Stoke City on the 13th of September 1996 for £250,000.  His debut takes place on the 14th of September against Birmingham City and he scores his first goal for the Potters against Bolton Wanderers just two weeks later.

* Kavanagh had a somewhat irregular season at Stoke City, switching between brilliant moments and others that weren't so.  At the end of the league he was even squeezed out of the team to prevent the hard criticisms from denting his moral too much.  In total he played 38 games and scored 4 goals.

880.name: Donaldson
pages:
* Signed for Stoke City in March 1998. 
* Since he arrived at Hillsborough in January 1995 O'Neill Donaldson has had very few chances to show his ability.  The Sheffield Wednesday forward had been labelled as a marksman, but the lack of playing minutes has prevented him from crediting his fame.  He finished last season on good form, something which gives him hope that the 97-98 season will see his definitive explosion.

* A strong forward, quick and with a scent for goal, O'Neill Donaldson is a marksman for the box.  He has a solid finish with either foot and is good in the air, although he doesn't stand out for his technique.  In any case, he always guarantees commitment and physical effort, constantly pressuring rival defences.
x
x

* He started his career in the modest team Hinckley Town, then signed for Shrewsbury Town in 1991. 
* On the 10th of August 1994 he was transferred to Doncaster Rovers, who loan him to Mansfield Town in this same year. 
* His signing by Sheffield Wednesday on the 9th of January 1995 was the last by the then manager Trevor Francis.  He made his debut in the Premier League on the 14th of March of this same year with an away defeat against Manchester City (3-2). 
* On the 9th of September he played his first game as a starter for the Owls against Queens Park Rangers, and he celebrates the occasion by scoring the last goal of the game (0-3) and his first for Sheffield Wednesday.

* It wasn't a good season for Donaldson who only played 5 games in the league, just two of them from the start.  Despite playing so little, the Wednesday forward managed to score 2 goals, one against Wimbledon and the other against Liverpool in the last game of the season.  He did, without doubt, deserve to have more chances.

881.name: Lightbourne
pages:
* Signed for Stoke City on the 17th of February 1998. 
* Kyle Lightbourne arrives at Stoke via Coventry with the label of marksman earned in his last three seasons at Walsall, where he finished as the team's top scorer.

* A born goalscorer, Kyle is a classic centre forward; strong and a good finisher.  He has a powerful shot with both feet and is dominant in the air.  He scores a lot of goals with headers.  His speed allows him to also play out towards the touchlines.
x
* 24 full international appearances for Bermuda.

* His first club in England was Scarborough, from where he moved to Walsall in September 93.
* The 97-98 season is his first as a Premier League player, and he will make his debut for Coventry as the Sky Blues paid Walsall £500,000 for the move.

* He was Walsall's top scorer for the third consecutive year, only missing one game and scoring 20 goals.  The coaches at Coventry decided to offer him a contract after he had shown once more that he is a useful forward in any team.

882.name: Macari
pages: * Mike Macari is a young centre forward who hasn't had it easy to get into the Stoke City squad.  After several years in the reserves, where he managed to score a lot of goals, he had to wait until last year to make his debut. What's more, he had the added pressure of being the son of the manager, Lou Macari, but managed to silence his critics, playing a dignified role and forming an attacking partnership with Mike Sheron.  His is not a starter but his determination could mean that Bates will turn to him during the course of the league.

* Macari is a young forward who has an excellent turn of speed, a great shot and a lot of maturity as some of his virtues.  This combination of factors makes him a dangerous opponent and although he isn't a natural goalscorer, at least not yet, he could have what it takes to be a forward who notches up quite a few.
x
x

* Originally from the West Ham United juniors, Mike Macari signs for Stoke City on the 31st of July 1991.  His debut had to wait until the 24th of August 1996 against Manchester City and he scored his first goal as a professional on the 29th of January 1997.

* Macari had a good season at Stoke City, at last making his debut for the Potters after several years in the reserves, playing in 30 games and scoring 3 goals, one of which was pretty sensational against Oxford United.

883.name: Thorne
pages:
* Peter Thorne is a very powerful forward with a lot of physical strength that allows him to create some good chances in front of the rival keeper. A regular in Steve McMahon's plans at Swindon Town, his irregular performances forced him onto the bench. 
* The situation did not improve as he didn't reach an agreement with the Robins but, luckily for him, Stoke City stepped in and offered him the chance to be the first choice centre forward after Sheron's departure.  His performance at the beginning of this league is impressive, staying at near the top of the scorers' list and trying to be a bit more consistent and not switch between brilliant spells and horrific ones.

* A very strong forward, he can use both feet equally well.  He has no problem when it comes to having a go, trying his luck whenever he can.  He works hard to pressure the defence when they are trying to play the ball out from the back.
* Second Division Champion 95-96 with Swindon Town.
x

* Originally from the lower ranks of Blackburn Rovers, he signs as a professional in June 1991. 
* The competition for places in the forward line is very great and so he is loaned to Wigan Athletic in March 1994 until the end of the season.  He makes his debut in the league on the 12/3/94 against Northampton Town. 
* He is finally transferred to Swindon Town in January 1995 for £225,000. In his league debut on the 4/2/95 he scores two goals against Burnley. 
* His transfer to Stoke City comes through in the summer of 1997 for £350,000 as a starting price which depends on the number of league games played.

* A disappointing season for Peter Thorne who didn't have the chance to keep up any sort of regular form during the season.  He was able to produce moments of brilliance but had spells when he vanished from the game.  At the end of the league, his manager at Swindon Town, Steve McMahon, decided to sit him on the bench, looking for a more resolute forward.  In total he played 31 games and scored 8 goals.

884.name: McMahon
pages: * Gerard McMahon is a player with a lot of potential and who, if he manages to keep up the continuity and regularity in his game, could be one of the best players in the First Division.  However, this very young player has perhaps one problem, himself, as at times he is too passive in his game and disappears from the match.  Even so, he could polish out this defect and become an excellent footballer as he has talent.  He great performance during last season has led him to be included in Chic Bates' starting elevens this year.

* McMahon is a very fast winger who turns very well.  He likes to hug the touchline and from there, make dangerous use of his speed, dodging rivals to then put over a cross or have a go himself.  He also passes a lot in diagonal, does one-twos on the run before having a go.  He doesn't help out much in defence.
x

* McMahon has been a Northern Ireland international at the schoolboy, youth, under-21, B and full levels, making seven appearances in the latter category. His debut was on the 22/5/95 in the Canadian Cup in a game against the host nation after coming on as a substitute for Keith Gillespie.

* Tottenham Hotspur sign him from the Irish team Glenavon in July 1992 for £100,000.  He makes his debut on the 9/5/95 against Coventry City. 
* He is loaned to Barnet in October 1994.  He makes his debut in the league on the 22/10/94 against Carlisle United and he scores his first goal as a professional against Chesterfield on the 29/10/94. 
* Stoke City sign him in exchange for £450,000 in September 1996, and he plays his first game for Huddersfield Town this same month.

* Although he didn't find it easy to get into Lou Macari's team last year as he was a new arrival, McMahon finally managed a regular place for himself in the starting line-up, showing some of the things he can do.  His importance is underlined by the 35 games he played and the three goals he scored during the season.

885.name: Forsyth
pages: * Richard Forsyth takes care of the dirty work on the pitch.  His role is almost indispensable for a lot of teams, before for Birmingham City and now at Stoke.  Despite playing in amateur football just three years ago, the change in level hasn't seemed to have affected him much.  The hard man on the pitch, his role isn't just one of defending but he is also quite prolific in attack as was seen last year.  He is a regular in Chic Bates' teams.

* Forsyth is a very strong player who is basically a defensive midfielder. He uses his strength to win back a lot of balls in his zone of the pitch. He joins in the attack well and can finish off a move, arriving well from deep positions and having an acceptable shot with both feet.  He also has a good shot from long range which should be watched.  He is very hard when fighting for the ball.
x
* He has been an English international 3 times.

* Birmingham City sign him from Kidderminster Harriers in the summer of 1995 for £50,000.  He makes his debut in the league on the 12/8/95 against Ipswich Town and he scores his first goal against Barnsley on the 2/9/95. 
* He is transferred to Stoke City in the summer of 1996 for £250,000.  He plays his first game for the Potters on the 17th of August against Oldham Athletic and he scores his first goal against Manchester City one week later.

* A sensational season for Richard Forsyth in his first year at Stoke City. This hard-working midfielder also had enough energy to score 8 league goals, the second best tally in the team behind Sheron.  Even so, his defensive duties limited him in attack and prevented him from producing a tremendous season.

886.name: Keen
pages: * Now in his fourth season at Stoke City, Kevin Keen has shown that he was a useful player for Lou Macari first and now is for Chic Bates. Both men have trusted in his ability and his capability very solidly.  In his sporting maturity, this footballer could can contribute something in attack and, what's more, help out the defence at all times, being a person who makes a lot of sacrifices in this aspect.  Obviously he will be one of the regulars in his manager's team.

* Keen is a very quick right half who has a great capacity for sacrifice as he pushes up and drops back constantly along the touchline helping out in attack or defence.  He has a good shot with his left foot.  Technically he is acceptable but he has always given the sensation that he is a player who isn't fully aware of his talent, not trying out individual plays due to this lack of confidence.  He helps out a lot in defence when they are surprised by a counter-attack, dropping back quickly to cover the gaps.
x
* He has been a schoolboy and youth international for the England team.

* Trained in the West Ham United youth squad, he signs as a professional in March 1984.  He makes his debut in the league on the 6/9/86 against Liverpool and scores his first goal for the Hammers on the 5/12/87. 
* In July 1993 he is transferred to Wolverhampton Wanderers for £600,000. He makes his debut on the 14/8/93 against Bristol City and scores his first goal on the 2/10/93 against Charlton Athletic. 
* In October 1994 he is signed by Stoke City for £300,000.  He plays his first game for the Potters on the 22/10/94 against Oldham Athletic and scores his first goal 8 days later against his old team, Wolverhampton Wanderers.

* Once again, Keen had a disappointing season, not due to his performance, but to the continual bad run of injuries which haunted him and prevented him from settling at Stoke City.  In total he played 16 games and scored a goal.

887.name: Sturridge
pages: * The brother of the Derby County player, Dean Sturridge, Simon arrived at Stoke from Birmingham City for a very low price, but his effort and know-how have allowed him to finally figure on the teams put out by Lou Macari. Unfortunately for this brave forward, a serious injury to his knee kept him out of the team last year and has limited his options at the beginning of the league.  Even so, we will have to watch his recovery and see if he is able to regain what he earned with so much hard work and effort.

* Sturridge is a very quick forward, right-footed, who doesn't think twice before shooting at goal.  He works hard to find space, not stopping for a second during the game.  His header is acceptable, anticipating the rival defenders.  As was said earlier, he works hard for his opportunities but then is unable to take full advantage of the chances he creates.  Very much a battler, he is a nuisance for the rival defenders during the course of the game.Physically he is strong and can take the rhythm of the game almost perfectly.
x
* He has been an England youth international.

* Originally from the lower ranks of Birmingham City, he signs as a professional in July 1988.  He makes his debut in the league on the 15/10/88 against WBA and scores his first goal as a professional on the 27/3/89 against Shrewsbury Town. 
* He is transferred to Stoke City in September 1993 for £70,000.  He makes his debut on the 25/9/93 against Southend United and scores his first goal for the club on the 25/3/95 against Notts County, the Potters' winner.

* Bad luck came Simon Sturridge's way last year has he had managed to work his way into the team after a lot of hard work, but then a knee injury kept him out from the month of September onwards and finished his season. In total he only got to play 5 games.

888.name: Williams
pages: * Ryan Williams is a very talented forward who has played for England at the youth level and who has aroused a lot of expectations for the future. Tranmere Rovers have been the quickest in the jostle to sign him and it will be Aldridge, the top scorer in the history of English football, who will have to lend a helping hand to Williams. He will notice the step up in divisions but there is no hurry for this player with a brilliant future.

* Williams is a very mobile forward in the opponents' half, looking to find space. He takes advantage of his speed and technical quality to create opportunities although he still hasn't honed the assassin instinct needed to be a great forward. Even so, he has a great future ahead.
x
* England youth international.

* Originally from the lower ranks of Mansfield Town, Williams makes his debut on 13th January 1995 against Leyton Orient. His first goal comes on 16th April against Rochdale. 
* Tranmere Rovers sign him during the summer of 1997.

* A very good season for this young player last year despite not finding the net once. His great performance brought him his call-up for the England under-18 team, being the only Third Division player to be chosen. In total he played 16 games.

889.name: Kelly
pages: * A good buy on the part of John Aldridge in the pre-season, David Kelly's signing has given a new lease of life to this marksman's prolonged career, who had seen a reduction in his opportunities in recent times, even forced into the midfield at Sunderland. This position was completely alien to this player who is at home in the box. Since his arrival at Rovers he has made a big impact and forms an excellent partnership with Lee Jones.

* A very hard-working forward with an accurate shot, David Kelly operates expertly in the rival box. A man with very quick reactions, he is able to anticipate defenders and look for a shooting position. He is a very mobile player and oozes enthusiasm and effort in every game. Opportunistic and intelligent in the danger zone, his experience gives him some resources to successfully resolve the chances that come his way.
* First Division Champion 93.

* 23 full international appearances for Ireland. 
* 3 B-international appearances. 
* 1 under-23 international appearance. 
* 1 under-21 international appearance.

* David Kelly was trained at Alvechurch, a modest club in a minor league. He stayed there until the 21st of December 1983 when he signed for Walsall who were managed by Alan Buckley. 
* A member of the starting line-up since 84-85, he was transferred to West Ham on the 1st of August 1988 for £600,000.  However, after his first season at Upton Park, the club is relegated to the Second Division. 
* Leicester City paid £300,000 for his transfer in March 1990. He scored 14 goals in the 90-91 season, but on the 4th of December 1991 he signed for Newcastle in exchange for £250,000. 
* In his second season at St. James Park he contributed to their promotion to the Premier League with 24 goals, but didn't get to make his debut in the top flight so, on 23rd June 1993, he was transferred to Wolverhampton Wanderers for £750,000. 
* He made his debut for Wolves on 2nd October 1993 at home to Charlton Athletic (1-1). 
* A full Irish international, he was the scorer of the goal that opened the scoring in the sadly famous game between against England played in Dublin in the 94-95 season. The game was suspended due to crowd trouble. 
* On 19th September 1995 he signs for Sunderland. He makes his debut four days later with a win over Millwall (1-2). One week later, in his home debut, he scores his first goal for the Rokerites against Reading. 
* After his first season at Roker Park the club is promoted to the Premier League. This means a £100,000 increase in the cost of his transfer, making him momentarily Sunderland's most expensive signing (£1 million). 
* He is signed by Tranmere Rovers during the summer of 1997.

* It wasn't the season that David Kelly would have wanted in his second and last year at Sunderland. He started the league as a member of the starting eleven in the forward line, but he lost momentum little by little, and was forced into the midfield, a position unknown to him. In his defence, it should be said that most of his interventions were from the right of the pitch and during the 24 games he played Kelly was able to score a single goal.

890.name: Jones
pages: * Looking for a marksman to substitute for the veteran Rush, Liverpool signed Jones with an eye on the future. The Welshman showed both in the reserves and in the youth squad that he is a good footballer, but unfortunately players such as Fowler and Collymore kept him out of the Reds team. His definitive destination has been Tranmere Rovers, a club where he he hopes to demonstrate his talent at the highest level, and where he caused a good impression last year when he was on loan. Since his arrival, the partnership with Kelly has been giving some excellent results for Aldridge and it is hoped that this year will be the one in which Lee Jones' career truly takes off after so many delays due to competition at Anfield.

* In every team where he has played Lee Jones has shown his scoring ability. However, he still hasn't reached the level demanded by top competition. He makes up for his lack of height with good positioning in the area. Speed and his first touch, the way he scores most of his goals, are his most outstanding characteristics.
* League Cup Champion 94-95.

* Twice Welsh B-international. 
* 11 under-21 international appearances.  9 goals.

* Originally from the lower ranks of Wrexham, he signs as a professional on 5th July 1991. 
* Liverpool sign him on 12th March 1992 in exchange for £300,000.
* In the 93-94 season he is loaned to Crewe Alexandra. 
* He is the holder of the record of the number of goals scored for the Welsh under-21 side (9). 
* Tranmere Rovers sign him in the summer of 1997 for £100,000. His first game for Rovers is on 28th March 1997 against Southend when he is on loan to the club prior to his transfer.

* Lee Jones season comprised two distinct phases. His spell at Liverpool ended with just two appearances, and he was unable to keep a place in the side. He was then loaned to Wrexham and Tranmere, and at this last club, he showed his excellent talent scoring 5 goals in 8 games.

891.name: Aldridge
pages: * Ver perfil en entrenador.

* John Aldridge is a true predator in the box, and is a forward who despite the years, still has a sensational finish. He still has some of his turn of speed, and can't be left to receive the ball alone with a little bit of advantage as he will make use of the situation. He doesn't pressure the defence overwhelmingly, basically trying to look for a slight mistake, saving his energy. He has an excellent header, placing them accurately as well as anticipating and positioning himself as in the text books. Despite being a tremendous scorer, he rarely tries individual plays, receiving the ball, laying it off, and looking to find some space. He is better with his right than his left although he will shoot with both.

* League Cup Champion with Oxford United in the 85-86 season. 
* League Champion with Liverpool 87-88. 
* FA Cup Champion with Liverpool 88-89. 
* FA Cup runner-up with Liverpool 87-88. 
* Top scorer at Newport County in 79-80 and 83-84. 
* Top scorer at Oxford United in 84-85, 85-86 and 86-87. 
* Top scorer at Liverpool in 87-88 and 88-89. 
* Top scorer at Real Sociedad in 89-90 and 90-91. 
* Top scorer at Tranmere Rovers in 91-92, 92-93, 93-94, 94-95 and 95-96.
* Top scorer in the Second Division 84-85.

* Aldridge has 68 full caps for Ireland. His debut for the national side came on 26th March 1986 against Wales in Jackie Charlton's first game as manager of the Irish side. Ireland go down 1-0 to a goal from Ian Rush.
* Curiously, he hasn't had so much luck in front of goal with the national side as with the club sides. However, this doesn't stop him from being the second highest scorer of all time for his country, beaten only by Frank Stapleton who has scored one more. 
* His retirement from the national side took place last season. He bowed out one goal away from Frank Stapleton's record.
* See manager's anecdotes.

* Aldridge was once again one of the top scorers in the First Division, something he is used to, and was Tranmere's top marksman. Despite the advanced years, his killer instinct hasn't left him, and probably never will. He scored 18 goals in 43 games.

892.name: Challinor
pages: * Dave Challinor is a young player who arrived at the club from amateur football three years ago and who has been waiting patiently for his chance. A youth international for England, his talent hasn't passed unnoticed by the national selectors of the lower categories, nor for that matter by Aldridge. The manager hasn't hesitated to play him from the start in the Rovers backline after seeing his evolution in the reserves team. It could be his big chance although it remains to be seen if he keeps his place.

* Challinor is a player who basically operates in the centre of the defence, and is pretty competent. He has one of the most powerful kicks in the whole of the league, important for long balls to the rival box. He is composed and it looks like he has a good future.
x
* Youth and schoolboy international for England.
* Originally from the amateur club Brombrough Pool, Challinor signs for Tranmere Rovers on 18th July 1994. His debut is on 28th February 1997 against Stoke City.
* Challinor appeared on the scene at Tranmere Rovers at the end of last season, producing some performances that showed his excellent talent for the centre back position. He played 5 league games.

893.name: Thompson
pages:
* Andy Thompson was, alongside Steve Bull, one of the most loved players at Wolverhampton Wanderers. In fact, both arrived together from WBA in 1986 and on completing 19 years for the club, he had a testimonial game in his honour against Chelsea.  25,000 spectators were at the ground, a sign of the affection the had for him. 
* However, his connection with Wolves ended during last summer. He was a free agent and decided to sign for Tranmere Rovers. A very experienced man, he could be an interesting acquisition for John Alderidge going into the present season, in which he is an undisputed starter for the manager.

* Thompson can play both at left back or right back, though he uses his right better. He is pretty quick and tough, and his tackling is one of his strong points. Thanks to his speed, he joins in the attack dangerously and has a good shot from a distance. A penalty specialist, he is one of the safest spot-kick takers in England.

* Fourth Division Champion with Wolverhampton Wanderers in the 87-88 season.
* Third Division Champion with Wolverhampton Wanderers in the 88-89 season.
x

* Originally from the lower ranks of WBA, he signs as a professional in November 1985. He makes his debut in the league on 16th November 1985 against Liverpool and his first goal in the league is the winner against Southampton on 29th March 1986. 
* He is transferred to Wolverhampton Wanderers in November 1986 for £35,000. Steve Bull also moves to Wolves at the same time. He plays his first game on 22nd November 1986 against Wrexham and scores his first goal in the league on 27th december 1986 against Exeter City. 
* His contract with Wolves finishes and he signs for Tranmere Rovers in the summer of 1997.

* Thompson had a good season, playing 32 games for Wolves and scoring 2 goals. His season started with him playing in the midfield, the position where he had started his career.  However, a muscle injury forced him to miss some games and, from this moment on, his presence in the Mark McGhee's team was somewhat irregular, sometimes playing from the start, sometimes sitting on the bench.

894.name: Thorn
pages: * Andy Thorn is a tremendously experienced central defender who started last season at the Scottish team Hearts, but then moved to Tranmere Rovers with the season under way. His signing was made to reinforce the zone of the pitch in which the team was OK but was lacking a restrained man. His arrival helped the team a lot although he couldn't play many games. He is not a member of the starting line-up but his presence will be important for the present edition of the league.

* Thorn is a central defender who has a lot of experience and who has an excellent sense of positioning. Thanks to this, he is able to make a lot of interceptions without having to commit fouls. He is sure of himself with the ball at his feet but doesn't usually push up with it, restricting himself to passing well and not making things too complicated.  He is exceptional in the air, despite not being so tall, and is dangerous at set-plays. He isn't the quickest player but he positions himself intelligently.
* FA Cup Champion with Wimbledon 1988.
* Thorn has made 5 under-21 international appearances for England, making his debut on 18th September 1987 against the Federal Republic of Germany.

* Originally from the lower ranks of Wimbledon, he signs as a professional in November 1984. He makes his league debut on 6th April 1985 against Notts County and scores his first goal as a professional on 23rd August 1986.
* He is transferred to Newcastle United in August 1988 for £850,000. He plays his first game for the Magpies on 27th August 1988 against Everton and his first goal comes on 3rd September 1988 against Tottenham Hotspur.
* Crystal Palace sign him in December 1989 in exchange for £650,000. He makes his debut on 9th December 1989 against Manchester United and scores his first goal seven days later against Charlton Athletic. 
* When his contract finishes he returns to Wimbledon in 1994. He plays the first game of his second spell at Wimbledon on the 8th October 1994 against Arsenal and scores his first goal on 21st March 1995 against Manchester City.
* At the beginning of the 96-97 season, Thorne plays for the Scottish team Hearts but in September 1996 he signs for Tranmere Rovers. He makes his debut on 28th September against Norwich City.

* Signed by Aldridge to bolster the Tranmere Rovers backline, Thorn showed that he was an excellent buy during the games he played. His figure was influential in the club but was limited to 19 games due to injuries.

895.name: Coyne
pages:
* A home-grown man, Danny Coyne has shown that he is the best person to occupy the Tranmere Rovers goal. He became the first choice in the 94-95 season and, since then, hasn't looked back, except for a period when he was unavailable due to a bad injury last year. His great form has forced Eric Nixon to leave the club and join Stockport County during the summer. 
* Many see him as the successor to Neville Southall, the veteran Wales goalkeeper, to defend his country's colours. His great performance has also made him an appetising target for Premier League clubs, who have been sending their scouts to watch his progress.  Nothing indicates that Danny Coyne's situation as the undisputed Rovers keeper will change.

* Danny Coyne is a complete keeper. A brave player, he takes risks at the feet of rival forwards, and is quick and decisive in this type of action. He is agile and has good reflexes allowing him to make exceptional saves. His positioning is good. His big fault is when he has to come for an aerial ball, as he doesn't always judge the distances well, being brilliant sometimes and making a mess other times.
x

* Under-21 international with Wales. 
* One full international appearance for Wales, Coyne makes his debut on 4th April 1996 against Switzerland in Lugano.
* Trained in the Tranmere Rovers youth squad, he makes his league debut on 8th May 1993 against Peterborough United, coming on as a substitute for injured Eric Nixon.

* Coyne started as the first choice keeper at Tranmere Rovers, and had some great performances until November when Eric Nixon took over. He returned to the team but a horrible incident in a game against WBA caused damage to his neck ligaments and he had to miss the rest of the league. Even so, his recovery went well he returned towards the end of the season to play in the reserves but not with the first team. In total he played 21 games.

896.name: McGreal
pages:
* Despite his youth, John McGreal has been a fundamental piece in the Tranmere Rovers schemes in past seasons. In fact, when he is out the team has felt it, loosing some of the firmness that the Rovers youth squad product provides. 
* However, his importance dropped after the signing of Andy Thorn at the beginning of last season, creating a difficult situation for this excellent central defender. Compared with his idol, Alan Hansen, for his calmness and playing vision, McGreal is another of Tranmere's players who attracts the attention of powerful English clubs who study every detail of the player's evolution. Despite the presence of Thorn he is playing from the start for Aldridge's team.

* McGreal is a central defender who is good in the air although only really in defence and not in attack, his record showing few goals. He is a player with good technique allowing him to play the ball out from the back and join in the attack. Very safe and calm when pressured by the rivals, he doesn't just boot the ball away in these situations. He is pretty quick and agile.
x
x

* Trained in the Tranmere Rovers youth squad, he signs as a professional in July 1990. He makes his league debut on 25th April 1991 against Southend United and scores his first goal on 23rd MArch 1994 against Leicester City.

* Made Rovers captain by the John Aldridge, McGreal didn't disappoint at all although he only played 24 league games. The performance of the central defender was so outstanding that the scouts of some Premier League clubs followed his progress attentively.

897.name: Higgins
pages: * With more than 400 games for Tranmere Rovers under his belt, Dave Higgins is a true institution at the club, thanks to his veteran status, leadership qualities and charisma. He is a team player who never lets the side down, always giving 100%. He has a lot of experience although this isn't helping him find a place in the team right now, giving way to the impetus of men like McGreal and Teale. Even so, it is important for the team to know that he is there and he hopes to fully enjoy his twilight years as a footballer.

* Higgins is a central defender, who is a very sticky marker and who tries to anticipate the forwards actions, helped by his excellent positioning. Very strong, he is tough but fair. He is noted for his aerial power, being dominant in his own area and dangerous at the other end at set-plays, though more for the attention paid to him freeing other players than for his own attempts. Even so, he has a good scoring record. He doesn't stand out with the ball at his feet and never complicates things unnecessarily, as he knows his limitations.
x
x

* Originally from the amateur club Eagle, he signs as a professional for Tranmere Rovers in August 1983. His debut takes place on 17th September 1983 against Mansfield Town. 
* After two seasons at Tranmere Rovers he signs for the amateur club Caernarfon Town, where he plays for two more years. 
* He returns to Tranmere Rovers in the 87-88 season, making his debut on 3rd October 1987 against Darlington.  His first goal as a professional is against Leyton Orient on 2nd May 1988.

* Higgins turned in the type of season we are used to seeing from him, with solid performances always stepping in perfectly for the absence of his team-mates. This idol of the Rovers crowd played 22 games in total and scored 2 goals.

898.name: Irons
pages:
* This his eighth season at Tranmere Rovers. Kenny Irons is a product of the youth squad, and  has managed to play 30 or more games in 7 of the last eight seasons, being an important player for John King, under whose orders he was for longest. 
* However, in recent times things weren't going so well but he managed to win his place back after John Aldridge was made manager. His place, just behind the forwards, was an innovation for the team and he earned Aldridge's trust for the rest of the season. In view of this, Irons hopes to be able to contribute as much as possible to Rovers' season, although, at the moment, he is not playing from the start but is coming on as a sub and causing a lot of danger.

* Irons can play as a midfielder or as a link-man with the forwards. This player is blessed with a great shot from long range and creates a lot of problems for rival keepers. He controls and shoots with both feet although his right is a little better for passing the ball. Very tenacious and hard-working, he helps a lot in the midfield pressuring the other team. He has good technique and dribbles well. When he plays as a link-man he tries to take the other defence by surprise popping up from deeper positions. He is not so quick but he wins back a lot of possession during the course of a game.
x
x

* Originally from the lower ranks of Tranmere Rovers, he signs as a professional in November 1989. He makes his debut in the league on 2nd December 1989 against Bury and scores his first goal against Birmingham City on 21st December 1990, a goal that turns out to be the winner.

* Kenny Irons had a sensational season, playing in the position that had been previously allotted to Aldridge, that is, just behind the centre forward. He performed well at this position.  In total he played 41 games and scored 5 goals.

899.name: Morrisey
pages:
* Son of the former Everton and Liverpool star, Johnny Morrisey Sr, the current Tranmere Rovers player tried to follow in his father's footsteps and find a place at Everton. However, the coaches didn't take a shine to him and he moved to Wolverhampton Wanderers. From here he moved back to Merseyside, not to one of the big clubs but to Tranmere Rovers. 
* After a somewhat ill-defined season, Morrisey hopes to relive old successes wearing the Tranmere shirt and he has the quality to do so. A regular in John Aldridge's schemes, he has a testimonial game pending as he has been 10 years at the club.

* Morrisey occupies the position of right wing at Tranmere Rovers, taking good advantage of his speed and skill to create chances for his team-mates. What's more, he is not a born scorer, although he will find the net a reasonable number of times. He dribbles sensationally before putting over a good cross, helped by his individual technical quality. He has a good shot with his right and is very safe and efficient in a one-on-one and with one-twos.  is excellent playing vision allows him to make some excellent passes.
x
* England youth international.

* Trained in the Everton youth squad, he signs as a professional in March 1983. He plays his only game for the Toffees in the last game of the 84-85 season against Luton Town when the team was already mathematically League Champion. 
* In August 1985 he is transferred to Wolverhampton Wanderers. He makes his league debut on 17th August 1985 against Brentford and scores his first goal on 7th September 1985 against Bolton. 
* He is transferred to Tranmere Rovers in October 1985 when his contract finishes. He makes his debut on 4th October 1985 against Southend, scoring his first goal for them this same day. 
* He is the son of the former Liverpool and Everton player Johnny Morrisey Sr.

* Morrisey spent most of the season coming into and then leaving the Tranmere side and only at the end of the League did he get to play a little more regularly. Even so, his plays were much appreciated by his team-mates as they produced plenty of danger in the rival box. In total he played 31 games and scored a goal.

900.name: Cross
pages: * Signed for Tranmere in March 1998.

* A versatile footballer, he usually plays at right half, although he is able to operate at centre forward or even as a defender.  Powerful on the run, he has a good turn and it is difficult to get the ball off him.
x
x
x

* He only played 18 league games with Wrexham, 11 of these from the start, and scored two goals before being loaned to Hereford United in December. At his new club things didn't go so well for him and he only played in five games, all from the start.

901.name: Mellon
pages: x

* A classy midfielder, he shows himself to be attack minded in everything he does,something which sees him regularly getting on the scoresheet. Technically sound andwith a powerful stride, his youth is another one of his assets.
x
x
x

* Mellon played in a total of 43 games during the course of last season,all of those as a member of the starting line up, scoring four goals in the process .One of the sides key men, Mellon was always involved in attacking moves although he failed to show the same goalscoring touch as the year before.

902.name: Mahon
pages: * Alan Mahon is another example of the excellent work being done in the club's youth squad, which has produced a lot of players with good futures in recent years. An Ireland international at the under-18 and under-21 levels, it won't be long before he makes his debut for his country's first team, though he should first try and settle in John Aldridge's eleven.

* Mahon is a midfielder with an obvious attacking nature who is as yet undiscovered ability for this sport. He is skilful, with good playing vision, and is quick, as well as possessing a tremendous determination for such a young lad. He doesn't score so many goals but does create chances for his team-mates.
x
x

* Originally from the lower ranks of Tranmere Rovers, Mahon signs as a professional on 7th April 1995. His first game for the club comes on 3rd February 1996 against Huddersfield Town and he scores against Port Vale on 27th August 1996.

* A sensational first full season for Alan Mahon at Tranmere Rovers as he managed to play in 25 matches and score 2 goals, though his appearances dropped off from October onwards. Even so, his most important event in the season was his step up from the Ireland under-18 to under-21 team, showing plenty of promise.

903.name: Branch
pages:
* The cousin of the Everton forward, Michael Branch, Graham is a player who has prodigious technique allowing him to do things impossible for most of the players in the First Division. He had to wait until two years ago before he could show his quality, but when he did so he caused a great impact. Very classy, Oldham Athletic were interested in him but in the end an agreement was not reached. 
* Graham Branch does, however, have a fault.  His performance is inconsistent, able dazzle one moment showing his vision, strength, shooting, speed and technique with his impressive left foot. However, despite this, Branch is a hard-working, and if he were more consistent, he could become one of the best players in the First Division and perhaps, one day, in the Premier League. An undisputed starter on John Aldridge's teamsheet.

* Graham Branch is a winger with a simply quite amazing technique. He can play on the left or right, and even as a centre forward to help out John Aldridge. He has an impressive physique and so it is a job to get the ball off him without committing a foul, and this also helps him in collisions with adversaries, where he comes out on top. Very left-footed, if he plays on the right, he tends to cut infield, trying a classy powerful move and either passing or shooting, as his shot with the left is tremendous. He crosses pretty well and is good in the air.
x
x

* Originally from the amateur club Heswall Athletic, he signs as a professional for Tranmere Rovers in May 1991. He makes his debut in the league on 17th September 1991 against Middlesbrough and scores his first goal for the club on 17th January 1996 against WBA, the equaliser for Rovers. 
* In November 1992 he is loaned to Bury, scoring in his debut game on 21st November 1992 against Hereford United.

* Branch had plenty of opportunities last year playing in 35 games and scoring 5 goals for Tranmere Rovers. However, his performances were just as irregular as ever and so he still didn't meet the expectations placed in him.

904.name: Jones
pages: * Aged 22, Gary Jones is the most versatile player at Tranmere Rovers, having played in just about every position except goalkeeper. Blessed with a good technique for such a tall man, his figure could be very important for the team when injuries come along as he can play anywhere without too much problem always doing his duty to perfection. Although it is not known where he will play, Gary Jones will be used a lot by John Aldridge.

* Gary Jones is a very versatile player and is just as good at centre back, in the midfield or even as centre forward. He is very tall and also very strong physically. He is not so quick but his power allows him to go from box to box to finish off a move. He has a good touch, basically with the right. A good passer, he doesn't make life too complicated and will normally look for the short pass. He is good in the air and so is dangerous at set-plays. Very hard-working, he always gives his all.
x
x
* Originally from the Tranmere Rovers schoolboys, he scores in his league debut on 20th November 1993 against Millwall.

* A series of injuries prevented him from having a good a season as usual, though he did finish as the second top scorer at the club behind, who else, John Aldridge. It was mostly for the player-manager that Gary Jones covered during most of the season but his enormous versatility allowed him to play 30 games for the Rovers.

905.name: Teale
pages:
* After his successful spells at Bournemouth and Aston Villa, especially at the latter of these with the League Cup title, the veteran English central defender was Tranmere Rovers' most expensive signing in their history, costing £450,000. 
* Shaun Teale is a back who give his all, being a true fighter on the pitch. Despite the cost he was a fantastic investment for Tranmere Rovers who brought a leader to the team. He has already fully justified his fee. Currently he is not playing from the start but can step onto the pitch as a good replacement for one of his team-mates.

* Teale is a very experienced central defender who is very left-footed, using his right just as a support. He is a very hard player, running the risk of a yellow card for his tackles. He is technically acceptable, and with his left he passes well over short and long range although, at times, he looses the ball because he delays too much. He doesn't usually push up at set-plays. He is good in the air but is not dominant in this department. Physically strong, he takes advantage of this in the collisions with the forwards. He is quite quick despite the years but he is not so agile.
* League Cup Champion 1994 with Aston Villa.
x

* Originally from the amateur club Weymouth, he signs as a professional in January 1989 for Bournemouth. He makes his debut in the league on 4th February 1989 against WBA and scores his first goal as a professional against Bradford City on 18th September 1990. 
* In July 1991 he is transferred to Aston Villa for £300,000, making his league debut on 17th August 1991 against Sheffield Wednesday. His first goal comes on 17th January 1993 against Middlesbrough. 
* In the summer of 1995 he is transferred to Tranmere Rovers for £450,000, making his debut in the league on 12th August 1995 against Wolverhampton Wanderers. 
* He is loaned to Preston North End on 6th February 1997. His first game comes on 8th February against Rotherham United.

* Teale had a season which changed a lot after the new year. Before then he was an undisputed starter for Aldridge, playing 25 games for Tranmere Rovers. However, from this moment on, he never regained his place on the teamsheet, coming on for the odd game as a substitute and was loaned to Preston North End where he played 5 games.

906.name: O´Brien
pages: * Liam O´Brien is a veteran Irish midfielder who likes to play just in front of the defence, from where he initiates the attacking moves of his team-mates, distributing the ball efficiently and safely. His magnificent season at Tranmere Rovers gave him the chance to increase his number of appearances for his country, being called up to play and show his undeniable qualities.

* O´Brien is a player who plays in front of the defence and from this position he distributes the ball adequately. He has very good positioning on the pitch which helps him in his role as playmaker at Tranmere Rovers, passing well in short and moving the ball fluidly to give a rapid outlet for the attack. He has good technique allowing him to get out of difficult situations. He is physically strong and goes in hard for the ball. O'Brien doesn't join in the attack, covering for the centre backs when they go up for corners or free-kicks. He is a good free-kick taker with his right from long range, powerful and well placed.
x
* O´Brien has been an Ireland international in the schoolboy, youth, under-23 and full categories 15 times, the first on 23rd April 1986 against Uruguay in Dublin.

* Manchester United sign him from the Irish team Shamrock Rovers in October 1986, being one of Ron Atkinson's last signings before he was sacked as the Reds manager. He makes his debut in the league on 6th February 1988 against Leicester City and scores his first league goal against Coventry City, the winner, at Old Trafford. 
* He is transferred to Newcastle United in November 1988 for £350,000. He makes his debut on 19th November 1988 against Millwall and scores his first goal on 26th February 1989 against Middlesbrough. 
* In January 1994 he is transferred to Tranmere Rovers in exchange for £300,000. He plays his first game on 23rd January 1994 against Bolton Wanderers and scores his first goal on 29th March 1994 against Derby County.

* In general terms, O'Brien's season could be classified as good even managed to be included in the Ireland squad under the command of Mick McCarthy. He played 41 games but his performance dropped with regards to his goalscoring, he only found the net once. Even so, he was one of the most important men in the team last season.
