907.name: Stevens
pages:
* Gary Stevens has been one of the best right backs in English football in the last decade, playing 46 times for England and for first class teams such as Everton and Glasgow Rangers for many years. 
* In his fourth year at Tranmere Rovers, this summer the English defender has already shown that he is a player who is perfectly viable for a modest team such as Tranmere Rovers. Thanks to his broad experience, Stevens is an almost irreplaceable player, and the calmness he brings to the side is almost priceless. 
* Hoping that this season will be quieter than the last, Gary Stevens is playing out his last few moments with good football at Rovers.

* Gary Stevens normally plays at right back, the position he has occupied during his career, but at Tranmere he has played at left back and even as a central defender. He has great positioning, the product of his broad experience. He is calm, and in difficult moments resolves the situation efficiently. He prefers to use his right and has a good individual technique allowing him to pass well both over short and long range. 
* Physically very strong, he takes advantage of this in the fight for the ball. Despite the passing of the years, he still has a good turn of speed. He doesn't push up into the attack as much as he used to when he was a lad, but when he does so he is decisive and puts over good crosses. He has a good shot from a distance with his right. He is good in the air in defence but doesn't usually try out his header in attack. He puts the ball over from free-kicks very well.

* League Champion with Everton in 84-85 and 86-87. 
* FA Cup Champion with Everton 1984. 
* FA Cup Runner-Up with Everton 1985 and 1986. 
* Scottish League Champion with Glasgow Ranger from 88-89 till 93-94.
* Scottish Cup Champion with Rangers 91-92. 
* Scottish Cup Runner-Up with Rangers 88-89 and 93-94. 
* League Cup Champion with Rangers in 88-89, 90-91 and 93-94. 
* League Cup Runner-up with Rangers in 89-90.

* 46 full international appearances for England, he makes his debut on 6th June 1985 in a triangular tournament in Mexico between Italy, England and the Mexican side. 
* Stevens participates in the Mexico 86 World Cup with his country, playing in the 5 games that England played, and in the Italy 90 World Cup, but he only appeared in the first game against the Republic of Ireland as he had a disastrous game, and didn't reappear for the whole of the competition. He also played in the Germany 88 European Championship, playing in his country's three games. 
* His last game for England was on 3rd June 1992 against Finland in Helsinki.

* Trained in the Everton youth squad, Stevens signs as a professional in March 1981. His league debut takes place on 10th October 1981 against West Ham United and seven days later, his first goal for the Toffees comes as the winner against Ipswich Town. 
* After more than 200 appearances for Everton, he is transferred to Glasgow Rangers in the summer of 1988 for £1 million. His first game for the Scottish team comes on 13th August 1988 against Hamilton Academicals, also scoring in this game. 
* Finally he is signed by Tranmere Rovers in October 1994 for £350,000. He makes his debut on 24th September 1994 against Sunderland and scores his first goal for the Merseyside club against Swindon Town. 
* In the final of the Scottish Cup with Glasgow Rangers, a mistake of his when playing back to Chris Woods let in Joe Miller to score Glasgow Celtic's winner.

* A magnificent season for Gary Stevens, who was indispensable for John Aldridge when he was choosing his team.  His presence on the pitch helped Tranmere a lot and he continued to give signs of his good football. Unfortunately this run was cut short when he broke his forearm in February against Charlton Athletic, and his season suddenly ended. In total he played 31 games.

908.name: Carbon
pages:
* Signed for WBA in January 1998. 
* Matt Carbon is destined to be one of the stars at WBA in the coming years. His progress in the last few years has been quite simply spectacular. An under-21 international for England, every one of his actions oozes maturity. He has all the qualities necessary to be successful.  A classy left-footed player, his technique announces a good player. And there are even those who compare him with Mick Harford due to his dominance in the air. He is on the right tracks.The 97-98 season awaits his confirmation.

* Despite his youth, Matt Carbon shows some resources of a veteran footballer. Still learning, he has been played in several positions, from central defender to centre forward passing through the midfield. Left-footed, with time ahead to polish up his technique, he stands out for his capability to win aerial balls. He judges the timing of the jump to perfection, hanging in the air to, at the right moment, connect with the header. Although he has a goalscoring instinct, his natural position is on the left of the midfield, a position where his contribution to the team is greater.
x
* 4 under-21 appearances for England.

* A product of the Lincoln City youth squad, Carbon turned professional on the 13th of April 1993. Shortly afterwards he made his debut as a professional in one of the last games of the 92-93 season.
* On the 27th of December 1994 Carbon has a sensational game at home against Darlington. He scored his first two goals as a professional, one of them extraordinary, a lob over the rival goalie. He finished the 94-95 season as one of Lincoln's top scorers, hitting the target 7 times, the same number as his team mate Bannister.
* 1996 is, without doubt, his year. On the 8th of March he was transferred to Derby County for £385,000. The following day he makes his debut in the First Division, although the team lose 3-0 at Sunderland. Months later Matt celebrates his team's promotion to the Premier League and his first appearance for the England under-21 team. 
* Signed for WBA in January 1998.

* Carbon was in the starting line-up for 6 of the 10 games he played. He showed that he is a footballer on the up. He played as a centre back and even did his duty at right back, but the strong competition for a place in the team prevented him from playing more often. Even so, he was once again called up for the England under-21 team, whose colours he defended three more times.

909.name: Kilbane
pages: * A talented young Irish player who has already made his under-21 debut for his country, Kevin Kilbane is the most expensive signing in West Bromwich Albion's history, with the final total in the deal that took him to the Hawthorns reaching somewhere around the £1.25 million mark. Nevertheless, despite the fee, the money seems to have been well spent by the Baggies, who have acquired the services of a sensational footballer who already has plenty of admirers among the clubs in the Premier League, which is where he could be heading in the not too distant future. In the meantime he will be out to help his new club as much as he possibly can.

* Kilbane is a winger who operates down the left hand side of the field and possesses lightning speed which allows him to take on and beat any defender he seems to come up against. Nevertheless, he is not a player who relies on speed alone since he is also blessed with tremendous individual technique and skill, which, combined with his explosiveness makes him a fearsome opponent. He possesses a maturity beyond his years, even when he is in the thick of the action. His skill and ability to create chances for others makes him an automatic choice in the side. He can also carve out opportunities for himself although he needs to work on his own final touch in front of goal.
x
* Kilbane has made 4 under-21 international appearances for Ireland.

* A product of the Preston North End youth system, he signed professional  terms for the club on 6th July 1995. His first game for Preston came on 12th March 1994 against Torquay United, while he opened his professional goalscoring account on 3rd February 1996 against Wigan Athletic 
* In the summer of 1997, he became West Bromwich Albion's first million pound player.

* Kevin Kilbane had a magnificent season at Preston North End, putting together some tremendous peformances for them and managing to attract the attention of WBA, who offered £900,000 for the player, a sum which was turned down by Preston North End. Despite a loss in form and a series of minor injuries, Kilbane finally mangaged to make a total of 36 appearances, finding the back of the net twice during the course of last season.

910.name: Flynn
pages: * Sean Flynn is one of WBA's main reinforcements for this season, a season in which he will be looking to make himself a regular member of the starting line up. He brings tremendous experience to the side, most of it Premier League experience, as well as the versatility which allows him to play in virtually any position anywhere on the park. Given the qualities he possesses he will no doubt become an important player this season for Ray Harford's side.

* Versatility and team spirit are Sean Flynn's main assets. During the course of his still relatively short career he has played in all kinds of positions, from defence through to the forward line, although, at Derby County, manager Jim Smith generally line him up at right back or as a right sided midfield player. An energetic player with great speed and stamina, he never gives a ball up for lost and is constantly making himself available to his teammates. He always gives 100% and never hesitates when he has to go up to try to win the ball in the air, despite his lack of height. Skillful with the ball at his feet, although he he doesn't often score, Sean Flynn's hard working style of play is always well appreciated by his managers.
x
x

* Sean Flynn was playing for modest Halesowen Town when he caught the eye of the Coventry City coaching staff. As a result, on 1st December 1991, he was transfered to Highfield Road for £20,000. 
* He made his debut on 1st January 1991 at Brammal Lane against Sheffield United, and scored a superb goal from all of 40 yards. Manager Terry Butcher played him down the right hand side, where he soon became a regular member of the Sky Blues' starting line up. His versatility and will to win saw him playing regularly in the Premier League. 
* On 1st April 1995 he suffered an ankle injury in a league game against Queens Park Rangers. Shortly afterwards on 11th August, he was transfered to Derby County for £250,000 in a deal which  saw Paul Williams move in the opposite direction to Coventry City. 
* On 13th August, in the first game of the season, he made his debut for Derby County at the old Baseball Ground against Port Vale (0-0). On 6th September he scored his first goal for the Rams against Portsmouth (2-2).
* Flynn went out on loan to Stoke City on 27th March 1997, making his debut two days later against Oldham Athletic. 
* He was signed by WBA in the summer of 1997.

* Flynn found it difficult to get into the starting line up at Derby County at the beginning of the season, although his versatility and determination proved to be vital in allowing him to force his way into the side for a spell. Unfortunatelly, he lost his place once again and eventually had to move on to Stoke City, on loan, where he made 5 appearances for the Potters, who he helped to turn into a more compact side. With Derby County he ended the season with 17 appearances and one goal to his name.

911.name: Butler
pages: * Unable to reproduce his best form at Notts County, Peter Butler saw  himself loaned out to two different clubs. At the second of those he made a tremendous impression and proved to be one of the main reasons why the Baggies managed to avoid relegation to the Second Division. He is hoping to be able to fight back after a season in which a serious injury put him out of action for five months preventing him from being the focal point for the team that he proves to be, in the centre of the midfield alongside Sneekes. This time out he will no doubt form a partnership once again with the Dutchman, providing he suffers no more setbacks with injuries.

* Butler is player of great strength in the middle of the park. He is a good ballwinner, is hard, very competitive and important in giving the side balance in the midfield. Despite his fighting spirit, he shows good touches of skill and is a good passer of the ball, distributing the ball efficiently although he is not a player who should be thought of as a midfield playmaker.
x
x

* Butler learnt his trade in the youth ranks at Huddersfield Town, signing professional for the club in August 1984. He made his league debut for Huddersfield on 25th August 1984, against Oxford United.
* He went out on loan to Cambridge United in January 1986. He played his  first game for the club on 25th January 1986 against Port Vale and scored his first goal as a professional on 18th March 1986 against Preston North End.
* He completed his contract with Huddersfield Town and signed for Bury in July 1986, making his debut for the club on 23rd August 1986 against Bristol City. 
* He once again became a free agent and signed for Cambridge United in December 1986. He played his first game for the club on 10th December 1986 against Wrexham and struck his first goal in a Cambridge shirt on 31st January 1987 against Exeter City. 
* He was transfered to Southend United in February 1988 for £75,000. He made his debut on 13th February 1988 against Bristol Rovers and scored his first goal for the club on 5th March 1988 against Rotherham United. 
* Huddersfield Town signed him once again, this time on loan, in March 1992. He made his debut the second time round for the Terriers on 28th March 1992 against WBA. 
* West Ham United signed him in October 1992, for £125.000. He made his Hammers debut on 16th August 1992 against Barnsley, and opened his account for the east London club on 9th February 1993 against Peterborough.
* He was transfered to Notts County in October 1994 for £350,000, making his debut on 15th October 1994 against Watford.
* Loaned out to Grismby Town, in January 1996, he played his first game for Grimsby on 3rd February 1996 against Derby County. 
* He moved to WBA on loan in March 1996. He made his debut on 20th March 1996 against Portsmouth. His loan spell finally became a permanent transfer during the summer of 1996 for £175,000.

* A very unfortunate season for Peter Butler, following a serious injury  in a pre-season freindly which kept him out of action for five months. On his return he made a total of 17 appearances during the second part of the season, in which he showed how valuable he is to the Baggies.

912.name: Sneekes
pages:
* During the 94-95 season Sneekes was a key player in Bolton Wanderers' promotion to the Premier League, but, following Bruce Rioch's departure to Arsenal, he fell from grace both with Roy McFarland and Colin Todd. 
* He was transfered to West Bronwich Albion, where he has one again been able to show his ability, although he hasn't improved his goalscoring record. Without doubt Sneekes was the key to WBA managing to remain in the First Division with his attacking style of play and the character he gave to the side. He is at the very heart of Albion's side, and, if he is playing well, then the club can hope to reach the very top of the First Division, although their first priority must obviously be to avoid relegation.

* An excellent passer of the ball, Richard Sneekes is a player who is always involved in the game and is always available for his teammates and likely to set up a goalscoring chance. He has a good shot both from long distance and closer to goal. However if one characteristic of his  game stands out this is his attacking ability, where he is a tremendous  player, quick and decisive, always looking to link up with his teammates  or to play one-twos to penetrate the opposition's penalty area. Inside the area he is a good finisher finding in the back of the net with both powerful shots as well as more subtle touches. He is also a good ball winner and battles away for ninety minutes.
x
* He has made 2 full international appearances for Holland - against USSR and Germany.

* Signed for Fortuna Sittard by Bolton Wanderers in the summer of 1994 in  exchange for £150,000. He made his league debut for Bolton on 13th August 1994 against Grismby Town, and opened his goalscoring account in English football against Luton Town on 13th September 1994. 
* WBA signed him for £500,000 in March 1996. His debut couldn't have been better, managing to find the back of the net against Watford on 12th March 1996. 
* He made his league debut for Ajax at just 16 years of age, which was a record which he held until it was beaten by Clarence Seedorf, now playing for Real Madrid.

* The beginning of the season for Richard Sneekes wasn't as good as it could have been, losing his place in the Baggies starting line up. Neverthless, this poor run didn't last too long, and, soon after, he once again became the team's focal point in midfield, managing to also occasionally find the back of the net. In short, it was a tremendous season for the Dutch midfielder who made 45 appearances, managing to hit the target 8 times.

913.name: Gilbert
pages: * After seven seasons at Grimsby Town, Gilbert surprised the club's supporters by moving on to join WBA. A man of great quality and a very unselfish attitude, his signing brought to the club a player who is a tremendous performer down the left hand side of the park which is where he operates. Despite his qualities though, following the arrival of Ray Harford in the hot seat at the Hawthorns, he seems to have fallen out of favour and is finding it very difficult to force his way into the manager's plans. Nevertheless, he remains a valuable player and will be hoping to show the manager that he is still a player who could do an important job for the side.

* An experienced left sided midfield player, Gilbert posses good dribbling ability and is a very skillful player with the ball at his feet. He has a good shot with either foot, although he is stronger on his left. Technically he is quite a complete player and, added to his ability on the ball, shows great vision which allows him to spray some excellent passes around to his teammates. A very hard worker, he is apparently untiring both in attack and defence. He is also an excellent crosser of the ball.
* Top goalscorer at Grimsby Town 90-91.
x

* After coming the youth ranks at Lincoln City, he signed professional in June 1981. He made his league debut on 4th May 1981 against Bury  and scored the first goal of his professional career on 12th September 1981 against Plymouth Argyle. 
* In August 1982 he was transfered to Scunthorpe United. He played his first game for the club on 19th September 1982 against York City.
* He returned to the professional game, signing for Northampton Town. He made his debut on 23rd August 1986 against Scunthorpe United, while he scored his first goal for the club against Lincoln City on 21st December 1986.
* After a good career with Northampton Town, he was transfered to Grimsby Town in March 1989 for £55,000. 
* Surprisingly, Grimsby Town decided to sell him to WBA at the beginning of last season. He scored on his debut for WBA against Charlton Athletic on 12th May 1995, a goal which clinched a victory for his side. 
* He was loaned out to York City on 7th March 1997. His first game for the club came on 8th March against Blackpool.

* It wasn't the best of seasons for Dave Gilbert, who saw his form affected by a series of injuries. His contribution to the Baggies' season was limited to just 18 games and one goal. The worst moment of the season for him personally came when Alan Buckley was forced to leave the club and he saw himself relegated to the reserves following the arrival of new manager Ray Harford. In order to get a taste of regular first team football, he had to move on to York City, who he joined on loan in March. He played 9 games for the club and managed to add one more goal to his tally, before the season ended.

914.name: Coldicott
pages: * Stacy Coldicottt is a player who, having come through the youth ranks at WBA, finally managed to force his way into Alan Buckley's side on a regular basis, winning the manager's trust when it came to naming the starting line up. Following Buckley's departure, he battled to become a part of new manager Ray Harford's plans, something he managed to achieve towards the end of the season. Despite not having been a regular over the course of recent seasons, He remains a good competitor out on the park, and, when he plays, always gives 100%. He is not currently a part of Ray Harford's side, although he will no doubt have a contribution to make as the season progress.

* A player of great strength in the middle of the park, he is an excellent ballwinner. A hard player, he keeps opponents under constant pressure and is always a very uncomfortable opponent to come up against. Right footed, he possesses a good shot from around 25 yards out. Technically he is quite mediocre, although he makes up for that with his strength and enthusiasm.
x
x

* Coldicott learnt his trade in the youth ranks at WBA, and played his first game for the club on 2nd September 1992 against Stockport County. He had to wait for his first goal until 13th November 1996 against Sheffield United. 
* He was loaned out to Cardiff City during the 1996-97 season, making his first appearance on 31st August 1996 against Cambridge United.

* Loaned out to Carlisle United at the beginning of the season Coldicott made 6 appearances for the club before returning to the Baggies. He was only very occasionally a first choice, under both Alan Buckley as well as Ray Harford, having to battle with at least half a dozen other similar players for a midfield place. However, he managed to force his way in towards the end of the season, making by the end of the campaign a total of 19 appearances, and finding the back of the net for WBA on 3 occasions.

915.name: Van Blerk
pages: * Jason Van Blerk is one of the real globetrotters of European football. This Australian international has played for teams in Belgium, Holland and now finds himself at WBA after a short spell at Manchester City. Jason will be hoping that he can show his best form after recently getting over a serious injury which last year prevented him from making more than just a handful of appearances. Although not an automatic first team choice he may well force his way into the side, given his versatility and undoubted ability.

* He is a versatile player who can operate in a number of different positions although his natutal position is left back. A hard running, mobile player he is quick, has good stamina and shows both intelligence and technique. When he lines up in midfield he generally does so out wide on the left hugging the touchline, from where he puts some good accurate service through into the strikers. He can also do a good job as a central defender.
x
* 22 full international appearances Australia.

* The Australian international signed for Millwall on 8 th September 1994, from Dutch club Go Ahead Eagles, in exchange for £300,000. His first game for the London club came on 17th September against Bristol Rovers, while he struck his first goal on English soil on 1st March 1995 against  Swindon Town.  
* He was signed by Manchester City during the summer of 1997.
* Van Blerk was just another one of Millwall's injury victims, having a number of problems which limited him to just four games all season.

916.name: Potter
pages:
* The signing of Graham Potter was Southampton's most important acquisition as the 96-97 season approached, and represented the biggest fee that the Saints paid out during that particular season. The player's youth, and, above all, the brilliant progress he had shown the previous season at Stoke City, finally encouraged the clubs directors to tie up a deal to bring him to the club. 
* Aunque teóricamente no entrar  de salida en los esquemas de Graeme Souness, nuevo entrenador del Southampton, nadie duda de que el joven Potter disfrutar  de la oportunidad de debutar en la Premier League, el sueño de todos los futbolistas de Inglaterra.

* Potter does an excellent job both at left back as well as on the left hand side of the midfield. He moves forward to the line, staying tight on the touchline, he regularly gets forward to support the attack, helped out by the technique he possesses in his left foot, as well as his reserves of stamina. Defensively he does an effective job, although, on occasions his lack of experience is all too evident. Still a very young player, he is making rapid progress, improving both his positional play as well as his vision and reading of the game.
x
* An England youth international.

* After coming through the ranks at Birmingham City, he signed professional  on 1st July 1992. 
* He was loaned out to Wycombe Wanderers on 17th September 1993. He played in 3 Third Division games.
* On 20th December 1993 he was transfered to Stoke City for £73,000 making his debut on 15th January 1994 against Grimsby Town (0-0). 
* In the summer of 1996 Southampton took him on, after paying out £500,000.

* Con 41 partidos disputados, Graham Potter fue uno de los futbolistas m s importantes del Stoke City durante la pasada temporada, en la que se clasificaron en el cuarto puesto final de la Primera División, posición que pudieron rubricar con el ascenso a la Premier League. Jugó pr cticamente toda la temporada en el centro del campo, y su buena campaña no pasó desapercibida para los técnicos del Southampton, que no dudaron en ficharlo para reforzar al equipo de The Dell.

917.name: Murphy
pages: * Shaun Murphy is a central defender who is a regular in the Australian national squad, being called up by Australian national coach Terry Venables. He was a key member of the side that won the Bronze medal in the 1996 Olympic games in Atlanta. Nevertheless, after returning to Notts County, he had a contractual dispute with the club and was placed on the transfer list. He was effectively put up for auction, with West Bromwich Albion outbidding Southampton for a player who went on to make a fine impression during his first year with the Baggies. He is not a regular member of the side, but will be waiting patiently to get his chance as the season unfolds.

* A central defender, he generally takes up the position on the right hand side of the defence. Forceful in the air, he moves forward to join the attack at free kicks and corners, occasionally managing to get on the scoresheet. Technically speaking he is a player who can certainly look after himself and has the ability to bring the ball out at the back.
* A bronze medal winner in the Olympic Games in Atlanta with the Australian national side.
* Murphy has made 9 full international appearances for Australia.

* Murphy signed for Notts County from Australian club Perth Italia on 4th September 1992. His first appearance for the club came on 5th September 1992 against Barnsley, while he hit his first goal in English football on 29th of that same month against Tranmere Rovers. 
* He was transfered to West Bronwich Albion on 31st December 1996 for £500,000. He played his first game for the Baggies on 12th January 1997 against Wolverhampton Wanderers. He scored his first goal for the club on 5th March against Southend United.

* Murphy arrived at Notts County after a series of superb performances for the Australian side that won the bronze medal in the Olympic Games in Atlanta. He was once gain a regular for County, but, suprisingly, was transfered to WBA, a club where he also gave a fine account of himself. In total he played in 17 games for the Baggies, scoring twice. He also made a total of 16 league appearances for Notts County.

918.name: McDermott
pages: * Andrew McDermott is a young player of whom great things are expected, and who is one of the brightest young Australian players around at the moment. His natural footballing ability has shone out both at QPR and WBA, the two clubs he has played for, both of which have been well satisfied with his performances. Although he still has plenty to learn, he is not daunted by the task facing him, and, as a result of his excellent performances, he has managed to force his way into the Baggies line up as a regular member of the back four. He is, certainly, a player to keep an eye on in the future.

* Andrew McDermott is a very young player who basically plays at right back, although his natural ability also allows him to operate on the right hand side of the midfield. He is comfortable in possession and is a decisive player in everything he does. One of his greatest assets is his composure out on the park, which is exceptional for such a young player. As well as all these qualities he is technically very sound and possesses good pace.
x
* McDermott is an Australian international.

* QPR signed him from the Australian Institute of Sport on 4th August 1995. McDermott made his debut on 14th December 1996 against Southend United and found the back of the net on 26th of that same month against Norwich City.
* The Australian defender was transfered to WBA on 27th March 1997 for £400,000. He made his first appearance for the Baggies on 5th April against Sheffield United.

* McDermott began the league season as a QPR player, making sporadic appearances for west London club, although he made a fine impression every time he played. With Rangers he made 6 appearances, managing to score twice, before being transfered to WBA. He played in another 6 games for the Baggies and stood out for his composure and security in possession, making himself a regular member of the side in the final weeks of the season.

919.name: Dobson
pages: * During the course of the last few seasons, Tony Dobson had seen himself relegated to the bench at Portsmouth, and had only managed to get into  the action when injuries and suspensions left the manager with no other option. After being released by Portsmouth during the summer, Dobson  is now out to try to make himself a more regular part of Ray Harford's plans at WBA, although the beginning of the season has not yet turned  out to be as promising as he might have hoped. Nevertheless, if he doesn't achieve his ambition he will be happy to go out and do the job he did as a member of the squad at Portsmouth.

* A left footed player, he can do a job either at the heart of the defence or at left back. He stands out for the aggresion and forcefulness he shows when he goes in to win the ball from opposing forwards, qualities which make him an important player when it comes to ball winning responsibilites. However he rarely makes a contribution in an attacking sense, an aspect of his game he should try to improve.
* F.A. Youth Cup Winners medal 1987.
* 4 under-21 international appearances for England.

* After coming through the ranks at Coventry City, he signed professional in July 1986. 
* In January 1991 he was transfered to Blackburn Rovers for £300,000. 
* He became a Portsmouth player in September 1993, for £150,000. 
* In December 1994 he was loaned out to Oxford United while in January 1996 he went out on loan once again this time to Peterborough United. 
* He joined the Baggies in the summer of 1997.

* Dobson had a season which became an all too familiar tale for him, proving unable to force his way into Portsmouth's side, only getting into the action when a teammate's injury meant he had to come in to make a contribution. At the end of the league season, he had made just 6 appearances.

920.name: Nicholson
pages: * A regular member of the side, but by no means an automatic choice, at Derby County over the last few seasons, the arrival at the club of Chris Powell saw him lose his place at right back. It seemed unlikely that his situation was about to get better, and so, as a result, he decided to move on to West Bromwich Albion, a club, who, at the time, were looking for a player of his type. Well used to playing as an attacking left back at Derby, his arrival at West Brom gave the club a player of tremendous attacking potential. In fact, from the moment he signed, he made himself an automatic choice in the side, apart from a period last year when he picked up a serious injury. Now, fortunately, fully recovered, he is once again a first team regular, under Ray Harford, just as he was under Alan Buckley.

* Nicholson is a tremendously attack minded full back who is continually  up and down the flank, showing strength and determintation. He is a very quick player who is also a good, though slightly inconsistent crosser of the ball. Occasionally, in his eagerness to get forward he leaves gaps at the back, although he has the pace to get back into position when the side lose possession. He is a hard tackler when he goes in to try to win the ball.
x
x

* After coming through the ranks at Lincoln City, Nicholson signed as a professional in July 1988. He made his league debut on 22nd November 1986 against Burnley, and scored his first league goal, and his first as a professional, against Darlington on 22nd October 1988. 
* In April 1992, he was transfered to Derby County for £80,000. He made his first appearance on 24th February 1993 against Leicester City, while his first league goal for the club came his way on 16th  March 1994 against Peterborough United. 
* He was transfered to WBA in February 1996 for £150,000. He made his debut for Albion on 10th February 1996 against Southend United.

* Shane Nicholson had an unfortunate season last time around time with WBA. He was showing some good form and was an automatic choice for Alan Buckley, until a serious leg injury caused him to miss virtually the whole of the rest of the season, only managing to get back into action for the Baggies reserve side as he attempted to battle his way back from his injury.

921.name: Raven
pages: * A key man at the heart of the defence, Paul Raven forms a magnificent partnership at the back for WBA alongside Daryl Burgess. Despite being technically weak, his tremendous security in the rest of his defensive duties make him a real pillar of the side's defence. He is also a player who has character in abundance, and likes to take charge of things at the back, qualities which make him a fantastic leader out on the park for for the Baggies. His form during the course of last season made him an important player for the side, and, if WBA don't want to suffer too much this time around, they will have to make sure that they have Paul Raven on their side.

* Paul Raven is a classical central defender, tremendously strong, hard but fair and excellent in the air, a quality which allows him to move forward to join the attack for dead ball situations where he is especially dangerous. A quick player, he is nothing out of this word technically speaking and prefers to keep things simple, being, as he is, fully aware of his limitations. Bearing in mind that he is not completely comfortable in possession, then it is unusual to see him attempting to bring the ball out from the back under control.
x
* An England schoolboy international.

* A product of the youth system at Doncaster Rovers, Raven signed as a profesional in June 1988. He made his league debut on 31st October 1987 against Bury, and scored his first goal on 26th December 1987 against York City.
* After some tremendous pereformances for Rovers he was transfered to WBA in March 1989 for £100,000. He played his first game for the club on 1st May against Portsmouth. 
* He went back to Doncaster Rovers on loan in November 1991, making his debut on 30th November 1991 against Lincoln City.
* He returned to WBA where he scored his first league goal for the club on 21st March 1992 against Reading.

* Once again Raven proved to be a key figure at the heart of the Baggies' defence last season, playing in 33 games and scoring once. His performances didn't let anyone down, despite being partnered by a number of different players such as Burgess, Murphy and Mardon, which denied him the opportunity to develop a genuine understanding with any of them over a reasonable period of time.

922.name: Mardon
pages: * Paul Mardon formed a magnificent partnership at the heart of the WBA defence along with Paul Raven, proving to be one of the best duos in the First Division. Due to his ability on the ball Mardon is a player who is capable of bringing the ball out of defence. Nevertheless this season he has seen his place in the side taken from him by Burgess, meaning that, for the moment he will have to settle for a place on the bench. Even so, if he carries on producing the right kind of performance, when he gets the chance, and if luck is on his side, then it shouldn't be long before he takes the definitive step up to the full Welsh side, and gets back into the starting line up at Albion.

* Paul Mardon is a very complete central defender. A dominant player, he shows good positional sense and anticipation. Powerful in the air he makes the most of his physical power to impose himself on opposing forwards. A hard, quick player he has enough technical ability to bring the ball out from the back, an ability which also makes him capable of doing a job in midfield or even at right back. He is occasionally guilty of losing his concentration at the back and getting caught out at dead ball situations, though these occasions are very few and far between.
x
* He has made one full international appearance for Wales.

* After coming trhough the youth ranks at Bristol City, he signed professional in January 1988. He made his league debut on 9th January 1988 against Preston North End. 
* In September 1990 he was loaned out to Doncaster Rovers, making his first appearance for the club on 15th September 1990 against Rochdale.
* He was transfered to Birmingham City in the summer of 1991 in exchange for £65,000 pounds. His debut came on 17th August 1991 against Bury, while he scored his first goal for the club on 1st May 1993 against Bristol Rovers.
* Finally, he moved on to WBA in November 1993. He played his first game for the Baggies on 21st November 1993 against Nottingham Forest, and scored his first goal for the club on 25th February 1994 against Wolverhampton Wanderers.

* Mardon, obviously, didn't have the season that he had been hoping for at the start of the campaign. A muscle injury put him out of action from October right through until March, missing a large part of the Baggies season as a result. On his return he played in a number of games for the reserves as well as the first team. He eventually made a total of 14 appearances.

923.name: Burgess
pages: * Daryl Burgess is a player who always does a good job, keeping things simple but always giving an effective performance. A player who has spent the whole of his career at WBA, his solid consistent performances make him a player who regularly forms part of the starting line up as statistics in recent seasons demonstrate. The good form he showed last season alongside Paul Raven at the heart of the defence has allowed him to win a place in the side under Ray Harford. Although he will have to be wary of Mardon, who, naturally, will be out to take his place in the side off him.

* Daryl Burgess can play either as a central defender, a full back or even as a sweeper. In any of these positions he is a very consistent player, who is rarely seen to make an unforced error, being very secure in just about everything he does. He is quick, is a good marker and goes in hard, never giving opponents a moments respite as he shows himself to be a tremendous threat in the opposition's penalty area at dead ball situations. It is a rare sight to see him moving forward with the ball, only doing so when the opportunity clearly presents itself, with his more likely option being to quickly play the ball forward into the midfield area.
x
x

* After coming through the youth ranks at WBA, he signed as a professional in July 1989. He made his league debut on 26th August 1989 against Port Vale, while he scored his first goal on 21st September 1991 against Chester City, a goal that clinched a victory for his side.

* As is customary in Daryl Burgess, his season was characterised by the consistency of his performances. He hit his best form when he teamed up alongside first of all Paul Raven, and, later, Shaun Murphy at the heart of the Baggies' defence. In total he played In 33 games, scoring one goal.

924.name: Holmes
pages: * After a number of years in the lower divisions plus a couple of seasons at Everton, where he was never really given a chance, Paul Holmes joined WBA, where he surprised a lot of people with the tremendous form he showed after forcing his way into the side. His presence in the side gave the Baggies a new dimension in attack and brought to the club a player who can make good forward runs down the flank, causing great danger to the opposition. Despite these good moments with WBA, the arrival of Andrew McDermott at the Hawthorns has temporarily blocked his path to the first team although his verstatility could be the crucial factor in finally allowing him to force his way into Ray Harford's plans.

* Holmes is a very attack minded right back who moves forward in support whenever he gets even the slightest of opportunities. He constantly goes off on overlaps and is untiring in his support of the right sided midfield man playing just in front of him. Technically he is quite competent, and posesses good dribbling skills and is an effective passer of the ball. He puts over good quality crosses looking primarily for Hunt and Taylor. He is secure defensively, and shows himself top be fast  and hard in the tackle. Given his ability and his approach to the game, he can also do a job as a right sided midfield player.

925.name: Miller
pages: * Alan Miller knows exactly what it feels like to go through months and months on the bench, waiting for an opportunity to come along. He unfortunately had the opportunity to go through that experience during his time at Arsenal as well as during his spell at Middlesbrough, who he left last year in an attempt to carve out more of a future for himself than he seemed to have under Bryan Robson at 'Boro. Since his arrival at Albion he has managed to dislodge Paul Crichton from the number one spot, and make the goalkeeping position his own. At last the opportunity that he has waited so long for has finally come his way, and Alan Miller will no doubt be out to make sure that he takes full advantage.

* A brave keeper with tremendous reflexes, Miller is a very safe performer in goal, due, to a large extent, to his fantastic agility. He organises his defenders well and demonstrates enviable positional sense, which together  with his sense of anticipation allows him to efficiently close down the angles on opposing forwards. He his also recognised as having a tremendously powerful as well as accurate kick. However, his ability as as shot stopper when he is on his goal line occasionally leads to him becoming indecisive when he is required to come off his line to go up for high balls into the box, an aspect of his game he needs to try to work on.

* European Cup Winners Cup winners medal 1994. 
* F.A. Cup winners medal 1993. 
* League Cup winners medal  1993. 
* First Divisions winners medal 1995.
* 4 Under-21 international appearances for England.

* Alan Miller is a product of the youth set up at Arsenal, moving up to the first team squad on 5th May 1988. However, the presence of first Lukic, and then Seaman, prevented him from making a name for himself At Highbury. In fact, his professional debut came while he was out on loan, playing for Plymouth Argyle. He arrived at the club on 24th November 1988, and, two days later, made his first appearance in a game against Oldham Athletic. 
* Once back at Arsenal, he spent two seasons without getting a taste of first team football before going out on loan once again, this time to West Bromwich Albion (15th August 1991). In December of that same year, he went out on loan again, this time to Birmingham City. 
* Arsenal's signing of David Seaman in 1990 proved to be the final straw for Alan Miller, who had to settle for making the most of the England  international's occasional absences through injury to enjoy just a handful of opportunities to play in goal for the Gunners. 
* With an apparently bleak future ahead of him at Highbury, he was transfered to Middlesbrough on 12th August 1994. He made his debut one day later in a 2-0 home victory against Burnley. In his first season with 'Boro he made himself a regular member of the starting line up and made a decisive contribution to the club's promotion to the Premier League, winning the  First Division along the way. 
* In the first game of the 95-96 season, Miller returned to Highbury, this time wearing a  Middlesbrough shirt. He went on to become the star of that particular game, his tremendous performance against strikers of the quality of Bergkamp and Wright allowing 'Boro to earn a 1-1 draw. Following the third game of the season he picked up an injury and was replaced by Gary Walsh, recently signed from Manchester United, who, went on to put together some tremendous performances, relegating Miller to the role of substitutes for the rest of the campaign. 
* During the 96-97 season, a loan spell at Huddersfield Town was organised, although he never got to make a first team appearance for the club. However he did make three appearances during a loan spell at Grimsby Town. 
* He was signed by WBA on 28th February 1997 for £400,000. His debut with the Baggies came on 2nd March against Bolton Wanderers.

* Alan Miller had spells at four different clubs, during the course of  last season. He began the season at Middlesbrough, where he gave some good performances although he was dislogde from the side by keepers such as Ben Roberts and Mark Schwarzer. He later went out on loan to Huddersfield Town, Grimsby Town and WBA, who he eventually joined on a permanent basis in February. From the moment he arrived at the Hawthorns, he replaced Crichton in goal, bringing a lot more security to the Baggies' defence. He eventually made a total of 12 appearances for Albion, during the course Of the season.

926.name: Crichton
pages: * After a number of years at Grimsby Town where he showed on plenty of occasions exactly what he is capable of, Crichton finally joined WBA, a club who had high expectations of this magnificent goalkeeper. However, a lack of confidence when he is required to uses his fit to clear the  ball saw him become the target for criticism form a section of the club's supporters. Since the arrival of Alan Miller last season, Crichton has  totally disappear from Ray Harford's line up although he will be trying  to turn that situation around as the current season progresses. Paul Crichton and Alan Miller form one of the best pairs of goalkeepers in the whole of the First Division, and are without doubt one of the teams strong points.

* Crichton is a keeper with tremendous ability which makes him very  difficult for opposing forwards to beat. He shows great positional sense, always in the right place at the right time. He has great reflexes which allows him to get the side out of tight situations. His main weakness is his insecurity in the air and when he has to use his feet, although he is more consistent in this aspect of his game. A very quick keeper he is always alert to the possibility of a long through ball. He is outstanding in one on one situations and covers angles perfectly.

* After coming thorugh the youth ranks at Nottingham Forest, he signed professional in May 1986, although he never made a first team appearance for the Nottingham club. 
* In September 1986 he was loaned out  to Notts County, where he made his debut on 21st October 1986 against Middlesbrough. 
* In January 1987 he was loaned out to Darlington, playing his first game for the club on 31st January 1987 against Notts County. 
* He was loaned out to Peterborough United in March 1987 making his debit on 25th April 1987 against Torquay United.

* He moved to Peterbrough United on a permanent basis for £20,000 in November 1988, making his debut on 5th November 1988 against Leyton Orient. 
* He completed his contract and signed  for Doncaster Rovers in August 1990, and made his first appearance for the club on 25th August 1990 against Carlisle United. 
* He became a free agent and moved on to Grimsby Town in August 1993. His first game for the Mariners came on 14th August 1993 against Bolton Wanderers.

* Last time out the WBA keeper did a good job replacing the veteran  Nigel Spink who was out through injury. However, in spite of playing 30 games for the club, he became the target for criticism from the supporters when things didn't go right for him, especially when he was required to used his feet to clear the ball. Since the arrival of Alan Miller he has seem himself condemned to the substitutes bench.

928.name: Hunt
pages: * Andy Hunt provides the class and talent up front for WBA and is undoubtedly one of the best striker in the First Division. He has a good understanding with Peschisolido, Taylor and also with Richard Sneekes, and is a player who has the ability to get out of tight situations. He wasn't a regular at Newcastle United but is very much a part of the side at WBA pues and for Ray Harford is an automatic choice. The Baggies' season will, to a large extent, depend on Hunt's performances.

* A left footed striker Hunt shows great technical ability and balance in everything he does. A very dangerous player he has good dribbling ability although he also goes looking to win the ball himself and is a good passer when he wins possession. He has a good touch in his right  foot and likes to play one-twos with his teammates. Good at losing his marker he is capable of getting in a shot on goal from almost any position. He is good in the air not only because of his height but also for the quality he shows when he connects with his head. A very quick player, he is always looking to score goals. Defensively he makes only a limited contribution. Hunt is WBA's penalty taker, striking them home with his left foot.
* Top scorer at WBA seasons 95-96 and 96-97.
x

* Hunt began his playing career with amateur club Kettering Town, later signing for Newcastle United in January 1991. He made his league debut on 9th March 1991 against Watford. He scored his first goal as a professional against Oxford United on 10th April 1991. 
* He was loaned out to WBA in March 1993 and managed to score in his first game for the Baggies on 28th March 1993 against Bradford City. 
* He had a sensational end to that season, scoring 9 goals in 10 games, including a hat trick on 3rd April 1993 against Brighton & Hove Albion, which convinced the club to paid out £100,000 to take him to the  Hawthorns on a permanent basis in June 1993. 
* He was chosen as the club's Player of the Year by the WBA supporters in the 95-96 season.

* Last season was a fantastic one for Andy Hunt who ended the season as WBA's top scorer for the second year in succession. Nevertheless, despite his magnificent statistics for the season, Hunt wasn't absolutely satisfied with his form although he always gave everything he had out on the park, a commitment which was always acompanied with touches of genuine class. In total he played in 45 games scoring 5 goals, including 4 penalties.

929.name: Claridge
pages:
* Signed for Wolverhampton Wanderers in March 1998. 
* Steve Claridge will be eternally remembered at Filbert Street. Always with his socks halfway down his legs, the Leicester forward has against his name the honour of being the scorer of two of  the most important goals in the club's history the one that won promotion to the Premier League in 1996 and the one that clinched the League Cup one year later. A great reward for one of the globetrotters of English football, and a great reward for a veteran player on whom fortune has finally smiled.

* Steve Claridge is an opportunist striker with a well developed goalscoring instinct. An untiring worker, he fights for every ball that falls in the rival's penalty area. He uses his body to protect the ball, like very few others, and is ready to get in a shot on goal, given the slightest opportunity. Although he is not a specialist with his head, he has the peculiar ability to take advantage of other peoples errors and turn apparently harmless situations into goals. His intelligence and determination make him a decisive player and real focal point for his colleagues..

* League Cup Winners medal 1997.
* Second Division Championship winners medal 1995.
* Third Division Championship winners medal 1991.
* Associated Members Cup Winners Medal 1995.
x

* Steve Claridge arrived at Bournemouth 30th November 1984 from non-league Fareham.
* In October 1985 he was transfered to Weymouth for £10,000.
* On 11th October 1988 he signed for Crystal Palace but just two days later was transfered to Aldershot for £14,000.
* He arrived at Cambridge United on 8th February 1990 in exchange for £75,000. In three seasons his contribution helped the club from the Fourth to the Second Division.
* On 17th July 1992 he signed for Luton Town. His fee: £160,000. However, shortly after (20th November) he returned to Cambridge in exchangefor £195.000.
* Birmingham City was to be his next destination. His transfer fee, which was finalized on 7th January 1994, was set at £350,000.
* He scored 20 goals during the 1994-95 season becoming the first player to reach that figure for the club since Trevor Francis. After helping the club to win theSecond Division title he was chosen "Player of the Year" by the Birmingham City supporters.
* He began the 95-96 season at Birmingham but on 1st March 1996 he was transfered to Leicester City for £1,000,000. He made his debut on 3rd March in a 4-2 defeat in the "Foxes" visit to Ipswich Town. On 2nd April of that same year he scored his first goal as a Leicester player against Charlton Athletic.
* Claridge scored the goal that took Leicester back to the Premier Leaguein 1996, a fierce right foot shot against Crystal Palace at Wembley in the final minute of extra time in the final of the play offs for promotion. 
* On 16th April 1997 it was a goal of his against Middlesbrough saw Leicester lifting the League Cup for the first time in their history.

* Steve Claridge wrote another page in Leicester's history books during the 96-97 season. His goal in the League Cup final replay gave the trophy to the Foxes for the first time in the history of the club. Nobody else could have scored it. A regular member ofMartin O'Neill's line up, Claridge ended the season as the side's leading scorer with 11 league goals, 1 in the F.A. Cup and 2 in the League Cup.

930.name: Paatelainen
pages: * Paatelainen is a player who is all about honesty and commitment, which is how he attempts to make up for the technical weaknesses in his game which don't prevent him from doing a fine job for the side. Following a couple of basically disappointing seasons for for the Finnish striker, and, realising how difficult it was proving to get into the side at Bolton Wanderers, he decided to join Wolves, where he is also kept in the shadows by Steve Bull and Don Goodman, although, during the course of the season he is likely to get an opportunity to start a game.

* A very strong centre forward, he is excellent at playing with his back to goal and holding the ball up as he waits for his teammates to come through in support from the midfield. He is good in the air, although, as is the case with his ex-Bolton teammate John McGinlay, he generally wins the ball through good anticipation and positioning. He has a good shot in his left foot from distance and also works tremendously hard to keep rival defenders under constant pressure.

* Scottish League Cup runners up medal with Aberdeen 92-93.
* Scottish Cup runners up medal with Aberdeen 92-93
* League cup runners up medal with  Bolton Wanderers 94-95.
* Top scorer at Dundee United, 88-89 and, together with Darren Jackson, in 89-90.
* 49 full international appearances for Finland 13 goals.

* Scottish club Dundee United signed him from Valkeakosken Haka in October 1987. He scored on his league debut against St. Mirren on 31st October 1987.  
* He was transfered to Aberdeen in March 1992 for £250,000, making his league debut on 4th April 1992 against Dunfermline Athletic and scoring  his first league goal for the club on 18th April 1992, against Hibernian.
* Bolton Wanderers signed him in July 1994 for £300,000. His debut couldn't have been better, scoring twice for his side against Grimsby Town, on 13th August 1994.
* He scored Bolton Wanderers' fourth goal in the play off for promotion to the Premier League in May 1995. in Mayo de 1995. 
* He was signed at the beginning of the 97-98 season, by Wolverhampton Wanderers, who paid out £250,000.

* Paatelainen didn't have a good season, given that the Blake and McGinlay partnership worked to perfection for Bolton Wanderers limiting the Finnish striker to just 10 appearances, in which he found the net twice. He did though see enough of the action to receive a medal in commemoration of the club's title triumph.

931.name: Goodman
pages: * A player who guarantees a good goals return each season, Don Goodman has made a magnificent recovery form a serious injury he suffered two years ago when he broke his skull, a blow which saw him forced to undergo a long period of rehabilitaion. As brave as anybody else in the game, he came back to make life difficult for Iwan Roberts, eventually dislodging him from the side, taking over from him as the man who, this season, will partner Steve Bull at the sharp end of the Wolves attack. It would be no surprise at all if he went on to have a superb season for a side which has genuine aspirations of winning promotion to the Premier League.

* Don Goodman is a player who is blessed with great power and speed, showing himself to be both brave and decisive in everything he does. He keeps opposing defenders under constant pressure making life very difficult for them at all times. He is not the best of players technically speaking but he makes up for those weaknesses with his tremendous enthusiasm. Nevertheless he does have a good first touch on the ball, allowing him the time and space to get in good accurate strikes on goal, or to make quick forward runs from deep positions. Better on his right foot than he is on his left, he is also very dangerous in the air, due to his ability to get up high, and his speed in the penalty area. Although he normally plays as a centre forward he can also do a job  when he is playing pushed out towards the right hand side.

* 3rd Division Championship winners medal with Bradford City, 84-85. 
* Top scorer at WBA in the seasons 88-89 and 89-90. 
* Top scorer at Sunderland in the seasons 91-92 and 92-93. 
* Top scorer at Wolverhampton Wanderers in the 95-96 season.

932.name: Bull
pages:
* One of the best English goalscorers of the last decade, at the end of the 1980's Steve Bull managed to attract the attention of the country's most powerful clubs, with his impressive appearances for Wolverhampton Wanderers. As a result, he was called up to the England side on 13 occasions and even played in the 1990 World Cup finals in Italy, during what was probably the best spell of his career.
* However, slowly but surely, injuries began to take their toll, something which was refected in his statistics each season. Nevertheless, he decided to stay with the club, despite the offers on the table from a number of Premier League clubs, the most concrete of which came from Coventry City, a couple of summers ago, when agreement was actually reached on a transfer fee. At that moment Bull poured cold water on the controversy surrounding his imminent move by rejecting the Premier League club's offer and deciding to stay with Wolves. His performances, and the example he sets, have made Steve Bull the most popular player with the Molineux fans, who will be able to enjoy the Englishman's goals over the coming years without worrying abour where he might be moving onto next.
* Steve Bull has one thorny subject still to resolve with the club over the coming season; finally achieving Wolves' long awaited promotion to the Premier League. For that to become reality, he will have to continue his incredible goalscoring record if Wolves are going to have a real chance of winning promotion back to the top flight of English football.

* Steve Bull is very much an old fashioned centre forward. Excellent in air, he shows great strength when he sets off on powerful runs getting in shots on goal when even the slightest of opportunities presents itself, although he is stronger on his right foot than he is on his left. One of his greatest assets in his ball control, which, when he picks the ball up in deep positions allows him to set it up for himself perfectly to turn, go for goal and get in a shot, very often with great success. He is also a tremendously unselfish worker, keeping opponents under constant pressure and always fighting to win back possession for his side, and constantly looking for spaces from where he can create more danger. However, he is not a particularly giffed dribbler, although when he gets one on one with keepers, his limited ability to beat a man is often merely anecdotal. He keeps his nerve well in goalscoring situations, something which more often than not allows him to find the back of the net.

* 4th Division winners medal with Wolverhampton Wanderers, 87-88.
* 3rd Division winners medal with Wolverhampton Wanderers, 88-89.
* Top scorer with Wolverhampton Wanderers in seasons, 86-87, 87-88, 88-89, 89-90, 90-91, 91-92. 92-93, 93-94, 94-95 and 96-97.
* Top scorer in the history of Wolverhampton Wanderers.
* Top scorer in the 4th Division in 1987-88.
* Top scorer in the 3rd Division in 1988-89.

* An under-21, "B", and full international for England. He made his full international debut on 27th May 1988 against Scotland in Glasgow, a game which ended in a 2-0 victory for England, with Bull socring the side's second goal. In the 13 full international appearances he made, 9 came as a substitute, while he managed to find the back of the net 4 times.

* He became a free agent at amateur club Tipton Town and signed for WBA in August 1985 for £35,000. He made his league debut on 12th April 1986 against QPR and scored his first two goals on 13th September 1986 against Ipswich Town.
* He was transfered to Wolverhampton Wanderers in November 1986 for £35,000. His first game for Wolves came on 22nd November 1986 against Wrexham, while he hit his first goal in the famous old gold shirt of Wolves on 13th December 1986 against Hartlepool United, a goal which also clinched a victory for the side.
* Before the start of the 97-98 season, Steve Bull's career total of goals had reach the 303 mark, including the goals he scored for the full England side.
* Down the years with Wolverhampton Wanderers he has scored a total of 17 hat tricks, a club record.

* Bull completed one of the most fruitful seasons of his whole career, scoring 23 times in 43 games, once again making him the club's leading scorer, and the second top scorer in the division, behind Bolton's John McGinlay, who scored a proportion of his goals from the penalty spot. Nevertheless, Bull had a tremendous season, helping the club reach the play-offs where they eventually lost to Crystal Palace, giving the season something of a bitter-sweet taste for Wolves.

934.name: Kubicki
pages: * Since his arrival in England in the summer of 1991, Dariusz Kubicki has shown plenty of glimpses of his talent both at Aston Villa as well as with Sunderland. The polish international went through a troublesome period when Peter Reid, manager at Sunderland, told him of his intention to make more use of the younger playes he had at the club. Fortunately for him, Wolverhampton Wanderers' boss Mark McGhee came in for him and, in fact, he now plays down the left hand side of the park for Wolves as though he has been doing so all his life. An automatic choice in the side he provides a lot of the experience that will be needed if Wolves are to finally win promotion to the Premier League.

* Basically a right back who can also play as a central defender or as a wing back down the right hand side of the field, Dariusz Kubicki stands out for his consistency and solidity in defensive duties, for which reason it is no surprise to find out that he was dubbed with the tag, "Mr. Consistency" by the Sunderland fans. The Polish international is a very solid player, capable of always offering a high level of performances, without too many ups and downs in his form. A good passer of the ball he links up with the midfield and is always available when his teammates are looking for someone to give the ball to, although he is not a player who tends to create too much danger in the opposition's penalty area. Nevertheless, he is a very difficult player for forwards to beat, whilst, added to his speed and security at the back he possesses all the know how that he has picked up from his vast international experience.
* First Division champions medal 96.
* 49 full international appearances for Poland.

* Born in Warsaw, Dariusz Kubicki has spent the majority of his career at Legia Warsaw, a club based in the Polish capital, and from where he took the step up to the full Polish national side.
* He arrived in England in 1991, Aston Villa signing him on 28th August for £200,000. Kubicki made his debut on 31st on that same month in the away game at Southampton. A first choice at right back for the Villa Park club, he later lost his place when Earl Barrett arrived.
* On 4th March 1994 he was transfered to Sunderland for £100,000. He made his debut the following day in a 2-0 victory against Notts County.
* During the 94-95 and 95-96 seasons he played in every league game that Sunderland played, although he didn't manage to score his first goal for the "Rokerites". Neverthless, he was chosen in the First Division's ideal side for 1996, the year in which Sunderland celebrated their promotion to the Premier League.
* He was signed by Wolverhampton Wanderers in August 1997.

* Kubicki enjoyed a good season last time out with Sunderland, though it didn't go by without a note of controversy. When he was on the verge of breaking the record number of consecutive appearances for Sunderland, held by George Mulhall, he was inexplicably left out of the side in favour of George Hall. He later won back his place, making it his own, almost until the end of the season. In total he played in 29 games for the Rokerites.

935.name: Gilkes
pages: * Almost a part of the scenery at Reading, Michael Gilkes left the club after playing for them for 13 years, totalling more than 500 games and 50 goals. His destination was to be Wolverhampton Wanderers, where he managed to force his way into the side only for injury to cut his season short. Now fully recovered, expectations are high regarding this now veteran player, who could prove to be a very important man for Wolves.

* Michael Gilkes is a player who can operate both as a left back as well as on the left hand side of the midfield. Despite the years, he remains one of the quickest players in English football, and is a very attacking player in either of the two positions in which he generally lines up. He is constantly getting up and down the line and is a player whose pace makes him a very difficult man to stop. Very much a left footed player, he has a tremendous ability to beat a man and puts good quality crosses over into the penalty area. He fights for every ball, is a great competitor, and and is clearly a dificult defender to get the better of given his pace and positional sense. In recent times he has shown himself to be less inclined to have a go at goal.

* Third Division winners medal with Reading. 
* Second Division winners medal with Reading.
x

* He moved to Reading, from the Leicester City youth ranks, in July 1984 signing professional for the club that same month. He made his league debut on 27th October 1984 against Lincoln City, while he scored his first goal for the club on 11th May 1985 against Bristol City.
* He was loaned out to Chelsea in January 1992 although he played in just one game, on 12th February 1992 against Southampton.
* He had another loan spell, at Southampton in March 1992, making his debut on 11th March 1992 against Crystal Palace. 
* Finally he moved on to Wolverhampton Wanderers on 27th March 1997 for £155,000. His first game came on 5th April against Norwich City, and scored his first goal for his new club on 23rd April against Grimsby Town.

* Michael Gilkes had a great season with Reading, playing in 32 games, scoring once and making himself an automatic choice in the first team. Nevertheless, despite being a permanent fixture in the side, he eventually moved on to Wolverhampton Wanderers, ending his long association with Reading. He had a good start to his career with Wolves, but a knee injury he picked up in his fifth game for the club, put him out of action for the remainder of the season. In the few games he played, he also managed to find the back of the net once for his new club.

936.name: Sedgley
pages:
* Steve Sedgley is Wolverhampton Wanderers' major reinforcement as the club attempt to win promotion to the Premier League. Wolves paid out £350,000 plus Mark Venus to bring Sedgley to Molineux from Ipswich Town, the player's previous club. A player who can do a job both in defence as well as in midfield, performing equally as well in either position, he provides the club with a man who can cover a number of positions out on the park with a guarantee that he will do a fine job.
* Though presently forming a central defensive partnership with Keith Curle, Steve Sedgley is equally at home in midfield. A very important player for the side Steve Sedgely is likely to be an automatic choice in the side for Mark McGhee, who has every confidence in the player's abilty.

* As a central defender he is excellent in the air, although he is also technically good enough to bring the ball out under control, allowing him to set up counter attacks like a midfielder, which is a position where he has also played a great number of games during the course of his career. A left footed player, he makes some tremendous late runs into the penalty area, and is also very dangerous at dead ball situations. He is also an expert from the penalty spot and even takes free kicks from outside the penalty area.
* F.A. Cup Winners medal with Tottenham Hotspur in 1991.

* An England under-21 international, he made his debut in the Toulon International Tournament on 9th June 1987 against the Soviet Union  in a 0-0 draw. The England side that day included Tony Dorigo and Paul Gascoigne, amongst others.

* After coming through the youth ranks at Coventry City, he signed professional in June 1986. His league debut came on 26th August 1986 against Arsenal, while he opened his goalscoring account for Coventry on 31st August 1987 against Sheffield Wednesday.
* He was transfered to Tottenham Hotspur in July 1989 for £750,000. His first game for the north London club came on 19th August 1989 while he scored his first goal in a Spurs shirt on 22nd  August 1992, against Crystal Palace.  
* Ipswich Town signed him for £1,000,000 in June 1994, making him the club's first million pound player. He suffered an injury which prevented him from making his debut until the day of the East Anglian derby against Norwich City on 19th September 1994. His first goal, five days later, gave Ipswich victory against Manchester United.
* He was transfered to Wolverhampton Wanderers in the summer as part of a deal that took Mark Venus, plus £350,000, to Ipswich Town.

* The English midfielder had a great season at Ipswich Town, proving  himself to be one of the club's most consistent performers. He continued to set a tremendous example to the youngsters at the club, showing them what the game was all about every time he took the field. A foot injury forced him to take a brief break at the end of 1996 in order to fully recover from the problem. Those proved to be the only games he missed throughout the whole of the season, as he went on to play in 39 games scoring 7 times.

937.name: Williams
pages: * Adrian Williams was signed in the summer of 1996 from Reading by Mark McGhee,his ex-manager at the Berkshire club, to strengthen the defence and give the back line a central defender of real quality. However, things could hardly have gone worse for the young Welshman who has been dogged by serious injury problems which have significantly limited his contribution at Wolves. Now, attempting to force his way  into the side's defensive line up once again, a far from easy task, for the moment he will have to settle for coming on as a substitute or replacing an injured teammate.

* A powerful central defender he can also play as a man to man marker in midfield, picking up the opposition's play maker, or in emergencies can ever do a job as centre forward. He is composed in possession  when he picks the ball up deep in defence, bringing it out under control. Good in the air both in defence and in attack, he likes to move forward to add his presence to set pieces and dead ball situations. He is basically a right footed player, who is not uncomfortable with the ball at his feet.
x
x

* After coming through the Reading football school known as the "Centre of Excellence", Williams is the first player from that school to go on to become an international. He signed professional terms in March 1989. He played his first game for the club on 22nd October 1988 against Notts County, and scored his first goal in the league goal, which was the equalizer, on 25th August 1989, against Crewe Alexandra.
* A neck injury in the Autumn 1994 saw him miss 4 months of the season and even put his professional career in danger. Nevertheless he recovered in time to play in the run in to the end of the season, and in the play off for promotion to the Premier League against Bolton Wanderers, although Reading lost.
* He was transfered to Wolverhampton Wanderers in June 1996 for £750,000. His first game for Wolves was on 24th January 1997 against Sheffield United.

* Serious injury problems limited Williams to just 6 games throughout the whole of last season league campaign.He had to undergo surgery to  correct a problem with the cruciate ligaments in one of his knees and, once he had returned from that operation, a series of minor injuries and knocks conspired to do the rest. However, he fought back and even managed to play in the play-offs, hitting the cross-bar in one of the games before Reading were finally eliminated at the hands of Crystal Palace.

938.name: Richards
pages:
* Dean Richards is one of the most promising young central defenders in English football, who, if, he can steer clear of injuries could well go on to become a full England international in the not too distant future. Contrary to the typical image of a central defender, Richards has outstanding ability which should see him go on to become a genuine star at the heart of the Wolves defence.
* Unfortunately, a recurring problem with a knee injury he picked up in a car accident a year ago is currently keeping out of action. When he is fully recovered, he should have no problem in reclaiming his place in Mark McGhee's starting line up, and go on to continue the progress which could eventually take him to the pinnacle of English football.

* An extremely safe central defender, despite his height, he is a very quick player. He is excellent in the air, as he is with the ball at his feet. He has the ability to bring the ball out from the back, either with the time and space to set up attacks, or when he wins back possession, robbing the ball and breaking out with strength and power, before thoughtfully laying the ball off. He possesses good technique, which allows him to play his way out of tight situations when he is put under pressure by opponents. He is a dangerous player at set pieces, while he also packs a powerful shot from 20-25 yards out. As if all that wasn't already enough, when he finds himself in one on one situations with opposing goalkeepers, he shows a composure, uncommon in defenders, which allows him to finish the job off.

* Chosen in the Second Division's ideal team for 94-95.
* Chosen in the First Division's ideal team for 95-96 and  96-97.

* An England under-21 international on 4 occasions, Richards made his debut for the under-21's in the Toulon International Tournament on 6th June 1995 against Brazil, a game the English lost 2-0. In the English side that day among others were Phil Neville and David Beckham.

* After coming through the youth ranks at Bradford City, he signed professional terms in July 1992. He made his league debut on 26th October 1991 against Bournemouth, managing to find the back of the net.
* He was loaned out to Wolverhampton Wanderers in March 1995. He played his first game for the club on 1st May 1995 against Southend United and scored his first two league goals in a Wolves shirt against Derby County on 12th April 1995, earning his side a point. Finally, Richards was transfered to Wolves for £1,300,000 at the end of the season.

* Richards had an impressive start to the season with Wolves, although an incident during a training session revealed that he would require further surgery to solve a problem related to a traffic accident a year previously which left him with a knee injury. This limited him to just 21 games all season, plus one goal, although he still managed to force his way into the First Division's ideal team, his fine performances being acknowledged by his fellow professionals.
