939.name: Curle
pages: * Keith Curle has been considered among the best central defenders in English football in recent years and gained himself a reputation that even took him into the national side. Now at the veteran stage of his career but still a very capable performer, Curle will no doubt  become one of the side's defensive pillars once again this season, a campaign in which Wolves feel sure that they can finally get back into the top flight after so many years of trying. One of the favourites of the Maine Road crowd, he hasn't taken long to win over the Wolves fans.

* A central defender of tremendous power, Curle is a hard player when he goes in to win the ball, and knows how to make use of his physique to impose himself on opposing forwards. Good in the air, he is dangerous at dead ball situations. Occasionally after winning possession, he will move forward into the attack showing pace, power and determination.
x

* A "B" international for England, plus 3 appearances for rhe full side, Curle made his debut on 29th April 1992 in the Lenin stadium against the CIS, replacing Andy Sinton. He was a member of the England squad for the 1992 European Championships in Sweden, although he played in just one game, the opening encounter for England against Denmark, playing at right back as a result of the number of injuries that England had at the time both in that position as well as in central defence.

* After coming through the youth ranks at Bristol Rovers, he signed professional in November 1981. On his league debut, on 29th August 1981, he managed to find the back of the net against Chester City.
* He was transfered to Torquay United in November 1983 for £5,000. He also managed to score on his debut for Torquay on 5th November 1984 against Northampton Town.
* He was signed by Bristol City in March 1984 for £10,000. He made his debut on 3rd March 1984 against York City and opened his account for the club on 4th March 1986 against Newport County.
* In October 1987 he was transfered to Reading for £150,000, making his first appearance on 24th October 1987 against Bradford City.
* He moved on to Wimbledon for £500,000 in October 1988. His debut for the Dons came on 22nd October 1988 at Old Trafford against Manchester United. He scored his first goal for the club from the penalty spot on 26th December 1989 against Charlton Athletic.
* He was transfered to Manchester City for £2,500,000 in August 1991, which at the time was a record for a defender. He made his league debut for the Maine Road club on 17th August 1991 against Coventry City, and opened his goalscoring account as a City player on 23rd November 1991. 
* Wolverhampton Wanderers paid £650,000 to take him to Molineux on 2nd August 1996. His first game in a Wolves shirt came on 10th September against Oxford United, while his first goal in the famous old gold colours, came from the penalty spot against QPR on 31st March 1997.

* Curle had an unfortunate start to his career with Wolverhampton Wanderers, when he ended up getting injured in a friendly game, a knock which became a real thorn in his side. He didn't play his first full game for the club until January. From that moment on he went on to do everything he was signed to do, bringing decisiveness, security and leadership to the side. In total he played in 21 games finding the back of the net twice.

940.name: Slater
pages:
* Signed for Wolverhampton Wanderers in March 1998.
* Since his arrival in England in August 1994 Robbie Slater has played in three different clubs: Blackburn, West Ham and Southampton.  In such a short space of time he has known the sweet taste of victory when Blackburn won the League, and also the bitterness of spending anonymous weeks on the bench. At the Dell the fans appreciate him after the goals he scored against Everton and Blackburn, goals that were vital for Southampton to accumulate crucial points to keep them in the Premier League.

* A very mobile midfielder, Robbie Slater operates well on either flank.  A very quick and skilful footballer, he runs with the ball close to his feet dodging rival defenders before putting over a cross.  He can play in tight spaces, preferably near the touchline.  Although he is a little selfish at times, when he is on form his dynamic nature make him a man who can provide the breakthrough.  In any case, he needs to finish better, as his shot is not so good, and he doesn't put so many goals away.
* League Champion 95.
* 17 full international appearances for Australia.

* Although he was born in England, Robbie Slater has Australian nationality as his family immigrated to the southern hemisphere when he was a kid. 
* On the 4th of August 1994 he arrived at Blackburn Rovers from Lens.  The price for his transfer was £300,000.
* In principle, Slater was destined to substitute for the injured David Batty.  He made his debut in the Premier League on the 20th of August 1994, in a game against Southampton played at the Dell (1-1).  At the end of his first season in England the Australian is celebrating his team's league title. 
* On the 15th of August 1995 he was transferred to West Ham United for £600,000, as part of an operation that saw Matty Holmes move to Blackburn Rovers.  He made his debut for the "Hammers" on the 26th of August, in a game against Nottingham Forest played at the City Ground (1-1).
* On the 2nd of December of this year he scores his first goal in England. Strangely enough, the rival was Blackburn Rovers, and the ground Ewood Park.  
* He has been a Southampton player since August 1996.  His transfer was set at £250,000.

* He played in the first three games of the season for West Ham, but then moved to Southampton.  With Southampton, he took part in 30 games, and scored two very important goals which contributed to the Saints survival in the top division.

942.name: Simpson
pages: * Paul Simpson was the one of most veteran players at Derby County, but also one with the most quality. Without any chances of playing from the start in Jim Smith's line-ups, Paul carried out his role of luxury substitute with dignity. Simpson signed for Wolverhampton in November 1997.

* The positioning, power and security with which he takes free-kicks are the three big virtues of Paul Simpson. A specialist in all types of set-play, he is needed for the corner keeps, dangerous with direct free-kicks and lethal from the penalty spot. Very left-footed, he has wonderful technique making him a very valuable player. He usually plays in the midfield on the left, although at times he moves up to the attack on this side. A good passer, he constantly sets up his team mates. The passage of time has eaten into his speed and resistance, and his game has lost consistency. Even so, his left foot is still capable of deciding a game with just one kick of the ball. In any case, he will have to watch his weight, as he has a tendency to put on pounds, if he wants to keep up his level of performance an the top flight competition.
x

* 5 times under-21 international for England. 
* Youth international.

* Paul Simpson starts his professional career on the 4th of August 1983 in the ranks of Manchester City, after having passed through the lower ranks of the club. A precocious footballer, he makes his debut with the first team aged just 16. 
* Without playing during the 84-85 season, from the following season on he starts to figure regularly in the City line-ups. 
* On the 31st of October 1988 he is transferred to Oxford United for £200,000. Soon he became first choice for the manager, B. Horton. 
* His arrival at Derby County occurs on the 20th of February 1992. The Rams pay £500,000 for his services. 
* In the summer of 1995 he scores three goals in the second half of a game between Derby County and Portsmouth at the Baseball Ground (3-0).  The second of theme, from a direct free-kick, is extraordinarily beautiful, and ITV name it the "Goal of the Month". 
* In the 95-96 season he scores a new hat-trick in his career against Tranmere Rovers.  Months before there had been persistent rumours of a move Leicester City, but finally he stayed put at the Baseball Ground.  In May, Derby County becomes a Premier League team. 
* In the 96-97 season he plays 19 league games for Derby County, but in all of these he comes on as a sub. On the 6th of December 1996 he is loaned to Sheffield United, where he makes 6 appearances.

* Definitively condemned to the role of substitute, Paul Simpson came on 19 times for the whole of last season, but in none of these was he a starter. However, in all of his performances he showed that he has a huge quality stored up in his left foot. In December he was loaned to Sheffield United, who were fighting to return to the Premier League, but Simpson only took part in 6 games.

943.name: Corica
pages:
* Steve Corica has had to wind his way through a maze of problems in order to finally get to play in English football. The amount of his transfer to Leicester City was finally decided by a FIFA tribunal. Neverthless, despite these problems he was soon on the move again, following Mark McGhee, who was the man who first showed full confidence in his ability, when he moved on to take charge of Wolverhampton Wanderers. With his signing, Mark McGhee brought to Molineux a man who can do a fine job of linking up between the midfield and the forwards.
* A player who has done a fine job for the club, although one that doesn't seem to have been appreciated by a large section of the club's supporters, Corica hopes to be able to once again force his way into Mark McGhee's plans after getting over a knee injury which he suffered towards the end of last season, and which may well yet see him being pushed down in the pecking order for a place in the side. Nevertheless, he possesses the ability he needs to make himself a player in whom the manager can place full confidence.

* Steve Corica is an attack minded midfielder who generally lines up  in between the strikers and the midfield. He possesses a powerful shot at goal and tremendous vision. A quick player, he is occasionally guilty of trying to do too much on his own, something which has earned him the criticism of the supporters. He has good reserves of stamina and good fighting spirit, although defensively he makes only a limited contribution. He carrys the ball well, keeping it under tight control at all times.
x
* He is an Australian international, and, on making his full international debut, became the first player to play for Australia at all levels.

* Leicester City signed from Australian club Marconi Sidney in August 1995, for £325,000 following the decisions of a FIFA tribunal.  He made his debut for Leicester, on 12th August against Huddersfield Town, managing to find the back of the net.
* He was transfered to Wolverhampton Wanderers in February 1996 for £1,000,000. He played his first game for Wolves on 17th February 1996 against Norwich City. He opened his goalscoring account in Wolves' colours on 23rd November 1996 against Crystal Palace.

* Corica had an up and down season, no sooner putting together a tremendous run of performances, than finding himself either back on the bench or even in the reserves. In general though he had a good campaign, making a very active contribution to Wolves' play. Unfortunately his league season came to something of an unfortunate end when he picked up a serious injury against Port Vale. In total he played in 36 games, finding the back of the net twice.

944.name: Wright
pages: * Jermaine Wright is on old style winger who, unfortunately for him, doesn't enjoy the full confidence of manager Mark McGhee, and as a result doesn't get more than just a few minutes of action to show what he can do. Players such as Bull, Goodman and Paatelainen have, for the moment, blocked his path to the first team. Nevertheless, Wright has has shown some good progress, whilst his age, far from being a handicap, gives him plenty of time to improve his game in the future.

* A winger who normally plays down the left, he is stronger on his right than his left, as a result of which, at the end of another mazy dribble he will generally look to get onto his right hand side, in order to get in a shot on goal or play a one-two with a teammate. A very quick player he can also do a good job in other positions along the front line, although it is out on the flanks where he is most at home. He possesses a powerful shot at goal, though almost always with his stronger right foot.
x
* He has played for England as a youth international.

* After coming through the ranks at Millwall, he signed as a professional in November 1992.  * He was transfered to Wolverhampton Wanderers in December 1994 for £60,000 after proving unable to get even a minute of first team football with Millwall. He made his league debut on 8th March 1995 against Sunderland, replacing the injured Steve Bull.

* The young Wolverhampton Wanderers winger had very few opportunities to show his undoubted quality in the 3 games he played in during the course of the season. He will have to wait a little longer yet to really get the chance he is waiting for.

945.name: Osborn
pages:
* A player of enormous class, quality and technique, to a large extent the way Simon Osborn plays in a game very often dictates  the way Wolverhampton Wanderers play. He picks the ball up from the defence, buiding up the sides attacks from the back.
* A key player in Reading's tremendous season in 1994-95, he failed to settle at QPR, although he quickly adapted to life at Molineux. This season, as was the case last time out, great things are expected of the English midfielder, especially bearing in mind that the Wolves' manager Mark McGhee is the man who got the best out of him at Reading.

*  With his tremendous elegance and technique, Simon Osborn is Wolverhampton Wanderers' midfield play maker. A fairly quick-moving player, he plays both long and short passes with great accuracy. He has good reserves of stamina and the ability to make good forward runs into the box. Very often, when the ball is in and around opposition box he will take up a position on the edge of the area to pick up clearances and rebounds and connect with a powerful shot on goal from 20 to 25 yards. He is also a specialist at taking free kicks which he curls over the top of the wall with his right foot.
x
x

* After coming through the ranks at Crystal Palace, he signed professional in January 1990. He made his league debut on 19th April 1991 in the London derby against Tottenham Hotspur, while he scored his first goal for the club on 7th December 1991 against Norwich City, clinching a point for Palace. 
* He was transfered to Reading in August 1994 for £90,000 and made his debut for them on 13th August 1994 against Wolverhampton Wanderers. His first goal for Reading came on 27th August 1994 against Barnsley.
* QPR sigend him for £1 million in the summer of 1995. He made his debut on 19th August 1995 against Blackburn Rovers and struck his opening goal for the London club against Bolton Wanderers on 16th December 1995.
* Finally he moved on to Wolverhampton Wanderers for £900,000 in December 1995. His first game for Wolves came on 26th December 1995 against Millwall, and he scored his first two goals for his new club on 30th March against Watford.

* Osborn completed a good season for Wolverhampton Wanderers playing in 35 games finding the back of the net 5 times. Osborn's form seemed to dictate the way the side played, apparently when he was on top of his game then so were Wolves. He played in the play offs, although at the time he wasn't fully match fit, lacking the competitiveness that comes only with regular first team football.

946.name: Froggatt
pages:
* Steve Froggatt's move to Wolverhampton Wanderers from Aston Villa was a genuine surprise, bearing in mind the young English winger's progress. However over the last couple of seasons that progress has been seriously hindered by his bad luck with injuries.
* Fortunately, despite not fully shaking off his injury problems, he seems to have got back to something approaching his best form, and even attracted the attention of big clubs, such as Liverpool. If evertyhing goes according to plan, Froggatt should be an automatic choice for Mark McGhee, either in the midfield or at left back.

* A very quick player, he is constantly getting up and down the flank from deep positions, forming a vital part of Mark McGhee's tactical approach, using two full backs who almost form part of the midfield. A very direct player, he likes to take on opposition defenders, beating them with his fine dribbling ability and change of pace and direction. He is a good crosser of the ball, putting over some fine centres either on the run or from dead ball situations. He also strikes a very powerful free kick. He is constantly making himself available to his teammates, as the side attempts to start off another attack.
* Chosen in the ideal team for the First Division during 96-97.

* Froggatt has made 2 under-21 international appearances on 2 occasions. He made his debut on 8th September 1992 against Spain,  in a game which ended in a victory for England, with Darren Anderton getting the winning goal.

* A product of Aston Villa's youth system, Froggatt signed professional in January 1991. He made his league debut on 26th December 1991 against West Ham United while he scored his first goal as a professional On 5th September 1992 against Crystal Palace.
* He was transfered to Wolverhampton Wanderers in July 1994 for £1,000,000. On his league debut for Wolves in the first game of the 94-95 season, he managed to hit the winning goal against Reading.

* Froggatt had possibly his best season as a professional, doing a tremendous job which was acknowledged by his fellow professionals in the First Division who voted for him to be included in the First Division's ideal team. Nevertheless despite having a marvellous campaign, injuries once again prevented him from making as many appearances as he would have liked. In total he played in 27 games, scoring twice.

947.name: Ferguson
pages:
* The young midfielder didn't have an easy time of things whilst at Manchester United, where some people decided that he was only in the side because he was the manager's son. However, it wasn't the supporters who got Darren Ferguson out of the United side, but the so called Fergies Babes, the wave of young players who came through at United, first of all blocking his path to the first team, and, secondly, hastening his departure from Old Trafford, as he was forced to look elsewhere for first team football and the opportunity to make his name in the English game.
* Currently with Wolverhampton Wanderers, he has managed to win himself a place in Mark McGhee's starting line up, without people looking upon his inclusion in the side with suspicion. A very honest player, he is doing a fine job at the moment and, if he carries on the way he is going, will no doubt continue to enjoy the privilige of regular first team football throughout the rest of the season, making as much of a contribution as he can to help the club clinch the promotion to the Premier League that they came to close to last time out.

* Darren Ferguson is a very strong midfielder, a left footed player with a good shot from long distance. He basically does a defensive job, covering his part of the pitch well and winning plenty of possession for the side, an aspect of the game in which he stands out. His contribution in an attacking sense is less significant although when he does move forward he is powerful and decisive. Although a hard tackler when he goes in to win the ball, he always does so fairly.
x

* A Scotland youth and under-21 international, he made his debut for the under-21 side on 25th May 1992 against the United States, in a 5-0 defeat for the Scots. In total he has made 5 appearances for the Scotland under-21 side.

* After coming through the youth ranks at Manchester United he signed professional in July 1990. He made his league debut on 26th February 1991 against Sheffield United.
* He was transfered to Wolverhampton Wanderers in January 1994 for £250,000. He made his Wolves debut on 5th January 1994 against Crystal Palace and scored his first goal as a professional against Barnsley on 8th April 1996.

* Ferguson didn't have a great season for Wolverhampton Wanderers never really forcing his way into Mark McGhee's plans as a regular member of the side. His season was also significantly affected by the events which surrounded his sending off in a game against Bolton, an incident which saw him given a long suspension. In  total he played in 16 games, scoring 3 times.

948.name: Atkins
pages:
* A very hardworking footballer, Mark Atkins began his career at Blackburn Rovers as a right back, although, following Kenny Dalglish's arrival at Ewood Park, he moved forward into the midfiedl. His signing for Wolves gave the side a player who can do an excellent ballwinning job in midfield, as well as giving a good account of himself in defence.
* Since Mark McGhee decided to abandon the three centre back system Atkins has seen himself pushed forward once again into the midfield, joining Ferguson in doing the midfield ballwinning job which never gets the credit it deserves. However, he also makes a goalscoring contribution and constantly supports the forwards. Obviously, he is an automatic choice for manager Mark McGhee.

* A powerful midfield player, he has tremendous reserves of stamina which allow him to cover an enormous amount of ground in the midfield. He is a tremendous ball winner and keeps the opposing side under constant presure. He makes good forward runs into the penalty area, making the most of his speed and strength, coming from deep to surprise opposing defenders to get in efforts on goal, preferably with his stronger right foot, although he is useful with his left and is a good header of the ball. A very tenacious hard worker, he never drop his guard, although, technically, he is no superstar.
* Premier League winners medal with Blackburn Rovers in the 94-95 season. .
* An England youth international.

* After coming through the youth ranks at Scunthorpe United, he signed as a professional in July 1986. He made his league debut on 5th October 1986 against Wolverhampton Wanderers, scoring his first goal for the club on 19th September 1987 against Newport County.
* He was transfered to Blackburn Rovers in June 1988 for £45,000. He played his first game for the club on 27th August 1988 against Chelsea, while he scored his first goal in a Rovers shirt on 2nd January 1989 against Stoke City.
* Wolverhampton Wanderers signed him for £1,000,000 in December 1995. He made his debut on 10th December 1995 against Luton Town, while he opened his goalscoring account As a Wolves player on 3rd February 1996 against Sunderland.

* Mark Atkins had a tremendous season for Wolves, proving to be one of the most important players in the side throughout the whole of the season. He began the campaign by playing as a sweeper giving an excellent account of himself in the position, although, once Mark McGhee reverted to a flat back four, he momentarily lost his place in the side. However, he didn't take long to force his way back in, in a different position, playing futher forward, which allowed him to add four goals to the 45 appearances he made for Wolves.

949.name: Segers
pages: * Dutch keeper Hans Segers has gone through a real nightmare over  the past two years, after finding himself presumably implicated, together with John Fashanu, and Bruce Grobelaar, in a match fixing scandal, surroundding bets placed on English Premier League matches. At present, though, Segers can feel very satisfied not only with the fact he has been declared innocent together with Fashanu and Grobelaar, but also at being able to renew his playing career at Wolverhampton Wanderers, withough any further worry. As a stand in for Mike Stowell he will be out to do the best he can in goal for Wolves whenever injuries or suspension sees him called into the side. In the meantime he will have to concentrate on teaching the finer points the job to the young keepers in the Wolves youth system, to whom he will be trying to set the right type of example.

* Segers is a keeper who is tremendously quick, helped out by his physique and his excellent reflexes. Nevertheless, he is often insecure when he comes off his line for high balls into the area. Something of an inconsistent performer, he alternates between fantastic saves and schoolboy errors; errors which have often made him the centre of attention in a number of games.

* Before arriving in England, Segers played for PSV Eindhoven. His moved formed part of a deal which also involved Hans Van Breukelen,another Dutch goalkeeper. On 14th August 1984, he signed for Nottingham Forest, who paid £50,000 to take him to the City Ground.
* His debut came on 17th November 1984 in a game against Coventry. Segers was replacing Steve Sutton, and managed to eventually hang on to the first team spot.
* His career has been laced with a number of loan spells. On 13th February 1987 he was loaned out to Stoke City on 19th November of that same year he moved to Sheffield United on loan, while on 1st March 1988, he found himself at Dunfermline Athletic.
* Bobby Gould, ex-manager of Wimbledon, decided to sign him following the departure of Dave Beasant. He joined the Dons on 28th September 1989 in exchange for £150,000 pounds. He made his debut against Everton at Goodison Park, in a game which Wimbledon won 2-1.
* He found himself presumably implicated, together with Grobelaar and Fashanu in a scandal, surrounding the fixing of the results of Premier League matches to favour bets placed on the games in question. All three were later found to be innocent.
* He was signed by Wolves in the summer of 1996.

* Segers didn't get to make a single first team appearance for Wolves throughout the whole of last season. Mike Stowell was an ever present in goal in the league for Wolves, denying the Dutch keeper the opportunity to get a taste of the action.

950.name: Stowell
pages: * An automatic choice in goal for Wolves, he is one of the best keepers in the First Division with his tremendous reflexes, as well his amazing composure, two of the reasons why Mike Stowell's contribution forms a fundamental part of the hopes that Wolves have of winning promotion to the Premier League.

* Stowell has fantastic positional sense, and shows good judgement when he comes off his line for high balls, although, ocasionally, he gives the sensation of lacking dominance in the air, hesitating over balls that he should be claiming as his. Nevertheless, in this type of situation he prefers to remain on his line rather come out and misjudge things completely.
x
x

* He completed his contract with amateur club Leyland Motors, and moved to Preston North End, in February 1985. 
* He became a free agent and moved on to Everton in December 1985. However the presence of Neville Southall in the Toffees' goal prevented him from breaking through into the side.
* He was loaned out to Chester City in September 1987, playing his first game for the club on 16th December 1987 against Aldershot.
* He was loaned out to York City in December 1987, he played his firstgame for the club on 16th December 1987 against Doncaster Rovers. 
* Manchester City also took him on loan in February 1988, for almost 4 months. He made his first appearance for the Manchester club on 6th February 1988 against Blackburn Rovers.
* He was loaned out to Port Vale in October 1988, making his debut on 22nd October 1988 against Blackpool.
* Sent out on loan to Wolverhampton Wanderers in March 1989, he played his first game for Wolves on 18th March 1989 against Bury.
* His final loan spell saw him return to his first club, Preston North End, in February 1990, for just 2 games, the first of which came on 10th February 1990, against Bristol Rovers.
* He was finally transfered to Wolverhampton Wanderers in June 1990 for £250,000, making his league debut on 25th August 1990 against Oldham Athletic.

* Stowell had a superb season, making himself the only player at the club to play in all 51 games that Wolves played, 46 of those being league games. He made a crucial contribution to Wolves finally ending the season in a respectable position, although finally it didn't prove to be enough to get the club promoted to the Premier League.

951.name: Kiely
pages: * Dean Kiely is considered as one of the best goalies there is in the lower divisions of English football and also as the best goalie that Bury have had since the departure of Neville Southall, the keeper who has defended the Everton goal for so many years. His signing was a good bet on the part of Stan Ternent which brought a very solid keeper to defend the Shakers' aspirations in the First Division.

* Dean Kiely is a very safe keeper between the posts, with agility and good reflexes.  However, his effectiveness drops the further from the line he goes. He needs to work on meeting crosses and the coming out to forwards feet. One of his great strengths is his punt with his foot. However, his biggest weakness is the lack of communication that he has with his defenders which leads him to concede some absurd goals.
* Second Division Champion with Bury.
* Youth and schoolboy international for England.

* Originally from the lower ranks of Coventry City, he signed with the club on 30th of October 1987.  However, he didn't get to play a single game for the team. 
* He was loaned to Ipswich Town during the 89-90 season but he doesn't get to play here either. 
* He reaches an agreement with York City on the 9th of March 1990. Right from the start he was essential for the team, being the first choice keeper. He made his debut on 26th of January 1991 against Hartlepool United, keeping a clean sheet. 
* Eventually, his signing for the Shakers takes shape and his move occurs on 15th of August 1996 for £125,000, an amount set by a tribunal. His first game with the team is a few days later against Brentford.

* Kiely had a sensational season last year which was rewarded with promotion to the First Division. His contribution was very important, playing in every single game and keeping 22 clean sheets stopping some penalties along the way.

954.name: Jemson
pages:
* Transfered to Bury during the 97-98 season.
* Life was as sweet as can be for Nigel Jemson, when, 6 years ago, he won a League Cup winners medal, against Oldham Athletic, and was battling for a place in the England side. However he had a car accident which he was lucky to come out of alive, crashing into a lorry when he was on his way home from a training session with Sheffield Wednesday. After being thrown from his car, he suffered injuries to his ankle, face and elbow. He himself has gone on record as saying that, had he been driving his sports car, he may well have ended up being decapitated.

* Jemson is a striker with great class, who is very comfortable in possession. He is good with both feet and is capable of holding the ball up as he waits for support to come through from midfield. A very dangerous player both inside and outside the the area, he strikes a ball well with either foot. He is also a good header of the ball, due more to his positioning than his ability to get up above defenders, and shows the ability to keep his nerve when he is face to face with the keper, allowing him to show his clinical finishing. He is not  physically strong, and often fades in the later stages of games. Defensively he drops back to help out at dead ball situations.

* League Cup winners medal with Nottingham Forest in the 89-90 season. 
* Oxford United's top scorer, 96-97.
* Jemson has made one under-21 international appearance for England. That came on 5th December 1990, against Wales, in an England side that also included Steve McManaman and Alan Shearer.

* After coming through the ranks at Preston North End, Jemson signed professional in July 1987. He made his debut on 3rd May 1986 against Aldershot and opened his goalscoring account on 17th January 1987 against Swansea City. 
* He was transfered to Nottingham Forest in March 1988, in exchange for £150,000. He made his debut for the club on 26th December 1989 against Luton Town and scored his first goal for Forest on 20th January 1990 against Derby County.
* He was loaned out to Bolton Wanderers in December 1988, making his first appearance on 26th 1988 against Preston North End. 
* Jemson also had a loan spell at Preston North End in March 1989. He played his first game for the club on 27th March 1989 against Bolton Wanderers, and struck his first goal on 22nd April 1989 against Chester City, a goal which clinched a victory for Preston North End.
* He was transfered to Sheffield Wednesday, who paid £800,000 to take him to Hillsborough. Making his debut for the Yorkshire club on 18th September 1991against Norwich City, he scored his first two goals for the Owls against Manchester United on 26th October 1991, goals which gave the Sheffield club victory.
* Loaned out to Grismby Town in September 1993, he managed to score on his first league appearance on 11th September 1993, against Watford. His goal came from the penalty spot.
* Notts County signed him in September 1994 for £300,000. He had an excellent debut, managing to find the back of the net against Bristol City on 10th September 1994.
* He went out on loan to Watford In January 1995, making his debut on 14th January 1995 against Bolton Wanderers. 
* He also had a loan spell at Coventry City, although he failed to make an apperance.
* Rotherham United was the final club he joined on loan. He made his first appearance for the Yorkshire club on 17th February 1996 against Bristol Rovers, and hit his first goal 10 days later, against Brentford. 
* Finally, he was transfered to Oxford United for £60,000 in July 1996.

* Jemson had the most outstanding season of his career, and, thanks to the astuteness Denis Smith showed in signing him, went on to become the season's bargain buy. His tremendous appetite for hard work, as well as his natural ability to find the back of the net, made him the club's top scorer with 18 goals in 44 games.

955.name: Swan
pages: * Peter Swan has been one of Bury's incorporations for this season in the First Division. This ex-Leeds United player can contribute with his experience acquired during the course of his long career, and make sure the Shakers are capable of performing well during the league.

* A hard central defender, strong and aggressive, he is very solid in all of his actions. Very powerful in the air, he joins in the attack at corners and free-kicks, situations where he is very dangerous due to his enormous power. 
* Although he normally plays at the back, Bury have been using him as a link-man just behind the forwards where he can take advantage of his great stride and strength.
x
x

* Originally from the lower ranks of Leeds United, he signed as a professional on 6th of August 1984. His first game came on the 1st of January 1986 against Oldham Athletic, scoring twice exactly one month later against Stoke City. 
* He is transferred to Hull City on 23rd March 1989 for £200,000. He makes his debut two days later against Plymouth Argyle and manages to open his goal account on the 4th of April against Oxford United. 
* Port Vale sign him on the 16th of August 1991 in exchange for £300,000. He plays his first game four days later against Ipswich Town, his first goal having to wait until the game against Sunderland on the 19th of October.
* He is signed by Plymouth Argyle on 22nd July 1994 for £300,000. Swan makes his debut with the team on the 13th of August against Brentford. 
* Burnley acquire his services on 4th August 1995 for £200,000. He plays his first game for the side on the 12th of August against Rotherham United and scores his first goal against Brighton & Hove Albion on 21st October.
* Bury sign him in August of 1997 for £50,000.

* It was not an easy season for Swan. He was not used at the beginning of the season but became an important man in Burnley's plans from the month of November onwards, above all, in the heart of the defence. Unfortunately, after some injury problems, he was unable to regain his place. In total, he played 17 games and scored 2 goals.

956.name: Small

* Without ever being considered the automatic first choice, Small showed that he is a dependable footballer every time he stepped onto the pitch.  This is his third season at Bolton and it is likely that he can improve on the number of games he played last season, although he has to compete with some good players.

He can play at left half but in defensive tasks this player is skilful and quick.
x

958.name: Swailes
pages:
* Chris Swailes was transfered to Bury during the 97-98 season. 
* His progress at Ipswich has been genuinely spectacular and would certainly have been deserving of an award as the club's most improved player. Last year he made an important contribution to the side.

* A central defender or a right back, Swailes is a quicker player than he might at first appear to be. Technically he is not a player who stands out, being quite weak in possession, while physically he lacks the power to really command the respect of rival forwards..
x
x

* After coming through the youth ranks at Ipswich Town he went on to sign professional in May 1989. 
* Without managing to make a first team appearance, he was transfered to Peterborough United in March 1991 for 90,000 pounds, where he was also unable to break into the side.
* He signed for amateur club Boston United, from where, after compelting his contract, he moved to Birmingham City, in March 1992. 
* He became a free agent once again and signd for amateur side Guisborough.  
* He completed his contract and moved on to Doncaster Rovers in October 1993. His league debut came on 27th November 1993, against Hereford United. 
* He was transfered to Ipswich Town in March 1995 for £225,000. His first league outing couldn't have been more unfortunate. On 1st  April 1995 against Aston Villa, he scored an own goal in the closing minutes of the game, a goal which meant defeat for his new club. His first goal at the right end came last season against Swindon Town on 12th April 1997.

* The great progress which Chris Swailes has been making came to full fruition last season, when he managed to force his way into George Burley's starting line up towards the end of the season, playing in the last 20 games of the season, of which Ipswich Town lost just three. He even had time to open his goalscoring account, finding the target against Swindon.

959.name: Butler
pages: * The money invested in the signing of Paul Butler last year from Rochdale was a good investment for the club, firming up the centre of the Shakers' defence and forming a formidable trio alongside Chris Lucketti and Andy Woodward. Although at times he is susceptible to some losses of concentration, he will form a partnership to be reckoned with this year in the First Division.

* A strong and consistent central defender, Butler is noted for his good marking and his mastery in the air. This native of Manchester makes his presence felt in the heart of the defence, being dangerous at set plays, where Bury manages to take effective advantage.
* Second Division Champion with Bury in the 96-97 season.
x

* Originally from the lower ranks of the club, he signed as a professional for Rochdale on 5th July 1991. His debut takes place on 8th September against Stockport County, his first goal coming on 6th February 1993 against Halifax Town. 
* He is transferred to Bury on 22nd July 1996 in exchange for £100,000. He plays his first game on the 28th of August against Chesterfield and his first goal comes on the 31st of March against Wycombe Wanderers.

* Butler was one of the regular features in the heart of the Bury defence during last season, his first one under Stan Ternent's orders. His signing from Rochdale was a great success and was able to make 40 league appearances during the championship, scoring one goal.

960.name: Woodward
pages: * Andy Woodward is a young defender who hasn't had so much luck at Bury until last season when he took advantage of the transfer of Michael Jackson to Preston North End to find a spot in the first team, making progress during the season. With a promising future ahead of him, he could be one of the important men in the team if he manages to find a place for himself in the starting eleven as he did last season.

* Woodward is a defender who operates well both in the centre of the defence and at right back. Last year he contributed basically as a centre back, where his long balls were outstanding, powerful and accurate.
* Second Division Champion with Bury in the 96-97 season.
x

* Originally from the lower ranks of Crewe Alexandra, Woodward signed as a professional on 29th July 1992. He makes his debut on the 17th of April against Walsall. 
* He signs for Bury on 13th March 1995. He plays his first game for the club on the 4th of April against Gillingham.

* Woodward produced a great season, much better than might be thought from the 23 games he played for the Shakers. Without doubt, the most important thing was to demonstrate that he was a valid man to step in for Michael Jackson, who left for Preston North End. In short, it could be considered the start of a new epoch for this young defender.

961.name: West
pages: * Dean West has been an outstanding man at Bury in the last two seasons. He is one of the most constant features in Stan Ternent's line-ups. A member of the solid Bury defence, his best moments come when he joins in the attack quickly from the right, always creating a lot of danger with his power and determination.

* He can play both in the heart of the defence and on the right. He is noted for his attacking vocation, which leads him to join in the attack when he has the slightest opportunity. He guarantees an enormous amount of work for the ninety minutes, however, his anxiety to join the attack leads him to neglect his defensive area a little, causing problems for the team.  Finally, it has to be said that he is a player who works the ball well and who dominates in the air despte his slim size.
* Second Division Champion with Bury in the 96-97 season.
x

* Originally from the Leeds United schoolboy teams, West finally joins Lincoln City and signs as a professional on 17th August 1991. His first game with the club couldn't be better as he scores on his debut against Carlisle United on the 11th of May 1991. 
* He signs for Bury on 29th September 1995. He makes his debut on the 30th of September against Gillingham and scores his first goal against Fulham on the 2nd of April 1996.

* Once again Dean West produced a notable season under the orders of Stan Ternent. He was an omnipresent man in the plans, playing 46 League games and scoring four goals. His contribution to the attack was very important for the team.

962.name: Lucketti
pages: * Chris Lucketti has become the first player in the history of Bury to win the vote of Player of the Season by the fans for three consequtive seasons. This is not due to chance as Lucketti is one of the centre backs with most future in the lower divisions and who now can put his aptitudes to the test against the forwards of the First Division. Many clubs are watching his progress as they reckon that he could have good prospects in any of the Premier League sides.

* Chris Lucketti is a strong, powerful and consistent centre back, who is noted for his firmness in the air. However, he is not a man who has bad individual technique allowing him to play the ball out of defence. These virtues and his winning spirit make him an appetising fruit for the clubs of the division above to pick.
* Second Division Champion with Bury in the 96-97 season.
x

* Lucketti comes from the lower ranks of Rochdale, signing with this club as a professional.  The only game he plays for them is against Hereford United on 5th May 1989. 
* He signs for Stockport County as a free agent on 23rd August 1990 although he doesn't get to play a single game for them. 
* Once again as a free agent he signs for Halifax Town on 12th July 1991. His debut takes place on 27th September against Mansfield Town and his first goal as a professional comes against Lincoln City on 12th September of the following year. 
* His transfer to Bury comes to pass on 1st October 1993 in exchange for £50,000. His debut with the Shakers occurs on 2nd October of this same year against Mansfield Town and he scores his first goal against Doncaster Rovers on the 15th of January.

* Despite missing the first six weeks of the season due to a knee injury in the inaugural game, Lucketti was one of the most important men for Bury in the Shakers' defence. In total, he played 38 games.

963.name: Peake

x
* England youth and schoolboy international.
x

* Chosen player of the month for October, Peake put together an acceptable campaign, although more can always be asked of a player like him. Didn't score his first goal until Brighton's game against Northampton Town.

965.name: Patterson
pages: * Mark Patterson is a key man in Sheffield United's plans due to all the hard works he puts in during the course of a game. One of Howard Kendall's first signings after taking charge at Sheffield United and a player who enjoyed the complete confidence of the former manager and that of the new manager, Nigel Spackman, as well. Thanks to his almost priceless work in the midfield, though work that is not always appreciated, he will be a member of the starting line-up for the Blades this season.

* A very strong midfielder, he wins back a lot of balls in dangerous positions and is very valuable for Sheffield United. Very tough when fighting for the ball, his privileged physique allow him to impose himself on his rivals relatively easily. He is basically left-footed and is a good passer, above all over short distances in his position as a pivot in front of the defence, although without having the talent of a playmaker. He is quick and has a magnificent shot with his left at free-kicks. If the situation requires he can man-to-man mark the brains of the rival team.
x
x

* Trained in the youth squad at Blackburn Rovers, he signs as a professional in May 1983.  He makes his league debut on 17th September 1983 against Manchester City and he scores his first goal as a professional against Grimsby Town on 4th december 1983.
* Patterson is transferred to Preston North End in June of 1988 for £20,000. He makes his debut on 27th August 1988 against Port Vale and scores his first goal on 10th September 1988 against Blackpool.
*  He signs for Bury in February 1990 and plays his first game for the club on 3rd February 1990 against Shrewsbury Town. He scores his first goal one month later against Notts County.
* Bolton Wanderers sign him for £65,000 in January 1991. He plays his first game for Bolton on 12th January 1991 against Bradford City and scores his first goal for the team on 1st March 1991 against Tranmere Rovers.
* He is finally transferred to Sheffield United in December 1995 for £450,000, and opens his account on his debut on 22nd december 1995 against Stoke City.
* Patterson goes to Southend United as a loan player during the 96-97 season.
* Signed for Bury during the 97-98 season.

* Once again Patterson has had a very solid season and was one of the references for the team in the midfield at Sheffield United. Even so, despite his good performance, he was loaned to Southend United for four games before returning to Bramall Lane to complete a league in which he disputed 35 games and scored a goal.

966.name: Randall
pages: * Adrian Randall is a footballer who has not been respected by injuries in recent times but this his not prevented him from showing signs of good technique and ability for the attacking football as he displayed last year with Bury. A skilful man, he will be an important whether he plays as a starter or coming on as a substitute for the Shakers during the present campaign.

* A physically strong player, with attacking tendencies who is very intelligent and has a good playing vision when he finally joins in the attack. He is technically good with the ball at his feet and has a good shot on goal. He has the reputation for being a good footballer, although diverse injuries have detracted from his credentials in recent times.

* 4th Division Champion with Burnley in the 91-92 season. 
* 2nd Division Champion with Bury in the 96-97 season.
* Youth international for England.

* Originally from the lower ranks of Bournemouth, he signs as a professional on 2nd September 1986. His debut in the league competition takes place on the 19th of April against Doncaster Rovers. 
* He signs for Aldershot on 15th September 1988. He plays his first game on 20th September against Wolverhampton Wanderers and his first goal is scored on 4th October against Wigan Athletic. 
* He is transferred to Burnley on 12th December 1991. He plays his first game for the team on 26th December against Rotherham United and scores his first goal on 18th January against Gillingham. 
* York City acquire his services on 28th December 1995 in exchange for £140,000. He makes his debut for the team on 6th January 1996 against Rotherham United and scores his first goal on 28th September against Brentford.
* Finally, he signs for Bury on 12th December 1996, also for £140,000. His first league game with the club is on 14th December against Gillingham. He manages to open his account for the Shakers in this same game.
* Adrian Randall's season was outstanding. Once more, he made important contributions to York City, the club where he has only been one year.

967.name: Armstrong
pages: * Gordon Armstrong is a footballer who has been prevented from showing what he has inside in his first year at Bury due to injuries. Even so, in many of his games, he did his duty sufficiently, whether he was in the midfield or substituting for Dave Pugh, the regular left back. At the beginning of this season he has been seen in the starting line-up and it will be important to see if he can keep his place faced with the pressure from Pugh.

* Armstrong is a player who operates on the left of the pitch, either as left back or in the midfield, always doing what is asked of him and putting in a lot of effort. He has a good touch when taking free-kicks either for a cross to the box or shooting directly for goal.

* Third Division Champion with Sunderland in the 87-88 season. 
* Second Division Champion with Bury in the 96-97 season.
x

* Originally from the lower ranks of Sunderland, he signs as a professional on 10th July 1985.  He plays his first game for the team against West Bromwich Albion and opens his account in a game against Crystal Palace on 22nd December 1986. 
* He is loaned to Bristol City on 24th August 1995. His first game is against Stockport County two days after his move. 
* He is loaned once again, this time to Northampton Town on 5th January 1996. He makes his debut with the club on 6th January against Darlington and his first goal only has to wait one week, conceded by Cardiff City. 
* He finally signs for Bury on 16th July 1996 as a free agent. His debut takes place on 17th August against Brentford and he scores his first goal against Shrewsbury Town on 14th September.

* Although he had some injury problems during the course of the season which prevented him from being available for selection, Armstrong managed to play in 32 of the Shakers' matches and added two goals to his account.

968.name: Rigby
pages:
* Tony Rigby is possibly the most skilful man that Stan Ternent has available at Bury.  However, it seems that he has a bit of a difficult character which means he does not respond to the enormous expectations aroused by the great talent he possesses. 
* This young midfielder is capable of the best and the worst as shown last year. Even so, his talent for football does not assure him of a place in Ternent's sides and he will have to work hard to find a gap for himself with the Shakers. This may be the most important year of his career, marking a turning point in his sporting life.

* Tony Rigby is an attacking minded midfielder. He has great technique, and doesn't hesitate to demonstrate this at the slightest opportunity. A good passer and very skilful, he is a true specialist at taking free kicks, allowing him to score an appreciable number of goals during the season.
* Second Division Champion with Bury in the 96-97 season.
x

* Originally from the lower ranks of Crewe Alexandra, he turns professional on 16th May 1990. However, he doesn't play a single game for them.
* He moves to amateur football, playing for Lancaster City, Runcorn & Burscough and Barrow, from where he finally moves to Bury on 6th January 1993. His first game with the Shakers is on 16th January against Torquay United and his first goals come on the 20th March against York City, the winners.
* He is loaned to Scarborough on 14th February 1997. His first game with the club is on 15th February against Swansea City and he gets his goal tally rolling two weeks later against Colchester United.

* It wasn't the best season from Tony Rigby as he never figured regularly in Stan Ternent's plans, alternating between good and bad performances. The low point of the season was when he was loaned to Scarborough, the team where, strangely enough, he left a good impression in the games he played. For Bury, Rigby played 15 games and, with Scarborough, 5, scoring one goal.

969.name: Pugh
pages:
* David Pugh was one of the players with the worst luck last year in the whole of English football. 
* The Bury captain will find it hard to return to his usual position as the players who operate in his position, especially Armstrong, are performing well and it will be hard for him to work his way back into the side. Even so, the determination and courage of this brave footballer could open the doors of success. His presence in the league could be vital for Bury's aspirations.

* David Pugh is a very attacking left winger, although he does not shirk on the work of winning back possession. He oozes enthusiasm in every move and is always looking for the rival goal. His experience and charisma make him an important player for the team. 
* He is a player who has a scent for goal as was demonstrated in the first two seasons with the Shakers, accumulating 25 goals in this time. He can play in any position on the left, from wing back in the five man defence to his habitual place on the wing.
* Second Division Champion with Bury in the 96-97 season.
x

* He is transferred from Runcorn to Chester City in exchange for £35,000 on 21st July 1989.  He makes his debut on 19th August against Mansfield Town and score his first goal against Birmingham City on 17th October. 
* He is signed by Bury on 3rd August 1994 for £22,500. He plays his first game on 13th August against Rochdale and manages his first goal against Doncaster Rovers.
* Last season was very different for David Pugh compared with the previous ones at Bury.  Continual injuries haunted him and limited him to just 18 games and two goals.

970.name: Johnrose
pages: * Lenny Johnrose forms a solid Bury midfield alongside Nick Daws. He is the more attacking of the two and his participation is important if the team want to achieve something positive this season in the First Division. Normally a certain choice, he earns the respect of the fans for his commitment on the pitch and will have to bear a lot of the responsibility during the course of the Shakers' season.

* Lenny Johnrose is a midfielder who basically plays as left half, a zone where he doesn't rest a second during the games. He gets into some good positions allowing him to score goals with a certain regularity. His consistency in the games and his sacrifices in defence are facets much appreciated by Stan Ternent.
* Second Division Champion with Bury in the 96-97 season.
x

* Originally from the lower ranks of Blackburn Rovers, he signs as a professional on 16th June, 1988. He plays his first game for the team in December 1987 against WBA and scores his first goal on 11th November 1989 against Ipswich Town. 
* He is loaned to Preston North End on the 21st of January 1992. He makes his debut on 25th January against Brentford and his first goal comes on 8th February against Fulham. 
* His transfer to Hartlepool United comes through on 28th February 1992 for £50,000. His debut occurs one day later against Swansea City and he opens his account against Shrewsbury Town on the 28th of March of the same year.
* He is finally signed by Bury on 7th December 1993. Four days later he plays in his first game for the Shakers against Scunthorpe United, and has to wait until 10th September 1994 to score his first goal against the same team as in his debut, Scunthorpe United.

* Only suspensions prevented Lenny Johnrose from completing every game that Bury played.  He appeared in 43 games and scored various important goals, above all, his second against Millwall which sewed up the title for the Shakers.

971.name: Daws
pages: * Nicholas Daws is one of the most constant features of the Shakers, always available for his coach and sweating blood in every game for the team's benefit. Alongside Lenny Johnrose he formed a partnership in midfield for almost all the last season and, if nothing untoward happens, he will be one of the men most called upon by Stan Ternent.

* A very complete midfielder, he is able to play both at right half and centre half. A footballer who covers a lot of ground, he has an acceptable technique. His progress in the last few years has been particularly eye-catching. His battling in the heart of the midfield is very much appreciated by the coach and the fans.
* Second Division Champion with Bury in the 96-97 season.
x

* Originally from the amateur club Altrincham, Nick Daws signs for Bury in exchange for £10,000 on the 13th of August 1992. He makes his debut for the club on 22nd August against Gillingham and scores his first goal against Rochdale on 16th March of the following year.

* Once again Nick Daws was one of the most outstanding players for the Shakers, contributing an enormous amount of work and battling on the pitch. He was a regular feature on Stan Ternent's team sheet, and did not miss a single game, scoring two goals.

972.name: Battersby
pages: * The progress of Anthony Battersby has been so significant that Bury were prepared to pay £120,000 for this young forward who has a good future ahead of him. Although, at the moment, he hasn't scored too many goals, his panorama is promising and, more importantly, his trainer trusts him and is giving him opportunities. Time will tell whether he was right or not.

* A young centre forward, his main virtue is his header. However, his progress with the ball at his feet is notable and he is on the way to becoming a good footballer. What's more, he is a player who has the ability to hold onto the ball and pass it to his team mates arriving from the midfield.
x
x

* Originally from the Sheffield United youth squad, Battersby signs as a professional on 5th July 1993 but doesn't get to play a single game for the Bramall Lane team. 
* He is loaned to Southend United in March 1995. His first game with them is played on the 25th of this same month against Bristol City and he scores his first goal on 8th April against Burnley. 
* He is transferred to Notts County on 8th January 1996. He makes his debut on 13th January against Wycombe Wanderers and only has to wait until the 3rd of February to score his first goal against Peterborough United. 
* He is loaned to Bury on 3rd March 1997 although he ends up staying on 22nd May of this same year.  A day after his arrival on loan, he makes his debut against Shrewsbury Town.  He opens his goalscoring account on 15th March against Gillingham.

* Anthony Battersby's season consisted of two halves as in the first of these, he didn't play much at Notts County, not reaching the twenty game mark. His best moments, were, without doubt, when he arrived at Bury, where he made some telling appearances, which was the motive for his definitive move in the month of May.

973.name: Matthews
pages:
* Unfortunately, Robert Matthews was one of the players with the worst luck at Bury together with David Pugh, an unfortunate injury cutting short his season. 
* Now in this new campaign in the First Division, Matthews hopes to be to recover his place and contribute actively in whatever way he can to Stan Ternent's men.

* A versatile hard-working forward, he operates throughout the attack. A good finisher, he takes advantage of his speed in the box to look for space and surprise the opposing defence. His best moments come when he is acting as a winger where he can use his speed and skill to get by rival defenders.
* Second Division Champion with Bury in the 96-97 season.
* Schoolboy international for England.

* Originally from the Loughborough University team, Matthews signs as a professional for Notts County on 26th February 1992. His fist game with the club is on 11th April of this same year against Coventry City, and he doesn't have to wait long for his first goal, which comes the following week against Norwich City, a goal which turns out to be the winner. 
* He is transferred to Luton Town on 17th March 1995 for £80,000. He doesn't play much, playing his first game on the 4th of March against Millwall.
* His next club is York City, who pay £90,000 for him on 8th September 1995. He makes his debut for them on 9th September against Bristol Rovers, scoring his only goal on 18th November against Blackpool. 
* His final destination is Bury who pay £100,000 for his services on the 12th of January 1996.  One day later he makes his debut against Chester City, and also scores his first goal, the Shakers' winner, against this same team.

* It wasn't Robert Matthews season, a knee injury keeping him out for most of the season. Fortunately, he played in enough games to receive a commemorative title medal. In total he played 27 games and scored 5 goals.

975.name: Kearton
pages:
* Since leaving Australia to join Everton, Jason Kearton has had to get used to watching games from the bench, while his mentor at the club, Neville Southall, proved to be an immoveable object in goal for the Goodison Park club.
* Fortunately, Crewe Alexandra became interested in him, and eventually signed him last season. Since his arrival at the club he has demonstrated both his ability and everything he managed to learn during his time under Neville Southall at Everton. The Australian became, and remains, an automatic choice in goal for Dario Gradi.

* His main asset is his ability to come out on top in one on one situations, against opposing forwards. He also shows himself to be very safe when taking shots from distance, demonstrating excellent handling and only very rarely giving forwards the chance of getting onto a parry or a rebound. Against him he has his relative lack of height for a goalkeeper while he also has occasional lapses in concentration, though that could be put down to a lack of regular football, and is something he can work on. Obviously, more games will be needed before his real potential can be properly judged. Nevertheless he will no doubt have learnt plenty from having worked alongside such an outstanding keeper as Neville Southall.
* F.A. Cup winners medal 94-95.

* Kearton joined Everton on 31st October 1988 from Australian club Brisbane Lions as the Goodison Park club's third choice keeper behind Neville Southall and  Mike Stowell, although shortly after his arrival on Merseyside, Stowell left to join Wolverhampton Wanderers. 
* On 13th August 1991 he went out on loan to Stoke City. Four days later he made his debut against Bradford. He eventually made 16 league appearances for the Potters.                       * On 9th January 1992 Everton sent him out on another loan spell,  this time to Blackpool, where he played in 14 games. 
* On 19th January 1995 he began his third loan spell, this time at Notts County, a club he made 12 appearances for. 
* Throughout his careeer he has managed to keep a total of 10 clean sheets. His average goals conceded was, at the end of the 94-95 season, 1.152 per game. 
* He finally left Everton on a permanent basis when he joined Crewe Alexandra, after the Goodison Park club gave him a free transfer in October 1996. His debut came on 19th October 1996 against Chesterfield.

* After seeing how his opportunities at Everton were becoming more limited all the time , Kearton obtained a free transfer from his ex-club, and moved to Crewe Alexandra, whose goalkepers, at that time, were suffering from serious injury problems. During his spell at Crewe last season, Kearton went on to play in 30 games, and managed to keep a clean sheet in 16 of those. His fine season was rewarded when the side won promotion to the First Division, via the play offs.

979.name: Pemberton
pages: * It took a long time and plenty of hard work for John Pemberton to finally make it to the top flight of English football. A real grafter of a footballer, his dour style of play saw him force his way into the side at a number of clubs, finishing up at Leeds United. Now at the veteran stage of his career, Pemberton has moved on to Crewe Alexandra, a club full of talented young players, but who will need the experience of a man like Pemberton alongside them in their first season in the First Division. He will be an important man in Dario Gradi's line up.

* His natural position is at the heart of the defence, preferably on the right hand side. He stands out for his strength and aggression, never shirking a physical challenge, as well as for the energy he shows in everything he does. He is a very forceful player in the air at the back, although he shows certain technical weaknesses with the ball  at his feet. He has a few difficulties when he is required to bring the ball out from the back, often opting to play it long. A specialist man to man marker, he barely contributes to his team's attacks. Although he does move forward for set pieces it is very rare to see him get on the scoresheet. He struck up a very good understanding at Leeds with central defensive partner David Wetherall, forming a partnership which proved very difficult for rival forwards to break down.

* While playing for his local side, Chadderton, in the modest North West League  he was loaned out to Rochdale, where he made his debut on 2nd October 1984 against Aldershot. 
* He signed for Crewe Alexandra as a free agent, on 29th March 1985.
* On 24th March 1988, he was transfered to Crystal Palace for £80.000. In the 1990  F.A. Cup semi-final he played the game of his life to help Crystal Palace defeat Liverpool by four goals to three. Shortly afterwards, Pemberton  played in, and lost, the Wembley final against Manchester United.
* On 27th July 1990, he was transfered to Sheffield United for £300,000.
* He was transfered to Leeds United on 12th November 1993, a date on which the "Whites" paid out £250,000 for his signature. 
* At Elland Road he played in a number of reserve games for the club. Having played the whole of his career as a central defender, he was put to the test as a centre forward and managed to score three times in one game against Sunderland. 
* Pemberton joined Crewe Alexandra in the summer of 1997.
* He failed to make an appearance all season, incapable of breaking through into the Leeds United side during the course of the whole campaign.

980.name: Johnson
pages: * Seth Johnson is another of the young talents to emerge from the Crewe Alexandra youth system, and managed to make himself an important part of Dario Gradi's plans last season and will no doubt be hoping to do the same this time out. Capable of operating either at the back or in midfield, he undoubtedly has a bright future ahead of him.

* Johnson is quite a versatile player who can do a job playing at the back or, even, up front, although always playing out towards the left hand side of the field. He has good technique and shows great maturity for such a young player.
x
x

* After coming through the youth ranks at Crewe Alexandra, Johnson signed professional in July 1996. His first game for the club came on 21st September 1996 against Milwall, and managed to score his first goal on 22nd April 1997 against Wrexham.

* Despite playing in just 11 games, Seth Johnson made an excellent impression on Dario Gradi, who put him in the side in the run in to the season, including the play offs. Quite significant achievements for a young man of just 18 years of age. He also managed to open his goalscoring account.

981.name: Westwood
pages: * At Crewe Alexandra Ashley Westwood has managed to get the regular first team football he needed to develop his game that he couldn't get at his previous club Manchester United. Well settled down in the team's defence, he looks set to form an important part of Dario Gradi's plans this season.

* He is a strong player, who reads the game well and is dominant in the air, despite not  being the tallest man in the side. He is forceful when he covers across the back as the last line of defence and is a fearless tackler. He works hard in every game, and shows great positional sense for such a young player.
x
x

* He came through the youth ranks at Manchester United, signing professional for the Old Trafford club in July 1994. However he was never given the opportunity to make his debut for the Red Devils.
* He was transfered to Crewe Alexandra in July 1995 for £40,000. His debut for the club came on 12th August 1995, and he scored his first goal as a professional on 9th September 1995 against Shrewsbury Town

* Westwood had a highly acceptable season making 44 appearances and scoring twice during the course of the league season. He managed to settle down in the side and made an important contribution to the sides promotion to the First Division.

982.name: Unsworth
pages: * Lee Unsworth is a first team regular down the right hand side for Crewe Alexandra, bringing great enthusiasm and speed to the team from that position. With plenty of room for improvement and a great future ahead of him, he is a player who may not take too long in taking the step up a division.

* Unsworth is a full back whose play is characterised by his speed and ability to raise the  pace of the game. He can play down either flank and has noticeably improved his ability on the ball. One of his main assets is that he is quick to learn, as he has more than demonstrated in recent seasons.
x
x
* Unsworth was signed from amateur side Ashton United in February 1995. He made his debut for the club on 12th August that same year.

* Unsworth was one of the players who made most progress over the course of last season. He began the season at right back but was forced out of action due to injury for two months, although he came virtually straight back into Dario Gradi's side once he had recovered. He was a key member of the team, helping to win promotion to the First Division. He played in a total of 29 games.

983.name: Smith
pages: * Shaun Smith is the man who went down in the club's history during the summer when he scored the goal against Brentford that gave Crewe promotion, for the first time in their history, to the First Division. For his value down the left hand side and for his effectiveness from dead ball situations, he is an automatic choice for Dario Gradi.

* An attack minded full back, Shaun Smith has become a key man for Crewe due to his ability to get forward in support of the attack as well as the danger he represents from dead ball situations. He is a genuine free kick specialist scoring several goals each season, making the most of his power and accuracy.
x
x

* After coming through the youth ranks at Halifax Town, Smith signed professional in July 1989. His first game was on 23rd September 1988 against Tranmere Rovers. 
* He completed his contract with the club and moved on signing for amateur club Embley, in 1991. 
* He returned to professional football, under the guidance of Dario Gradi, in December 1991.  Smith's debut for Crewe Alexandra came on 28th March 1992 against Blackpool. He opened his goalscoring accout as a professional on 3rd October 1992 against Gillingham.

* Shaun Smith completed an outstanding season in the ranks of Crewe Alexandra. A regular in Dario Gradi's side, he played in 38 games scoring 4 times, including several scored direct from free kicks. The highlight of his season came when he scored the goal that gave Crewe victory over Brentford, in the play offs, taking the club up to the First Division.

984.name: Lightfoot
pages: * Chris Lightfoot is Dario Gradi's jack-of-all-trades, a player who can play in a number of different positions all over the pitch, and still do a fine job. Although not a first team regular, he is generally chosen at least as a substitute. He will no doubt do a key job this season in the First Division.

* Chris Lightfoot is a basically defence minded player, who doesn't hesitate to go in hard if he thinks he needs to. However, on occasions he does show off his ability to pass the ball around thoughtfully. His greatest asset is his versatility, being a player who can do a fine job for the side whether he is playing in defence or in the midfield.
x
x

* After coming through the ranks at Chester City, Lightfoot signed professional in July 1988. He made his debut on 18th September 1987 against Grimsby Town and scored his first goals as a professional on 7th November 1987 against Walsall. 
* He was transfered to Wigan Athletic in July 1995 for £87,500. His first game for the club took place on 12th August 1995 against Gillingham, and, one week later, he struck his first goal for the Latics against Scunthorpe United, a goal which clinched a victory for Wigan. 
* He was transfered to Crewe Alexandra in March 1996 for £50,000. He made his debut on 30th March 1996 against Chesterfield.

* Lightfoot made a total of 25 appearances during the course of the season, proving himself a tremendously valuable memeber of Dario Gradi's squad, due to the variety of positions in which he is able to perform. His value to the club was such that he played in two of the three play off games from which Crewe emerged triumphant, winning promotion to the First Division
