985.name: Holsgrove
pages:
* Signed for Crewe during the 97-98 season. 
* In his fourth season at Reading, Paul Holsgrove has shown his worth. A defensive midfielder and a great ball-winner, his role is very important in his zone of the pitch and, what's more, he is very versatile which means he can play in several key positions. A bad season last year has had a negative effect going into this one and he isn't figuring on Terry Bullivant's teamsheets.

* Holsgrove is a very strong player who operates as a defensive centre half.  A good ball winner, he has an acceptable technique for passing the ball in short, working as a pivot. He can play as a sweeper as he is good at making interceptions and he knows when he should and shouldn't play the ball out from the back. He reads the games very well. He doesn't often join in the attack and doesn't have a good finish.
x
x

* Trained in the Aldershot youth squad, he signs as a professional in February 1987. He makes his league debut on 23rd February 1988 against Notts County. 
* His contract finishes and he signs for the amateur club Wokingham Town in 1990. 
* Luton Town sign him in January 1991 for £25,000. He makes his debut on 2nd February 1991 against QPR. 
* Free of contractual obligations he moves to the Dutch club Heracles in November 1991. 
* His contract with the team finishes and he joins Millwall in August 1992. He plays his first game on 5th September 1992 against Swindon Town. 
* Finally he joins Reading in August 1994. He plays his first game on 30th August 1994 against Stoke City and his first goal as a professional is the winner against Middlesbrough on 4th February 1995.
* Last season was a disappointing one for Paul Holsgrove, a series of injuries and the loss of form leading to few chances. He finished up with 14 games under his belt and two goals.

986.name: Lunt
pages: * Kenny Lunt is the latest young talent to emerge from Crewe Alexandra's youth system, and is a player who has been called up by Dario Gradi this season. At just 17 years of age he has already made himself a first team regular, and he seems to have the ability to go make the step up to a bigger club very soon.

* Lunt is a midfielder who generally plays down the left hand side of the park, although he possesses the ability to take up a more central midfield position at sometime in the future. He possesses excellent passing ability and shows plenty of intelligence in everything he does.
x
x
* Lunt came though the youth ranks at Crewe Alexandra. He made his debut for the club on 9th  August 1997 against Swindon Town.
x

987.name: Smith
pages: * Peter Smith is another Crewe Alexandra player who broke into the side last year and who is being very highly spoken of. Still very young, he is waiting patiently for his opportunty, although his chances in the midfield are likely to be limited. He is though a player to watch, with one eye on the future.

* Smith is a midfielder who possesses great vision and touch, and has an equally exciting  future ahead of him. However, lacking in experience, he will have to improve his consistency although that is not something he should be worrying about given the amount of time he has on his side.
x
* Smith has played for England at youth international level.
* A product of the Crewe Alexandra youth system, Smith signed professional in July 1996. He made his debut on 15th March 1997 against Luton Town.
* Smith was able to make just one appearance during the course of last season, when he  played for  Crewe against Luton Town, making a good impression on those who saw him in action.

988.name: Charnock
pages: * Phil Charnock is a young player, who, after coming through the ranks at  Liverpool, was unable to break through into the plans of Roy Evans, after having made his debut during Graeme Souness' time as manager. After deciding that his future at Anfield was not a particularly promising one, Charnock moved on to join Crewe Alexandra, a club where he made himself an automatic and vital member of the side for Dario Gradi last season, and will no doubt prove to be equally as important for his manager this season.

* A midfielder capable of adapting to a number of different midield positions. His versatility allows him to play down either flank. Technically good, one of his  greatest assets is his tremendous work rate, something which is well appreciated by his manager Dario Gradi.

* Charnock signed professional for Liverpool on 27th May 1992, although he was never given the opportunity to make a league appearance for the Reds.
* He made his debut at 17 years of age in a European Cup Winners Cup tie, making his the youngest player ever to play for Liverpool in a European competition. The game took place during the 92-93 season against Cypriate side Apollon Limasol, Charnock coming on in place of Steve Harkness. 
* During the 95-96 season he was loaned out to Blackpool where he made 4 appearances. He made his debut on 10th February 1996 against Wycombe Wanderers.
* He finally completed his contract with Liverpool and signed for Crewe Alexandra in December 1996. He played his first game for the club on 1st October against Blackpool, and opened his goalscoring account as a professional on 20th December against Notts County.

* Once again Charnock was unable to break through into Roy Evans' side, and so, as a result, decided to accept an offer from Crewe Alexandra in December, after a spell of a few months at the club on loan. From the moment he joined the club he made himself an important part of Dario Gradi's plans, and made a vital contribution to the club finally clinching promotion to the First Division. He made a total of 32 appearances, scoring once.

989.name: Whalley
pages:
* Gareth Whalley is one of the best young players that Dario Gradi has under him at Crewe Alexandra. It seems sure that it won't be long, providing he can steer clear of injury, before he is signing for one of the big clubs in English football. He is, in fact, currently being followed by the chief scouts of a number of big clubs, who are all tracking his progress. The club who have so far come closest to signing him has been Liverpool. He had a spell training with the Anfield giants although finally nothing was eventually sorted out with regards toa permanent move. 
* A footballer with a tremendous future ahead of him, it is quite possible that he will soon be following in the foosteps of his ex-teammate Danny Murphy in the near future and moving to a big club. However until that moment comes along, then he will be giving 100% as he helps Crewe Alexandra in their adventure in the First Division.

* A talented midfield player he makes a fundamental contribution to the team's attacking play. He possesses outstanding individual skill, ball control in both feet, vision and accurate pasing ability. If all of that wasn't enough he is also a tremendously hard worker, and has no hesitation in helping out with defensive duties as much as possible.
* Chosen in the Second Division's ideal side for the 96-97season.
x

* After coming through the ranks at Crewe Alexandra, Whalley signed as a professional in July 1992. His first game for the senior side came on 22nd August 1992 against Scarborough  while he scored his first goal as a profesional on 8tt May against Barnet.

* Whalley completed a sensational season for Crewe Alexandra. On a personal level, not only did he managed to be chosen in the Second Division ideal team, but he also he maintained his excellent progress and gained a reputation as a player to be closely watched. He was one of the  key men in the club's promotion to the First Division, playing in 38 games and scoring 3 times.

990.name: Tierney
pages: * Francis Tierney is regarded as one of the players that Dario Gradi has at Crewe, who is most likely to carve out a really bright future for himself. At one time he looked certain to be joining Liverpool, although finally no deal was reached. A tremendously attack minded player, Tierney possesses the talent and the quality to be a success at a big club, but first of all he will have to concentrate on being a regular for Crewe Alexandra and maintain the sort of progress that could eventually see him making his dream move.

* A young midfielder with an attack minded approach to the game, he is at his best when he plays out wide on the flank. Together with his outstanding basic technique, he also possesses great enthusiasm and a genuine will to win, all of which makes him a highly promising young player.
x
* He is an England youth international.

* After coming through the youth ranks at Crewe Alexandra, Tierney signed as a professional on 22nd March 1993.His first game for the club came on 18thMay 1993 against Barnet, while he scored his first goal as a professional on 12th February 1994 against Scunthorpe United.

* Despite not being a member of the starting line up for many of Crewe Alexandra's games, Tierney was still followed by a number of scouts form the big Premier League clubs. He played in a number of different positions, although he always gave a good account of himself. He played in a total of 32 games, scoring 3 times.

991.name: Anthrobus
pages: * Steve Anthrobus is one of the regular strikers in Dario Gradi's side, forming a partnership with Dele Adebola. A very strong player, he is the perfect complement for his striking partner, creating plenty of opportunities which Adebola takes advantage of. A very popular player witth the Shrewsbury Town supporters, he will no doubt  go on to prove to be every bit as popular with the Crewe Alexandra supporters for all the same reasons.

* A classic centre forward, strong and powerful, Anthrobus makes the most of his physical  attributes to get in efforts on goal in the opposition penalty area. He possesses outstanding ability in the air and keeps opposing defenders under constant pressure, forcing them into  errors which he takes full advantage of. In recent years he has noticeably improved the technical side to his game, becoming much more reliable with the ball at his feet.
x
x

* After coming through the youth ranks at Milwall, Anthrobus signed as a professional in August 1986. He made his debut for the club on 20th October 1988 against Plymouth Argyle, while his first goal came on 29th August 1989 against Wimbledon 
* He was transfered to Wimbledon in february 1990 for £150,000. His debut for the Dons came on 24th February 1990 against Aston Villa.
* He went out on loan to Peterborough United in January 1994. His first game for the club came on 22nd January 1994 against Portsmouth.
* He had another loan spell, this time with Chester City, in August 1994. His first game was on 27th August 1994 against Huddersfield Town.
* Finally he was transfered to Shrewsbury Town, in August 1995, for £25,000. Despite not being a member of the starting line up he had an excellent debut, coming off the bench to find the back of the net for his new club against Swansea City on 12th August 1995. 
* Crewe Alexandra became his latest destination when they paid out £75,000 to sign him on in March 1997. His first game for the club came on 25th March 1997 against  Bristol City.

* Although not a goalscorer, Anthrobus showed enough qualities during his 33 games for his previous club, Shrewsbury Town, to win himself a move to Crewe Alexandra. He played in a total of 10 games for his new side and struck up a fine understanding with the club's goalscorer Adebola. In short, it was a satisfactory season for the giant Crewe striker.

992.name: Rivers
pages: * Mark Rivers is the only player in the whole of the Crewe Alexandra squad who was born in the town, and, as a result, has become a source of real pride for the club's supporters. A striker with a genuine goalscorer's instinct, he has made himself, thanks to his fine performances, a regular member of Dario Gradi's line up.

* Despite his youth, Rivers has demonstrated that he is a very natural goalscorer. He is always alert and ready to get onto the end of his teammates crosses into the box, or to pounce onto the goalkeepers parries or fumbles. He gives an equally good account of himself down either the right or the left flank, although it is down  the right hand side where he is generally to be found.
x
x

* After coming through the youth ranks at Crewe Alexandra, Rivers signed as a professional in May 1994. His debut for the club couldn't have been better, scoring twice against Brentford on 28 October 1995.

* Although his form wasn't quite up to the level he had shown the previous season, Rivers still did an outstanding job for Crewe Alexandra. During the course of the season he switched positions from the left flank to the right, where he found it easier to get among the scorers. A series of injuries kept him out of the side for a spell, although that didn't prevent him from from making a contribution to the club's promotion to the First Division which they achieved through the play offs. In total he played in 27 games, scoring 6 times.

993.name: Moralee
pages: * Jamie Moralee is a young centre forward who so far has shown his best form during his spell with Millwall, which eventually won him a move to Watford in exchange for a fair sum of money. Unfortunately he was unable to repeat his success and eventually moved on to Crewe Alexandra, where, due to injuries, he was restricted to just 7 appearances throughout the whole of  the season. Although he has plenty of ability he faces a difficult task in trying to dislodge Adebola or Anthrobus from the starting line up. He will have to show plenty of patience and be able to take his chance when it comes along.

* A goalscoring centre forward, he possesses good technical ability which allows him to create his own goalscoring chances. He is also adept at protecting the ball and holding it up as he waits for support to come through from midfield. He also has a good turn of pace when he is going for goal.
* Top scorer for Millwall 92-93.
x

* After coming through the youth ranks at Crystal Palace, Moralee signed professional  in July 1990. His first game for the Eagles came on 1st February 1992 against Coventry City. 
* Palace allowed him to leave and in September 1992 he joined Millwall. His debut came on 3rd October 1992 against Sunderland, and he opened his goalscoring account as a professional two weeks later against Charlton Athletic.
* He was transfered to Watford in July 1994 for £450,000. His first game for the club was on 13th August 1994 against Sheffield United, while he scored his first goal for his new club on 17th September 1994 against Luton Town.
* Finally he became a free agent and signed for Crewe Alexandra in August 1996. He played his first game for the club on 17th August 1996.

* Jamie Moralee was unable to play as much of a part as he would no doubt have liked,  being limited to just 7 appearances all season due to injury. Nevertheless he gave glimpses of  the fine striker that he undoubtedly is, although he didn't manage to score his first goal for his new club.

994.name: Little
pages: * Colin Little is a player who has proved to be Dario Gradi's secret weapon when he has come off the bench over the last couple of seasons. He has a reputation as a prolific goalscorer in amateur football, and it was a reputation he confirmed in the best moment of his career so far with Crewe. His goals against Luton Town gave Crewe the opportunity of winning promotion to the First Division which they finally clinched after overcoming Brentford. With a new outlook this season,  Little is, though, once again, a regular on the bench, waiting for the chance to get into the action to show that what he did last season wasn't just down to good luck.

* Well known as a goalscorer in amateur football, Little puts in a tremendous amount of hard work out on the park which allows him to sniff out goalscoring chances in situations where they don't  apparently exist.
x
x

* Little was signed from Hyde United in February 1996 for £50,000. His debut for the club came on 2nd March 1996 against Wrexham and he scored his first goals for them against Peterborough United on 30th 1996.

* He saw his contribution limited to just 17 appearances for Crewe Alexandra during the course of last season, the majority of those after coming off the substitutes bench. Nevertheless, his big moment was to come in the play offs for promotion to the First Division. He found the back of  the net twice in the semi-finals against Luton Town giving Crewe the opportunity to go up if they could beat Brentford, which they eventually did.

995.name: Garvey
pages: * Steve Garvey is another product of the Crewe Alexandra youth system although he has got a tough job on his hands trying to force his way into the plans of manager Dario Gradi. He is a team player, who has plenty of ability but whose appearances are limited to the occasions when he manages to come into the action off the substitutes bench. Nevertheless, Garvey will no doubt be out to change things during the course of the present season.
* A quick, skillful striker, he can play down either flank. Although he is not a goalscorer, he is capable of creating moments of danger around the opposition goal area.
x
x

* Afer coming through the youth ranks at Crewe Alexandra, Garvey signed as a professional in October 1991. His debut came on 11th May 1991 against Mansfield Town and he opened up his goalscoring account when he found the back of the net against Doncaster Rovers on 12th September 1992.
* Garvey didn't have a particularly good season last time out, being limited to just 17 appearances, the majority of those coming as a substitute.

996.name: Gray
pages: x
* A young player, he shows talent as a goalie. He is agile, has good reflexes, is secure when catching the ball and dominant in the air. His future is, therefore, promising.
x
x
x
* He was the first choice keeper and didn't miss a single game, producing an excellent season.

997.name: Nixon
pages: * A very experienced goalkeeper who had been at Tranmere Rovers a long time, being the first choice keeper almost since his arrival there in 1988. This situation remained unchanged until rise of Danny Coyne, the young goalie, forced him out of the team and has finally led to his departure to Stockport County, the club that has found a very experienced keeper who could be very useful to them in this first year in the First Division. He is undisputed first choice since the arrival of Gary Megson.

* Nixon is a very experienced keeper who is very complete.  He stands out, above all, for his aerial game where he dominates, being a true life insurance in this respect.  He positions himself very well allowing him to remedy difficult situations.  He makes some good saves thanks to his good positional play and reflexes.
x
x

* Originally from the amateur club Curzon Ashton, he signs as a professional for Manchester City in December 1983.  He makes his debut on the 21/9/85 against West Ham United.
* In August 1986 he is loaned to Wolverhampton Wanderers, playing his first game for Wolves on the 30/8/86 against Aldershot.
* He is loaned to Bradford City in November 1986, his debut taking place on the 29/11/86 against Stoke City.
* In December 1986 he is loaned to Southampton when Peter Shilton is injured, playing his first game on the 26/12/86 against Chelsea.
* In January 1987 he is loaned to Carlisle United, making his debut on the 24/1/87 against Blackpool.
* He starts the 87-88 season as the first choice at Manchester City but in March 1988 he is loaned to Tranmere Rovers.  He makes his debut on the 25/3/88 against Carlisle United staying until the end of the season with the Merseyside Club.
* He is finally transferred in July 1988 to Tranmere Rovers for £20,000 and from this moment on, he is the first choice keeper.
* Nixon was loaned to Bradford City on the 13th of September 1996, making his debut a day later against Oxford United.
* His signing for Stockport County comes through in the summer of 1997.

* Nixon started last season on loan to Bradford City, the club where he played 12 games before returning to Tranmere Rovers.  He shared the goalkeeping duties with Coyne equally, Nixon being the keeper who played from January until the end of the season, always producing good performances and not disappointing.  He played 25 games for the Rovers.

998.name: McIntosh
pages: * Andrew McIntosh has been one of Stockport's incorporations going into this season in the First Division.  Coming from Rotherham United, he has settled down as a starter in Gary Megson's starting elevens and hopes to play a significant role in the team's first year at this level.

* A man who used to play in the midfield, he has been converted into a defender at Stockport County, playing in the middle of the defence on the left.He is comfortable with the ball at his feet and he plays it out from the back, helped by his experience as a midfielder.  He is professional and controls the aerial game well.
x
x
* Stockport County sign him from Rotherham in the summer of 1997.
x

999.name: Woodthorpe
pages: * A veteran player who has been in a great number of teams, Woodthorpe has been one of the new players brought to the club for the first season in the First Division.  He plays as a sweeper in the centre of defence of the team managed by Gary Megson and, although he isn't used to playing in this position, he isn't doing so badly.

* Colin Woodthorpe is a player who basically takes on the functions of central defender but with Stockport County he is playing as a sweeper in the three-man central defence.  He has a good positional sense and brings the ball out with good judgement although he doesn't stand out in the technical aspect of the game.  He is dominant in the air but has problems with fast forwards as he is not so quick.
x
x

* Trained in the lower ranks of Chester City, Woodthorpe makes his debut for the team on the 30th of August 1986 against Bury and he scores his first goal against Gillingham, his first as a professional, on the 14th of February 1987.
* In July 1990 he moves to Norwich City for £175,000.  His first game with the Canaries is on the 11th of Mary 1991 against Sheffield United and he scores his first goal in the English First Division on the 22nd of February 1992 against Liverpool.
* He moves North of the border to play for Aberdeen in the Scottish First Division.
* He finally returns to English football to sign for Stockport County during the summer of 1997.

* Woodthorpe was playing at Aberdeen last year, taking part in 19 games during the course of the league, essentially being a substitute but managing a good run at the end of the Championship, in which he played from the start in several games.

1000.name: Searle
pages: * Damon Searle is a very attacking left back who was on the verge of being called up by Wales to make his full international debut.  However, last year wasn't his best as he lost his place in favour of Todd and was unable to regain it, thus making his debut for Wales seem ever farther away.  However, Gary Megson, the new manager at the team, has started to rely on him and play him from the start, and with this vote of confidence he might finally have the chance to make his debut for his country.
* A left back who covers a lot of ground, he likes to take part in the attacking moves.  He is quick and has a good touch, qualities that make him an interesting footballer.

* Welsh Cup Champion in 92 and 93 for Cardiff City.
* Third Division Champion in 93 with Cardiff City.

* 1 B international appearance for Wales.
* 6 times under-21 international.
* A youth and schoolboy international.

* Originally from the lower ranks of Cardiff City, Searle signs as a professional in August 1990.  His debut is against York City on the 13th of October 1990 and he scores his first goal as a professional against Walsall on the 3rd of March 1992, a goal which turns out to be the winner.
* He signs for Stockport County in May 1996 as a free agent, making his league debut on the 17th of August 1996 against Crewe Alexandra.

* After starting the season as the first choice left back at Stockport County, Searle lost his place to Lee Todd and couldn't regain it thanks to the sensational performances of the man who stepped into his place.  In total he played 10 games for the team.

1001.name: Gannon
pages: * James Gannon is a central defender who has managed to come back from a serious injury two years ago when he broke his leg.  He is once again in the side, leading the team from the back.  Currently, he isn't figuring in the starting line-ups except when there is an emergency.  This experienced central defender is now in his eighth season at County.

* A powerful central defender who dominates in the aerial game, he is solid and professional in all his actions.  He effectively makes up for his lack of technical resources.  He can also play in the midfield at times of emergency but as a man who tries to break up the opponents' game rather than construct his own team's moves.
x
x

* Sheffield United sign him from the Irish club Dundalk in April 1989.  He never manages to play for the Blades.
* He is loaned to Halifax Town in February 1990, making his debut on the 24th of February against Maidstone United.
* Stockport acquired his services after paying Sheffield United £40,000 in March 1990.  His debut for County is on the 9th of March 1990 in a game against Wrexham and he scores his first goal as a professional on the 29th of May of this same year against Carlisle United.
* He is loaned to Notts County January 1994, playing his first game on the 15th of January against Luton Town.

* Gannon started the season on the bench but he took advantage of the suspension of Matthew Bound, forced his way into the team, and didn't relinquish his status as a starter for the rest of the season. 1002.name: Dinning
pages: * Tony Dinning is a player who, ever since his arrival from Newcastle United, has had to be content with being a team player, coming onto the pitch to replace an injured or suspended team-mate, but always doing his duty. Fortunately his big chance is arriving this year. Gary Megson is placing his trust in him and playing him from the start.  Dinning, obviously, will try not to waste this chance.

* Tony Dinning is a central defender who can occupy the position of defensive midfielder, whose role is almost entirely that of breaking up the opponents' game as he is not capable of acting as a playmaker.  He takes advantage of his tall stature to dominate in the air, but he needs to work on his individual technique to play the ball out from the back.
x
x

* Originally from the lower ranks of Newcastle United, Dinning signs as a professional in October 1993.  He doesn't get to play for the Magpies. 
* Free of contractual obligations he signs for Stockport County in June of 1994.  He makes his league debut on the 27th of August 1994 against Brentford and scores his first goal against Plymouth Argyle on the 28th of March 1995.

* Last year, Tony Dinning had the difficult task of stepping in for his team-mates when they were injured but his performance was dignified, contributing a lot of consistency and firmness to Stockport County whether he was playing at centre back or defensive centre half.  In total he played 20 games and managed to score a couple of goals.

1003.name: Connelly
pages: * After a somewhat irregular start in his spell at Stockport County after arriving from the amateur team Hallam, Sean Connelly has almost become the official owner of the right back position in the team, performing well in defensive tasks on his flank.  A sure bet for Megson, he hopes to be one of the key players in helping the team stay in the First Division.

* He normally plays at right back, and when the circumstances demand, as a central defender.  He is a very reliable footballer who likes to push up along his flank supporting his team-mates and getting into some good positions for creating danger but these are not translated into goals for him but he does put over some good crosses.
x
x

* Originally from the amateur club Hallam, Connelly signs for Stockport County in August 1991.  His league debut is one the 20th of March 1993 against Preston North End.
* He scores the winning goal in the victory over Middlesbrough in the semi-finals of the League Cup in the Riverside Stadium in the 96-97 season. Despite his heroic action, County are knocked out.
* He is the assistant to the club's physio.

* As well as playing as a starter for Stockport County, Sean is the physio's assistant, taking advantage of his physio title.  For yet another year he was a regular feature in the team, performing to a very satisfactory level in the 45 games which he played for the club.

1005.name: Cook
pages:
* Signed for Stockport during the 97-98 season. 
* Left without many chances at Coventry City, his signing for Tranmere Rovers was a new chance for this skilful left half to show his already known technical skills.

* A left-footed midfielder, he is a very technical player. He has good ball control, being able to play long balls with a lot of accuracy or switch wings to change the direction of the attack. A good short-range passer, he distributes the ball effectively. He takes corners masterfully and with great effect. His long-range shot is good. Pretty strong, he steals balls easily but has more attacking tendencies than defensive ones.
x
x

* Originally from the amateur club Marine, he signs as a professional in July 1984 for Wigan Athletic. He makes his debut in the league on 13th May 1985 against Reading and scores his first goal against Swansea City on 18th January 1986.
* In May 1988 he is transferred to Norwich City for £25,000, making his league debut on 19th April 1989 against Southampton.
* He is transferred to Wolverhampton Wanderers for £200,000 in November 1989. He makes his debut in the league on 1st November 1989 against Leicester City and scores his first goal for Wolves on 2nd December 1989 against Middlesbrough.
* In the summer of 1994 he is transferred to Coventry City for £600,000. He plays his first game on 20th August 1994 against Wimbledon and scores his first goal in the Premier League on 10th September 1994 against QPR. 
* He is transferred to Tranmere Rovers in February 1996 for £250,000.
* Despite various injuries last season, Cook managed to play 36 games for the team in the league and scoring 3 goals, including a double against Norwich City.

1006.name: Cooper
pages: * A supersub for Derby County, Kevin Cooper was a player whose chances stood out by their absence, not letting him show his ability to the coaches at the club.  Finally he has had to move to Stockport County to be able to do so, his arrival being very positive for the team.  He helped for a part of last season, a season in which the team earned promotion to the First Division.  An undisputed starter for Gary Megson, he hopes to be able to demonstrate to the coaches of his former team that they made a mistake when they let him go.

* Cooper is a very skilful left wing who is able to penetrate rival defences very easily and is good in the one-on-one thanks to his quality and speed. He gets into some dangerous positions, and is able to take his chances or make a pass to a team-mate.  What's more, he works hard in defence and is able to make sacrifices.
x
x

* Originally from the lower ranks of Derby County, Cooper signs as a professional in July 1993.  His league debut takes place on the 7th of May 1993 against Watford.
* He is loaned to Stockport County in March 1997 to cover for the absence of Cavaco.  His debut for County can not be better as he scores the winner against Bristol Rovers on the 29th of March 1997.

* On the substitutes' bench at Derby County, Cooper was loaned and then later transferred to Stockport County last year and ever since his arrival he made a large impact, pleasing both the coaches and the fans.  In total he played 12 games and scored three goals, all of them in the final stretch of the league which finished in promotion to the First Division.

1007.name: Bennett
pages: * Thomas Bennett is a hard-working midfielder who is also has some good technical details.  He has been essential for Stockport County when they were trying for promotion of the First Division.  What's more, his great performances in the televised League Cup games brought him a certain fame in England.  In this competition the club made it to the semi-finals and they were on the brink of knocking out Middlesbrough.  Important in Megson's scheme for his untiring work, he is almost certain to be a starter.

* Tom Bennett is a defensively minded midfielder, excellent at winning back the ball, this perhaps being his greatest virtue.  He almost always passes in short looking for the best-placed team-mate.  He is improved his contribution to the attacking game, and is currently appearing more in attack.
x
x

*Originally from the lower ranks of Aston Villa, he signs as a professional in December 1987.
* Free of contractual obligations he signs for Wolverhampton Wanderers in July 1988.  He makes his debut in the league on the 5th of November 1988 against Southend United and scores his first goal for Wolves against Charlton Athletic on the 15th of January 1992.
* He is transferred to Stockport County in June 1995 for £75,000.  He plays his first game for the club on the 12th of August 1995 against Walsall and his first goal can't be more decisive: he scores the winner from the penalty spot in a game against Peterborough United on the 19th of December 1992.

* Bennett was one of the best players at Stockport County last year, only missing 3 of the possible 46 possible games during the league and scoring 3 times for the club.  In his second year with County, he managed to perform to the level expected of him at the beginning of the season.

1008.name: Marsden
pages: * Chris Marsden was, perhaps, the most important player at Stockport County last season, the season in which the club earned promotion to the First Division.  As the director of the team's play, he moved the ball around at his pleasure and his work was very significant for his club and for the players who voted him a member of the Second Division Dream Team.  He is currently not playing for the team but he has enough class to enter into the Megson's plans, or those of any other manager for that matter.

* Chris Marsden is a midfielder with a lot of class.  He is able to direct and organise the team's game and set the most appropriate rhythm at any given moment.  He is a good passer, and uses his technique intelligently.
* Voted member of the Second Division Dream Team in the 96-97 season.
x

* Originally from the Sheffield United youth squad, he signs as a professional in January 1987.  His debut with the Blades can not be better as he scores a goal against Blackburn Rovers on the 29th of August 1987.
* He signs for Huddersfield Town in July 1988.  He plays his first game on the 3rd of September 1988 and scores his first goal in league competition on the 11th of February 1989.
* He is loaned to Coventry City in November 1993, making his debut on the 25th of November 1993 against Blackburn Rovers.
* Wolverhampton Wanderers sign him in 1994 in exchange for £250,000.  His first game for Wolves is on the 15th of January 1994 against Bolton Wanderers. 
* His next destination is Notts County in November 1994 for the same amount as his previous transfer, that is to say, £250,000.  His debut for the club is on the 13th of January 1996 against Barnsley.
* Finally, his transfer to Stockport County comes through for £70,000 in the summer of 1996.  He plays his first game for County on the 13th of January 1996 against Barnsley and he scores his first goal for his new club against Oxford United on the 30th of March 1996.

* Chris Marsden's season was sensational.  He was a vital figure in  Stockport County's successful promotion bid.  His great role was recognised by his own team-mates and rivals, who voted him a member of the division's Dream Team.  In total he played 35 games and scored 3 goals.

1009.name: Flynn
pages: * Michael Flynn was the Stockport County captain during last season, the season in which the team managed to get promoted to the First Division, and was a true support pillar for the team in the team's defence.  His charisma and leadership made him irreplaceable for the manager at the time, Dave Jones, but this is not the case of Gary Megson, who is not using him at the start of the league although he might get his chance.

* His fighting spirit is the most notable characteristic of Mike Flynn, whose sacrifice and push in defensive tasks make him an important man in any team.  He plays at centre back or sweeper and always gives his best. His powerful shot from a distance makes him a dangerous player when he gets into positions just outside the box.
* Voted a member of the Second Division Dream Team in the 96-97 season.
x

* Originally from the lower ranks of Oldham Athletic, Flynn signs as a professional in February 1987.  He makes his debut in the league on the 18th of August 1987 against Bradford City and scores his only goal in league competition against Sheffield United on the 2nd of January 1988.
* He is transferred to Norwich City in December 1988 in exchange for £100,000 but he never gets to make his debut for the Canaries.
* He changes club again in December 1989, moving to Preston North End, who pay £125,000 to acquire his services.  His first game with the team is on the 16th of this same month against Birmingham City and he scores his first goal on the 14th of April 1990 against Bristol City.
* He is signed by Stockport County in March 1993 for £125,000.  His debut for County takes place on the 27th of March 1992 against Plymouth Argyle and he scores his first goal for his new team on the 5th of March 1994 against Hartlepool United.

* For yet another year Mike Flynn was an undisputed starter in the Stockport County scheme.  His charisma makes him an essential man in any line-up. Last season he played 46 games in the championship and rounded off a great all-round performance scoring two goals for his team.

1010.name: Durkan
pages: * Kieran Durkan was another very important player for Stockport County during last season, showing that he has more than enough ability to be successful in the team.  Although he is not particularly quick nor skilful, he does what he does well, supplying balls to the forwards.  He does not have an assured place in the team this year with Megson but he is playing more or less regularly, either as a starter or coming on as a substitute.

* A right half, he can also play as a winger.  He stands out for the accuracy of his crosses to the heart of the rival box, presenting a lot of chances on a plate for his forwards.  A player making great progress, his best is yet to come.
* Welsh Cup Champion 95.
* 3 under-21 international appearances for Ireland.

* Originally from the lower ranks of Wrexham, Durkan signs as a professional in July 1992.  His debut takes place on the 3rd of September 1992 against Mansfield Town and he scores his first goal as a professional against Fulham on the 22nd of February 1994.
* He is transferred to Stockport County in February 1996 for £95,000.  He plays his first game for County on the 17th of February 1996 and he opens his account for the club with a goal against Crewe Alexandra on the 17th of August 1996.

* A man who Dave Jones used a lot.  He played 41 games and scored 3 goals, showing that the people who had doubted his ability to be Stockport County were wrong.  He was also one of the essential players in the successful promotion bid.

1011.name: Cavaco
pages: * Luis Cavaco was a signed last season by Stockport County and made a great impact thanks to his excellent ability for this sport.  He was a regular in David Jones schemes.  Unfortunately, a double fracture in his leg in the month of April forced him to miss the rest of the season.  Capable of doing great things, Cavaco will have to make a satisfactory recovery from his injury and try to regain his place in Gary Megson's team.

* Cavaco is a player who plays as a winger on either side, performing equally well on either.  He is very quick and technically capable, allowing him to go past defenders.  All these attributes make him ideal for attacking football, and what's more he is still progressing.
x
x

* After his contract with Estoril finishes, Cavaco signs for Stockport County in August 1996.  His debut takes place on the 31st of August 1996 against Bristol Rovers and he scores his first goal on English soil against Brentford on the 9th of November 1996.

* Since his arrival at the club, Luis Cavaco has made a great impact at Stockport County thanks to his excellent ability for the attacking game. Everything was going well until he received a double fracture in his leg in April which, obviously, meant that he missed the rest of the league.  Up until this moment he had played 27 games and scored 5 goals.

1012.name: Nash
pages: * Martin Nash is a very young player who has the honour of being the first international to sign for Stockport County since 1924, his country being Canada.  He has a lot of ability, and has appeared fairly regularly on Megson's teamsheet and he hopes to be an important man for County in the future.
* Nash is a winger who can play on either wing and who is very quick and skilful in his actions.  He also has a special touch which contributes to the high quality of his crosses.
x
* 6 international appearances for Canada.
* Stockport County sign him after his contract with the Canadian club Regina had expired.  His first game for County is on the 7th of February 1997 against Bristol City.
* Although Nash could only play 3 games for Stockport County, his role was very important and this young Canadian showed plenty of signs of promise.

1013.name: Angell
pages: * Brett Angell is a footballer who has been at a whole host of clubs but he has never managed to settle at any of them.  However, it seems that he has finally found a little bit of peace at Stockport County in this his second spell at the club.  His enormous scoring capacity has assured him of being a starter and his excellent start to the league has placed him amongst the top scorers in what is his best season as a professional to date.  A fixed member of the team for Megson, he could hold the key to the club avoiding relegation to the Second Division.

* Angell is an enormous centre forward whose has as his biggest virtues the enormous power and his dominance in the air.  In this type of play he is very dangerous and his scent for goal has allowed him to score goals fairly regularly during his career.  He does not stand out with the ball at his feet and he limits himself to doing what he can and waiting for the chance to finish off a chance created by his team-mates.

* Top scorer at Stockport County in the 89-90 and 96-97 seasons.
* Top scorer at Southend United in the 90-91 and 91-92 seasons.
x

* Originally from the lower ranks of Portsmouth, he signs as a professional in August 1986.  However, he moves to play for the amateur team Cheltenham Town.
* He is transferred to Derby County in February 1988 for £40,000 but he doesn't get to play.
* He is transferred again, but this time to Stockport County in October 1988 for £33,000.  His debut takes place on the 22nd of October 1988 and he scores his first goal as a professional against Hartlepool United just two days later.
* Southend United is his next destination.  The club sign him for £100,000 in August 1990.  His first game is very good, he scores a goal against Huddersfield Town on the 25th of August 1990.
* He is loaned to Everton in September 1993, playing his first game on the 25th of this same month against Norwich City.
* Finally the Toffees decide to acquire his services in January 1994 for £500,000.  The first game of this second spell at the Merseyside club is on the 15th of January 1994 against Swindon Town and this first goal has to wait until the 5th of February against Chelsea.
* He is transferred to Sunderland in March 1995 for £600,000.  He makes his debut on the 24th of March 1995 against Barnsley.
* He is loaned to Sheffield United in January 1996.  He plays his first game for the Blades on the 31st of this month against Luton Town and WBA is the on the receiving end of his first goal on the 20th of February 1996. 
* He is loaned once again, this time to West Bromwich Albion in March of 1996, making his debut on the 2nd of April against Luton Town.
* He is finally loaned to Stockport County in August 1996 then transferred for £120,000.  His first game for County is on the 24th of August against Notts County and his first two goals come in the same game on the 21st of September against York City.

* Angell became the player who had most luck in front of goal for Stockport County last season, the club where he was firstly a loan player before thethe definitive move in November.  His magnificent campaign allowed him to play 34 games and score 15 goals, the most important of which was one against Chesterfield in the last-but-one game of the season which earned County automatic promotion to the First Division.

1014.name: Mutch
pages: * Andy Mutch is a veteran forward who has a special scent for goal as he has shown during his entire sporting career.  He formed a spectacular partnership with Steve Bull at Wolves, one of the most prolific partnerships in recent years.  Currently, he almost has to be content with coming on as a substitute and contributing his special touch to Stockport County.  He can also step in for some of the first choice players if they become injured.

* Andy Mutch is an opportunistic forward.  He converts every loose ball in the box into a goal.  Although he is technically limited his positional sense, intelligence and experience make him a constant danger for the rival keepers.  He is also useful as a support for strikers such as Angell, more limited technically who need men like Mutch who can supply them with chances.

* Third Division Champion 89.
* Fourth Division Champion 88.
* Associated Members Cup Champion 88.

* 3 times B international for England.
* 1 under-21 international.

* The coaches at Wolverhampton Wanderers took notice of him and signed him from the amateur club Southport in February 1986.  His debut with the club is on the 8th of March 1986 against Rotherham United and his first game for Wolves doesn't have to wait a long time.  He scores on the 22nd of this same month against Bristol City.
* He is transferred to Swindon Town in August 1993 for £250,000.  He plays his first game for the Robins on the 22nd of August 1993 against Liverpool and on the 18th of September 1993 he scores his first goal against Newcastle United.
* He is loaned to Wigan Athletic in August 1995.  His debut is impressive, scoring a goal against Preston North End on the 26th of August.
* As a free agent he moves to Stockport County in March 1996.  He plays his first game for County on the 16th of March 1996 against Wrexham and one week later he scores his first goal against Brighton & Hove Albion.  His first hat-trick comes one week later against Oxford United.

* Andy Mutch's season was good and the team finally earned promotion to the First Division.  His good finishing and the chances he created for other players were much appreciated by the coaches and fans alike.  In total he played 33 games and scored 4 goals.

1015.name: Coleman
pages:
* Signed for Southend United in the 97-98 season. 
* Simon Coleman is a typical central defender who is good in the air but rather clumsy with the ball at his feet.  Last season he didn't play a single game and if this season looks like turning out the same he will probably look for a chance at another club.

* A very strong defender who is good in the air, at times untouchable in this respect.  He is pretty clumsy with the ball at his feet and will usually boot it away when under the slightest pressure.  He is not very flexible and has a lot of problems when faced with quick, skilful forwards.

* Originally from the lower ranks of Mansfield Town he signs as a professional in July 1985.  He makes his league debut on the 21/4/87 against Notts County, scoring his first league goal on the 20/10/87 against Northampton Town.
* He is transferred to Middlesbrough in September 1989 for £400,000, making his debut on the 30/9/89 against Watford and he scores his first goal against the same team on the 7/3/90. 
* He is transferred to Derby County in August 1991 for £300,000, and makes his debut in the league on the 17/8/91 against Sunderland and his first league goal is the winner in a game against Bristol Rovers on the 15/2/92.

* Signed by Bolton Wanderers for £350,000 in October 1994, he scores a goal on his league debut against Burnley on the 8/10/94.

1016.name: Roget
pages: * A product of the Southend United youth system, Leo Roget is a player who has a great future ahead of him, taking into account what he has already achieved at just 19 years of age. Last year he demonstrated that he possesses tremendous maturity for someone so young, as well as fantastic natural ability as a central defender. It remains to be seen if this is to be the year that Roget takes the step up to becoming a regular member of the side, or whether Ronnie Whelan decides that he is not yet ready for the responsibility.

* Roget is a tall central defender who is good in the air and is physically very strong. While his height makes him dominant in the air, his speed makes him difficult to beat on the ground. He is good on the ball, showing good technique and control. He can also play as a centre forward, a position where he demonstrates the ability already mentioned, as well as his capacity for getting in shoots on goal with either foot, as was well illustrated with his goal, so far the only one of his career, last season against Watford.
x
x

* After coming through the ranks at Southend United, he signed professional in September 1995. He made his league debut on 27th February 1996 against Sunderland and scored his first goal - the equalizer - against Watford on 8th April 1996.

* Last season he made 25 appearances, all of those as a member of the starting line up. The injury to Mike Lapper allowed him to take his place in the side, a position he held onto without any problems until the end of the campaign.

1017.name: Harris
pages: * At just 19 years of age, Andrew Harris had to leave Anfield to try to carve out a career for himself due to the intense competition for a place at Liverpool. With men such as Jason McAteer and Rob Jones ahead of him in the queue, it proved to be impossible for him to make the breakthrough into the first team. Many people have compared him to ex-Liverpool player Sammy Lee, who is currently in charge of Liverpool's reserve side. Still with a good future ahead of him Harris will now, no doubt, get his chance to play in the first team at Southend United, and hopefully go on to confirm the expectations that a lot of people had in this young right back.

* Harris is a right back in the classical Liverpool style, playing the ball around thoughtfully, never wasting possession. He will play the ball both short and long, although always making sure that it is played accurately and with purpose. A quick player, he is a good marker although he doesn't often move forward into the attack, preferring to stay back and cover in defence. He needs to gain more confidence in his own ability in order to develop the attacking side of his game. He also needs to become harder if he is to make opponents pay him more respect.
x
x
x
* Last season he played in 44 games, starting in 43 of then. He was at the top of his form throughout the campaign and at no time was he let down by his lack of professional experience.

1018.name: Stimson
pages: * After a season in which Mark Stimson seemed to be unable to settle down at any club, he finally managed to do so at Southend United, who were looking for a player of his experience and efficiency. He didn't let Ronnie Whelan down, and had an almost immediate impact following his arrival at the Blues. His magnificent form during the course of last season will be the standard by which he is judged this time out, a campaign in which he will be hoping to settle down in his possession on the left hand side of the Southend United defence.

* Stimson is an experienced left back who brings great stability to Southend United. He is a hard player when he goes in to win the ball and is a difficult opponent to get the better of. He is also good in the air although he is not particularly tall. He is very comfortable in possession, and is a good passer of the ball, especially over short distances, playing the ball around intelligently. He regularly gets forward to support the attack, and puts over some good, quality crosses. He has exemplary positional sense, which allows him to beat opponents to the ball. In short, he is a solid player who rarely lets anybody down.
x
x

* After coming through the ranks at Tottenham Hotspur, he signed professional in July 1985. His first game for the London club came on 11th May 1987 against Everton.
* He was loaned out to Leyton Orient in March 1988, making his debut on 22nd March 1988 against Burnley.
* He was also loaned out to Gillingham in January 1989, playing his first game for the club on 21st January 1989 against Sheffield United. 
* His transfered to Newcastle United was agreed in June 1989, in exchange for £200,000. He made his debut for the Magpies on 26th August 1989 against Leicester City and scored his first goal as a professional against Oxford United on 9th December 1989.
* He had a spell on loan at Portsmouth in December 1992, making his debut against Peterborough United on 12th December 1992. 
* His next destination was also Portsmouth, in July 1993, this time on a permanent basis in exchange for £100,000. He made his debut on 14th August 1993 against Oxford United, while his first goal for Pompey proved to be the winner against Birmingham City on 20th November 1993. 
* He was loaned out to Barnet in September 1995. He played his first game for the club on 23rd September 1995 against Bury. 
* Finally, he was transfered to Southend United in March 1996 for £25,000, making his debut on 16th March 1996 against Charlton Athletic.

* Last season he played in nine games making seven starting appearances. He looked set to become one of the most important members of the side until injuries pevented him from playing more regularly, forcing him to watch the majority of the season unfold from the stands.

1020.name: Nielsen
pages: * John Nielsen is one of the few new signings that Southend United made during the pre-season, and could well prove to be the most important, bearing in mind the quality that the player could bring to the Blues. In the short time he has been at the club, he has shown that he is a very complete player, and that he made well go on to make a key contribution this season.

* Nielsen is a very strong player who is a good ballwinner. Basically left footed, he has an excellent shot, powerful and accurate which he shapes up to make the most of when he gets the slightest opportunity. He is a very attack minded player, who gets forward, whenever he can, to support the attack, where he shows great decisiveness. He has good dribbling ability when he is in full flight, and good vision. He is a good passer of the ball, and is very comfortable with the ball at his feet, distributing it efficiently. He likes to make quick runs from deep positions, going past opposing defenders, before getting good quality crosses into the forwards.
x
x
* Southend United signed him in the summer of 1996 from Danish club Ikast.

* Last season he played in 24 games, making 17 starting appearances, scoring 3 times. He was an important man in the midfield, and one of the most popular players with the supporters. He was unable to play in the final run in to the season due to an injury.

1021.name: Byrne
pages: * Signed from Scottish club Glasgow Celtic, Byrne last season proved to be one of the bargain buys of the First Division, and a great signing for very little money, on the part of manager Ronnie Whelan. His great performances last season, including his galloping runs  down the right hand side, deservedly won him the admiration of the club's supporters. Byrne's form this time round will be important in deciding the fate of Southend United, since he is undoubtedly one of the manager's main men.

* Byrne is a midfielder who always operates down the right hand side, where he shows great speed and decisiveness in everything he does. He loves to get down the flank, where he can make life difficult for defenders, with his pace and ability to carry the ball. An unselfish player, he also works hard to help out the defence and always gives 100%. He has a good  shot from long distance and is a good crosser of the ball, looking to pick out the heads of Boere and Williams.
x
* Byrne has played for the Republic of Ireland at Youth intyernational level.

* After coming through the youth ranks at Oxford United, he signed as a professional in July 1989. He made his league debut on 21st October 1989 against Barnsley.
* He became a free agent and signed for Welsh amateur club Bangor City, in September 1991.
* Byrne signed for Celtic in May 1993. He played his first game for the Scottish club on 6th October 1993 against St. Johnstone and scored his first goal for Celtic, and his first as a professional against Aberdeen on 19th January 1994. The Irish midfielder even managed to score 2 goals in the Old Firm game, between Celtic and Rangers, the first of those coming at Parkhead, home of Celtic, on 30th October 1994, while he also scored, this time at Ibrox, on 4th January 1995.
* He was loaned out to Brighton & Hove Albion in March 1995. He made his  debut on 11th March 1995 against Wrexham, and scored his first goal for the club on 28th March 1995 against Rotherham United.
* He was transferd to Southend United in autumn 1995 for £80,000. He made his first appearance for the Blues on 26th August 1995 against Millwall and scored his first goal for the club against Birmingham City on 2nd December 1995.

* Last season he played in 32 games, making 23 starting appearances, managing to find the back of the net once. He failed to reproduce the form of previous seasons, and, although he was a regular member of the starting line up, he wasn't the decisive player he had been in other campaigns.

1022.name: Dublin
pages: * Keith Dublin does an invaluable job for Southend United, bearing in mind the versatility that this ex-England youth international brings to the side. In his third season at the club this good all round footballer will be hoping to repeat the tremendous form which has seen him become one of the most popular players with the club's supporters, as a result of the tremendous job he does and the image he creates out on the park, always giving 100% in every game he plays.

* Keith Dublin is a player who has the advantage of being able to play almost anywhere, although it is at the heart of the defence where he is  most comfortable. Very much a left footed player, his main assets are his speed, which he still retains despite the advancing years, and his ability in the air, where he made the most of his good positional play as well as his ability to get up above opposing forwards. Due to his speed, he can cut out attacks almost before they begin, although he seldom moves forward into the attack, except for when the opportunity clearly presents itself.
x
* He has played for England at yourh international level.

* After coming through the ranks at Chelsea, he signed professional in January 1984. He made his league debut on 7th May 1984 against Barnsley due to an injury to first team regular Joey Jones.
* He was transfered to Brighton & Hove Albion for £3,500 in August 1987. He played his first game for the club on 15th August 1987 against York City and scored his first goal as a professional against Gillingham on 7th November 1987.
* Watford signed him for £275,000 in July 1990. He made his debut on 25th August 1990 against Millwall, and scored his first goal for the Hornets on 22nd August 1992 against Grimsby Town. 
* He sigend for Southend United in July 1994. He played his first game for the Blues on 13th August 1994 against Millwall and scored his first goal on 27th August 1994 against Luton Town.

* He played in all 46 league games as a member of the starting line up. He was the side's best player, as was recognised by the club's supporters, who voted him as their "Player of the Year". He once again demonstrated his versatility, going on to play in four different defensive positions.

1023.name: Gridelet
pages: * Phil Gridelet is the man who does the spade work in midfield for Southend United, where he does a tremendous job due to his strength and fighting spirit, always giving it everything he has got. Despite the stiff competition for a place in the midfield, whenever he is called upon, he always does the job expected of him. Once again this season he will no doubt be one of Ronnie Whelan's most regular performers.

* Gridelet is a midfielder of tremendous strength and who is a great ballwinner. A very hard player when he is battling for possession, his aggressive approach has occasionally got him into trouble with referees, which has too often been transformed into yellow cards. He is basically a defensive player, although he occasionally pushes forward to provide an extra option in attack. He seldom finds the back of the net.
x
x

* Barnsley signed him for amateur club Barnet in January 1990 for £175,000, he made his debut on 17th November 1990 against Newcastle United. 
* He was loaned out to Rotherham United in March 1993, where he played his first game on 6th March 1993 against Huddersfield Town. 
* He became a free agent and signed for Southend United in September 1993. He made his debut on 9th October 1993 against Grimsby Town and scored his first goal in the league, and his first as a professional, on 10th December 1994, clinching, in the process, three points for his club against Middlesbrough.

* Last season he played in a total of 41 games, making 37 starting appearances, managing the back of the net once. He kept up a tremendous level of performers throughout the whole season, and became one of the key members of the midfield, where he stood out for his work-rates and unselfish approach to the game.

1024.name: Hails
pages: * Julian Hails is a very complete midfielder who is an important member of Ronnie Whelan's Southend United side. Last year, due to the club's injury problems he was forced to play in almost every possible position except goalkeeper, and did, in general, a tremendous job in all of them. Due to his experience, he is a player who will almost always be in the side, although, he might not know in what position he is going to play.

* A good all round midfield player, Julian Hails possesses great experience. Despite playing in almost every position, he is at his most comfortable in the midfield. He is an excellent ballwinner, and is a hard player, who, due to his physical power is able to keep working for ninety minutes. He shows good touches and ball control, and is comfortable with the ball on either foot.
x
x

* Fulham signed him from amateur club Hemel Hempstead in August 1990. He made his league debut on 18th January 1992 against Shrewsbury Town, and scored his first goal as a professional on 4th April 1992 against Swansea City. 
* He became a free agent and signed for Southend United in December 1994. His first game for the Blues came on 3rd December 1994 against Swindon Town while he struck his first goal for the club 7 days later against  Middlesbrough.

* Last season he played in 37 games making 32 starting appearances. He showed an unselfish attitude throughout the whole season, which benefitted the whole side, and, at all times, enjoyed the full backing of the club's coaching staff.

1026.name: Royce
pages:
* Signed for amateur club Haybridge Swifts, Simon Royce could become one of Southend United's best signings in recent years, due both to the amount of money he cost as well as the performances the young goalkeeper has put together for the Blues. He has recently attracted the attention of a number of Premier League clubs, although as yet nothing has been agreed.
* The security he shows in goal [excpet for when he has to deal with high balls into the box], spreads confidence to his defensive colleagues, who know that they have a guarantee behind them in goal should something go wrong in the back line. Royce has become a real leader in the side and is very popular with the Blues' supporters. He will be an almost automatic first choice in goal once again this season.

* Simon Royce is a keeper with fantastic reflexes which allow him to make great saves at point blank distance. He is also very brave and quick when he has to come out at the feet of opposing forwards. He has good positional sense and judges distances well. His weakness however is in the air, where he is inconsistent and occasionally guilty of making simple schoolboy errors.
x
x

* Southend United signed him from amateur club Heybridge Swifts, in October 1991, for £10,000. His first game for the club came on 28th March 1992 against Grimsby Town.
* He was chosen as Southend United's Player of the Year for 95-96 by the club's supporters.

* He played in 43 games, all of those being starting appearances. He was one of the side's most outstanding players and showed tremendous form right throughout the campaign, although it wasn't enough to prevent Southend from being relegated.

1027.name: Marsh
pages:
* One of the best players to have arrived at Southend United in recent seasons, Mike Marsh made himself the side's leader in his first season at the club.
* A product of the Liverpool youth system, he couldn't manage to establish himself in the side at Anfield, alongside players such as Steve McManaman and Jamie Redknapp, although he did have a couple of good seasons with the Reds. Later, he moved on to West Ham United and then Coventry City before arriving in Turkey where he played for Galatasaray. However, he failed to adapt to the lifestyle in Turkey, his time in the country turning into something of a nightmare.
* Southend United manager and Marsh's ex-Liverpool colleague Ronnie Whelan, swooped to quickly take him back to England. At present Marsh is well settled down in the side, and will be hoping that he can help the Blues go as far as possible.

* Marsh is a player through whom all of the side's attacking play flows. He has great ball control, though he is stronger on his right than his left. He is an accurate passer of the ball over both long and short distance. He is always available to recieve the ball, and keeps his composure well when he has to bring it out from the back in tight situations. He has a good ability to beat a man, which he showed during the early stages of his career at Liverpool where he played up front. He has a sensational shot from distance in his right foot and is also an expert  penalty taker. Despite his fragile appearance, he is quite a strong player, who goes in hard for the ball, winning plenty of possession for the side.
* F.A. Cup winners medal 1992 with Liverpool.
x

* Marsh completed his contract with amateur club Kirkby Town, and signed for Liverpool in August 1987. He made his league debut on 1st March 1989 against Charlton Athletic, replacing Barry Venison. His first league goal, on 28th November 1992, against Crystal Palace, was a stinging right foot shoot from 30 yards.
* He was transfered to West Ham United, together with David Burrows, as part of the deal that took Julian Dicks to Liverpool. He played his first game for the club on 25th September 1993 against Newcastle United, and scored his only goal for the Hammers in the London derby against Tottenham Hotspur, on 4th April 1994.
* Coventry City signed him in December 1994 for £450,000. He played his first game for the Sky Blues on 31st December 1994 against Tottenham Hotspur and scored his first goal for the side against his previous club West Ham United on 18th February 1995.
* He was transfered to Galatasaray in the summer of 1995 for £1 million. However, after a disastrous time in Turkey, he returned to England to sign for Southend United under the guidance of his ex-Liverpool colleague, and now manager Ronnie Whelan, in October 1995 in exchange for £500,000. He made his debut on 9th September 1995 against Sunderland and scored his first two league goals on 20th December 1995 against Port Vale, clinching a victory for Southend United.

* Last season he played in 35 games, all of those appearances as a member of the starting line up, and found the back of the net five times. He was one of the most important men in the side and only a serious knee injury kept him out of action.

1028.name: Williams
pages: * Paul Williams is an explosive centre forward who, in recent years, hasn't reproduced the form he showed in previous seasons, due partly to a lack of regular first team football at the clubs he has been playing for. At Southend United however, he seems to be enjoying a new  lease of life, and is once again putting together the types of performances he did a few years ago, which took him into the England "B" side and on the verge of the full international squad.

* Williams is a centre forward who has both great speed as well as a tremendous ability to lose his marker, getting on the blind side of  opposing defenders. He is not a player who has problems in getting in shoots on goal, doing so with either foot, never thinking twice about having a go inside the penalty area. Due to his tremendous speed, if he is allowed too much space, he can quickly creates plenty of  danger. Although he is not a tall player, he is good in the air, placing his headers with power and accuracy. Williams is not just an attacking player, but also does a good defensive job keeping opponents under constant pressure.

* League Cup winners medal with Sheffield Wednesday in 1991.
* First Division winners medal with Crystal Palace in 93-94.
* Topt goalscorer with Charlton Athletic  88-89 and 89-90.

* He signed for Crystal Palace in September 1992. His first game for the Eagles came on 12th September 1992 against Oldham Athletic and he scored his first goals for the south London club against Birmingham City on 31st August 1993.
* He went out on loan to Sunderland in January 1995, making his debut on 21st January 1995 against Notts County.

* Charlton Athletic decided to realease him, so he moved on to sign for Southend United in the summer of 1996.

1029.name: Rammell
pages: * As is the case with Jeroen Boere, Andy Rammell is a classical centre forward, with tremendous power, and who is a genuine nightmare for opposing defenders due to his strength and character. A hard, but always fair player, he has now recovered from the injuries which kept him out of action at the end of last season. Rammell will now be out to force his way into Ronnie Whelan's side, although he is likely to face very stiff competition.

* Rammell is a physically strong and very powerful striker. His main asset is his ability in the air which he takes full advantage of, going up to connect with some superb headers. He fight for every ball and is something of an opportunist although he is not particularly skillful with the ball at his feet. He is not a player who will produce many spectacular moments although he has good positional sense and will have a go at goal without thinking twice. He is not a very quick player but is very dangerous when he gets himself into positions inside the penalty area.
* Top scorer with Barnsley in the 90-91 season together with Andy Saville and also, on his own, in 91-92.
x

* Manchester United signed him from amateur club Atherstone United for £40,000, although he never got to make a first team appearance for the Red Devils.
* In September of 1990 Barnsley signed him for £100,000. He made his league debut on 25th August 1990 against Brighton & Hove Albion and scored his first goal against Blackburn Rovers on 15th August 1990.
* He signed for Southend United in February 1996 in the swap deal that took Dave Regis to Barnsley. He made his debut on 24th February 1996 against Wolverhampton Wanderers and opened his account for the club on 19th March 1996 against Reading.

* Last season he played in 36 games, starting in 26 of those, managing to score 9 times. Although he was the side's top scorer together with Boere, Rammell failed to maintain the form expected of him throughout the season.

1030.name: Boere
pages: * Jeroen Boere is a Dutch striker who is very much a typical centre forward; powerful but uncomfortable with the ball at his feet. However, his technical weaknesses don't prevent him from doing his job to the best of his ability. For all the qualities he bring to the side , he is likely to be the spearhead in the Southend United attack.

* Boere is a physical powerful centre forward who clearly possesses great ability in the air, where he makes the most of his strength. He gets up well above defenders, connecting with accurate powerful headers. With the ball at his feet, he leaves a lot to be desired, although he holds up possession well as he waits for support to come through from the midfield. He is dangerous at dead ball situations, and the special attention he is given by defenders often opens up spaces which his team mates can take advantage of. He is better on his right foot than his left and, when he is given even the slightest of opportunities to get in a shot on goal, he doesn't need to be asked twice.
x
x

* West Ham United signed him from Dutch club Go Ahead Eagles in September 1993 for £250,000. He made his league debut on 25th September 1993 against Newcastle United. He scored his first goal in English football on 4th December 1994 against QPR.
* He went out on loan to Portsmouth in March 1994, he played his first game on 26th March 1994 against Nottingham Forest.
* He was also loaned out to WBA in September 1994, playing his first game for the club on 10th September 1994 against Millwall.
* Crystal Palace signed him in September 1995 for £375,000. He made his debut on 22nd November 1995 against Wolverhampton Wanderers and scored  his first and only goal for the club against Tranmere Rovers on 20th February 1996.  
* He was transfered to Southend United in March 1996 for £150,000. He made his league debut for the club on 2nd March 1996 against Norwich City, and scored his first goal 7 days later against Port Vale.

* Last season he played in 36 games making 27 starting appearances and finding the back of the net 9 times. He was top scorer, and one of the side's most important players, although his contribution wasn't enough to prevent Southend from being relegated.

1031.name: Thomson
pages:
* Andy Thomson had put together some good career statistics with Queen of the South, in his native Scotland, which eventually saw the Southend United coaching staff sign him for the Essex club. However, at Southend he hasn't proved to be as effective, despite his good technical ability.
* He has failed to make himself a key part of the plans of manager Ronnie Whelan who has regularly prefered other strikers to play up front, leaving Thomson on the bench. Nevertheless, he has the ability to convince Ronnie Whelan to put him in the side, or at least, that he is worth a try.

* Thomson is a centre forward who gives everything he has got out on the park, keeping opponents under pressure and maintaining a tremendous work rate. He has good ball control which allows him to carve out his own  goalscoring opportunities. He strikes the ball well with either foot, is a good header of the ball, and also keeps his cool when he is confronted by the opposition goalkeeper. Brave and unselfish, he is always looking to pick out his teammate who is in the most likely scoring position. He has good technical ability and is skillful, with good vision.

* Top scorer with Queen of the South in 90-91, 91-92, 92-93 and 93-94. 
* Top scorer with Southend United in 94-95 together with Gary Jones.
x

* Thomson completed his contract with amateur club Jerviston Boys Club, and signed for Queen of the South in the summer of 1989. He made his league debut on 16th September 1989 against Brechin City and scored his first goal as a professional against East Stirling on 30th September 1989.
* He was transfered to Southend United in July 1994 for £250,000. He played his first game for the club on 13th August 1994 against Millwall and opened his goalscoring account on 30th August 1994 against Portsmouth.

* Last season he made 17 appearances playing in 14 games as a member of the starting line up, and manage to find the back of the net 5 times. His season was affected by injury problems, as was the case with many of his club colleagues. As a result he was unable to really demonstrate what he is genuinely capable of.

1032.name: Gallimore
pages:
* Tony Gallimore was the undisputed left back at Carlisle United, producing a string of performances that made Grimsby Town sit up and take notice, and then opt for signing him after the departure of Gary Croft to Blackburn Rovers. 
* Although he didn't have much time to make people forget the aforementioned Croft, he showed that he has a more than acceptable capability, and that he is fairly complete in every aspect.  His great confidence in his own skills make him a man with a lot of aplomb, possibly the best bet that Grimsby have to cover the left flank.

* Gallimore is a left back with an elegant game on the pitch, and who has a good left allowing him to pass the ball accurately and effectively to his Team-mates. In attack, he is a man who constantly pushes up into enemy territory and who helps out the winger a lot, putting over some good crosses. Solid and safe when making interceptions, he is disciplined and is very cool in his actions and, above all, when under pressure from his rivals.  Fairly quick, perhaps he is lacking a little bit of toughness to earn him more respect from his rivals.
* Third Division Champion in 1995.
x

* Trained in the Stoke City youth squad, Gallimore signs as a professional in July 1990. He makes his league debut on the 21st April 1990 against Blackburn Rovers. 
* He is loaned to Carlisle United in November 1991, playing his first game against Burnley on 5th October 1991. 
* He is loaned to Carlisle United once again in February 1992, playing his first game on the 29th February 1992 against Chesterfield. 
* Finally he departs for Carlisle United in March 1993 for £15,000 making his debut on 27th March 1993 against Doncaster Rovers and he scores his first goal as a professional on 10th April 1993. 
* He is transferred to Grimsby Town in exchange for £125,000 in March 1996. He plays his first game on the 30th March 1996 against Birmingham City and his first goal comes on 6th April 1990 against Stoke City.

* He enjoyed the continuity that he had missed the previous year and showed that he has more than enough capability to occupy a place in the starting eleven at the club. He played 42 league games, 36 of those from the start, and scored a goal.
