1033.name: Donovan
pages:
* Signed for Grimsby Town during the 97-98 season.
* Kevin Donovan's constant, threatening runs down the flank, make him him a player that opposing defenders need to keep a close eye on. However he is a player who comes and goes, both in games as well as throughout the season as a whole, occasionally giving the impression that he is not fully commited. After initially asking for a transfer around the Chirstmas period, he beneffited from the arrival of Ray Harford and went on to continue his run of playing in more than 30 games in each of the last few consecutive seasons.

* Kevin Donovan is a right sided midfield player who, on his day is especially dangerous down that side of the pitch. A very quick player, he possesses good dribbling skills and can often prove to be a real headache for opposing defenders. Nevertheless he is something of an inconsistent performer. He gets into the opposition penalty area well, surprising defenders by coming late from deep positions. He is a good accurate crosser of the ball, and possesses a reasonable shot on goal. He can also perform in the middle of the midfield.
x
x

* After coming through the youth ranks at Huddersfield Town, Donovan signed as a professional in October 1989. He made his debut in the league on 13th March 1990 against Crewe Alexandra, while he scored his first goal for the club on 29th September 1990 against Chester City.
* In February 1992 he was loaned out to Halifax Town, playing his  first game for the club on 15th February 1992 against Wrexham. 
* He was transfered to WBA in October 1992 for £25,000. He made his debut on 10th October 1992 against Burnley, and scored his first goal for the club on 24th October 1992 against Rotherham United.

* The season didn't start particularly well for Kevin Donovan, with his appearances in the side proving to be very few and far between, without any real continuity. He even asked for a transfer, around Christmas time, although, following the arrival of Ray Harford, his situation improved considerably, playing more much more frequently. In total he played in 32 games.

1034.name: Burnett
pages: * Wayne Burnett is a midfield player who was hardly given a chance to show what he could do at the two most competitive clubs where he has played, Blackburn Rovers and Bolton Wanderers. Despite that, he hasn't let his head drop and with his arrival at Huddersfield Town he will once again be feeling optimistic about his future. Although he is a very classy midfielder his tendancy to go missing from games is one of his biggest weaknesses, having long spells where he drifts out the action. If he manages to put this problem right then he will almost certainly make himself a key man in Brian Horton's team.

* Burnett is a midfield player who possesses finely tuned ability. He has good dribbling ability and is comfortable on either foot although he is basically right footed. He shows greattouch in his passing, either long or short, with the inside or the outside of the foot. Quick in his movements he is clever at getting out of tight situations, again taking full advantage of his fantastic ability on the ball. He seldom has a shot on goal nor does he push forward to support the attack with great regularity.
x
x

* A Leyton Orient youth product he signed professional in November 1989. He made his league debut on 24th April 1990 against Crewe Alexandra.
* He was transfered to Blackburn Rovers in August 1992 for £90,000 but never got the chance to make his debut for the Ewood Park club.
* Afeter just one season at Rovers, he signed for Plymouth Argyle in August 1993, making his debut on 14th August 1993 against Stockport County while he managed to score his first goal as a professional against Hull City on 11th December 1993. 
* Bolton Wanderers signed him for £100,000 in November 1995. His only game for the club came on 27th December 1995 against Leeds United. 
* He was loaned out to Huddersfield Town in September 1996, a loan spell which became a permanent deal in exchange for £150,000.

* Shortly after the start to the season Wayne Burnett was signed by Huddersfield Town from Bolton Wanderers where he had made just one first team appearance. He did an excellent job for the Terriers playing in a total of 33 games, making himself a regular in Brian Horton's line up. However his tendency to go missing in games saw him substituted in a good many of the games in which he played.

1035.name: Smith
pages:
* Signed for Grimsby in 1997.
* David Smith is a player who hasn't enjoyed too many opportunities or, to be more precise, continuuity, to allow him to show what he can do for WBA. In previous seasons he had to be prepared to play in almost any position, never being able to settle down, and focus himself on making some genuine progress. He has also recently even come in for some criticism form Albion's supporters. His objective in the present campaign is to repay the faith that Ray Harford showed in him when he made him a regular in the side, although for the moment he will have to settle for a place on the bench, from where, clearly, things can only get better.

* A left back, or left sided midfield player, depending on the circumstances. Smith is very much a left footed player although he is also happy enough with the ball on his right. A quick, attack minded player he likes to constantly get up and down the flank, going past defenders and, if he can, getting crosses over into the strikes. He has good dribbling skills and is a very direct player, although he is weaker defensively.
x
* He has made 10 under-21 international appearances for England. He made his debut in the Toulon International Tournament against Mexico on 5th June 1988.

* After learning his trade in the youth ranks at Coventry City, he signed professional for the club in July 1986. He made his league debut on 6th February 1988 against Manchester United, while he scored his first league goal on  5th March 1988 against Chelsea. From that moment on he became an automatic choice in the side until the end of the 92-93 season when he lost his place.
* He was loaned out to Bournemouth in January 1993, playing just one  game for the club on 30th January 1993, against Port Vale. 
* Smith was eventually transfered to Birmingham City in March 1993 in a swap deal that saw David Rennie move to Coventry City in the opposite direction. He played in his first game for the Blues of Birmingham on 13th March 1993 against Bristol City, while he scored his first goal for the club on 1st May 1993 against Bristol Rovers. 
* WBA signed him in January 1994 for £90,000. Smith made his debut on 1st February 1994 against Grimsby Town.

* David Smith had an up and down season, in which he seldom forced his way into the side under Alan Buckley and had to wait until Ray Harford's arrival at the club. Under Harford's management, he established himself as a regular member of the side and managed to go on to play in 24 games for the club, finding the back of the net twice.

1036.name: Groves
pages:
* Paul Groves is an almost indispensable man and after his contract expired he decided to join WBA. However, his former club wanted £1 million for him. Finally, the tribunal  set the amount at £600,000. 
* Once this mess is sorted out, Groves is presented as an acquisition for the WBA midfield, a man who gets into some dangerous positions and who has a lot of personality, a leader on the pitch who takes part a lot in the team's attacking moves. He will be a man who Alan Buckley will use in his starting eleven.

* A man who plays in the midfield, he is a dominant player, strong and able to rob the ball in defence, pass it on then culminate the move in the other area as he finishes well with either feet or with his head. Quick and powerful, Groves has a great shot with his right although he can also use his left to good effect. He possesses good technique, passes well, but does not stand out for his dribbling or his long range passes, preferring the short ball.
* Top scorer at Grimsby Town in the 92-93 season.
x

* Leicester City signed him from the amateur club Burton Albion in April 1988 for £12,000. In his league debut he scored a goal against Huddersfield Town on 2nd May 1988. 
* In August 1989 he is loaned to Lincoln City and makes his debut in the league competition on 26th August 1989 against Aldershot and his first goal is the winner against Doncaster Rovers on 2nd September 1989. 
* He is transferred to Blackpool in January 1990 for £60,000 and makes his league debut on 3rd February 1990 against Mansfield Town. His first goal in the league competition is the winner for his team in a game against Walsall on the 3rd March 1990. 
* Grimsby Town sign him in August 1992 for £150,000. He plays his first game for the club on 15th August 1992 against Charlton Athletic and his first goals arrive in the form of a hat-trick on 7th November 1992 against Luton Town. 
* In the summer of 1996 he is signed by WBA for £600,000, the price set by tribunal. 
* Paul Groves has the record of having played in every league game disputed by Grimsby Town 4 seasons in a row.

* Groves had an irregular season. During the months that Alan Buckley was manager Groves was one of the normal choices in the starting eleven, but since Ray Harford had taken over at the club, Groves lost his place in the starting line-up. He played 29 league games and scored four goals.

1037.name: Widdrington
pages:
* Tommy Widdrington is the most expensive signing in the history of Grimsby Town, costing £300,000 from Southampton. He is a very strong player who does a good job in front of the defence as a ball-winner but he can't play a constructive role. 
* However, this is not a problem as there are other players at Grimsby Town who can do this job, so Widdrington will be allowed to occupy his normal position doing what he knows best and what he has been signed for. Thanks to his importance in the team, he will be a starter for John Cockerill.

* Widdrington is a defensively minded midfielder who is noted for being a very strong player.  He is a magnificent ball-winner in his zone and his work makes his rivals very uncomfortable. Rather hard, he takes advantage of physical contact to come out on top. He is fast but is not noted for attacking capability. He can also play as a wide defender or even as a sweeper, perhaps his best position.
x
x

* Trained in the lower ranks of Southampton, Widdrington signed as a professional in May 1990.  He makes his league debut on 1st April 1992 against Everton and scores his first goal for the Saints against Chelsea on 27th December 1993. 
* He is loaned to Wigan Athletic in September 1991, playing his first game on 14th September 1991 against Hull City. 
* Finally he is transferred to Grimsby Town in the summer of 1996 in exchange for £300,000, a record transfer for the Mariners.

* Tommy Widdrington was one of Grimsby Town's important men and was a satisfactory substitute for Paul Groves, transferred to WBA. He played 42 league games, 41 of those from the start, and scored four goals.

1038.name: Smith
pages:
* Richard Smith is a central defender who was trained in the youth squad at Leicester City but the club didn't give him many chances and so he spent a lot of time on loan to multiple teams. 
* Now he might have found some peace and calm at Grimsby Town, though the club also has some notable players in the heart of the defence such as Lever and Handyside, who will make things very hard for this player to find a slot in the team except in the case of injuries or suspensions.

* Smith is basically a right-footed central defender. He is fairly quick for a player so bulky. A good marker, his speed allows him to try to anticipate the rival forward. As is normal for a centre back, he is outstanding in the air and, therefore, joins in the attack at set-plays. He is hard when fighting for the ball and very disciplined in his zone. With the ball at his feet he can't really be trusted, but he knows this and so doesn't complicate life unnecessarily.
x
x

* Originally from the lower ranks of Leicester City, he signed as a professional in December 1988. He makes his debut on 3 April 1990 against Oldham Athletic and scores his first goal for the team on the 28th December 1991 against Southend United. 
* He is loaned to Cambridge United in September 1989, playing his first game on the 9th September 1989 against Chesterfield. 
* He is also loaned to Grimsby Town in September 1995. He makes his debut on the 9th September 1995 against Wolverhampton Wanderers. 
* Grimsby Town sign him in exchange for £50,000 in March 1996, playing his first game on the 12th March 1996 against Wolverhampton Wanderers.

* Just has happened to almost all his team mates at the back, Smith spent the most part of the season injured and had to be content with watching his team play from the terrace. He only played in 14 games, 12 of these from the start.

1039.name: McDermott
pages: * John McDermott is a player originally from the youth squad at Grimsby Town, whose consistency and good performance during his time at the club have made him an almost undisputed first choice for the last ten years. We are not talking about a very impressive footballer, but he always does what is asked of him, never disappointing. As a general rule, he will be a regular sight at right back.

* McDermott is a very quick right back who is hard when fighting for the ball. He pushes up the touchline when he has the chance to join in the attack, but he is not someone who scores goals easily, basically being a player who crosses pretty well and who passes the ball effectively.
x
x

* Originally from the lower ranks at Grimsby Town, he signed as a professional in June 1987.  His league debut is on 7th February 1987 against Bradford City. He scored his first goal on the 5th November 1988 against Stockport County.

* Last season he took part in 29 league games, all of them from the start, and scored a goal.  He performed to a high level, both as a marker, and when he joined in the attack, where he became of good complement to the wide midfielders and forwards.

1040.name: Handyside
pages:
* Peter Handyside is a centre back who has risen to the first team from the lower ranks of Grimsby Town, who have one of the best youth squads in the First Division. Handyside has fully benefited from playing alongside the veteran Paul Futcher. 
* Already an under-21 international for Scotland, it is possible that he will take over the baton from players such as Colin Hendrie and Richard Gough amongst others. Also, his outstanding capabilities to play in the centre of defence have made him a target for some powerful teams. 
* For the moment he concentrates on gradually improving as a player and trying to help Grimsby Town survive in the First Division. Handyside will be one of those chosen to form the Mariners' defence.

* Handyside is a right-footed centre back who is very strong, both in the air and on the ground and who is very dangerous at set-plays although he still hasn't managed to take full advantage of his dominance as is shown by his goal tally. He has sufficient technique to play the ball out of defence to the midfield.
x
* An under-21 international for Scotland, he makes his debut on 22nd March 1993 against Iceland. In total, he has played 7 games at this level.
* Originally from the lower ranks of Grimsby Town, he signed as a professional in November 1992.  He made his debut for the team on 30th August 1992 against Birmingham City.

* An injury kept him out for almost all the season, and his absence was sorely felt as the team could not find a solid replacement for him. He only played nine league games, eight of them from the start, and scored a goal.

1041.name: Jobling
pages:
* Things seemed to be going well for Kevin Jobling two years ago when he played 38 games, a player well settled in the team, benefiting from an injury to McDermott which allowed him to play regularly. 
* However, a serious injury at the beginning of last season led not only to an almost null season, but he also lost his automatic choice for the place. Currently, he doesn't figure in the starting line-ups but he could, little by little, and with some work, reach his best form and make a new entrance in the team aligned by John Cockerill.

* Although he is normally aligned as left back, he prefers to play in the midfield. He uses his right foot better than his left, and knows how to get the best out of this situation, especially when he moves down the wing and cuts inside. He fights hard for the ball and has a great sense of positioning on the pitch. As speed is perhaps his most outstanding feature, Jobling is one of the quickest wide defenders in the First Division, as well as being a solid player.
x
x

* Originally from the lower ranks of Leicester City, he signs as a professional in January 1986.  He makes his league debut on 4th April 1987 against Newcastle United. 
* He is transferred to Grimsby Town in February 1988 and plays his first game for the Mariners on 20th February 1988 against Doncaster Rovers. He scores only three days later against Brentford.

* Recovered from the injury that kept him out for the best part of the previous season, Jobling earned the confidence of the manager little by little and played a total of 28 league games, in 24 of which he was a starter.

1042.name: Lever
pages:
* Mark Lever is another product of Grimsby Town's excellent youth squad, who has become one of their best players after his sensational season last year, possibly his best since his debut in 1988. 
* Just as happened with Handyside, he benefited enormously from what he learned playing alongside the veteran Paul Futcher, who converted Lever into an outstanding centre back.  What's more, he has a lot of character on the pitch, a true personality who promises to be one of the pillars at Grimsby Town in the present season.

* Lever is a central defender who plays on the right of the centre of Grimsby's defence, as is safe both in the air and on the ground. What's more, he is a footballer who goes in hard for the ball, taking advantage of his great strength. He never tries intricate things when he has to play the ball out of defence and doesn't get at all nervous when bringing it up to midfield.
x
x

* Originally from the lower ranks of Grimsby Town, he signs as a professional in July 1988.  He makes his league debut on 13th February 1988 against Port Vale and scores his first goal on 17th December 1988 against Leyton Orient.

* Last season he played 21 league games, 20 of those from the start. He enjoyed the full confidence of the coaches, but continual injuries and suspensions prevented him from playing in a larger number of games.

1043.name: Rodger
pages:
* Graham Rodger is a veteran central defender who, in recent times, seems inevitably relegated to the substitutes' bench due to the sensational form of the good young players from Grimsby Town's youth squad such as Handyside and Lever, which is limiting his appearances. 
* Even so, Rodger gives his all when he steps out onto the pitch and shows that he is a very aggressive centre back who makes the forwards' work difficult. In any case, despite being a substitute, this former England under-21 international can show the centre backs a thing or too, as well as trying to change the current situation.

* Rodger is an enormously powerful centre back who is very dangerous at set-plays. Although he is perhaps a little too aggressive on the pitch, he certainly makes his strength count, going in hard for the ball. His great physical bulk leads him into trouble against skilful forwards, who cause him a lot of difficulty. He is not very safe with the ball at his feet although he recognises his limitations and doesn't attempt plays he is aware he cannot complete.
* FA Champion in 1987 with Coventry City.

* England under-21 international, he makes his debut in the International Tournament at Toulon on the 9th June 1987 against the USSR, with an England team that boasted amongst others, Paul Gascoigne, Tony Dorigo, Nigel Clough and Martin Keown. In total, he played 4 games at this level.

* Originally from the lower ranks of Wolverhampton Wanderers, he signed as a professional in August 1983. His only game with Wolves in the league is on 21st April 1984 against Ipswich Town. 
* He signs for Coventry City as a free agent in February 1985 and makes his debut for the team at Anfield against Liverpool on the 9th November 1985 scoring his first goal on 31st August 1987 against Sheffield Wednesday.
* In July 1989 he is transferred to Luton Town for £50,000 making his debut on 14th October 1989 against Aston Villa. He scores his first goal against Coventry City, his former team, on 13th March 1991. 
* In January 1992 he signs for Grimsby Town for £135,000, and plays his first game for the Mariners on 11th January 1992 against Oxford United. His first goal in the league is the Grimsby winner against Watford on 22nd August 1992. 
* He was a member of Coventry City, FA Cup Champion in 1987, who beat Tottenham Hotspur in the final 3-2 after extra-time. Rodger played in the final, coming on as a substitute for the injured Brian Kilcline in the 88th minute of the game.
* The injuries that haunted most of the centre backs at Grimsby allow him to find a place in the starting line-ups. He played 28 games, 27 of those from the start, and scored two goals.

1045.name: Black
pages:
* Kingsley Black is a sensational footballer who, several years ago, was a much talked-about signing for Nottingham Forest, the club who had just acquired the services of a player who could help them to a large extent in their aspirations. 
* However, luck didn't accompany Black and after a good start at the club, his last two years have been a true nightmare as he has hardly played. Frank Clark almost kept him out the team entirely which has cost him his place in the national side of Northern Ireland. 
* This summer he got the chance to relaunch his still unfinished sporting career at Grimsby Town, a club who were interested in a footballer of his talent and who finally acquired his services. Now, with a little bit of continuity with the Mariners, Kingsley Black could make an authoritative come-back and show that he is not a player whose career is over. He will certainly not let his chance go begging.

* Black is a very technically adept left winger who, thanks to his skill, is able to make a lot of good passes, fruit also of his excellent playing vision. A player who has a wonderful left, he plays hugging the touchline and has the ability to set things in motion from there. He is quick and dribbles well, able to put over great crosses dripping quality but is not very strong physically. Very enthusiastic, he gives his all on the pitch.

* League Cup Champion with Luton Town in 1988. 
* Top scorer at Luton Town in the 89-90 season.

* Despite being an English schoolboy international, Black has ended up representing Northern Ireland in the under-21, B and full categories, the latter on 30 occasions, his debut occuring on the 27th April 1988 against France after coming on for Robbie Dennison.

* Originally from Luton Town juniors, Black signed as a professional in July 1986 making his debut on 26th September 1987 against QPR. He scores his first goal against Wimbledon on 3rd September 1988. 
* He is transferred to Nottingham Forest in September 1991 for £1.5 million. He makes his league debut on 7th September 1991 against Sheffield Wednesday and scores his first goal a week later against Wimbledon. 
* He is loaned to Sheffield United in March 1995 and plays his first game for the Blades on 4th MArch 1995 against Port Vale, his first goal coming 3 days later against Tranmere Rovers. 
* He is also loaned to Millwall in September 1995, making his debut on 1st December 1995 against Derby County. 
* He finally signs for Grimsby Town in September 1996.

* Black didn't perform to the level that was expected of him and although he started the season well, his contribution fell away as the championship progressed. He played 24 league games, 19 of these from the start, but didn't manage to score a single goal.

1046.name: Wrack
pages:
* Another product of the Derby County youth squad headed towards Grimsby Town, a club where he will surely have more opportunities to show off his quality than with the Rams. 
* Already with his former team, Wrack was very promising with a capacity for playing football, so it is hoped that he will meet the expectations placed in him. For the moment, this young winger will have to go step by step, and try and continue his progress and become the good footballer his promise indicates he can become.

* Wrack is a player who can be used both as a right wing back and as a right winger, perhaps being more comfortable in the second of these. He is skilful, quick and decisive, something surprising in a footballer his age. During the case Wrack is seen constantly pushing up and dropping back along his touchline, not only attacking but helping the defence a lot, above all with the pressure. He crosses well, supplying his forwards with a good service. A good passer, he has playing vision and a notable shot on goal with his right foot, although he doesn't score so many goals.
x
x

* Trained in the lower ranks of Derby County, he signs as a professional in July 1994.  He plays his first game for the Rams on 31st December 1994 against Sunderland, scoring his first goal for the club on 1st April 1995 against Bristol City. 
* He is transferred to Grimsby Town in the summer of 1996.

* Black had an irregular season, which included a brief loan period to Shrewsbury in February 1997. He disputed 12 matches for Grimsby, five from the start, and scored a goal, while for Shrewsbury he only played four games.

1047.name: Livingstone
pages:
* Steve Livingstone is a centre forward of the old school. He is dominant in the air but has very little technique, although he tries to get round this with a great enthusiasm for his work,  constantly battling with the rival backs. 
* However, despite not being the most skilful of players, this has not prevented him from finishing as Grimsby Town's top scorer, or from being a basic man in Brian Laws schemes.  He now has a difficult task, as he will have to compete with Forester and Woods for a slot in the forward line.

* Livingstone is a very powerful centre forward who is physically very strong and tall, making him very dangerous in the set-plays. Despite his lack of technique, he has a lot of fighting spirit and pressures rival defenders constantly, working hard to block the balls progress. He uses his right a lot better than his left when moving the ball about.
* Top scorer at Grimsby Town in the 95-96 season.
x

* Originally from the lower ranks of Coventry City, he signed as a professional in July 1986, making his league debut on 18th April 1987 against Luton Town, scoring his first goal on the 3rd February 1990 against Chelsea.
* In January 1991 he is transferred to Blackburn Rovers for £450,000. He makes his debut on 19th January 1991 against Ipswich Town opening his account seven days later against Luton Town. 
* The arrival of Kenny Dalglish to the bench at Ewood Park relegates him to ostracism, from which he manages to escape in 1993 when he forms part of a transfer operation that saw Graeme Le Saux go to Blackburn Rovers from Chelsea, the club to which Livingstone moves. The move was set at £350,000. His debut came on 17th April 1993 against Manchester United. 
* In September 1993 Livingstone is loaned to Port Vale for a month, making his debut in the league on 4th September 1993 against Cardiff City.
* In January 1994 he is transferred to Grimsby Town for £140,000 although he had already been there since the month of October 1993 on loan. His league debut is on 30th October 1993 against Crystal Palace, scorinng his first goal on 27th December 1993 against Notts County.
* Last season he played 32 games and scored six goals. The injuries that most of the centre backs suffered forced him to play once in the centre of defence, where he carried out his job acceptably.

1050.name: Jepson
pages: * Jepson is a very hard working forward, both pressuring the rival defence and looking for space, something which makes him uncomfortable to mark for opposing defenders. He fights bravely for the ball. One of his favourite plays is to receive the ball, hold onto it if he is alone and then pass to a midfielder who is arriving from deep. He is not quick but he hides this with good positioning on the pitch. He has a good shot with his right and fires away at the slightest opportunity in the box.

* Top scorer at Exeter City in the 93-94 season.
* Second Division Champion with Bury in the 96-97 season.
x

* His contract with amateur Nantwich Town finishes and he signs for Port Vale in March 1989. He makes his league debut against Chesterfield.
* He is loaned to Peterborough United in January 1990. He plays his first game against Doncaster Rovers and scores his first goal as a professional on 17th February 1990 against Carlisle United.
* Transferred to Preston North End in February 1991, he makes his debut on 16th February 1991 against Huddersfield Town. He scores his first two goals in March against Mansfield Town.
* Exeter City sign him for £60,000 in July 1992. He plays his first game for the team on 15th August 1992 against Rotherham United and scores his first goal on 29th August 1992 against Stoke City.
* Finally he is transferred to Huddersfield Town in December 1993 for £80,000. He makes his debut against Rotherham United and scores his first league goal against Hartlepool United on 27th December 1993.
* He is voted best player of the year 94-95 by the fans at Huddersfield Town.
* After several successful years at Huddersfield Town, he is transferred to Bury in July 1996 in exchange for £40,000. His first game with the club is on 17th August against Brentford, where he manages to score the equaliser.

* Jepson was a good acquisition on the part of Stan Ternent as he was a man used a lot during the course of the season which brought the Shakers to the First Division.  In total, he played 31 games and scored 9 goals.

1054.name: Kelly
pages: * Gary Kelly has made a good impression on the Oldham Athletic supporters, a far from easy task bearing in mind that he had to take over from Paul Gerrard,  the young goalkeeper who moved to Everton this summer. The Irish goalkeeper has tremendous natural ability which makes him more than capable of taking on the responsibility of keeping the Latics' goal intact.

* A keeper with excellent reflexes and good positional sense, Kelly has the disadvantage of being relatively short  for a goalkeeper something which gives him problems in dealing with high balls into the area, preveted him from being dominant in this aspect of the game. He is also occasionally hurried in his actions, causing him to misjudge his movements of his line. Nevertheless, his excellent positional play allows him to make some great saves which prevent plenty of goals. He is also a very brave keeper when he comes out to go down at the feet ofd opposing forwards in 50-50 challenges.
* F.A. Youth Cup winners medal 1985.
* He has made under-21, under-23 and "B" international appearances for the Republic of Ireland.

* Gary Kelly came through the ranks at Newcastle United, making his debut for the Magpies on 20th September 1986 against Wimbledon. 
* He was loaned out to Blackpool in October 1988. He played his first game for the club on 8th October 1988 against Bolton Wanderers. 
* He was transferd to Bury in October 1989 for £60,000, making his debut on 7th October 1989 against Chester. 
* Finally he went out on loan to Oldham Athletic in September 1996. He played his first game on 13th September 1996 against Huddersfield Town. That same month, his move to the Latics became a permanent one in exchange for £50,000. 
* Gary is the son of Alan Kelly, ex-Preston North End and Ireland goalkeeper, and the brother of Alan Kelly who plays in goal for Sheffield United and the Irish national side.
* Kelly was a member of the starting line up in all 42 of the games he played in. As a result he was voted the club's Player of the Year.

1057.name: Hodgson
pages: * An old style central defender, Doug Hodgson is a very competitive player who gives everything he has got out on the park. He wasn't a regular member of the side at Sheffield United, only playing when teammates were either injured or suspended. Although he is not a brilliant defender the enthusiasm he puts into the game makes him a very difficult opponent to get the better of. A brave and courageous player, he will no doubt be battling for a place in the starting line up.

* Hodgson is excellent in the air and, as a result, is also very dangerous at dead ball situations. A hard tackler when he goes in to win the ball, he takes full advantage of his great physical strenght. Technically average, he keeps things as simple as possible, fully aware of his limitations in this aspect of the game. Not particularly quick, he is, perhaps, a little on the slow side, something which gives him problems when he is pulled out from the centre of defence by quick, skillful strikers.
x

* Hodgson was signed from Australian club Heildelberg Alex in July 1994 for £30,000 by Sheffield United, following a game in which he played against the Blades during a club tour of Australia during that summer. He made his debut for the Blades on 22nd October 1994 against Luton Town. 
* He went out on loan to Plymouth Argyle in August 1995. His first game for the club came on 12th August 1995 against Colchester United.

* Hodgson began the season with Sheffield United, where he played in six games before going out on loan to Burnley in October. His spell at Burnley couldn't have been more brief, picking up a neck injury on his debut which forced him to return to Sheffield United, where he played in another 7 games before being transfered to Oldham in February 1997. He finished the season at Boundary Park rather better that he had started it with his previous club. He played in 12 games making 11 starting appearances.

1059.name: Serrant
pages: * Carl Serrant is one of the good young players to have come through the Oldham Athletic youth system in recent years and is a bright prospect of whom the Boundary Park club expects great things. He has the ability to go on to become a fine full back and will be, no doubt one of the most important players for the manager during the course of the season.

* In his first few games, Serrant played at left back although he later moved across to play on the opposite flank. A very quick player he helps out the midfield with his quick tuns down the flank although he still needs to work on some of his weak points such as his crossing. When he finally manages to improve this aspect of his game, he will make himself a much more decisive player. He is a hard player when he is fighting for posession, although his speed allows him to avoid too many physical challenges with strikers, preferring to win the ball through his sense of anticipation. He stands out in the air and this physically strong, a quality which means he can also do a job as an emergency central defender.
x
* An England youth international.

* After coming through the youth ranks at Oldham Athletic, he signed professional in July 1994. He made his league debut on 20th January 1996 against Huddersfield Town, and scored his first goal as a professional against Leicester City on 16th March 1996.
* Last season he played in 40 games, making 34 starting appearances. He was a key man for Oldham throughout the whole of the season and prove himself to be one of the brightest prospect in the squad.

1060.name: McNiven
pages: * One of the sensations of Oldham Athletic, this young Scottish full back has shown, at a very young age, tremendous talent, and, most importantly, enormous potential for the future. Despite his youth, he has put together a number of performances which have surprised everybody at the club. Although he faces stiff competition from Fleming down the right flank, this new product of the Oldham Athletic youth system surely won't take long to make himself a regular member of the side.

* A very quick full back, he constantly makes impressive runs down the flank thorughout the course of the game. Still inexperienced, he needs  to work on some aspects of his game, and occasionally is too eager to get forward and is sometimes erratic with his crosses. He is a good passer of the ball.
x
* McNiven has made youth and under-21 international appearances for Scotland. He made his under-21 debut on 14th November 1995 against San Marino.
* A product of the Oldham Athletic youth system, he made his league debut on 2nd May 1995 against Barnsley.

* He made 12 appearances, 11 of those as a member of the starting line up. He showed some great form whenever he was called up into the side and showed some glimpses which suggested that he has a promising career ahead of him.

1061.name: Redmond
pages: * After 5 seasons with Oldham Athletic, Steve Redmond has shown himself to be an important member of the side his presence in the team is invaluable. His experience and leadership at the heart of the defence make him a key part of the manager's plans. He helps out the less experienced players who have come through the youth system into the first team. If nothing out of the ordinary happens, he will once again be an automatic choice in the Boundary Park's club defence.

* A central defender, his experience gives him tremendous positional sense which helps to make up for his lack of speed. Despite not being particularly tall he is good in the air and is also an excellent tight marker, going in hard but always fairly. He is a very difficult defender to get the better of. Right footed, he is safe with the ball at his feet who not only passes the ball on to his teammates, but occasionally, will even carry it forward himself.
x

* An England youth and under-21 international, he made his under-21 debut on 27th April 1988 against France at Highbury, replacing Martin Keown. The game ended in a 2-2 draw. In the England team that day was Paul Gascoigne. For France, both goals were scored by Eric Cantona.

* After coming through the ranks at Manchester City, he signed professional in December 1984. He made his league debut on 8th February 1986, against QPR and scored his first two league goals against Coventry City on 21st December 1986. 
* In August 1992 he was transfered to Oldham Athletic for £600,000. He made his debut on 15th August 1992 against Chelsea and scored his first goal for the Latics against Swindon Town on 7th December 1993.

* Last season he played in 24 games, scoring twice. He was one of the most important members of the side until a serious knee injury, which he picked up against Manchester City, put him out of action and forced him to undergo two operations.

* He is the cousin of Stoke City player, Larus Sigurdsson.

* He played in 27 league games, making 23 starting appearances, scoring once. He was one of the most important men in the midfield, bringing to the side his tremendous work rate and unselfish attitude.

* Woods is a reliable goalkeeper between the posts, although not so safe when meeting crosses.  Despite being a veteran, he is still agile, which, combined with his great flexibility allows him to stop low shots. His experience helps him in the one-on-ones, perhaps his best virtue. However, Woods doesn't manage much regularity, he switches between great saves and beginners mistakes, making him an unpredictable goalkeeper.

* Scottish League Champion in 1987, 89, 90 and 91.
* Scottish League Cup Champion in 1987,88 and 89.
* Second Division Champion in 1986.
* League Cup Champion in 1978 and 1985.

* English international 43 times.
* On the 16th of June 1985 he makes his full international debut for England. It was in the Colliseum in Los Angeles, in a game against the United States as part of an American tour that the English team was making. His last performance in the international arena was one the 6th of June, 1993, coincidentally against the U.S. team, in Boston.
* He was in the Mexico World Cup Finals in 86 and in Italy in 90, but he didn't play a single minute. In the European Championships in Germany in 88 he played 1 game; and 3 in Sweden in 92.
* Two international B caps.
* Six under-21 international appearances.
* Youth international.

* Woods holds the British record for the longest time unbeaten: as the Rangers keeper he played 1196 minutes without letting in a goal, from the 26th of November 1986 till the 31st of January 1987.
* In March 1978 he becomes the youngest goalkeeper to play in a final at Wembley, in the League Cup Final which his team played against Liverpool. In the twilight of his career, Woods has played part of the 95-96 season on loan at Reading, a First Division club, as he found it hard to get a game with Sheffield.  In fact, the 94-95 season he only played nine times.
* He signs for Nottingham Forest in December 1976, just turned 18. He makes his debut in October 1977 in a League Cup game against Notts County. This season, the recently promoted Forest win the league, although Woods did not participate in any League outings.  However, just as in his debut, the goalkeeper from Boston had played in the League Cup, also won by Forest. The following season, Brian Clough signs Peter Shilton, who is a magnificent teacher for Woods. Chris plays in the first team in the League Cup games from the third round onwards and becomes one of the youngest players to take part in a Wembley final. It was against Liverpool and the match finished 0-0. Woods made a great save from Kenny Dalglish. In the replay, Liverpool beat Forest 2-1. In February 79 he makes his first under-21 international appearance in a game between Wales and England at Swansea.
* Without having made his league debut, he is transferred to Queens Park Rangers in July 1979, where he plays 63 league games. In February 81 he signs for Norwich City, the club where he stays until the summer of 85, the date when he moves north of the border to join Rangers for the price of £600,000. 
* He played 173 League games with Rangers.
* He has been a Wednesday player since the summer of 1991. With this club he played 99 league games up to the 94-95 season. His arrival at Hillsborough was not well received by the Wednesday fans, who considered him to the responsible for the crushing defeats of the team: 6-1 against Leeds, and 7-1 against Arsenal. * Chris Waddle is a sensational player who has such an extraordinary technical foundation that he can do almost whatever he wants. However, the years don't forgive as he now lacks the speed and strength of the his better years when he was a true nightmare for the rival defenders.
* Waddle has a very wide repertoire which makes him an unpredictable man when dribbling and he has a truly magnificent turn, with an amazing flexibility at the waist allowing him to unsettle the best defences. His passes are very accurate, either in short or long range, up to 40 or 50 metres switching wings. He can use either the inside or outside of the foot with equal efficiency.
* His aerial game should not be neglected although it does not form an important part of his armoury. His playing vision and intelligence are a lot more significant on the pitch, where he seems to know what to do in every instant. He has a great shot on goal with the left although the right isn't so bad either for a left-footed player. His free-kicks, accurate and powerful, are very good and the same goes for the corners, either to the near or far post.
* Physically he is not so good these days so he saves himself for the attacks, and hardly helps out at all in defence. However, he is a strong player and usually comes out on top in a collision although he prefers to make his technique count. Furthermore, he is not selfish in front of goal and if he sees a team mate in a better position he will pass to him.

* He was transfered to Luton Town in March 1998. 
* For many supporters, the sight of Simon Davies moving forward with the ball under control, reminds them, inevitably, of Ryan Giggs, something which says a lot about one of the members of the latest wave of players to come through the Old Trafford youth system. This similarity between the two players is a real source of pride to Davies, who is also well on the way to sharing a good many years alongside Giggs in the Welsh national side. Still very young but blessed with a magical talent, the future of Manchester United will depend upon the feet of Simon Davies.

* A skillful midfield player with great technique. Despite his youth Simon Davies shows great class in everything he does. He possesses great vision, superb contro,l and is an accurate passer of the ball. He is also very quick and has great reserves of stamina, all of these qualities making him a very fine footballer. Blessed with genuine attacking flair, he is a player who is destined to become a big name in English football over the course of the next few years.
* F.A. Youth Cup Winners medal  91-92.
* 1 full international appearance for Wales. He made his debut in 1996 in a game against Switzerland.

* Simon Davies has been a professional since 6th July 1992. Up to that date he had enjoyed a succesful career in the youth set up at Manchester United, eventually being named captain of the youth team. On the day of his league debut however, he wasn't wearing a Manchester United shirt but an Exeter City one, having been sent out on loan to the Devon club on 17th December 1993. He made his debut the following day against Brentford. 
* Back at Old Trafford he played his first game for Manchester United on 19th November 1994, in a 3-0 victory against  Crystal Palace.
* During the 94-95 season he managed to find the back of the net against Turkish club Galatasaray in the Champions League.

* Probably the highlight of last season for Simon Davies was his full international debut for Wales in a game against Switzerland. At United he wasn't given too many opportunitues by Alex Ferguson. In fact, he made just one starting appearance all season. The rest of his appearances in the first team, a total of 6, came as substitute. As a result Davies ended up making less of a contribution than he had the previous season.

1256.name: Nethercott
pages: * Signed for Millwall in March 1998. Trained in the lower ranks of Tottenham Hotspur, Stuart Nethercott is the natural replacement for men of the stature of Gary Mabbutt and Colin Calderwood.  However, the extended career of both of them, above all that of the Spurs' captain, prevents Nethercott from consolidating his position in the centre of the Spurs' defence.

* A very competitive central defender.  His winning character pushes him on, always playing to the limit of his capability thus overcoming his technical shortcomings that he should try and correct.  His aerial game is very powerful in both areas, in fact he usually joins in the attack at free-kicks and corners and, sometimes, scores spectacular goals with his head.  He operates well in any position in the centre of defence and stands out for his long-range pass, helped by his powerful kick, able to send the ball from area to area bringing plenty of danger to the rival box.  He is not a very accurate player, and could contribute more to the attacking game if he mastered the ball better and was more accurate in his passes.  He is young and should progress.
* Youth Cup Champion 89-90.
* 8 under-21 international appearances for England.

* He started at Tottenham as an apprentice in July 1989, turning professional two years later, on the 17th of August 1991.  Loaned to Maidstone United on the 5th of September of this same year, he makes his debut in the league against Scunthorpe two days later.  In this same season he is loaned again, this time to Barnet in January 1992. 
* Up until the end of the 94-95 season he had just received one yellow card in his entire career.

* He didn't have many chances to play due to the presence of Scales and Campbell.  Even so, in the few opportunities he had to intervene he caught the eye of the England under-21 team selector who called him up several times.

1257.name: Gray
pages:
* He was transfered to Millwall during the 97-98 season.
* After several years outside England, playing in teams as different as Atletico Marbella in the Spanish Second Division or the Scottish Falkirk, Andy Gray had been signed for Bury in the summer to join in this year's project.

* Andy Gray is a midfielder who operates in the centre of the pitch, contributing a lot of battling spirit to the team. He doesn't stop running for the whole 90 minutes and is a ferocious enemy for the rivals. He has a good shot from a distance and is sure when taking penalties, although he is not noted for his elegance but rather his power when converting them. 
* At the beginning of the season, Stan Ternent has placed him behind the centre backs as a sweeper, a new position for him, but he hopes to do his best in his new role.

* Runner-up in the FA Cup in 1990 with Crystal Palace. 
* Zenith Data Systems Cup Champion in 1991 with Crystal Palace.

* Gray has been an international only once, in a vital qualifying game for the European Championships in Sweden in 1992. Surprisingly, the English manager at the time, none other than Graham Taylor, played him from the start when he was lacking significant international experience, and the stakes were very high. The game was played in Varsovia on 13th November 1991. In the same game Andy Sinton and Tony Daley made their debuts. A sensational goal from Gary Lineker allowed the English team to come away with a draw and reach the final stages. 
* He was also an under-21 international for his country twice.

* Signed from the amateur team Dulwich Hamlet, Gray joins Crystal Palace in November 1984. His first game with the Eagles is on 9th December of this same year against Cardiff City and he scores his first goal on the following week against Grimsby Town. 
* He signs for Aston Villa in November 1987. He makes his debut with the Villains on 28th November 1987 against Bradford City and scores his first goal for the Birmingham team on 1st January against Hull City. 
* His next destination is QPR in February 1989, staying with them for that season. His first game is on 11th February against Millwall and he scores his first goal against Manchester United on 8th May, and finishes the game with two. 
* He returns to his first professional club, Crystal Palace, in August 1989. In his second spell his first game is on 4th August against his former team, QPR, and he scores his first goal against Sheffield Wednesday on 25th November. 
* Still in London, he moves northwards to Tottenham Hotspur in February of 1992. He makes his debut for Spurs on 7th March against Leeds United and has to wait until 11th April to score his first goal. 
* He is loaned to Swindon Town during 1992. His first game with the team is on 9th January against Oxford United. 
* Gray decides to try his luck in Spanish football and signs for Atletico Marbella, the team where he stays until 1996. 
* Last season he played for the Scottish season Falkirk, the team he leaves to sign for Bury at the beginning of this season.
* He spent last year at the Scottish team of Falkirk and performed notably, contributing his experience and know-how on the pitch. He played 18 games and scored 1 goal.

* Sheffield United signed him from Australian club Adelaide, in July 1994 for 250,000 pounds. He made his debut on 27th August 1994 against Notts County while he scored his first two goals for the Blades against Bolton Wanderers on 10th April 1994.
* He was transfered to Crystal Palace in March 1994 together with David Tuttle, in a deal which also saw Gareth Taylor move in the opposite direction to Sheffield United. He made his league debut on 12th March 1996 against Tranmere Rovers.
* Veart scored the goal in a third round F.A. Cup replay which knocked out Arsenal in January 1996 at Bramall Lane home of Sheffield United.

* Carl Veart's excellent performances soon won over the Selhurst Park supporters. He scored nine goals during the course of the season, six of those in the league. However, he was surprisingly relegated to the substitutes bench in the play offs by manager Steve Coppell.

1274.name: Wilkinson
pages: * After several years making pilgrimages from team to team, Paul Wilkinson returns to the maximum category of English football. Without doubt his experience will be an important contribution to the team trained by Danny Wilson. However, the arrival of the Macedonian, Georgi Hristov, threatens his chances of being present in the starting line-ups. Paul will have to extract the best from himself and show that he still has the necessary quality to play in the Premier League.

* Wilkinson is a centre forward whose best weapon is the header, an aspect of his game which allows him to get the most out of his sense of anticipation. He is very hard working, fights constantly with the rival defence.Technically, he is limited, but makes up for these shortcomings with commitment and experience. He is able to shield the ball well when he has his back to the goal, hiding it from the rivals while he waits for his team mates to join in the attack. At the slightest opportunity he tries out his shot on goal.

* League Champion with Everton in the 86-87 season. 
* First Division Champion with Middlesborough in the 94-95 season.
* Charity Shield Medal in 86.
* 4 under 21 international appearances for England. He made his debut on 25th March 1985 in a game against the Republic of Ireland.

* Trained in the youth squad at Grimsby Town, Wilkinson signs as a professional in November of 1982. His debut with the club can not be bettered.
* He is transferred to Everton in March 1985 in exchange for £250,000. He plays his first game with the Toffees against Southampton, coming on as a substitute for Paul Bracewell, and his first goal comes against Everton's archenemy, Liverpool, giving his team the victory on 23rd May 1985. 
* Nottingham Forest decide they need his services and sign him in March of 1987 for £200,000. He makes his debut on 28th March 1987 against Manchester United and scores his first goal with the Nottingham team on 5th September 1987 against Chelsea. 
* He is transferred to Watford in August of 1988 for £300,000 pounds. He plays in his first game against Birmingham City and scores his first goal against Crystal Palace on 3rd September 1988. 
* Middlesborough take an interest in him and pay £550,000 for Wilkinson in August of 1991.  He makes his league debut on 17th August 1991 against Millwall and scores his first goal one week later against Ipswich Town.
* He is loaned to Oldham Athletic in October 1995. His first game is on 28th October 1995 against Derby County and he manages to score against Port Vale on 5th November 1995. 
* He is loaned to Watford in December 1995, making his debut on 12th December 1995 against Millwall. 
* He is also sent on loan to Luton Town in March of 1996, making his debut against Ipswich Town. 
* He has been a Barnsley player since 19th of July 1996 costing £250,000. He makes his debut on the 17th of August of the same year. Barnsley won at West Bromwich Albion by 1-2. On the 25th of August he scores his first goal with the Tykes, against Huddersfield Town at Oakwell Ground. 
* During the course of his career he has been top goalscorer with his team four times. In 1985 with Grimsby Town, sharing the honours with Kevin Drinkell, in 1990 and 1991 with Watford and in 1993 and 1994 with Middlesborough

* In his first season at Oakwell Ground, Paul Wilkinson justified the faith placed in him by those who advised his signing. The former Middlesborough striker formed an excellent attacking partnership with John Hendrie, another former Boro player. Paul played in 45 league games, all of these from the start, and also scored 9 goals.

* Chris Day is a footballer with a great future ahead of him, and, if he maintains his progress, could well become a candidate to play in goal for the full England side. Although he learnt his trade in the youth ranks at Tottenham Hotspur, the tremendous form, first of Erik Thorsvedt and then Ian Walker, made it impossible for him to  make the breaktrhough into the first team. 
* He had to move on to Crystal Palace in order to get the opportunity of regular first team football. To  some extent he was signed by Palace as a stand in for Nigel Martyn, although his departure to Leeds United  opened the way up for him to take over as the club's regular number one goalkeeper.
* Nevertheless his move to the Eagles wasn't a completely smooth one, and had to go to an F.A. tribunal to decide upon the fee. Although fortunately everything was sorted out and Chris Day was able to get his opportunity to play first team football.

* Day is a very complete goalkeeper who shows great maturity out on the park. He is dominant in the air, an area of the game in which he shows tremendous security, although he is occasionally indecisive and prefers to stay on his line rather than misjudge crosses into the box. He also possesses great reflexes which allow him to make some sensational saves.

1438.name: Beardsley
pages:
* He was loaned to Fulham in March 1998.
* As a sportsman, Peter Beardsley is a champion of good football, the sort that is constructed around good players.  Now, the Bolton fans are the ones fortunate enough to enjoy the text-book football of this illustrious veteran.  Without doubt, he will be a reference for all the components of the squad, both on and off the pitch.

* Peter Beardsley is a footballer of exceptional class.  In the first years of his career he played as a forward, where his speed and skill made him hard to stop.  With the passing of the years his game has matured, he has perfected his individual technique and learnt to read the games to set the appropriate rhythm.  Currently, he plays as a link-man, operating between lines easily when he receives the ball, controlling it well helped with his good technique with both feet he dispatches measured passes to his team-mates or invents a play, penetrating the rival defence before having a dig. Unpredictable and creative, he has a lot of resources for making the breakthrough.  He makes up for the logical loss of speed with the passing of the years with the knowledge which experience brings. 
* Good at taking free-kicks and sure of himself from the penalty spot, he is capable of scoring a good number of goals each season.  Also when the ball is in play, he is able to find space to have a go with either foot. When shooting he always aims to make his technique and skill count rather than brute force.

* League Champion in 87-88 and 89-90. 
* FA Cup Champion 88-89. 
* Charity Shield Medal 88, 89 and 90.

* 57 full international appearances for England.  8 goals.  He made his debut coming on for Gary Lineker during a game which England won 4-0 against Egypt in Cairo on the 26th of January 1986.  His first goal for his country was on the 17th of May 1986 in a game against Mexico played in Los Angeles.
* He played in the Mexico 86 and Italy 90 World Cups.  In Mexico he played 4 games against Portugal, Poland, Paraguay and Argentine, scoring a goal against Paraguay.  In Italy he played five games against the Republic of Ireland, Egypt, Cameroon, Germany and the host nation itself. 
* He also played two games in the Germany 88 European Championship against the Republic of Ireland and Holland. 
* 3 B-international appearances.

* He took his first steps in the footballing world in the ranks of the modest Walsend Boys Club.  As a free agent, he is signed by Carlisle United on the 9th of August 1979.  On the 21st of this month he makes his debut in a game against Blackburn Rovers. 
* After three seasons at Brunton Park, he is transferred to the Vancouver Whitecaps on the 1st of April 1982 for £275,000.  An unsettled phase of his career starts.  On the 9th of this same year Manchester United acquire his services for £300,000, but in March 1983 he returns to Vancouver. 
* His first spell at Newcastle United, the team of his hometown, starts on the 23rd of September 1983.  His asking-price had dropped considerably, so much so that the club at St. James Park only paid £150,000 for his move, but Arthur Cox, the then manager of the club, was confident about his game.  The following day he made his debut for Newcastle in a game against Barnsley.  Shortly afterwards, on the 19th of October he scores his first goal for the Magpies against Cardiff City. 
* Alongside Keegan he forms a devastating strikeforce.  In one season Beardsley scores 20 goals and Keegan 27. 
* His good performances, both for Newcastle and for the England team arouse the interest of several clubs.  After playing in the Mexico 86 World Cup and turning in a good 86-87 season for his team, he is finally transferred to Liverpool for £1.9 million.  The date was the 24th of July 1987. 
* After four seasons, two league titles, one FA Cup triumph and 46 goals for Liverpool, he moves to the team's sworn rival, Everton, on the 5th of August 1991.  The transfer fee is set at £1 million. 
* At Goodison Park it seems that his career experiences a slight period of stagnation and after two seasons he returns to Newcastle, who pay £1.4 million to bring him back.  He scores 21 goals in the league on his return and is the team's second top scorer after Andy Cole. 
* In the 94-95 season he scores 13 league goals and 2 in the UEFA Cup, and this time he is the team's top marksman. 
* A very noble footballer, during his career he has only seen 5 yellow cards. In this same period he has scored 5 hat-tricks, the first of which is on the 29th of October 1983 against Manchester City.  The last is one the 30th of October 1993, against Wimbledon.  In between, Sunderland, Manchester United and Coventry have been on the receiving end of Peter Beardsley's marksmanship. 
*  He is known as "Peter Pan" or "Pedro". 
* After becoming one of Newcastle's most celebrated players, Beardsley was transferred to Bolton on the 18/8/97 for £450,000.

* Once more Beardsley showed that he is one of the best professionals in the Premier League.  When he played he gave his all and when he was confined to the bench he didn't look to cause problems and accepted Keegan's decisions. Beardsley took part in 25 games and scored 5 goals.

1439.name: Brazier
pages:
* Signed for Fulham in March 1998. 
* Matthew Brazier is a strong midfielder, though not without good technical ability, his chances of making himself a regular in the side this season are greater, as a result of the fine peformances he put together last time out.

* Brazier is a player who plays in the middle of the midfield, and who possesses good physical attributes. A very dynamic player, he plays a good short passing game. He is not just a good player, technically, but also also wins back plenty of possession for the side and is a hard player when he goes in to win the ball. However he lacks a powerful shot and needs to be slightly more selfish if he wants to make more of the chances that come his way.
x
x
* A product of the QPR youth systen, Brazier signed as a professional in July 1994. His first game for the club came on 28th October 1995 against Nottingham Forest.

* Last season Brazier managed to settle down as a regular in Stewart Houston's side for a large part of the season. It proved to be an outstanding season for this young player who showed that he has an eye for a goal, managing to find the net twice in the 27 games in which he played.

1440.name: Collins
pages: * Wayne Collins turned professional aged 24.  At this age most footballers have four seasons under their belts.  However, the progress of this player has been pretty interesting.  In just three seasons he has made the step up from the Second Division to the Premier League, moving from Crewe Alexandra to Sheffield Wednesday.  Last season an inopportune injury halted his meteoric rise.  But, used to fighting, Wayne will once again try to make a name for himself at the top level of English football.

* Although he has played most of his career at left half, in recent times he has shown his capacity to play at right back.  Collins is a quick footballer who covers a lot of ground.  He has a marked attacking vocation, which leads him to neglect his responsibility for winning the ball back at times.  Dynamic and generous in the effort he puts in, he has a good shot and doesn't hesitate to try it out at the slightest opportunity.
x
x

* Originally from Winsford United, he signed for Crewe Alexandra on the 29th of July 1993.  His price was set at £10,000. 
* He made his debut on the 14th of August 1993, with a 0-2 win in the side's visit to Preston North End.  On the 25th of September of this year he scores his first goal as a professional against Torquay United. 
* He finishes the 94-95 season as Crewe Alexandra's top scorer with 11.
* In the summer of 1996 he is transferred to Sheffield Wednesday for £600,000. 
* He made his debut in the Premier League on the 17th of August 1996, in a game against Aston Villa played at Hillsborough (2-1).  On the 19th of February 1997 he scored his first goal against Derby County.

* He started the season as a starter in David Pleat's line-ups and even enjoyed seeing the team top of the table.  Unfortunately an injury cut short his seemingly unstoppable rise and kept him out until December. But once recovered physically it was impossible for him to regain his place in the side and he had to be content with sporadic appearances.

1441.name: Trollope
pages:
* Signed for Fulham in November 1997.
* Last season Paul Trollope showed that he had progressed enough to perform in the Premier League. His versatility allows him to adapt to playing in different positions, a condition that makes him a particularly valuable player for the coaches.

* A very versatile midfielder, he can play in different positions. From the position of centre half he is able to organise and distribute the team's play, helped by his vision and passing accuracy. However, he is also effective in ball-winning tasks and even as a marker. Still very young, he needs to gain some experience and trust in his abilities.
x

* 1 full international appearance for Wales. 
* Trollope made his debut on the 27th of May 1997, against Scotland. In the same game, Christian Dailly, a team mate of his at Derby County, was making his debut for Scotland.

* Paul is the son of John Trollope, the former player who has made the most number of appearances for Swindon in the whole of their history.
* He was trained in the youth squad at Swindon. On the 23rd of December 1989 he signed his first professional contract. However, he never got to make his league debut with the first team. 
* On the 26th of March 1992 he signed for Torquay United, where he became an undisputed starter. 
* On the 16th of December 1994 he was transferred to Derby County for £100,000. He made his debut the following day, with victory over Barnsley (1-0) at the Baseball Ground. 
* On the 30th of August 1996 he was loaned to Grimsby Town, defending their colours in 7 games. 
* On the 11th of October of the same year he was loaned once again, this time to Crystal Palace. He played in 9 games, but did so as substitute in all of them.

* Paul Trollope made his debut in the Premier League at the end of January and managed to find a place in the Derby County line-ups until the end of the season. Previously he had been loaned on two occasions to First Division teams: to Grimsby Town in August and Crystal Palace in October. His excellent performance lead him to make his first appearance for the full Welsh national team, in a friendly against Scotland played in May.

1442.name: Selley
pages: x

* A physically powerful midfielder, and a good man-to-man marker, Ian Selley stands out for his ball winning ability. A hard working player, he covers plenty of ground, constantly supporting his teammates. Though blessed with good vision, he lacks a good shot at goal and does not bring much to the team in an attacking sense.

* European Cup-Winners-Cup winners medal 1994.
* F.A. Cup winners medal 19943.
* League Cup winners medal 1993.

* Three times an England under-21 international.
* Twice an England youth international.

* Ian Selley began to learn his trade as a footballer with Surrey County before moving on to form part of Arsenal's youth ranks. On 6th May 1992 he turned professional and made his debut on 12th September that same year against Blackburn Rovers.
* In his first season in the first team he won an FA Cup winners medal and a League Cup winners medal.
* In February 1995, during a game against Leicester City at Highbury, Selley suffered a broken leg. His recovery took a more than a year, not being able to play in a single game during the 1995-96 season.
* Having recovered from the broken leg suffered in 1995, Ian Selley was loaned out to Southend United in december in an effort to help re-establish him.

1443.name: Taylor
pages: * Ray Clemence, the mythical Liverpool keeper, said that Maik Taylor was one of the most promising goalies in England.  Graeme Souness, probably on the advice of his former Liverpool team-mate, decided to sign him in January 97.  He arrival was a great help as it contributed to a new serenity in Southampton's defence. However he was transfered to Fulham in November 1997.
* Secure on the line and with excellent positioning, Taylor is a pretty complete keeper who transmits calmness to the defence.
x
x

* Trained at Barnet, Mark Taylor has gone from being a Third Division goalie to rubbing shoulders with the cream of English football in a very short space of time.
* In January 97 Southampton pay Barnet £500,000 for Taylor.  He makes his debut in the Premier League for the Saints on the 11/1/97 in the Riverside Stadium against Middlesbrough (0-1). 
* He was transfered to Fulham in November 1997.

* He produced some excellent performances.  First he played 25 games for Barnet, keeping a clean sheet in 13 of these.  This caught Southampton's eye and they signed him in January.  With the team at the Dell he played in 18 games transmitting a lot of calmness to the defence.

1445.name: Coleman
pages:
* He was transfered to Fulham in March 1998. 
* The first thing that is immediately noticeable about Chris Coleman is his imposing physical presence which gives him the look of a top class athlete. Undernead this appearance there lies a good footballer, a specialist in defensive responsibilities, but also capable of scoring goals relatively frequently. Unfortunately, an injury last season prevented him from settling down in the side, although now, under the guidance of Roy Hogson he will be hoping that luck is on his side.

* Blessed with outstanding athletic ability, Chris Coleman is a strong,  powerful central defender, and, is a tight marker with good pace. Left footed, he can also play in the left back position, from where he sends over good accurate crosses to the forwards. Occasionally he has also played at tight back. A good ballwinner, he is effective when it comes to stopping the other team from playing the football they want. He moves  forward to support the attack, causing some dangeur at dead balls situation taking full advantage of his power in the air and his heading ability.

* Welsh Cup Winners medals 89 and 91. 
* First Division winners medal 94.

* 17 full international appearances for Wales. He made his debut in a friendly game against Austria, scoring Wales' equalizer.
* 3 under-21 international appearances.
* Youth and schoolboy international.

* Born in Swansea,he tried his luck with the junior side at Manchester City before returning to Wales in June 1987 to play for Swansea City. He made his debut on 15th August 1987 in a game against Stockport County. Two weeks later, on 1st September, he signed professional terms. As an automatic first choice, Chris Coleman won two Welsh Cups with his home town club, in 1989 and 1991.
* On 19th July 1991 he was transfered to Crystal Palace for 275,000 pounds. His signing caused something of a surprise, since the London club already had both Paul Bodin and Richard Shaw to cover the left back spot. However it was eventually Lee Sinnot who made himself first choice in the position. Throughout his time with the London club he was continually  up and down between the Premier League and the First Division. He formed the partnership, eventually, with Richard Shaw at the heart of the defence and also settle down in the Wales national side.
* He began the 95-96 season with Crystal Palace, but he was transfered to Blackburn Rovers on 16th December 1995 for 2,800,000 pounds. Coleman arrived at Ewood Park to cover for the absence of the injured Graeme Le Saux. 
* In the 95-96 season he became, for all the wrong reasons, the star of the game between Switzerland and Wales, scoring an own goal, giving away a penalty and also ending up injured.
* At the beginning of the 96-97 season he suffered an achilles tendon injury which kept him out of action until the end of the season.

* He began last season as a regular member of the side, lining up on the right hand side of the Blackburn defence. However a serious achilles tendon injury forced him onto the sidelines for the rest of the season. Up to that point he had played in 8 league games.

1446.name: Brevett
pages:
* He was transfered to Fulham during the 97-98 season.
* Rufus Brevett is a player who is currently enjoying the best spell of his career, and last year wais one of the most regular member of Stewart Houston's side.

* An extremely quick full back who can play both at left back as well as on the left hand side of midfield. He is quite a complete player who is very difficult to beat for speed. His forrays into the opposing half of the field often create plenty of danger as the opposition attempt to contain his tremendous pace which is well backed by his direct approach to the game. Nevertheless he lacks the confidence to have a shot at goal or to take on the goalkeeper, almost always prefering to play the ball off to a teammate. An aspect of his game which he should really try to work on is his crossing, which fails to create any real danger for goalkeepers and defenders.
x
x

* After coming through the ranks at Doncaster Rovers he signed professional in July 1988. He made his league debut on 29th August 1987 against Sunderland, while his first goals, one of which was a penalty, came on 26th December 1990 against  Maidstone United. 
* He was transfered to Queens Park Rangers in February 1991 for £250,000. He made his league debut on 23rd March 1991 against Tottenham Hotspur and scored his first goal for Rangers on 30th March 1996, against Southampton.

* Brevett had a sensational season, last time out, missing just 2 out of a possible 46 games, being outstanding at the back. However, he also managed to improve other aspects of his game as the season went on, and over the duration of the whole campaign proved to be one of QPR's most outstanding players.

1447.name: Neilson
pages: * Signed for Fulham in November 1997.

* He usually plays as a central defender, although he has also played at right back at times.  He has an acceptable technique, which means he can play the ball out from defence with quick short passes.  Good in the air, he is hard get the better of in defence and, at times, he joins in the attack at set-plays where his headers create a certain amount of danger.  However, he doesn't usually stand out in attacking tasks.  Reasonably quick for someone of his bulk, this speed allows him to play as a wide defender, although it is obvious that he thinks more about defending than attacking. In any case, thanks to his good playing vision, Alan Neilson should be used more in attacking moves.
x

* 5 international appearances for Wales.
* 2 B-international appearances.
* 7 under-21 international appearances.

* Although he was born in Germany in 1972 he trained as a footballer in the Newcastle United youth squad.  A professional since the 11th of February 1991, he makes his debut in the league on the 9th of March of this year against Watford.
* A Welsh international, he wasn't used much by the Magpies' trainer, Kevin Keegan, and so he is transferred to Southampton in the summer of 1995 for £500,000.  He makes his debut for the Saints on the 26th of August of this same year, coming on for Gordon Watson in the second half of a game which Southampton eventually lose to Everton at Goodison Park (2-0).
* Up until the end of the 94-95 season he had received 2 yellow cards.

* He started the season as the first choice right back, but the changes made by the manager to the back line before arriving at the ideal combination meant he had to spend some time on the bench.  Alan shone in attack and was the man who set up Ostenstad for the winner against Sunderland, a goal which saved Southampton's skin.  Neilson was also called up by the Wales team.

1448.name: Watson
pages: x

* A left footed player, he does a fine job for the side in the left back position, as well as when he's pushed further forward as a left sided midfielder. Characterised by the forcefulness of his play, he shows himself to be particularly dangerous at dead ball situations.
x
x
x

* Paul Watson was one of the most important members of the Fulham side, maintaining a high level of performance throughout the course of the season despite being used in a number of different positions. He played in a total of 44 league games all as a member of the starting line up. He also managed to put his name on the scoresheet three times .

1449.name: McGuckin
pages: x

* A man of great character, Ian McGuckin imposes himself on the game from his central defensive position. Strong and powerful, he stands out for the forcefulness he shows in the air. Although he is occasionally too impulsive his presence out on the pitch is almost always a guarantee of security.
x
x
x

* Managed to make only 22 appearances last season, a knee injury forcing him to miss out for a large part of the season. In the games he played he did a fine job and was very much the focal point at the heart of the central defence for Hartlepool.
